records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in collaboration with entities like Petroleum Development Oman (PDO), OQ, and...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in collaboration with entities like Petroleum Development Oman (PDO), OQ, and the Oman Agriculture Development Company, has accelerated an integrated suite of smart agronomical and afforestation initiatives designed to curb carbon emissions across the country's plant, livestock, and aquaculture sectors. Driven by advanced technological transitions—such as AI-based precision fertilization systems that minimize input waste and pollution—the ministry has deployed and monitored multiple sustainability projects targeted at carbon sequestration, organic fertilizer production, and blue carbon ecosystems. Key structural developments include targeted commercial fruit and forestry initiatives—such as the OQ Green project, the cultivation of carbon-capturing hackberry trees, and expansive lemon and jojoba plantations across Shalim and Al Wusta designed to combat desertification while drastically boosting domestic fruit yields. Additionally, specialized research at the Animal Production Research Centre has successfully optimized livestock feed efficiency using local moringa and palm resources, lowering production costs by over 58% to harmonize national agricultural expansion with long-term climate sustainability targets.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the Food...
records.description: The Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), has conducted a specialized technical training program for 18 female livestock farmers in the town of Yabroud. Financed by the European Union under the broader "Strengthening the Skills and Practices of Livestock Breeders at All Stages of the Animal Value Chain in the West Bank – Palestine" project, the capacity-building initiative delivers focused instruction on advanced farm management protocols, hygiene practices, and safety mechanisms for processing and handling dairy products. By equipping rural women with standardized technical skills to reduce contamination risks and lower operational overheads, the structural intervention directly scales up regional production efficiency, elevates product quality for broader market opportunities, and reinforces smallholder household incomes.

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA) oversaw the signing of 13 strategic bilateral agreements between Saudi Arabia...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA) oversaw the signing of 13 strategic bilateral agreements between Saudi Arabia and Russia, totaling SR4.8 billion in investments, on the sidelines of the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum. Orchestrated to advance the food security, biotechnology localization, and supply-chain resilience targets of Saudi Vision 2030, the public-private partnerships focus heavily on stabilizing livestock and agrifood systems. Key structural provisions within the agreements mandate the domestic manufacturing and localization of veterinary vaccines to enhance regional biosecurity, the development of specialized broiler poultry strains to accelerate meat self-sufficiency, and the security of long-term grain and feed input supply chains. Additionally, the investment framework opens new international distribution channels for Saudi aquaculture and niche agricultural exports, establishing trade protocols for Russian firms to market and distribute Saudi shrimp, fish, camel milk derivatives, and specialty coffee products globally.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is accelerating its net-zero emissions strategy for the agricultural sector by...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is accelerating its net-zero emissions strategy for the agricultural sector by scaling up the deployment of smart farming technologies and climate-resilient frameworks. The initiatives emphasize the adoption of artificial intelligence, internet-of-things (IoT) devices, automated irrigation networks, and precision fertilization methods designed to minimize water, energy, and chemical inputs. To offset emissions, the national program incorporates environmental restoration projects, including blue carbon ecosystem management, organic fertilizer manufacturing, and large-scale afforestation using high-capacity carbon-sequestering tree species. Furthermore, the modernization of livestock supply chains via the upcycling of local agricultural waste into sustainable animal feed aims to reduce operational overheads for farmers while driving down carbon footprints.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The South Hebron Agriculture Directorate, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the United Nations D...
records.description: The South Hebron Agriculture Directorate, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), has executed the seventh training session of its "Field Schools" series for 32 sheep farmers in the Al-Sarra region. Formulated under the "My Initiative – Empowering Marginalized Communities through Investment in Agricultural Business Development" project, which receives structural financial support from the IBSA Fund (India, Brazil, South Africa), the program delivers critical veterinary and nutritional training to protect regional flocks against summer parasitic diseases and lethal epidemics like brucellosis and foot-and-mouth disease. By training smallholders in balanced seasonal feeding methodologies to reduce ewe abortion rates and optimize newborn survival metrics, the inter-institutional intervention lowers livestock mortality overheads, enhances meat and dairy production efficiency, and stabilizes rural family incomes.

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality has substantially expanded Qatar's urban green infrastructure, driving the nation’s total green area to 21.9...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality has substantially expanded Qatar's urban green infrastructure, driving the nation’s total green area to 21.9 million square metres and increasing the average citizen's allocation of green space to 6.8 square metres. Designed to fulfill the environmental sustainability and urban planning metrics of the Qatar National Vision 2030, the multi-sector initiative encompasses the planned scaling of public parks to 156 installations alongside the widespread rollout of 1,864 water-efficient irrigation networks across 715 domestic farms. To catalyze a localized circular economy, municipal authorities simultaneously modernized national waste management operations, processing over 755,000 tonnes of municipal waste, recovering approximately 4 million tonnes of recycled construction aggregates, treating 10,470 tonnes of end-of-life tires, and generating 276,000 megawatt-hours of electricity via dedicated waste-to-energy facilities while yielding 34,213 tonnes of organic compost for agricultural replenishment.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation, specifically its General Secretariat for Food Security and Directorate of Seeds, has collabor...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation, specifically its General Secretariat for Food Security and Directorate of Seeds, has collaborated with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) to execute an intensive four-day technical capacity-building training workshop focused on Seed Security Assessment (SSA). Designed to mitigate compounding economic and climate pressures on localized farming systems, the program establishes data-driven field methodologies to precisely survey, evaluate, and analyze regional seed accessibility, quality, and market availability. By standardizing indicators across decentralized administrative territories, the institutional partnership aims to equip production and economic resource personnel with advanced metrics to accurately plan structural agricultural interventions and strengthen smallholder baseline food security.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced highly positive initial harvest results for tissue-cultured potato seeds at the Upper Euphrates...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced highly positive initial harvest results for tissue-cultured potato seeds at the Upper Euphrates Station in Anbar Governorate. Managed by the Horticulture Department as a key component of the National Potato Development Program, the project's technical staff have successfully initialized the extraction of localized seed tubers propagated through advanced biotechnological methods. Initial yield metrics point to exceptional productivity and field adaptation, validating the meticulous field monitoring and operational plans established by the ministry. By prioritizing the micropropagation of high-grade, pathogen-free local seed varieties, the strategic program aims to substantially reduce dependency on foreign seed imports, lower seasonal production overheads for domestic farmers, and build long-term, sustainable food security across the country.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Civil Aviation Authority—acting in coordination with national environmental and water resource management bodies—has expanded the Sul...
records.description: The Civil Aviation Authority—acting in coordination with national environmental and water resource management bodies—has expanded the Sultanate of Oman's artificial rainfall enhancement network to 14 operational stations to strengthen national water security. Distributed across highly strategic topographic vectors including the Hajar Mountains, Musandam, and Dhofar, the infrastructure utilizes advanced chemical-free ionization technology to emit negative ions into the atmosphere, accelerating cloud condensation nuclei formation during suitable meteorological windows. This technological framework has successfully optimized seasonal precipitation yields, accelerated groundwater aquifer recharge rates, and mitigated dust pollution levels to bolster climate resilience across the country's arid zones. This report focuses on innovative water resource management, climate-adaptive technology deployment, and regional groundwater infrastructure; it is not related to the current Middle East conflict.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Directorate General of Agricultural Wealth and Water Resources in A’Dhahirah has overseen a substantial expansion in the regional api...
records.description: The Directorate General of Agricultural Wealth and Water Resources in A’Dhahirah has overseen a substantial expansion in the regional apiculture sector, with local honey production surging to 97.8 tons managed by 1,054 beekeepers operating 24,862 beehives. Driven by strategic public-private partnerships and the integration of advanced scientific methods in apiary management, the institutional framework focuses on diversifying rural incomes through the manufacturing of value-added transformational products—including beeswax, pollen, specialized queen rearing, and honey-infused cosmetic and therapeutic goods. To guarantee the long-term sustainability of the sector and optimize production efficiency, the directorate deploys structured support systems consisting of technical field inspections, pest-control training workshops, and dedicated commercial marketing exhibitions to bridge the gap between local producers and consumer markets.
records.institution: The Directorate General of Agricultural Wealth and Water Resources in A’Dhahirah

records.title: The National Consumer Institute (INC), operating under the auspices of the Ministry of Trade and Export Development and in technical part...
records.description: The National Consumer Institute (INC), operating under the auspices of the Ministry of Trade and Export Development and in technical partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), is finalizing a comprehensive national strategy to combat food waste. Framed as a critical macroeconomic and ecological necessity, the upcoming roadmap aims to align government administrations, civil society, and market actors to restructure supply chains and curb the estimated 570 million dinars lost annually to discarded food. National diagnostics indicate that 5% of average household monthly expenditures are lost to food waste, with subsidized staples bearing the highest rates of depletion; specifically, families discard an average of 42 kilograms of bread annually, culminating in a nationwide loss of roughly 900,000 loaves per day (113,000 tonnes per year). By executing targeted public workshops, establishing steering committees, and standardizing monitoring mechanisms, the initiative establishes a coordinated framework to alleviate pressure on Tunisia's heavily strained water resources, improve regional agrifood sector competitiveness, and mitigate the sharp spikes in organic waste observed during festive consumption periods.

records.title: The Agricultural Marketing Sector at the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has commenced procedures to export surplu...
records.description: The Agricultural Marketing Sector at the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has commenced procedures to export surplus local potato production. This initiative follows the achievement of self-sufficiency in potato seeds, which triggered a significant surge in domestic crop yields. By opening external marketing channels for the excess supply, the ministry aims to stabilize local market prices, balance supply and demand, and improve economic returns for domestic farmers to ensure production sustainability. Furthermore, the agency highlighted this production surplus as a viable investment opportunity for the private sector to develop agro-processing industries—such as frozen potato processing—to maximize the added value of local agricultural goods and generate new employment opportunities.
records.institution: The Agricultural Marketing Sector at the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The World Bank Group has approved a new five-year Country Partnership Framework alongside four development operations totaling 285 millio...
records.description: The World Bank Group has approved a new five-year Country Partnership Framework alongside four development operations totaling 285 million U.S. dollars to drive sustainable recovery, expand public service delivery, and stimulate job creation within a fragile, conflict-affected landscape. Strategically aligned with national stabilization priorities, the foundational investments target rapid rehabilitation across critical multi-sector networks including public health systems, nutrition programs, primary electrical grids, municipal water harvesting installations, and agricultural and fisheries management. By pivoting toward an agile, localized deployment model, the programmatic framework seeks to rebuild institutional capacities, enhance macroeconomic governance, and empower vulnerable populations by expanding the economic participation of women and scaling private sector infrastructure investments.

records.title: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) and the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) hosted a Millet Har...
records.description: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) and the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) hosted a Millet Harvest Day event to advance the National Agricultural Initiative for the Adoption of Climate-Smart Crops in the UAE. The initiative focuses on cultivating resilient varieties like millet—which features high nutritional value and superior tolerance to drought, extreme heat, and soil salinity—to reduce water consumption and decrease dependence on food imports. Backed by the UAE’s National Food Security Strategy 2051, the program's initial phase spans from 2026 to 2027 and will deploy 45 field trials across local farms, alongside training programs for 45 farmers and 50 agricultural extension officers to accelerate local adoption. A subsequent phase will focus on driving commercial growth and scaling private-sector market partnerships for climate-smart crop derivatives and prototype food products.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) and the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has announced that Egypt has procured over 4.3 million tonnes of locally produced wheat...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has announced that Egypt has procured over 4.3 million tonnes of locally produced wheat during the current harvest season, achieving 86% of its 5-million-tonne state procurement target. This milestone follows a record cultivation area of 3.7 million feddans—a 600,000-feddan increase over the previous season—incentivized by an increased state purchase price of EGP 2,500 per ardeb. To optimize the supply chain, the government established a network of more than 400 localized collection centers and instituted a rapid 48-hour payment system for farmers. With joint committees and a central operations room managing quality control and logistics, these domestic enhancements, alongside expanded access to certified seeds and upgraded silos, are projected to boost total production to 9.8 million tonnes, progressively strengthening strategic grain reserves and reducing reliance on foreign wheat imports.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, with direct bilateral procurement support from the People's Republic of China and in collaboration with the...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, with direct bilateral procurement support from the People's Republic of China and in collaboration with the Association for Forest Wealth and Development (AFDC), has launched a comprehensive precision agritech initiative in Qornayel to integrate advanced drone platforms into its national sector system. Structured under the framework of the ministry's strategic transformation masterplan, the modernization program deploys automated aerial hardware to run optimized, low-impact pesticide crop sprayings, manage vulnerable natural pollinator ecosystems, and establish continuous remote-sensing monitoring across rugged mountainous forests to combat volatile wildfire hazards and invasive biological blights. By capturing highly accurate spatial field data, the institutional framework aims to rationalize raw inputs such as water and fertilizers while establishing data-driven traceability and food safety tracking structures to elevate the trade competitiveness of national agrifood exports.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) of Oman has announced two new localized agricultural investment projec...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) of Oman has announced two new localized agricultural investment projects in the Al Ghuwayl area of the Ibri Wilayat, situated within the Al Dhahirah Governorate. Part of a broader state-backed strategy to expand modern agricultural production through private sector capital, the first venture establishes an advanced 10-acre tissue culture laboratory designed for the rapid and large-scale cultivation of disease-free, high-quality botanical seedlings and saplings to supply the domestic farming market. The second concurrent project allocates an additional 10 acres to the intensive cultivation of leafy vegetables utilizing a combination of protected greenhouse environments and traditional open fields. By introducing advanced agricultural technologies such as controlled-environment greenhouse systems and automated resource-efficiency workflows, the integrated initiatives are engineered to maximize year-round crop yields, conserve local groundwater resources, and accelerate import substitution to fortify national food security architecture in line with Oman Vision 2040.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) has finalized a memorandum of understanding with the Russian Ministry of...
records.description: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) has finalized a memorandum of understanding with the Russian Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment to expand bilateral coordination on environmental preservation and ecological sustainability. Signed by administrative leadership from both nations, the cooperation framework outlines joint operational initiatives to expand vegetation cover, mitigate land degradation, enforce sustainable forestry practices, and modernize management models for natural and protected areas. Additionally, the partnership institutes data-sharing protocols and a joint working group to coordinate environmental monitoring, expand waste management infrastructure, protect migratory bird routes, and conduct scientific research to counter the illegal trade of endangered flora and fauna.
records.institution: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: Syria has launched its 2026 wheat procurement season with an expected harvest of 2.5 million tons, aiming to strengthen domestic food sec...
records.description: Syria has launched its 2026 wheat procurement season with an expected harvest of 2.5 million tons, aiming to strengthen domestic food security and reduce reliance on imports. The government is supporting farmers through Decree No. 120, offering a bonus of 9,000 Syrian pounds (about $70) per ton in addition to a procurement price of 46,000 pounds (about $380) per ton, while expanding storage capacity to nearly 1 million tons across 37 silos and 98 facilities and rehabilitating key infrastructure, including the Adra silos with a capacity of 200,000 tons. Efforts also include digital systems for delivery and registration, and regional production estimates such as 1.025 million tons from 750,000 hectares in Hasakah, all contributing to improved supply stability and long‑term food security.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (DoE) has officially launched the Abu Dhabi Water and Energy Resilience Framework during the third edi...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (DoE) has officially launched the Abu Dhabi Water and Energy Resilience Framework during the third edition of the Water and Energy Majlis, held under the umbrella of Abu Dhabi Water & Power Week. Structured around three foundational pillars—infrastructure, human capital and governance, and technology and innovation—the newly introduced framework mandates 15 strategic measures designed to optimize supply security, capacity planning, emergency preparedness, and the diversification of vital resource networks. Developed to align with the UAE Water Security Strategy 2036 and the Net Zero 2050 charter, the initiative integrates advanced reverse osmosis desalination technologies, artificial intelligence for meteorological forecasting, and cloud-seeding methodologies advanced by the National Centre of Meteorology. Multi-lateral collaborations emphasized treating water, energy, and food security as a single interconnected system, anchored globally by strategic platforms like the Mohamed bin Zayed Water Initiative to mitigate regional resources vulnerabilities and enhance climate-smart distribution networks.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (DoE)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) continues to expand its utility-scale infrastructure portfolio to accelerate carbon emis...
records.description: The Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) continues to expand its utility-scale infrastructure portfolio to accelerate carbon emission reductions and support the overarching Dubai Clean Energy Strategy 2050 and the Dubai Net Zero Carbon Emissions Strategy 2050. Anchored by the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park—the largest single-site solar park in the world utilizing the independent power producer model—the authority has reached an operational capacity of 3,860 MW utilizing photovoltaic and concentrated solar power systems, on track to exceed 8,000 MW by 2030. This scaling capacity is projected to elevate clean energy to 36% of Dubai's total generation mix by 2030, mitigating over 8.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually. Concurrently, the authority operates the Middle East and North Africa region’s first industrial-scale solar-powered Green Hydrogen facility, generating 20 kilograms of hydrogen per hour with 240 kilograms of storage capacity to serve as a flexible testing platform for zero-emission grid re-electrification and secondary industrial applications.
records.institution: The Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA)

records.title: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), in direct partnership with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, hos...
records.description: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), in direct partnership with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, hosted "Millets Harvest Day" to advance the National Agricultural Initiative for the Adoption of Climate-Smart Crops in the UAE. Geared toward translating agronomic research into scalable field applications, the initiative promotes the widespread cultivation of millet varieties specifically optimized to tolerate drought, extreme heat, and high soil salinity while requiring significantly less water than conventional grains. The multi-partner event engaged local farmers, researchers, and policymakers through field demonstrations and live harvesting, while introducing value-added food prototypes—such as millet milk and bio-fortified baked goods—to establish more resource-efficient, climate-resilient agrifood supply chains across the UAE's hyper-arid environments.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in coordination with the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority (DECCA)...
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in coordination with the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority (DECCA) and the Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA) in Sharjah, launched a series of community-centric environmental preservation initiatives timed with World Environment Day. Structured to advance the UAE's strategic target of planting 100 million mangroves by 2030 and fulfilling its obligations under the international Mangrove Alliance for Climate (MAC), the multi-regional field operations encompassed a large-scale mangrove restoration drive at Khor Kalba, an endangered marine turtle release at the Jebel Ali Wildlife Sanctuary, and specialized public health workshops at the Thukher Club to embed food safety systems and sustainable consumption habits within family units. Backed by quantitative gains in national metrics—including elevating the domestic environmental awareness index to 89% and the environmental behavior index to 85% through volunteer-led tree distribution campaigns—these initiatives utilize nature-based carbon sequestration and public ecology programs to reinforce regional biodiversity protection and long-term climate change mitigation.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: The Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture, has collaborated with the Land Researc...
records.description: The Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture, has collaborated with the Land Research Center, the Welfare Association, and the Beitillu Agricultural Association to implement an agricultural development project funded by Islamic Relief Denmark. The climate-adaptation initiative targeted 40 farmers across the villages of Silwad, Beit Liqya, Beitillu, and Deir Ammar by distributing 4,600 specialized fruit seedlings—including grape, fig, almond, and citrus varieties—to optimize land utilization rates and boost domestic crop production efficiency. By monitoring the deployment of these inputs according to strict technical standards, the institutional partnership aims to expand the local agricultural base, enhance long-term soil productivity, and reinforce smallholder food security against environmental and economic pressures.
records.institution: The Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate of Agriculture

records.title: The South Hebron Agriculture Directorate, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the Land Research Ce...
records.description: The South Hebron Agriculture Directorate, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the Land Research Center and the Beit al-Roush al-Fouqa Village Council, has distributed specialized agricultural equipment and maintenance tools to 22 farmers in the region. Executed as a key component of the "Enhancing Land Productivity and Adapting to Climate Change through Afforestation" project, the logistics deployment provides essential hardware to smallholders who have successfully completed intensive land reclamation and planting phases. By delivering technical and material resources to rural and marginalized areas, the institutional framework aims to scale up soil efficiency, accelerate tree-planting initiatives, and lower operational overhead costs, thereby enabling farmers to sustainably manage and protect their newly reclaimed acreage against environmental degradation.

records.title: The Horticulture Department has conducted an inspection of the newly completed and equipped refrigerated storage facility built for the N...
records.description: The Horticulture Department has conducted an inspection of the newly completed and equipped refrigerated storage facility built for the National Potato Development Program. The facility is designed to safeguard the quality and efficiency of premium potato seeds produced through laboratory tissue culture, propagation, and field cultivation stages across operational units in Nineveh and Anbar. This infrastructure is critical for replacing specialized storage assets previously destroyed, helping to stabilize local seed supply chains, minimize dependency on foreign imports, and strengthen national food security. This report focuses on domestic agricultural infrastructure, cold storage logistics, and regional food security; it is not related to the current Middle East conflict.
records.institution: The Horticulture Department at the Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: The Ministry of Economy and Trade of Libya has implemented comprehensive regulatory measures—specifically via Decree No.
records.description: The Ministry of Economy and Trade of Libya has implemented comprehensive regulatory measures—specifically via Decree No. 289/2026—to restrict the import of essential grains and agricultural raw materials, including wheat, maize, barley, and soybeans, exclusively to active domestic manufacturing and production units. Engineered to dismantle speculative market brokerage, artificial price manipulation, and hoarding by non-producing traders, the new state-backed framework strictly links allowed import volumes directly to the verified operational capacities of local agricultural and processing facilities. By introducing enhanced supply-chain monitoring, compliance oversight, and digital traceability systems, the policy has stabilized the distribution of foundational feed ingredients, resulting in a gradual correction of retail prices for meat, poultry, and eggs. This public asset intervention optimizes domestic value-chain efficiency and insulates household spending from market distortions, thereby advancing the state's long-term macro-level food security and economic stabilization objectives.
records.institution: The Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.title: The Jerusalem Governorate Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct coordination with the Foo...
records.description: The Jerusalem Governorate Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct coordination with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), has executed a specialized technical training program for 20 women from the Abu Dis Cooperative Society for Livestock Development. Funded through a broader West Bank animal value chain optimization framework, the capacity-building initiative delivers theoretical and practical instruction on public safety, rigorous sterilization protocols, and advanced livestock care methodologies. To enhance domestic marketing opportunities and maximize economic returns for smallholders, the curriculum introduces product diversification techniques—such as the manufacturing of specialized cheese varieties like mozzarella—alongside strategic farm management frameworks. By explicitly targeting the economic participation and technical literacy of rural women, the structural intervention drives production efficiency and scales up localized food safety standards to reinforce smallholder family livelihoods.
records.institution: The Jerusalem Governorate Directorate of Agriculture

records.title: The Tulkarm Governorate Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the Food a...
records.description: The Tulkarm Governorate Directorate of Agriculture, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and in direct partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), has conducted a specialized technical training session for 20 beneficiaries from the Shweika Cooperative Society. Financed by the European Union under a broader West Bank animal value chain development framework, the capacity-building initiative trains smallholders and livestock breeders in advanced sheep farm management protocols and optimal sanitation procedures for raw milk handling, processing, and dairy production. By standardizing hygiene benchmarks from initial milking to final product marketing, the structural intervention aims to maximize regional livestock production efficiency, eliminate food safety hazards, and elevate the economic returns and long-term livelihood sustainability of rural farming families.
records.institution: The Tulkarm Governorate Directorate of Agriculture

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality, through its 2025 Annual Report and the targeted work of the Animal Wealth Department, has accelerated the l...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality, through its 2025 Annual Report and the targeted work of the Animal Wealth Department, has accelerated the licensing of 45 livestock and animal production projects to enhance domestic production and reduce import reliance. In line with the sustainable agricultural objectives of the Qatar National Vision 2030, the portfolio comprises 30 operational initiatives and 15 facilities under active development, spanning 14 meat production farms, 11 general poultry and livestock ventures, 8 broiler chicken facilities, 6 table egg production sites, and 4 dairy operations, alongside specialized broiler parent stock and turkey breeding installations. Driven by these integrated public-private investments, the country has achieved a 99% domestic self-sufficiency rate in both local dairy production (reaching 171,283 tonnes) and poultry meat output (totaling 26,376 tonnes). This programmatic scaling is backed by rigorous annual livestock assessments tracking over one million animals—including sheep, goats, camels, and cattle—to stabilize national food supply chains through technological and structural modernization.

records.title: The Ministry of Finance of Egypt, operating in tandem with the Egyptian Customs Authority, has enacted a comprehensive package of regulat...
records.description: The Ministry of Finance of Egypt, operating in tandem with the Egyptian Customs Authority, has enacted a comprehensive package of regulatory facilitation measures by amending the Executive Regulations of the Customs Law to accelerate cross-border trade flows. Under the new state-backed framework, maritime cargo handlers and commercial operators are permitted to initiate formal customs declarations immediately upon a vessel's arrival at national ports using only the bill of lading issued in the importer's name. This policy effectively decouples the initial declaration stage from the immediate submission of a delivery order, which can now be finalized at a later phase prior to the cargo's definitive release. Developed through technical consultations with the Ministry of Transport, regional shipping chambers, and commercial logistics agencies, the structural reform is engineered to shorten port clearance times, lower administrative overhead, and compress logistics performance index deficits while maintaining strict regulatory oversight to safeguard public fiscal rights.

records.title: The General Company for Food Commodities Trading has confirmed the arrival of a 44,000-tonne shipment of American rice at the Jordanian p...
records.description: The General Company for Food Commodities Trading has confirmed the arrival of a 44,000-tonne shipment of American rice at the Jordanian port of Aqaba aboard the vessel Equinox Dream. Despite logistical and maritime hurdles stemming from regional shipping disruptions, the institution is successfully moving forward with its 2026 marketing plan to secure food basket and social welfare items. The company is coordinating distribution protocols to ensure that these strategic grain reserves reach storage warehouses and distribution branches across all Iraqi governorates without operational delay.
records.institution: The General Company for Food Commodities Trading

records.title: The Veterinary Department at the Ministry of Agriculture has authorized the release of 21 imported veterinary products for local distribu...
records.description: The Veterinary Department at the Ministry of Agriculture has authorized the release of 21 imported veterinary products for local distribution following rigorous quality and compliance inspections. Conducted by the Central Veterinary Inspection Division, the clearance process involved field visits to specialized companies to verify regulatory alignment, review laboratory testing data, and audit official documentation. The approved batch includes 12 veterinary pharmaceuticals, 7 vaccines, and 2 additional medicinal substances, all of which met the strict technical and sanitary criteria enforced by the Veterinary Health Authority. This regulatory oversight ensures the availability of safe and effective animal health treatments to support domestic livestock breeders and bolster national food security.
records.institution: The Veterinary Department at the Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in active coordination with the Association for Forest Resources and Development (AFDC) and the Lebanese Arm...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in active coordination with the Association for Forest Resources and Development (AFDC) and the Lebanese Army, has launched a specialized multi-day technical training course at the AFDC Center in Ramlieh, Aley District. The technical program aims to train agricultural engineers, technicians, and military personnel on the operation, maintenance, and flight logistics of advanced agricultural drones donated by the People's Republic of China. This bilateral technology transfer establishes a digital monitoring and surveillance infrastructure across Lebanon's dense woodlands and agricultural zones, optimizing early detection vectors for crop diseases and invasive forest pests—particularly affecting cedar and pine ecosystems. By replacing traditional, high-risk ground applications with precision drone-based aerial mapping and localized pesticide spraying, the inter-institutional partnership lowers operational deployment costs, enhances spatial data accuracy, and accelerates environmental disaster response times.

records.title: The Customs and Indirect Tax Administration (ADII) of Morocco has temporarily reinstated a 170% import tariff on soft wheat and its deriv...
records.description: The Customs and Indirect Tax Administration (ADII) of Morocco has temporarily reinstated a 170% import tariff on soft wheat and its derivatives, ending a multi-year tax exemption policy that has been in place since November 2021 to counter severe climate-driven droughts and volatile global commodity pricing. This protective trade mechanism is activated in response to an exceptional recovery in domestic agricultural yields, with national cereal production projected to surge to approximately 90 million quintals following improved rainfall patterns across major agricultural basins. Operating in tandem with the National Interprofessional Office for Cereals and Legumes (ONICL), which has implemented state reference prices and storage incentives to build national strategic grain reserves, this regulatory intervention is engineered to incentivize domestic millers and grain processors to prioritize purchasing from Moroccan smallholders. By establishing a robust trade barrier against cheaper foreign agricultural imports, the temporary policy aims to protect domestic rural incomes and stabilize the national grain market before transitioning back to a zero-rate import framework later in the year.
records.institution: The Customs and Indirect Tax Administration (ADII)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in structural coordination with the grains agency ONICL, the National Millers Federation (FNM), and the Grai...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in structural coordination with the grains agency ONICL, the National Millers Federation (FNM), and the Grain Traders Federation (FNCL), will suspend its 135% customs duty on soft wheat on August 1 to resume international imports and bolster national strategic stockpiles through January 2027. The temporary import tariff had been enacted from June 1 to July 31 to prioritize the marketing and industrial collection of the domestic harvest, which is projected to double to 9 million metric tons following the conclusion of a severe seven-year drought cycle. To ensure adequate supply-side stability, the state framework tied the tariff suspension to a domestic collection target of 80% of its 1.5 million ton soft wheat baseline by July 15, utilizing specialized handling and storage premiums for traders to counteract traditional farmer retention. Consequently, the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) forecasts Moroccan wheat imports to drop by 40% down to 4 million tons for the upcoming 2026/27 trading season.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has broken ground on a $4.2 billion, 65-square-kilometer agricultural city nea...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has broken ground on a $4.2 billion, 65-square-kilometer agricultural city near Saham in the Batnah region. Supervised by the Singapore-based consultancy Surbana Jurong Group and built by a conglomerate of local companies, the mega-project is slated for completion in the third quarter of 2028. The initiative aims to enhance national food self-sufficiency and insulate the sultanate from global market volatility by distributing free land and offering subsidized advanced farming equipment to local producers. The smart city will leverage agritech innovations—such as hydroponics, aeroponics, and aquaculture—to feed 25,000 people annually, serving as a flagship blueprint among 140 development projects designed to curb the nation's rising reliance on foreign food imports.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in coordination with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, has official...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in coordination with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, has officially launched construction on a 65-square-kilometer, $4.2 billion sustainable agricultural city near Saham in the Al Batinah North region. Supervised by the infrastructure consultancy Surbana Jurong Group, the mega-project aims to aggressively mitigate import reliance—which currently drives 30% of national market purchases—by integrating high-efficiency agritech systems, including hydroponics, aeroponics, and advanced aquaculture networks designed to secure baseline nutrition for 25,000 residents annually. Operating as a structural anchor under the national food sufficiency strategy, which encompasses roughly 140 parallel development projects to buffer global supply chain volatility, the development model leverages subsidized hardware allocations and free land distributions to scale localized farming outputs and reinforce climate-resilient economic diversification.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources
records.source: Oman starts work on agricultural city with focus on food security | AGBI

records.title: Tunisia’s fruit export sector recorded a significant revenue increase to US$15.57 million during the initial five months of the seasonal...
records.description: Tunisia’s fruit export sector recorded a significant revenue increase to US$15.57 million during the initial five months of the seasonal cycle, expanding from US$13.09 million during the corresponding period of the previous year, according to national trade statistics compiled by Tunis Afrique Presse. The country successfully distributed 12 distinct fruit categories across approximately 23 international destination markets, with plums and strawberries emerging as the primary revenue-generating categories while peaches led total export volumes. Regional trade flows positioned Libya as the largest market destination by volume, the United Arab Emirates as the highest revenue generator, and India as a rapidly growing market for high-value blueberry configurations. This positive performance underscores broader international market diversification strategies and robust global demand for Tunisian agricultural produce.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in a direct multilateral partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO),...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in a direct multilateral partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), has distributed financial grants totaling 620,000 shekels to 280 beneficiaries across the Ramallah, Al-Bireh, and Jerusalem governorates. Funded by the Danish government, this distribution initiates the first phase of a broader 4.4 million shekel Field and Fodder Crops Development Project designed to cultivate approximately 7,750 dunams of land and support 1,550 young farmers aged 19 to 29. By providing targeted capital to expand the localized production base of essential staples—including wheat, barley, lentils, vetch, broad beans, and chickpeas—the structural intervention aims to absorb displaced workforces affected by severe economic crises, scale up land utilization rates, and build sustainable rural livelihoods to reinforce national food security.

records.title: The National Center for Palms and Dates has announced a 25% year-on-year increase in Saudi Arabian date exports to India.
records.description: The National Center for Palms and Dates has announced a 25% year-on-year increase in Saudi Arabian date exports to India. This growth is driven by shifting Indian consumer preferences toward healthier, high-quality alternatives to sugar-based confectionery, alongside an expanding trend of purchasing dates as year-round gifts rather than exclusively for seasonal religious periods. Indian trade operators, including commercial entities like Hindustan Foreign Traders and Vishal Enterprise, report robust demand spikes for premium varieties such as Safawi (locally termed Kalami) and Sukkari. Importers attribute the competitive edge of Saudi products over regional alternatives—such as Iranian varieties—to superior quality, enhanced shelf-life stability, and balanced pricing, which have collectively expanded market penetration across diverse consumer demographics in urban hubs like New Delhi.
records.institution: The National Center for Palms and Dates

records.title: The Homs Agriculture Directorate, through its Agricultural Affairs and Prevention Department, has projected a seasonal strawberry harvest...
records.description: The Homs Agriculture Directorate, through its Agricultural Affairs and Prevention Department, has projected a seasonal strawberry harvest of approximately 9,500 tonnes from nearly 11,800 greenhouses concentrated across the Talkalakh region and the Al-Bqy’ah Plain. To safeguard this vital regional supply—of which roughly 5,000 tonnes have already been successfully distributed to provincial markets—the state entity is deploying field inspections, laboratory diagnostic testing, and targeted disease-management programs. Local agricultural extension services are actively delivering technical guidance to growers in highly concentrated hubs like Umm Jameh village on greenhouse ventilation, irrigation optimization, and certified seedling selection. However, the sector faces mounting operational headwinds, including escalating costs for fuel and agricultural inputs, uncertified seedling quality, seasonal import competition, and recent severe flood damage that compromised yields in 255 greenhouses by up to 70%. Despite these local challenges, high economic returns are driving a geographic expansion of strawberry cultivation into the eastern countryside of Lattakia, western Idlib, and northwest Syria, where regional trade networks have introduced dedicated agricultural festivals to market raw fruit alongside value-added processing goods like jams, juices, and confectionery.

records.title: Egypt’s pumpkin exports to Italy have reached record levels for the third consecutive year, exceeding 8,000 tonnes valued at nearly $5 mi...
records.description: Egypt’s pumpkin exports to Italy have reached record levels for the third consecutive year, exceeding 8,000 tonnes valued at nearly $5 million between January and August 2025, driven by rising European demand and reduced local production due to climate challenges. Export volumes have grown significantly—about three times higher than 2023, four times higher than 2022, and 73% above the 2024 record—with an average annual growth rate of 62%. Egypt’s market share in Italy rose from 14% in 2022 to 46% in 2025, and during peak months, Egyptian pumpkins accounted for more than half of Italy’s imports, highlighting the country’s strengthening position as a key supplier amid increasing reliance on imports.

records.title: A public company, in cooperation with government authorities and local farmers, is expanding support for ginger and turmeric production b...
records.description: A public company, in cooperation with government authorities and local farmers, is expanding support for ginger and turmeric production by purchasing harvests directly from farms to strengthen food security and promote sustainable agriculture. The initiative benefits 78 farms, with production reaching over 98,447 kg of turmeric and 468 kg of ginger, and aims to develop stable market channels, encourage cultivation of high-value crops, and enhance the competitiveness of local agricultural products through improved access to domestic markets.
records.institution: Oman Agriculture Development Company (OADC) and the Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: Egypt has begun exporting dried egg products to the Middle East, shipping an initial 30‑tonne consignment to Jordan, with further shipmen...
records.description: Egypt has begun exporting dried egg products to the Middle East, shipping an initial 30‑tonne consignment to Jordan, with further shipments planned for the UAE and negotiations underway with Iraq. The move comes as rising regional demand—driven by food processing industries—coincides with domestic oversupply, estimated at 15–20% of production, prompting producers to seek export markets. Egypt produces about 2.4 million tonnes of chicken and 16.6 billion eggs annually, and expanding exports is seen as a way to absorb surplus, generate foreign currency, and stabilize the local poultry market.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt launched a 6 kWp desert agrivoltaics (agri-PV) pilot project in South Sinai through a multi-partner initiative involving 3E, ORG, E...
records.description: Egypt launched a 6 kWp desert agrivoltaics (agri-PV) pilot project in South Sinai through a multi-partner initiative involving 3E, ORG, Engazaat, Habiba Community, and Alexandria University. The project integrates solar energy, agriculture, and water management in a decentralized system to test a scalable model for arid regions. Building on this pilot, a larger 100 kWp agri-PV installation is being implemented in Marsa Matrouh to further evaluate long-term feasibility. The system is designed to reduce heat stress and water evaporation while generating renewable electricity, supporting both agricultural productivity and local energy access.
records.institution: 3E, projects design firm ORG, power and water producer Engazaat, Habiba Community and the Alexandria University Center of Excellence for Water.

records.title: FPS Food Process Solutions has partnered with MAF Gateways to install a fully integrated french fry processing, freezing, and packaging l...
records.description: FPS Food Process Solutions has partnered with MAF Gateways to install a fully integrated french fry processing, freezing, and packaging line in Egypt, aimed at boosting large-scale production efficiency, improving food safety and product quality, and strengthening export capabilities to regional and international markets.
records.institution: FPS Food Process Solutions and MAF Gateways

records.title: Iraq expects wheat production to reach about 5 million tons in the 2025–2026 season, keeping the country self-sufficient for a fourth yea...
records.description: Iraq expects wheat production to reach about 5 million tons in the 2025–2026 season, keeping the country self-sufficient for a fourth year thanks to strong rainfall, higher water reserves, and expanded cultivation. At the same time, the government has reduced the wheat procurement price from 850,000 to 700,000 dinars per ton, citing fiscal pressures, a move that has drawn criticism from farmers despite officials arguing it remains competitive with global prices.

records.title: Egypt used meetings at the May 21–23 Russian Grain Forum in Sochi to advance its strategy of diversifying and strengthening food supplies...
records.description: Egypt used meetings at the May 21–23 Russian Grain Forum in Sochi to advance its strategy of diversifying and strengthening food supplies, focusing on deeper cooperation with major suppliers like Russia’s Demetra Holding. Discussions emphasized expanding beyond wheat imports into strategic investments, improving storage and transport infrastructure, and potentially creating a regional grain logistics hub in Egypt that could include value-added industries such as flour, pasta, oil, and animal feed production. With Egypt remaining the world’s largest wheat importer heavily reliant on competitively priced Russian wheat, the talks align with broader efforts to enhance food security, stabilize supply for its large subsidized bread program, and ensure long-term availability of essential commodities.
records.institution: Minister of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Yemen has achieved self-sufficiency in potato seed production after halting imports 3 years ago, with domestic output now exceeding 8,000...
records.description: Yemen has achieved self-sufficiency in potato seed production after halting imports 3 years ago, with domestic output now exceeding 8,000 tons during the latest spring season. The General Company for Potato Seed Production in Dhamar supplies 9 locally developed seed varieties, supporting expanded cultivation and stabilizing prices in the local market. Government officials are promoting the use of locally produced seeds, encouraging farmers to rely on domestic varieties, and are now considering exporting surplus production, reflecting a broader strategy to strengthen agricultural self-sufficiency and reduce import dependence.
records.institution: the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and The General Company for Potato Seed Production in Dhamar Governorate

records.title: Yemen’s agricultural sector is undergoing a major transformation toward self-sufficiency, supported by government policies that expand pr...
records.description: Yemen’s agricultural sector is undergoing a major transformation toward self-sufficiency, supported by government policies that expand production, restrict imports, and strengthen food security. Crop production increased significantly, with cereals rising by 21% and legumes by 31% between 2015 and 2025, while wheat cultivation expanded to 18,000 hectares and maize reached 40,000 hectares with output of about 120,000 tonnes. New crops such as soybean now cover 1,350 hectares with expected production of 3,200 tonnes, involving over 300 farmers. The government has also banned imports of more than 52 agricultural products, contributing to savings of over $134 million, including $86.9 million in poultry imports. Livestock numbers exceed 10.7 million sheep, 10.3 million goats, and nearly 2 million cattle, while poultry production reached about 200,000 tonnes and 1.5 billion eggs in 2025, alongside investments such as 8.8 billion rials in dairy development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Morocco is transforming its agricultural sector toward a more resilient and high-value model under climate pressures, supported by invest...
records.description: Morocco is transforming its agricultural sector toward a more resilient and high-value model under climate pressures, supported by investments from the African Development Bank. The strategy focuses on modernizing irrigation, strengthening value chains, promoting climate adaptation, and increasing the inclusion of youth and women in rural areas to enhance productivity, sustainability, and long-term food security
records.institution: Morocco governmwnt and African development bank

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture in Palestine, in partnership with the FAO and international donors, signed 25 agricultural investment agreeme...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in Palestine, in partnership with the FAO and international donors, signed 25 agricultural investment agreements worth over 7.4 million shekels to support farmers and strengthen food security. The projects span multiple regions and sectors—including crop production, livestock, and food processing—and aim to promote market-driven investments, innovation, and sustainable agricultural development while improving farmers’ resilience and livelihoods.
records.institution: The ministry of Agriculture and FAO

records.title: Iraq is implementing a 2026 summer agricultural plan focused on modern irrigation and improved water management to address severe drought...
records.description: Iraq is implementing a 2026 summer agricultural plan focused on modern irrigation and improved water management to address severe drought and water shortages. The plan includes adopting advanced irrigation technologies and organizing water distribution, as annual water inflows have dropped to 25–40 billion cubic meters (around 30–40% of historical levels) compared to national needs exceeding 50 billion cubic meters, while reserves have declined to 7–10 billion cubic meters. It also targets the cultivation of about 361,900 dunams (≈90,475 hectares) of rice alongside other crops, with planting scheduled to begin on June 20, 2026.
records.institution: The ministries of Water Resources and Agriculture

records.title: Al-Maghrabah Cooperative launched the rice harvest in one district of Yemen, producing more than 7 tonnes of rice as part of efforts to i...
records.description: Al-Maghrabah Cooperative launched the rice harvest in one district of Yemen, producing more than 7 tonnes of rice as part of efforts to improve farmers’ incomes and expand cultivation. The initiative reflects growing interest among farmers and plans to increase rice production in the coming period, with support from local associations to promote agriculture and help communities cope with economic challenges.

records.title: Egypt has secured a $40 million investment agreement to expand sugar beet production as part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on...
records.description: Egypt has secured a $40 million investment agreement to expand sugar beet production as part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on imports, strengthen food security, and enhance economic resilience. Although domestic production covers about 80% of demand, rising consumption, population growth, and global market disruptions continue to expose the country to external risks. The project supports multiple national priorities, including water efficiency, regional development in Upper Egypt, and industrial growth, while reflecting a wider shift toward import substitution and the integration of agriculture into long-term economic and industrial policy.
records.institution: the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and Nile Sugar

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Morocco is facing a growing agricultural biodiversity crisis, having lost nearly 75% of its native wheat and barley varieties over the pa...
records.description: Morocco is facing a growing agricultural biodiversity crisis, having lost nearly 75% of its native wheat and barley varieties over the past 50 years, largely due to the expansion of intensive farming, reliance on imported hybrid seeds, and environmental pressures. While the agricultural sector remains vital—contributing up to 15% of GDP—current practices are weakening long-term resilience, soil quality, and ecosystem health, raising concerns about food security and sustainability as climate challenges intensify.
records.institution: The Economic, Social and Environmental Council

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture in Palestine, following field visits by a ministerial delegation, launched an urgent response program to supp...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in Palestine, following field visits by a ministerial delegation, launched an urgent response program to support farmers affected by recent damages, including the distribution of agricultural inputs and interventions to restore production. The initiative aims to strengthen farmers’ resilience, ensure continuity of agricultural activities, and safeguard food security under challenging conditions by addressing immediate needs on the ground.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Jerusalem directorate and in partnership with an agricultural relief organization and internatio...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Jerusalem directorate and in partnership with an agricultural relief organization and international funding support, implemented an emergency intervention to assist livestock farmers by distributing 198 tonnes of barley to 165 beneficiaries in vulnerable communities. The initiative aims to reduce economic pressure on farmers, sustain livestock production, and strengthen resilience in areas facing ongoing challenges, thereby supporting food security and rural livelihoods.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) obtained two international ISO certifications (ISO 26000 for social responsi...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) obtained two international ISO certifications (ISO 26000 for social responsibility and ISO 21502 for project management) following successful assessments of its governance and operational practices. The achievement reflects ADAFSA’s commitment to global standards, sustainability, and institutional efficiency. The Authority has also strengthened community engagement through initiatives like the “Auwn” programme, which organised 292 events with 3,114 volunteers contributing 14,568 hours between 2019 and 2025. These efforts support improved project management, resource use, transparency, and the integration of social responsibility into agriculture, food security, and community development.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Edita Food Industries reported strong Q1 2026 results, with revenues rising 34.7% year-on-year to EGP 5.8 billion and net profits more th...
records.description: Edita Food Industries reported strong Q1 2026 results, with revenues rising 34.7% year-on-year to EGP 5.8 billion and net profits more than doubling, driven by higher sales volumes, price increases, and strong demand across product categories. Growth was supported by solid performance in key segments like cakes and croissants, expanding exports, and improved margins, reflecting effective business execution and a diversified product portfolio.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Oman has launched a national project to recycle agricultural and animal waste into 25,000 tonnes of organic fertiliser annually, along wi...
records.description: Oman has launched a national project to recycle agricultural and animal waste into 25,000 tonnes of organic fertiliser annually, along with animal feed and palm frond-based construction materials, aiming to turn waste into economic value while improving soil fertility and reducing environmental harm. Using advanced recycling technologies, the initiative supports local farmers, cuts reliance on chemical fertilisers and imported wood, lowers emissions, and promotes a circular economy by converting farm residues into sustainable products.

records.title: Under the supervision of the Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC / Agricultural Rel...
records.description: Under the supervision of the Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC / Agricultural Relief) implemented, in partnership with Oxfam, a project to install and operate molokhia processing, washing, and packaging machinery at Montana Company in Tulkarm, with a total value of $15,000 (approximately 55,000 shekels). The project was funded by the Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid (DGD) and aims to enhance agro-processing capacity, improve product quality, create new marketing channels, and support employment especially for women and youth while strengthening local agricultural value chains and food security.
records.institution: the Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC / Agricultural Relief), Oxfam, Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid (DGD)

records.title: Egypt has launched the $15 billion New Delta project, a massive land reclamation initiative to convert about 2.2 million feddans of deser...
records.description: Egypt has launched the $15 billion New Delta project, a massive land reclamation initiative to convert about 2.2 million feddans of desert into farmland, boosting cultivated land by 15% and aiming to reduce reliance on food imports. Centered on a large wastewater treatment and irrigation system, the project will support staple crops like wheat and corn as well as export products, while also creating jobs, infrastructure, and new communities. However, it has raised concerns over costs, transparency, and environmental sustainability in a water-scarce country.

records.title: DP World has signed a 30-year concession with Syria to invest US$800 million in modernizing the Port of Tartous, aiming to transform it i...
records.description: DP World has signed a 30-year concession with Syria to invest US$800 million in modernizing the Port of Tartous, aiming to transform it into a major regional maritime hub. The project will upgrade infrastructure, expand cargo capacity, and introduce advanced digital and handling systems to improve efficiency and restore key trade routes. Strategically located on the Mediterranean, the port will enhance connectivity across Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa, support Syria’s reconstruction, and strengthen growing UAE-Syria trade ties, which reached US$1.4 billion in 2025.

records.title: Egypt has opened new export markets in Peru, Panama, and Mexico for oranges, grapes, and strawberry seedlings as part of efforts to boost...
records.description: Egypt has opened new export markets in Peru, Panama, and Mexico for oranges, grapes, and strawberry seedlings as part of efforts to boost agricultural exports and generate foreign currency. The achievement followed technical negotiations led by plant quarantine authorities, with importing countries approving specific products and setting requirements now being finalized for shipments. This expansion reflects Egypt’s continued push to access global markets by ensuring compliance with international phytosanitary standards and maintaining high product quality.

records.title: Ecuador’s banana industry has reached record export volumes in early 2026, but production has dropped by about 30% due to low rainfall, i...
records.description: Ecuador’s banana industry has reached record export volumes in early 2026, but production has dropped by about 30% due to low rainfall, inadequate irrigation preparation, and rising input costs influenced by geopolitical tensions. Despite these challenges, the sector has shown resilience by opening new trade routes to Saudi Arabia and Turkey, creating alternative supply chains and opportunities for investors. However, risks remain significant, particularly from the deadly Fusarium disease and ongoing global instability, which continue to drive higher prices and uncertainty even as the industry adapts and grows.
records.institution: Ecuadorian banana exporters and producers, government and investors in Saudi arabia and turkey

records.title: Tunisia’s GDP grew by 2.6% year-on-year in Q1 2026, driven mainly by a 7% rise in the agricultural sector, particularly olives and olive...
records.description: Tunisia’s GDP grew by 2.6% year-on-year in Q1 2026, driven mainly by a 7% rise in the agricultural sector, particularly olives and olive oil, with exports increasing by 38% to TD1.99 billion ($686 million) from TD1.44 billion in Q1 2025. However, this growth was partly offset by a sharp contraction in construction, which fell by over 7% year-on-year and more than 10% quarter-on-quarter due to regional instability, while Tunisia continues to face trade imbalances, including deficits of about $3 million with China and $1.6 million with Russia.

records.title: Morocco will suspend soft wheat imports from June 1 to July 31, 2026, to support local farmers and stabilize prices during the harvest se...
records.description: Morocco will suspend soft wheat imports from June 1 to July 31, 2026, to support local farmers and stabilize prices during the harvest season, following a strong recovery in domestic cereal production driven by above-average rainfall. After years of drought and heavy reliance on imports, the country expects its harvest to more than double to about 9 million tons, reducing the need for foreign wheat. The government is also backing this shift with measures like guaranteed purchase prices, storage subsidies, and transport support to strengthen local supply and build reserves while preventing cheaper imports from undercutting domestic producers.

records.title: Oman Food Investment Company (OFIC), in partnership with Al Saffa Poultry and private financial investors, is developing a $260 million p...
records.description: Oman Food Investment Company (OFIC), in partnership with Al Saffa Poultry and private financial investors, is developing a $260 million poultry farm (Namma Poultry) as part of a national strategy to reduce reliance on imports and strengthen food security. The project responds to high regional import dependence—around 90% of food consumption and aims to increase domestic production of poultry, alongside parallel investments in dairy and livestock imports to expand local supply capacity.
records.institution: Oman Food Investment Company (OFIC), in partnership with Al Saffa Poultry and private financial investors

records.title: Orascom Construction has announced plans to reach financial close on a new 900 MW build-own-operate (BOO) wind farm in the Gulf of Suez b...
records.description: Orascom Construction has announced plans to reach financial close on a new 900 MW build-own-operate (BOO) wind farm in the Gulf of Suez by the early third quarter of 2026. This 25-year project will effectively double the company’s total wind capacity to 1.8 GW, adding to its existing operational portfolio of 912.5 MW. Beyond wind energy, the institution reported that the Dammam Independent Sewage Treatment Plant (ISTP) in Saudi Arabia is now operational, and construction is advancing on Project Wave, a 30-year seawater treatment and water supply project in Abu Dhabi. Financially, the company reported a robust first quarter for 2026, with revenue jumping 73.2% to $1.47 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders rising 112.7% to $53.4 million. The consolidated backlog reached $9.38 billion, supported by $1.88 billion in new awards primarily driven by infrastructure projects across Egypt, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia.

records.title: The International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC), a member of the Islamic Development Bank Group, has signed a $1.5 billion loa...
records.description: The International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC), a member of the Islamic Development Bank Group, has signed a $1.5 billion loan agreement with the Egyptian government to bolster national food and energy security. According to the strategic allocation, the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) will receive $700 million to support essential food imports, particularly wheat, while the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation will be allocated $800 million. This funding is part of a long-standing partnership in which the institution has provided $25 billion to Egypt since 2008 to ensure the stability of supply chains for basic commodities.
records.institution: The International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC)
