records.title: The Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) showcased its role in advancing global clean energy under the theme "Our Power, Our Planet." By...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) showcased its role in advancing global clean energy under the theme "Our Power, Our Planet." By financing high-impact renewable projects, the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) is helping developing nations, particularly small island states, transition away from conventional fuels toward sustainable energy systems. Major investments highlighted include the AED 551 million Sheikh Zayed Solar Power Complex in Jordan, which powers 50,000 homes, and a AED 25.7 million solar plant in the Comoros. Additionally, the fund has tapped into wind resources through a AED 103 million farm in the Seychelles and coastal stations in Mauritania that provide both clean power and technical training for local communities. These efforts, often coordinated with the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), reflect the UAE’s strategic commitment to climate action and international development.

records.title: To mark Earth Day, the UAE has reinforced its global leadership in climate action and biodiversity through the UAE Cabinet's approval of...
records.description: To mark Earth Day, the UAE has reinforced its global leadership in climate action and biodiversity through the UAE Cabinet's approval of the seventh national biodiversity report and the expansion of protected areas to 55 reserves. Key institutions such as the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi, the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund, and Mubadala are spearheading critical marine initiatives, including the restoration of mangrove ecosystems and the protection of endangered species like the dugong. In the energy sector, Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company - Masdar and Global South Utilities are expanding renewable capacity across three continents, while the Sharjah Environment and Protected Areas Authority continues to advance scientific research into local biodiversity. Furthermore, the Mohamed bin Zayed Water Initiative and Suqia UAE underscore a commitment to global water security as the nation prepares to co-host the upcoming United Nations Water Conference.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries and the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Regulation of the National Market hav...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries and the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Regulation of the National Market have launched a joint initiative to reorganize the tomato sector, focusing on enhancing financing, insurance, and distribution mechanisms to ensure price stability. During a national meeting, officials highlighted that the country has achieved self-sufficiency in industrial tomatoes and is now prioritizing the elimination of illegal market practices and the reduction of production costs through local hybrid seed production. To support these goals, the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries announced upcoming measures, including an executive decree to simplify the issuance of farmer cards and the establishment of dedicated industrial zones for agricultural processing. Furthermore, the National Chamber of Agriculture (CNA) and other stakeholders are working to address critical challenges such as irrigation, labor shortages, and climate change to maintain a consistent supply from producers to consumers.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: On the sidelines of EGYPES 2026, a memorandum of understanding was signed between AlexFert, Valmore Holding, Orascom Construction, Abu Qi...
records.description: On the sidelines of EGYPES 2026, a memorandum of understanding was signed between AlexFert, Valmore Holding, Orascom Construction, Abu Qir Fertilizers and Chemical Industries, and UEG Green Hydrogen Development Holding Limited (UEG) to explore the development of a green hydrogen hub in Alexandria. This strategic partnership aims to bolster the national clean energy strategy by integrating green hydrogen into low-carbon ammonia production, with UEG Green Hydrogen Development Holding Limited (UEG) and Orascom Construction leading feasibility studies for 500 megawatts of renewable energy generation. Simultaneously, Abu Qir Fertilizers and Chemical Industries and AlexFert will evaluate the technical transition of their existing infrastructure to support the production of 480 tons of sustainable ammonia per day. By leveraging local resources and scalable green energy platforms, these institutions seek to establish a competitive export gateway and advance industrial sustainability in alignment with long-term national development goals.
records.institution: Abu Qir Fertilizers and Chemical Industries

records.title: The National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) significantly intensified its regulatory oversight by conducting dozens of inspections and over...
records.description: The National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) significantly intensified its regulatory oversight by conducting dozens of inspections and overseeing the export of 230,000 tons of food consignments to 191 countries. During a single week in April 2026, the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) facilitated the shipment of 80,000 tons of fruit and 56,000 tons of vegetables, with major markets such as Saudi Arabia, Russia, and the Netherlands benefiting from these high-quality standards. By registering new food establishments and enforcing strict compliance with international safety requirements, the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) is bolstering global buyer confidence and strengthening the national agricultural strategy. This dual focus on expanding trade volumes and modernizing logistics near major ports positions the country as a reliable, diversified leader in the global fresh produce market.

records.title: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation has signed the final technical and legal agreements for the National Water Carrier project, a massiv...
records.description: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation has signed the final technical and legal agreements for the National Water Carrier project, a massive desalination and conveyance scheme linking Aqaba to Amman. Executed as a Public-Private Partnership under a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model with the National Carrier Project Company (NCPC), the $5.8 billion project is slated for financial close in July 2026. This critical infrastructure is supported by a global coalition, including grants and concessional financing from the United States, European Union, and JICA, alongside substantial loans from the World Bank, EIB, and EBRD. By negotiating a reduction in the water tariff to $2.7 per cubic metre, the Ministry of Water and Irrigation and its partners, Meridiam and Suez, aim to provide a sustainable solution to the nation's water scarcity, with full ownership of the system returning to the state after 26 years of operation.
records.institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation

records.title: To address the prevalence of transboundary animal diseases, the Ministry of Agriculture has banned meat imports from Sudan, Djibouti, and...
records.description: To address the prevalence of transboundary animal diseases, the Ministry of Agriculture has banned meat imports from Sudan, Djibouti, and Ethiopia while increasing testing protocols for other sources. Although domestic self-sufficiency stands at 42%, the Ministry of Agriculture has secured supply from 21 approved international origins and recently resumed imports from Syria and Egypt to stabilize the market. To mitigate global price hikes and bypass maritime disruptions, authorities have diverted trade routes to utilize Tartus Port and overland transport, a move expected to lower logistical costs. Additionally, the Ministry of Agriculture and the Greater Amman Municipality (GAM) have intensified oversight at slaughterhouses and abattoirs to ensure safety and prevent market manipulation by traders ahead of peak demand periods.

records.title: During the 18th edition of the International Agricultural Show in Morocco, the National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) and the Mo...
records.description: During the 18th edition of the International Agricultural Show in Morocco, the National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) and the Moroccan Association of Conservation Agriculture (AMAC) formalized a strategic partnership to accelerate the nation’s agro-ecological transition. This framework agreement structures collaboration around the promotion of conservation agriculture—specifically reduced tillage, cover cropping, and crop rotation—to combat soil degradation and increasing water scarcity. Under the partnership, the National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) will provide scientific evaluation and monitoring of pilot platforms, while the Moroccan Association of Conservation Agriculture (AMAC) utilizes its field expertise to train farmers and technicians in resilient production models. Aligned with the Generation Green 2020-2030 strategy, the initiative aims to enhance soil fertility and water efficiency, ensuring the long-term sustainability of the agricultural sector in the face of climate change.
records.institution: The National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA)

records.title: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources have launched...
records.description: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources have launched a high-value investment portfolio via the Invest Oman platform to bolster national food security. The initiative features ten primary projects across the Al Najd Agricultural Zone and various coastal regions, including large-scale cultivation of onions, garlic, and potatoes, as well as sophisticated aquaculture ventures for abalone, tuna, and shrimp. With investment values ranging from OMR 1.6 million to OMR 32 million, these opportunities aim to leverage the strategic location and infrastructure of the Invest Oman ecosystem to enhance self-sufficiency and resource sustainability. By integrating production, manufacturing, and logistics, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources seek to attract global investors to support the economic diversification goals of Oman Vision 2040.
records.institution: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion

records.title: The Hebron Agriculture Directorate, specifically its General Directorate of Plant Protection, partnered with the Red Cross to conduct a f...
records.description: The Hebron Agriculture Directorate, specifically its General Directorate of Plant Protection, partnered with the Red Cross to conduct a field training workshop focused on controlling the Mediterranean fruit fly in grape vineyards. During the session, farmers received practical demonstrations on early pest detection and the implementation of integrated pest management programs, highlighting environmentally friendly control methods. To support these efforts, the Red Cross distributed 400 attractant traps to twelve participating farmers, aiming to reduce pest spread and enhance the quality of one of the region's most vital crops. This collaboration between the Ministry of Agriculture and international partners underscores a commitment to sustainable agricultural practices and the protection of local harvests against significant biological threats.

records.title: The North Hebron Agriculture Directorate conducted a training workshop in Halhul for beneficiaries of a rural food security project imple...
records.description: The North Hebron Agriculture Directorate conducted a training workshop in Halhul for beneficiaries of a rural food security project implemented by the Land Research Center and funded by the CRIK Foundation. In partnership with the Ministries of Agriculture and Social Development, the initiative provided women managing egg-laying chicken farms with hens, specialized cages, and feed to bolster home-based production and household income. By focusing on sustainable productive projects and technical training, the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, the Land Research Center, and the Ministries of Agriculture and Social Development aim to empower economically vulnerable families and enhance food security and resilience within rural communities.

records.title: The South Hebron Directorate of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Agricultural Development Association (Agricultural Relief), the Al...
records.description: The South Hebron Directorate of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Agricultural Development Association (Agricultural Relief), the Al-Ramadin Municipality, and the German Agency for International Development (GIZ), has signed agreements to rehabilitate rainwater harvesting wells for 43 sheep farmers. Funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), the 210,000-shekel project focuses on the Arab Al-Ramadin and Arab Al-Frijat areas to combat water scarcity through sustainable management and greywater reuse. By providing supplementary water sources for livestock and home gardening, the Ministry of Agriculture and its partners aim to bolster the resilience of families in marginalized rural areas. This initiative is a core pillar of a broader strategy to ensure stability, improve living conditions, and promote self-reliance through the efficient use of natural resources.
records.institution: The South Hebron Directorate of Agriculture

records.title: The Tulkarm Directorate of Agriculture, in partnership with the Union of Agricultural Cooperative Societies in Palestine, distributed 130...
records.description: The Tulkarm Directorate of Agriculture, in partnership with the Union of Agricultural Cooperative Societies in Palestine, distributed 130,000 thyme seedlings to 50 farmers across the governorate. This initiative, part of the Emergency Humanitarian Response Program funded by Oxfam Novib, aims to bolster rural resilience and support home gardening amidst challenging economic conditions. By collaborating with local entities like the Palestinian Farmers Association and various town cooperatives, the Ministry of Agriculture is enabling families to secure food needs and improve income through land investment. Ultimately, the Union of Agricultural Cooperative Societies in Palestine and its partners seek to mitigate the impact of regional instability and sustain the agricultural sector through these targeted productive interventions.

records.title: In the highlands of Asir, avocado cultivation is being established as a viable agricultural alternative to reduce reliance on imported fr...
records.description: In the highlands of Asir, avocado cultivation is being established as a viable agricultural alternative to reduce reliance on imported fruit and strengthen domestic supply chains. Local trials conducted in regions like Al-Namas have demonstrated a success rate exceeding 80%, with the moderate mountain climate proving suitable for maintaining the specific temperature and irrigation levels required for the crop. While initial reports indicate that the texture and taste of the harvest are comparable to international varieties, future growth depends on scaling production volumes and formalizing distribution channels. By leveraging these favorable environmental conditions, the regional agricultural sector aims to integrate locally grown avocados into the national market, marking a significant shift toward diversified mountain farming.

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Nada Development Organization, the Executive Director of the Al-Dinder Locality has l...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Nada Development Organization, the Executive Director of the Al-Dinder Locality has launched a livestock input support project designed to aid 200 vulnerable households. The initiative targets four villages in rural Al-Dinder, focusing specifically on families whose livelihoods were severely impacted by looting and conflict involving the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Representatives from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) emphasized that the project is a strategic effort to transition from immediate emergency relief toward long-term sustainable development, effectively strengthening the community's resilience and food security.

records.description: The Ministry of Energy has successfully cleared the regulatory and logistical hurdles for the 10 MW Shendi Solar Power Plant, officially handing over the allocated land to the implementing company to begin construction. This project is strategically designed to stabilize the electricity supply within the River Nile State, specifically targeting the energy needs of the industrial, residential, and burgeoning agricultural sectors. With site preparation—including land leveling and soil testing—already underway, the Ministry of Energy expects the facility to be operational within four to five months. Furthermore, the Shendi Locality administration confirmed that the site selection includes provisions for future expansion, ensuring that the plant can scale alongside the region's increasing demand for renewable power.

records.title: According to the Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA), approximately 45,000 head of livestock are currently available...
records.description: According to the Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA), approximately 45,000 head of livestock are currently available at structured fattening farms across the Kasserine Governorate in preparation for Eid al-Adha. This supply includes over 30,000 lambs and a significant number of rams and kids, with an additional 30,000 to 35,000 sheep estimated to be available through traditional raising methods. The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) has confirmed that the health status of the livestock remains stable and satisfactory, supported by a continuous surveillance system. To ensure safety and hygiene during the upcoming period, the institution is mobilizing 30 public and private sector veterinarians to conduct inspections and monitor compliance across various districts.
records.institution: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA)

records.description: The Ministry of Industry, Mines and Energy has inaugurated a 50-megawatt photovoltaic solar power plant in El Khobna as part of a strategic push to achieve 35% renewable energy in the electricity grid by 2030. This project, overseen by the National Agency for Energy Conservation (ANME) and the Tunisian Electricity and Gas Company (STEG), is expected to cover 70% of the region's consumption needs and significantly reduce annual electricity production and gas costs. Financed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and developed through an international partnership, the facility marks a major step in the National Energy Strategy for 2035. With additional large-scale projects planned for the area, the Tunisian Electricity and Gas Company (STEG) aims to bolster energy security and financial stability while transforming the Sidi Bouzid governorate into a self-sufficient hub for solar electricity.
records.institution: The National Agency for Energy Conservation (ANME)

records.description: The Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) emphasized its commitment to global energy transitions under the theme "Our Power, Our Planet," highlighting a portfolio of high-impact renewable projects in developing nations. Through strategic partnerships with organizations like the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) has financed diverse initiatives, including the AED 551 million Sheikh Zayed Solar Power Complex in Jordan, which powers over 50,000 homes, and a AED 25.7 million solar plant in the Union of Comoros. The fund’s reach extends to wind energy, having supported a 6-megawatt farm in the Seychelles to replace diesel reliance and multiple coastal wind stations in Mauritania that include local technical training programs. These investments not only reduce carbon emissions and reliance on fossil fuels but also strengthen long-term climate resilience and socioeconomic stability across partner countries, reinforcing the UAE's role as a primary driver of international sustainable development.

records.title: The NATIONAL AGRICULTURAL MUTUAL FUND (CNMA) recently convened a regional summit in Constantine to address the critical "technical backbo...
records.description: The NATIONAL AGRICULTURAL MUTUAL FUND (CNMA) recently convened a regional summit in Constantine to address the critical "technical backbone" of Algerian farming: agricultural mechanization. The meeting underscored a sobering reality—production losses in certain sectors are reaching 40%, primarily due to delayed technical interventions and plant diseases. By positioning mechanization as a strategic lever for food security, the CNMA and industry stakeholders are pushing for the rapid integration of modern equipment to ensure earlier, more effective field operations. This modernization drive, supported by specialized insurance and financial frameworks, aims to reduce labor intensity, optimize yields, and build farm resilience against escalating climate and health risks.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has announced a landmark achievement in Egypt’s food security, confirming that the state...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has announced a landmark achievement in Egypt’s food security, confirming that the state has reached 100% self-sufficiency in five strategic commodity groups: fresh milk, table eggs, poultry, rice, and sugar. Minister Alaa Farouk highlighted that this "breakthrough" was achieved despite the logistical pressure of providing for 108 million citizens and 9 million residents. By implementing flexible strategies to maximize horizontal and vertical agricultural productivity, the Ministry has successfully shielded these core sectors from global supply chain volatility, establishing a robust "technical backbone" for national nutrition.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND LAND RECLAMATION has approved a new financing tranche of EGP 154 million through the National Veal Projec...
records.description: The MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND LAND RECLAMATION has approved a new financing tranche of EGP 154 million through the National Veal Project to support the rearing of 2,200 head of livestock by small-scale breeders and young graduates. Integrated into the broader Decent Life initiative, the project has now disbursed a total of EGP 10.562 billion to over 45,000 beneficiaries, facilitating the breeding of more than 529,000 livestock for meat and dairy production. To ensure the project’s technical success, the LIVESTOCK AND POULTRY DEVELOPMENT SECTOR and the GENERAL AUTHORITY FOR VETERINARY SERVICES conduct rigorous field inspections and provide subsidized insurance and comprehensive veterinary care in coordination with the AGRICULTURAL BANK OF EGYPT and the NATIONAL BANK OF EGYPT. This strategic intervention acts as a "technical backbone" for Egypt’s livestock sector, aiming to stabilize market prices, enhance the supply of red meat, and create sustainable employment opportunities in rural communities.
records.institution: THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND LAND RECLAMATION

records.title: The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) is nearing the completion of the first phase of the Erbil Green Belt Project, a massive 78-kilome...
records.description: The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) is nearing the completion of the first phase of the Erbil Green Belt Project, a massive 78-kilometer environmental "shield" designed to fundamentally alter the capital's micro-climate. With an initial investment of $6.2 million covering 4,200 acres, the project has already seen the planting of 700,000 saplings. Once all eight phases are complete, the belt will span 2 kilometers in width and host 7 million productive trees, including olive and pistachio. This initiative serves as a critical "technical backbone" for Erbil’s urban resilience, capable of sequestering up to 210,000 tonnes of $CO_2$ annually while providing a sustainable economic resource through large-scale fruit and nut production.

records.title: Jordan’s Ministry of Agriculture and the Supreme Council for Food Security have reported a landmark performance for the national food sys...
records.description: Jordan’s Ministry of Agriculture and the Supreme Council for Food Security have reported a landmark performance for the national food system, achieving a 7% growth rate in the final quarter of 2025. This expansion has elevated the agricultural sector’s contribution to the GDP to 5.4%, with output reaching JD 2.26 billion. Despite regional volatility and logistical fractures, Jordan has successfully decoupled domestic prices from global inflationary spikes through proactive fiscal interventions, such as a six-month tax suspension on shipping surcharges. Backed by strategic reserves that exceed international safety thresholds—including a 10-month wheat supply—and a 10% surge in exports, the Kingdom has institutionalized a "technical backbone" that ensures both market stability and a measurable improvement in national nutrition profiles.

records.title: Following a formal notification to the World Trade Organization, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has initiated a safeguard investigati...
records.description: Following a formal notification to the World Trade Organization, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has initiated a safeguard investigation into the significant surge of white and parboiled rice imports, which increased by 116% between 2022 and 2025. This probe seeks to determine if the influx of foreign supply, totaling over 118,000 tons in the most recent recorded year, poses a substantial threat to domestic producers already weakened by adverse climate conditions. Should the findings confirm a risk of serious injury to the local sector, the government may implement protective measures such as elevated duties or import quotas to stabilize the market and support internal harvests.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: Nama Water Services has successfully transitioned treated water from a secondary utility into a strategic asset through its "Manhal Nama"...
records.description: Nama Water Services has successfully transitioned treated water from a secondary utility into a strategic asset through its "Manhal Nama" initiative. By shifting from traditional resource management to a value-based model, the company is maximizing the utility of every cubic meter of water to support Oman Vision 2040. Leveraging advanced treatment technologies that meet international standards, the initiative provides a "technical backbone" for agriculture and industry, resulting in a 36% increase in beneficiaries by late 2025. With key infrastructure projects like the 12-kilometer Nizwa-Manah pipeline and the Al Shakhakhit distribution scheme (serving 60+ farms), Nama is effectively de-risking the agricultural sector while preserving the Sultanate's precious freshwater reserves.

records.description: The MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES AND WATER RESOURCES (MAFWR) has launched a high-velocity investment roadmap for the first half of 2026, targeting 400 projects with a total valuation of RO 400 million. As of April 2026, the ministry has already activated 55% of these opportunities via the Tatweer platform, signaling a rapid transition toward a private-sector-led food security model. By focusing on industrial-scale poultry expansion and localized livestock breeding, Oman is moving closer to total self-sufficiency in key proteins, effectively decoupling the national food supply from global market volatility.

records.description: The signing of 18 new agricultural usufruct contracts marks a significant expansion of the "technical backbone" supporting Oman’s food security and rural economy. By transitioning government lands into high-value production hubs for everything from grape and sapodilla cultivation to industrial water purification, the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning are fostering a robust environment for entrepreneurs. Bringing together 100 exhibitors from 20 governorates, the event serves as a technical springboard for structuring the sector and enhancing its global competitiveness. By blending commercial exchange with technical workshops and a national organic olive oil competition, the exhibition aims to bridge the gap between local producers and high-value international export markets, ensuring that Tunisian organic agriculture meets the rigorous standards of the 21st-century consumer.
records.institution: THE TUNISIAN UNION OF INDUSTRY, TRADE AND HANDICRAFTS (UTICA)

records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries has established a 10 million dinar financing line through a performance contract with the Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS) to provide seasonal loans for small farmers. Designed to support agricultural productivity without requiring self-financing or traditional guarantees, these loans carry a 5% interest rate and are specifically available to farmers under the age of 70. While the Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS) manages the financial review and approval process, the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries oversees technical evaluations, field visits, and farmer guidance, with all debts structured for repayment in a single installment following the agricultural season.

records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) is spearheading a major showcase of "Agri-Tech 4.0" at the Emirates Agriculture Conference 2026, positioning Abu Dhabi as a regional laboratory for climate-resilient food systems. From the unveiling of the first dedicated Emirati sheep breed to the strategic introduction of cassava and mushrooms as alternative crops, ADAFSA is hard-wiring innovation into every link of the value chain. By integrating Artificial Intelligence and sensor-based analytics with hands-on livestock management workshops and a AED 910,000 prize fund for breeding excellence, the authority is bridging the gap between high-level policy and field-level productivity. This comprehensive approach, supported by the Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Agricultural Excellence Award, ensures that the transition to a sustainable food system is both technologically advanced and economically rewarding for the UAE’s farming community.

records.description: The General Establishment for Seed Multiplication (GESM) in Syria has reached a critical milestone in its "National Potato Seed Production Plan," completing the planting of 38,000 virus-free potato seedlings within specialized greenhouses in Tartous and Aleppo. This operation moves beyond mere replanting; it focuses on restoring the structural resilience of weakened production systems through the introduction of adapted varieties and rigorous technical oversight. By combining material aid with specialized guidance on soil fertility and responsible irrigation, the Ministry of Agriculture is working to secure the long-term economic stability and environmental heritage of the Tata province.

This joint action document serves as the "technical and financial backbone" for Sudan’s health security, moving from emergency reactive measures to a structured, multi-sectoral defense against waterborne epidemics. By synchronizing disease surveillance with safe water infrastructure and dedicated national funding, the strategy aims to institutionalize the lessons learned from the 2024–2026 cholera outbreaks, ensuring that future spikes are contained within 24–48 hours of detection.

Launched in April 2026, this initiative directly manifests the directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr. Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Ruler of Sharjah, to embed agricultural sustainability into the fabric of daily life. By combining diverse crop production with a "circular economy" waste-to-fertilizer system, the farm serves as a technical and social blueprint for Sharjah’s vision of a self-reliant, environmentally conscious community.

records.title: The Ministry of Local Development and the Ministry of Environment in Egypt have entered into a strategic partnership with Drone Tech to l...
records.description: The Ministry of Local Development and the Ministry of Environment in Egypt have entered into a strategic partnership with Drone Tech to launch a sophisticated aerial monitoring network, serving as the "digital eye" for Egypt’s environmental and urban governance. By integrating AI-powered drones and geospatial analysis, the system provides a high-tech solution for tracking building violations, waste management, and the seasonal "black cloud" pollution phenomenon. This initiative acts as a "technical backbone" for Egypt’s Vision 2030, utilizing spectral imaging to monitor natural reserves and the 100 Million Trees initiative. This phased rollout represents a qualitative leap in government oversight, transitioning from traditional field inspections to real-time, data-driven decision-making across all governorates.
records.institution: The Ministry of Local Development and the Ministry of Environment

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its autonomous export monitoring body, has implemented an immediate suspension of tomato exports to...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its autonomous export monitoring body, has implemented an immediate suspension of tomato exports to European and African markets. This strategic "market correction" was triggered by domestic price surges that saw retail costs hit 15 dirhams per kg ($1.50/kg). By restricting outward shipments, the Ministry successfully engineered a 70% drop in wholesale prices in southern markets, bringing the cost of a standard box down from 350 dirhams to 100 dirhams. While this intervention provides essential relief to Moroccan consumers, it creates significant supply gaps in the EU and Africa, forcing international retailers to pivot toward competitors like Spain and Turkey. This move serves as a "technical backbone" for domestic food security but highlights the delicate tension between maintaining global trade reputation and ensuring local affordability.

records.title: The Directorate General of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has launched a high-precision aerial spraying campaign across the S...
records.description: The Directorate General of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has launched a high-precision aerial spraying campaign across the South Al Batinah Governorate to combat the "spring generation" of the Palm Dubas Bug (Al Mataq). Utilizing helicopters to cover 1,800 acres, the three-day operation targets the wilayats of A’Rustaq, Al Awabi, Nakhal, and Wadi Al Maawil. This intervention serves as a critical "technical backbone" for the palm sector, as the current biological cycle of the pest coincides with the sensitive fruit-setting and growth phases. By neutralizing the bug and its harmful honeydew secretions—which otherwise trigger fungal infections and stunt photosynthesis—the campaign protects the marketable quality and long-term sustainability of Oman’s most vital agricultural resource.
records.institution: The Directorate General of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The GULF UNITED FISH PRODUCTS FACTORY has been inaugurated as the first fully automated, integrated facility of its kind in the Sultanate...
records.description: The GULF UNITED FISH PRODUCTS FACTORY has been inaugurated as the first fully automated, integrated facility of its kind in the Sultanate of Oman, representing a significant advancement in the national food security system. With initial investments totaling OMR 6.2 million and a focus on high-yield industrial outputs, the plant specializes in producing fishmeal, fish oil, and soluble fish paste for the aquaculture and animal feed sectors. By converting marine resources into essential secondary products under strict quality and sustainability standards, the facility reduces import reliance and enhances self-sufficiency. This project, supported by the MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES AND WATER RESOURCES through regulatory facilitation and sustainable resource management, is set to lead a major expansion phase involving future investments of OMR 75 million in shrimp farming, seafood processing, and integrated agricultural initiatives.
records.institution: The GULF UNITED FISH PRODUCTS FACTORY

records.title: The FOOD AND AGRICULTURE ORGANIZATION OF THE UNITED NATIONS (FAO), in partnership with the Jericho and Jordan Valley Directorate of Agric...
records.description: The FOOD AND AGRICULTURE ORGANIZATION OF THE UNITED NATIONS (FAO), in partnership with the Jericho and Jordan Valley Directorate of Agriculture, has finalized two cooperation agreements to provide a grant of approximately 692,000 shekels for critical infrastructure and production initiatives. Operating under the Multi-Donor Agricultural Business Programme (MAP II) and funded by the European Union and the governments of Denmark, Switzerland, and Spain, these projects focus on enhancing food and water security through market-oriented investments. The grant facilitates the development of agricultural infrastructure, provides improved production inputs, and supports food processing initiatives specifically designed to empower women and youth. By strengthening value chains and technical skills in the Jordan Valley, the MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE and its international partners aim to boost rural household incomes and build a more resilient, sustainable agricultural sector capable of navigating modern economic and environmental challenges.

records.title: The Jenin Directorate of Agriculture, in a strategic partnership with the Rural Women's Development Society (RWDS), has completed a large...
records.description: The Jenin Directorate of Agriculture, in a strategic partnership with the Rural Women's Development Society (RWDS), has completed a large-scale distribution of specialized agricultural processing machinery to 11 women-led cooperatives and societies. Funded by the German Federal Ministry (BMZ) and implemented alongside GIZ, this initiative serves as the "technical backbone" for 375 women beneficiaries by providing crisis-responsive business tools. By equipping societies like the Al-Jalama Women's Cooperative and the Kafr Dan Irrigation Cooperative with modern production units tailored to their specific needs, the Ministry of Agriculture is transitioning these rural organizations from traditional farming to "value-added" industrial processing. This move is designed to stabilize household incomes and reinforce the economic resilience of the Jenin governorate.

records.title: The Al-Baha Region is strategically positioning itself as a hub for high-value horticulture by expanding banana cultivation across its go...
records.description: The Al-Baha Region is strategically positioning itself as a hub for high-value horticulture by expanding banana cultivation across its governorates. Leveraging a unique micro-climate characterized by warm temperatures, fertile soil, and sufficient water resources, the region is transforming banana farming from a traditional practice into a competitive investment sector. This expansion serves as a "technical backbone" for Al-Baha’s agricultural economy, supported by the introduction of modern irrigation and fertilization techniques and rigorous extension programs. By focusing on production efficiency and crop quality, the region ensures a steady, high-grade supply to local markets, directly contributing to the economic resilience of Saudi Arabia’s southwestern agricultural belt.

records.title: The signing of these agreements between the Ministry of Investment, the Shareek Program Center, and Almarai Company marks a transformativ...
records.description: The signing of these agreements between the Ministry of Investment, the Shareek Program Center, and Almarai Company marks a transformative shift in Saudi Arabia’s "technical backbone" for food security. By integrating one of the region’s largest food producers into the fisheries sector, the Kingdom aims to localize up to 85% of its food industries. This strategic partnership focuses on moving beyond raw harvesting toward sophisticated seafood processing and value-chain engineering. This initiative directly supports Saudi Vision 2030 by reducing import reliance, enhancing supply chain transparency, and leveraging private sector innovation to establish the Kingdom as a premier regional hub for sustainable food manufacturing.

records.title: The scientific debate held at ESPRIT UNIVERSITY established that water stress in Tunisia has evolved from a technical problem into a stra...
records.description: The scientific debate held at ESPRIT UNIVERSITY established that water stress in Tunisia has evolved from a technical problem into a strategic, multi-dimensional crisis involving economic, social, and geopolitical risks. In an arid landscape where abundant rainfall no longer guarantees sufficient dam reserves due to hydrological imbalances and runoff issues, the focus has shifted toward "smart agriculture" to maintain productivity with fewer resources. The discussions highlighted that competition for water between irrigation, urbanization, and tourism—particularly in the Medjerda basin—directly threatens food sovereignty and increases production costs. Ultimately, the institution emphasized that recognizing the economic value of water and addressing the distribution gap are critical steps for protecting farms and ensuring national food security in the face of escalating climate hazards.

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has activated emergency import protocols to stabilize the domestic tomato market after wholesale prices...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has activated emergency import protocols to stabilize the domestic tomato market after wholesale prices surged from 500 IQD to over 2,250 IQD ($1.46) per kilogram in April. This 400% increase was triggered by a combination of seasonal gaps in domestic production and a sudden export ban from Iran, Iraq's primary supplier. While the ministry approved alternative imports from Turkey and Jordan in late March, these remain at higher price levels due to transport costs. This supply volatility has created a "technical squeeze" on food businesses, such as kebab vendors, who are currently operating at a loss or reducing staff. Relief is expected by the end of April as local Iraqi harvests enter the market, allowing the Ministry of Agriculture to re-stabilize the national food supply chain.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture in Iraq has concluded a specialized two-week training course focused on "Energy and Environmental Sustainabil...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in Iraq has concluded a specialized two-week training course focused on "Energy and Environmental Sustainability and Addressing Climate Change," organized by its Planning and Follow-up Department. Held in alignment with the Ministry of Environment’s directives, the course serves as a "technical backbone" for the National Initiative for Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction. By training staff on renewable energy roles, consumption rationalization, and practical sustainability solutions, the Ministry of Agriculture is directly integrating climate resilience into its institutional performance. This initiative supports Iraq’s broader goals of achieving sustainable development and mitigating the environmental impacts of climate change on the nation’s agricultural and natural resources.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Department of Animal Resources, has successfully released approximately 6 million common carp fi...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Department of Animal Resources, has successfully released approximately 6 million common carp fingerlings into the waters of Al-Qurna district, Basra Governorate. This large-scale release serves as a "technical backbone" for Iraq's fisheries sector, following advanced breeding operations at the newly modernized Al-Maymouna fish hatchery in Maysan. By completing infrastructure improvements and operational upgrades at government hatcheries, the Ministry of Agriculture is scaling its national production capacity to replenish aquatic resources, support local artisanal fishing communities, and strengthen long-term food security across the southern governorates.

records.title: The inauguration of the World Food Forum (WFF) African Regional Chapter in Nouakchott marks a milestone in the "technical backbone" of Af...
records.description: The inauguration of the World Food Forum (WFF) African Regional Chapter in Nouakchott marks a milestone in the "technical backbone" of African agricultural diplomacy. Held during the 34th Session of the FAO Regional Ministerial Conference for Africa, the launch signifies a shift toward localizing global food solutions to meet the continent's specific demographic and environmental needs. By focusing on innovation, youth empowerment, and women-led development, the forum aims to bridge the gap between high-level policy and field-level implementation. Mauritania’s leadership in this initiative aligns with its structural reforms to achieve food sovereignty through improved infrastructure, expanded production bases, and integrated public-private partnerships.

records.title: Morocco’s decision to temporarily halt soft wheat imports between May and the end of August 2026 marks a significant shift from the emerg...
records.description: Morocco’s decision to temporarily halt soft wheat imports between May and the end of August 2026 marks a significant shift from the emergency import footing of the past two years. This regulatory move, traditionally managed by the National Interprofessional Office of Cereals and Legumes (ONICL), is a direct response to a "bumper crop" projection that could see cereal output nearly double compared to the previous season. By closing the borders during the peak marketing period, the government aims to insulate local farmers from international price volatility and ensure that the domestic harvest—estimated to reach between 8 million and 9 million tonnes—is fully absorbed by industrial mills at stable producer prices.
records.institution: The National Interprofessional Office of Cereals and Legumes (ONICL)

records.title: The Jaida, Al Mada, and Tamwilcom partnership represents a high-level institutional "technical fix" for Morocco’s agricultural credit gap.
records.description: The Jaida, Al Mada, and Tamwilcom partnership represents a high-level institutional "technical fix" for Morocco’s agricultural credit gap. By combining the financial expertise of Jaida (specializing in microfinance support), the strategic investment power of Al Mada, and the state-backed guarantee mechanisms of Tamwilcom, this initiative creates a resilient secondary lending environment. It is designed to act as a "financial backbone" for small and medium-sized farms (SMEs) that often struggle to meet the collateral requirements of traditional banks, especially as seven years of persistent drought have increased the perceived risk of agricultural lending.

records.title: The National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) in Morocco has solidified its role as a "technical backbone" for international agricu...
records.description: The National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) in Morocco has solidified its role as a "technical backbone" for international agricultural innovation through two high-level strategic partnerships announced in Rabat in April 2026. By hosting a specialized agricultural mission from North Dakota and formalizing priorities with the Netherlands, INRA is focusing on bridging the gap between advanced agronomic research and field-level food security. These initiatives prioritize the transfer of high-yield pulse and grain technologies alongside Dutch expertise in smart greenhouse systems and water management. This global cooperation framework aims to enhance Morocco's climate resilience and genetic resource preservation, with significant technical momentum expected to peak during the 2026 International Agricultural Show in Morocco (SIAM).
records.institution: The National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA)

records.title: The Syngenta Innovation Center recently hosted the "Tomato Excellence Experience" in Aït Amira, a high-level technical symposium that ser...
records.description: The Syngenta Innovation Center recently hosted the "Tomato Excellence Experience" in Aït Amira, a high-level technical symposium that serves as a "technical backbone" for the Souss-Massa region—Morocco's primary vegetable export hub. By moving beyond traditional seed demonstrations, the event focused on the intersection of market intelligence, genetic resilience, and post-harvest logistics. As Morocco eyes a massive rebound in exports for the 2026 season, this initiative aims to equip producers with the specific tools needed to conquer the increasingly demanding European market, where consistency and resistance to the ToBRFV virus have become non-negotiable standards for market access.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) is spearheading a strategic expansion of mango cultivation in the Wila...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) is spearheading a strategic expansion of mango cultivation in the Wilayat of Barka, South Al Batinah, to solidify Oman's food security and fruit self-sufficiency. This project, which integrates over 40,000 trees across 4,000 acres, utilizes a usufruct land model in partnership with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning. By combining high-quality seedlings from national research centers with elite imported varieties, the initiative establishes a "technical backbone" for high-yield horticulture. Managed by Omani investors and experts, the project is anchored in modern water management, specifically fountain irrigation, to maximize productivity in the Sultanate's arid environment, with the first commercial harvest slated for 2027.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: The network of 10 dams across the South Al Batinah Governorate has become a vital "technical backbone" for Oman’s water and food security...
records.description: The network of 10 dams across the South Al Batinah Governorate has become a vital "technical backbone" for Oman’s water and food security, providing a total storage capacity of 25 million cubic meters. These structures do more than just prevent flood damage; they serve as active groundwater recharge systems that have successfully revived the traditional aflaj networks by raising the water table. By integrating advanced hydrological monitoring and controlled release protocols—including a "three-day settlement" rule to ensure high-quality, sediment-free recharge—the Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) is creating a resilient ecosystem that captures rainwater otherwise lost to the sea.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE, through its General Directorate of Rangelands and Forests, convened a specialized scientific seminar to inte...
records.description: The MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE, through its General Directorate of Rangelands and Forests, convened a specialized scientific seminar to integrate sustainable renewable energy into the management of Palestine's natural resources and agricultural systems. Collaborative discussions with the WILDLIFE SOCIETY, the ENERGY AUTHORITY, and the ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AUTHORITY emphasized that transitioning to solar and alternative energy is essential for protecting nature reserves, mitigating desertification, and reducing the operational burdens on farmers and Bedouin communities. By prioritizing practical applications—such as solar-powered water pumps, desalination plants, and olive press operations—the initiative seeks to enhance the resilience of the agricultural sector against global energy challenges while preserving biodiversity and ensuring long-term food security.

records.title: The Nablus Directorate of Agriculture, through its Agricultural Extension Department, has launched a specialized training initiative for...
records.description: The Nablus Directorate of Agriculture, through its Agricultural Extension Department, has launched a specialized training initiative for the Naqoura Charitable Society, focusing on "safe food manufacturing" and rural economic resilience. Led by Engineer Mona Al-Omari, Head of the Rural Development Department, the program provides 12 women with the technical skills to produce high-quality, preservative-free food products using home-based resources. By bridging the gap between theoretical safety standards and practical manufacturing, the Ministry of Agriculture is empowering these households to transition from simple consumption to "value-added" production. This initiative serves as a "technical backbone" for rural families, enhancing public health while creating sustainable pathways for income diversification and localized food security.

records.title: The Tulkarm Directorate of Agriculture, under the directives of the Minister of Agriculture, Professor Rizq Salimiya, has initiated an em...
records.description: The Tulkarm Directorate of Agriculture, under the directives of the Minister of Agriculture, Professor Rizq Salimiya, has initiated an emergency distribution of mature, three-year-old olive saplings to support farmers recently targeted by agricultural destruction. Supported by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), this project serves as a "technical backbone" for land rehabilitation following the uprooting of over 1,500 olive trees and the loss of 100 dunams of productive land. By providing older, more resilient saplings to 22 farmers across locations like Safarin, Qaffin, and Shuweika, the Ministry of Agriculture is accelerating the recovery of the olive sector, ensuring that livelihoods are restored and agricultural sustainability is maintained in the face of ongoing regional challenges.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has launched the Syrian National Livestock Statistics Platform to modernize agricultural data management and...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has launched the Syrian National Livestock Statistics Platform to modernize agricultural data management and drive digital transformation within the livestock sector. Developed in cooperation with the MADAD FOUNDATION FOR DEVELOPMENT AND PEACEBUILDING, this digital census platform utilizes a unified electronic application linked to GPS for real-time data verification and geographic monitoring of field operations. By establishing an accurate, centralized database on animal numbers and types, the system enables the formulation of realistic agricultural policies, ensures the precise distribution of feed and vaccines, and enhances the capacity for rapid response to climate or health crises. This strategic initiative serves as a technical foundation for organizing production chains and designing targeted financing programs, ultimately supporting national food security and the rural economy.
