records.title: Morocco is participating in the Fruit Attraction trade show in Madrid to promote its fruit and vegetable exports and address industry cha...
records.description: Morocco is participating in the Fruit Attraction trade show in Madrid to promote its fruit and vegetable exports and address industry challenges. The Morocco Foodex (EACCE) pavilion is showcasing the diversity of Moroccan produce, including the tomato, which is a strategic export for the country. The event, organized by IFEMA and FEPEX, provides a strategic platform for Morocco to leverage its competitive advantages, differentiate itself on quality and sustainability, and maintain its market share against rivals like Spain, Turkey, and Egypt.

records.title: The Belgian company Den Berk Délice has launched a project in Morocco to produce high-end tomatoes for the European export market.
records.description: The Belgian company Den Berk Délice has launched a project in Morocco to produce high-end tomatoes for the European export market. The project, which uses modern greenhouses and controlled irrigation, views Morocco as a strategic partner and aims to ensure complete control of the value chain from varietal selection to export logistics. This initiative is part of a broader trend of European agri-food investors being attracted to Morocco's favorable climate and modern infrastructure for high-value greenhouse crops, with a focus on sustainability, quality, and compliance with international standards.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has launched two major water infrastructure projects—the Jubail 3B Independent Water Project (IWP) and the Dammam West Indep...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has launched two major water infrastructure projects—the Jubail 3B Independent Water Project (IWP) and the Dammam West Independent Sewage Treatment Plant (ISTP)—to enhance water security and network efficiency in the Kingdom. The Jubail plant, with a capacity of 570,000 m³/day of desalinated water, was developed by a consortium of Engie, Ajlan, and Nesma, and will serve Riyadh and Qassim regions. Meanwhile, the Dammam West plant, with a capacity of 200,000 m³/day, was developed by a consortium of Metito, Orascom, and Mowah. The projects were inaugurated under the patronage of the Governor of the Eastern Province, and highlight the country’s integrated strategy for sustainable water management.

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has inaugurated two major projects in the Riyadh Region: a state-of-the-art poultry pr...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has inaugurated two major projects in the Riyadh Region: a state-of-the-art poultry production and processing plant and an advanced feed production plant. These projects are intended to enhance food security, increase operational efficiency, and create job opportunities for local communities, aligning with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. The ministry stated that these initiatives will help to strengthen the competitiveness and overall growth of the poultry sector, which continues to grow rapidly thanks to government support, investor incentives, and the National Agricultural Strategy.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The second Unaizah International Dates Forum has been inaugurated in the Qassim Region, with broad participation from local and internati...
records.description: The second Unaizah International Dates Forum has been inaugurated in the Qassim Region, with broad participation from local and international experts. Organized by the National Center for Palms and Dates in cooperation with the Unaizah Chamber of Commerce and the International Dates Council, the forum focuses on sustainability, innovation, and modern technologies in the palm and date sector. The program includes scientific sessions and workshops aimed at addressing challenges and exploring opportunities from farm to global markets.
records.institution: National Center for Palms and Dates

records.title: The Tanmiah Food Company, a leading poultry and food producer, has launched two new facilities in Saudi Arabia's central region: a poultr...
records.description: The Tanmiah Food Company, a leading poultry and food producer, has launched two new facilities in Saudi Arabia's central region: a poultry processing plant in Al-Majma’ah and a feed mill in Dahna. Inaugurated under the patronage of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, these facilities are part of Tanmiah's commitment to advancing food security, enhancing operational efficiency, and creating local jobs in line with Saudi Vision 2030. The Majmaa 2 plant, which features the latest technology, has a biological wastewater treatment system that recycles water for tree plantations. The Dahna Feed Mill, with a capacity of 40 metric tons per hour, further reinforces the company’s integrated business model. These projects are complemented by the company's "One Million Trees" initiative and other sustainability efforts, reflecting a commitment to environmental responsibility and innovation.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The first-ever Dragon Fruit Festival was held in Bizerte, Tunisia, to highlight the potential of pitaya as a new, high-value agricultural...
records.description: The first-ever Dragon Fruit Festival was held in Bizerte, Tunisia, to highlight the potential of pitaya as a new, high-value agricultural crop. The fruit, which has adapted well to the local climate with low water consumption, is being successfully cultivated in regions like Bizerte, Béja, and Sfax. The festival showcased a significant increase in production over the past two years and promoted modern farming techniques like climate-controlled greenhouses and specialized LED lighting. The event attracted producers and investors, emphasizing dragon fruit as a strategic opportunity to diversify agricultural income and position Tunisia as a regional player in the exotic fruit market through exports to Europe and the Middle East.

records.title: The Manouba governorate in Tunisia has launched a pilot project for smart water management, utilizing artificial intelligence (AI), geogr...
records.description: The Manouba governorate in Tunisia has launched a pilot project for smart water management, utilizing artificial intelligence (AI), geographic information systems (GIS), and remote sensing. This project, which is part of the international PRIMA initiative, is supported by the Ministry of Agriculture, the University of Tunis El Manar, and the General Directorate of Water. It aims to provide farmers with precise recommendations for optimizing irrigation and improving soil quality. With a second pilot area in the Gabès governorate, the initiative seeks to strengthen the resilience of agricultural systems to climate challenges and position Tunisia as a regional pioneer in agricultural AI, all while contributing to food security.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Horticulture Department, has inaugurated the first training course on integrated palm pest manag...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Horticulture Department, has inaugurated the first training course on integrated palm pest management, a collaborative effort with the International Date Council. Experts from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the College of Agriculture at the University of Baghdad are providing lectures on the latest pest control methods. The course is part of the ministry's broader effort to develop the palm and date sector and provide farmers with the expertise and knowledge needed to enhance the global competitiveness of Iraqi dates.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) organized a workshop at its Tripoli headquarters to address the reality and ch...
records.description: The National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) organized a workshop at its Tripoli headquarters to address the reality and challenges facing Libya's fisheries, grain production, and supply chains. The workshop, attended by officials from the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources and the Ministry of Economy and Trade, focused on issues such as the impact of climate change on fish production, marketing difficulties, and legislative challenges. The event concluded with recommendations to enhance food security strategies and activate partnerships between various sectors to ensure sustainable production.
records.institution: The National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB)

records.title: Morocco's horticultural export sector is anticipating a promising 2025/2026 season, following a strong performance in the previous campai...
records.description: Morocco's horticultural export sector is anticipating a promising 2025/2026 season, following a strong performance in the previous campaign that saw a nearly 18% increase in exports to 1.6 million tonnes. While a significant success, this growth is shadowed by structural challenges, including a loss of 40,000 hectares of citrus groves due to water scarcity and persistent drought. The country’s exports, driven by crops like tomatoes, citrus, and berries, are primarily destined for the European Union and the United Kingdom. To sustain this momentum, the sector is focused on targeted investments in sustainable irrigation and refrigerated logistics, and developing new, resilient crop varieties.

records.title: The Sultanate of Oman has signed a technical cooperation agreement with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to implement a...
records.description: The Sultanate of Oman has signed a technical cooperation agreement with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to implement a master plan for the development of the Al Najd area in Dhofar Governorate. The agreement, signed by officials from Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and JICA, aims to leverage the area's natural potential, including abundant water resources and fertile lands, to attract agricultural investment and boost domestic production.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Grape and Pomegranate Cultural Festival is set to launch in Taif Governorate, organized by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agr...
records.description: The Grape and Pomegranate Cultural Festival is set to launch in Taif Governorate, organized by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture in partnership with the private sector. For the first time, the festival will feature an auction for the finest varieties of grapes and pomegranates, alongside cultural events and programs. The festival aims to support seasonal agricultural products, open new marketing channels for farmers, and boost the governorate’s economic and tourism activity.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Early Warning Unit of the General Administration of Nile Water Affairs at the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation has issued a red...
records.description: The Early Warning Unit of the General Administration of Nile Water Affairs at the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation has issued a red alert warning for the states of Blue Nile, Sennar, Khartoum, River Nile, and White Nile. The alert, which was also echoed by the Meteorological Authority, is in response to forecasts of flooding along the Nile due to rising water levels. Citizens are urged to take urgent precautionary measures, such as moving crops, fodder, and livestock to higher ground and securing important documents. The warning also cautioned against the risk of electric shock and called on local authorities to prepare for immediate evacuation if needed.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation

records.title: The olive and date harvests are looking promising, with public services, the Olive Oil Office, and the State Land Office mobilized to sup...
records.description: The olive and date harvests are looking promising, with public services, the Olive Oil Office, and the State Land Office mobilized to support the season. The Ministry of Agriculture's strategy for these harvests focuses on implementing significant storage programs and providing subsidies to farmers to manage abundance and maintain prices. For cereals, efforts are being made to double the quantity of selected seeds, building on the previous season's 12 million quintals harvest. The ministry official also confirmed that farmers will have no difficulty in obtaining seeds or fertilizers.

records.title: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has refuted social media claims that tomatoes are being artificially ripened wi...
records.description: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has refuted social media claims that tomatoes are being artificially ripened with "ethryl" to enhance their color. The Ministry clarified that the white coloration sometimes observed inside tomatoes is a natural occurrence, primarily caused by high temperatures, known as heat stress, which affects the production of the red pigment lycopene. Additionally, nutritional imbalances, such as deficiencies in potassium and calcium or excessive nitrogen, can also contribute to this phenomenon.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia will host the 27th session of the Near East Forestry and Range Commission in Jeddah, a collaborative effort w...
records.description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia will host the 27th session of the Near East Forestry and Range Commission in Jeddah, a collaborative effort with the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification. The session will focus on integrated solutions for forests and rangelands to mitigate the effects of climate change, improve food systems, and support sustainable rural development. Key topics include land restoration, combating desertification, and the use of artificial intelligence for climate-resilient land systems.
records.institution: The National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Yemen Bounty Festival is set to kick off its second season in Sana'a, organized by the Capital Sana'a Local Council and the Ministry...
records.description: The Yemen Bounty Festival is set to kick off its second season in Sana'a, organized by the Capital Sana'a Local Council and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources. The five-day event aims to reinforce Yemen's agricultural reputation by highlighting the quality and diversity of its products and opening new prospects for marketing and investment. This year's festival will particularly focus on key crops such as pomegranates, grapes, apples, and dates. It will feature a range of activities including exhibitions, workshops, and seminars, serving as a national platform to encourage farmers to improve crop quality and promote the agricultural sector to enhance its global competitiveness.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Iraq's wheat harvest has concluded with an estimated production of 5.1 million tonnes, which is about 13 percent above average.
records.description: Iraq's wheat harvest has concluded with an estimated production of 5.1 million tonnes, which is about 13 percent above average. According to a UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) report, this impressive yield was achieved despite a period of below-average rainfall. The success is credited to improved rainfall during crucial months, the use of modern irrigation systems, and the implementation of high-yielding seed varieties, which collectively helped to overcome water deficits and ensure an abundant harvest.

records.title: A conference is being held in Rabat to discuss the future of sustainable food systems in Morocco.
records.description: A conference is being held in Rabat to discuss the future of sustainable food systems in Morocco. Organized by the AMAECO and AMEIA associations, the event will gather experts, institutional representatives, researchers, and professionals from the agricultural and agri-food sectors. The conference will focus on the transformations needed to create more resilient and sustainable food systems in response to climate, economic, and social challenges. The discussion will also highlight potential actions and development prospects to support Morocco's agri-food transition.
records.institution: AMAECO and AMEIA associations, IAV Hassan II

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Morocco is facing significant challenges in its agricultural sector due to water scarcity and droughts.
records.description: Morocco is facing significant challenges in its agricultural sector due to water scarcity and droughts. To combat this, the Moulouya Hydraulic Basin Agency (ABH) and other stakeholders are promoting the rational management of water resources. This is being done through a consultation meeting in Driouch, which is part of the National Drinking Water Supply and Irrigation Program 2020-2027. The objective is to involve farmers and user associations in the effort to combat overexploitation and encourage more efficient irrigation practices.

records.title: Morocco's citrus sector, a major agricultural powerhouse, is facing a crisis due to water scarcity and high salinity levels, particularly...
records.description: Morocco's citrus sector, a major agricultural powerhouse, is facing a crisis due to water scarcity and high salinity levels, particularly in the Souss-Massa region. In response, Morocco has launched a massive desalination program, with the Agadir-Chtouka plant already providing water for irrigation. The government aims to produce 1.7 billion cubic meters of desalinated water annually by 2030. Despite challenges like labor shortages and competition from Spain, the sector is expected to export around 669,000 tons of citrus in the 2025–26 season, a 10% increase over the previous year, according to Morocco Foodex. This strategic effort, which is being showcased at the Fruit Attraction trade show, highlights the country’s resilience and its ambition to remain a leading global citrus supplier.

records.title: The Syrian Ministry of Agriculture has initiated a campaign to vaccinate cattle against foot-and-mouth disease.
records.description: The Syrian Ministry of Agriculture has initiated a campaign to vaccinate cattle against foot-and-mouth disease. In the first phase, 400,000 doses of the preventive vaccine will be administered across all governorates. The remaining cattle will be vaccinated in a subsequent second phase.

records.title: The Algerian provinces of Batna and Khenchela are expecting a significant increase in apple production for the current agricultural season.
records.description: The Algerian provinces of Batna and Khenchela are expecting a significant increase in apple production for the current agricultural season. The Directorate of Agricultural Services (DSA) in Batna forecasts a production of nearly 2 million quintals, a significant rise from the 1.6 million quintals of the previous year. Apple orchards in the province cover over 5,878 hectares, with the most common varieties being "Golden Delicia," "Star Crimson," "Royal Gala," and "Hana." Similarly, the DSA in Khenchela predicts a production of 1.75 million quintals, a 100,000 quintal increase from the last season. This growth is a result of state support, with farmers benefiting from irrigation and new varieties. In Khenchela, efforts are also underway to create an activity zone for apple processing industries and to provide farmers with interest-free investment credits for building cold rooms to preserve the harvest.

records.title: The first Bahrain Veterinary Conference and Exhibition has been inaugurated, with broad local and international participation.
records.description: The first Bahrain Veterinary Conference and Exhibition has been inaugurated, with broad local and international participation. The two-day event emphasizes Bahrain's dedication to supporting the livestock sector, which is considered a crucial element of the nation's food security and sustainable development goals.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture

records.title: The International Association of Horticultural Producers (AIPH) has approved Expo 2029 Garden in Baghdad, Iraq’s first AIPH-recognized In...
records.description: The International Association of Horticultural Producers (AIPH) has approved Expo 2029 Garden in Baghdad, Iraq’s first AIPH-recognized International Green Expo. Scheduled to take place from October 2029 to April 2030 on a 375-hectare site along the Tigris River, the event will feature cultural gardens, national pavilions, renewable energy projects, and business centres under the theme “Green Light in Desert.” Organizers expect participation from 50 countries, with 4 million international and 8 million domestic visitors, while boosting Iraq’s infrastructure, tourism, and research capacity. Legacy plans include transforming the site into a permanent hub for culture, sports, and green innovation, marking a milestone in Iraq’s commitment to sustainable urban development.

records.title: The agricultural producers' price index (APPI) rose by 4.8% during the first eight months of the year compared to the same period the pre...
records.description: The agricultural producers' price index (APPI) rose by 4.8% during the first eight months of the year compared to the same period the previous year. This cumulative increase was primarily driven by higher prices for certain crops, most notably hot peppers, green sweet peppers, and bananas. However, prices for other crops, including potatoes, colored sweet peppers, and eggplants, saw a decline. On a monthly basis, the index dropped in August, which was mainly attributed to lower prices for tomatoes, colored sweet peppers, and figs, despite some increases for other produce.

records.title: Oman has initiated its first pilot oyster farming project on Masirah Island to diversify food resources and bolster the economy in line w...
records.description: Oman has initiated its first pilot oyster farming project on Masirah Island to diversify food resources and bolster the economy in line with Oman Vision 2040. The project, implemented by a private company, utilizes a semi-automated system imported from New Zealand to efficiently raise oysters. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, this aquaculture initiative is a crucial, sustainable solution to meet the growing national demand for seafood, which is increasing with the country's economic and social development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: The Development Bank of Oman received a Sustainable Project Finance Award from the European Organization for Sustainable Development (EOSD).
records.description: The Development Bank of Oman received a Sustainable Project Finance Award from the European Organization for Sustainable Development (EOSD). The award recognizes the bank's efforts in financing sustainable farming projects in Al Najd, Dhofar, an agricultural zone crucial to Oman's food security and economic diversification.

records.title: A specialized workshop was held in southern Hebron to address the impact of drought, climate change, and geopolitical issues on agricultu...
records.description: A specialized workshop was held in southern Hebron to address the impact of drought, climate change, and geopolitical issues on agricultural development. The Minister of Agriculture, along with local authorities, international organizations, and farmers, participated in the event. During the workshop, the need to reclaim and cultivate mountainous areas was emphasized as a way to counter expansion, and a pioneering project was proposed to reduce the costs of drilling wells. The Ministry highlighted its achievements and future projects, calling on local authorities to submit well-planned project ideas to secure funding. The workshop concluded with discussions and recommendations aimed at developing the agricultural sector and strengthening the resilience of farmers.

records.title: Tadweer Group has launched a new company, Tadweer Collection (Tajmee’e), to revolutionize waste collection in Abu Dhabi.
records.description: Tadweer Group has launched a new company, Tadweer Collection (Tajmee’e), to revolutionize waste collection in Abu Dhabi. This initiative is a critical step towards a cleaner and more sustainable emirate, aligning with the UAE's national environmental goals and circular economy vision. The new company will use AI-powered systems for route optimization and digitally-enabled safety monitoring tools to enhance operational efficiency, reduce emissions, and improve safety standards. This next-generation fleet is designed to provide consistent, high-quality service while delivering measurable benefits in emissions reduction and resource recovery, positioning the group as a leader in sustainable waste management.

records.title: In the Al-Hodeidah governorate, several economic empowerment projects have been launched with a total cost exceeding 1.032 billion riyals...
records.description: In the Al-Hodeidah governorate, several economic empowerment projects have been launched with a total cost exceeding 1.032 billion riyals, aimed at transforming aid-dependent families into self-sufficient producers. These projects, funded by the General Authority for Zakat and implemented by the General Authority for the Development of Small and Micro Projects, include the distribution of cows to hundreds of families to create sustainable income and enhance food security. Additionally, support is being provided to the palm sector through the distribution of solar systems to farmers to help replant hundreds of thousands of damaged palm trees, thereby reviving a crucial agricultural resource and strengthening the local economy.
records.institution: General Authority for the Development of Small and Micro Projects

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), has established an in...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), has established an integrated dairy processing and marketing center in Basra’s Madinah district to support and empower rural women while promoting sustainable livelihoods. Equipped with modern machinery, the center helps reduce physical effort and boost production levels, while training programs on equipment use and marketing enable the production of high-quality dairy products. This initiative is part of broader efforts by the Ministry and FAO across several governorates to provide sustainable job opportunities, strengthen women’s participation in the agricultural sector, and enhance the local economy.

records.domain: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Horticulture Department at Hawija Station, has successfully multiplied the Al-Nahrain variety of...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Horticulture Department at Hawija Station, has successfully multiplied the Al-Nahrain variety of yellow corn under the National Fodder Crop Multiplication and Processing Program. The crop achieved high germination rates and strong plant growth, demonstrating the quality of local seeds and the effectiveness of agricultural plans. This achievement supports the Ministry’s strategy to strengthen food security and advance the agricultural sector by providing high-yield, high-quality seeds that meet farmers’ needs and promote the adoption of local varieties.

records.title: Morocco has become the second-largest tomato supplier to the European Union, surpassing Spain and ranking just behind the Netherlands.
records.description: Morocco has become the second-largest tomato supplier to the European Union, surpassing Spain and ranking just behind the Netherlands. This shift reflects the country’s growing production capacity, favorable climatic conditions, competitive costs, and effective export strategies supported by logistics improvements and government policies. While Spanish producers face challenges from rising water costs and stricter environmental standards, Morocco’s exporters continue to strengthen their market position by ensuring quality, meeting EU requirements, and adapting to climate and cost pressures. This achievement highlights Morocco’s strategic role in European agricultural trade while underscoring the challenges of sustaining competitiveness in a demanding market.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Oman’s first utility-scale solar and battery storage project will be developed through a partnership between Nama Power and Water Procure...
records.description: Oman’s first utility-scale solar and battery storage project will be developed through a partnership between Nama Power and Water Procurement and a consortium led by Masdar alongside Al Khadra Partners, Korea Midland Power, and OQ Alternative Energy. The Ibri III Independent Power Project will combine a 500 MW solar photovoltaic plant with a 100 MWh battery energy storage system, covering nearly 10 million square meters. With an investment of around $299 million, the project will reduce carbon dioxide emissions by about 505,000 tonnes annually, contribute up to 4 percent of renewable energy to the national electricity mix, and advance Oman’s Vision 2040 goals of energy diversification, sustainability, and enhanced energy security.

records.title: The Janaen Salalah Project, led by Omran Group’s subsidiary Janaen in partnership with Oman Agriculture Development, is a landmark agri-t...
records.description: The Janaen Salalah Project, led by Omran Group’s subsidiary Janaen in partnership with Oman Agriculture Development, is a landmark agri-tourism initiative in Dhofar Governorate that combines large-scale farming with tourism experiences. Spanning over 786,000 square metres, the project will cultivate coconuts, papayas, and cashews—introducing cashew farming commercially in Oman for the first time—while implementing advanced irrigation and sustainable agricultural systems. By integrating modern agriculture with interactive tourism activities, the project aims to strengthen food security, promote sustainable use of natural resources, create jobs, support SMEs, and establish Oman as a distinctive agri-tourism destination.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the European Union, inaugurated the “Baladi Market” marketing day in Ramalla...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the European Union, inaugurated the “Baladi Market” marketing day in Ramallah, bringing together around 20 exhibitors from Hebron and Jenin to showcase grapes, grape-based products, and various rural goods. The event, held semi-annually, aims to support farmers facing difficult conditions by opening new marketing opportunities, enhancing resilience, preserving agricultural heritage, and strengthening the local economy through joint efforts to promote the Palestinian agricultural sector.

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has launched three private sector investment opportunities in the Makkah Region to boo...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has launched three private sector investment opportunities in the Makkah Region to boost agricultural development, vegetation cover, and food security. These include establishing an agricultural city for fruit tree cultivation and marketing services in Al-Qunfudhah, setting up a seedling nursery in Adham, and creating a wild seedling nursery in Al-Qunfudhah. The initiatives aim to attract investors through the “Furas” platform, supporting local production, job creation, and the broader goals of Saudi Vision 2030.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The date season in Tozeur governorate is expected to yield over 60,000 tons with higher quality compared to last year, supported by favor...
records.description: The date season in Tozeur governorate is expected to yield over 60,000 tons with higher quality compared to last year, supported by favorable growing conditions and limited pest issues. Nearly 70% of palm groves have already been sold at encouraging prices, with ripening rates advancing well and some farmers beginning early harvests. While the official harvest is set to take place from early October to early November under exporters and collectors, part of the crop has already reached markets. Around 60% of date bunches were protected with mosquito nets this season, a figure supplemented by stocks from the previous year.
records.institution: The Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (URAP)

records.title: The National Food Safety Authority (INSSPA), in coordination with security forces, conducted field operations in several governorates tha...
records.description: The National Food Safety Authority (INSSPA), in coordination with security forces, conducted field operations in several governorates that led to the seizure of three tonnes of poultry and red meat unfit for consumption, most of which were stored in illegal slaughterhouses. Significant quantities of spoiled and expired meat were confiscated, while live poultry was reintegrated into official distribution channels in collaboration with municipal guards and relevant authorities. The operations also resulted in the closure of non-compliant premises and the issuance of official reports, reinforcing efforts to uphold food safety regulations.

records.title: Tunisia’s olive oil sector, rooted in centuries of tradition, is undergoing a transformation driven by strategic investments, export init...
records.description: Tunisia’s olive oil sector, rooted in centuries of tradition, is undergoing a transformation driven by strategic investments, export initiatives, and sustainability measures supported by the Tunisian government and the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI). Despite recent declines in revenue due to falling global prices, export volumes have grown, with Spain, Italy, and Canada being key destinations, while organic olive oil is gaining a stronger foothold in markets such as Italy, Spain, and the USA. National programs emphasize environmentally friendly practices, packaging, and marketing strategies to strengthen competitiveness, improve quality, and enhance resilience to climate change. These efforts aim to position Tunisia as a global leader in high-value olive oil production and exports.

records.title: Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) and Food Tech Valley have partnered to establish a 260,000-square-foot logistics hub in Dubai aimed at boosting...
records.description: Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) and Food Tech Valley have partnered to establish a 260,000-square-foot logistics hub in Dubai aimed at boosting food distribution efficiency and sustainability. The project will cut delivery distances, reduce carbon emissions by an estimated 2,500 tonnes annually, and lower fleet-related emissions by up to 35 percent, while increasing distribution efficiency by about 33 percent. Scheduled to begin construction in late 2025 and complete in early 2027, the hub will create over 100 jobs and feature advanced technologies. Designed to support AAFG’s integrated operations in dairy, poultry, eggs, and juices, the facility aligns with the UAE’s National Food Security Strategy 2051 and Net Zero 2050 goals, while strengthening supply chains and positioning Dubai as a leader in food innovation and resilience.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries and the Ministry of Internal Trade and National Market Regulation agreed, du...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries and the Ministry of Internal Trade and National Market Regulation agreed, during a coordination meeting in Algiers, to launch a joint information system for monitoring prices and ensuring the supply of consumer products. According to a press release from the Ministry of Agriculture, the system will use modern technologies to track availability, anticipate fluctuations, and prevent shortages or price increases. The two ministries also agreed to establish a permanent working group to carry out daily monitoring of product availability and maintain market stability.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries and the Ministry of Internal Trade and National Market Regulation

records.title: Egypt has introduced a binding protocol requiring fertilizer manufacturers to commit to supply quotas for agriculture, local auctions, an...
records.description: Egypt has introduced a binding protocol requiring fertilizer manufacturers to commit to supply quotas for agriculture, local auctions, and exports, following a government decision to raise natural gas prices for factories. The Ministry of Industry and Transport announced the measure during a meeting of the Ministerial Group for Industrial Development. Regulatory oversight will be carried out by the Competition Protection Authority and the Consumer Protection Agency, while a study by the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS) highlighted rising costs of gas supply. The initiative reflects the government’s strategy to safeguard food security and support fertilizer production as a cornerstone of the agricultural sector.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry and Transport

records.title: The International Grains Council (IGC) projects global wheat flour trade to fall to 15.5 million tonnes in 2024-25, a three-year low, dri...
records.description: The International Grains Council (IGC) projects global wheat flour trade to fall to 15.5 million tonnes in 2024-25, a three-year low, driven largely by reduced imports from Iraq, the world’s second-largest buyer. Iraq’s record harvest, export authorizations, and tariff measures cut imports to 1.2 million tonnes, the lowest in 14 years. While Turkey’s exports declined sharply, Egypt emerged as a major supplier with 2 million tonnes, mainly to sub-Saharan Africa. The IGC anticipates a rebound in 2025-26, supported by stronger demand in Near East Asia and Africa, and recovering imports from Iraq.
records.institution: The Ministry of Trade, Grain Board of Iraq (GBI).

records.title: Den Berk Délice has expanded its operations in Morocco’s Souss-Massa region, where it established modern greenhouses for cultivating snac...
records.description: Den Berk Délice has expanded its operations in Morocco’s Souss-Massa region, where it established modern greenhouses for cultivating snack tomatoes and seedless snack peppers to supply the European market year-round. Operating under Den Berk Délice Maroc, the company combines Belgian expertise with Morocco’s natural conditions, supported by mid-tech systems such as efficient irrigation, advanced ventilation, and closed water systems to ensure sustainable production. With investments in social facilities, fair wages, and quality control in both Morocco and Belgium, the company emphasizes flavor, quality, and partnership while planning further expansion to meet growing demand.

records.title: The National Dialogue on the Development and Valorization of Seaweed was launched in Rabat, under the chairmanship of the Ministry of Agr...
records.description: The National Dialogue on the Development and Valorization of Seaweed was launched in Rabat, under the chairmanship of the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Water and Forests, responsible for Maritime Fisheries. Organized by the National Agency for the Development of Aquaculture (ANDA) in partnership with the World Bank, the initiative aims to establish seaweed farming as a key pillar of Morocco’s blue economy. With 3,500 kilometers of coastline and diverse marine ecosystems, Morocco has the potential to produce up to 100,000 tons of algae, offering significant economic and environmental opportunities. The dialogue brings together public institutions, experts, economic operators, and investors to explore the wide range of applications of algae—food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, biomaterials, and textiles.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Water and Forests

records.title: The Applied Research Institute – Jerusalem (ARIJ), in cooperation with the Ministry of Agriculture through its North Hebron Directorate,...
records.description: The Applied Research Institute – Jerusalem (ARIJ), in cooperation with the Ministry of Agriculture through its North Hebron Directorate, distributed hydroponic equipment to farmers as part of the “Developing Livelihoods and Adaptation to Climate Change in Palestine” project. This initiative promotes modern agricultural technologies to enhance sustainability, improve production efficiency, and help farmers adapt to climate change while safeguarding their livelihoods.

records.title: FAO, with support from Swiss cooperation, organized a training workshop in Tunis under the BIOREST project to strengthen professional org...
records.description: FAO, with support from Swiss cooperation, organized a training workshop in Tunis under the BIOREST project to strengthen professional organizations in the organic farming sector. The event brought together 23 participants, including 13 women and five women-led organizations, to build a shared vision for improved performance, governance, and management. Participants analyzed their structures, identified strengths and challenges, and developed strategic objectives with an action plan for the coming years. The workshop emphasized collaboration among organizations and highlighted the key role of women in driving and shaping the organic farming sector in Tunisia.

records.title: The DINAMO project, led by the Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency (APIA) with joint financing from the European Union and the Inter...
records.description: The DINAMO project, led by the Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency (APIA) with joint financing from the European Union and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), aims to strengthen the resilience of small mountain farmers in northwest Tunisia. With a budget exceeding 100 million dinars, it targets over 10,000 beneficiaries across Jendouba, Béja, Le Kef, and Siliana through infrastructure improvements, technical training, and rural entrepreneurship support. Implemented in coordination with institutions like the Office of Development of the Northwest (ODNO) and regional agricultural development commissions (CRDA), the project promotes sustainable farming, environmental protection, and inclusive governance.

records.title: The Export Promotion Center (CEPEX) and the Food Industries Promotion Agency (APIA) are jointly coordinating Tunisia’s participation in t...
records.description: The Export Promotion Center (CEPEX) and the Food Industries Promotion Agency (APIA) are jointly coordinating Tunisia’s participation in the international trade fair “Food Ingredients Europe (FIE) 2025” in Paris. This global platform, considered the largest for agri-food additives and ingredients, showcases innovations and trends in natural and food ingredients. Tunisian companies taking part will represent sectors including intermediate food products, supplements, vitamins, and plant extracts. Registration for the national pavilion is available through the E-CEPEX platform.

records.title: The Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS), in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture and the National Agricultural Bank (BNA), launched a...
records.description: The Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS), in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture and the National Agricultural Bank (BNA), launched a financing program to support 450 small cereal producers with 6.5 million dinars to strengthen production and resilience. The initiative includes relaxed lending conditions, expanded budgets, and collaboration with private cooperatives to improve financial inclusion and reach underserved areas. By easing access to credit and removing traditional barriers, the program enhances food security, reduces disparities, and empowers farmers, including women and the elderly. Public institutions highlighted the initiative as a key step in advancing sustainable and inclusive agricultural development in Tunisia.

records.title: The United Arab Emirates has announced a nationwide ban on single-use plastic products, covering the import, production, and trade of ite...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates has announced a nationwide ban on single-use plastic products, covering the import, production, and trade of items such as cups, lids, cutlery, food containers, and plates. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed the measure as part of the country’s broader transition toward a circular economy and sustainable waste management. Abu Dhabi’s Environment Agency (EAD) has already pioneered incentive-based bottle return schemes that recovered over 130 million bottles, while Dubai and Sharjah have each introduced bans and restrictions on plastic bags and other single-use items. The policy reflects the UAE’s commitment to protecting the environment, cutting plastic waste at the source, and encouraging businesses and consumers to adopt reusable alternatives, positioning the country among a growing group of nations phasing out single-use plastics.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment

records.title: Bahrain signed an agreement with the International Dates Council to establish the International Date Observatory, which will serve as a g...
records.description: Bahrain signed an agreement with the International Dates Council to establish the International Date Observatory, which will serve as a global hub for collecting, analyzing, and publishing data on the date industry to support transparency, international trade, and Bahrain’s agricultural heritage. The observatory aims to provide a reliable reference for decision-makers and member countries, reflecting Bahrain’s efforts to strengthen its position as a regional and international center for the date sector. Hosting the observatory highlights Bahrain’s role in promoting agricultural innovation and advancing the date industry as a knowledge- and innovation-driven sector in line with global cooperation and development goals.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipalities and Agriculture

records.title: DP World has announced a $29 million investment to build a large cold storage facility in Egypt’s Al Oula region within the Elsewedy Indu...
records.description: DP World has announced a $29 million investment to build a large cold storage facility in Egypt’s Al Oula region within the Elsewedy Industrial Park. The warehouse will cover over 174,000 square feet, with eight temperature-controlled chambers and capacity for 25,000 pallets of refrigerated and frozen goods. This project, supported by DP World Egypt, aims to strengthen the country’s cold chain capacity, reduce post-harvest losses, and improve food supply stability, positioning Egypt as a key player in the growing regional cold chain market.

records.title: Egypt’s agricultural exports have surpassed 7.2 million tons so far in 2025, an increase of more than 600,000 tons compared to the same p...
records.description: Egypt’s agricultural exports have surpassed 7.2 million tons so far in 2025, an increase of more than 600,000 tons compared to the same period last year, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation. Citrus fruits led the exports at over 1.9 million tons, followed by fresh potatoes (1.3 million tons) and onions (256,000 tons), alongside beans, sweet potatoes, grapes, mangoes, tomatoes, garlic, pomegranates, strawberries, and guavas. The ministry highlighted that this growth reflects the sector’s rising competitiveness, expanded market access, and the combined efforts of farmers, exporters, and quarantine services, while contributing to foreign currency inflows and job creation across the value chain.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has continued its autumn spraying and dipping campaign in Basra Governorate to curb animal diseases suc...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has continued its autumn spraying and dipping campaign in Basra Governorate to curb animal diseases such as hemorrhagic fever. Supervised by the Veterinary Department, the campaign targets ticks through spraying and dipping animals and their pens, aiming to protect livestock and safeguard public health. Veterinary teams highlighted field challenges, and the ministry pledged to provide the needed support to ensure the campaign’s success.

records.title: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation, through the Jordan Valley Authority, has received newly constructed water harvesting pits and sites...
records.description: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation, through the Jordan Valley Authority, has received newly constructed water harvesting pits and sites across Jordan, implemented in two phases by the Inter-Islamic Network on Water Resources Development and Management (INWRDAM) with a total capacity of 2.1 million cubic metres. The initiative, part of the 2023–2024 strategic plan and the Economic Modernisation Vision, aims to maximise water harvesting, improve living and environmental conditions, create agricultural and tourism opportunities, and reduce poverty and unemployment. It also seeks to mitigate desertification, adapt to climate change, and replenish groundwater while promoting community participation, particularly by women and youth.
records.institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation

records.title: The World Food Programme (WFP) has intensified efforts to support Jordanian agriculture in adapting to climate change by introducing low-...
records.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) has intensified efforts to support Jordanian agriculture in adapting to climate change by introducing low-interest loan products through the Agricultural Credit Corporation, training nearly 450 farmers, cooperatives, and agri-food companies in Jerash, Mafraq, and Balqa, and promoting modern technologies such as drip irrigation and integrated climate-smart practices on more than 120 farms. These interventions aim to boost productivity, reduce post-harvest losses, and strengthen crop resilience to extreme weather. In parallel, WFP is working with the National Centre for Security and Crisis Management to provide technical and logistical support to the National Technical Committee on Drought, including preparation of a 2024/2025 national drought monitoring report through the PRISM platform, which enables real-time monitoring, analysis, and forecasting of climate risks.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture launched the "Our Lands" (ARADINA) project in Beirut, with the participation of representatives from official...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture launched the "Our Lands" (ARADINA) project in Beirut, with the participation of representatives from official bodies, diplomatic missions, international organizations, civil society, and farmers’ cooperatives. The four-year initiative, funded by the French Development Agency (AFD) in partnership with the Mediterranean Agronomic Institute of Montpellier (CIHEAM Montpellier), Action Against Hunger, and Fair Trade Lebanon, will support around 2,500 farmers and 145 cooperatives across the country by promoting sustainable agroecological practices and strengthening production and marketing chains. The project aligns with national strategies to assist crisis-affected farmers, improve their skills, enhance market access, and encourage environmentally friendly practices that safeguard natural resources, contributing to food security, environmental protection, and rural development through stronger engagement of civil society, cooperatives, and SMEs.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Baalbek-Hermel Agriculture Department and Nabi Othman Agricultural Center, in cooperation with t...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Baalbek-Hermel Agriculture Department and Nabi Othman Agricultural Center, in cooperation with the Federation of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture in Lebanon and with the support of Jbouleh Municipality, organized an advisory seminar in Jbouleh on climate change challenges and adaptation methods. The session gathered farmers and municipal representatives to discuss the causes and impacts of climate change on agriculture in Lebanon, particularly in the Bekaa Valley, and highlighted adaptation strategies such as modern irrigation, improved water management, covered agriculture, and drought-resistant crops. Presentations showcased successful local and international models, while discussions emphasized the need for stronger Ministry support, coordination with the Ministry of Energy on water scarcity, wider dissemination of guidance seminars, and support for rainwater harvesting.

records.title: Libya and Italy discussed finalizing a draft Memorandum of Understanding on fisheries cooperation during a meeting in Tripoli, focusing o...
records.description: Libya and Italy discussed finalizing a draft Memorandum of Understanding on fisheries cooperation during a meeting in Tripoli, focusing on training and capacity building, scientific research, support for fish processing centres, and expanding marketing channels to European markets in line with international standards. The talks also addressed steps to obtain a European Union export number for Libyan maritime products and the establishment of the first Libyan-Italian joint venture in the fisheries sector, with both sides agreeing to maintain communication between technical teams to ensure effective implementation.

records.title: The Moroccan producer Cap Growers is diversifying its products by introducing the Rojo Brillante variety of persimmons in the Chichaoua r...
records.description: The Moroccan producer Cap Growers is diversifying its products by introducing the Rojo Brillante variety of persimmons in the Chichaoua region. This new addition, which has an export season from October to December, comes despite challenging climatic conditions, including persistent drought and a hot summer. These conditions have led to a 20% drop in overall persimmon production in the region and a trend toward smaller fruit sizes. The persimmons will join the company's existing portfolio of fruits, which are exported to markets in Canada, Europe, the UK, the Middle East, and Russia.

records.title: The inaugural IFAT Saudi Arabia exhibition will debut in Riyadh to serve as a hub for environmental innovation, focusing on technologies...
records.description: The inaugural IFAT Saudi Arabia exhibition will debut in Riyadh to serve as a hub for environmental innovation, focusing on technologies related to waste, water, and the environment. Organized by dmg events and licensed by Messe München, with the National Center for Waste Management (MWAN) as a key partner, the event is timed to support over $192 billion in private investment opportunities in the kingdom’s waste and water sectors. The exhibition aligns closely with Saudi Vision 2030 and Net Zero 2060 goals, aiming to accelerate technology adoption to achieve targets such as meeting 90% of water demand through desalination by 2030 and a 90% landfill diversion rate by 2040. The event will feature over 450 exhibitors and a strategic summit for policymakers.

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has adopted 40 innovative technologies for water treatment and reuse, such as algae-ba...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has adopted 40 innovative technologies for water treatment and reuse, such as algae-based treatment, nanobubbles, zero liquid discharge, pyrolysis, and AI-assisted methods. The decision followed the Kingdom’s first national report on innovation trends in the water sector, which analyzed over 10,000 sources and 100 million data points using the OECD 2024 framework. The report reviewed 27,000 signals related to wastewater treatment and reuse, evaluating technical indicators and investment feasibility. Wastewater treatment and reuse is identified as a national priority under “Environmental Sustainability and Basic Needs,” with the report highlighting innovation trends, policies, and investment opportunities for policymakers, investors, and entrepreneurs. It also featured insights from ENOWA, NEOM’s energy and water company, ensuring a practical perspective aligned with Saudi Vision 2030.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation praised Al-Gadarif State’s efforts in rehabilitating forests damaged by encroachments and exce...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation praised Al-Gadarif State’s efforts in rehabilitating forests damaged by encroachments and excessive logging, during an inspection of the replanting of 1,000 feddans in Al-Rawashda Forest with the state government. He emphasized the initiative as a crucial step toward restoring forest cover, protecting the environment, and combating climate change, stressing that citizens are key partners in this effort. The state government reaffirmed its commitment to restoring forests, calling for surveys of affected areas, awareness campaigns on the importance of forest conservation, and support to overcome challenges facing Al-Gadarif in its rehabilitation projects.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation

records.title: Supported by the Agricultural Innovation Mechanism for Scale (AIM for Scale), researchers from Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial...
records.description: Supported by the Agricultural Innovation Mechanism for Scale (AIM for Scale), researchers from Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) and the University of Chicago are collaborating to help low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) adopt AI-powered weather forecasting early and build world-class national services. Backed by a UAE Presidential Court grant, the program is training staff from national meteorological and agricultural ministries to use AI models tailored to local needs, with the first cohort from Bangladesh, Chile, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Nigeria trained in the UAE. The initiative, hosted by MBZUAI and the National Centre of Meteorology, provides hands-on capacity building and high-performance laptops to ensure sustainability, while engaging ministries of agriculture to tailor forecasts to farmers’ needs. By extending access to accurate, cost-effective, and hyper-local forecasts, the program aims to improve farm planning, yields, and livelihoods.
records.institution: The Agricultural Innovation Mechanism for Scale (AIM for Scale), Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)

records.title: The Future Food Forum in Dubai, organized by the UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism and the UAE Food & Beverage Business Group, serves a...
records.description: The Future Food Forum in Dubai, organized by the UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism and the UAE Food & Beverage Business Group, serves as a key platform to align on strategies for resilient and sustainable food systems. The event is a central initiative of the UAE Food Cluster, a national strategic program designed to unify stakeholders from farming to trade to drive the nation's food security and sustainability agenda. The forum aims to connect with global food ecosystems, while launching new initiatives such as a Knowledge Hub and a Global Buyers Programme. These efforts are intended to strengthen local supply chains and reinforce the United Arab Emirates' position as a regional hub for trade and food security, in line with the We the UAE 2031 vision.
records.institution: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Sharjah Agricultural and Livestock Production Department organised a Farmers’ Forum in collaboration with local companies and retail...
records.description: The Sharjah Agricultural and Livestock Production Department organised a Farmers’ Forum in collaboration with local companies and retail outlets to discuss developing and marketing local agricultural products, with a focus on sustainable farming, knowledge exchange, and balancing productivity with environmental preservation. The forum, aligned with Sharjah’s vision of a competitive agricultural sector and the UAE’s National Food Security Strategy, highlighted challenges farmers face in reaching markets and explored solutions such as contract farming, modern technologies, and quality standards aligned with global best practices. Participants reviewed successful practices, discussed innovative approaches to sustainability, and emphasised efficient resource use, improved production quality, and the shift from traditional to model farms.
records.institution: The Sharjah Agricultural and Livestock Production Department

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in collaboration with the UAE Alliance for Climate Action (UACA), held a ses...
records.description: The UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in collaboration with the UAE Alliance for Climate Action (UACA), held a session to support private sector stakeholders in advancing climate action. The meeting focused on familiarizing companies with national climate priorities and the new Federal Decree-Law No. (11) of 2024, which provides a framework for reducing emissions. The UAE's approach, aligned with its Net Zero by 2050 goal, emphasizes transparency and partnerships to accelerate innovation and stimulate low-carbon economic growth. The session aimed to bridge the knowledge gap by providing practical guidance on measuring and reporting carbon footprints and highlighted the role of the National Register for Carbon Credits in enabling a green economy.
records.institution: The UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: UAE: Ewec to source 60% power from carbon-free sources by 2035
records.description: Emirates Water and Electricity Company (Ewec) is leading the decarbonization of Abu Dhabi’s water and power sectors by integrating renewable and clean energy with low-carbon desalination. This strategy supports the UAE Net Zero by 2050 Strategic Initiative and the Abu Dhabi Department of Energy’s (DoE) goal for 60% of the emirate's power to be from carbon-free sources by 2035. By 2030, Ewec forecasts a 54% reduction in the carbon intensity of its electricity generation and a 94% reduction in emissions from its water production.

records.title: A campaign was launched in the Al-Mur‘adah and Al-Wasi‘ sub-districts of Al-‘Ashah District, Amran Governorate, to control fall armyworm...
records.description: A campaign was launched in the Al-Mur‘adah and Al-Wasi‘ sub-districts of Al-‘Ashah District, Amran Governorate, to control fall armyworm pests in maize crops and raise farmers’ awareness on effective control methods. The initiative focused on educating farmers about the causes of infestations, early-stage elimination techniques, and the use of natural materials to eradicate the pest. Field teams also carried out diagnostic work to identify infestations, provided preventive guidance, and supported efforts to strengthen the agricultural sector and protect crops from widespread pests.
records.institution: Plant Protection at the Governorate’s Agriculture Sector

records.title: The Water Basin Committee in Taiz governorate held a meeting to review the status of the main water basin and discuss requests for drilli...
records.description: The Water Basin Committee in Taiz governorate held a meeting to review the status of the main water basin and discuss requests for drilling and expanding wells. The session assessed measures taken following previous approvals, postponements, and rejections of drilling requests. Officials emphasized the need to preserve water reserves, balance consumption with replenishment, and construct dams, barriers, and reservoirs to support agriculture and food self-sufficiency. The committee also called for a comprehensive report on basin conditions, clear legal frameworks for permits, and building on past technical studies. Recent activities included studies on rainwater harvesting sites and citizen well-drilling requests within the basin area.
records.institution: The Water Basin Committee in Taiz Governorate

records.title: In partnership with the Egyptian Food Bank (EFB), Unilever Egypt has launched the "Sustainable Agricultural Water Efficiency Project for...
records.description: In partnership with the Egyptian Food Bank (EFB), Unilever Egypt has launched the "Sustainable Agricultural Water Efficiency Project for Farmers" in the Moghra Aquifer Region of Egypt. The project, fully funded by Unilever, is a 12-month initiative that will introduce smart irrigation and other sustainable practices to 153 farmers in its first phase. The project, which has the support of the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation and the Ministry of Social Solidarity, aims to conserve water, with an expected annual saving of 720,000 m³, and strengthen farmers' resilience to drought. It aligns with both Unilever's global sustainability goals and Egypt's national water management priorities.
records.institution: Unilever Egypt, and Egyptian Food Bank

records.title: The Jordanian government has earmarked JD139 million (US$196 million) for wheat subsidies to bolster food security and stabilize bread pr...
records.description: The Jordanian government has earmarked JD139 million (US$196 million) for wheat subsidies to bolster food security and stabilize bread prices. The Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply announced that it will continue providing direct cash assistance to bakeries to protect citizens from fluctuating global commodity prices. Although Jordan’s domestic wheat production is minimal, the country maintains substantial reserves, with its wheat stockpiles reported to cover over 10 months of domestic consumption. To secure its supply, the government is actively engaged in the global grain market by issuing tenders, while also supporting local farmers through a grain purchase program with subsidized prices.
records.institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture organized a seminar in Kahlounieh, Lebanon, as part of its National Agricultural Extension Program.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture organized a seminar in Kahlounieh, Lebanon, as part of its National Agricultural Extension Program. The event, attended by 98 farmers, provided guidance on good agricultural practices and included a practical workshop on fruit tree pruning. The seminar highlighted the importance of pruning for stimulating growth and improving production quality, while also addressing challenges posed by climate change. A separate workshop was held by the Deir el-Qamar Agricultural Center and the "This Land Is Ours" Association to register farmers in the agricultural registry, which is key to receiving support. The event concluded with the distribution of battery-powered pruning tools, funded by the "Sil" Association, to registered farmers.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: In partnership with bp Oman, the company 4Elements launched the "Water for Earth, Water for Life" initiative to install wastewater treatm...
records.description: In partnership with bp Oman, the company 4Elements launched the "Water for Earth, Water for Life" initiative to install wastewater treatment plants and irrigation systems in eight schools in Oman's Ad'Dahirah and Ad'Dakhiliyah regions. The project utilizes Kubota's advanced Japanese Johkasou technology to treat wastewater and reuse it for irrigating school grounds. This effort aims to reduce the consumption of fresh water, expand green spaces, and raise environmental awareness among students, serving as a model of public-private partnership for social and environmental development. The installed systems have a production capacity of 4.2 cubic meters of treated water per day, directly supporting afforestation initiatives in the face of water scarcity.

records.title: The Jericho and Jordan Valley Agriculture Directorate, in cooperation with Palestinian exporters, is conducting daily laboratory tests on...
records.description: The Jericho and Jordan Valley Agriculture Directorate, in cooperation with Palestinian exporters, is conducting daily laboratory tests on Medjool date samples for export to Turkey. These tests check for pesticide residues to ensure the products meet high food safety and quality standards, which is part of the Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture's broader strategy to regulate and develop the date sector. The ministry reports that these measures have been successful in proving the safety of Palestinian dates, helping to enhance their reputation and open new markets globally.
records.institution: Jericho and Jordan Valley Agriculture Directorate

records.title: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦 and the Republic of Poland 🇵🇱 have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen agricultur...
records.description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦 and the Republic of Poland 🇵🇱 have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen agricultural cooperation. The agreement, signed by officials from the two countries' agriculture ministries, aims to support and develop the production and manufacturing of agricultural and livestock products. The MoU focuses on the exchange of technology, support for production, and the implementation of rural development projects, all in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Najran branch of the National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) hosted a delegation from the Om...
records.description: The Najran branch of the National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) hosted a delegation from the Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources. The visit was part of a scientific cooperation effort between Saudi Arabia and Oman to review research programs and modern technologies in citrus cultivation. The program included specialized lectures on micropropagation and biological control, as well as a tour of the center's specialized laboratories and model nurseries. The visit aimed to strengthen research partnerships and facilitate the exchange of knowledge to support sustainable agricultural development.
records.institution: National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah)

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation affirmed his ministry’s commitment to training Al-Gadarif State cadres and supporting digital...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation affirmed his ministry’s commitment to training Al-Gadarif State cadres and supporting digital transformation in agriculture, highlighting plans for partnerships with the state government to promote animal tracks, forests, and water harvesting programs. During a visit to the Mechanized Agriculture Corporation in Al-Gadarif, he stressed the importance of advancing agricultural development, while the state’s acting Wali called for continued farmer support, accurate listing of agricultural holdings, and proper revenue collection. Officials underscored the role of technology in preserving resources, citing the acquisition of early warning units to counter climate risks. The visit also included inspections of the Sudanese-Arab Company for Seed Production’s field models and the Al-Gadarif Grain Silos.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation

records.title: The Abs Multipurpose Agricultural Cooperative Association has launched a new agricultural project in Abs District, Hajjah Governorate, Ye...
records.description: The Abs Multipurpose Agricultural Cooperative Association has launched a new agricultural project in Abs District, Hajjah Governorate, Yemen, to cultivate 20,000 acres of hard soils and sand dunes with sorghum and other grains. The project, which aims to achieve food security and self-sufficiency, is a top priority for the association. It is funded by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and the Agricultural Project Financing Unit. The initiative also seeks to combat desertification and builds on a successful two-year experience in reclaiming desertified land.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: In celebration of World Cleanup Day, Orange Jordan organized a volunteer initiative at the Orange Jerash Forest to promote environmental...
records.description: In celebration of World Cleanup Day, Orange Jordan organized a volunteer initiative at the Orange Jerash Forest to promote environmental sustainability, collecting 81 kilograms of waste for disposal or recycling. This is part of a broader collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture that has resulted in the planting of 2,200 trees at the forest and over 5,000 trees across the Kingdom. These efforts reinforce Orange Jordan's commitment to sustainability, which is a strategic approach that supports the Orange Group's global goal of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2040.

records.title: The World Food Programme (WFP) is expanding its cooperation with Jordanian institutions to support the agriculture sector against climate...
records.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) is expanding its cooperation with Jordanian institutions to support the agriculture sector against climate change. The WFP, in partnership with the National Centre for Security and Crisis Management, is helping to prepare a national drought monitoring report. It is also providing technical support to the Agricultural Credit Corporation to offer low-interest loans to farmers. Over 450 farmers, agri-food companies, and cooperatives in Jerash, Mafraq, and Balqa have been trained to access these loans and adopt water-efficient technologies, such as drip irrigation, to increase productivity and build resilience against climate-related challenges.
records.institution: National Centre for Security and Crisis Management

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture organized a guidance seminar on sustainable agriculture and soil biodiversity in Kfar Qouq, Lebanon, as part...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture organized a guidance seminar on sustainable agriculture and soil biodiversity in Kfar Qouq, Lebanon, as part of its National Agricultural Extension Program. The seminar, attended by over 100 smallholder farmers, featured a presentation on the ministry's role in agricultural extension and the benefits of registering in the agricultural registry. Engineers from REMER COMPANY provided a technical presentation on sustainable farming practices. The event aimed to enhance agricultural awareness, disseminate sound practices, and support the resilience of farmers in Lebanon.

records.title: The Libya Export Development Authority (LEDA) has launched a new initiative to support the national olive oil export sector.
records.description: The Libya Export Development Authority (LEDA) has launched a new initiative to support the national olive oil export sector. As part of a broader government strategy to diversify the economy away from hydrocarbons, LEDA is providing partially subsidized storage tanks of international specifications to olive presses. The goal is to help producers maintain the quality of their olive oil and increase its competitiveness in international markets, thereby supporting a promising sector of the national economy

records.title: The Al Moutmir program, an initiative led by OCP and its scientific partners, has deployed 1,102 demonstration platforms across Morocco t...
records.description: The Al Moutmir program, an initiative led by OCP and its scientific partners, has deployed 1,102 demonstration platforms across Morocco to introduce optimized farming techniques to farmers. The platforms, which cover cereals and legumes, have led to significant yield increases of 21-23% for cereals and 26-33% for legumes compared to traditional practices. Despite challenges posed by climate conditions like droughts and heat waves, the program aims to improve farmers' economic margins and enhance the national agricultural sector's resilience and competitiveness.
