records.title: Undersecretary of Al-Jouf Region Principality Hussein Al Sultan inaugurated the second dates festival in Sakaka yesterday, organized by t...
records.description: Undersecretary of Al-Jouf Region Principality Hussein Al Sultan inaugurated the second dates festival in Sakaka yesterday, organized by the Al-Jouf branch of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture. More than 30 farmers are participating in the five-day festival, showcasing some of the finest dates from Al-Jouf Region. Additionally, 18 families working in the cottage industry, representing the palm and date-related processing industries, are participating. The festival offers direct technical and advisory services to farmers and producers through three specialized laboratories affiliated with the ministry’s branch, providing agricultural testing and consultations. It aims to support farmers and producers, enhance the quality of palm trees and date products from Al-Jouf, and open new marketing channels to strengthen the region’s agricultural presence.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: According to data from the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI), the filling rate of Tunisian dams is at 29.3%.
records.description: According to data from the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI), the filling rate of Tunisian dams is at 29.3%. While this marks a 27% improvement from the previous year, it remains below the average of the last three years. The report highlights a significant regional disparity, with dams in the North holding 92% of the total water volume, while dams in the Centre and Cap-Bon are at critically low filling rates. Daily water consumption far exceeds inflows, jeopardizing the sustainability of reserves. With the agricultural sector consuming nearly 80% of available water, the country is facing a water crisis that requires a profound transformation of management practices, including strengthening storage capacity, modernizing irrigation networks, and promoting awareness campaigns.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The African Union and the Ethiopian government co-hosted the second Africa Climate Summit (ACS2) in Addis Ababa to develop a unified Afri...
records.description: The African Union and the Ethiopian government co-hosted the second Africa Climate Summit (ACS2) in Addis Ababa to develop a unified African position ahead of COP30. A Tunisian delegation participated to ensure that Mediterranean issues were represented on the agenda. The summit provided a platform for Tunisia to share its experiences in sustainable natural resource management and advocate for equitable climate financing to meet its national climate goals. The event also included an Innovation Hub to showcase climate solutions from youth and entrepreneurs, with Tunisia leveraging its own green startups and local initiatives.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Bizerte green waste recovery center in Tunisia is a pioneering project that uses an innovative aeration composting technique to trans...
records.description: The Bizerte green waste recovery center in Tunisia is a pioneering project that uses an innovative aeration composting technique to transform plant waste into high-quality organic compost. This compost is used to maintain local green spaces and supply the municipal nursery, creating a closed-loop recycling system. By recovering approximately 2,000 tons of green waste annually, the center helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions and landfill use, while also lowering waste transportation costs. The initiative, which is based on strategic partnerships with institutions such as the municipality of Rust in Germany and the National Waste Management Agency, has proven successful and has been replicated in other municipalities, demonstrating a concrete step towards a circular economy and sustainable waste management.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Mount Lebanon Agriculture Department and the Jbeil Agricultural Center, organized a seminar in c...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Mount Lebanon Agriculture Department and the Jbeil Agricultural Center, organized a seminar in cooperation with the Ehmej Municipality to educate farmers on the rational use of pesticides and proper apple pruning techniques. As part of the National Agricultural Guidance Program, the seminar highlighted the health and environmental risks of indiscriminate pesticide use and stressed the importance of adhering to proper usage methods. The event also encouraged farmers to register in an official registry to facilitate agricultural planning and support. This initiative aims to protect farmers and consumers, develop the agricultural sector, and enhance the confidence of local and foreign markets in Lebanese products.

records.title: The AGF company is participating for the third time in the SIEMA Food Expo, the International Exhibition of Food Processing, Packaging an...
records.description: The AGF company is participating for the third time in the SIEMA Food Expo, the International Exhibition of Food Processing, Packaging and Machinery. The eighth edition of the expo is being held at the Casablanca Fairs and Exhibitions Office (OFEC). During the event, AGF will showcase its innovations in the agro-industry, including turnkey production lines for fruits and vegetables, IQF Tunnels and Spiral Freezers, as well as Canadian-engineered freezing and cooling equipment. A highlight of the company's participation will be a presentation on "Smart factories: when innovation reinvents productivity."

records.title: The Moroccan avocado sector is facing a period of contrasts, with record export growth masking significant challenges for producers.
records.description: The Moroccan avocado sector is facing a period of contrasts, with record export growth masking significant challenges for producers. The Moroccan Avocado Association reported that the country has surpassed the 100,000-ton export mark for the first time, placing it among the leading suppliers to Europe. However, this commercial success has been complicated by a heatwave that caused an estimated 30% loss in expected volumes, particularly for small-scale producers. Additionally, a surplus in the European market led to a mid-season drop in export prices, while production costs continued to rise. To ensure the long-term resilience of the industry, experts are calling for better sector organization, sustainable irrigation support, and the promotion of Moroccan avocados through quality labels.

records.title: The Ad Hoc Technical Committee on Conservation and Sustainable Use of Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ACSU-10) held its...
records.description: The Ad Hoc Technical Committee on Conservation and Sustainable Use of Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ACSU-10) held its tenth meeting in Doha, organized by the Ministry of Municipality's Agricultural Research Department. The event focused on strengthening regional and international cooperation to conserve and sustainably use plant genetic resources as a fundamental pillar for food security. Discussions covered major challenges in the sector, best practices for adapting to climate change, and a review of the relevant international treaty. The meeting's outcomes are expected to contribute to a clear roadmap for joint action and reflect Qatar's pioneering efforts in this field through its Agricultural Research Department and Gene Bank.

records.title: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) has partnered with a civil society organization to implement the Saba' Sana...
records.description: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) has partnered with a civil society organization to implement the Saba' Sanabel project in Idlib and Aleppo in northern Syria. The initiative aims to enhance food security and sustainability by providing 750 farming families with essential agricultural tools, energy sources, seeds, and training on best practices. As part of a broader humanitarian effort by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the project also seeks to create job opportunities for approximately 500 daily wage workers in the region.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

records.title: The Saudi Irrigation Organization (SIO) took part in the 4th World Irrigation Forum in Kuala Lumpur, where representatives from over 60 c...
records.description: The Saudi Irrigation Organization (SIO) took part in the 4th World Irrigation Forum in Kuala Lumpur, where representatives from over 60 countries discussed irrigation and drainage challenges, innovation, financing, and nature-based solutions for resilience. SIO President Mohammed Abuhaid highlighted Saudi Arabia’s efforts to enhance water use efficiency, expand treated water reuse, and implement over 65 projects nationwide in line with Vision 2030 and the National Water Strategy. He emphasized the Kingdom’s commitment to cooperation with ICID, adopting innovation, and learning from global best practices to advance sustainability in the irrigation sector.

records.title: According to the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI), the filling rate of Tunisian dams is 29.3%, with water reserves reaching 6...
records.description: According to the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI), the filling rate of Tunisian dams is 29.3%, with water reserves reaching 692.6 million m³. While this represents a 27% increase compared to the previous year, it is only an 8.3% rise from the average of the last three years. The northern dams account for the vast majority of these reserves at 34.4% capacity, while dams in the center and Cap-Bon have significantly lower filling rates. In response to a five-year drought, the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries has implemented water rationing measures, including nightly cutoffs for drinking water, and is pushing for the use of non-traditional resources like desalination and treated wastewater. The Tunisian Water Observatory and other experts have called for a formal state of water emergency to be declared to address the ongoing crisis.
