The Ministry is prioritizing food production and developing agricultural industries through initiatives like the Agricultural Industries Complex and the Agricultural Production, Marketing and Manufacturing Accelerator Project, attracting private investment and creating jobs.

records.title: Qatar's livestock sector is experiencing significant growth in 2024, with a total population of over 1.1 million animals, primarily sheep...
records.description: Qatar's livestock sector is experiencing significant growth in 2024, with a total population of over 1.1 million animals, primarily sheep and goats, and 7,089 registered breeders. The Ministry of Municipality has facilitated 50 licensed animal production projects, with 32 operational and 18 under construction, spanning meat, milk, and poultry production. The Ministry is also strengthening its regulatory and supervisory role through licensing, inspection, and certification of veterinary professionals and establishments to ensure food security and sustainable agricultural development in line with Qatar National Vision 2030.

records.title: A Saudi official has denied recent media reports claiming the kingdom would lift its 73-year-old ban on alcohol.
records.description: A Saudi official has denied recent media reports claiming the kingdom would lift its 73-year-old ban on alcohol. Despite the denial, the article notes that Saudi Arabia has eased various restrictions to attract tourism and diversify its economy, and recently opened its first alcohol store in Riyadh exclusively for non-Muslim diplomats. This maintains the longstanding prohibition on alcohol for the general public, with minor exceptions.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The inaugural MENAT Regenerative Agriculture Summit in Riyadh, hosted by Goumbook under the patronage of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Envir...
records.description: The inaugural MENAT Regenerative Agriculture Summit in Riyadh, hosted by Goumbook under the patronage of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA), brought together over 150 regional and global stakeholders to advance sustainable, climate-resilient food systems in the Middle East, North Africa, and Türkiye. The summit focused on "Cultivating Soil Capital: Regenerative Food Systems & Nature-Based Solutions," featuring discussions on policy, innovation, and finance, and showcasing science and research-based innovations from Goumbook’s Regenerative Agriculture Venture Programme. MEWA highlighted national initiatives supporting this transition, and a regional consultation aimed to develop a regenerative agriculture framework for the MENAT region.
records.institution: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: Soaring meat prices, especially for sacrificial sheep, in Tunisia have made Eid al-Adha unaffordable for many families.
records.description: Soaring meat prices, especially for sacrificial sheep, in Tunisia have made Eid al-Adha unaffordable for many families. This situation is worsened by inflation, economic stagnation, and a seven-year drought that has devastated agriculture and livestock supply. In response, the Ministry of Commerce announced a capped pricing scheme for lamb and beef, urging consumers to buy from authorized vendors and calling on retailers to maintain reasonable prices. However, enforcement of these price caps has been inconsistent. While some have suggested suspending the Eid sacrifice, Tunisia's religious leadership has rejected this idea, maintaining it as a sacred rite. Unlike Algeria, Tunisia has not imported livestock since 2012, leaving its local markets to bear the full impact of the crisis.

records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment announced the Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition 2025.
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment announced the Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition 2025. This event, held under the patronage of high-ranking officials, aims to support the national agricultural sector, enhance sustainable food security, empower Emirati farmers, and foster innovation. A key focus will be promoting modern technologies like smart and vertical farming and presenting solutions to combat climate and water challenges, thereby improving local production efficiency and advancing agricultural transformation.

records.title: Algeria's General Directorate of Forests (DGF) will launch the first investment project for timber production within the Green Dam initia...
records.description: Algeria's General Directorate of Forests (DGF) will launch the first investment project for timber production within the Green Dam initiative by the end of this year. This pilot project will involve planting "Paulownia" trees across 500 hectares in the wilaya of Laghouat, aiming to add economic value to the Green Dam and enhance its existing reforestation efforts, which currently span 24,000 hectares with various resistant and fruit trees. Ongoing efforts are focused on rehabilitating and expanding the Green Dam to its target of 400,000 hectares using modern methods and carefully selected species. The DGF is also fully mobilizing resources for the national plan to prevent and control forest fires, leveraging advanced technological means.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Algerian Energy Company (AEC), a subsidiary of the Sonatrach group, plans to integrate 30% to 35% renewable energy into six new seawater...
records.description: Algerian Energy Company (AEC), a subsidiary of the Sonatrach group, plans to integrate 30% to 35% renewable energy into six new seawater desalination plants currently in development. This initiative aims to reduce conventional electricity consumption, lower the carbon footprint, and align with Algeria's national energy transition goals. The tender specifications for these plants will require the construction of photovoltaic and wind energy farms to offset high energy costs. Each plant will have a capacity of 300,000 m³ and will be strategically located across six different wilayas, with the goal of increasing desalinated seawater's contribution to 60% of Algeria's total drinking water supply by 2030.

records.title: Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources reported that the country's water reserves have fallen to their lowest level in 80 years, holding just...
records.description: Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources reported that the country's water reserves have fallen to their lowest level in 80 years, holding just 10 billion cubic meters instead of the required 18 billion for summer. The crisis stems from poor rainfall, reduced snowmelt, and diminished water flow from the Tigris and Euphrates due to upstream dams in Turkey and Iran. As a result, Iraq has sharply reduced agricultural activity to prioritize drinking water and preserve 375,000 hectares of green and productive land. A 10-year water cooperation framework with Turkey, signed in 2024, aims to improve water management.

records.title: Agricultural lands in Gaza have been severely impacted, with less than 5% of croplands cultivable due to damage and access restrictions,...
records.description: Agricultural lands in Gaza have been severely impacted, with less than 5% of croplands cultivable due to damage and access restrictions, leading to a heightened risk of famine. Over 80% of Gaza's cropland has been damaged, with 77.8% inaccessible, and nearly three-quarters of greenhouses and over 80% of wells have been affected, particularly in Rafah and northern areas.

records.title: The UN World Food Program (WFP) has called for a "sustained, and daily" flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza, stating that families are on...
records.description: The UN World Food Program (WFP) has called for a "sustained, and daily" flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza, stating that families are on the brink of starvation and that current aid levels are insufficient. They emphasize the need for safe and timely distribution of aid within Gaza. This comes amidst reports that Israel has kept Gaza crossings closed to essential aid since March 2, leading to a severe humanitarian crisis, despite claims of allowing aid. The WFP highlighted that the few trucks allowed in are merely "a drop in the ocean" for the nearly 2.4 million people dependent on humanitarian aid.

records.title: the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) launched the Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition 2025 in Al Ain as...
records.description: the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) launched the Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition 2025 in Al Ain as part of its national strategy to enhance sustainable agriculture and food security. The four-day event includes over 35 workshops and panel sessions, showcases agri-tech innovations, and features the launch of the National Agriculture Museum. The initiative emphasizes empowering Emirati farmers, promoting youth involvement through the Youth Farmers Council, and strengthening local production efficiency via smart farming practices and stakeholder collaboration. Key partners include Silal, FAO, Al Ain Farms, and Lulu Hypermarket.
records.institution: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: Over 300 parliamentarians from multiple continents signed a petition titled “Urgent Call for Action to End Starvation in Gaza and Ensure...
records.description: Over 300 parliamentarians from multiple continents signed a petition titled “Urgent Call for Action to End Starvation in Gaza and Ensure Humanitarian Access,” demanding the immediate and unconditional opening of all crossings into Gaza, particularly the Rafah crossing. The petition calls on Israel and Egypt to facilitate unrestricted aid flow, condemns the obstruction of food, fuel, and medical supplies, and urges international monitoring to prevent starvation as a weapon of war. The appeal follows alarming reports from UN agencies about severe famine conditions and rising child mortality in Gaza.

records.title: the U.S.
records.description: the U.S. administration granted six-month waivers on key sanctions against Syria, marking a significant easing of the Caesar Act restrictions. The move allows expanded foreign business activities in Syria, enabling humanitarian operations and support for essential infrastructure like electricity and sanitation. Syria’s interim government, led by Ahmad Al-Sharaa, welcomed the decision as critical for attracting reconstruction investment. Damascus also celebrated the announcement, viewing it as a vital step toward economic revival after over a decade of conflict and isolation.
records.institution: U.S. Departments of State and Treasury

records.title: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) has announced the upcoming Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition 2025, a...
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) has announced the upcoming Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition 2025, an event held under the patronage of a high-ranking official, which aligns with the UAE's strategic vision to bolster its agricultural sector and enhance sustainable food security. The conference and exhibition, taking place at ADNEC Centre Al Ain, aim to empower Emirati farmers, foster innovation, and promote sustainable food security by highlighting national agricultural potential and encouraging the adoption of modern technologies. A significant announcement is the launch of the National Agriculture Museum, the first national institution dedicated to documenting the history of agriculture in the UAE. The event's success is supported by strong national and international partnerships, including Silal and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: Morocco announced a 6.2 billion dirham ($670 million) livestock recovery program for 2025–2026 to counter a 38% reduction in cattle and s...
records.description: Morocco announced a 6.2 billion dirham ($670 million) livestock recovery program for 2025–2026 to counter a 38% reduction in cattle and sheep herds caused by six years of drought. Agriculture Minister Ahmed El Bouari stated that the plan includes debt relief, feed subsidies, veterinary services, and genetic improvement measures, including artificial insemination. The government also offers support to farmers retaining breeding females, with 3 billion dirhams allocated for 2025 and 3.2 billion for 2026.

records.title: the UN confirmed it had collected and begun dispatching approximately 90 truckloads of humanitarian aid into Gaza through the Kerem Shalo...
records.description: the UN confirmed it had collected and begun dispatching approximately 90 truckloads of humanitarian aid into Gaza through the Kerem Shalom crossing, the first such delivery since early March. The trucks carried flour, baby food, and medical supplies. Initial delays were due to Israeli restrictions on movement and security concerns. The UN hopes the supplies will reach warehouses for distribution amid worsening famine conditions. The current volume remains far below pre-war and ceasefire-period levels, when hundreds to thousands of trucks entered weekly.

records.title: the UN World Food Programme (WFP) announced that a limited number of bakeries in southern and central Gaza had resumed bread production a...
records.description: the UN World Food Programme (WFP) announced that a limited number of bakeries in southern and central Gaza had resumed bread production after receiving overnight deliveries of aid via the Kerem Shalom crossing. These bakeries are now distributing bread through hot meal kitchens. The WFP emphasized the need for scaled-up assistance, warning that bread alone is insufficient to avert famine.

records.title: EU foreign ministers agreed to lift broad economic sanctions on Syria, aiming to support the country’s recovery after 14 years of civil war.
records.description: EU foreign ministers agreed to lift broad economic sanctions on Syria, aiming to support the country’s recovery after 14 years of civil war. While sanctions tied to the Assad regime and security-related restrictions remain, the EU announced additional targeted measures against human rights violators. The Syrian government welcomed the move, expressing readiness to deepen economic engagement with European partners. The EU had already eased sanctions in sectors like energy, transport, and reconstruction but now signals a more comprehensive policy shift.

records.title: In Mahdha, Buraimi Governorate, Omani farmer Ali bin Hamad al Badi is transforming arid land into a productive farm cultivating figs, dat...
records.description: In Mahdha, Buraimi Governorate, Omani farmer Ali bin Hamad al Badi is transforming arid land into a productive farm cultivating figs, dates, mangoes, and lemons. With technical and on-ground support from the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, his farm has become a model of successful, sustainable agriculture. Notably, Badi harvests up to 100kg of Turkish brown figs daily and plans to expand with 550 yellow Spanish fig seedlings. His success story is part of a broader national initiative promoting food security, diversification of crops, and investment in high-value, commercially viable agriculture. The Ministry's efforts emphasize hands-on assistance and knowledge transfer to support innovative farmers and increase Oman’s agricultural self-reliance.
records.institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: the UN received Israeli approval to allow approximately 100 aid trucks into Gaza, easing an 11-week total blockade.
records.description: the UN received Israeli approval to allow approximately 100 aid trucks into Gaza, easing an 11-week total blockade. While nine trucks were cleared a day earlier via the Kerem Shalom crossing, only five had entered and remained under Israeli control pending final checks. These trucks carried baby food and nutritional supplements urgently needed to save infant lives. UN officials warned that famine is looming and malnutrition is rising, with humanitarian aid deliveries described as insufficient amid Israel’s continued military operations in the enclave.
records.institution: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

records.title: Saudi Arabia and China signed 57 agreements and MoUs worth US$3.7 billion in May 2025, focusing on agriculture, water, and food security.
records.description: Saudi Arabia and China signed 57 agreements and MoUs worth US$3.7 billion in May 2025, focusing on agriculture, water, and food security. These deals, led by Saudi Arabia's Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture, aim to bolster food security and industrial supply chains through initiatives like water recycling, a smart food security city, and vertical farming. The collaboration also seeks to increase Saudi agricultural exports to China, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030 and China's Belt and Road Initiative.
records.institution: Ministries of Environment, Water and Agriculture; Agriculture and Rural Affairs

records.title: Saudi Arabia's General Food Security Authority (GFSA) purchased 621,000 metric tons of hard wheat via international tender, to be deliver...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's General Food Security Authority (GFSA) purchased 621,000 metric tons of hard wheat via international tender, to be delivered between August and October 2025, as part of efforts to strengthen strategic reserves. The wheat was sourced from various regions, with expected heavy supply from the Black Sea. The average price per ton was US$252, lower than the February 2025 tender. The purchase, worth approximately US$156.6 million, was distributed across Jeddah, Yanbu, and Dammam ports. The GFSA also emphasized the growing role of overseas agricultural investments in its food security strategy.

records.title: Syria is facing a severe wheat crisis, with the UN FAO warning that 75% of its local wheat crop may fail due to drought, threatening food...
records.description: Syria is facing a severe wheat crisis, with the UN FAO warning that 75% of its local wheat crop may fail due to drought, threatening food security for over 16 million people. Historically reliant on wheat imports from Russia to support its bread subsidy programme, Syria now faces compounded challenges due to suspended Russian supplies and international sanctions. With potential sanctions relief signaled by the U.S. and EU, hopes are rising for the revival of Syria’s agricultural sector through renewed access to irrigation technologies and infrastructure investment. The crisis highlights the fragile state of Syria’s food systems, worsened by years of war and climate shocks. Although no new Syrian government policy is explicitly mentioned, the situation centers around import dependency and subsidy mechanisms as key survival strategies during past droughts.

records.title: In celebration of World Bee Day, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) is actively supporting Emirati beekeepers t...
records.description: In celebration of World Bee Day, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) is actively supporting Emirati beekeepers to ensure the sustainability of the sector and boost premium local honey production. This commitment includes providing high-quality queen bees from the Emirati honeybee breed, with thousands already distributed and more planned for this year. ADAFSA is also promoting local honey through events like the Al Wathba Honey Festival, producing educational videos, and conducting workshops and training courses on beekeeping fundamentals, queen bee rearing, and pest control. Furthermore, ADAFSA co-organized the International Meeting of Young Beekeepers (IMYB) in Dubai, published a comprehensive scientific guide on beekeeping, and launched a national project to monitor honeybee diseases, all aimed at fostering a robust and healthy beekeeping industry crucial for the UAE's biodiversity and food security.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: On World Bee Day 2025, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) announced the production of 2,100 tenth-generation Em...
records.description: On World Bee Day 2025, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) announced the production of 2,100 tenth-generation Emirati queen bees and the distribution of 1,350 queens to 39 beekeepers, with a target of 5,300 queens by year-end. ADAFSA organized the Al Wathba Honey Festival, supported training courses and workshops on beekeeping, published a scientific guide on bees in the UAE, and launched a national project to monitor honeybee diseases and pests, with results expected in early 2026.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority

records.title: The launch of Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) marks a major consolidation of five prominent UAE food brands into a unified entity aimed at stre...
records.description: The launch of Al Ain Farms Group (AAFG) marks a major consolidation of five prominent UAE food brands into a unified entity aimed at strengthening local food production, advancing innovation, and supporting the country’s National Food Security Strategy 2051. Backed by Ghitha Holding and Yas Holding, AAFG brings together leaders in dairy, poultry, eggs, and juice production, with a roadmap for scaling operations, developing sustainable packaging, reducing import dependency, and investing in R&D for alternative proteins and camel milk. The initiative is positioned as a transformation of the UAE's agri-food industry, enhancing self-reliance, food system resilience, and the country’s regional export capabilities. The consolidation supports the creation of a fully integrated, locally driven, and technologically advanced food production ecosystem.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Iraq is formulating a portfolio of projects to enhance its climate adaptation and greenhouse gas mitigation strategies as part of its Gre...
records.description: Iraq is formulating a portfolio of projects to enhance its climate adaptation and greenhouse gas mitigation strategies as part of its Green Climate Fund (GCF) country programme, which focuses on the agriculture and water sectors. This follows the GCF's approval of a $39 million project aimed at strengthening vulnerable agricultural livelihoods. This initiative, implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organization, is expected to improve the livelihoods of two million Iraqis and contribute to the country's long-term food security and economic stability by empowering water user associations and improving water management through policy reforms, enhanced irrigation technologies, and the integration of renewable energy solutions.

records.title: The Department of Crop Protection has begun field visits to wheat fields in Kirkuk and Nineveh Governorates to monitor and evaluate the e...
records.description: The Department of Crop Protection has begun field visits to wheat fields in Kirkuk and Nineveh Governorates to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of pesticides used. A specialized technical team conducted field tests in key wheat cultivation areas to assess pesticide performance. The aim of these visits is to verify the effectiveness of herbicides and determine the best methods and timing for their use, as well as to study the compatibility of approved pesticides and their impact on productivity and crop quality, while also monitoring potential environmental and crop safety side effects. As part of this effort, a presentation by a private sector company in Sulaymaniyah Governorate specializing in agricultural drone technologies was attended, showcasing the capabilities of drones for agricultural pest control as a step towards adopting modern technology for food security.

records.title: Jordan is facing a severe water crisis, ranking among the most water-scarce countries globally.
records.description: Jordan is facing a severe water crisis, ranking among the most water-scarce countries globally. The government is implementing strategies such as the National Water Carrier Project to supply desalinated water and a nationwide effort to reduce water losses through infrastructure upgrades and modern technology. Addressing ageing infrastructure and water theft are also critical. The water crisis is affecting key economic sectors like tourism and agriculture. To improve efficiency, the Ministry of Water and Irrigation is using advanced control systems and exploring private sector involvement in wastewater treatment. Some farmers are adopting smart irrigation systems to reduce water usage. Efforts are underway to expedite the National Water Carrier Project, increase investment in water-saving technologies, and raise public awareness on conservation. The ministry is committed to transparency and collaboration to tackle this critical issue.
records.institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Hema Energy, through its X2E LLC arm, has begun a trial cultivation of Camelina sativa in Oman in collaboration with ARA Petroleum LLC, m...
records.description: Hema Energy, through its X2E LLC arm, has begun a trial cultivation of Camelina sativa in Oman in collaboration with ARA Petroleum LLC, marking the region's first initiative focused on green energy and sustainable agriculture. The project aims to establish a zero-waste model using Camelina as a sustainable biofuel feedstock. ARA Petroleum LLC is providing land, water, and co-funding for the trial, which aligns with Hema Energy’s “greener barrel” strategy. The company is also exploring the use of treated water for cultivation, supporting Oman’s water reuse goals. While government coordination on wastewater reuse is a challenge, optimism remains regarding Camelina's adaptability to Oman's climate. The Environmental Authority is aware of the project, and successful results could lead to expanded cultivation and potential international outreach.

records.title: Oman: Sustainability at the core of national progress
records.description: Oman is strategically pursuing sustainability through its Vision 2040 plan, aiming to balance economic growth with environmental preservation and align with UN sustainable development goals. Collaborating with the Environment Authority, the Ministry of Energy and Minerals, and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, Oman is focused on renewable energy expansion, sustainable urban development, biodiversity protection, and securing food and water resources. Key initiatives include solar and wind energy projects, investment in green hydrogen, modern and traditional water management systems, the establishment of protected natural reserves, and the promotion of sustainable agriculture practices. Urban development emphasizes green cities with smart infrastructure, and efforts are underway to address climate change through emission reduction goals and adaptation strategies.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture opened a new agricultural office in the town of Sinjil, north of Ramallah Governorate.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture opened a new agricultural office in the town of Sinjil, north of Ramallah Governorate. This initiative aims to enhance the provision of agricultural services and improve farmers' access, considering transportation difficulties. The office's opening is part of the ministry's plan to empower farmers and support their resilience by establishing sub-agricultural offices across various governorates for more efficient service delivery. The visit included an inspection of the historic hill area in Sinjil, which has faced attempts to seize control, and olive seedlings were distributed to local farmers for replanting on affected lands.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture launched a three-day training course on "Forage and Alternative Forage Production" in Marj Na'ja,...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture launched a three-day training course on "Forage and Alternative Forage Production" in Marj Na'ja, Jericho Governorate, as part of a project funded by Italian Cooperation and implemented with the CIHEAM-Bari Institute. This course aims to enhance farmers' technical capabilities in feed production, crucial for food security and livestock. Targeting 20 fodder specialists, it covered modern methods, alternative fodder, productivity, quality, and sustainable practices, delivered by a specialized Ministry of Agriculture team. Officials emphasized the importance of these programs for farmer empowerment and feed sector innovation, highlighting that investing in agricultural knowledge is key to production development and self-sufficiency. The Ministry affirmed its commitment to ongoing training for the agricultural sector to achieve sustainable agriculture and national food security as a strategic priority.

records.title: Pure Harvest Smart Farms, a UAE-based agri-tech company, is demonstrating resilience amid regional conflict by using climate-controlled t...
records.description: Pure Harvest Smart Farms, a UAE-based agri-tech company, is demonstrating resilience amid regional conflict by using climate-controlled technology to produce fruits and vegetables in the Gulf desert, with minimal supply chain disruption despite the Iran war. As import routes face pressure, demand for locally grown produce has surged, highlighting the importance of domestic agriculture for food security. The company produces 13 million kilograms annually for a population of 11 million, using significantly less water than traditional farms, while advocating for policies such as limiting cheap imports and supporting local producers to strengthen long-term agricultural resilience in the region.

records.title: The University of Sharjah (UoS), in collaboration with IBM through the IBM Sustainability Accelerator, has launched My FarmWell, a mobile...
records.description: The University of Sharjah (UoS), in collaboration with IBM through the IBM Sustainability Accelerator, has launched My FarmWell, a mobile application to tackle water scarcity and promote sustainable agriculture in the UAE and the wider MENA region. Utilizing IBM Environmental Intelligence and the UoS Welly Chatbot, the app integrates IBM Cloud and regional water/climate data to offer farmers timely, farm-level insights for optimized irrigation and sustainable practices. The bilingual app provides well-specific data like water levels, groundwater trends, water quality indices, and crop recommendations for smarter decisions in water-scarce environments. Representatives from UoS and IBM highlighted this collaborative research as a practical application of sustainability innovations, addressing environmental challenges and advancing resilient agriculture through data-driven insights. Key features include weather information, well monitoring, crop recommendations, a water consumption calculator, educational resources, and market price integration.

records.title: The Egyptian Swiss Group for Pasta, Milling, and Concentrates participated in the international GrainCom conference in Geneva, a major gl...
records.description: The Egyptian Swiss Group for Pasta, Milling, and Concentrates participated in the international GrainCom conference in Geneva, a major global event for the grain and oilseeds sector. Representing the Egyptian market during panel discussions, the group highlighted Egypt's wheat market and recent changes in import mechanisms, as well as the relevant government entities. Egypt saw a significant rise in wheat imports in 2024 due to improved dollar availability and lower global wheat prices. Egypt's grain sector is large, encompassing over 33,000 companies across various areas like pasta and milling. The country remains a top global wheat importer and consumer, with increasing imports of corn and soybeans also noted. The Egyptian Swiss Group aimed to showcase Egypt's potential as a regional hub for grain-related industries and expand international partnerships at GrainCom, a strategic platform addressing food security, technology, and risk, with participation from global stakeholders and exchanges.
records.institution: The Egyptian Swiss Group for Pasta, Milling, and Concentrates

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture is actively monitoring the epidemiological situation of foot-and-mouth disease in the Al-Chibayish Marshes th...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture is actively monitoring the epidemiological situation of foot-and-mouth disease in the Al-Chibayish Marshes through the Dhi Qar Teaching Veterinary Hospital and the Veterinary Department. Field monitoring campaigns are being conducted in Dhi Qar Governorate to investigate potential infections among buffalo herds following reports of suspected cases. A technical delegation found no previous cases and noted that most herds were vaccinated. Thorough examinations were carried out, epidemiological measures were implemented, a report was issued, samples were taken for confirmation, and livestock movement in affected areas of Al-Chibayish district was banned, with local clinic staff providing treatment. The Veterinary Hospital administration in Dhi Qar and its clinics aim to reassure the public and counter rumors by quickly responding to contain any disease outbreaks.

records.title: The Ministry of Economy and Trade revealed that US$ 77 million in credits were opened for livestock imports during the first four months...
records.description: The Ministry of Economy and Trade revealed that US$ 77 million in credits were opened for livestock imports during the first four months of the year, exceeding two-thirds of the total livestock supplies in 2021. The ministry stated that import activity is proceeding normally, and the credited amounts are sufficient to meet local market needs and enhance the national food safety stock. This was disclosed during a meeting held by the Ministry of Economy and Commerce in Tripoli to monitor economic conditions, commercial activity, consumer prices, and market readiness for Eid Al-Adha, following instructions from the Minister. The Ministry expressed appreciation for the cooperation of the Central Bank of Libya and relevant authorities in facilitating import procedures to ensure market stability. The meeting was attended by the Ministry’s undersecretaries and directors.
records.institution: The Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture inaugurated a new agricultural office in the Beita Municipality in Nablus Governorate.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture inaugurated a new agricultural office in the Beita Municipality in Nablus Governorate. This opening is part of the ministry's efforts to enhance its advisory and technical services in agricultural communities, with the office staff already providing support to farmers in Beita and surrounding areas to develop the agricultural sector and raise production efficiency. The inauguration included a visit to an agricultural area targeted for infrastructure development under the municipality's plan, in preparation for future projects aimed at serving farmers and improving agricultural production quality and quantity.

records.title: The Minister of Investment and the Khartoum Governor visited the 'Savannah' project for the production of various agricultural goods west...
records.description: The Minister of Investment and the Khartoum Governor visited the 'Savannah' project for the production of various agricultural goods west of Karari. The minister assessed production capabilities and challenges, pledging to resolve issues to increase output and help citizens affected by the ongoing war. The Khartoum Governor emphasized the state government's support for investments benefiting citizens and its commitment to enhancing production and food supply to demonstrate Sudan's resilience despite the conflict. The company's director expressed gratitude for the state government and the Ministry of Agriculture's support in encouraging increased production to alleviate citizens' suffering.

records.title: For the first time in Syria, Ryan Food, located in the Bab al-Hawa Industrial City, has received the FSSC 22000 certification.
records.description: For the first time in Syria, Ryan Food, located in the Bab al-Hawa Industrial City, has received the FSSC 22000 certification. This international accreditation for food safety management systems, under the Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI), was awarded by the Syrian Center for ISO Experts. This achievement, witnessed by officials from the Ministries of Economy and Industry and the Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry, underscores Ryan Food's commitment to the highest quality standards and signifies a qualitative leap for the Syrian food sector. It also serves as an encouragement for other industrial establishments in the country to pursue excellence and international accreditation.

records.title: The services of the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries reported a 2.8% increase in the 2025 summer stone fruit harves...
records.description: The services of the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries reported a 2.8% increase in the 2025 summer stone fruit harvest, reaching 251.5 thousand tons compared to 244.7 thousand tons in the previous season, despite a 2.1% decrease in cultivated areas to 197.5 thousand ha. Peach harvest is estimated at 121 thousand tons, slightly down from 122.3 thousand tons, while plum harvest is expected to rise by 4.7% to 42.7 thousand tons. Dried almond harvest is projected to increase significantly by 25% to 56.5 thousand tons from 45.2 thousand tons in 2024. However, plum production is expected to decrease by 10.5% to 17 thousand tons. National cherry production saw a 6.1% increase to 9.6 thousand tons, while the medlar harvest decreased by 12.7% to 2,750 tons from 3,150 tons in 2024.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Tunisia views the energy transition as crucial for enhancing energy security, reducing emissions, and creating jobs through diversified e...
records.description: Tunisia views the energy transition as crucial for enhancing energy security, reducing emissions, and creating jobs through diversified energy sources and less reliance on fossil fuels, setting an ambitious goal of 30% renewables by 2030. The importance of strengthened Mediterranean partnerships for this transition was emphasized at an international forum, with Tunisia offering its expertise for a sustainable regional and national energy future. The country's energy strategy for 2035 and diversification reforms were highlighted, along with the need for regional integration to stabilize energy markets. Discussions included the ELMED project, an electrical link with Italy supported by the EU, and potential electricity interconnections with Algeria and Libya, as well as energy innovation cooperation with an Italian group. Domestically, the National Agency for Energy Management (ANME) has launched a second funding call for municipalities' energy management projects focusing on efficiency, renewable self-consumption, and territorial energy studies, under the Acte program in collaboration with several entities.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Mines and Energy, National Agency for Energy Management (ANME)

records.title: Egypt has procured 2.5 million metric tons of wheat from local farmers since mid-April, a slight decrease from the previous year despite...
records.description: Egypt has procured 2.5 million metric tons of wheat from local farmers since mid-April, a slight decrease from the previous year despite reduced cultivation. The government aims to purchase 4 to 5 million tons domestically this season, exceeding the typical 3.5 million tons, by offering a 10% price increase to reduce reliance on approximately 6 million tons of projected imports for its subsidized bread program. Farmers are incentivized with rewarding prices, quick payments, and streamlined logistics. In early May, Egypt’s strategic wheat reserves were estimated to last 4.5 months. A policy shift has transferred strategic commodity imports, including wheat, to the military-affiliated Mostakbal Misr Agency for Sustainable Development, which has contracted 1.267 million metric tons, mainly from Russia, through June. To bolster food security, Egypt and the European Commission agreed on a €90 million funding deal in March to enhance grain storage and logistics.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has affirmed the stability of Egypt's poultry industry, stating it is under continuous s...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has affirmed the stability of Egypt's poultry industry, stating it is under continuous supervision by the General Authority for Veterinary Services and the Livestock and Poultry Development Sector to ensure the health and safety of poultry nationwide. The Ministry asserts that no mortality cases have been reported, and all necessary vaccines are readily available. Ongoing epidemiological surveillance is conducted by trained professionals who regularly monitor farms and provide support. The authorities urge breeders to report any issues. Real-time data collection and flock monitoring are carried out nationwide, highlighting the poultry industry's significant development and self-sufficiency, with surplus production now being exported. The government provides comprehensive support to modernize farms for both small and large producers, with no abnormal mortality rates observed.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture announced that Brazilian authorities have decided to lift the 9% customs duty on olive oil imports,...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture announced that Brazilian authorities have decided to lift the 9% customs duty on olive oil imports, creating a significant opportunity to boost Lebanese olive oil exports to the Brazilian market. This measure is expected to reduce olive oil prices in Brazil by up to 10%, according to the Brazilian Supermarkets Association, potentially increasing demand and enhancing the competitiveness of Lebanese products in terms of quality and price, especially given the presence of a large Lebanese community. The Ministry called on Lebanese producers and exporters to seize this promising opportunity, affirming its continued support for efforts aimed at opening new markets for Lebanese agricultural products.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has enhanced the marketing of Palestinian agricultural products to Arab and international markets by adding g...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has enhanced the marketing of Palestinian agricultural products to Arab and international markets by adding grapes to the existing list of marketed items, which includes dates, avocados, lemons, and peppers, aiming to maximize benefits for farmers and the agricultural sector through new marketing outlets. This initiative focuses on delivering high-quality Palestinian agricultural products to the global market, leveraging their competitiveness based on quality and origin, leading to the opening of Arab markets. Palestinian grapes from the Al-Buqai'a area in the northern Jordan Valley are being marketed to Gulf markets, specifically Dubai and Qatar, through the Jordanian Palestinian Agricultural Marketing Company. The Ministry of Agriculture emphasized the high quality of Palestinian grapes, meeting international standards and enhancing their marketing potential, thus improving returns for Palestinian farmers. This move is part of the ministry's strategy to open new markets and address marketing challenges for farmers, with a comprehensive marketing plan implemented by the Jordanian-Palestinian company to export grapes from various Palestinian governorates from May through September, starting in the northern Jordan Valley and progressing through other regions.

records.title: For several years, Tunisia's rural water distribution has been managed by hydraulic groups, local entities facing financial and governanc...
records.description: For several years, Tunisia's rural water distribution has been managed by hydraulic groups, local entities facing financial and governance challenges, including significant debt. These groups struggle with poor infrastructure maintenance leading to water losses and ineffective billing. To address these persistent issues in areas like Kairouan, Sidi Bouzid, and Siliana, the Tunisian government plans a gradual transfer of water management to SONEDE (National Water Exploitation and Distribution Company) to stabilize and improve the water supply. This transition involves a debt rescheduling for hydraulic groups, an infrastructure modernization program to reduce water losses, and the introduction of a single pricing system for rural and urban areas. While considered a necessary solution for better water resource management and stable rural supply, this reform has raised concerns among farmers and rural residents about potential tariff increases and over-centralization.
records.institution: SONEDE (Société Nationale d'Exploitation et de Distribution des Eaux)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Secretary of State for Energy Transition stated in Italy that strengthening the Mediterranean partnership is crucial for the energy t...
records.description: The Secretary of State for Energy Transition stated in Italy that strengthening the Mediterranean partnership is crucial for the energy transition, and Tunisia is ready to contribute its expertise for a sustainable energy future and secure energy supplies regionally and nationally. During an international forum, Tunisia's energy strategy for 2035 and reforms aimed at diversifying the energy mix were reviewed, emphasizing the importance of regional integration to address energy market instability and foster industrial development. Discussions also focused on the ELMED project, a planned electrical interconnection between Tunisia and Italy, seen as a key link between Europe and Africa with EU support. On the sidelines, meetings were held with the Algerian Energy Minister and the CEOs of Sonatrach and Sonelgaz regarding the development of a tripartite electricity interconnection between Tunisia, Algeria, and Libya, as well as with the CEO of the Italian energy group Edison to explore cooperation in energy innovation.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Mines and Energy

records.title: Ghitha Holding PJSC, a subsidiary of International Holding Company PJSC (IHC), is set to participate in the Make it in the Emirates (MIIT...
records.description: Ghitha Holding PJSC, a subsidiary of International Holding Company PJSC (IHC), is set to participate in the Make it in the Emirates (MIITE) Forum, organized by the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MoIAT) at the ADNEC Centre. With a broad portfolio covering the entire food value chain, Ghitha Holding aims to highlight its critical role in improving food security and advancing industrial growth in the UAE, embodying the key objectives of MIITE. The company is focused on driving the future of manufacturing in the UAE through technology-driven innovation, local talent empowerment, and expanded access to cross-border markets. A representative of Ghitha Holding stated the company's pride in playing a leading role at the forum, emphasizing its commitment to fostering growth aligned with food security and the UAE’s vision for a resilient, diversified, and globally competitive economy. Ghitha’s expanding portfolio of dairy and protein companies supports the UAE’s industrial strategy and Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030 by promoting local manufacturing and reducing import dependence in essential food sectors.

records.title: A project for the construction of five water lakes (Kurof) in the Amran Basin was inaugurated, funded by the General Authority for Water...
records.description: A project for the construction of five water lakes (Kurof) in the Amran Basin was inaugurated, funded by the General Authority for Water Resources at an estimated cost of 238 million riyals. The project aims to collect rainwater and floods to recharge groundwater and address declining water levels due to excessive depletion, with site selection based on thorough studies. It was confirmed that the project aligns with leadership directives to enhance rainwater utilization, calling for linking well drilling permits to contributions for groundwater recharge. The project was considered the start of a strategic phase in water resource management, emphasizing community and contractor cooperation for its success and announcing a mechanism for a special account to ensure continuity. The head of the water resources authority indicated the lakes' capacity is 235,000 cubic meters in the first phase of a 75-site plan, highlighting the project's role in reducing flood damage and building sustainable water infrastructure.
records.institution: The General Authority for Water Resources

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: AlexFert, a subsidiary of Egypt Kuwait Holding Company (EKH), has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with United Energy Group (UE...
records.description: AlexFert, a subsidiary of Egypt Kuwait Holding Company (EKH), has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with United Energy Group (UEG), a renewable energy pioneer, to develop a hydrogen-powered green ammonia production project. This strategic partnership signifies a key step for Egypt towards a low-carbon industrial future, aligning with global net-zero carbon standards and strengthening Egypt's role as a regional energy hub. According to a press release, UEG will be in charge of developing the green hydrogen production project in conjunction with AlexFert’s existing facilities in Alexandria. The project will produce hydrogen using renewable energy sources for subsequent use in the creation of green ammonia.

records.title: The Moroccan avocado export campaign for 2024-2025 concluded in late April with very encouraging results, featuring a record national pro...
records.description: The Moroccan avocado export campaign for 2024-2025 concluded in late April with very encouraging results, featuring a record national production of 130,000 tons and unprecedented export volumes of nearly 100,000 tons, marking a substantial increase of over 60% from the previous season due to strong international demand. This significant growth, however, led to an average price decrease of 21%, considered a normal market adjustment during strong supply expansion, with prices now stabilizing and expected to rise as production nears capacity amid growing global consumption. The Moroccan sector also achieved notable progress in fruit quality and professionalism, with improvements in agricultural practices. This robust performance highlights Morocco's increasing strength in the global avocado market, where continued sector consolidation and improved organization are seen as crucial for sustained growth.

records.title: The Moroccan citrus industry, as highlighted at the recent 1st National Citrus Congress led by Maroc Citrus in Marrakech, faces significa...
records.description: The Moroccan citrus industry, as highlighted at the recent 1st National Citrus Congress led by Maroc Citrus in Marrakech, faces significant challenges, notably a drought that has reduced the planted area by nearly a third between 2016 and 2024. This decline from 128,000 to approximately 91,000 hectares endangers a vital sector supporting over 13,000 families and generating substantial employment. Despite these hardships, there's optimism due to orchard rejuvenation with half the plantations being under 15 years old and variety diversification, including the successful Nadorcott mandarin exported to over 40 countries. However, oranges face competition and trade barriers. While a government export bonus exists, it's seen as insufficient against Egyptian competition. The prevailing view is the need to strengthen the sectoral strategy, increase public support, anticipate future threats, and continue modernization for sustainability in a challenging national and international context. This collective awareness, backed by scientific expertise and stakeholder engagement, could be crucial for the future of Moroccan citrus agriculture.
records.institution: The National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries announced the reference prices for purchasing cereals for the upcoming agricul...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries announced the reference prices for purchasing cereals for the upcoming agricultural campaign, in anticipation of the next harvest and collection season. The Ministry established new cereal collection prices that include an incentive bonus for deliveries made within specified deadlines: durum wheat at 140 dinars per quintal (including a 40 dinar rapid delivery bonus), soft wheat at 110 dinars per quintal (with a 30 dinar bonus), and barley and triticale at 90 dinars per quintal (including a 25 dinar bonus). According to the announcement, these bonuses are contingent upon deliveries being made before certain dates.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries announced grain collection prices for the current season, featuring early del...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries announced grain collection prices for the current season, featuring early delivery bonuses. Official prices per quintal are 140 dinars for durum wheat (with a 40 dinar bonus), 110 dinars for soft wheat (with a 30 dinar bonus), and 90 dinars for barley and triticale (including a 25 dinar bonus), with these bonuses available until early July for barley/triticale and late August for wheat. The main harvest regions, including Béja and Kairouan, are significant contributors to Tunisia's cereal production, which reached approximately 1.2 million tonnes in 2024. The government aims to stabilize prices and ensure rapid collection to meet national needs through these bonuses, optimizing inventory management and strengthening the cereal sector for sustainable food security despite ongoing challenges.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) of Zaghouan, in collaboration with the General Directorate of Organic Agricul...
records.description: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) of Zaghouan, in collaboration with the General Directorate of Organic Agriculture, organized a workshop to strengthen the transition to organic farming in the region, as part of a project launched in 2022 with funding from the African Development Bank (AfDB). The workshop aimed to define a roadmap for establishing organic zones across 6,500 hectares. By the end of 2024, organically farmed land in the Zaghouan region reached 12,000 hectares. The Director General of Organic Agriculture at the Ministry of Agriculture highlighted Tunisia's commitment to organic farming since 1999, with 230,000 hectares cultivated organically by 2024, generating 1,130 million dinars in exports. The CRDA of Zaghouan also announced a 2 million dinar budget to support organic product development in sectors like beekeeping and olive growing, including farmer training by the Technical Center for Organic Agriculture in Chott Mariem (Sousse) and provision of equipment. This workshop is a key step in structuring organic farming in Zaghouan, aiming to establish the region as a major sustainable agriculture hub in Tunisia due to increasing demand and financial support.
records.institution: Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) of Zaghouan

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC – Masdar announced another US$1 billion green bond issuance, bringing its total outstanding green bo...
records.description: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC – Masdar announced another US$1 billion green bond issuance, bringing its total outstanding green bonds to US$2.75 billion, reinforcing its global sustainable finance leadership. The bond was issued in two US$500 million tranches with 5 and 10-year tenors and coupons of 4.875% and 5.375%, respectively, attracting significant oversubscription with strong regional and international demand. The pricing achieved was Masdar’s tightest to date, with allocation split 85% international and 15% MENA investors. This issuance follows previous green bonds in 2023 and 2024, which were fully allocated to new global greenfield projects. Masdar also issued US$6 billion in non-recourse financing in 2024 for over 11 GW of clean energy capacity. The raised funds will help Masdar meet portfolio targets and support global energy transformation, especially in emerging markets, with all bond proceeds dedicated to new 'dark green' renewable energy projects.
records.institution: Masdar Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture is continuing its campaigns to combat the tomato leaf miner (Tuta absoluta) pest in Salah al-Din and Karbala...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture is continuing its campaigns to combat the tomato leaf miner (Tuta absoluta) pest in Salah al-Din and Karbala governorates. These efforts are carried out by technical personnel in the Crop Protection Department, with oversight from the Director General of the Department. Field visits monitor the implementation of technical measures by the Crop Protection Department and local agricultural divisions during the spring season. The Ministry emphasizes the ongoing free provision of safe environmental control supplies to farmers, including pheromones, special traps, and environmentally friendly pesticides, as part of an integrated plan to limit the pest's spread and protect agricultural crops.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, via the Veterinary Department, conducted veterinary health awareness campaigns for breeders in Diyala and Sa...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, via the Veterinary Department, conducted veterinary health awareness campaigns for breeders in Diyala and Salah al-Din Governorates. The Veterinary Health Awareness Team educated breeders on the risks of communicable epidemic diseases affecting livestock, particularly hemorrhagic fever, overseen by the Director General of the Veterinary Department. The campaigns involved meetings to emphasize preventive measures and cooperation with veterinary teams for animal vaccinations, alongside distributing informational materials on disease risks and the importance of contacting veterinary services for advice and animal protection, thereby safeguarding national livestock resources.

records.title: An orientation seminar focused on sustainable olive growing and pest control practices was organized in Tripoli by the Ministry of Agricu...
records.description: An orientation seminar focused on sustainable olive growing and pest control practices was organized in Tripoli by the Ministry of Agriculture, through the North Lebanon Agriculture Department, in cooperation with the Tripoli Olive Growers Cooperative Association and the Minieh Agricultural Center. The seminar aimed to improve agricultural knowledge and promote sustainable practices in the olive sector of northern Lebanon, with over 45 farmers participating. Technical sessions covered integrated pest management techniques for olive pests, including orchard monitoring, rational pesticide use, and modern methods like pheromone traps. The importance of timely treatments, proper pruning, and balanced fertilization for tree health and pest resistance was also discussed to enhance production and crop quality. The seminar included welcoming remarks highlighting the value of such meetings and the need for continued collaboration. The importance of farmers registering officially for easier access to support and services was also emphasized. The Ministry reiterated its commitment to supporting farmers with technical guidance, field visits, and workshops, stressing the adoption of environmentally friendly scientific practices in olive grove management.

records.title: The 2024-2025 Moroccan tomato export season is concluding, demonstrating resilience in European markets despite logistical and climatic p...
records.description: The 2024-2025 Moroccan tomato export season is concluding, demonstrating resilience in European markets despite logistical and climatic pressures. Strong European demand, particularly in France, Spain, Germany, and the United Kingdom, has extended the season into mid-May; however, this occurs with dwindling stocks and increasing transportation costs to Europe. End-of-season harvests in the Souss region face challenges from irregular temperatures and ongoing water restrictions affecting greenhouse production, leading to lower yields and pressure on remaining export volumes, especially in the Chtouka-Aït Baha region. Despite these production issues, European markets remain strong due to weakened Spanish competition. European customers value the quality and responsiveness of Moroccan exporters. This situation frames the upcoming Morocco Tomato Conference, where industry players will assess the season and discuss future prospects, including water management and new markets in the Middle East and sub-Saharan Africa.

records.title: During an official visit to China by the Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the CEO of the National Center for Vegetation Co...
records.description: During an official visit to China by the Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the CEO of the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC) signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Gansu Desert Control Research Institute. The agreement intends to foster collaboration in combating desertification, sand encroachment, drought, land degradation, and the impacts of drought in arid areas, while promoting the sustainable management of drylands. As part of the official mission, strategic meetings were held with several prominent Chinese companies to explore potential collaborations and attract investments to Saudi Arabia. Discussions focused on initiatives such as natural asset management, rangeland rehabilitation, desert resort development, and the transfer of greening and desertification control technologies—supporting Saudi Arabia's vision for a green economy and sustainable land use.
records.institution: The National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC)

records.title: Fourteen memoranda of understanding (MoUs) were signed between the National Centre for Palms and Dates, Chinese companies, and government...
records.description: Fourteen memoranda of understanding (MoUs) were signed between the National Centre for Palms and Dates, Chinese companies, and government entities to expand the Kingdom's exports of dates and date-based products, enhancing the global presence of Saudi dates. The agreements were signed during the Saudi-Chinese Business Forum in Beijing, focused on promoting Saudi product exports and agricultural sustainability. According to the National Centre for Palms and Dates, the MoUs aim to foster collaboration between the centre, Saudi date companies, and Chinese partners to develop the Kingdom's palm and date sector. These agreements also seek to introduce advanced technologies for increased production and improved marketing strategies.
records.institution: The National Centre for Palms and Dates

records.title: An international workshop on sustainable land and water management was held in Hammamet, Tunisia, as part of the "Nature-based Solutions...
records.description: An international workshop on sustainable land and water management was held in Hammamet, Tunisia, as part of the "Nature-based Solutions for Resilient Agriculture" project, led by the FAO in collaboration with its Regional Office for the Near East and the Khibra network. The project promotes innovative approaches to combat soil degradation, improve water resource management, and enhance farm resilience. A Secretary of State at the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries, emphasized the critical water challenges in arid and semi-arid regions due to climate change, urbanization, and agricultural needs, highlighting the opportunity for food system transformation. Officials and experts from ten African and Asian countries convened to discuss nature-based solutions for sustainable land and forest management. The workshop showcased tools developed under the project, including integrated water resource management platforms, agricultural landscape analysis models, and sustainable production frameworks aimed at land degradation neutrality. These resources provide real-time water flow data, analyze human-ecosystem interactions for adapted agricultural practices, and structure strategies for increased productivity with natural resource preservation.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: The filling rate of Tunisian dams reached 40.2% with a total volume of 952 million cubic meters due to exceptional recent rainfall, parti...
records.description: The filling rate of Tunisian dams reached 40.2% with a total volume of 952 million cubic meters due to exceptional recent rainfall, particularly in the Northwest and Center-East regions, where rainfall significantly exceeded the annual average. This improvement follows several years of low water levels in dams. The North-West dams saw a 15% increase in water volume, while Centre-East dams experienced an 18% rise, benefiting crops. Southern dams had a more moderate 7% increase. Despite this positive change, concerns remain about potential evaporation during the dry season. The Ministry of Agriculture has implemented measures like water tanks to limit evaporation. Long-term strategies to improve water use efficiency include smart irrigation technologies, strengthening hydraulic infrastructure, and raising farmers' awareness of water-efficient practices.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: The increasing overfishing of marine species off the Tunisian coast, particularly endangered sharks and rays listed by the IUCN, is alarm...
records.description: The increasing overfishing of marine species off the Tunisian coast, particularly endangered sharks and rays listed by the IUCN, is alarming environmentalists. They have denounced social media videos showing fishermen boasting about large catches and alleged torture of these animals. Conservationists warn that this trend threatens the marine ecosystem and the livelihoods of traditional fishermen already experiencing dwindling fish stocks. They are urging the Ministries of Agriculture, Interior, and Trade, along with other relevant authorities, to enforce laws and controls in line with Tunisia's international biodiversity commitments, emphasizing that this is a matter of survival and food security, given the sea's role in oxygen production and as a primary livelihood source for many Tunisians.

records.title: Tunisia actively participated in the International Olive Oil Exhibition, a significant biennial gathering in Jaén, Spain, dedicated to th...
records.description: Tunisia actively participated in the International Olive Oil Exhibition, a significant biennial gathering in Jaén, Spain, dedicated to the olive oil sector. The Tunisian delegation's involvement in this key industry event was spearheaded by the Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency (APIA), collaborating with the National Oil Office (ONH). At their pavilion, Tunisian representatives presented a diverse array of olive oils originating from the country, including several varieties that have achieved distinction through awards in both national and international olive oil competitions. This participation underscores Tunisia's presence and quality in the global olive oil market.

records.title: Tunisia is addressing youth unemployment and aiming to boost its agricultural sector through initiatives that encourage investment among...
records.description: Tunisia is addressing youth unemployment and aiming to boost its agricultural sector through initiatives that encourage investment among young agri-entrepreneurs. The FAO, in collaboration with INRAT and APIA, has pinpointed high-potential sectors and incentives for youth to enter agriculture, particularly in regions with high graduate unemployment like Kasserine, Siliana, El Kef, and Sidi Bouzid, which possess strong agricultural potential in areas such as olive and fruit growing, livestock, and organic farming. Proposed incentives include facilitated access to financing via dedicated funds with favorable terms, and a total income tax exemption for the first five years under the Investment Incentive Code. Technical support is also emphasized through specialized training centers and mentoring to integrate modern agricultural technologies. Innovative sectors like organic farming and agroecology offer new opportunities due to increasing international demand. Initial support programs have shown promising results, funding over 200 projects in Sidi Bouzid and Kasserine with significant investment. However, challenges persist in simplifying administrative processes and improving rural infrastructure.

records.title: The UAE and the US are reinforcing their strategic energy partnership for a sustainable future through substantial joint investments in c...
records.description: The UAE and the US are reinforcing their strategic energy partnership for a sustainable future through substantial joint investments in clean and renewable energy to bolster global energy security and support emerging economies. A key initiative, PACE, aims to mobilize US$100 billion to deploy 100GW of clean energy by 2035, including a $20 billion allocation to develop 15GW of US clean energy projects led by Masdar. ADNOC has also invested in a blue hydrogen project in Texas. To support innovation, the Abu Dhabi Department of Energy has agreements with the University of Arizona and IRENA for advanced clean energy technologies.

records.title: Egypt and the African Development Bank Group (AfDB) signed a financing agreement for the fourth phase of the Abu Rawash Water Treatment P...
records.description: Egypt and the African Development Bank Group (AfDB) signed a financing agreement for the fourth phase of the Abu Rawash Water Treatment Plant, aiming to expand its daily treatment capacity from 1.6 million to 2 million cubic meters. This project is intended to benefit Giza residents through improved health infrastructure, public health, and environmental quality, while also creating agricultural opportunities and protecting the ecosystem. The agreement underscores the AfDB’s role in empowering the private sector, and Egypt looks forward to further financing mechanisms to promote investment. The collaboration also extends to the NWFE program and renewable energy desalination projects. The AfDB had provided a guarantee for Egypt's first sustainable Panda bonds in 2023.
records.institution: The Ministry of Planning, Economic Development, and International Cooperation

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with IFAD, has launched a workshop focused on the sustainability of agricultural progra...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with IFAD, has launched a workshop focused on the sustainability of agricultural programs for small farmers in Iraq. This writing workshop aims to equip smallholder farmers with the necessary skills to adopt modern and sustainable agricultural methods and to highlight successful farming practices. The initiative is a collaborative effort with the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). The workshop underscores the importance of cooperation with international organizations to support the agricultural sector, exchange global expertise, and implement best practices for agricultural development in the country. This effort is part of the Ministry's broader initiatives, in partnership with international organizations, to support the agricultural sector and achieve sustainable development in Iraq.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Veterinary Department, conducted a veterinary health awareness campaign in Dhi Qar Governorate t...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Veterinary Department, conducted a veterinary health awareness campaign in Dhi Qar Governorate targeting livestock breeders as part of the ministry's efforts to prevent communicable diseases. The campaign focused on raising awareness of the risks of epidemic diseases, primarily hemorrhagic fever, and the importance of vaccination and cooperation with veterinary teams. The ministry also distributed guidance folders to enhance veterinary awareness among breeders, which contributes to protecting livestock and supporting the national economy.

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture launched the National Campaign for the Integrated Management of Olive Trees.
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture launched the National Campaign for the Integrated Management of Olive Trees. Representatives from the plant wealth and agricultural extension sectors, the National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC), and stakeholders in the olive industry participated in the event held at the ministry headquarters. The campaign aligns with the Economic Modernisation Vision and the ministry’s plan to achieve food security and enhance the competitiveness of national agricultural products, especially olives, a cornerstone of Jordan’s agricultural economy. It aims to promote best agricultural and manufacturing practices, as well as climate-smart farming methods, through field schools and training courses across all governorates. The ministry will fund training courses and field schools, with additional schools funded by international organisations, focusing on regions most affected by the olive fruit fly pest. The Minister stressed that this collaborative campaign will contribute to the sector’s development, especially through agricultural extension services delivering campaign messages to farmers. Addressing pests and enhancing olive oil quality will positively impact farmers and the national economy.

records.title: The Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) received a delegation from the Republic of Maldives, with several Kuwaiti business own...
records.description: The Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) received a delegation from the Republic of Maldives, with several Kuwaiti business owners present. KCCI expressed appreciation for the delegation’s visit, noting the growing ties between Kuwait and the Maldives based on friendship and shared aspirations for economic and cultural cooperation. Trade relations between the two countries have significantly strengthened over the past decade, with a notable increase in Kuwaiti exports to the Maldives. The partnership is further strengthened by Maldivian excellence in tourism and maritime industries, attracting Kuwaiti investors, while Kuwaiti companies excel in finance, logistics, healthcare, and energy, providing a solid foundation for productive cooperation and investment. The Maldives Foreign Minister outlined prominent investment opportunities available in his country, mainly in sectors such as tourism, investment, alternative energy, logistics, ports, housing cities, agriculture, and fisheries.
records.institution: Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI)

records.title: As part of Morocco's "Green Generation 2020-2030" agricultural strategy, the National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA) is inten...
records.description: As part of Morocco's "Green Generation 2020-2030" agricultural strategy, the National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA) is intensifying efforts to provide innovative solutions to farmers through its plant breeding program, aiming to develop 30 to 50 new varieties with at least a 50% yield increase to enhance agricultural competitiveness while addressing climate change and sustainable resource management. INRA has established "demonstration platforms" in key production areas to showcase these new plant varieties under real conditions for easier adoption by farmers and sector operators. Examples include the durum wheat variety "Jawahir" (registered in 2023 with 30% higher yield) and the hulless barley "Chifaa" (registered in 2016, rich in beta-glucan). Demonstration days throughout May 2025 highlight these innovations and crucial agricultural practices like supplemental irrigation. Upcoming events are planned for the Haouz, Saïs, and Zaër regions, the latter with ICARDA's partnership.
records.institution: The National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA)

records.title: Mauritania is extending its watermelon export campaign unusually long, creating competition for Morocco in the European market.
records.description: Mauritania is extending its watermelon export campaign unusually long, creating competition for Morocco in the European market. This extended season, from mid-December into May, carries risks but allows Mauritania to occupy less competitive periods. While volumes haven't surged, prices have been satisfactory due to lower production costs than Morocco, potentially weakening Morocco's market position, especially with increasing water restrictions there. Mauritania's main European markets are Germany, Italy, and the Netherlands, showing export growth. The Mauritanian industry is also improving volume regulation. This development poses a challenge for Morocco, requiring adaptation due to water resource issues and growing regional competition, particularly in the off-season, especially with shifting agricultural calendars potentially increasing market overlap.

records.title: Morocco is projected to decrease its wheat imports to 6.7 million tons for the 2025-2026 season, a reduction of 200,000 tons due to impro...
records.description: Morocco is projected to decrease its wheat imports to 6.7 million tons for the 2025-2026 season, a reduction of 200,000 tons due to improved domestic harvests and strategic stock management, providing greater self-sufficiency amidst global price volatility.
