The country strategically balances imports with domestic reserves and diverse trade partnerships, engaging with major exporters like France, Russia, and Kazakhstan through modulated tenders and flexible tariffs. In contrast, maize imports are expected to rise by 200,000 tons to 2.9 million tons to meet the growing demand of the poultry and livestock sectors, primarily sourced from Ukraine, Brazil, and the US. The National Interprofessional Office for Cereals and Legumes (ONICL) plays a key role in stabilizing supply through strategic reserves and subsidies, aligning domestic forecasts with global markets to ensure food security and support local farmers.
records.institution: The National Interprofessional Office for Cereals and Legumes (ONICL)

records.title: The Interprofessional Federation of the Poultry Sector in Morocco (FISA) has refuted recent rumors circulating in media and social media...
records.description: The Interprofessional Federation of the Poultry Sector in Morocco (FISA) has refuted recent rumors circulating in media and social media about China allegedly suspending imports of Moroccan poultry products. FISA clarified that Morocco has no health agreement with China for poultry exports, meaning no such products have ever been sent there, rendering any suspension claims baseless. This statement follows suggestions that Beijing reacted to a past Newcastle disease outbreak in the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra region, which FISA stated last occurred in February 2024 and was quickly contained according to health protocols, with no new alerts since. The Federation also noted that Newcastle disease is present in many countries but is generally controlled and poses no risk to human health, making poultry consumption safe. FISA reaffirmed its commitment to traceability and health safety, urging caution with unverified information and highlighting close collaboration with the French National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA) to maintain high health standards.
records.institution: The Interprofessional Federation of the Poultry Sector in Morocco (FISA)

records.title: Oman's wheat production is projected to exceed 7,700 tonnes for the 2024-2025 season as harvesting commences across key agricultural regi...
records.description: Oman's wheat production is projected to exceed 7,700 tonnes for the 2024-2025 season as harvesting commences across key agricultural regions. While the cultivated area has decreased in some areas due to crop diversification, government support and improved farming practices are helping maintain strong yields. Dhofar's Najd region is expected to be the top producer, despite a slight reduction in acreage as farmers shift to more water-efficient crops. Wheat remains strategically important for national food security, supported by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and the Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund, which distributed 30 tonnes of wheat seeds at a 50% subsidy and provided free harvesting machinery, with collection managed by Oman Flour Mills Company. Dhahirah and Dakhliyah also anticipate significant wheat production with government support, including subsidized seeds and modern irrigation. Buraimi expects over 250 tonnes of wheat due to high-quality seeds provided to farmers. Despite a modest decrease in total wheat acreage, ongoing government support and infrastructure continue to position wheat as a key element of Oman’s food security strategy.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, through its General Directorate of Veterinary Services, organized a workshop in Ramallah to disc...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, through its General Directorate of Veterinary Services, organized a workshop in Ramallah to discuss a continuing education plan for the veterinary sector. This initiative is part of a project funded by the World Bank's Pandemic Fund and implemented with the FAO. Representatives from the Veterinary Syndicate and several universities, along with official bodies, attended and emphasized the importance of continuing education in promoting "One Health" and responding to public health challenges. The workshop focused on reviewing a proposed plan by an FAO expert to build a sustainable and effective continuing education system that enhances veterinary personnel efficiency in addressing common diseases and epidemics. Discussions also covered plan implementation and creating an advanced educational environment to meet national needs and support preparedness for health emergencies.

records.title: A comprehensive six-month census of state-owned agricultural land was ordered to identify underutilized land, combat illegal exploitation...
records.description: A comprehensive six-month census of state-owned agricultural land was ordered to identify underutilized land, combat illegal exploitation, and optimize public land management. This aims to address the lack of accurate data hindering efficient land use by creating a detailed record of available and unauthorized land. The census focuses on governorates with high land pressure and agricultural needs, affecting an estimated 500,000 hectares, much of which is currently unusable. Efforts also include combating illegal logging and facilitating access for cooperatives and community businesses to develop agro-industrial projects for food sovereignty. A digital platform is planned for real-time monitoring of land distribution and permits to ensure transparency. The Ministry of Agriculture projects this initiative could significantly boost agricultural production, reduce food import dependence through modern farm growth, and stimulate rural job markets.

records.title: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) of Zaghouan, in coordination with the General Directorate of Organic Agricult...
records.description: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) of Zaghouan, in coordination with the General Directorate of Organic Agriculture, organized a workshop to officially launch the promotion of organic agriculture in the region. This initiative is part of a project funded by the African Development Bank (ADB) since 2022, allocating 150 million dinars for developing agricultural sectors. The project aims to establish seven organic zones across approximately 6,500 hectares, featuring diverse products adapted to each area's specific conditions. By the end of 2024, nearly 12,000 hectares in the region were under organic cultivation. This workshop aligns with the national strategy for promoting organic agriculture, a sector Tunisia has been involved in since 1999, marking the first such project in the Arab and African world.

records.title: Tunisia is advancing a bill, spearheaded by the Ministry of State Property and Land Affairs, to enable the transfer of state-owned agricu...
records.description: Tunisia is advancing a bill, spearheaded by the Ministry of State Property and Land Affairs, to enable the transfer of state-owned agricultural land to community enterprises, aiming to boost agricultural investment, food self-sufficiency, and the efficient use of public land. This proposed legislative change would ease access to agricultural land for these enterprises through favorable payment terms and priority exploitation, a shift from the strict prohibition in place since the 1995 law. The initiative involves digitally mapping state agricultural lands to identify available areas for transparent management, potentially including around 10,000 hectares annually, focusing on governorates like Béja, Siliana, Kairouan, Sidi Bouzid, Medenine, and Tataouine. Complementing this, the President has ordered a national census of state-owned agricultural land, in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, to identify underutilized land and combat illegal exploitation, alongside efforts to simplify administrative procedures for community business developers to access land leases.
records.institution: The Ministry of State Property and Land Affairs

records.title: Tunisia is developing a digital platform, led by the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries and in collaboration with th...
records.description: Tunisia is developing a digital platform, led by the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries and in collaboration with the General Directorate of Governance, to improve public water resource management by increasing transparency and efficiency. The platform, expected by the end of 2025, will centralize hydrological data, simplify permit processes for the public hydraulic domain, and streamline groundwater exploration permits with set deadlines to encourage legal compliance and reduce uncontrolled well drilling for sustainable groundwater use. Initial trials will be in Kairouan, Sidi Bouzid, and Medenine, benefiting from real-time water table monitoring and withdrawal data, potentially reducing illegal withdrawals by 20% and optimizing over 500 million cubic meters of water annually. Simultaneously, another digital platform is being developed with the Ministry of Communication Technologies to analyze hydrological data for better real-time resource management.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: The UAE National Codex Committee (NCC), under the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology, in collaboration with ADAFSA and GFoRSS,...
records.description: The UAE National Codex Committee (NCC), under the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology, in collaboration with ADAFSA and GFoRSS, has inaugurated a two-day workshop in Abu Dhabi to evaluate and strengthen the UAE’s alignment with Codex Alimentarius standards. The workshop gathers members of the UAE NCC, international and local experts, and ADAFSA representatives. Opening remarks emphasized national collaboration and the FAO/WHO self-assessment tool for evaluating the UAE’s Codex initiatives and ensuring alignment with scientific and legislative developments. The workshop features presentations on the self-assessment tool's methodology and procedures, covering institutional mechanisms, consultation processes, understanding Codex work, policy frameworks, and activity utilization. Interactive working groups discuss assessment criteria, scoring, consistency, and documentation to ensure participant understanding. Organizers highlight the workshop's importance in bolstering the UAE’s food security and agricultural sustainability strategies by aligning national Codex activities with international standards to enhance national food safety regulations.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has announced a $30m loan to Obelisk Solar Power, owned by Scatec ASA, to sup...
records.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has announced a $30m loan to Obelisk Solar Power, owned by Scatec ASA, to support the construction of a 1 GWac solar power plant and a 200 MWh battery energy storage system in Upper Egypt. This will be Egypt’s first hybrid solar and battery storage project, intended as a model for integrating battery storage with renewable energy. The initiative supports Egypt’s green energy transition and grid stability under the country’s Nexus on Water, Food, and Energy (NWFE) platform, led by the EBRD. The NWFE program aims to establish Egypt as a regional renewable energy hub. Upon completion, the plant is projected to reduce CO₂ emissions significantly annually, contributing to Egypt’s climate goals. Egypt has been a major area of investment for the EBRD since 2012, with over €13.8bn invested in numerous projects across various sectors.
records.institution: The Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy

records.domain: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Horticulture Department, has commenced harvesting barley at the Qaim Horticulture Station in Anb...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Horticulture Department, has commenced harvesting barley at the Qaim Horticulture Station in Anbar Governorate as part of a program focused on fodder seed multiplication and processing. This initiative aims to supply farmers with high-quality, locally sourced seeds at subsidized prices. This step is intended to support the livestock sector by providing affordable fodder, thereby reducing costs and enhancing local production. The program is a key agricultural undertaking by the Ministry, overseen by its technical staff, and contributes to strengthening national food security and reducing reliance on imported fodder.

records.domain: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
records.title: The Minister of Agriculture in Lebanon inaugurated the National Seed Bank at the Lebanese Agricultural Research Institute (LARI) headquar...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture in Lebanon inaugurated the National Seed Bank at the Lebanese Agricultural Research Institute (LARI) headquarters to support the agricultural sector and protect biodiversity. The project, supported by the Government of Norway and the Global Crop Diversity Trust, aims to preserve plant genetic resources, ensure food security, and address climate change through seed storage and documentation. During a tour of LARI's laboratories, the Minister was briefed on various research efforts and services for farmers and sustainable agriculture, including soil and water analysis, climate monitoring via a smart application, local variety analysis, tissue culture, biodiversity documentation, seed distribution, olive oil studies, mushroom cultivation, plant disease monitoring, new crop projects, biopredator production, feed analysis, and animal health monitoring.

records.title: On the occasion of the first edition of the National Citrus Congress, the National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) will highlight...
records.description: On the occasion of the first edition of the National Citrus Congress, the National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA) will highlight its major scientific and technological advances to support the sustainable development of the citrus industry in Morocco. As a strategic component of national agriculture facing challenges like limited varietal diversification, orchard yields, and value-added processing, INRA offers solutions such as new high-yielding citrus varieties, adapted variety/rootstock associations, and optimized irrigation, fertilization, and phytosanitary techniques focused on sustainability and climate change adaptation. Under the "Green Generation" strategy, INRA has also developed a digital platform for precision agriculture in citrus using technologies like drones and sensors. For valorization, INRA has created agri-food innovations for citrus fruits and by-products, including pectin, seed oil, and processed products like biscuits, jellies, jams, syrups, and pastes.
records.institution: The National Institute of Agronomic Research (INRA)

records.title: Oman’s Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth, and Water Resources is expected to award a tender for consultancy services for the Wadi...
records.description: Oman’s Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth, and Water Resources is expected to award a tender for consultancy services for the Wadi Ahin Flood Protection Dam in North Al Batinah Governorate in the third quarter. The design and supervision consultancy tender was issued with bid submissions due in the second quarter. The contract is anticipated to be awarded in the third quarter, with project completion scheduled for the third quarter of 2027. The consultant will review the existing dam design, propose modifications, and supervise construction, evaluating various conditions, topography, safety, and land allocation. The scope also includes construction oversight to ensure compliance with updated specifications and standards.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Environment Authority and Japan Ministry of Environment signed a memorandum of cooperation (MoC) on environmental matters.
records.description: The Environment Authority and Japan Ministry of Environment signed a memorandum of cooperation (MoC) on environmental matters. The MoC seeks to enhance cooperation towards sustainable development and the implementation of environmental multilateral agreements, like the Paris Agreement, establishing a framework for cooperation based on equality, reciprocity, and mutual benefits. The agreement provides for cooperation in mitigating climate change effects, adapting to related impacts, waste management, and biodiversity conservation as nature-based solutions. The two sides will conduct training courses, expert visits, research, interactive discussions, and information exchange in areas of cooperation and joint projects.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has initiated the Palestinian Communities Support Project to enhance the resilience and sustainable economic...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has initiated the Palestinian Communities Support Project to enhance the resilience and sustainable economic growth of marginalized Palestinian communities in the occupied territories. As an initial step, partnership agreements were signed with 46 farmers, including greenhouse operators in specific towns, to provide fertilizers, irrigation networks, and greenhouse rehabilitation to support their livelihoods and address economic and environmental challenges. This effort is a collaboration with the Palestinian Center for Economic and Social Development, with support from the German Cooperation, as part of international partnerships aimed at improving the agricultural sector's economy and strengthening local communities in marginalized areas. The Ministry of Agriculture reaffirms its ongoing commitment to developing the agricultural sector and providing necessary farmer support to enhance their capabilities and achieve sustainable development in the Palestinian territories.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate, held an introductory workshop for beneficiaries of a European...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate, held an introductory workshop for beneficiaries of a European Union-funded agricultural assistance program to enhance farmers' capacities and access to support. The workshop, attended by farmers, explained program implementation, financial payment guidelines, application procedures, and workflow. Ministry representatives emphasized the program's importance in supporting farmers affected by the occupation in a transparent and organized manner, with time for questions on maximizing support. This event is part of ongoing meetings by the Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture with international partners to improve agricultural development programs and strengthen farmers' resilience and the sector.

records.title: The Tunisian Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (UTAP) has urgently called on the government to review the milk reference price due to gr...
records.description: The Tunisian Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (UTAP) has urgently called on the government to review the milk reference price due to growing challenges in the dairy sector and rising production costs for farmers. UTAP highlighted significant losses for milk producers due to price freezes and increased operating costs, noting the sector's economic vulnerability and the migration of dairy herds. UTAP and UTICA are jointly requesting an immediate increase in milk prices for farmers, collectors, and manufacturers, along with a review of subsidies to ease financial pressure and prevent farm abandonment. They also emphasize the need for dialogue with authorities to implement sustainable solutions for market stability and food sovereignty. While the Ministry of Agriculture has not yet announced specific measures, discussions are reportedly ongoing to find a compromise.
records.institution: The Tunisian Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (UTAP)

records.title: Tunisia will commission the Sousse seawater desalination plant in June to boost drinking water supply in regions facing high water stress.
records.description: Tunisia will commission the Sousse seawater desalination plant in June to boost drinking water supply in regions facing high water stress. This strategic project, with a significant investment, aims to alleviate shortages, especially in summer, and will complement existing water sources. Authorities expect it to reduce water cuts and stabilize supplies in drought-prone areas, noting a current increase in dam filling rates. The government is focusing on advanced water management technologies like desalination, wastewater reuse, and aquifer replenishment, also developing a digital platform for real-time monitoring. The Sousse plant's commissioning marks a major step in national water security, combining technology and optimized management for a more sustainable and transparent approach to address climate challenges and growing water needs.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: The FoodTech Challenge (FTC) has shortlisted 42 early-stage startups with tech solutions to transform global food systems.
records.description: The FoodTech Challenge (FTC) has shortlisted 42 early-stage startups with tech solutions to transform global food systems. Organized by UAE entities and partners, the third FTC offers a $2 million prize. The competition, announced in 2024, will award four winners cash grants, support, and network access for deployment in the UAE and the Global South, leveraging the UAE's climate as a launchpad. Judges reviewed over 1,200 entries from 113 countries, showcasing innovations from lab-grown dairy to AI crop monitoring. UAE startups comprise 16 percent of the semifinalists, with significant female and youth co-founder representation. The cohort includes startups from numerous countries offering solutions in smart packaging, urban farming, and AI analytics, with a focus on reducing food loss and waste. Selected startups will undergo interviews and pitches for a top 10 shortlist, judged by representatives from organizing entities and international organizations. Launched under the UAE’s National Food Security Strategy 2051, FTC aims to support solutions related to the food-water-energy nexus, reduce food loss, and accelerate globally replicable innovations.
records.institution: International Affairs Office at the UAE Presidential Court, Tamkeen

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Wilo, a multinational technology group, and Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company – Masdar, the UAE’s clean energy leader, have formed a cooper...
records.description: Wilo, a multinational technology group, and Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company – Masdar, the UAE’s clean energy leader, have formed a cooperation agreement emphasizing efficiency technology and renewable energy. This strategic partnership aims to significantly expand their collaboration in the Middle East and beyond, highlighting the necessity of both renewable energy expansion and energy efficiency initiatives to address the global energy shortage. The agreement combines Masdar’s green energy expertise with Wilo’s technologies and manufacturing capabilities to deliver integrated solutions for a cleaner, more efficient world, also strengthening ties with Germany as a key market. The signing occurred at Wilo Group’s expanded production plant in Dubai. Wilo’s evolution into a provider of sustainable water and energy-efficient technology demonstrates the potential for climate-friendly innovations to offer global solutions, considered vital for regions aiming to become climate-neutral industrial leaders.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company – Masdar

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture announced the release of approximately 8.7 million common carp swimmers and 5,400 fingerlings of various Iraq...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture announced the release of approximately 8.7 million common carp swimmers and 5,400 fingerlings of various Iraqi fish into Haditha Lake and Dam in Anbar Governorate. The release was attended by the Central Release Committee of the Department of Animal Resources, Fish Hatcheries Division, and representatives from the Anbar Agriculture Directorate and the Haditha Agriculture Division. The head of the committee explained that the common carp swimmers were produced by the Al-Suwaira Fish Hatchery, affiliated with the Department of Animal Resources. This initiative aims to increase fish stocks in water bodies and preserve fish resources in the country.

records.title: As part of the National Agricultural Extension Program, the Ministry of Agriculture – North Lebanon Agriculture Department held an orient...
records.description: As part of the National Agricultural Extension Program, the Ministry of Agriculture – North Lebanon Agriculture Department held an orientation seminar in Zgharta, focusing on forest management and fire prevention. The seminar, attended by over 20 farmers, environmental activists, and Ministry experts, aimed to raise awareness and promote sustainable agricultural practices, particularly concerning forest preservation given environmental and climate challenges. Discussions highlighted the importance of preserving forests and cooperating with local authorities for environmental sustainability, as well as the need to continue such initiatives and strengthen coordination with the Ministry for the benefit of farmers and the community. A technical presentation covered fire prevention, the Forest Law, and sustainable natural resource management, leading to attendee interaction and practical recommendations.

records.title: A ministerial council in Rabat assessed Morocco’s water management recovery plan and its impact on agriculture, following prolonged drought.
records.description: A ministerial council in Rabat assessed Morocco’s water management recovery plan and its impact on agriculture, following prolonged drought. The Minister of Agriculture reported positive effects from recent rainfall on crops, vegetation, and livestock. The government was instructed to ensure the rebuilding of the livestock herd. To stabilize water and agriculture sectors, the Eid Al Adha sacrifice was cancelled, and female livestock slaughter was banned. The Minister of Water reported an increased dam filling rate, allowing for greater water mobilization, though the agricultural sector remains affected by water rationing due to priority water allocation for other sectors.

records.title: Morocco and Mauritania are strengthening integration in their agriculture and maritime fisheries sectors to achieve sustainable developme...
records.description: Morocco and Mauritania are strengthening integration in their agriculture and maritime fisheries sectors to achieve sustainable development and food security. At the first Moroccan-Mauritanian Parliamentary Economic Forum, Morocco expressed its commitment to supporting initiatives that advance these sectors for mutual benefit, emphasizing the need for deeper integration to achieve sustainability and food sovereignty. The aim is to increase bilateral trade in agricultural products, with discussions on removing obstacles for investors through joint commissions. Moroccan producers are interested in investing in Mauritania's agriculture, and expertise in water management is offered. A technical mission focused on livestock, particularly sheep, will visit Mauritania. The potential for partnership in maritime fishing and aquaculture is significant, with a focus on scientific research, training, aquaculture, maritime security, and artisanal fishing, encouraging mutual investments in related value chains.

records.title: The EU melon market is undergoing a significant shift with declining overall purchases, although the value per kilo is increasing.
records.description: The EU melon market is undergoing a significant shift with declining overall purchases, although the value per kilo is increasing. Spanish melon sales have significantly decreased since 2019, despite Spain remaining the top supplier. Morocco, while selling less by volume, achieves the highest unit value, indicating a focus on a premium market. Despite reduced volumes, Spanish revenue remains substantial due to higher average prices. Competition is intensifying from other suppliers, while Italy shows notable sales growth. This market restructuring reflects changing demand, with producers adapting strategies towards maintaining volume or prioritizing profitability per kilo, influenced by climate, logistics, and quality demands.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: France's energy regulator advised governments against sudden changes to renewable energy support, as even reform announcements can underm...
records.description: France's energy regulator advised governments against sudden changes to renewable energy support, as even reform announcements can undermine investor trust and create power sector uncertainty. The regulator stated that altering support contracts without system-level consideration risks market destabilization and erodes trust in long-term public support. While acknowledging past subsidy issues, the focus should shift to incentivizing renewables to meet real-time grid demands through balancing markets, exposing them to system constraints. However, prolonged negative electricity prices, common with high renewable penetration, can impede new project financing. Increasing system instability due to limited storage and balancing needs is also a concern. Instead of new frameworks, modifying distorting older contracts could maintain investor confidence. The regulator stressed that policy must be tailored to each country's energy system and renewable mix, advocating for practical dialogue and context-specific solutions rather than simply adopting others' policies.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources celebrated the opening of Wadi Adawnib Dam in the Wilayat of Salalah, Governor...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources celebrated the opening of Wadi Adawnib Dam in the Wilayat of Salalah, Governorate of Dhofar. The dam, with an 83 million cubic metre storage capacity and costing about OMR24 million, is the second largest of its kind in Oman and aims to enhance flood protection. It features an integrated monitoring system, including wells, sensors, and cameras, with data directly transmitted to a control room for immediate decisions during emergencies.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Sultanate of Oman participated in the annual International Day of Plant Health, themed “The Importance of Plant Health for a One Heal...
records.description: The Sultanate of Oman participated in the annual International Day of Plant Health, themed “The Importance of Plant Health for a One Health Approach.” This day emphasizes the vital role of plant health in food security, human and animal well-being, and environmental sustainability, as healthy plants are fundamental to nutritious food systems and ecological balance. The international observance aims to raise global awareness about safeguarding plants and crops from pests and diseases, conserving natural resources, and improving plant health, thereby contributing to global food security, environmental protection, biodiversity, pollution reduction, safe trade, and socio-economic progress. Global and regional organizations are marking the occasion with scientific events to promote the importance of plant health in global economic development. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources continues to monitor laboratory reports and pest risk analyses from exporting countries and is improving workforce training to enhance plant health efficiency.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture visited Tulkarm Governorate, delivering agricultural supplies to 96 farmers with damaged greenhouses near the...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture visited Tulkarm Governorate, delivering agricultural supplies to 96 farmers with damaged greenhouses near the Annexation Wall as part of a project to enhance food security in the northern West Bank. Funded by OCHA and implemented by ARIJ in partnership with CARE International, under the Ministry's supervision, the project targeted five communities, providing materials to rehabilitate one dunum of greenhouses per farmer. During the tour, the Minister visited the Tulkarm Agriculture Directorate, discussing staff needs and emphasizing the importance of strong capabilities to provide agricultural services in affected areas. Representatives from implementing partners and OCHA accompanied the Minister, expressing support for the Ministry's work and continued collaboration to assist Palestinian farmers. The Minister stressed that this project aligns with the Ministry's vision to strengthen farmers' resilience and ensure sustainable production, highlighting the successful cooperation between official and partner institutions in serving the agricultural sector.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and China have signed two export protocols allowing Saudi dairy and aquaculture products into the Chinese market.
records.description: Saudi Arabia and China have signed two export protocols allowing Saudi dairy and aquaculture products into the Chinese market. The agreements, finalized during an official visit, aim to expand trade in high-quality food and strengthen customs cooperation. Discussions focused on enhancing trade in these sectors, streamlining export procedures, and encouraging Saudi companies' expansion in China, aligning with national export goals. This cooperation reflects growing trust and will facilitate the entry of leading Saudi companies into the Chinese market. The Kingdom reaffirmed its commitment to robust regulations and private sector empowerment through international best practices, expressing optimism about increasing exports to China, deepening economic and food security partnerships, and future trade agreements.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia, through the National Center for Wildlife (NCW), has joined the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands to conserve environmental reso...
records.description: Saudi Arabia, through the National Center for Wildlife (NCW), has joined the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands to conserve environmental resources, habitats, and biodiversity while supporting sustainability and the economy. This reflects the NCW's leadership in wetland protection plans, including research, monitoring, and conservation, coordinating national implementation of the Convention. Saudi Arabia aims to manage sites for the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance according to global standards. Wetlands are vital ecosystems for biodiversity, carbon storage, water, food, energy, climate, agriculture, and ecotourism, also serving as migratory stopovers. This accession is a strategic step enhancing environmental and economic benefits, with a commitment to global best practices in wetland conservation aligning with national visions. The Ramsar Convention, established in 1971, provides a global framework for wetland conservation and sustainable use, covering various wetland types.

records.title: On the sidelines of an international meeting in Bari, Italy, the Syrian Minister of Agriculture, discussed the state of Syria's agricultu...
records.description: On the sidelines of an international meeting in Bari, Italy, the Syrian Minister of Agriculture, discussed the state of Syria's agricultural sector with the Director-General of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). The Minister detailed the challenges facing the sector, including the consequences of conflict, and emphasized the Syrian people's determination to revitalize both crop and livestock production. He underscored the critical need for cooperation with international organizations, particularly FAO, to support agriculture and farmers. The Minister also highlighted the importance of training agricultural personnel and providing farmers with necessary supplies.

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture announced Tunisia's first artificial cloud seeding experiment, conducted in the Sidi Salem dam basin, in coll...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture announced Tunisia's first artificial cloud seeding experiment, conducted in the Sidi Salem dam basin, in collaboration with the Ministries of National Defence and Transport, to combat water scarcity, with results under evaluation. Cloud seeding aims to increase precipitation by introducing chemicals into clouds. On the National Day of Agriculture, the minister also highlighted projects to improve energy efficiency, like electricity production from dams for pumping stations, and reported a 130 million cubic meter increase in dam water reserves compared to the previous year, which is encouraging given the upcoming commissioning of the Sousse desalination plant, supplementing the Sfax and Zarat plants. However, it's worth noting that reports from late 2024 indicated the Sidi Salem dam faced critically low filling rates, around 16-17%, and overall dam reserves had decreased significantly compared to the three-year average, despite some improvement in early 2025 following rainfall.

records.title: The Tunisian red meat sector is being modernized to address rising production costs and distribution challenges.
records.description: The Tunisian red meat sector is being modernized to address rising production costs and distribution challenges. A strategic meeting involving multiple ministries agreed to form working teams focused on breeder and butcher qualification, infrastructure upgrades for livestock markets and slaughterhouses, genetic improvement, distribution optimization, analyzing past reform obstacles, and developing a strategic document. The reform targets key livestock producing regions, aiming to increase local red meat production by 15-20% by 2027 while ensuring quality and safety, as current production doesn't meet domestic demand. Challenges include social and regulatory acceptance, the need for significant infrastructure investment, and ensuring food safety standards are met. This initiative seeks to strengthen food security, stabilize prices, and enhance the sector's competitiveness through stakeholder commitment and institutional cooperation.

records.title: Tunisia is implementing a program to irrigate 20,000 hectares of farmland with treated water, a collaboration between the Ministry of Agr...
records.description: Tunisia is implementing a program to irrigate 20,000 hectares of farmland with treated water, a collaboration between the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries and the Ministry of the Environment, to address growing water stress and enhance food security. Supported by the World Bank, this initiative aims to optimize treated wastewater use for agricultural irrigation, reducing pressure on conventional water resources for various crops. Simultaneously, another project with Italy targets the irrigation of 11,500 hectares of state-owned land with treated wastewater to improve water resource management and sustainable agriculture. Key challenges include public and regulatory acceptance of treated wastewater for irrigation, the necessity of significant investment in infrastructure, and ensuring the quality and safety of the treated water for crops and soils.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries and the Ministry of the Environment

records.title: Tunisia, a country rich in biodiversity with numerous ecosystems and species, is facing increasing pressure on its natural resources.
records.description: Tunisia, a country rich in biodiversity with numerous ecosystems and species, is facing increasing pressure on its natural resources. To counter this, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is collaborating with the Ministry of Environment and the Ministry of Finance to develop a national biodiversity financing plan. This initiative aims to integrate biodiversity into public policies, strengthen environmental governance, and mobilize sustainable funding. While Tunisia has signed international agreements like the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Ramsar Convention, effectively incorporating biodiversity into economic decisions remains a challenge. The financing plan prioritizes ecologically sensitive areas such as protected wetlands like Ichkeul National Park, marine zones, and Mediterranean forests threatened by urbanization and fires. Funding mechanisms being explored include green bonds, international funds like the Global Environment Facility and UNDP BIOFIN, and public-private partnerships.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment and the Ministry of Finance

records.title: In observance of the International Day of Plant Health, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) reaffirms its commit...
records.description: In observance of the International Day of Plant Health, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) reaffirms its commitment to initiatives safeguarding plant health and agricultural sustainability across the emirate through crop inspections, integrated pest management, and farmer education. ADAFSA employs a comprehensive biosecurity strategy, including the Integrated Palm Pest Management Programme targeting key pests with environmentally safe methods like pheromone traps, resulting in the capture of millions of weevils. A palm survey programme identifies and treats infestations with high success rates. ADAFSA also removes and repurposes severely infested palm trees. Embracing integrated pest management, the Authority combines economic and environmental practices for sustainable pest elimination and has an emergency response plan for agricultural pests, positioning the region as prepared for such challenges. ADAFSA is dedicated to best practices, innovative technologies, regular pest monitoring, farmer education, a comprehensive pest database, biological pest control, agricultural quarantine, advanced laboratories, and expert teams with research stations to inform pest control and the selection of pest-resistant plant varieties.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: A field school promoting smart agricultural practices in okra cultivation has opened in the southern Qazwiniya region in Abbasiya, Najaf.
records.description: A field school promoting smart agricultural practices in okra cultivation has opened in the southern Qazwiniya region in Abbasiya, Najaf. The Director General of the Agricultural Guidance and Training Department participated in the opening, which was held in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Directorate of Agriculture in Najaf Governorate, with representatives from FAO and IFAD also present, along with the Governorate's Director of Agriculture. During the opening, the importance of modern technologies in vegetable cultivation to address climate challenges, water scarcity, and high soil salinity was emphasized. The need for cooperation to achieve sustainable agricultural development was also highlighted.
records.institution: Directorate General of the Agricultural Guidance and Training Department

records.title: Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture launched a cooperative lending system to support small farmers, part of the Second Dutch Agricultural Su...
records.description: Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture launched a cooperative lending system to support small farmers, part of the Second Dutch Agricultural Support Project. Implemented by Advance Consulting and Wageningen University, and funded by the Netherlands Embassy, the SACO system offers revolving microloans for water-saving technologies via the Dinarak e-wallet. A 60,000 Jordanian dinar fund will be managed through the e-wallet, which will also handle loan repayments and cooperative revenue allocation for sustainability. The initiative includes training in financial literacy and aims to empower cooperatives with self-sustaining financial systems, enabling farmers to adopt modern technologies and build rural community resilience.

records.title: The Water Authority and the Embassy of Spain to Jordan inaugurated the Al-Lajoun Wells Rehabilitation Project in Karak Governorate.
records.description: The Water Authority and the Embassy of Spain to Jordan inaugurated the Al-Lajoun Wells Rehabilitation Project in Karak Governorate. The project aims to enhance efficiency, improve water supply, and reduce water loss. Funded by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) at a cost of 1.214 million Jordanian dinars, the initiative is part of Jordan’s national efforts to reduce water loss as per the 2023–2040 Water Sector Strategic Plan. The project included rehabilitating seven wells in the Al-Lajoun area by replacing pumps, cables, and electrical panels, and renovating part of the Al-Lajoun water station by replacing several pumps, the main control panel, valves, and an old turbidity meter, as well as refurbishing internal water barriers and maintaining the chlorine room. Approximately 5.5 kilometers of ductile iron pipes were also installed to interconnect the wells and improve water delivery. The Ambassador of Spain emphasized Spain's commitment through AECID to supporting Jordan in improving water services, reducing water loss, and enhancing water infrastructure and management for stronger water security.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture – North Lebanon Agriculture Department, through its center in Bsharri and in cooperation with the CDDG Associ...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture – North Lebanon Agriculture Department, through its center in Bsharri and in cooperation with the CDDG Association, organized a training course in Diman, Bsharri District, on "Apple Irrigation Management in Light of Climate Challenges and Irrigation Network Design Principles." This course is part of the Ministry's extension program to support farmers and enhance their efficiency. Over twenty farmers, along with agricultural experts and engineers, participated in the training. Topics covered improving irrigation management due to climate change and adopting effective practices for water use rationalization and enhanced apple crop productivity. The training presented the principles of irrigation scheduling in apple orchards, emphasizing consideration of plant growth stages, soil quality, and climate, along with using soil moisture meters and weather stations for accurate irrigation decisions. A detailed explanation of drip irrigation network design, including components and even water distribution, was provided, also addressing the importance of regular maintenance for efficiency and reduced water loss.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture's Akkar Agriculture Department - Agricultural Center in Abdeh conducted a field survey of potato fields in th...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture's Akkar Agriculture Department - Agricultural Center in Abdeh conducted a field survey of potato fields in the Akkar Plain. This is part of ongoing cooperation with a program supporting agricultural exports to European markets and the Ministry's plan to monitor crop health and ensure compliance with international standards. The survey involved collecting crop and soil samples following scientific protocols for laboratory tests to assess crop health and plant safety standards. This activity is part of preventive and rehabilitation measures to enhance European markets' confidence in Lebanese agricultural produce quality and improve export opportunities by fully complying with international plant health and food safety standards. The Ministry affirms these steps are part of its continuous efforts to ensure a sound and competitive production environment, enabling Lebanese farmers to access new markets, particularly in the European Union, positively impacting the local agricultural economy.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources celebrated the opening of Wadi Anaar Dam in Salalah, Governorate of Dhofar.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources celebrated the opening of Wadi Anaar Dam in Salalah, Governorate of Dhofar. The project, costing about OMR23 million, aims to enhance protection against flood risks and promote water security by capturing large volumes of rainwater from nearby mountains that flow towards Salalah Port, Raysut Industrial City, and Salalah Free Zone. The dam is equipped with advanced technologies for safety during emergencies, including smart monitoring systems for water levels, seismic sensors to track geological activity, and surveillance cameras for comprehensive coverage. Automatic control gates regulate water flow and can be operated remotely through a secure central system that receives and analyzes data in real-time.

records.title: The Jerusalem Agriculture Directorate and Action Against Hunger today distributed 621.3 tons of fodder to 145 beneficiaries in several ea...
records.description: The Jerusalem Agriculture Directorate and Action Against Hunger today distributed 621.3 tons of fodder to 145 beneficiaries in several eastern Jerusalem Governorate communities, including Khan al-Ahmar and Bir al-Maskub. These communities are among 24 Bedouin communities facing settler harassment and restricted pasture access due to occupation practices. This distribution is part of a project by Action Against Hunger to support the livestock sector in marginalized areas affected by settlers and the Israeli occupation in eastern Jerusalem. The initiative aims to alleviate the costs of agricultural production inputs (fodder) for livestock farming, as farmers cannot access pastures due to occupation restrictions. This fodder will also help improve the health and productivity of sheep.

records.title: The Jerusalem Agriculture Directorate, in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), delivered s...
records.description: The Jerusalem Agriculture Directorate, in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), delivered specialized agricultural equipment to 30 livestock farmers in the Jerusalem Governorate. The equipment was distributed to two field schools in agricultural communities southeast and central-west of Jerusalem. This initiative is part of the Field School Support Program, aiming to enhance farmers' use of modern technologies in ruminant rearing and improve production amidst challenging economic and environmental conditions. This step is part of a series of interventions by the Ministry of Agriculture and FAO to support livelihoods and achieve food security in rural areas lacking basic agricultural services.

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture signed agreements supporting agricultural projects in northern Hebron during a tour of the local Agriculture...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture signed agreements supporting agricultural projects in northern Hebron during a tour of the local Agriculture Directorate, Veterinary Department, and Chamber of Commerce. The Ministry affirmed its commitment to strengthening farmers' resilience amidst sector challenges. A meeting at the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate addressed the directorate's needs and the implementation of over 700 agricultural projects, including those under the Relab "MAP 2" program, emphasizing projects with direct economic benefits for rural families. At the North Hebron Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture, support agreements were signed under the "RELAB" project, funded by IFAD and OFID, focusing on empowering rural families and improving small farmer marketing. Progress in agricultural exports and a partnership with Jordan to market Palestinian crops were also highlighted.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its directorate in the Ramallah and Al-Bireh Governorate, in cooperation with the Welfare Associatio...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its directorate in the Ramallah and Al-Bireh Governorate, in cooperation with the Welfare Association, the Palestinian Hydrology Group, and the Kharbatha Al-Misbah Village Council, undertook the construction and rehabilitation of four kilometers of agricultural roads and the laying of one kilometer of basecourse in the town of Kharbatha Al-Misbah, as part of the "Investment in Water, Land, and Agricultural Roads" project. This project is supported and funded by the Dutch Representative Office and the Welfare Association, and implemented by the Palestinian Hydrology Group, in partnership with the Directorate of Agriculture and the Village Council. It aims to improve the agricultural infrastructure in the region, facilitate farmers' access to their lands, boost agricultural production, and support rural development efforts, thus contributing to stimulating the local economy and improving farmers' living standards.

records.title: Qatar's abundant marine biodiversity and increasing emphasis on environmental conservation are establishing it as a leader in sustainable...
records.description: Qatar's abundant marine biodiversity and increasing emphasis on environmental conservation are establishing it as a leader in sustainable tourism within the region. By consistently working to protect its marine environment and promote ecotourism, the country is not only safeguarding its natural heritage but also supporting broader global environmental objectives. Qatar's marine environment is recognized as the most diverse in the region due to its unique peninsular geography. The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC) highlights Qatar's extensive coastline, stretching around 563 kilometers along the Arabian Gulf, which supports a wide variety of coastal and marine ecosystems. The depth of Qatar’s territorial waters ranges from sea level to approximately 60 meters.
records.institution: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC)

records.title: The 21st Mango and Tropical Fruits Festival, organized in Sabya Governorate by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture’s Jazan...
records.description: The 21st Mango and Tropical Fruits Festival, organized in Sabya Governorate by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture’s Jazan branch, continues to attract large crowds of all ages. The week-long festival offers children an engaging experience to explore tropical fruits, learn about their environmental importance, and enjoy mango flavors. Interactive competitions encourage participation in a fun, family atmosphere. Educational workshops introduce children to agriculture and the role of healthy fruits in a balanced diet. A theater features magic shows and animated presentations, adding to the lively atmosphere and visitor enthusiasm.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture assured that sheep for Eid El-Kebir will be available in sufficient quantities nationwide.
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture assured that sheep for Eid El-Kebir will be available in sufficient quantities nationwide. He also announced an upcoming cap on reference prices. Regarding the major crops season, he expressed optimism for a good harvest, stating the ministry's preparations began six months prior. On the threat of desert locusts, he affirmed the situation is "under control" but called for collective mobilization to eradicate infestation centers originating from neighboring countries.

records.title: In Dubai, the Global Olive Corporation (GOC) unveiled a project to tokenize 100 million olive trees globally, starting with a million alr...
records.description: In Dubai, the Global Olive Corporation (GOC) unveiled a project to tokenize 100 million olive trees globally, starting with a million already planted in Georgia. This initiative aims to link investors with real olive trees through blockchain tokens representing ownership in a productive asset. Token holders are promised a share of profits from olive oil and fruit sales, as well as carbon credits, while supporting afforestation across four continents. The GOC's olive-backed token, tentatively named Olive Cash, will be formally introduced in Singapore in October. Future expansion includes countries across multiple continents. Each tree will have a unique digital token trackable via blockchain, with real-time data on its condition. Tokenization aims to boost agricultural productivity and resource management. The model includes a replacement system for dead or diseased trees. GOC aims to tap into the demand for verified carbon offsets linked to each token. The initiative seeks to offer a sustainable investment with environmental benefits.

records.title: Egypt's wheat harvesting season has begun, with the Ministry of Supply receiving a significant initial amount and expecting a substantial...
records.description: Egypt's wheat harvesting season has begun, with the Ministry of Supply receiving a significant initial amount and expecting a substantial total local harvest, priced well compared to lower international rates. The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation anticipates a strong total domestic wheat production due to increased cultivation and improved yields. Experts attribute recent global wheat price decreases to international trade disputes, which create global commerce uncertainty. Despite significant wheat imports in the previous year driven by consumption and lower global prices, Egypt's import trend is expected to continue. Reports indicate relative global price stability due to increased global wheat supplies. Egypt has already contracted substantial wheat imports to strengthen its reserves. Farmers are optimistic about the current season due to the early-announced favorable government purchase price and stable economic conditions during cultivation, with prompt payment by the Ministry of Finance being commended.

records.title: Exports from the Amman Chamber of Industry have shown continued growth since the start of the year, highlighting the strength and adaptab...
records.description: Exports from the Amman Chamber of Industry have shown continued growth since the start of the year, highlighting the strength and adaptability of Jordanian industry in international markets. During the initial months, exports saw a notable increase, exceeding two billion dinars compared to the same period in the previous year. Most industrial sectors experienced an uptick in exports, with some exceptions like wood and furniture, medical supplies, and packaging, which faced declines. Several sub-sectors recorded varying growth rates, with construction materials showing the most significant rise and plastics and rubber the least. Collectively, India, the United States, Saudi Arabia, and Iraq accounted for over half of Amman's total exports. While exports to some of these key markets increased, others saw a slight decrease, though the United States remained the top importer. Exports to Syria and Palestine witnessed substantial surges.

records.title: The World Food Program (WFP) reported a slight increase in Libya's minimum food basket cost for March, reversing a prior downward trend a...
records.description: The World Food Program (WFP) reported a slight increase in Libya's minimum food basket cost for March, reversing a prior downward trend and raising concerns about inflation and currency stability. The WFP's monthly assessment showed a modest rise in the basic food basket price, driven by widespread food price increases across all regions. The western region saw the most significant increase, largely due to a sharp price spike in Zuwara following the closure of a border crossing that disrupted trade. In eastern Libya, one city remained the most expensive market due to a continuous influx of refugees straining limited local supplies. Meanwhile, a southern city recorded the highest price increase at the city level, reflecting market isolation, insecurity, and recent military actions. Despite these general increases, the WFP observed considerable price variations across different regions during March, with some municipalities experiencing moderate to significant price decreases.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: To address climate change challenges, organic farming is presented as a sustainable way to enhance the resilience of Tunisia's agricultur...
records.description: To address climate change challenges, organic farming is presented as a sustainable way to enhance the resilience of Tunisia's agricultural sector. The FAO, in partnership with the Swiss Research Institute for Organic Agriculture (FIBL) and with Swiss cooperation support, organized a training course on organic plant production as part of the Biorest project. This project aims to develop integrated organic agriculture in suitable Tunisian regions to promote sustainable and agroecological practices. With nearly 9,000 operators, mainly producers, in Tunisia's organic sector, there's a need for enhanced technical support to improve competitiveness and meet international standards. The training focused on soil management, reduced tillage, agroforestry, functional biodiversity, and crop diversification. The Biorest project aligns with a national strategy to promote sustainable, inclusive, and resilient organic agriculture, supporting food security, natural resource protection, and territorial development. Ultimately, the Biorest project aims to build the capacities of producers and institutions, establishing organic farming as a key tool for adapting to climate change in Tunisia.

records.title: Edita Food Industries S.A.E.
records.description: Edita Food Industries S.A.E. has announced its Board of Directors' approval for the sale of a production line and machinery to an Iraqi company for US$3 million. The Board authorized the necessary actions to complete this sale. This follows an Extraordinary General Assembly Meeting where a capital increase was approved, funded by retained earnings, and sanctioned by the Economic Performance Department. Amendments to the company’s articles of association were also made, including implementing cumulative voting for board elections and allowing the appointment of a CEO to act for the chairman. These amendments also permit designated board members to sign on behalf of the company, and the ordinary general assembly meeting will now be valid with 50% shareholder representation, with cumulative voting allowed for board elections. These changes aim to align governance with regulations and support growth. Edita Food Industries S.A.E., a leading Egyptian snack food company dual-listed on the Egyptian and London stock exchanges, reported significant revenue growth for the previous fiscal year.

records.title: Continuous veterinary supervision of the Karkh slaughterhouse is part of the Ministry of Agriculture's efforts to protect consumers.
records.description: Continuous veterinary supervision of the Karkh slaughterhouse is part of the Ministry of Agriculture's efforts to protect consumers. The Ministry of Agriculture stated that the Veterinary Department is maintaining veterinary health supervision of calf slaughter at the Karkh red meat slaughterhouse, which serves the Ministry of Defense's needs. The Director General of the Veterinary Department confirmed that veterinary teams are conducting field supervision in coordination with the Directorates of Medical Affairs and Inspection and Acceptance at the Ministry of Defense to ensure safe veal meat for consumption. Competent veterinary committees have implemented all inspection and preventive measures before and after slaughter, and provided health instructions to workers. These efforts reflect the Ministry of Agriculture's commitment to food safety and public health through ongoing veterinary oversight of meat intended for consumption.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Renewable Energy Authority of Libya (REAoL), in partnership with GIZ Libya through the Sustainable Transition, Energy and Environment...
records.description: The Renewable Energy Authority of Libya (REAoL), in partnership with GIZ Libya through the Sustainable Transition, Energy and Environmental Partnership (STEP), held a ceremony at REAoL's Tripoli headquarters to celebrate key achievements in Libya's renewable energy development. The event marked the finalization and handover of a report designed to enhance Libya’s capabilities in resource assessment and quality assurance for future photovoltaic projects, serving as a valuable guide and educational resource. Opening remarks were delivered by representatives from REAoL, the EU Delegation to Libya, and the German Embassy in Libya. Subsequently, the newly established Coordination Committee convened its first meeting to review ongoing support under the STEP Project and discuss future collaboration. The event concluded with a knowledge-sharing session on Tunisia’s sustainable energy policy experience, led by a STEP Project Advisor. This occasion underscored the shared commitment of Libya, the European Union, and Germany to advancing reliable and sustainable renewable energy systems throughout Libya. The STEP Project is jointly funded by the European Union and the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and is implemented by GIZ and the Prime Minister’s Office of Libya.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Libyan Iron and Steel Company (LISCO) have signed an agreement to strengthen thei...
records.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Libyan Iron and Steel Company (LISCO) have signed an agreement to strengthen their joint efforts in improving energy efficiency and reducing industrial greenhouse gas emissions in Libya. Recognizing LISCO's significant energy consumption and emissions, the partnership aims to lower these through better energy performance, renewable energy integration, and low-carbon practices. UNDP will provide technical support and capacity building to help LISCO become more competitive, efficient, and low-carbon, aligning with Libya's national carbon goals and international mechanisms. This collaboration will support a joint program focused on energy management at LISCO, expected to benefit thousands of employees and the broader Libyan economy through reduced emissions and enhanced energy security, building on UNDP's wider work in Libya promoting climate action and sustainable development.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture's nurseries, including Al-Arroub and Tulkarm Forestry Nurseries, are working to produce tens of thousands of...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture's nurseries, including Al-Arroub and Tulkarm Forestry Nurseries, are working to produce tens of thousands of high-quality forest and pastoral seedlings for distribution during the upcoming agricultural season. Al-Arroub Nursery focuses on tasks to prepare seedlings for afforestation programs. The Tulkarm Agriculture Directorate is producing around 80,000 seedlings, implementing necessary agricultural operations for sustainable afforestation. The Ministry annually distributes these seedlings free to various institutions and farmers to strengthen resilience, promote volunteerism, enhance partnerships, conserve the environment, and prepare for climate change challenges.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has signed an agreement with a global packaging solutions provider to explore establishing local manufacturing operations wi...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has signed an agreement with a global packaging solutions provider to explore establishing local manufacturing operations within the Kingdom. This move underscores Saudi Arabia's commitment to attracting international partners for advanced manufacturing and technology transfer in key industrial sectors, aligning with its Vision 2030 goals for economic diversification and private sector growth. Representatives from the Saudi National Industrial Development Center and the packaging company formalized the agreement, highlighting the packaging provider's expertise and the collaboration's aim to build competitive industrial capabilities and attract long-term investment. The partnership will jointly assess the feasibility of local services and training programs for the Kingdom’s food and beverage packaging sector, following a market assessment for high-value contributions to Saudi manufacturers. This development occurs as the packaging company expands its sustainable packaging innovations, recently introducing a high-speed solution for still beverages using 100% recycled materials, featuring patented technology for improved efficiency and reduced environmental impact, compatible with existing lines and various bottle formats.

records.title: The Syrian Minister of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform recently met with a delegation from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the U...
records.description: The Syrian Minister of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform recently met with a delegation from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) to discuss a proposed cooperation plan aimed at achieving recovery in the agricultural sector. The Minister outlined the challenges and conditions faced by Syria's agricultural sector in recent years, including the impact on infrastructure, production, and farmers. He emphasized the critical need for support to sustain agricultural production, especially given declining financial resources, reduced production capacity, and the low technical and technological level of farmers. The FAO delegation confirmed that Syria is a top priority for the organization in the upcoming phase, stating that their proposed plan, developed earlier, is open for discussion and amendment to align with the Ministry of Agriculture's vision and priorities, particularly concerning the wheat crop due to its link to food security.

records.title: The Tunisian date sector, a key export for the country, has seen a slower than anticipated start to the current season, with data from th...
records.description: The Tunisian date sector, a key export for the country, has seen a slower than anticipated start to the current season, with data from the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI) showing a decrease in both export volume and value, indicating a more challenging international market. Over the initial six months, date exports fell by 6.6% in volume to 100,000 tonnes, and revenue decreased by 5% to 640.8 million dinars compared to the previous year. While the European Union remains the primary market, followed by Africa and Asia, Morocco is the top individual importer. This slowdown is attributed to increased competition from countries like Algeria and Egypt, fluctuating demand in key markets, and rising logistics costs due to global tensions and tariff changes. To overcome these challenges, the sector is focusing on diversifying markets, particularly towards North and West Africa, promoting organic dates, and optimizing supply chains for better cost-efficiency and delivery times.

records.title: Tunisia is addressing major environmental challenges by implementing ambitious strategies to transform its agriculture and fishing sector...
records.description: Tunisia is addressing major environmental challenges by implementing ambitious strategies to transform its agriculture and fishing sectors, supported by the European Union-funded ADAPT program. This program analyzed six key production systems, including mixed livestock and crops, oasis agriculture, olive oil production, agro-industrial systems, agro-sylvo-pastoral practices, and fishing/aquaculture, to identify sustainable alternatives. A workshop in Tunis brought together representatives from the Ministry of Agriculture, funding bodies, and research institutions to discuss findings and ecological transition strategies, emphasizing the need for better environmental and economic performance monitoring and increased awareness of sustainable practices. The EU's significant funding for ADAPT aims to promote sustainable development in these sectors. Strategic recommendations include supporting farmers' adoption of agroecological practices with training and technology, improving access to green financing, and diversifying crops and practices through enhanced collaboration.
records.institution: ADAPT (Support for Sustainable Development in the Agriculture and Artisanal Fishing Sector)

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Tunisia is marking National Agriculture Day with a "From Producer to Consumer" market in Tunis, running for three days, aiming to directl...
records.description: Tunisia is marking National Agriculture Day with a "From Producer to Consumer" market in Tunis, running for three days, aiming to directly connect citizens with fresh agricultural products at competitive prices. Organized under the supervision of the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries, in collaboration with Mixed Professional Associations and the State Land Office, the market will feature around twenty exhibitors offering a range of fresh and processed goods, including fruits, vegetables, meat, poultry, fish, and dairy, within a large exhibition space. A key aspect is the commitment to wholesale market prices for consumers. A representative from the Mixed Professional Fruit Association emphasized the importance of respecting current prices for accessibility. This event, coinciding with the celebration of Tunisia's agricultural progress, demonstrates the authorities' commitment to supporting local producers and providing affordable, quality products.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: Fotouh Al-Kuwait International will invest in a new packaging materials factory in Egypt’s Sokhna Industrial Zone, a key development for...
records.description: Fotouh Al-Kuwait International will invest in a new packaging materials factory in Egypt’s Sokhna Industrial Zone, a key development for local manufacturing and industrial investment within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE). The facility, under SCZONE's umbrella to localize supply chains and enhance its regional hub status, was agreed upon by representatives of SCZONE's primary developer and Fotouh Al-Kuwait, with SCZONE's Chairperson present. The project aims for significant exports, leveraging the zone’s logistical advantages. SCZONE continues to attract investors through incentives and connectivity. Fotouh Al-Kuwait International, an Egyptian-Kuwaiti venture with substantial experience in distribution, is partnering with a Chinese packaging technology firm for the project, expected to create jobs. This investment highlights Egypt’s growing appeal for the packaging industry, further evidenced by a recent project from a global packaging leader to build a sustainable facility with a strong export focus and local sourcing, reinforcing Egypt’s drive for sustainable industrial growth and technological advancement in packaging.

records.title: Continuous veterinary supervision of the Karkh slaughterhouse is a part of the Ministry of Agriculture's consumer protection efforts.
records.description: Continuous veterinary supervision of the Karkh slaughterhouse is a part of the Ministry of Agriculture's consumer protection efforts. The Veterinary Department oversees the slaughter of calves at the Karkh red meat slaughterhouse, which serves the Ministry of Defense's supplies. Veterinary teams from the Slaughterhouse Department conduct ongoing field supervision in coordination with relevant directorates at the Ministry of Defense to ensure safe and suitable veal for consumption. Competent veterinary committees implement all necessary inspection and preventive measures throughout the slaughtering process and provide health instructions to workers. These efforts reflect the Ministry of Agriculture's commitment to ensuring food safety and protecting public health through consistent veterinary oversight of meat for consumption.

records.title: The Department of Prevention is actively working to protect Baghdad's palm trees by combating the red palm weevil in the capital.
records.description: The Department of Prevention is actively working to protect Baghdad's palm trees by combating the red palm weevil in the capital. Ongoing field surveys, investigations, and control measures are being conducted by the Department of Plant Protection in infested agricultural areas under the Baghdad Agriculture Directorate, following ministerial directives and departmental supervision. Specialized technical teams are diligently monitoring and treating infestations using pheromone traps and are educating farmers on early detection and prevention, while also emphasizing reporting suspected cases and adhering to preventive measures for transporting palm seedlings. These efforts are part of broader plans by the Ministry of Agriculture to protect and develop the vital palm tree sector within the country's agricultural landscape.
records.institution: Department of Prevention, Ministry of Agriculture

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: On the occasion of the International Year of Cooperatives, an exhibition of cooperative products was held at the Dbayeh Port, organized b...
records.description: On the occasion of the International Year of Cooperatives, an exhibition of cooperative products was held at the Dbayeh Port, organized by the General Directorate of Cooperatives with the "Atayeb Al-Rif" and "Fishermen of Dbayeh" cooperatives. Over 30 cooperatives from Lebanese regions participated, attended by representatives from international and agricultural organizations. The Director General of Cooperatives highlighted their role as community initiatives. A representative from the European Union emphasized cooperatives for economic empowerment and sustainable development. The Minister of Agriculture stressed that cooperatives are central to the ministry's vision for sustainable agriculture, alongside other national agricultural bodies, urging their independence from political influence. The Minister also addressed the marine fishing sector, promising action against illegal practices to protect food security and fishermen, and called for reporting violations. International partners were thanked for their support, emphasizing the importance of cooperatives for small farmers.
