A review of the agricultural equation was called for, with cooperatives at its core.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture, under the leadership of the Minister of Agriculture and with the direct support of the Prime Minist...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture, under the leadership of the Minister of Agriculture and with the direct support of the Prime Minister, is strategically integrating industrial and medical cannabis into a national vision for a green bioeconomy and environmental and social justice. This initiative aims to implement the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by promoting high-value-added agroecology. Environmental experts highlight medical cannabis as an integrated agricultural solution that enhances soil fertility, rehabilitates degraded lands, naturally controls weeds, and supports integrated pest management. Hemp also demonstrates high climate adaptability, requiring little water and absorbing significant amounts of carbon dioxide. A key advantage is its "zero waste" potential, with all parts usable in various industries, including green building materials. Studies also indicate hemp's ability for soil phytoremediation. The Ministry of Agriculture is updating agricultural policies based on scientific and experiential knowledge, conducting consultations to establish legal frameworks and pilot areas for medical cannabis cultivation, adhering to international standards. This initiative positions cannabis as a potential national symbol of clean agriculture and sustainable development in Lebanon.

records.title: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources in Al Buraimi Governorate has begun its wheat harvest across the governorate's...
records.description: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources in Al Buraimi Governorate has begun its wheat harvest across the governorate's districts, expecting a total production exceeding 250 tons due to a significant expansion in cultivation of this key food security crop. The Director General of Agriculture and Water Resources noted that over 200 acres were planted, with a substantial quantity of high-quality seeds distributed to farmers, emphasizing the Directorate's ongoing support with necessary resources for a successful harvest and their commitment to expanding wheat cultivation for the governorate's food security. Plans are in place to further increase wheat cultivation next season, utilizing the governorate's advantages in wheat production, with new investments planned and local seed sourcing to encourage sustainable domestic production.
records.institution: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture concluded a three-day training course in Dura on "Forage and Alternative Forage Production." This...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture concluded a three-day training course in Dura on "Forage and Alternative Forage Production." This was part of a project funded by the Italian Cooperation and implemented with the CIHEAM-Bari Institute, in partnership with the Ministry. The course aimed to enhance Palestinian farmers' capabilities, improve local production, and support sustainable agriculture and national food security. Directors from the Ministry and the project highlighted the importance of such training for farmer empowerment and fodder sector development. Targeting 20 fodder producers, the course covered advanced methods and technologies in fodder production and sheep farm management. Technical personnel from the Ministry provided expertise. A Ministry director affirmed the ongoing strategic plan to improve farmers' efficiency, expand knowledge, and promote sustainable agriculture and food security nationally.

records.title: The Undersecretary of the Ministry of Agriculture followed up on cooperation with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) at...
records.description: The Undersecretary of the Ministry of Agriculture followed up on cooperation with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) at the Ministry's headquarters. Discussions centered on supporting the agricultural sector and farmers facing ongoing challenges due to occupation conditions, aiming to enhance their resilience. This follow-up builds on previous understandings to establish a partnership for information and expertise exchange to support the affected agricultural sector and enhance food and water security. Planned interventions in West Bank governorates were discussed, including support for livestock breeders and activities to combat the olive fruit fly to protect the sector and local production. The ICRC delegation reiterated its commitment to supporting Palestinian agriculture and strengthening rural communities. Representatives from both the ICRC and the Ministry of Agriculture attended the meeting.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture announced the Kingdom's joining of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture announced the Kingdom's joining of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Agreement on Port State Measures (PSMA) to combat illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, supporting marine biodiversity protection and global environmental sustainability. The ministry stressed this reflects a commitment to international environmental agreements and safeguarding marine resources, aligning with national laws and enhancing local authorities' monitoring of ports and vessels. PSMA aims to improve coordination among national entities, enforce penalties on illegal fishing, and raise awareness in coastal communities. The agreement will boost international cooperation on IUU fishing data, improve global fisheries management through standardized monitoring, promote compliant investment, prevent offending vessels' port access, and offer technical support to developing nations.

records.title: An epidemic of contagious lumpy skin disease has been affecting a region in a governorate for several days, with estimates suggesting at...
records.description: An epidemic of contagious lumpy skin disease has been affecting a region in a governorate for several days, with estimates suggesting at least eight cows have died, and potentially more unreported losses. The viral disease, characterized by severe skin lesions, high fever, and reduced productivity, spreads primarily through biting insects. Local livestock farmers are urgently calling for intervention from the relevant ministry and local authorities to accelerate the incomplete vaccination campaign and limit the disease's spread to protect remaining livestock. The economic consequences include direct losses from deaths, reduced milk production, impaired hide quality, and decreased market value. Veterinarians recommend mass vaccination, increased health surveillance, limiting cattle movement, and symptomatic treatments.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: An international workshop in Tozeur brought together 130 experts from over 20 countries to discuss Sahel-Saharan biodiversity conservation.
records.description: An international workshop in Tozeur brought together 130 experts from over 20 countries to discuss Sahel-Saharan biodiversity conservation. Organized by Sahara Conservation and the General Directorate of Forests (DGF) of the Ministry of Agriculture, the event aimed to strengthen regional cooperation for wildlife preservation and ecosystem restoration. Specialists exchanged ideas to define local strategies, addressing endangered species like the scimitar-horned oryx and threats like poaching and climate change. The goal is to establish cooperation between the DGF and international organizations for better conservation and monitoring. Concrete solutions were discussed, with technical partners contributing expertise on actions such as providing resources for protected species, health monitoring, and protective measures. The DGF plans to implement interventions in Tunisian nature reserves based on workshop recommendations to enhance ecosystem resilience. Regional cooperation is crucial for sustainable management of the region's biodiversity.

records.title: Tunisia will participate in the International Seafood Exhibition – Seafood Expo Global in Barcelona, Spain, an event that gathers profess...
records.description: Tunisia will participate in the International Seafood Exhibition – Seafood Expo Global in Barcelona, Spain, an event that gathers professionals from over 150 countries. Organized by the Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency and the Interprofessional Group of Fisheries Products, Tunisia's participation aims to enhance the international visibility of its seafood products through a 210 m² national pavilion. The pavilion will showcase a variety of seafood, including fresh and frozen fish, farmed fish like sea bass, mussels, and oysters, as well as cephalopods, crustaceans, and shellfish, which are key export products. This participation offers Tunisian companies the opportunity to strengthen their international market position, increase visibility, and forge new business partnerships by promoting the quality and traceability of their products and engaging in meetings with international stakeholders, aligning with Tunisia's broader goals of diversifying export markets and increasing aquaculture production while sustainably managing marine resources.
records.institution: Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency (APIA) and the Interprofessional Group of Fisheries Products (GIPP)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture – North Lebanon Agriculture Department, in cooperation with the Lebanese Association for Farmers' Markets All...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture – North Lebanon Agriculture Department, in cooperation with the Lebanese Association for Farmers' Markets Alliance, organized a specialized workshop titled "Sensory Tasting and Quality of Olive Oil" at the Tripoli Farmers' Market. Twenty-five consumers, producers, and olive oil sector stakeholders participated in the workshop, which featured theoretical and practical training on the sensory characteristics of olive oil and how to distinguish quality. Participants tasted four samples from traditional and modern presses from different Lebanese regions. The workshop covered olive oil's benefits, factors affecting quality, production principles, quality-impacting factors, classification and sensory evaluation standards (according to LIBNOR), and positive/negative characteristics of virgin olive oil and tasting methods. Attendees learned to accurately classify samples, enhancing their consumer and professional awareness. Participants appreciated the information and requested a repeat workshop for a wider audience. The North Lebanon Agriculture Department affirmed that these workshops will continue as part of a national plan to promote sustainable agriculture based on knowledge and innovation, supporting farmers and enhancing local production quality.

records.title: Morocco announces new subsidy plan for citrus exports to Europe
records.description: To enhance the competitiveness of its citrus industry, particularly orange exports facing increased competition, the Moroccan government has introduced a five-year subsidy plan. This initiative provides financial support per tonne for fresh citrus exports (excluding a specific mandarin variety) to key markets, exclusively for licensed exporters with a track record, subject to a rising annual volume cap. The Moroccan citrus federation highlighted that this aims to aid struggling orange producers, potentially extending the export season, improving industry profitability, and benefiting workers. Additional benefits could include more fruit for juicing and earlier harvesting for better tree health and yields. However, the federation noted that currency devaluations in competitor countries still present a significant competitive challenge, even with this support, while also commenting on Morocco's strong position in easy peelers and the uncertain future for oranges due to global production factors.

records.title: To advance Morocco's sustainable agricultural development goals outlined in the "Generation Green 2020-2030" strategy, the National Insti...
records.description: To advance Morocco's sustainable agricultural development goals outlined in the "Generation Green 2020-2030" strategy, the National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA) is central to varietal innovation. Aiming to develop numerous high-yield, climate-resilient plant varieties by 2030, INRA has established "Demonstration Platforms for its New Breedings" in key agricultural zones. These platforms showcase the performance of new cereal, legume, and oilseed varieties to farmers, industry partners, and the media, encouraging their adoption by producers and seed companies. Examples include a high-yielding durum wheat and a health-benefiting hulless barley. These events will also feature seed multiplication programs and the importance of irrigation in water-scarce conditions. Scheduled for May 2025 across various agricultural regions, these demonstration days are intended to significantly promote a more productive, resilient, and sustainable national agricultural sector.
records.institution: The National Institute for Agricultural Research (INRA)

records.title: While Spain previously dominated the Mediterranean avocado market, Morocco has emerged as a significant force.
records.description: While Spain previously dominated the Mediterranean avocado market, Morocco has emerged as a significant force. The traditional avocado season is shifting as supplies from other regions now follow the Moroccan, Spanish, and Portuguese harvests. This change reflects difficulties faced by Spanish producers due to adverse weather, while Moroccan avocado production significantly increased in a recent year thanks to favorable conditions, leading to price drops affecting European growers. Experts anticipate Morocco will capture a larger market share if its production and quality remain consistent. This growth is part of a sustained upward trend in Moroccan avocado cultivation and production over the last several years, indicating a long-term strategic expansion in the sector.

records.title: Oman's fisheries sector significantly contributes to food security and economic growth, with a substantial total fish production in the p...
records.description: Oman's fisheries sector significantly contributes to food security and economic growth, with a substantial total fish production in the past year, primarily driven by sustainable artisanal fishing. The Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund has supported numerous projects across various specialized areas, including advisory services, aquaculture, resource development, quality control, and marketing. Key advancements include the introduction of electronic marketing in fish markets, ongoing efforts for a central fish drying unit, and the deployment of artificial coral reefs to enhance fish stocks. The fund has also backed initiatives in statistical and knowledge development, such as a Fishermen’s Village to support artisanal fishing and a program to preserve maritime heritage. The fund's overall focus has been on increasing productivity through modernizing techniques, diversifying income through aquaculture and industrial growth, and promoting environmental conservation via sustainable practices and marine protection, ultimately advancing Oman's fisheries sector.
records.institution: The Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund

records.title: Tunisia recently hosted Water Expo 5.0 in Tunis, a major water technology and innovation event.
records.description: Tunisia recently hosted Water Expo 5.0 in Tunis, a major water technology and innovation event. The exhibition, held at the Tunisian Union of Industry, Commerce, and Crafts (UTICA), brought together over 60 exhibitors and hundreds of participants from public and private sectors to exchange ideas on sustainable water resource management. The event showcased technological advances and featured a scientific conference on water technology innovation. Organized with the Water Research and Technology Center (CERTE) and the National Institute for Research in Rural Engineering, Water and Forests (INRGREF), and supported by various ministries, the expo highlighted innovations like wastewater treatment and smart irrigation. In response to water scarcity and climate change, Tunisia is emphasizing innovation for efficient water management, and Water Expo 5.0 aimed to foster cooperation and the adoption of new technologies in the sector.
records.institution: The Tunisian Union of Industry, Commerce, and Crafts (UTICA)

records.title: The National Food Loss and Waste Initiative, ne’ma, has launched the country’s first National Baseline Study with 3,000 participants to m...
records.description: The National Food Loss and Waste Initiative, ne’ma, has launched the country’s first National Baseline Study with 3,000 participants to measure actual food loss and waste, aiming to halve it by 2030 in line with UN SDG 12.3. This 18-month study will assess the entire food value chain across all Emirates, with findings expected in the first half of 2026 to establish national indices and inform intervention strategies for food security and sustainability. The effort involves partners like the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment and various municipal and statistical authorities. Data collection includes a field survey in September 2025 to identify where and why food is lost or wasted. The study's results will be shared nationally and internationally to advance sustainable food systems and the UN's 2030 Agenda.
records.institution: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: A meeting led by the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources addressed the implementation of programs to increase grain a...
records.description: A meeting led by the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources addressed the implementation of programs to increase grain and legume production through contract farming. Officials from the General Corporation for Grain Development and Production and the Agricultural Cooperative Union discussed the implementation processes and the collaborative roles of various involved entities. The Minister emphasized the need for inter-agency coordination to efficiently execute agricultural and fisheries programs aimed at boosting production, reducing import dependence, and achieving self-sufficiency, also highlighting the importance of expanding grain and legume cultivation for food security. A call was made for a training program to improve the capabilities of local branches and agricultural cooperatives in managing contract farming data and product tracking.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: A meeting was held under the chairmanship of the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources with members of the Fertilizers...
records.description: A meeting was held under the chairmanship of the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources with members of the Fertilizers and Pesticides Committee at the ministry. The meeting, attended by the Director General of the Quality Control Department for Production Inputs, focused on the committee’s workflow and performance as the first of its kind established by the ministry to reform fertilizer and pesticide management policies and operations. The committee approved the formation of a team of experts and academics to review the foundations, standards, and regulations for correcting the fertilizer and pesticide management policy prepared by the ministry's specialists. This is considered crucial for improving work procedures, removing obstacles, and protecting land resources, especially given the current challenges the country is facing. The Minister praised the committee’s performance in aligning with the current phase’s requirements and contributing to increased production and enhanced food security.

records.title: In coordination with local authorities in Dhamar Governorate and several agricultural nurseries, an afforestation and vegetation cover pr...
records.description: In coordination with local authorities in Dhamar Governorate and several agricultural nurseries, an afforestation and vegetation cover project has been launched across the governorate's districts. This initiative involves the planting of 400,000 sidr and eucalyptus seedlings. During the project launch in Al-Manar District, the Director of the Agriculture Sector in the Governorate explained that a significant number of sidr seedlings will be distributed throughout the district's villages and sub-districts, following a pre-determined plan that identifies suitable planting locations for these seedlings.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: During the Arab Water Week in Amman, the water ministers of Egypt and Jordan met to discuss enhanced collaboration on water and natural r...
records.description: During the Arab Water Week in Amman, the water ministers of Egypt and Jordan met to discuss enhanced collaboration on water and natural resources, focusing on joint initiatives within the "Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems Nexus" framework and exploring cooperation through the Islamic Network on Water Resources Development and Management. The Egyptian minister underscored desalination's role in food production, noting a regional initiative with Jordan and Saudi Arabia for desalination technology exchange to support sustainable agriculture. Discussions also involved Egypt's wastewater treatment projects and potential knowledge sharing in wastewater reuse, as well as the importance of subsurface drainage and joint research on climate-resilient crops. The urgency of climate adaptation projects was highlighted, with a call for industrialized nations to provide climate financing to Arab countries as grants.
records.institution: The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation (MWRI)

records.title: Iraq's Higher Committee for Water, chaired by the Prime Minister, announced comprehensive directives to address national water scarcity a...
records.description: Iraq's Higher Committee for Water, chaired by the Prime Minister, announced comprehensive directives to address national water scarcity and pollution caused by climate change. Key measures include prioritizing strategic land reclamation and closed irrigation systems, using pipelines for declining inflows, and focusing on desalination in southern governorates. The committee mandated strict pollution control, regulated wastewater discharge, and ordered summer water rationing on major rivers. The Ministry of Agriculture was directed to finalize the agricultural card system and adhere to planting schedules. Additional decisions involve a nationwide canal dredging campaign, improved groundwater use, and adherence to the national water release schedule for Dokan Dam. Each province will establish a coordination center led by its governor, involving water, agriculture, environmental, and security agencies.

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture announced that agricultural exports reached a significant volume in the initial months of the year, wit...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture announced that agricultural exports reached a significant volume in the initial months of the year, with projections indicating a substantial increase by year-end. This growth is attributed to the adoption of modern irrigation and farming methods that have boosted production, leading to a considerable surplus exported in the previous year, with dates and vegetables being the primary exports. The Ministry is actively working to expand its market reach into the European Union by organizing exhibitions and engaging with EU embassies in Iraq, building upon existing export routes to Gulf countries and Jordan.

records.title: Moroccan snack tomato specialist Duroc is gaining prominence in the European market through its focus on quality, sustainability, and inn...
records.description: Moroccan snack tomato specialist Duroc is gaining prominence in the European market through its focus on quality, sustainability, and innovation. With significant annual production from its greenhouses, the company supplies numerous European supermarket chains, holding notable market shares in key countries. Duroc distinguishes itself through its dedication to sustainable practices, including waste reduction and efficient resource management, as well as its involvement in social projects and Fairtrade collaborations. This proactive approach aligns with the overall growth of Moroccan tomato exports to Europe. With substantial annual growth and turnover, Duroc exemplifies the dynamism and international potential of the Moroccan agricultural sector.

records.title: Zagora's watermelon season was abruptly halted by a severe hailstorm that ravaged the main production area, destroying a significant port...
records.description: Zagora's watermelon season was abruptly halted by a severe hailstorm that ravaged the main production area, destroying a significant portion of the region's harvest and causing total losses for hundreds of farmers who had not yet harvested. This disaster has dramatic consequences for the local economy, including substantial agricultural losses, inability to meet financial obligations, and a sudden stop in employment for numerous workers. Producers reported a "total failure," also noting disease outbreaks in unaffected areas. Exporters estimated a loss of a substantial tonnage of watermelons, representing nearly half the expected seasonal production, leading to an anticipated shortage and price surge. Losses varied by area, with subsequent harvests in other regions expected to take weeks to compensate. Poor rural road conditions further complicate the situation by hindering access to remaining farms.

records.title: The Ministers of Agriculture and National Economy convened at the Ministry of Agriculture headquarters to address the sharp increase in r...
records.description: The Ministers of Agriculture and National Economy convened at the Ministry of Agriculture headquarters to address the sharp increase in red and white meat prices. They agreed to establish a permanent joint committee, including representatives from both ministries and relevant agencies, to monitor the situation and implement urgent market control measures. A subsequent technical meeting at the Ministry of Economy is planned to analyze the causes of rising prices and develop practical mechanisms for market control, potentially including opening imports to ensure price stability and product availability for consumers. This collaboration aims to enhance cooperation between the two ministries in tackling economic challenges related to food security and consumer protection from unjustified price increases.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Arab Construction Project Association have signed an agreement to establish the Palestinian Center fo...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Arab Construction Project Association have signed an agreement to establish the Palestinian Center for Agricultural Technology Transfer, with the involvement of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO). This center aims to serve as a scientific hub for the Palestinian agricultural sector, facilitating the adoption of modern technology to boost productivity and competitiveness through partnerships with agricultural engineers and veterinarians, with full ministerial support pledged to the Arab Construction Project Association. The Chairman of the Arab Construction Project Association praised the vision for revitalizing their role in agriculture and rural development through this partnership. A representative from UNIDO highlighted the center as a successful unification of public, private, and civil efforts, anticipating a significant transformation in Palestinian agriculture via technology and capacity building. The center will focus on technology transfer, demonstration, knowledge exchange, capacity building, financing, and policy advocacy, offering training programs and operating from the Arab Construction Project Association.

records.title: Modern and innovative farming techniques are significantly benefiting the Najran Region, with methods like greenhouse and vertical agricu...
records.description: Modern and innovative farming techniques are significantly benefiting the Najran Region, with methods like greenhouse and vertical agriculture boosting production, saving land, and conserving water. Utilizing agricultural waste as fertilizer has further supported the region's agricultural growth, establishing it as a key economic sector and contributor to food security. The adoption of advanced technologies and sustainable practices, alongside favorable environmental conditions, has made Najran ideal for year-round diverse crop cultivation, including grains, dates, citrus fruits, vegetables, and new additions like coffee and strawberries, replacing traditional farming methods. A representative from the Najran Coffee Agricultural Cooperative Society highlighted the region's advantages for cultivating diverse crops without pesticides or chemical fertilizers, emphasizing the cooperative's role in promoting modern agricultural practices.
records.institution: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Al-Baha branch of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture presented the contract for an agricultural city project to the A...
records.description: The Al-Baha branch of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture presented the contract for an agricultural city project to the Agricultural Production and Marketing Cooperative in Bani Kabir on Monday. This project, covering a significant area, is dedicated to cultivating almond and fruit trees. The handover is part of the ministry’s broader efforts to promote sustainable agricultural development and support agricultural cooperatives across the Kingdom, aiming to enhance food security and boost the local agricultural sector. A representative from the ministry highlighted the project as a promising way to utilize the Al-Baha Region’s natural resources, noting the economic value of almond and fruit tree cultivation in the area. The branch emphasized its commitment to empowering agricultural cooperatives and fostering a supportive environment for their success, hoping this project will serve as a model for sustainable agricultural investment, with expectations of creating jobs, improving local produce quality, and generating economic benefits for the region.
records.institution: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Tunisian citrus export campaign is experiencing significant growth, with both export revenues and volumes showing substantial increases.
records.description: The Tunisian citrus export campaign is experiencing significant growth, with both export revenues and volumes showing substantial increases. The Maltese orange remains a key export, while lemons find a strong market in Libya, and new opportunities are emerging in the UAE and Saudi Arabia. This success highlights the quality of Tunisian citrus and the adaptability of its exporters. Future strategies focus on modernizing infrastructure, improving supply chains, and enhancing product certification to sustain this positive trend and further strengthen Tunisia's position in the international citrus market.

records.title: Despite economic and social growth, Algeria deliberately resists international supermarket chains to maintain its traditional shopping cu...
records.description: Despite economic and social growth, Algeria deliberately resists international supermarket chains to maintain its traditional shopping culture, which emphasizes personal connections with local traders over impersonal transactions. This preference for frequent shopping at family-run local stores supports community ties and vendors who understand individual needs, a loyalty reinforced by the government's concern over job losses and foreign economic influence, rooted in its history. Fragmented urban land and localized supply chains also hinder the entry of large supermarket chains, as Algerian shoppers prefer interacting with vendors and using cash. While not opposing modernization, Algeria is selectively adopting hybrid retail models like local mini-markets and exploring digital services and co-operatives, forging an alternative path that prioritizes community, local character, and economic independence, potentially offering a model for modernization that preserves cultural identity.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Egypt has signed an agreement to establish two facilities for converting plastic and textile waste into valuable fibers, demonstrating a...
records.description: Egypt has signed an agreement to establish two facilities for converting plastic and textile waste into valuable fibers, demonstrating a growing commitment to a green economy and circular manufacturing. Overseen by the Ministry of Public Business Sector, the agreement involves Misrayon, a UAE-based group, and an investor. Located at Misrayon’s industrial complex, the facilities will use advanced European recycling to process significant amounts of industrial waste into polyester fiber and synthetic felt. These projects aim to reduce pollution, create jobs, and boost Egypt’s international trade. The first facility will focus on plastic recycling for substantial annual polyester fiber production, with significant investment and export targets. The second will recycle textile waste into a large quantity of synthetic felt annually, also with considerable investment and export plans. Officials highlight these plants as part of a larger strategy to integrate recycling, reduce import reliance, and support environmental conservation, while also strengthening international cooperation in sustainable waste-to-resource technologies.
records.institution: Misrayon (Misr for Industrial Silk and Polyester Stable Fiber Company)

records.title: Morocco's strawberry sector is facing a downturn despite the country's growing success with blueberries and avocados.
records.description: Morocco's strawberry sector is facing a downturn despite the country's growing success with blueberries and avocados. Grower interest in strawberries has significantly decreased, leading to a substantial reduction in cultivated land, jeopardizing future production targets set with the Ministry of Agriculture due to declining profitability compared to other berries and avocados. Intense international competition, particularly from countries offering lower prices, and a limited duty-free export window to key markets further threaten the Moroccan strawberry industry, pushing it towards less lucrative alternatives like frozen strawberries. Production challenges, including deteriorating plant quality and labor shortages, compound these issues. While family farms provide some resilience, the overall future of Moroccan strawberries remains uncertain as the sector seeks solutions, contrasting sharply with the thriving blueberry industry, which enjoys strong international demand and new market opportunities.
records.institution: Interprofessional Federation of Berries of Morocco

records.title: The Moroccan avocado season of 2024/2025, despite a record volume, is causing difficulties for producers due to a sharp slowdown in expor...
records.description: The Moroccan avocado season of 2024/2025, despite a record volume, is causing difficulties for producers due to a sharp slowdown in exports since last December, leading many to delay harvest in hopes of better prices, a gamble that appears to have failed. This situation is partly attributed to a significant increase in avocado cultivation area, resulting in oversupply and depressed market prices, forcing producers in regions like Gharb to harvest urgently despite poor price prospects, with a notable percentage of fruit still unharvested. This season's commercial challenges are expected to influence future decisions regarding harvest timing and the number of producers remaining in the sector. Paradoxically, Moroccan avocado production has surged dramatically, more than doubling compared to the previous season, highlighting the sector's potential but also the international market's struggle to absorb such rapid growth, necessitating an adjustment in commercial strategies and future planning within the Moroccan avocado industry.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Oman's green hydrogen industry orchestrator, has launched a Single Permit System to significantly ease the permitting process for green h...
records.description: Oman's green hydrogen industry orchestrator, has launched a Single Permit System to significantly ease the permitting process for green hydrogen developers, announced during the introduction of Oman’s third green hydrogen auction round for a substantial land block near the Duqm Special Economic Zone. Previously, developers had to engage with over a dozen government bodies to secure land access. This new one-stop system, a key outcome of a collaborative national laboratory, aims to provide developers with immediate land access upon award, eliminating the need for multiple individual approvals from entities such as the Ministry of Energy and Minerals, Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, Environment Authority, Public Authority for Special Economic Zones and Free Zones (OPAZ), and others. While developers still have obligations to fulfill, the Single Permit System is expected to greatly reduce administrative complexity and save time, enabling earlier project commencement.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Yatta - Hebron directorate, provided water tanks to farmers in the Khallet Amara area to bolster...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Yatta - Hebron directorate, provided water tanks to farmers in the Khallet Amara area to bolster their resilience. A local agricultural director highlighted the significance of this support for farmers' stability on their land, particularly amid challenging conditions. This initiative is part of the Ministry's continuous efforts to enhance food security and support the agricultural sector through various programs aimed at improving farmers' livelihoods and their capacity to overcome difficulties. The Ministry of Agriculture reiterates its ongoing commitment to supporting farmers and developing the agricultural sector within its means.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture has initiated a three-day specialized training course on fodder and alternative fodder production...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture has initiated a three-day specialized training course on fodder and alternative fodder production, as part of the Agri-Food Cooperation Network Support Project in Palestine, funded by the Italian Cooperation and implemented with the CIHEAM-Bari Institute. This course aims to enhance the capabilities of Palestinian farmers, improve local agricultural production quality, and support sustainable agriculture by focusing on economically viable crops for national food security. Organized by the South Hebron/Dura Agriculture Directorate, the training targeted fodder production specialists, with officials emphasizing the importance of such programs for farmer capacity building and sustainable agricultural development, outlining project activities. Technical staff from the Ministry of Agriculture delivered the training, which covered the latest scientific methods and technologies in fodder production, along with best practices for sheep farm management, to improve farmer efficiency and keep pace with agricultural advancements.

records.title: In preparation for the harvest season, the Technical Agency for Land Transport, in collaboration with the Regional Union of Agriculture a...
records.description: In preparation for the harvest season, the Technical Agency for Land Transport, in collaboration with the Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries of Béja, initiated a national technical inspection campaign for agricultural tractors and trailers. The campaign focused on examining the condition of vehicles, particularly brakes, steering, signaling, and safety devices, with fire prevention being a key concern during harvest. This initiative aims to mitigate the increased risk of accidents associated with higher agricultural traffic during the harvest season, which saw a significant number of incidents involving tractors and trailers in the previous year. Authorities are stressing the importance of regular vehicle maintenance, proper trailer loading, and driver awareness of traffic rules. The Béja region, a major grain producer with a large cultivated area and promising harvest conditions, faces logistical challenges related to farm roads and collection center preparation.

records.title: The city of Sfax will host the first AGRI WATER TECH Exhibition, a major event dedicated to agriculture, water resources, and innovative...
records.description: The city of Sfax will host the first AGRI WATER TECH Exhibition, a major event dedicated to agriculture, water resources, and innovative technologies, organized by the Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (URAP) in partnership with the General Society for the Organization and Promotion of Exhibitions. This exhibition aims to gather key players to discuss sustainable management of agricultural and water resources, showcasing over 50 exhibitors from the Sfax region featuring irrigation systems, hydraulic equipment, and agricultural startups with cutting-edge technologies for more resilient agriculture amidst climate and water challenges. The event will include conferences and scientific meetings on topics like sustainable water management, innovative irrigation, desalination, olive oil sector promotion with emerging technologies like AI, climate change impacts on agriculture, and biotechnology for environmental adaptation. Welcoming private companies, public organizations, financial institutions, and rural women's initiatives, the fair seeks to strengthen cooperation and promote locally adapted solutions, reflecting Sfax's growing importance in agriculture and water, with AGRI WATER TECH 2025 potentially accelerating innovation and developing new agricultural strategies for climate and economic challenges through professional, researcher, and investor interactions.
records.institution: Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (URAP)

records.title: Tunisia is facing a renewed outbreak of animal plague, posing a significant threat to its livestock and requiring urgent action from agri...
records.description: Tunisia is facing a renewed outbreak of animal plague, posing a significant threat to its livestock and requiring urgent action from agricultural authorities. Several recent cases have led to a national eradication plan supported by international health organizations. Despite prior control efforts, the disease persists in some livestock farms in key agricultural regions. In response, the Ministry of Agriculture has announced a large vaccination program aiming for national eradication by 2030, with international funding for vaccines and training. A surveillance system has also been implemented for rapid outbreak detection through collaboration between veterinary services, farmers, and laboratories. Challenges remain in raising farmer awareness and controlling stray animals, which can spread the disease. Achieving the eradication goal requires combined efforts from the government, international bodies, and the agricultural sector through enhanced vaccination, surveillance, and awareness initiatives to ensure a safer future for Tunisian livestock.

records.title: Fresh Chinese vegetables are reaching supermarket shelves in Dubai, UAE, within 48 hours of harvest, meeting the significant demand in th...
records.description: Fresh Chinese vegetables are reaching supermarket shelves in Dubai, UAE, within 48 hours of harvest, meeting the significant demand in this vegetable-import-reliant region due to the UAE's challenging desert climate for leafy green production. This rapid delivery is facilitated by efficient cold-chain logistics, ensuring freshness from harvest in China to display in Dubai within two days. A major produce procurement group reports that Chinese vegetables account for a substantial portion of their total vegetable sales in the UAE throughout the year. These imports are also enriching the local culinary scene, with chefs and consumers embracing the unique flavors of Chinese vegetables like bok choy, which has become a popular ingredient in various dishes, garnering praise from a diverse customer base.

records.title: A meeting in Sana'a, chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Administration and Local and Rural Development, focused on affo...
records.description: A meeting in Sana'a, chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Administration and Local and Rural Development, focused on afforestation efforts and plans to improve vegetation cover nationwide. The Deputy Prime Minister stressed governmental work to find sustainable alternatives for those dependent on logging, emphasizing shared responsibility for environmental protection and the need for central support to local authorities for afforestation, urging the use of the autumn season for expanding green areas and increasing seedling production for future sustainability. The importance of media and community leaders in environmental awareness was noted, highlighting Yemeni society's potential for agricultural-ecological transformation through community mobilization. The Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources announced a national million-seedling planting project. The Minister of Health and Environment discussed establishing new nurseries and integrating agricultural awareness into education, emphasizing the impact of vegetation loss on public health and the need to prevent excessive logging.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The marketing of locally produced chicken has been launched in Bajil district, Hodeida province, aiming to substitute imported chicken.
records.description: The marketing of locally produced chicken has been launched in Bajil district, Hodeida province, aiming to substitute imported chicken. This initiative is led by the Bajil District Multipurpose Agricultural Cooperative Society in collaboration with local poultry farmers, intending to boost local production and regulate the poultry sector through cooperative efforts that support food security and small producers. A local official emphasized this as a practical step towards empowering local producers and improving poultry farmers' capabilities via a regulatory framework that stabilizes prices and ensures quality. A poultry sector representative explained that the current output resulted from organized collaboration between cooperatives, farmers' associations, and the private sector, enabling the marketing of high-quality local frozen chicken to meet market needs, as part of a national program to decrease imports and foster investment in the poultry sector. Representatives from the Bajil Cooperative Society affirmed their readiness to provide the necessary quantities of local frozen chicken, highlighting the project as a practical model of farmer and supporter integration, and praised the role of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources in sponsoring such initiatives to develop local production and expand its marketing.
records.institution: The Bajil District Multipurpose Agricultural Cooperative Society

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, via its Environment Department, took part in the "Spring of the Earth" Festival, organized by the University...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, via its Environment Department, took part in the "Spring of the Earth" Festival, organized by the University of Baghdad/College of Administration and Economics, as part of its ongoing strategy to disseminate environmental awareness and combat climate change. A representative from the Environment Department delivered a lecture detailing the Ministry's primary initiatives to tackle environmental challenges and cultivate a sustainable environment. These actions encompass the adoption of advanced irrigation methods for water efficiency, widespread afforestation programs, projects aimed at stabilizing sand dunes, and the cultivation of plant species resilient to drought and heat. The lecture also underscored the Ministry's promotion of clean energy and organic fertilizers to decrease greenhouse gas emissions, alongside its efforts to prevent epidemic diseases in livestock, such as hemorrhagic fever, and to safeguard both livestock and plant resources in support of national food security. The representative from the Environment Department was presented with a certificate of appreciation by the college for their active involvement.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan has announced the commencement of import licenses for all types of lemons...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan has announced the commencement of import licenses for all types of lemons starting May 10, with import applications being accepted in the days leading up to this date. This decision follows direct coordination between the Lebanese and Jordanian Ministers of Agriculture. The Lebanese Minister conveyed appreciation for the positive and prompt response, viewing this action as genuine support for the Lebanese agricultural sector and a step towards stronger agricultural ties between the two brotherly nations.

records.domain: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
records.title: The Najd agricultural region in Dhofar Governorate has cultivated approximately 6,400 acres of wheat across 52 farms, expecting a 6,000-t...
records.description: The Najd agricultural region in Dhofar Governorate has cultivated approximately 6,400 acres of wheat across 52 farms, expecting a 6,000-ton production for the 2024/2025 season, with harvesting commencing in early April under the supervision of the Directorate General of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources in Dhofar, in collaboration with the Agriculture and Fisheries Development Fund. While wheat cultivation area saw a decrease due to some farmers shifting to other crops for environmental and economic reasons, and more seeking government subsidies exploring alternatives like onions and tomatoes, the ministry provided subsidized wheat seeds and free harvesters, also facilitating delivery to Oman Flour Mills Company, emphasizing wheat's importance in food security.
records.institution: The Directorate General of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources in Dhofar

records.title: A delegation from the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC) attended the Earthna Summit i...
records.description: A delegation from the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC) attended the Earthna Summit in Doha, Qatar, alongside representatives from international organizations. The summit focused on advancing sustainability in hot and arid regions through innovation and knowledge, addressing environmental, economic, and social dimensions, and sharing best practices in sustainable agriculture and climate change adaptation. During the summit, the NCVC delegation highlighted Saudi Arabia’s pioneering efforts in mangrove forest development and preservation, community support through volunteer work, and the promotion of mangrove honey production, which received significant praise. The NCVC continues its extensive work to foster a thriving and sustainable vegetation cover across Saudi Arabia by protecting and enhancing vegetation, rehabilitating degraded lands.
records.institution: The National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC)

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The 21st Mango and Tropical Fruits Festival in the Jazan Region is scheduled to begin, organized by the local branch of the Ministry of E...
records.description: The 21st Mango and Tropical Fruits Festival in the Jazan Region is scheduled to begin, organized by the local branch of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) in collaboration with Sabya Governorate and various partners. This annual event, the oldest agricultural festival in Jazan since its start, has been a key promoter of mango and tropical fruit cultivation for over two decades, playing a vital role in public awareness, supporting local farmers, and fostering regional socio-economic development. This year, the ministry has increased its efforts to ensure the continued success of this annual celebration, which serves as a platform for farmers and entrepreneurs to market their produce and expand their customer base in a region boasting over 3,360,000 tropical fruit trees with an annual production of 123,311 tons.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) is making notable advancements in mango and tropical...
records.description: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) is making notable advancements in mango and tropical fruit cultivation in the Jazan Region as part of its efforts to promote sustainable agriculture. The center's research fields feature over 70 varieties of mangoes and tropical fruits, where they are evaluated to improve production quality and increase farmers’ economic returns. Estidamah also focuses on transferring successful agricultural practices to farmers and investors, contributing to regional economic growth and enhanced food security. The center's initiatives aim to support farmers and promote the use of modern agricultural techniques, thereby fostering sustainable development in the sector, raising productivity, improving farmers' incomes, and strengthening Jazan's position as a key agricultural hub in the Kingdom.
records.institution: - The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah)

records.title: Abu Dhabi is launching Nutri-Mark, a mandatory Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling (FOPNL) system, set to begin in July.
records.description: Abu Dhabi is launching Nutri-Mark, a mandatory Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling (FOPNL) system, set to begin in July. Developed by the Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council and the Abu Dhabi Public Health Centre, this system will feature an A–E color-coded rating to quickly inform consumers about a food product's nutritional profile. While drawing inspiration from Europe's Nutri-Score, Nutri-Mark is specifically adapted to the UAE's dietary patterns and Halal requirements. Initially, the system will apply to five key food categories, with a phased expansion planned to eventually cover all food products, including unpackaged items and restaurant meals. This initiative is a strategic public health effort to combat high rates of overweight and obesity by empowering consumers to make healthier choices.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council

records.title: Morocco’s Agriculture Minister highlighted the importance of the Dakhla seawater desalination plant during a regional visit, describing i...
records.description: Morocco’s Agriculture Minister highlighted the importance of the Dakhla seawater desalination plant during a regional visit, describing it as innovative, environmentally sustainable, and socially inclusive. The project is expected to create a significant agricultural hub with considerable economic impact while running on wind energy and protecting groundwater. It is also projected to generate over 25,000 permanent jobs for the region's youth and strengthen local water and food security. The desalination plant is anticipated to produce 37 million cubic meters of water annually, with 30 million cubic meters allocated for irrigating 5,200 hectares of farmland and 7 million cubic meters for supplying drinking water to Dakhla city and the future Atlantic port.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia is aggressively pursuing a leading role in the hydrogen economy by investing significantly in both green and blue hydrogen p...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is aggressively pursuing a leading role in the hydrogen economy by investing significantly in both green and blue hydrogen production, aiming to power half of its electricity with renewables by 2030 and achieve net-zero emissions by 2060 through strategic alliances and initiatives like NEOM. Major Saudi energy companies are at the forefront of these efforts, undertaking substantial projects in line with national sustainability objectives. The Kingdom intends to invest heavily in green hydrogen manufacturing and become a major global producer of blue hydrogen, with ambitious production targets for blue ammonia by 2030. Saudi Arabia is actively exploring diverse applications of hydrogen across industrial, power generation, and transportation sectors, a strategy driven by its Vision 2030, strong international partnerships, technological advancements, and government support. Integrating hydrogen into the national blue economy is considered vital for sustainable growth, with green hydrogen expected to revolutionize transportation and heavy industry.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries called on farmers to vaccinate animals intended for Eid Al Adha against infec...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries called on farmers to vaccinate animals intended for Eid Al Adha against infectious diseases according to the schedule from the Regional Commission for Agricultural Development's veterinary services. Farmers were also advised on proper feed dosage and sufficient fiber to prevent enterotoxemia in slaughter animals. The ministry's veterinary services recommended separating slaughter animals by size and age and following biosecurity measures by avoiding animals of unknown origin. They emphasized treating animals for internal and external parasites and consulting veterinarians if necessary. Farmers were urged to ensure animal welfare by providing comfortable, shaded areas, a balanced diet without harmful substances, and constant access to water. Additionally, respecting medication withdrawal periods and contacting veterinary services for sick animals, while isolating them, was emphasized.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: Taiz officials launched agricultural activities in summer schools, in coordination with the Agriculture Sector, emphasizing the leadershi...
records.description: Taiz officials launched agricultural activities in summer schools, in coordination with the Agriculture Sector, emphasizing the leadership's interest in agriculture as a national development priority. They highlighted the importance of equipping students with agricultural and development skills for the country's future, improving living standards, and enhancing food security. It was stressed that agricultural knowledge is a key focus of national development alongside other educational activities, requiring trained scientific personnel. An official from the Province's Agriculture Sector expressed hope that students would benefit from the agricultural program, learning about methods, fertilization, and pruning, and acknowledged teachers' role in providing this knowledge.

records.title: As part of the Ministry of Agriculture's National Agricultural Extension Program, an orientation seminar was held in Baysour, Aley Distri...
records.description: As part of the Ministry of Agriculture's National Agricultural Extension Program, an orientation seminar was held in Baysour, Aley District, in collaboration with local agricultural organizations and with the participation of community leaders and agricultural center staff. The seminar, targeting around 45 smallholder farmers, focused on sustainable agricultural practices, particularly the concept and importance of fertilization for fruit trees, covering scientific principles, application methods, and timing. Different types of fertilizers and essential tree nutrients were discussed. The significance of farm registry enrollment for sector regulation and the role of agricultural extension in enhancing production efficiency and farmer income through updated information were emphasized. Forest fire protection as a shared responsibility was also addressed. An expert lectured on the scientific and practical fertilization of fruit trees for optimal results, leading to active engagement from farmers with questions on various fertilization techniques and nutrient deficiencies.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture - Akkar Agriculture Department is distributing "Aksad 1133" soft wheat seeds for free to farmers in Akkar Gov...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture - Akkar Agriculture Department is distributing "Aksad 1133" soft wheat seeds for free to farmers in Akkar Governorate as part of a national project to expand wheat cultivation and enhance food security in Lebanon. This initiative is part of a larger program to support sustainable agriculture by providing improved, high-quality seeds known for their high yields and disease resistance, making them suitable for various Lebanese agricultural environments. The effort aims to empower farmers, increase their production, and achieve greater self-sufficiency in the strategic wheat sector, thereby reducing import costs and strengthening food sovereignty amidst economic challenges. Akkar Governorate, with its fertile land and willing farmers, is a key area for the success of these national efforts to build a resilient and sustainable agricultural sector.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture – Marjayoun Center, as part of the National Agricultural Extension Program, held a specialized agricultural w...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture – Marjayoun Center, as part of the National Agricultural Extension Program, held a specialized agricultural workshop in Deir Mimas for twenty local farmers, focusing on three key areas. The first area covered the importance of soil analysis in specialized laboratories for optimal crop quality and sustainable production. The second addressed olive tree diseases and control methods, emphasizing the use of surveillance traps for pests. The third area explained the administrative services available at the Marjayoun Agricultural Center, including service conditions and required documentation. The workshop saw significant farmer engagement and discussions on improving agricultural practices.

records.title: Facing its worst wheat harvest in over 15 years, with a significant drop in overall grain production due to prolonged drought, Morocco is...
records.description: Facing its worst wheat harvest in over 15 years, with a significant drop in overall grain production due to prolonged drought, Morocco is increasing wheat imports, including a substantial shipment from Kazakhstan facilitated by its national railway company. This shipment marks a key diversification in Morocco's grain supply chain. Despite a reported increase in overall grain production compared to the previous year, domestic supply remains insufficient to meet national consumption, leading to an anticipated rise in imports. Kazakhstan, having experienced a record grain harvest, has emerged as a crucial partner, boosting its wheat exports to North Africa. A significant number of trains loaded with Kazakh wheat are being routed through Latvia for maritime transport to Morocco, bypassing traditional Black Sea routes and indicating growing logistical cooperation between the two nations. Morocco significantly increased its imports of Kazakh wheat in the first part of 2025, and officials from both countries are exploring closer ties, including the potential development of a logistics hub in Morocco to streamline future grain exports to Africa.

records.title: Following recent CJEU rulings that weaken agricultural agreements between Morocco and the EU, producers in the Dakhla region are consider...
records.description: Following recent CJEU rulings that weaken agricultural agreements between Morocco and the EU, producers in the Dakhla region are considering diversifying their export markets. The ruling, requiring specific labeling for products from the Moroccan Sahara, has raised concerns among local agricultural operators who export under the "made in Morocco" label. While continuing operations in the EU with hopes for a political solution, Dakhla producers are exploring alternative markets like the United Kingdom, West Africa, and North America due to their growth potential. The Dakhla region's favorable climate allows for early harvests and year-round production of fruits and vegetables, attracting international buyers. Infrastructure investments, such as a future desalination plant, are expected to further boost production. An economic interest group of young farmers in the region exemplifies this growth, cultivating various crops for export and the domestic market.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, under the direction of its minister, successfully launched sub-agricultural offices in rural areas like the...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, under the direction of its minister, successfully launched sub-agricultural offices in rural areas like the Central Jordan Valley District, quickly achieving significant progress despite logistical challenges. This initiative aims to enhance access to agricultural services for all farmers and empower rural communities by providing technical guidance, assessing needs, and implementing field development projects, supported by a strategic partnership with the Ministry of Local Government and municipal councils. These offices have improved farmers' access to services and facilitated direct communication with officials, aiding in problem-solving. Despite a recent launch and some infrastructure limitations, the field staff's strong performance has yielded exceptional results in agricultural guidance, partner networking, and farmer support programs, representing successful cooperation between government and local authorities for comprehensive agricultural development.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC – Masdar, the UAE’s clean energy leader, announced that its subsidiary TERNA ENERGY has 1 completed...
records.description: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC – Masdar, the UAE’s clean energy leader, announced that its subsidiary TERNA ENERGY has 1 completed its delisting from the Athens Stock Exchange following Masdar’s full acquisition of the company. A delegation from Masdar visited TERNA ENERGY’s Athens headquarters to discuss Masdar’s strategy for expanding the business and accelerating renewable energy growth in Southeastern and Central Europe. The acquisition aims to strengthen Masdar's position in Greece and the wider region, expedite renewable energy solutions, and unlock necessary investment for clean energy targets, demonstrating the commitment of both the UAE and Masdar to affordable, secure, and sustainable energy. This move will support Greece’s National Energy and Climate Plan, the EU’s net-zero emissions ambition, and Masdar’s global target of 100 GW clean energy capacity by 2030, with TERNA ENERGY aiming for 6GW by 2030 with Masdar’s backing. The integration of the two companies is expected to maximize their combined expertise to accelerate clean energy projects in Greece and the region, establishing TERNA ENERGY as Masdar’s flagship platform there.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC – Masdar

records.title: The Mleiha Wheat Farm in Sharjah, UAE, has cultivated a new wheat variety, Saba Sanabel, with a record-high native protein content, signa...
records.description: The Mleiha Wheat Farm in Sharjah, UAE, has cultivated a new wheat variety, Saba Sanabel, with a record-high native protein content, signaling a major step in the UAE's efforts to reduce food import dependence and become a wheat exporter. The farm, covering over 1,400 hectares, aims to boost local food production through sustainable, chemical-free agriculture in a country with limited arable land and high import reliance. This desert-grown, nutrient-dense wheat variety has the potential to significantly alter the national food landscape, with the farm eventually aiming to meet Sharjah's entire wheat demand. The project demonstrates the transformation of harsh conditions into fertile opportunities through innovation and climate-resilient practices. The farm's flagship variety was selected for its drought and salinity tolerance, with advanced technology and AI-driven irrigation optimizing growth. Organically cultivated and quality-certified, this high-protein wheat has been used to launch a product line, indicating plans for commercial expansion and positioning Sharjah as a potential premium wheat supplier in international markets.

records.title: The United Arab Emirates continued its global engagement for the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, which it is co-hosting with Senega...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates continued its global engagement for the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, which it is co-hosting with Senegal, by participating in the 41st UN-Water Meeting in Rome and the 12th Roundtable on Financing Water in Jeddah, co-organized by the OECD and the Islamic Development Bank. These forums gathered stakeholders to discuss leveraging finance, including Islamic finance, for sustainable water investments, aiming to inform the agendas of upcoming water conferences, given the significant investment needed to achieve Sustainable Development Goal 6. High-level officials from various nations underscored the global commitment to water finance. Representing the UAE, a senior official emphasized the importance of the 2026 conference in accelerating progress and unlocking new capital, particularly from the private sector, alongside aligning policy and innovation. The UAE also highlighted its water innovation initiatives. Its participation in the UN-Water Meeting strengthened coordination with partners, including Senegal and UN DESA, discussing preparations for the 2026 conference and encouraging input on dialogue themes that will inform a background note for a preparatory meeting.
