records.title: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) announced the first Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition at ADNEC Centr...
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) announced the first Emirates Agriculture Conference and Exhibition at ADNEC Centre Al Ain. This event supports the UAE’s agricultural sector and food security goals under the ‘Plant the Emirates’ National Programme. It will gather officials and global agricultural leaders to discuss sustainable agriculture. The Minister highlighted the UAE's focus on agricultural development for national food security using climate-smart solutions and the event's role in empowering local farmers and promoting dialogue. The conference and exhibition aim to address challenges like water scarcity with smart technologies, foster innovation, and engage the community in building a resilient agricultural sector. It will showcase local produce and facilitate partnerships among various stakeholders, including farmers, universities, and tech companies. Key features include a National Agricultural Extension Forum and sessions on sustainability, food security, and modern agriculture. The event will display agricultural innovations and promote sustainable practices. Specialized zones will feature farmers, youth, technology, schools, corporations, startups, government entities, and food and beverage.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: Algeria and China have strengthened their strategic partnership by signing eight agreements in Algiers across industrial, automotive, rai...
records.description: Algeria and China have strengthened their strategic partnership by signing eight agreements in Algiers across industrial, automotive, railway, and agricultural sectors during an investment forum. These partnerships aim to bolster economic relations and foster sustainable multi-sector cooperation, with Chinese companies undertaking significant projects. In agriculture, a Chinese firm will invest in southern Algerian crops, and Agrolog with CRCC will develop a poultry project. Industrially, Algeria's SNTF will partner with CRRC's subsidiary for railway equipment manufacturing, while Fondal and Jetour will invest in an automotive plant in Batna, and Iris with Chery in a body painting and welding site. Additionally, Condor and Hisense will build a household appliance factory, and Madar and CCECC will form an industrial partnership, with a ninth agreement planned for bicycle and motorcycle production between Cycma and QJ Motor. These deals highlight a mutual ambition to diversify cooperation and leverage investment for growth, positioning China as a key player in Algeria's industrial and agricultural advancement.

records.title: Egyptian fresh green bean exports are decreasing annually as frozen and canned options gain favor.
records.description: Egyptian fresh green bean exports are decreasing annually as frozen and canned options gain favor. A co-founder of Egyfarm noted a continuous rise in IQF green beans and a decline in fresh exports, though the latter now commands higher value due to improved quality. Fresh green bean export prices significantly increased in a recent year, while frozen exports also saw a substantial rise, indicating growing global demand for processed vegetables. This trend occurs during a favorable fresh bean harvest season from June to September, aligning with European, North American, and Middle Eastern demand. Following a pattern seen in citrus processing, the green bean sector is increasing IQF capacity and traceability to meet changing buyer needs, competing on reliability and food safety against major exporters. The primary destination for fresh Egyptian green beans is Russia, followed by the USA and Uganda, while Germany, the UK, and Saudi Arabia lead demand for frozen and processed beans.

records.title: A team of youth in Iraq, inspired by the ancient Mesopotamian god of agriculture NABU, is tackling the significant issue of tomato waste...
records.description: A team of youth in Iraq, inspired by the ancient Mesopotamian god of agriculture NABU, is tackling the significant issue of tomato waste in the Ninewa region. Originating from an EU-funded hackathon, the team developed an innovative business, named Rabiyan after a tomato-producing region in Mosul, to transform surplus tomatoes into valuable dried food products like slices, powders, and tomatoes preserved in olive oil. Winning a grant, they invested in product development and packaging, focusing on creating nutritious and sustainable options for consumers. While facing challenges in building customer trust for these new products in the Iraqi market, Rabiyan is actively working to increase awareness through social media, local exhibitions, and samples, with ambitions to expand across Iraq and into Gulf countries like Saudi Arabia.

records.title: The Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) highlighted the importance of improving cargo transport with Kazakhstan, especially in...
records.description: The Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) highlighted the importance of improving cargo transport with Kazakhstan, especially in livestock, to enhance food security, following a meeting with Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister and the Kazakh Ambassador. The KCCI lauded Kazakhstan's economic growth and natural resources, expressing a desire to strengthen cooperation through renewed agreements and business meetings. The Kazakh Minister emphasized his country's commercial potential due to its strategic location linking the GCC, Russia, and China, its investor-friendly environment with incentives, and its efforts to improve the business climate through digitalization, inviting Kuwaiti businesses to invest in various sectors, particularly given the visa exemption for Kuwaiti citizens.
records.institution: The Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture – Bint Jbeil Center held a specialized guidance seminar for beekeepers as part of the National Agricultural G...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture – Bint Jbeil Center held a specialized guidance seminar for beekeepers as part of the National Agricultural Guidance Program. The seminar, attended by many beekeepers and others interested in agriculture and the environment, aimed to boost the skills of those in the sector and develop beekeeping as a key part of the local agricultural economy. The goal was to improve cooperation, provide scientific and practical knowledge for better honey production, and enhance working conditions amid environmental challenges. The head of the Agricultural Center in Bint Jbeil gave a lecture on optimal spring apiary management, including hive care, reproduction, disease protection, and food sources. He also stressed preserving the natural environment for sustainable beekeeping and the crucial role of bees in ecology and pollination. The seminar saw significant interaction and discussion among attendees. Participants thanked the Ministry for supporting the vital beekeeping sector, believing such events improve production quality and economic returns.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its National Agricultural Extension Program, issued a guidance bulletin for farmers on the best prac...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its National Agricultural Extension Program, issued a guidance bulletin for farmers on the best practices for purchasing, handling, and using pesticides to protect agricultural production, ensure food safety, and safeguard the health of farmers and consumers. The bulletin advises purchasing from licensed stores after consulting with an agricultural engineer and obtaining a written prescription and invoice. Proper use includes carefully reading the label, avoiding unauthorized mixing, ensuring secure storage, and applying pesticides only when necessary. Safety measures during spraying emphasize avoiding adverse weather, not leaving solutions in tanks, cleaning equipment, and taking immediate action in case of exposure. Post-spraying guidelines cover safe disposal of containers and leftover solutions, and adherence to the pre-harvest interval. The bulletin also warns against the dangers of unregulated pesticides and advises spraying based on the economic threshold, urging farmers to monitor crops and seek agricultural guidance while reminding them to report any violations to the Ministry.

records.title: Spanish agricultural exporters, represented by the Proexport and Apoexpa associations from the Murcia region, are actively working to str...
records.description: Spanish agricultural exporters, represented by the Proexport and Apoexpa associations from the Murcia region, are actively working to strengthen their presence in the Canadian market. They recently concluded a commercial mission to Montreal during the "CPMA Fresh Week" fair. This proactive approach follows significant exports of Spanish fresh fruits and vegetables (over 40,000 tonnes worth 64.6 million euros, mainly citrus, peppers, and persimmons) to Canada in 2024. This activity underscores the urgency for Moroccan exporters, as previously advised by AgriMaroc, to swiftly establish themselves in the promising Canadian market before Spanish competitors further solidify their market share amidst global trade uncertainties.

records.title: The YNNA Group has announced its participation in the International Agriculture Show in Meknes (SIAM), showcasing new products designed t...
records.description: The YNNA Group has announced its participation in the International Agriculture Show in Meknes (SIAM), showcasing new products designed to support a more resilient and eco-friendly agriculture in Morocco. The group will present products from its subsidiaries: Dimatit, Fibrociment, GPC Papier et Carton, and Afrique Câbles, across a large exhibition space. Fibrociment is introducing new energy-efficient and durable panels and sandwich boards for rapid construction of agricultural buildings. GPC Papier & Carton is presenting 100% recyclable agricultural packaging with high-definition digital printing for enhanced product traceability and branding. Afrique Câbles is focusing on green energy with maintenance-free batteries for vehicles and solar GEL batteries suited for rural areas. Dimatit aims to support the national “Generation Green” plan with sustainable irrigation solutions. The YNNA Group's participation reflects its commitment to innovation and environmental responsibility in addressing the challenges faced by Moroccan agriculture.

records.title: The General Administration of Agricultural Control at the Ministry of Agriculture held a national meeting with agricultural control teams...
records.description: The General Administration of Agricultural Control at the Ministry of Agriculture held a national meeting with agricultural control teams to discuss improving oversight and transportation of agricultural products, especially given market access challenges. The Director General of Agricultural Control emphasized the role of control in protecting national products from illegal goods that threaten farmers and consumers, and in ensuring product quality and safety through permits and inspections. The meeting presented and discussed the agricultural inspection guide and new procedures to ease product transportation for farmers and traders while maintaining standards. This initiative is part of the Ministry's efforts to enhance agricultural protection and secure access for Palestinian produce, while addressing restrictions impacting trade.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, with FAO, held a workshop on carob cultivation and grafting under the "Climate-Smart Carob Graft...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, with FAO, held a workshop on carob cultivation and grafting under the "Climate-Smart Carob Grafting Intervention" (CSI) project, funded by the Multi-Donor Agricultural Programme (MAP II). Agricultural officials and FAO representatives highlighted the project's role in strengthening agricultural value chains and building technical skills for climate-smart agriculture. An agricultural expert provided practical training on modern carob grafting and seedling care for ministry nursery staff. The project aims to graft 15,000 seedlings and plant 10,000 more, expecting to increase carob production to 25 kg/tree in five years, boosting farmer income and food security. This training supports the Ministry's strategy for sustainable agriculture and building capacity to address climate change and improve rural livelihoods.

records.title: During a visit to the governorate of Kef on Wednesday, the Minister of State Property and Land Affairs handed over 24 contracts for the a...
records.description: During a visit to the governorate of Kef on Wednesday, the Minister of State Property and Land Affairs handed over 24 contracts for the acquisition of land for public infrastructure projects like roads and dams. Simultaneously, 12 contracts for the exploitation of state lands were given to young farmers, along with 10 decisions making state lands available to public companies for their projects in various delegations within the region. These projects are expected to boost job creation and accelerate investment. Additionally, the Minister emphasized the need to expedite the sorting of files to regularize the situation of 36 agricultural plots operated by unemployed higher education graduates.
records.institution: Ministry of State Domains and Land Affairs

records.title: During an award ceremony, the “International Consortium for Red Palm Weevil Control” was launched.
records.description: During an award ceremony, the “International Consortium for Red Palm Weevil Control” was launched. This initiative is a partnership between the International Affairs Office (IAO) at the Presidential Court, the Gates Foundation, the International Centre for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA), the Award’s General Secretariat, and various national, regional, and international organizations. The Consortium aims to address the growing global challenge of the Red Palm Weevil, building on a commitment to agricultural innovation. Founding institutions, including the IAO, ICARDA, and the Khalifa International Award, were represented at the launch. The Consortium is funded and overseen by the IAO and the Gates Foundation, in collaboration with the Khalifa International Award, ICARDA, United Arab Emirates University, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, and the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA). The initiative will test and refine technologies in the UAE for controlling the pest and then scale and deploy them in affected low and middle-income countries, focusing on bio-based innovations (led by ICIPE), biotechnological innovations (led by IITA), digital innovations & AI (led by ICRISAT), Good Agricultural Practices (led by ICBA), and policy and global access (led by ICARDA). The UAE, through this Consortium, aims to be a science-driven partner supporting vulnerable agricultural communities globally.
records.institution: Khalifa International Award for Date Palm and Agricultural Innovation

records.title: Tadweer Group has signed an agreement with China’s SFECO Group to explore developing a manufacturing facility in Abu Dhabi that will conv...
records.description: Tadweer Group has signed an agreement with China’s SFECO Group to explore developing a manufacturing facility in Abu Dhabi that will convert industrial solid waste into green building materials. This collaboration supports Tadweer Group’s commitment to unlocking the value of waste and fostering circular economy practices in line with Abu Dhabi’s wider sustainability objectives, with the potential facility utilizing SFECO’s mineralisation and low-carbon cement technologies to transform industrial waste into sustainable construction materials for the local market. The Managing Director and CEO of Tadweer Group commented that this agreement reflects their ongoing strategy to forge international partnerships that bring innovative, scalable waste-to-value solutions to the UAE, supporting their ambition to lead in sustainable industrial waste management and contribute to the nation’s green growth. A joint working committee will be formed to assess the project’s viability and shape future collaboration, with the intention of progressing towards a definitive agreement subject to feasibility outcomes, as this partnership forms part of Tadweer Group’s broader mission to advance integrated waste management through strategic investments and technology transfer, supporting the UAE’s journey towards net zero and a more circular economy.

records.title: A workshop on the Agricultural Expansion Program was held in Marib province, organized by the local agriculture sector.
records.description: A workshop on the Agricultural Expansion Program was held in Marib province, organized by the local agriculture sector. The workshop aimed to provide agricultural sector officials in the directorates, members of the Executive Unit for Financing Agricultural Projects, Initiatives, and program supporters in the province with skills and expertise to implement the project to expand the cultivation of staple crops. A representative of the Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing Unit in the province highlighted the need to benefit from the outcomes of the workshop and apply them on the ground to achieve the desired goals. The workshop saw interaction from the participants and included technical explanations by the Ministry's agricultural expansion project engineer about the mechanisms for entering data through the electronic application and building a comprehensive database for the province in the agricultural field.
records.institution: The Agriculture Sector in Marib Province

records.title: Egypt is actively seeking $6.5 billion in new Kuwaiti investments by the end of 2026, with a significant $4 billion targeted within 2025,...
records.description: Egypt is actively seeking $6.5 billion in new Kuwaiti investments by the end of 2026, with a significant $4 billion targeted within 2025, as part of a broader strategy involving high-level government engagement, including the President's visit to Kuwait to enhance economic cooperation. This drive aims to attract Kuwaiti capital across diverse sectors such as automotive, tourism, real estate, pharmaceuticals, renewable energy, logistics, infrastructure, agriculture, banking, telecommunications, petrochemicals, food production, and transportation, with Egypt offering new incentives, particularly in industrial localization and tourism, to facilitate these investments. This effort underscores Egypt's aim to strengthen its position as an attractive investment destination for Kuwait, which already ranks as a significant foreign investor in the country.

records.title: The Chairman of the General Authority for the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) laid the foundation stone of a $500 million chlor-alkali...
records.description: The Chairman of the General Authority for the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) laid the foundation stone of a $500 million chlor-alkali plant by China’s Befar Group in the Sokhna Industrial Zone. The green chemical facility, the first of its kind in Egypt and globally, will be developed in two phases on 400,000 square meters within the TEDA-Egypt industrial area. The first phase, covering 200,000 square meters and costing $300 million, is expected to be completed within 18 months. It will be powered by clean energy and will provide about 800 jobs. The project will also contribute to localizing strategic industries and feed into complementary sectors, particularly in mineral extraction from seawater and bromine production.
records.institution: The General Authority for the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone)

records.title: The Egyptian government will direct EGP 17.5 billion in public investments toward agriculture and irrigation projects under the fiscal ye...
records.description: The Egyptian government will direct EGP 17.5 billion in public investments toward agriculture and irrigation projects under the fiscal year development plan, which also targets $5 billion in agricultural exports, according to the Minister of Planning and Economic Development, and International Cooperation. Presenting the plan to the House of Representatives, the Minister said the agriculture and irrigation sectors remain a priority in the real economy reforms outlined in the government’s work program. The plan will continue expanding agricultural reclamation projects in areas such as Toshka, North and Central Sinai, and the New Delta. It also aims to raise crop productivity per feddan by 5% to 10% through the development of high-yield, early-maturing, and water-efficient crops, as well as modernizing irrigation systems, aiming for 10% modern field irrigation systems. Plans also involve expanding greenhouse agriculture, reducing agricultural losses, strengthening the agricultural extension system, broadening the contract farming system, diversifying agricultural import sources, increasing wheat storage capacity, surpassing 21 million cultivated feddans with specific targets for key crops, completing eighteen agricultural clusters in North and South Sinai, and expanding the farmer’s card system to cover 80% of holdings.

records.title: Lebanon's Minister of Agriculture met with delegations from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and CABI In...
records.description: Lebanon's Minister of Agriculture met with delegations from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and CABI International to discuss strengthening cooperation for the development of the agricultural sector and promoting sustainable biological treatments for pest management. Discussions with FAO centered on advancing agricultural programs and implementing a comprehensive development strategy for the sector. The Minister emphasized Lebanon's agricultural potential, and the FAO affirmed its commitment to supporting Lebanese farmers. Separately, discussions with CABI focused on Lebanon joining the CABI BioProtection Portal to encourage the adoption of natural pest control solutions. The Minister stressed the importance of regulating biopesticides and partnering with CABI to enhance the quality and safety of Lebanese agricultural products.

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture has issued a warning about the heightened risk of Foot and Mouth Disease entering Lebanon due to con...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture has issued a warning about the heightened risk of Foot and Mouth Disease entering Lebanon due to concerning epidemiological trends and new, unusual virus strains in neighboring countries. Citing border interactions and shared animal activity, the ministry urges all livestock breeders to strictly adhere to preventative measures to safeguard their animals and prevent a nationwide outbreak. Recommended actions include bolstering farm biosecurity through controlled access and regular disinfection, preventing animal commingling, especially in border regions, and ensuring livestock vaccination with ministry-approved vaccines at the owners' expense (twice yearly for cows, annually for sheep). The ministry stressed the significant economic repercussions of Foot and Mouth Disease, including reduced productivity, increased animal deaths, and potential trade limitations. Emphasizing that prevention is a collective responsibility, the ministry calls for strong collaboration between farmers and official authorities to protect the nation's food security and animal resources. Further details and guidance are available through the ministry's agricultural centers and website.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture – Akkar Agriculture Department organized a field tour on apiary management and beekeeping in Akkar, as part o...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture – Akkar Agriculture Department organized a field tour on apiary management and beekeeping in Akkar, as part of its agricultural guidance plan to support the agricultural sector and enhance farmers' efficiency. Specialized technical teams conducted periodic inspections of beehives in the region, assessing colony strength, queen activity, brood quality, food stocks, and disease/parasite presence, adhering to health monitoring standards. A natural bee swarm was successfully captured near an apiary, an important step for increasing colonies and production. This tour supports beekeepers, particularly those in a project funded by the Government of Canada aimed at enhancing the resilience of smallholder farmers affected by economic crises and the pandemic. The Ministry affirms that these field activities are essential for improving agricultural and livestock production quality, especially in the bee and honey sector, which is vital for food security, environmental balance, and rural income in Lebanon.

records.title: The Libyan United Beverage Bottling Company (LUBBC) is enhancing its manufacturing capabilities through an expanded partnership with a Sw...
records.description: The Libyan United Beverage Bottling Company (LUBBC) is enhancing its manufacturing capabilities through an expanded partnership with a Swiss packaging specialist, adding four new aseptic carton filling lines to its existing two lines used for its Safi beverage range. This expansion aims to meet growing demand for safely packaged non-carbonated soft drinks and liquid dairy products in Libya and improve LUBBC's competitiveness domestically and internationally. LUBBC's CEO expressed pride in the partnership, highlighting the specialist's role in ensuring access to safe beverages, while the specialist's Libya Country Manager noted the move as a key step in expanding their regional market position. This announcement aligns with the specialist's broader sustainability efforts in the region, including a recent collaboration in Egypt to establish a full-cycle recycling system for used beverage cartons, involving several organizations.
records.institution: e Libyan United Beverage Bottling Company (LUBBC)

records.title: Mauritania and the Khalifa International Award for Date Palm and Agricultural Innovation have signed an agreement in Abu Dhabi to organiz...
records.description: Mauritania and the Khalifa International Award for Date Palm and Agricultural Innovation have signed an agreement in Abu Dhabi to organize the fourth International Mauritanian Date Festival in Kiffa, Assaba Province. The memorandum of understanding was signed by the Secretary-General of Mauritania's Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty and the Secretary-General of the Khalifa International Award, during the award's closing ceremony overseen by the UAE's Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence. Attended by officials from both sides, this agreement underscores the ongoing cooperation between Mauritania and the UAE to support and develop Mauritania's date sector, enhance its local and international presence, and foster investment and innovation in sustainable agriculture and the rural economy through this annual festival showcasing oases products.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty

records.title: A bilateral agreement has resulted in Moroccan watermelon being grown locally in Mauritania, significantly impacting the local market.
records.description: A bilateral agreement has resulted in Moroccan watermelon being grown locally in Mauritania, significantly impacting the local market. This production has led to a substantial price reduction, creating enthusiasm among traders and consumers due to lower logistics costs and the removal of customs duties. Wholesalers from both countries have observed improved profitability and reduced prices, while consumers enjoy more affordable watermelon without compromising quality. Small traders also benefit from increased profit margins. This cross-border production experiment demonstrates the positive economic impact of such agreements and establishes a sustainable South-South cooperation model for agricultural food sovereignty.

records.title: Cooperative M’Brouka, a long-established Moroccan citrus exporter, is strategically targeting Southeast Asia with a trade mission to Sing...
records.description: Cooperative M’Brouka, a long-established Moroccan citrus exporter, is strategically targeting Southeast Asia with a trade mission to Singapore and Malaysia, supported by the FAO and EBRD. Leveraging nearly six decades of experience in the Souss-Massa region, known for its ideal citrus-growing conditions, M’Brouka aims to strengthen ties with importers and showcase its high-quality Moroccan citrus, particularly its popular mandarins, which have already seen positive reception in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur due to their taste, size, and shelf life. Having already navigated regulatory processes and established delivery partnerships, M’Brouka is well-positioned to build on the increasing traction of Moroccan citrus in the ASEAN region, while concurrently, Morocco's watermelon sector anticipates a promising season with improved yields and quality after overcoming previous challenges of drought and disease.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Omani government, through its state-owned energy group OQ, has announced an agreement to construct the world's first commercial-scale...
records.description: The Omani government, through its state-owned energy group OQ, has announced an agreement to construct the world's first commercial-scale liquid hydrogen corridor connecting Oman to the Netherlands and Germany. The government's green hydrogen entity, Hydrom, will manage the upstream production in line with national targets and integrate the project into Oman's hydrogen infrastructure. OQ will be responsible for developing the hydrogen plant and associated storage and export facilities at the Port of Duqm. The corridor will facilitate the export of compliant liquid hydrogen from Duqm to the Port of Amsterdam and key logistics hubs in Germany. ECOLOG, based in the UAE, will handle the shipping using specialized vessels. On the European end, import terminals will be established in the Port of Amsterdam for re-gasification and distribution to industrial users in the Netherlands and Germany via various transportation methods.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its directorate in Salfit Governorate, distributed 790 enlarged olive seedlings to farmers in Kafr a...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its directorate in Salfit Governorate, distributed 790 enlarged olive seedlings to farmers in Kafr ad-Dik and Deir Istiya under the Greening Palestine project, an initiative designed to bolster farmers' resilience, improve their income, and support the broader agricultural sector. This distribution, targeting families identified as most affected by difficult conditions and recognizing the economic, heritage, and environmental significance of olive trees, reflects the directorate's commitment to increasing green areas and strengthening Palestinian farmers' resilience, aligning with the Ministry's efforts to achieve sustainable development in agriculture and enhance food security and environmental sustainability in Palestine through the Greening Palestine project.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Bethlehem Governorate Agriculture Directorate and in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture O...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Bethlehem Governorate Agriculture Directorate and in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), distributed 300 shelters to 300 livestock farmers in several villages and rural communities within the governorate. This development activity, part of the Sustainable Production Inputs Support Program, aims to improve environmental infrastructure on sheep farms, protect livestock from harsh weather, and enhance farmers' productivity and economic stability. The Director General of the Bethlehem Governorate Agriculture Directorate highlighted that this initiative is part of strategic interventions to enhance the resilience of rural and Bedouin communities, emphasizing the importance of partnerships with international organizations like the FAO in implementing development projects that support food security and sustainable agricultural development, representing a successful collaboration between government institutions and international organizations to support the Palestinian agricultural sector and provide sustainable solutions for farmers facing current economic and environmental challenges.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the Jerusalem YMCA, distributed fencing to environmental parks in the Abu al...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the Jerusalem YMCA, distributed fencing to environmental parks in the Abu al-Arqan area, south of Hebron, to support sustainable agriculture and empower marginalized Palestinian communities. Supervised by representatives from the South Hebron Agriculture Directorate and the YMCA, the distribution benefited ten women in the Environmental Gardens Project, as part of a broader initiative aimed at improving livelihoods and empowering rural women through sustainable agricultural projects, with remaining supplies to be distributed after fence installation to further empower women and achieve food security in the region.

records.title: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia actively safeguards its environment through national initiatives and policies to preserve natural resources,...
records.description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia actively safeguards its environment through national initiatives and policies to preserve natural resources, foster sustainability, and increase environmental awareness. This commitment is highlighted by Environment Week, a Kingdom-wide event, which underscores the nation's dedication to conservation and public awareness, aligning with its comprehensive vision for sustainable development. Environment Week is an annual national event through which the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture aims to cultivate community environmental awareness and stimulate broad participation from all segments of society—governmental, private, and non-profit entities—to protect the environment and achieve sustainable development. This year's program includes tree-planting and clean-up campaigns, environmental exhibitions, educational workshops, and volunteer initiatives held across the Kingdom. These events reflect a shared commitment to environmental protection and an enhanced quality of life.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: A day of BtoB meetings in Tunis brought together Tunisian packaged olive oil producers and European buyers to foster strategic partnershi...
records.description: A day of BtoB meetings in Tunis brought together Tunisian packaged olive oil producers and European buyers to foster strategic partnerships and business development. This meeting is part of the Competitiveness and Export Support Program (PACE), under the Support for the Modernization of Tunisian Industry (AMIT) component, co-financed by the European Union (EU) and implemented by GIZ through the Qualitative Growth for Employment (CQE) project. The event facilitated direct exchange between selected Tunisian producers and major European players, allowing Tunisian companies to showcase their diverse, high-quality olive oils and adherence to quality standards. The initiative aims to strengthen existing commercial ties and create new export opportunities for authentic, certified Tunisian olive oil in European markets. The CQE project, mandated by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Industry, Mines and Energy, supports Tunisian companies' internationalization, with a focus on strategic sectors like packaged olive oil, to promote local expertise and ensure sustainable access to European markets.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Mines and Energy

records.title: A small Cabinet meeting convened to finalize preparations for Tunisia's first national agricultural census.
records.description: A small Cabinet meeting convened to finalize preparations for Tunisia's first national agricultural census. The meeting emphasized the importance of this national project as a comprehensive statistical operation in agriculture, carried out for the first time in Tunisia. The results will provide a georeferenced digital database of all farms down to the smallest territorial unit. The census will enable the development of sectoral strategies based on scientific evidence and improve the management of development programs. This will contribute to stimulating and directing investment, promoting small and medium-sized enterprises, and further valorizing and rationalizing the agricultural real estate stock as a lever for economic development. It will also contribute to the development of the statistical program of the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries and promote the Ministry's strategy for the digitalization of the agricultural sector.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: Tunisia is embarking on a path towards smarter and more sustainable agriculture through a strategic partnership with South Korea.
records.description: Tunisia is embarking on a path towards smarter and more sustainable agriculture through a strategic partnership with South Korea. An agency announced a $13.5 million grant to support the modernization of Tunisia's agricultural sector over a five-year project. This initiative, to be implemented with the Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources and the State Lands Office (OTD), will focus on optimizing irrigation, improving seeds, and integrating advanced technologies for more efficient farm management, with priority given to large-scale cereal crops and olive plantations in several governorates. The project aims to increase productivity while mitigating climate-related risks through pilot sites and farmer training. At a forum, representatives from both sides emphasized the importance of this cooperation, with smart agriculture being a key focus of support. This project signifies a crucial step in Tunisia's agricultural modernization strategy, potentially leading to further investment in the agrifood and water sectors and establishing a more resilient, sustainable, and profitable future for Tunisian agriculture.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources

records.title: Tunisian date export revenues for the first six months of the current season reached 640.8 million dinars, a 5% decrease compared to the...
records.description: Tunisian date export revenues for the first six months of the current season reached 640.8 million dinars, a 5% decrease compared to the corresponding period of the previous season, according to data from ONAGRI. The average price during this time was 6.40 D/kg, with "DEGLET ENNOUR" averaging 7 D/kg. The total quantity of dates exported was 100.1 thousand tonnes, a 6.6% drop from the previous season, with "DEGLET ENNOUR" making up the majority (85.9%). The European Union was the top destination (39.7%), followed by Africa (27.5%) and Asia (22.4%), with Morocco being the leading single importer (21.8%). Organic date exports saw a larger decline, falling by 11.5% in quantity and 30.5% in revenue, representing a small share of total exports (4.4%) and an average price of 9.33 D/kg. Germany was the primary destination for organic dates (31%).

records.title: The "International Consortium for Red Palm Weevil Control" has been launched through a partnership between the International Affairs Offi...
records.description: The "International Consortium for Red Palm Weevil Control" has been launched through a partnership between the International Affairs Office (IAO) at the Presidential Court and the Gates Foundation, with collaboration from ICARDA, the Khalifa International Award, and other organizations. This initiative, following a UAE-Gates Foundation commitment to agricultural innovation, aims to unite global efforts against a significant agricultural challenge. Funded and overseen by the IAO and the Gates Foundation, partners include the Khalifa International Award, ICARDA, UAE University, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, and ICBA. Officials emphasized the Consortium's potential for global impact through science and collaboration. The initiative aims to protect the date palm and develop sustainable solutions for communities.

records.title: A meeting in Sana'a province, chaired by the governor, focused on establishing the implementation mechanism for a project aimed at signif...
records.description: A meeting in Sana'a province, chaired by the governor, focused on establishing the implementation mechanism for a project aimed at significantly expanding tree planting of Sidr seedlings to enhance vegetation cover, increase green spaces, provide a natural food source for bees and honey production, support biodiversity, protect agricultural soil from erosion, combat desertification, and contribute to environmental preservation. The discussed mechanism included seedling distribution, planting, monitoring, evaluation, and target areas, involving the governor's undersecretaries, directors of various provincial units and funds, district directors, and heads of cooperative development sector associations, with a key outcome being further meetings with local officials and association heads for effective implementation and the formation of committees for field visits to engage communities and establish local teams, as the governor emphasized the crucial role of district and sector associations and the resilience of Sidr trees, urging community cooperation for the project's multiple benefits.

records.title: The Bahrain Smart Cities Summit 2025, themed "Building the Future: Smart Cities, Sustainable Growth," was inaugurated by the Deputy Prime...
records.description: The Bahrain Smart Cities Summit 2025, themed "Building the Future: Smart Cities, Sustainable Growth," was inaugurated by the Deputy Prime Minister, focusing on Bahrain's dedication to developing cities with advanced infrastructure and sustainable urban environments. Organized by the Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture, the summit brought together public and private sector representatives and experts to discuss future-oriented city development, emphasizing sustainability, innovation, and community participation. The Deputy Prime Minister highlighted the importance of public-private collaboration in achieving these goals. The Minister of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture underscored Bahrain's commitment to integrating technological innovation with human and social dimensions in urban planning, noting the Kingdom's improved ranking on the IMD Smart City Index 2024. The event also included the Bahrain Smart Cities Awards 2025, recognizing outstanding projects in sustainable smart city development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture

records.title: Egyptian researchers have discovered a sustainable method to purify Nile River water using discarded eggshells, a common waste product.
records.description: Egyptian researchers have discovered a sustainable method to purify Nile River water using discarded eggshells, a common waste product. Published in BMC Research Notes, the study demonstrates that processed eggshells effectively remove heavy metals like lead, cadmium, and iron, as well as harmful bacteria such as E. coli, from raw Nile water. This innovation is crucial for Egypt, which faces increasing water scarcity and pollution. Researchers from Ain Shams University found that eggshells, rich in calcium carbonate, act as a natural, low-cost bioadsorbent. The eggshells significantly reduced heavy metal concentrations and eliminated E. coli within 24 hours. The process, requiring minimal treatment and no hazardous chemicals, is particularly beneficial for rural and low-income communities. While further research is needed for large-scale implementation, this discovery offers a promising, environmentally friendly approach to water purification, repurposing agricultural waste to address a critical environmental challenge.
records.institution: The Faculty of Agriculture at Ain Shams University

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture inaugurated the 16th Agricultural Week at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, an event focused on machiner...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture inaugurated the 16th Agricultural Week at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, an event focused on machinery, agricultural and animal production, food industries, and packaging. Under the Prime Minister's patronage, the Minister highlighted achievements in serving the agricultural sector and emphasized ongoing efforts to expand green spaces, diversify products, and introduce modern agricultural technologies to address climate change. The opening ceremony was attended by various officials, including the Prime Minister's Advisor, parliamentary agriculture committee members, diplomatic missions, and representatives from the FAO.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Karbala Agriculture Directorate, conducted a workshop focused on "Promoting Sustai...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Karbala Agriculture Directorate, conducted a workshop focused on "Promoting Sustainable Development in the Agricultural and Environmental Sectors." This workshop, organized by the Ministry's Planning and Follow-up Department - Environment Division, aimed to introduce sustainable development goals and their achievement within the agricultural and environmental sectors. Participants included Agriculture Directorate staff and specialists. The event addressed the Ministry's plans to expand agricultural land, ensure sustainable food security, combat climate change, reduce waste and desertification, and promote environmental sustainability. The workshop highlighted key sustainable agricultural practices, including modern irrigation technologies, solar energy use, and the adoption of organic fertilizers, all under the guidance of the Minister of Agriculture.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Karbala Agriculture Directorate

records.title: The Ministers of Agriculture and Youth Empowerment visited a pilot project in Arkeez and Rosso focused on creating agricultural jobs for...
records.description: The Ministers of Agriculture and Youth Empowerment visited a pilot project in Arkeez and Rosso focused on creating agricultural jobs for youth. The project, covering 612 hectares for rice cultivation, aims to generate 279 direct jobs for young graduates and local workers, enhancing food security and providing sustainable employment. The ministers emphasized the project's importance for job creation and youth empowerment in the agricultural sector, highlighting it as a model for sustainable development. They urged beneficiaries to seize the opportunities and reaffirmed governmental support, noting the transparent selection process and alignment with national agricultural development goals. The project has achieved near-full land utilization and aims to integrate youth into the economic cycle, promoting agricultural self-sufficiency.

records.title: Morocco has achieved a new record in carrot exports for the fifth consecutive year, shipping 69,000 tons in 2024 and generating $18.3 mil...
records.description: Morocco has achieved a new record in carrot exports for the fifth consecutive year, shipping 69,000 tons in 2024 and generating $18.3 million in revenue, a 35% increase from the previous year. The country has experienced consistent annual growth in carrot exports, averaging 27% over the past eight years, demonstrating a thriving sector. Moroccan producers have extended their export season, enhancing their market competitiveness. While West Africa remains the primary market, new markets in other African countries are emerging, expanding Morocco's export destinations. Despite this growth, European exports remain minimal. Morocco is now targeting Southeast Asia for further expansion, with a trade mission planned to facilitate access to these markets. Carrots have become one of Morocco's top three exported vegetables, reinforcing the country's position as a major fruit and vegetable exporter in Africa.

records.title: Recent rainfall in the Doukkala region, especially during February and March, has given sugar beet producers hope for better harvests aft...
records.description: Recent rainfall in the Doukkala region, especially during February and March, has given sugar beet producers hope for better harvests after years of drought. The rainfall has eased water supply issues for irrigation, benefiting the Sidi Bennour province and other areas. The Doukkala Regional Office for Agricultural Development (ORMVAD), along with beet producers and the sugar factory, has taken measures to adapt to the water deficit, including increasing the cultivated area by 28% and raising the beet price per ton. Producers are optimistic about this season's prospects due to the rainfall and production incentives. Beet cultivation is significant for farmers' income and animal feed, prompting plans to expand the cultivation area further. The crop is seen as contributing to the region's overall economic development.
records.institution: Doukkala Regional Office for Agricultural Development (ORMVAD)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, via the Tubas and Northern Jordan Valley Agriculture Directorate, distributed agricultural supplies to 11 fa...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, via the Tubas and Northern Jordan Valley Agriculture Directorate, distributed agricultural supplies to 11 farmers under the "Supporting the Resilience of Farmers in Area C of the Jordan Valley" project. This initiative, funded by the Mennonite International Foundation and implemented by the Applied Research Institute – Jerusalem (ARIJ) in collaboration with the Ministry, aims to bolster farmers' resilience by providing necessary agricultural inputs and enhancing their technical skills to address the difficulties in Area C.

records.title: ANDRITZ, A global technology firm has secured a major contract to build a high-capacity animal feed plant in Riyadh Province, aimed at bo...
records.description: ANDRITZ, A global technology firm has secured a major contract to build a high-capacity animal feed plant in Riyadh Province, aimed at boosting Saudi Arabia’s self-sufficiency in livestock feed production. The facility will produce 90 tons per hour—divided between poultry and ruminant feed—and is part of a broader strategy to improve feed quality and enhance integrated operations. The company will deliver a complete production line, including core machinery and services such as installation, commissioning, and after-sales support, with key components manufactured in Europe. This partnership follows a thorough evaluation process and aligns with national goals under Vision 2030 to strengthen food security. The project highlights the firm’s growing presence in the region and its commitment to sustainable, high-performance feed solutions.

records.title: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef) is prominently featured at the Rose and Aromatic Plants Global Forum,...
records.description: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef) is prominently featured at the Rose and Aromatic Plants Global Forum, showcasing its advancements in the rose and aromatic plant sector, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030's objectives of enhancing food security and rural development. The program's participation underscores its role in empowering farmers and promoting initiatives that have led to a significant increase in rose production, with ambitions to further elevate the Kingdom's standing in the global rose market.

records.title: A workshop introducing the Food Safety and Management System took place at the Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection to impr...
records.description: A workshop introducing the Food Safety and Management System took place at the Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection to improve food safety for all citizens across the entire food supply chain, from production to market. Discussions addressed the challenges and opportunities within the food industry and explored the potential implementation of the HACCP system to identify and manage biological, chemical, or physical hazards to food safety.
records.institution: The Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection

records.title: The Drinking Water Institution in Damascus and its countryside has announced a water rationing schedule for Damascus and its surrounding...
records.description: The Drinking Water Institution in Damascus and its countryside has announced a water rationing schedule for Damascus and its surrounding areas due to a significant decrease in rainfall, which has reduced the water supply from surface springs, the main water source for the region. This year's rainfall is less than 30% of previous years' levels. To prevent the depletion of existing spring water, the institution will implement a rationing program and has launched an awareness campaign, "Together we ensure the continuation of water," urging citizens to rationalize their consumption. The institution clarified that adjustments to the water supply program are necessary for its 1.2 million subscribers in Damascus and its countryside, considering the scarcity of water resources, declining rainfall, and increasing demand. Damascus and its Ghouta rely on the Fijeh and Barada springs, with the abundant and pure Fijeh spring being a key source.
records.institution: The Public Institution for Drinking Water in Damascus

records.title: Djerba has launched a pilot project, "Towards a Circular Model for the Treatment and Recovery of Waste and Materials," to revolutionize w...
records.description: Djerba has launched a pilot project, "Towards a Circular Model for the Treatment and Recovery of Waste and Materials," to revolutionize waste management in Tunisia. Led by the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) in partnership with the National Agency for Energy Management (ANME) and the National Waste Management Agency (ANGED), the three-year initiative aims to convert household organic waste into clean, renewable energy. Funded by the Government of Japan and supported by Italy, the project includes establishing sorting and recycling stations, developing biomethanization facilities, and implementing citizen awareness campaigns. This integrated approach seeks to create a resilient, job-creating, and environmentally friendly waste management model, with Djerba becoming a benchmark for sustainable recovery. The innovative model is already attracting interest for potential replication in other Tunisian cities, showcasing a pathway towards a circular economy and sustainable resource management.

records.title: Tunisian Agritech Week in Dakar aims to boost African agriculture through digital solutions, fostering collaboration between Tunisian and...
records.description: Tunisian Agritech Week in Dakar aims to boost African agriculture through digital solutions, fostering collaboration between Tunisian and Senegalese stakeholders. The event will showcase agricultural technologies, facilitate exchanges among entrepreneurs, farmers, and policymakers, and address climate change and resource optimization. The program includes lectures and workshops on farm digitalization, smart irrigation, and market access. Organized by STECIA International with Tunisian and Senegalese partners, it seeks to share best practices and develop scalable agricultural technology projects.
