This initiative, carried out by the South Hebron Agriculture Directorate, aims to enhance farmers' resilience and improve livestock production in rural areas through the Field Schools Support Program. The program focuses on developing farmers' skills in modern ruminant breeding techniques to improve production amidst challenging economic and environmental conditions. Representatives from the Agriculture Directorate highlighted the importance of this contribution in empowering farmers and enhancing veterinary and technical services, emphasizing the Ministry's partnership with international institutions to promote sustainable agricultural development in the southern regions. Farmers were selected based on specific criteria within the field school program to ensure effective equipment utilization.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, through the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, implemented the "Emergency Support for Vulnera...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, through the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, implemented the "Emergency Support for Vulnerable Female and Male Shepherds and Farmers" project throughout North Hebron. Supported and funded by the Canadian government and implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the project distributed essential agricultural inputs to 95 beneficiaries, receiving 106 rolls in total. This initiative aims to protect livestock, sustain and revitalize agricultural production, meet the urgent needs of vulnerable groups, enhance food security, and achieve sustainable agricultural production in the region amidst current challenges. The project highlights the Ministry's dedication to supporting vulnerable populations and bolstering agricultural productivity.

records.title: Al Baha, situated in the Sarawat Mountains at a high altitude, is a renowned natural destination for nature lovers and hikers due to its...
records.description: Al Baha, situated in the Sarawat Mountains at a high altitude, is a renowned natural destination for nature lovers and hikers due to its diverse terrain of deep valleys, towering mountains, and dense forests. The Director General of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture in Al-Baha highlighted a project focused on agricultural terraces in the region, which has benefited a total of 355 farms across preliminary and three subsequent phases. Al Baha's valleys, characterized by natural beauty, green mountains, and waterfalls, offer ideal environments for walking and hiking. Notable valleys include Al-Ahsabah Valley, Dhark Valley, Bida Valley with its water and pomegranate orchards, and Al Hamdah Valley known for its streams and waterfalls. Beyond natural landscapes, visitors can also explore traditional villages and archaeological sites, making Al Baha a prominent tourist destination in Saudi Arabia that blends adventure with cultural discovery.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) has signed its first development loan agreement with the Solomon Islands, pledging $10 million for a...
records.description: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) has signed its first development loan agreement with the Solomon Islands, pledging $10 million for a renewable energy project. This project will fund the construction of 35.5 megawatt solar power plants with hourly energy storage systems. The initiative aims to decrease the Solomon Islands' dependence on traditional energy sources, align with global sustainability goals, and support economic growth and environmental resilience. This agreement marks the start of development cooperation between the SFD and the Solomon Islands, underscoring the Fund’s increasing support for small island developing states facing developmental, economic, and environmental challenges. Since its establishment, the SFD has financed over 800 development projects in more than 100 countries, totaling over $21 billion, across sectors like health, education, transport, water, and energy, with the goal of improving living conditions, enhancing skills, and creating jobs worldwide.

records.title: Tunisian fruit exports faced difficulties in 2025, contributing to an overall drop in agricultural exports due to lower volumes of dates...
records.description: Tunisian fruit exports faced difficulties in 2025, contributing to an overall drop in agricultural exports due to lower volumes of dates and olive oil, alongside logistical issues and price competition. While citrus exports to Libya increased, declines in European markets necessitate diversification. Tunisia is seeking new markets in Africa, Asia, and North America, but rising production costs and the need for logistics upgrades remain challenges. Efforts to improve standards for demanding markets are also underway. Recovery hinges on market diversification and structural reforms.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt and France have signed a cooperation agreement for the development, financing, construction, and operation of a large-scale green h...
records.description: Egypt and France have signed a cooperation agreement for the development, financing, construction, and operation of a large-scale green hydrogen and ammonia production facility in Ras Shukheir. The agreement involves the Red Sea Ports Authority and the New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA) in partnership with the Green Fuel Alliance, consisting of France’s EDF Renewables and the Egyptian-Emirati firm Zero Waste. This agreement aims to support Egypt's goal of localizing the green hydrogen industry, attracting foreign investment, and becoming a regional energy hub. The facility is planned to produce 1 million tons of green ammonia annually in three phases, starting in 2029, for clean ship fuel and export. The project, led entirely by the private sector, will not burden the state financially or require state infrastructure or electricity transmission. The first phase involves a €2 billion investment to produce 300,000 tons of green ammonia annually, with a total investment of €7 billion across all phases, fully financed by the project company. The allocated land includes areas for renewable energy production and the plant itself, along with a desalination unit and electricity transmission corridor. The project company will also build and fund a loading dock at the Red Sea Ports Authority. The state will generate revenue through various fees and taxes in foreign currency, and the project is expected to create thousands of jobs, with a focus on training and achieving a high percentage of local workforce participation.

records.title: A meeting was held to discuss smart digital solutions for managing Iraq's water systems.
records.description: A meeting was held to discuss smart digital solutions for managing Iraq's water systems. The session included presentations on advanced technologies like smart water meters that can read, record, and transmit data. Participants explored the use of these tools for monitoring urban water distribution, considering their advantages and disadvantages. The meeting ended with suggestions to test these technologies through pilot projects in Baghdad and other provinces to improve national water resource efficiency.

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has issued a ban on the import and circulation of 37 specific agricultural products within local market...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has issued a ban on the import and circulation of 37 specific agricultural products within local markets, acting on the directives of the Minister of Agriculture. Simultaneously, the Ministry has authorized the import of seven agricultural crops: tomatoes, potatoes, scallions, cauliflower, lettuce, turnips, and sugar beets, and has instructed relevant authorities to take legal action against any unauthorized entry of the banned products. The comprehensive list of prohibited items includes various seeds, animals, animal products, plants, plant parts, soil, and specific fruits and vegetables, among other agricultural materials.

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has launched a free, nationwide spring campaign for 30 days starting in early April to combat hemorrhag...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has launched a free, nationwide spring campaign for 30 days starting in early April to combat hemorrhagic fever in all governorates except the Kurdistan Region. The campaign involves 246 veterinary teams spraying cows and buffalo, dipping sheep and goats, and spraying barns to eliminate ticks, the primary cause of the disease. The Veterinary Department has equipped veterinary hospitals with necessary supplies like Delta Methrin, dipping basins, sprinklers, and transportation for the teams to support and develop the country's livestock.

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture's Veterinary Department is continuing its field monitoring of slaughterhouse operations and the supply...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture's Veterinary Department is continuing its field monitoring of slaughterhouse operations and the supply of safe meat products to cooperative societies to ensure consumer safety. The Health Supervision Department for Slaughterhouses has initiated a campaign to monitor the Karkh slaughterhouse, ensuring beef and sheep meat are provided according to high health and veterinary standards. The slaughtering process involves direct veterinary supervision, full compliance with health requirements from pre-slaughter inspection to refrigerated transport and official stamping. Processed meat is provided with a veterinary health certificate, and guidance is given on common diseases and adherence to proper veterinary health regulations.

records.title: To boost local honey production and support beekeepers, the Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture's Crop Protection Department, through its Bee D...
records.description: To boost local honey production and support beekeepers, the Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture's Crop Protection Department, through its Bee Division, conducted field monitoring of bee health and queen bee insemination in the Mansouriya and Al-Hadid apiaries in Diyala Governorate. Specialized teams monitored cell division and queen bee insemination, assessed the overall health of the bees, and checked for pests like the Varroa mite. Beekeepers also received field guidance on environmental prevention and control measures. This initiative is part of the Ministry's plan to increase technical and advisory support for beekeepers to ensure the sustainability of the beekeeping sector.

records.title: The Director of Agriculture in Ajloun Governorate reported the apprehension of an individual damaging forest trees, resulting in a 10,000...
records.description: The Director of Agriculture in Ajloun Governorate reported the apprehension of an individual damaging forest trees, resulting in a 10,000 dinar fine. The Ajloun Governor has been notified for further legal action. Forestry teams are continuing to monitor forests and address violations in cooperation with security agencies and regulatory bodies to protect national resources.
records.institution: The Department of Agriculture in Ajloun Governorate

records.title: A large seminar on the responsible use of agricultural pesticides was held in Mayrouba as part of the National Agricultural Extension Pro...
records.description: A large seminar on the responsible use of agricultural pesticides was held in Mayrouba as part of the National Agricultural Extension Program, with significant official and farmer attendance. The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture organized the event to promote sustainable farming. Speakers stressed the importance of official guidance for safe and high-quality production, particularly in apple regions, emphasizing that rational pesticide use is crucial for healthy crops that meet international standards for both local and export markets. Farmers were advised to obtain prescriptions from certified engineers, purchase from licensed stores, and strictly follow pesticide label instructions, especially regarding withholding periods. The dangers of unregistered pesticides were highlighted. Attendees agreed on the need for continued awareness seminars to advance clean and safe agriculture, balancing production with public and environmental health for sustainable food security.

records.title: Libya and Tunisia have agreed to increase cooperation in vocational training, with Tunisia providing expertise to meet Libya's labor mark...
records.description: Libya and Tunisia have agreed to increase cooperation in vocational training, with Tunisia providing expertise to meet Libya's labor market needs. A joint committee discussed expanding their existing agreement to include electronic links, trainer development, and transferring Tunisian skills to Libya, where a shortage of vocational training exists despite new centers. Libya seeks Tunisia's help to re-establish vocational training, addressing the lack of skills among university graduates for the growing private sector. Cooperation also involves Tunisia assisting with skilled worker recruitment and formalizing contracts for Tunisians in Libya, plus linking labor ministries for data exchange. New Libyan training areas like fisheries and aircraft maintenance will benefit from Tunisian trainers. Both countries aim to strengthen economic and social ties and improve employment.
records.institution: The Ministry of Labour and Rehabilitation

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Morocco intends to seek bids for a large power storage facility with a capacity of almost 1,600 megawatts (MW) as part of its long-term s...
records.description: Morocco intends to seek bids for a large power storage facility with a capacity of almost 1,600 megawatts (MW) as part of its long-term strategy to increase renewable energy integration into its national power grid, according to a newspaper report. This battery storage facility will be located in Northwest Morocco and will supply electricity to Kenitra and surrounding regions. The National Office for Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE) will issue the tender for the project, with a phased commissioning expected to begin in 2026. The contract will encompass design, operation, and long-term maintenance, and the facility will store power generated from Morocco's solar and wind energy plants.
records.institution: The National Office for Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE)

records.title: Morocco's significant agricultural sector, contributing 14% to GDP and employing 40% of the workforce, faces a major issue with post-harv...
records.description: Morocco's significant agricultural sector, contributing 14% to GDP and employing 40% of the workforce, faces a major issue with post-harvest losses of fruits and vegetables, impacting producers, markets, food security, farmer incomes, and the environment. These losses are due to insufficient storage infrastructure like cold rooms in rural areas and the vulnerability of produce to climatic variations and unrefrigerated transport. Climate constraints, including droughts and erratic rainfall, exacerbate the problem, particularly for small farmers lacking resources for modern conservation. Key export sectors like tomatoes, citrus fruits, melons, and watermelons can see losses up to 30% for some perishable fruits, representing economic and resource waste. To address this, Morocco is exploring solutions like community cold rooms, improved refrigerated transport, natural and biodegradable coatings, digital technologies with smart sensors, and farmer training on best practices. Managing post-harvest losses is crucial for the Moroccan economy by increasing export value, strengthening agricultural competitiveness, and attracting investment, as well as for environmental sustainability by reducing unnecessary resource consumption. Addressing this challenge requires collaboration between public authorities, cooperatives, agricultural associations, and consumers promoting local products.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, guided by its Minister, conducted two training courses on plum and alternative feed production as part of a...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, guided by its Minister, conducted two training courses on plum and alternative feed production as part of a sustainable development project funded by Italian Cooperation and implemented with CIHEAM-Bari. Held in Hebron and the Jericho/Jordan Valley, these workshops aimed to enhance farmers' skills, improve local production quality, and promote sustainable agriculture. The plum course targeted almond sector farmers, while the feed production course was for livestock farmers. Led by ministry directors and specialists, these initiatives seek to provide farmers with modern agricultural knowledge to improve crop quality, increase production, enhance food security, and support the long-term sustainability of Palestinian agriculture.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, distributed agricultural equipment, including sprinklers a...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, distributed agricultural equipment, including sprinklers and livestock drinkers, to 15 farmers. This initiative is part of the Field Schools Project - Agricultural Value Chain Development Project, implemented in partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The distribution aims to enhance agricultural practices and improve the efficiency of livestock farming in northern Hebron, thereby increasing productivity and product quality. This activity is part of a broader plan to develop value chains and promote field extension, empowering farmers with practical tools to overcome challenges and achieve agricultural sustainability.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture held a workshop to present results of soil classification studies in the northern and southern We...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture held a workshop to present results of soil classification studies in the northern and southern West Bank, attended by representatives from various national and international organizations. A high-ranking official from the Ministry emphasized the studies' importance for establishing a national soil classification system to improve sustainable agricultural resource management for Palestinian farmers. The research, funded externally and implemented by local groups, covered significant land areas and aims to create a database for better agricultural planning, land and water use, and crop selection, ultimately enhancing farmer productivity. The project also included training for agricultural engineers. Partner organizations praised the collaboration and pledged continued support. The Director General of a local research center highlighted the crucial partnership with the Ministry and the goal of expanding the project nationwide. This initiative is vital as Palestine currently lacks a national soil classification system.

records.title: To support livestock farmers, enhance productivity, achieve sustainable economic development, and address water scarcity, the Ministry of...
records.description: To support livestock farmers, enhance productivity, achieve sustainable economic development, and address water scarcity, the Ministry of Agriculture, through the South Jenin Agriculture Department, distributed water tanks to farmers in five villages and communities. This initiative is part of the "Enhancing Economic Growth through Developing Agricultural Value Chains in the West Bank" project, implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in cooperation with the Ministry of Agriculture and funded by the Canadian government. The handover event was attended by the Director of Agriculture in South Jenin, guidance staff, the FAO project representative, the beneficiary farmers, and local council and cooperative leaders.

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture is launching Saudi Environment Week with wide participation from various sectors and i...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture is launching Saudi Environment Week with wide participation from various sectors and individuals, emphasizing the Kingdom's dedication to environmental preservation and sustainable development, aligning with the "Saudi Green Initiative" to improve quality of life and protect natural resources for future generations, aiming to raise environmental awareness, promote responsible practices, encourage community engagement, and foster a culture of sustainability by educating the public and mobilizing collective efforts for environmental stewardship and the protection of natural ecosystems.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) has initiated a technology and agricultural practice...
records.description: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah) has initiated a technology and agricultural practices transfer program in Al-Kharj Governorate to promote Azolla cultivation as a supplementary protein source for poultry and livestock feed. The program provides farmers with hands-on training in modern agricultural techniques, including pond construction, fertilization, and harvesting, along with educational materials on crop care and effective usage. This initiative demonstrates Estidamah's role in transferring knowledge and research outcomes to support farmers and enhance their technical skills, aligning with agricultural sector goals and improving local production efficiency through sustainable technologies and practices.
records.institution: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah)

records.title: Agents from the regional directorate of the National Authority for Food Safety (INSSPA) in Mahdia, along with law enforcement, destroyed...
records.description: Agents from the regional directorate of the National Authority for Food Safety (INSSPA) in Mahdia, along with law enforcement, destroyed a large amount of expired frozen poultry stored in an illegal cold room in El Jem, as the poultry was improperly packaged and posed a health risk. The El Jem municipal police alerted INSSPA after being informed of unfit poultry being sold, leading to the destruction of the goods following judicial authorization. INSSPA's regional management in Mahdia is pursuing legal action against the responsible party in coordination with security services, and the public is reminded of a hotline to report food safety violations.
records.institution: The National Authority for Food Safety (INSSPA)

records.title: Despite a decrease in the land used for growing strawberries in the Nabeul region, the harvest is showing positive signs.
records.description: Despite a decrease in the land used for growing strawberries in the Nabeul region, the harvest is showing positive signs. This reduction in area is largely attributed to climate change and agricultural policies focused on reducing water usage for irrigation. The Cap Bon area is a key region for this crop, with Korba being the main production hub, known for its exported varieties and advanced greenhouse farming methods, alongside other actively involved neighboring areas. Despite the smaller growing area, production levels remain strong, with a significant average yield per hectare. Harvesting starts in late winter and continues through spring, providing a valuable market presence when few other fruits are available. Retail prices for strawberries vary in major cities, while wholesale prices fluctuate based on quality and time of sale. Prices in the main production area are influenced by supply and demand. However, the costs of production are substantial, mainly due to expenses related to greenhouses, irrigation systems, and quality plants, with potential increases for specific farming methods. As a result, profit margins for producers are generally low, though efficient producers with good resource management and export access can achieve slightly better returns. The strawberry sector also provides important employment opportunities for agricultural workers and vendors.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The Soil Matters project has been launched in Tunis to advance agroecological innovations in partnership with the private sector.
records.description: The Soil Matters project has been launched in Tunis to advance agroecological innovations in partnership with the private sector. Funded by a German ministry, the multi-year initiative will be implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries and a German cooperation agency as part of a larger global program. Building on the successes of a previous project focused on soil restoration and sustainable agriculture, Soil Matters will emphasize the private sector's crucial role in promoting environmentally friendly farming methods. The project aims to enhance the adoption of these practices by producers through an improved administrative and financial structure, the development of innovative solutions, and the creation of collaborations for sustainable natural resource management. The new program will continue to support resilient and environmentally sound agriculture, fully integrating private companies as key drivers of change and addressing farmers' needs for soil improvement resources and market options. The prior project successfully rehabilitated a significant amount of agricultural land, improving its fertility and water retention, and resulted in substantial yield increases on treated areas.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Tunisia remains the top olive oil exporter outside the EU and anticipates a strong production season.
records.description: Tunisia remains the top olive oil exporter outside the EU and anticipates a strong production season. The country achieved first place at an international olive oil competition in Abu Dhabi, securing numerous gold medals for quality and healthy oil. This success is attributed to the government's initiatives promoting high-quality olive oil through investment, marketing, and sustainable practices, aiming for bottled oil exports and access to valuable markets. Olive oil export revenue saw an increase due to a rise in export volume, despite a price decrease, with packaged olive oil exports also showing growth.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has finished installing solar energy systems on 22 of its buildings and facilities to increas...
records.description: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has finished installing solar energy systems on 22 of its buildings and facilities to increase renewable energy use and lessen environmental impact. This project reflects RTA’s dedication to environmental sustainability and clean energy, aligning with its Zero-Emissions Strategy 2050, the Dubai Clean Energy Strategy 2050, and the Dubai Integrated Energy Strategy 2030. A Director at RTA stated that the project supports Dubai’s vision for sustainable development and is expected to generate about 32 million kilowatt-hours annually, reducing carbon dioxide emissions by around 10,000 tonnes each year. Solar panels were installed at 16 RTA facilities, including bus depots, bus stations, maintenance workshops, and metro depots. RTA is committed to following the standards of Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) for solar panel distribution and installation, ensuring they suit each facility’s specific conditions. Energy production is monitored using DEWA’s Shams Dubai Calculator for real-time efficiency tracking.

records.title: The Professional Exhibition of Agri-Food Production (Djazagro) is being held at the Palais des Expositions Pins Maritimes (Algiers) with...
records.description: The Professional Exhibition of Agri-Food Production (Djazagro) is being held at the Palais des Expositions Pins Maritimes (Algiers) with the participation of 650 national and international exhibitors. Co-organized by Comexposium and Promosalons Algérie, this event is expected to attract 23,000 visitors and will highlight significant advances in the agri-food sector, with a particular focus on packaging. The exhibition includes "Djaz'Pack," a dedicated space for packaging that emphasizes sustainable materials, and the "Djaz'Innov" competition, which recognizes promising innovations within the Algerian agri-food industry. Furthermore, the event will feature "The Agora of Experts," where specialists will discuss market trends, and an area dedicated to training provided by educational institutions. Considered a benchmark trade fair for the agri-food sector in Algeria and North Africa, Djazagro will also offer a comprehensive program of conferences, demonstrations, and networking opportunities.

records.title: Significant changes are impacting the Egyptian citrus industry this season, leading to a widespread halt in fresh citrus packing at most...
records.description: Significant changes are impacting the Egyptian citrus industry this season, leading to a widespread halt in fresh citrus packing at most facilities recently. The rise of orange juice concentrate factories in Egypt has created strong competition for oranges, reducing the supply available for fresh citrus exporters. According to a representative from TC Fruits, packers can no longer compete with the high prices demanded by farmers, who are now seeking over EGP 20 per kilo for Valencia oranges and lemons. Concentrate factories offer attractive prices and payment terms, including prepayment, and can handle large volumes, making them more appealing to growers. Exporters find these raw material costs unprofitable after accounting for processing and the portion of fruit unsuitable for export. This situation is disrupting the end of the orange season, with many packing houses shifting focus to other fruits like grapes. Only orange exporters with their own production can likely continue fresh citrus programs. This shift towards citrus processing over fresh export is seen as a lasting change in the industry, driven by better conditions offered by processing factories to growers, who prefer dealing with buyers that don't penalize smaller sizes or impose unfavorable payment terms. Processing also offers a longer shelf life, benefiting both large and small-scale operators, signaling a radical transformation in the Egyptian citrus industry.

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has made enhancing wheat production a top priority for Egypt's food security.
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has made enhancing wheat production a top priority for Egypt's food security. The Ministry is providing comprehensive support to wheat farmers through the Agricultural Research Centre and other relevant departments. This includes developing high-yielding and climate-resilient wheat varieties, providing subsidized approved seeds based on a varietal map, offering technical and advisory support through national campaigns and advisory fields, supplying modern agricultural and harvesting machinery, and funding a national campaign to combat weeds. In preparation for the wheat harvest season, the state has increased the procurement price to encourage delivery and ensure prompt payment, provided modern harvesting machinery nationwide, and initiated early wheat procurement. The Ministry has also intensified advisory activities for farmers on pre-harvest measures to minimize crop losses and ensure optimal grain maturity.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture, through its Modern Irrigation and Mechanization Technologies Project, has completed a database of mode...
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture, through its Modern Irrigation and Mechanization Technologies Project, has completed a database of modern irrigation systems implemented for farmers in the Wasit and Anbar governorates by both the Ministry and the private sector. The project team conducted site surveys of wheat farms in these governorates that were part of the winter agricultural plans for the (2023-2024) and (2024-2025) seasons. They are also preparing a report on the winter agricultural plan under these systems for both seasons, as well as the wheat yield achieved in the (2022-2023) and (2023-2024) seasons. This database creation is ongoing across all governorates except the Kurdistan Region to identify agricultural areas utilizing modern irrigation within the winter agricultural plan.

records.title: The Jordanian agricultural sector experienced substantial economic growth of nearly 7 per cent in the past year, contributing 6.9 per cen...
records.description: The Jordanian agricultural sector experienced substantial economic growth of nearly 7 per cent in the past year, contributing 6.9 per cent to the national economy in 2024 and driving an 8.4 per cent increase in GDP during the fourth quarter. This progress aligns with the Kingdom's Economic Modernisation Vision and sustainable agriculture plan, which aim to boost plant and livestock production. Agricultural exports also saw a significant rise, reaching over JD1.5 billion, a 39 per cent increase from the previous year, indicating growing global demand for Jordanian produce. While stakeholders acknowledge the positive momentum driven by farmers' efforts, they emphasize the ongoing challenges of high production costs, water scarcity, and the need for advanced technologies to ensure the sector's long-term sustainability and growth, requiring continued government support.

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and the Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon (SPNL) have signed a memorandum of understan...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and the Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon (SPNL) have signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen national efforts against poaching and wildlife trafficking, aligning with Lebanon's environmental commitments. This agreement aims to combine official institutional work with community initiatives for sustainable biodiversity management. The signing was attended by national and international environmental figures who emphasized the importance of CITES and the need for local legislation, awareness campaigns, and community involvement. The Anti-Poaching Unit (APU), a field initiative by SPNL and CABS, was highlighted for its success in reducing environmental violations. SPNL's Director General emphasized that the memorandum is a roadmap for implementing international environmental obligations and that SPNL will fund its provisions based on its long history of nature protection. The Minister of Agriculture stressed the Ministry's pivotal role in environmental protection, including forest management and hunting regulation, highlighting the socio-economic importance of fishing communities and the progress in establishing marine reserves.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture - Baalbek-Hermel Authority organized a scientific symposium on "Good Agricultural Practices for Olive Trees"...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture - Baalbek-Hermel Authority organized a scientific symposium on "Good Agricultural Practices for Olive Trees" as part of the official national extension program. The symposium, presented by an expert, was attended by mayors, municipality members, local leaders, olive growers, and agricultural professionals from the Ministry and the private sector. Participants highlighted the importance of providing farmers with current scientific agricultural information to improve olive and olive oil production and quality. They also emphasized that effective agricultural extension is crucial for supporting the agricultural sector and enhancing food security in Lebanon.

records.title: A group of Moroccan lawmakers has initiated the formation of a parliamentary fact-finding committee to scrutinize government support for...
records.description: A group of Moroccan lawmakers has initiated the formation of a parliamentary fact-finding committee to scrutinize government support for livestock imports and the broader livestock sector. This move follows public discussion regarding government support and exemptions for livestock importers since late 2022, including customs duty exemptions, state coverage of VAT on imports, and direct financial support for sheep imports during Eid Al Adha in 2023 and 2024, estimated to cost billions of dirhams. Three parliamentary groups are jointly calling for an inquiry into the decision-making process, the effectiveness and achieved impacts of these policies, the total financial cost to the state, the beneficiaries and their compliance with conditions, and concerns about transparency and equal opportunity, questioning whether the support truly served the public interest.
records.institution: The Moroccan Parliament, The Haraki Group

records.title: As Morocco begins its melon production season, farmers in key areas like Souss-Massa, Marrakech, and Dakhla are preparing for a potential...
records.description: As Morocco begins its melon production season, farmers in key areas like Souss-Massa, Marrakech, and Dakhla are preparing for a potentially successful but challenging period. Moroccan melons, especially the Charentais and Galia varieties, are a major agricultural export, with approximately 57,000 tonnes exported in 2023, establishing Morocco as a key European supplier. Early harvests from Dakhla are already meeting strong European demand, positioning Morocco favorably before Spanish melons arrive. However, fluctuating temperatures have slowed growth and delayed harvests in some regions, and phytosanitary issues require careful management. Moroccan producers are using modern farming techniques like drip irrigation and fertigation to optimize yields and conserve water. While melons are popular domestically, especially during Ramadan, producers aim to balance local demand with export volumes. Current international prices are competitive, offering revenue opportunities, but competition from Spain and Italy will increase later in the season. The current high demand exceeding supply presents a significant advantage for Moroccan producers.

records.title: Enactus Morocco has launched the "Green Forward" program, an EU-funded initiative designed to strengthen organizations that support green...
records.description: Enactus Morocco has launched the "Green Forward" program, an EU-funded initiative designed to strengthen organizations that support green businesses in Morocco. The program aims to provide these support organizations with the necessary tools to help micro, small, and medium enterprises adopt environmentally friendly practices by addressing challenges such as limited resources, access to green financing, and organizational needs. "Green Forward" will enhance the capabilities of business support organizations through practical tools and training, create networking opportunities among stakeholders, and develop policy recommendations for integrating green economy principles into public policy. This initiative is part of a larger effort across seven countries in the Southern Neighborhood region to promote a green and circular economy.

records.title: The cactus industry rehabilitation project was officially launched in the rural commune of Maadna, Khouribga province.
records.description: The cactus industry rehabilitation project was officially launched in the rural commune of Maadna, Khouribga province. This initiative, part of the national "Generation Green" strategy, involves planting 720 hectares of cochineal-resistant cacti across four municipalities with a funding of 7.27 million dirhams. The project aims to revitalize the agricultural sector, support farmers affected by the cochineal pest, stabilize and improve cactus production quality, and ensure adaptation to local climates. It also seeks to create approximately 32,000 workdays and provide farmers with training in product development and marketing. The initiative includes modern plantation monitoring infrastructure, regular irrigation, and plot maintenance to ensure success and integrate cactus into the region's sustainable development. By promoting agricultural entrepreneurship, this program aims to be a model for other affected regions and reflects the "Green Generation" strategy's approach to combining agricultural development with environmental considerations.

records.title: The SaudiFood Manufacturing show is a key event for the Kingdom's growing F&B manufacturing industry, bringing together numerous global b...
records.description: The SaudiFood Manufacturing show is a key event for the Kingdom's growing F&B manufacturing industry, bringing together numerous global brands and country pavilions to showcase the latest in processing, packaging, ingredients, supply chain solutions, and automation, with the Saudi Authority for Industrial Cities and Technology Zones (MODON) as a strategic partner; occurring amidst a significant valuation and growth in Saudi Arabia's food sector and government plans for localization, the event also features the Food Forward Summit with international experts discussing crucial industry topics like AI and food security, offering a vital platform for business solutions and strategic insights.
records.institution: The Saudi Authority for Industrial Cities and Technology Zones (MODON)

records.title: The governorate of Monastir, Tunisia, will receive an exceptional allocation of 400,000 cubic meters of irrigation water from the Ministr...
records.description: The governorate of Monastir, Tunisia, will receive an exceptional allocation of 400,000 cubic meters of irrigation water from the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries to support early vegetable production during April and May. However, this amount is considered insufficient by the Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA) in Monastir, as the region's over 6,000 greenhouses require significantly more water. Farmers in the area, where public irrigation from the Nebhana Dam has been absent for two years, have resorted to expensive alternatives like water transportation and rainwater collection. The president of the Monastir Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries has emphasized the need for fair and efficient distribution of the allocated water through local committees, highlighting the tense agricultural context due to prolonged water shortages.
records.institution: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development (CRDA)

records.title: SEE Holding is unveiling The Sustainable City 2.0 (TSC 2.0) at the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) Congress 2025 in Abu Dhabi.
records.description: SEE Holding is unveiling The Sustainable City 2.0 (TSC 2.0) at the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) Congress 2025 in Abu Dhabi. Building on the success of The Sustainable City, TSC 2.0 is an AI-driven, net-zero, and human-centric next-generation city. Smart systems will optimize environmental sustainability through vertical farms, precision agriculture, clean energy from various sources, intelligent grids, and comprehensive water conservation technologies. Waste will be repurposed, recycled, or converted to energy, and a cooler microclimate will be maintained through design and technology. Mobility will be fully electric and autonomous. The city prioritizes people with pedestrian-friendly neighborhoods, wellness infrastructure, immersive learning environments, and proactive healthcare supported by digital monitoring. The Chairman and CEO of SEE Holding emphasized that TSC 2.0 is a model being built today, designed for future generations by integrating AI and focusing on human well-being. The original Sustainable City in Dubai has already achieved significant environmental and economic outcomes, and its model is expanding across the UAE and Oman. AIM Congress 2025 attendees can experience TSC 2.0 through an interactive showcase.

records.title: Casablanca is hosting the Annual International Poultry Council (IPC) Meeting, a gathering of global poultry industry leaders organized in...
records.description: Casablanca is hosting the Annual International Poultry Council (IPC) Meeting, a gathering of global poultry industry leaders organized in partnership with Morocco’s Interprofessional Federation of the Poultry Sector (FISA). The event aims to enhance international cooperation and the sharing of best practices in poultry production, trade, and regulation through sessions, presentations, and workshops led by international experts. Attendees will also participate in field visits to Moroccan poultry facilities to observe local innovations and technologies, and the meeting is expected to foster valuable networking opportunities among industry professionals, government officials, global company executives, and experts from FISA, the regulatory body for Morocco's poultry sector.
records.institution: The Interprofessional Federation of the Poultry Sector (FISA)

records.title: As part of the "Promoting Economic Growth through the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in the West Bank" project, the Ministry of...
records.description: As part of the "Promoting Economic Growth through the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in the West Bank" project, the Ministry of Agriculture, represented by the Tubas and Northern Jordan Valley Agriculture Directorate, delivered five 3.5-cubic meter water tanks to farmers in the Al-Aqaba area. This initiative aims to enhance water security for agricultural purposes in the region, supporting the project's goal of strengthening agricultural value chains and promoting economic growth in the West Bank.

records.domain: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing
records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), provided...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), provided agricultural aid to farmers in southern Hebron who suffered losses from previous weather depressions. The South Hebron Agriculture Directorate distributed 200 plastic rolls for greenhouse roofs to these affected farmers. This support is part of the Ministry's ongoing efforts to compensate farmers, strengthen their resilience, and sustain their agricultural activities, with plans to expand support to all those affected in previous years. The intervention aims to mitigate the negative impacts of harsh weather conditions on agricultural production and restore the production capacity of greenhouses, contributing to the resilience of the Palestinian agricultural sector.

records.title: The agriculture sector in Qatar is experiencing significant growth, projected to reach $180.30m in 2025 and $235.31m by the end of the de...
records.description: The agriculture sector in Qatar is experiencing significant growth, projected to reach $180.30m in 2025 and $235.31m by the end of the decade, driven by increasing food demand and government initiatives focused on food security through measures like PPP laws and financial incentives. Despite its arid climate, Qatar is adopting sustainable agricultural practices and technologies such as automated irrigation, aquaponics, and hydroponics to enhance yield and quality. While making strides in local food production, the country remains a major importer of cereals, fruits, and vegetables, with key suppliers including Brazil, the United States, India, and Australia. Qatar is actively working to diversify its economy by increasing local food production, supported by events like AgriteQ showcasing agri-tech advancements, and by investing in both domestic and international agribusiness ventures, with the agriculture sector expected to see a compound annual growth rate of 5.47 percent by the end of 2030.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry has announced plans to change the cropping pattern to prioritize food security crops and advance...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry has announced plans to change the cropping pattern to prioritize food security crops and advance processing industries and scientific research. This decision was shared during a briefing meeting with ministry staff, which recommended activating agricultural acts with the Ministry of Justice, improving communication within the ministry and with states, revitalizing the Agricultural Research Corporation, enhancing service conditions, expanding irrigated land, and separating agricultural engineering from the Extension Department in the states. The meeting also involved assessing infrastructure damage and human resources in war-affected regions, reviewing personnel matters and service conditions, and discussing proposals and solutions to address the war's impact on the ministry, given its importance in achieving food security.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry

records.title: A meeting chaired by the President focused on the executive status of providing electrical power for new agricultural reclamation project...
records.description: A meeting chaired by the President focused on the executive status of providing electrical power for new agricultural reclamation projects, particularly the "New Delta" project supervised by the "Egypt's Future" Authority. Discussions covered the timeline for required electrical loads and the progress of establishing necessary transformer stations to support agricultural reclamation areas, all within the state's efforts to ensure food security. The meeting also addressed the government's endeavors to guarantee the sustainable availability of energy for domestic consumption and national economic development, including enhancing reliance on renewable energy sources in line with sustainable development goals. The President gave directives to expedite the completion of the additional electrical power supply system required for the "New Delta" project and for the agricultural sector in general, in order to ensure the availability of strategic crops for Egypt in light of international fluctuations. The President emphasized the necessity of continuously updating the comprehensive plan to achieve energy security and increase reliance on renewable energy sources.
records.institution: The Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) for the first time...
records.description: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) for the first time, is organizing the Spring Flowers Exhibition. This initiative aims to elevate the exhibition to a global level, attract more international exhibitors, and explore opportunities for further cooperation and expansion abroad. According to Agriculture Ministry spokesman, the exhibition will serve as a training and qualification gateway for those interested in cultivation and offer a chance to learn about agricultural history through the agricultural museum, where the event will be held. Considered the second most important agricultural fair globally, the exhibition is expected to host foreign delegations presenting diverse ideas and feature sessions and symposiums with experts.

records.title: Iraq's Ministry of Water Resources has announced that it has planted 54,000 seedlings across 102 sites in Baghdad and other provinces (ex...
records.description: Iraq's Ministry of Water Resources has announced that it has planted 54,000 seedlings across 102 sites in Baghdad and other provinces (excluding the Kurdistan Region) as part of Prime Minister's initiative to plant five million trees nationwide. This effort, part of a broader plan spanning 2023 to 2025, has led the ministry to increase its target to 500,000 seedlings for the current spring planting season, with seedlings received from the Ministry of Agriculture being initially focused on ministry sites in Baghdad before expanding to other regions.

records.title: Oman Water Week will take place at the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre, attracting significant international participation for disc...
records.description: Oman Water Week will take place at the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre, attracting significant international participation for discussions on water sustainability, innovation, and technology. The event, hosted by Nama Water Services with support from the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and the Authority for Public Services Regulation, will feature field visits to key water infrastructure projects, a conference with global experts and officials, and specialized workshops to promote knowledge exchange and collaboration in addressing water resource management challenges and ensuring water security in line with national development goals.

records.title: The Tunisian Embassy in Rabat is organizing Tunisian participation in the International Agricultural Show in Morocco (SIAM), which will b...
records.description: The Tunisian Embassy in Rabat is organizing Tunisian participation in the International Agricultural Show in Morocco (SIAM), which will be held in Meknes. This significant event for agriculture and agri-food stakeholders offers Tunisian companies an opportunity to promote flagship products such as olive oil, dates, harissa, canned tuna, and pasta, with the aim of exploring new markets and establishing valuable partnerships. Interested companies must confirm their participation, according to the CEPEX press release.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has launched a national awareness campaign to educate consumers on how to distinguish between natural dairy p...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has launched a national awareness campaign to educate consumers on how to distinguish between natural dairy products and those made with hydrogenated vegetable oils, addressing growing concerns about the quality of dairy and cheese in the market. The campaign provides guidelines for identifying natural laban, labneh, and white cheese based on their texture, color, aroma, taste, and how they melt, while also outlining characteristics of products made with vegetable oils, which are not recommended. Consumers are advised to check for vacuum-sealed packaging, clear labeling with ingredients and dates, and to be wary of unhygienic or unlabeled products. The Ministry also provided a guideline price for fresh cow's milk and the approximate liters of milk required to produce various types of natural cheeses and labneh, warning that prices significantly lower than these costs may indicate the fraudulent use of hydrogenated oils. Citizens are urged to report any suspected food fraud to the Ministry of Agriculture or the Ministry of Economy hotlines.

records.title: The Moroccan blueberry season, which experienced delays due to unfavorable weather, is now reaching its peak in April and May, a timing t...
records.description: The Moroccan blueberry season, which experienced delays due to unfavorable weather, is now reaching its peak in April and May, a timing that has inadvertently created favorable commercial opportunities by avoiding early market saturation. Moroccan producers are strategically focusing on the high-demand jumbo varieties for European and Asian markets while navigating labor challenges during the intensified harvest period, reinforcing Morocco's significant position in the global berry trade.
records.institution: Moroccan Association of Red Fruit Producers

records.title: The Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) and the Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources are launching a long-term...
records.description: The Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) and the Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources are launching a long-term smart agriculture cooperation project in 2026, funded by a $13.5 million grant from KOICA. The five-year project aims to enhance agricultural productivity and climate change resilience, focusing on improving field crop and olive tree yields and investing in research and development for these strategic crops. The initiative will identify context-specific solutions for irrigation and seed improvement and will be implemented in partnership with the Office of State Lands (OTD) on pilot sites in the governorates of Nabeul, Kairouan, and Beja. KOICA emphasizes smart agriculture as a priority, aiming to improve productivity through climate-resilient technologies and agricultural policy capacity building, with plans to expand and diversify cooperation between the two countries. Korean cooperation with Tunisia has provided $82.31 million in financial support and 26 official development assistance projects until 2025, alongside volunteer programs and training scholarships in Korea.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture is actively monitoring the foot-and-mouth disease situation in Dhi Qar Governorate.
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture is actively monitoring the foot-and-mouth disease situation in Dhi Qar Governorate. Through its Veterinary Department, it is conducting field visits to monitor cases, providing veterinary medicines and treatments to breeders in the Souq Al-Shuyukh area, and sterilizing barns with antiviral agents. The ministry emphasizes the importance of continued monitoring, immediate reporting of suspected cases, and conducting awareness programs for breeders in coordination with the Agricultural Guidance and Training Department to prevent further infection spread. They are also collaborating with veterinary teams to contain the disease.

records.title: Jordan's state grain buyer has issued international tenders to purchase up to 120,000 metric tons each of milling wheat and animal feed b...
records.description: Jordan's state grain buyer has issued international tenders to purchase up to 120,000 metric tons each of milling wheat and animal feed barley, signaling the country's ongoing efforts to ensure food security amidst fluctuations in the global market. The wheat tender seeks shipments in consignments of 50,000 to 60,000 tons during July and August. Similarly, the barley tender requests shipments in 50,000 to 60,000-ton consignments during late July, August, and early September. These procurement activities follow Jordan's recent purchase of 60,000 tons of milling wheat and align with previous barley tenders. Despite some variations in specific import categories, Jordan's total imports experienced a modest increase in 2024. Major trading companies are expected to participate in these tenders, which are closely monitored by global suppliers due to Jordan's reliance on international trade for its food security as a highly arid nation with a growing population. The US Department of Agriculture anticipates Jordan's wheat imports will reach 1.2 million tonnes as the government works to fill its strategic grain reserves.

records.title: Moroccan tomato exports have seen a significant 19% increase this season, reaching 690,000 tons, with non-round varieties making up 58% o...
records.description: Moroccan tomato exports have seen a significant 19% increase this season, reaching 690,000 tons, with non-round varieties making up 58% of the total, and the UK being a major importer, particularly of snack tomatoes. Notably, direct exports to the German market have grown substantially, bypassing French intermediaries, indicating an improved perception of Moroccan tomato quality and service. Despite this positive trend, the sector faces challenges from the ToBRFV virus, causing significant losses, prompting growers to adopt resistant varieties. Additionally, a new social agreement will raise the minimum agricultural wage, and while the government's investment in desalination is crucial for addressing drought in key agricultural regions like Souss, the higher cost of desalinated water presents a financial burden for growers.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Sultanate of Oman is strategically positioning itself as a global leader in the emerging green hydrogen sector by leveraging its abun...
records.description: The Sultanate of Oman is strategically positioning itself as a global leader in the emerging green hydrogen sector by leveraging its abundant renewable energy resources to foster economic growth and facilitate energy transition. The managing director of Hydrom emphasized that Oman's ambition is supported by strategic planning, regulatory frameworks, and substantial investments in hydrogen infrastructure. While currently producing hydrogen from natural gas, Oman is actively pursuing blue and green hydrogen production, with green hydrogen produced via electrolysis using renewable energy being the ultimate goal, capitalizing on the nation's abundant solar and wind resources. Oman has allocated significant land for hydrogen projects, aiming for a total capacity of 35 gigawatts and creating opportunities for localizing manufacturing of related technologies. The government is focused on creating a favorable regulatory environment to attract private sector investment, both local and international. Despite challenges in technological development and cost reduction, Oman's commitment to hydrogen is driven by the need for energy security and sustainability under Oman Vision 2040, aiming to become a key hydrogen-exporting hub in the global market.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) has announced the commencement of commercial operations for the Madinah 3 Wastewater plant, a...
records.description: The Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) has announced the commencement of commercial operations for the Madinah 3 Wastewater plant, a SAR964 million ($257 million) project. Developed by a consortium led by Acciona, with Tawzea and Tamasuk as partners, the plant has a capacity of 200,000 cu m/day, expandable to 375,000 cu m/day in emergencies. Operated under a BOOT model, Acciona will manage the facility for 25 years, treating wastewater for industrial and agricultural use. The plant successfully treated over 5 million cu m of wastewater during Ramadan. The project also achieved a safety milestone of two million man-hours without LTI.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: UAE-based Hotpack Global has partnered with the Saudi Ministry of Industry to establish a SR1 billion ($266 million) food packaging proje...
records.description: UAE-based Hotpack Global has partnered with the Saudi Ministry of Industry to establish a SR1 billion ($266 million) food packaging project in Saudi Arabia, aiming to produce environmentally friendly, recyclable, and biodegradable products over seven years. This initiative seeks to reduce packaging waste and explore the use of agricultural waste as raw material. The agreement aligns with the Saudi Ministry of Investment’s objective to enhance the Kingdom's investment appeal and foster sustainable economic growth. This venture follows Hotpack's previous plans to invest in biodegradable packaging plants in Malaysia.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: In celebration of 2025's "Year of the Community," Abu Dhabi City Municipality, Miral, and ALEC launched the "Planting the Roots of a Sust...
records.description: In celebration of 2025's "Year of the Community," Abu Dhabi City Municipality, Miral, and ALEC launched the "Planting the Roots of a Sustainable Future" initiative, planting 300 trees in Al Masar Park, Khalifa City. The project, aligning with Miral's environmental CSR strategy, engaged over 200 participants, including students, in planting Ghaf, Flame, and Neem trees, fostering environmental awareness and sustainability.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: TAQA and EWEC are partnering to develop new energy infrastructure in the UAE, including a 1GW gas turbine plant and advanced grid infrast...
records.description: TAQA and EWEC are partnering to develop new energy infrastructure in the UAE, including a 1GW gas turbine plant and advanced grid infrastructure, to support the nation's AI and Net Zero 2050 goals; this collaboration will also bolster EWEC and Masdar's project for 24/7 renewable energy dispatch, driving approximately AED36 billion in investment and establishing a global benchmark for sustainable energy systems that balance technological advancement with environmental responsibility.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi National Energy Company (TAQA), Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC)

records.title: The Egyptian garlic export campaign is thriving, driven by high demand and significantly increased volumes of large, high-quality garlic,...
records.description: The Egyptian garlic export campaign is thriving, driven by high demand and significantly increased volumes of large, high-quality garlic, capitalizing on production issues faced by competitors. European demand, including from Spain, is strong, with Spanish importers purchasing Egyptian garlic for redistribution. Egyptian exporters are finding success with competitive pricing, targeting markets like the Netherlands with red and purple garlic varieties. The price of Egyptian dry garlic is around USD 1,000 per ton, making it an attractive option compared to competitors. Exporters, like Al Wadi, aim to leverage this season's opportunities to expand their market share in Europe.
records.institution: Al Wadi for Agricultural Investments and Export

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture has launched a national campaign to promote water conservation in irrigation due to low rainfall and...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture has launched a national campaign to promote water conservation in irrigation due to low rainfall and climate challenges. The campaign urges farmers to adopt modern, efficient irrigation methods, including drip irrigation, precise water metering, and timing irrigation for early morning or evening to reduce evaporation. Farmers are also encouraged to plant drought-tolerant and short-cycle crops, improve soil quality through no-till farming and organic matter additions, use balanced fertilization, and expand rainfed agriculture. The Ministry emphasizes the importance of farmer participation in training and workshops and cooperation with authorities to ensure sustainable water use and food security.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Morocco is progressing with its "water highways" project, a strategic plan to move excess water from surplus watersheds to those with def...
records.description: Morocco is progressing with its "water highways" project, a strategic plan to move excess water from surplus watersheds to those with deficits. This initiative, part of the National Plan for Drinking Water Supply and Irrigation, aims to transfer 1.2 billion cubic meters of water annually. The first phase, connecting two major basins, is operational, and the second phase, connecting another two, is under study, demonstrating a strategy of territorial solidarity and efficient water resource management.
records.institution: The Ministry of Equipment and Water

records.title: Morocco's blueberry season has experienced a significant delay this year, with peak harvest expected in April and May, nearly a month lat...
records.description: Morocco's blueberry season has experienced a significant delay this year, with peak harvest expected in April and May, nearly a month later than usual. This delay, caused by unfavorable temperatures during flowering in the northern regions, has resulted in a staggered harvest, with Agadir experiencing normal production levels. Despite the late start, growers anticipate a surge in production in the coming weeks. However, the peak harvest period coincides with the second cycles of raspberries and strawberries, creating a labor shortage that may lead to fruit losses. Commercially, the delayed season has proven advantageous, as it aligns with a more favorable market due to similar delays in other regions, allowing Moroccan growers to capitalize on higher prices and the demand for jumbo varieties in European and Asian markets.
records.institution: Moroccan Association of Soft Fruit Producers

records.title: The Al-Gezira State's Technical Secretariat for Food Security has launched an assessment program for the 2024-2025 agricultural season, f...
records.description: The Al-Gezira State's Technical Secretariat for Food Security has launched an assessment program for the 2024-2025 agricultural season, funded by the FAO. Teams are conducting surveys in multiple localities to evaluate food security and identify challenges from the previous season, utilizing specialized training and a digital application for data collection.
records.institution: Technical Secretariat for Food Security in Al-Gezira State

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) has significantly improved its electricity and water production efficiency by 43.61% since 2...
records.description: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) has significantly improved its electricity and water production efficiency by 43.61% since 2006, resulting in a cumulative reduction of 104 million tonnes of CO2 emissions.This achievement, equivalent to planting 527 million trees, has also yielded substantial financial savings. DEWA attributes this success to continuous innovation, technology deployment, and operational enhancements, including co-generation and hybrid desalination systems that optimize energy use and minimize costs.

records.title: The Italian group BF Spa is leading the Timimoun agricultural mega-project in the Algerian Sahara, a $420 million initiative aimed at add...
records.description: The Italian group BF Spa is leading the Timimoun agricultural mega-project in the Algerian Sahara, a $420 million initiative aimed at addressing Africa's food challenges. Initially focused on durum wheat, pasta, and legume production for the Algerian market, the project plans to expand into livestock farming, animal feed production, and seed genetic research. BF Spa's CEO envisions Timimoun as a strategic food reserve for Africa, praising the Algerian government's support. The project will integrate livestock and agriculture, using manure as fertilizer to reduce chemical inputs. The animal feed segment is seen as a growth opportunity, and genetic seed research aims to improve agricultural yields.

records.title: Egypt is projected to maintain steady wheat imports at 13.0 MMT in 2025/26, despite a slight increase in domestic production, driven by p...
records.description: Egypt is projected to maintain steady wheat imports at 13.0 MMT in 2025/26, despite a slight increase in domestic production, driven by population growth and rising consumption. Corn production and imports are also expected to increase due to a recovering poultry industry, while rice production remains stable amidst changing consumer preferences. The Egyptian government is implementing reforms, including the establishment of the FoESD for wheat tenders and adjusting bread subsidies, to manage food security amid population growth and economic pressures, while the aquaculture sector sees growth and increased demand for feed.
records.institution: The Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development (FoESD)

records.title: The imperial city of Meknes will host the International Agricultural Show in Morocco (SIAM) under the theme "Agriculture and the Rural Wo...
records.description: The imperial city of Meknes will host the International Agricultural Show in Morocco (SIAM) under the theme "Agriculture and the Rural World: Water at the Heart of Sustainable Development." Under royal patronage, SIAM, the largest agricultural trade show in Africa, will spotlight France and showcase agricultural innovations, local products, and solutions for resilient agriculture across twelve thematic areas, including agri-digital, livestock, and scientific conferences focusing on water governance. The event, expecting over one million visitors and featuring 1,500 exhibitors from 70 countries, will serve as a platform for networking and exploring the future of sustainable agriculture.

records.title: The Trilokeswar Farmer Producer Company (FPC), in partnership with the Department of Horticulture and Palladium marketing agency, success...
records.description: The Trilokeswar Farmer Producer Company (FPC), in partnership with the Department of Horticulture and Palladium marketing agency, successfully exported 12 tons of G9 bananas from Kalampur, Kalahandi, to Dubai. The bananas were sourced from local farmer shareholders. The initiative, supported by Trilokeswar FPC, Mahashakti Foundation, NABARD, and the Government of India, introduced new agricultural techniques and provided farmers with quality planting materials, organic fertilizers, training, and marketing support. A 150-acre banana cluster was established to improve market access and boost Kalahandi's fruit export capabilities.

records.title: Algeria has signed a $3.5 billion agreement to implement a large-scale powdered milk production project in the southern region, covering...
records.description: Algeria has signed a $3.5 billion agreement to implement a large-scale powdered milk production project in the southern region, covering 117,000 hectares. This project, a collaboration between Algerian institutions and Baladna Algeria (a subsidiary of Qatar's Baladna), aims to achieve food self-sufficiency by covering 50% of the country's powdered milk needs. It includes fodder farms, cattle ranches, and a milk production plant. The initiative is also expected to supply red meat, create jobs, and increase the national cattle herd. The project site in Adrar province was chosen for its land and water potential, and preliminary work is underway. This project signifies Algeria's strategic push for sustainable development and reduced import dependence.

records.title: Egypt is experiencing a surge in the international garlic market, surpassing Spain due to increased acreage, better sizing, and weather-r...
records.description: Egypt is experiencing a surge in the international garlic market, surpassing Spain due to increased acreage, better sizing, and weather-related issues impacting Spain's crops. Egypt's high-quality garlic is meeting strong demand in key markets like the EU, North America, Latin America, and Australia, leading to increased buyer confidence and a positive outlook for further market share growth.

records.title: Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture is planning to introduce vertical farming to improve land use and decrease the use of chemical fertilizers...
records.description: Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture is planning to introduce vertical farming to improve land use and decrease the use of chemical fertilizers.This method, using hydroponics and aeroponics, allows crops to grow in stacked layers, eliminating the need for soil and chemical fertilizers. The controlled environment enables year-round production, and integrating fish farming can provide natural fertilizer. The initiative aims to enhance Iraq's food security and agricultural sustainability.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Tunisia, projected to be a leading olive oil producer, faces the challenge of managing substantial olive waste, which entrepreneur Yassin...
records.description: Tunisia, projected to be a leading olive oil producer, faces the challenge of managing substantial olive waste, which entrepreneur Yassine Khelifi's Bioheat startup addresses by converting it into sustainable fuel briquettes, offering a cleaner alternative to firewood with lower carbon emissions; these briquettes are sold domestically and exported, reducing deforestation, decreasing Tunisia's reliance on fuel imports, and creating jobs, though financing remains a significant hurdle for such ventures aiming to contribute to the country's clean energy transition.

records.title: Tunisia's Ministry of Commerce addressed recent supply disruptions of bananas and potatoes, which caused price increases, by releasing st...
records.description: Tunisia's Ministry of Commerce addressed recent supply disruptions of bananas and potatoes, which caused price increases, by releasing stored supplies and ensuring market distribution; this intervention successfully stabilized banana prices at the ministry's set ceiling and rectified the potato supply imbalance.

records.title: Algeria is projected to import approximately 9.2 million metric tons of wheat in the 2025-26 marketing year, maintaining levels similar t...
records.description: Algeria is projected to import approximately 9.2 million metric tons of wheat in the 2025-26 marketing year, maintaining levels similar to the previous season, according to the USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service. This forecast is influenced by stable domestic production and ongoing efforts to bolster strategic reserves. Wheat and barley are Algeria’s primary cereal crops, with durum wheat being a significant portion of the planting area. The wheat harvest for 2025-26 is anticipated to remain steady at 3 million metric tons, with barley production projected at 1.2 million metric tons. Despite government initiatives to expand irrigated land, most cereal cultivation depends on rainfall. Wheat remains a staple in the Algerian diet, with consumption expected to rise with population growth. The Algerian Office of Cereals (OAIC) continues to be the sole wheat importer, and Russia has emerged as a significant supplier. Durum wheat imports remain substantial, despite aspirations for self-sufficiency. Barley imports are forecasted to rise due to increased demand for animal feed, with the Algerian Office of Feed Grains (ONAB) actively procuring barley and corn.

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture organized a two-day training workshop on "Effective Presentation Skills for Agricultural Extension W...
