Chia, a drought-resistant plant from the mint family, is well-suited to Saudi Arabia's climate, growing in warm temperatures and requiring minimal water. The "Saudi Rural" program supports farmers in cultivating chia, which has applications in food, beverages, and cosmetics. Field experiments in Taif Governorate have demonstrated its successful localization. The cultivation of chia, fertilized with organic and chemical fertilizers, contributes to self-sufficiency goals under Saudi Vision 2030.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia's tomato production reached over 691,875 tons in 2023, achieving a 76% self-sufficiency rate, according to the Ministry of E...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's tomato production reached over 691,875 tons in 2023, achieving a 76% self-sufficiency rate, according to the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA). Production was split between open farms (392,294 tons) and greenhouses (299,581 tons). MEWA is promoting modern agricultural methods, supporting farmers with advanced technologies, and encouraging consumers to choose local products, especially during Ramadan, to reduce food waste and enhance food security. These efforts align with Saudi Vision 2030's goals for agricultural sustainability.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) is significantly improving livelihoods and rural resilience in Yemen t...
records.description: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) is significantly improving livelihoods and rural resilience in Yemen through various development projects. Collaborating with SMEPS, the SDRPY's Livelihood Support for Vulnerable Communities Initiative focuses on agriculture, fisheries, and livestock, creating over 13,000 job opportunities. These initiatives build local community capacities through training and rehabilitation, supporting food security and economic empowerment. SDRPY has implemented 264 projects across Yemen, contributing to vital sectors and enhancing the Yemeni government's capabilities.
records.institution: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and the Director General for Economic Policy in the German Federal Ministry for Economic...
records.description: The Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and the Director General for Economic Policy in the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy and Ministry Coordinator for Sustainable Development discussed ways to enhance cooperation in the fields of natural gas, hydrogen production, and carbon storage.They covered Germany's purchase of Cypriot gas through Egypt's liquefaction facilities and explored utilizing Germany's surplus gasification capacity by renting a floating regasification and storage unit (FSRU). An Egyptian delegation will visit Germany to finalize the rental agreement.
records.institution: The Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources

records.title: The New Egyptian Countryside Development Company, in partnership with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Migration, has launched "Your...
records.description: The New Egyptian Countryside Development Company, in partnership with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Migration, has launched "Your Farm in Egypt" to attract investments from Egyptians living abroad. This initiative allows expatriates to participate in the 1.5 Million Feddan Project, Egypt's major agricultural development. The initiative aims to enhance food security and economic growth by offering agricultural land, technical support, and logistical assistance to expatriate investors. The government plans to launch further initiatives to encourage diaspora participation in national development.
records.institution: New Egyptian Countryside Development Company, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Migration and Egyptians Abroad Affairs

records.title: A three-day training course on artificial intelligence in agriculture and sustainable development has been launched by the Ministry of Ag...
records.description: A three-day training course on artificial intelligence in agriculture and sustainable development has been launched by the Ministry of Agriculture's Baalbek-Hermel Agriculture Department. The course, aimed at employees and technical staff, is being held in collaboration with the Knights of Malta, and emphasizes the importance of technological innovation in the agricultural sector.

records.title: Domseeds (Morocco) and Apexagri (France) have formed a strategic partnership to enhance agricultural development projects in Africa and t...
records.description: Domseeds (Morocco) and Apexagri (France) have formed a strategic partnership to enhance agricultural development projects in Africa and the Middle East. The collaboration combines their expertise in life sciences, sustainable agriculture, and sector structuring. This partnership aims to support projects addressing challenges like climate change, food sovereignty, and market access. By pooling resources and expertise, they intend to provide comprehensive services, from strategic planning to field implementation, for clients in the agrifood sector.

records.title: The filling rate of dams in the Sebou hydraulic basin is 37.10%, holding over 2,060 million cubic meters of water.
records.description: The filling rate of dams in the Sebou hydraulic basin is 37.10%, holding over 2,060 million cubic meters of water. Some dams, like Allal El Fassi, have high filling rates, while others, like Al Wahda and Idriss 1st, have lower rates. The Sebou Basin, with its numerous dams and lakes, is essential for Morocco's water supply, facing challenges from climate and growing water needs.
records.institution: The Ministry of Equipment and Water

records.title: The Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund in Oman is crucial for achieving Oman Vision 2040's goals, focusing on environmental sust...
records.description: The Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund in Oman is crucial for achieving Oman Vision 2040's goals, focusing on environmental sustainability, economic diversification, innovation, human capital development, and food security. The Fund supports projects using modern technologies, promotes biodiversity, and aims to increase the agricultural and fisheries sector's GDP contribution. It fosters innovation through e-marketing and advanced production technologies, empowers women and youth, and strengthens public-private partnerships. The Fund also focuses on transitioning to a green economy and combating pests and diseases, aligning with the vision's principles of supporting advanced technologies, financing innovative projects, strengthening partnerships, developing infrastructure, and ensuring product quality and safety.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's potato production reached 621,751 tons in 2023, achieving an 87% self-sufficiency rate.
records.description: Saudi Arabia's potato production reached 621,751 tons in 2023, achieving an 87% self-sufficiency rate. The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture promotes local potatoes as a nutritious option during Ramadan, supporting food security and aligning with Saudi Vision 2030's goals for agricultural sustainability and self-sufficiency.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Greenhouse Management and Agri Marketing Co.
records.description: Saudi Greenhouse Management and Agri Marketing Co. (SGH) and Topian are partnering to establish the Horticulture Innovation Center (HIC) at the University of Tabuk, aiming to advance controlled-environment agriculture in Saudi Arabia. Designed with expertise from the World Horti Center, the HIC will be a hub for horticultural education and innovation, showcasing diverse technologies and growing methods. SGH will lead construction and joint operation, while Topian will manage daily operations. The center will foster collaboration and develop skilled greenhouse operators, contributing to sustainable agricultural practices in the Kingdom. Construction is set to begin in Q2 2025.
records.institution: Saudi Greenhouse Management and Agri Marketing Co. (SGH)

records.title: Sudan's grain production has surged to a five-year high of 6.6 million tons, surpassing national food needs, according to the Ministry of...
records.description: Sudan's grain production has surged to a five-year high of 6.6 million tons, surpassing national food needs, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry. This represents a significant increase from the previous year. However, the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has severely disrupted the agricultural sector, causing activity to halt in RSF-controlled areas due to looting and security concerns. The conflict, which began in April 2023, has also led to widespread displacement and significant loss of life.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry

records.domain: Establishment or modification of food stock
records.title: The Tunisian Trade Office (OTC) assures that consumer products like sugar, tea, coffee, and rice are adequately stocked, with supplies la...
records.description: The Tunisian Trade Office (OTC) assures that consumer products like sugar, tea, coffee, and rice are adequately stocked, with supplies lasting two to four months. There are no reported queues for these products. Specifically, sugar stocks are at 100,000 tonnes, with an additional 28,000 tonnes expected soon. Rice reserves are at 8,000 tonnes, exceeding the average monthly consumption. Coffee consumption is expected to decrease during Ramadan.

records.title: The Council of Ministers has decided to strengthen agricultural vocational training for young people, focusing on family livestock farmin...
records.description: The Council of Ministers has decided to strengthen agricultural vocational training for young people, focusing on family livestock farming, tree cultivation, and horticulture. A national fair for small livestock breeders will be organized to promote the integration of modern technologies into these sectors. This initiative follows the adoption of a new market-driven approach to vocational training by the Ministry of Agriculture.

records.title: Egypt has launched the National Flour Fortification Programme to combat iron deficiency anaemia by enriching subsidized wheat flour with...
records.description: Egypt has launched the National Flour Fortification Programme to combat iron deficiency anaemia by enriching subsidized wheat flour with iron and folic acid. This initiative, led by the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade and the Ministry of Health and Population, aims to improve the nutritional value of 'Baladi' bread, a staple food. The program addresses high anaemia rates, particularly among children and women. It involves training millers and distributing fortified bread in 13 high-prevalence governorates, with support from the World Food Programme and initial funding from the German government. The program aligns with national goals to enhance food security and public health.
records.institution: The Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade (MOSIT)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt's 650 MW GOS II Wind Farm is complete, a key step in its renewable energy goals.
records.description: Egypt's 650 MW GOS II Wind Farm is complete, a key step in its renewable energy goals. EWA Group provided crucial logistics, including heavy lift transport, port operations, and customs clearance. The project, with 104 turbines, featured the transport of Egypt's longest 92-meter wind turbine blade. The wind farm supports Egypt's Vision 2030, aiming for 14 GW of wind power by 2030. EWA's expertise in handling complex logistics has solidified its role in Egypt's renewable energy sector. Egypt's strong wind resources in the Gulf of Suez make it attractive for wind energy investments.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: KarmSolar is expanding its Farafra Solar Grid in Egypt through a partnership with Daltex, tripling the grid's capacity to 8.37 MVA.
records.description: KarmSolar is expanding its Farafra Solar Grid in Egypt through a partnership with Daltex, tripling the grid's capacity to 8.37 MVA. This expansion will supply electricity to Daltex and other agricultural businesses. The Farafra Solar Grid, Egypt's first hybrid microgrid, integrates solar PV, battery storage, and diesel generators to provide sustainable energy to off-grid areas. The expansion, funded by equity investments, increases the grid's utilization rate. Daltex, a major agricultural player in the region, is supporting the transition to renewable energy. KarmSolar aims to achieve 100% solar dependency for the grid, reflecting the growing demand for solar energy solutions in Egypt's agricultural sector.

records.title: The Egyptian garlic season is experiencing a positive harvest, with high volumes and good quality garlic, larger than previous seasons.
records.description: The Egyptian garlic season is experiencing a positive harvest, with high volumes and good quality garlic, larger than previous seasons. Increased production, driven by last year's strong demand, has doubled compared to the previous year. Despite the loss of a major client, strong demand from other customers is expected to compensate. The green garlic season may be extended to the end of April through storage, while the dry garlic season begins. Quality remains a priority, with the company focusing on fulfilling orders that meet its high standards. The company also received the spring add-on for its Global Gap certificate.

records.title: The National Seed Bank, part of the National Center for Agricultural Research, was inaugurated in Jordan.
records.description: The National Seed Bank, part of the National Center for Agricultural Research, was inaugurated in Jordan. It aims to preserve plant genetic resources and enhance food security. The bank includes laboratories and storage for 50,000 seed samples, some dating back to 1927. It addresses climate change, water scarcity, and food system disruptions. The bank features storage, drying, and testing facilities, with cooling technology extending seed life. It builds on a previous Seed Storage Unit and aligns with national agricultural strategies. The project was funded by Al-Hussein University.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture is building strategic partnerships to boost sector sustainability.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture is building strategic partnerships to boost sector sustainability. This includes enhancing guidance, fostering academic collaboration, and supporting farmers through various projects. Key initiatives involve coordinating exhibitions, developing research, and implementing environmental agreements. The Ministry aims to support farmers, develop markets, and create a national food security plan, ensuring the sector's long-term viability.

records.title: A new maritime link will connect the Port of Huelva with Tanger Med, Morocco.
records.description: A new maritime link will connect the Port of Huelva with Tanger Med, Morocco. Operated by Suardiaz Group and GTO, the line will provide frequent rotations and short transit times. This initiative aims to strengthen trade between Spain and Morocco. The Port of Huelva seeks to become a key hub for maritime trade between Europe and Africa.

records.title: An analysis of 2023 FAOSTAT data shows significant price differences for eggplants from Spain, the Netherlands, Turkey, and Morocco.
records.description: An analysis of 2023 FAOSTAT data shows significant price differences for eggplants from Spain, the Netherlands, Turkey, and Morocco. Dutch producers charged the highest (€0.99/kg), followed by Spain (€0.73/kg), Turkey (€0.45/kg), and Morocco (€0.27/kg). Moroccan prices were significantly lower than Spanish prices. Prices fluctuated over the past decade in all countries, with Morocco showing a modest but steady increase. The low Moroccan prices present both challenges and potential competitive advantages.

records.title: Moroccan fruit and vegetable exporters are finishing their early fruit season and preparing for watermelons and summer fruits.
records.description: Moroccan fruit and vegetable exporters are finishing their early fruit season and preparing for watermelons and summer fruits. Despite strong demand in Europe for products like tomatoes, peppers, and avocados, exporters faced challenges including higher costs due to drought, transportation, and disease, as well as delays at Spanish customs. Issues within Morocco, such as tomato coloration problems and local market competition, also impacted export volumes. While Spain, France, the UK, Germany, and the Netherlands remain key markets, there's a growing need to diversify into Eastern Europe, Scandinavia, and Southeast Asia due to increasing tensions with European growers.

records.title: The National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA) in Morocco has reassured the public about the safety of its livestock despite social media cl...
records.description: The National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA) in Morocco has reassured the public about the safety of its livestock despite social media claims of harmful antibiotics in red meat. ONSSA emphasizes continuous monitoring and strict regulation of veterinary medicines. The controversy coincides with a decline in Moroccan livestock due to drought, leading to the decision not to hold the traditional sheep sacrifice for Eid al-Adha in 2025. To address red meat shortages, Morocco is importing sheep from Australia and planning to import more sheep and goats from various sources. The country is also working to stabilize its red meat supply, which has been impacted by reduced grazing land and increased feed costs.
records.institution: The National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: GS Enima Barka 5 Desalination Company in Oman has signed a power purchase agreement (PPA) to integrate solar energy into its desalination...
records.description: GS Enima Barka 5 Desalination Company in Oman has signed a power purchase agreement (PPA) to integrate solar energy into its desalination plant in Barka. A 6.5-megawatt peak photovoltaic (PV) solar plant will supply up to 11% of the desalination plant's energy needs by 2044, reducing its carbon footprint. Construction is set to begin, with operation expected in the first quarter of 2026. This project aligns with GS Enima's goal to incorporate renewable energy into the water sector. Once operational, it will be the second solar-powered desalination facility in Oman, following Veolia's Sharqiya Desalination Company's 17 MW peak plant.

records.title: Palestine ranks fifth in the Arab world and eighth globally for date exports, valued at $69 million, according to World Bank data.
records.description: Palestine ranks fifth in the Arab world and eighth globally for date exports, valued at $69 million, according to World Bank data. This achievement reflects government reforms, particularly within the Ministry of Agriculture, focusing on transparency and governance. Corrective measures, including national committees and anti-smuggling efforts, have improved farmers' economic returns. Palestine's 2024 date production reached 22,000 tons, supporting the Palestinian economy and sustainable agricultural development.

records.title: Hilton Foods, NADEC form joint venture to expand meat production in Saudi Arabia
records.description: Hilton Foods is entering the Saudi Arabian market through a 10-year joint venture with The National Agricultural Development Company (NADEC). Hilton Foods will hold a 49% stake and invest US$8.3 million. The partnership aims to establish modern meat processing facilities in Saudi Arabia, with NADEC supplying red meat and integrating products into its distribution network. This aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, enhancing food security and local production. The venture will begin operations in the second half of 2026, pending regulatory approval. Saudi Arabia is a major meat consumer, with beef being the most popular red meat.

records.title: The United Nations Water Committee (UN-Water) has recognized Saudi Arabia as a leading model for integrated water resources management.
records.description: The United Nations Water Committee (UN-Water) has recognized Saudi Arabia as a leading model for integrated water resources management. A workshop, hosted by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture in Riyadh, examined the Kingdom's progress. UN-Water is conducting a case study of Saudi Arabia's approach, which aligns with Vision 2030 and the National Water Strategy 2030, to serve as a model for other nations. The workshop reviewed findings on how Saudi Arabia's practices can accelerate progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6).
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The Ministry of Trade and Export Promotion in Tunisia is addressing market stability and consumer affordability by continuing the importa...
records.description: The Ministry of Trade and Export Promotion in Tunisia is addressing market stability and consumer affordability by continuing the importation of chilled lamb and cattle meat through the Ellouhoum Company. Quantities of both meats are being distributed at set retail prices, with butchers required to contact the company's sales department for purchase. This initiative aims to ensure a steady supply of meat at prices that are accessible to citizens.
records.institution: Share The Ministry of Trade and Export

records.title: The Secretary of State for Water Resources has urged the allocation of water from the Nebhana Dam to support regional farmers, ensuring f...
records.description: The Secretary of State for Water Resources has urged the allocation of water from the Nebhana Dam to support regional farmers, ensuring fruit tree sustainability and optimal agricultural production. He also advocated for funding to dig deep wells for irrigation and stressed the priority of drinking water during summer, calling for the expedited completion of the Sousse desalination plant.
records.institution: The State Secretariat for Water Resources

records.title: ADQ has become the majority shareholder of Aramex PJSC, achieving 58% ownership.
records.description: ADQ has become the majority shareholder of Aramex PJSC, achieving 58% ownership. This includes shares from a tender offer and those already owned by AD Ports Group. Aramex will join ADQ’s Transport & Logistics cluster, alongside other companies. ADQ intends to develop Aramex into a globally competitive business. ADQ is a sovereign investor focused on infrastructure and supply chains, with a large portfolio across various sectors.

records.title: The General Federation of Algerian Traders and Craftsmen (FGCAA) has criticized banana importers for driving up prices in Algeria.
records.description: The General Federation of Algerian Traders and Craftsmen (FGCAA) has criticized banana importers for driving up prices in Algeria. They allege importers sell at inflated prices to agents and traders, leading to market inflation. The FGCAA denies responsibility, citing their role as a weak link in the distribution chain. They demand transparency in purchasing and customs transactions, regulation of profit margins, and potentially, exclusive state-controlled banana imports through the Ministry of Agriculture. The FGCAA is calling for immediate regulatory intervention to stabilize prices and punish those responsible for the increase.
records.institution: General Federation of Algerian Traders and Craftsmen (FGCAA)

records.title: Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture has partnered with Royal Jordanian (RJ) and the Jordan Exporters and Producers Association for Fruit and...
records.description: Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture has partnered with Royal Jordanian (RJ) and the Jordan Exporters and Producers Association for Fruit and Vegetables (JEPA) to boost fruit and vegetable exports. The US$2.8 million funding, from the Agricultural Risk Fund, will simplify export processes and reduce air freight costs. RJ will expand market access, increase flights, and lower shipping costs. This initiative aligns with Jordan's economic modernization vision and aims to enhance the global competitiveness of Jordanian agricultural products.

records.title: The Saudi Jordanian Investment Company (SJIC) will indirectly invest in Alyoum Bakery, a major Jordanian baked goods producer, to support...
records.description: The Saudi Jordanian Investment Company (SJIC) will indirectly invest in Alyoum Bakery, a major Jordanian baked goods producer, to support its growth strategy. This includes expanding operations and introducing new products in Jordan and neighboring markets. The investment, through new share issuance, is subject to regulatory approvals. SJIC aims to foster economic partnerships and achieve sustainable returns, aligning with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. Alyoum Bakery, with a large production capacity and distribution network, will use the investment to enhance efficiency and expand its reach. SJIC, a partnership between Saudi Arabia and Jordan, is primarily owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia.

records.title: A Moroccan-French agreement to regulate cherry tomato imports is expected in mid-March, aiming to reduce competition with French growers.
records.description: A Moroccan-French agreement to regulate cherry tomato imports is expected in mid-March, aiming to reduce competition with French growers. Increased Moroccan greenhouse production and competitive pricing have caused tensions. Discussions, led by both countries' agriculture ministries and a reactivated joint committee, have been ongoing. The agreement will define seasonal import commitments. This development signals improved economic relations after recent diplomatic tensions.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests

records.title: A new agreement between Moroccan and French tomato producers is expected in mid-March to regulate Moroccan cherry tomato presence in the...
records.description: A new agreement between Moroccan and French tomato producers is expected in mid-March to regulate Moroccan cherry tomato presence in the French market. This aims to avoid direct competition with French producers at the start of their season. Increased Moroccan greenhouse production and competitive pricing have created tensions. Discussions, facilitated by both countries' Ministries of Agriculture and a reactivated joint committee, have been ongoing. The agreement will likely define seasonal import commitments for Moroccan tomatoes.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests

records.domain: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
records.title: Berry producer and distributor Hortifrut has obtained LEAF Marque certification for its operations in Morocco and Peru.
records.description: Berry producer and distributor Hortifrut has obtained LEAF Marque certification for its operations in Morocco and Peru. This certification is intended to expand LEAF brand coverage in the EMEA region, adding to existing certifications in Spain, Portugal, and the Americas. Hortifrut's Managing Director for EMEA highlighted this achievement.

records.title: Morocco's OCP reported a 6% revenue increase in 2024, reaching US$9.7 billion, driven by rising global demand for fertilizers.
records.description: Morocco's OCP reported a 6% revenue increase in 2024, reaching US$9.7 billion, driven by rising global demand for fertilizers. Exports grew by 13.1%, with fertilizers leading shipments. OCP plans to invest US$14.06 billion between 2025 and 2027 to expand operations. The company is committed to sustainability, aiming for full reliance on renewable energy and desalinated water by 2027, and becoming entirely green by 2040. OCP is also investing in desalination projects and green hydrogen production. In the first half of 2024, revenue increased by 15%, with fertilizers comprising 69% of sales. Key export markets include Africa, South America, and Europe.

records.title: Oman Investment Authority (OIA) has invested in Tidal Vision, a US-based biopolymer technology company, during its Series B funding round.
records.description: Oman Investment Authority (OIA) has invested in Tidal Vision, a US-based biopolymer technology company, during its Series B funding round. Tidal Vision specializes in converting crustacean shells into chitosan-based biopolymer solutions for various industries, including water treatment, agriculture, and oil and gas. OIA's investment, through its Future Generations Fund (FGF), aims to localize innovative solutions for the Omani market and support sustainable returns. Tidal Vision's technology focuses on a zero-waste extraction process and repurposes byproducts from the fishing industry, contributing to a circular economy.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Oman is becoming a leader in the Middle East's green hydrogen sector, with five major projects expected to be operational by 2030.
records.description: Oman is becoming a leader in the Middle East's green hydrogen sector, with five major projects expected to be operational by 2030. These projects, including the ACME Duqm Hydrogen Project and others by POSCO Consortium, Amnah Consortium, Fortescue Future Industries, and EDF, leverage Oman's abundant solar and wind resources. Oman's strategic location, particularly the Duqm Special Economic Zone, and government support through Hydrom and OPAZ, are attracting international investors. While facing regional competition from Saudi Arabia and the UAE, Oman's focus on green hydrogen provides a competitive advantage in the global transition to net-zero emissions.
records.institution: Hydrom, Public Authority for Special Economic Zones and Free Zones (OPAZ)

records.title: Preliminary data from Oman's National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI) shows a minor decline in the nation's tomato output fo...
records.description: Preliminary data from Oman's National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI) shows a minor decline in the nation's tomato output for 2024, with total production reaching 219,775 tons. This figure represents a 2.5% decrease compared to the production levels recorded in 2023. Despite this slight dip, the agricultural sector remains a vital part of Oman's economy. Notably, the North Batinah Governorate has maintained its position as the country's primary tomato-producing region, contributing a substantial 155,241 tons to the overall yield. This region's consistent productivity is attributed to its advantageous climate and strong farming infrastructure, reinforcing its status as a key agricultural center within Oman.
records.institution: The National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI)

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture opened a new agricultural office in Tulkarm Governorate to improve farmer access to services.
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture opened a new agricultural office in Tulkarm Governorate to improve farmer access to services. He also inaugurated several agricultural projects, including a water tank and road paving project, a solar energy project for a well, and distributed nylon rolls to greenhouse farmers. These projects, funded by FAO/Canada and the Palestinian Hydrology Group/Netherlands, aim to develop the agriculture and water sector, improve infrastructure, and support farmers affected by challenges. The Minister met with local officials and farmers to discuss needs and enhance cooperation, emphasizing the Ministry's commitment to supporting farmers and achieving food security.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has implemented projects in the northern Jordan Valley, Bethlehem, and southern Hebron to support farmers and...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has implemented projects in the northern Jordan Valley, Bethlehem, and southern Hebron to support farmers and enhance food security. In the Jordan Valley, agricultural inputs were distributed to 31 farmers. In Bethlehem, 145 churns were provided to farmers. In southern Hebron, 38 farmers received support for home garden rehabilitation, including water tanks, irrigation systems, and seeds, along with training and psychological support. These projects, in cooperation with local and international institutions, aim to improve agricultural production, increase rural incomes, and build farmer resilience against economic challenges.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Ministry of Municipality in Qatar is highlighting the success of local produce sale yards, particularly during Ramadan, where they se...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality in Qatar is highlighting the success of local produce sale yards, particularly during Ramadan, where they see increased consumer demand and trust. These markets, established in 2012, have developed significantly, offering fresh, local products at competitive prices, reducing intermediaries, and boosting farmers' profits. Open during specific hours throughout Ramadan, these markets are regulated to ensure fair pricing and product quality, balancing producer and consumer interests. The Ministry supports farmers by providing free sales outlets, technical assistance, and packaging, while also collaborating on initiatives to distribute produce to low-income families and support home-based businesses.
records.institution: The Agricultural Affairs Department at the Ministry of Municipality

records.title: Researchers at King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology (KACST) have developed a vertical farming system that drastically reduces s...
records.description: Researchers at King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology (KACST) have developed a vertical farming system that drastically reduces saffron cultivation time to 10 days, compared to the traditional four to six weeks. Utilizing artificial lighting with specific wavelengths and climate control, they've created an optimal growing environment, addressing Saudi Arabia's challenging climate. This innovation aims to capitalize on the growing global saffron market and reduce the Kingdom's substantial saffron imports. The technology not only enhances agricultural productivity and crop quality but also contributes to environmental and economic sustainability by reducing carbon emissions, conserving resources, and promoting self-sufficiency in alignment with Saudi Vision 2030.
records.institution: Saudi researchers at King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology (KACST)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) has significantly improved Yemen's energy sector through various proje...
records.description: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) has significantly improved Yemen's energy sector through various projects. These initiatives enhance essential services like education and healthcare by improving energy efficiency and promoting renewable energy use. SDRPY projects have ensured 100% reliability of electricity in its healthcare facilities via independent power systems. They've also expanded the Al-Ghaydah power plant, improved distribution networks, and implemented solar-powered lighting in public spaces. These energy sector projects are part of a broader effort supporting eight key sectors across Yemen.
records.institution: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY)

records.title: Tunisia is focusing on its hill lakes and dams to bolster water security and adapt to climate change, according to the Ministry of Agricu...
records.description: Tunisia is focusing on its hill lakes and dams to bolster water security and adapt to climate change, according to the Ministry of Agriculture. The country currently has 925 hill lakes, storing approximately 17 million cubic meters of water and irrigating 11,000 hectares of farmland. A rehabilitation program for 74 lakes, with a budget of 4.15 million dinars, is underway, and 11 new lakes are planned for construction by 2025-2026 at a cost of 7 million dinars. The government also plans to restore 235 hill dams with a 400 million cubic meter storage capacity. These efforts, emphasized by the Secretary of State for Water Resources, aim to ensure a stable water supply for agriculture and enhance resilience against climate change.

records.title: Edita Food Industries S.A.E.
records.description: Edita Food Industries S.A.E. reported a record-breaking financial year in 2024, with revenues surging by 33.2% to EGP 16.1 billion. This growth was driven by strategic diversification, successful pricing strategies that countered inflation, and significant regional expansion. Net profit reached EGP 1.4 billion, fueled by revenue increases across all product segments, notably the cake segment, which contributed over 50% of total revenue. The company's regional expansion, especially in Morocco and its entry into the Iraqi market, significantly boosted export sales.

records.title: Tomato producers from France and Morocco are set to sign a bilateral agreement in mid-March to regulate tomato seasonality and ensure fai...
records.description: Tomato producers from France and Morocco are set to sign a bilateral agreement in mid-March to regulate tomato seasonality and ensure fair market competition. This agreement aims to prevent overlap between Moroccan and French cherry tomato seasons, addressing tensions stemming from price competition. Negotiations have been ongoing, with multiple meetings held to reach a consensus.

records.title: The Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources reported that nearly 290,000 livestock animals were made available to co...
records.description: The Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources reported that nearly 290,000 livestock animals were made available to consumers in the first two months of 2025, with a significant majority being sheep and goats. To meet increased demand during Ramadan and Eid Al Fitr, the Ministry has issued numerous import permits, allowing for a larger total potential import. Veterinary quarantine measures are being strictly enforced to prevent the spread of animal diseases.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) is developing an AI-powered robotic system to automate date palm harvesting, a...
records.description: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) is developing an AI-powered robotic system to automate date palm harvesting, aiming to revolutionize Saudi Arabia's agriculture sector. The system, featuring robotic arms with high-precision visual sensors, will automate tasks like harvesting, pollination, and tree maintenance, promising increased yields and improved date quality. Field trials are planned for 2025, with full operation expected within three years. KAUST envisions a Robots-as-a-Service model to make the technology accessible to smaller farmers. The project is expected to enhance Saudi Arabia's agricultural technology and expertise, attracting talent and providing training opportunities for local laborers.
records.institution: The King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: A new direct producer-consumer sales point opened in Jendouba, initiated by the Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries, with support...
records.description: A new direct producer-consumer sales point opened in Jendouba, initiated by the Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries, with support from local cooperatives and traders. This initiative aims to provide citizens with affordable products, especially during Ramadan, by offering goods at prices lower than those in the municipal market. The sales point also offers producers a platform to sell directly to consumers, and further trader participation is expected to expand the product range.
records.institution: The Regional Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (URAP)

records.title: During the first week of Ramadan, economic control brigades in Manouba, Tunisia, seized significant quantities of subsidized goods, inclu...
records.description: During the first week of Ramadan, economic control brigades in Manouba, Tunisia, seized significant quantities of subsidized goods, including flour, sugar, semolina, and superior flour. Following nearly 1,500 inspection visits, 177 economic violations were recorded across various sectors, including fruit and vegetables, food products, and bakeries. The violations primarily involved failure to display prices, illegal price increases, use of unapproved weighing tools, and non-compliance with subsidy regulations.

records.title: Tunisia's dams are at a concerning fill level, with reserves showing minimal change from the previous year but a slight decline compared...
records.description: Tunisia's dams are at a concerning fill level, with reserves showing minimal change from the previous year but a slight decline compared to the recent average, as reported by the National Observatory of Agriculture. Northern dams hold the bulk of the country's water, while central dams are critically low. Water inflow into the dams is limited, and the Ministry of Agriculture is exploring solutions like increasing dam heights and building new ones. Tunisia experiences significant water insecurity, ranking poorly in global drought and water stress indices, worsened by climate change. The agricultural sector, a major water consumer, is heavily impacted. The country's low water availability per person highlights the urgent need to address scarcity, with both public and official actions contributing to the problem.

records.title: Emirati seeds, studied at the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), have been deposited in the Svalbard Global Seed Vaul...
records.description: Emirati seeds, studied at the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), have been deposited in the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, the "Doomsday Vault," in the Arctic. This first-of-its-kind deposit from the Gulf region safeguards climate-resilient crops, including those from the UAE's Ghaf tree. ICBA's seeds, chosen for their tolerance to extreme conditions, represent decades of research and ensure future access to vital genetic resources. This initiative, with over 1.3 million seed samples stored, reinforces the UAE's commitment to global food security and sustainability.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: A meeting in Sana'a province, Yemen, addressed the development of contract farming and the empowerment of agricultural associations to bo...
records.description: A meeting in Sana'a province, Yemen, addressed the development of contract farming and the empowerment of agricultural associations to boost agricultural output. Discussions centered on improving farmer coordination, achieving self-sufficiency, and establishing collection centers. Participants highlighted the potential of local associations and the need for institutional development, including training for contract farming coordinators. Challenges such as input shortages were discussed, along with the importance of product quality and water initiatives. Officials emphasized the need for trained coordinators, diversified crop production, and collaboration between associations and traders. The local authority reiterated its commitment to supporting agricultural associations and enhancing food production. Efforts to provide improved seeds, implement agricultural projects, and offer training in various agricultural practices were also outlined, aiming to achieve food security.

records.title: Egypt's wheat procurement, now handled by Mostakbal Misr, has caused a 10% price increase and supply chain strain.
records.description: Egypt's wheat procurement, now handled by Mostakbal Misr, has caused a 10% price increase and supply chain strain. The shift from GASC has reduced transparency and increased reliance on local importers of Russian wheat. Mostakbal Misr faces financing complications as international partners still recognize GASC, and delivery delays have occurred, reducing Egypt's wheat reserves.

records.title: Iraq is experiencing a severe outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, leading to public anger and accusations of government mismanagement.
records.description: Iraq is experiencing a severe outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, leading to public anger and accusations of government mismanagement. Videos showing dead livestock have fueled these criticisms. There are allegations that the outbreak stemmed from the import of infected African calves using forged documents, a claim the government denies. An Iraqi MP has suggested political involvement in the alleged import, while others point to lax monitoring of legal imports. Farmers, particularly in Basra, report a lack of support, including vaccine shortages and abandoned quarantine procedures. Some analysts are even alleging that the outbreak has been intentionally worsened to discredit the Prime Minister's administration.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Jordan is developing its $6.3 billion uranium reserves to boost energy security and economic growth, partnering with Kazakhstan for minin...
records.description: Jordan is developing its $6.3 billion uranium reserves to boost energy security and economic growth, partnering with Kazakhstan for mining technology. They'll produce yellowcake domestically, using cost-effective extraction methods and addressing water scarcity with treated groundwater. Jordan aims for both domestic nuclear energy use and exports, investing in local workforce training and adhering to international safety standards.

records.title: Jordan's olive oil production significantly increased by 43.2 percent in the 2024/2025 season, reaching 35,828 tonnes.
records.description: Jordan's olive oil production significantly increased by 43.2 percent in the 2024/2025 season, reaching 35,828 tonnes. This surge is due to favorable agricultural conditions and improved olive yields. Irbid Governorate led in olive processing and oil production, while Aqaba had the lowest output. The total value of olive oil produced is estimated at JD223.9 million. Jordan is also focusing on grain procurement, issuing tenders to import 120,000 metric tons of milling wheat and 120,000 tons of animal feed barley. These efforts aim to secure food supplies and meet local demand.

records.title: Oman Flour Mills (OFM), a government-owned food company, is introducing millet cultivation in Oman to reduce grain import reliance.
records.description: Oman Flour Mills (OFM), a government-owned food company, is introducing millet cultivation in Oman to reduce grain import reliance. Millet, a nutrient-rich cereal, is adaptable to Oman's climate and supports food security. OFM is importing millet seeds and leveraging its existing grain storage and milling infrastructure. This initiative aligns with global trends and UN efforts to promote millet. It also builds on Oman's recent increase in domestic wheat procurement, demonstrating OFM's commitment to a more self-sufficient and sustainable agricultural sector.

records.title: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture has launched a project in Qalqilya to improve farmers' access to land and water, enhancing food a...
records.description: The Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture has launched a project in Qalqilya to improve farmers' access to land and water, enhancing food and water security. In partnership with the "Together" Development Center and with support from the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development, the project targets communities in Azzun, Asla, and Ezbet al-Tabib. Key components include rehabilitating a groundwater well, reclaiming agricultural land, building an agricultural road, installing water transmission lines, and distributing individual water networks. This initiative aims to promote sustainable agriculture, empower farmers, and build resilience against environmental and economic challenges, aligning with the "Green Palestine" vision and national food security goals.

records.title: Emirati seeds, studied at the International Centre for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), have been deposited in the Svalbard Global Seed Vaul...
records.description: Emirati seeds, studied at the International Centre for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA), have been deposited in the Svalbard Global Seed Vault in the Arctic. This marks the first deposit from the Gulf region, safeguarding climate-resilient crops. The seeds, including those from the UAE's national Ghaf tree, are selected for their tolerance to drought, heat, and salinity. The "Doomsday Vault" protects seeds from global crises, and ICBA's contribution, representing decades of research, ensures future access to vital genetic resources. ICBA, with its extensive gene bank, focuses on crops for arid environments, reinforcing the UAE's commitment to food security and sustainability.
records.institution: The International Centre for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: Morocco is significantly increasing its fresh raspberry exports to the UK, becoming the leading supplier in that market.
records.description: Morocco is significantly increasing its fresh raspberry exports to the UK, becoming the leading supplier in that market. Export volumes have more than doubled in the first six months of the current season compared to the previous one, and Morocco has become the world's second-largest raspberry exporter. The country is benefiting from growing demand, favorable climate, and increased producer expertise, leading to record export revenues. The export season runs from September to June, with peak shipments expected in the coming months, suggesting further record-breaking potential.

records.title: Balady Poultry Company reported a net profit of SAR 118.11 million in 2024, marking a 17.04% year-on-year increase from SAR 100.91 millio...
records.description: Balady Poultry Company reported a net profit of SAR 118.11 million in 2024, marking a 17.04% year-on-year increase from SAR 100.91 million in 2023. The company's revenue also saw substantial growth, soaring by 16.58% to SAR 887.11 million, up from SAR 760.97 million in the previous year. The earnings per share (EPS) improved to SAR 17.98, compared to SAR 15.36 in 2023. These positive results reflect strong performance throughout the year, with notable increases in both net profit and revenue observed during the first nine months and the first half of 2024.

records.title: The Syrian Grain Corporation is issuing an internal, expedited request for proposals to procure 165 grinding cylinders for its mills, wit...
records.description: The Syrian Grain Corporation is issuing an internal, expedited request for proposals to procure 165 grinding cylinders for its mills, with detailed specifications provided, presenting a time-sensitive opportunity for local industrial equipment suppliers specializing in milling equipment.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Abu Dhabi's TAQA and Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power, along with other international and local firms, have been awarded green hydrogen projects...
records.description: Abu Dhabi's TAQA and Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power, along with other international and local firms, have been awarded green hydrogen projects in Morocco, totaling nearly $32 billion. The Moroccan government selected these companies, including Chinese, German, and Spanish firms, for six projects in South Morocco. The projects will focus on producing ammonia, industrial fuel, and green steel. Consortia include ORNX (American, Spanish, German), TAQA/Cepsa (Emirati, Spanish), Nareva (Moroccan), ACWA Power (Saudi), and a Chinese consortium of UEG and China Three Gorges.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (Dewa) is seeking international developers for the 1,600MW (expandable to 2,000MW) seventh phase of...
records.description: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (Dewa) is seeking international developers for the 1,600MW (expandable to 2,000MW) seventh phase of the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park. This phase will feature photovoltaic solar panels and a 1,000MW battery energy storage system with a 6,000MWh capacity, making it one of the world's largest solar-plus-storage projects. Implemented under an independent power producer (IPP) model, it's expected to produce 4.5 terawatt-hours annually, reducing natural gas consumption and carbon emissions. The project will increase the solar park's capacity to 7,260MW, raising Dubai's clean energy share to 34% by 2030. The project is scheduled for phased operation between 2027 and 2029, with a March 21 deadline for expressions of interest.

records.title: The agricultural sector in Marib province has begun distributing pesticides to combat wheat rust and fall armyworm in maize crops.
records.description: The agricultural sector in Marib province has begun distributing pesticides to combat wheat rust and fall armyworm in maize crops. The distribution, overseen by the director of the agricultural sector, will be done through local agriculture sector branches to ensure the pesticides reach affected farmers. This initiative is part of an agricultural expansion project and aims to protect crops and maintain agricultural production.

records.title: Iraq's Supreme Council for Youth has launched the "Mubadara Al-Khair" (Initiative of Goodness) program to support young entrepreneurs in...
records.description: Iraq's Supreme Council for Youth has launched the "Mubadara Al-Khair" (Initiative of Goodness) program to support young entrepreneurs in agriculture, food security, livestock, and climate sectors. The program, directed by the Prime Minister, provides loans, training, mentorship, modern equipment support, and follow-up to ensure project sustainability.

records.title: The Jerash Agriculture Directorate has temporarily closed the Jumla Forestry Nursery for rehabilitation and investment to benefit the loc...
records.description: The Jerash Agriculture Directorate has temporarily closed the Jumla Forestry Nursery for rehabilitation and investment to benefit the local community. The Directorate plans to improve nurseries in the governorate, planting one million forestry seedlings in other locations affected by fires. They will also organize an exhibition for local agricultural products. Market inspections are being intensified to ensure the quality of plant and animal products. The Jumla Nursery, established in 1953, will undergo maintenance to align with regional needs.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has maintained the suspension of lemon imports due to an oversupply of domestic lemons, while continuing to m...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has maintained the suspension of lemon imports due to an oversupply of domestic lemons, while continuing to monitor market conditions. It also announced the start of Clementine imports from all sources in mid-March. Furthermore, watermelon imports from Saudi Arabia have been approved, with a deadline for entry set for the 15th of the current month.

records.title: The Agropole of Béni Mellal, an industrial hub aimed at boosting agro-industrial transformation, is attracting new investors, including a...
records.description: The Agropole of Béni Mellal, an industrial hub aimed at boosting agro-industrial transformation, is attracting new investors, including a factory specializing in irrigation pipe accessories. This project, led by Webrick's SARL, represents a 40 million dirham investment and will create around 30 jobs. However, the Agropole is developing at a measured pace, with only about 20 projects operational out of 360 available lots since its 2021 launch. Despite this, the Agropole offers attractive land prices, strategic location near the Tadla agricultural basin, and good transportation access.

records.title: Date production in Oman is a vital part of the nation's economy, with significant yields reported.
records.description: Date production in Oman is a vital part of the nation's economy, with significant yields reported. Several regions contribute, and a variety of date types are cultivated. The average consumption of dates per person is high, reflecting their cultural and nutritional importance. The date sector supports numerous livelihoods and related industries. Efforts are underway to further develop the industry through initiatives aimed at increasing production and research focused on preserving unique date varieties. Priorities include improving supply chains, marketing strategies, and ensuring sustainable agricultural practices to enhance the country's position in the global date market.
records.institution: The National Centre for Statistics and Information

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), distributed plastic...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), distributed plastic roofs for greenhouses to one hundred farmers in Jericho and the Jordan Valley Governorate. This initiative aims to empower greenhouse farmers and enhance their resilience.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture reports a significant increase in red meat production, exceeding 270,000 tons.
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture reports a significant increase in red meat production, exceeding 270,000 tons. This growth has led to a 61% self-sufficiency rate, supporting food security and aligning with Vision 2030 goals. The increase is attributed to livestock sector development, support for local breeders, and the adoption of advanced technologies. The Kingdom's livestock inventory includes millions of sheep, goats, cows, and camels.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), in coordination with the Animal Wealth Department and the Agriculture...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), in coordination with the Animal Wealth Department and the Agriculture Department, held a training workshop in Al-Fashqa locality. The workshop, attended by producers and investors, focused on studying value-added chains in agricultural and animal products. It aimed to help small farmers, herders, and fishermen increase their incomes by transforming local products into higher-value industries for regional and global markets. The workshop also addressed financing and modernization of agricultural cooperatives and business models.
records.institution: Animal Wealth Department and the Agriculture Department

records.title: Tunisia's agricultural sector saw significant growth in 2024 due to strong private investment support.
records.description: Tunisia's agricultural sector saw significant growth in 2024 due to strong private investment support. The Tunisian Agency for the Promotion of Agricultural Investments (APIA) reported 444.6 million Tunisian dinars invested in 3,001 projects, creating 3,000 jobs. These investments included new projects, expansions, and renewals, with notable job creation in Kairouan and Kasserine. Grants totaling 129.4 million dinars were provided, encouraging investment in sectors like aquaculture and agri-food processing. This investment surge highlights Tunisia's efforts to modernize and diversify its agricultural sector.
records.institution: The Tunisian Agency for the Promotion of Agricultural Investments (APIA)

records.title: The Central Wholesale Market in Amman, Jordan, processed a significant amount of produce, with notable price increases for okra and molok...
records.description: The Central Wholesale Market in Amman, Jordan, processed a significant amount of produce, with notable price increases for okra and molokhia. Prices for other vegetables and fruits varied, with some remaining relatively stable while others, like grape leaves and zucchini, remained high. The price fluctuations are attributed to increased demand during Ramadan and seasonal production factors. The market continues to supply local markets with large shipments to meet consumer demand.
records.institution: The Central Wholesale Market in Amman

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and the FAO have launched an initiative to support farmers in the Bekaa and Baalbek-Hermel regions b...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and the FAO have launched an initiative to support farmers in the Bekaa and Baalbek-Hermel regions by distributing 166 tons of potato seeds. This initiative aims to help farmers recover from economic and environmental crises, enhance food security, and ensure sustainable local production. The distribution targets small farmers to improve potato production, a key crop in the Lebanese agricultural economy. Officials emphasized the importance of supporting farmers for the country's food security and pledged continued cooperation to find sustainable solutions for the agricultural sector.

records.title: Moroccan mandarin imports are experiencing significant growth, with importers noting excellent fruit quality and abundant supply.
records.description: Moroccan mandarin imports are experiencing significant growth, with importers noting excellent fruit quality and abundant supply. The fruit is seen as a valuable addition to domestic offerings, particularly for promotional purposes. Imports of a specific variety begin in January and continue through spring, primarily targeting the northeastern United States. Increased demand has led to the expansion of supply networks.

records.title: The Moroccan greenhouse sector is expanding, challenging Spain's dominance in the European market.
records.description: The Moroccan greenhouse sector is expanding, challenging Spain's dominance in the European market. Morocco's competitive production costs, driven by affordable labor and favorable climate, are attracting European buyers. Modernization efforts, including high-tech greenhouses and sustainable practices like drip irrigation and reduced pesticide use, are boosting yields and meeting European standards. While facing climate challenges, especially water management, Morocco's adaptation strategies and strong European demand position it as a key player in greenhouse agriculture.

records.title: As part of a project to boost economic growth through agricultural value chain development, implemented by the FAO and the Ministry of Ag...
records.description: As part of a project to boost economic growth through agricultural value chain development, implemented by the FAO and the Ministry of Agriculture, farmers from a field school received mango crop support. This support included electric scissors, compost bags, organic fertilizer, and an irrigation network for a demonstration site. The field school consists of 15 farmers from the Qalqilya, Habla, and Al-Azab areas.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Konya Food and Agriculture University in Turkey visited Gedaref University in Sudan, inspecting...
records.description: The Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Konya Food and Agriculture University in Turkey visited Gedaref University in Sudan, inspecting its agricultural facilities, including nutrition laboratories, a remote sensing center, engineering workshops, and a vegetable farm. The visit aimed to explore potential cooperation between the two universities in agricultural investment, student training, and joint research projects. Gedaref University officials expressed openness to partnerships and knowledge exchange.

records.title: The General Corporation for Grain Trade, Storage, and Manufacturing is conducting an internal tender for the expedited procurement of ele...
records.description: The General Corporation for Grain Trade, Storage, and Manufacturing is conducting an internal tender for the expedited procurement of electric motors, an air compressor, and a dryer for use in specific mills, with detailed terms and conditions provided, offering a time-sensitive opportunity for local industrial equipment suppliers.
records.institution: The General Organization for Grain Trade, Storage and Processing

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Algeria, Tunisia, Austria, Germany, and Italy have agreed to build the SoutH2 hydrogen pipeline to transport green hydrogen from North Af...
records.description: Algeria, Tunisia, Austria, Germany, and Italy have agreed to build the SoutH2 hydrogen pipeline to transport green hydrogen from North Africa to the EU by 2030. However, doubts have been raised about the feasibility of this project, with experts suggesting that neither Algeria nor Tunisia will be able to produce enough green hydrogen for export by the pipeline's operational date. The EU aims to import large quantities of green hydrogen to decarbonize its industries, and North Africa's potential is seen as crucial. However, large-scale production in Algeria and Tunisia is not expected for at least a decade, and infrastructure projects like pipelines face significant challenges and potential delays.

records.title: Private agricultural investments in Tunisia have seen substantial growth, with thousands of operations approved, totaling hundreds of mil...
records.description: Private agricultural investments in Tunisia have seen substantial growth, with thousands of operations approved, totaling hundreds of millions of dinars. These investments span various sectors, including agriculture, fisheries, and related services, and are expected to generate thousands of jobs. Community-based organizations and agricultural groups have also benefited from these investments and associated subsidies. Foreign investment has focused on specific areas like geothermal culture. Land acquisition has been facilitated through approved land credits.

records.title: Etihad Water and Electricity (EtihadWE) is supporting the UAE's food and water security efforts by providing sustainable solutions for th...
records.description: Etihad Water and Electricity (EtihadWE) is supporting the UAE's food and water security efforts by providing sustainable solutions for the agricultural sector. They are promoting the use of desalinated water for irrigation, which reduces reliance on groundwater and offers cost savings for farmers through a revised tariff structure. Over 1,300 farmers have benefited from these reduced tariffs. EtihadWE, in collaboration with the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure and the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, is committed to the UAE Water Security Strategy 2036, the National Food Security Strategy 2051, and other national initiatives. The focus is on enhancing water consumption efficiency and promoting responsible resource management for sustainable agriculture.

records.title: A new trivalent poultry vaccine is being introduced to the Egyptian market to protect against three major poultry diseases.
records.description: A new trivalent poultry vaccine is being introduced to the Egyptian market to protect against three major poultry diseases. This vaccine offers protection against viral infections that cause paralysis, tumors, and immune system weakening, as well as avian influenza. The vaccine is administered early, providing protection by bridging the gap between maternal antibodies and active immunity. Developed with advanced technologies, it offers broad protection and allows for differentiation between infected and vaccinated birds. Avian influenza continues to pose a major threat to poultry production globally, causing significant losses in poultry farms and household flocks.

records.title: Egypt has secured €90 million in soft funding from the European Commission, through the European Investment Bank (EIB), to upgrade its gr...
records.description: Egypt has secured €90 million in soft funding from the European Commission, through the European Investment Bank (EIB), to upgrade its grain storage and logistics infrastructure. This funding, part of a larger Food Resilience Project supported by the EU and World Bank, will enhance the General Authority for Supply Commodities' (GASC) wheat importation and storage capacity. Egypt is also investing in new grain storage facilities in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) and partnering with China's FAMSUN to improve agricultural infrastructure and ensure food security.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt's Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy, outlined the government's commitment to ensuring a stable and high-quality electric...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy, outlined the government's commitment to ensuring a stable and high-quality electricity supply. The ministry is implementing an urgent plan to enhance generation, transmission, and distribution systems, aiming to improve efficiency, reduce losses, and ensure reliability. Egypt is focused on expanding renewable energy, targeting 42% of the energy mix by 2030 and 65% by 2040, while modernizing the grid. The ministry is also integrating modern technology, upgrading infrastructure, and improving customer service through smart meter installations and digital platforms.
records.institution: The Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Shouf Beekeepers Association and the Shouf Biosphere Reserve, held a workshop to p...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in collaboration with the Shouf Beekeepers Association and the Shouf Biosphere Reserve, held a workshop to promote sustainable beekeeping practices in the Shouf region of Lebanon. The workshop focused on transitioning to organic treatments, such as oxalic and formic acids, to combat the Varroa mite. The Minister of Agriculture emphasized the Ministry's commitment to supporting the beekeeping sector through policies and training. Participants discussed best practices and agreed to establish a national committee to improve honey quality and protect the beekeeping sector.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, The Shouf Beekeepers Association

records.title: Morocco: Saray Immo partners with Empower New Energy for a major solar project
records.description: Saray Immo, a major Moroccan industrial and logistics platform, has partnered with Norway's Empower New Energy in a 12-year solar energy agreement. The $3.5 million investment will fund the construction and operation of two solar power plants, totaling 5.8 MWp, on Saray Immo and Tanakoo sites in Berrechid. Covering 49,000 square meters of rooftop space, the solar installation is expected to generate 9,600 MWh of clean electricity annually, reducing operational costs.

records.title: Soil salinity is a significant agricultural challenge worldwide, particularly in Africa and Morocco, leading to land degradation and redu...
records.description: Soil salinity is a significant agricultural challenge worldwide, particularly in Africa and Morocco, leading to land degradation and reduced crop yields. Biosaline agriculture is presented as a crucial solution, utilizing salt-tolerant crops and saline groundwater irrigation. Research institutions are actively involved in developing and testing these methods, working closely with farmers through experimental platforms. Challenges include limited availability of suitable crop varieties, farmer resistance to change, and policy gaps. Biosaline agriculture is seen as a complementary approach to desalination, offering a sustainable way to address water scarcity and soil degradation. Integrating salinity management into national agricultural policies is essential to ensure long-term food security and land productivity.

records.title: Oman Water Week (OWW) 2025, hosted by Nama Water Services under the patronage of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth & Water Re...
records.description: Oman Water Week (OWW) 2025, hosted by Nama Water Services under the patronage of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth & Water Resources, will serve as a crucial platform for advancing water sector dialogue, innovation, and collaboration in the region. The event, held in Muscat, will feature over 2,500 participants, expert speakers, and exhibitors, focusing on solutions for water resilience, efficiency, and sustainability. Through strategic, municipal, and industrial conference tracks, alongside an exhibition showcasing the latest technologies, OWW 2025 aims to facilitate knowledge sharing, strategic discussions, and new partnerships to address pressing water challenges. The event will also include site visits to key water infrastructure projects, and is organized by Raya Services. It is designed to bring together industry leaders, policymakers, and innovators to drive progress towards sustainable water solutions.
records.institution: Nama Water Services, The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth & Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources in Oman, in partnership with Zubair Enterprises Development Centre and the FAO...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources in Oman, in partnership with Zubair Enterprises Development Centre and the FAO, has launched an 'Agricultural Ecotourism in Aflaj Systems' project in Balad Sayt. The project aims to revitalize rural areas, promote sustainable agriculture, and preserve cultural heritage by showcasing the village's unique aflaj systems. Balad Sayt, with its rich agricultural heritage and terraced fields, was chosen for the pilot program, which could expand to other areas. The project will support the local economy by promoting local products and creating opportunities for farmers.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in collaboration with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, has announc...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, in collaboration with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, has announced 21 new investment opportunities in Al Buraimi Governorate, Oman, through the "Tatweer" platform. These opportunities, covering 659.4 acres, include agricultural projects, animal production units, and water bottling units, aimed at boosting food security and agricultural investment. Projects include palm tree and date production, and large-scale potato and onion cultivation in various areas.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning

records.title: Halal Products Development Company (HPDC) and Al Watania Poultry have formed a strategic agreement to expand their presence in the Middle...
records.description: Halal Products Development Company (HPDC) and Al Watania Poultry have formed a strategic agreement to expand their presence in the Middle East, focusing on innovation and supply chain enhancement in the halal industry. Al Watania Poultry, a major Saudi poultry producer, is also partnering with Kantar for market research. These collaborations are part of Al Watania's efforts to adapt to market changes and strengthen Saudi food security. Despite potential ownership changes being evaluated, Al Watania Poultry continues to invest in infrastructure and production capacity.
records.institution: Halal Products Development Company (HPDC), Al Watania Poultry

records.title: The Qassim Region witnessed the signing of an SAR 8.5 billion contract for the Jubail-Buraydah Independent Water Transmission Pipeline Pr...
records.description: The Qassim Region witnessed the signing of an SAR 8.5 billion contract for the Jubail-Buraydah Independent Water Transmission Pipeline Project, aimed at enhancing water security in Saudi Arabia. The project, linking the Eastern and Qassim regions, will transport up to 650,000 cubic meters of desalinated water daily over 587 kilometers. It features a reverse pumping capability and includes the construction of strategic reservoirs in Al-Shimasiyah Governorate and Jubail City. The initiative reflects the government's commitment to developing water infrastructure and aligns with Saudi Vision 2030, emphasizing private sector partnerships for improved service quality and efficiency.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: an external tender announcement for the direct and expedited procurement of 100,000 metric tons of soft bread wheat, inviting internation...
records.description: an external tender announcement for the direct and expedited procurement of 100,000 metric tons of soft bread wheat, inviting international companies to submit competitive price offers, indicating a large-scale, time-sensitive opportunity for grain suppliers.
records.institution: Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection

records.title: The government approved a national waste reduction and valorization strategy, focusing on infrastructure projects like waste treatment pl...
records.description: The government approved a national waste reduction and valorization strategy, focusing on infrastructure projects like waste treatment plants and recycling centers across various regions. Policy changes will incentivize a circular economy through tax benefits and regulations, including mandatory use of recycled materials in construction. International partnerships and technological advancements are prioritized to improve waste management, alongside enhanced medical waste sterilization and public awareness campaigns. The strategy emphasizes sustainable financing, improved governance, and a strong legal framework with penalties to ensure compliance, aiming for a nationwide shift towards environmentally responsible practices.
records.institution: The Prime Ministry, The Ministry of Interior

records.title: Tunisia is distributing five million mosquito nets to protect dates from weather and pests, with plans for another five million.
records.description: Tunisia is distributing five million mosquito nets to protect dates from weather and pests, with plans for another five million. The government will also procure sulfur for pest control.
