records.title: Tunisian organic agricultural exports reached 50,769 thousand tons by the end of December 2024, with a value of 1,224 million dinars.
records.description: Tunisian organic agricultural exports reached 50,769 thousand tons by the end of December 2024, with a value of 1,224 million dinars. Compared to the same period the previous year, this represents a 23% decrease in quantity but a 7% increase in value. Italy is the primary destination for these exports (44%), followed by Spain (22%) and France (11%). The main exported organic products are olive oil and dates, followed by forest products.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Crown Farms, a UAE-based organic farm management company, has launched a new line of organic fertilizers to support sustainable agricultu...
records.description: Crown Farms, a UAE-based organic farm management company, has launched a new line of organic fertilizers to support sustainable agriculture and organic farming in the UAE. The fertilizers are designed to improve soil fertility, water retention, and nutrient absorption, promoting long-term sustainable crop growth. They contain essential nutrients and adhere to UAE organic standards, being free from harmful chemicals. This protects the environment and reduces reliance on synthetic fertilizers. The fertilizers are certified for use in organic farming and promote strong root growth.

records.title: The UAE is the top importer of Pakistani mangoes, importing $159.74 million worth over five years, according to a Ministry of Commerce re...
records.description: The UAE is the top importer of Pakistani mangoes, importing $159.74 million worth over five years, according to a Ministry of Commerce report. Other significant markets include the UK ($131.96 million), Kazakhstan ($93.86 million), Oman ($39.88 million), Afghanistan ($35.98 million), and Saudi Arabia ($29.61 million). Total Pakistani mango exports over the past five years reached $632.003 million. Pakistan's citrus exports for the current fiscal year have reached $30.9 million. The global demand for Pakistani mangoes, due to their unique flavor and quality, boosts the country's agricultural exports. The government continues to work on improving market access and expanding export opportunities to strengthen international trade and economic growth.

records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI), in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI), in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD), has launched the Geospatial Data Platform for Agriculture and Water Resources. This platform aims to enhance agricultural sustainability and water resource management. By 2027, it aims to reduce groundwater use in agriculture by 2% and increase the use of unconventional water resources by 8-13%, while also improving water productivity and contributing to food security through improved local produce and innovative agricultural strategies. The platform provides farmers and government entities with accessible geospatial maps and comprehensive agricultural and water data for informed decision-making and improved water demand management.
records.institution: The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI)

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: A meeting at Ibb University, chaired by the university president, discussed ways to improve the educational process at the College of Agr...
records.description: A meeting at Ibb University, chaired by the university president, discussed ways to improve the educational process at the College of Agriculture and Food Sciences, both theoretically and practically. Attendees included university vice presidents and the college dean. The meeting reviewed the outcomes of a previous meeting with the Deputy Minister of Agriculture and the head of the Agricultural Research and Extension Authority to explore joint cooperation in developing the educational process. The focus is on aligning programs and courses with applied aspects to improve plant and animal production and food industries. The university president emphasized teamwork and utilizing available resources to enhance theoretical and practical performance according to quality standards.

records.domain: Establishment or modification of food stock
records.title: Algeria's Ministry of Domestic Trade and National Market Regulation has mandated importers to bring in over 20,000 tons of red meat in Ma...
records.description: Algeria's Ministry of Domestic Trade and National Market Regulation has mandated importers to bring in over 20,000 tons of red meat in March to meet the high demand during Ramadan. This measure aims to ensure market stability and the successful implementation of the planned import program.
records.institution: The Ministry of Domestic Trade and National Market Regulation

records.title: Egypt's MSMEDA has signed an agreement with Erada Microfinance, securing EGP 60m to support approximately 1,700 micro-enterprises, priori...
records.description: Egypt's MSMEDA has signed an agreement with Erada Microfinance, securing EGP 60m to support approximately 1,700 micro-enterprises, prioritizing productive and agricultural projects. This initiative aims to generate employment, particularly for youth and women, and aligns with the state's strategy to foster micro-enterprise growth. Funding of up to EGP 242,000 per project will be available. Erada focuses on using financial technology to enhance financial inclusion and empower women and youth in the agricultural sector.

records.title: The Jordanian Parliamentary Agriculture and Water Committee discussed amendments to the Agricultural Risk Management Law of 2021.
records.description: The Jordanian Parliamentary Agriculture and Water Committee discussed amendments to the Agricultural Risk Management Law of 2021. The proposed changes aim to promote mutual support among farmers through an Agricultural Risk Solidarity Fund, mitigating the impact of agricultural risks and encouraging investment. A key amendment would allow the fund to compensate even non-participating farmers for frost damage. Discussions covered immediate compensation for natural disasters, risk insurance, compensation rates, and fund participation. MPs also called for postponing loan repayments, stabilizing feed prices, and addressing livestock health issues.
records.institution: The Parliamentary Agriculture and Water Committee

records.title: Efforts to ensure market supply have helped stabilize prices for most agricultural products, according to the Minister of Agriculture.
records.description: Efforts to ensure market supply have helped stabilize prices for most agricultural products, according to the Minister of Agriculture. Measures taken include suspending import duties and VAT on livestock and red meat imports, banning the slaughter of breeding female bovines, exempting customs duties on imported chicks, and providing financial incentives for investments in refrigeration, production units, and poultry processing facilities. An emergency program supporting seeds, plants, and fertilizers for key crops has also helped lower vegetable prices and reduce pressure on livestock.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.title: Morocco's agricultural dams currently hold 3.71 billion m³ of water, representing a 26% filling rate, with 70% of these reserves concentr...
records.description: Morocco's agricultural dams currently hold 3.71 billion m³ of water, representing a 26% filling rate, with 70% of these reserves concentrated in the Sebou and Loukkos basins. 722 million m³ has been allocated for large-scale irrigation, currently covering 52% of Morocco's irrigated land. The government has implemented measures to optimize water use in irrigated areas. Morocco is accelerating seawater desalination projects, aiming to produce over 1.7 billion m³ of desalinated water by 2030. Key projects include the near-complete Dakhla plant (37 million m³ annual capacity) and a Casablanca plant (300 million m³, with 50 million m³ for irrigation).
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Marine Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forestry

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Moroccan vegetable sector is facing a production decline, coinciding with similar challenges in other key producing regions.
records.description: The Moroccan vegetable sector is facing a production decline, coinciding with similar challenges in other key producing regions. This has disrupted the global supply of various vegetables, most notably tomatoes. In one major European production area, low temperatures and pest infestations are impacting yields and quality, particularly for peppers. While some vegetables were abundant previously, supply has decreased significantly, and the reduced Moroccan output has further strained the global market, leading to higher prices. Cold weather is also affecting harvests elsewhere, keeping prices elevated. This situation demonstrates the vulnerability of agricultural supply chains to both climate and pest-related issues, as well as the interconnectedness of global production.

records.title: A recent desert locust survey and control campaign in Oman has found the situation to be stable and under observation.
records.description: A recent desert locust survey and control campaign in Oman has found the situation to be stable and under observation. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources monitored locust propagation, breeding locations, and environmental conditions. Monitoring in Al Wusta, North A’Sharqiyah, and South A’Sharqiyah governorates revealed "individual cases" and "transitional cases" of desert locusts, prompting a successful early intervention campaign. The Ministry emphasizes regular monitoring to detect and address any developments. Desert locusts pose a significant threat to food security and cause substantial economic damage, with a small swarm capable of consuming enough food for 35,000 people daily. Each adult locust can consume its own weight in food each day.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has begun work on a pilot marine fish farming project using Recirculating A...
records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has begun work on a pilot marine fish farming project using Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) technology, a first for the country. The 8-tonne capacity project, focused on Sea Bream, is being built in Al Musannah with funding from the Ministry’s Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund. RAS technology reuses water through filtration and treatment, minimizing water and space requirements. The pilot aims to introduce new sustainable aquaculture technology, support diverse fish species cultivation, provide training for the fishing community and entrepreneurs, and encourage the growth of SME-sized fish farms, creating jobs for young Omanis.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Saudi Arabia's date exports have significantly increased, reaching 1.5 billion tonnes in 2024, up from 579 million tonnes in 2016.
records.description: Saudi Arabia's date exports have significantly increased, reaching 1.5 billion tonnes in 2024, up from 579 million tonnes in 2016. The Kingdom has over 123,000 agricultural holdings producing around 300 date varieties from more than 37 million palm trees, yielding over three million tonnes of dates annually. Over 137 factories specialize in date products. The Al-Qassim region has the highest concentration of palm trees, followed by Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province. The Kingdom has achieved a 124% self-sufficiency rate for dates, with annual production exceeding 1.6 million tonnes.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.domain: Establishment or modification of food stock
records.title: A joint decision by multiple Tunisian ministers established the regulatory stock of sterilized fresh milk at 19.6 million liters, with pe...
records.description: A joint decision by multiple Tunisian ministers established the regulatory stock of sterilized fresh milk at 19.6 million liters, with peak production lasting from March to August. Dairy processing centers were granted storage subsidies for milk from March to December. Additionally, appointments and dismissals within the higher education and research sector were announced, including the assignment of a new secretary general at the Faculty of Sciences in Tunis. The Minister of Youth and Sports also issued a decree delegating signature authority within the ministry.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Mines, and Energy, Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Trade and Export Development

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The second Al Dhaid Agriculture Exhibition is set to begin at Expo Al Dhaid.
records.description: The second Al Dhaid Agriculture Exhibition is set to begin at Expo Al Dhaid. Organized by Expo Centre Sharjah with support from the Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry and in cooperation with the Department of Agriculture and Livestock, the event brings together key players in the agricultural and farming sectors. This year's edition has expanded to include over 40 specialized companies and stakeholders across the agricultural supply chain. The exhibition will cover various aspects of agriculture, including aquaculture, ornamental plants, farm equipment, financial services, pesticides, beekeeping, and food processing. It will showcase advanced agricultural technologies and solutions, with a focus on wheat and grain cultivation in the Gulf region, hydroponic and vertical farming, smart irrigation, modern horticulture, and eco-friendly organic pesticides and fertilizers.
records.institution: Expo Centre Sharjah, The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry

records.title: Lebanon's Minister of Agriculture has signed a cooperation agreement with the German Corporation for International Cooperation (GIZ) to s...
records.description: Lebanon's Minister of Agriculture has signed a cooperation agreement with the German Corporation for International Cooperation (GIZ) to strengthen their partnership in developing Lebanon's agricultural sector. Discussions focused on joint projects to address challenges facing the sector, with an emphasis on supporting Lebanese farmers and improving food security. The agreement aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices and provide technical and financial support to farmers. The Minister highlighted the importance of this cooperation in improving Lebanon's agricultural situation, especially given the economic and environmental challenges.

records.title: Authorities in Zagora, Morocco, are enforcing new regulations on watermelon cultivation due to severe drought and water scarcity.
records.description: Authorities in Zagora, Morocco, are enforcing new regulations on watermelon cultivation due to severe drought and water scarcity. A specialized commission is conducting field checks, destroying non-compliant crops and installations. The regulations limit watermelon and yellow melon cultivation to a small area per farm and prohibit them near sensitive water sources. Joint commissions are monitoring farm water usage to ensure compliance. These actions aim to preserve crucial water resources for sustainable agriculture in the region, which has been significantly affected by the water-intensive nature of watermelon farming and the ongoing drought.

records.title: Morocco participated in the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture (GFFA) in Berlin, focusing on the theme of a sustainable bioeconomy.
records.description: Morocco participated in the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture (GFFA) in Berlin, focusing on the theme of a sustainable bioeconomy. The Minister of Agriculture highlighted Morocco's sectoral strategies (Generation Green, Halieutis, and Forests) and its commitment to transforming its food system to enhance resilience and food security, with bioeconomy development as a key component. Morocco showcased innovative practices in utilizing agri-food residues for gas production and transforming olive oil and fishing by-products into energy, biofertilizers, and aquaculture feed. The country emphasized prioritizing food security during the transition to a bioeconomy and highlighted its South-South cooperation efforts in sharing technical innovations within Africa.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.title: Morocco's Minister of Agriculture announced an upcoming meeting with the Ministries of the Interior and of Industry and Trade to address...
records.description: Morocco's Minister of Agriculture announced an upcoming meeting with the Ministries of the Interior and of Industry and Trade to address the significant price difference between agricultural production areas and local markets. This disparity, exemplified by tomatoes selling for MAD 2 per kilogram at farms but MAD 6 in markets, has drawn criticism from MPs concerned about the impact of rising prices on households, especially with Ramadan approaching. MPs highlighted the high cost of red meat (over MAD 120/kg), poultry (MAD 25-30/kg), fish, vegetables, and fruit. The Minister attributed high poultry prices to increased demand due to unaffordable red meat.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.title: Russia aims to nearly double its wheat exports to Morocco in the 2024/2025 marketing year, targeting 1 million tonnes.
records.description: Russia aims to nearly double its wheat exports to Morocco in the 2024/2025 marketing year, targeting 1 million tonnes. This comes as Morocco, a major wheat importer, faces severe drought and supply chain issues, and as France, its traditional primary supplier, experienced a significantly reduced harvest. Russia has already shipped substantially more wheat to Morocco than France in the first five months of the campaign, becoming Morocco's leading wheat supplier. Competitive pricing and high protein content have made Russian wheat attractive to Moroccan buyers. Morocco's wheat imports are projected to reach a record high to meet domestic demand.

records.title: The blueberry harvest is underway in Morocco's Larache region, with favorable weather predicting high yields and good quality.
records.description: The blueberry harvest is underway in Morocco's Larache region, with favorable weather predicting high yields and good quality. While current export volumes are respectable (80-100 tons per week), peak harvest is expected between February and April. Demand in the European market is moderate due to competition from Latin America and Spain, resulting in lower prices. Moroccan exporters are targeting alternative markets like Asia, the Gulf, and Russia, with new exports to Hong Kong.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Sales at the first Al-Kharj Festival of Saudi Dates and Coffee have surpassed SR10 million ($2.6 million).
records.description: Sales at the first Al-Kharj Festival of Saudi Dates and Coffee have surpassed SR10 million ($2.6 million). The 10-day festival, featuring 30 date companies and shops offering over 26 varieties, and 20 coffee shops selling 2-5 tonnes of coffee daily, attracted visitors with special offers, the approaching Ramadan, and access to specialized markets. Supported by government entities, the festival highlighted the cultural importance of dates and coffee in Saudi Arabia, recognizing dates as a key agricultural export and coffee as a symbol of national identity. The event also provided a platform for SMEs and specialized companies to showcase their products and aimed to enhance Al-Kharj’s reputation.

records.title: Tunisia's Trade Office (OCT) has announced its readiness to supply sufficient quantities of essential goods (rice, tea, coffee, and sugar...
records.description: Tunisia's Trade Office (OCT) has announced its readiness to supply sufficient quantities of essential goods (rice, tea, coffee, and sugar) for the month of Ramadan, a period of high consumption. The Minister of Trade and Export Development called for improved organization and transparency in distribution to prevent speculation. He also visited a red meat sales point and was briefed on plans to import refrigerated red meat to stabilize the market

records.title: The UAE launched the largest phase of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3 to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, coinciding with a newly announce...
records.description: The UAE launched the largest phase of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3 to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, coinciding with a newly announced truce. A 20-truck convoy carrying over 200 tonnes of food, winter clothing, and essential items was dispatched. This phase represents the largest effort within the operation, which has already delivered approximately 29,784 tonnes of aid via 156 convoys. The operation utilizes airlifts, ships, and trucks to transport aid from Egypt to Gaza and includes a field hospital in Gaza, a floating hospital in Arish, transfer of critical cases to UAE hospitals, water projects like desalination plants in Rafah, and airdropped aid to inaccessible areas in northern Gaza.

records.title: A "Ramadan Vegetables from Your Home" campaign, now in its fourth season and themed "Together towards self-sufficiency," has been launched.
records.description: A "Ramadan Vegetables from Your Home" campaign, now in its fourth season and themed "Together towards self-sufficiency," has been launched. Implemented by the Women's Development Department and the Women's Authority in cooperation with agricultural funding and support organizations, the campaign promotes home farming, supports food security, and aims to provide additional income for Yemeni families. Officials praised the campaign's efforts to promote self-reliance and local production as a way to address economic challenges and strengthen national sovereignty. Plans were also announced to establish a large shopping center for products from productive families and small projects to further support their development and reduce unemployment.
records.institution: The Women's Development Department and the Women's Authority

records.title: A rainwater harvesting project, funded at approximately 180 million riyals, has been inaugurated in the Sana'a basin.
records.description: A rainwater harvesting project, funded at approximately 180 million riyals, has been inaugurated in the Sana'a basin. The project, supervised by the Water Resources Authority, aims to replenish groundwater levels and support the agricultural sector by providing irrigation water. The first stage of the project involved creating a storage area with a capacity of over 135,000 cubic meters. The second stage will focus on creating entrances, exits, and sedimentation basins. This initiative aligns with directives to enhance water resource sustainability. Officials emphasized the importance of expanding such projects to preserve water resources and support agricultural development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fish Resources and Water Resources

records.title: In Tarim, Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), in partnership with local authorities and with funding from KOICA, h...
records.description: In Tarim, Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), in partnership with local authorities and with funding from KOICA, has inaugurated two infrastructure projects to address water-related issues. A surface bridge with a gabion weir in Dammon and protective gabion walls in Al-Sabir aim to mitigate flood risks, improve agriculture, and promote peace. The projects are part of the "Water for Peace" initiative launched in late 2023 to address water scarcity and environmental degradation exacerbated by climate change. The Dammon project slows floodwaters, protects farmland, recharges groundwater, and ensures safe passage during floods. The Al-Sabir project's gabion walls protect farms, distribute water more evenly, and reduce disputes among farmers.

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture inaugurated the rehabilitated fish farming center in Anjar, a joint project with the UNDP.
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture inaugurated the rehabilitated fish farming center in Anjar, a joint project with the UNDP. The project aims to strengthen the fish farming sector and contribute to sustainable development and food security in Lebanon. The Minister emphasized the importance of the project in supporting the Lebanese economy and reducing fish imports. The project, originally established in the 1940s, was renewed in partnership with the Ministry of Environment and the UNDP and includes a plan to address pollution in Lake Qaraoun. It is also intended to support the rural economy, provide equal opportunities, and protect the environment through nature-friendly technologies. Plans are in place to expand these efforts to other areas, including the upper Litani Basin, the Orontes River, and coastal rivers, as well as to fully invest in marine fish resources.

records.title: Germany's Minister for Food and Agriculture recognized Morocco as a key partner for Germany and the EU in the agricultural sector during...
records.description: Germany's Minister for Food and Agriculture recognized Morocco as a key partner for Germany and the EU in the agricultural sector during a meeting at Berlin’s Green Week. Following the meeting with Morocco's Minister of Agriculture, a declaration was signed to create a joint working group focused on strengthening collaboration in food and agriculture. The working group will address shared challenges like climate change, water management, and supporting farmers, building on existing knowledge exchange between the two countries. Morocco's presence at Green Week showcases its agricultural heritage and sustainable products, with 21 exhibitors representing 39 cooperatives from across the country.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Oman participated in the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture and the 17th Agriculture Ministers Conference in Berlin, focusing on "Farm...
records.description: Oman participated in the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture and the 17th Agriculture Ministers Conference in Berlin, focusing on "Farming a Sustainable Bioeconomy." Oman highlighted its investment program for food security (2021-2024), involving 314 projects in agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and water, with a total investment of RO 1.266 billion. These projects aim to increase productivity, reduce imports, create added value, and provide jobs, aligning with Oman Vision 2040. Oman emphasized the importance of balancing food needs with environmental preservation and enhancing the bioeconomy through sustainable use of biological resources.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Egyptian agricultural exports reached a record high in 2024, exceeding 8.6 million tons, an increase of over one million tons compared to...
records.description: Egyptian agricultural exports reached a record high in 2024, exceeding 8.6 million tons, an increase of over one million tons compared to 2023. The Minister of Agriculture credited local farmers and exporters, along with the Export Council for Agricultural Crops, the Egyptian Commercial Representation Service, the Plant Quarantine administration, and Egyptian embassies abroad. Top exports included citrus fruits, potatoes, onions, grapes, beans, sweet potatoes, mangoes, tomatoes, garlic, strawberries, guavas, and pomegranates.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Morocco's pavilion has opened at the 89th International Green Week in Berlin.
records.description: Morocco's pavilion has opened at the 89th International Green Week in Berlin. The event, focused on agriculture and food, runs until January 26th. The inauguration was led by the Moroccan and German Ministers of Agriculture. Morocco's participation aims to promote its agricultural products as benchmarks for quality and sustainability and share its expertise in environmentally friendly agriculture. The pavilion features 21 exhibitors representing 39 cooperatives from all 12 Moroccan regions, including first-time participants and women from rural areas. Key Moroccan products showcased include argan oil, olive oil, saffron, dates, and medicinal and aromatic plants, all adhering to international standards.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has made significant progress in its water sector projects, adhering to the...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has made significant progress in its water sector projects, adhering to the National Water Strategy. The Kingdom is the world's leading desalination producer, with a 4.19 million cubic meter annual capacity and operates an extensive 14,210 km water transmission network managing 19.42 million cubic meters daily. Through this strategy, the Kingdom has achieved multiple Guinness World Records for its water storage and production facilities, including the largest drinking water tank and evaporation desalination unit, and the world's largest mobile desalination plant. The Kingdom also boasts the lowest energy consumption in desalination plants. In 2024, the National Water Company (NWC) completed numerous water and sanitation projects, adding significant capacity and infrastructure.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Tunisia's dams have reached a filling rate of over 30% after recent rainfall, according to the Minister of Agriculture.
records.description: Tunisia's dams have reached a filling rate of over 30% after recent rainfall, according to the Minister of Agriculture. While this has helped replenish the water table, Tunisia continues to face a severe, multi-year water crisis, with experts advocating for a state of water emergency. The rainfall has only marginally improved the situation, as dam levels remain low. Climate change is contributing to this issue by shifting rainfall patterns southward, while most of Tunisia's dams are located in the north.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Dubai Municipality launched the second Hatta Farming Festival as part of the ‘Dubai Farms’ program, under the Hatta Winter initiative.
records.description: Dubai Municipality launched the second Hatta Farming Festival as part of the ‘Dubai Farms’ program, under the Hatta Winter initiative. The festival showcases local agricultural products and services from 25 Emirati farmers and companies, aiming to support the UAE's agricultural market and promote Hatta as an agri-tourism destination. The event aligns with Dubai's vision for sustainable agriculture, the Hatta Comprehensive Development Plan, and the ‘Grow UAE’ program. The festival includes exhibitions, workshops, dialogue sessions with experts, livestock auctions, and awards for outstanding farmers. It also provides an agricultural extension platform with free guidance and services like testing and veterinary consultations.

records.title: Egypt's state grain buyer, Mostakbal Misr, has signed wheat supply agreements with European producers to diversify sources and secure bet...
records.description: Egypt's state grain buyer, Mostakbal Misr, has signed wheat supply agreements with European producers to diversify sources and secure better prices, including some barter deals. Details on quantities, prices, and origins were not disclosed. In 2024, Egypt imported approximately 14.7 million metric tons of wheat, mainly from Russia, to supply subsidized bread. Following challenges in securing imports and replenishing strategic reserves, Mostakbal Misr replaced the GASC as the main grain buyer. Recent import increases suggest a focus on building wheat reserves. After a large, but unsuccessful, wheat purchase attempt in August 2024 due to high prices, Egypt plans to reduce wheat imports by mixing corn or sorghum into subsidized bread starting in April 2025.

records.domain: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
records.title: Juhayna, a leading Egyptian dairy and juice company, expanded into agriculture in 2008 with Enmaa, focusing on high-quality crop cultivat...
records.description: Juhayna, a leading Egyptian dairy and juice company, expanded into agriculture in 2008 with Enmaa, focusing on high-quality crop cultivation and export. The company owns citrus orchards producing oranges and lemons, with successful initial production and export volumes. Enmaa is expanding its citrus cultivation significantly over the next few years and plans to export Valencia oranges to the UK this year, leveraging its adherence to EU standards. The company already exports to the EU, the Gulf, and Russia, and is exploring new markets in the Asia Pacific region. By combining traditional farming with technology like the Dacom system, Enmaa ensures high quality.

records.title: Chicken prices in Jordan have decreased, with promotional offers appearing in stores and commercial centers, accompanied by increased sup...
records.description: Chicken prices in Jordan have decreased, with promotional offers appearing in stores and commercial centers, accompanied by increased supply. The price of dressed chicken has reached 1.75 Jordanian dinars per kilogram, while fresh chicken ranges from 2.35 to 2.5 dinars per kilogram. Average monthly fresh chicken consumption in 2024 was 14.5 million birds (21,000 tons), with annual consumption reaching 175.5 million birds. The Ministry of Industry, Trade, and Supply is monitoring prices and supply in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture and has observed a significant decrease in dressed chicken prices and both wholesale and retail fresh chicken prices.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Trade, and Supply

records.title: Morocco's watermelon exports have significantly declined in 2024 due to an ongoing drought.
records.description: Morocco's watermelon exports have significantly declined in 2024 due to an ongoing drought. Exports dropped to 113,500 tons, a 55% decrease from 2023's 249,000 tons, marking the lowest volume in eight years. Water scarcity and restrictions on watermelon farming in several provinces, due to the crop's high water consumption, are the main causes. This decline has resulted in a significant drop in export revenue, from USD 190 million in 2023 to USD 96 million in 2024, causing hardship for businesses reliant on watermelon exports. Consequently, Morocco has fallen out of the top 10 global watermelon exporters. While watermelon exports struggle, Morocco's avocado sector is projected to grow, with targeted production and exports of 90,000 tons. However, the avocado sector also faces concerns about water usage, prompting a focus on water-efficient farming techniques.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Masdar, a UAE-based renewable energy company, has announced preferred suppliers and contractors for a gigawatt-scale solar and battery st...
records.description: Masdar, a UAE-based renewable energy company, has announced preferred suppliers and contractors for a gigawatt-scale solar and battery storage project in Abu Dhabi. Developed in collaboration with EWEC, the project will provide up to 1 GW of baseload power 24/7. Larsen & Toubro (India) and POWERCHINA (China) are the preferred EPC contractors. JA Solar, Jinko Solar (both China), and CATL (China) have been selected as preferred suppliers for PV modules and battery storage. The project will include a 5.2 GW (DC) solar PV plant and a 19 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS), making it the world's largest of its kind. Jinko Solar and JA Solar will each supply 2.6 GW of PV modules using TopCon technology, and CATL will supply its TENER technology for the BESS.

records.title: Imports from non-EU countries made up 66% of the total (€2.696 billion), also a 12% increase, while EU imports accounted for 34% (€1.390...
records.description: Imports from non-EU countries made up 66% of the total (€2.696 billion), also a 12% increase, while EU imports accounted for 34% (€1.390 billion), up 13%. Overall import volume rose by 7% to 3.5 million tonnes, with third countries supplying 1.8 million tonnes and EU countries providing 1.7 million tonnes. Morocco remains Spain's top trading partner in this sector (€801 million, up 13%), followed by Peru (€501 million, up 22%), France (€426 million, up 22%), and Portugal (€350 million, up 19%). The Netherlands saw a 3% decrease in sales to Spain (€205 million).

records.title: Morocco's citrus season began poorly, particularly for Clemenules and Nour clementines shipped to the US in late 2024.
records.description: Morocco's citrus season began poorly, particularly for Clemenules and Nour clementines shipped to the US in late 2024. Quality issues like granulation, soft fruit, and poor color, combined with strong competition from California and Chile, resulted in low prices and weak demand. Hopes are now focused on the Nadorcott mandarin variety, known for its quality, with the first shipments expected soon. The Moroccan Nadorcott harvest is estimated as normal, with good quality despite slightly smaller fruit. These mandarins should be available in the US until late March or early April with no expected supply issues.

records.title: Saudi Arabian private sector leaders and Nigerian officials have agreed on a joint strategy to attract Saudi investment to Nigeria.
records.description: Saudi Arabian private sector leaders and Nigerian officials have agreed on a joint strategy to attract Saudi investment to Nigeria. The focus will be on mining, agriculture, food products, banking services, and financial technologies. During a meeting between representatives from both countries, the President of the Federation of Saudi Chambers emphasized the importance of the Saudi-Nigerian Business Council and Saudi Arabia's interest in collaborating on agriculture, livestock, and mining. Nigerian officials encouraged Saudi investment in their mining sector, highlighting untapped mineral wealth and investment incentives like tax exemptions and duty-free trade.

records.title: The National Forage Office (ONF), established in early 2024, plans to begin importing maize, oilseed meals, and other forage products in...
records.description: The National Forage Office (ONF), established in early 2024, plans to begin importing maize, oilseed meals, and other forage products in 2025. An initial call for expressions of interest has been issued for shipments ranging from 13,000 to 25,000 tons, aiming to create a shortlist of suppliers. Interested suppliers must have at least two years of experience and have completed at least one export operation of these products in the past two years. The ONF's primary missions include producing, importing, distributing, and marketing forage products, as well as maintaining reserve stocks and regulating the forage market.

records.title: The National Forage Office has announced price reductions on imported maize to benefit livestock farmers and feed manufacturers.
records.description: The National Forage Office has announced price reductions on imported maize to benefit livestock farmers and feed manufacturers. The standard selling price will be set based on actual import costs and adjusted with each shipment. Additional discounts are available for direct port collection and for those with annual supply contracts who maintain a two-month stock or confirm orders in advance. Payment terms include immediate bank transfers with a 0.5% discount or deferred payments under certain conditions. An internal unit has been established to monitor forage market prices and developments in animal nutrition, aiming to enhance market regulation.

records.title: Silal and Borouge have strengthened their partnership to promote sustainable agriculture and food security in the UAE.
records.description: Silal and Borouge have strengthened their partnership to promote sustainable agriculture and food security in the UAE. This collaboration combines Silal's expertise in sustainable farming practices, including digital farming solutions and farmer capacity building, with Borouge's innovative polyolefin solutions. The partnership will focus on research and development, implementing sustainable farming practices, and developing solutions for regional agricultural challenges. A key goal is enhancing UAE food security by increasing local food production and reducing reliance on imports.

records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, launched the ‘100,000 See...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, launched the ‘100,000 Seedlings’ initiative, distributing seedlings to public schools nationwide. This initiative aims to educate students about the importance of agriculture and greening, aligning with the ‘Plant the Emirates’ National Programme and its ‘National Agriculture Centre.’ The initiative emphasizes sustainable agriculture, community participation, and national food security. The first phase involves distributing 15,000 seedlings, provided by the Khalifa Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology and Jenaan Investment Company, with the Environment Friends Society engaging volunteers in planting.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: A four-day training course for field school facilitators, funded by the Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and In...
records.description: A four-day training course for field school facilitators, funded by the Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing, concluded in Dhamar. The course equipped 36 agricultural guides with skills to facilitate field school activities across the province, focusing on expanding grain, legume, and livestock cultivation. The importance of community involvement in agricultural cooperatives was also emphasized. Participants gained practical skills in agricultural decision-making, guidance principles, and field school facilitation methods.
records.institution: The Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing in Dhamar

records.title: Bahrain and Oman have signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) during a state visit.
records.description: Bahrain and Oman have signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) during a state visit. One MoU focuses on municipal work, aiming to exchange information, expertise, and research in this field. The second MoU, concerning agriculture, livestock production, and food security, aims to support and develop these sectors through enhanced cooperation. This includes promoting sustainable farming practices, developing advanced agricultural techniques, improving agricultural infrastructure, and encouraging collaboration in agricultural product processing. The MoU also covers cooperation in tree planting (especially mangroves), joint exhibitions, and the use of artificial intelligence in marketing agricultural products and honey. In animal production, the MoU focuses on improving techniques, animal health, training, disease control, and information exchange.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Egypt has become Europe's second-largest exporter of fresh fruits and vegetables for the 2023-2024 season, shipping 917,000 tonnes, a 7%...
records.description: Egypt has become Europe's second-largest exporter of fresh fruits and vegetables for the 2023-2024 season, shipping 917,000 tonnes, a 7% increase from the previous year. Citrus fruits led exports (500,000 tonnes, up 8%), followed by sweet potatoes (117,000 tonnes) and potatoes (over 400,000 tonnes). Despite a drop in onion exports (92,000 tonnes compared to 135,000 due to a six-month export ban), Egypt remains a strong supplier, exporting a range of other produce including carrots, lemons, garlic, beans, mangoes, peppers, strawberries, and watermelons.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Prime Minister reviews with the Head of the Food Safety Authority
records.description: The Egyptian Prime Minister met with the Head of the National Food Safety Authority to review progress on its 2023-2026 strategic plan. The plan focuses on enhancing food safety, supporting the Egyptian food production sector, building trust in Egyptian food products, promoting research and innovation, and improving human capacity and monitoring infrastructure, aligning with Egypt Vision 2030. Key achievements include: establishing technical inspection lists for food producers, launching food safety awareness campaigns, simplifying procedures for food facility operators, updating food safety legislation and regulations, establishing a risk-based food monitoring system, updating shelf-life standards for certain products, publishing an electronic magazine for legislation and research, and streamlining import procedures.

records.title: The UK and Iraq have announced a £12.3 billion ($15 billion) trade and investment package to significantly boost their economic partnership.
records.description: The UK and Iraq have announced a £12.3 billion ($15 billion) trade and investment package to significantly boost their economic partnership. The agreement, encompassing a tenfold increase in trade, includes major UK-led projects in Iraq focusing on critical infrastructure development across various sectors. Key investments target de-mining, airbase rehabilitation, water infrastructure (including large-scale water projects in Southern Iraq and Basra), power grid enhancements (including interconnection with Saudi Arabia), 5G rollout by Vodafone, railway and sanitation projects, and improvements to emergency services and border security. The UK will also support the establishment of Iraq's Strategic Investment Fund to attract further private investment. The two countries have also committed to enhanced cooperation on defense, security, migration, culture, education, women's empowerment, climate change, and sports, with a focus on shared regional and global interests.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced it is seeking investors to establish a sugar production and refining factory using sugar beet i...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced it is seeking investors to establish a sugar production and refining factory using sugar beet in the Azraq and Wadi Araba regions. This initiative aligns with the economic modernization vision, the national sustainable agriculture plan, and investment goals. Interested investors are invited to submit comprehensive economic feasibility studies, which will be evaluated by a specialized technical committee. Proposals should be submitted to the Ministry's Investment Encouragement Directorate by a specified deadline.

records.title: The Prime Minister and the Minister of Agriculture joined approximately 200 young people in Maan for a tree-planting event at Maan Univer...
records.description: The Prime Minister and the Minister of Agriculture joined approximately 200 young people in Maan for a tree-planting event at Maan University College as part of national Arbor Day celebrations. Similar events with widespread community participation took place across all governorates, with tens of thousands of trees planted. This initiative is part of a sustainable agricultural plan that includes afforestation projects in artificial forests and along roadsides to promote tree planting and preserve forestry resources. The government aims to expand green spaces in line with royal interest in the agricultural sector.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture distributed 38 tons of livestock feed to 7 beneficiaries in the northern Jordan Valley to aid those affected...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture distributed 38 tons of livestock feed to 7 beneficiaries in the northern Jordan Valley to aid those affected by settler attacks. This project, implemented with partner organizations and funded by the Protection Coalition, aims to support livestock farmers facing challenges like limited rainfall and restricted access to pastures due to the occupation, ultimately strengthening Palestinian resilience in the West Bank and East Jerusalem.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, held a workshop on beekeeping, focusing on the...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the North Hebron Agriculture Directorate, held a workshop on beekeeping, focusing on the impact of climate change on the bee sector and related seasonal activities like wintering procedures and disease control. The workshop aimed to develop and support the beekeeping sector to improve honey production quality and quantity in Palestine. Experts delivered lectures on maintaining bee colony strength through feeding during drought, combating Varroa mites using non-chemical methods, and queen bee management. Discussions covered various topics, particularly the importance of providing pastures and planting nectar-producing seedlings. The Ministry of Agriculture thanked the North Hebron Chamber of Commerce for hosting the event.

records.title: Market activity in Deir Ezzor city has declined despite a price drop of over 20% on most food items due to deteriorating economic conditi...
records.description: Market activity in Deir Ezzor city has declined despite a price drop of over 20% on most food items due to deteriorating economic conditions and delayed salary payments following the fall of the Assad regime. The price decreases are attributed to the Syrian pound's improved value against the US dollar. However, the delay in salaries, on which most residents rely, has significantly weakened purchasing power, causing people to buy smaller quantities. Prices of essential items like sugar, rice, coffee, and tea have decreased, but market activity remains weak.

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: A ministerial council was held to address challenges in the maritime fishing and aquaculture sector, focusing on illegal fishing, regulat...
records.description: A ministerial council was held to address challenges in the maritime fishing and aquaculture sector, focusing on illegal fishing, regulatory protection, governance, and infrastructure development. Eleven measures were adopted, including finalizing a national plan to combat illegal fishing, revising maritime laws, improving stakeholder coordination, amending bluefin tuna fishing regulations, strengthening public-private partnerships for port digitalization, and revising the tax system to encourage investment. These steps aim to enhance sustainability, efficiency, and growth in the sector.
records.institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: The UAE and Kenya have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to strengthen their economic ties.
records.description: The UAE and Kenya have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to strengthen their economic ties. The agreement aims to boost trade and investment, improve supply chains, and expand market access across key sectors such as agriculture, retail, healthcare, financial services, technology, and agriculture. This builds on existing trade growth between the two nations and seeks to further accelerate investment in areas like ICT, banking, infrastructure, and renewable energy, aligning with the UAE's broader economic growth objectives.

records.title: Algeria is implementing a strategy to revitalize its livestock sector and increase red meat production, aiming to reduce import dependenc...
records.description: Algeria is implementing a strategy to revitalize its livestock sector and increase red meat production, aiming to reduce import dependence and enhance food security. This plan addresses a decline in livestock numbers revealed by a recent census, highlighting issues such as illegal slaughter of breeding ewes and insufficient dairy cow numbers, exacerbated by recurring droughts and fodder shortages. The recovery plan focuses on reducing imports, utilizing local resources like corn and oil factory residues, developing pastoral reserves and fodder plantations, and supporting cereal production. Specialized centers for red meat production have been established in key regions, and a national commission has been formed to develop tailored solutions.

records.title: Egypt is becoming a dominant force in the international orange market, surpassing traditional players like Spain and Morocco due to compe...
records.description: Egypt is becoming a dominant force in the international orange market, surpassing traditional players like Spain and Morocco due to competitive pricing and an aggressive export strategy. While European citrus markets are experiencing lower-than-expected demand, Egyptian exporters have increased shipments, particularly of the Valencia variety. Egypt's increased production stems from investments in converting desert land to farmland. Lower labor costs give Egypt a significant price advantage, making it difficult for Spain and Morocco to compete. Egypt is also diversifying its export markets, targeting regions like Brazil, Canada, and Asia, despite logistical challenges.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture has implemented a solar energy project to operate an agricultural well in Qalqilya Governorate.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has implemented a solar energy project to operate an agricultural well in Qalqilya Governorate. Implemented by the ARIJ Center, supervised by the Ministry, and funded by the UNDP, this project is part of the ongoing "Tarabot" project in the area behind the wall, particularly in northern Qalqilya. It aligns with the Ministry's strategy of enhancing farmer resilience and sustainably managing natural resources to achieve food and water security. This project is the first of its kind in Palestine, using a SCADA control system to automatically operate the well pump using both solar cells and an electric generator. It also employs a solar cell guidance system to maximize energy conversion.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian government funding, provided dairy processing equipment to 105...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian government funding, provided dairy processing equipment to 105 farmers in rural areas of Bethlehem Governorate. This initiative is part of the "Supporting Economic Growth through the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in the West Bank" project, which aims to improve rural livelihoods and enhance the sustainability of the agricultural sector by increasing livestock farmers' income and addressing challenges related to rising prices and production costs. Representatives from the Bethlehem Governorate Agriculture Directorate and local organizations oversaw the equipment distribution.

records.title: The Sharjah Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA), in partnership with Emirates Nature-WWF, the UAE Ministry of Climate Change...
records.description: The Sharjah Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA), in partnership with Emirates Nature-WWF, the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, and Bee’ah, has completed a mangrove planting program in the AlQurm Protected Area, Khor Kalba. Over two weeks, 11,600 mangrove seedlings were planted. This initiative supports the UAE's goal of planting 100 million mangrove trees by 2030 and contributes to the Net Zero by 2050 Strategy. The program aims to enhance environmental sustainability, promote collaboration, and address climate change. It is part of a larger effort to expand mangrove coverage in Sharjah, with ongoing monitoring to ensure sustainability.
records.institution: The Environment and Protected Areas Authority (EPAA)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The World Future Energy Summit 2025 (WFES 2025), hosted by Masdar, has commenced in Abu Dhabi as part of Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week (A...
records.description: The World Future Energy Summit 2025 (WFES 2025), hosted by Masdar, has commenced in Abu Dhabi as part of Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week (ADSW). This three-day summit gathers global leaders, including heads of state, ministers, and industry experts, to discuss energy transition and circular economies, aiming to unlock a potential $10 trillion economic transformation. The event features numerous sessions and speakers focusing on topics like AI's role in creating a sustainable future, as well as the impact of renewable energy and climate technologies. Expected to draw over 30,000 attendees, the summit showcases innovations in renewable energy, AI, circular economy, green financing, and sustainable cities, with over 400 exhibitors presenting solutions in various sectors.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company – Masdar

records.title: An operation has been launched to distribute 122,000 hectares of agricultural land across 12 wilayas through a digital platform, in line...
records.description: An operation has been launched to distribute 122,000 hectares of agricultural land across 12 wilayas through a digital platform, in line with Executive Decree 21-432. This initiative aims to expand agricultural acreage, enhance food security, reduce imports, and promote exports. Digitization plays a key role in ensuring transparency, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making. Since the platform’s launch, over 81,000 hectares have been allocated across multiple perimeters. The Office is also investing in Geographic Information System (GIS) training to modernize field inspections and improve agricultural project management.
records.institution: The Office National des Terres Agricoles (ONTA)

records.title: The Djelfa region in Algeria is expecting a substantial late-season potato harvest, with production forecasts exceeding previous amounts.
records.description: The Djelfa region in Algeria is expecting a substantial late-season potato harvest, with production forecasts exceeding previous amounts. Harvesting has already begun, with significant yields achieved. The total area under cultivation is extensive, with key production areas contributing to the overall output. Preparations are also underway for the next planting season, with plans for even greater cultivation. These efforts aim to meet consumer demand and contribute to Algeria's goal of food self-sufficiency, reinforcing Djelfa's importance as a key agricultural region.
records.institution: The Local Directorate of Agricultural Services (DSA)

records.title: SEKEM Group, an Egyptian social enterprise, has been recognized as a 2024 Champion of the Earth by the UNEP for its "Entrepreneurial Visi...
records.description: SEKEM Group, an Egyptian social enterprise, has been recognized as a 2024 Champion of the Earth by the UNEP for its "Entrepreneurial Vision" in combating land degradation and promoting sustainable development. SEKEM's CEO, was also named one of the 100 Most Influential Africans of 2024. SEKEM's "Economy of Love" (EoL) model, prioritizing ethical practices, social responsibility, and environmental sustainability, has been developed into a certification standard by the Egyptian Biodynamic Association (EBDA) to aid farmers in transitioning to biodynamic and organic agriculture. This model has helped over 15,000 farmers convert over 55,000 acres of land.

records.title: Morocco is establishing itself as a significant avocado exporter, with a large portion of its harvest intended for international markets,...
records.description: Morocco is establishing itself as a significant avocado exporter, with a large portion of its harvest intended for international markets, primarily in Europe. While export volumes are growing, lower prices due to reduced European demand present a challenge. Moroccan farmers are encouraged to expedite harvesting to maintain competitiveness. Farm prices within Morocco have recently seen an increase. Previous export seasons have demonstrated the sector's growth, driven by expansion of cultivation areas.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian government support, distributed 5-cup water tanks to 100 sheep...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian government support, distributed 5-cup water tanks to 100 sheep farmers in several areas of the Nablus Governorate. This initiative is part of the "Supporting Economic Growth through the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in the West Bank" project, which aims to improve the living conditions of sheep farmers and their families and alleviate challenges facing the agricultural sector. These projects aim to enhance food and water security, especially given the threats and attacks faced by citizens in areas near settlements.

records.title: Qatar eyes 55% self-sufficiency in vegetables by 2030
records.description: Qatar's National Food Security Strategy 2030 aims to achieve 55% self-sufficiency in vegetable production, a 50% increase in agricultural land productivity, 30% self-sufficiency in red meat, 80% in fish, and 100% in dairy and fresh chicken. Significant progress has been made in recent years, with over 950 productive farms operating and a doubling of organic farming land last year. In 2024, over 26 million kg of local vegetables were marketed, and livestock numbers reached 1.4 million. The new strategy, building on the previous 2018-2023 strategy, includes 17 initiatives focused on promoting healthy consumption, ensuring food safety and quality, promoting sustainability and climate change adaptation, and building strong partnerships. It aligns with Qatar National Vision 2030 to develop a resilient and adaptable food system.

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Saudi Arabia is bolstering its food security strategy with a new trout farming project developed by KACST and King Abdulaziz University,...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is bolstering its food security strategy with a new trout farming project developed by KACST and King Abdulaziz University, supported by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. This initiative introduces a nutrient-rich fish species suitable for diverse environments, aiming to meet growing domestic seafood demand and reduce supply chain vulnerabilities. Aligned with Vision 2030's goal of 600,000 tonnes of annual fish production, the project uses a water-efficient recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) to enhance fish health and quality. Trout have been successfully farmed to commercial size, prompting private sector adoption of RAS technology in several regions. The focus on trout and other cold-water fish addresses the demand for protein-rich, omega-3-rich food sources.
records.institution: King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology (KACST) and King Abdulaziz University

records.title: the Saudi Reef program has provided SAR 2.4 billion in financial support to rural communities in Saudi Arabia.
records.description: the Saudi Reef program has provided SAR 2.4 billion in financial support to rural communities in Saudi Arabia. This program supports small farmers and rural producers, improving livelihoods and promoting sustainable rural development in line with Saudi Vision 2030. Over 77,400 beneficiaries have received support, with a focus on empowering rural women, who make up over 57,400 of the recipients. Saudi Reef is a key national initiative aimed at transforming rural communities and enhancing their economic and environmental sustainability.
records.institution: The Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef)

records.title: The Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA), in collaboration with 14 government agencies, has enhanced the "Saudi Authorized Econ...
records.description: The Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA), in collaboration with 14 government agencies, has enhanced the "Saudi Authorized Economic Operator Program." This program offers administrative, procedural, and financial benefits to importers, exporters, and logistics service providers (including customs brokers and shipping agents). The program aims to empower the logistics sector, facilitate trade, streamline procedures, boost competitiveness, enhance supply chain efficiency, and improve access to global markets. Participating entities include various ministries and authorities related to key economic & Agriculture sectors. Since its launch, over 550 businesses have joined the program, which is globally recognized and approved in 80 countries, aligning with World Customs Organization standards. Interested parties can find more information on ZATCA's website.
records.institution: The Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA)

records.title: Tunisia's Ministry of Trade and Export Development is collaborating with stakeholders to expand the global reach of Tunisian olive oil, t...
records.description: Tunisia's Ministry of Trade and Export Development is collaborating with stakeholders to expand the global reach of Tunisian olive oil, targeting markets in Asia, the Gulf, Russia, and Libya. The ministry is also focusing on strengthening its presence in non-traditional European markets like Switzerland, the UK, and Scandinavian countries. Statistics indicate a 12% growth in demand for extra virgin olive oil in 2024.
records.institution: The Ministry of Trade and Export Development

records.title: An organic honey products factory and laboratory has been approved for the central region of Sharjah, aiming to contribute significantly...
records.description: An organic honey products factory and laboratory has been approved for the central region of Sharjah, aiming to contribute significantly to the production and innovation of honey-based products. The facility will specialize in producing high-quality honey alongside pharmaceutical and cosmetic materials derived from honey, supporting both local and international markets. In its initial phase, the factory plans to achieve a production capacity of 120 tonnes of honey annually, emphasizing the use of organic methods to ensure sustainability and product quality. This project is expected to enhance the region's reputation as a hub for organic and health-focused products, aligning with broader agricultural and economic development goals.
records.institution: The Department of Agriculture and Livestock

records.title: Farm and land owners in Sharjah have been warned against illegally renting out their plots, a practice common during the winter season.
records.description: Farm and land owners in Sharjah have been warned against illegally renting out their plots, a practice common during the winter season. Sharjah Municipality emphasizes that these lands are allocated for authorized activities like agriculture and livestock rearing to support citizens economically, contribute to self-sufficiency, and strengthen food security. Using the land for other purposes is harmful to neighboring farms and tenants, potentially violating tenant rights. The Farm Violations Removal Committee urged owners to comply with permitted land use regulations.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) held its first Agricultural and Veterinary Quarantine Forum to discuss prev...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) held its first Agricultural and Veterinary Quarantine Forum to discuss preventing transboundary animal diseases and agricultural pests from entering the country. The forum aimed to increase cooperation between government entities and the private sector, aligning with the National Food Security Strategy 2051. Discussions focused on leveraging global best practices, updating legislation, incorporating advanced technology, and enhancing the capabilities of UAE nationals in quarantine procedures. Presentations were given by experts from Australia, UAE University, and the University of Al Dhaid, covering topics such as biosecurity best practices, transboundary animal diseases, and challenges facing agricultural quarantine in the GCC.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

records.title: A four-day training course for field school facilitators has begun in Dhamar province.
records.description: A four-day training course for field school facilitators has begun in Dhamar province. Organized by the agriculture sector and funded by the Executive Unit for the Management of Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing, the course aims to train 36 agricultural guides to facilitate field schools within the "Implementing Field Schools in the Directorates" program. The training focuses on equipping participants with the skills to conduct effective guidance sessions and train field school members in grain, legume, and livestock cultivation. The course emphasizes analyzing agricultural problems and developing effective solutions.

records.title: The first phase of a shrimp factory rehabilitation project has been inaugurated in Hodeida city.
records.description: The first phase of a shrimp factory rehabilitation project has been inaugurated in Hodeida city. Funded by the Agricultural Projects and Initiatives Financing Unit, the project included rehabilitating the factory hangar, providing new equipment, and creating a modern production environment. The Minister of Agriculture emphasized the project's importance for developing the fisheries sector, increasing fish exports, and improving fishermen's livelihoods. The Hodeida governor highlighted its contribution to food security and local self-sufficiency.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The millet harvest has begun in Al-Munirah District, Hodeidah Governorate, as part of a project to cultivate hard lands and sand dunes.
records.description: The millet harvest has begun in Al-Munirah District, Hodeidah Governorate, as part of a project to cultivate hard lands and sand dunes. The Minister of Agriculture emphasized the importance of expanding cultivation in these areas, noting that over 100,000 acres were planted with millet. He stressed that this season's harvest will significantly contribute to self-sufficiency and reduce imports, urging consumers to prioritize local millet. The Minister framed the harvest as a sign of Yemen's progress towards self-sufficiency. The Governor of Hodeidah highlighted the region's success in producing large quantities of grain, particularly millet.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian government funding, provided dairy processing equipment to 65...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian government funding, provided dairy processing equipment to 65 farmers in several West Bank communities. This initiative is part of the "Supporting Economic Growth through the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in the West Bank" project, which aims to improve rural livelihoods and enhance agricultural sustainability. The project focuses on increasing farmer income and addressing challenges related to rising prices and food supply issues. Through such projects, the Ministry and its partners seek to empower Palestinian farmers and support their presence on their land, aligning with government policy to support the agricultural sector and achieve sustainable economic development.

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Fish production has significantly increased along the Aseer region's coast, generating substantial revenue.
records.description: Fish production has significantly increased along the Aseer region's coast, generating substantial revenue. This growth is attributed to government initiatives aimed at supporting the fishing industry. Further production increases are planned within the next few years. Support is provided to both commercial and independent fishermen, including the distribution of new boats and a mentorship program connecting experienced fishermen with younger generations. The region recently hosted a fish and marine heritage festival showcasing local seafood, businesses, and cultural activities. Aseer's coastline is a diverse marine environment.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: KSrelief, the humanitarian arm of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has provided substantial aid to earthquake-affected individuals in norther...
records.description: KSrelief, the humanitarian arm of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has provided substantial aid to earthquake-affected individuals in northern Syria. In the town of Jindires, located in the Aleppo Governorate, the center distributed 1,476 food baskets and an equal number of health kits. This distribution directly benefited 8,856 individuals and constitutes the second phase of a larger project focused on delivering essential food and health resources to those impacted by the earthquake.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

records.title: Iraq's Veterinary Department has announced that the country is free of highly pathogenic bird flu.
records.description: Iraq's Veterinary Department has announced that the country is free of highly pathogenic bird flu. This announcement follows laboratory tests and preventative measures taken by veterinary hospitals to prevent the spread and smuggling of infected birds. The department's efforts have been recognized by the World Organization for Animal Health. The department encourages breeders and farmers to continue following its advice and instructions.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture sponsored a meeting in Akkar between industrialists and farmers from the Akkar and Bekaa regions to promote l...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture sponsored a meeting in Akkar between industrialists and farmers from the Akkar and Bekaa regions to promote local industrial potato cultivation. The meeting resulted in an agreement to provide industrial potato seeds to interested farmers, ensuring quality and suitability for production. Official contracts will be signed between processing plants and farmers, guaranteeing the purchase of agreed quantities and quality of potatoes. Participants praised the Ministry's role in facilitating this agreement, which supports farmers, helps reduce smuggling, and promotes cooperation between the Ministry, farmers, and industrialists. This initiative aims to improve farmers' conditions, achieve agricultural sustainability, and protect the national economy.

records.title: A technical team in Ibb province has begun a survey and evaluation of water resources and agricultural lands in the Maitam Basin area.
records.description: A technical team in Ibb province has begun a survey and evaluation of water resources and agricultural lands in the Maitam Basin area. The survey, involving the General Authority for Water Resources, the Local Corporation for Water and Sanitation, Agricultural Sector Offices, and the Geological Survey Authority, aims to assess agricultural land and water needs, study the current water situation, and address challenges like the use of unsuitable irrigation water, particularly sewage water. Officials stressed the importance of preventing sewage water use due to its harmful effects and affirmed that measures will be taken to stop this practice.
records.institution: The General Authority for Water Resources

records.title: Egypt's wheat imports saw a significant increase, prompting a strategic shift to bolster national reserves.
records.description: Egypt's wheat imports saw a significant increase, prompting a strategic shift to bolster national reserves. This increase is attributed to higher private sector purchases. With domestic production unable to meet national consumption, imports are necessary to cover the deficit. A large-scale purchase attempt faced challenges due to market conditions. To mitigate reliance on wheat imports and manage subsidy costs, Egypt plans to introduce corn or sorghum into its subsidized bread. Wheat procurement responsibility has also been transferred to a new military agency to optimize purchasing. This new agency has secured a substantial amount of wheat, primarily from Russia. However, some have expressed doubt about the new agency's ability to handle such large operations.
records.institution: The General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Morocco is rapidly becoming a key player in the global avocado market, anticipating a substantial harvest with the vast majority intended...
records.description: Morocco is rapidly becoming a key player in the global avocado market, anticipating a substantial harvest with the vast majority intended for export, mainly to Europe. Export volumes have shown significant growth. However, lower prices in European markets due to decreased demand pose a challenge. Moroccan farmers are being encouraged to accelerate harvesting to maintain a competitive edge against other exporting nations. Farmgate prices are currently favorable for growers. Previous export figures demonstrate Morocco's increasing global presence. This growing export volume is intensifying global competition, with other countries diversifying their export destinations.

records.title: Morocco's apple imports have reached a record high since 2011, with 9.3 thousand tons imported in the first ten months of 2024, valued at...
