records.description: Morocco's apple imports have reached a record high since 2011, with 9.3 thousand tons imported in the first ten months of 2024, valued at over $65 million. This nearly 50% increase compared to 2020 reflects growing demand despite significant local production, where Morocco ranks second in Africa behind South Africa. While Moroccan consumers generally prefer local apples, imports increase during spring and summer when domestic stocks are low. Popular imported varieties include "Gala Royal," "Golden Delicious," "Fuji," and "Golden Smoothie." Italy is the leading supplier, followed by Spain and Poland.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the YMCA, distributed 2,500 olive seedlings to 52 farmers in Hebron Governorate.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the YMCA, distributed 2,500 olive seedlings to 52 farmers in Hebron Governorate. This initiative, part of a joint cooperation program, aims to support farmers in Area C and threatened areas, enhancing their resilience and protecting their land. This reflects the commitment of both organizations to supporting agriculture and farmers facing ongoing challenges in the region.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with Agricultural Relief, distributed 60 tons of Synergy potato seeds to 130 farmers in sever...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with Agricultural Relief, distributed 60 tons of Synergy potato seeds to 130 farmers in several West Bank villages, including those within the Marj Ibn Amer Municipality and others like Burqin, Kafr Dhan, Qabatiya, and Masiliya. Each farmer received enough seeds to plant two dunums (approximately 0.2 hectares). This distribution is part of a project to improve livelihoods, food security, and economic growth in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, implemented by Agricultural Relief and funded by the Dutch representative office. The project aims to enhance cooperation with civil institutions, reduce potato shortages, and achieve self-sufficiency in potato production, ultimately stabilizing prices for consumers, in line with the Palestinian government and Ministry of Agriculture's plan.

records.title: Hafr Al Batin, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, has announced a SAR9 billion ($2.4 billion) plan to develop the Middle East's largest...
records.description: Hafr Al Batin, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, has announced a SAR9 billion ($2.4 billion) plan to develop the Middle East's largest "livestock city." This project aims to supply 30% of Saudi Arabia's red meat demand and will include livestock facilities, feed factories, a veterinary hospital, and meat processing plants. Powered by renewable energy (solar panels producing 15 billion kilowatt-hours annually), the city is projected to produce 140,000 liters of milk daily, require 100 tonnes of feed per hour, and generate 1.5 million square meters of leather annually.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: A case of bovine nodular skin disease has been detected in Saouaf, in the Zaghouan governorate.
records.description: A case of bovine nodular skin disease has been detected in Saouaf, in the Zaghouan governorate. Following the discovery, vaccinations were administered to livestock within a 30-kilometer radius, and insecticide spraying was conducted in nearby stables. Farmers have been advised to eliminate stagnant water to prevent insect breeding, which can spread the disease. Officials report the infection was isolated and quickly contained, and that the overall health of the cattle herd in Zaghouan remains stable, with 82% of the approximately 10,000 cattle in the region already vaccinated against the disease.
records.institution: The Regional Commission for Agricultural Development ( CRDA )

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is preparing to launch "Tabseet," an e-services platform and portal, along wit...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources is preparing to launch "Tabseet," an e-services platform and portal, along with a new official website. The project aims to simplify and expedite services for farmers, fishermen, exporters, and other beneficiaries. The first phase of "Tabseet" will offer 50 services, with plans to expand to 250 services across various ministry sectors. The project emphasizes automation and service facilitation through governorate offices. Several ministries and institutions are collaborating on the project, and the launch will coincide with the launch of the ministry's unified website and a service guide.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Algeria, via its OAIC, has made a record purchase of 1.17 million tonnes of milling wheat through an international tender, the largest su...
records.description: Algeria, via its OAIC, has made a record purchase of 1.17 million tonnes of milling wheat through an international tender, the largest such acquisition in a decade. Initial estimates were much lower, but the final order exceeded one million tonnes. The wheat's origin is uncertain, but it may come from the Black Sea region. Eight international companies participated in the tender, reflecting growing interest in the Algerian market. This large purchase has already impacted global wheat prices, causing a slight increase on the Chicago Board of Trade. This move aims to bolster Algeria's food security amid global supply uncertainties and may also be in anticipation of market tensions in 2025, especially given Algeria's stated intention to halt durum wheat imports next year.

records.title: Algeria's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development has completed construction of its first grain storage center in Tiaret, with a 5,...
records.description: Algeria's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development has completed construction of its first grain storage center in Tiaret, with a 5,000-ton capacity, as part of a national program to expand storage capacity. This center will be ready for the 2024-2025 harvest, with ten more planned for the Tiaret region. This is part of a larger project to build 350 community storage centers across 52 wilayas, totaling 1.75 million tons of capacity. The program aims to modernize harvest management, reduce post-harvest losses, improve grain conservation, support farmers, and strengthen Algeria's food autonomy.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Following an intense autumn drought, snowfall in western Algeria, particularly in Tiaret, has presented new challenges for livestock farm...
records.description: Following an intense autumn drought, snowfall in western Algeria, particularly in Tiaret, has presented new challenges for livestock farmers. While snow is generally beneficial for soil moisture, it creates difficulties in feeding herds, especially young sheep. The resistance to cold varies by breed, with the El Hamra breed being more robust than the Ouled Djellal. The recent drought has exacerbated the existing fodder shortage, driving up prices for barley and wheat bran. This forces herders to travel long distances in search of pasture. Reforestation efforts using fodder shrubs like attriplex have shown some success in improving pasture capacity. However, overgrazing and unsustainable resource exploitation remain significant obstacles. Experts advocate for collective and sustainable resource management involving livestock farmers, and the proposed revision of the communal code could provide further support for agricultural infrastructure development.
records.institution: The Scientific and Technical Research Center

records.title: Pico Modern Agriculture, an Egyptian producer-exporter, is expanding its reach with new products and varieties while maintaining its focu...
records.description: Pico Modern Agriculture, an Egyptian producer-exporter, is expanding its reach with new products and varieties while maintaining its focus on quality and timely delivery. The company is enhancing its strawberry offerings with new varieties, expanding avocado production with early- and late-season options, and extending grape harvesting to provide a more consistent supply. Mango production is also increasing to meet growing demand. Pico has diversified into value-added products like ready-to-eat sweetcorn, honey, and frozen fruit, and launched an e-commerce platform with a mobile app for direct-to-consumer sales. The company invests in advanced technologies and logistics to maintain high standards and efficient service.

records.title: The Jordan Valley Authority and the Dates Cooperative Agricultural Society (DCAS) have signed a land lease agreement to establish worksho...
records.description: The Jordan Valley Authority and the Dates Cooperative Agricultural Society (DCAS) have signed a land lease agreement to establish workshops for sorting, packing, packaging, and refrigerating dates, aiming to support Jordanian date farmers. The Jordan Valley Authority intends to stimulate investment in the region and support cooperative societies in the growing palm sector. The project is expected to create over 80 jobs and establish a palm sector research station. This initiative aligns with efforts to develop the date sector and promote Jordanian dates globally. Recent data shows a 7% increase in date exports in 2024 compared to 2023.
records.institution: The Jordan Valley Authority, the Dates Cooperative Agricultural Society (DCAS)

records.title: Maltese orange exports to France are set to begin with an initial shipment.
records.description: Maltese orange exports to France are set to begin with an initial shipment. Total orange exports are projected to increase compared to last season, along with the total citrus harvest. Preparatory meetings have been held to address transportation costs, market competition, and promotional strategies, including marketing events and digital campaigns. Participation in international trade fairs is also planned. Organizational and logistical measures are in place to ensure a smooth export season, including monitoring of quantities and prices and facilitated freight operations. Quality control and exports to Libya will also be monitored. Citrus exports (clementines and navels) have already begun and show a significant increase in both volume and value compared to the same period of the previous season.

records.title: Tunisia has allocated nearly 950,000 hectares for cereal cultivation in the 2024/2025 season and is providing 120,000 tons of ammonium ni...
records.description: Tunisia has allocated nearly 950,000 hectares for cereal cultivation in the 2024/2025 season and is providing 120,000 tons of ammonium nitrate fertilizer for large-scale crops. Recent rainfall is expected to increase fertilizer demand, but sufficient stocks are available. The Ministry of Agriculture is closely monitoring transport chains to ensure fertilizer availability. Approximately 80% of the planned areas have already been sown. Recent rainfall, especially in the north, is crucial for crop success, replenishing water tables and benefiting various agricultural sectors and water resources.

records.title: Tunisia has ratified an agreement with Libya and Algeria to establish a consultation mechanism for managing shared groundwater in the nor...
records.description: Tunisia has ratified an agreement with Libya and Algeria to establish a consultation mechanism for managing shared groundwater in the northern desert, as published in its Official Gazette. This follows high-level meetings emphasizing regional cooperation on water resources. A tripartite summit in April 2024 resulted in the formation of a joint working group to develop large-scale projects and accelerate groundwater management efforts. Signed in Algeria, the agreement outlines the framework for consultation among the three countries to ensure sustainable exploitation of these critical water resources.
records.institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: Tunisia's olive harvest is progressing well, with an expected production of around 340,000 tonnes of olive oil.
records.description: Tunisia's olive harvest is progressing well, with an expected production of around 340,000 tonnes of olive oil. Despite initial challenges like price drops, support measures such as increased storage capacity, monthly bonuses for stakeholders, additional bonuses for farmers, and facilitated credits have aided the sector. Tunisia exports about 85% of its olive oil production, highlighting its strategic importance to the national economy. The Ministry of Agriculture's measures aim to address economic challenges and enhance competitiveness, ensuring Tunisia remains a key player in the global olive oil market while stabilizing farmers' incomes and meeting local demand.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, The National Oil Office (ONH)

records.title: Tunisian date exporters face increased demand alongside a significant production drop of 30-40% due to heavy rains and temperature variat...
records.description: Tunisian date exporters face increased demand alongside a significant production drop of 30-40% due to heavy rains and temperature variations between August and November. This has also increased production costs due to the need for more intensive sorting. Maison des dattes will prioritize the Moroccan market due to its stability and historical ties, reducing exports to Europe and the Americas. Tunisian date prices are expected to rise by 10-15% to reflect the lower volumes and higher costs, though this increase is not expected to fully compensate producers for their losses.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Commercial Bank International (CBI), a UAE bank, has invested in Boomitra, a carbon project developer and Earthshot Prize winner, to prom...
records.description: Commercial Bank International (CBI), a UAE bank, has invested in Boomitra, a carbon project developer and Earthshot Prize winner, to promote regenerative agriculture in the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. Boomitra uses AI and satellite data to measure soil carbon sequestration, improving soil health and crop yields while generating carbon credits for farmers. CBI's investment reflects its commitment to sustainability and aligns with the UAE's vision for sustainable agriculture. This partnership aims to address issues like land degradation, prevalent in the Middle East and North Africa, by using technology to restore soil health and promote sustainable farming practices.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC) has launched a tender for a 1.5-GW greenfield solar power project in Abu Dhabi's Al Zarraf...
records.description: Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC) has launched a tender for a 1.5-GW greenfield solar power project in Abu Dhabi's Al Zarraf area. Following a pre-qualification stage, 16 companies are now invited to submit proposals by the second quarter of 2025. The winning bidder will own up to 40% of the project, with the Abu Dhabi government holding the remaining equity. The selected developer will be responsible for all aspects of the project, including development, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance, and will sign a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) with EWEC.

records.title: The "Buthoor Al Bahrain" (Seeds of Bahrain) campaign, a three-month initiative promoting green spaces and supporting Bahrain's national a...
records.description: The "Buthoor Al Bahrain" (Seeds of Bahrain) campaign, a three-month initiative promoting green spaces and supporting Bahrain's national afforestation plan, has concluded. Conducted in partnership with UN-Habitat, the FAO, and NIAD, the campaign distributed over 13,000 saplings across 57 sites in Bahrain. The initiative aimed to increase Bahrain's tree count to 3.6 million by 2035 and fostered public engagement, environmental responsibility, and partnerships between various stakeholders.
records.institution: The Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture

records.title: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation issued 13,238 licenses for livestock, poultry, and feed projects in 2024, including...
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation issued 13,238 licenses for livestock, poultry, and feed projects in 2024, including a significant number for small-scale livestock farms and digital licenses. The ministry also approved thousands of feed mix registrations, supported feed factories, and conducted compliance inspections. Support initiatives included distributing layer hens and selling discounted table eggs. The National Veal Project disbursed substantial funds to beneficiaries, supporting the raising of thousands of cattle. Additionally, the ministry facilitated the import of production inputs and the export of various animal feed and poultry products.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade, and Supply has issued a tender to purchase 100,000 to 120,000 tons of wheat.
records.description: Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade, and Supply has issued a tender to purchase 100,000 to 120,000 tons of wheat. Interested bidders can obtain tender documents for a non-refundable fee of 650 Jordanian Dinars. Bidders must provide a valid business license, a recent commercial register copy, and Chamber of Commerce registration.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Trade, and Supply

records.title: The 6th Libya Food exhibition will host 130 international exhibitors from 17 countries and 86 local exhibitors in Tripoli.
records.description: The 6th Libya Food exhibition will host 130 international exhibitors from 17 countries and 86 local exhibitors in Tripoli. The event will showcase food industries, packaging, processing, and commercial markets. International participants will come from various countries, including Italy, France, Turkey, the UAE, Tunisia, and others. The Ministry of Economy and Trade has directed efforts to support the event and facilitate networking between local and foreign businesses to enhance trade and create export opportunities for Libya.
records.institution: The Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.title: Morocco's citrus exports are projected to increase by 31% to 597,000 tons in the upcoming marketing year, according to the USDA.
records.description: Morocco's citrus exports are projected to increase by 31% to 597,000 tons in the upcoming marketing year, according to the USDA. This growth is attributed to favorable weather, improved irrigation, and new trade measures, including a new shipping route between Agadir and Dakar to facilitate trade with West Africa. Mandarins are expected to be the dominant export (83% of the total). Citrus fruits are a major contributor to Morocco's agricultural exports, generating over $456.5 million in 2023.

records.title: In Oman, the Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the water treatment company Nada Al Rabeei, is offering technical support to fa...
records.description: In Oman, the Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the water treatment company Nada Al Rabeei, is offering technical support to farms for the installation of desalination units. This initiative addresses the increasing problem of water salinity impacting agricultural productivity. The support includes on-site assessments of water quality and crop needs, recommendations for appropriate desalination unit specifications, and provision of maintenance and operation manuals to ensure sustainable use of the technology.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, The Water Treatment Company Nada Al Rabeei

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Oman's agriculture and fisheries sectors are experiencing significant growth and attracting investment under Oman Vision 2040.
records.description: Oman's agriculture and fisheries sectors are experiencing significant growth and attracting investment under Oman Vision 2040. Agricultural output reached 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, with consistent growth in livestock and fisheries production as well. Exports, particularly in fisheries, have generated substantial revenue. The Oman Food Investment Holding Company plans significant investments in food-related ventures, focusing on modern technologies like hydroponics and aquaculture. Key projects include Al Najd and Saham Agricultural Cities and the Barr Al Hikman Shrimp Aquaculture Farm. Investment opportunities exist across various areas, including livestock farming, greenhouses, aquaculture, and food processing.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: In Saudi Arabia's Northern Borders region, women are skilled in producing wild ghee, a cultural staple linked to the region's large lives...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia's Northern Borders region, women are skilled in producing wild ghee, a cultural staple linked to the region's large livestock population (over 7 million cattle and camels). Production is highest in winter due to demand for dishes like porridge. The process involves multiple stages, from milking to creating "Khathir" (a fermented milk product), churning it in a "Samil" (a goatskin or sheepskin container), and then melting the resulting butter into ghee, which is stored in leather containers ("Al-Nahw" or "Al-Dharf"). Local women display their ghee and other handicrafts at events, with the Arar market and Lavender Hall providing key venues and training opportunities.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company's subsidiary, Agricultural Development Company (ADC), signed a 165 million Saudi riyal ($43.95 million) contract wit...
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company's subsidiary, Agricultural Development Company (ADC), signed a 165 million Saudi riyal ($43.95 million) contract with China's Chengdu Design & Research Institute to build 100 poultry broiler houses in Saudi Arabia. These modern farms will utilize automation and Industry 4.0 technologies and are expected to be operational by January 2027. The project aligns with Tanmiah's overall expansion strategy in primary poultry processing.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The "Reef Saudi" program launched the "Our Winter is Rural" initiative at the "Rural Village Agricultural Fair – Ghee and Honey" event in...
records.description: The "Reef Saudi" program launched the "Our Winter is Rural" initiative at the "Rural Village Agricultural Fair – Ghee and Honey" event in Riyadh. This initiative aims to promote Saudi Arabia's rural regions as unique tourist destinations, showcasing their natural beauty, cultural diversity, and local products like ghee and honey. It seeks to empower rural communities and contribute to sustainable development in line with Saudi Vision 2030. The fair allows visitors to experience rural life and discover local products. The Reef Saudi program, recognized by the FAO as the largest global development program of its kind, has supported over 77,000 agricultural projects and contributed to job creation in rural areas.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The Gafsa region of Tunisia has reported a strong potato harvest, producing 13,664 tonnes from 854 hectares.
records.description: The Gafsa region of Tunisia has reported a strong potato harvest, producing 13,664 tonnes from 854 hectares. The Sned delegation had the largest cultivated area, followed by Gafsa North, Zannouch, Sidi Aich, and Gafsa South. Of the total harvest, over 3,400 tonnes are held as a strategic reserve for the local market, helping to stabilize supply and meet increasing demand while reducing reliance on imports. This successful harvest highlights the importance of potato cultivation to Gafsa's agricultural economy and its contribution to Tunisia's food security.

records.title: Dubai International Chamber facilitated the expansion of Dubai-based agri-food technology provider Farm To Plate into Eswatini.
records.description: Dubai International Chamber facilitated the expansion of Dubai-based agri-food technology provider Farm To Plate into Eswatini. The Chamber connected Farm To Plate with key stakeholders, leading to a partnership with the Royal Science and Technology Park. This collaboration aims to modernize Eswatini's agri-food supply chain, empower local farmers, enhance sustainability, and optimize agricultural practices using Farm To Plate's technology. The partnership will introduce end-to-end supply chain tools to boost farmer incomes, improve food quality assurance, promote local products, enhance export readiness, and strengthen local food production.
records.institution: Dubai International Chamber, Farm To Plate

records.title: The UAE provided 700 tons of food aid to Somalia to assist families impacted by severe drought.
records.description: The UAE provided 700 tons of food aid to Somalia to assist families impacted by severe drought. The aid was delivered to Somalia's Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA) and will be distributed to drought-stricken regions, including Kismayo, Garowe, areas near Mogadishu, and regions between Mogadishu and Jowhar. SoDMA expressed gratitude to the UAE for its ongoing humanitarian support. Somalia has been struggling with recurring droughts and famine, which have devastated agriculture and livestock.

records.title: Moroccan cucumber exports to Spain have seen explosive growth, increasing by 182.5% in five years.
records.description: Moroccan cucumber exports to Spain have seen explosive growth, increasing by 182.5% in five years. Spain's total cucumber imports have also risen significantly, with Morocco now dominating the market, supplying over 75% of Spain's cucumber imports (10.11 million kilos worth €13.09 million). While Portugal is the second-largest supplier, their market share and average price are considerably lower. Morocco's success is attributed to large export volumes and competitive pricing, suggesting continued market dominance in the coming years.

records.title: The World Bank has approved a USD 250 million financing package for Morocco's Agri-Food Systems Transformation Program.
records.description: The World Bank has approved a USD 250 million financing package for Morocco's Agri-Food Systems Transformation Program. This program aims to increase the resilience of Morocco's agri-food sector to climate change, enhance food safety and health standards, introduce climate-smart farming practices, establish agricultural insurance, improve water and soil management, expand organic farming, and upgrade food outlet health standards. It is projected to impact over 1.3 million people. This support comes as Morocco's agricultural sector faces challenges, including a significant decline in cereal production due to drought.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the FAO and with Canadian funding, provided dairy processing equipment to 85 farmers in...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the FAO and with Canadian funding, provided dairy processing equipment to 85 farmers in South Hebron - Dura. This initiative, part of a larger project supporting agricultural value chain development, aims to increase family incomes, enhance resilience to food supply shocks and rising prices, and improve the sustainability of the agricultural sector. The project provides farmers with tools to improve dairy processing and increase productivity.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the YMCA, distributed 6,350 olive seedlings to 148 beneficiaries in southern Hebron, spe...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the YMCA, distributed 6,350 olive seedlings to 148 beneficiaries in southern Hebron, specifically in Area C, to protect lands threatened with confiscation. This initiative aims to enhance food security, protect Palestinian lands from settlement activities, and support Palestinian citizens' resilience. The distribution focused on areas facing increasing threats of confiscation and emphasizes the importance of olive trees as a Palestinian symbol.

records.title: The Northern Borders Region of Saudi Arabia is rich in diverse wild plants, including the arta plant (calligonum comosum), which has retu...
records.description: The Northern Borders Region of Saudi Arabia is rich in diverse wild plants, including the arta plant (calligonum comosum), which has returned to Wadi Arar after being nearly extinct due to overgrazing and illegal logging. Environmental laws and natural reserves have aided in the revival of various plant species. The arta is described as a thornless shrub with white branches, green tips, and fragrant white and red flowers, producing hairy, spherical fruits that range from red to yellowish-green.

records.domain: Establishment or modification of food stock
records.title: A ministerial meeting discussed measures to ensure a stable supply of basic products, maintain price stability, and support vulnerable gr...
records.description: A ministerial meeting discussed measures to ensure a stable supply of basic products, maintain price stability, and support vulnerable groups, especially during Ramadan and Eid. Key decisions included allocating 68.8 MD for social assistance, building buffer stocks of essential goods such as frozen meat, eggs, and 45,000 tons of potatoes, and strengthening market oversight to combat monopolistic practices and illegal trade. Health and safety inspections will target food warehouses, dairy production sites, and slaughterhouses. Efforts will also focus on increasing direct sales from producers to consumers, securing commercial areas, and modifying public transport schedules to accommodate Ramadan activities.

records.title: Despite overall inflation in Tunisia decreasing to 6.2% in December 2024, some food prices have continued to rise.
records.description: Despite overall inflation in Tunisia decreasing to 6.2% in December 2024, some food prices have continued to rise. Lamb and mutton saw the largest increase at 21.3%, followed by poultry at 19.7%. Other significant increases were seen in dried fruits (14.8%), fresh vegetables (14.2%), and fresh fish (12.8%). Beef also rose by 9.2%. Chocolate and condiments exceeded the general inflation rate with increases of 7.5% and 6.3%, respectively. Mineral waters and beverages increased by 5.4%, and cereal derivatives by 5%. Edible oils were the only category to see a price decrease (-8.3%). While inflation is trending downwards, it remains above the desired 3% threshold, continuing to affect Tunisians' purchasing power.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Egypt has launched an initiative to recycle agricultural waste into peat moss, a valuable soil enhancer.
records.description: Egypt has launched an initiative to recycle agricultural waste into peat moss, a valuable soil enhancer. A cooperation protocol between the Agricultural Research Centre and Abu Zaabal Chemical Fertilizers Company will oversee the project, aiming to reduce peat moss imports and boost organic farming. The initiative will provide farmers with affordable, natural soil conditioners, improving productivity and incomes while also managing agricultural waste and benefiting the environment. The research institute will handle technical aspects and quality control, while Abu Zaabal will manage production and distribution. Educational campaigns will also inform farmers about the benefits of using peat moss.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: A study examining blockchain technology's application in supply chains within emerging economies, particularly Morocco and Brazil, highli...
records.description: A study examining blockchain technology's application in supply chains within emerging economies, particularly Morocco and Brazil, highlights the crucial role of blockchain technology providers. In Morocco, OCP Group serves as a successful example in the agri-food sector, demonstrating how blockchain can address industrial challenges and drive innovation. While blockchain offers benefits like enhanced transparency, reduced inefficiencies, and improved branding, challenges such as limited awareness, infrastructure, high costs, and training needs exist. The study identifies key roles for providers, including developing tailored solutions, offering operational support, facilitating stakeholder collaboration, and ensuring access to international markets.

records.title: Morocco has begun importing rice to address a severe domestic production shortfall caused by drought.
records.description: Morocco has begun importing rice to address a severe domestic production shortfall caused by drought. The Ministry of Industry and Trade has authorized the import of 55,000 tons of rice, suspending customs duties and VAT to stabilize local prices. This is a short-term solution, however. Negotiations are underway with suppliers in India, Thailand, Brazil, and Argentina to secure imports of good quality rice at reasonable prices. The drought has severely impacted traditional rice-producing regions, shrinking cultivated areas significantly. This crisis has also increased Morocco's reliance on wheat imports. While a government program and industry investments aim to revitalize the rice sector, the immediate focus is on imports to ensure market stability and affordable access to rice for consumers.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: Morocco's 2024/2025 agricultural campaign has begun favorably due to recent rainfall that has improved water resources.
records.description: Morocco's 2024/2025 agricultural campaign has begun favorably due to recent rainfall that has improved water resources. Rainfall has nearly doubled compared to last year, and dam filling rates have also increased, raising hopes for a recovery after a significant drop in cereal production last season. While experts welcome the improved conditions and government support measures like subsidized seeds, fertilizers, and an irrigation program, they caution that continued rainfall and effective irrigation are crucial for sustained recovery. They also emphasize the need for easier access to agricultural credit, supply chain improvements to prevent price speculation, and targeted support for arid regions. Experts advocate for the use of modern technologies like remote sensing for irrigation and further support for small farmers and local agricultural sectors to enhance resilience and sustainability.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival has solidified its position as a key tourism and economic event for Saudi Arabia and the Al-Jouf...
records.description: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival has solidified its position as a key tourism and economic event for Saudi Arabia and the Al-Jouf region. Showcasing Al-Jouf's status as the "land of olives," the festival features local and international participants, highlighting olive and oil production, processing, and related industries. It supports local businesses and families, providing platforms for their products. The event also includes product quality testing and cultural displays showcasing Saudi heritage.

records.title: The Tihama area in Al-Baha region is a significant agricultural area in Saudi Arabia, covering over 900 hectares and producing a diverse...
records.description: The Tihama area in Al-Baha region is a significant agricultural area in Saudi Arabia, covering over 900 hectares and producing a diverse range of crops including mangoes, coffee, bananas, citrus fruits, and grains. This agricultural diversity supports the local economy and creates job opportunities. Local farms have also become tourist destinations, offering guided tours and hands-on experiences to promote sustainable agriculture and further support the local economy.
records.institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Jordan's agricultural exports saw a substantial increase in 2024, reaching JD1.276 billion by the end of October, a 37.16% rise (JD346 mi...
records.description: Jordan's agricultural exports saw a substantial increase in 2024, reaching JD1.276 billion by the end of October, a 37.16% rise (JD346 million) compared to the same period in 2023 and exceeding the total export value of 2023 (JD1.1 billion). This growth was driven by increases in livestock exports (38%), fruit exports (80%), and vegetable exports (15%). Live sheep exports increased by 48% to 754,000 head, while exported fruits and vegetables reached 586,700 tonnes, a 12% increase. Specifically, vegetable exports rose by 8% to 405,900 tonnes, fruit exports by 20% to 180,800 tonnes, date exports by 7% to 16,280 tonnes, and table egg exports by 8% to 94 million eggs.

records.title: The Agricultural Producers' Price Index increased by 0.8% in the first 11 months of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023, driven by h...
records.description: The Agricultural Producers' Price Index increased by 0.8% in the first 11 months of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023, driven by higher prices for potatoes, zucchini, and eggplants. However, prices for tomatoes, sweet peppers, and bananas declined. On a monthly basis, the index rose significantly in November 2024 compared to both November 2023 (26.3% increase) and October 2024 (19.8% increase), primarily due to higher prices for tomatoes, cabbage, and thyme. Price decreases were seen for cucumbers, carrots, bananas, cauliflower, lemons, and oranges.

records.title: Iraq exports 13 different agricultural commodities, including potatoes, dates, and fodder, and has plans to increase these exports.
records.description: Iraq exports 13 different agricultural commodities, including potatoes, dates, and fodder, and has plans to increase these exports. The Ministry of Agriculture is prioritizing water conservation through improved irrigation techniques. While Iraq imports some agricultural products, particularly fruits due to climate challenges, it aims to expand exports of surplus local produce.

records.title: A workshop introducing a water map and strategies for revitalizing community initiatives was held in Jawf Governorate, Yemen.
records.description: A workshop introducing a water map and strategies for revitalizing community initiatives was held in Jawf Governorate, Yemen. Organized by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, the workshop aimed to educate over 40 participants on utilizing water resources for agricultural advancement and sustainable development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: Iraq has partnered with Switzerland's Bühler and Egypt's Samco to build five modern grain silos, each holding 60,000 tonnes.
records.description: Iraq has partnered with Switzerland's Bühler and Egypt's Samco to build five modern grain silos, each holding 60,000 tonnes. Located in Kirkuk, Anbar, Wasit, Najaf, and Muthanna, these silos are part of a larger plan to enhance Iraq's grain storage capacity, which includes expanding granaries and building 20 more silos, totaling one million tonnes of storage. This is a significant infrastructure development for Iraq, which hasn't built silos of this size since 1980. This initiative supports Iraq's recent achievement of wheat self-sufficiency and record wheat production of 6.302 million tonnes in 2024.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Libya's Tatweer Research has launched the AgroLEAP project, a component of the broader USAID-funded Libyan Economic Acceleration Project...
records.description: Libya's Tatweer Research has launched the AgroLEAP project, a component of the broader USAID-funded Libyan Economic Acceleration Project (LEAP), to support and empower the agricultural sector in southern Libya. AgroLEAP focuses on helping farmers transition from traditional electricity to solar energy, offering expert consultations and facilitating partnerships between farmers and solar energy providers to achieve energy self-sufficiency and sustainability.

records.title: Saudi Arabia pre-qualifies bidders in 2-GW battery storage tender
records.description: Saudi Arabia has pre-qualified 33 companies to bid on four battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, each with a capacity of 500 MW/2,000 MWh, totaling 2,000 MW/8,000 MWh. These projects will be developed under the build-own-operate (BOO) model. The winning developers will own the projects and sign a 15-year energy storage service agreement with the Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC). The BESS projects will support Saudi Arabia's goal of achieving 50% renewable energy in its electricity mix by 2030.

records.title: Tunisia's National Oil Office (ONH) is selling extra virgin olive oil to cooperatives, associations, and public institutions for 12 dinar...
records.description: Tunisia's National Oil Office (ONH) is selling extra virgin olive oil to cooperatives, associations, and public institutions for 12 dinars per liter, with promises of increased supply soon. An ONH quality control manager confirmed the oil's high quality, meeting international extra virgin standards through rigorous testing. While explaining the three main classifications of olive oil (extra virgin, virgin, and common virgin), the report raises the question of why ordinary olive oil is currently being sold at the same price as extra virgin olive oil.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Arctech Solar will supply its SkyLine II single-axis solar tracking system for the 1.5-GW Al Ajban solar PV plant in Abu Dhabi.
records.description: Arctech Solar will supply its SkyLine II single-axis solar tracking system for the 1.5-GW Al Ajban solar PV plant in Abu Dhabi. The project, owned by EDF Renewables, Korea Western Power (KOWEPO), and Masdar, is expected to begin commercial operations in Q3 2026. Arctech has been active in the Middle East since 2017 and is currently building a manufacturing facility in Jeddah, expected to be operational in 2025.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: the first Al Ain Dates Festival has commenced.
records.description: the first Al Ain Dates Festival has commenced. Organized by the Abu Dhabi Heritage Authority, the festival celebrates the historical significance of the palm tree in Emirati heritage and promotes Al Ain's cultural, economic, and agricultural importance. The festival features seven date competitions showcasing different varieties, a date auction, date shops, and a traditional market.

records.title: Algeria has chosen Romania as its new source of sheep imports to satisfy high demand for fresh meat, particularly during Ramadan.
records.description: Algeria has chosen Romania as its new source of sheep imports to satisfy high demand for fresh meat, particularly during Ramadan. This decision strengthens trade relations between the two countries. Algerian veterinary services have approved the necessary health certificates for these imports following negotiations facilitated by the Algerian Ambassador to Bucharest. Romania successfully met Algeria's technical requirements, leading to the finalization of the import agreement.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: ACWA Power and its partner HAU Energy have secured USD 703.6 million in financing for the 1.1-GW Suez wind farm project in Egypt, represe...
records.description: ACWA Power and its partner HAU Energy have secured USD 703.6 million in financing for the 1.1-GW Suez wind farm project in Egypt, representing a total investment of USD 1.2 billion. ACWA Power holds a 70% stake in the project, which is considered the largest single-contracted wind farm in the Middle East. The financing comes from a consortium of international banks. The wind farm will be implemented in two phases and is expected to be fully operational by the second quarter of 2027, contributing to Egypt's renewable energy goals. ACWA Power is already active in Egypt with existing solar projects and is also pursuing a 10-GW wind project and a green hydrogen initiative.

records.title: A UK Food Security Report highlighted the strengthening agricultural trade relationship between Morocco and the UK.
records.description: A UK Food Security Report highlighted the strengthening agricultural trade relationship between Morocco and the UK. Morocco is a significant supplier of fresh produce, including 7.5% of the UK's fresh vegetable imports in 2023. The report also recognized Morocco as a major fertilizer producer. Morocco's Ministry of Agriculture has implemented support measures for farmers, including subsidized seeds and fertilizers, and an extensive irrigation program, as part of its "Green Generation 2020-2030" strategy. Morocco's advanced farming techniques, investments in irrigation, and sustainable practices, along with its favorable climate and proximity to Europe, contribute to its ability to meet international demand. The country is increasingly seen as a model for sustainable agricultural development.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries

records.title: Morocco's dam water reserves have shown a significant improvement in filling rates compared to the previous year.
records.description: Morocco's dam water reserves have shown a significant improvement in filling rates compared to the previous year. This increase, attributed to recent rainfall, represents a total volume of 4.79 billion cubic meters. Several key dams have seen notable improvements, particularly in agriculturally important regions. This offers relief amid ongoing efforts to combat water scarcity caused by a nearly six-year drought. Despite this improvement, rainfall remains below normal, and groundwater resources are still depleted. The government has implemented various water management strategies, including desalination plants and water-saving measures, and King Mohammed VI has emphasized the national importance of water conservation.
records.institution: The Ministry of Equipment and Water

records.title: Oman to set up ‘Net Zero Centre’ to meet 2050 targets
records.description: Oman will establish a "Net Zero Centre" to help achieve its goal of net-zero emissions by 2050. The center will be responsible for developing strategies, monitoring net-zero projects (including energy efficiency initiatives), and providing technical support to public and private entities. It will also focus on adopting international best practices and technologies, supporting research and innovation, and developing national expertise. Furthermore, the center will manage carbon, hydrogen, and low-carbon product certifications and oversee carbon certificate trading in line with international standards.

records.title: A 10-day training course for leaders of development associations in Sa'afan district, Sana'a province, has concluded.
records.description: A 10-day training course for leaders of development associations in Sa'afan district, Sana'a province, has concluded. The course, funded by the Agricultural and Fisheries Projects and Initiatives Financing Unit, trained 18 participants in management, planning, evaluation, and financial systems relevant to development work. Local officials emphasized the importance of applying this knowledge to strengthen communities and support sustainable development, particularly in agriculture and community services, despite ongoing challenges. Participants received completion certificates at a closing ceremony.
records.institution: The Social Affairs and Labor Office,The Western Sector Multipurpose Agricultural Cooperative Association

records.title: A protocol has been signed to localize the production of veterinary vaccines in Egypt.
records.description: A protocol has been signed to localize the production of veterinary vaccines in Egypt. The agreement involves the Egyptian Company for Drugs and Veterinary Vaccines, part of VACSERA, and Canada’s Korveda. The initiative aims to achieve self-sufficiency in veterinary vaccines, open export opportunities, and enhance Egypt’s role in regional and international health security. It supports the strategic vision of localizing critical industries, utilizing raw materials, and improving health and food security. The collaboration includes technology transfer, joint research, and local manufacturing of poultry vaccines as an initial step.
records.institution: Ministry of Health and Population, Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) is launching the Citrus Season to support local farmers and promote agritourism.
records.description: The Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) is launching the Citrus Season to support local farmers and promote agritourism. This event aims to support local farmers, promote AlUla as an agritourism destination, and stimulate economic growth. The season will showcase the region's diverse citrus production, which includes 29 varieties grown on over 5,000 farms, yielding 14,000 tons of fruit annually. The Citrus Season will feature exhibitions for local farmers and families, various events, and a training course on using citrus fruits in cooking. Along with the AlUla Dates Season, it serves as a key economic driver, promoting local products in regional markets and contributing to sustainable development.

records.title: The Egyptian Parliament approved a $131 million agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) to finance the first phase of the Priv...
records.description: The Egyptian Parliament approved a $131 million agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) to finance the first phase of the Private Sector Development and Economic Diversification Program. This program aims to stimulate private sector investment by improving the investment climate and supporting economic diversification, particularly in industry and agriculture, while also promoting a green transition. Key measures under the program include establishing the Supreme Investment Council, amending investment laws, creating the Egyptian Intellectual Property Office, regulating unlicensed industrial facilities, and allocating land for renewable energy investments. This initiative complements other efforts with international partners, such as a one billion euro agreement with the European Union, to support Egypt's structural reform program and macroeconomic stability.

records.title: Water reservoirs in large dams in Morocco's Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima region have reached over 876 million cubic meters, a 45.87% fillin...
records.description: Water reservoirs in large dams in Morocco's Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima region have reached over 876 million cubic meters, a 45.87% filling rate compared to 38.91% during the same period last year. The Oued El Makhazine dam, the region's largest, is at 69.29% capacity. Other dams in the region show varying filling rates, from 14.77% to 81.22%, indicating a general improvement in water storage compared to the previous year.
records.institution: The Ministry of Equipment and Water

records.title: A’Saffa Foods SAOG has announced an expansion plan to increase its broiler chicken production from 48 million to 60 million birds per year.
records.description: A’Saffa Foods SAOG has announced an expansion plan to increase its broiler chicken production from 48 million to 60 million birds per year. This expansion is part of a five-year growth strategy to meet rising demand for poultry products, address food security challenges, and solidify the company's leading position in the sector. The investment also aims to strengthen the supply chain, improve operational efficiency, and create more jobs in Oman, contributing to the nation's economic development under Oman Vision 2040.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian funding, distributed dairy processing equipment to 215 sheep f...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the FAO and with Canadian funding, distributed dairy processing equipment to 215 sheep farmers across Hebron, Ramallah and Al-Bireh, Jericho, and Salfit. The equipment, including various tools for processing and animal care, aims to improve product quality, increase farmer incomes, and promote sustainable economic development. This initiative is part of a larger project to empower Palestinian farmers and support their resilience on their land

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival will take place at the Prince Abdulilah Urban Center in Sakaka.
records.description: The Al-Jouf International Olive Festival will take place at the Prince Abdulilah Urban Center in Sakaka. The festival aims to support olive producers, stimulate economic and agricultural activity, promote tourism, and enhance food security. The event will include an olive exhibition, olive park, and dedicated spaces for various vendors and activities. Several international olive-exporting countries are participating.

records.title: In Tunisia, the 2025 Finance Act includes measures to support the beef sector, but they are viewed as short-term fixes rather than addres...
records.description: In Tunisia, the 2025 Finance Act includes measures to support the beef sector, but they are viewed as short-term fixes rather than addressing structural issues. UTAP highlighted the urgent need for long-term strategies, higher milk prices, and solutions to rising costs, which have caused a 30-35% decline in the cattle herd since 2019. While packaged milk production improved due to favorable grazing, concerns remain over nodular dermatitis in cows, with UTAP criticizing delays in preventive measures.
records.institution: The Tunisian Union of Agriculture and Fisheries (UTAP)

records.title: Egypt's Foreign Minister participated in the Egypt-Gabon Business Forum in Libreville, attended by Gabonese President and several ministe...
records.description: Egypt's Foreign Minister participated in the Egypt-Gabon Business Forum in Libreville, attended by Gabonese President and several ministers, along with business leaders from both countries. The forum emphasized strengthening economic ties through increased trade and joint investments. Egypt expressed its willingness to support Gabon's development initiatives and share expertise in key sectors like infrastructure, energy, construction, pharmaceuticals, and agriculture. The importance of public-private partnerships in driving African economic growth was also highlighted, with mention of Egypt's over $14 billion investment across the continent. Discussions focused on potential projects in road construction, port development, renewable energy, agricultural cooperation, and technology/manufacturing expertise exchange.

records.title: The Asian Arab Business Forum 2024 in Muscat highlighted Oman's strategic role as a global trade hub connecting Asia, the Arab world, and...
records.description: The Asian Arab Business Forum 2024 in Muscat highlighted Oman's strategic role as a global trade hub connecting Asia, the Arab world, and beyond. The forum emphasized collaboration in sectors like renewable energy, technology, logistics, tourism, and agriculture. Attendees discussed Oman's investment-friendly policies and its potential as a key link in the global economy. The event also focused on building connections with Europe, particularly Greece, to bridge the gap between East and West. Organizers emphasized their commitment to ongoing engagement and future initiatives to solidify Oman's position in global trade.
records.institution: The College of Banking and Financial Studies (CBFS)

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture announced 5.3 million shekels worth of development and relief projects for farmers in Salfit Governorate, fun...
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture announced 5.3 million shekels worth of development and relief projects for farmers in Salfit Governorate, funded by various partners. These projects, approved for 2025, aim to support farmers facing increasing attacks from settlers, including paving agricultural roads, building wells, planting crops, providing food processing equipment, distributing supplies for livestock, and rehabilitating plastic houses. The projects will benefit over 1,900 farmers.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, with FAO funding, provided relief to 100 livestock farmers in Qalqilya Governorate through an urgent respons...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, with FAO funding, provided relief to 100 livestock farmers in Qalqilya Governorate through an urgent response initiative. This support, aimed at assisting farmers affected by occupation and settler attacks, included water tanks, energy cubes, veterinary bags, fodder seeds, and cheese-making tools. The initiative seeks to bolster farmers' resilience, enhance food and water security, and develop the livestock sector.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Tunisia has made significant strides in renewable energy in 2024, selecting four solar projects totaling 500 MW from a larger 1,700 MW te...
records.description: Tunisia has made significant strides in renewable energy in 2024, selecting four solar projects totaling 500 MW from a larger 1,700 MW tender. These projects, awarded to companies like Qair International, Scatec ASA, and Voltalia SA, are expected to be operational by 2027, generating approximately 1,000 GWh annually, representing about 5% of Tunisia's electricity production and saving 250,000 tons of natural gas per year.
records.institution: The Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mines (Tunisia)

records.title: Tunisia's Minister of Agriculture announced a forthcoming assessment of the past date production season to identify challenges and improv...
records.description: Tunisia's Minister of Agriculture announced a forthcoming assessment of the past date production season to identify challenges and improve management for 2025. During a visit to Tozeur, the Minister emphasized learning from the current season's difficulties, including ensuring a sufficient supply of mosquito nets for the next two years through the Interprofessional Date Group (GIDATTES). He also addressed the issue of stalled agricultural projects in the region, promising local and central-level review and coordination.
records.institution: The Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries
