records.title: he Agricultural Excellence Award concluded registration for its third edition, recognized as a benchmark for quality and innovation in th...
records.description: he Agricultural Excellence Award concluded registration for its third edition, recognized as a benchmark for quality and innovation in the agricultural sector. The event attracted significant interest from farmers and livestock breeders, with 451 submissions across four main categories and 13 subcategories. With total cash prizes of AED5.3 million, the award aims to stimulate excellence in plant and animal agriculture, promote sustainable practices, and strengthen the food security system. It honors distinguished farmers, livestock breeders, and productive families, encouraging the adoption of modern agricultural systems and fostering positive competition to ensure the sector's sustainability.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Egypt aims to cultivate 3.1 million acres of wheat this season, targeting an increased yield of up to 25 ardab (150 kilograms) per acre,...
records.description: Egypt aims to cultivate 3.1 million acres of wheat this season, targeting an increased yield of up to 25 ardab (150 kilograms) per acre, up from the 2023 average of 20 ardab. The goal is to further increase productivity to 28 ardab per acre in the coming years, aiming for a total harvest of over 9.5 million tons. A national campaign to combat weeds will be launched, providing approved pesticides at the Ministry of Agriculture's expense. The Ministry also emphasizes the importance of agricultural guidance and the development of climate-resilient, water-efficient wheat strains.
records.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture provided a farmer in the northern Jordan Valley with potato tubers, fertilizers, and pesticides to encourage...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture provided a farmer in the northern Jordan Valley with potato tubers, fertilizers, and pesticides to encourage crop diversification in the area. This initiative aims to increase agricultural productivity, improve farmer incomes, and enhance food security. The introduction of potato cultivation, not currently common in the Jordan Valley, is intended to encourage other small farmers to adopt this crop. Specialists will monitor the project and collect data as part of a larger project supporting marginalized Palestinian communities, funded by German Cooperation BMZ and implemented by the Palestinian Center for Economic and Social Development in partnership with Oxfam and the Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the FAO and with Canadian funding, distributed dairy processing equipment to 65 sheep fa...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the FAO and with Canadian funding, distributed dairy processing equipment to 65 sheep farmers in Hebron. The equipment, including shakers, stainless steel tractors, cheese buckets, wool shears, gloves, and water drinkers, aims to improve product quality, enhance local economic development, and empower farmers facing challenges from the Israeli occupation.

records.title: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) distributed 747 food baskets and 747 hygiene kits to Syrian families in Al-...
records.description: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) distributed 747 food baskets and 747 hygiene kits to Syrian families in Al-Dana, Idlib Governorate. The aid, benefiting 4,482 individuals, is part of the second phase of a project to assist those affected by the recent earthquake in northern Syria. This distribution underscores Saudi Arabia's continued dedication to humanitarian support through KSrelief.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

records.title: Organic farming in Kairouan has expanded dramatically, growing from 200 hectares in 1995 to approximately 40,000 hectares today, along wi...
records.description: Organic farming in Kairouan has expanded dramatically, growing from 200 hectares in 1995 to approximately 40,000 hectares today, along with 5,000 hectares of organic forests. The region primarily focuses on exporting organic products, with olive oil exports increasing significantly from 3,000 tonnes in 2015 to over 10,000 tonnes currently, along with substantial exports of hyssop and prickly pears. While the number of organic farmers has grown to 200 and the state offers incentives for equipment, there are calls for increased subsidies for control and export processes to further support the sector and enhance the visibility of Tunisian organic brands on the global market.
records.institution: The Regional Directorate of Agricultural Development

records.title: The Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE) is prioritizing agricultural sector development and rural support, with 80% of its loans now allocat...
records.description: The Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE) is prioritizing agricultural sector development and rural support, with 80% of its loans now allocated to agriculture and related industries. This year, the bank doubled its financing for crop production, offering small farmers 5% interest loans. As of September 2024, this loan portfolio reached EGP 25.6 billion, benefiting approximately 252,000 farmers, an EGP 8.2 billion increase from the previous year. ABE is also focused on supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and empowering young entrepreneurs through initiatives like NilePreneurs, with over 64% of its credit portfolio dedicated to MSME financing. In the past five years, ABE has significantly increased its business volume and hired approximately 5,000 university graduates.

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture has announced a guide price of 35,000 Lebanese pounds per kilogram for bananas at the farm gate.
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture has announced a guide price of 35,000 Lebanese pounds per kilogram for bananas at the farm gate. This decision aims to support banana farmers affected by recent conflicts and ensure the sustainability of this important agricultural sector. The Ministry hopes this measure will help compensate farmers for losses, encourage continued banana cultivation, and support local production for both domestic and international markets. The set price is intended to balance the interests of farmers and consumers, and the Ministry urges all parties to adhere to it.

records.title: Morocco enters the 2024-2025 agricultural season with cautious optimism due to recent rainfall that has improved groundwater and dam levels.
records.description: Morocco enters the 2024-2025 agricultural season with cautious optimism due to recent rainfall that has improved groundwater and dam levels. While this offers potential for better crop yields, challenges remain, including climate unpredictability and ongoing water shortages in some areas. Recent rainfall has nearly doubled compared to the same period last year, and dam reserves have also increased, offering hope after a significant decline in cereal production last season. The government is supporting farmers with subsidized seeds and fertilizers, and an irrigation program. The agricultural sector remains vital to Morocco's economy, with recent export growth driven by vegetables, cereals, and legumes. Continued adaptation through modern technologies and support for small-scale farmers will be crucial for long-term sustainability.
records.institution: The Directorate of Studies and Financial Forecasts (DEPF), The Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: Tunisia has secured $29.6 million in funding from the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) for the "DINAMO" project, wh...
records.description: Tunisia has secured $29.6 million in funding from the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) for the "DINAMO" project, which will support small-scale mountain farming in the North-West region. This $47.7 million project aims to improve socio-economic conditions, enhance climate resilience, and generate income for low-income families, including women, youth, and small farmers/breeders. Targeting 19,375 rural households across five governorates by 2032, "DINAMO" will be implemented by the North-West Sylvo-Pastoral Development Office and focus on integrating small farmers into the local economy.

records.title: The Ouargla province in Algeria, particularly the Hassi Messaoud region, is seeing significant agricultural growth.
records.description: The Ouargla province in Algeria, particularly the Hassi Messaoud region, is seeing significant agricultural growth. A successful first experiment with sunflower cultivation is projected to yield over 12,500 quintals, while corn production is expected to reach nearly 14,000 quintals. Date production, a traditional strength of the region, is also projected to be high, with over 727,000 quintals expected. Supporting this agricultural expansion is an ongoing effort to electrify farms, with hundreds already connected to the grid and more planned. These developments highlight the region's increasing importance as an agricultural hub and the commitment of local authorities to supporting the sector.

records.title: Morocco has introduced a new support system for soft wheat imports to assist traders, cooperatives, and flour mills.
records.description: Morocco has introduced a new support system for soft wheat imports to assist traders, cooperatives, and flour mills. This system provides financial aid by covering the difference between the average import cost and a fixed price. This measure comes in response to a significant decline in Morocco's wheat harvest due to drought, which has led to increased reliance on imports, especially from Russia.
records.institution: The Ministry of Economy and Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: Oman has achieved 100% self-sufficiency in cucumber production, with over 103,000 tonnes produced in 2023, primarily in North al Batinah.
records.description: Oman has achieved 100% self-sufficiency in cucumber production, with over 103,000 tonnes produced in 2023, primarily in North al Batinah. The country also boasts high self-sufficiency rates for peppers (95%) and tomatoes (83%), with significant production also concentrated in North al Batinah. While some re-exporting and importing of these crops occurs, Oman is largely meeting its domestic needs.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture distributed 50 tons of animal feed to cattle breeders in the northern Jordan Valley (Tubas Governorate).
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture distributed 50 tons of animal feed to cattle breeders in the northern Jordan Valley (Tubas Governorate). This support aims to help farmers remain on their land despite challenges like the destruction of livestock pens, grazing restrictions, and attacks by settlers. This assistance also helps offset the high cost of feed and the prevention of access to pastures. The distribution, which benefited 40 farms, was part of a Jordanian grant project supporting livestock farmers in Palestine.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Hatta Honey Festival, a UAE event supporting Emirati beekeepers and honey production.
records.description: The Hatta Honey Festival, a UAE event supporting Emirati beekeepers and honey production. Organized by Dubai Municipality, the festival features 51 Emirati beekeepers and aims to promote the honey sector, support local businesses, and enhance Hatta's appeal as a tourist destination. The festival includes a honey auction, a best Emirati honey competition, educational workshops, entertainment, and children's activities. Dubai Municipality is also providing on-site laboratory testing to ensure honey quality and food safety. The event aims to generate economic opportunities for Hatta residents and contribute to the emirate's overall development.

records.title: A 40-day training course on agricultural and livestock value chains concluded, qualifying 38 agriculture graduates from Sana'a, Dhamar, a...
records.description: A 40-day training course on agricultural and livestock value chains concluded, qualifying 38 agriculture graduates from Sana'a, Dhamar, and Ibb universities. The course focused on preparing value chain studies, designing field surveys, and implementing data collection methods. Officials emphasized the importance of value chain analysis for identifying areas of improvement in agricultural products and calculating farmer returns. Trainees were encouraged to apply their new skills to advance the agricultural sector and contribute to food security. The course included both theoretical knowledge and practical application, covering data analysis, report writing, and field survey implementation.
records.institution: The General Authority for Agricultural Research and Extension.

records.title: A training course in Sana'a concluded, educating 300 rural women from Hamdan district about the benefits of compound flour as a substitut...
records.description: A training course in Sana'a concluded, educating 300 rural women from Hamdan district about the benefits of compound flour as a substitute for white flour and promoting improved dietary patterns. Organized by the General Organization for Grain Development and Production, the course highlighted the risks of relying on imported flour and taught methods for producing food items using compound flour, emphasizing self-sufficiency and a return to local dietary traditions. Accompanying the training was the opening of a bazaar featuring local compound flour products, further promoting domestic production and reducing dependence on imports.
records.institution: The General Organization for Grain Development and Production

records.title: Juhayna Food Industries' agricultural arm, El Enmaa for Agricultural Development, has been awarded three international certifications for...
records.description: Juhayna Food Industries' agricultural arm, El Enmaa for Agricultural Development, has been awarded three international certifications for sustainability and ethical practices: GLOBAL G.A.P. Version 6.0 SMART, GRASP Version 2.0, and SPRING Version 2.0. These certifications highlight Juhayna's commitment to environmental responsibility, fair labor practices, and sustainable water management. El Enmaa has also been listed on the SEDEX platform, further confirming its ethical supply chain. These achievements are expected to enhance the farm's operational efficiency, global competitiveness, and contribute to Egypt's national economy.

records.title: The Egyptian and Jordanian Ministers of Agriculture co-chaired the seventh session of their Joint Agricultural Technical Committee.
records.description: The Egyptian and Jordanian Ministers of Agriculture co-chaired the seventh session of their Joint Agricultural Technical Committee. They emphasized the strong historical relationship between the two countries and their shared vision for enhancing cooperation across all sectors, particularly agriculture. Discussions focused on increasing agricultural trade and removing obstacles to facilitate the flow of exports between the two nations. Both ministers highlighted the importance of mutual reliance for strategic depth and food security, and agreed to encourage agricultural investment and private sector involvement. They concluded with a commitment to addressing each other's needs for exportable commodities and food products.
records.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Proper harvesting and post-harvest management are essential for successful blueberry cultivation in Morocco.
records.description: Proper harvesting and post-harvest management are essential for successful blueberry cultivation in Morocco. Harvesting should occur 3-5 days after the berries turn uniformly blue, picking carefully to avoid damaging the fruit and keeping harvested berries in the shade. Picking frequency increases during peak season, requiring more pickers per hectare. Post-harvest, small farms can hand-sort and pack, while larger operations use mechanized packing lines. Maintaining a clean packing area, avoiding washing the berries, and rapidly cooling them to 0-1°C are crucial for maximizing shelf life and maintaining quality for market.

records.title: Syngenta has launched five new zucchini varieties in Morocco that are resistant to the New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV) and the Moroccan Type Wa...
records.description: Syngenta has launched five new zucchini varieties in Morocco that are resistant to the New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV) and the Moroccan Type Watermelon Mosaic Virus (MWMV). This announcement was made at a "Courgette Day" event in Agadir. These new varieties offer increased resistance, adaptability, and optimized yield, addressing the challenges posed by these viruses. The varieties also offer resistance to other viruses like CMV, ZYMV, and WMV, as well as powdery mildew. Each variety has specific strengths, such as adaptability to open fields or targeted resistance to specific viruses. The launch represents a significant advancement for zucchini production in Morocco and globally.

records.title: Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) is causing significant financial losses for tomato producers in Morocco, estimated at 15-20% of...
records.description: Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) is causing significant financial losses for tomato producers in Morocco, estimated at 15-20% of production. The virus reduces yields, lowers fruit quality, and creates market access challenges. This leads to decreased income for producers, compounded by increased costs for prevention and control measures. To mitigate these losses, Moroccan tomato producers are implementing various strategies: diversifying crops, adopting resistant varieties, strengthening biosecurity measures, seeking alternative markets, and collaborating with industry stakeholders to share knowledge and best practices. Supporting producers with resources and information is crucial for the Moroccan tomato industry.

records.title: Saudi Arabia significantly expanded its protected areas in 2023.
records.description: Saudi Arabia significantly expanded its protected areas in 2023. Protected land areas increased by 7.1% to 361,000 square kilometers (18.1% of the total land area), while marine protected areas grew by 17.7% to 14,000 square kilometers. The country also saw a 53.4% increase in average annual precipitation and a substantial rise in floodwater collected by dams. Other positive environmental developments include increased reuse of treated water, a decrease in collected municipal waste, and expansion of green spaces and parks.

records.title: Three rainwater harvesting projects, costing 75 million riyals, have been inaugurated in Bani Matar district in Sana'a governorate, Yemen.
records.description: Three rainwater harvesting projects, costing 75 million riyals, have been inaugurated in Bani Matar district in Sana'a governorate, Yemen. These projects aim to provide water for agriculture, replenish groundwater reserves, and support the expansion of crop cultivation, particularly almonds and cereals. Officials emphasized the importance of these projects for promoting agricultural production and urged farmers to utilize them effectively. The projects, implemented through the National Irrigation Program, include supporting farmers with irrigation networks and constructing rainwater harvesting tanks. Community involvement and local associations were also praised for their role in implementing these initiatives.

records.title: The newly formed Egyptian-Moroccan Joint Business Council held its first meeting to discuss ways to increase trade and investment between...
records.description: The newly formed Egyptian-Moroccan Joint Business Council held its first meeting to discuss ways to increase trade and investment between the two countries. The council plans to address investment challenges, explore opportunities in various sectors (including renewable energy, agriculture, and tourism), and organize a delegation of Egyptian businessmen to visit Morocco. The goal is to boost mutual investments, increase trade beyond the current $1.3 billion annually, and position Egypt as a gateway for Moroccan exports to East Africa. Additionally, four joint industrial projects will be presented to the Moroccan Minister of Trade for collaborative implementation. Egypt exports a range of goods to Morocco, including building materials, fertilizers, food products, and electrical appliances.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture is closely monitoring the daily fluctuations in wholesale and retail prices of essential food items, includin...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture is closely monitoring the daily fluctuations in wholesale and retail prices of essential food items, including meat, vegetables, fruits, and milk. As part of this effort, the Ministry is publishing average price bulletins on a weekly basis to provide transparency for the public and ensure a smooth flow of goods in the markets.

records.title: Agricultural authorities in the Béni Mellal-Khénifra region of Morocco are conducting a livestock census of sheep and goats.
records.description: Agricultural authorities in the Béni Mellal-Khénifra region of Morocco are conducting a livestock census of sheep and goats. Over 120 investigators, supported by agricultural advisors, are collecting data on livestock populations, distribution, and the impact of drought on breeders. This operation is part of a national census aimed at rebuilding livestock and strengthening the red meat sector.
records.institution: the Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: ADAFSA is working to achieve agricultural sustainability in Abu Dhabi through various programs and initiatives.
records.description: ADAFSA is working to achieve agricultural sustainability in Abu Dhabi through various programs and initiatives. These include promoting best practices through awards, optimizing water use, implementing modern agricultural technologies and climate-smart practices, and ensuring food safety. ADAFSA also provides training for farmers, supports beekeeping and honey production, offers veterinary services and maintains a livestock database, and focuses on reducing food loss and waste.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Goumbook, in partnership with several organizations, has opened applications for the second Menat Regenerative Agriculture Venture Progra...
records.description: Goumbook, in partnership with several organizations, has opened applications for the second Menat Regenerative Agriculture Venture Programme. This program aims to empower researchers, students, and innovators in the Middle East, North Africa, and Turkey (MENAT) to develop regenerative agricultural solutions addressing food systems, biodiversity loss, climate change, and water management. The program bridges the gap between research and business, focusing on scalable solutions for small to medium-sized farms. Twenty selected participants will receive intensive training and mentorship, with three winners receiving $20,000 grants and further support. The program emphasizes local solutions to the MENAT region's unique agricultural challenges, such as arid climates and water scarcity.

records.domain: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
records.title: A new model nursery has been inaugurated in Dhamar City.
records.description: A new model nursery has been inaugurated in Dhamar City. Supervised by a local fund, the nursery will produce seedlings for various purposes, including fruit trees, ornamental plants, and forestry. Local officials emphasized the importance of expanding seedling production and distribution to support local agriculture, promote environmental sustainability, and achieve self-sufficiency. The nursery is projected to produce over 100,000 seedlings annually, building on previous tree-planting initiatives in public areas and along roads.
records.institution: The Haran Park Administration in Dhamar City

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt is prioritizing a stable and reliable electricity supply through grid modernization, renewable energy expansion, and increased reli...
records.description: Egypt is prioritizing a stable and reliable electricity supply through grid modernization, renewable energy expansion, and increased reliance on clean energy. The Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC) has invested significantly in upgrading high and ultra-high voltage infrastructure, integrating renewable energy sources (reaching 22.8 GW in various stages), and initiating battery storage projects. These efforts aim to achieve 42% renewable energy in the national mix by 2030. Egypt is also enhancing power interconnectivity with neighboring countries to become a regional energy hub. The focus is on efficient grid operation, reduced technical losses, and human resource development in advanced energy technologies.

records.title: The Egyptian Minister of Agriculture has announced an initiative to support young graduates and agricultural college students in developi...
records.description: The Egyptian Minister of Agriculture has announced an initiative to support young graduates and agricultural college students in developing and implementing agricultural projects. The Ministry is open to receiving practical ideas and will provide support through funding, training, and technical assistance in collaboration with organizations like the Agricultural Research Center and the Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE). The initiative aims to promote youth involvement in the agricultural sector, which is a key driver of Egypt's economic development, food security, and agricultural exports. ABE also highlighted its commitment to supporting young entrepreneurs in the agricultural sector through various financing programs and initiatives.
records.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and the Knights of Malta signed a memorandum of cooperation to promote agricultural and rural develo...
records.description: The Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and the Knights of Malta signed a memorandum of cooperation to promote agricultural and rural development. This agreement aims to enhance collaboration between the public sector and civil society to support farmers, improve agricultural conditions in needy areas, and implement sustainable development projects in rural communities. The memorandum focuses on providing technical support to farmers and strengthening sustainable initiatives within the agricultural sector.

records.title: A study was conducted to monitor the seasonal changes in nutrient levels within fig tree leaves to optimize fertilization timing and foli...
records.description: A study was conducted to monitor the seasonal changes in nutrient levels within fig tree leaves to optimize fertilization timing and foliar diagnosis. Foliar analyses of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), calcium (Ca), and magnesium (Mg) were performed every 15 days throughout the growing cycle of mature fig trees. The results showed that N, P, and K levels decreased as leaves aged, likely due to nutrient mobilization towards developing fruit. Conversely, Ca and Mg levels increased with leaf age. These findings suggest optimal periods for foliar diagnosis when nutrient content is relatively stable.

records.title: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture has announced several new food security projects in partnership with government and private sector entities.
records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture has announced several new food security projects in partnership with government and private sector entities. These include a large-scale sugar refinery at Sohar Port with a production capacity of one million tonnes per year, a food industries center in Khazaen Economic City, expanded wheat silos at Sohar Port increasing storage capacity to 160,000 tonnes, and the expansion of a fodder factory in Muttrah to increase production capacity to 20 tonnes. These projects aim to boost local food production, increase storage capacity, and enhance overall food security in Oman.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

records.title: The Fisheries Research Centre in Dhofar Governorate, Oman, is implementing an initiative to release 40,000 locally produced abalone seeds...
records.description: The Fisheries Research Centre in Dhofar Governorate, Oman, is implementing an initiative to release 40,000 locally produced abalone seeds into key fishing areas. This program aims to replenish natural abalone stocks, which have been declining due to overfishing and habitat loss. The initiative seeks to ensure the sustainability of this valuable marine resource, which is important for both the local ecosystem and the economy. The program also focuses on supporting local fishermen, promoting sustainable practices, and gathering data to improve fisheries management. While challenges remain, such as ensuring abalone survival rates and habitat restoration, the initiative is considered a significant step towards sustainable fisheries management.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The inaugural Al Ain Dates Festival will take place in Al Ain City, under the patronage of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
records.description: The inaugural Al Ain Dates Festival will take place in Al Ain City, under the patronage of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The festival will feature date competitions with substantial prizes, a date auction, a traditional market, a heritage village, and various cultural activities. The event aims to highlight the importance of date production to the UAE's economy, food security, and cultural heritage, while supporting local farmers and promoting modern agricultural techniques.

records.title: In Ibb Governorate, Yemen, 50 tons of improved wheat seeds were distributed to local farmers as part of an emergency agricultural program...
records.description: In Ibb Governorate, Yemen, 50 tons of improved wheat seeds were distributed to local farmers as part of an emergency agricultural program for the winter season. This initiative aims to expand the cultivation of essential grain and legume crops.
records.institution: The Agriculture Sector in Ibb Governorate

records.title: Yemen has launched the second phase of manufacturing locally-made agricultural machinery, including harvesters, corn threshers, and fodde...
records.description: Yemen has launched the second phase of manufacturing locally-made agricultural machinery, including harvesters, corn threshers, and fodder choppers. This initiative, overseen by the Ministry of Agriculture and produced by the Bunyan Development Foundation, aims to reduce reliance on imports, provide affordable equipment to local farmers, and boost local manufacturing capabilities. Government officials emphasized the importance of this development for food security and praised the quality of the locally produced machinery, which rivals imported equipment. The initiative also seeks to increase agricultural productivity and support local farmers through the provision of these locally manufactured tools.

records.title: Egypt is investing heavily in agricultural development in Upper Egypt, particularly in Minya, with a focus on sustainability and improvin...
records.description: Egypt is investing heavily in agricultural development in Upper Egypt, particularly in Minya, with a focus on sustainability and improving the livelihoods of smallholder farmers. Significant funds have been allocated to the region, including EGP 62.4 billion this fiscal year and EGP 43.2 billion under the "Decent Life" initiative. Key projects, implemented in partnership with IFAD and FAO, include upgrading irrigation systems to more efficient drip irrigation powered by solar energy, establishing solar energy units and pumps, and providing training in climate-smart agricultural practices and natural resource management through farmer field schools. These initiatives aim to modernize agriculture, optimize water use, boost productivity, create jobs, and enhance the sector's contribution to the Egyptian economy.
records.institution: The Ministry of Irrigation and Water Resources

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The World Bank has approved $250 million in funding for Morocco to enhance the resilience of its agri-food system to climate change and i...
records.description: The World Bank has approved $250 million in funding for Morocco to enhance the resilience of its agri-food system to climate change and improve food safety and quality. The program will promote climate-smart agricultural practices, improve water and soil management, expand organic farming, enhance food quality control, and reduce food loss and waste. It aims to benefit over 1.36 million people, including farmers and consumers, by improving livelihoods, increasing incomes, and strengthening food security. A $5 million grant from the Livable Planet Fund will further support smallholder farmers in transitioning to climate-smart practices.

records.title: The Oman Association for Consumer Protection (OACP) held a symposium in Muscat to explore the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in imp...
records.description: The Oman Association for Consumer Protection (OACP) held a symposium in Muscat to explore the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving food security and ensuring the sustainability of food resources in Oman. The symposium emphasized the importance of integrating AI technologies into the agricultural sector to achieve sustainable development and enhance consumer awareness of AI's applications in this field.
records.institution: The Oman Association for Consumer Protection (OACP)

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture held an advisory workshop in Hebron focused on modern agricultural technologies and the development of agricu...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture held an advisory workshop in Hebron focused on modern agricultural technologies and the development of agricultural cooperatives. Horticultural farmers from North and South Hebron participated in the three-day training program, which was provided by Nexus International Consulting and Training Company. records.description: Farmers in the Qassim region of Saudi Arabia have successfully cultivated strawberries and other berries, demonstrating their commitment to innovation and reducing reliance on imports. The use of hydroponics has significantly boosted yields while simplifying plant care and minimizing the need for fertilizers and pesticides. This success story highlights the region's agricultural potential and its contribution to local food security.

records.title: Algerian public banks will begin offering agricultural credit in 2025 to boost productivity in the agricultural sector.

This initiative follows agreements between the Ministry of Agriculture and individual banks, as well as an existing agreement with the Professional Association of Banks and Financial Institutions. While the Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (BADR) currently handles the majority of agricultural financing, other banks will introduce new financing options, including Islamic finance. The government aims to streamline the loan application process and is working to digitize banking services, allowing for online applications and tracking.

records.title: The Egyptian citrus season has begun with strong global demand but faces challenges due to erratic weather that has slightly reduced frui...
records.description: The Egyptian citrus season has begun with strong global demand but faces challenges due to erratic weather that has slightly reduced fruit size and yield. While exports to Europe and the Middle East are positive, overall production in Egypt has declined. Despite this, improved farming techniques have helped maintain quality. Exporters are looking to expand into Asian and African markets to reduce logistical costs and diversify their reach. Competition from Spain and Turkey remains significant, but opportunities for collaboration also exist. Prices have moderately increased due to lower supply and higher freight costs. Despite these challenges, a positive outlook remains for the season, with expectations of sustainable growth and market expansion.

If the pilot is successful, production will be scaled up, marking a major step in local shrimp production and reducing reliance on imports.

While the project is successful, there is a desire to expand production with additional tools and resources.

records.title: Morocco has launched a national direct seeding program to promote sustainable and productive agriculture.
records.description: Morocco has launched a national direct seeding program to promote sustainable and productive agriculture. The program aims to cover 260,000 hectares during the current agricultural campaign and eventually reach one million hectares by 2030. Direct seeding offers several advantages, including water conservation, reduced erosion, and improved soil health. The government is providing support to farmers through seed subsidies, technical assistance, and the distribution of direct seeding equipment. This initiative is part of a broader effort to address water scarcity and enhance agricultural productivity in Morocco.

records.description: Egypt's wheat production is expected to increase to 9.2 million tonnes in the 2024/25 season, up from 8.87 million tonnes the previous year, according to a report by the Foreign Agricultural Service of the USDA. This increase is due to government-led initiatives to expand the wheat planting area and improve yield strategies, including attractive procurement prices that have encouraged more farmers to cultivate wheat. Despite this boost in domestic production, Egypt will still import an estimated 12.5 million tonnes of wheat to meet local demand, maintaining its position as one of the world's largest wheat importers. The total value of wheat imports in the first half of 2024 increased significantly, indicating Egypt's continued reliance on imported wheat, driven by its robust milling industry and regional supply needs.

The agreement is designed to promote sustainable economic development in Libya and will operate within the legal frameworks of both nations. During the ceremony, the Libyan representative highlighted Libya’s potential as an emerging market and invited more American business involvement while acknowledging the need to address potential challenges.

records.description: Saudi Arabia has called for urgent international action on land degradation, drought, and desertification at the "Road to Riyadh" event during the UN General Assembly in New York. This call comes as the country prepares to host the 16th UN Convention to Combat Desertification (COP16) in Riyadh this December. Saudi officials, including the Foreign Minister and the Minister of Environment, emphasized the pivotal role of the upcoming conference in promoting land restoration and sustainable resource use globally. They also highlighted Saudi Arabia's contributions through initiatives like the Saudi Green Initiative and the G20 Global Land Initiative. The UNCCD has warned that significant land restoration is needed by 2030 to meet sustainability targets, making the discussions at COP16 crucial for global environmental efforts.

records.title: Danone Egypt has launched the "Gawda" project to enhance milk collection with advanced cooling technology in the Beni Suef and Gharbia go...
records.description: Danone Egypt has launched the "Gawda" project to enhance milk collection with advanced cooling technology in the Beni Suef and Gharbia governorates. This initiative, part of the 'Alban Baladna' program, aims to preserve the quality and nutritional value of milk by maintaining low temperatures during collection, thereby reducing bacterial growth and contamination. The project is also integrated into Danone’s broader sustainability and "Zero Food Waste" efforts. By improving milk safety and transportation, the initiative supports Danone's goal of delivering nutritious dairy products while aligning with its "Danone Impact Journey" to significantly reduce contamination risks. Additionally, the project supports economic empowerment through a $50 million co-investment in the AWRAS initiative, aimed at enhancing the role of women in agriculture across Africa.

records.title: The potential for Egypt to surpass its previous potato export record to Eastern Europe in the 2024/25 season faces significant challenges...
records.description: The potential for Egypt to surpass its previous potato export record to Eastern Europe in the 2024/25 season faces significant challenges due to a complex European market. After setting a record in the 2023/24 season, Egyptian exporters are contending with a turbulent European potato market, impacted by poor weather conditions and a crisis in the seed potato market. Additionally, an oversupply of lower-quality potatoes from Western EU countries could increase competition and affect market dynamics. These factors, combined with the ongoing adjustments in the seed potato sector that also impact Egypt, suggest that despite previous successes, the upcoming season may present tougher conditions for increasing exports.

records.title: Morocco achieved record blueberry exports to Eastern Europe in the first half of 2024, delivering 2.1 thousand tons, surpassing the total...
records.description: Morocco achieved record blueberry exports to Eastern Europe in the first half of 2024, delivering 2.1 thousand tons, surpassing the total exports for 2023. Key destinations included Poland, which imported 1.5 thousand tons, along with Estonia, Ukraine, and the Czech Republic. While direct exports to Ukraine and the Czech Republic declined slightly, overall demand for Moroccan blueberries in the region remains strong. The growth in exports reflects increased off-season consumption in Eastern Europe, with Morocco benefiting from peak demand between January and June, competing with other major exporters such as Spain, Chile, and Peru.

records.description: The Institutes of Specialized Technicians in Agriculture (ITSA) in Témara launched the 2024-2025 school year, focusing on new projects in agricultural vocational training. The initiatives include training programs in desalination and water treatment, the inauguration of a 70-bed boarding school for girls, and visits to technology halls, laboratories, and a precision agriculture station. The Minister of Agriculture emphasized the importance of vocational training in addressing challenges related to resource management, modernization, and climate change. The system aims to train 140,000 graduates by 2030, with efforts to improve governance, teaching quality, and employability through digital learning and practical internships.

This initiative is part of a comprehensive flood control strategy following Cyclone Gonu, including the upgrade of the Al Khawd Recharge Dam and the addition of three new dams—Al Khawd, Nafah, and Multaqa—with capacities to manage significant volumes of water. The consultancy will involve preparing detailed designs, tender documents, and supervising construction to improve the region’s resilience against future flooding.

records.title: Ahead of the 2024-2025 plowing-sowing campaign, Algeria’s Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development announced plans to cultivate 3.7...
records.description: Ahead of the 2024-2025 plowing-sowing campaign, Algeria’s Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development announced plans to cultivate 3.7 million hectares starting October 1, aiming to produce 1.645 million tons of durum wheat. The goal is to achieve self-sufficiency in durum wheat by 2025 and end barley imports by 2026, with 1.17 million hectares allocated for barley cultivation. Favorable rainfall and the distribution of 4.2 million tons of certified seeds are expected to support the campaign. Advance provision of seeds and fertilizers, along with adherence to technical processes, are emphasized to ensure success. Four workshops addressed key areas, including financing, insurance, fertilizer use, and irrigation methods, contributing to the development of the campaign’s roadmap.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries

records.title: Precision agriculture in Algeria, driven by artificial intelligence (AI), is showing significant promise in improving yields and resource...
records.description: Precision agriculture in Algeria, driven by artificial intelligence (AI), is showing significant promise in improving yields and resource management. AI-based systems help optimize water use, potentially reducing consumption by 30% while increasing yields by 25%. Notable projects include the "Sakai" initiative, developed by Algerian researchers, using autonomous solar-powered robots for precise irrigation and fertilization, attracting international interest from NASA and Chinese research centers. Remote smart irrigation systems notify farmers via smartphones, enabling real-time adjustments based on soil conditions. Additional initiatives include fully automated farms focused on cherry tomato production and "Farm AI," a startup leveraging drones to detect plant diseases. These advancements are positioning Algeria as a leader in digital agricultural transformation, opening doors for further international partnerships and investments.

records.title: In Cairo, pollution in the Nile has severely impacted its ecosystem, causing local fishermen to shift from fishing to collecting plastic...
records.description: In Cairo, pollution in the Nile has severely impacted its ecosystem, causing local fishermen to shift from fishing to collecting plastic waste for recycling, which now proves more profitable. The river, contaminated with garbage and dead animals, has seen a dramatic decrease in fish populations and quality. Despite efforts by the government to clean the river, significant gaps remain, filled by initiatives like VeryNile that work with local communities to recycle the waste into useful products. This change reflects the ongoing environmental challenges faced by the river and its surrounding communities.

Additionally, an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Code has been established to set standards and practices for integrating ESG considerations into banking operations, aligning with global best practices and laws.

records.description: The European Union (EU) has banned the sale of Algeria's popular dairy spread, El Mordjene Cebon, due to its failure to meet EU standards on hygiene, residue, and animal health. The ban highlights the broader challenge Algeria faces in aligning its dairy production with stringent EU regulations, as opposed to the less rigorous standards it adheres to under Australian guidelines. As Algeria aims to boost its domestic dairy output to reduce import reliance, the country continues to struggle to meet its own high demand for milk, leading to significant imports from both traditional and new suppliers.

These strategies collectively aim to enhance sustainability, protect the livelihoods of farmers, and secure the nation's food supply.

Together with Algeria’s National Investment Fund, Baladna is launching a dairy and milk powder production project in southern Algeria, poised to meet 50% of the country's domestic powdered milk demand upon completion in 2026. This venture, part of a broader strategy initiated with the Algerian Ministry of Agriculture, involves stages from exploratory drilling for water to constructing a powdered milk factory. Additionally, Baladna has partnered with the Algerian Ministry of Industry for an infant milk production project in Algiers, with plans for a facility producing 15,000 tons of powdered milk and 10,000 tons of infant flour annually by 2025, aiming to significantly reduce Algeria’s reliance on imported infant milk.

records.title: Egypt's agricultural exports have surpassed 6.4 million tons year-to-date, marking an increase of over 529,000 tons compared to 2023.
records.description: Egypt's agricultural exports have surpassed 6.4 million tons year-to-date, marking an increase of over 529,000 tons compared to 2023. Citrus fruits led the exports with over 2.2 million tons, followed by fresh potatoes with nearly 965,796 tons. Onions ranked third, while beans, grapes, and sweet potatoes also contributed significantly. Other key exports included mangoes, pomegranates, tomatoes, garlic, strawberries, and guava, highlighting Egypt's strong agricultural output in 2024.

records.title: Egypt's food exports to Libya have increased by 18%, reaching US$183 million in the first seven months of 2024, according to the Egyptian...
records.description: Egypt's food exports to Libya have increased by 18%, reaching US$183 million in the first seven months of 2024, according to the Egyptian Food Export Council. This growth continues from a previous increase of 8% in 2023, bringing the total to US$291 million for that year. This represents 5.3% of Egypt's total food exports in 2023. Egyptian manufacturers are pushing to position locally made products as competitive alternatives to European imports in the Libyan market. Additionally, investments by multinational FMCG companies like Mars and Kraft Heinz in Egypt indicate a growing confidence in Egyptian products' potential in both domestic and regional markets, particularly Libya. Trade logistics have been facilitated by the Amsaad-Sallum crossing, although recent political tensions have led to new fees on both sides, potentially complicating future trade dynamics.

records.title: Farmers in Jordan's Koura district have begun the pomegranate harvest, which will continue until mid-December.
records.description: Farmers in Jordan's Koura district have begun the pomegranate harvest, which will continue until mid-December. Spread across 2,000 dunums, the orchards are concentrated near perennial streams, including Wadi Zeqlab and Wadi Abu Zeyad. Early harvesting started in areas with climates similar to the Jordan Valley, while other regions, such as Wadi Rayyan, will conclude later in the season. The district produces various pomegranate-based products, including juice, molasses, vinegar, and cosmetics, providing a crucial source of income for local families.

records.title: Facing a severe water scarcity crisis exacerbated by climate change and rising temperatures, Egypt plans to reduce rice cultivation by 32...
records.description: Facing a severe water scarcity crisis exacerbated by climate change and rising temperatures, Egypt plans to reduce rice cultivation by 32% to 315,000 hectares by 2025. As Africa's second-largest rice producer, this move addresses the critical water shortage threatening its agricultural sector. Despite producing an average of 3.8 million tonnes of milled rice annually, Egypt consumes about 4.3 million tonnes, leading to a reliance on imports to bridge the gap. The country faces a significant water deficit, with a demand of 114 billion cubic meters annually versus an availability of just 60 billion cubic meters. In response, the Egyptian government, with support from international agencies, is trialing new hybrid rice varieties that require up to 33% less water, potentially offering a more sustainable solution to maintain production levels amid environmental challenges.

The plan aims to identify vulnerable sites in need of conservation interventions and potential rainwater collection areas, forming the foundation for a national action plan under the Generation Green strategy. The study will focus on sustainable resource management, addressing agricultural land degradation, water shortages, and erosion. It will also involve mapping priority sites and defining techniques for rainwater collection, ensuring sustainable agricultural practices in the region.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s Agricultural Development Fund has approved $533 million in loans and credit facilities to enhance food sustainability and...
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s Agricultural Development Fund has approved $533 million in loans and credit facilities to enhance food sustainability and security throughout the Kingdom. The funding will support various agricultural initiatives such as red meat and poultry production, greenhouse farming, fish aquaculture, and cold storage facilities. This move is aimed at increasing domestic crop production and reducing reliance on imported food. The fund has made strides toward self-sufficiency in dates, fresh dairy products, and table eggs. The initiative also involves financing working capital in collaboration with banks to support the importation of key agricultural products, aiming to stabilize supply chains and strengthen food reserves.

records.description: The Saudi Agricultural Development Fund (ADF) has approved over $533 million in loans and credit facilities for projects across the Kingdom. records.description: Agricultural investments in Gabès, Tunisia, increased by 35% by the end of August 2024, reaching 21 million dinars, compared to 15.5 million dinars during the same period last year, according to the Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency (APIA). These investments encompass 141 operations across agriculture, fisheries, aquaculture, and related services, creating 130 jobs. The delegation of Gabès-Ville led with 6.2 million dinars in approved investments, followed by El Hamma with 6.1 million dinars and Mareth with 2.9 million dinars.

records.description: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune reaffirmed Algeria’s goal of achieving self-sufficiency in strategic crops by 2025-2026, emphasizing progress in agricultural production through scientific planning and international partnerships. The targets include self-sufficiency in durum wheat by 2025 and in barley and corn by 2026. Tebboune announced plans to expand irrigated areas by one million hectares, generating 450,000 new jobs, and stressed the importance of supporting start-ups, aiming to grow their number to 20,000 by the end of his term.

records.description: Egypt is preparing a long-term vision for its 2024-2030 investment and trade policies to enhance investor confidence, boost exports, and diversify the economy. The government aims to improve trade through streamlined procedures and has established carbon certification units to align with global environmental standards.

records.title: Tomato prices in Egypt, which have increased by 400% since the start of the year, reaching EGP 25 per kilogram up from EGP 5, are expecte...
records.description: Tomato prices in Egypt, which have increased by 400% since the start of the year, reaching EGP 25 per kilogram up from EGP 5, are expected to decrease by November, according to the Head of the Farmers Union. The price hike has been attributed to rising costs, inflation, reduced tomato cultivation areas, and farmers switching to more profitable crops. The expected price drop is due to the overlapping growing seasons across different regions and increased production. Additional economic pressures stem from global tensions affecting the cost of imported tomato seeds and agricultural supplies.

records.title: Iraq Unveils Ambitious National Strategy to Protect the Environment and Address Climate Change
records.description: Iraq has introduced a six-year National Strategy for the Protection and Improvement of the Environment to tackle climate change, pollution, and resource depletion. The strategy, covering 2024-2030, aims to improve air and water quality, restore biodiversity, and combat desertification. It identifies five key areas of focus, including climate adaptation and public awareness. Challenges like water scarcity, due to regional dam projects, and improper waste disposal are addressed. The plan also emphasizes the need for government funding and international support to achieve its environmental goals.
records.institution: Iraqi Ministry Of Health And Environment

records.title: Libya's Minister of Economy and Trade met with the Japanese ambassador to Libya to discuss strengthening economic and trade relations bet...
records.description: Libya's Minister of Economy and Trade met with the Japanese ambassador to Libya to discuss strengthening economic and trade relations between the two nations. The discussions, held in Tripoli, focused on enhancing cooperation across various sectors including clean energy, industrial and free zones, and potentially opening a branch of the Libyan-Japanese Center for Training and Consulting Agency in Libya. Both parties agreed to prepare a memorandum of understanding to protect investors' rights and expressed commitment to facilitating the operations of Japanese companies and investors in Libya. They also planned a Libyan-Japanese forum in Tripoli for 2025, aiming to involve the private sector from both countries and increase trade exchange.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.title: For the 2024-2025 agricultural campaign, Morocco’s Ministry of Agriculture has introduced state support for new certified seed varieties,...
records.description: For the 2024-2025 agricultural campaign, Morocco’s Ministry of Agriculture has introduced state support for new certified seed varieties, including legumes such as oats, triticale, beans, lentils, and chickpeas. Subsidies will vary by crop, with oats and triticale receiving 180 dirhams per quintal, beans and vetches 205 dirhams, and chickpeas and lentils 395 dirhams. The initiative aims to diversify crops and boost national seed production, extending subsidies previously limited to cereal seeds to pulses. The ministry plans to mobilize 1.26 million quintals of certified cereal seeds, with key contributions from Sonacos and private operators. Additional support includes storage subsidies for seed distributors and subsidies for vegetable crops like tomatoes, potatoes, and onions, covering up to 70% of costs. Fertilizers will also be provided at subsidized rates to ensure sustainable agricultural practices and stable market prices.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests

records.title: In Guercif Province, the Integrated Rural Development Project for the Mountain Areas of the Oriental Region (PADERMO) has been launched,...
records.description: In Guercif Province, the Integrated Rural Development Project for the Mountain Areas of the Oriental Region (PADERMO) has been launched, with an investment of 410.9 million dirhams over seven years. The project aims to improve living conditions and agricultural production for more than 40,000 farmers across five municipalities. Key initiatives include the development of climate-resilient fruit crops, support for animal sectors, and the launch of saffron planting through the distribution of 46 tons of saffron bulbs to 30 beneficiaries. Additionally, 100 hectares of cochineal-resistant cactus will be planted, with plans to plant 500 hectares by 2030. Other infrastructure projects include boreholes, water storage basins, and mobile tanks to support sustainable agriculture in the region.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests

records.title: The Kurdistan Regional Government has initiated a $480 million emergency water supply project in Erbil to tackle the city's water shortage.
records.description: The Kurdistan Regional Government has initiated a $480 million emergency water supply project in Erbil to tackle the city's water shortage. Scheduled to be completed in 550 days, the project plans to treat 480,000 cubic meters of water daily, providing 20,000 to 21,000 cubic meters of drinkable water per hour to various neighborhoods. The source of the water will be the Greater Zab River, and the project will incorporate modern filtration and sterilization methods that comply with WHO standards. It also aims to conserve groundwater by closing over 1,000 wells.

The closure followed several infractions recorded in previous inspections during the past year. The bakery will be permitted to reopen only after it implements corrective actions that align with UAE food safety laws and addresses the specific reasons for the closure. These include issues such as improper display of ready-to-serve foods and the presence of personal items in storage areas. ADAFSA's ongoing efforts to uphold food safety standards include regular inspections and public campaigns to encourage reporting of food safety concerns.

records.description: Over 80% of Gaza’s estimated 640,000 children under 10 have received their first polio vaccination in a UN-led campaign, which began on September 1. Parents have shown concern for their children's health, though many question the sincerity of international efforts. The campaign, taking place during humanitarian pauses, continues in northern Gaza and is set to end Thursday, as airstrikes and deteriorating conditions raise concerns about the spread of diseases.

The agreement aims to make the heat-reducing technology more accessible to Egyptian farmers, enhancing crop yields while reducing water and energy use by over 30%. This innovation has been tested in Egypt, proving its effectiveness in extreme climates. The collaboration also supports iyris' global expansion in sustainable agriculture solutions.

records.title: Rebound has launched a subscription-based platform in the UAE to promote recycling and support the circular economy.
records.description: Rebound has launched a subscription-based platform in the UAE to promote recycling and support the circular economy. The platform connects global buyers, sellers, and partners of recyclable materials, such as plastics, metals, and paper, offering a 0% commission on trades. Subscribers receive access to account managers, price indices, and an industry discussion hub.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Boumerdes leads Algeria’s national table grape production, contributing over 50% of total output.
records.description: Boumerdes leads Algeria’s national table grape production, contributing over 50% of total output. For the 2023/2024 season, 17,000 hectares are dedicated to vine cultivation, with an estimated yield of 4.5 million quintals. Dominant varieties include Sabéle (49%), Red Globe (20%), and Cardinal (18%). Boumerdes supplies grapes to other regions and is exploring opportunities in processing for soft drinks, packaging, and exports, aiming to expand its presence in international markets.
records.institution: Algerian Regional Directorate of Agricultural Services (DRA)

records.title: Bahrain’s agricultural sector is expected to grow by 1.9% annually from 2024 to 2029, according to a report.
records.description: Bahrain’s agricultural sector is expected to grow by 1.9% annually from 2024 to 2029, according to a report. Despite its dependence on imported food, Bahrain remains a top global producer of dates. The government is enhancing local agriculture through financial assistance and partnerships with tech firms to reduce reliance on imports. The National Initiative for Agricultural Development focuses on modern farming techniques, water efficiency, and expanding green spaces. Key crops include dates, figs, and potatoes, with local dairy and poultry mainly serving the domestic market.

records.title: Al Ahram Beverages Company, a subsidiary of Heineken, announced a €30 million (US$33.1M) investment to expand its operations in Egypt.
records.description: Al Ahram Beverages Company, a subsidiary of Heineken, announced a €30 million (US$33.1M) investment to expand its operations in Egypt. This includes relocating its headquarters to New Cairo and enhancing its Sharkiya plant with new production lines, increasing capacity to 3.7 million hectoliters. The investment supports sustainability initiatives such as reducing carbon emissions, aiming for net-zero by 2030 for Scope 1 and 2, and by 2040 across its value chain. The company is also focused on waste management and water conservation projects.

records.title: Oman Krishikkottam, a group promoting pesticide-free agriculture, held its 14th seed distribution event in Ruwi, providing 17 varieties o...
records.description: Oman Krishikkottam, a group promoting pesticide-free agriculture, held its 14th seed distribution event in Ruwi, providing 17 varieties of vegetable seeds to over 200 people. This initiative encourages sustainable, home-grown food practices, particularly within Oman's Indian diaspora. The event featured educational sessions on organic farming techniques, aimed at empowering families to grow vegetables at home. With a community of over 4,500 families, the group continues to advocate for organic farming and a healthier environment.

records.title: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources (MAFWR) has launched the National Animal Wealth Vaccination Project in Sou...
records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources (MAFWR) has launched the National Animal Wealth Vaccination Project in South Batinah. The project aims to vaccinate livestock against major epidemic and infectious diseases over an eight-month period. This initiative is part of the national strategy to improve animal health, lower treatment costs, and ensure the production of safe, high-quality animal products. Last season, over 288,964 animals were vaccinated. The program also focuses on educating livestock breeders on modern practices.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Preparations for the 2024-2025 agricultural season are underway in the governorate of Kef, with efforts focused on ensuring the supply of...
records.description: Preparations for the 2024-2025 agricultural season are underway in the governorate of Kef, with efforts focused on ensuring the supply of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides. The region requires 40,000 quintals of durum wheat and 80,000 quintals of barley, along with selected seeds amounting to 35,000 quintals of durum wheat, 5,000 quintals of soft wheat, and 5,000 quintals of barley to cover 200,000 hectares, including 5,500 hectares for irrigated cereals. Authorities have allocated 232,000 hectares for major crops, alongside 35,000 hectares for fodder and legumes. To support these efforts, 150,000 quintals of ammonium nitrate, 50,000 quintals of di-ammonium phosphate, and 20,000 quintals of superphosphate are being distributed to farmers.

records.title: The Emirates Development Bank (EDB) launched the AGRIX Accelerator to advance the UAE’s agricultural sector through innovative technologi...
records.description: The Emirates Development Bank (EDB) launched the AGRIX Accelerator to advance the UAE’s agricultural sector through innovative technologies and sustainable farming practices. The 20-week program provides participants with access to expert-led workshops, mentorship, and agri-tech tools, supporting the UAE's National Food Security Strategy 2051. EDB also offers tailored financing solutions, such as the AgriTech Loans Programme, aimed at boosting local food production and reducing reliance on imports, contributing to sustainable growth and food self-sufficiency.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The UAE's Minister of Climate Change and Environment, Dr.
records.description: The UAE's Minister of Climate Change and Environment, Dr. Amna Al Dahak, emphasized the country's alignment with GCC nations on harmonizing efforts to enhance regional food security. At the 36th GCC Agricultural and Food Security Committee meeting, she highlighted the UAE’s initiatives in sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, and modern agricultural technologies. The minister also called on GCC countries to participate in the World Food Security Summit in Abu Dhabi in November 2024, aimed at fostering collaboration and innovation in global food security.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment

records.title: Egypt's trade deficit decreased by 5.1% in June 2024, reaching $2.87 billion compared to $3.02 billion in June 2023, according to the Cen...
records.description: Egypt's trade deficit decreased by 5.1% in June 2024, reaching $2.87 billion compared to $3.02 billion in June 2023, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics. Exports fell by 1.6%, with declines in fertilizers and crude oil, while imports decreased by 3.3%, notably in wheat and medicines. However, exports of petroleum products and fresh fruits saw increases, as did imports of petroleum products and natural gas.
records.institution: Egyptian Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: National Strategy for Sustainable Land Management in Iraq
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Iraq's Ministry of Environment (MoE) are collaborating to develop the National Strategy for Sustainable Land Management (SLM) in Iraq, aiming to improve livelihoods in degraded areas. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the project is in partnership with Iraq’s Ministries of Agriculture and Water Resources, focusing on conservation agriculture and agroecological practices in Thi Qar and Al Muthanna governorates. The initiative has already increased wheat and barley yields by 20-25% through conservation agriculture. Next steps include finalizing the national SLM strategy, training officials, and establishing Farmer Field School demonstration plots to promote sustainable practices.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) & Iraqi Ministry of Environment

records.title: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) held discussions with Nepal’s Ambassador to the UAE to explore opportunities for enha...
records.description: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) held discussions with Nepal’s Ambassador to the UAE to explore opportunities for enhancing trade and investment cooperation between the UAE and Nepal's private sectors. The talks focused on the potential signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen ties in sectors such as trade, handicrafts, gold, and agriculture. This initiative aims to increase exports, bolster food security, and promote sustainable development. Additionally, SCCI emphasized Sharjah's attractive business environment and invited Nepali companies to participate in events like the Watch and Jewellery Middle East Show and ExpoCulinaire.
records.institution: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI)

records.title: Morocco is advancing a bill aimed at reducing food wastage nationwide, set to take effect in three months.
records.description: Morocco is advancing a bill aimed at reducing food wastage nationwide, set to take effect in three months. This legislation, currently in the preliminary adoption phase in Parliament, targets all stakeholders in the food chain, from farmers to consumers, promoting responsible management of food resources. Key measures include reallocating unused surplus food and imposing fines—twice the market value of the wasted food—on those found guilty of significant wastage. The National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA) will oversee enforcement. According to recent data, Morocco saw households waste over 4.2 million tons of food in 2022, an increase from previous years. The bill is part of broader efforts to address both the environmental impact of food waste, which contributes significantly to global greenhouse gas emissions, and economic losses, which are substantial on both a national and global scale.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s KSrelief continues its humanitarian efforts, delivering aid across multiple regions.
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s KSrelief continues its humanitarian efforts, delivering aid across multiple regions. In Libya, it distributed 2,916 food baskets in Derna to assist 14,580 people affected by Storm Daniel. In Sudan, the agency provided 600 shelter bags in Northern State, aiding 3,479 people impacted by flash floods. KSrelief also carried out medical missions in Turkiye’s Gaziantep and Hatay, focusing on orthopedic surgeries for victims of recent earthquakes. In Lebanon, through the Al-Amal Charitable Bakery project, 150,000 bread bags were distributed to Syrian, Palestinian, and local families, benefiting 62,500 individuals.

records.title: Morocco reaffirmed its commitment to enhancing the China-Africa partnership during the 2024 China-Africa Cooperation Summit in Beijing.
records.description: Morocco reaffirmed its commitment to enhancing the China-Africa partnership during the 2024 China-Africa Cooperation Summit in Beijing. Representing the country, Morocco’s Prime Minister emphasized Morocco's role as a strategic partner for the development of agriculture, infrastructure, and renewable energy across Africa. Highlighting key initiatives like the Nigeria-Morocco gas pipeline and fertilizer plants in Ethiopia and Nigeria, the Prime Minister underscored Morocco's efforts in promoting regional integration and food security. Additionally, he outlined Morocco's progress in addressing global warming impacts, improving water management, and advancing renewable energy, electric vehicles, and green hydrogen to support sustainable development across the continent.

records.description: The Sustainable Oases Charter, launched in collaboration with ANDZOA and the FAO, focuses on the preservation, restoration, and development of oasis areas. This initiative, discussed at a two-day workshop in Errachidia, aims to provide a framework for sustainability, social inclusion, and resilience in oases, addressing challenges such as climate change, desertification, and demographic pressure. It emphasizes the importance of collaboration among stakeholders and will generate data on water management within ecosystems.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (UN)

records.title: Oman's first commercial saffron farm, Saffron Oman, has begun operations in Al Jabal Al Akhdar.
records.description: Oman's first commercial saffron farm, Saffron Oman, has begun operations in Al Jabal Al Akhdar. The farm spans over 25,000 square meters and aims to harvest its first saffron crop by the end of 2024. The project, led by Ahmed Ali al Hanshi, is focused on cultivating saffron due to its high value and ideal growing conditions in the region. The farm plans to become self-sufficient by producing saffron bulbs and avoiding future imports, positioning Oman as a regional and global player in saffron production.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia views Italy as a key partner in its efforts to deliver green energy and fuels, such as renewable-powered hydrogen, to Europe.
records.description: Saudi Arabia views Italy as a key partner in its efforts to deliver green energy and fuels, such as renewable-powered hydrogen, to Europe. As part of its energy strategy to diversify from oil and gas, Saudi Arabia is expanding its production capacity for low-carbon products like blue and green hydrogen. The country is seeking allies to facilitate the export of these products, with Italy being identified as a "partner of choice" for bringing them to the European market. Saudi Arabia is also exploring partnerships with other European nations, including Germany, to invest in infrastructure like ports and pipelines to transport green energy.

records.title: Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani chaired a meeting of the High Committee for the Development Road Project, which reviewed pro...
records.description: Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani chaired a meeting of the High Committee for the Development Road Project, which reviewed progress on key infrastructure components, including energy, gas, electricity, and internet. The railway design has been completed, while road designs are 75% finished. Al-Sudani directed the creation of a detailed land acquisition plan for the project route, including cost estimates and a timeline. He also called for security coordination and set November 1, 2024, for the next quadrilateral committee meeting with Iraq, Qatar, the UAE, and Turkey. Additionally, committees were formed to plan long-term strategies and study energy investment along the project's route.

records.title: Libya's First Deputy Prime Minister held talks with officials on a proposal for the digital transformation of the agriculture and livesto...
records.description: Libya's First Deputy Prime Minister held talks with officials on a proposal for the digital transformation of the agriculture and livestock sector by 2030. The discussions addressed challenges and outlined steps required to boost the sector’s productivity and efficiency through technology. The talks also emphasized the importance of developing the sector's digital infrastructure and highlighted the need for adequate financial and human resources to carry out the transformation.

records.title: Oman has launched Phase 1 of a ginger cultivation project in Dhofar, involving 30 farmers across three acres in the wilayats of Rakhyut a...
records.description: Oman has launched Phase 1 of a ginger cultivation project in Dhofar, involving 30 farmers across three acres in the wilayats of Rakhyut and Dhalkut. Supported by the Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund, the project expects to yield 20 to 30 tonnes by February 2025. It offers technical support, promotes modern irrigation systems, and aims to expand into the private sector. A total of 60 farmers are expected to benefit over the next two years, reducing reliance on imports and creating local economic opportunities.
records.institution: Omani Directorate General of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources in Dhofar

Supported by the Agricultural and Fisheries Development Fund, the project involves 30 farmers over three acres, with the first harvest expected by February 2025, yielding 20-30 tonnes.
