records.title: The UAE and Jordan have signed a $2.3 billion investment agreement aimed at boosting Jordan's railway sector.
records.description: The UAE and Jordan have signed a $2.3 billion investment agreement aimed at boosting Jordan's railway sector. The memorandum of understanding focuses on developing a 360-kilometer railway network in Jordan to connect phosphate and potash mines to the Port of Aqaba. UAE's Etihad Rail also signed agreements with Jordan’s transport ministry, Jordan Phosphate Mines Company, and Arab Potash Company to transport 16 million tons of minerals annually. This project, set to begin construction bids in 2026, will enhance logistical efficiency, create job opportunities, and strengthen Jordan’s export capabilities. It follows a $2 billion agreement between the two countries signed in 2023.

records.title: Egypt plans to expand its grain storage capacity by 76%, reaching 6 million tons by 2030.
records.description: Egypt plans to expand its grain storage capacity by 76%, reaching 6 million tons by 2030. The first phase, costing EGP 19 billion ($615 million), will add 1.4 million tons by 2027, while the second phase, costing EGP 15 billion ($485 million), will add 1.2 million tons by 2030. This initiative aims to enhance food security amid global market fluctuations. The plan includes new silo construction, integration with railways and the Nile, and a public-private partnership to boost wheat supplies and stabilize local food prices.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: The Egyptian mango season is nearing its end, marked by a production volume exceeding two million tons across more than 100,000 hectares.
records.description: The Egyptian mango season is nearing its end, marked by a production volume exceeding two million tons across more than 100,000 hectares. Despite the high supply, demand has remained strong, particularly from Europe, Russia, and Gulf countries. While some exporters have expressed concerns about low prices due to abundant production, others, like Citrus Agro, report stable pricing and anticipate price increases as the season wraps up. Export activity is expected to continue robustly, with increased volumes projected in the coming month.

records.title: Trade exchange between Iraq and Iran has surpassed $10 billion, according to Iraq's ambassador to Iran.
records.description: Trade exchange between Iraq and Iran has surpassed $10 billion, according to Iraq's ambassador to Iran. During a meeting with the governor of Semnan province, the ambassador expressed optimism that the trade figure could rise to $20 billion. He also discussed plans for joint industrial facilities between Iraq and Semnan, focusing on sectors such as mining, agriculture, and industry. Additionally, more than 1,200 Iraqi students are currently enrolled in Iranian universities, particularly in Semnan, due to its proximity to Tehran and cultural ties between the two nations.

records.title: The Moroccan raspberry campaign has officially started, with the first harvests underway and initial shipments already sent out.
records.description: The Moroccan raspberry campaign has officially started, with the first harvests underway and initial shipments already sent out. The industry has stabilized, with raspberry acreage holding steady at 4,200-4,500 hectares in the Loukkos and Souss Massa regions, producing around 50,000-60,000 tonnes of fresh raspberries and 10,000-12,000 tonnes of frozen raspberries annually. Despite improved weather conditions this season, challenges such as water stress, pests, and rising production costs persist. Europe remains the primary market for Moroccan raspberries, with efforts to expand into the Gulf and Russian markets through air shipments. The campaign will run until May-June 2025.
records.institution: Moroccan Association of Soft Fruit Growers

records.title: The khareef season in Dhofar, known for its lush landscapes and tourist appeal, also offers significant potential for agricultural research.
records.description: The khareef season in Dhofar, known for its lush landscapes and tourist appeal, also offers significant potential for agricultural research. With around 800 of Oman’s 1,200 plant species found in Dhofar, the monsoon season provides ideal conditions for scientists to study plant growth, ecological interactions, and water management. Continuous rainfall reduces evaporation, enhances crop growth, and lowers soil salinity, benefiting agriculture year-round. Researchers are also exploring fog harvesting as a sustainable water source for farming in arid climates.
records.institution: Director of the Department of Agricultural and Livestock Research in Dhofar

records.title: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture has sought assistance from the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority's (ADAFSA) Collabora...
records.description: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture has sought assistance from the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority's (ADAFSA) Collaborating Centre for Camel Disease to investigate a mysterious disease causing camel deaths in Ethiopia and East Africa. A team of experts, recommended by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the FAO, began working in July to identify the cause and develop treatment methods.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture, following recommendations from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the FAO, has so...
records.description: The Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture, following recommendations from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the FAO, has sought assistance from ADAFSA's Collaborating Centre for Camel Disease to address unexplained camel deaths threatening livestock across Ethiopia, Sudan, Somalia, and Kenya. A team of experts from the centre began work in Ethiopia in July to investigate the cause and develop preventive and treatment methods.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Algeria has officially joined the BRICS New Development Bank (NDB), marking a significant step in its global financial integration.
records.description: Algeria has officially joined the BRICS New Development Bank (NDB), marking a significant step in its global financial integration. The approval, announced by NDB President Dilma Rousseff during a meeting in South Africa, highlights Algeria's growing economic strength and its classification as an "upper-tier emerging economy." As Africa's top natural gas exporter, Algeria's membership is expected to open new opportunities for economic growth. The NDB, founded in 2015 by Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, aims to support sustainable development in emerging markets. Algeria is set to have a strong presence at the upcoming BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia, in October.

records.title: Egypt is exploring the issuance of green bonds and sukuk as part of a broader strategy to diversify its investor base and reduce its debt...
records.description: Egypt is exploring the issuance of green bonds and sukuk as part of a broader strategy to diversify its investor base and reduce its debt burden. The government is also focused on stimulating private sector growth in key areas like renewable energy and technology, alongside implementing comprehensive tax reforms to boost investment. During a meeting with the US Ambassador to Cairo, the Finance Minister highlighted Egypt’s efforts to foster both domestic and foreign investments, emphasizing the country's competitive advantages and infrastructure.

records.title: Kraft Heinz has announced a $50 million expansion of its Cairo facility to boost production capacity by 65%, enhancing its export capabil...
records.description: Kraft Heinz has announced a $50 million expansion of its Cairo facility to boost production capacity by 65%, enhancing its export capabilities across the Middle East and Africa. This move is part of the company's strategy to tap into Africa's growing tomato ketchup market, projected to generate $3 billion in revenue in 2024 with a 10.4% annual growth rate.

records.title: On 3 September 2024, the Kurdistan Regional Government and the United Kingdom signed a strategic trade agreement aimed at enhancing trade...
records.description: On 3 September 2024, the Kurdistan Regional Government and the United Kingdom signed a strategic trade agreement aimed at enhancing trade and investment between the two parties. The agreement focuses on key sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, human resource development, and technology. Discussions also highlighted the potential for further economic collaboration between the UK and the Kurdistan Region.

records.title: Morocco's upcoming tomato season is expected to be more stable, with early harvests in the Souss Massa region and a predicted decrease in...
records.description: Morocco's upcoming tomato season is expected to be more stable, with early harvests in the Souss Massa region and a predicted decrease in overall production volume. Tomato acreage has dropped by 10-15% as many growers have shifted to soft fruits. There will be no overproduction this season, unlike last year when excess supply led to price drops. Prices are anticipated to be about 20% higher than last season. While some tomato varieties are showing resistance to the Tobrfv virus, challenges remain for large-caliber tomatoes. The first harvests are expected in October, and the season will last until May.

records.title: Oman Flour Mills Company reported a 25% increase in export volumes, reaching 40,449 metric tonnes of flour products this year.
records.description: Oman Flour Mills Company reported a 25% increase in export volumes, reaching 40,449 metric tonnes of flour products this year. This growth is attributed to the company's efforts in expanding its infrastructure, improving packaging standards, and enhancing transportation to meet demand in local and international markets. The company is also exploring new opportunities in the food industry, including acquisitions in the animal feed sector and plans to diversify into sweets and confectionery. OFM’s expansion has also created over 500 new jobs in Oman.

records.title: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources is undertaking a project to restore 100 aflaj irrigation systems in Dhahir...
records.description: Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources is undertaking a project to restore 100 aflaj irrigation systems in Dhahirah at a cost of over RO848,000. The initiative addresses the damage caused by recent climatic events and aims to preserve these traditional water systems, essential for irrigation and cultural heritage. So far, 20 aflaj have been rehabilitated, with work ongoing on the remaining 80.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has provided recycling containers to 80% of households in Doha, allowing residents to separate recyclabl...
records.description: Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has provided recycling containers to 80% of households in Doha, allowing residents to separate recyclable materials like plastic, glass, paper, and metal from organic waste. The recyclable waste is transported to a recycling hub in Mesaieed, which currently has 11 operational factories, with seven more nearing completion and an additional 12 under construction. The initiative will expand to other municipalities, including Umm Salal, Al Daayen, Al Khor, and Al Shamal, by 2026, and further to Al Rayan, Al Wakra, and Al Sheehaniya by 2027.

records.title: Ma Hawa, an Emirati brand, has launched its innovative Water-from-Air bottles in the UAE, using atmospheric moisture to produce pure drin...
records.description: Ma Hawa, an Emirati brand, has launched its innovative Water-from-Air bottles in the UAE, using atmospheric moisture to produce pure drinking water. The bottles are now available at select Union Coop stores and ADNOC outlets, with plans to expand further across the country. This technology offers a sustainable solution to the UAE’s water scarcity issues, providing an eco-friendly water source in one of the most water-stressed regions globally.

records.title: Silal, a leading UAE food and technology company, has announced its acquisition of a majority stake in Al Bakrawe Holding, a key regional...
records.description: Silal, a leading UAE food and technology company, has announced its acquisition of a majority stake in Al Bakrawe Holding, a key regional importer and distributor of fresh fruits and vegetables. This acquisition aims to enhance Silal's position as a major supplier of fresh produce in the UAE, leveraging Al Bakrawe’s extensive global sourcing network. The collaboration will improve supply chain capabilities and expand market reach, contributing to a more sustainable food ecosystem in the region. This is Silal's third strategic acquisition.

records.title: UAE-based Future Food Foundry (3F) has invested over $20 million in NextGen Farms (NGF) and Sustenir Group to create the largest plant su...
records.description: UAE-based Future Food Foundry (3F) has invested over $20 million in NextGen Farms (NGF) and Sustenir Group to create the largest plant superfood ecosystem in Singapore. The partnership aims to enhance food security in the region by leveraging controlled environment farming techniques to produce nutrient-rich superfoods. This move strengthens 3F’s agri-tech presence in MENA and Asia-Pacific, with plans for sustainable agriculture and food innovation expansion. Both NGF and Sustenir specialize in advanced farming technologies and superfood production.

records.title: Yemeni fishermen are increasingly turning to artificial reefs (ARs) made from scrap materials to boost fish stocks as they face the combi...
records.description: Yemeni fishermen are increasingly turning to artificial reefs (ARs) made from scrap materials to boost fish stocks as they face the combined challenges of civil war, environmental decline, and dwindling catches. These DIY reefs, created from firewood, tyres, and metal, are meant to replace dying coral reefs, providing habitat for marine life and helping fishermen maintain their livelihoods. However, the use of manmade materials has raised environmental concerns, with critics warning of potential water pollution and harm to marine ecosystems. Despite these risks, the practice persists, driven by the steep decline in fish stocks, economic hardship, and dangerous conditions for fishermen.

records.title: Egyptian Countryside Development Company has signed a contract with Al Magd Group to cultivate 29,000 feddans of oil crops, such as sunfl...
records.description: Egyptian Countryside Development Company has signed a contract with Al Magd Group to cultivate 29,000 feddans of oil crops, such as sunflower and soybeans, in South Safola, west Minya. The project includes an agricultural-industrial complex focused on producing edible oil and animal feed.
records.institution: Egyptian Countryside Development Company & Al Magd Group

records.title: The Iraqi Cabinet has authorized the Finance Minister to sign a loan agreement with Austria's Erste Bank, backed by the Austrian Export C...
records.description: The Iraqi Cabinet has authorized the Finance Minister to sign a loan agreement with Austria's Erste Bank, backed by the Austrian Export Credit Agency (OeKB). This loan will fund an irrigation technology project under Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture, aligned with the Federal Budget Law for 2023-2025. The project follows an earlier agreement between Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture and Austrian company Bauer for the supply of 12,000 pivot sprinklers. The Cabinet has also approved the financing terms for the project.

records.title: The escalating conflict between Hezbollah and Israel has intensified tensions in Lebanon, where thousands of Christian refugees have soug...
records.description: The escalating conflict between Hezbollah and Israel has intensified tensions in Lebanon, where thousands of Christian refugees have sought sanctuary. Amid this instability, the Christian ministry Help The Persecuted (HTP) continues to provide spiritual and practical support to persecuted Christians and vulnerable individuals. HTP's efforts, including distributing food from their Seeds of Hope farm and operating emergency shelters, have expanded as people flee the southern region. Despite the growing challenges, HTP remains committed to serving those in need, calling for prayers for peace and endurance for their workers on the ground.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: QatarEnergy is set to build a new urea production complex in Mesaieed Industrial City, doubling the country's output from 6 million to 12...
records.description: QatarEnergy is set to build a new urea production complex in Mesaieed Industrial City, doubling the country's output from 6 million to 12.4 million tonnes per annum. This expansion will make Qatar the world’s largest producer of urea, a key agricultural fertilizer, as global demand rises due to population growth. The project will include three ammonia production lines supplying feedstock to four new urea production trains, with the first train expected to be operational by the end of the decade.

records.title: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company, a leading flour milling firm in Saudi Arabia, has announced the price range for its Initial Publ...
records.description: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company, a leading flour milling firm in Saudi Arabia, has announced the price range for its Initial Public Offering (IPO) at SAR62 to SAR66 per share. The offering is expected to raise between SAR954 million and SAR1,016 million ($255 million to $271 million), with a market capitalization ranging from SAR3.182 billion to SAR3.387 billion ($848 million to $903 million). The institutional book-building period began on September 1 and will close on September 5. The IPO consists of 15,394,502 shares, representing 30% of the company’s issued share capital, being sold by existing shareholders. Proceeds from the sale will be distributed to the selling shareholders, with the shares to be listed on the Saudi Exchange following the IPO. HSBC Saudi Arabia is serving as the financial advisor and lead manager for the offering.
records.institution: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company

records.title: Due to an oversupply following last year's shortage, prices for Egyptian onions have dropped by half this season compared to last year.
records.description: Due to an oversupply following last year's shortage, prices for Egyptian onions have dropped by half this season compared to last year. Onion production increased significantly, reaching over 3 million tonnes, a million more than last year, as many growers switched to onions. Despite the increased supply, demand has been lower than expected, and global competition from countries like Spain and the Netherlands has further reduced demand. However, new markets in West and Central Africa, such as Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire, are showing interest in Egyptian onions.

records.title: Egypt has become the leading supplier of sweet potatoes to the European market, overtaking the USA with a 45% increase in shipments to th...
records.description: Egypt has become the leading supplier of sweet potatoes to the European market, overtaking the USA with a 45% increase in shipments to the EU in the 2023/24 season, totaling 109,000 tonnes. The sector has seen significant growth, with a 30% increase in acreage, ensuring continuous supply. Egypt exports primarily to the Netherlands, France, and Italy, with rising demand in Scandinavia. Despite challenges like price drops due to large volumes, the industry remains strong, with promising prospects for extending the export season.

records.title: Egyptian pomegranates are now available in the market until November, with a peak harvest expected in October.
records.description: Egyptian pomegranates are now available in the market until November, with a peak harvest expected in October. Production volumes are anticipated to increase by 15% due to expanded cultivation and improved yields. Prices have risen by 5-10%, driven by strong local demand and favorable export markets, particularly in Europe and the Middle East. However, challenges such as logistical issues, rising shipping costs, and unpredictable weather conditions during flowering have impacted some crops, raising concerns about fruit quality in certain areas.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Norway is considering increasing investments in Egypt's renewable energy sector.
records.description: Norway is considering increasing investments in Egypt's renewable energy sector. Egyptian and Norwegian officials, along with the Norwegian firm Scatec, discussed potential collaboration in areas such as green hydrogen, solar, and wind energy. These talks also covered local production of clean energy equipment, including solar panels, water desalination equipment, hydrogen generation facilities, and wind turbines.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Industry and Transport

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Lebanon has joined the Middle East Green Initiative (MGI), led by Saudi Arabia, to address climate change.
records.description: Lebanon has joined the Middle East Green Initiative (MGI), led by Saudi Arabia, to address climate change. This initiative aims to restore 200 million hectares of degraded land, plant 50 billion trees, and increase vegetation cover in the region. A high committee has been established in Lebanon to ensure the project's sustainability and promote cooperation. The MGI, launched in 2021, seeks to support local green transitions across the Middle East.

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Saudi Arabia has launched a tender for a fish farming project in the Jubail governorate on the northeastern coast as part of its Vision 2...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has launched a tender for a fish farming project in the Jubail governorate on the northeastern coast as part of its Vision 2030 development plan. The initiative, covering a four-hectare area, aims to promote healthier eating habits and enhance food security through aquaponics. This method synergizes fish farming with plant cultivation in tanks, where fish waste serves as natural fertilizer for the plants while the plants clean the water, eliminating the need for chemicals. The tender deadline is set for November 27, and this project follows the issuance of 18 aquaculture licenses in the Mecca region, which represents about one-third of the country's Red Sea coastline.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has lifted a 21-year ban on South African meat imports, allowing South African producers to export beef, lamb, and mutton to...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has lifted a 21-year ban on South African meat imports, allowing South African producers to export beef, lamb, and mutton to the Kingdom. Twelve South African companies have been approved for beef exports, while seven have been approved for lamb and mutton. This development was discussed during a virtual trade session attended by officials and industry stakeholders from both countries, focusing on the potential to increase trade and export market share.

records.title: Saudi authorities have sentenced four board members of Raydan Food Co, including the vice chairman, to 90 days in prison for market viola...
records.description: Saudi authorities have sentenced four board members of Raydan Food Co, including the vice chairman, to 90 days in prison for market violations such as insider trading and providing misleading financial information. In total, 14 individuals connected with the Tadawul-listed company were penalized, with some ordered to pay SAR 77 million ($20 million) in compensation for illegal trading activities. The group also faces fines totaling SAR 50.6 million, and 11 members have been banned from working with entities supervised by the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) for up to three years. The violations involved false representation of the company’s financial statements from 2018 to 2020 and insider trading prior to a public announcement in March 2022. Affected parties are invited to file compensation claims through the CMA's website.

records.title: Algeria has reopened the Agrodiv Complex in Corso after 21 years of inactivity, boosting its grain storage capacity.
records.description: Algeria has reopened the Agrodiv Complex in Corso after 21 years of inactivity, boosting its grain storage capacity. The facility, housing 36 silos with a capacity of 100,000 tons and a flour mill, was restored following damage from a 2003 earthquake. This move aligns with the government's plan to triple national storage capacity by 2025. Algeria aims to address its growing cereal import needs, projected at 14.1 million tonnes for 2024/2025.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Egypt and Germany discussed cooperation on water and climate change issues during a meeting in Stockholm.
records.description: Egypt and Germany discussed cooperation on water and climate change issues during a meeting in Stockholm. The discussion centered around Germany's support for Egypt's priority water projects, including initiatives to rationalize water use, upgrade irrigation systems, and establish large-scale agricultural wastewater treatment plants. They also explored coordination for the upcoming 29th United Nations climate change conference (COP29) and discussed supporting the African Center for Water and Climate Adaptation to train specialists in climate change mitigation related to water resources in Africa.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation

records.title: Egypt is preparing to expand its mango exports to Southeast Asia, targeting premium markets with its unique, high-quality "super-mangoes....
records.description: Egypt is preparing to expand its mango exports to Southeast Asia, targeting premium markets with its unique, high-quality "super-mangoes." Despite competition from major regional mango producers like Vietnam, Thailand, and Indonesia, countries such as Singapore, Hong Kong, and Malaysia are promising markets due to their significant mango imports. By focusing on lesser-known varieties with exceptional sweetness and flavor, Egyptian exporters aim to capture a niche in the premium segment, using airfreight to overcome regional competition and logistical challenges.

records.title: Egypt’s Agriculture Ministry Launches Strategic Plan to Strengthen Seed Industry
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture has launched a strategic plan to enhance the seed industry, aiming to modernize production and increase private sector participation. This initiative plans to strengthen the seed industry will be implemented by modernizing seed production methods, involving the private sector more actively, and leveraging scientific research to create high-quality seeds. The initiative will also focus on producing seeds that can withstand challenges like salinity, climate change, and water scarcity. Additionally, the plan aims to promote local seed production for key crops, reduce the reliance on imports, and educate farmers through agricultural extension services to ensure better seed quality and proper sourcing.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Egypt's Medjool date industry is facing several challenges this season despite its rapid expansion.
records.description: Egypt's Medjool date industry is facing several challenges this season despite its rapid expansion. Issues include delays due to conflict in the Red Sea, political unrest in key importing countries like Bangladesh, and domestic difficulties such as fluctuating currency exchange rates. Additionally, rising labor costs and shortages have impacted fruit thinning, resulting in fewer jumbo and super-jumbo dates, which could reduce overall revenue. Growing domestic competition may also lead to price drops in the future as more exporters enter the market.

records.title: Trouw Nutrition Egypt hosted a seminar in Ain Sokhna, unveiling innovations in animal nutrition, particularly showcasing the IntelliBond...
records.description: Trouw Nutrition Egypt hosted a seminar in Ain Sokhna, unveiling innovations in animal nutrition, particularly showcasing the IntelliBond trace mineral additive. Known for its superior bioavailability, it improves livestock feed efficiency and safety.

records.title: Iraq's Prime Minister met with Egyptian business leaders in El Alamein to discuss investment opportunities, focusing on infrastructure, h...
records.description: Iraq's Prime Minister met with Egyptian business leaders in El Alamein to discuss investment opportunities, focusing on infrastructure, housing, and industrial projects. The meeting highlighted Iraq's recovery and development program and invited Egyptian businesses to invest in sectors such as transportation, healthcare, and construction. Partnerships on key projects, including the Development Road and industrial zones, were also discussed. Both sides emphasized their commitment to economic integration and cooperation following a separate meeting between the Iraqi Prime Minister and Egypt's President.

records.title: Morocco plans to lease 5,200 hectares of state-owned agricultural land to private investors to counter the effects of prolonged drought o...
records.description: Morocco plans to lease 5,200 hectares of state-owned agricultural land to private investors to counter the effects of prolonged drought on its agricultural sector. This initiative, covering nine regions, aims to attract investment and improve farming practices. Leases vary from 17 to 40 years, depending on the project type. The agricultural sector has faced job losses due to drought, with a significant decline in wheat and barley production.

records.title: Saudi tomatoes achieved high prices in the European market following their first export to the Netherlands by Dava in February 2024.
records.description: Saudi tomatoes achieved high prices in the European market following their first export to the Netherlands by Dava in February 2024. The successful trial involved six shipments and has set the foundation for plans to export 1,500 tonnes by 2025. The company is now focusing on increasing production and launching new packaging options. Additionally, Dava is targeting the Gulf States for exports during the summer, with agreements in place with regional supermarket chains. The company is also trialing the cultivation of new vegetable varieties despite challenging summer temperatures.

records.title: Al Ghurair Foods has begun construction on the Middle East's first corn starch manufacturing plant in Abu Dhabi's Khalifa Economic Zones.
records.description: Al Ghurair Foods has begun construction on the Middle East's first corn starch manufacturing plant in Abu Dhabi's Khalifa Economic Zones. The facility will produce various starch products, including glucose syrups and maltodextrin, to serve sectors like food, pharmaceuticals, and industrial applications. The plant will initially process 650 tons of corn daily, with plans to expand to 1,000 tons.

records.title: Algeria has launched the MyGeocycle digital platform to modernize waste management, part of the country’s strategy to manage and recover...
records.description: Algeria has launched the MyGeocycle digital platform to modernize waste management, part of the country’s strategy to manage and recover waste by 2035. Developed by France’s Geocycle, the platform will enable real-time waste tracking, enhance operational efficiency, and reduce environmental impact. The initiative aims to tackle Algeria's waste management challenges, aiming for a 10% reduction in household waste and recycling 60% of inert waste by 2035. Additional waste-to-energy projects in Sétif and Constantine will further contribute to sustainable waste recovery.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of the Environment and Renewable Energies

records.title: Egypt's exports to Iraq increased by $34.4 million during the first five months of 2024, reaching $308.5 million, compared to $274.7 mill...
records.description: Egypt's exports to Iraq increased by $34.4 million during the first five months of 2024, reaching $308.5 million, compared to $274.7 million in the same period in 2023, as reported by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS). Imports from Iraq also rose to $4.1 million from $2.3 million in 2023. This trade growth is part of strengthened trade relations within the Common Arab Market, with Egyptian exports to the market reaching $1.639 billion in the same period.
records.institution: Egyptian Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: Halfway through the Egyptian sweet potato season, prices have halved compared to the start due to increased supply and heightened competi...
records.description: Halfway through the Egyptian sweet potato season, prices have halved compared to the start due to increased supply and heightened competition among exporters. Early season prices were higher due to limited availability, but with volumes now exceeding expectations, prices have dropped. Factors such as exporter cost structures and processing methods, including weight loss during curing, affect price fluctuations. Despite falling prices, some exporters, like GFresh, benefit from owning curing facilities, allowing them to maintain competitive pricing throughout the season.

records.title: Iraq and Turkey are set to launch 13 new water projects as part of a framework agreement signed in April.
records.description: Iraq and Turkey are set to launch 13 new water projects as part of a framework agreement signed in April. These projects will focus on water resource management, sanitation, and irrigation. Iraq's Prime Minister directed the immediate start of the first phase, with funding already allocated and technical teams to be formed for collaboration with Turkish experts. The projects include irrigation networks, drainage canals, and dams, distributed across the Ministries of Water Resources, Construction, Housing, and Agriculture.

records.title: Iraq's Prime Minister met with Egyptian business leaders in El Alamein to discuss investment opportunities, focusing on economic integrat...
records.description: Iraq's Prime Minister met with Egyptian business leaders in El Alamein to discuss investment opportunities, focusing on economic integration between the two countries. The discussions centered on Iraq's recovery and ambitious development plans, inviting Egyptian businesses to invest in infrastructure, housing, and other sectors like transportation, healthcare, and construction. Strategic partnerships, including Iraq's Development Road project, were also highlighted, with existing collaborations involving Qatar, Turkey, and the UAE. Egyptian businesses expressed readiness to invest, and both countries committed to fostering successful projects as a model for regional cooperation.

records.title: The General Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture in Libya has expressed its full support for the Presidential Council...
records.description: The General Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture in Libya has expressed its full support for the Presidential Council's decision to appoint a new Board of Directors for the Central Bank of Libya (CBL). The Union views this as a critical step towards improving efficiency and transparency in managing national institutions, aligning with efforts to drive sustainable development and advance the Libyan economy. Emphasizing the importance of governance and transparency, the Union highlights the necessity of collective governance in effectively responding to current challenges and enhancing the financial sector's credibility. The Union also expressed hope that the new board will positively impact the business environment and support Libya's commercial, industrial, and agricultural sectors. It urged its members and other relevant parties to support the new board to ensure it meets its goals and fosters economic and social stability.
records.institution: The Libyan General Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture

records.title: The Rabat-Salé-Kénitra region is tackling water stress through an innovative wastewater management project, reusing treated wastewater to...
records.description: The Rabat-Salé-Kénitra region is tackling water stress through an innovative wastewater management project, reusing treated wastewater to irrigate green spaces and support industrial activities. Launched in 2019, this initiative is part of the National Drinking Water Supply and Irrigation Program (PNAEPI), treating 56,000 m³ of wastewater daily across six plants. The system has reduced drinking water consumption by 11.7 million m³ and aims to mobilize 137 Mm³ by 2027 for further irrigation projects, enhancing water sustainability in the region.

records.title: An Omani vertical farming venture, Trufud Farm, is seeing positive consumer feedback for its pesticide-free leafy greens and herbs.
records.description: An Omani vertical farming venture, Trufud Farm, is seeing positive consumer feedback for its pesticide-free leafy greens and herbs. Located in Barka, the farm utilizes hydroponic and vertical farming systems to produce various products like kale, basil, and cherry tomatoes. Trufud supplies major supermarkets and wholesale markets in Oman and aims to expand its agricultural output. The company focuses on pesticide-free cultivation rather than organic farming, citing cost challenges. Vertical farming is seen as a solution to issues in traditional agriculture, especially in the face of climate change.

records.title: The Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi and the Emir of Qatar met in Doha to discuss strengthening bilateral ties and areas of common interest.
records.description: The Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi and the Emir of Qatar met in Doha to discuss strengthening bilateral ties and areas of common interest. During the meeting, the Deputy Ruler conveyed the well-wishes of the UAE's leaders for the health and prosperity of the Emir and the Qatari people, with the Emir reciprocating similar greetings for the UAE's leaders and citizens. The discussions emphasized cooperation and mutual support for regional stability and development.

records.title: Iraq's Prime Minister visited Tunisia, holding high-level talks with officials at the Carthage Presidential Palace.
records.description: Iraq's Prime Minister visited Tunisia, holding high-level talks with officials at the Carthage Presidential Palace. The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation across various sectors, and both sides agreed to establish a joint business council to enhance economic ties. The two countries have recently signed nearly 20 memoranda of understanding in different fields. Additionally, the leaders discussed the situation in Gaza and called for action to address ongoing violence.

records.title: Ain Defla is dedicating 691 hectares to sunflower and rapeseed cultivation for the 2024-2025 season as part of efforts to diversify crops...
records.description: Ain Defla is dedicating 691 hectares to sunflower and rapeseed cultivation for the 2024-2025 season as part of efforts to diversify crops and enhance food security. Local authorities aim to expand oilseed crops across various regions, with a focus on private and pilot farms. The recent sunflower harvest on a 27-hectare pilot farm yielded more than 20 quintals per hectare.

records.title: Egypt received a 66,000 metric ton shipment of Russian wheat at Damietta Port, which plays a critical role in the country's grain distrib...
records.description: Egypt received a 66,000 metric ton shipment of Russian wheat at Damietta Port, which plays a critical role in the country's grain distribution. The port holds over 181,000 metric tons of wheat. This move is part of Egypt's ongoing efforts to diversify its wheat sources. Egypt has been increasing domestic wheat procurement alongside its international imports. For the 2024/25 fiscal year, Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) plans to secure 8.25 million metric tons of wheat for bread subsidies.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: The IMF has eased certain conditions of its $8 billion financial support package to Egypt, giving the country more time to implement refo...
records.description: The IMF has eased certain conditions of its $8 billion financial support package to Egypt, giving the country more time to implement reforms. While Egypt met half of the structural benchmarks, the IMF extended deadlines for other requirements, such as publishing audit reports and preparing a recapitalization plan for the Central Bank. The IMF expects Egypt's economic growth to recover in FY2024-25, reaching 5.5% in the medium term, with inflation decreasing as policy tightening takes effect.

records.title: Jordan's Agriculture Minister recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with officials from the Kurdistan Region to increase ag...
records.description: Jordan's Agriculture Minister recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with officials from the Kurdistan Region to increase agricultural imports. The agreement will allow Jordan to directly import products such as potatoes and garlic, with plans to expand to wheat, bulgur, and flour. Jordan aims to import 10,000 tons of potatoes and 5,000 tons of garlic. The Kurdistan Region's strategic location, including the Ibrahim Khalil border crossing, was emphasized as a key route for accessing markets in Turkey, Europe, and Russia.

records.title: The European Union's imports of Moroccan tomatoes declined by 6.8% in the 2023/24 season, with 464,052 tons imported compared to 497,928...
records.description: The European Union's imports of Moroccan tomatoes declined by 6.8% in the 2023/24 season, with 464,052 tons imported compared to 497,928 tons the previous year. This marks the steepest drop in the past five years. While Morocco remains the largest supplier of tomatoes to the EU from non-EU countries, growing competition from Turkey and Tunisia has contributed to the decline. Turkish tomato imports to the EU increased by 40.4%, and Tunisia's exports rose by 37.1%, challenging Morocco’s dominance in the EU market.
records.institution: Spainish Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Food (MAPA)

records.title: The Moroccan avocado season is set to begin in week 38/39 for green skin varieties and week 43 for Hass, with a projected volume of 80,00...
records.description: The Moroccan avocado season is set to begin in week 38/39 for green skin varieties and week 43 for Hass, with a projected volume of 80,000 tonnes, a 33% increase from last year. Companies will ship 200 trucks filled with avocados, focusing on quality over quantity. Major markets will continue to be Spain and the Netherlands, with efforts to expand into new markets. The company also imports avocados during the off-season, bringing in avocados from Peru and Brazil to meet local demand in Morocco.

records.title: Officials from the Syrian and Iraqi Ministries of Agriculture met to discuss enhancing agricultural relations and trade.
records.description: Officials from the Syrian and Iraqi Ministries of Agriculture met to discuss enhancing agricultural relations and trade. The Syrian Minister of Agriculture highlighted Syria's significant exports of vegetables and fruits to Iraq, with an emphasis on strengthening these ties. Discussions also covered a quadripartite agreement involving Syria, Iraq, Jordan, and Lebanon, aimed at unifying agricultural protocols, standardizing certificates of origin, streamlining product arrival, and reducing fees. The Iraqi delegation affirmed their commitment to advancing these initiatives to foster cooperation.
records.institution: Syrian Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform of Syria

records.title: The Agriculture and Irrigation Authority of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES) announced plans to compensate f...
records.description: The Agriculture and Irrigation Authority of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES) announced plans to compensate farmers affected by fires and support the upcoming 2024-2025 agricultural season. This includes providing free wheat seeds, purchasing cotton crops from farmers, setting prices for organic compost, and introducing new wheat types. A weather station center will be established, and agricultural licensing and organization will begin in September. These decisions follow unrest over wheat pricing and longstanding farmer complaints about inadequate support for cotton crops.
records.institution: The Agriculture and Irrigation Authority of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES)

records.title: Tunisia's president has directed the drafting of a law to create a social protection fund for female farm workers.
records.description: Tunisia's president has directed the drafting of a law to create a social protection fund for female farm workers. This fund will provide health care, insurance against workplace accidents and diseases, and pension benefits. The initiative was discussed during a meeting at Carthage Palace, where the president also emphasized the importance of integrity and dedication from officials in serving citizens. The move comes amid concerns over the dismissal of workers in the Siliana governorate.

records.title: Abu Dhabi's Khalifa Port has inaugurated a new veterinary quarantine facility, spanning 32,700 square meters, aimed at enhancing biosecur...
records.description: Abu Dhabi's Khalifa Port has inaugurated a new veterinary quarantine facility, spanning 32,700 square meters, aimed at enhancing biosecurity and food safety. The facility supports livestock imports and re-exports, positioning Abu Dhabi as a regional hub for live animal trade. The facility features state-of-the-art equipment, including a veterinary laboratory, and is designed to process over one million livestock annually.

records.title: Packaging costs in Egypt have risen by approximately 45% this season due to increasing raw material prices and production expenses.
records.description: Packaging costs in Egypt have risen by approximately 45% this season due to increasing raw material prices and production expenses. Exporters are feeling the strain as these costs impact the entire supply chain. To mitigate the effects, companies are optimizing efficiency and exploring sustainable, eco-friendly packaging solutions. There is growing demand for environmentally-friendly materials like biodegradable paper, especially for exports to the EU. Efforts are also underway to develop innovative packaging solutions for products like grapes and strawberries, enhancing freshness and reducing environmental impact.

records.title: The construction of the Ratba Dam in Taounate, Morocco, is progressing rapidly, with 26% of the work completed.
records.description: The construction of the Ratba Dam in Taounate, Morocco, is progressing rapidly, with 26% of the work completed. As one of the largest dams in the country, it aims to strengthen water security through its projected capacity of over one billion cubic meters. The project, part of the National Program for Drinking Water Supply and Irrigation (PNAEPI), also provides socio-economic benefits, including 1.5 million workdays during construction. Completion is targeted for 2028, with hopes to capture floods from the 2028/2029 rainy season.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Equipment, Transport, Logistics and Water (METLW)

records.title: KSrelief, the Kingdom’s aid agency, is actively providing medical aid across Yemen, Jordan, and Iraq.
records.description: KSrelief, the Kingdom’s aid agency, is actively providing medical aid across Yemen, Jordan, and Iraq. In Yemen's Wallan camp, KSrelief’s mobile clinics served 444 individuals in a month with comprehensive services including emergency care and surgery. In Jordan, the agency offered essential medical aid to 2,301 Syrian refugees at the Zaatari camp within a week. Additionally, KSrelief delivered 15 tonnes of medical supplies to Iraq's Ministry of Health to support health services for citizens and displaced individuals.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia have established a new business council to strengthen economic relations and boost trade and investment opportu...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia have established a new business council to strengthen economic relations and boost trade and investment opportunities between the two nations. The Saudi-Ethiopian Business Council, approved by the General Authority for Foreign Trade for the 2024-2028 term, aims to support Saudi exports and focus on key Ethiopian sectors like agriculture, mining, and tourism. This initiative follows a recent agreement at the Saudi-Ethiopian Business Forum and is part of Saudi Arabia's broader strategy to deepen ties with Africa, particularly with Ethiopia, one of the continent's largest economies.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Algeria has announced plans to achieve self-sufficiency in durum wheat, barley, and corn as part of a broader strategy to bolster nationa...
records.description: Algeria has announced plans to achieve self-sufficiency in durum wheat, barley, and corn as part of a broader strategy to bolster national food security. Durum wheat production is close to meeting national demand, with full self-sufficiency expected next year. Barley, mainly used for animal feed, is also making progress despite seed market challenges. However, achieving self-sufficiency in grain corn remains difficult, with current production still low compared to high import needs. These goals face logistical and climatic challenges.

records.title: A major operation in Bizerte, Tunisia, uncovered contaminated agricultural production linked to illegal irrigation using untreated wastew...
records.description: A major operation in Bizerte, Tunisia, uncovered contaminated agricultural production linked to illegal irrigation using untreated wastewater. The campaign, initiated by the regional commission, identified ten cases of farmers using this hazardous method. Authorities seized equipment involved and noted connections to the National Water Exploitation and Distribution Company (SONEDE) networks, which caused drinking water shortages. The campaign extends nationwide, with similar violations found in Kasserine and Sidi Bouzid, highlighting public health risks and ongoing efforts to combat unsafe practices.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Saudi Arabia’s grape production has surpassed 110,500 tonnes, with a self-sufficiency rate of 58%, according to the Ministry of Environme...
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s grape production has surpassed 110,500 tonnes, with a self-sufficiency rate of 58%, according to the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture. Grapes are cultivated on more than 4,720 hectares, with Tabuk being the top producing region, yielding 46,939 tonnes annually. Other regions contributing significantly include Qassim, Hail, and Asir. The ministry highlighted grapes for their profitability and suitability for various soils, as well as their nutritional benefits, including cancer prevention and immune system support. The harvest season runs from June to September.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Fish prices in Bahrain have surged due to a shortage of local fish and increased reliance on imports.
records.description: Fish prices in Bahrain have surged due to a shortage of local fish and increased reliance on imports. The hot weather has made it difficult to catch larger local fish, leading to the sale of smaller fish at higher prices, with some imported varieties also contributing to the price hike. Currently, about 70% of fish in Bahrain’s Central Market are imported from countries like India, Pakistan, and Oman. The situation has caused strain on consumers, with prices rising significantly for both local and imported fish.

records.title: Morocco plans to lease 5,200 hectares of state-owned agricultural land to private investors to counter the effects of prolonged drought o...
records.description: Morocco plans to lease 5,200 hectares of state-owned agricultural land to private investors to counter the effects of prolonged drought on its agricultural sector. This initiative, covering nine regions, aims to attract investment and improve farming practices. Leases vary from 17 to 40 years, depending on the project type. The agricultural sector has faced job losses due to drought, with a significant decline in wheat and barley production.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture committed to removing export barriers and highlighted the importance of agricultural exports for generati...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture committed to removing export barriers and highlighted the importance of agricultural exports for generating foreign currency and aiding the economy. He emphasized expanding agricultural land and enhancing agricultural processing to increase exports and reduce waste. The Minister encouraged collaboration between the government and private sector and acknowledged the importance of scientific research in supporting the agricultural sector. He also promised to address challenges faced by exporters and invited stakeholders to propose solutions for growth.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Morocco has raised fruit prices for Spain by 30% in the first half of 2024, despite reducing export quantities by 23.8 million kilograms...
records.description: Morocco has raised fruit prices for Spain by 30% in the first half of 2024, despite reducing export quantities by 23.8 million kilograms compared to last year. Spain paid €434.1 million for 125.5 million kilograms of Moroccan fruit, increasing the cost per kilogram from €2.7 to €3.46. This has caused protests among Spanish farmers, who are selling their produce at a loss. Health concerns regarding Moroccan strawberries have also added tension, as recent imports were linked to a hepatitis A contamination scare.

records.title: Morocco set a new record for blueberry exports during the 2023/24 season, exporting 67,300 tons, a 25% increase from the previous season.
records.description: Morocco set a new record for blueberry exports during the 2023/24 season, exporting 67,300 tons, a 25% increase from the previous season. This marks a nearly fourfold increase since the 2017/18 season. While Spain's share of Moroccan blueberry exports decreased from 80% to 30%, it remained the top market with 20,100 tons shipped, an 11% increase. Other key destinations in Europe, such as the UK, Netherlands, Germany, and France, also saw significant growth in imports. Beyond Europe, Morocco exported 1,800 tons to the Middle East and increased shipments to North America and Southeast Asia, where it ranks among the top five suppliers.

records.title: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company plans to sell a 30% stake through an IPO in Riyadh, marking its entry as the third flour milling...
records.description: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company plans to sell a 30% stake through an IPO in Riyadh, marking its entry as the third flour milling company to go public in Saudi Arabia. The company operates mills in Riyadh, Jazan, and Hail with a daily production capacity of 4,920 tons of flour. The IPO comes after approval from the Capital Market Authority in June 2024. Shares will be offered in two tranches to institutional and retail investors, with the final price set after a book-building period in September.
records.institution: Arabian Mills for Food Products Company

records.title: Egypt has become the top exporter of fresh strawberries to Kazakhstan, with shipments reaching nearly 1.4 thousand tons by the end of the...
records.description: Egypt has become the top exporter of fresh strawberries to Kazakhstan, with shipments reaching nearly 1.4 thousand tons by the end of the 2023/24 marketing year. This represents over 55% of Kazakhstan's total fresh strawberry imports, surpassing previous top suppliers like Azerbaijan and Turkey. Egypt's rapid growth in this market marks a significant leap from previous years, where exports ranged between 5 and 23 tons. Egyptian exporters have successfully capitalized on the rising demand for off-season products in Central Asia, positioning Egypt as a key player in Kazakhstan's fruit and vegetable market. Egypt is also expanding its presence in other Asian markets, including Southeast Asia, Japan, and China.

records.title: Iraq Investment Map 2024
records.description: Iraq's National Investment Commission (NIC) has released its Iraq Investment Map 2024. The 283-page report provides comprehensive details on available investment opportunities, along with sectoral and regional data.

records.title: As part of Morocco's National Irrigation Water Saving Program (PNEEI), a project in Kenitra will convert 12,440 hectares to localized irr...
records.description: As part of Morocco's National Irrigation Water Saving Program (PNEEI), a project in Kenitra will convert 12,440 hectares to localized irrigation, benefiting 4,713 farmers. The initiative aims to modernize irrigation systems, reduce water consumption by 20-40%, cut energy use, and boost crop yields by 50%. The project is expected to be completed by 2025 and includes infrastructure improvements, such as replacing old cement channels with HDPE over 181 km, improving water efficiency in the region.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, Water, and Forests

records.title: Oman is advancing its food security agenda by initiating 65 investment opportunities, totaling over $78 million, across the South Al Bati...
records.description: Oman is advancing its food security agenda by initiating 65 investment opportunities, totaling over $78 million, across the South Al Batinah Governorate in collaboration with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning. These projects, spanning the farm, livestock, and fisheries sectors, aim to bolster self-sufficiency in food production. Highlighted initiatives include enhancing poultry, dairy, and honey production, supporting local livestock breeds, and fostering organic agriculture. Additional efforts focus on establishing facilities like a date factory and a bee research station, alongside community-empowering projects such as training centers for rural women.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning

records.title: Maersk has inaugurated its largest logistics park in the Middle East at Jeddah Islamic Port, Saudi Arabia.
records.description: Maersk has inaugurated its largest logistics park in the Middle East at Jeddah Islamic Port, Saudi Arabia. The facility, covering 225,000 square meters, enhances Saudi Arabia’s logistics capabilities with advanced warehousing solutions for various industries, including FMCG, automotive, and pharmaceuticals. It also integrates multi-modal transport connectivity. The park supports sustainability by sourcing 70% of its electricity from solar panels and using electric trucks and energy-efficient lighting.

records.title: Algeria has announced the construction of a new production unit for powdered milk and infant flour in El-Harrach, Algiers.
records.description: Algeria has announced the construction of a new production unit for powdered milk and infant flour in El-Harrach, Algiers. This project, involving an investment of 4 billion dinars (approximately US$29.8 million), is a collaboration between the private company Algerian Baby Healthcare and the state-owned pharmaceutical group Saidal. The facility, expected to begin operations in the second quarter of 2025, aims to produce 15,000 tons of powdered milk and 10,000 tons of infant flour annually, targeting children aged 0 to 36 months. This initiative is expected to create over 200 jobs and significantly reduce Algeria’s reliance on imported powdered milk, which currently costs the country over US$800 million annually.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Industry and Pharmaceutical Production

records.title: Egypt’s foreign debt decreased by $7.4 billion in the first quarter of 2024, as reported by the Central Bank of Egypt.
records.description: Egypt’s foreign debt decreased by $7.4 billion in the first quarter of 2024, as reported by the Central Bank of Egypt. This reduction was influenced by the sale of development rights for Ras El-Hekma on the Mediterranean coast to the UAE for $35 billion in late February. The total foreign debt was reported at $160.6 billion at the end of March, down from $168.0 billion at the end of December. Additionally, Egypt secured a $8 billion financial support package from the International Monetary Fund in March, committing to a free-floating currency, with the IMF disbursing an initial $820 million. The remaining funds are scheduled for semi-annual disbursements until September 2026. This debt reduction and financial strategy have been part of Egypt’s broader efforts to finance infrastructure, military acquisitions, and support its currency, with foreign debt now accounting for 39.8% of its GDP.

records.title: Egyptian fertilizer manufacturer Biogrand is planning to establish a factory in Saudi Arabia with an investment of up to SAR 25 million.
records.description: Egyptian fertilizer manufacturer Biogrand is planning to establish a factory in Saudi Arabia with an investment of up to SAR 25 million. Scheduled to be operational by the end of February 2025, the factory is being set up in partnership with Saudi investors. The new facility intends to meet the demand of the Saudi market and aims to export 50% of its production to four Arab countries.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: In Egypt, the strawberry industry is facing severe challenges due to climate change, impacting the cultivation and economic viability of...
records.description: In Egypt, the strawberry industry is facing severe challenges due to climate change, impacting the cultivation and economic viability of this crop. Advisors and industry experts report increasing temperature fluctuations, irregular rainfall, and extreme weather events affecting plant health and soil quality. The 2023-2024 season was particularly difficult for strawberry growers, with heightened temperatures causing the fruit to ripen too quickly, reducing both size and quality. These conditions have led to a decrease in productivity and an increase in production costs, including irrigation, pest control, and the cost of strawberry plants. As a result, both fresh and frozen strawberry prices have risen significantly, and the outlook for the 2024-2025 season remains grim, with expectations of more severe weather conditions and even higher costs.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation & Fayruz Nurseries

records.title: This year, Egypt is witnessing a significant increase in mango production, resulting in lower market prices for the fruit.
records.description: This year, Egypt is witnessing a significant increase in mango production, resulting in lower market prices for the fruit. Favorable weather conditions during crucial growth phases have led to an abundance of high-quality mangoes, prompting a decrease in prices due to a surplus supply. Egypt has managed to produce enough mangoes to not only satisfy domestic demand but also to bolster exports. By mid-August, mango exports had reached 37,038 tons, making it the seventh highest in Egypt’s agricultural exports for the year. Major markets for Egyptian mangoes include Saudi Arabia, Russia, the UAE, Bahrain, Oman, and the UK. Moreover, the expansion of mango cultivation on reclaimed land in various regions of Egypt has supported the increase in production. The Ministry of Agriculture is actively working to access new export markets through collaborative efforts with Export Councils, enhancing the international reach of Egyptian mangoes.

records.title: Iraq's Prime Minister chaired a meeting to discuss relocating old brick factories in Nahrawan, which are near residential areas and contr...
records.description: Iraq's Prime Minister chaired a meeting to discuss relocating old brick factories in Nahrawan, which are near residential areas and contribute to pollution. These factories, often operating without permits and using outdated machinery, also exploit vulnerable workers. The Prime Minister instructed the Ministry of Industry to conduct a geological survey to find environmentally compliant sites away from urban areas. Future factories will be required to use modern, eco-friendly technologies, and a detailed plan will be presented at the next High Committee for Provincial Coordination meeting.

records.title: Lebanon announced plans to require state institutions to pay their overdue electricity bills as a means to raise funds for paying off its...
records.description: Lebanon announced plans to require state institutions to pay their overdue electricity bills as a means to raise funds for paying off its significant fuel import debts to Iraq. Lebanon's caretaker Energy Minister stated that around $150 million would be paid to Iraq from these collections. This move aims to address the more than $1.6 billion in total dues expected by November 2024. This strategy is part of efforts to manage the criticism Lebanon has faced over handling its fuel contract with Iraq, initiated in 2021, which has led to delivery delays and widespread power outages. Despite these challenges, an Iraqi official indicated that the fuel supply contract is not canceled, with the next shipment expected to arrive on August 26, contingent on resolving financial issues. Additionally, Algeria has pledged immediate fuel support to help alleviate Lebanon's ongoing energy crisis.
records.institution: Lebanese Ministry of Energy and Water

records.title: Moroccan pepper growers, particularly in the Souss Massa region, are anticipating an earlier start to the season around November, recover...
records.description: Moroccan pepper growers, particularly in the Souss Massa region, are anticipating an earlier start to the season around November, recovering from last year's setbacks caused by a severe heatwave. This incident led to scorched plantations and a seed shortage, delaying the season and complicating trade. This year, conditions have improved, with stable temperatures and smooth seed supply. At Universal Peppers, acreage for the Kapi variety has doubled to 30 hectares in response to strong demand, particularly from Germany, Switzerland, and Eastern Europe. Growers in the region are also adopting new pepper varieties to mitigate challenges from pests and diseases, with successful trials leading to a shift to a new Dutch-origin Kapi variety.

records.title: Qatar is on track to double its economy by 2031, driven by strategic initiatives that have restored government revenues to levels seen be...
records.description: Qatar is on track to double its economy by 2031, driven by strategic initiatives that have restored government revenues to levels seen before the 2014 oil price shock. The country's significant position in the global energy market, particularly as the world's sixth-largest gas producer with the third-largest gas reserves, has been pivotal. With planned increases in LNG output by 85% at the North Field by 2025, Qatar's natural gas production is expected to nearly double by 2030. Beyond hydrocarbons, Qatar's economic diversification efforts have reduced its reliance on oil and gas, with two-thirds of its GDP now coming from non-oil sectors like real estate, construction, financial services, trade, manufacturing, logistics, and tourism. Additionally, foreign investment reforms and infrastructural developments linked to the World Cup and National Vision 2030 have further fueled economic growth across various sectors.

records.title: The Citrus Office / Syrian Ministry of Agriculture estimated citrus production for the 2023-2024 season at about 688 thousand tons, a dec...
records.description: The Citrus Office / Syrian Ministry of Agriculture estimated citrus production for the 2023-2024 season at about 688 thousand tons, a decrease of about 18% compared to the previous season due to the prevailing climatic conditions

records.title: The Abu Dhabi wealth fund ADQ has partnered with the UAE’s National Food Loss and Waste Initiative (ne’ma) in a multi-year agreement to t...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi wealth fund ADQ has partnered with the UAE’s National Food Loss and Waste Initiative (ne’ma) in a multi-year agreement to tackle food loss throughout the entire value chain, from production to consumption. Ne’ma, established in 2022 in collaboration between the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment and the Emirates Foundation, aims to halve food loss and waste by 2030, aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goal 12.3.
records.institution: ADQ & UAE’s National Food Loss and Waste Initiative (ne’ma)

records.title: Egypt is exploring Türkiye as a new wheat import source as part of its strategy to diversify grain suppliers amid global market challenges.
records.description: Egypt is exploring Türkiye as a new wheat import source as part of its strategy to diversify grain suppliers amid global market challenges. This move follows disruptions caused by the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, Egypt's traditional suppliers. Egypt, which secured 3.6 million tons of local wheat in 2024, aims to bolster reserves through potential imports, including a record-breaking tender for 3.8 million tons. Current wheat reserves are estimated to last for over six months, ensuring stability in essential food supplies.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Morocco's cannabis legislation, which recently came into effect, offers innovative support for farmers.
records.description: Morocco's cannabis legislation, which recently came into effect, offers innovative support for farmers. It allows producers to form cooperatives that guarantee the sale of their production through contracts with authorized operators under the National Agency for the Regulation of Activities Relating to Cannabis (ANRAC). The law ensures price visibility before cultivation, restricts cannabis farming to specific regions, and offers access to public subsidies. The regulations also aim to prevent unauthorized expansion of cannabis farming and strengthen small farmers' negotiating power.
records.institution: Morrocan National Agency for the Regulation of Activities Relating to Cannabis (ANRAC)

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The prolonged drought in Morocco has severely impacted the wild rosemary harvest, with plants stunted and lower in essential acids.
records.description: The prolonged drought in Morocco has severely impacted the wild rosemary harvest, with plants stunted and lower in essential acids. Producers are increasingly shifting to cultivated, irrigated plantations to compensate for the reduced quality and availability of wild rosemary. Some regions have halted harvesting entirely to allow plants to regenerate. New plantations are being established to ensure a reliable supply, though challenges remain due to unpredictable weather.

records.title: Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC) has launched Abu Dhabi's first residential rental index.
records.description: Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC) has launched Abu Dhabi's first residential rental index. Available on the ADREC website, this index provides updated and reliable data on residential, commercial, and industrial properties across the emirate. It includes quarterly pricing information for various areas, enabling users to access current rental values.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC)

records.title: In response to a cholera outbreak in Sudan and the spread of mpox in some African countries, Egypt has enhanced its border controls, espe...
records.description: In response to a cholera outbreak in Sudan and the spread of mpox in some African countries, Egypt has enhanced its border controls, especially at southern airports and seaports. Health Ministry spokesman Hossam Abdel Ghaffar highlighted that Egypt has not reported any cholera cases since 2006 and is implementing numerous preventive measures at land crossings from Sudan. The tightening of border controls follows a significant cholera outbreak in Sudan, with the World Health Organization reporting 78 deaths and over 2,400 infections this year.

records.title: Oman recorded a trade surplus of RO2.989 billion in the first five months of 2024, a slight increase from RO2.986 billion in the same per...
records.description: Oman recorded a trade surplus of RO2.989 billion in the first five months of 2024, a slight increase from RO2.986 billion in the same period last year. During this period, total exports rose by 5% to RO9.689 billion, driven by a 1.8% increase in oil and gas exports. Crude oil exports saw a 7.6% increase, while refined oil and liquefied natural gas exports declined. Non-oil exports increased by 11.2%, with minerals, base metals, and chemical products leading this growth. Additionally, re-exports grew by 8.1%. The UAE was the largest market for Oman’s non-oil exports and re-exports, with significant increases in both categories.
records.institution: Omani National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI)

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company has achieved the prestigious AA+ certification from the BRCGS for its poultry facility, marking a significant milest...
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company has achieved the prestigious AA+ certification from the BRCGS for its poultry facility, marking a significant milestone as the first fresh chicken producer in Saudi Arabia to earn this rating. The certification highlights Tanmiah's dedication to food safety, quality control, and excellence, validated by an unannounced audit. This accomplishment aligns with global food safety standards and supports Saudi Vision 2030, reinforcing Tanmiah’s position as a leader in the halal food industry.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: AMEA Power, a UAE-based renewable energy company, has signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and Implementation Agreement (IA) with Ethi...
records.description: AMEA Power, a UAE-based renewable energy company, has signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and Implementation Agreement (IA) with Ethiopian Electric Power for a 300-megawatt (MW) wind energy project in Aysha, Ethiopia's Somali Region State. The project, valued at $620 million and set to be the largest wind farm in the Horn of Africa, was launched during COP28 in Dubai. The agreements also include a Land Lease Agreement with the Somali Region State Government. The Aysha-1 Wind Project is expected to generate 1,400 GWh of clean energy annually, sufficient to power over four million households and reduce carbon emissions by more than 690,000 tonnes per year. The project will also create over 1,500 direct jobs during its construction and operation phases.

records.title: DP World reported a 3.3% revenue growth to USD 9.33 billion in the first half of 2024, driven by increased container volumes in various r...
records.description: DP World reported a 3.3% revenue growth to USD 9.33 billion in the first half of 2024, driven by increased container volumes in various regions. However, its adjusted EBITDA dropped by 4.3% to USD 2.5 billion, affected by geopolitical tensions in the Red Sea and logistics expansion investments. The company generated USD 2.09 billion in cash from operations and maintained leverage of 3.8x net debt to adjusted EBITDA. DP World emphasized resilience amid global supply chain disruptions and is cautiously optimistic about future performance.

records.title: Arab ministers responsible for disaster risk reduction are set to meet in Cairo this Wednesday, under the auspices of the Arab League, to...
records.description: Arab ministers responsible for disaster risk reduction are set to meet in Cairo this Wednesday, under the auspices of the Arab League, to discuss and enhance regional cooperation in mitigating natural disasters. The agenda includes monitoring natural hazards, implementing the Arab Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction, and initiating a new program to tackle marine disasters. The meeting will also involve selecting a slogan for the Arab Day for Disaster Risk Reduction 2025 and planning for the Arab Regional Platform on Disaster Risk Reduction in Kuwait.

records.title: Between January and August 2024, Egypt's agricultural exports exceeded 5.6 million tons.
records.description: Between January and August 2024, Egypt's agricultural exports exceeded 5.6 million tons. Citrus fruits led the exports with over 2 million tons, followed by fresh potatoes at 957,481 tons. Onions, grapes, and beans held the next positions, with exports totaling 236,907 tons, 164,430 tons, and 156,644 tons, respectively. Other notable exports included potatoes, mangoes, tomatoes, garlic, strawberries, guava, and pomegranates. In April 2024, Egypt's trade deficit decreased by 2.5%, while exports saw a slight increase of 0.8%, reaching $3.29 billion.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform estimated the total apple production in Syria for the 2023-2024 season at about 186 thous...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform estimated the total apple production in Syria for the 2023-2024 season at about 186 thousand tons, a decrease of about 16% compared to the previous season
records.institution: Syrian Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform
