records.description: The Plant Variety Accreditation Committee approved a new variety of rainfed wheat (Sham 12) suitable for cultivation in the second agricultural stability areas

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt has partnered with Infinity Power and UAE's Masdar to construct a 200-megawatt wind power plant in Ras Ghareb, located in the Gulf...
records.description: Egypt has partnered with Infinity Power and UAE's Masdar to construct a 200-megawatt wind power plant in Ras Ghareb, located in the Gulf of Suez. The consortium, which includes Egypt’s Infinity Group and UAE-based Masdar, will develop, finance, and operate the onshore wind project. A Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) was signed with the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company. The wind farm is expected to begin commercial operations in October 2026 and will generate 810,000 megawatt-hours of electricity annually, reducing carbon dioxide emissions by 403,672 tonnes per year.

records.title: The Ambassador of Sri Lanka to Saudi Arabia met with the Governor of the Saudi General Authority of Foreign Trade (GAFT) in Riyadh to dis...
records.description: The Ambassador of Sri Lanka to Saudi Arabia met with the Governor of the Saudi General Authority of Foreign Trade (GAFT) in Riyadh to discuss enhancing bilateral trade and investment. The discussions centered on potential sectors such as food, agriculture, IT, manufacturing, hospitality, real estate, and construction. The Sri Lankan Ambassador expressed the country's readiness to support Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 and invited a Saudi trade delegation to Sri Lanka for a fact-finding mission. The meeting was also attended by GAFT's Deputy Governor of International Relations and other senior officials.
records.institution: Saudi General Authority of Foreign Trade (GAFT)

records.title: Zimbabwe is exploring a potential collaboration with the Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company (SALIC) to enhance its lives...
records.description: Zimbabwe is exploring a potential collaboration with the Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company (SALIC) to enhance its livestock value chain. The Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development permanent secretary met with a SALIC delegation in Harare to discuss mutual investment opportunities. This partnership aims to modernize Zimbabwe’s agricultural sector, improve food security, and extend its market reach both regionally and internationally. The discussions also focused on introducing new technologies and advanced livestock management practices to Zimbabwean farmers, with further plans to develop a detailed roadmap for cooperation.
records.institution: Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company (SALIC)

records.title: Fruit and vegetable prices in Casablanca’s wholesale market are dropping, with apples now selling between 6-11 dirhams per kilo and banan...
records.description: Fruit and vegetable prices in Casablanca’s wholesale market are dropping, with apples now selling between 6-11 dirhams per kilo and bananas at 9-10 dirhams, due to increased harvests and seasonal factors. However, peaches have seen a price rise, reaching 6 dirhams per kilo due to water shortages affecting certain agricultural regions. Potato prices range from 3-4.5 dirhams, while vegetables like carrots and onions are at particularly low prices. Despite abundant production, demand remains low, likely due to the summer season.
records.institution: Casablanca Fruit and Vegetable Wholesale Market Association (AMGFLC)

records.title: In the 2023/24 season, Egypt set a new record by surpassing the USA in sweet potato exports to the EU, according to EastFruit.
records.description: In the 2023/24 season, Egypt set a new record by surpassing the USA in sweet potato exports to the EU, according to EastFruit. Egypt exported 109,000 tons of sweet potatoes to the EU during this period, marking a 45% increase from the previous season and a nearly tenfold rise from the 2018/19 season. This growth in exports has led Egypt to account for nearly half of the EU's total sweet potato imports, which reached a record 219,000 tons. The USA, in contrast, saw a significant reduction in its EU market presence, exporting only 78,000 tons.

records.title: Rwanda has allocated a logistics zone for Egyptian investments, aiming to enhance trade relations between the two nations.
records.description: Rwanda has allocated a logistics zone for Egyptian investments, aiming to enhance trade relations between the two nations. The agreement, formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed on August 12, focuses on collaboration in transport and logistics.

records.title: Iraq is bolstering local flour production by selling domestically produced wheat to mills at competitive prices and increasing tariffs on...
records.description: Iraq is bolstering local flour production by selling domestically produced wheat to mills at competitive prices and increasing tariffs on imported flour. Starting September 1, 2024, a 10% tariff on imported flour will rise to 25% by January 2025, with further evaluations in six months. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to promote self-sufficiency in food security. The government has set local wheat prices for mills and imposed additional duties on imported packaged flour, aiming to reduce reliance on imports.

records.title: Morocco remains heavily reliant on France for soft wheat imports, with France holding a 35.8% market share in 2023.
records.description: Morocco remains heavily reliant on France for soft wheat imports, with France holding a 35.8% market share in 2023. Despite a 43% drop in national cereal production, Morocco imported wheat valued at nearly 20 billion dirhams. The global wheat price decline has benefited Morocco, which continues to strengthen its reserves. While direct storage subsidies have been removed, the state supports the price gap between acquisition and delivery. Industry professionals see this as an opportunity to secure supplies before global prices rise again.

records.title: An Egyptian trade union delegation visited the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions (GFJTU) in Amman to discuss operational strat...
records.description: An Egyptian trade union delegation visited the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions (GFJTU) in Amman to discuss operational strategies and reinforce collaborative efforts. The visit focused on exploring the GFJTU’s current trade union strategies, comprehensive reform plans, and their impact on the economic and social spheres. The delegation also congratulated the leadership of the GFJTU on recent electoral outcomes and expressed support for its modernization initiatives and efforts to defend workers' rights.
records.institution: The Arab Federation for Petroleum, Mining and Chemical Workers & The Egyptian Trade Union Federation

records.title: Sun World International won a significant legal case in Egypt, with the Cairo and Tanta economic courts ruling in its favor regarding the...
records.description: Sun World International won a significant legal case in Egypt, with the Cairo and Tanta economic courts ruling in its favor regarding the unauthorized production and sale of its licensed table grapes. The courts issued injunctions against two Egyptian growers, stopping them from propagating Sun World’s proprietary grape varieties and ordering the destruction of illegally planted vines. This action follows the company's registration of its Plant Variety Rights in Egypt. Sun World, which holds over 200 patents and PVRs globally, actively monitors grape-growing regions and markets worldwide to enforce its intellectual property rights. The company recently expanded its portfolio by acquiring Biogold Group, enhancing its offerings in citrus, mangoes, and avocados.

records.title: Uganda has sent its first shipment of 50 tonnes of beef to Egypt, marking a significant milestone in agricultural trade between the two n...
records.description: Uganda has sent its first shipment of 50 tonnes of beef to Egypt, marking a significant milestone in agricultural trade between the two nations. This trial shipment was facilitated by the Egypt-Uganda Food Security Company, overcoming logistical challenges. The trade is supported by recent agreements aimed at strengthening economic ties. Egypt, which is importing livestock from several African countries to stabilize meat prices, could increase beef imports from Uganda following this successful trial, contributing to Uganda's export diversification.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Chad has expressed its desire to benefit from Morocco's expertise in agriculture and new technologies.
records.description: Chad has expressed its desire to benefit from Morocco's expertise in agriculture and new technologies. During a joint press conference in Dakhla, Chad's Foreign Minister highlighted the deep historical ties between the two nations and emphasized the significance of Morocco's support in various sectors, including education and international cooperation. The minister also reaffirmed Chad’s backing of Morocco's territorial integrity and discussed plans to strengthen bilateral economic relations through reactivating the Joint Commission between the two countries.
records.institution: Chadian Ministry of State for Foreign Affairs, African Integration, Chadians Abroad, and International Cooperation

records.title: The upcoming Moroccan avocado season is expected to be promising with an anticipated increase in production volumes and improved fruit si...
records.description: The upcoming Moroccan avocado season is expected to be promising with an anticipated increase in production volumes and improved fruit sizes. The season will commence in week 38/39 for Green Skin varieties and week 43 for Hass. Favorable weather conditions have contributed to minimal impact from adverse winds and a smooth flowering process, setting the stage for an excellent harvest with better size distribution. Following a record production of 60 thousand tonnes last season, the Moroccan Avocado Association (MAVA) forecasts this season's output to reach 80-90 thousand tonnes, driven by the maturation of young trees and stable climatic conditions.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi-listed ACWA Power has signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) for a 60-megawatt (MW) floating solar photovoltaic (PV) project in In...
records.description: Saudi-listed ACWA Power has signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) for a 60-megawatt (MW) floating solar photovoltaic (PV) project in Indonesia. ACWA Power will hold a 49 percent equity stake in the Saguling project, with the remaining share held by Indonesia Power, a subsidiary of the state-owned PLN, which is also the project’s offtaker.

records.title: The fourth session of the UAE-Kenya Joint Committee was held in Abu Dhabi to enhance economic cooperation between the two countries.
records.description: The fourth session of the UAE-Kenya Joint Committee was held in Abu Dhabi to enhance economic cooperation between the two countries. The meeting, co-chaired by the UAE Minister of State and the Kenyan Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, covered topics such as trade, investment, tourism, aviation, renewable energy, education, agriculture, transport, and defense. The session ended with the signing of the minutes and a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) focused on governance and expertise exchange in the government sector.

records.title: The province of El-Oued has allocated 33,000 hectares for late-season potato cultivation in 2024/2025, marking a 10% increase from the pr...
records.description: The province of El-Oued has allocated 33,000 hectares for late-season potato cultivation in 2024/2025, marking a 10% increase from the previous year. This expansion reflects the region's growing role in Algeria's agricultural sector, with potato farming accounting for 30% of the region’s cultivated land. Major producing areas include El-Magrane, Hassi-Khelifa, and Trifaoui. El-Oued is the top potato-producing region in Algeria, contributing 40% of the country's production, with expected yields of 11.5 million quintals for the upcoming season.

records.title: Egypt has extended the deadline for Dutch seed potato exports to December 23, 2024, offering Dutch exporters more time to ship after last...
records.description: Egypt has extended the deadline for Dutch seed potato exports to December 23, 2024, offering Dutch exporters more time to ship after last year's shortened season caused losses. Rising potato prices in Egypt, caused by seed shortages and extreme weather, have compounded economic challenges. A shortage of seeds and high temperatures have reduced yields, leading to a significant drop in supply and price increases in the local market.
records.institution: Egyptian Central Authority of Plant Quarantine

records.title: One month into the Egyptian sweet potato season, despite high and stable demand, prices are continuing to decrease.
records.description: One month into the Egyptian sweet potato season, despite high and stable demand, prices are continuing to decrease. This season's production has significantly increased, largely due to an early and abundant harvest from the Damietta region, which has also boosted the availability of popular larger sizes. Although prices started higher at the beginning of the season, they have dropped due to a greater initial supply and the quick liquidation of stocks by less experienced exporters. The expectation is that prices will continue to decrease until stocks are exhausted, after which they will likely rise again towards the end of the season.

records.title: The Iraqi Prime Minister inaugurated three significant infrastructure projects in Baghdad via video link.
records.description: The Iraqi Prime Minister inaugurated three significant infrastructure projects in Baghdad via video link. The projects include the expansion of the main entrance road from Diyala-Kirkuk, which was widened from 10 to 16 meters to improved highway standards. The Nahrawan Water Project, previously stalled since 2012, now provides 4,000 cubic meters of water per hour to address water shortages in the area. Additionally, a series of overpasses on the Army Canal were completed, linking the Jamila area to Bab Al-Muazzam Street as part of the first phase of traffic decongestion projects in the capital.

records.title: In Mauritania, a significant initiative known as the "Great Green Wall" is being implemented to combat the encroachment of desert sands o...
records.description: In Mauritania, a significant initiative known as the "Great Green Wall" is being implemented to combat the encroachment of desert sands on homes and agricultural lands. This project, launched in 2007 and involving more than 20 African countries, aims to halt the advance of the desert by planting a vast stretch of vegetation across the Sahel region. Local residents have adopted various techniques to nurture plants despite challenging conditions such as rare rainfall, employing methods like using solar-powered pumps to irrigate palm groves. Despite these efforts, only about four percent of the project's original goals have been met. The Mauritanian government, recognizing the urgency of the situation, is supporting community projects that combine environmental preservation with rural development to improve the living conditions of vulnerable populations. The overarching goal is to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.

records.title: Oman recorded an 11.6% increase in the value of fruit and vegetable imports, totaling over OMR 110 million from May 2023 to May 2024.
records.description: Oman recorded an 11.6% increase in the value of fruit and vegetable imports, totaling over OMR 110 million from May 2023 to May 2024. Vegetable imports saw a significant rise of 44.9%, while fruit imports slightly declined by 2.5%. The UAE and Yemen were primary sources for these imports. In contrast, Oman's fruit exports surged by 40.1%, with substantial growth in exports to Qatar and the UAE, though vegetable re-exports decreased and fruit re-exports increased considerably.

records.title: Due to the war in Gaza, Israel stopped issuing work permits for Palestinians, leading many in the West Bank to return to farming.
records.description: Due to the war in Gaza, Israel stopped issuing work permits for Palestinians, leading many in the West Bank to return to farming. Former workers, including those who previously worked in Israel, have set up greenhouses and resumed agriculture. Despite lower wages compared to working in Israel, many now prefer cultivating their own land, seeing it as more independent and peaceful. The war has also led to a sharp rise in unemployment in the West Bank, increasing from 12.9% to 32% by the end of 2023.

records.title: The total amount of wheat received by the Grain Trade and Processing Corporation/ Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection for...
records.description: The total amount of wheat received by the Grain Trade and Processing Corporation/ Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection for the 2023-2024 season amounted to about 701 thousand tons, compared to 710 thousand tons in the previous season.

records.title: Tunisia is set to host the third Annual International Conference and Exposition of the African Chapter of the World Aquaculture Society (...
records.description: Tunisia is set to host the third Annual International Conference and Exposition of the African Chapter of the World Aquaculture Society (AFRAQ2024) from November 19 to 22, 2024. The event, themed "Blue Farming: New Horizons for Economic Growth," will draw over a thousand participants globally, focusing on the role of aquaculture in economic development across Africa. Preparations are underway, with significant backing from the Tunisian government and leading local aquaculture companies like Nutrifish, the event's Gold Sponsor.
records.institution: Annual International Conference and Exposition of the African Chapter of the World Aquaculture Society (AFRAQ2024)

records.title: Brazilian exports of chicken meat to Iraq more than doubled in July, with a total shipment of 15.3 thousand tons, representing an increas...
records.description: Brazilian exports of chicken meat to Iraq more than doubled in July, with a total shipment of 15.3 thousand tons, representing an increase of 118.6 percent compared to the same month last year. This total includes both fresh and processed products.

records.title: Morocco is addressing challenges in its dairy sector caused by persistent drought through various support strategies.
records.description: Morocco is addressing challenges in its dairy sector caused by persistent drought through various support strategies. These include ongoing livestock feed programs, importing animal feed, developing regulations for livestock, and encouraging resilient forage crops. The government is also promoting artificial insemination, boosting high-yield mixed breeds, and protecting female livestock to ensure future productivity. Morocco produces around 2.5 million tons of milk annually, with 60-70% processed formally. The focus is on sustaining milk production and enhancing its quality despite climate-related hurdles.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, Water, and Forests

records.title: Sudan has enforced a 10% allocation of irrigation land for sorghum production to address the escalating food shortage caused by the ongoi...
records.description: Sudan has enforced a 10% allocation of irrigation land for sorghum production to address the escalating food shortage caused by the ongoing conflict. This move follows the UN’s famine declaration in North Darfur and aims to mitigate food insecurity as agricultural activities in key regions, such as Al Jazirah and Sennar, have been severely disrupted. The conflict has led to reduced cultivation, infrastructure damage, and looting, further exacerbating the food crisis and increasing commodity prices across the region.

records.title: UAE Amends Labour Law, Introduces Stricter Fines for Violations
records.description: The UAE government has significantly amended its Labour Law, introducing a range of stricter regulations and higher fines for violations in employment relationships. According to the new federal decree-law, penalties for employment violations can now reach between Dhs100,000 and Dhs1 million. These amendments include severe fines for employers who engage in illegal practices such as hiring without proper permits, failing to provide jobs after recruitment, misusing work permits, and shutting down operations without settling workers' rights. Additional penalties are set for the illegal employment of minors and fictitious recruitment practices, including fraudulent Emiratisation. The decree also shifts the jurisdiction for labor disputes from the Court of Appeal to the Court of First Instance unless already adjudicated. Additionally, MOHRE is empowered to initiate criminal proceedings for fictitious employment, with provisions for employers to settle cases before court sentencing by paying a substantial portion of the fines and returning any unduly received incentives.

records.title: Riyadh Air has introduced the first electric bus into its fleet as part of its initiative to support sustainable transport and reduce car...
records.description: Riyadh Air has introduced the first electric bus into its fleet as part of its initiative to support sustainable transport and reduce carbon emissions in Saudi Arabia. This development is part of a collaboration with National Transportation Solutions Co., a division of Petromin Corp., and TAM-Europe, aligning with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030 to promote digital solutions in public transportation and enhance urban sustainability.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Saudi Arabia has achieved 124% self-sufficiency in date production, with an annual yield exceeding 1.6 million tons, supported by the exp...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has achieved 124% self-sufficiency in date production, with an annual yield exceeding 1.6 million tons, supported by the expansion of palm cultivation to about 165,000 hectares across the Kingdom. The Riyadh region is the leading producer, contributing 436,112 tons, followed by the Qassim region with 390,698 tons, and other regions also making significant contributions. The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture highlighted these figures as part of the Harvest Season campaign, which promotes local fruit production and consumption.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia has announced a comprehensive update to its investment law, aiming to bolster its attractiveness to international investors...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has announced a comprehensive update to its investment law, aiming to bolster its attractiveness to international investors as part of its Vision 2030 reform strategy. The revised law enhances investor protections, streamlines the registration process, and introduces service centers to facilitate business operations and government transactions. The changes include robust protections for intellectual property, easier fund transfers, and simplified licensing requirements, with an aim to foster fair competition and ensure equal treatment for all investors.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Saudi Arabia's Culinary Arts Commission, in partnership with the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, will host farmers' marke...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Culinary Arts Commission, in partnership with the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, will host farmers' markets to promote local agriculture and culinary arts. Scheduled at Al-Nakheel Avenue in Unaizah from August 15-17 and 22-24, and at Aseeb Farm in Buraidah from April 29-31, 2025, the markets will showcase Qassim’s renowned crops like dates and vegetables, alongside family activities and live music to enhance the experience and support national products.
records.institution: Saudi Culinary Arts Commission & Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s King Abdulaziz Port in Dammam has introduced a new shipping service called “Milaha Gulf Express 2” (2-MGX), operated by th...
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s King Abdulaziz Port in Dammam has introduced a new shipping service called “Milaha Gulf Express 2” (2-MGX), operated by the Qatari company Milaha. This service will connect the port to seven key regional and international ports, including those in China, India, Oman, and Qatar, enhancing its global trade capabilities. The port, which features 43 berths and a capacity for handling 105 million tons annually, will run this service bi-monthly, accommodating up to 9,000 standard containers per voyage.

records.title: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen has significantly enhanced the country's healthcare infrastructure, benefiting...
records.description: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen has significantly enhanced the country's healthcare infrastructure, benefiting over 4.4 million individuals. This comprehensive initiative includes constructing and equipping medical facilities, training healthcare professionals, and executing specialized projects such as the King Salman Medical and Educational City and the Prince Mohammed bin Salman Hospital. These facilities offer a range of services from general medical consultations to specialized surgical and cardiac care. Additional projects like the Taiz Cancer Treatment Center and the Aden Rehabilitation Center for Disabled Children cater to specific health needs. The program has also improved existing hospitals and supports 26 medical facilities across nine governorates.

records.title: The National Agricultural Mutual Fund (CNMA) is set to introduce a new insurance product called "Saisonnier Agricole," specifically for d...
records.description: The National Agricultural Mutual Fund (CNMA) is set to introduce a new insurance product called "Saisonnier Agricole," specifically for daily and seasonal agricultural workers. This coverage will protect workers from accidents occurring during various agricultural activities, such as harvesting and planting. The product is designed to be flexible and affordable, tailored to different agricultural seasons. It will be available at CNMA’s regional and local offices, aiming to support worker safety and ensure the sustainability of agricultural activities in Algeria.

records.title: Iraq has resumed purchasing rice from the United States, according to the USA Rice Federation.
records.description: Iraq has resumed purchasing rice from the United States, according to the USA Rice Federation. This follows a period of uncertainty due to financial restrictions imposed by the U.S. government. ADM Rice has sold a vessel of American rice that will be loaded and shipped to Iraq early this autumn. Iraq was previously a significant market for U.S. rice, ranking as the fourth largest export market overall in 2023 and the second largest for long grain milled rice.

records.title: The sharp increase in feed prices has significantly driven up food inflation in Morocco, with the poultry industry experiencing particula...
records.description: The sharp increase in feed prices has significantly driven up food inflation in Morocco, with the poultry industry experiencing particularly severe impacts. This surge has escalated chicken prices to 25 dirhams per kilogram, nearing record highs, and raising concerns among Moroccan households about their food budgets. The rise in feed costs, which make up 80% of poultry production expenses, is largely due to Morocco's reliance on imports of corn, soybeans, and sunflower oil. The situation is worsened by global market fluctuations and logistical issues, such as those in the Red Sea. With poultry production costs now at 18 dirhams per kilogram for broiler meat, industry sustainability is in question, further strained by a prolonged drought affecting local feed production.

records.title: Oman’s A’Dhahirah Governorate is planning a major expansion in wheat cultivation to boost food security and reduce reliance on imports.
records.description: Oman’s A’Dhahirah Governorate is planning a major expansion in wheat cultivation to boost food security and reduce reliance on imports. A recent meeting between the Directorate General of Agriculture and private investors discussed strategies to enhance wheat production, including improving soil and water management. Challenges such as soil quality and irrigation were addressed, with plans to adopt modern farming techniques.
records.institution: Omani Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources in A’Dhahirah Governorate

records.title: Olam Food Ingredients (OFI) is considering selling its remaining 64.57% stake in Olam Agri to the Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Invest...
records.description: Olam Food Ingredients (OFI) is considering selling its remaining 64.57% stake in Olam Agri to the Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company (SALIC). SALIC had previously acquired a 35.43% stake in 2022. This sale may delay OFI's planned IPO. The deal follows Olam Agri's recent US$625 million financing and its acquisition of Senegal's Avisen SARL.

records.title: Saudi Printing and Packaging Company (SPP) reported a 10.29% year-on-year revenue loss for the first half of FY24, dropping to SAR 361.35...
records.description: Saudi Printing and Packaging Company (SPP) reported a 10.29% year-on-year revenue loss for the first half of FY24, dropping to SAR 361.35 million. Net loss increased by 164.50%, reaching SAR 93.74 million, and the company’s accumulated losses now account for 32.50% of its capital. In Q2-24, net loss surged by 253.47% compared to Q2-23. Additionally, Labelexpo Global Series announced the launch of Gulf Print & Pack in Riyadh for 2025.

records.title: Egypt has set a goal to reduce its inflation rate to less than 10% by the end of 2025 or the beginning of 2026, according to an announcem...
records.description: Egypt has set a goal to reduce its inflation rate to less than 10% by the end of 2025 or the beginning of 2026, according to an announcement by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly. This target is part of the country's broader economic strategy to stabilize its financial environment.

records.title: In July, Egypt's annual urban consumer price inflation decreased to 25.7%, down from 27.5% in June, according to the national statistics...
records.description: In July, Egypt's annual urban consumer price inflation decreased to 25.7%, down from 27.5% in June, according to the national statistics agency Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS). This decline was steeper than anticipated, with a poll of analysts predicting a median rate of 26.6%. The month-on-month prices also fell by 0.4% in July, with food prices dropping slightly by 0.3%, yet still standing 28.5% higher than the previous year. These changes follow Egypt's engagement with a stringent monetary policy under an $8 billion IMF support package, which has also necessitated hikes in domestic prices and a significant devaluation of the currency. Subsidized product prices have been raised, and interest rates have seen a cumulative increase of 800 basis points in 2024, as part of efforts to manage the country's budget deficit.
records.institution: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: Oman has instituted a two-month ban on the catching and trading of kingfish, effective from August 15 to October 15, 2024, to protect mar...
records.description: Oman has instituted a two-month ban on the catching and trading of kingfish, effective from August 15 to October 15, 2024, to protect marine life and promote sustainable fishing practices. This regulation, mandated by Ministerial Resolution No. (230/2014 AD), requires fishermen, transporters, and businesses involved in the fishing industry to comply strictly with the ban. All kingfish stocks must be registered prior to the commencement of the ban, and any trading or exporting of unregistered kingfish during this period is prohibited. The Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources urges full cooperation to avoid legal consequences and penalties for non-compliance.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Alesayi Beverage Corporation, a top beverage manufacturer in Saudi Arabia, has partnered with SIG to introduce advanced Bag-in-Box (BIB)...
records.description: Alesayi Beverage Corporation, a top beverage manufacturer in Saudi Arabia, has partnered with SIG to introduce advanced Bag-in-Box (BIB) technology. The collaboration will utilize SIG's SureFill 42 Aseptic BIB filling system, with 10-liter bags made from SIG 2Pure Film for high-quality water and beverages. This initiative, focused on the HoReCa market, marks Alesayi's first venture into BIB packaging, aiming to expand its product range and offer more sustainable solutions, with plans to include juices and sauces.

records.title: UAE-based Spinneys, a prominent fresh food retailer, reported a second-quarter profit of 72 million dirhams ($20 million) for 2024, marki...
records.description: UAE-based Spinneys, a prominent fresh food retailer, reported a second-quarter profit of 72 million dirhams ($20 million) for 2024, marking a 17.8% increase from the previous year. This financial update follows the company's recent debut on the Dubai Financial Market. For the first half of the year, Spinneys achieved a profit of 146 million dirhams from revenues totaling 1.598 billion dirhams. Despite the new UAE corporate tax and one-off IPO-related expenses, the company maintained profitability and declared its first post-IPO dividend of 103 million dirhams.

records.title: Egypt continues to perform strongly in strawberry exports to Malaysia and Singapore, despite a slight drop from 1,700 tons last season to...
records.description: Egypt continues to perform strongly in strawberry exports to Malaysia and Singapore, despite a slight drop from 1,700 tons last season to an expected 1,500 tons this season. Egypt remains the second-largest exporter to these countries, with the market demand driven by growing consumption in Malaysia. Other major suppliers include South Korea, Australia, and the U.S. Meanwhile, Egypt’s frozen strawberry exports increased by 15% in 2024, reaching 120,000 tons and generating USD 180 million, mainly to Germany, the UK, and the Netherlands.

records.title: Egypt has launched its largest wheat tender to date, aiming to procure 3.8 million metric tons to ensure supply from October 2024 to Apri...
records.description: Egypt has launched its largest wheat tender to date, aiming to procure 3.8 million metric tons to ensure supply from October 2024 to April 2025. This ambitious move by the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) seeks to stabilize the nation’s wheat reserves amid fluctuating global prices and economic challenges. The tender, unusual for its extensive timeframe and volume, aligns with the government’s strategy to bolster economic stability with the backing of the International Monetary Fund and Gulf state support. However, the extended 270-day payment term has raised concerns among traders about the feasibility of fulfilling such a large order.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: The pomegranate season in Egypt has commenced and is set to continue through November.
records.description: The pomegranate season in Egypt has commenced and is set to continue through November. Despite challenges posed by climate change, which have reduced yields from the usual 12 tonnes per feddan to 8 tonnes, Egyptian producers, including Abdelkader Al Alhaboney, are committed to sustaining production. Efforts to manage the decline include adopting more resilient seeds and enhancing farming techniques with government support. The primary varieties available this season are 'Wonderful' and '116', as well as local varieties like 'Baladi', 'Asyouti', and 'Sukkari'. Despite competitive pressures from other summer fruits and among exporters, Alhaboney’s company is keeping prices consistent with the previous season to remain competitive in the market.

records.title: The Iraqi Cabinet has implemented protective measures for local fertilizer production, setting import prices at 800,000 dinars ($610) per...
records.description: The Iraqi Cabinet has implemented protective measures for local fertilizer production, setting import prices at 800,000 dinars ($610) per ton for Di-ammonium Phosphate (DAP) and 550,000 dinars per ton for urea. This policy aims to shield domestic producers from the competition posed by imported fertilizers.
records.institution: Iraqi Ministry of Industry and Minerals

records.title: Morocco's Tan-Tan port experienced a 48% decline in fish landings by June 2024, dropping to 14,890 tonnes from 28,567 tonnes in 2023.
records.description: Morocco's Tan-Tan port experienced a 48% decline in fish landings by June 2024, dropping to 14,890 tonnes from 28,567 tonnes in 2023. The financial value of these landings decreased by 24%, with significant reductions in pelagic fish (63% drop in quantity). Whitefish and mollusk landings also saw decreases, while crustaceans increased by 26%. Nationwide, coastal and artisanal fishing products saw a 10% drop in volume and a 4% decline in value. Other major ports like Laayoune also reported significant reductions in fish landings.

records.title: From July 10 to 16, KSrelief mobile clinics in Hajjah, Yemen, provided healthcare services to 1,443 patients across various departments i...
records.description: From July 10 to 16, KSrelief mobile clinics in Hajjah, Yemen, provided healthcare services to 1,443 patients across various departments including epidemic control, internal medicine, and pediatrics. The clinics dispensed medications to 1,401 individuals and conducted laboratory tests for 363 people. Additionally, KSrelief distributed essential supplies like shelter bags and food parcels in other regions of Yemen and Sudan, benefiting thousands more.

records.title: The Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE) has expanded its network with 10 new branches across six governorates, increasing its total to 1,114...
records.description: The Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE) has expanded its network with 10 new branches across six governorates, increasing its total to 1,114 branches. The bank has also renovated 16 existing branches and launched a new banking technology system to improve services like account management and loans. ABE is focusing on digital transformation by introducing online banking products and smart applications.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The International Labour Organization (ILO), alongside Iraq's Ministry of Planning and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, ho...
records.description: The International Labour Organization (ILO), alongside Iraq's Ministry of Planning and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, hosted a two-day conference to discuss a national policy for the development of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Iraq. The event brought together representatives from government entities, international organizations, financial institutions, and worker groups to focus on enhancing MSME development. Discussions included government strategies to simplify regulations and improve resource access for MSMEs, financial support measures such as the Central Bank of Iraq's National Banking Lending Strategy, and initiatives to promote entrepreneurship among youth and women. The conference also addressed the importance of international and cross-sector collaboration for sustainable development and the support of green business initiatives.
records.institution: The International Labour Organization (ILO), Iraqi Ministry of Planning, & the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation,

records.title: Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture has introduced a policy to gradually restrict tomato exports and increase imports to stabilize domestic...
records.description: Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture has introduced a policy to gradually restrict tomato exports and increase imports to stabilize domestic market prices. This strategy will potentially halt exports entirely if the current trend of rising market prices and decreasing imports persists. The aim is to ensure a sufficient supply of tomatoes for local consumers amidst fluctuations caused by changes in production cycles and rising temperatures. The Ministry anticipates that by mid-August, the supply situation will stabilize, meeting or exceeding domestic demand and consequently reducing prices.

records.title: The Republic of Korea has donated 11,520 metric tons of rice to the World Food Programme (WFP) to support school meal programs and refuge...
records.description: The Republic of Korea has donated 11,520 metric tons of rice to the World Food Programme (WFP) to support school meal programs and refugee relief efforts in Guinea-Bissau, Mauritania, and Sierra Leone. This donation will benefit 81,600 Malian refugees and 287,000 schoolchildren, addressing acute hunger exacerbated by climate change, conflicts, and economic instability in these regions. In Guinea-Bissau, the rice will be distributed across 850 schools, aiding 180,000 children. In Mauritania, it will assist both refugees and local students by enhancing food security at the Mbera refugee camp and surrounding areas. Sierra Leone will use this aid to support 106,700 students in 494 primary schools, reinforcing food security amid economic challenges and the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic.

records.title: In 2023, Morocco's imports of US tree nuts surged to USD 137.03 million, reflecting a significant 1755% increase over the past decade.
records.description: In 2023, Morocco's imports of US tree nuts surged to USD 137.03 million, reflecting a significant 1755% increase over the past decade. Morocco imported 32,381 tons of tree nuts such as almonds, cashews, and pistachios, indicating a robust demand for these products. This growth in tree nut imports is part of a broader expansion in US agricultural exports to Morocco, which reached a record USD 610.17 million in 2023. The increase is facilitated by the free trade agreement between the US and Morocco, enhancing economic ties and fostering trade.

records.title: Moroccan raspberry exports are set for a boost with the introduction of the Pink Hudson variety, which complements the popular Adelita va...
records.description: Moroccan raspberry exports are set for a boost with the introduction of the Pink Hudson variety, which complements the popular Adelita variety. Pink Hudson, known for its flavor and extended production cycle, is attracting interest from European retailers. VitaBlue, a major grower, has expanded its raspberry cultivation significantly and will use Pink Hudson to extend its production season from October to mid-June. Despite a 9% drop in export volume, Morocco remains the third-largest global raspberry exporter, facing challenges like water scarcity and rising domestic prices.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Oman is actively advancing low-carbon transport strategies to combat climate change, aiming for net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 as part...
records.description: Oman is actively advancing low-carbon transport strategies to combat climate change, aiming for net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 as part of Oman Vision 2040. The strategy includes promoting electric vehicles through incentives, developing hydrogen fuel cell technologies for long-distance transport, and integrating biofuels to reduce fossil fuel dependence. Additionally, Oman is enhancing public transportation infrastructure and promoting behavioral changes through public awareness campaigns and car-sharing initiatives, demonstrating a comprehensive approach to reducing the transport sector's carbon footprint.

records.title: In July, Saudi Arabia emerged as the largest buyer of Russian grain, marking the beginning of the new agricultural season.
records.description: In July, Saudi Arabia emerged as the largest buyer of Russian grain, marking the beginning of the new agricultural season. The country secured a total of 712,000 tonnes of barley and wheat, surpassing Egypt, which ranked second with 529,000 tonnes. Egypt, however, maintained its lead in wheat purchases specifically, acquiring 500,000 tonnes. Libya followed as the third largest importer, taking in 317,000 tonnes of wheat and other grains. Morocco also made significant purchases totaling 314,000 tonnes, positioning itself as a potential mainstay in the top five buyers for the season, which could impact wheat exporters from France negatively. Bangladesh rounded out the top five, purchasing 253,000 tonnes of wheat amid political instability that could affect its future grain buying policies.

records.title: Egypt has raised the costs for wheat and flour used in producing subsidized bread, marking significant increases of 20% and 35%, respecti...
records.description: Egypt has raised the costs for wheat and flour used in producing subsidized bread, marking significant increases of 20% and 35%, respectively. Despite these cost adjustments, consumer prices for subsidized bread will remain unchanged, as the government plans to absorb the additional costs. This measure comes amidst Egypt's ongoing economic challenges, including high inflation and a devalued currency, but aims to maintain the stability of bread prices for over 70 million beneficiaries of the nation's food subsidy program..
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Egypt plans to import significant quantities of livestock from Somalia and Djibouti to tackle rising meat prices and address local shorta...
records.description: Egypt plans to import significant quantities of livestock from Somalia and Djibouti to tackle rising meat prices and address local shortages. The move, announced by the head of the African Livestock Importers Association, aims to stabilize meat prices and ensure a consistent supply throughout the year. Egypt will begin importing 15,000 to 25,000 goats and sheep monthly through the Safaga area, where veterinary quarantines are prepared for immediate slaughter. This strategy is a shift from Egypt’s previous reliance on Sudan for livestock, prompted by military disruptions in Sudan.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt's government has announced an initiative to install solar panels on poultry farms to enhance electricity supply and reduce costs in...
records.description: Egypt's government has announced an initiative to install solar panels on poultry farms to enhance electricity supply and reduce costs in the sector. The solar panels will generate daytime electricity, while the national grid will supply power at night. The project, backed by financial incentives and private sector management, aims to modernize poultry farm operations and promote renewable energy use.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy & Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Iraq has launched measures to enhance local flour production, including selling local wheat to licensed mills at competitive prices and i...
records.description: Iraq has launched measures to enhance local flour production, including selling local wheat to licensed mills at competitive prices and introducing a progressively increasing customs tariff on imported flour, starting at 10% in September 2024 and rising to 25% by January 2025. The government also mandates the use of local wheat for producing zero flour, which will be supplied to social welfare beneficiaries and various ministries, and imposes a 30% customs duty on imported packaged flour starting October 2024.

records.title: Libya's imports of food and raw materials necessary for its local food industries are estimated at $5 billion annually, according to the...
records.description: Libya's imports of food and raw materials necessary for its local food industries are estimated at $5 billion annually, according to the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Economy and Trade for Technical Affairs. The country's food industry primarily involves the remanufacturing of these imported materials. The Ministry is focusing on strategies to localize food industries to enhance food security and expand the industrial and investment base, particularly in packaging industries.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Saudi Arabia has achieved 111% self-sufficiency in fig production, with annual outputs surpassing 28,000 tons across approximately 1,421...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has achieved 111% self-sufficiency in fig production, with annual outputs surpassing 28,000 tons across approximately 1,421 hectares. The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture reported that Jazan leads in production, followed by Riyadh and Asir among other regions. The fig production season extends from February to November. Efforts are ongoing to enhance fig production and marketing through the Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program, leveraging regional agricultural strengths.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) has launched a program to enhance the skills of agricultural extension agen...
records.description: The UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) has launched a program to enhance the skills of agricultural extension agents, aiming to boost agricultural production and national food security. The initiative includes specialized training in areas such as soil, irrigation, pest control, and crop production. The program also offers practical field courses and workshops to improve communication and technical skills.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment

records.title: Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture has initiated a significant feed distribution campaign aimed at supporting buffalo breeders in the souther...
records.description: Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture has initiated a significant feed distribution campaign aimed at supporting buffalo breeders in the southern part of the country who have been affected by climate change and water scarcity. This campaign, which started in Muthanna, is set to expand to other southern governorates in the coming months. The initiative was launched in collaboration with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and funded by the European Union. The campaign involves distributing molasses and bran to help improve the livelihoods of the breeders and encourage them to continue their activities locally instead of migrating.

records.title: Erbil-based Prime Water Technology has secured contracts with the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) to restore three wat...
records.description: Erbil-based Prime Water Technology has secured contracts with the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) to restore three water boreholes in Sinjar. The contracts include the restoration of the Al-Qabousiyah borehole for $225,063, the Beir Shireen borehole for $307,389, and the Al-Jazeera borehole for $225,032. These efforts aim to improve water access in the region.

records.title: Egypt and Saudi Arabia are taking steps to enhance their economic relationship with new investment initiatives discussed in a recent meet...
records.description: Egypt and Saudi Arabia are taking steps to enhance their economic relationship with new investment initiatives discussed in a recent meeting in Cairo. The session was attended by key figures including Egypt's Minister of Planning, Economic Development, and International Cooperation, and the Saudi Minister of Investment. They focused on improving the investment climate to bolster private sector investments and stimulate economic growth. Efforts to diversify the Egyptian economy and enhance its competitiveness were highlighted as priorities. Both nations acknowledged the significant role of private investments in driving economic development and agreed on strategies to make their investment environments more attractive.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Planning, Economic Development, and International Cooperation

records.title: India's Ostwal Group plans to invest $300 million in a fertilizer production factory in Egypt, aiming to produce 700,000 tons annually.
records.description: India's Ostwal Group plans to invest $300 million in a fertilizer production factory in Egypt, aiming to produce 700,000 tons annually. The factory will target markets in the Middle East, Africa, Europe, and India. The investment takes advantage of Egypt’s resources, strategic location, and qualified workforce, positioning it as a global production and export hub.

records.title: The Tunisian Assembly of People's Representatives (ARP) has approved a credit agreement between Tunisia and the Arab Fund for Economic an...
records.description: The Tunisian Assembly of People's Representatives (ARP) has approved a credit agreement between Tunisia and the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development (AFESD), valued at 10 million Kuwaiti dinars (TND 100 million). Signed on May 22, 2024, the agreement supports an integrated agricultural development project in the Oued Tassa basin, Kef governorate. The project focuses on erosion control, flood protection, forest development, agricultural water management, and income-generating agricultural ventures, particularly for small-scale and sustainable projects.

records.title: Iraq has amended loan agreements with the German Development Bank (KfW) to extend financing for key developmental projects.
records.description: Iraq has amended loan agreements with the German Development Bank (KfW) to extend financing for key developmental projects. The amendments will extend the disbursement period for loans supporting the rehabilitation of electricity infrastructure in liberated areas and infrastructure for roads, bridges, water, and sewage systems. The total funding includes €140 million for electricity infrastructure, extended until January 15, 2027, and €90 million for other infrastructural developments, extended until December 31, 2026.
records.institution: Iraqi Government and German Development Bank (KfW)

records.title: Iraq has inaugurated a joint management program for modern hospitals in collaboration with Italy's Gruppo Ospedaliero San Donato.
records.description: Iraq has inaugurated a joint management program for modern hospitals in collaboration with Italy's Gruppo Ospedaliero San Donato. The program, starting at Najaf Ashraf Educational Hospital, is intended to reduce medical treatment abroad by enhancing local facilities. It will be implemented across six provinces: Najaf, Basra, Maysan, Dhi Qar, Karbala, and Babil.
records.institution: Iraqi Government and Gruppo Ospedaliero San Donato (San Donato Hospital Group)

Funded by the Italian government through the Italian Agency for Development and Cooperation (AICS), the project will focus on enhancing the value chain of agricultural products and food commodities, benefiting 200 families in the provinces of Balqa, Jerash, and Ajloun. The initiative also aims to empower the agricultural sector through guidance, water harvesting, and the adoption of modern technologies.

records.title: First Milling Co.
records.description: First Milling Co. (First Mills) reported a significant increase in earnings for the second quarter of 2024, with a 30.4% year-on-year rise, totaling SAR 45.51 million. This boost in earnings was primarily fueled by a 13.3% increase in revenue across all product categories, with particularly strong sales growth in the feed segment and small-package products. The company also noted an improvement in net profit margins from 15.1% in Q2 2023 to 18.8% in Q2 2024. Despite this growth, earnings saw a quarterly decline due to seasonal consumption patterns post-Ramadan. Additionally, First Mills is expanding its production capacity, including a recent upgrade at its Jeddah plant, which has already contributed to revenue growth. The company anticipates continued robust performance in the upcoming quarters as it expands into new high-margin segments.

First Mills is optimistic about future growth, especially with ongoing expansions that are expected to further increase production capacity and diversify product offerings into high-margin segments.

records.description: An international workshop titled "Maritime Trade: Opportunities and Challenges" was inaugurated by the Minister of Economy and Trade in Tripoli. Organized under the ministry's auspices and by the Libyan Trade Network along with the Arab Academy for Science, Technology, and Maritime Transport, the event aims to highlight and address the pivotal role of maritime trade in the global economy. The workshop features presentations from local and international experts, including specialists from Libya, Egypt, Belgium, Denmark, Spain, and Singapore. Discussions will focus on enhancing international cooperation in the transport sector and diversifying national economies, with a particular emphasis on the critical nature of maritime trade, through which 80% of global goods and 90% of Africa's imports and exports are transported.

records.description: Libya and Algeria have agreed to enhance cooperation in the energy sector, with the National Oil Corporation (NOC) of Libya signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Algeria's Sonatrach Company. This collaboration focuses on providing drilling and well intervention equipment, alongside maintenance and training services. The agreement builds upon previous protocols and includes new areas of cooperation such as exploration, development of oil and gas resources, renewable energy projects, and oil services.

records.title: More than 2,500 cows have died in Misrata since last year due to an outbreak of lumpy skin disease, prompting concerns about the city’s c...
records.description: More than 2,500 cows have died in Misrata since last year due to an outbreak of lumpy skin disease, prompting concerns about the city’s classification as an epidemic area. Despite repeated requests, vaccination supplies from the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Health in Tripoli have not been forthcoming. The disease, primarily linked to the unavailability of vaccinations for a decade and the illegal importation of cattle from Sudan, has severely impacted milk production, which has plummeted from 70,000 liters per day to less than 20,000. This significant reduction threatens the economic viability of local dairy-dependent projects and could worsen with the onset of colder temperatures, which facilitate the disease's spread.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Health

records.title: The Libyan Minister of Economy and Trade, inaugurated the international workshop "Maritime Trade: Opportunities and Challenges" in Tripol...
records.description: The Libyan Minister of Economy and Trade, inaugurated the international workshop "Maritime Trade: Opportunities and Challenges" in Tripoli, organized by the Libyan Trade Network and the Arab Academy for Science, Technology, and Maritime Transport. The event focuses on the pivotal role of maritime trade, which accounts for 80% of global goods trade, with Africa's imports and exports making up 90% of this via sea routes. Over the next two days, the workshop will feature panels with specialists and academics from Libya, Egypt, Belgium, Denmark, Spain, and Singapore, discussing ways to develop maritime trade, enhance international cooperation, and diversify the national economy.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Morocco is grappling with a severe wheat harvest shortfall this year, with an estimated production of 3.1 billion kilograms, a sharp 44%...
records.description: Morocco is grappling with a severe wheat harvest shortfall this year, with an estimated production of 3.1 billion kilograms, a sharp 44% decline from the previous year’s 5.5 billion kilograms, due to prolonged drought and climate change impacts. This drastic reduction in yield is forcing the Moroccan government to increase grain imports and subsidize staple food prices to prevent market spikes that would affect consumers nationwide. The drought, which has persisted for six years, is causing significant agricultural disruption, compelling many farmers to abandon their fields and others to face reduced productivity. The nation, heavily reliant on cereal crops, is facing acute challenges in managing water resources, with restrictions placed on both urban and rural water use. Despite spring rains providing some relief, the overall outlook remains bleak, pushing Morocco to become the world’s sixth-largest wheat importer as it struggles to maintain food security amidst shrinking global wheat supplies.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: Morocco is grappling with its sixth consecutive year of severe drought, placing substantial stress on its agricultural and livestock sect...
records.description: Morocco is grappling with its sixth consecutive year of severe drought, placing substantial stress on its agricultural and livestock sectors. The drought has led to a significant 44% reduction in cereal harvests, compelling farmers to modify their agricultural practices to cope with the ongoing water scarcity. Farmers, like an olive and cereal producer in the narrative, have shifted from high water-demand crops like watermelons and melons to less thirsty ones such as potatoes. However, challenges persist, such as depleted wells and failed new boreholes. In the Drâa-Tafilalet region, one of the hardest hit, the introduction of drought-resistant crops like quinoa, moringa, cactus, and pistachio is part of a broader initiative to enhance agricultural resilience. Meanwhile, livestock farmers are also adapting, substituting traditional feed with alternative sources like crushed date waste due to fodder shortages, though this change impacts productivity and leads to herd reduction.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is intensifying its efforts to conserve its mangrove forests, essential for environmental and economic stability.
records.description: Saudi Arabia is intensifying its efforts to conserve its mangrove forests, essential for environmental and economic stability. The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, alongside the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification, is spearheading several initiatives to enhance the growth and protection of these vital ecosystems. Key actions include extensive mangrove planting along the Red Sea and Arabian Gulf coasts, aligning with the Saudi Green Initiative. Moreover, the center is undertaking research to overcome the challenges of mangrove restoration in severe environments and has committed to planting 13 million mangrove trees by 2030. Additionally, community engagement and education are pivotal components of their strategy, aiming to enhance local understanding and involvement in mangrove conservation.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The UAE and Chile have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to significantly enhance their bilateral relations, p...
records.description: The UAE and Chile have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to significantly enhance their bilateral relations, particularly in non-oil trade, which stood at $306 million in 2023. Both nations aim to triple this figure by 2030. This agreement, signed during Chilean President Gabriel Boric Font's historic first visit to the UAE, seeks to eliminate or reduce customs duties, streamline customs procedures, and remove trade barriers, thus fostering increased investment flows and private sector partnerships.

records.title: Ghardaïa, a region in Algeria, achieved an outstanding cereal harvest this year, producing a total of 55,231 quintals of various cereal t...
records.description: Ghardaïa, a region in Algeria, achieved an outstanding cereal harvest this year, producing a total of 55,231 quintals of various cereal types. This significant increase in production was realized over an area of 1,426 hectares, primarily under pivot irrigation systems. The harvest included 53,990 quintals of durum wheat and 1,241 quintals of soft wheat, as reported by the local directorate of agricultural services. Despite challenging weather conditions such as winds, sandstorms, and drought, the region managed an average yield of 40 quintals per hectare. This year's success is part of a broader effort to expand cereal farming in the region, with plans to increase the cultivated area to 3,000 hectares next season.

records.title: Jordan has witnessed a significant 25.3 percent growth in agricultural exports from January through May, pushing agricultural revenues to...
records.description: Jordan has witnessed a significant 25.3 percent growth in agricultural exports from January through May, pushing agricultural revenues to 500 million Jordanian dinars ($705 million). This increase is largely attributed to fruit and vegetable exports, which surged to 178,000 tons, marking a 32 percent rise over the same period last year. The growth in exports is underpinned by government initiatives that have introduced advanced irrigation and modern farming techniques, enhancing productivity despite the country’s heavy reliance on food imports, which account for nearly 98 percent of its food consumption.

records.title: In Berkane, Morocco, the Minister of Agriculture initiated several agricultural and rural development projects as part of the Throne Day...
records.description: In Berkane, Morocco, the Minister of Agriculture initiated several agricultural and rural development projects as part of the Throne Day celebrations. These projects are part of the Regional Agricultural Plan under the Génération Green strategy and aim to diversify agricultural production and enhance self-employment. Key initiatives include planting fruit trees, distributing beehives, and providing livestock to farmers, alongside infrastructural improvements such as developing roads and water points. These efforts are designed to improve local agriculture, enhance market access, and support the community's economic and living standards, reflecting a broader commitment to sustainable development and food sovereignty in the region.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: In Es-Semara, Morocco, a series of development projects were initiated to enhance the infrastructure and community facilities in celebrat...
records.description: In Es-Semara, Morocco, a series of development projects were initiated to enhance the infrastructure and community facilities in celebration of the 25th anniversary of Throne Day. These projects include the construction of a ring road, improvements to the city's northern entrance, enhancements to the industrial zone, and the development of a new area for festivals. Additionally, a modern livestock market is near completion, aimed at boosting the local red meat sector. Educational developments are also a priority, with the expansion of the multidisciplinary faculty and new facilities at several high schools, alongside a resource center for preschool education, all intended to improve local educational offerings and infrastructure.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has introduced the Seasonal Markets System, a significant upgrade to the trading infrastructure for dates.
records.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced the Seasonal Markets System, a significant upgrade to the trading infrastructure for dates. Initiated by the National Center for Palms and Dates in cooperation with the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, this mandatory electronic platform is designed to regulate and enhance date trading in seasonal markets across the kingdom. By requiring registration for sellers, buyers, and marketers, the system aims to streamline sales, ensure financial security, and provide access to market data and marketing services. It's a strategic move to boost the sustainability and global competitiveness of Saudi Arabia's prominent date sector, which is a key economic contributor with over 36 million palm trees producing more than 1.6 million tons of dates annually.
records.institution: The National Center for Palms and Dates

records.description: The farms of Qatif Oasis play a crucial role in supplying a wide variety of seasonal produce throughout Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. Stretching across 800 square kilometers from Safwa to Dammam, this region is home to over 3,700 farms, of which 2,454 are active and produce crops including vegetables, fruits, and fresh dates. Notably, these farms contribute significantly to the local economy, annually providing 29.5 tonnes of dates from over 540,000 fruit-bearing palm trees.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The UAE's renewable energy firm, Masdar, has broadened its footprint in the European green energy landscape with a substantial $887 milli...
records.description: The UAE's renewable energy firm, Masdar, has broadened its footprint in the European green energy landscape with a substantial $887 million investment in Spain. This investment secures a 49.99 percent stake in 48 solar plants, managed by Endesa, an Enel subsidiary. This move not only underscores Masdar's commitment to fostering the energy transition in Spain and Europe but also marks a strategic expansion into renewable energy markets across the continent. This agreement paves the way for future collaborations, including a memorandum of understanding with Endesa to explore the development of an additional 3 gigawatts of solar capacity. As European utilities navigate the high-interest rate environment by divesting minority stakes in renewable assets.

records.title: A Mauritanian business delegation is currently visiting Algeria to explore cooperation opportunities in the agricultural sector.
records.description: A Mauritanian business delegation is currently visiting Algeria to explore cooperation opportunities in the agricultural sector. This initiative, led by the Confederation of Algerian Industrialists and Producers (CIPA), aims to facilitate the export of Algerian-manufactured agricultural equipment to Mauritania. The delegation, which includes representatives from various public and private companies, is particularly interested in Algerian products for use in dairies, industrial slaughterhouses, and animal parks. They are also looking to collaborate on packaging, animal feed production, dietary supplements, and veterinary medicines.

records.description: The Governor of the Central Bank of Libya, along with his deputy, has approved eight new initiatives to enhance financial inclusion during an expanded meeting in London. Held at the headquarters of the Arab Banking Corporation, the meeting highlighted the Central Bank's strategy for advancing financial inclusion, particularly through accelerating electronic payment systems in partnership with Oliver Wyman. The initiatives focus on leveraging financial technology and digital transformation to broaden financial services across society, encompassing instant payments, open banking, and the development of the national distributor, along with establishing regulatory controls based on best practices.

This festival has become a critical platform for farmers to access the latest in agricultural technologies, sustainable practices, and organic products aimed at enhancing palm cultivation and date production. Participants include companies specializing in organic farming and agricultural machinery, presenting alternatives to chemical inputs and showcasing cutting-edge equipment designed to boost farm productivity while preserving environmental health.

records.title: Egypt is gearing up to enhance its wheat storage capabilities by establishing a local company focused on manufacturing grain silos, accor...
records.description: Egypt is gearing up to enhance its wheat storage capabilities by establishing a local company focused on manufacturing grain silos, according to Sherif Farouk, the Minister of Supply and Internal Trade. This move is part of a broader government initiative to increase the national storage capacity from 3.4 million tonnes to 5 million tonnes. The plan includes constructing new silos and upgrading existing facilities, which will be integrated with the national railway network and the Nile transportation routes to streamline wheat logistics. This strategy is aimed at reducing Egypt's reliance on imported storage solutions and foreign currency expenditures. Currently, Egypt's Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade manages 83 silos, some located strategically at seaports, developed in collaboration with international firms.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Tunisia's cereal production has seen a notable increase of 25% in the marketing year (MY) 2023/24, reaching 660,000 tonnes, up from 530,0...
records.description: Tunisia's cereal production has seen a notable increase of 25% in the marketing year (MY) 2023/24, reaching 660,000 tonnes, up from 530,000 tonnes in the previous year. This rise comes despite the country grappling with a persistent drought over the past five years. Durum wheat is the predominant crop, making up 88% of the harvest with 578,000 tonnes produced. Other cereals such as barley, soft wheat, and triticale also contributed to the total output. Regionally, Beja led with 27% of the total production, followed by Bizerte and Jendouba. While the increase is significant, it still falls short of the five-year average of 1.6 million tonnes, and domestic production satisfies less than 20% of Tunisia's annual cereal demand, which nearly reaches 4 million tonnes. Despite favorable winter rainfall and moderate temperatures boosting the outlook for the 2024-25 season, Tunisia remains heavily reliant on wheat imports to meet its national demand.

records.title: Egypt has announced a significant increase in fuel prices by up to 15%, as part of a broader strategy to phase out subsidies by December...
records.description: Egypt has announced a significant increase in fuel prices by up to 15%, as part of a broader strategy to phase out subsidies by December 2025. This move is aligned with the conditions of an International Monetary Fund (IMF)-backed economic reform program that began in 2022. The latest fuel price adjustments are part of Egypt's commitments under an IMF loan program, which necessitated the lifting of subsidies on food and fuel. Despite these changes being crucial for securing further IMF funding, they have intensified public dissatisfaction, especially in light of ongoing power cuts across the country. These disruptions, attributed to high consumption and technical issues, continue despite promises from the government to halt them until September.

records.title: The United Nations in Iraq, in collaboration with the Iraqi Ministry of Water Resources, has launched a significant campaign called "Wate...
records.description: The United Nations in Iraq, in collaboration with the Iraqi Ministry of Water Resources, has launched a significant campaign called "Water is Life - Every Drop Counts" to tackle the severe water crisis in Iraq. This year-long awareness initiative seeks to educate Iraqi citizens about the critical condition of their water resources and encourage actions to preserve and efficiently use water. The campaign was inaugurated with an event that included detailed presentations and discussions, highlighting the need for updated water management strategies and the adoption of modern irrigation technologies. Key phases of the campaign will focus on raising awareness, enhancing accountability and collaboration among stakeholders, showcasing successful initiatives, and planning future strategies to manage water resources effectively.
records.institution: Iraqi Ministry of Water Resources & United Nations
