records.description: In Rabat, the Minister of Agriculture presided over the Ordinary General Assembly of the National Association of Sheep and Goat Breeders, which focused on evaluating the association's moral, technical, and financial activities. The session underscored the livestock sector's significant contribution to Morocco's food security and rural employment, highlighting the extensive national livestock numbers and substantial red meat production. The meeting addressed various crucial initiatives, such as genetic improvement programs, livestock identification for religious festivals, and the establishment of temporary regional markets. Additionally, the assembly reviewed extensive governmental support for farmers amid challenging climatic conditions, including subsidized feed and the development of water resources, aimed at enhancing the resilience and productivity of the sector. The assembly concluded with recognition of the association's pivotal role in advancing the sector, integral to the Generation Green strategy, and an acknowledgment of the stakeholders' dedication to the agricultural community.
records.institution: The Association Nationale Ovine et Caprine (ANOC)

records.title: Morocco has implemented new regulations for importing animal meal used in pet food production, marking the first establishment of such gu...
records.description: Morocco has implemented new regulations for importing animal meal used in pet food production, marking the first establishment of such guidelines in the country. These regulations are detailed in a USDA GAINS report, which notes that the rules will facilitate the use of these byproducts in other types of animal feeds as well. The National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA) will conduct thorough reviews of the exporting country's health standards and production conditions before permitting imports. Companies must comply with stringent health control plans and traceability procedures based on risk analysis and the HACCP method. Non-compliance could lead to revocation of the company's operational authorization. These changes come as economic factors influence Moroccan consumers' buying habits, leading to an increased preference for homemade pet foods over commercial options.

records.title: Morocco has introduced new regulations for importing animal meal used in pet food production, a first for the country.
records.description: Morocco has introduced new regulations for importing animal meal used in pet food production, a first for the country. These regulations, outlined by the National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA), include a review process by a technical committee to assess the country of origin and ensure compliance with production and certification conditions. Importers must obtain authorization and provide a health certificate, create a health control plan using the HACCP method, and establish a traceability procedure for the imported rendered products. Non-compliance can lead to the revocation of authorization.
records.institution: The National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA)

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Aquaponics, an innovative farming method that merges aquaculture with hydroponics, is making strides in sustainable agriculture in Oman.
records.description: Aquaponics, an innovative farming method that merges aquaculture with hydroponics, is making strides in sustainable agriculture in Oman. This method cultivates fish and plants together in a closed-loop system that recycles water. Fish waste provides a nutrient-rich source for the plants, while the plants clean the water, which is then recirculated back to the fish tanks. Highly efficient and conserving up to 90% more water than traditional farming, aquaponics supports year-round food production without the need for soil or chemical fertilizers.

records.title: At a global summit in Rome, Saudi Arabia showcased its environmental initiatives, particularly in combating land degradation.
records.description: At a global summit in Rome, Saudi Arabia showcased its environmental initiatives, particularly in combating land degradation. The presentation was led by the CEO of the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification. The delegation highlighted Saudi Arabia's readiness to host the upcoming 16th Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification and Land Degradation in Riyadh. The efforts discussed included the restoration of ecosystems and the launch of forest and dryland initiatives.

records.title: Egyptian Alexandria Flour Mills has reported a significant 34.3% year-on-year increase in net profits for the fiscal year 2023/2024.
records.description: Egyptian Alexandria Flour Mills has reported a significant 34.3% year-on-year increase in net profits for the fiscal year 2023/2024. The company's after-tax profits surged to EGP 55.797 million, up from EGP 41.545 million in the previous fiscal year. This growth is attributed to robust operational efficiency and strategic market positioning despite challenging economic conditions. Additionally, the company's sales increased substantially, reaching EGP 304.804 million compared to EGP 257.235 million in the previous year.

records.title: Iraq has resumed rice cultivation after a two-year suspension due to severe water shortages, dedicating 150 square kilometers to rice fie...
records.description: Iraq has resumed rice cultivation after a two-year suspension due to severe water shortages, dedicating 150 square kilometers to rice fields this season with an anticipated yield of 150,000 tons. The restart was made possible by substantial winter rainfall and expected increased water flows from Turkiye. Previously, rice cultivation was restricted to small areas for seed extraction due to upstream dams and climate challenges affecting water availability. Despite restarting local cultivation, Iraq anticipates importing about 1.25 million tons of rice to meet national demand. Alongside traditional rice varieties, Iraqi scientists have introduced a new hybrid strain, Ghiri, designed for water efficiency and adaptability to local conditions. This strain supports fixed sprayer irrigation rather than traditional flooding, aligning with efforts to modernize agricultural practices and conserve water resources.

records.title: In Morocco, the Minister of Agriculture announced the extension of the National Water Saving Program in irrigation, aiming to expand it t...
records.description: In Morocco, the Minister of Agriculture announced the extension of the National Water Saving Program in irrigation, aiming to expand it to cover one million hectares by 2030. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to enhance water efficiency and support sustainable irrigated agriculture. Key efforts include the continuation of irrigation extension downstream of dams and the rehabilitation of small to medium-sized hydraulic perimeters. The ministry also plans to increase water supply through the construction of additional dams and the creation of seawater desalination plants for irrigation purposes..
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: In North Sharqiyah, Oman, a significant agricultural expansion has contributed to the region's food security and economic growth, with th...
records.description: In North Sharqiyah, Oman, a significant agricultural expansion has contributed to the region's food security and economic growth, with the area now producing 250,000 tonnes of various crops annually. This development was highlighted by Dr. Abdul Aziz bin Ali al Mashaikhi, Director General of Agriculture and Water Resources in North Sharqiyah. The region has seen a notable increase in fruit crop areas by 2.3%, totaling nearly 285 hectares, and a 1.3% increase in date palm cultivation, covering over 3,000 hectares and producing 54,188 tonnes of dates. North Sharqiyah, ranking fourth in date production nationally, offers substantial investment opportunities aimed at employing modern agricultural technologies, including greenhouses.
records.institution: Agriculture and Water Resources in North Sharqiyah

records.title: During a visit to Brazil, a senior Saudi minister engaged with major Brazilian companies to advance food production localization and avia...
records.description: During a visit to Brazil, a senior Saudi minister engaged with major Brazilian companies to advance food production localization and aviation cooperation. Discussions with executives from Minerva Foods and JBS focused on bringing food production expertise and technology to Saudi Arabia, aiming to enhance the Kingdom's production capabilities. Additionally, meetings with Embraer explored possibilities for advancing the aviation industry within Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, Minerva Foods, & JBS

records.title: In Tunisia, the prickly pear industry, a vital component of the national agriculture sector, is facing a severe threat from the prickly p...
records.description: In Tunisia, the prickly pear industry, a vital component of the national agriculture sector, is facing a severe threat from the prickly pear cochineal insect. This pest, which has devastated vast areas of plantations since its detection in 2021, saps the life from cactus plants, causing them to yellow and die. The economic implications are significant, impacting not just the farmers who cultivate these cacti but also the broader agricultural economy of Tunisia. The country, where prickly pears are second only to olive trees in agricultural prevalence, relies heavily on this fruit for income, especially in rural areas where thousands of women are employed in its harvesting and sale. The infestation has prompted a multifaceted response, including government and international efforts to implement biological control strategies and improve agricultural practices to manage and hopefully overcome this invasive pest.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has launched a new agriculture and food security data platform to support de...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has launched a new agriculture and food security data platform to support decision-making and enhance food security management in Abu Dhabi. This comprehensive platform provides detailed insights across all aspects of the agriculture and food sectors, from production to consumption. It facilitates informed policymaking by analyzing current data to improve the efficiency of food security strategies and develop a sustainable and resilient food system for the emirate. The platform integrates data from 16 strategic partners and covers over 335 indicators, enabling proactive management of food emergencies, diseases, and pests, thereby minimizing supply chain disruptions. Additionally, it includes a sophisticated warning system to handle various risks and threats.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The United Arab Emirates and Morocco have completed negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), poised to enh...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates and Morocco have completed negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), poised to enhance trade and investment relationships between the two countries. This agreement aims to streamline the flow of goods and services by lowering or abolishing tariffs, simplifying trade barriers, and ensuring more accessible market access. It encompasses cooperation across various sectors, including renewable energy, tourism, and infrastructure, reflecting a shared vision for economic growth and expanded private sector engagement.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of State for Foreign Trade

records.title: The Egyptian Countryside Development Company (ECDC) has joined forces with Nile Sugar Company to develop 14,000 feddans in the West El Mi...
records.description: The Egyptian Countryside Development Company (ECDC) has joined forces with Nile Sugar Company to develop 14,000 feddans in the West El Minya area for sugar beet cultivation. This agreement is part of Egypt’s larger 1.5 million-feddan project, which aims to boost national agricultural output. Under the partnership, Nile Crops will manage large-scale sugar beet production intended for white sugar and other crops, contributing to Egypt’s goal of self-sufficiency in sugar. This project plans to establish agricultural processing facilities to bolster the local economy. The project also focuses on sugar beet due to its water conservation properties, crucial in areas reliant on groundwater.
records.institution: Egyptian Countryside Development Company (ECDC) & Nile Sugar Company

records.title: Libya, Algeria, and Tunisia are actively working to enhance their economic ties through the Carthage Pathway initiative, aiming to establ...
records.description: Libya, Algeria, and Tunisia are actively working to enhance their economic ties through the Carthage Pathway initiative, aiming to establish free trade zones and foster economic integration. This initiative was reinforced during a recent meeting in Algeria, where business leaders discussed expediting the establishment of mechanisms that facilitate the easy movement of goods and develop border regions. Key proposals include the protection of trademarks and product origins, leveraging existing logistics infrastructures, and creating efficient land, sea, and air connections to boost trade. A unified approach is being urged to remove financial and practical barriers, encouraging joint investments, and establishing a shared economic information database.
records.institution: The Algerian Council for Economic Renewal,The General Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture in Libya, & The Tunisian Union of Industry, Trade and Handicrafts

records.title: In Morocco, an investment totaling 28 billion dirhams has been channeled into the water sector since the inception of the "Green Generati...
records.description: In Morocco, an investment totaling 28 billion dirhams has been channeled into the water sector since the inception of the "Green Generation" strategy. The Minister of Agriculture detailed that 8 billion dirhams of this investment were directed towards localized and complementary irrigation projects, and the remaining 20 billion towards the expansion and modernization of irrigation networks, along with seawater desalination initiatives. These projects are part of broader efforts to enhance water efficiency and advance sustainable agricultural practices under the Generation Green strategy. The initiatives aim to develop water resource supplies through significant projects focusing on water transfer and the interconnection of hydraulic basins, thus preparing the agricultural sector to manage a strategic water reserve estimated at 3 billion cubic meters.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: Morocco is experiencing a severe wheat harvest crisis this year, with drastic reductions in crop yields due to ongoing drought and the br...
records.description: Morocco is experiencing a severe wheat harvest crisis this year, with drastic reductions in crop yields due to ongoing drought and the broader impacts of climate change. The crisis has led to a significant decrease in wheat production, with estimates suggesting a harvest of only 31.2 million quintals, marking a 43% drop from the previous year. This stark decline has forced some regions to completely abandon wheat cultivation. The reduction in arable land for cereals—from 3.67 million hectares to just 2.47 million—compounds the issue, necessitating increased imports to meet domestic demand. Morocco, already one of the world's top wheat importers, is expected to see a 19% increase in wheat imports, reaching 7.5 million tons in 2024. The country's reliance on international markets for cereal, particularly from suppliers like France, Germany, Russia, and Ukraine, is set to intensify. Farmers are contending with delayed and insufficient rainfall, temperature extremes, and frequent hailstorms, disruptions that pose significant challenges to traditional farming practices and threaten the agricultural sector's sustainability.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: First Milling Company ("First Mills"), a leading Saudi milling enterprise, has reported robust financial results for the first half (H1)...
records.description: First Milling Company ("First Mills"), a leading Saudi milling enterprise, has reported robust financial results for the first half (H1) and second quarter (Q2) of 2024. The company saw a 10.5% year-on-year increase in H1 revenue, reaching SAR 518.8 million, fueled by a 31.1% increase in Feed sales due to favorable market conditions and product diversification. Despite a decrease in Bran sales, Flour sales rose by 7.3% driven by popular retail products. The company also enjoyed a 13.4% increase in net profit for H1, totaling SAR 123.2 million, with a notable net margin of 23.8%. This financial success was supported by capacity upgrades at its Jeddah plant and effective cost management, leading to broad-based growth across all product categories in Q2, culminating in a 13.3% increase in revenue for the quarter.

records.title: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Youcef Cherfa, announced plans to initiate agricultural micro-enterprises acr...
records.description: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Youcef Cherfa, announced plans to initiate agricultural micro-enterprises across several regions, including the North, the High Plateaus, and the Green Dam. This initiative, aligned with directives from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, aims to enhance job creation, wealth, and national food security. Set to kick off with a national meeting in October, the program will gather young academics and project leaders to discuss infrastructure needs and the integration of innovative agricultural practices. Special emphasis will be placed on modern irrigation and monitoring technologies, in collaboration with startups.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: Iraq has reached a significant agricultural milestone by purchasing a record 6.302 million tons of local wheat, the highest amount ever r...
records.description: Iraq has reached a significant agricultural milestone by purchasing a record 6.302 million tons of local wheat, the highest amount ever recorded for the country. This achievement marks a major step in enhancing national food security and self-sufficiency, as announced by the Iraqi Ministry of Trade. The wheat, acquired during the current harvest season beginning in April, reflects the success of government policies aimed at boosting local production and reducing dependence on imports. In support of these goals, the Ministry of Commerce has also initiated the construction of new grain storage facilities, including four silos and 17 underground bunkers across six governorates, to accommodate the expected increase in wheat production driven by favorable weather conditions and improved irrigation techniques.

records.description: Azura, a leading Moroccan cherry tomato supplier, has publicly denounced what it views as an unfair and misleading campaign by French producers against its products. The campaign highlights concerns from French producers about Moroccan tomatoes being priced too competitively, which they argue undermines local European markets. Azura's Deputy General Manager defended the company’s practices at a press briefing in Paris, asserting their compliance with regulatory standards and expressing dismay over the targeted attacks on their products, especially in France.

records.title: In Fez, the importance of strengthening Morocco's food sovereignty was emphasized, focusing on the challenges posed by the Covid-19 pande...
records.description: In Fez, the importance of strengthening Morocco's food sovereignty was emphasized, focusing on the challenges posed by the Covid-19 pandemic and the government's response to ensure food security. Discussions covered initiatives to boost investment in agriculture and rural development, which are crucial for economic recovery post-pandemic. Additionally, efforts to combat inflation, particularly for basic food items, were highlighted to protect citizens' purchasing power. The seminar also addressed the need to adapt agricultural practices to the realities of climate change, reinforcing the commitment to strategic goals despite new challenges. Furthermore, the crucial role of higher education in national development and policy-making was discussed, advocating for greater involvement of university professors in these processes.

records.title: In June 2023, Morocco emerged as the third largest exporter of fertilizers to Brazil, with exports increasing 2.3 times from the previous...
records.description: In June 2023, Morocco emerged as the third largest exporter of fertilizers to Brazil, with exports increasing 2.3 times from the previous year to reach $147 million. This surge is largely due to Morocco's extensive phosphate reserves, which make up over 70% of the world's total and are essential for producing phosphorus fertilizers. Russia and Canada maintained the first and second spots, respectively, in fertilizer exports to Brazil. Morocco's strategic use of its phosphate resources has bolstered its position as a key player in the global fertilizer market, contributing significantly to agricultural sustainability worldwide.

records.title: In Meknes, development projects were initiated as part of the "Green Generation" strategy, involving investments totaling over 51 million...
records.description: In Meknes, development projects were initiated as part of the "Green Generation" strategy, involving investments totaling over 51 million dirhams. Among these projects, a 23 million dirham initiative funded by the Islamic Development Bank aims to construct an olive crushing unit on a 2,120 square meter site, enhancing olive oil production quality and reducing costs. This project is expected to boost local olive oil production, increase the income of over 160 farmers, and create job opportunities in the region. Additionally, a food technology hall was inaugurated at the Qualipole food center, covering a 7,200 square meter area with a built space of 765 square meters, at a cost of 28.20 million dirhams. This hall will support agri-food companies, including start-ups, by fostering innovation and knowledge transfer in food technology, thereby enhancing the competitiveness of Moroccan agri-food products nationally and internationally.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: The Moroccan coastal and artisanal fishing sectors have observed a significant downturn, according to the latest figures from the Nationa...
records.description: The Moroccan coastal and artisanal fishing sectors have observed a significant downturn, according to the latest figures from the National Fisheries Office (ONP). The total value of marketed fishery products has dropped by 4%, while the volume of catches has declined by 10% to 469,715 tons. Notably, shellfish landings plummeted by 82%, amounting to only 24 tons. Similarly, decreases were seen in other categories such as seaweed, crustaceans, and pelagic fish. In contrast, some species like white fish and cephalopods experienced increases in their landings. The Mediterranean ports were particularly affected, with a 20% reduction in landings, whereas the Atlantic ports saw a 10% decrease in tonnage and a 4% fall in value. Despite a brief period of value increase in March 2024, the overall trend points towards a challenging period for this traditional sector that plays a crucial role in the local economies along Morocco’s coasts.

records.title: In Dhofar, Oman, efforts to combat invasive plant species, particularly the Parthenium weed, have intensified with the distribution of ov...
records.description: In Dhofar, Oman, efforts to combat invasive plant species, particularly the Parthenium weed, have intensified with the distribution of over 40 billion local grass seeds by the Dhofar Municipality. Parthenium has significantly impacted the region's plains and agricultural fields by releasing chemicals that inhibit the growth of other plants and cause allergies in humans and livestock. The initiative, which includes the distribution of 68 varieties of wild plant seeds, aims to restore the local ecosystem, enhance biodiversity, and strengthen agricultural productivity.

records.title: In Baha, Saudi Arabia, a farmer has transformed earthworms, traditionally considered a garden nuisance, into a valuable resource for orga...
records.description: In Baha, Saudi Arabia, a farmer has transformed earthworms, traditionally considered a garden nuisance, into a valuable resource for organic farming. The farmer has set up a vermicomposting operation, using worms to convert organic waste into high-quality fertilizer. This initiative began with a modest setup and has expanded significantly due to its success. The organic fertilizer produced through this method has proven to enhance plant growth, fruit production, and soil health, demonstrating a sustainable alternative to chemical fertilizers.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is set to enhance its bilateral relations with Brazil and Chile, focusing on attracting investments in the mineral and indus...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is set to enhance its bilateral relations with Brazil and Chile, focusing on attracting investments in the mineral and industrial sectors. The delegation, led by the Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources, will visit major cities in both countries from July 22-30, engaging in high-level discussions with senior officials and leading global companies involved in mining, aviation, food processing, and other industries. The visit includes meetings with significant entities in Brazil such as the Brazilian Mining Association and Vale, and in Chile with the Minister of Mining and major industry leaders. These meetings are geared toward leveraging Brazil's diverse economy and Chile's status as a major lithium producer to foster cooperation in sectors crucial for the future, such as electric vehicle production and renewable energy. The visit is expected to conclude with the signing of important agreements that will further mutual growth in mining and industrial capacities.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources

records.title: The UAE and Mauritius have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), marking the UAE's first such agreement with an A...
records.description: The UAE and Mauritius have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), marking the UAE's first such agreement with an African nation. This agreement aims to bolster economic growth by removing most tariffs, enhancing trade and investment, and creating new job opportunities. From January to April 2024, non-oil trade between the two countries rose significantly, reflecting growing economic ties. This CEPA is expected to increase the UAE's GDP by 0.96% and Mauritius's economy by over 1% by 2030.

Discussions have highlighted areas such as livestock, poultry farming, and fish processing, with an emphasis on exchanging expertise and initiating projects to breed highly productive animals.

The delegation engaged in a series of meetings and factory visits across Tunis, Sousse, and Sfax to explore investment opportunities in sectors like textiles, automotive parts, food industries, tourism, logistics, and medical supplies. records.description: Egypt has seized an opportunity in the global markets by placing its largest wheat order since 2022, capitalizing on the recent decline in global wheat prices. The State Buyer of Grains (GASC) secured 770,000 tons of wheat through an international tender, with the majority sourced from Russian exporters and a smaller portion from Bulgaria. This move reflects a strategic adjustment to the country's agricultural policy, emphasizing the diversification of exports rather than increasing domestic wheat production. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has advocated for using agricultural land to cultivate export-oriented crops and using the revenue to import essential commodities like wheat. This procurement aligns with a broader global trend where falling wheat prices, driven by an anticipated increase in global supply, have encouraged other nations to boost their imports. With wheat prices dropping by 22% since late May, Egypt's strategy aims to strengthen its food security while adapting to changing economic conditions.

records.description: The Zubair Enterprises Development Centre (Zubair EDC) in Oman is spearheading a feasibility study on the use of Azolla as fish feed, in collaboration with Tuhlub and the Leaders Consultancies and Development Centre. This study aims to enhance the aqua feed industry and boost food security in Oman. Azolla, known for its rapid growth rate and nutritional properties, could offer a sustainable alternative to conventional feed.

records.title: Abu Dhabi's clean-energy company, Masdar, has successfully raised $1 billion through its second green bond issuance, which was highly ove...
records.description: Abu Dhabi's clean-energy company, Masdar, has successfully raised $1 billion through its second green bond issuance, which was highly oversubscribed with an orderbook that peaked at $4.6 billion. This issuance, split into two tranches with tenors of five and ten years, will support Masdar's investments in new greenfield projects, particularly in developing economies, aiming to expand its portfolio capacity to 100GW by 2030. The funds are part of a broader Green Finance Framework under which Masdar plans to raise up to $3 billion. This follows their inaugural green bond sale of $750 million in 2023. The proceeds are allocated primarily to international investors, with a significant portion also going to MENA region investors.

records.title: Coca-Cola HBC has successfully obtained a US$130 million loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to support...
records.description: Coca-Cola HBC has successfully obtained a US$130 million loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to support its sustainable business initiatives in Egypt. This loan is complemented by a US$750,000 grant from the Global Environment Facility (GEF), aimed at enhancing wastewater treatment and water management systems in the country. The funding will be directed towards various sustainable projects including energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy, sustainable packaging, and digital innovations, as well as training and development for employees.

records.title: Jordan is set to launch a significant climate change adaptation initiative with a total budget of US$60.5 million, supported by the Green...
records.description: Jordan is set to launch a significant climate change adaptation initiative with a total budget of US$60.5 million, supported by the Green Climate Fund and additional funding from the Jordanian government and NGOs. This initiative, the Jordan Integrated Landscape Management Initiative (JILMI), aims to mitigate the effects of climate change in one of the world's most water-scarce and drought-prone regions. Focused on the northern Jordan Valley, particularly the Yarmouk, Amman Zarqa, and Jordan Rift Valley Basins, the project plans to enhance water security and climate resilience for 750,000 residents. It will incorporate capacity building, climate-resilient agriculture, ecosystem restoration, and improved water management to boost local food security and governance. A unique feature of this project is the creation of a Water Fund, where downstream industrial water users will pay upstream communities for sustainable land management, improving the overall resilience and sustainability of water resources in Jordan.
records.institution: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) & United Nations Envrionment Programme (UNEP)

This meeting, chaired by the respective Ministers of Commerce and Industry from both countries, highlighted their mutual commitment to deepen bilateral relations. records.title: MVW Lechtenberg Projektentwicklungs- und Beteiligungsgesellschaft GmbH, a consultancy known for its focus on alternative fuels, has launc...
records.description: MVW Lechtenberg Projektentwicklungs- und Beteiligungsgesellschaft GmbH, a consultancy known for its focus on alternative fuels, has launched a significant plastic waste management project in Saudi Arabia. This venture is in partnership with Empower, which specializes in traceability solutions, and involves a joint venture with the Saudi Investment Recycling Company (SIRC), the government's key entity for waste management initiatives. The project aims to process around 3 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually across six governorates, converting it into refuse-derived fuels (RDF) and potentially reducing CO2 emissions by about 1,791,300 tonnes per year. A notable feature of this project is the use of blockchain technology by Empower to ensure a transparent and traceable waste management process from collection to RDF conversion. This will enable real-time monitoring and provide critical data to stakeholders. Additionally, the project will incorporate Plastic Credits, which are financial incentives for verified plastic waste recycling activities, helping to close the financial gaps in waste processing and make the initiative financially viable and attractive to investors.
records.institution: MVW Lechtenberg Projektentwicklungs- und Beteiligungsgesellschaft GmbH

records.title: Saudi Aramco's Wa’ed, established to support Saudi entrepreneurs and SMEs, aims to double its support to startups by 2023.
records.description: Saudi Aramco's Wa’ed, established to support Saudi entrepreneurs and SMEs, aims to double its support to startups by 2023. Since its inception in 2011, Wa’ed has backed around 90 companies with loans and investments, and it plans to increase this number through additional deals in 2021. Wa’ed is focused on high-impact business ideas and has a success rate of 83% among its supported companies.

records.title: The Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) has entered into an $8 million contract with the Saudi-based waste management company Reviva to establ...
records.description: The Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) has entered into an $8 million contract with the Saudi-based waste management company Reviva to establish a recycling waste complex in Jeddah. The project, which covers an area of 10,000 square meters, aims to enhance waste utilization by transforming it into valuable resources, thus promoting a circular economy within the kingdom. This initiative is part of Saudi Arabia's broader environmental sustainability efforts, aligning with the National Transport and Logistics Strategy and the Green Ports Initiative. It seeks to position Saudi Arabia as a global logistics hub and elevate Jeddah Islamic Port among the top ten ports worldwide. The collaboration between Mawani and Reviva is expected to advance the kingdom's waste management capabilities significantly, in line with Saudi Vision 2030 and boosting the private sector's role in economic growth.

records.title: During a high-level meeting in Abu Dhabi, leaders from the UAE and Indonesia reviewed their strategic relationship under the Comprehensiv...
records.description: During a high-level meeting in Abu Dhabi, leaders from the UAE and Indonesia reviewed their strategic relationship under the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), focusing on key areas like economy, investment, renewable energy, food security, infrastructure, education, health, climate action, and the environment. They discussed the growth in non-oil trade between the two nations, from $2.7 billion in 2014 to $4.4 billion in 2023, and the completion of projects worth over $21 billion in Indonesia last year. Several Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and agreements were announced, covering various sectors including solar energy, public budget management, smart systems, peaceful nuclear energy use, and real estate development.

records.title: Plenty, a U.S.
records.description: Plenty, a U.S. vertical farming startup, has teamed up with Mawarid, a subsidiary of Alpha Dhabi Holding, to launch a $680 million joint venture aimed at developing indoor farms across the Middle East. The venture plans to establish five farms over the next five years, starting with a facility in Abu Dhabi scheduled to begin construction next year. This farm is expected to produce over 4.5 million pounds of premium strawberries annually for local and Gulf Cooperation Council markets, beginning in 2026. The venture is financed through a combination of equity and debt, the latter provided by a regional bank.

records.title: Tadweer Group, a leader in waste management in the UAE, has introduced four new subsidiaries to innovate and enhance its recycling and wa...
records.description: Tadweer Group, a leader in waste management in the UAE, has introduced four new subsidiaries to innovate and enhance its recycling and waste management services. These subsidiaries—Tadweer Environmental Services and Solutions, Tajmee’e, UpCycle, and Tahweel—reflect the group's commitment to transforming waste into valuable resources, supporting decarbonization, and fostering a circular economy through advanced technologies. Tadweer Environmental Services and Solutions will handle public waste collection and management using digital tools, while Tajmee’e will focus on optimizing pre-collection and collection processes. UpCycle is set to advance technology integration at waste treatment and recycling centers, including a new Material Recovery Facility. Tahweel aims to expedite the development of waste conversion technologies, crucial for waste-to-energy and waste-to-value projects. These initiatives are part of Tadweer's strategic aim to divert 80% of waste from landfills by 2030 and leverage its expertise to boost sustainability efforts across Abu Dhabi and beyond. This strategic expansion follows Tadweer’s acquisition of e-waste leader Enviroserve and its recent progress on Abu Dhabi’s dedicated facility for material recovery from waste, marking significant advancements in regional waste management solutions.

records.title: The UAE has committed to investing Dh550 million over the next decade to construct up to 10 hospitals worldwide as part of its Global Hos...
records.description: The UAE has committed to investing Dh550 million over the next decade to construct up to 10 hospitals worldwide as part of its Global Hospitals Programme, starting with a medical center in Indonesia. This initiative, part of the Zayed Humanitarian Legacy Initiative, aims to promote global health equity and provide specialized medical care in underserved areas. Additional efforts include supporting health services in conflict zones and establishing facilities like a cardiovascular center in Cairo and field hospitals in Chad and Gaza.

records.title: In Egypt, the strawberry industry is witnessing a notable shift with frozen strawberries becoming more expensive than fresh ones, driven...
records.description: In Egypt, the strawberry industry is witnessing a notable shift with frozen strawberries becoming more expensive than fresh ones, driven by significant changes in agricultural and market dynamics. This season, adverse weather conditions have drastically reduced strawberry yields from 15-30 tonnes per feddan to 12-15 tonnes, leading to a shortage in supply while demand remains high. As a result, the price of frozen strawberries has surged by 30-40% compared to the previous season. The frozen strawberry market, which commands a robust international demand, especially from European countries and certain Arab nations, now dictates the strategic decisions of growers. They are increasingly planting freeze-resistant varieties and planning to expand their acreage by at least 30% next season, despite the lower profitability of fresh strawberries. This shift occurs amidst Egypt's broader economic challenges, including an energy crisis that has spiked production costs, although industrial zones where processing occurs are shielded from power cuts.

records.title: The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has unveiled a plan to significantly expand its national maritime fleet.
records.description: The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has unveiled a plan to significantly expand its national maritime fleet. This initiative includes the construction of eight new ships set for 2025 and the acquisition of additional ships through a Japanese loan, which will fund the building of five ships and the purchase of two more. The current fleet consists of six ships, including commercial vessels and tankers. Operations remain robust, with ongoing cargo transportation across the Middle East and Europe, and comprehensive maintenance ensuring the vessels meet international standards. Several ships have recently completed or are scheduled for maintenance in Dubai, further extending their operational lifespan by five years.

records.title: At the close of a challenging season for Moroccan watermelon growers, characterized by reduced volumes and quality issues, the local mark...
records.description: At the close of a challenging season for Moroccan watermelon growers, characterized by reduced volumes and quality issues, the local market has emerged as a bright spot. Despite difficulties in other regions, the Gharb and Loukkos areas along Morocco's Atlantic coast have reported better-than-expected outcomes, with no significant impacts from viruses or pests and good fruit sizes, some reaching up to 17 kg. While exports have largely stagnated, strong domestic demand has driven local prices higher than those for exports, with farm-gate prices reaching 4-4.5 MAD/kg, which is considered very satisfactory. Although the European market currently favors watermelons from Greece and Turkey, Moroccan exporters remain optimistic about a potential increase in demand later in the summer as those supplies diminish, potentially revitalizing exports in August.

records.title: Tunisia has inaugurated the Zarat Desalination Plant to address its critical water scarcity issues.
records.description: Tunisia has inaugurated the Zarat Desalination Plant to address its critical water scarcity issues. The facility, developed by the Indian company Va Tech Wabag, starts with the capacity to produce 50,000 cubic meters of drinking water per day, aiming to double this by 2027. This development is part of Tunisia's strategy to counteract the overexploitation of groundwater and depletion of surface water sources due to prolonged droughts. The plant, which cost $105 million, co-financed by the Tunisian government and the German development agency Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau (KfW), is set to provide water to approximately one million residents across several governorates by 2035.

records.title: During a state visit to the UAE, Indonesian President Joko Widodo and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed engaged in significant talks...
records.description: During a state visit to the UAE, Indonesian President Joko Widodo and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed engaged in significant talks, resulting in the signing of several agreements aimed at enhancing cooperation in areas such as the environment, tourism, and renewable energy. The meeting, a culmination of sustained efforts to deepen ties between the two nations, addressed expanding economic partnerships and joint initiatives in combating climate change and improving global education. The visit, marking the end of President Widodo's final term, also saw him receiving the Order of Zayed, the highest civilian honor in the UAE, recognizing his contributions to strengthening bilateral relations. Additional agreements included collaborations in solar energy, nuclear energy, public budget management, and smart banking systems, alongside plans for a new research center and real estate and tourism projects.

records.title: G.D.

Foods Manufacturing (India) served as the official condiment partner at the 4th edition of the India-GCC Buyers-Sellers Meet (BSM) on Food & Beverage in Dubai, offering a key platform for Indian exporters in the sector. This event, held over two days, gathered a delegation of 35 to 40 Indian food and beverage exporters and connected them with about 150 top distributors, importers, buyers, and retail outlets from GCC countries including Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE. G.D. Foods showcased an extensive range of products from its TOPS brand, which includes items such as ketchup, culinary sauces, pickles, and more. The participation aimed to enhance the visibility of Indian culinary tastes globally and establish significant business relationships within the FMCG sector.

records.title: The UAE and Indonesia have strengthened their cooperation by signing eight agreements during a state visit by the Indonesian President to...
records.description: The UAE and Indonesia have strengthened their cooperation by signing eight agreements during a state visit by the Indonesian President to the UAE. These agreements span various sectors, including the installation of solar energy systems, public budget management, smart banking systems, peaceful nuclear energy use, and environmental research with the establishment of a mangrove research center. Additionally, there are agreements related to financial cooperation, real estate development, tourism investment, and maritime security. This collaboration is part of the broader Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), enhancing bilateral relations in priority areas such as economy, renewable energy, food security, infrastructure, health, and climate action. This partnership has already seen a significant increase in non-oil trade between the two countries, rising from $2.7 billion in 2014 to $4.4 billion in 2023, with further investments valued at over $21 billion in 2023 alone.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Algeria has extended the General Agricultural Census (RGA) until July 27, which was...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Algeria has extended the General Agricultural Census (RGA) until July 27, which was originally set to conclude on July 17. This decision follows requests from various wilayas and the need to accommodate disruptions such as sandstorms, the Eid El-Adha holiday, and end-of-year exams that have affected progress. The Director of Statistics, Digitization and Foresight at the Ministry, highlighted that this extension is crucial for reaching all remaining farms. As of now, the census has covered 93% of farms, and is expected to achieve a 95% coverage soon. The goal is to document up to 1.2 million farms by the end of the extended period.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: The Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE) reported a substantial growth in its loan portfolio, reaching EGP 75.27 billion ($1.57 billion) in J...
records.description: The Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE) reported a substantial growth in its loan portfolio, reaching EGP 75.27 billion ($1.57 billion) in June 2024, which represents a significant increase from the previous year. This growth reflects the bank's ongoing commitment to supporting the agricultural sector and related industries, aligning with the state’s vision to enhance productivity in agriculture, livestock, poultry, and fisheries. The number of beneficiaries from these loans reached approximately 518,040, encompassing both individuals and companies.

records.title: The Iraqi Prime Minister hosted a meeting with business leaders from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Iraq, focusing on investment opportunities...
records.description: The Iraqi Prime Minister hosted a meeting with business leaders from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Iraq, focusing on investment opportunities in Iraq’s real estate and smart city sectors. The discussion involved top executives from major groups specialized in real estate development, including Egypt's Talaat Moustafa Group and Saudi Arabia's Al-Muhaidib Group. During the meeting, the Prime Minister encouraged the delegates to invest in Iraq's burgeoning tourism industry and highlighted the significant need for housing, with an emphasis on building three million units and developing new integrated cities connected by advanced transportation networks. The government plans to initiate projects for 16 new cities aimed at mitigating the housing shortage and supporting low-income families.

records.title: Jordan has received a $45 million grant from the Green Climate Fund for the Jordan Integrated Landscape Management Initiative (JILMI).
records.description: Jordan has received a $45 million grant from the Green Climate Fund for the Jordan Integrated Landscape Management Initiative (JILMI). This initiative is spearheaded by the Jordanian Ministry of Environment in collaboration with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) West Asia Office, IUCN members, and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). The funding aims to mitigate climate change impacts and boost water and agriculture sectors' resilience in Jordan.
records.institution: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)

records.title: In the Gharb region, despite experiencing significant water stress, the sugar beet harvest yielded an impressive 286,000 tonnes from an a...
records.description: In the Gharb region, despite experiencing significant water stress, the sugar beet harvest yielded an impressive 286,000 tonnes from an area of 5,100 hectares. This represents an average yield of 56 tonnes per hectare, marking an 8.7% increase from the previous year's 51.5 tonnes per hectare. This achievement is notable given the challenging conditions, including a pronounced water deficit due to low rainfall and depleted dam reserves. The state contributed to these efforts by raising the price of sugar beet by 80 DH per tonne in 2024, building on a similar increase from the previous year, cumulatively adding 160 DH per tonne over two years. Additionally, the state subsidized fertilizer prices as part of a program to lessen the impact of the rainfall deficit, which helped mitigate the cost increase in the market.
records.institution: Rabat Salé Kénitra Regional Directorate of Agriculture (DRA)

records.title: The Saudi General Food Security Authority has distributed US$78.7 million to local wheat farmers for the 2024 season, rewarding 792 farme...
records.description: The Saudi General Food Security Authority has distributed US$78.7 million to local wheat farmers for the 2024 season, rewarding 792 farmers for their combined delivery of 175,703 tonnes of wheat. This payout marks the first installment processed through the Mahsoly electronic platform. The initiative is part of a broader strategy authorized by the Cabinet, allowing the purchase of up to 1.5 million tonnes of wheat annually from local farmers over five years, aimed at bolstering domestic wheat production. This move is in line with Saudi Arabia's efforts to improve agricultural self-sufficiency and meet the food demands of its growing population and expanding economy. With a forecasted 25% increase in wheat production for the 2024-25 season, reaching 1.5 million tonnes, the country adapts its agricultural practices based on environmental factors and global market conditions. This strategy includes competitive pricing to encourage wheat cultivation over alfalfa hay, anticipating a continuation of last year's price of US$467 per tonne. As domestic consumption is expected to rise by 5% to 4.75 million tonnes, driven by a booming tourism sector, Saudi Arabia is preparing to meet increasing food demands with higher imports of essential grains.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has expanded its partnership with Spinneys and Circa Biotech to reduce food...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has expanded its partnership with Spinneys and Circa Biotech to reduce food waste by transforming it into agricultural feed using black soldier fly larvae. During a trial in Abu Dhabi, Spinneys successfully reduced landfill-bound food waste by 54 percent, redirecting it instead to Circa Biotech where it was converted into nutritious animal feed, organic fertilizers, and sustainable biofuel.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: After a six-year hiatus, the Iraq-Qatar Joint Committee reconvened in Baghdad, culminating in the signing of the final report of their 7t...
records.description: After a six-year hiatus, the Iraq-Qatar Joint Committee reconvened in Baghdad, culminating in the signing of the final report of their 7th session by Iraq's Minister of Trade, Atheer Daoud Al-Ghurairy, and Qatar's Minister of Commerce and Industry, Sheikh Mohammed bin Hamad Al Thani. This meeting underscored a renewed commitment to enhancing economic, trade, and investment relations between the two nations. Key outcomes included the signing of an Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement, aimed at boosting bilateral investments and fostering a conducive investment climate. Furthermore, Iraq invited Qatar to be the guest of honor at the upcoming Baghdad International Fair, encouraging Qatari investment in Iraq's Development Road initiative. The session facilitated extensive discussions on expanding cooperation across various sectors including trade, industry, energy, and more.

records.title: In a recent meeting focused on irrigation water management and preparation for the upcoming agricultural campaign, various measures were...
records.description: In a recent meeting focused on irrigation water management and preparation for the upcoming agricultural campaign, various measures were discussed to address the severe drought affecting the current agricultural cycle. This drought has impacted sowing of autumn crops due to delayed rains, leading to a reduction in the area sown with main cereals by 33%. To combat these issues, the Ministry has implemented short-term actions to preserve tree heritage and perennial crops through supplementary irrigation, especially for young plantations. Additionally, structural measures are planned to modernize irrigation systems and improve water efficiency, including developing localized irrigation, safeguarding groundwater resources, and undertaking seawater desalination and hydraulic basin interconnection projects. These efforts are part of the broader Generation Green 2020-2030 strategy and the national program for water supply and irrigation, aimed at securing food sovereignty and adapting the agricultural sector to new environmental realities.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: Morocco has lifted its export ban on potatoes and onions to other African countries, a move aimed at balancing the needs of local produce...
records.description: Morocco has lifted its export ban on potatoes and onions to other African countries, a move aimed at balancing the needs of local producers with market dynamics. This decision comes after the initial ban was put in place to control domestic price surges. To regulate the flow of exports and mitigate potential market disruptions, the Moroccan government has introduced a quota system that caps exports at 1,500 tons, distributed evenly across three major regions: Casablanca-Settat, Meknes-Tafilalet, and Souss-Massa, each allocated 500 tons. Despite the reopening of exports, the Moroccan Association of Producers and Exporters to Africa and Abroad has raised concerns regarding the quota system, arguing that the domestic price increases are due to internal factors and advocating for more collaborative decision-making with authorities.

records.title: In Rakhyut, Dhofar Governorate, a series of training programs aimed at increasing camel milk production and its derivatives has been laun...
records.description: In Rakhyut, Dhofar Governorate, a series of training programs aimed at increasing camel milk production and its derivatives has been launched through a collaboration between the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). The initiatives are designed to empower productive families in the Niyabat of Asa’ib, with a focus on financial management and enhancing the skills of women camel breeders. Dhofar Governorate, where 60% of Oman's camels are located, is set to benefit significantly from these programs. Targeting 20% of rural women in the Wilayat of Rakhyut.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources & Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: A partnership between NEOM and King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) focuses on combating the threat posed by insect...
records.description: A partnership between NEOM and King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) focuses on combating the threat posed by insects to Saudi Arabia's extensive palm tree population, which numbers around 36 million. This collaboration utilizes advanced optical fiber sensing technology developed by AK-Sens, a startup from KAUST, aiming for early detection of harmful pests like the red palm weevil. Initial trials show promising results, achieving high accuracy in detecting infestations quickly across large numbers of trees.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Thailand are stepping up their collaborative efforts in the realms of environment and food security, as evidenced by a r...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Thailand are stepping up their collaborative efforts in the realms of environment and food security, as evidenced by a recent high-level meeting in Riyadh. Saudi Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, Eng. Abdulrahman Alfadley, and Thai Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maris Sangiampongsa, discussed ways to enhance bilateral relations, focusing specifically on food security, livestock sector development, environmental cooperation, and increasing vegetation cover. The meeting, which included key officials like the Governor of the General Food Security Authority and the CEO of the National Center for Vegetation Development, aimed to deepen cooperation and share expertise in critical sectors to mutually benefit both nations in sustainable development and food production.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia has committed $46 million to construct a state-of-the-art veterinary laboratory in Riyadh, designed to advance the developme...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has committed $46 million to construct a state-of-the-art veterinary laboratory in Riyadh, designed to advance the development and production of vaccines targeting local disease strains in animals. This initiative, part of a broader strategy to boost local veterinary capabilities, will focus on disease diagnosis, vaccine development, and the localization of these vaccines to address region-specific animal health challenges. The facility aims to enhance the control and prevention of animal diseases through sophisticated diagnostic tools, including DNA sequencing, and will also support the creation of vaccines derived from local microbial strains.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia has introduced a financial reward program designed to support and retain professional fishermen, offering up to SR54,000 (ap...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced a financial reward program designed to support and retain professional fishermen, offering up to SR54,000 (approximately $15,000) to those who meet specific criteria. Managed by the Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Programme (Reef), the initiative targets Saudis with a valid fishing license who are actively engaged in fishing and are not employed in any other public or private sector jobs. Eligible participants must be at least 18 years old and reside in Saudi Arabia during the support period. Each fishing expedition must last a minimum of six hours. The program also provides financial aid during times when fishermen are unable to sail due to adverse weather, security measures, or maritime accidents, as well as compensation for injuries that temporarily prevent fishing.
records.institution: Saudi Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Programme (Reef)

records.description: Saudi Arabia is set to enhance its food security with the introduction of five new agricultural investment projects in the Al-Baha region. These projects, announced through the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture's FURAS portal, aim to bolster domestic production and reduce reliance on imported food, aligning with the Kingdom's Vision 2030 goals. The initiatives include the development of orchards, coffee cultivation, and the production of flowers and wild plants, emphasizing the strategic importance of these ventures in boosting agricultural productivity. Key projects include a coffee city with the capacity to cultivate over 150,000 trees and an Al-Ennab Village project focused on palm and fruit trees, among others.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: BAPCO Energies is contributing to the afforestation of the East Sitra waterfront, supporting the National Initiative for Agricultural Dev...
records.description: BAPCO Energies is contributing to the afforestation of the East Sitra waterfront, supporting the National Initiative for Agricultural Development's (NIAD) campaign, Forever Green. This initiative, in partnership with the Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture and the Supreme Council for the Environment, aligns with Bahrain's environmental objectives and government strategies for expanding green spaces.

records.title: Maaden el Ervane, an oasis nestled in the Mauritanian desert, epitomizes sustainable agriculture and communal living, principles instille...
records.description: Maaden el Ervane, an oasis nestled in the Mauritanian desert, epitomizes sustainable agriculture and communal living, principles instilled by its Sufi founder, Mohammed Lemina Sidina. Established in 1975, this village transformed a remote fertile land into a thriving, self-sufficient community, rejecting societal norms like caste and race, and embracing equality and cooperation. The community's commitment to sustainability is evident in their rejection of chemical fertilizers for compost and their adoption of solar-powered irrigation systems. These eco-friendly practices have allowed the village to cultivate a variety of crops such as tomatoes, peppers, onions, and watermelons, effectively using techniques like drip irrigation to maximize water efficiency in the harsh desert environment.

records.title: In Morocco, severe drought conditions have drastically reduced the amount of arable land available for agriculture, leading to significan...
records.description: In Morocco, severe drought conditions have drastically reduced the amount of arable land available for agriculture, leading to significant job losses in the sector. The area available for cultivation has shrunk from four million hectares to about 2.5 million hectares, contributing to the displacement of roughly 159,000 agricultural workers since early last year. This downturn is intensifying the country's unemployment rate, which has climbed to a record 13.7 percent in the first quarter of 2024.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has introduced a new financial support program for its fisheries sector, overseen by the Minister of Environment, Water, and...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced a new financial support program for its fisheries sector, overseen by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. This program, part of the Reef Saudi initiative, aims to develop the fisheries industry and enhance the livelihoods of small fishermen and rural families by increasing productivity and ensuring food security. Aligned with Vision 2030, the program will bolster the local economy and support the sustainable development of the fisheries sector. This includes modernizing infrastructure, such as ports on the Red Sea and Arabian Gulf, and providing concessional loans for equipment purchases. Eligible fishermen must hold a valid fishing license, not be employed in other sectors, be at least 18 years old, and reside in the Kingdom.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The National Water Company (NWC) of Saudi Arabia has launched 14 water and environmental enhancement projects worth over $150 million in...
records.description: The National Water Company (NWC) of Saudi Arabia has launched 14 water and environmental enhancement projects worth over $150 million in the Qassim region. These initiatives, which are part of the country's broader strategy to meet the increasing demand for water services and improve quality, include the construction of extensive sewerage channels and networks, a lifting station, and numerous water projects such as pipelines and a water distribution system for specific well areas.

records.title: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture recently conducted a comprehensive review of renewable water resources and thei...
records.description: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture recently conducted a comprehensive review of renewable water resources and their economic utilization during a workshop at its headquarters in Riyadh. This initiative aimed to refine strategies for water supply and demand management across all regions. Key discussions during the workshop, held in collaboration with the Sharqia Development Authority, focused on enhancing water transmission systems and optimizing the distribution and use of treated water in the Eastern Province.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Fertiglobe and Egypt Green Hydrogen have entered into a significant 20-year ammonia offtake agreement, which was signed at the Egypt-EU I...
records.description: Fertiglobe and Egypt Green Hydrogen have entered into a significant 20-year ammonia offtake agreement, which was signed at the Egypt-EU Investment Conference held on June 29, 2024. This collaboration underpins the Egypt Green Hydrogen project based in Ain Sokhna, within the Suez Canal Economic Zone, which is projected to reach its final investment decision by the first half of 2025. The project, developed by a consortium including Scatec and Orascom Construction, among others, plans to start supplying renewable ammonia to European markets by 2027. The agreement is a critical step towards scaling up production, with a target to deliver up to 397,000 tonnes by 2033, facilitated by substantial financial and technological backing from international institutions and powered by a robust setup of solar and wind capacities.

records.title: Morocco is grappling with a significant crisis in its tomato plantations due to the devastating impact of the Tuta Absoluta pest.
records.description: Morocco is grappling with a significant crisis in its tomato plantations due to the devastating impact of the Tuta Absoluta pest. This infestation has affected growers nationwide, with losses reaching up to 35% when combined with the Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus (ToBRFV), and in some cases, leading to the complete destruction of crops. The situation is compounded by the pest's growing resistance to traditional pesticides, and recent European regulations that limit the types of active ingredients allowed in these products. Additionally, the hot and humid conditions this summer have accelerated the spread of the infestation. Despite the proven efficacy of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) methods, including the use of biological controls such as the Nesidiocoris tenuis insect, many Moroccan farmers remain skeptical. They fear these biological agents might facilitate the spread of ToBRFV, though this linkage lacks strong scientific consensus. While the timing of the infestation aligns with the end of Morocco's tomato season, minimizing its impact on exports, its effect on future planting and the upcoming season remains uncertain.

records.title: The National Initiative for Agricultural Development (NIAD) has successfully completed the third phase of its national afforestation camp...
records.description: The National Initiative for Agricultural Development (NIAD) has successfully completed the third phase of its national afforestation campaign, "Forever Green," planting over 40,000 trees and shrubs across Bahrain. This effort spanned 14,243 square meters and involved 47 afforestation projects at various locations, collaborating with the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Agriculture and the Supreme Council for Environment.
records.institution: The National Initiative for Agricultural Development (NIAD)

records.title: Egypt has experienced a significant increase in agricultural exports, with the value rising by $600 million year-on-year to reach approxi...
records.description: Egypt has experienced a significant increase in agricultural exports, with the value rising by $600 million year-on-year to reach approximately $2.69 billion in the first half of 2024. The total volume of these exports also grew, reaching over 4.90 million tons, an increase of 300,000 tons from the previous year. Citrus fruits led the charge, accounting for over two million tons of exports, followed by fresh potatoes at 930,000 tons, and onions at 131,000 tons. Other notable exports included beans, grapes, and sweet potatoes, with beans exporting 84,000 tons, and grapes and sweet potatoes contributing 72,000 tons and 64,000 tons respectively.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) has officially launched ICC Iraq at its Global Headquarters in Paris, marking a significant e...
records.description: The International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) has officially launched ICC Iraq at its Global Headquarters in Paris, marking a significant expansion of its global network. This new national committee aims to amplify the voice of Iraqi business and chambers on the international stage, increasing the total number of ICC national committees to 92. The inauguration included a delegation from ICC Iraq and culminated in a celebration at the Iraqi Embassy in Paris. ICC Iraq will engage in various institutional objectives including arbitration, digital economy, intellectual property, and trade and investment to promote peace, prosperity, and opportunity in Iraq. Founding members include Abdulrazaq Al-Zuheere, Mohsin Al Hamed, and Ahmed Alyasiri, who will guide ICC Iraq in influencing ICC policies and addressing international business concerns through their local commissions.

records.title: At Columbia University in New York, the Saudi Green Building Forum recently hosted a forum dedicated to decarbonization in built-up areas.
records.description: At Columbia University in New York, the Saudi Green Building Forum recently hosted a forum dedicated to decarbonization in built-up areas. The event, part of the UN high-level political forum, attracted leading global experts who deliberated on strategies to reduce carbon footprints in urban environments, a crucial step toward achieving global sustainable development goals. Discussions emphasized the need for integrating sustainable practices into urban planning and development to foster environmentally friendly cities that align with the 'Urgent Green Actions for Global Agenda 2030.' Highlights included insights from distinguished speakers who shared innovative approaches to sustainable urban development, including the use of renewable energy and education on climate resilience.

records.title: The Tunisian President inaugurated a seawater desalination plant in Zarat, Gabes governorate, marking the first completed project under t...
records.description: The Tunisian President inaugurated a seawater desalination plant in Zarat, Gabes governorate, marking the first completed project under the Tunisian Desalination Programme, which began in 2016. The plant, now operational, will benefit 1.1 million citizens. The President emphasized the need for effective water management and called for urgent solutions to address water scarcity affecting drinking water, irrigation, and livestock, ahead of a national water strategy set for 2035.

records.title: Dubai to Develop ‘World’s Largest’ Fresh Food Hub
records.description: Dubai has announced its plan to develop what is described as "the world's largest" logistics center for fresh food, significantly expanding its current fruit and vegetable market in collaboration with DP World. This initiative, part of the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33), aims to double the emirate's economy to $8.7 trillion by 2033 and reinforce its status as a global hub for trade. The project, which will connect to international markets, is designed to enhance Dubai’s capacity in the global food trade sector, particularly in the handling and distribution of fruits and vegetables. This expansion is expected to create substantial commercial and investment opportunities, leveraging Dubai's strategic location and advanced infrastructure to attract global companies and integrate them into its economic projects.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has introduced a resolution to regulate food and fodder sampling for control...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has introduced a resolution to regulate food and fodder sampling for control and inspection purposes, ensuring the safety and quality of food products within Abu Dhabi. This resolution, issued by the Director General of ADAFSA, Saeed Al Bahri Salem Al Ameri, classifies samples into two categories: objective samples for routine checks and selective samples for identifying violations or detailed lab analysis. It stipulates precise requirements for the sampling process, including methods of collection, packaging, transportation, and storage to preserve sample integrity for chemical or bacteriological analysis. Furthermore, the resolution outlines procedures for re-analysis if initial results are unsatisfactory, allowing establishments to request additional tests at their expense in neutral, accredited laboratories.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Egypt's agricultural sector has experienced a notable surge in exports, achieving a $600 million increase year-on-year, reaching approxim...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural sector has experienced a notable surge in exports, achieving a $600 million increase year-on-year, reaching approximately $2.69 billion in the first half of 2024. During this period, the volume of exports grew to over 4.90 million tonnes, a significant rise from the previous year's figures. Citrus fruits led the export charts with over two million tonnes, followed by fresh potatoes and onions, highlighting the diverse range of produce that Egypt offers to international markets. Other significant exports included beans, both fresh and dried, grapes, and sweet potatoes, underlining the robust performance and potential of Egypt's agricultural export sector.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Egypt's inflation rate slightly decreased to 27.1% in June, marking the fourth consecutive month of decline, despite looming concerns ove...
records.description: Egypt's inflation rate slightly decreased to 27.1% in June, marking the fourth consecutive month of decline, despite looming concerns over potential fuel price hikes. The Central Agency for Public Mobilisation and Statistics (Capmas) reported a drop in prices across several product groups, although certain categories like cereals and bread saw price increases. The overall monthly inflation also rose, reflecting higher costs in food and beverages, healthcare, and other sectors. Economic analysts warn that while the downward trend in inflation is notable from a year-on-year perspective, the potential increase in fuel and electricity prices could reverse these gains. The government's imminent adjustments to fuel subsidies, coupled with ongoing economic reforms and external pressures like geopolitical tensions and import restrictions, suggest that Egypt's economic recovery may face further challenges ahead.
records.institution: Central Agency for Public Mobilisation and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: Egyptian agricultural firm Fresh Energy Egypt has partnered with Dutch company GREEFA, a specialist in sorting and packaging machinery, t...
records.description: Egyptian agricultural firm Fresh Energy Egypt has partnered with Dutch company GREEFA, a specialist in sorting and packaging machinery, to enhance the efficiency and quality of its vegetable exports to the European market. Fresh Energy recently acquired advanced equipment from GREEFA for sorting and packaging peppers, cucumbers, and tomatoes, aiming to meet the rigorous standards of European supermarkets and retail chains. The collaboration was officially celebrated with a signing ceremony attended by key representatives from both companies, marking GREEFA's first significant venture into the vegetable sector in the region. This partnership is expected to significantly improve production processes at Fresh Energy, ensuring the delivery of high-quality vegetables to Europe and fostering long-term growth and innovation for both firms.

records.title: Discussions aimed at enhancing Saudi-Iraqi business relations have been taking place in Riyadh, involving key figures like Hassan Al-Huwa...
records.description: Discussions aimed at enhancing Saudi-Iraqi business relations have been taking place in Riyadh, involving key figures like Hassan Al-Huwaizi, Chairman of the Federation of Saudi Chambers, and Sheikh Shaalan Al-Karim from the Iraqi-Saudi Parliamentary Friendship Committee. These talks have centered on boosting investment and trade between the two countries, with a specific focus on forthcoming legislation designed to protect Saudi investments in Iraq. This prospective law is expected to pass in the coming months, signaling stronger investment security for Saudi entities. Concurrently, the Saudi-Iraqi Business Forum has been actively exploring investment opportunities for Saudi businesses in Iraq and addressing challenges faced by investors, with significant participation from Iraqi parliamentarians.
