records.title: Saudi Arabia has initiated several substantial environmental and water infrastructure projects to enhance sustainability across the region.
records.description: Saudi Arabia has initiated several substantial environmental and water infrastructure projects to enhance sustainability across the region. Key among these is the Rayyis and Rabigh Independent Water Transmission Pipeline Project, with a capacity of 500,000 cubic meters per day and an estimated cost of 2.4 billion riyals. This project is notable for its private sector involvement and innovative design, which facilitates bi-directional water transmission, ensuring a steady water supply to the Makkah and Madinah regions. Additionally, the Yanbu Independent Water Production Project, costing 3.3 billion riyals, will provide 450,000 cubic meters of drinking water daily using advanced reverse osmosis technology powered by solar energy. These initiatives, spearheaded by the Saudi Water Partnership Company, highlight the nation's commitment to developing sustainable infrastructure and utilizing renewable energy in water production, with completion targeted for early 2026.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia recently concluded its two-year presidency of the 36th session of the Committee on Fisheries (COFI36) of the UN Food and Agr...
records.description: Saudi Arabia recently concluded its two-year presidency of the 36th session of the Committee on Fisheries (COFI36) of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), showcasing its contributions to the fisheries sector. This session, held in Rome, Italy, was chaired by Saudi Arabia's Permanent Representative at the FAO, with participation from over 19 ministers and more than 300 delegates from FAO member states. The FAO Director-General commended Saudi Arabia for its significant efforts in promoting sustainable practices within the fisheries sector. The presidency focused on implementing prior recommendations and enhancing member state performance in fisheries management and aquaculture development. Saudi Arabia facilitated discussions on adhering to responsible fishing practices and expanding aquaculture, underlining the sector's importance in sustainable economic growth and environmental conservation.

records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia has initiated the "Harvest Season" campaign to enhance public awareness about the benefits of consuming locally produced fruits and to improve the marketing effectiveness for the support of local farmers. Announced on a Wednesday, this campaign is part of broader efforts to promote healthier lifestyles through the consumption of local produce and to educate the public on the nutritional benefits of various fruits available throughout the year. The campaign also aims to support the production and quality of local goods, increase awareness of agricultural products, and assist in the marketing of these products, thereby boosting farmer incomes.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: In central Tunisia, a village near Kairouan faces a critical water shortage, forcing residents to depend on an irrigation pipe for drinki...
records.description: In central Tunisia, a village near Kairouan faces a critical water shortage, forcing residents to depend on an irrigation pipe for drinking water. This situation is emblematic of a broader issue affecting the rural areas of Tunisia, where only about half have access to the national water grid, with the rest relying on wells managed by local agrarian associations. These wells are often shut down due to unpaid bills, leaving communities without a viable source of water. The persistent drought exacerbates the situation, driving residents to use water from unauthorized and often polluted wells. This leads to health issues among the population, who have no choice but to use this contaminated water.

records.title: The UAE and Japan recently held discussions to enhance cooperation in food security and climate-smart agriculture as part of their Compre...
records.description: The UAE and Japan recently held discussions to enhance cooperation in food security and climate-smart agriculture as part of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Initiative (CSPI). The meeting, between UAE's Minister of Climate Change and Environment and Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, focused on expanding collaboration in agriculture, fisheries, and sustainable practices. They discussed technology transfer, innovative agricultural techniques, and shared priorities for COP29.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment

records.title: Amid economic uncertainty and soaring inflation, Egyptians are increasingly turning to agriculture as a stable source of income and a saf...
records.description: Amid economic uncertainty and soaring inflation, Egyptians are increasingly turning to agriculture as a stable source of income and a safe haven for savings. The demand for agricultural land is surging, driving up prices for both buying and renting, especially near the nutrient-rich Nile banks, known as "black land." The country's economic challenges, coupled with high food prices, have propelled both individuals and investors to seek opportunities in agriculture. This shift is also supported by the availability of newly developed agricultural land and government incentives aimed at enhancing food security and reducing dependency on food imports. As a result, agriculture is not only a source of revenue and food but also a strategic choice in response to economic pressures, with a growing number of Egyptians engaging in farming activities across the country.

records.title: The Agricultural Research Department at Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has achieved significant advancements in agricultural technology...
records.description: The Agricultural Research Department at Qatar's Ministry of Municipality has achieved significant advancements in agricultural technology, notably using gamma rays to develop new vegetable varieties that are well-suited to Qatar's environmental conditions. According to the director of the department, this innovative technique has led to promising research and production outcomes, including the imminent introduction of a new tomato variety. Additionally, the department has enhanced meat and dairy production by developing and utilizing advanced fodders adapted to local conditions. These fodders have significantly increased production levels over traditional options. The department's efforts extend to the cultivation of Al Labid fodder, which is both water-efficient and climate-resilient, marking a crucial step towards sustainable livestock management and water resource conservation in Qatar. Moreover, the department's research stations have incorporated cutting-edge technology like climate-controlled greenhouses and automated fertilization systems, furthering efficiency in water and fertilizer use through sophisticated hydroponics systems.
records.institution: Omani Agricultural Research Department at the Ministry of Municipality

records.title: Agthia Group, a UAE-based food and beverages company, has expanded its operations into Saudi Arabia with the opening of a Dhs 90 million...
records.description: Agthia Group, a UAE-based food and beverages company, has expanded its operations into Saudi Arabia with the opening of a Dhs 90 million protein manufacturing facility in Jeddah’s Industrial City 1. This new facility, spanning over 9,000 square meters with an annual production capacity of over 9,000 tonnes, is designed to meet growing demand for Agthia’s protein brands in the GCC's largest market. Equipped with advanced production lines, in-house labs for microbiology and sensory evaluation, and a supply chain supporting over 69 raw materials, the facility is poised to capitalize on the processed meat market in Saudi Arabia, which is expected to reach $7.11 billion by the end of the decade. This strategic expansion aims to enhance Agthia’s market presence, solidify its position in the region, and contribute to the diversification of its product portfolio. The company has also reported a significant increase in quarterly revenue and profit, despite economic challenges, underscoring its successful growth strategy.

records.title: In Saudi Arabia, a new cooperative insurance scheme was introduced by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture to mitigate eco...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia, a new cooperative insurance scheme was introduced by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture to mitigate economic losses caused by plant pests and animal diseases. This initiative, launched under the National Transformation Program and operated by the Weqaa Center, aims to bolster the sustainability of the agricultural sector. The insurance model focuses on a cooperative and solidarity-based approach that considers the humanitarian and social needs of the agricultural community, including farmers and livestock breeders. It seeks to shield agricultural producers from financial setbacks and promote investment in the sector by reducing the risks associated with agricultural production.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Tunisia is advancing a partnership with Russian grain companies to secure regular, fixed-price grain shipments, aiming to stabilize its s...
records.description: Tunisia is advancing a partnership with Russian grain companies to secure regular, fixed-price grain shipments, aiming to stabilize its supply amidst fluctuating domestic production. This strategy was unveiled following a significant meeting between Tunisian and Russian agricultural representatives, facilitated by both countries' agriculture ministers. Tunisia, which relies on domestic production for about 70% of its grain needs, faces challenges from variable harvests exacerbated by rising temperatures and prolonged droughts. In response, the Office of Cereals in Tunisia is actively pursuing this deal to import diverse grains including wheat, barley, and corn, alongside legumes and vegetable oils. This move comes as Tunisia seeks to diversify its economic partnerships amid stalled IMF loan negotiations, which have pushed the country to explore alternative alliances.

records.title: Algeria and Italy have inked a monumental €420 million ($455 million) agricultural agreement, marking a significant expansion in bilatera...
records.description: Algeria and Italy have inked a monumental €420 million ($455 million) agricultural agreement, marking a significant expansion in bilateral relations. This project, the largest Italian agricultural investment in the southern Mediterranean, spans 36,000 hectares in Algeria's Timimoune province. Primarily focused on boosting Algerian agricultural exports, the initiative will cultivate wheat, lentils, and beans, among other crops. Italian officials highlighted the dual benefits of this partnership: enhancing non-hydrocarbon exports for Algeria and creating approximately 6,700 jobs. This agreement follows closely on the heels of Algeria’s $3.5 billion deal with Qatar’s Baladna for a major dairy production facility, emphasizing Algeria's broader strategy to utilize its vast desert regions for agricultural expansion.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: British energy giant BP has partnered with the Masdar, Hassan Allam Utilities, and Infinity Power consortium to launch a green hydrogen p...
records.description: British energy giant BP has partnered with the Masdar, Hassan Allam Utilities, and Infinity Power consortium to launch a green hydrogen project in Egypt, underpinning Egypt’s ambitions to become a leader in the renewable energy sector. This collaboration, formalized through a Joint Development Agreement (JDA), positions BP as the main developer and operator, exploring the creation of green hydrogen and its derivatives for export. The partnership aligns with Egypt’s strategic energy transition plans, aiming to increase its renewable energy output to 42% by 2035. A Framework Agreement signed with the Egyptian government at the Egypt-EU Investment Conference supports this initiative, allowing the consortium to conduct necessary feasibility studies. This project is part of Egypt’s broader efforts to fill the energy export gap left by declining natural gas production and to capitalize on its natural resources for renewable energy, further demonstrated by recent plans to develop solar power stations funded by the European Union.

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture have initiated a project aimed at enhancing the operatio...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture have initiated a project aimed at enhancing the operational efficiency of decentralized agricultural departments across Jordan. This project, named "Enhancement of the efficient response of the decentralized agricultural departments in Jordan," focuses on improving service quality and responsiveness. A comprehensive capacity building program will be implemented for veterinarians, paravets, extensionists, agricultural engineers, and staff within the Ministry who interact directly with farmers and other service recipients. The project also includes the development of tools to evaluate service quality and timeliness, which will aid decision-makers in identifying areas for improvement. Launched under the patronage of Minister of Agriculture Eng. Khaled Hnaifat, and fully funded by the FAO, the project is set to conclude in October 2025.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Jordanian Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: FarmERP, a leader in sustainable technology solutions for agriculture, has announced a partnership with Saudi Arabian tech company Seiyaj...
records.description: FarmERP, a leader in sustainable technology solutions for agriculture, has announced a partnership with Saudi Arabian tech company Seiyaj Tech to enhance its presence and impact in Saudi Arabia's agricultural sector. This strategic collaboration, formalized by a Memorandum of Understanding in Riyadh, leverages Seiyaj Tech’s extensive network and expertise in localizing green energy technologies. The alliance aims to address the unique agricultural challenges of Saudi Arabia, such as extreme weather and water scarcity, by providing advanced technological solutions to boost productivity, profitability, and sustainability.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has opened bidding for the construction of a "coffee city" in the Qalwah Governorate of the Al-Baha Region, as part of its e...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has opened bidding for the construction of a "coffee city" in the Qalwah Governorate of the Al-Baha Region, as part of its efforts to boost local coffee production under the Saudi Vision 2030 initiative. Spanning over 5.5 million square meters, this ambitious project aims to augment the existing coffee sector by adding 300,000 trees. The initiative reflects the kingdom's broader strategy to localize production and expand its agricultural footprint. Currently, Saudi Arabia is among the top ten nations globally in coffee consumption and has significant coffee farming activities primarily in Jizan, Aseer, and Al Baha. The deadline for bid submissions is set for 9 September 2024, with reviews to follow immediately. This development is backed by substantial investment, including a significant allocation from the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund to elevate coffee production to new heights by 2030.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s largest dairy company, Almarai, reported a 6% decline in Q2 revenue for 2024, dropping to SAR 5.2 billion from SAR 5.46 bi...
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s largest dairy company, Almarai, reported a 6% decline in Q2 revenue for 2024, dropping to SAR 5.2 billion from SAR 5.46 billion the previous year, largely due to seasonal consumption shifts. This also resulted in a 10% decrease in Q2 net profit, amounting to SAR 620 million. However, the company's performance for the first half of 2024 remains positive, with an 8% increase in revenue to SAR 10.6 billion and a 10% rise in net profit to SAR 1.31 billion, driven by solid volume growth in dairy and poultry and effective cost controls. Despite the challenging quarter, Almarai anticipates continued growth throughout 2024, supported by stable macroeconomic conditions. Additionally, Almarai has launched the "Almarai Chefs Program" in collaboration with the Social Development Bank to support small cooking projects in Riyadh, aiming to enhance the contributions of emerging entrepreneurs to the Saudi food sector and promote sustainable business growth.

records.title: With the participation of 55 companies from 5 countries, the second international exhibition in Damascus, Agroceria, for agricultural mac...
records.description: With the participation of 55 companies from 5 countries, the second international exhibition in Damascus, Agroceria, for agricultural machinery and agricultural production inputs, was launched.

records.title: Tunisia and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) are advancing discussions on the development of a continental trade...
records.description: Tunisia and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) are advancing discussions on the development of a continental trade corridor linking Tunisia and Libya with landlocked African nations. This project emphasizes the strategic importance of the Ben Guerdane Free Trade and Logistics Zone and the Ras Jedir border crossing, which is the continent's largest land crossing.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Trade & United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA)

records.description: Abu Dhabi will host the World Food Security Summit for the first time on November 26-27, 2024, at the Abu Dhabi Exhibition Centre. The summit, part of Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Security Week, will bring together global experts and decision-makers to address the pressing issue of global hunger. The event will focus on innovative solutions to bolster food security, with participation from stakeholders worldwide, including representatives from developing countries, women, and youth.

records.title: The UAE and Japan have reinforced their strategic partnership through high-level meetings and the signing of multiple Memorandums of Unde...
records.description: The UAE and Japan have reinforced their strategic partnership through high-level meetings and the signing of multiple Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs), focusing on sustainable economic growth and technological innovation. These agreements, which emphasize energy security, clean energy projects, and digital transformation, aim to deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, and renewable energy. Significant agreements include a $3 billion green financing deal between ADNOC and the Japan Bank for International Cooperation to support low-carbon solutions and a Memorandum of Cooperation with Japan's Natural Resources and Energy Agency to enhance energy sustainability.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology

records.title: Algeria is emerging as a significant destination for international investors, notably from the United States, which plans to double its i...
records.description: Algeria is emerging as a significant destination for international investors, notably from the United States, which plans to double its investment volume in the country. The U.S. is already the largest direct investor in Algeria, and intends to enhance its economic engagement further. This expansion aims to include technology transfer, job creation, and support for local economic development across various sectors such as agriculture, heavy industries, energy, industrial processing, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. The U.S. Ambassador to Algeria highlighted the favorable investment environment in Algeria, characterized by political stability, abundant natural resources, and ongoing efforts to diversify its economy away from hydrocarbons. The Algerian government has facilitated this through reforms aimed at attracting foreign investment, simplifying administrative procedures, and offering attractive tax incentives.

records.title: The Alexandria Fertilizers Company (AlexFert) in Egypt has temporarily shut down operations at its three factories due to a disruption in...
records.description: The Alexandria Fertilizers Company (AlexFert) in Egypt has temporarily shut down operations at its three factories due to a disruption in natural gas supplies, which are crucial for electricity generation. This precautionary closure aims to ensure operational safety and affects an ammonia plant, a urea plant, and an ammonium sulfate plant, impacting both domestic supply and exports, which constitute 70 percent of its production to Europe and the US. This natural gas shortage has similarly affected other major Egyptian fertilizer manufacturers, prompting some, like SIDPEC and Abu Qir Fertilizers, to either gradually resume operations with restored gas supplies or explore alternative fuels like hydrogen for operation sustainability. The shortage, exacerbated by regional tensions and a significant heatwave that spiked local electricity demands, has prompted the government to implement measures to curb electricity use and allocate substantial funds to stabilize energy supplies. Despite these challenges, the Egypt Kuwait Holding Company, which owns a significant share of AlexFert, reported a slight profit increase in the first quarter of the year.

records.title: In the first half of 2024, Morocco imported over 200,000 tons of grain, predominantly wheat, from Russia, aiming to bolster its food secu...
records.description: In the first half of 2024, Morocco imported over 200,000 tons of grain, predominantly wheat, from Russia, aiming to bolster its food security amid global market fluctuations. This strategic importation reflects Morocco's efforts to preempt potential food shortages by diversifying its grain sources. The bulk of these shipments were sourced from the Vysotsk grain terminal near St. Petersburg, renowned for its stringent quality control managed by the regional branch of Russia's Federal State Institution “Grain Quality Assessment Center.” This collaboration underscores the growing trade ties between Morocco and Russia, highlighted by a recent visit from Moroccan food safety officials to Russia to observe its grain quality management practices firsthand.

records.title: In Jazan, a region in southwest Saudi Arabia renowned as the Kingdom’s fruit basket, a concerted effort is underway to bolster sustainabl...
records.description: In Jazan, a region in southwest Saudi Arabia renowned as the Kingdom’s fruit basket, a concerted effort is underway to bolster sustainable coffee production. Over 2,000 coffee farms operate in Jazan, collectively producing over 1,000 tons of coffee annually. The National Center for the Prevention and Control of Plant Pests and Animal Diseases, known as "Weqa," alongside relevant authorities, recently held a workshop aimed at expanding the number of coffee trees and enhancing sustainable cultivation practices in the area. The workshop brought together government and private sector stakeholders to align efforts and introduce innovative agricultural practices.
records.institution: The National Center for the Prevention and Control of Plant Pests and Animal Diseases (Weqa)

records.title: In Saudi Arabia, a strategic shift toward renewable energy is underway as the nation aims to source half of its electricity from renewabl...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia, a strategic shift toward renewable energy is underway as the nation aims to source half of its electricity from renewables by 2030. This transition is part of the broader Vision 2030 initiative, which seeks to diversify the economy and reduce carbon emissions. Significant investments have been made in both wind and solar energy, with major projects across the country. The wind energy sector has seen the development of the Middle East's largest wind farm, while the solar sector is expanding with several large-scale projects aiming to capitalize on the country’s abundant sunlight. Additionally, the country is exploring other renewable sources like bioenergy, geothermal, and small-scale hydroelectric power to further its sustainability goals.

records.title: SABIC Agri-Nutrients has announced a significant development in Saudi Arabia with the launch of a new blue ammonia project in Jubail Indu...
records.description: SABIC Agri-Nutrients has announced a significant development in Saudi Arabia with the launch of a new blue ammonia project in Jubail Industrial City. This initiative, supported by an allocation of feedstock from the Ministry of Energy, aims to produce 1.2 million metric tons per annum (MMTA) of low-carbon ammonia, along with 1.1 MMTA of urea and specialized agricultural nutrients. The project aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, focusing on clean energy production and export. SABIC Agri-Nutrients will conduct engineering studies to identify and implement the most efficient technologies for energy and feedstock utilization, marking a crucial step towards enhancing the kingdom’s position in the global clean energy sector.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Romania have signed a memorandum of understanding to bolster agricultural cooperation, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030's...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Romania have signed a memorandum of understanding to bolster agricultural cooperation, aligning with Saudi Vision 2030's national goals. This agreement, established between the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture and the Romanian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, focuses on enhancing economic support in agriculture and rural development. The collaboration will leverage modern technologies to boost agricultural production and improve the management of animal and plant resources. Key areas of this partnership include advancing livestock breeding, promoting animal health, achieving food security, and ensuring sustainable economic growth. Additionally, the agreement aims to increase the trade of agricultural products and collaborate on agricultural research, with particular emphasis on field crops, plant varieties, and modern beekeeping technology.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: In the agricultural year 2023/2024, Egypt reclaimed its status as the leading importer of Russian wheat, purchasing 8.6 million tons and...
records.description: In the agricultural year 2023/2024, Egypt reclaimed its status as the leading importer of Russian wheat, purchasing 8.6 million tons and marking a 6% increase from the previous year. This resurgence places Egypt ahead of Turkey, making it the primary destination for Russian wheat in a region where North Africa accounts for over 60% of the world's wheat imports. Despite this, Egypt's total wheat imports dropped by 24% to 7 million tons due to higher domestic production. In response to an increased domestic supply, the Egyptian government has set a goal to reduce wheat imports by 17% to 5 million tons. This strategy aligns with President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi's initiative to expand Egypt's agricultural land significantly. Meanwhile, Russia's global wheat export share rose to 28%, with the country shipping 55.4 million tons globally during this period.

records.title: Iraq's Ministerial Council for Economy has approved an exemption for fertilizer contracts from standard governmental contracting procedures.
records.description: Iraq's Ministerial Council for Economy has approved an exemption for fertilizer contracts from standard governmental contracting procedures. This special exemption applies specifically to the agreements between the General Company for Agricultural Supplies and the Southern State Company for Fertilizer Industries regarding the supply of urea fertilizer. This decision facilitates a deviation from the norms set in the Government Contracts Execution Instructions and the Federal General Budget Facilitation Instructions, aiming to streamline and expedite the supply process for essential agricultural inputs.

records.title: In response to increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices, Saudi Arabia has established the Saudi Alliance for Agricultural...
records.description: In response to increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices, Saudi Arabia has established the Saudi Alliance for Agricultural and Food Technologies. This new coalition, consisting of forty public and private entities, aims to enhance the nation's food supply chain. Launched in Riyadh by the deputy minister at the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the alliance includes notable founding partners such as the Research, Development and Innovation Authority, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, and Topian—a food subsidiary of NEOM. This initiative seeks to foster collaboration across the agricultural and food technology sectors, aiming to preserve natural resources and ensure sustainable water and food security.
records.institution: Saudi Alliance for Agricultural and Food Technologies

records.title: Saudi Arabia has established a new agency dedicated to advancing agricultural and food technologies.
records.description: Saudi Arabia has established a new agency dedicated to advancing agricultural and food technologies. This initiative aims to enhance the nation's agricultural sector through the adoption of cutting-edge technologies, improving both efficiency and productivity. The new body will focus on fostering innovation in food production methods, ensuring sustainability, and enhancing food security, aligning with the broader goals of Saudi Vision 2030. This move is part of Saudi Arabia's ongoing efforts to diversify its economy and reduce its dependence on oil by investing in and modernizing its agricultural sector.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Abu Dhabi-based Ghitha Holding, through its subsidiary Al Ain Farms, has completed the acquisition of Arabian Farms Investments LLC for $...
records.description: Abu Dhabi-based Ghitha Holding, through its subsidiary Al Ain Farms, has completed the acquisition of Arabian Farms Investments LLC for $65.3 million, securing all of the company's assets in both the UAE and Saudi Arabia. This acquisition, which is part of a strategic expansion, is subject to regulatory approvals and conditions outlined in the share purchase agreement. Arabian Farms, renowned for its Saha brand of poultry products, adds to Ghitha Holding's diverse portfolio, which spans food, agriculture, and more, across various regions. The deal reflects Ghitha's aggressive growth strategy, which has already seen substantial revenue increases and expansion into new markets and product categories.

records.title: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development announced a significant initiative to develop 500,000 hectares of agricultural...
records.description: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development announced a significant initiative to develop 500,000 hectares of agricultural land in the southern regions of the country. This project aims to bolster national cereal production and enhance food security. The initiative, set to commence this year, is part of a broader national strategy to cultivate strategic crops including cereals, pulses, oilseeds, and seeds. The development is scheduled over the next three years in collaboration with international firms from Italy and Qatar. Additionally, the plan includes constructing a new pilot silo in El-Affroune with a capacity of one million quintals to store cereals, alongside building thirty new silos nationwide to support increased cereal production and manage surpluses effectively.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: In Rabat, a strategic meeting took place between officials from the Commission for the Control of the Desert Locust in the Western Region...
records.description: In Rabat, a strategic meeting took place between officials from the Commission for the Control of the Desert Locust in the Western Region and the Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, focusing on enhancing regional efforts against the desert locust. This gathering sets the stage for the upcoming Joint Meeting of the CLCPRO, aiming to bolster collaborative strategies and responses to this agricultural threat. The discussions emphasized the need for effective prevention measures and regional cooperation to mitigate the impacts of locust invasions. Additional talks with civil protection and locust control leaders highlighted the importance of strengthening local capacities and fostering partnerships to improve preparedness and response mechanisms against locust outbreaks, which are vital for ensuring food security and economic stability in the affected regions.
records.institution: Commission for the Control of the Desert Locust in the Western Region & the Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.title: Morocco has imported over 200,000 tonnes of grain, predominantly wheat, from Russia in the first half of the year to bolster its food sec...
records.description: Morocco has imported over 200,000 tonnes of grain, predominantly wheat, from Russia in the first half of the year to bolster its food security amid declining local grain production due to dry and hot weather conditions. The majority of these shipments originated from the Vysotsk grain terminal near St. Petersburg. To ensure the quality of the imported grain, officials from Morocco’s National Food Safety Office visited Russia to observe grain loading and quality control processes.

records.title: The Maroc Fruit Board hosted its 6th annual international conference at the Sofitel Royal Bay Agadir Hotel, focusing on "Green Logistics:...
records.description: The Maroc Fruit Board hosted its 6th annual international conference at the Sofitel Royal Bay Agadir Hotel, focusing on "Green Logistics: Sustainable Pathways to Decarbonization." The event gathered key logistics sector figures to tackle the challenges and explore opportunities in reducing carbon emissions. Discussions centered on the importance of sustainable practices and decarbonization as both an ecological necessity and a competitive advantage for Moroccan exports. Industry leaders from various sectors, including global logistics, shipping, and the fruit and vegetable industry, shared innovative solutions to achieve decarbonization goals. The conference underscored Morocco's potential to lead in green logistics, particularly through initiatives linking Morocco to European markets, thereby enhancing Morocco's role in the ecological transformation of global logistics.

records.title: Alila Jabal Akhdar, a luxury hotel situated at 2000 meters in the Hajar mountains of Oman, has inaugurated the country's first hydroponic...
records.description: Alila Jabal Akhdar, a luxury hotel situated at 2000 meters in the Hajar mountains of Oman, has inaugurated the country's first hydroponic farm within a hotel setting, marking a significant advancement in sustainable hospitality. This hydroponic initiative, which began earlier this year, involves a soil-free cultivation method that uses nutrient-rich water, allowing for the year-round, rapid growth of fruits and vegetables like lettuces, strawberries, and cucumbers. The farm not only enhances the guest experience by offering fresh, tailor-made dining directly from garden to table but also emphasizes the hotel's commitment to sustainability. This project, which is set to expand in its second phase, also aims to support the local community by providing jobs and educational tours to inspire sustainable practices. With this venture, Alila Jabal Akhdar reinforces its dedication to eco-conscious luxury, integrating various sustainability initiatives across its operations.

records.title: Oman is advancing a draft law on Personal Income Tax (PIT), aimed at high earners, to the State Council as part of its efforts to diversi...
records.description: Oman is advancing a draft law on Personal Income Tax (PIT), aimed at high earners, to the State Council as part of its efforts to diversify its economic policies and reduce reliance on oil revenues. This proposed tax, introduced first in 2022, would levy rates between 5% and 9% on high income levels, distinguishing between foreign nationals and Omani citizens based on income thresholds. Currently, Oman's tax system focuses primarily on corporate income and withholding taxes for non-residents. The move to introduce PIT aligns with the country's Medium-Term Fiscal Plan (2020-2024) and marks a significant shift in fiscal policy, potentially impacting high-earning expatriates and wealthy Omani citizens. This legislative progression is part of broader discussions that include enhancing vocational education and adjusting VAT policies for new homeowners.

records.title: Iraq's Prime Minister recently announced a comprehensive development initiative for the city of Adhamiya in Baghdad.
records.description: Iraq's Prime Minister recently announced a comprehensive development initiative for the city of Adhamiya in Baghdad. The projects span a variety of sectors including traffic management, urban services, electricity, education, healthcare, and heritage conservation. Highlights include constructing a new bridge to improve traffic flow, developing the banks of the Tigris River, installing electricity substations, building new schools, renovating health centers, and restoring significant heritage sites such as local mosques. These efforts are aimed at enhancing public services and infrastructure to accommodate urban growth and improve the quality of life for residents. The implementation of these projects will be overseen by a dedicated committee, ensuring they meet the city's evolving needs.

records.title: World Bank Approves $700 Million Grant to Jordan to Boost Human Capital, Education
records.description: The World Bank Group has allocated $700 million to Jordan for enhancing human capital through two major initiatives focused on improving education, health, and social assistance. The first initiative, funded with $300 million, aims to bolster social sector governance and sustainability, enhancing overall resilience, including against climate change. The second, a $400 million program, seeks to equip Jordanian youth with vital skills for the labor market, emphasizing transitions from school to work and enhancing vocational training. These efforts are designed to support Jordan's economic modernization and public sector enhancement, contributing to sustainable and inclusive growth.

records.title: The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a $17 million grant for Mauritania under the Global Agriculture and Food Security Progra...
records.description: The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a $17 million grant for Mauritania under the Global Agriculture and Food Security Programme (GAFSP). This funding supports the Project for Promotion of Gender-Sensitive Agricultural Value Chains and Women's Entrepreneurship (PCVASGEF), aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity, adding value to products, and boosting women's incomes through entrepreneurship in Mauritania. Key components of the project include the creation of new market gardening plots managed by women, development of improved drainage basins, and establishment of internet-connected centers to promote female employment. Additionally, the project will equip vegetable packaging and storage units and local vegetable markets, fostering an entrepreneurial culture among women, including training and support for young entrepreneurs.

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company, a prominent Saudi Arabian halal food brand, has attained the esteemed AA+ rating from the BRCGS International Certi...
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company, a prominent Saudi Arabian halal food brand, has attained the esteemed AA+ rating from the BRCGS International Certification for its poultry facility, marking a significant milestone in the food industry. This recognition underscores Tanmiah’s commitment to upholding superior food safety and quality standards, distinguishing it as a leader in the sector. The BRCGS Global Standard for Food Safety, recognized worldwide, mandates rigorous safety and quality protocols. Tanmiah's achievement as the first fresh chicken producer in Saudi Arabia to receive an AA+ rating during an unannounced audit reflects its consistent adherence to these stringent standards. The unannounced audits assess the facility's daily operations and adherence to critical areas including food safety management, site standards, product control, and personnel hygiene, emphasizing Tanmiah's dedication to excellence.

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company, a prominent Saudi halal food brand, has achieved the highest AA+ BRCGS International Certification for its poultry...
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company, a prominent Saudi halal food brand, has achieved the highest AA+ BRCGS International Certification for its poultry facility, making it the first fresh chicken producer in Saudi Arabia to earn this distinction in an unannounced audit. This certification underscores Tanmiah's dedication to food safety and quality standards, aligning with global best practices. The rigorous evaluation by BRCGS confirms the company's consistent adherence to stringent food safety management, site standards, and personnel hygiene. This accomplishment reflects Tanmiah's commitment to excellence and its ongoing effort to meet the expectations of its customers and partners, reinforcing its leadership in the food industry within the region.

records.title: Iyris, previously known as RedSea, has announced an exclusive distribution agreement with Sherwood Middle East, a prominent agricultural...
records.description: Iyris, previously known as RedSea, has announced an exclusive distribution agreement with Sherwood Middle East, a prominent agricultural supplies distributor and subsidiary of Silal, to promote its SecondSky greenhouse covers in the UAE. This agreement marks a significant expansion for Sherwood, now the exclusive distributor of SecondSky in the region. SecondSky covers are designed to block near-infrared heat radiation, which significantly reduces energy consumption by over 40%, cuts water use by 30%, and boosts profitability by 28%. These covers are set to transform farming operations in the UAE by enhancing yield, quality, and profit margins, particularly suited for the region's hot climate.

records.title: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development announced a key initiative aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in durum wheat...
records.description: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development announced a key initiative aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in durum wheat by 2027. This plan is a component of the National Plan for the Development of Strategic Crops, intended to enhance the nation's food security. During a visit to Tindouf, it was revealed that construction will soon begin on 30 new grain storage silos with a capacity of 30 million quintals, underscoring a major step towards self-sufficiency in durum wheat. The minister emphasized the critical role of new investment laws in fostering partnerships with foreign companies to bring in needed expertise and technology to boost crop yields. Additionally, an ambitious initiative was disclosed to plant 3,000 hectares of argan trees, positioning Algeria to become a future producer of argan oil.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has recently approved access to approximately $130 million for Jordan following the first review of...
records.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has recently approved access to approximately $130 million for Jordan following the first review of its economic reform initiatives under a $1.2 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF). This development marks a positive beginning for the reform program, which aims to manage public debt effectively, enhance social and capital expenditures, and expand the tax base. Although Jordan’s economy faces challenges such as high unemployment and regional instability, the IMF commends its resilience and the effectiveness of its macroeconomic policies. These efforts are geared towards fostering economic stability, strengthening resilience, and promoting inclusive growth, despite a slight downward revision in this year’s growth forecast.

records.title: Oman has experienced a remarkable 300% increase in wheat production over the past five years, culminating in a harvest of 7,119 tonnes du...
records.description: Oman has experienced a remarkable 300% increase in wheat production over the past five years, culminating in a harvest of 7,119 tonnes during the 2022/2023 agricultural season. This growth reflects the nation's commitment to agricultural productivity and food security, driven by strategic government initiatives and partnerships with academic institutions. The introduction of high-yielding, stress-resistant wheat genotypes and the expansion of cultivated areas have played critical roles in this success. The government's backing has been crucial in addressing challenges like water scarcity and labor shortages. Innovations such as super-absorbent biopolymers for soil moisture retention and advanced seed priming techniques have further enhanced wheat resilience against drought and climate variations.
records.institution: Agricultural and Marine Sciences Department at Sultan Qaboos University

records.title: Dubai Approves $6.8 Billion FDI Program to Attract $176.96 Billion in Investments by 2033
records.description: Dubai has launched a significant $6.8 billion Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Development Program, aimed at attracting approximately $176.96 billion in investments by 2033 to establish itself as one of the world’s top three urban economies. This initiative is part of a broader economic strategy that includes the introduction of new economic models and incentive programs to attract international businesses and support the expansion of existing ones. Alongside economic development, Dubai is also focusing on urban planning enhancements around Metro stations to improve public transport efficiency and reduce carbon emissions. Additionally, the Executive Council has approved social and cultural programs like the 'Manbar' and 'Ghras Al Khair' to promote national identity and societal values. These combined efforts are designed to fortify Dubai’s position as a global commercial hub and an attractive destination for living and working.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Environment, Yasmine Fouad, unveiled significant investment opportunities totaling $2 billion in Egypt's green circul...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Environment, Yasmine Fouad, unveiled significant investment opportunities totaling $2 billion in Egypt's green circular economy during the "Promoting Green and Circular Economy in Egypt" session at the Egypt-EU Investment Conference. Held under the auspices of Egypt’s President and the President of the European Commission, the conference gathered key figures including World Bank Vice President for North Africa Ousmane Dione and European Bank for Reconstruction and Development Vice President Matteo Patrone. Minister Fouad highlighted Egypt's pioneering steps, such as designating all national projects as green and publicly funded during the COVID-19 pandemic, stimulating private sector investment in green initiatives. She underscored the country's legislative frameworks, including the Waste Management Regulation Law, fostering private sector participation in waste management and the development of the largest integrated waste management complex in cooperation with the World Bank. Fouad emphasized sectors ripe for investment, including waste management, renewable energy, resource efficiency, industry, and tourism, underpinned by robust infrastructure, legal frameworks, and economic incentives outlined in Egypt's new investment law.

records.title: Iraq's Ministerial Council for Energy has approved significant procurement exemptions to facilitate the strategic Common Seawater Supply...
records.description: Iraq's Ministerial Council for Energy has approved significant procurement exemptions to facilitate the strategic Common Seawater Supply Project (CSSP). These exemptions allow the CSSP and its consultancy agreements, including a tender with an Austrian consulting firm, to bypass standard contracting procedures outlined in the Government Contracting Execution Instructions and the federal budget implementation guidelines for 2023-2025. This decision, aimed at expediting the desalination project, aligns with previous Council of Ministers decisions to streamline operations critical for national infrastructure development.

records.title: Turkmenistan and the UAE have seen a notable 15.8 percent increase in their trade turnover, reaching $1.29 billion last year, according t...
records.description: Turkmenistan and the UAE have seen a notable 15.8 percent increase in their trade turnover, reaching $1.29 billion last year, according to Deputy Minister Kerimberdi Kurbanov of Turkmenistan's Ministry of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations. This growth reflects a 13.3 percent rise in Turkmenistan's exports to the UAE and a 16.2 percent increase in imports from the UAE. The trade is predominantly driven by Turkmenistan's chemical products, fuel and energy sectors, and agricultural goods exported to the UAE, while imports consist largely of metallurgical products, vehicles, and machinery. This development underscores both nations' commitment to expanding economic cooperation through mutual investments, trade diversification, and joint projects in energy, infrastructure, and digital sectors, aimed at fostering sustainable economic growth and enhancing international partnerships.
records.institution: Turkmenistani Ministry of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations

records.title: Saudi Arabia has shown keen interest in importing 200,000 tonnes of red meat and one million tonnes of soybeans annually from Nigeria, ac...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has shown keen interest in importing 200,000 tonnes of red meat and one million tonnes of soybeans annually from Nigeria, according to Agriculture Minister Mohammad Abubakar. This move comes as Nigeria aims to diversify its exports away from its dominant oil and gas sectors, seeking to bolster foreign exchange earnings amidst dollar shortages that have impacted its economy. The discussions followed a visit by Saudi Arabia's agriculture minister to Nigeria, where meetings with local agribusiness leaders paved the way for Saudi Arabia's expression of interest. Abubakar highlighted that Nigeria has outlined a roadmap to meet Saudi Arabia's demand, signaling a significant step in bilateral trade relations between the two countries.

records.title: Tetra Pak has announced a significant partnership with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) through...
records.description: Tetra Pak has announced a significant partnership with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) through its commercial arm, Ektifa, to equip the Meliha Dairy Factory with advanced processing and filling solutions. Located in the UAE, Meliha Dairy Factory is the country’s first farm integrating authentic organic production methods. Tetra Pak’s collaboration will introduce state-of-the-art processing equipment and sustainable filling lines, including the innovative Tetra Top Filling Line, which offers recyclable packaging solutions for chilled products, yogurt, and still drinks. This initiative underscores Sharjah’s commitment to environmental sustainability and local organic dairy production, enhancing production efficiency and product quality while minimizing environmental impact.

records.title: Tetra Pak has partnered with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock and its commercial arm, Ektifa, to enhan...
records.description: Tetra Pak has partnered with the Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock and its commercial arm, Ektifa, to enhance the Meliha Dairy Factory in the UAE with cutting-edge processing and sustainable packaging solutions. This collaboration aims to equip the factory with the latest technology, including the innovative Tetra Top Filling Line for recyclable packaging and systems for utilities generation essential for the dairy processing. The partnership underscores Sharjah's commitment to sustainable agriculture and aligns with Tetra Pak’s expertise in providing comprehensive, environmentally friendly production capabilities. This initiative not only promises to boost production efficiency and reduce environmental impact but also supports the production of organic, locally sourced dairy products, advancing the region's focus on authentic organic production methods.
records.institution: Tetra Pak & The Government of Sharjah’s Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL)

records.title: In Egypt, a shortage of fertilizers has emerged due to the suspension of multiple fertilizer plants, redirected natural gas supplies towa...
records.description: In Egypt, a shortage of fertilizers has emerged due to the suspension of multiple fertilizer plants, redirected natural gas supplies towards power generation amid heightened demand from increased temperatures. Abdel-Rahman highlighted that the scarcity of subsidized fertilizers predates these production halts, exacerbated by soaring market prices for unsubsidized alternatives. This situation significantly affects the cultivation of essential crops such as tomatoes, yellow corn, grains, and rice. Urgent calls have been made for the Ministry of Agricultural and Land Reclamation to expedite the distribution of subsidized fertilizers, while advocating for governmental intervention to address production challenges. Abdel-Rahman also proposed transitioning towards renewable energy sources like solar and wind to mitigate reliance on natural gas and ensure adequate supply for both power generation and industrial needs, including fertilizer production.

records.title: Prime Minister Masrour Barzani of the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has inaugurated the Chamrga Dam in Erbil, marking a significant...
records.description: Prime Minister Masrour Barzani of the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has inaugurated the Chamrga Dam in Erbil, marking a significant achievement in water resource management and infrastructure development. Joined by Begard Talabani, Minister of Agriculture and Water Resources, and Erbil Governor Omed Khoshnaw, Prime Minister Barzani highlighted the dam's strategic importance in safeguarding water resources across the region. The Chamrga Dam, constructed at a cost of IQD 4.3 billion, stands 17.5 meters tall, spans 262 meters in length, and measures 8 meters in width. It is expected to play a crucial role in enhancing water retention for agricultural purposes, generating power, promoting tourism through scenic vistas, and controlling floods. Prime Minister Barzani underscored the KRG's commitment to furthering water conservation efforts and maximizing the benefits of such infrastructure projects to meet both current and future water needs in Kurdistan.
records.institution: Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) & Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources

records.title: To Boost Foreign Investments, Iraq signs Singapore Convention
records.description: Iraq has marked a significant milestone in boosting foreign investments by signing the United Nations Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation, commonly known as the Singapore Convention. This move underscores Iraq's commitment to creating a favorable environment for global investors, as highlighted during a high-profile conference hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the National Investment Commission (NIC) under the patronage of Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani. The convention aims to streamline the enforcement of mediated settlement agreements, thereby enhancing international trade and commerce opportunities for Iraq. With the support of international partners like the European Union, Iraq seeks to combat corruption, promote transparency, and stimulate economic growth through effective dispute resolution mechanisms. The signing of the Singapore Convention signals Iraq's readiness to strengthen its global collaborations and attract diversified investments, paving the way for a more secure and attractive business environment.

records.title: ACWA Power, the Water and Electricity Holding Company (Badeel), and Saudi Aramco Power Company (SAPCO) have inked power purchase agreemen...
records.description: ACWA Power, the Water and Electricity Holding Company (Badeel), and Saudi Aramco Power Company (SAPCO) have inked power purchase agreements (PPAs) with the Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC) for three substantial solar photovoltaic (PV) projects in Saudi Arabia. These projects, including the Haden and Muwayh plants in the Makkah region with capacities of 2,000MW each, and the Al Khushaybi plant in the Qassim region with a capacity of 1,500MW, are pivotal to Saudi Arabia's renewable energy sector growth under Vision 2030. Jointly owned by Badeel, ACWA Power, and SAPCO, the projects are part of a broader initiative encompassing multiple facilities totaling 13,600MW and involving over $9 billion in investment from the Public Investment Fund (PIF) and its partners. The new solar PV facilities, valued at SAR 12.3 billion ($3.3 billion), are slated to contribute 5,500MW of renewable energy to the national grid by the first half of 2027, reinforcing Saudi Arabia's commitment to sustainable energy development and economic diversification.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: In Saudi Arabia, several companies have inked power purchase agreements for three major solar projects aimed at bolstering the country's...
records.description: In Saudi Arabia, several companies have inked power purchase agreements for three major solar projects aimed at bolstering the country's renewable energy capacity as part of its Vision 2030 goals. These projects, located in the Makkah and Qassim regions, will contribute an additional 5,500MW to the national grid, representing a significant stride toward modernizing and diversifying the economy through enhanced renewable energy initiatives. The projects, with an investment of over $9 billion, are set to be completed by the first half of 2027, marking a pivotal development in Saudi Arabia's transition to renewable energy sources.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has launched the Supervisory Council for the Ibex protected area, marking a significant stride in wildlife conservation and...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has launched the Supervisory Council for the Ibex protected area, marking a significant stride in wildlife conservation and community involvement. Spearheaded by the Saudi National Center for Wildlife (NCW) in collaboration with the Riyadh Region Emirate, this initiative aims to enhance management practices and preserve biodiversity within the 1841 square kilometers Ibex protected area in southern Saudi Arabia. The council's formation emphasizes local community engagement, aligning with global standards of conservation that promote sustainable use of natural resources and foster environmental awareness among residents. The area, renowned for its diverse wildlife and unique geological features, offers ecotourism opportunities such as camping, hiking, and beekeeping, contributing to local economic growth while safeguarding the region's natural and cultural heritage. Saudi Arabia's commitment to conservation through initiatives like the Ibex Supervisory Council reflects its adherence to Vision 2030 goals and sets a precedent for future conservation efforts nationwide.

records.title: BEAM Launches Initiatives for Graduates of Creative Science Schools
records.description: Chairman Salah Bukhatir of BEAM unveiled two transformative initiatives during the recent end-of-year ceremonies for graduates of Creative Science Schools (CSS). The BEAM University Scholarship Programme aims to support academic high achievers in pursuing tertiary education goals, while the Graduates’ Career Pathways Programme prioritizes CSS alumni for job placements within BEAM and its educational network. These initiatives underscore CSS's commitment to nurturing holistic student development, equipping graduates not only with academic excellence but also with the practical skills and opportunities needed to excel in education and leadership roles.

records.title: Egypt’s PM Mostafa Madbouly Targets $100 Billion Exports by 2030
records.description: Egypt's Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has set an ambitious target for the country to achieve $100 billion in exports by 2030, emphasizing a strategy focused on enhancing industrialization, boosting investments, and making Egyptian products more competitive in global markets. The initiative, discussed at a meeting held in the New Administrative Capital, highlighted efforts to support exporters and increase market share. Key officials, including Ali El-Sisi from the Ministry of Finance and Ahmed Samir from the Ministry of Trade and Industry, underscored the success of export support initiatives from 2019 to 2023, which contributed to a 40 percent increase in non-petroleum exports. The government aims to streamline export processes, improve payment mechanisms for exporters, and enhance the efficiency of export support systems through automation to foster sustained economic growth and achieve national economic goals.

records.title: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering a $79.1 million long-term senior loan to support the developme...
records.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering a $79.1 million long-term senior loan to support the development of a 200-megawatt (MW) wind farm in Ras Ghareb, located in Egypt's Gulf of Suez region. This project, part of Egypt's ambitious renewable energy goals under the Nexus Water-Food-Energy Programme (NWFE), will supply electricity to the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC) under a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) with backing from a sovereign guarantee by the Ministry of Finance. Masdar IPH Wind, a special purpose vehicle owned 51% by UAE’s Masdar and 49% by Egypt’s Infinity Energy, is overseeing the project, which is expected to cost around $214.8 million.

records.title: The gas crisis in Egypt has led to a sharp 54% increase in fertilizer prices within a month, soaring from 13,000 to 20,000 Egyptian pound...
records.description: The gas crisis in Egypt has led to a sharp 54% increase in fertilizer prices within a month, soaring from 13,000 to 20,000 Egyptian pounds per ton by June, as reported by Asharq. This spike is attributed to reduced local gas production affecting fertilizer factories, causing either complete shutdowns or partial operations. Factories like Abu Qir Fertilizers and Sidi Kerir Petrochemicals have halted production due to gas interruptions, exacerbating market demand amidst peak fertilizer needs for summer crops. Importing liquefied gas has become necessary, driven by rising dollar exchange rates, inflating production costs and escalating fertilizer prices, especially for urea and ammonia. Despite stabilized subsidized fertilizer prices at 5,000 pounds per ton, concerns persist over potential smuggling and shifts in crop cultivation choices due to heightened costs and production disruptions.

records.title: Trade between the UK and Iraq has seen a notable increase, with total trade in goods and services rising by 15.4% to £1.1 billion for the...
records.description: Trade between the UK and Iraq has seen a notable increase, with total trade in goods and services rising by 15.4% to £1.1 billion for the year ending in Q4 2023. This growth includes an 18.3% increase in UK exports to Iraq, totaling £770 million, and an 8.3% rise in UK imports from Iraq, which amounted to £287 million. These figures position Iraq as the UK's 89th largest trading partner, accounting for 0.1% of the UK's total trade. This upward trend highlights strengthening economic ties between the two nations.
records.institution: UK Department for Business and Trade

records.title: Osool Poultry Company has entered into a strategic collaboration with Aviagen, a renowned U.S.-based poultry industry expert, to launch a...
records.description: Osool Poultry Company has entered into a strategic collaboration with Aviagen, a renowned U.S.-based poultry industry expert, to launch a groundbreaking OMR10 million (US$26 million) poultry project in Oman named ‘Jaddat’ (mother hens). This project aims to establish local production of fertilized eggs and high-quality chicks, significantly enhancing Oman’s poultry industry’s self-sufficiency and reducing dependence on imported one-day-old chicks, which currently support Osool’s annual production capacity of 150 million eggs. The initiative will leverage Aviagen’s extensive technical expertise and support, focusing on advanced production technologies to improve product quality and operational efficiency.

records.title: The Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA) has approved Arabian Mills Company for Food Products to list 15.4 million shares, representing 3...
records.description: The Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA) has approved Arabian Mills Company for Food Products to list 15.4 million shares, representing 30% of its total shares, on the Tawadul stock exchange. This move aligns with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, aimed at economic diversification away from oil revenues. Arabian Mills, formerly the Second Mills Company, operates three mills in Riyadh, Jazan, and Hail, with a daily flour production capacity of around 4,920 tons. The IPO approval underscores Saudi Arabia’s commitment to privatization and market reforms, following the successful IPO of the Modern Mills Company earlier in the year, which raised US$314.6 million.

records.title: Vietnam has successfully exported dragon fruit with red and yellow flesh to Saudi Arabia for the first time, marking a significant milest...
records.description: Vietnam has successfully exported dragon fruit with red and yellow flesh to Saudi Arabia for the first time, marking a significant milestone in bilateral trade. The fruit debuted at Spinneys, a prestigious UAE-based supermarket chain, during its recent opening. Vietnamese Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Dang Xuan Dung, highlighted the growing presence of Vietnamese agricultural products in the kingdom and expressed optimism for expanding the range of Vietnamese goods at Spinneys. He pledged the embassy's support in facilitating connections between the supermarket and Vietnamese exporters, aiming to foster increased trade between Vietnam and Saudi Arabia.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Masdar, the Abu Dhabi-based renewables company, is set to expand significantly in the United States, aiming to grow 'more than tenfold' w...
records.description: Masdar, the Abu Dhabi-based renewables company, is set to expand significantly in the United States, aiming to grow 'more than tenfold' within the next three to seven years. Philip Haddad, president and CEO of Masdar Americas LLC, outlined ambitious plans to invest in development and operational platforms, emphasizing the US as pivotal to Masdar's goal of achieving a global renewable energy portfolio of at least 100 gigawatts by 2030. The company recently announced the acquisition of a 50% stake in Terra-Gen, a major US-based independent renewable energy producer, and continues to strengthen its presence with strategic investments like the acquisition of California-based solar and battery storage project, Big Beau. Masdar's expansion underscores its role as a key player in advancing sustainable energy solutions internationally, supported by its ownership under Abu Dhabi-listed ADNOC, TAQA, and sovereign investor Mubadala.

records.title: The UAE’s Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with the Republic of Georgia has officially come into effect, marking a sig...
records.description: The UAE’s Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with the Republic of Georgia has officially come into effect, marking a significant milestone in bilateral economic relations. This agreement aims to enhance trade cooperation by eliminating or reducing customs duties on 95 percent of tariff lines, covering more than 90 percent of non-oil bilateral trade. It is expected to more than triple the total value of non-oil trade between the UAE and Georgia to $1.5 billion within five years, contributing $3.9 billion to the UAE’s GDP and $291 million to Georgia’s GDP by 2031. The CEPA also anticipates boosting UAE exports to Georgia to $1.3 billion by 2031, benefiting sectors such as refined sugar, electrical appliances, vehicles, polymers, and machinery. This move solidifies the UAE’s position as Georgia’s leading trading partner in the Arab world and aims to accelerate bilateral investment across various key sectors, fostering economic growth and strengthening ties between the two nations.

records.title: UAE: New Guidelines for Public-Private Partnerships, Sandbox Conditions Regulation
records.description: The UAE has introduced two significant regulatory frameworks aimed at enhancing its business ecosystem: the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Manual and the Sandbox Conditions regulation. Approved by the UAE Cabinet, the PPP Manual establishes guidelines for federal government entities to collaborate effectively with the private sector on developmental projects. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and the efficient utilization of private sector capabilities to achieve societal and economic benefits. Concurrently, the Sandbox Conditions regulation, introduced by the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), aims to attract global fintech companies and startups by providing a structured environment to test innovative financial products and services. Both initiatives underscore the UAE's commitment to fostering innovation, driving economic growth, and optimizing public-private collaborations across key sectors such as infrastructure, energy, healthcare, and finance.

records.title: Egypt is considering a significant price increase of 30% for subsidized fertilizers due to economic strains and a natural gas shortage af...
records.description: Egypt is considering a significant price increase of 30% for subsidized fertilizers due to economic strains and a natural gas shortage affecting production costs. The proposed hike would adjust the price of a ton of subsidized fertilizer from 4,800 pounds to 6,250 pounds. This shortage of natural gas, crucial for fertilizer production, has forced manufacturers to operate at substantial losses, selling their products at about 48% of production costs. The Egyptian government requires that 55% of all fertilizer production be sold at subsidized prices to the Ministry of Agriculture, intensifying the financial pressure on producers. As a result, manufacturers are incurring losses of approximately 4,000 pounds per ton. This situation is exacerbated by the sharp rise in market fertilizer prices, which saw a 54% increase in June alone, posing significant challenges to the sustainability of Egypt's agricultural sector.

records.title: Hussein Abdel Rahman Abu Saddam, the General Secretary of the Farmers Syndicate, has raised concerns over a crisis in Egypt's agricultura...
records.description: Hussein Abdel Rahman Abu Saddam, the General Secretary of the Farmers Syndicate, has raised concerns over a crisis in Egypt's agricultural sector stemming from the suspension of subsidized fertilizer disbursements and the halting of production by some fertilizer factories due to gas supply shortages. In an exclusive statement to Cairo 24, Abu Saddam highlighted that these issues are driving up fertilizer prices, which is expected to result in a 25% increase in prices for agricultural commodities such as fruits, vegetables, grains, rice, and corn. He emphasized the urgent need for the Ministry of Agriculture to swiftly address the fertilizer shortage by expediting subsidy disbursements and exploring alternative energy sources like solar and wind power to sustain fertilizer production in Egypt's farms.

records.title: Iraqi Govt to Launch Tech Incubators in Universities
records.description: The Iraqi government is set to launch technological and scientific incubators across universities, as announced by the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research. This initiative is designed to foster innovation and entrepreneurship within the academic community, aligning with broader goals for national economic development. The program emphasizes the need for reduced bureaucracy and improved collaboration between universities and the wider community. This includes enhancing opportunities for practical application of theoretical knowledge and adapting to evolving job market demands and development needs. These efforts were highlighted during the first conference dedicated to technological and scientific incubators in the country.
records.institution: Iraqi Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research

records.title: Osool Poultry Company has signed an agreement with Aviagen (Ross) to establish a major poultry project named “Jaddat” (mother hens), with...
records.description: Osool Poultry Company has signed an agreement with Aviagen (Ross) to establish a major poultry project named “Jaddat” (mother hens), with an investment of OMR10 million. Aviagen will provide full technical support for the project, which aims to enhance food security and achieve self-sufficiency in Oman by meeting the country's chicken needs and reducing imports. The project will produce fertilized eggs, quality chicks, and other poultry products, reducing the risks associated with poultry imports. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources supports the poultry industry by transferring global knowledge, training Omani cadres, and promoting food security.

records.title: Siemens Energy has secured a $1.5 billion contract to build and maintain two gas-fired power plants in Saudi Arabia, named Taiba 2 and Qa...
records.description: Siemens Energy has secured a $1.5 billion contract to build and maintain two gas-fired power plants in Saudi Arabia, named Taiba 2 and Qassim 2. Scheduled to commence operation in 2026, these plants will deliver nearly 4GW of electricity to the kingdom, enhancing its energy infrastructure and replacing older oil-dependent facilities. The project, spanning 25 years, will initially operate in simple cycle mode before transitioning to combined cycle operation in subsequent years. Siemens Energy's advanced gas turbine technology is expected to significantly reduce CO₂ emissions by up to 60% compared to traditional oil-based power plants, supporting Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals for economic diversification and sustainable development.

records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture of Saudi Arabia has entered into a partnership with the Brazilian government aimed at...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture of Saudi Arabia has entered into a partnership with the Brazilian government aimed at enhancing environmental sustainability. This collaboration, initiated during the G20 Young Entrepreneurs Alliance Summit in Goiania, Brazil, involves implementing Saudi digital technology to plant trees in Jataí, Brazil. Dr. Ali Al-Sabhan, Director General of the General Department of Entrepreneurship at the Research and Innovation Agency in the Saudi Ministry of Environment, emphasized the significance of international cooperation in supporting entrepreneurs and advancing sustainable development goals. The partnership will leverage Saudi digital technology to manage carbon emissions and enhance environmental sustainability, marking a pivotal moment in global environmental cooperation.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: Tunisia has received valuable aid from the FAO and Morocco to combat the cactus mealybug infestation.
records.description: Tunisia has received valuable aid from the FAO and Morocco to combat the cactus mealybug infestation. The FAO delivered one hundred *Hyperaspis trifurcata* ladybugs, natural predators of the mealybug, in response to a request from the Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture. This initiative, supported by FAO offices in Tunisia and Morocco, involves a collaboration between Tunisian and Moroccan agricultural authorities. The integrated strategy includes mechanical control, using tolerant cactus varieties, and biological control through these ladybugs.

records.title: Abu Dhabi launches First-of-its-kind Family Business Index
records.description: Abu Dhabi has launched the groundbreaking Family Business Index in partnership with UAE University and the Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development (ADDED). This initiative aims to rank and analyze family-owned businesses based on key metrics such as revenue, industry impact, governance structures, leadership diversity, and socio-economic contributions. It seeks to deepen understanding of these businesses' role in Abu Dhabi's economy, providing crucial insights for investors, policymakers, and academics. Aligned with Abu Dhabi's family business governance law, the index promotes sustainable economic models and supports smooth generational transitions, reinforcing the emirate's commitment to economic diversification and growth through robust research and strategic planning.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development (ADDED) & United Arab Emirates University (UAEU)
