records.title: ADNOC expands into Europe with strategic deals across chemicals, renewables, and oil and gas sectors, enhancing its global footprint and...
records.description: ADNOC expands into Europe with strategic deals across chemicals, renewables, and oil and gas sectors, enhancing its global footprint and diversifying operations. Key moves include advanced talks for Covestro's acquisition, stake acquisitions in OMV and Fertiglobe, and LNG supply agreements with SEFE and EnBW, marking significant steps in securing Europe's energy market amidst geopolitical shifts.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Dubai-based Alcazar Energy plans to invest $500 million (€466 million) in North Macedonia's largest wind energy project.
records.description: Dubai-based Alcazar Energy plans to invest $500 million (€466 million) in North Macedonia's largest wind energy project. The 400MW Shtip project, located 75km south of Skopje, will increase the country's wind energy capacity more than fivefold. Expected to create over 630 construction jobs, the project will provide clean energy for over 100,000 households annually and reduce CO2 emissions by over 670,000 tonnes per year. This investment aligns with North Macedonia's goal to phase out coal by 2030, as announced at the COP28 climate summit. Alcazar Energy's total planned investments in the western Balkans will reach around $1 billion (€932 million) with this project, alongside the 118MW Bijela wind farm in Montenegro.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Mitsui, in partnership with TA'ZIZ (owned by Adnoc), Fertiglobe, and South Korea's GS Energy Corporation, will construct an ammonia produ...
records.description: Mitsui, in partnership with TA'ZIZ (owned by Adnoc), Fertiglobe, and South Korea's GS Energy Corporation, will construct an ammonia production facility in Al Ruwais, UAE. Starting in 2027, the plant will produce 1 million tons of low-CO2 ammonia annually. To reduce emissions, CO2 capture and storage facilities will be installed, with clean ammonia production planned by 2030. Mitsui will offtake a portion of the clean ammonia for supply to Japan and other Asian markets, supporting decarbonization in fuel, chemical, and fertilizer industries. This project aligns with Mitsui's Global Energy Transition initiative, focusing on next-generation fuels to achieve a decarbonized society.

records.title: Non-oil trade between the UAE and Colombia rose to $553 million in 2023, a 43% increase from 2022 and more than double the 2021 levels.
records.description: Non-oil trade between the UAE and Colombia rose to $553 million in 2023, a 43% increase from 2022 and more than double the 2021 levels. This growth comes as the UAE and Colombia signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (Cepa) and launched a new Emirates flight to Bogota. The Cepa, expected to be implemented by the end of 2024, aims to eliminate tariffs on over 95% of product lines, enhance customs cooperation, and improve market access. Sectors of interest include renewable energy, agriculture, tourism, AI, and free zones. The UAE sees potential in collaborating on green hydrogen and technology with Colombia, the third-largest IT services provider in Latin America. Colombia's exports to the UAE include coffee, flowers, fruits, beef, and agro-industrial products, with total exports reaching $289.4 million in 2023. Emirates' new daily flight to Bogota via Miami will facilitate business and leisure travel, enhancing supply chains and economic ties between the two countries. The UAE’s non-oil trade with Latin America hit a record $13.1 billion in 2023, reflecting the growing importance of these markets to the UAE's diversified economic partnerships.

records.title: Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has planted 3.1 million trees under President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi’s initiative to p...
records.description: Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has planted 3.1 million trees under President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi’s initiative to plant 100 million trees nationwide. The initiative aims to combat climate change, desertification, and boost local wood production while offering environmental, aesthetic, and economic benefits. Coordinating with the Ministry of Local Development and governorates, the project spans 13 governorates and targets various locations including roads, medians, schools, and industrial areas. The first phase delivered 1.3 million trees to seven governorates, while the second phase is supplying 995,000 trees to six more. An additional 800,000 trees have been planted in ministry forests and surrounding areas.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The World Bank has approved a $700 million budget support package for Egypt, the first tranche of a $6 billion program over three years.
records.description: The World Bank has approved a $700 million budget support package for Egypt, the first tranche of a $6 billion program over three years. Aimed at boosting private sector participation, economic resilience, and green growth, the program includes investments in renewable energy and efficiency improvements in sectors like electricity and water. This initiative, titled “Generating Resilience, Opportunities, and Welfare for a Thriving Egypt” Development Policy Financing (DPF), will also enhance state-owned enterprise governance, strengthen the competition authority, improve tax collection, and support climate adaptation measures. This support follows significant financial agreements from the IMF, EU, and UAE, reinforcing Egypt's economic stability and growth.

records.domain: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
records.title: Morocco has announced a substantial investment of MAD 7.47 billion (USD 751.6 million) over the next decade to enhance its date sector, a...
records.description: Morocco has announced a substantial investment of MAD 7.47 billion (USD 751.6 million) over the next decade to enhance its date sector, aiming to increase production to 300,000 tons by 2030. This plan, formalized at the International Agricultural Show in Morocco (SIAM) last year, includes rehabilitating traditional palm groves, establishing new date plantations, and introducing advanced agricultural practices and technologies. Investments will also be made in modern storage and processing infrastructure to efficiently handle the increased production. Morocco aims to boost exports and obtain organic certification for dates from Moroccan oases. Despite a 7% increase in local production in 2023, Morocco imported 103,000 tons of dates between October 2023 and March 2024, maintaining high import volumes primarily from the UAE, Egypt, Tunisia, and Algeria. The investment seeks to strengthen Morocco's presence in the global date market and enhance the cultural and nutritional value of dates, particularly the prized Mejhoul variety.

records.title: Morocco is set to become one of the world’s top six wheat importers in 2024, with imports projected to increase by 19% to 7.5 million ton...
records.description: Morocco is set to become one of the world’s top six wheat importers in 2024, with imports projected to increase by 19% to 7.5 million tons, according to a recent FAO report. This surge is due to a significant 40% drop in domestic wheat production, forecasted to be around 2.5 million tons, due to severe climatic conditions. The Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture estimates the total cereal production for the 2023/2024 season at 31.2 million quintals, a 43% decline from the previous year. The area sown has also decreased by 33%, now covering 2.47 million hectares. To mitigate the shortfall, Morocco is preparing for a sharp increase in wheat imports. This shift highlights the growing import demand from Africa, with the FAO projecting total wheat demand on the continent to reach a record 55.6 million tons. Despite stable or slightly increasing production in neighboring Algeria and Tunisia, Morocco's import needs will significantly rise. Global wheat production in 2024 is expected to stagnate, with a slight decrease to 787 million tons due to reduced harvests in key regions like the EU, Ukraine, and Turkey.
records.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Moroccan Government Council approved a project for the direct marketing of fruits and vegetables, implementing Law No.
records.description: The Moroccan Government Council approved a project for the direct marketing of fruits and vegetables, implementing Law No. 37.21. The decree, presented by Agriculture Minister Mohammed Sadiki, outlines the terms for granting, renewing, and withdrawing authorization for aggregators to market produce directly without using wholesale markets. A technical committee will oversee the authorization process, and a regional committee will ensure compliance with the established conditions and specifications.

records.title: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) continues its humanitarian efforts in Lebanon and Sudan.
records.description: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) continues its humanitarian efforts in Lebanon and Sudan. In northern Lebanon's Miniyeh region, KSrelief-funded Souboul Al-Salam Social Association ambulance service completed 56 emergency missions, transporting patients to hospitals and providing first responder services. In Sudan, KSrelief distributed 620 food packages to displaced families at the Shelter Center in Blue Nile State, benefiting approximately 6,131 individuals as part of the third phase of the Food Security Support Project.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

records.title: Spinneys 1961 Holding has opened its first store in Riyadh's An Nuzha district, with plans to expand to 12 more locations in Saudi Arabia...
records.description: Spinneys 1961 Holding has opened its first store in Riyadh's An Nuzha district, with plans to expand to 12 more locations in Saudi Arabia by 2028. The new store, part of La Strada Yard development, offers premium products and in-house production capabilities. This expansion aligns with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, aiming to boost the retail sector. Spinneys' recent $375 million IPO attracted significant investor interest, reflecting the company's growth and profitability, with a 12.8% year-on-year increase in quarterly net profit to Dhs75 million and a 10.9% rise in revenue to Dhs815 million.

records.title: Tunisia’s olive oil exports have nearly doubled, reaching almost US$1 billion in five months, helping to reduce the current account defic...
records.description: Tunisia’s olive oil exports have nearly doubled, reaching almost US$1 billion in five months, helping to reduce the current account deficit to 2.3% of GDP in 2023 from 8.5% the previous year. This surge has bolstered Tunisia's economy, making it the world’s leading exporter outside the EU. From November 2023 to March 2024, export earnings rose to nearly TND 2.9 billion (US$923 million), an 83% increase from the same period last year. Despite the boost, economic expert James Swanston warns that this is a temporary relief masking deeper financial issues. The 2023/2024 olive oil campaign is optimistic, projecting 200,000 tonnes of production due to favorable conditions and effective pest control. The Sfax region, with 33% of plantations, remains the main production hub.

records.title: Dubai's ruler, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al-Maktoum, announced an ambitious $8 billion plan for a comprehensive stormwater runoff system...
records.description: Dubai's ruler, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al-Maktoum, announced an ambitious $8 billion plan for a comprehensive stormwater runoff system aimed at addressing the aftermath of unprecedented floods that paralyzed the city two months earlier. Set to be completed by 2033, the new rainwater drainage network will cover all areas of Dubai, capable of absorbing over 20 million cubic meters of water daily. Sheikh Mohammed highlighted that this initiative will increase the emirate's rainwater drainage capacity by 700 percent, significantly boosting its resilience against future climate challenges. The plan marks Dubai's largest infrastructure project of its kind, addressing the fallout from record-breaking rains that severely impacted the UAE in April, resulting in casualties and extensive damage across the region.

records.title: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, has approved the Dh30 billion ($8.16 billion) Tasreef project to improve w...
records.description: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, has approved the Dh30 billion ($8.16 billion) Tasreef project to improve water drainage in Dubai. Scheduled for completion by 2033, this initiative will enhance the city's ability to manage climate-related challenges by increasing the drainage network's capacity by 700%, capable of handling over 20 million cubic meters of water daily. The project, the largest rainwater collection system in the region, aims to serve Dubai for the next 100 years. Utilizing advanced tunnel boring machines (TBM) with automated control systems, the project ensures continuous monitoring and safety for workers and equipment. This strategic effort follows previous drainage projects launched in 2019 covering areas like Expo Dubai, Al Maktoum International Airport City, and Jebel Ali, and addresses the heavy rainfall challenges experienced in April, the heaviest in 75 years.

records.title: Ibtissem Mahtout and Amira Messous run an eco-friendly farm near Algiers, pioneering in Algeria's male-dominated agricultural sector.
records.description: Ibtissem Mahtout and Amira Messous run an eco-friendly farm near Algiers, pioneering in Algeria's male-dominated agricultural sector. Graduates in plant ecology and biodiversity, they left the capital four years ago to start their farm in Douaouda. They grow produce without pesticides, promoting ecological farming. Despite initial challenges integrating into a male-dominated field, they received support from local male farmers. With the help of the Torba association, they learned essential farming skills. Using social media, they sell their produce, and on weekends, they offer educational and cultural activities at a larger farm in Zeralda.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) is advancing agricultural sustainability through innovative programs and sma...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) is advancing agricultural sustainability through innovative programs and smart practices, enhancing the sector to support national food security. Operating three applied agricultural research stations, ADAFSA focuses on optimizing resource use and addressing environmental challenges. A key project is the KOREA-UAE Smart Farm Research Project, developing advanced greenhouse models and hydroponic systems. ADAFSA collaborates with Khalifa University to implement modern agricultural technologies, including ICT, AI, post-harvest management, and climate-smart practices, aiming to boost productivity and sustainability in the UAE's agriculture.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) ..

records.title: The UAE and Hungary are exploring ways to strengthen their economic partnership.
records.description: The UAE and Hungary are exploring ways to strengthen their economic partnership. In a recent meeting, officials discussed various strategies to enhance bilateral trade and investment opportunities. This fourth session of the joint economic committee focused on sectors such as renewable energy, technology, and tourism, aiming to foster collaboration and mutual growth.

records.title: Egypt has set a new record for citrus exports to Brazil in the first four months of this year, significantly increasing from previous years.
records.description: Egypt has set a new record for citrus exports to Brazil in the first four months of this year, significantly increasing from previous years. Entering the Brazilian market in 2020 with just 75 tons, Egypt's citrus exports surged to over 14,000 tons by 2023. From January to April 2024, Egyptian exporters sold over 31,000 tons of citrus to Brazil, surpassing Spain, their main competitor, by threefold. Oranges are the primary export, with Egypt supplying nearly 12,000 tons in 2023 and 24,000 tons in the first four months of 2024. Additionally, Egypt exported almost 7,000 tons of mandarins, up from 2,000 tons last year, while lemon and grapefruit exports were 500 tons and 190 tons, respectively. Brazil, a major citrus producer, imports fresh oranges, mandarins, and grapefruits due to its focus on orange juice production, with Egypt and Spain being the leading suppliers from December to May.

records.title: Morocco continues to maintain high import rates for dates during the 2023/24 season, importing 103,000 tons between October 2023 and Marc...
records.description: Morocco continues to maintain high import rates for dates during the 2023/24 season, importing 103,000 tons between October 2023 and March 2024, nearly matching the previous season's figures. However, imports may fall slightly short of last year's total due to a 7% increase in local date production, which reached 115,000 tons. The peak of date imports aligns with Ramadan, which in 2024 occurred in February, suggesting lower volumes for the remainder of the season. Morocco, the second-largest global date importer after India, sources 90% of its imports from the UAE, Egypt, Tunisia, and Algeria. Notably, Egypt may surpass the UAE this season, having already supplied 33,000 tons of dates to Morocco.

records.title: Abu Dhabi’s Silal has launched a new 41,000-square-meter food distribution facility in Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (KEZAD).
records.description: Abu Dhabi’s Silal has launched a new 41,000-square-meter food distribution facility in Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (KEZAD). Equipped with 36,800 storage platforms, advanced cold rooms, and the latest logistical technologies, this facility is set to become a major food distribution hub in the UAE. It features 38 loading docks and 36 loading points, enhancing transportation logistics and trading opportunities. The facility also includes re-export and repackaging capabilities, helping manage supply chain disruptions. It aims to foster sustainable partnerships with local and global distributors, ensuring a continuous supply of essential food products. This launch is part of Abu Dhabi’s strategy to become a global supply chain hub, supporting the UAE’s food security agenda. Earlier this year, Silal opened a high-tech packhouse in Al Ain, capable of processing 216 tons of fresh produce daily. The packhouse uses advanced technology for efficient post-harvest operations, reinforcing Silal’s commitment to sustainability and local agriculture.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Masdar, the UAE's renewable energy company, has agreed to acquire an initial 67% stake in Greece's Terna Energy from GEK Terna and other...
records.description: Masdar, the UAE's renewable energy company, has agreed to acquire an initial 67% stake in Greece's Terna Energy from GEK Terna and other shareholders for EUR 20 ($21.45) per share, valuing the company at EUR 2.4 billion with an enterprise value of EUR 3.2 billion. Following regulatory approvals, Masdar plans a mandatory tender offer to acquire the remaining shares, aiming for full ownership. This move is part of Masdar's strategy to expand in Europe, Asia, and the US, with a goal of reaching 100 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2030. Owned by TAQA, Mubadala, and ADNOC, Masdar's investment underscores the UAE’s commitment to clean energy in Greece and Europe.

records.title: UAE Ministry of Finance Unveils Key New Projects to Boost Competitiveness
records.description: The UAE Ministry of Finance has unveiled strategic projects aimed at boosting the country's financial sector and enhancing global competitiveness. These initiatives align with the UAE's broader strategy to future-proof its economy and reinforce its status as a leading global financial hub over the next decade, in line with the ‘We the UAE 2031’ vision. Minister Mohamed Hadi Al Hussaini emphasized the focus on digital transformation, improving government operations, and attracting foreign investments. Key projects include developing the local debt capital market in collaboration with the Central Bank of the UAE and enhancing the presence of specialized Emirati leaders in international financial forums through partnerships with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. These efforts aim to position the UAE as a prominent player in international cooperation and strengthen its economic partnerships worldwide.

records.title: From September 2023 to February 2024, Egypt exported 45,000 tons of strawberries worth $129 million, comprising 2% of the total agricultu...
records.description: From September 2023 to February 2024, Egypt exported 45,000 tons of strawberries worth $129 million, comprising 2% of the total agricultural export volume and 6% of the value. These exports, part of Egypt's 2.82 million tons of vegetable and fruit exports valued at about $2 billion, were primarily sent to Saudi Arabia, Russia, and Britain.

records.title: Morocco's agricultural sector is poised to break its own record for fresh asparagus exports for the fourth consecutive season.
records.description: Morocco's agricultural sector is poised to break its own record for fresh asparagus exports for the fourth consecutive season. According to EastFruit, Morocco exported 320 tons of asparagus between November 2022 and March 2024, surpassing the 260 tons exported in the same period last year. Traditionally harvested between January and March, Moroccan asparagus has seen strong sales extend through May in the past two years. The European Union remains a key market, with Belgium now the top recipient of Moroccan asparagus, followed by Spain, France, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom. Morocco is also exploring new markets in the Middle East, with small shipments to Bahrain, Qatar, and Jordan. The global market for asparagus is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.2%, reaching USD 33.8 billion by 2030, driven by increasing consumer awareness of healthy eating. Morocco's growing asparagus exports and market diversification efforts position it well to capitalize on this global demand.

records.title: An emergency wheat production project in Sudan, financed by the African Development Bank and executed by the United Nations World Food Pr...
records.description: An emergency wheat production project in Sudan, financed by the African Development Bank and executed by the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), has significantly boosted wheat production by up to 70% in targeted areas across five states over the past year. With a $75 million funding from the African Development Bank, the Sudan Emergency Wheat Production Project has been crucial amid ongoing conflict and looming hunger crises. This initiative has yielded 645,000 metric tonnes of wheat this year alone, meeting 22% of Sudan's national wheat demand. It has provided critical food security and livelihood support to over 170,000 smallholder farmers, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), demonstrating resilience amidst challenging conditions.
records.institution: African Development Bank & World Food Programme (WFP)

records.title: Sotipapier, a Tunisian supplier of corrugated and kraft sack paper, has acquired a 70% stake in Eco-Gad, a prominent recycling company ba...
records.description: Sotipapier, a Tunisian supplier of corrugated and kraft sack paper, has acquired a 70% stake in Eco-Gad, a prominent recycling company based in Sidi Hassine, Tunisia. This acquisition positions Sotipapier as the majority shareholder of Eco-Gad, known for its extensive operations across North Africa in collecting and processing paper, cardboard, and plastic waste. Eco-Gad's six centers cater to various sectors with B2B solutions, supported by its innovative subsidiary, Colibris, which facilitates waste collection through a specialized application. The partnership aims to expand Eco-Gad's footprint in Tunisia with new sorting centers and explore international opportunities, enhancing recycling capabilities and reinforcing Sotipapier's commitment to environmental sustainability in the North African region.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Masdar, a UAE-based renewable energy firm owned by ADNOC, has struck a landmark deal to acquire a majority stake in Greece's Terna Energy.
records.description: Masdar, a UAE-based renewable energy firm owned by ADNOC, has struck a landmark deal to acquire a majority stake in Greece's Terna Energy. The acquisition, valued at €2.4 billion in equity and €3.2 billion in enterprise value, marks the largest energy transaction on the Athens Stock Exchange. Masdar plans to initially purchase 67% of Terna's outstanding shares, with intentions to eventually acquire the remaining shares through a mandatory tender offer, aiming for full ownership. This move aligns with Masdar's goal to achieve 100 gigawatts of global renewable energy capacity by 2030, emphasizing their strategic expansion in the European Union's renewables sector.

records.title: Algeria has partnered with the Italian company Bonifiche Ferraresi (BF) to enhance wheat production with a US$420 million investment.
records.description: Algeria has partnered with the Italian company Bonifiche Ferraresi (BF) to enhance wheat production with a US$420 million investment. Announced on June 3 by Omar Rekkache, General Director of the Algerian Investment Promotion Agency (AAPI), this initiative will establish a large agricultural project in the Wilaya of Timimoun, backed by the National Investment Fund (FNI). The project aims to cultivate cereals over 36,000 hectares to reduce Algeria's reliance on wheat imports, currently over 75%, and strengthen food security. Additionally, the project includes constructing a pasta manufacturing factory for export. This investment aligns with Algeria's broader agricultural strategy and comes as the country anticipates a significant wheat harvest increase. According to USDA projections, Algeria’s wheat production is expected to rise by 11%, reaching 3 million tonnes in the 2024/2025 season, potentially making Algeria the second-largest wheat producer in North Africa after Egypt.
records.institution: Algerian Investment Promotion Agency (AAPI) & Bonifiche Ferraresi (BF)

records.description: Algeria's collaboration with Italian company Bonifiche Ferraresi (BF) to boost wheat production involves a significant US$420 million investment facilitated by the Algerian Investment Promotion Agency (AAPI) and the National Investment Fund (FNI). The project aims to cultivate cereals across 36,000 hectares in Timimoun, focusing on reducing wheat imports and enhancing food security. It includes plans for a pasta manufacturing factory for export, promising to create jobs and stimulate agricultural innovation, aligning with Algeria's strategic goals to bolster its cereal industry amidst high domestic wheat consumption and favorable production forecasts for the upcoming season.

records.title: American engineering firm KBR has secured a $46 million, five-year contract to support the Iraqi government's infrastructure and future e...
records.description: American engineering firm KBR has secured a $46 million, five-year contract to support the Iraqi government's infrastructure and future energy goals, including megaprojects and sustainable development. Under this contract, KBR will provide advisory and consultancy services to the Ministry of Planning, focusing on economic planning, strategy development, feasibility studies, technical reviews, and large-scale project management. This initiative aims to elevate Iraq's energy sector and align with its long-term vision for growth and environmental stewardship. KBR plans to expand its presence in Iraq by establishing an operational office in Baghdad and potentially creating an engineering design center to enhance local engineers' skills.

records.title: The watermelon season in Morocco has been severely impacted by factors such as water scarcity, production restrictions, and pest infestat...
records.description: The watermelon season in Morocco has been severely impacted by factors such as water scarcity, production restrictions, and pest infestations, particularly aphids affecting quality in regions like Taroudante and Marrakech. The Ministry of the Interior's recommendation to reduce acreage has exacerbated these challenges, leading to a significant drop in harvests and shortages in local and export markets. To address these issues, Moroccan company Valyour has sought solutions abroad, including consulting Italian growers on combating aphids and exploring Dutch techniques to optimize water usage in cultivation, aiming to enhance future harvest quality and sustainability.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Chinese PV cell manufacturer Hainan Drinda New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.
records.description: Chinese PV cell manufacturer Hainan Drinda New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. has announced plans to establish Oman's inaugural solar PV cell factory, aimed at producing up to 10 GW of TOPcon solar photovoltaic cells annually. The project, backed by a preliminary agreement with the Oman Investment Authority (OIA), entails an estimated investment of USD 700 million (EUR 653.3m). Hainan Drinda intends to deploy the production capacity in two phases of 5 GW each, marking a significant milestone in Oman's strategy to bolster its solar energy infrastructure and advance green hydrogen initiatives. This initiative aligns with Oman's broader ambitions to integrate substantial solar power capacity to support its burgeoning green hydrogen production targets, aiming to produce over 1 million tonnes of green hydrogen annually by the decade's end.
records.institution: Hainan Drinda New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.

records.title: Qatar Charity has made a significant impact through its 'Qurbani Program' in Bangladesh, benefiting over 20,000 underprivileged individua...
records.description: Qatar Charity has made a significant impact through its 'Qurbani Program' in Bangladesh, benefiting over 20,000 underprivileged individuals, including orphans and widows. The initiative involved distributing sacrificial animal meat across 18 locations, including orphan care centers, throughout the country. Led by Dr. Mohammad Amin Hafiz Omar, Qatar Charity ensured the efficient and heartfelt delivery of meat, fostering solidarity and compassion during Eid ul-Azha. Government officials also supported the program, underscoring its importance in alleviating food insecurity and bringing joy to vulnerable communities. Recipients, such as widow Salma Akhter and farmer Sultan Ahmed, expressed deep gratitude for Qatar Charity's generosity, highlighting the program's profound impact on their Eid celebrations.

records.title: Seafood Souq, based in Dubai, has forged an exclusive partnership with Argentine seafood supplier Newsan Food, marking a pivotal developm...
records.description: Seafood Souq, based in Dubai, has forged an exclusive partnership with Argentine seafood supplier Newsan Food, marking a pivotal development in direct seafood exports from Argentina to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region and beyond. This strategic alliance, highlighted in a recent press release, grants Seafood Souq exclusive distribution rights for Newsan Food products in the GCC. Seafood Souq, known for its innovative digital platform facilitating seafood trading, will leverage this partnership to expand its market reach and enhance trade transparency. Newsan Food, a significant player with annual revenues exceeding US$1 billion, operates a fleet of 40 fishing vessels, 16 processing plants, and three large cold storage facilities, ensuring a robust supply chain for its premium seafood offerings worldwide.

records.title: Under the Sheikh Zayed Falcon Release Programme, established in 1995 by the late founding father of the UAE, over 2,000 falcons have been...
records.description: Under the Sheikh Zayed Falcon Release Programme, established in 1995 by the late founding father of the UAE, over 2,000 falcons have been successfully reintroduced into their natural habitats after undergoing extensive veterinary examinations, training, and implantation of electronic chips. This milestone marks the programme's 30th edition, with 63 falcons recently released across migratory areas spanning Kazakhstan, Russia, China, Mongolia, and neighboring regions. Supervised by Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture, the initiative underscores Abu Dhabi and the UAE's commitment to wildlife conservation, particularly for falcons and other ecologically significant species. The programme aligns with Sheikh Zayed's legacy of preserving falconry traditions and safeguarding species from extinction through scientific research and habitat restoration efforts.
records.institution: The Forestry and Wildlife Committee in the Kazakh Ministry of Agriculture

records.title: Brazilian poultry has established a foothold in Algeria, opening new trade avenues.
records.description: Brazilian poultry has established a foothold in Algeria, opening new trade avenues. Since October 2023, Algeria has welcomed over 10,000 tons of Brazilian frozen chicken, signaling a promising start to this market entry. Regulatory changes by the Algerian government have streamlined import procedures, enhancing Brazil’s competitiveness. Luis Rua from ABPA highlights the strategic importance of this development, foreseeing Brazil becoming a major chicken supplier to Algeria. This trade surge underscores Algeria's growing demand for Brazilian chicken, benefiting both nations by ensuring food security and expanding market access.
records.institution: Algerian Government & Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (APBA)

records.title: Egypt has achieved significant success in agricultural exports, particularly in citrus fruits, exporting 1.143 million tons valued at $57...
records.description: Egypt has achieved significant success in agricultural exports, particularly in citrus fruits, exporting 1.143 million tons valued at $576 million over a six-month period from September 2023 to February 2024. This accounts for 40% of Egypt's total export volume and 29% of its export value during that period. Overall, Egypt exported approximately 2.82 million tons of vegetables and fruits worth around $2 billion, with Saudi Arabia, Russia, and Britain leading as top importers of Egyptian produce. The robust export performance underscores Egypt's pivotal role in the global agricultural market.

records.title: Recent data from the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture highlights a significant decline in orange imports from Egypt into the EU, with cons...
records.description: Recent data from the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture highlights a significant decline in orange imports from Egypt into the EU, with consecutive monthly drops of 22% in April and 27% in May compared to the previous year. Despite these declines, overall imports from Egypt for the 2024 season remain slightly higher than the same period in 2023 and significantly above the five-year average. This trend underscores challenges in the citrus market, particularly affecting Egyptian exports, while highlighting shifts in consumer preferences and market dynamics within the EU citrus trade.

records.title: Sudan has experienced a remarkable 70% increase in wheat production, reaching 645,000 metric tonnes this year, thanks to the AfDB-finance...
records.description: Sudan has experienced a remarkable 70% increase in wheat production, reaching 645,000 metric tonnes this year, thanks to the AfDB-financed Sudan Emergency Wheat Production Project. This initiative, supported by the World Food Programme, addresses severe humanitarian crises by providing food security to vulnerable populations, including Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) across five states. The project's impact includes significant productivity gains per hectare and the distribution of climate-adapted seeds and fertilizers to over 170,000 smallholder farmers, underscoring its role in both short-term relief and long-term resilience building amidst ongoing conflict and food insecurity in Sudan.
records.institution: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) & the African Development Bank (AfDB)

records.title: The Syrian Interim Government (SIG) has sparked controversy by setting low wheat purchase prices for the 2023-2024 agricultural season in...
records.description: The Syrian Interim Government (SIG) has sparked controversy by setting low wheat purchase prices for the 2023-2024 agricultural season in its controlled areas, with first-grade soft wheat priced at $220 per ton. This decision, significantly lower than previous seasons and other regional authorities' rates, has triggered dissatisfaction and protests among farmers in areas like Ras al-Ain. Critics argue that the SIG's pricing strategy neglects the high costs incurred by farmers for seeds, fertilizers, and labor, potentially jeopardizing food security and prompting farmers to consider abandoning wheat cultivation altogether. Economic pressures and limited financial resources are cited by SIG officials as reasons for maintaining these lower prices, despite concerns about their impact on agricultural sustainability and rural livelihoods.

records.title: The UAE has significantly bolstered its support for humanitarian efforts in Sudan with a pledge of $70 million in aid to UN agencies, as...
records.description: The UAE has significantly bolstered its support for humanitarian efforts in Sudan with a pledge of $70 million in aid to UN agencies, as announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. This funding will be directed towards various UN bodies including the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, the World Food Programme, and others, focusing on critical needs such as food, health services, protection for vulnerable groups, and emergency shelter. This initiative underscores the UAE's commitment to addressing the multifaceted humanitarian crisis in Sudan, reflecting its ongoing efforts to provide substantial aid and relief amidst ongoing conflict and displacement.

records.title: The Relizane region in Algeria has achieved a historic milestone in citrus production, harvesting over 650,000 tonnes this year.
records.description: The Relizane region in Algeria has achieved a historic milestone in citrus production, harvesting over 650,000 tonnes this year. Headed by Bachir Koudri of the Directorate of Agricultural Services (DSA), the region recorded 653,530 quintals of citrus fruits across 4,691 hectares, primarily in irrigated areas like lower Cheliff and the “Mina” plain. Benefiting from favorable climatic conditions and enhanced water access through modernized infrastructure, farmers have seen an average yield of 140 quintals per hectare, led by varieties like "Thomson" oranges, clementines, and lemons. This record-breaking production not only underscores the region's agricultural dynamism but also its economic importance, sustaining local livelihoods and reinforcing agricultural diversity amidst ongoing challenges and opportunities for innovation.

records.title: The Iraqi government aims to enhance economic and trade integration with Lebanon and other regional countries.
records.description: The Iraqi government aims to enhance economic and trade integration with Lebanon and other regional countries. Discussions included rehabilitating oil pipelines between Syria and Lebanon with Iraqi investment and extending an Arab optical fiber communications network. The NIC promotes an attractive investment environment under the amended Investment Law No. 13 of 2006, ensuring investor rights and offering advantages for successful projects. The Lebanese minister expressed readiness for joint development efforts.

records.title: ACWA Power Co, in partnership with UzKimyoSanoat, has applied for USD 21.2 million in debt funding from the European Bank for Reconstruct...
records.description: ACWA Power Co, in partnership with UzKimyoSanoat, has applied for USD 21.2 million in debt funding from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to finance a 20-MW hydrogen plant in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region. The project aims to establish an electrolyser in Chirchiq capable of producing 3,000 tonnes of green hydrogen annually. This initiative will leverage electricity from a 52-MW wind farm within the EBRD-backed 500-MW Bash wind complex in Bukhara, southwestern Uzbekistan. The funding request, part of a broader loan package totaling USD 55.4 million, is set for approval by June 26, supporting Uzbekistan's renewable energy ambitions and hydrogen production capabilities.

records.title: Thailand has received authorization from Saudi Arabia to export live cattle, sheep, and goats, marking a significant development in bilat...
records.description: Thailand has received authorization from Saudi Arabia to export live cattle, sheep, and goats, marking a significant development in bilateral trade relations. Under the agreement, which includes hygiene certificates for livestock, Thai animals can now be imported into Saudi Arabia for rearing and slaughter. This approval, conveyed through Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture to Thailand's embassy in Riyadh, follows earlier approvals for the export of Thai chicken products. The move aims to boost trade between the two countries, with Thailand directing relevant agencies to inform and assist exporters in meeting the necessary regulatory requirements for this new market opportunity.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Emirates Red Crescent (ERC) has initiated a project to distribute sacrificial meat from animals slaughtered during Eid Al Adha in Yem...
records.description: The Emirates Red Crescent (ERC) has initiated a project to distribute sacrificial meat from animals slaughtered during Eid Al Adha in Yemen's Hadhramaut province. On the first day of Eid, 279 portions of meat were distributed to 1,116 families, including vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities and hospital patients. By the end of the holiday, the ERC aims to distribute a total of 904 portions of meat, benefiting approximately 6,328 individuals. This effort is part of the UAE's ongoing humanitarian and relief initiatives, aimed at improving living conditions and supporting underprivileged communities across the Middle East.

records.title: The UAE is projected to see a substantial increase in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), with these vehicles potentially constituti...
records.description: The UAE is projected to see a substantial increase in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), with these vehicles potentially constituting up to 25% of all new passenger cars and light commercial vehicle sales by 2035, driven by the country's decarbonisation goals. Currently, EVs account for only 3% of vehicle sales in the UAE, but this figure is expected to rise to over 15% by 2030. Factors influencing this growth include expanding EV model options, investments in charging infrastructure, and declining total ownership costs. The UAE aims to enhance its EV ecosystem swiftly, leveraging lessons from earlier adopter countries to accelerate its transition towards a low-carbon economy under its Energy Strategy 2050.

records.title: Bahrain's livestock industry faces a critical challenge following Bahrain Flour Mills' abrupt decision to double the price of wheat bran,...
records.description: Bahrain's livestock industry faces a critical challenge following Bahrain Flour Mills' abrupt decision to double the price of wheat bran, a vital feed for livestock and poultry, effective June 16, 2024. This unexpected hike has stirred deep concerns among farmers and officials alike, with MP Mohammed Yousif Al Maarafi labeling it as a significant threat to food security and a potential detriment to the entire agricultural sector. The move, implemented without prior consultation or explanation, has prompted fears of higher food prices and a shift towards imported livestock, exacerbating the already precarious situation for local breeders and traders.

records.title: The Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has extended fee discounts in response to a significant drop in traffic and revenues amidst ongoing region...
records.description: The Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has extended fee discounts in response to a significant drop in traffic and revenues amidst ongoing regional tensions affecting global shipping routes. May 2024 saw revenues decline by 64.3% to $337.8 million from $648 million in May 2023, with ship transits falling sharply to 1,111 from 2,396 and cargo tonnage decreasing by 68.5% to 44.9 million tons. Major shipping lines are diverting around Africa due to the Red Sea crisis, impacting canal traffic. Finance Minister Mohamed Maait has acknowledged potential further revenue challenges despite last year's record earnings of $9.4 billion, prompting the SCA to sustain fee reductions through year-end across various vessel categories and introduce special discounts for yachts to promote marine tourism during the Egypt International Yacht Show from July to October.

records.title: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has released an 18-page report titled 'Climate Vulnerability Assessment in the Kurdist...
records.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has released an 18-page report titled 'Climate Vulnerability Assessment in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq', highlighting critical issues exacerbated by climate change and environmental degradation. These include rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, severe droughts, water scarcity, and frequent sand and dust storms. These challenges are compounded by factors such as inadequate water management policies, inefficient infrastructure, population growth, and intensive irrigation practices. Despite the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) having distinct climate and geographical features compared to central and southern Iraq, there remains a significant lack of specific data and analysis. The region's reliance on rain-fed agriculture further exposes it to vulnerabilities, impacting farmers, livestock rearers, and fishers alike. The report underscores the urgent need for targeted interventions and data-driven strategies to mitigate these risks and enhance resilience in the face of climate change impacts.

records.title: Under the auspices of Oman's Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, the...
records.description: Under the auspices of Oman's Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, the Saham Agricultural City (SAC) project is poised to revolutionize agricultural and urban development in Oman. Spanning 65 square kilometers, with 70% dedicated to agriculture, SAC aims to ensure food security for 25,000 people annually through innovative practices like hydroponics and aquaculture. Located strategically in Saham for its fertile soil and existing infrastructure, SAC integrates sustainable urban planning with modern agricultural techniques, aligning closely with Oman Vision 2040's goals for economic diversification and environmental sustainability.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning & Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.description: Broaden Energy has partnered with the Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development (ADDED) to establish Abu Dhabi’s inaugural hydrogen equipment manufacturing facility, a venture valued at over Dhs1 billion. This initiative, aligned with Abu Dhabi's Industrial Strategy, aims to bolster sustainability efforts, strengthen value chains, and enhance the emirate's industrial competitiveness. Supported by the UAE National Hydrogen Strategy and Net Zero 2050 Strategy, the project seeks to propel the UAE into the top 10 global producers of green hydrogen by 2031, targeting an annual production of 1.4 million tonnes. By fostering hydrogen hubs and infrastructure, the collaboration intends to drive widespread industry adoption and attract international energy leaders, contributing significantly to a sustainable future aligned with the UAE's strategic vision.

records.title: Kidzink, a Dubai-based educational and architectural firm, in collaboration with UK's Waste to Wonder Worldwide, is set to establish a co...
records.description: Kidzink, a Dubai-based educational and architectural firm, in collaboration with UK's Waste to Wonder Worldwide, is set to establish a community culinary school and sustainable farm in West Africa, specifically in The Gambia. This initiative aims to empower young people with skills in sustainable cooking, agriculture, hospitality, and tourism, fostering environmental consciousness and community development. The project will also engage local community members in employment opportunities and support local businesses. Chef Conor Spacey, renowned for his 'Zero-waste' culinary approach, will contribute expertise in sustainable practices, ensuring the project aligns with circular economy principles. Waste to Wonder Worldwide's involvement will further enhance educational facilities through ethical furniture redistribution, promoting sustainable outcomes and socio-economic empowerment in The Gambia and beyond.

The meeting, which took place recently, highlighted the ministry's initiatives in monitoring local market goods and services to ensure compliance with health standards. The discussions also encompassed exploring opportunities in African and European export markets to contribute to the overall economic development goals of the country.

records.title: The World Food Programme (WFP) has been actively supporting humanitarian efforts in Libya, providing food aid to 64,835 people in May alo...
records.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) has been actively supporting humanitarian efforts in Libya, providing food aid to 64,835 people in May alone, which included distributing five tons of food supplies and $1.43 million in cash transfers. The WFP's operations also extend to assisting Sudanese refugees in Libya, with a total of 40,081 registered refugees by May 2024. Recognizing ongoing needs, the WFP has launched a funding appeal totaling $15.8 million for the period from June to November 2024, and a separate appeal of $43.8 million specifically aimed at supporting 55,000 food-insecure Sudanese refugees through its Refugee Response Plan for Sudanese in Libya (RPSL). Additionally, the WFP has bolstered its emergency food stocks in Tripoli and Benghazi, and plans to implement a supplementary nutrition program benefiting children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and girls in Kufra with ready-to-use supplementary food and family rations.

records.description: Egypt's Minister of International Cooperation, Dr. Rania Al-Mashat, has emphasized the deepening collaboration with the Spanish Agency for International Cooperation for Development during a recent meeting with its President, Natwan Les Garizia. They discussed enhancing bilateral relations and expanding joint efforts across various sectors. Currently, the Spanish Agency supports 20 programs in Egypt, focusing on areas such as women's empowerment, water resources management, and skills development in Upper Egypt. Minister Al-Mashat highlighted the importance of broadening cooperation to further bolster Egypt's private sector, economic development, and job creation initiatives. She also underscored initiatives like the "Hafiz" platform, aimed at integrating financial and technical support for businesses.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of International Cooperation & Spanish Agency for International Cooperation for Development

records.title: Over the past five years, Egypt has made substantial strides in its export of vegetables and fruits to Poland, culminating in its rise to...
records.description: Over the past five years, Egypt has made substantial strides in its export of vegetables and fruits to Poland, culminating in its rise to the ninth position among suppliers by the end of 2023, up from fourteenth in 2019 and sixteenth in 2020. This growth has been particularly pronounced in categories such as frozen strawberries and oranges, where exports have nearly tripled and doubled, respectively, since 2019. Egypt has solidified its position as a leading supplier of frozen strawberries to Poland, contributing around 80% of the total imported volume in 2023. Additionally, Egypt ranks prominently in other categories like garlic, oranges, red onions, and potatoes, highlighting its increasing significance in Poland's agricultural imports. In 2023 alone, Poland spent approximately $85 million on vegetable and fruit imports from Egypt, marking a significant increase from just over $36 million recorded five years earlier.

records.title: Norwegian company Waterise has teamed up with Jordan's sole phosphate producer, Jordan Phosphate Mines Company (JPMC), to build and manag...
records.description: Norwegian company Waterise has teamed up with Jordan's sole phosphate producer, Jordan Phosphate Mines Company (JPMC), to build and manage a desalination plant near Aqaba, aimed at addressing water scarcity in Jordan. This partnership plans to produce 18 million cubic meters of desalinated water annually, primarily for JPMC's fertilizer plant, replacing freshwater sourced from nearby aquifers. Niels Petter Wright, CEO of Waterise, highlighted the environmental benefits of their deep sea desalination technology, which requires less energy and land area compared to conventional methods. The project, expected to span two years, is a collaborative effort with Jordanian authorities to meet water demands and support economic expansion in the region.

records.title: In Doha, Qatar, the Ministry of Municipality, represented by the Agricultural Affairs Department, has launched 13 new electronic services...
records.description: In Doha, Qatar, the Ministry of Municipality, represented by the Agricultural Affairs Department, has launched 13 new electronic services aimed at enhancing digital transformation within the agricultural sector. These services, accessible through the ministry's website, streamline processes such as importing permits for fruits, vegetables, plants, seedlings, palm trees, offshoots, natural wood, and plant parts. Additionally, permits for green and dry grain fodder, fertilizers, agricultural soil enhancers, cut flowers, honeybees, pesticides, and restricted-use fertilizers are now available online. This initiative aligns with Qatar's National Development Strategy 2024-2030 and Qatar National Vision 2030, emphasizing efficiency gains, paperless transactions, and enhanced service accessibility across sectors including agriculture, urban planning, and public services. The project integrates advanced technologies like blockchain, big data analytics, machine learning, and AI to ensure secure, efficient, and user-friendly service delivery round the clock.

records.description: The UAE has expressed keen interest in investing across various sectors in Türkiye, highlighting energy, agriculture, transportation, tourism, and others as potential areas for collaboration. This sentiment was underscored by UAE Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazrouei, who emphasized Türkiye's robust economy and strategic importance as a partner. Al-Mazrouei noted Türkiye's openness to renewable energy, an area where the UAE has significant expertise, suggesting opportunities for expanding renewable energy projects and partnering with Turkish companies. The UAE aims to strengthen bilateral relations through increased investments and strategic partnerships, leveraging Türkiye's role as a crucial hub for energy infrastructure and regional connectivity.

records.title: Yemen Signs Its First Country Programme Framework (CPF) for 2024–2029
records.description: Yemen recently signed its inaugural Country Programme Framework (CPF) for 2024–2029 with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). The agreement, signed by HE Mr. Haytham Adbulmomen Hassan Shoja’aadin and Mr. Hua Liu, outlines strategic areas for technical cooperation to support Yemen's national development goals. These priorities include enhancing nuclear and radiation safety, advancing food and agriculture capabilities, improving health and nutrition services, managing water resources sustainably, and fostering nuclear science and technology. This CPF signifies Yemen's commitment to leveraging nuclear technology for socio-economic progress and environmental sustainability under the guidance and support of the IAEA.

records.title: Egypt and the United States have solidified their longstanding partnership with the signing of eight non-refundable development grants to...
records.description: Egypt and the United States have solidified their longstanding partnership with the signing of eight non-refundable development grants totaling $130 million from USAID. The agreements, signed by Egyptian Minister of International Cooperation Dr. Rania Al-Mashat and US Ambassador Hero Mustafa Garg, aim to support Egypt's development vision across various sectors. These include economic governance, higher education, basic education, health outcomes improvement, agribusiness, trade and investment environment enhancement, climate change, and water support solutions. Dr. Al-Mashat highlighted the significance of these grants in advancing Egypt's sustainable development goals and managing economic relations with international partners. Ambassador Garg underscored the US government's commitment to fostering economic opportunities and improving living conditions in Egypt through these initiatives.
records.institution: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)

records.description: President Mohammed Menfi of the Presidential Council (PC) met with the Greek Ambassador to Libya, Nikolaos Garilidis, to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral relations between Libya and Greece. The meeting, held on Wednesday, focused on exploring opportunities for mutual benefit and enhancing cooperation in various sectors. Specifically, they reviewed current bilateral relations comprehensively and strategized on ways to bolster and advance these ties. Key topics included facilitating trade exchanges, reintroducing Greek companies into Libya, and reinstating air travel between the two nations. This dialogue underscores efforts to deepen diplomatic and economic collaboration between Libya and Greece.

records.title: In 2023, trade between Egypt and Arab states reached $26 billion, according to a report from the Central Agency for Public Mobilization a...
records.description: In 2023, trade between Egypt and Arab states reached $26 billion, according to a report from the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS). This figure includes exports totaling $13.6 billion and imports amounting to $12.4 billion. Saudi Arabia emerged as the largest importer from Egypt with $2.7 billion, followed by the UAE with $2.2 billion, Libya with $1.8 billion, Sudan with $984.4 million, and Algeria with $850.3 million. Egypt's top exports included vegetables and fruits valued at $1.3 billion, home appliances and machinery at $1.1 billion, pearls, precious stones, and jewelry at $1 billion, fuel and mineral oils at $753 million, and plastics at $712 million.
records.institution: Egyptian Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: The winners of the International Trade Centre's Agriculture Innovation Hackathon, held in Nineveh province, have been announced, highligh...
records.description: The winners of the International Trade Centre's Agriculture Innovation Hackathon, held in Nineveh province, have been announced, highlighting innovative solutions to address water scarcity and promote sustainable agriculture in Iraq. Nabu focused on transforming excess tomato crops into valuable products, BSF utilized black soldier fly larvae for organic waste disposal and fertilizer production, and Aero Plant introduced vertical aeroponics to reduce water usage. Each winner received a seed grant to further develop their ideas, with Zaid Jaber from Nabu securing a larger grant to implement their solution. The hackathon, supported by Mosul Space and funded by the EU through the SAAVI project, underscored the potential of technology to enhance agricultural resilience and sustainability amid local challenges.

records.title: China is seeking to forge a new fisheries cooperation agreement with Mauritania, focusing on wild fisheries capture, aquaculture developm...
records.description: China is seeking to forge a new fisheries cooperation agreement with Mauritania, focusing on wild fisheries capture, aquaculture development, and combating illegal fishing practices. During talks in Nouakchott, China's Deputy Minister for Agriculture Ma Youxiang discussed enhancing collaboration with Mauritania's Fisheries Minister Mokhtar El Housseinou Lam. Mauritania welcomes Chinese investments in aquaculture and fish processing, highlighting past agreements and ongoing infrastructure projects that support seafood exports to China and Europe. Chinese involvement also extends to port redevelopment initiatives aimed at bolstering local industries, generating employment, and improving food security in Mauritania.
records.institution: Mauritanian Ministry of Fisheries and Maritime Economy

records.title: Egypt and Equatorial Guinea are strengthening their bilateral ties across security, trade, and infrastructure following high-level talks...
records.description: Egypt and Equatorial Guinea are strengthening their bilateral ties across security, trade, and infrastructure following high-level talks in Egypt's New Administrative Capital. Led by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and Equatorial Guinea's Vice President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, the discussions focused on deepening cooperation in various sectors. Egypt reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Equatorial Guinea's economic and security development, including sending experts to enhance internal security and facilitating trade agreements. Plans also include supporting infrastructure projects like the Malabo oil refinery and exploring new initiatives such as a diplomatic academy and agricultural partnerships. The meeting underscored mutual cooperation with agreements in health, academic exchanges, and security cooperation, highlighting both nations' commitment to strengthening their partnership.

records.title: Egypt is actively pursuing a $1 billion soft loan from the New Development Bank (NDB) associated with the BRICS bloc, as revealed by Fina...
records.description: Egypt is actively pursuing a $1 billion soft loan from the New Development Bank (NDB) associated with the BRICS bloc, as revealed by Finance Minister Mohamed Maait. Expected to be secured by the end of 2024, the loan aims to fund mutually agreed-upon projects, with disbursement possible in dollars or alternative currencies. Maait expressed optimism about finalizing the loan either by late 2024 or early 2025. The collaboration with NDB aligns with Egypt's economic and social development goals, supporting infrastructure and sustainable projects, as outlined in NDB President Dilma Rousseff's strategy to allocate $30 billion for 2022-2026, prioritizing climate change and sustainable energy initiatives.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Finance & the New Development Bank (NDB)

records.title: Egypt's commitment to bolstering its agricultural sector continues with the allocation of 44 billion Egyptian pounds (approximately US$92...
records.description: Egypt's commitment to bolstering its agricultural sector continues with the allocation of 44 billion Egyptian pounds (approximately US$922.4 million) for purchasing locally produced wheat, announced by Finance Minister Mohamed Maait. This initiative aims to reduce Egypt's reliance on wheat imports by stimulating domestic production through financial incentives for farmers. The government's strategy includes increasing the domestic wheat supply target to 3.7 million tons while decreasing imports by 17%, underscoring efforts to ensure stable food security. Additional investments in agriculture, such as land reclamation projects and modern technologies, highlight Egypt's push to enhance productivity, competitiveness in international markets, and rural employment opportunities.

records.title: Egypt's urban inflation dropped to 28.1% in May 2024 from 32.5% in April 2023, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization an...
records.description: Egypt's urban inflation dropped to 28.1% in May 2024 from 32.5% in April 2023, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS), marking a significant economic recovery amid declining food prices. The consumer price index (CPI) also declined by 0.7%, the first negative movement since June 2022. Core inflation fell to 28.1%, dropping below 30% for the first time since January 2023. Significant price reductions were observed in cereals, bread, meat, poultry, fish, seafood, cheese, eggs, oils, fats, vegetables, and sugar. However, prices for fruit, coffee, tea, cocoa, textiles, and utilities increased. CAPMAS predicts further core inflation reduction in early 2025, potentially returning to pre-March 2022 levels, supported by stringent monetary policies, foreign exchange market stability, increased foreign investment, and higher foreign exchange reserves. In March, Egypt secured a $5 billion IMF loan contingent on economic reforms to mitigate inflation. Analysts foresee sustained economic growth for North Africa due to these investments and market confidence.
records.institution: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: In 2023, Egypt's trade with Jordan amounted to $864 million, down from $990 million in 2022, according to CAPMAS.
records.description: In 2023, Egypt's trade with Jordan amounted to $864 million, down from $990 million in 2022, according to CAPMAS. Egyptian exports to Jordan totaled $658 million, decreasing from $732 million in 2022, while imports from Jordan were valued at $206 million, down from $259 million the previous year. Key exports included fuel, mineral oils, vegetables, fruits, and machinery, while imports primarily comprised fertilizers, pharmaceuticals, and plastics. Jordanian remittances to Egypt totaled $415.3 million, down from $792.9 million, with investments from Jordan to Egypt at $134 million, and Egyptian investments in Jordan amounting to $183.6 million during the fiscal year 2022/2023.
records.institution: Egyptian Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)

records.title: Iraq's Council of Ministers, under the leadership of Prime Minister Mustafa Al-Kadhimi, has approved a 20 percent increase in customs dut...
records.description: Iraq's Council of Ministers, under the leadership of Prime Minister Mustafa Al-Kadhimi, has approved a 20 percent increase in customs duties on imported steel rebar (10-32 mm) from all origins. Effective from October 3, 2024, for a duration of four years, this tariff adjustment specifically targets products classified under tariff code 72142000. The Ministry of Industry and Minerals will oversee the implementation of these measures, monitoring import trends over the past three years to prevent unjustified price increases, ensure sufficient market supply, and assess the tariff's role in safeguarding the national economy.

records.title: Orange Jordan has successfully concluded its 5G Agriculture Bootcamp, marking a significant milestone in the advancement of sustainable a...
records.description: Orange Jordan has successfully concluded its 5G Agriculture Bootcamp, marking a significant milestone in the advancement of sustainable agriculture in Jordan. Over the past two months, the program empowered 18 innovators, 5G experts, entrepreneurs, and students with cutting-edge technologies aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity while preserving natural resources. The bootcamp, initiated by Orange Jordan, is poised to catalyze Jordan's agricultural sector by addressing critical challenges such as desert locust infestations, which threaten food security and production. By fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in technology-based agriculture, Orange Jordan aims to drive real transformations in food security, economic growth, and job creation, particularly benefiting farmers in vulnerable regions. This initiative underscores the growing importance of technology in Jordan's economic development, leveraging artificial intelligence, 5G, and other advanced technologies to overcome traditional agricultural challenges and empower the next generation of agricultural leaders.

records.title: Oman and Mauritania have engaged in discussions aimed at enhancing their cooperation across various sectors, including fishing, mining, e...
records.description: Oman and Mauritania have engaged in discussions aimed at enhancing their cooperation across various sectors, including fishing, mining, energy, agriculture, logistics, and tourism. During political talks in Nouakchott, Foreign Ministers Sayyid Badr Hamad Al Busaidi of Oman and Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug of Mauritania explored ways to deepen business partnerships between their private sectors. They also exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual concern, emphasizing their commitment to promoting security, stability, and peace globally. Additionally, they voiced support for efforts to address the conflict in Gaza through ceasefire agreements and humanitarian aid initiatives, advocating for international law and humanitarian principles to guide these efforts.

The agreement, signed by Oman's Ambassador to Sri Lanka, Ahmed Ali al Rashdi, and Sri Lanka's Minister of Agriculture and Plantation Industries, Mahinda Amaraweera, aims to enhance bilateral collaboration in agricultural technologies, research, and sustainable farming methods.

records.title: KSrelief is maintaining its commitment to food security in Sudan, as reported by SPA.
records.description: KSrelief is maintaining its commitment to food security in Sudan, as reported by SPA. In the Beheira locality of River Nile State, the agency distributed 581 food packages to support displaced and needy families, reaching a total of 3,340 individuals. Additionally, in Sennar, 500 food packages were delivered to displaced families, benefiting approximately 2,830 individuals in efforts to alleviate food insecurity in the region.

records.title: Silal, a leading agricultural company in the UAE, is pioneering the use of nanotechnology to revolutionize agriculture in the region.
records.description: Silal, a leading agricultural company in the UAE, is pioneering the use of nanotechnology to revolutionize agriculture in the region. This initiative aims to bolster food security, enhance crop productivity, and promote sustainability. Collaborating with Bayer, Silal focuses on integrated pest management, crop protection, and advanced irrigation techniques to optimize farming in the UAE's challenging climate. Additionally, Silal's solar-powered desalination project and partnerships with Khalifa University underscore its commitment to eco-friendly practices and agricultural innovation, positioning it as a key player in shaping the future of UAE agriculture.

records.title: The wilaya of Guelma in Algeria is gearing up for a remarkable agricultural season with expectations of a record industrial tomato harves...
records.description: The wilaya of Guelma in Algeria is gearing up for a remarkable agricultural season with expectations of a record industrial tomato harvest for 2023-2024. Directed by Rachid Rehamnia, the Directorate of Agricultural Services (DSA) anticipates a production of 2.456 million quintals, marking a significant increase from previous years. Spread across 3,063 hectares, the crop is supported by modern irrigation methods like drip irrigation, covering 3,049 hectares, which have been instrumental in optimizing water usage. This surge in production is set to not only benefit local farmers but also contribute positively to employment and economic growth in Guelma, underscoring a promising season ahead.

records.title: Bahrain Logistics Zone (BLZ) has finalized a lease agreement with Al Daaysi Holding for over 8,400 square meters of land, aimed at develo...
records.description: Bahrain Logistics Zone (BLZ) has finalized a lease agreement with Al Daaysi Holding for over 8,400 square meters of land, aimed at developing a specialized logistics hub for Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), including refrigerated and frozen products. This initiative, announced recently, seeks to enhance Bahrain’s re-exports to Africa and the Middle East while bolstering local food security and consumption. Managed by Ports and Maritime Affairs under Bahrain’s Ministry of Transportation and Telecommunications, BLZ offers customs-bonded zones and a logistics park, providing a range of services to local, regional, and multinational companies since its establishment in 2008 adjacent to Khalifa Bin Salman Port (KBSP) in northern Bahrain.
records.institution: Bahrain Logistics Zone (BLZ) & Al Daaysi Holding

records.title: In May 2024, revenues from the Suez Canal plummeted by 64.3%, totaling around $337.8 million compared to $648 million in May 2023.
records.description: In May 2024, revenues from the Suez Canal plummeted by 64.3%, totaling around $337.8 million compared to $648 million in May 2023. The decrease is attributed to a sharp decline in ship traffic, with 1,111 ships passing through the canal compared to 2,396 ships in May 2023, marking a drop of 1,285 ships. Additionally, total tonnage fell by 68.5% to about 44.9 million tons, down from 142.9 million tons the previous year. Minister of Finance Mohamed Maait had earlier predicted a nearly 60% decrease in canal revenues due to tensions in the Red Sea region, impacting global and regional trade dynamics.

records.title: A recent study conducted in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq has comprehensively classified Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) based on remote se...
records.description: A recent study conducted in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq has comprehensively classified Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) based on remote sensing data, covering a total area of 46,465.1 km². The study identifies several dominant LULC classes in the region, including grassland (28.7%), arable land (24.3%), and open forests and shrubland (16.1%). Other significant classifications include irrigated land (7.4%), dense forest (6.8%), and uncultivated land (6%). Urban areas occupy only 1.9% of the region, while water bodies and wetlands constitute 0.8% and 0.01% respectively. The findings emphasize the importance of sustainable management practices for agriculture, biodiversity conservation, and ecological services in the region, highlighting the need for strategic land management and conservation planning based on these detailed classifications.
records.institution: Kurdistan Region Statistics Office (KRSO) & World Food Programme (WFP)

records.description: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), along with Jordan's Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, finalized a EUR 4.13 million grant agreement aimed at enhancing climate change adaptation and resilience in Jordan's agriculture sector. This funding is part of the Rural Economic Growth and Employment Programme (REGEP) and complements existing IFAD investments. It focuses on promoting climate-resilient agricultural practices, improving water efficiency, and expanding project coverage to additional governorates in Jordan. The initiative aims to benefit rural populations by increasing yields, income, and sustainability while addressing climate challenges like water scarcity.
records.institution: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), Jordanian Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation in Jordan, & the Kingdom of the Netherlands

records.title: Al Hoceima: Launch of Agricultural and Rural Development Projects as Part of the Generation Green Strategy
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests, Mr. Mohammed Sadiki, visited the Province of Al Hoceima to oversee the implementation of various agricultural and rural development projects under the Generation Green strategy. This included launching the Province's 2024-2025 investment program, valued at MAD 300 million, aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity and resilience. Projects highlighted during the visit included distributing tanker trucks to mitigate the impact of rainfall deficits in 15 municipalities, initiating a solidarity agriculture program to plant 630 hectares of cochineal-resistant cacti, and advancing rural road construction to improve infrastructure and livelihoods across the region.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests
