records.title: Gotion High Tech, a Chinese-European consortium, has finalized a deal with the Moroccan government to establish a US$1.3 billion gigafact...
records.description: Gotion High Tech, a Chinese-European consortium, has finalized a deal with the Moroccan government to establish a US$1.3 billion gigafactory for electric vehicle (EV) batteries in Kenitra, Morocco. This significant investment, announced during a ceremony in Rabat attended by Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch, marks Morocco's entry into the electric mobility revolution. The gigafactory will begin with a production capacity of 20 GWh, scaling up to 100 GWh, with a total investment reaching 65 billion dirhams (US$6.8 billion). This initiative is expected to create 17,000 jobs initially, including 2,300 highly skilled positions, thereby enhancing Morocco's industrial capabilities and positioning it as a key player in the global EV battery market.

records.title: HRH Crown Prince Moulay El Hassan launched construction of the Casablanca seawater desalination plant, set to become Africa's largest, se...
records.description: HRH Crown Prince Moulay El Hassan launched construction of the Casablanca seawater desalination plant, set to become Africa's largest, serving up to 7.5 million people. This initiative, integral to Morocco's National Drinking Water Supply and Irrigation Program 2020-2027, addresses water scarcity amid rainfall deficits. With a phased approach, the plant aims to initially produce 548,000 m3 of water daily by 2026, expandable to 822,000 m3/day by mid-2028. The project, costing 6.5 billion dirhams and employing a public-private partnership, includes state-of-the-art desalination technology and a renewable energy-powered, automated management system to ensure sustainable water supply across Greater Casablanca and surrounding areas.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) have collabor...
records.description: Saudi Arabia’s King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) have collaborated to rehabilitate a fish landing center in Yemen’s Hodeidah, as reported by the Saudi Press Agency. This initiative is part of an emergency support program aimed at safeguarding the livelihoods of vulnerable populations in Yemen reliant on agriculture, livestock, and fisheries. The project focuses on revitalizing key fish landing centers along Yemen’s coastline and includes provisions such as 1,000 ice boxes and 3,000 life jackets for fishermen in Al-Mahrah governorate. Additionally, it supports local farmers and herders to sustain food production for home consumption and local markets. Hodeidah Governor Al-Hassan Taher expressed gratitude for KSrelief’s support, highlighting the center's role in boosting the marine fishing sector and improving livelihoods by providing essential facilities like solar-powered cold storage to preserve and protect the catch from pollution and damage.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) & Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) continues its humanitarian efforts in Yemen and Syria, focusing on providin...
records.description: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) continues its humanitarian efforts in Yemen and Syria, focusing on providing essential food supplies to vulnerable individuals and families. In Yemen, KSrelief distributed 2,251 food parcels to 2,251 families across several districts in Abyan and Al-Dhale Governorates, benefiting a total of 15,757 individuals. Meanwhile, in Syria, KSrelief assisted 470 families affected by an earthquake in Harem, Idlib Governorate, by distributing 470 food baskets and hygiene kits. These efforts highlight ongoing support aimed at alleviating hardships and enhancing the well-being of communities facing humanitarian crises in both countries.
records.institution: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

records.title: In Abu Dhabi, the launch of AgriFood Growth & Water Abundance (AGWA) represents a transformative initiative aimed at addressing global fo...
records.description: In Abu Dhabi, the launch of AgriFood Growth & Water Abundance (AGWA) represents a transformative initiative aimed at addressing global food shortages and water scarcity. Led by the Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development (ADDED) and Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO), AGWA has garnered support from major infrastructure partners including Abu Dhabi Ports, Abu Dhabi Airports, Abu Dhabi Distribution Company (ADDC), and Masdar City. These partnerships are crucial in establishing AGWA as a global hub for innovative food production, water technologies, and sustainable practices. The cluster aims to leverage Abu Dhabi's strengths in logistics, energy, and sustainability to support local suppliers, enhance food security, and drive economic growth through technological innovation and strategic infrastructure development. AGWA is set to play a pivotal role in advancing the UAE's National Food Security Strategy 2051 and contributing significantly to the economy with projections of substantial GDP growth, job creation, and investments in the coming years.

records.title: India has authorized an additional export of 10,000 tons of onions to the UAE to stabilize prices ahead of Eid al-Fitr, a period of heigh...
records.description: India has authorized an additional export of 10,000 tons of onions to the UAE to stabilize prices ahead of Eid al-Fitr, a period of heightened demand for consumables like vegetables and spices. This decision aims to impact onion prices in the UAE, which recently surged to over Dh7 per kilogram, contrasting with the usual retail range of Dh2 to Dh3, and promotional prices as low as Dh1. Facilitated through the National Cooperative Exports Ltd (NCEL) under the Ministry of Commerce and Trade's guidance, this export supplements the 14,400 tons shipped last month. The move follows a temporary export ban amidst domestic price increases and aligns with the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (Cepa) between India and the UAE, designed to bolster bilateral trade.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Razan Al Mubarak, UN Climate Change High-Level Champion for Cop28, highlighted the critical role of ocean conservation at the Mena Oceans...
records.description: Razan Al Mubarak, UN Climate Change High-Level Champion for Cop28, highlighted the critical role of ocean conservation at the Mena Oceans Summit in Dubai, stressing its integration into global climate strategies post-Cop28. She emphasized commitments to preserve coastal ecosystems and scale up ocean-based mitigation efforts, underscoring the UAE Consensus's pivotal role in advancing these goals regionally. Discussions at the summit focused on regional initiatives to protect oceans, including research on resilient corals and sustainable fisheries practices, alongside efforts to engage communities and explore innovative financing mechanisms like "blue bonds" for conservation. The event aimed to catalyze partnerships and actionable steps to safeguard ocean health amidst escalating global challenges.
records.institution: UN Climate Change High-Level Champion for Cop28

records.title: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, highlighted significant advancements in the Emirati Genome Programme durin...
records.description: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, highlighted significant advancements in the Emirati Genome Programme during a UAE Cabinet meeting in Abu Dhabi. With over 600,000 samples collected toward a goal of one million, the initiative aims to map genetic and hereditary diseases in the UAE population. Emphasizing the program's role in developing tailored medical treatments, Sheikh Mohammed also announced the launch of a premarital screening pilot program. The meeting also saw approvals for a federal traffic law accommodating self-driving vehicles and modern transportation technologies, alongside developments in the Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry to bolster economic growth and international partnerships.

records.title: Egypt and the European Union (EU) are set to engage in discussions aimed at securing 1.8 billion euros in guarantees from the EU to boost...
records.description: Egypt and the European Union (EU) are set to engage in discussions aimed at securing 1.8 billion euros in guarantees from the EU to boost foreign direct investment in Egypt's private sector. This initiative, announced by Egypt's Ministry of International Cooperation (MoIC), underscores the strategic economic ties between the two parties. Discussions, facilitated by Minister Rania Al-Mashat and Gert Jan Koopman from the European Commission's Directorate-General for Neighbourhood and Enlargement Negotiations (NEAR), focus on leveraging the European Fund for Sustainable Development to support private sector financing and investments in Egypt. This move aligns with efforts to deepen the Egypt-EU relationship following the elevation to a strategic partnership, with recent initiatives under the Team Europe Initiative having already allocated substantial funds to both public and private sectors in Egypt for sustainable development across various critical sectors.

records.title: The Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources, in partnership with the United Nations Development Progr...
records.description: The Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources, in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Iraq and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), celebrated the graduation of 200 women from a specialized training program focused on the agriculture food industry. Held across nine locations in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (IKR), including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, and Dohuk, the program equipped participants with skills in cultivating agricultural products, marketing strategies, and entrepreneurship tailored to local needs. Deputy Prime Minister H.E. Mr. Qubad Talabani highlighted the sector's potential for economic growth and sustainable development, underscoring the importance of empowering women in Iraq's agriculture sector. The collaboration aims to enhance food security, economic prosperity, and inclusive development by supporting graduates to establish their businesses and contribute actively to Iraq's agricultural advancement.
records.institution: Kurdistan Regional Government's (KRG) Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), & the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)

records.title: IsDB Group and State of Qatar Ink Strategic Cooperation Agreement
records.description: At the Qatar Economic Forum 2024, the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) and Qatar finalized a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for strategic cooperation, aiming to establish a comprehensive Member Country Partnership Strategy (MCPS) for 2024-2028. Signed by H.E. Dr. Muhammad Al Jasser, IsDB Chairman, and H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari, Qatar’s Finance Minister and IsDB Governor, the agreement aligns with Qatar's National Vision 2030 and IsDB's 2023-2025 strategy. This partnership emphasizes Qatar’s role in promoting sustainable economic development and South-South cooperation, focusing on pillars such as economic transformation and cross-cutting areas including women and youth empowerment, climate action, and institutional capacity building.
records.institution: Qatari Ministry of Finance & Islamic Development Bank (IsDB)

records.title: Broiler production in Tunisia showed a 1.3% growth during the first five months of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023, according to...
records.description: Broiler production in Tunisia showed a 1.3% growth during the first five months of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023, according to data from the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI). By May 2024, broiler production reached 12,500 tonnes, marking a 3.7% increase from May last year but a slight decrease of 0.6% from April 2024. Egg production for consumption also saw a steady increase during this period, with a growth rate of 1.2% overall and a 4.1% rise compared to May 2023, reaching 159,100 units in May 2024.

records.title: Farmers in southern Iraq, particularly in Basra, face a critical water crisis exacerbated by pollution and salinization of the Chatt el A...
records.description: Farmers in southern Iraq, particularly in Basra, face a critical water crisis exacerbated by pollution and salinization of the Chatt el Arab river. This has severely impacted irrigation and drinking water quality, leading to health concerns and economic hardships for local communities. Organizations like Action Against Hunger are pivotal in advocating for sustainable farming practices and implementing innovative technologies such as the Responsive Drip Irrigation system to improve water efficiency and crop yields. These efforts are crucial in mitigating the effects of climate change and ensuring long-term food security and livelihoods in the region.

records.title: The Ministry of Economy and Trade of Libya's Government of National Unity announced a significant milestone as the United States Agency f...
records.description: The Ministry of Economy and Trade of Libya's Government of National Unity announced a significant milestone as the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) pledged two million dinars through an agreement with Al-Saraya Bank. This initiative, set to commence in July, aims to bolster small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Libya's southern region. Led by Minister Mohammed Al-Huweij and USAID's Michelle Bradford, the project emphasizes technical support alongside financial backing from Al-Saraya Bank, with plans to extend support through Al-Wehda and Al-Sahara Banks. The effort underscores a concerted push to enhance economic growth, foster entrepreneurship, and create employment opportunities in Libya's southern communities.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Economy and Trade

records.title: Agreements signed at Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources this week mark a significant step towards establishin...
records.description: Agreements signed at Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources this week mark a significant step towards establishing commercial-scale microalgae farms for biofuel production in the Sultanate of Oman. This initiative, supported by three companies—Net Zero Solutions (NTZ), Al Tharmad Business and Services Company, and Green Gulf Industries—aims to contribute to sustainable low-carbon fuel production. With an estimated investment of RO 9 million, the project will utilize photobioreactor technology to cultivate microalgae, leveraging residual CO2, heat, and water for efficient production. At full capacity, the project is expected to yield 3,700 tonnes of biofuel annually, supporting Oman's goals in renewable energy and carbon capture efforts.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation in Yemen has reiterated its ban on importing frozen chicken, emphasizing the need for importer...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation in Yemen has reiterated its ban on importing frozen chicken, emphasizing the need for importers to obtain prior permits before bringing any shipments into the country. This measure aims to protect and promote local chicken production without adversely affecting small poultry producers and breeders. The ban, enforced under Ministerial Resolution No. (20) of 2024, reflects the government's commitment to achieving self-sufficiency in poultry production. The Ministry has warned of strict penalties for violators, including fines and measures to ensure compliance with health and quarantine regulations to safeguard public and animal health. It also plans to publish a blacklist of non-compliant importers and urges adherence to import laws and procedures to maintain food safety standards across the country.
records.institution: Yemeni Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation

records.title: Egypt's agricultural sector has seen a notable increase in exports, with the value rising by $500 million to reach approximately $2.60 bi...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural sector has seen a notable increase in exports, with the value rising by $500 million to reach approximately $2.60 billion in the first five months of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023. This growth, reported by El-Sayed El-Quseir, Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, corresponds with a rise in export volume to over 4.50 million tonnes, an increase of 400,000 tonnes year-on-year. Citrus fruits led the exports, totaling 1.97 million tonnes, followed by fresh potatoes at 862,226 tonnes. Onions, beans (both fresh and dried), potatoes, and grapes also contributed significantly to Egypt's export figures during this period, underscoring the country's robust agricultural output and export potential.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Egypt's strategic push to enhance domestic wheat production includes a targeted reduction of wheat imports by 17%, announced by Minister...
records.description: Egypt's strategic push to enhance domestic wheat production includes a targeted reduction of wheat imports by 17%, announced by Minister of Supply and Internal Trade, Ali Al-Moselhi. The new import target stands at 5 million tons, down from 6 million tons previously, reflecting President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi's initiative to expand agricultural land through a comprehensive land reclamation program. This program aims to reclaim approximately 3.5 million feddans, including projects like the New Delta and Toshka, which have the potential to significantly boost Egypt's agricultural output. The country aims to leverage these efforts to secure its food supply chain and potentially position itself as a key grain export hub in the region.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced on Thursday that Egypt is set to receive access to approximately $820 million, pending bo...
records.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) announced on Thursday that Egypt is set to receive access to approximately $820 million, pending board approval. This disbursement is part of the IMF's Extended Fund Facility, designed to assist countries facing significant payment imbalances due to structural weaknesses. The agreement follows Egypt's efforts to maintain macroeconomic stability through fiscal discipline, tight monetary policy adjustments, and transitioning to a flexible exchange rate system. These measures have started to yield positive outcomes, including improved foreign exchange availability, slowing inflation, and signs of recovery in private sector sentiment. The IMF emphasized the importance for Egypt to continue strengthening its economic resilience, enhancing competition in the banking sector, and accelerating structural reforms to foster private sector-led growth and improve the business environment.

records.title: A delegation from the Jordan Chamber of Commerce, attending the Arab-German Business Forum in Berlin, met with Omani Economy Minister Sae...
records.description: A delegation from the Jordan Chamber of Commerce, attending the Arab-German Business Forum in Berlin, met with Omani Economy Minister Saeed Al Saqri to discuss enhancing trade and investment relations between Jordan and Oman. Al Saqri emphasized the longstanding historical ties between the nations, highlighting Sultan Haitham Bin Tariq’s recent visit to Jordan as pivotal for strengthening bilateral relations. He called for leveraging the outcomes of this visit to bolster economic cooperation, encouraging increased networking and mutual visits between private sectors to capitalize on economic opportunities, particularly in logistics, tourism, medicines, and food security sectors.

records.title: Minister of Agriculture Khaled Hneifat recently visited Ajloun to inspect various agricultural projects aimed at bolstering the local eco...
records.description: Minister of Agriculture Khaled Hneifat recently visited Ajloun to inspect various agricultural projects aimed at bolstering the local economy. Among the initiatives he reviewed was a packing and cooling project at the Association of Northern Ajloun Villages, supported by a JD90,000 allocation from the ministry. This project focuses on enhancing production and storage capabilities. Additionally, Hneifat visited the Durat Ammoun factory, which produces tomato concentrate and provides employment for local residents. The minister emphasized the ministry's commitment to supporting agricultural associations and fostering economic development through strategic investments and guidance.

records.title: Morocco is grappling with critical water shortages as its agricultural reservoirs reach only 30% of capacity due to significantly low rai...
records.description: Morocco is grappling with critical water shortages as its agricultural reservoirs reach only 30% of capacity due to significantly low rainfall. Minister Mohamed Sadiki highlighted that despite March rains supporting springtime crops like chickpeas, corn, and vegetables, overall precipitation remains below average. The government has allocated substantial subsidies and implemented measures to support farmers, including subsidizing nitrogen fertilizers and supporting soil and water analysis. These efforts aim to mitigate the impacts of drought and ensure food security amid challenging climate conditions.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: A team led by an international expert from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), alongside local supervisors, visited Ain Berda an...
records.description: A team led by an international expert from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), alongside local supervisors, visited Ain Berda and El Hadjar in Annaba to assess the progress of Algeria's 2024 General Agricultural Census (RGA). They inspected pilot farms specializing in cereals, pulses, and potatoes, focusing on data collection and integration into digital platforms. With over 40% of farms inventoried and digitized in Annaba so far, this census serves as a critical tool for planning agricultural strategies to enhance food security and sustainability nationwide. The visit underscored the importance of precise data for guiding future agricultural policies effectively.
records.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) & General Agricultural Census (RGA)

records.title: Egypt's agricultural sector continues to thrive, with Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Al Sayed Al Qusair reporting that the...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural sector continues to thrive, with Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Al Sayed Al Qusair reporting that the country's agricultural exports reached 4.5 million tons valued at $2.6 billion in the first five months of 2024. Highlighting citrus as the leading export, with 1,978,112 tons shipped, the minister noted significant exports of potatoes, onions, and various fruits and vegetables. Egypt's success in diversifying its agricultural exports is evident, with plans to expand market reach further following successful engagements with global partners like South Korea and substantial export volumes to regions such as the European Union and Southeast Asia in recent years.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Egypt's livestock market, typically bustling in anticipation of Eid Al Adha, is experiencing significant stagnation this year amidst soar...
records.description: Egypt's livestock market, typically bustling in anticipation of Eid Al Adha, is experiencing significant stagnation this year amidst soaring inflation and economic challenges. The annual Muslim celebration involves the sacrifice of livestock, traditionally distributed to the less fortunate. However, this year, sales have plummeted compared to previous years due to record-high inflation, with meat and livestock prices rising over 15% from last year alone. This increase follows a drastic rise in living costs since 2022, outpacing income growth and straining household budgets. Wealthier consumers are also cutting back, purchasing smaller quantities of meat, while fewer families can afford the ritual sacrifice, dampening the spirit of giving during Eid. In response, Egypt's agriculture ministry has initiated discounted meat sales in Cairo to alleviate some financial burden, highlighting ongoing efforts to mitigate the economic impact on citizens ahead of the June 15 observance of Eid Al Adha.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Egyptian Ministry of Supply has initiated the formation of a committee to analyze the production costs of bread across public, privat...
records.description: The Egyptian Ministry of Supply has initiated the formation of a committee to analyze the production costs of bread across public, private, and sovereign entity bakeries, marking the first comprehensive study since 2020. This decision follows a recent government-mandated increase in subsidized bread prices by 300 percent, setting the new price at 20 piasters per loaf, the first adjustment in three decades. The committee's mandate includes evaluating various factors impacting production costs, such as bread type and fuel usage, without intending to raise consumer prices. Instead, the focus is on ensuring profitability for bakery owners amidst escalating production expenses and wages, driven by increasing local wheat costs and other economic factors.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: The Netherlands and Egypt have forged a robust partnership across multiple domains, strengthening their ties amidst evolving global dynam...
records.description: The Netherlands and Egypt have forged a robust partnership across multiple domains, strengthening their ties amidst evolving global dynamics. Recent discussions between the two nations underscore their deep-rooted connections in politics, diplomacy, economics, and culture. Trade between them reached €3.5 billion in 2023, emphasizing Egypt's pivotal role as a key economic partner in North Africa. Cooperation in 2024 focuses on security and conflict resolution, economics (including green hydrogen and agriculture), water management, climate change, and tourism. The Netherlands remains optimistic about the future of their relationship, buoyed by ongoing joint projects and initiatives aimed at sustainable development and global cooperation.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Iraqi Council of Ministers recently granted authorization for the Ministry of Electricity to extend a "sole offer" invitation to AMEA...
records.description: The Iraqi Council of Ministers recently granted authorization for the Ministry of Electricity to extend a "sole offer" invitation to AMEA Power, a UAE-based company, to propose a 500-MW solar power plant project in Iraq, with the potential to include battery storage. This initiative aligns with Iraq's Investment Law, aiming to bolster the nation's renewable energy capabilities and decrease dependency on fossil fuels. The planned solar projects are pivotal in addressing Iraq's persistent electricity deficits, meeting rising energy demands, and concurrently, reducing the environmental footprint associated with conventional energy sources.

records.title: The Governor of the Central Bank of Libya (CBL), Sadek Elkaber, hosted Heba Ahmed, CEO of the Islamic Solidarity Fund for Development (IS...
records.description: The Governor of the Central Bank of Libya (CBL), Sadek Elkaber, hosted Heba Ahmed, CEO of the Islamic Solidarity Fund for Development (ISFD), and senior officials from the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) to advance discussions on establishing the Waqf Solidarity Fund. The meeting, held at the CBL office, focused on enhancing the private sector's role and activating institutions supporting micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Libya. These efforts are part of ongoing initiatives aimed at strengthening economic resilience and fostering sustainable development through innovative financial mechanisms.

records.title: FAO recently convened a Regional Training of Trainers workshop in Muscat, Oman, focused on enhancing technical capacities for monitoring...
records.description: FAO recently convened a Regional Training of Trainers workshop in Muscat, Oman, focused on enhancing technical capacities for monitoring and surveillance of the Red Palm Weevil (RPW) using the "SusaHamra" App. Attended by specialists and officials from seven Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Yemen, and Oman, the workshop was part of the FAO's efforts under the RPW eradication program. Participants engaged in discussions on RPW management strategies, sharing national plans, and addressing gaps in monitoring systems. The workshop aimed to improve skills in visual inspection, trapping techniques, data collection, validation, and analysis through the SusaHamra platform, essential for decision-making and resource planning in pest control programs. This initiative underscores FAO's commitment to regional cooperation and sustainable management to safeguard palm tree health and agricultural productivity against RPW threats.
records.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia have solidified their economic cooperation with the establishment of a joint Saudi-Ethiopian Business Council.
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia have solidified their economic cooperation with the establishment of a joint Saudi-Ethiopian Business Council. Signed at the Ethio-Saudi Investment and Trade Forum in Addis Ababa, this agreement marks a significant milestone aimed at enhancing bilateral economic relations. The council will serve as a pivotal platform for Saudi and Ethiopian entrepreneurs to promote their activities, explore investment opportunities, and foster commercial partnerships. Discussions at the forum highlighted potential investments in industrial zones, agriculture, energy, and other key sectors of mutual interest, underscoring the commitment of both nations to deepen their economic ties.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has joined the multi-country central bank digital currency (CBDC) initiative known as Project mBridge, alongside China and t...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has joined the multi-country central bank digital currency (CBDC) initiative known as Project mBridge, alongside China and the UAE, as part of its strategy to modernize payment systems and reduce reliance on physical cash. The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) confirmed Saudi Arabia's participation as a full member, highlighting the kingdom's interest in leveraging wholesale CBDC to enhance cross-border payment efficiency and settlement between commercial banks. Project mBridge, launched in 2021, aims to facilitate faster and more cost-effective cross-border transactions, particularly in regions with limited financial access. It addresses concerns of financial inclusion by integrating Ethereum Virtual Machine compatibility, allowing for expanded technological solutions and interoperability. The initiative is a key component of the UAE's Financial Infrastructure Transformation program, supported by its Digital Dirham, aiming to bolster global payment infrastructure while ensuring robust security standards.

records.title: Egypt's House of Representatives has approved a substantial increase in public spending for the fiscal year 2024/2025, with expenditures...
records.description: Egypt's House of Representatives has approved a substantial increase in public spending for the fiscal year 2024/2025, with expenditures rising by 29% year-on-year to reach EGP 3.87 trillion, equivalent to 22.60% of GDP. Finance Minister Mohamed Maait announced that public revenues are expected to grow by 8.50% to EGP 2.60 trillion, comprising 15.40% of GDP. The budget deficit is projected to widen to EGP 1.20 trillion, or 7.30% of GDP, from EGP 555 billion in the previous fiscal year. The government aims for a primary surplus of EGP 591.40 billion, despite increased spending on health, education, wages, and social benefits.

records.title: In the final week of May, Egypt's food exports experienced a significant surge, totaling 250,000 tons according to the National Food Safe...
records.description: In the final week of May, Egypt's food exports experienced a significant surge, totaling 250,000 tons according to the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA). This marked a notable increase of 30,000 tons compared to the previous week. The exports included a diverse range of over 610 varieties of fresh fruits, vegetables, and processed food items. Among vegetables, potatoes led with 23,000 tons, followed closely by onions at 22,000 tons and beans at 5,000 tons. Citrus fruits were the most prominent in the fruit category, totaling 55,000 tons, with fresh grapes at 25,000 tons and strawberries at 13,000 tons also contributing significantly. The Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, Italy, and Sudan were the primary destinations for Egypt's food exports during this period.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: President Sheikh Mohamed praised the efforts of climate leaders and entrepreneurs during a meeting at Qasr Al Bahr in Abu Dhabi, undersco...
records.description: President Sheikh Mohamed praised the efforts of climate leaders and entrepreneurs during a meeting at Qasr Al Bahr in Abu Dhabi, underscoring their role in advancing the UAE's sustainability goals. On World Environment Day, he highlighted their contributions to environmental protection and emphasized the UAE's commitment to global leadership in sustainability. Sheikh Mohamed emphasized the importance of empowering individuals and communities to innovate solutions that support environmental conservation efforts worldwide. He reaffirmed the UAE's dedication to implementing the UAE Consensus, adopted at Cop28, aimed at transitioning global energy systems away from fossil fuels. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid echoed these sentiments, urging global collaboration to tackle environmental challenges and calling on youth to play a pivotal role in driving climate action for sustainable development.

records.title: Jordan's Agriculture Minister Khaled Hneifat disclosed that the country faces a daily lemon production of 60 tons, which falls short of t...
records.description: Jordan's Agriculture Minister Khaled Hneifat disclosed that the country faces a daily lemon production of 60 tons, which falls short of the market demand of 200 tons. To address this deficit, Jordan initiated lemon imports starting in mid-April, targeting to cover a shortfall of 7,000 tons expected from June to August. The imports, which include approximately 750 tons from Africa, are intended to alleviate current market prices. Hneifat anticipated a price reduction at the beginning of the following week and noted that the Ministry of Agriculture has issued 170 import licenses, predominantly for lemons from South Africa and Turkey, though shipment delays have occurred due to underutilization of these licenses by traders.

records.title: Jordanian security forces have seized over 9.5 million Captagon pills, including more than three million intercepted at the border with S...
records.description: Jordanian security forces have seized over 9.5 million Captagon pills, including more than three million intercepted at the border with Saudi Arabia, in their ongoing efforts against drug trafficking from southern Syria. The haul, which also included 143 kg of hashish, underscores Jordan's battle against narcotics networks operating in the region. The pills were concealed in vehicles and equipment like excavators and road rollers, with recent operations conducted across northern and southern Jordan. Investigations are ongoing to uncover all circumstances and external links involved in these smuggling activities, which have posed significant challenges despite Jordan's efforts to fortify its borders with assistance from the United States.

records.title: In early 2024, Morocco achieved unprecedented levels of fruit and vegetable exports to Germany, as reported by EastFruit.
records.description: In early 2024, Morocco achieved unprecedented levels of fruit and vegetable exports to Germany, as reported by EastFruit. Direct shipments of fresh and frozen produce surged significantly compared to previous years, totaling nearly 35,000 tons from January to March. This marked a 40% increase year-on-year and doubled the average volume of the past five years. Notably, Moroccan greenhouse tomatoes led the exports with nearly 13,000 tons, while sweet peppers reached 8,000 tons, both showing substantial growth. The export of frozen raspberries soared to 1.7 thousand tons, four times higher than the previous year, driven by a shortage in the market. Fresh blueberries also saw growth to 1.2 thousand tons, while fresh strawberries doubled to 560 tons during the same period.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: OCP Group, a leading Moroccan phosphate producer, has secured MAD 2.1 billion (approximately US$217 million) from Germany's KfW developme...
records.description: OCP Group, a leading Moroccan phosphate producer, has secured MAD 2.1 billion (approximately US$217 million) from Germany's KfW development bank to advance its ambitious green initiatives. This financing is a crucial part of OCP's broader US$13 billion (MAD 129 billion) green investment strategy spanning from 2023 to 2027. The funds will primarily support OCP's goals of achieving 100% non-conventional water use by 2024 and transitioning to 100% clean energy by 2027, aiming for 5 gigawatts of capacity. Additionally, the investment aims to achieve carbon neutrality across all emission scopes by 2030 (Scope 1 and 2) and by 2040 (Scope 3), while expanding production of green fertilizers. These efforts are expected to create an integrated ecosystem in Morocco, involving 600 companies and generating around 25,000 jobs, reinforcing OCP's commitment to sustainability and global food security.

records.title: On May 10, 2024, Morocco officially opened its market to U.S.
records.description: On May 10, 2024, Morocco officially opened its market to U.S. seed potatoes following the finalization of import requirements during bilateral meetings between the U.S. Department of Agriculture's APHIS and Morocco's ONSSA. This agreement, the culmination of a regulatory process dating back to 2015, allows Moroccan food processors to import U.S. potato varieties for planting, targeting uses like potato chips and French fries. The U.S. industry estimates the market potential for seed potatoes in Morocco to be approximately $8 million USD, with shipments expected to start once Moroccan buyers show interest. In 2023, Morocco imported over $42 million USD worth of seed potatoes, predominantly from the EU and the UK.
records.institution: Moroccan National Office of Food Safety (ONSSA)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia has announced significant environmental initiatives on World Environment Day 2024, including the establishment of a national...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has announced significant environmental initiatives on World Environment Day 2024, including the establishment of a national academy for the environment and a new program offering incentives and grants tailored to the environmental sector. Celebrated under the theme "Our land. Our future.", the day highlighted the importance of land as a fundamental aspect of global sustainability. Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, Eng. Abdulrahman AlFadley, outlined the academy's role in enhancing human capacity and promoting innovation in collaboration with national and international institutions. The incentives program aims to support eco-friendly practices, research, and investment opportunities across small and medium enterprises, universities, and non-profits. Saudi Arabia's efforts align with global strategies to combat land degradation and climate change, underscored by upcoming initiatives like hosting COP16 of the UNCCD to drive international cooperation on desertification and drought resilience.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: The Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES) has faced widespread protests within its controlled regions due to its deci...
records.description: The Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES) has faced widespread protests within its controlled regions due to its decision to set the purchase price of wheat at 31 US cents per kilogram for the 2023-2024 agricultural season. Despite discontent and sit-ins across Deir Ezzor, Raqqa, and al-Hasakah, AANES has affirmed it will not reverse its pricing policy. Officials cite economic blockades, Turkish attacks, and budget deficits as reasons for maintaining the current pricing, which they argue is necessary to sustain operations amid challenging economic conditions. However, critics, including local political parties and economic analysts, assert that the pricing favors regional smuggling networks and may discourage local farmers from selling their crops, potentially impacting future agricultural production and food security in the area.
records.institution: Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES)

records.title: Tunisia and Turkey are poised to strengthen their trade ties across multiple sectors following discussions between Trade Minister Kalthou...
records.description: Tunisia and Turkey are poised to strengthen their trade ties across multiple sectors following discussions between Trade Minister Kalthoum Ben Rejeb of Tunisia and Turkish Trade Minister Omer Bolat. They emphasized the potential for increased bilateral trade, inviting investments in manufacturing, agriculture, tourism, and renewable energy. The Türkiye-Tunisia Investment and Business Forum in Istanbul highlighted opportunities for Turkish companies in Tunisia's infrastructure and energy projects, leveraging Türkiye's expertise in renewable energy, construction, and manufacturing. The focus remains on fostering partnerships to access European, Asian, and African markets, with sectors like agriculture, textiles, and renewable energy identified for collaboration and mutual growth.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Trade and Export Development

records.title: Huhtamaki has announced plans to consolidate its three Flexible Packaging manufacturing sites in the United Arab Emirates, focusing on re...
records.description: Huhtamaki has announced plans to consolidate its three Flexible Packaging manufacturing sites in the United Arab Emirates, focusing on retaining its Jebel Ali factory while expanding operations at the Ras Al Khaimah facility. This strategic move, scheduled to unfold gradually in the latter half of 2024, aims to streamline manufacturing processes, enhance competitiveness, and lay a robust foundation for future growth in the region. The consolidation aligns with Huhtamaki's global strategy to drive efficiency improvements, expected to yield approximately €100 million (US$108.73 million) in savings over the next three years. Despite incurring consolidation-related costs of about €4 million (US$4.35 million) in Q2 2024, this restructuring underscores Huhtamaki's commitment to optimizing its operational footprint while supporting its workforce through transitions to new opportunities.

records.title: President Sheikh Mohamed of the UAE and President Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan held a phone conversation discussing bilateral cooperation a...
records.description: President Sheikh Mohamed of the UAE and President Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan held a phone conversation discussing bilateral cooperation and opportunities for further development between their countries. The leaders emphasized collaboration in economic sectors, development initiatives, renewable energy projects, and climate action efforts. A key topic was Azerbaijan's preparations to host Cop29, the upcoming global climate conference scheduled for November in Baku. This follows the UAE's hosting of Cop28 in Dubai, where the UAE Consensus was established to advance global climate action and sustainable development goals.

records.title: The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), in collaboration with the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre, the Ho...
records.description: The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), in collaboration with the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Bank of Thailand, and the Digital Currency Institute of the People’s Bank of China, has launched the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) platform of the mBridge project. This initiative aims to establish a multi-central bank digital currency (CBDC) common platform for wholesale cross-border payments and settlement, utilizing distributed ledger technology. The platform facilitates efficient, low-cost, and instant cross-border payments settled in central bank money. The mBridge project, a key initiative under the CBUAE’s Financial Infrastructure Transformation (FIT) programme, supports the UAE’s CBDC strategy, including Phase 1 implementation with the Digital Dirham. It marks a significant milestone in enhancing international trade and cooperation through improved cross-border payment systems.
records.institution: The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE)

records.title: Aqua Continentale and American firm ESE Intec are set to revolutionize Algeria’s aquaculture sector with an US$8M investment.
records.description: Aqua Continentale and American firm ESE Intec are set to revolutionize Algeria’s aquaculture sector with an US$8M investment. Signed on May 28th, the partnership aims to establish a state-of-the-art aquaculture facility in Relizane province. This initiative marks a pivotal moment for Algeria’s fledgling aquaculture industry, aiming to reduce dependence on wild catches by introducing local fish and shrimp production. ESE Intec’s expertise in food and feed production infrastructure will support the project’s four aquaculture units, focusing initially on shrimp farming. The venture promises significant local production, with plans to yield 10,000 tonnes of shrimp annually and create up to 200 new jobs, potentially positioning Algeria as a regional leader in aquaculture.
records.institution: Aqua Continentale & American firm ESE Intec

records.title: Egypt aims to attract $30 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) during the 2024-2025 fiscal year starting July 1st, as part of its e...
records.description: Egypt aims to attract $30 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) during the 2024-2025 fiscal year starting July 1st, as part of its economic strategy to boost growth and stabilize its financial metrics. The country's preliminary budget, recently approved by parliament, outlines ambitions to maintain inflation between 19% and 25% for the same period. Total revenues are projected at EGP 2.6 trillion, with expenditures expected to reach EGP 3.9 trillion, resulting in a deficit of approximately EGP 1.2 trillion, equivalent to 7.3% of GDP. Egypt's Ministry of Finance aims to reduce the debt-to-GDP ratio to below 80% by June 2027, signaling a commitment to fiscal sustainability amid economic expansion forecasts of 4.2% in the upcoming fiscal year, driven by increased investment, stronger net exports, and heightened consumer spending.

records.title: Egypt has decreased its potato exports to Russia, causing a price increase in the market.
records.description: Egypt has decreased its potato exports to Russia, causing a price increase in the market. However, the situation is expected to stabilize soon with the arrival of new domestic potatoes from southern regions of Russia within the next two weeks. Despite some regions reducing potato planting due to profitability concerns, overall planting volumes remain sufficient, including in key areas like the Moscow region. This suggests no critical shortages in potato supply are anticipated, despite recent price rises reported by Rosstat, indicating a 25.6% increase since the start of May.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt's government has allocated approximately 41,700 square kilometers (16,100 square miles) to the New and Renewable Energy Authority (...
records.description: Egypt's government has allocated approximately 41,700 square kilometers (16,100 square miles) to the New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA) for the development of green hydrogen projects, according to NREA's chairman Mohamed El-Khayat. This allocation, with an additional 900 square kilometers nearing finalization, aims to support the expansion of renewable energy initiatives focused on green hydrogen production. El-Khayat highlighted that this area will accommodate projects outlined in 27 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with various investors, totaling 115 GW of capacity, including 52 GW from solar and 63 GW from wind energy. Additionally, land plots have been designated in the Red Sea and Suez governorates for renewable energy projects capable of hosting approximately 4.4 GW of wind and 11 GW of solar energy. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly underscored the importance of expeditiously transforming framework agreements into formal contracts to advance Egypt's green hydrogen agenda. Randa Al-Minshawi, Head of the Technical Secretariat of the National Green Hydrogen Council, noted the signing of 27 MoUs and 10 binding framework agreements, with preparations ongoing for two additional binding agreements.
records.institution: Egyptian New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA)

records.title: Egypt's MPs Grant Private Sector Greater Role in Running Public Services
records.description: Egypt's Parliament has approved the government's economic and social development plan for the fiscal year 2024/2025, which includes a significant expansion of the private sector's role in health and education. Minister of Planning and Economic Development Hala Al Said presented the plan, aiming to increase private sector involvement in healthcare from 30% to 50% by 2030, and overall private sector participation in the economy to 50% by the same year. This move follows a recent controversial law allowing private companies to manage public hospitals, part of broader privatization efforts. Despite concerns about accessibility, especially for the underprivileged who rely on public services, the government asserts that these reforms will enhance service quality and efficiency, aligned with economic restructuring efforts supported by international partners like the IMF.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Egyptian Food Bank (EFB) recently hosted Dr.
records.description: The Egyptian Food Bank (EFB) recently hosted Dr. Abbas Al Hajj Hassan, the Lebanese Minister of Agriculture, and Dr. Salem Darwich, Advisor to the Minister, to share strategic insights on food security initiatives. Grounded in research and evaluation, EFB's efforts aim to provide healthy and safe food to millions of deserving individuals across Egypt. During the visit, EFB highlighted its comprehensive approach to addressing nutritional needs nationwide, serving over one million families through various programs and initiatives. The visit included discussions on innovative projects like the Food Secure Villages Project, which integrates fish farming to enhance food security and sustainability in Egypt's most vulnerable communities.

records.title: Iraq's General Union of Cooperative Agricultural Associations recently convened with Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, where discus...
records.description: Iraq's General Union of Cooperative Agricultural Associations recently convened with Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, where discussions centered on enhancing the agricultural sector. Prime Minister Al-Sudani underscored the union's pivotal role in bridging government-farmer relations and reiterated the administration's commitment to bolstering agriculture. This initiative aims to diversify the economy away from oil dependency, utilizing oil revenues to cultivate sectors like agriculture. Al-Sudani also announced increased purchase prices for crops cultivated with modern irrigation systems, highlighting Iraq's importation of 12,000 such systems. Additionally, a new water management agreement with Turkey is anticipated to further elevate Iraq's agricultural capabilities, while local fertilizer production will be supported, and import restrictions on fertilizers lifted, to bolster farming efficiency and productivity.
records.institution: Iraqi General Union of Cooperative Agricultural Associations

records.title: In Unaiza, Saudi Arabia, the annual date market showcases the region's pivotal role in the date industry, trading 280 tons of dates daily.
records.description: In Unaiza, Saudi Arabia, the annual date market showcases the region's pivotal role in the date industry, trading 280 tons of dates daily. Located in the Qassim region, the event highlights various date varieties, including the esteemed Sukkari. Prices vary widely, from 5 riyals for 3 kg to 700 riyals, reflecting quality differences. Auctioneers facilitate sales, crucial for global exports, reaching approximately 50 countries last year despite pandemic-related visitor restrictions. This year, exports aim to expand to 60 countries, targeting 20,000 tons of dates from Saudi Arabia's annual production of 1.4 million tons, supported by the National Center for Palms and Dates (NCPD).
records.institution: Saudi National Center for Palms and Dates (NCPD)

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources, Bandar bin Ibrahim Al-Khorayef, met with Moroccan counterparts to strengthen e...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources, Bandar bin Ibrahim Al-Khorayef, met with Moroccan counterparts to strengthen economic ties between the two nations. Discussions focused on enhancing cooperation in mining, developing economic sectors, and bolstering financial institutions. Key areas included advancing the phosphate industry, optimizing phosphate fertilizer competitiveness, and facilitating regional mineral trade. The talks also addressed collaborative efforts in export promotion and supporting Saudi exports in Morocco, underscoring mutual strategic interests in industrial and mining sectors.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources

records.title: Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabian ACWA Power are advancing joint investment projects following discussions between President Shavkat Mirziyoye...
records.description: Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabian ACWA Power are advancing joint investment projects following discussions between President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Muhammad Abunayyan, co-chairman of the Uzbek-Saudi Business Council and chairman of ACWA Power. The talks, held on June 4, focused on ongoing investment initiatives and expanding cooperation with Saudi firms. President Mirziyoyev praised the success of ACWA Power's contributions to Uzbekistan's energy sector, highlighting a combined project portfolio exceeding $17 billion. Emphasis was placed on accelerating joint projects in construction, airport management, digital and energy infrastructure modernization, heat supply networks expansion, waste processing, pharmaceuticals, oncology clinics, tourism, textile clusters, and agricultural development.

records.title: The Syrian Interim Government (SIG) has established wheat prices in its controlled territories, setting the rate for first-grade soft whe...
records.description: The Syrian Interim Government (SIG) has established wheat prices in its controlled territories, setting the rate for first-grade soft wheat at $220 per ton. Additionally, farmers receive a $25 bonus per ton delivered, as confirmed by Jumaa Bakour, director of the Aleppo branch of the Grain Corporation affiliated with the SIG. This pricing aligns with a September 2023 decision, with adjustments from previous seasons where higher rates were in effect. In contrast, other regional authorities like the Syrian Salvation Government and the Syrian regime have also adjusted wheat prices, reflecting differing economic conditions and geopolitical challenges impacting agricultural sectors across Syria.

records.title: Ambassador Abdulaziz Akkulov of Uzbekistan met with Raya Almazrouei, Director General of UAE's Etihad Credit Insurance, to discuss insuri...
records.description: Ambassador Abdulaziz Akkulov of Uzbekistan met with Raya Almazrouei, Director General of UAE's Etihad Credit Insurance, to discuss insuring export-import contracts for agricultural products between the two countries. They emphasized the growing interest of UAE companies in importing Uzbek agricultural goods and the need for reliable partnerships and connections. During the meeting, a memorandum of understanding was signed between Etihad Credit Insurance and Uzbekinvest, aiming to facilitate and secure trade transactions, reflecting mutual efforts to strengthen bilateral economic ties.

records.title: President Sheikh Mohamed of the UAE met with Afghanistan's Interior Minister, Sirajuddin Haqqani, at Al Shati Palace in Abu Dhabi to disc...
records.description: President Sheikh Mohamed of the UAE met with Afghanistan's Interior Minister, Sirajuddin Haqqani, at Al Shati Palace in Abu Dhabi to discuss bilateral relations and regional stability. The meeting focused on economic cooperation and supporting Afghanistan's reconstruction efforts following years of conflict. Haqqani expressed a desire to strengthen ties with Sheikh Mohamed, emphasizing mutual cooperation in various developmental sectors. Notably, no country has formally recognized the Taliban government in Afghanistan since its takeover in 2021, although several nations, including those in the Gulf region, have engaged with Kabul on diplomatic levels.

records.title: Zayed Lasheen, CEO of AfriGoodGrow, notes challenges in sourcing high-quality onions from Egypt, citing competition dynamics in the onion...
records.description: Zayed Lasheen, CEO of AfriGoodGrow, notes challenges in sourcing high-quality onions from Egypt, citing competition dynamics in the onion market. While Egyptian red onions dominate certain European markets like England, the Netherlands holds sway in yellow onion supply due to competitive pricing. Lasheen observes a significant drop in prices for Egyptian red onions this season, driven by abundant volumes. However, he anticipates price increases soon due to water content loss affecting costs and difficulties in obtaining superior quality onions, particularly those grown in desert sandy soil. Lasheen emphasizes the advantages of desert-grown onions for resilience and quality maintenance throughout the season at AfriGoodGrow.

records.title: The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has announced an allocation of approximately 3 trillion dinars ($2.3 billion) to facilitate housing loans...
records.description: The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has announced an allocation of approximately 3 trillion dinars ($2.3 billion) to facilitate housing loans through the Real Estate Bank and the Iraqi Housing Fund. This initiative aims to bolster the government's housing programs, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA). The CBI has directed the Real Estate Bank and the Iraqi Housing Fund to formulate a comprehensive plan for processing loan applications from citizens, ensuring adherence to governmental guidelines and regulatory standards, with a focus on fairness and prioritizing completed or ongoing applications. Moreover, the CBI's Board has urged government bodies and Parliament to allocate an annual budget to enhance the capital of these institutions, thereby enabling them to efficiently provide housing loans to Iraqi citizens.

records.title: Ministers Khalid Hneifat of Jordan and Rezq Salimia of Palestine recently convened to discuss enhancing agricultural cooperation and mark...
records.description: Ministers Khalid Hneifat of Jordan and Rezq Salimia of Palestine recently convened to discuss enhancing agricultural cooperation and marketing strategies through the Jordanian-Palestinian Agricultural Products Marketing Company (JPACO). They explored ways to overcome obstacles and expand marketing plans to promote agricultural products from both nations. Hneifat reaffirmed Jordan's support for rehabilitating Palestine's agricultural sector post-conflict, offering to leverage Jordanian private sector involvement. Salimia appreciated Jordan's steadfast support for Palestinian rights and explored potential collaborations, including transferring Jordan's expertise in horizontal grain silos to Palestine to enhance wheat storage capacity. JPACO aims to boost export markets for fresh and processed agricultural products, prioritizing small and medium-sized farmers and expanding market reach through strategic analyses and network utilization.

records.title: ACWA Power Co has signed an MoU with the Tunisian government to explore a significant green hydrogen project aimed at exporting to Europe.
records.description: ACWA Power Co has signed an MoU with the Tunisian government to explore a significant green hydrogen project aimed at exporting to Europe. This initiative, developed in three phases with a total of 12 GW in renewable energy capacity, including electrolysis and infrastructure for hydrogen export via the South2 Corridor, aligns with Tunisia’s ambitious green hydrogen strategy. Led by ACWA Power CEO Marco Arcelli and Tunisian Minister of Industry, Mines and Energy Fatma Thabet Chiboub, the project underscores ACWA Power's commitment to expanding its green hydrogen footprint beyond its ongoing projects in Saudi Arabia and Uzbekistan.

records.title: In Wenchang City, Hainan Province, the "China-UAE Friendship Forest of Date Palm" showcases accelerated fruiting of date palm trees, a re...
records.description: In Wenchang City, Hainan Province, the "China-UAE Friendship Forest of Date Palm" showcases accelerated fruiting of date palm trees, a result of successful cooperation between China and the UAE in the date palm industry. Led by Hu Wei of the Coconut Research Institute, advancements include the rapid fruiting of date palms within two years, compared to the typical three to five years in Arab countries. This collaboration, initiated with a UAE donation of 100,000 date palm seedlings in 2019, emphasizes technology transfer and cultivation techniques, enhancing ecological restoration efforts in hot regions like Hainan and Yunnan.
records.institution: Coconut Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences

records.title: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Youcef Cherfa, hosted his Mauritanian counterpart, Memma Beibatta Hmalla, in...
records.description: The Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Youcef Cherfa, hosted his Mauritanian counterpart, Memma Beibatta Hmalla, in Algiers to bolster economic ties and agricultural cooperation between their nations. Emphasizing mutual development through knowledge exchange, Minister Cherfa highlighted agriculture and industry as pivotal sectors for enhancing their partnership. Discussions centered on strategies to bolster food security and economic prosperity, underscoring the potential for joint initiatives to leverage Algeria's and Mauritania's resources and expertise. The meeting, coinciding with Mr. Hmalla's participation in the SIPSA FILAHA agricultural exhibition, signifies a proactive step towards fostering sustainable agricultural practices and economic advancement in both countries.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
