records.description: Saudi Arabia and the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) will host World Environment Day on June 5 in Riyadh under the theme "Our Land, Our Future." The event, at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center, aims to highlight Saudi Arabia's commitment to environmental protection and sustainable development in alignment with Vision 2030 goals. Focus areas include land restoration, combating desertification, and enhancing drought resilience, reinforcing global initiatives like the G20 Global Land Initiative and upcoming UNCCD COP16 session in Riyadh.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: Italian Ambassador to the UAE, Lorenzo Fanara, emphasizes the strong bilateral ties between Italy and the UAE, aiming to build enduring b...
records.description: Italian Ambassador to the UAE, Lorenzo Fanara, emphasizes the strong bilateral ties between Italy and the UAE, aiming to build enduring bridges through cultural diplomacy amid global challenges. He highlights the revitalization of relations, citing increased trade and significant cultural exchanges, including Italian cultural events in the UAE. Fanara also discusses Italy's humanitarian efforts in Gaza and its stance on immigration, stressing the need for legal and humane migration policies in Europe.

records.title: Iraq continues to integrate wheat supplies from Kurdistan Region farmers, with a reported 515,000 tons received from silos by May 20.
records.description: Iraq continues to integrate wheat supplies from Kurdistan Region farmers, with a reported 515,000 tons received from silos by May 20. Haidar Karrawi, General Director of the Grain Marketing Company, confirmed preparations to receive wheat from Erbil, Sulaimani, and Duhok provinces. Last year, Kirkuk led in wheat production with 495,000 tons, followed by Nineveh at 927,000 tons and Salahaddin at 830,000 tons. Discussions between Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani and KRG Minister of Agriculture and Water Resources Begard Talabani underscored broader agricultural cooperation and market strategies for Kurdistan Region produce.

records.title: Fisheries Development Oman (FDO) has proudly commissioned the state-of-the-art fishing vessel "ADAMAS" under its subsidiary Oman Pelagic,...
records.description: Fisheries Development Oman (FDO) has proudly commissioned the state-of-the-art fishing vessel "ADAMAS" under its subsidiary Oman Pelagic, marking a significant advancement in Oman's fisheries sector. Built to the highest international standards at Zamakona Shipyard in Spain, ADAMAS epitomizes FDO's commitment to sustainable fishing practices and economic growth. With a length of 84 meters and a capacity of 1200 tonnes, ADAMAS is equipped with advanced environmental instruments and biodegradable fish aggregation devices, ensuring operational efficiency and ecosystem conservation. This milestone underscores Oman's dedication to enhancing food security and bolstering its maritime legacy in line with Oman Vision 2040.

records.title: Fisheries Development Oman proudly announces the addition of ADAMAS to its fleet, a state-of-the-art vessel commissioned under Oman Pelagic.
records.description: Fisheries Development Oman proudly announces the addition of ADAMAS to its fleet, a state-of-the-art vessel commissioned under Oman Pelagic. Built to the highest international standards by Zamakona Shipyard in Spain, ADAMAS symbolizes Oman's commitment to sustainable fishing practices and economic growth in the fisheries sector. With advanced environmental instruments and biodegradable fish aggregation devices, the 84-meter vessel ensures operational efficiency and ecosystem conservation.

records.title: The Oman Flour Mills Company has doubled its purchase of Omani wheat in 2024, acquiring 10,000 tonnes compared to the previous year's 5,0...
records.description: The Oman Flour Mills Company has doubled its purchase of Omani wheat in 2024, acquiring 10,000 tonnes compared to the previous year's 5,000 tonnes. This increase supports local farmers and strengthens Oman's food security strategy by promoting domestic wheat cultivation. The initiative, conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries and Water Resources, aims to meet growing regional demand for high-quality Omani agricultural products while expanding market presence and farmer participation.

records.title: The Oman Flour Mills Company has increased its purchase of wheat from Omani farmers by 100%, acquiring 10,000 tonnes this year, up from t...
records.description: The Oman Flour Mills Company has increased its purchase of wheat from Omani farmers by 100%, acquiring 10,000 tonnes this year, up from the previous year's 5,000 tonnes. This initiative is part of their efforts to enhance food security and promote local wheat cultivation. CEO Haitham bin Mohammed al-Fannah highlighted the company's ongoing support for farmers, collaborating with the Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources to expand wheat production.

records.title: The Central Bank of Yemen, based in Sana’a, has issued a ban on 13 financial institutions, both local and international, prohibiting deal...
records.description: The Central Bank of Yemen, based in Sana’a, has issued a ban on 13 financial institutions, both local and international, prohibiting dealings with them due to violations of Yemeni laws and the Central Bank's regulations. These violations include conducting banking activities without proper licensing, breaching Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing laws, and collaborating with internationally convicted entities involved in corruption, money laundering, and terrorist financing. Furthermore, these institutions have been accused of leaking financial data to hostile entities, posing a threat to Yemen's national security.

records.title: Prime Minister Muhammad Shiaa Al-Sudani announced that for the first time in Iraq, 12,000 irrigation systems have been imported.
records.description: Prime Minister Muhammad Shiaa Al-Sudani announced that for the first time in Iraq, 12,000 irrigation systems have been imported. He emphasized the significance of supporting and advancing the agricultural sector as a priority goal of the government to diversify the economy beyond oil dependence.

records.title: Pakistan and Kuwait agreed on a $25 million loan for the Mohmand Dam during the 5th session of the Pakistan-Kuwait Joint Ministerial Comm...
records.description: Pakistan and Kuwait agreed on a $25 million loan for the Mohmand Dam during the 5th session of the Pakistan-Kuwait Joint Ministerial Commission. The session emphasized collaboration across sectors and saw the signing of agreements and MoUs. Abdul Aleem Khan highlighted the importance of private sector engagement and urged Kuwait to ease visa procedures. Dr. Kazim Niaz emphasized the potential of the JMC in fostering cooperation. Discussions covered various sectors, and both sides agreed to establish Joint Working Groups.

records.title: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has initiated an employment project aimed at providing opportunities for conflict-displac...
records.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has initiated an employment project aimed at providing opportunities for conflict-displaced Lebanese from southern border villages. Named "Work for Cash," the program offers cleaning and agricultural jobs, providing participants with $10 for five hours of daily work, totaling $200 for 20 working days a month. With approximately 81,000 displaced individuals in southern Lebanon, the program seeks to address their needs while supporting their integration into the workforce.

records.title: CESCO EPC and United Feed Co.
records.description: CESCO EPC and United Feed Co. (UFC) have partnered on a significant storage and conveying project in Saudi Arabia, focusing on enhancing UFC's capacity with 15 corrugated steel flat-bottom storage silos totaling 205,152 tonnes. Designed for storing grains, cereals, and oilseeds, the facility includes advanced features like high-capacity receiving lines, state-of-the-art cleaning processes, and a versatile reclaiming system for efficient material distribution. CESCO's comprehensive conveyor system ensures operational efficiency and supports future expansion plans, reinforcing UFC's role in Saudi Arabia's food industry and enhancing regional food security through stable feedstock supply capabilities.

records.title: Iyris, a startup operating in Riyadh, Abu Dhabi, and Delaware, has secured $16 million in Series A funding to address the challenges of c...
records.description: Iyris, a startup operating in Riyadh, Abu Dhabi, and Delaware, has secured $16 million in Series A funding to address the challenges of climate change in agriculture. Led by the San Francisco-based climate and sustainability fund Ecosystem Integrity Fund (EIF), the investment will support Iyris' innovative agricultural solutions, particularly its flagship technology, SecondSky. Developed from innovations at the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), SecondSky utilizes an additive in polyethylene manufacturing to block heat while allowing essential light for photosynthesis, enabling farmers to reduce cooling costs and water usage. This technology has gained traction globally, especially in regions facing harsh growing conditions due to climate change. By extending growing seasons and increasing yields, Iyris aims to enhance food security while maintaining profitability for farmers.

records.title: KSrelief, Saudi Arabia's aid agency, has extended its support to vulnerable populations in Jordan's Zaatari refugee camp and Yemen, provi...
records.description: KSrelief, Saudi Arabia's aid agency, has extended its support to vulnerable populations in Jordan's Zaatari refugee camp and Yemen, providing health and food aid. In Zaatari, over 2,349 patients were treated at KSrelief-operated clinics in May, with 335 procedures conducted for various ailments. In Yemen, food aid was distributed to 680 families in Aden and Lahj, benefiting 4,760 individuals.

records.title: Dr.
records.description: Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of State for Foreign Trade, engaged in constructive discussions with China's Commerce Minister, Wang Wentao, during the UAE-China Business and Investment Forum, coinciding with President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan's two-day state visit to China. The ministers explored avenues to stimulate bilateral trade and investment growth across high-potential sectors. Notably, 12 agreements and memorandums of understanding were exchanged between Emirati and Chinese entities spanning diverse sectors like aluminium, communications, and financial services. Alsuwaidi highlighted China's increasing investments in the UAE, rising by 16 percent in 2023 to reach US$1.3 billion, comprising 60 percent of China's investments in Arab nations. Dr. Al Zeyoudi projected the UAE-China non-oil trade to exceed $200 billion by 2023, building upon the $81 billion recorded in 2023.

records.title: The Ministry of Sustainable Development, in collaboration with the United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Bahrain and UN Women, or...
records.description: The Ministry of Sustainable Development, in collaboration with the United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Bahrain and UN Women, organized a workshop on Gender Equality, focusing on Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5. The workshop aimed to enhance Bahrain's statistical capabilities for SDGs and underscored the nation's commitment to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It addressed calculation methodologies for SDG 5 indicators, fostering discussions among stakeholders to strengthen data monitoring and analysis.

records.title: The head of the Jordan and Amman Chambers of Industry, Fathi Jaghbir, met with the Ambassador of Yemen to Jordan, Jalal Faqirah, aiming t...
records.description: The head of the Jordan and Amman Chambers of Industry, Fathi Jaghbir, met with the Ambassador of Yemen to Jordan, Jalal Faqirah, aiming to bolster economic ties between the two nations. Jaghbir highlighted Jordan's appeal for foreign investments, citing its strategic location and free trade agreements. He proposed organizing a workshop and an economic forum to introduce investment opportunities and strengthen bilateral relations. Despite modest current economic relations, with Jordanian exports to Yemen totaling $112.5 million in 2023 and imports at $200,000, both parties expressed optimism for future growth, given Yemeni interest in investing in Jordan due to favorable conditions and cultural affinities.
records.institution: Jordan and Amman Chambers of Industry

records.title: Morocco's agritech startup YoLa Fresh has closed a $7 million pre-Series A funding round, led by Al Mada Ventures and joined by Algebra V...
records.description: Morocco's agritech startup YoLa Fresh has closed a $7 million pre-Series A funding round, led by Al Mada Ventures and joined by Algebra Ventures, E3 Capital, Janngo Capital, and FMO. Founded in 2023 by Youssef Mamou and Larbi Alaoui Belrhiti, YoLa Fresh connects farmers directly with retailers and food service companies, ensuring transparency and minimizing waste in the fresh food supply chain. With plans to expand beyond Morocco, YoLa Fresh aims to address food security challenges and drive economic growth across Africa. This funding round will enable the company to enhance its logistics network, bolster technology, and empower more farmers to deliver high-quality produce directly to consumers.

records.title: The African Development Bank's (AfDB) board of directors has greenlit an €84 million fund to bolster a sustainable development project in...
records.description: The African Development Bank's (AfDB) board of directors has greenlit an €84 million fund to bolster a sustainable development project in Morocco, targeting 6.5 million rural residents across different regions. The initiative aims to enhance Morocco's economic resilience against climate change and improve water management, particularly in Rabat Sale Kenitra, Marrakech Safi, Tangier Tetouan Al Hoceima, and Souss Massa. Covering four watersheds and national parks, the project aims to foster a rural middle class through sustainable natural resource management, inclusive forest value chains, and entrepreneurship in forestry and aquaculture.

records.title: Oman has reached a significant milestone in its government digital transformation efforts, achieving a completion rate of 53% by Septembe...
records.description: Oman has reached a significant milestone in its government digital transformation efforts, achieving a completion rate of 53% by September 2023, according to H E Dr Ali bin Amer al Shidhani, Undersecretary for Communications and Information Technology in the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology. This achievement was highlighted during the second edition of the Government Digital Transformation Forum, held alongside the COMEX Show. The forum served as a platform to showcase government institutions' achievements in adopting digital technologies, discussing best practices, future trends, and innovative solutions to enhance public services and skill development within the sultanate. H E Shidhani outlined Oman's progress, emphasizing the commitment to digital transformation and the significant increase in electronic transactions and services digitization. Notably, efforts have simplified numerous services and digitized a substantial portion of basic government services, marking significant progress towards the goal of digitizing all essential services by 2025.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology

records.title: Omani Consul General expressed interest in importing agricultural products from Pakistan, citing the country's high-quality rice.
records.description: Omani Consul General expressed interest in importing agricultural products from Pakistan, citing the country's high-quality rice. He highlighted the need to expand trade relations, emphasizing Oman's reliance on imports from various countries. The meeting aimed to foster economic cooperation, with discussions on reducing trade barriers and exploring energy sector collaboration, including LNG and petroleum imports from Oman to address Pakistan's energy needs.

records.title: On May 30, 2024, the State of Qatar, represented by the Ministry of Finance, and the United Arab Emirates, represented by the UAE Ministr...
records.description: On May 30, 2024, the State of Qatar, represented by the Ministry of Finance, and the United Arab Emirates, represented by the UAE Ministry of Finance, signed an agreement to prevent double taxation and fiscal evasion regarding income taxes. HE Mr Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari, Qatar's Minister of Finance, and HE Mohamed Hadi Al Hussaini, UAE Minister of State for Financial Affairs, signed the agreement. The signing ceremony, attended by H.E. Mr. Khalifa bin Jassim Al-Kuwari, President of the General Tax Authority, symbolizes Qatar's commitment to bolstering economic relations and trade cooperation with sisterly countries. This agreement marks a significant step in eliminating double taxation and combating tax evasion between Qatar and the UAE, aligning with global transparency standards and facilitating the exchange of reliable financial information.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has initiated a new share sale for state oil giant Aramco, with plans to raise up to $13.1 billion.
records.description: Saudi Arabia has initiated a new share sale for state oil giant Aramco, with plans to raise up to $13.1 billion. The sale, aimed at funding Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's economic diversification agenda, involves offering approximately 1.545 billion Aramco shares, equivalent to about 0.64% of the company's stake, at a pricing range of 26.7 to 29 riyals per share. An additional greenshoe option could potentially increase the value to $13.1 billion, allowing the sale of nearly 1.7 billion shares. About 10% of the offering will be reserved for retail investors. Aramco's CEO, Amin Nasser, highlighted the opportunity to expand the shareholder base and increase liquidity through this offering. The move follows Aramco's record-setting IPO in 2019, which raised $29.4 billion. The proceeds from the latest sale will contribute to financing domestic projects aimed at diversifying Saudi Arabia's economy away from oil dependency. This initiative aligns with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's vision to invest in various sectors, including renewable energy, technology, tourism, logistics, and manufacturing, to stimulate long-term economic growth. Joint global coordinators for the deal include Morgan Stanley, Citi, Goldman Sachs, HSBC, Saudi National Bank, Bank of America, and JPMorgan, with several local banks serving as joint bookrunners.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia is prioritizing solar power as part of its energy transition efforts, despite its significant oil reserves.
records.description: Saudi Arabia is prioritizing solar power as part of its energy transition efforts, despite its significant oil reserves. The Sudair solar project near Riyadh exemplifies this commitment, with vast arrays of solar panels capable of powering thousands of homes. While renewables currently contribute minimally to the country's electricity generation, Saudi Arabia aims to increase its renewable energy output to around 50 percent by 2030. However, analysts anticipate challenges in achieving this ambitious target, emphasizing the need for continued investment and innovation in the renewable energy sector.

records.title: The Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation in Yemen's caretaker government, Eng.
records.description: The Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation in Yemen's caretaker government, Eng. Abdulmalik Al-Thawr, held a meeting with teams from the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) in Yemen. Discussions centered on enhancing cooperation with IFAD and expanding partnerships with FAO to bolster the agricultural sector's role in achieving food security. The meeting underscored the importance of IFAD's resumption of activities in financing agricultural projects, supporting development programs, and improving farmers' income sources amidst challenges posed by aggression and blockade.
records.institution: Yemeni Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation

records.title: Egypt and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are engaged in ongoing discussions regarding the Ras El Hekma development project on Egypt's Med...
records.description: Egypt and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are engaged in ongoing discussions regarding the Ras El Hekma development project on Egypt's Mediterranean coast. Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, ADQ, previously agreed to pay $24 billion for the rights to develop the extensive Ras El Hekma peninsula, with potentially an additional $150 billion in investments. Nader El Biblawi, chairman of the Egyptian travel agents association, highlighted that contract finalizations are still underway, and the project's timeline remains unclear. While the funds are being collected, specific schedules are yet to be disclosed. The Ras El Hekma project aims to establish a "next-generation city" spanning 170 square kilometers, featuring tourism and residential developments, investment zones, technology, light industry, amusement parks, a marina, and an airport. Talks for a similar development deal with Saudi Arabia for Ras Gamila are said to be in early stages, pending the outcome of the Ras El Hekma project. Ras Gamila's potential development could complement Saudi Arabia's NEOM project, creating an Egyptian-Saudi Riviera if realized.

records.title: Egypt will significantly increase the price of state-subsidized bread, raising it from 5 piastres to 20 piastres per loaf starting June 1.
records.description: Egypt will significantly increase the price of state-subsidized bread, raising it from 5 piastres to 20 piastres per loaf starting June 1. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly made this announcement as part of efforts to address economic challenges and reduce the strain of subsidies on the state budget. With over 70 million Egyptians entitled to subsidized bread, the adjustment marks the first in more than 30 years. The government spends approximately 100 billion Egyptian pounds annually on bread subsidies, generating only 5 billion Egyptian pounds in revenue. Madbouly affirmed the state's commitment to subsidizing essential commodities while considering a transition to a cash subsidy system, aiming to begin implementation in the 2025-2026 fiscal year. This move follows President Abdel Fattah El Sisi's recent 15 percent increase in pensions and amid public dissatisfaction over frequent power cuts. Madbouly assured that power cuts would cease by November or December and emphasized the necessity of subsidy reform due to the country's high population growth rate and economic challenges.

records.domain: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
records.title: Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has hinted at an imminent reduction in state subsidies on essential commodities, signaling poten...
records.description: Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has hinted at an imminent reduction in state subsidies on essential commodities, signaling potential cuts to bread and diesel subsidies by the beginning of the 2025/2026 fiscal year. Madbouly emphasized the unsustainable financial burden placed on the state, particularly concerning bread and diesel subsidies. This indication follows President Abdel Fattah El Sisi's recent 15 percent increase in pensions, with the government currently spending 100 billion Egyptian pounds annually to subsidize bread. Despite these subsidies, the state only generates five billion pounds in revenue, selling loaves at five piastres despite a production cost of one pound per loaf. Madbouly stressed the necessity of revisiting subsidy policies, particularly in light of ongoing economic challenges and the need to reduce state expenditure. The potential subsidy reduction has sparked concerns among the population, particularly among the underprivileged who heavily rely on these support systems.

records.title: Several agricultural development projects were launched and inaugurated in the Provinces of Rhamna and Kelâa des Sraghna as part of Moroc...
records.description: Several agricultural development projects were launched and inaugurated in the Provinces of Rhamna and Kelâa des Sraghna as part of Morocco's Generation Green strategy. The Minister of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development, and Water and Forests, Mr. Mohammed Sadiki, led a field visit to review the progress of the Provincial Agricultural Plans of both provinces. These plans include various projects aimed at water conservation, solidarity agriculture, and modernizing marketing infrastructures. Key initiatives include launching cactus plantations, inaugurating a new Agricultural Technical Institute, modernizing markets and slaughterhouses, and signing partnership agreements to promote agricultural entrepreneurship. These projects, with investments totaling billions of dirhams, aim to boost agricultural development and sustainability in the region, benefiting small farmers and contributing to economic growth.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests

records.title: Qatar, in collaboration with the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organization (JHCO), initiated a campaign to send 10,000 food parcels to Gaza t...
records.description: Qatar, in collaboration with the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organization (JHCO), initiated a campaign to send 10,000 food parcels to Gaza through Qatar Charity. The effort, attended by Qatari Ambassador Sheikh Saud bin Nasser bin Jassim Al Thani and Qatar Charity's Saleh Al Marri, aims to benefit around 50,000 people in Gaza. The parcels, containing essential food supplies for a month, underscore Qatar's commitment to supporting Palestinians in Gaza, reflecting the ongoing humanitarian cooperation between Qatar and Jordan.

records.title: Saudi Arabia reaffirmed its commitment to tackling challenges in agricultural development and food security, both domestically and intern...
records.description: Saudi Arabia reaffirmed its commitment to tackling challenges in agricultural development and food security, both domestically and internationally, during an extraordinary virtual meeting of the GCC Agriculture and Food Security Agents Committee. Engineer Ahmed Al-Eyada, the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, highlighted Saudi Arabia's dedication to achieving agricultural and food sustainability, emphasizing the importance of strategies to sustain the agricultural sector regionally and globally. The meeting focused on assessing the current food security situation in the GCC, exploring opportunities for regional cooperation, and developing strategies to enhance food security. Notably, the GCC countries have made significant progress in agricultural GDP growth and managing the Consumer Price Index for foodstuffs, reflecting efforts to strengthen food security in the region.

records.title: Tunisia and Italy have solidified their collaboration in digital technology and its industrial applications through a memorandum of under...
records.description: Tunisia and Italy have solidified their collaboration in digital technology and its industrial applications through a memorandum of understanding (MoU), underscoring joint efforts to enhance economic and industrial cooperation. Signed by Communication Technologies Minister Nizar Ben Neji and Italy's Minister of Enterprises and Made in Italy, Adolfo Urso, the MoU outlines the establishment of two national focal points and a joint team. This agreement aims to facilitate investment opportunities for Tunisian and Italian companies, organizing forums, conferences, and workshops. It also prioritizes technology transfer, research, innovation, and training, particularly in AI, to bolster projects in both the public and private sectors. The ministers highlighted the significance of this cooperation, with Italy expressing its commitment to supporting Tunisia's digital transition through knowledge exchange and expertise sharing in digital infrastructure, AI, and aerospace activities.

records.title: ADAFSA has concluded its "Mawhiba" agricultural program, a collaboration with the Emirates Schools Establishment (ESE) and the UAE Univer...
records.description: ADAFSA has concluded its "Mawhiba" agricultural program, a collaboration with the Emirates Schools Establishment (ESE) and the UAE University’s Continuing Education Center (UAEU), aimed at nurturing local talent in Abu Dhabi's agricultural sector. The program, designed to enhance agricultural skills and foster innovation, provided hands-on field training across various agricultural domains to sixty students. Through partnerships and field training at ADAFSA research stations and UAEU facilities, the initiative aimed to integrate scientific research with practical applications in biosecurity, agriculture, and food safety. The curriculum covered advanced agricultural techniques, plant protection, irrigation, beekeeping, fish farming, and more, encouraging students to develop creative agricultural projects to contribute to Abu Dhabi's food security goals.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The UAE and South Korea have entered into a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA), signaling a significant move towards fre...
records.description: The UAE and South Korea have entered into a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA), signaling a significant move towards free trade and enhanced investment between the two nations. Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of State for Foreign Trade, and Ahn Duk-geun, Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy of South Korea, inked the agreement in Seoul. As part of the UAE's CEPA foreign trade program, aimed at boosting non-oil foreign trade, the agreement will gradually eliminate tariffs on over 90 percent of imports from both countries over the next decade, fostering cooperation in key sectors like energy, healthcare, advanced industries, and more. The visit of President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to Seoul saw the signing of 19 business agreements, spanning investment, energy, defense, and technology. Noteworthy deals include the UAE's commitment to invest $30 billion in South Korea and cooperation frameworks on climate change and energy infrastructure development.

records.title: Kuwait's National Bank of Kuwait (NBK) is gearing up to issue its inaugural green bonds, marking a significant step towards sustainable f...
records.description: Kuwait's National Bank of Kuwait (NBK) is gearing up to issue its inaugural green bonds, marking a significant step towards sustainable finance. The bank intends to launch 6-year non-callable for 5-years green bonds, as revealed in a document reviewed by Reuters. Joint global coordinators for the issuance include Citi, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, and Standard Chartered Bank, while Emirates NBD Capital, First Abu Dhabi Bank, Goldman Sachs International, and National Bank of Kuwait are named as joint lead managers and joint bookrunners. Investor meetings are scheduled to commence from May 28, with the issuance of U.S. dollar-denominated senior unsecured Green Notes under NBK SPC Limited's Global Medium Term Note Programme to follow.

records.title: During the 91st Annual General Session of the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) in France, Minister of Municipality H E Abdulla...
records.description: During the 91st Annual General Session of the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) in France, Minister of Municipality H E Abdullah bin Hamad bin Abdullah Al Attiyah engaged in discussions with Minister of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty of France H E Marc Fesneau regarding cooperation between Qatar and France in agriculture, food security, and livestock development. The meeting aimed to explore opportunities for collaboration and ways to strengthen existing ties between the two countries in these critical areas.

records.title: Emirates Integrated Telecommunications Company (du) has joined forces with Gracia Group to introduce an agritech platform, aimed at revol...
records.description: Emirates Integrated Telecommunications Company (du) has joined forces with Gracia Group to introduce an agritech platform, aimed at revolutionizing the agricultural sector in the UAE in alignment with the nation's growth objectives. This digital ecosystem harnesses ICT, cloud computing, automation, IoT, data science, and AI to advance farming practices sustainably and securely. Offering a comprehensive range of services, the platform caters to farmers, suppliers, buyers, agritech entities, businesses, and retail outlets. Jasim Al Awadi, CICTO at du, emphasized the platform's role in bridging ICT with agriculture, meeting the diverse needs of the farming community. Through this collaboration and cutting-edge technology, the agritech platform is poised to accelerate digital transformation in the agricultural sector, supporting the government's goals for food security and sustainability. It also aims to enhance investment opportunities in agriculture and provide training programs to promote farming as a mainstream business.
records.institution: Emirates Integrated Telecommunications Company (du) & Gracia Group

records.title: Tecnimont (Integrated E&C Solutions) has received the go-ahead from Fertiglobe to commence construction on a low-carbon ammonia plant in...
records.description: Tecnimont (Integrated E&C Solutions) has received the go-ahead from Fertiglobe to commence construction on a low-carbon ammonia plant in TA’ZIZ Derivatives Park, Ruwais region, Abu Dhabi, UAE. Fertiglobe, MENA's largest nitrogen fertilizer producer, is spearheading the project with partners TA’ZIZ (a JV between ADNOC and ADQ), Mitsui & Co. Ltd, and GS Energy Corporation. Scheduled for operation by 2027, the plant will produce 3000 tpd (approximately 1 million tpy) of ammonia, contributing to local industry supply chains and in-country value requirements. Low-carbon ammonia serves as a transition fuel, pivotal in decarbonizing the maritime sector and reducing carbon footprints in various energy applications.

records.title: Danone Egypt has introduced its latest product, Danone Greek yogurt, featuring a protein-rich creamy texture and complemented by deliciou...
records.description: Danone Egypt has introduced its latest product, Danone Greek yogurt, featuring a protein-rich creamy texture and complemented by delicious fruit varieties. The company, a subsidiary of Danone, known for its leadership in the dairy industry, offers a wide range of products catering to various nutritional needs. From full cream to light, sugar, and fruit varieties, Danone's portfolio includes yogurt options like Dango and Activia, along with specialized products like Danette pudding and HiPro drinkable yogurt.

records.title: Egypt is gearing up to plant 3.5 million feddans (1.47 million hectares) of wheat in the upcoming fiscal year 2024/2025, marking an incre...
records.description: Egypt is gearing up to plant 3.5 million feddans (1.47 million hectares) of wheat in the upcoming fiscal year 2024/2025, marking an increase from the current year's 3.2 million feddans. President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi unveiled this ambitious initiative as part of a comprehensive land reclamation program aimed at expanding the nation's agricultural land. Major projects such as the New Delta, Toshka, and Middle Sinai, long unimplemented, are integral to this plan. The target aims to boost wheat storage capacity to 5.2 million tonnes, reducing imports and fostering agricultural self-sufficiency. Egypt's agricultural sector, experiencing a 25% increase in export volume in 2023, signifies its growing efficiency and international competitiveness, contributing significantly to the country's economic development.

records.title: Alonso Group, a prominent Spanish logistics company, has expanded its operations into Morocco by establishing Alonso Forwarding Morocco i...
records.description: Alonso Group, a prominent Spanish logistics company, has expanded its operations into Morocco by establishing Alonso Forwarding Morocco in Casablanca, strategically positioning itself to capitalize on the growing trade relations between Morocco and Spain. This move underscores Alonso Group's commitment to global expansion, with plans to open a second office in Tangiers. The expansion aims to facilitate seamless cargo exchanges between Morocco, the Iberian Peninsula, and Europe, leveraging Morocco's pivotal role as Spain's top non-EU supplier of fresh produce.

records.title: Morocco's greenhouse tomato exports saw a significant rebound in early 2024, surpassing both the previous year's figures and the five-yea...
records.description: Morocco's greenhouse tomato exports saw a significant rebound in early 2024, surpassing both the previous year's figures and the five-year average. Despite challenges such as extreme heat and the Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus in 2023, exports from January to March reached 266,000 tons, marking a 10% increase from the previous year and a 9% rise above the five-year average. France remained the primary market, with other European countries like the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and Spain also significant buyers. However, trade tensions and increased tariffs pose challenges for future export volumes, highlighting the need for continued efforts to maintain strong trade relations and ensure a steady supply of Moroccan tomatoes to international markets.

records.title: Morocco's OCP Group and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) have joined forces in a $100 million partnership t...
records.description: Morocco's OCP Group and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) have joined forces in a $100 million partnership to tackle agricultural challenges in Africa. OCP Group's subsidiary, OCP Africa, will invest $30 million to enhance fertilizer usage across sub-Saharan Africa, complementing USAID's $40 million contribution to expand the Space to Place Project. This collaborative effort aims to implement innovative initiatives, including the development of a Decision Support Tool for farmers to optimize fertilizer application and a Rock Phosphate Amendment Project to improve soil fertility and crop yields. By leveraging geospatial technology and fostering stakeholder engagement, the partnership endeavors to unlock Africa's agricultural potential sustainably.
records.institution: OCP Group & The United States Agency for International Development (USAID)

records.title: Oman and Jordan are exploring the possibility of establishing a direct shipping line between the Jordanian port of Aqaba and ports in Oma...
records.description: Oman and Jordan are exploring the possibility of establishing a direct shipping line between the Jordanian port of Aqaba and ports in Oman, as announced during the recent visit of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik to Jordan. The announcement came alongside the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for investments in various sectors during His Majesty's visit. The MoU, signed between the Oman Investment Authority (OIA) and the Social Security Corporation, represented by the Social Security Investment Fund (SSIF) in Jordan, aims to promote joint investment opportunities between the two countries across various fields, including information and communications technology, food, agriculture, medicines, medical supplies, energy, mining, tourism, and logistics services.

records.title: Tunisia and the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development (FADES) recently signed a financing agreement worth 100 million Tunisian di...
records.description: Tunisia and the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development (FADES) recently signed a financing agreement worth 100 million Tunisian dinars (10 million Kuwaiti dinars) to support an integrated agricultural development project in the Wadi Tassa basin. The agreement was signed during joint annual meetings of Arab financial authorities in Cairo. The project aims to address various aspects of agricultural development, including land protection, hydraulic development, flood prevention, forest development, and improvement of agricultural infrastructure. Both parties emphasized the importance of cooperation, with FADES expressing its commitment to continue supporting Tunisia's development efforts. Additionally, Tunisia's Minister of Economy and Planning, Feryel Ouerghi Sabïi, engaged in discussions with various Arab financial institutions to explore avenues for strengthening cooperation and addressing challenges such as climate change and food security.

records.title: Algeria has greenlit new projects totaling approximately 3.34 billion Algerian dinars ($25 million) within the initial five months of 202...
records.description: Algeria has greenlit new projects totaling approximately 3.34 billion Algerian dinars ($25 million) within the initial five months of 2024, as reported by a government official. The Algerian National Investment Promotion Agency has issued licenses for 7,230 projects, predominantly in the SME sector. These projects, with nearly 65% having a capital of around DZD150 million ($1.12 million), span various sectors including industry and agriculture.

records.title: Türkiye's citrus exports surged in early 2024, reaching $475 million, a 16% increase compared to the previous year, with Iraq emerging as...
records.description: Türkiye's citrus exports surged in early 2024, reaching $475 million, a 16% increase compared to the previous year, with Iraq emerging as a standout market with a 400% rise in shipments. President Hayrettin Uçak of the Aegean Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Exporters Association highlighted that Türkiye's citrus exports hit a milestone of $1.1 billion in 2023, aiming for $1.3 billion this year. Russia led as the top market with $148 million in exports, followed by Iraq at $90.2 million, showcasing significant growth. Tangerines dominated exports, contributing 49% of total citrus exports, with notable increases to key markets like Russia and Iraq, highlighting Türkiye's robust citrus industry expansion efforts.
records.institution: Aegean Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Exporters Association

records.title: Egypt and Lebanon are strengthening agricultural cooperation as ministers El Sayed Al-Quseir and Abbas Al-Haj Hassan recently convened to...
records.description: Egypt and Lebanon are strengthening agricultural cooperation as ministers El Sayed Al-Quseir and Abbas Al-Haj Hassan recently convened to discuss enhancing collaboration in the sector. Key topics included facilitating the exchange of agricultural products, addressing barriers to trade, and organizing exports such as potatoes, onions, and palm trees from Egypt to Lebanon. The meeting also highlighted Lebanon's interest in leveraging Egypt's expertise in fish farming and artificial insemination to enhance breeding practices and provide training opportunities. Additionally, discussions covered the export of citrus fruits to Lebanon. Al-Haj Hassan visited a fish hatchery in Alexandria Governorate and the Samarmon factory in Borg El Arab to observe fish production and packing processes, further underscoring the commitment to bilateral agricultural development.

records.title: The Egyptian-Swiss Group, a prominent family-owned company, is poised to double its pasta exports to Saudi Arabia in 2024 while expanding...
records.description: The Egyptian-Swiss Group, a prominent family-owned company, is poised to double its pasta exports to Saudi Arabia in 2024 while expanding into the Gulf countries and the broader Middle East region. Engineer Ahmed El-Sabai, the General Manager, unveiled this ambitious plan during the recent Saudi Food Show exhibition. Renowned for its quality pasta, flour, and concentrates, the group aims to capitalize on its past success, having doubled its pasta exports last year. With a manufacturing capacity of 7,000 tons per month, the company plans to leverage its presence in the Saudi market, which is increasingly pivotal for Egypt's food export sector, showcasing a 9% growth in 2023.`

records.title: Mars Egypt has unveiled a substantial US$250 million capacity expansion plan for its 6th October factory, slated to unfold over the next...
records.description: Mars Egypt has unveiled a substantial US$250 million capacity expansion plan for its 6th October factory, slated to unfold over the next 18 months. This investment aims to elevate annual production capacity from 250,000 tons to 400,000 tons, augmenting the factory's output significantly. The expansion strategy encompasses the addition of two new production lines, expanding the current six, and introducing 15 new products to its existing portfolio of 150 items. Anticipated to conclude by early 2026, this initiative aligns with Mars Egypt's broader objective of diversifying its confectionary offerings and expanding its market presence, particularly in the Middle East. With plans to extend market reach beyond the current 40 countries in the Middle East and Africa, Mars Egypt's investment underscores its commitment to sustained growth and market leadership in the region. This move follows previous successful investment ventures, including a US$42 million expansion in 2018, which bolstered the company's exports outside Egypt to US$100 million by year-end. Ehab AbouOaf, the former regional head for Africa and the Middle East, emphasizes Egypt's pivotal role in the company's industrial and export operations, highlighting the country's strategic importance. Mars Egypt's commitment to sustainability is also evident, with the expansion plan integrated into its broader sustainability strategy. By leveraging advanced technologies and efficient production processes, the company aims to minimize environmental impact, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, optimize waste management, and enhance water conservation measures.

records.title: Capturiant, renowned as the world's pioneer energy-derived carbon credit and environmental asset authenticator, registry, and regulated e...
records.description: Capturiant, renowned as the world's pioneer energy-derived carbon credit and environmental asset authenticator, registry, and regulated exchange, has unveiled its inaugural Middle Eastern franchise in Iraq. This collaboration with Sharp Mind Global Ventures Inc., a Canadian entity with a presence in Iraq, signifies a significant stride towards broadening access to open-access environments for the trading, purchase, sale, and retirement of high-quality carbon credits and other environmental assets. The partnership aims to revolutionize the carbon credit industry in Iraq, leveraging Capturiant's innovative platform and Sharp Mind's expertise in carbon neutrality strategies and decarbonization efforts. Maziar Rajabi, Chairman and Founder of Sharp Mind Global Ventures, praised Capturiant's commitment to regulatory compliance, while James C. Row, Founder and CEO of Capturiant, expressed enthusiasm for expanding investment opportunities in Iraqi carbon credit projects.
records.institution: Capturiant & Sharp Mind Global Ventures Inc.

records.title: A delegation of Saudi companies, coordinated by the National Center for Palms and Dates (NCPD), recently visited Alibaba Group's headquar...
records.description: A delegation of Saudi companies, coordinated by the National Center for Palms and Dates (NCPD), recently visited Alibaba Group's headquarters in Hangzhou to explore opportunities in the Chinese market and amplify the promotion of Saudi dates globally. Over the course of six days, representatives from 23 Saudi companies showcased premium date products to Chinese food industry stakeholders. This strategic move aims to leverage Alibaba's platform to enhance the visibility and export potential of Saudi dates, including in China. Mohammed Al Nuwairan, CEO of NCPD, emphasized that featuring Saudi dates on Alibaba's expansive platform would facilitate their access to global markets, building upon the partnership established during the World of Dates Expo in Riyadh last December. The visit underscores NCPD's commitment to supporting Saudi date exports and positioning them as a preferred choice worldwide. Saudi Arabia witnessed a significant 14 percent increase in date exports in 2023, reaching SAR 1.462 billion, marking a 152.5 percent surge since 2016, with exports reaching 119 countries.
records.institution: Saudi National Center for Palms and Dates (NCPD)

records.title: Saudi Arabia plans to invest $4 billion in 96 projects aimed at enhancing water reuse infrastructure across agricultural, urban, and indu...
records.description: Saudi Arabia plans to invest $4 billion in 96 projects aimed at enhancing water reuse infrastructure across agricultural, urban, and industrial sectors, according to Muhammad bin Zaid Abuhaid, acting CEO of the Saudi Irrigation Organization (SIO). These initiatives, part of the National Water Strategy, target to reuse 70% of locally treated water by 2030, totaling 1.8 billion cubic meters. Notably, water reuse in Saudi Arabia has seen a significant increase, with the volume reaching 508 million cubic meters by 2023, marking a 300% surge since 2016.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's recent accession to the International Drought Resilience Alliance (IDRA) marks a significant step towards global collabora...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's recent accession to the International Drought Resilience Alliance (IDRA) marks a significant step towards global collaboration in tackling droughts exacerbated by climate change and land mismanagement. With Saudi Arabia hosting the upcoming UNCCD COP16, commitment to environmental protection is underscored, aligning with initiatives like the Saudi Green Initiative and the Middle East Green Initiative. The alliance emphasizes the urgent need for collective action to combat drought and desertification, crucial for sustainable resource management and resilience against future crises.

records.title: Egypt's agricultural sector soared to new heights in 2023, achieving record exports of 7.5 million tons valued at $8.8 billion, as report...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural sector soared to new heights in 2023, achieving record exports of 7.5 million tons valued at $8.8 billion, as reported by Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Al Sayed Al Qusair during a cabinet meeting. Highlighting Egypt's global prominence, particularly in oranges and frozen strawberries, Al Qusair noted the diversification of export markets, with 400 agricultural products shipped to 160 countries. Notably, Egyptian oranges garnered interest from South Korean companies, with substantial exports to the European Union and Southeast Asian nations.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Iraq's General Directorate for Industrial Development (GDID) has introduced a new loan program aimed at supporting small, medium, and mic...
records.description: Iraq's General Directorate for Industrial Development (GDID) has introduced a new loan program aimed at supporting small, medium, and micro enterprises (MSMEs). Collaborating with the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), these loans can amount to a maximum of 20 million Iraqi dinars ($15,000) per loan. Dr. Ali Ibrahim Janaan, Director General of the Directorate, urged young people and graduates to approach the Directorate and register their industrial projects.
records.institution: Iraqi General Directorate for Industrial Development (GDID)

records.title: The Iraq Development Fund Board, led by Prime Minister Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani, convened for its third meeting, attended by key ministers.
records.description: The Iraq Development Fund Board, led by Prime Minister Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani, convened for its third meeting, attended by key ministers. Discussions centered on projects outlined in the Fund's work plan, attracting foreign investment, and localizing industries. Requests from the private sector, particularly for school construction projects, were reviewed, surpassing the initial offering. Additionally, proposals included establishing a factory for passenger buses, manufacturing electronic tablets for educational purposes, and partnerships with American, British, and Saudi companies for various initiatives such as modern irrigation technologies and lighting infrastructure. The meeting also addressed deadlines for the "Rent and Own" housing project, aiming to provide solutions to the housing crisis.

records.title: Eighty small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) benefited from the Tunisian-German cooperation programme "SME Business Training and Coac...
records.description: Eighty small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) benefited from the Tunisian-German cooperation programme "SME Business Training and Coaching Loop," aiding them in enhancing profitability post-COVID-19. Minister of Industry, Energy and Mines, Fatma Chiboub Thabet, highlighted the success of the nine-month initiative, providing technical support to SMEs in various sectors. Tailored to each company's needs, the project focused on improving skills, introducing innovative management practices, and enhancing human resources management to boost exports and digital marketing, particularly benefiting young entrepreneurs.

records.title: Al Ghurair Foods is spearheading a major poultry farm project at Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (Kezad) in the UAE, representing the fi...
records.description: Al Ghurair Foods is spearheading a major poultry farm project at Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (Kezad) in the UAE, representing the first of three food processing endeavors aimed at bolstering the nation's food security. Spanning 680,000 square meters, the farm, set to commence operations in 2025, is poised to create job opportunities for over 200 individuals. Backed by a Dh1 billion (US$272 million) investment commitment, the initiative underscores Al Ghurair's dedication to meeting the burgeoning demand for high-quality poultry products in the UAE. With the UAE striving to elevate its food and agriculture sector's contribution to the economy by US$10 billion and generate 20,000 jobs within five years, this initiative aligns with broader economic objectives.

records.title: The UAE's commitment of $10 billion to bolster Pakistan's economy marks a significant stride in strengthening bilateral ties and fosterin...
records.description: The UAE's commitment of $10 billion to bolster Pakistan's economy marks a significant stride in strengthening bilateral ties and fostering economic growth. Following a meeting between President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the pledge underscores mutual interests in advancing sustainable development and prosperity.

records.title: The Kuwaiti market is set to receive 800 Naimi sheep from Jordan ahead of Eid Al-Adha, part of a larger shipment of 10,000 sheep expected...
records.description: The Kuwaiti market is set to receive 800 Naimi sheep from Jordan ahead of Eid Al-Adha, part of a larger shipment of 10,000 sheep expected to enter the country. These sheep will enter through the Abdally border, marking the first time since 1990. Due to previous sheep shortages during Eid Al-Adha, alternative arrangements were made, with sheep being imported through Iraq instead of Saudi Arabia, which currently has blocked roads. The Kuwait General Administration of Customs and Public Authority for Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources have provided assistance in facilitating this process. Additionally, sheep from Turkiye and Syria will also be imported to ensure a sufficient supply in the local market, which is expected to reduce prices by approximately 15 percent.
records.institution: Al-Wawan Livestock and Animal Feed Trading Company

records.title: Morocco advances its ambitious water security plan at a high-level panel on desalination, led by Minister of Equipment and Water, Nizar B...
records.description: Morocco advances its ambitious water security plan at a high-level panel on desalination, led by Minister of Equipment and Water, Nizar Baraka, at the 10th World Water Forum in Indonesia. With climate change impacting water resources, Morocco focuses on maximizing traditional sources, developing desalination, and prioritizing conservation. Currently operating 15 desalination plants, Morocco plans construction on the continent's largest plant near Casablanca, aiming to produce 300 million cubic meters of desalinated water annually by 2026. To mitigate costs, Morocco plans to power desalination plants with renewable energy sources, ensuring sustainability.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Equipment and Water

records.title: A national campaign in the UAE has successfully eliminated 409 mosquito breeding sites, reducing the risk of dengue fever infections.
records.description: A national campaign in the UAE has successfully eliminated 409 mosquito breeding sites, reducing the risk of dengue fever infections. Specialist teams deployed by the Emirates Health Services Corporation conducted surveys and monitored virus-carrying mosquitoes using GPS trackers. The campaign included analyzing 309 blood samples for mosquito DNA to determine effective pesticides. Health facilities were equipped to handle dengue fever cases, as incidents increased due to population control measures and wet weather creating more breeding sites.

records.title: Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development Youcef Cherfa hosted Mauritanian counterpart Memma Beibatta Hmalla in Algiers, und...
records.description: Algerian Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development Youcef Cherfa hosted Mauritanian counterpart Memma Beibatta Hmalla in Algiers, underscoring ongoing efforts to bolster economic ties and agricultural collaboration. Emphasizing agriculture and industry as pivotal areas for enhanced partnership, both ministers highlighted the significance of exchanging expertise and experiences for mutual agricultural development. Discussions also revolved around reinforcing food security and wealth creation strategies, tapping into the potential of existing cooperation. Mr. Hmalla's visit coincides with his attendance at the SIPSA FILAHA International Exhibition, offering a platform for agricultural professionals to foster dialogue and explore synergies. This meeting signals a significant stride in bilateral relations, paving the way for joint initiatives to support farmers and catalyze agri-food industries, ultimately advancing common objectives of sustainable agricultural development, food security, and economic prosperity.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: During the 10th World Water Forum in Bali, Algerian Minister of Water Resources Mr.
records.description: During the 10th World Water Forum in Bali, Algerian Minister of Water Resources Mr. Derbal emphasized Algeria's formidable efforts to combat water stress aggravated by global warming. Under President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's leadership, Algeria has enacted a comprehensive strategy focusing on unconventional water resources, with seawater desalination being a central component. This strategy, supported by significant investments, aims to ensure universal water access and meet the population's increasing demands. Additionally, the reuse of treated water, particularly for agriculture, plays a crucial role in preserving drinking water reserves for future generations. Mr. Derbal also highlighted the importance of protecting ecosystems and maintaining ecological balance, criticizing irresponsible behavior by a neighboring country that disrupts Algeria's ecological integrity. He called for strong measures to address these challenges and safeguard the environment.

records.title: Iraq is set to launch the National Entrepreneurship Competition, aimed at supporting 100 youth-led entrepreneurial projects with loans of...
records.description: Iraq is set to launch the National Entrepreneurship Competition, aimed at supporting 100 youth-led entrepreneurial projects with loans of up to 100 million dinars each, in collaboration with the Riyada initiative. Prime Minister Mohammed Shia' Al-Sudani chaired the Supreme Council for Youth's fifth meeting, which also approved initiatives such as the "Eyes of Knowledge" platform, featuring monthly knowledge competitions for university students, and the "Youth Abroad" program to empower Iraqi youth living abroad. Additionally, the Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities will support young Iraqis participating in cultural and artistic events, promoting youth involvement in the creative sector.

records.title: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) has commenced the Sabah Hospital project in Yemen's Abyan Governorate,...
records.description: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) has commenced the Sabah Hospital project in Yemen's Abyan Governorate, marking a significant step in supporting the health sector. This initiative aims to enhance healthcare services across Yemen by providing essential facilities such as women and childbirth departments, maternity and childcare units, inpatient rooms, operating theaters, and emergency services. Additionally, the hospital will house various clinics including internal medicine, dental, and ENT clinics, along with radiology and laboratory rooms.
records.institution: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY)

records.title: The Assembly of People's Representatives (ARP) commenced the examination of a $300 million loan agreement between Tunisia and the Interna...
records.description: The Assembly of People's Representatives (ARP) commenced the examination of a $300 million loan agreement between Tunisia and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) for the Tunisia Emergency Food Security Response Project. Aimed at ensuring grain supply, the loan will support projects over 2024-2026 and includes components for urgent farmer support and wheat supply. The loan, reimbursable over 28 years, signifies ongoing efforts since 2022 to enhance Tunisia's grain sector, including measures to boost domestic production, reduce waste, and manage drought-related risks. The project has facilitated the provision of barley to dairy farmers, climate-smart wheat seeds to smallholders, and soft wheat for bread supply.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Abu Dhabi is set to implement a ban on certain Styrofoam products starting June 1 as part of its broader initiative to combat plastic pol...
records.description: Abu Dhabi is set to implement a ban on certain Styrofoam products starting June 1 as part of its broader initiative to combat plastic pollution in the emirate. The ban will target disposable items like cups, lids, plates, and takeaway containers made from expanded polystyrene, aligning with efforts to reduce single-use consumer products. Driven by the aim to protect the environment and decrease litter, the ban exempts items not intended for single use, such as large storage boxes and medical products, while promoting the adoption of sustainable alternatives.
records.institution: The Environment Agency in Abu Dhabi

records.title: Pure Food Technology, a sustainable agriculture firm in the UAE, has introduced a vertical hydroponic garden in the Jebel Ali Industrial...
records.description: Pure Food Technology, a sustainable agriculture firm in the UAE, has introduced a vertical hydroponic garden in the Jebel Ali Industrial Area, employing robotics, solar power, and artificial intelligence to cultivate crops like baby potatoes without soil. This innovative approach, tailored for desert conditions, aims to address water scarcity challenges while enhancing food production. Sebastian Carlton, CEO of Pure Food Technology, underscores the significance of advanced technology in meeting growing food demands, emphasizing the farm's potential to contribute to the UAE's self-reliance in food production and support sustainability goals. Similarly, in Atlantic Canada, researchers are exploring wild potato varieties from the Andes to develop drought-resistant potatoes, highlighting global efforts to enhance potato farming amid climate change challenges.

records.title: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, Crown Prince of Dubai, has unveiled a bold initiative to train one million individuals in artificial intellig...
records.description: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, Crown Prince of Dubai, has unveiled a bold initiative to train one million individuals in artificial intelligence (AI) prompt engineering over the next three years, aligning with Dubai's Universal Blueprint for Artificial Intelligence. Emphasizing the necessity of staying abreast of technological advancements, Sheikh Hamdan highlighted prompt engineering as a vital skill in today's labor markets, essential for Dubai to lead in innovation and prepare for the AI era. The announcement coincided with the recognition of winners at the Global Prompt Engineering Championship.

records.title: The appointment of a chief executive for artificial intelligence (AI) across UAE federal entities signifies a strategic move aimed at pre...
records.description: The appointment of a chief executive for artificial intelligence (AI) across UAE federal entities signifies a strategic move aimed at preparing the nation's talent pool for long-term benefits and positioning the country as a technology leader, experts suggest. This new role is anticipated to replicate the success of past positions such as chief data officer, aligning organizations globally on data management and insight generation. However, unlocking the transformative power of AI will require heightened focus on understanding ethical, safety aspects, and regulation surrounding AI, in addition to boosting the talent pool. The move is expected to accelerate the adoption of advanced technologies in all levels of government and complement existing initiatives and investments. With AI poised to contribute significantly to the UAE's economy, preparing individuals at all levels for AI-centric roles is crucial for streamlined integration and sustained growth.

records.title: The UAE is embarking on a comprehensive health and nutrition survey involving 20,000 families and 2,000 laborers to assess the nation's h...
records.description: The UAE is embarking on a comprehensive health and nutrition survey involving 20,000 families and 2,000 laborers to assess the nation's health needs and guide healthy living campaigns. Participants will complete questionnaires to evaluate their knowledge about health and nutrition, with additional blood tests conducted by health practitioners. The survey targets various demographics, including adults, women, pregnant women, and children. Collaboration between health authorities and data analysts will evaluate the collected information to inform strategic planning and decision-making.
records.institution: Dubai Data and Statistics & The Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre

records.title: The launch of Algeria's 3rd General Agricultural Census (RGA) from Blida's wilaya signifies a pivotal national undertaking for agricultur...
records.description: The launch of Algeria's 3rd General Agricultural Census (RGA) from Blida's wilaya signifies a pivotal national undertaking for agricultural sector planning and development, set to run until July 17. Supervised by Hamid Bensaâd, Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, the RGA aims to gather reliable data on the country's agricultural landscape, informing future sectoral policies with scientific precision. With a focus on revitalizing strategic sectors to achieve sustainable self-sufficiency and bolster national food security, the census sees substantial resource mobilization, including thousands of trained enumerators and supervisors. Abdellatif Dilmi of the National Union of Algerian Peasants (UNPA) urges active farmer participation, emphasizing the potential benefits. The census employs detailed questionnaires, ensuring confidentiality and data accuracy, and enjoys presidential support as a fundamental mechanism for understanding national agricultural capacities and needs. With the issuance of dedicated postal stamps, this ambitious census lays the groundwork for Algeria's agricultural sector development, anchored in robust data and stakeholder engagement.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: Iraq had procured 1.5 million metric tons of wheat by May 20, 2024, as reported by the official news agency (INA).
records.description: Iraq had procured 1.5 million metric tons of wheat by May 20, 2024, as reported by the official news agency (INA). records.title: Morocco donates 200 tons of fertilizer to aid struggling Guatemalan farmers, aiming to reach 10,000 families across seven provinces.
records.description: Morocco donates 200 tons of fertilizer to aid struggling Guatemalan farmers, aiming to reach 10,000 families across seven provinces. The initiative, launched in Totonicapán province, is hailed by Guatemalan officials as a significant boost to rural development efforts and poverty alleviation. Moroccan Ambassador Tarik Louajri emphasizes the kingdom's commitment to food security and South-South cooperation, echoing King Mohammed VI's vision.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is aggressively pursuing its goal to become a major player in the global ecommerce market, with plans to exceed $30 billion...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is aggressively pursuing its goal to become a major player in the global ecommerce market, with plans to exceed $30 billion in ecommerce sales by 2027 and $44 billion by 2030. Through initiatives such as simplifying licensing for domestic delivery providers, investing in logistics infrastructure, and implementing regulations to enhance consumer confidence and combat fraud, the country aims to foster the growth of small and medium-sized businesses and diversify its economy away from oil dependency, in line with its Vision 2030 strategy.

records.title: Russia is eyeing Algeria as a prime market for expanding its dairy exports, with plans to increase shipments by 15-20% annually, particul...
records.description: Russia is eyeing Algeria as a prime market for expanding its dairy exports, with plans to increase shipments by 15-20% annually, particularly targeting Arab nations and Southeast Asia. Algeria's status as the largest African importer of dairy products, spending approximately US$800 million yearly on milk powder imports alone, presents a lucrative opportunity for global suppliers. Russia's move to bolster its presence in Algeria aligns with its broader strategy to diversify export destinations, stabilize the domestic market, and sustain growth in the dairy industry.
records.institution: Russian National Union of Dairy Producers (Soyuzmoloko)

records.title: Prime Minister Mohammed Shiaa Al-Sudani announced the commencement of the sewerage project in Al-Wahda district, located south of Baghdad.
records.description: Prime Minister Mohammed Shiaa Al-Sudani announced the commencement of the sewerage project in Al-Wahda district, located south of Baghdad. This initiative is part of four strategic projects initiated by Al-Sudani to address sewerage issues across several areas of Baghdad province, with a total cost exceeding one trillion dinars ($764 million). The project aims to serve over 80,000 residents in the district, boasting a capacity of 48,000 cubic meters per day and an extensive network spanning 85 km for sewage and 67 km for rainwater drainage, alongside nine diverse stations.

records.title: The Jordanian Armed Forces-Arab Army (JAF), along with the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organisation (JHCO), collaborated to send a 91-truck...
records.description: The Jordanian Armed Forces-Arab Army (JAF), along with the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organisation (JHCO), collaborated to send a 91-truck food aid convoy to Gaza, in partnership with the World Food Programme (WFP) and international organizations. The convoy transported essential food items for distribution to Gaza's residents, highlighting Jordan's role as a crucial humanitarian gateway for aid to the region.

records.title: The Undersecretary of the Ministry of Agriculture in the Government of National Unity, Mohammed Al-Turki, has initiated discussions with...
records.description: The Undersecretary of the Ministry of Agriculture in the Government of National Unity, Mohammed Al-Turki, has initiated discussions with advisors regarding the potential introduction of digital agricultural technologies across Libya. The aim is to ensure widespread access to these technologies among farmers throughout the country. An expanded meeting is planned, involving relevant authorities affiliated with the Ministry, to further explore the benefits of digital agricultural technologies, including increased productivity and improved resource management. Challenges such as initial costs, infrastructure development, and training were also addressed, emphasizing the need for comprehensive planning and securing financial resources. Given Libya's heavy reliance on imports for 75% of its agricultural needs, the initiative aims to bolster the local agricultural sector and enhance food security.

records.description: Dr. Laila bint Ahmed Al Najar, Minister of Social Development, met with Amal Belhaj Musa, discussing collaboration between Oman and Tunisia to support and empower women across various spheres. The meeting addressed common concerns and strategies to leverage expertise from both sides. Topics included childhood and elderly sectors, women's empowerment programs, and the rights of women in public services and various societal spheres. Dr. Al Najar also visited the Sadiq Idris Centre for Elderly Care and the Centre for Research, Studies, Documentation, and Information on Women, gaining insight into their programs and services.
