records.title: In alignment with the UAE's commitment to bolster economic cooperation across Africa, an official delegation visited Benin from May 13-17...
records.description: In alignment with the UAE's commitment to bolster economic cooperation across Africa, an official delegation visited Benin from May 13-17, 2024. Led by Humaid Mohamed Bin Salem, Secretary-General of the FCCI, the UAE delegation engaged in high-level discussions with Benin's ministers, officials, and business leaders. The talks centered on opportunities to enhance trade and investment collaboration in various sectors, including artificial intelligence, fisheries, agriculture, infrastructure, energy, and metals. The delegation, comprising representatives from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, FCCI, Edge Group, and E20, aimed to strengthen economic ties and partnerships between the UAE and Benin.
records.institution: Federation of UAE Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FCCI)

records.title: Morocco's Institute for Agricultural Research (NIAR) is pioneering the development of high-yield, drought-resistant varieties of grains,...
records.description: Morocco's Institute for Agricultural Research (NIAR) is pioneering the development of high-yield, drought-resistant varieties of grains, legumes, and oilseeds with the aim of boosting production by 50%. At a seminar held at the Regional Agricultural Research Center in Kenitra, NIAR unveiled plans for this research program, showcasing 30 to 50 new plant varieties tailored to combat the adverse effects of climate change on agricultural yield. With persistent heatwaves impacting Morocco's agricultural output, NIAR's initiative responds to the urgent need for resilient crops. The program encompasses practical workshops to educate farmers on the innovative features of these new plants, along with trial platforms established in key regions. Collaborative efforts between NIAR and the International Center for Agricultural Research in Dry Areas (ICARDA) have resulted in over a decade of dedicated research into drought-resistant grains, employing hybridization and careful selection processes. While advancements are notable, the research remains in early stages, aligning with Morocco's Green Generation 2020-2030 initiative to bolster food security and enhance agricultural productivity. Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water, and Forests, Mohamed Sadiki, underscores the vital role of agricultural research in addressing drought challenges and emphasizes the need for continued investment in scientific endeavors to ensure crop resilience and sustainable productivity.

records.title: Dendra Systems recently secured $15.76 million in Series B funding led by Zouk Capital, with contributions from Aramco Ventures, Airbus V...
records.description: Dendra Systems recently secured $15.76 million in Series B funding led by Zouk Capital, with contributions from Aramco Ventures, Airbus Ventures, and others. The Oxford-based company specializes in ecological restoration using high-resolution data capture and AI-enabled ecosystem insights. This funding will support their expansion into new markets and further development of their AI-based ecology platform, aiming to address environmental challenges in industries like mining.

records.title: FAO hosted a national workshop on SDG indicators 2.1.1 "Prevalence of Undernourishment" and 2.1.2 "Prevalence of moderate or severe food...
records.description: FAO hosted a national workshop on SDG indicators 2.1.1 "Prevalence of Undernourishment" and 2.1.2 "Prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity, based on the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES)" in Baghdad (Iraq) from May 19 to May 23. As the custodian agency for these indicators, FAO supported the efforts of Iraq in monitoring target 2.1. The workshop provided technical support to the Central Statistical Organization (CSO), Kurdistan Regional Statistics Office (KRSO), and other national institutions related to food security indicators, aiming to strengthen their capacity in analyzing food security and nutrition data.
records.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: SACE, the state-owned Italian insurance and financial group, has collaborated with the Trade Bank of Iraq (TBI) to boost private sector d...
records.description: SACE, the state-owned Italian insurance and financial group, has collaborated with the Trade Bank of Iraq (TBI) to boost private sector development in Iraq and promote Made in Italy exports, culminating in agreements totaling 1 billion euros. These agreements involve Italian companies like Danieli & C., FalorniTech, B2FIRMS, Tecno Electric, and Bottero Spa, partnering with Iraqi buyers for projects valued at 775 million euros. These projects span vital sectors for Iraq's economic diversification, including pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, steel, and mechanical instrumental machinery.

records.title: Tunisian Foreign Minister Nabil Ammar and Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein led the 17th session of the Tunis...
records.description: Tunisian Foreign Minister Nabil Ammar and Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein led the 17th session of the Tunisian-Iraqi Joint Committee in Baghdad, emphasizing the economic potential in sectors like pharmaceuticals, agriculture, tourism, and transportation. records.title: Libya and Saudi Arabia are exploring avenues to enhance maritime trade, as Mohammed Al-Hweij, the Minister of Economy and Trade, met with...
records.description: Libya and Saudi Arabia are exploring avenues to enhance maritime trade, as Mohammed Al-Hweij, the Minister of Economy and Trade, met with Hamad Al-Shahri, Acting Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Libya, in Cairo. Discussions focused on bolstering commercial maritime routes between their ports to boost bilateral trade. Plans for the upcoming Libyan-Saudi Investment Forum and an exhibition showcasing Saudi products in Tripoli were also discussed, aiming to strengthen engagement among chambers of commerce and entrepreneurs from both nations.

records.title: The National Oil Corporation (NOC) has inked a deal to drill 17 water wells across various regions, including the Oil Crescent, central,...
records.description: The National Oil Corporation (NOC) has inked a deal to drill 17 water wells across various regions, including the Oil Crescent, central, and southern areas. Aimed at addressing water shortages in multiple areas, the agreement includes provisions for drilling and maintaining these wells. The initial phase will see the distribution of six wells in the Oil Crescent municipalities, four in Al-Wahat, four in the southern region, and three in the central region.

records.title: Qatar scientists have pioneered a groundbreaking solution to address food waste and enhance sustainability in the nation's livestock sector.
records.description: Qatar scientists have pioneered a groundbreaking solution to address food waste and enhance sustainability in the nation's livestock sector. Led by Dr. Kashif Rasool from the Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute, the project aims to repurpose food waste into microbial protein, reducing reliance on imported livestock feed. Supported by funding from the Ministry of Municipality and the Qatar National Research Fund, the initiative utilizes biogas for microbial fermentation, converting biomethane into protein-rich feed.
records.institution: Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute

records.title: Egypt has sealed a monumental deal for a $10 billion wind farm in Sohag, witnessing the signing of a land allocation agreement by Prime M...
records.description: Egypt has sealed a monumental deal for a $10 billion wind farm in Sohag, witnessing the signing of a land allocation agreement by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly. The project, backed by over $10 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI), will be developed by a consortium comprising Masdar, Hassan Allam Utilities, and Infinity Power. This agreement follows a memorandum of understanding inked during COP27 in Sharm El-Sheikh. Once construction commences after crucial technical studies and measurements, the wind park is poised to become the Middle East's largest wind energy endeavor and one of the world's largest onshore wind power initiatives. With an estimated annual energy generation of 48,000 gigawatt-hours and the potential to avert 23.8 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions, the project is anticipated to create approximately 23,000 direct and indirect job opportunities, marking a significant leap towards Egypt's renewable energy goals.

records.title: Iraq has inked three significant agreements for sulfur and fertilizers projects, involving companies from the UAE, US, and Iraq itself.
records.description: Iraq has inked three significant agreements for sulfur and fertilizers projects, involving companies from the UAE, US, and Iraq itself. Expected to generate 47,790 GWh annually and reduce Egypt’s carbon emissions by 9%, the project aligns with Egypt’s renewable energy goals, aiming for 42% renewable power by 2030 and significant cost savings in natural gas expenditure.

records.title: Silal, Abu Dhabi’s prominent food, agriculture, and technology company, has unveiled a state-of-the-art automated packhouse in Al Ain, UAE.
records.description: Silal, Abu Dhabi’s prominent food, agriculture, and technology company, has unveiled a state-of-the-art automated packhouse in Al Ain, UAE. Spanning 14,000 square meters, it boasts the capacity to process 216 tons of fresh produce daily, making it the largest facility of its kind in the UAE. Equipped with cutting-edge technology for post-harvest operations, the packhouse can pack locally grown produce in under 60 seconds, enhancing efficiency to meet rising client demands. With features like automated grading and packing systems, it aims to maintain top quality while processing over 180,000 packs daily.

records.title: UAE Announces 10-year Blue Residency Visa
records.description: The UAE Cabinet unveiled a landmark initiative, the 10-year Blue Residency visa, during a session chaired by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum. This visa is dedicated to individuals who have demonstrated exceptional commitment to environmental conservation, including marine life, land-based ecosystems, air quality, sustainability technologies, and the circular economy. Eligible candidates encompass supporters of environmental action from international organizations, companies, associations, NGOs, as well as distinguished activists and researchers in the field. Applications for the Blue Residency can be submitted through the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs, and Port Security, or through nominations by competent authorities.

records.title: Algeria's wheat production is anticipated to surge by 11% to 3 million tonnes by the end of the 2024/2025 campaign, according to a recent...
records.description: Algeria's wheat production is anticipated to surge by 11% to 3 million tonnes by the end of the 2024/2025 campaign, according to a recent report by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). This growth could potentially position Algeria to surpass Morocco and become the second-largest wheat producer in North Africa after Egypt, marking the third occurrence in the last five years. Persistent drought in Morocco for over five years has contributed to this shift, with improved rainfall in Algeria's central and eastern production areas driving positive prospects. Despite being among the world's largest consumers of wheat, with consumption constituting 60% of the country's food ration, Algeria heavily relies on imports due to domestic production meeting only a third of its needs, which are predominantly weather-dependent. The USDA projects elevated wheat imports to Algeria at 8.7 million tonnes in the 2024-25 period, attributing the high import forecast to below-average rain and soil moisture conditions, resulting in decreased production and cultivated areas.

records.title: Driscoll’s Maroc has embarked on the construction of a soft fruit conditioning plant in Morocco’s Loukkos agropole, south of Larache, wit...
records.description: Driscoll’s Maroc has embarked on the construction of a soft fruit conditioning plant in Morocco’s Loukkos agropole, south of Larache, with an investment of approximately USD 41 million. The project, spanning 5 hectares, not only aims to boost the province of Larache's economic landscape but also promises job creation, particularly benefiting the local community. Led by the governor of Larache province, Bouassam El Alamine, the inauguration ceremony signals a promising venture for both Driscoll’s and the region. Driscoll’s investment underscores its commitment to Morocco’s agricultural sector and highlights the favorable business environment fostered by collaborative efforts between private entities and local authorities. The support received from regional bodies, such as the Regional Investment Center of the Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima Region (CRITTA), has been pivotal in facilitating the project's success, showcasing the synergy between public and private sectors.

records.title: Abu Dhabi Authority Launches Educational Initiative to Cultivate Young Minds in Agriculture, Food Safety
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has introduced a pioneering educational initiative aimed at nurturing children's understanding of agriculture, livestock management, food safety, and beekeeping through engaging stories and informative leaflets. By providing accessible resources covering various aspects of these sectors, ADAFSA seeks to inspire the younger generation to appreciate the importance of food security while fostering potential careers in agriculture. With materials available online and distributed during events like the Abu Dhabi International Book Fair, ADAFSA ensures broad accessibility to promote awareness and understanding among children, educators, and parents, fostering a knowledgeable society poised to contribute to Abu Dhabi's food security goals.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The UAE and Oman are forging a strategic partnership to advance renewable energy and green technology projects, exemplifying the Middle E...
records.description: The UAE and Oman are forging a strategic partnership to advance renewable energy and green technology projects, exemplifying the Middle East's commitment to diversifying its energy sector beyond oil and gas. Saudi Arabia aims to develop Neom, a massive green energy-powered urban area, and achieve a 50% renewable energy mix by 2030, while the UAE targets a 44% renewable energy mix by the same year, with a focus on solar power and hydrogen production. Notably, the UAE and Oman recently signed a $35 billion investment partnership, with a significant portion allocated to renewable energy initiatives, including solar and wind projects, demonstrating their joint commitment to sustainable development and economic cooperation. Oman also seeks to emerge as a major green hydrogen producer, leveraging its expertise in oil and gas and utilizing its favorable natural conditions for solar and wind energy generation.

records.title: Egypt Announces Agricultural Project for Food Security
records.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El Sisi launched the first phase of the Future of Egypt initiative, aiming to enhance food security and reduce import dependence by reclaiming 1.8 million hectares of land by 2030, alongside modernizing irrigation systems and boosting agricultural production. Led by the Future of Egypt Authority, the project targets replacing imports of wheat, corn, and sugar, potentially saving $3.7 billion in foreign currency annually and increasing agricultural exports by 20 to 25 per cent over five years. The initiative includes the construction of 24 grain silos with a combined capacity of over 100,000 tonnes, equipped with drying units to minimize post-harvest losses. President El Sisi emphasized efficient water management and centralized planning, with much of the project undertaken by the armed forces.

records.title: Palestine Cola, crafted as an alternative to American soft drink giants, has experienced a surge in demand amid a boycott of these brands.
records.description: Palestine Cola, crafted as an alternative to American soft drink giants, has experienced a surge in demand amid a boycott of these brands. Sales have soared to approximately four million cans in under two months, driven by consumers' preference for a locally-owned option. Founded by the Hassoun brothers, the brand's distinctive cans feature symbols of Palestinian heritage, emphasizing a message of liberty and support for Palestine. Alongside offering a beverage alternative, Palestine Cola aims to raise awareness and support charities aiding those affected by the conflict. The surge in popularity coincides with a broader boycott of American soft drink giants over business ties with Israel, prompting plans for expanding Palestine Cola's product range and distribution across Europe.

The aim is to boost poultry production, elevating the company's market share in an industry currently totaling over 250 million birds annually, with plans to reach 450 million birds by 2027. The announcement, made during the expo's third edition inaugurated by the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, Eng. Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadhli, underscores Almarai's commitment to invest 7 billion riyals over the next five years, contributing to local self-sufficiency and supporting the national economy in alignment with Vision 2030. records.title: Since November, the UAE has delivered nearly 50,000 tonnes of urgent supplies to Gaza as part of its aid mission to assist those affected...
records.description: Since November, the UAE has delivered nearly 50,000 tonnes of urgent supplies to Gaza as part of its aid mission to assist those affected by the conflict in the enclave. According to figures from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, this aid was transported via 260 flights and 1,243 lorries up until May 13. Additionally, three aid ships carrying 13,190 tonnes of aid departed for Egypt’s Al Arish Port as part of Operation Gallant Knight 3, with the intention of distributing the aid to Gaza. As part of its assistance program, the UAE has established two hospitals in Gaza, one of which includes a center for amputees providing prosthetic limbs to Palestinians injured during the conflict. The field hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, staffed with over 100 medical professionals, has treated 20,503 cases since December 2, offering services such as general surgery, orthopedics, intensive care, internal medicine, dentistry, family medicine, and psychiatric treatment. Additionally, the UAE provided a 100-bed floating hospital in Al Arish Port, equipped with operating rooms, intensive care facilities, a laboratory, a pharmacy, and medical warehouses. Six desalination plants provided by the UAE are capable of producing 1.2 million gallons of clean drinking water per day for 600,000 people. Furthermore, the UAE supplied five automated bakeries in Gaza, producing bread for up to 72,000 people and enough flour for eight existing bakeries, feeding 17,140 people daily. Additionally, the UAE facilitated the transfer of 671 individuals from Gaza to the UAE for medical treatment, accompanied by 735 family members.

records.title: Tadweer Group is set to build Abu Dhabi’s first-ever dedicated Material Recovery Facility (MRF), a key milestone in diverting waste from...
records.description: Tadweer Group is set to build Abu Dhabi’s first-ever dedicated Material Recovery Facility (MRF), a key milestone in diverting waste from landfills and promoting recycling. This state-of-the-art facility will process 1.3 million metric tonnes of waste annually, recovering valuable recyclable materials like metals and plastics. The initiative aligns with Tadweer Group’s goal of diverting 80% of Abu Dhabi’s waste by 2030 and supports the circular economy principles. Expected to commence operations by the end of 2026, the MRF will not only contribute to waste management but also create job opportunities and promote private sector investment in the UAE.

records.title: The emergence of Citrus Black Spot (CBS) in Tunisian citrus imports has sparked significant concern within the country's agricultural sec...
records.description: The emergence of Citrus Black Spot (CBS) in Tunisian citrus imports has sparked significant concern within the country's agricultural sector. Initially detected in 2019 in Nabeul, CBS has rapidly spread to other citrus-growing regions across Tunisia, challenging previous assumptions about its adaptability and posing threats to local farmers and international trade partners. The escalation of CBS beyond Nabeul to areas like Sousse underscores the urgency of addressing this agricultural threat. Concurrently, South Africa's appeal to the European Commission (EC) for WTO consultations regarding EU regulations on fungal-infected citrus imports adds complexity to the situation. Inmaculada Sanfeliu, President of the Citrus Management Committee (CGC), emphasizes the need for stringent control measures and questions the scientific credibility of South African exporters and authorities. Recent scientific studies and transparent investigations conducted by Tunisian authorities underscore the widespread damage and economic risks posed by CBS, aligning with EFSA scientific opinions and current European regulations aimed at safeguarding against CBS. The economic impact of CBS's establishment in EU citrus-growing areas is substantial, with projected losses totaling approximately 1,182 million euros, highlighting the challenges posed by recurrent non-compliance with import regulations. In light of these developments, questions arise regarding the future of Mediterranean citrus production and the involvement of the Spanish lemon sector.

records.title: OCP Africa, a subsidiary of the Moroccan fertilizer giant OCP Group, has entered into a partnership with Sierra Leone's Ministry of Agric...
records.description: OCP Africa, a subsidiary of the Moroccan fertilizer giant OCP Group, has entered into a partnership with Sierra Leone's Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, aiming to bolster agricultural development in the country. The Memorandum of Understanding, signed by Mehdi Filali, Senior Vice President for West Africa at OCP, and Musa Kpaka, Sierra Leone’s Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, prioritizes soil health, farmer empowerment, and sustainable practices. Through initiatives like last-mile distribution of farm inputs, establishment of local production facilities for specialty fertilizers, and interventions for soil health and fertility, the partnership seeks to foster a resilient, inclusive, and sustainable agricultural sector in Sierra Leone. Leveraging digital technologies for real-time information and establishing integrated model farms to showcase best practices are among the strategies outlined.

records.title: Construction is set to begin on the $3bn UAE-Oman Hafeet Rail, spanning 303 km from Abu Dhabi to Sohar with a stop in Al Ain.
records.description: Construction is set to begin on the $3bn UAE-Oman Hafeet Rail, spanning 303 km from Abu Dhabi to Sohar with a stop in Al Ain. Trains will travel at speeds exceeding 200km/hour, reducing travel time between Abu Dhabi and Sohar to just 100 minutes. A shareholder agreement has been signed among Etihad Rail, Oman Rail, and Mubadala Investment Company to kick off the project, with civil works awarded to an Omani-Emirati alliance. Siemens and HAC will equip the railway fleet with advanced technologies, enhancing reliability through GPS-based train control and tracking.

records.description: Oman's livestock exports surged by 45% in 2023, reaching US$8.3 million, according to data from the National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI). Camels led the list of exported livestock, with the United Arab Emirates emerging as the top importer, followed by Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Additionally, livestock re-exports saw a significant 97% growth, reaching US$239.89 million. Oman's meat market is also on the rise, with revenue reaching US$913.30 million in 2024, and projections suggest continued growth in both consumption and production in the coming years.

records.description: Oman’s Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources is ramping up efforts to ensure water security by maintaining and enhancing the efficiency of dams and aflaj systems across the country. Through rigorous monitoring and targeted maintenance programs, the Ministry is safeguarding the operational integrity of dams while preserving Oman’s rich water heritage embodied in its aflaj networks. One notable project is the groundwater recharge dam in Wadi Imti, established in 2014, which plays a pivotal role in bolstering Izki’s groundwater reserve. With a storage capacity of approximately 0.7 million cubic meters, this dam significantly contributes to water levels in nearby wells and aflaj systems, benefiting various villages. Engineer Youssef bin Masoud bin Ali Al-Mandhari, Director of the Dams Department, highlighted the broader objective of enhancing water resources, particularly in agriculturally significant areas, while Mohammed bin Abdullah Al Riyami underscored the dam's critical role in sustaining agricultural productivity by increasing water levels in the Falaj system.

records.title: Forafric Maroc, a subsidiary of Forafric Global Plc, a Moroccan industrial group, is set to expand its wheat crushing capacity through a...

Situated in Morocco's Agadir region, Karam Green Agri specializes in high-quality vegetable production, including tomatoes, peppers, zucchini, cucumbers, cocktail tomatoes, and Baby Plum cherry tomatoes, all exclusively supplied to Port International. With 287 hectares cultivated along the Atlantic coast, the company leverages ideal conditions for top-tier vegetable growth, employing over 1,600 people committed to sustainable practices. Utilizing hydroponics and advanced tunnel facilities to minimize pesticide use, and sourcing over 35% of its water needs from a nearby desalination plant, Karam Green Agri aims to expand production by 60 to 80 hectares annually in partnership with Port International. André Lüling, Managing Director of Port International European Sourcing, expressed optimism about the collaboration, emphasizing its impact on product quality and availability across Europe. Jakob Lorenzen, a tomato expert at Port International, highlighted the state-of-the-art packaging facility at Karam Green Agri, ensuring optimal freshness and quality for retail partners and customers.

records.description: The Moroccan Agency for Sustainable Energy (Masen) has initiated the Nassim Nord wind farm complex tender, signaling a significant move toward renewable energy expansion in Morocco. This project, comprising the Koudia Al Baida and Nassim Dar Chaoui wind farms, aligns with Morocco's goal of increasing renewable energy capacity to 52% of its electricity mix by the decade's end.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Allocates $2.5 Billion to Middle East Green Initiative
records.description: Saudi Arabia has committed $2.5 billion to the Middle East Green Initiative, marking a significant step in its climate change strategy. This initiative, which has attracted numerous countries and is recognized as the largest green project globally, reflects Saudi Arabia's proactive approach to environmental leadership. Adel bin Ahmed Al-Jubeir, the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Envoy for Climate Affairs, highlighted this during a panel at the National Greening Forum. Saudi Arabia’s efforts include afforestation programs central to both environmental sustainability and the ambitious Saudi Vision 2030.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of State for Foreign Affairs

records.title: Abu Dhabi issues new regulations for small-scale plant production farms, aiming to ensure sustainable resource use, boost small farmers'...
records.description: Abu Dhabi issues new regulations for small-scale plant production farms, aiming to ensure sustainable resource use, boost small farmers' income, and promote local produce competitiveness. The regulations, overseen by the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA), set clear guidelines for plant production practices, emphasizing improved product quality and market competitiveness. Eng Ahmed Khalid Othman from ADAFSA highlights the government's commitment to supporting small farmers and enhancing food security. The regulations also address farm trade name use, documentation of agricultural operations, and production records, while urging society to buy local to bolster the agricultural sector and achieve food security goals.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, in his role as the Ruler of Dubai, issued Law No.
records.description: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, in his role as the Ruler of Dubai, issued Law No. (1) of 2024 concerning the taxation of foreign banks in Dubai. This law mandates a 20% tax on the annual taxable income of all foreign banks operating outside the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), including those in special development and free zones. The tax paid can be offset by any corporate tax already paid under Federal Law No. (47) of 2022. The law outlines the procedures for tax calculation, filing, audits, and voluntary disclosures. Additionally, banks have the right to object to tax assessments and fines—which can reach up to AED1 million for repeat offenses—with the Department of Finance. This law, effective from the tax year following its enactment, replaces Regulation No. (2) of 1996 and will be implemented by decisions published in the Official Gazette.

records.title: Iraq is advancing its first major solar power project to address its chronic electricity shortfall and meet rising demand due to populati...
records.description: Iraq is advancing its first major solar power project to address its chronic electricity shortfall and meet rising demand due to population growth. French energy company TotalEnergies is set to construct a 1-gigawatt solar plant, part of a larger $27 billion initiative that includes oil and gas field development and a gas hub project. The solar plant, which is the first utility-scale project in Iraq, aims to provide electricity to 350,000 homes by 2025. Despite having plans to add 12 gigawatts of solar capacity by 2030, Iraq currently faces significant infrastructure and legislative challenges that hinder the development of renewable energy.

records.title: The United Arab Emirates and New Zealand have agreed to commence negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA),...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates and New Zealand have agreed to commence negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), aimed at enhancing trade and investment ties between the two nations. Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister of State for Foreign Trade, and Todd McClay, New Zealand’s Minister for Trade, signed a joint declaration of intent to confirm the agreement. With non-oil trade between the two countries reaching US$764.5 million in 2023, the proposed CEPA aims to remove or reduce tariffs and trade barriers, improve market access, and establish investment pathways in sectors such as agriculture, renewable energy, logistics, education, professional services, and healthcare..
records.institution: UAE Ministry of State for Foreign Trade

records.title: For the fourth consecutive year, the Environmental Authority has launched a campaign to plant 4 million seeds of wild trees in the mounta...
records.description: For the fourth consecutive year, the Environmental Authority has launched a campaign to plant 4 million seeds of wild trees in the mountains of Dhofar Governorate. Running until June 30, the initiative aims to increase vegetation cover and combat desertification in the region, with support from both governmental and private entities.

records.title: Bühler Group, a Swiss milling technology provider, has partnered with Elsewedy Electric and IBC Group (IBC) to advance Egypt's grain silo...
records.description: Bühler Group, a Swiss milling technology provider, has partnered with Elsewedy Electric and IBC Group (IBC) to advance Egypt's grain silo localization efforts. This collaboration aims to enhance food security and promote sustainable development within the country's agricultural sector. Led by Elsewedy Electric and IBC, with Bühler Group providing advanced technology and support, the initiative promises significant progress in the grain silos industry. Ahmed El Sewedy, CEO of Elsewedy Electric, highlighted the strategic importance of nationalizing key industries and transitioning from imports to local production. Samuel Schär of Bühler Group and Akram Khreis of IBC Group emphasized the potential for innovation and efficiency improvements in grain storage and management systems. Meanwhile, Egypt's Supply Minister Ali Moselhy announced adequate strategic reserves of wheat, vegetable oils, and sugar, with plans to procure 3.5 million tons of local wheat in the 2024 season, demonstrating the country's commitment to bolstering its agricultural self-sufficiency.
records.institution: Bühler Group, Elsewedy Electric, & IBC Group

records.title: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation El Sayyed el Quseir engaged in discussions with his Jordanian counterpart, Minister of Agric...
records.description: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation El Sayyed el Quseir engaged in discussions with his Jordanian counterpart, Minister of Agriculture Khalid Al Hanifat, aimed at enhancing agricultural cooperation and integration between Egypt and Jordan. The focus was on facilitating the exchange of agricultural goods and sharing of expertise. These discussions align with directives from the political leaderships of both countries.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Oman and Hungary are enhancing their parliamentary relations through a recent memorandum of understanding aimed at boosting legislative c...
records.description: Oman and Hungary are enhancing their parliamentary relations through a recent memorandum of understanding aimed at boosting legislative cooperation and alignment at international parliamentary forums. During his visit to Hungary, Khalid bin Hilal al-Maawali, President of Oman's Consultative Assembly, met with Dr. Laszlo Kover, President of the Hungarian National Assembly in Budapest, to discuss ways to deepen bilateral ties, particularly in legislative matters. The discussions also extended to economic and investment sectors, where Oman's promising economic sectors were highlighted. Additionally, Al-Maawali received an honorary citizenship from Ludovica University for Public Service in recognition of his parliamentary achievements and contributions to strengthening Oman-Hungary bilateral relations.

records.title: Oman and the European Union (EU) are exploring avenues to enhance maritime security and deepen economic cooperation.
records.description: Oman and the European Union (EU) are exploring avenues to enhance maritime security and deepen economic cooperation. During a meeting between Sayyid Badr Hamad Al Busaidi, Oman's Foreign Minister, and Luigi Di Maio, the EU's Special Representative for the Gulf, areas of bilateral collaboration were discussed, including technical, economic, and cultural fields.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power has signed a power purchase agreement worth 18.2 billion Saudi riyals with Uzbekistan to construct Central Asia...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power has signed a power purchase agreement worth 18.2 billion Saudi riyals with Uzbekistan to construct Central Asia's largest wind farm in the Karakalpakstan region. The 5-gigawatt Aral wind power project was formalized at the Tashkent International Investment Forum, attended by key figures such as Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov, and Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud. The project, which is still in the development stage, promises significant economic benefits for the local area by creating numerous jobs and promoting the localization of services and supplies. This initiative will supply clean power to approximately 4.5 million homes in Uzbekistan, reflecting the country's commitment to its energy transition.

records.title: Bahrain Flour Mills Co., a Bahraini public shareholding company, is gearing up for expansion and modernization as its profits surge by 76%.
records.description: Bahrain Flour Mills Co., a Bahraini public shareholding company, is gearing up for expansion and modernization as its profits surge by 76%. With a strategic focus on ensuring long-term food security and delivering value-added products in the Gulf region, the company plans to construct a new, cutting-edge flour mill and prioritize digital transformation to meet Bahrain's flour demands. Basim Al Saie, the company's chairman, highlighted the significance of this project, emphasizing its role in enhancing food security and diversifying product offerings. The new mill, a national food security initiative, will feature advanced technology and cater to Bahrain's flour needs for the next few decades. Alongside physical expansion, the company is embracing digital solutions, transitioning to a new ERP system and establishing an e-commerce platform to enhance customer experiences. This strategic move comes on the heels of previous successful expansion plans and a significant surge in net profit for the year ended December 31, 2023. The company attributes this growth to record sales of subsidized products and increased market value of equity investments.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt is making significant strides in renewable energy, securing $9 billion in foreign direct investments for two wind energy projects w...
records.description: Egypt is making significant strides in renewable energy, securing $9 billion in foreign direct investments for two wind energy projects west of Sohag. These projects are expected to collectively generate 8 gigawatts (GW) of wind power. The first project, led by Scatec ASA of Norway, will contribute 5 GW, and was signed by Mohamed El-Khayat, chairman of the New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA). The second, contributing 3 GW, involves a consortium including Orascom Construction, ENGIE from France, and Eurus Energy from Japan, with the agreement signed by Khaled El Degwy, CEO of Orascom Construction.

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: Morocco's Competition Council is currently investigating alleged violations in the sardine market, particularly focusing on possible pric...
records.description: Morocco's Competition Council is currently investigating alleged violations in the sardine market, particularly focusing on possible price-fixing among suppliers. Preliminary findings suggest an agreement that could be distorting competition and affecting consumer prices, in violation of Moroccan Law 104-12 which guards against such market manipulations. This probe comes at a time when Morocco’s fisheries sector is seeing significant growth, with exports hitting a record $2.7 billion last year, driven by a robust international demand. The sector's exports have been growing annually by an average of 13% in volume and 16% in value. Specifically, demand for Moroccan canned sardines has surged by 33%, with frozen sardines and fishmeal/oil also seeing substantial increases. Additionally, the Competition Council is extending its scrutiny to potential price hikes at cafes nationwide, underscoring a broad effort to ensure competitive practices across various sectors.

records.title: Oman-based Hydrom has secured $11 billion in contracts to expand its green hydrogen production, partnering with major entities like the E...
records.description: Oman-based Hydrom has secured $11 billion in contracts to expand its green hydrogen production, partnering with major entities like the Electricité de France (EDF) Group consortium, Actis, and Fortescue. These initiatives aim to utilize 4.5 gigawatts of renewable energy to produce approximately 178,000 tons of green hydrogen annually by 2030, primarily for a new ammonia plant in the Salalah Free Zone. Highlighting Oman's strategic advantage between Europe and Asia, Salim Nasser Al Aufi, Oman’s Minister of Energy and Minerals, emphasized the country's strong infrastructure and early entry into the global hydrogen market. With additional agreements, including a recent $10 billion investment for projects in the Al Wusta governorate, Oman’s total hydrogen production capacity is expected to reach 1.38 million tons per year by the decade's end, positioning it as a key player in the international green hydrogen and ammonia production landscape.

records.title: The Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (ICIEC), a member of the Islamic Development Bank Group, has si...
records.description: The Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (ICIEC), a member of the Islamic Development Bank Group, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Infrastructure Fund of Saudi Arabia (INFRA) to enhance infrastructure development within Saudi Arabia. This agreement, signed during the IsDB Group Annual Meeting 2024 in Riyadh, establishes a cooperative framework between ICIEC and INFRA. The collaboration will explore mutual interests and development objectives, facilitate institutional cooperation, and enable knowledge exchange. Both parties aim to strengthen economic frameworks in member states, focusing on accelerating strategic infrastructure projects in line with Saudi Vision 2030. This partnership reflects a shared commitment to fostering sustainable development through improved insurance solutions and infrastructure investment in Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (ICIEC)

records.title: Tunisia and Iraq have strengthened their collaboration in the water sector by signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU).
records.description: Tunisia and Iraq have strengthened their collaboration in the water sector by signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU). This agreement was finalized by Tunisia's Agriculture Minister Abdelmonem Belati and Iraq's Water Resources Minister Aoun Diab Abdullah during the 4th International Water Conference in Baghdad, which took place from April 27-29, 2024. The MOU focuses on identifying and advancing technological development and research, sharing expertise, and promoting economic and scientific cooperation between the two nations.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: DP World leads the way as the first company globally to unveil a Sustainable Development Impact Disclosure (SDID), in collaboration with...
records.description: DP World leads the way as the first company globally to unveil a Sustainable Development Impact Disclosure (SDID), in collaboration with the Impact Disclosure Taskforce. This groundbreaking initiative provides a framework for illustrating large-scale infrastructure projects' contributions to the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and enhancing transparency in sustainable development efforts. Through a five-step process aligned with industry best practices, the SDID aims to empower global capital markets and inform financing decisions. During a four-month public consultation period, DP World invites industry feedback to refine the guidance, ensuring it effectively addresses stakeholders' needs.

records.title: Misr Digital Innovation (MDI) has received preliminary approval from the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) to launch Egypt's first digital bank...
records.description: Misr Digital Innovation (MDI) has received preliminary approval from the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) to launch Egypt's first digital bank, "onebank." This milestone marks the completion of the initial phase, which involved rigorous assessments of the infrastructure, banking systems, and cybersecurity protocols to ensure stability and security in service provision. MDI, a subsidiary of Banque Misr, aims to promote financial inclusion by delivering seamless banking services through digital channels. By offering a diverse range of tailored products aligned with customer lifestyles, onebank endeavors to enhance financial services in Egypt while prioritizing IT and cybersecurity strategies. Recognizing the increasing demand for digital banking solutions, onebank commits to providing online services to meet evolving consumer needs, thereby supporting the country's agenda for financial inclusion and digital transformation. Anticipated to launch in the last quarter of 2024, onebank will proceed with the second phase of due diligence and seek the operating license. The CBE's regulations for licensing digital banks, issued last July, outline prerequisites such as minimum capital requirements and shareholder qualifications, underscoring the regulatory framework guiding this transformative initiative.

records.title: The General Directorate for Industrial Development (GDID) of Iraq's Ministry of Industry and Minerals has issued 219 preliminary licenses...
records.description: The General Directorate for Industrial Development (GDID) of Iraq's Ministry of Industry and Minerals has issued 219 preliminary licenses for new industrial projects across various sectors including food, construction, chemicals, metals, and textiles. These licenses are distributed across different provinces, supporting the private sector with specialized services and facilities. In the first quarter of the year, GDID provided certificates of establishment completion to 10 industrial projects, allocated 114 land plots for new industrial ventures, and conducted 227 needs assessments for raw materials and fuel. Additionally, 1,110 industrial project identities were renewed. The directorate also undertook regular inspections, reinstated licenses for previously canceled projects, and facilitated legal actions and property transfers to foster industrial development.
records.institution: Iraqi General Directorate for Industrial Development (GDID)

records.title: The European Union unveiled a 1 billion euro aid package for Lebanon, primarily focusing on border control efforts to curb the influx of...
records.description: The European Union unveiled a 1 billion euro aid package for Lebanon, primarily focusing on border control efforts to curb the influx of asylum seekers and migrants to Cyprus and Italy. The aid, scheduled from this year until 2027, includes 736 million euros to support Syrian refugees and vulnerable groups in Lebanon. Additionally, 200 million euros are allocated to enhance Lebanese security services for border and migration enforcement. Some funds will also support Lebanese fishermen to deter them from selling their boats to smugglers.

records.title: A recent mission by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Mapa) of Brazil to Morocco has strengthened trade relations between the tw...
records.description: A recent mission by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Mapa) of Brazil to Morocco has strengthened trade relations between the two countries. During the visit, Brazilian delegates, led by Deputy Secretary of Trade and International Relations Julio Ramos, participated in the International Agriculture Fair in Morocco (Siam) in Meknes. They engaged in bilateral meetings with Moroccan officials, particularly with the National Office of Food Safety of Morocco (ONSSA), aiming to foster agreements in agriculture. Discussions focused on expanding the Moroccan market for Brazilian products, including dairy, natural bovine casings, honey, bee products, leather, and bovine genetic material. Talks also explored the possibility of tariff quotas for beef and poultry imports, addressing high Moroccan tariffs. Additionally, Mapa representatives agreed to allow the importation of mandarins from Morocco to Brazil.
records.institution: National Office of Food Safety of Morocco (ONSSA)

records.title: Oman's Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, alongside the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, and the Authority f...
records.description: Oman's Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning, alongside the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, and the Authority for Small and Medium Enterprises Development, sealed 62 agreements worth over RO12.5mn, focusing on enhancing both the agricultural and industrial sectors. The contracts include ventures spanning various regions like Dakhliyah, Dhofar, and South Batinah, targeting food security and agricultural sector growth. These agreements cover agricultural projects, wheat cultivation initiatives, and industrial and commercial endeavors, demonstrating a concerted effort to optimize land use, promote financial sustainability, and stimulate investment, thereby contributing to job creation and regional development. The oversight mechanism involves collaboration between ministries to ensure effective project implementation and alignment with strategic objectives, including initiatives aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in wheat production and supporting agricultural associations.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning (MHUP), Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, & Authority for Small and Medium Enterprises Development

records.description: Azerbaijan and Saudi Arabia are strengthening their economic ties with a focus on renewable energy projects, marking a significant expansion beyond their traditional cooperation in the oil and gas sectors. This collaboration includes the construction of a 240 MW wind power plant in Azerbaijan by ACWA Power, a leading Saudi renewable energy company. Additionally, both countries are exploring further investments in Azerbaijan's energy sector, with discussions around joint ventures and the development of green fertilizers and renewable energy projects.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is actively working to boost its seafood production to meet rising domestic demand, aiming for an output of 230,000 metric t...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is actively working to boost its seafood production to meet rising domestic demand, aiming for an output of 230,000 metric tons in 2024. This represents a significant increase from the 214,600 metric tons produced in 2023. The country's fish consumption has historically surpassed production, necessitating heavy reliance on imports. To address this, the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture is accelerating the development of 16 fishing ports along its extensive coastline, which spans 2,500 kilometers across the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea. These ports are expected to enhance marine fish production, which is a major component of the national seafood output. Additionally, the government is encouraging private investment in the sector by offering financial incentives, including covering 75% of capital expenditures for fisheries projects, providing interest-free loans, and offering discounts on fishing equipment.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: ARJ Holding LLC, a company based in the UAE, has entered into a contract to set up a compound fertilizer production plant in Baiji, locat...
records.description: ARJ Holding LLC, a company based in the UAE, has entered into a contract to set up a compound fertilizer production plant in Baiji, located in Iraq's Salah al-Din province. The new facility is expected to produce 249,000 tons of various compound phosphate fertilizers annually, including di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) and urea fertilizers. This development was confirmed by a statement from the Office of the Prime Minister of Iraq.

records.title: Municipalities Minister Wael bin Nasser Al Mubarak conducted field inspections to oversee the progress of emergency teams in managing rai...
records.description: Municipalities Minister Wael bin Nasser Al Mubarak conducted field inspections to oversee the progress of emergency teams in managing rainfall accumulations across various areas. Teams were deployed across governorates to address rainwater accumulation in internal roads, villages, residential neighborhoods, and key facilities. The Minister praised the teams for their efforts in mitigating the impacts of adverse weather conditions, including incidents like tree falls and billboard collapses.
records.institution: Bahraini Ministry of Municipalities and Agriculture

records.title: The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) has delivered its third batch of humanitarian aid to Gaza, providing 3,780 food package...
records.description: The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) has delivered its third batch of humanitarian aid to Gaza, providing 3,780 food packages through the Rafah border crossing with the assistance of Move One Logistics and the Egyptian Red Crescent. This aid aims to address the severe nutrition crisis in Gaza, offering balanced meals sufficient for a family of five for one week. The packages include a variety of food items such as canned chicken, beans, hummus, tuna, sardines, olive oil, high-energy biscuits, halawah, and dried fruits. Distributed by the Palestine Agriculture Development Association in coordination with the Palestinian Red Crescent, this assistance targets Internally Displaced Persons in Rafah and Khan Younis.

records.title: LG Chem, South Korea's prominent chemical company, is set to establish its first international water-desalination device plant in Saudi A...
records.description: LG Chem, South Korea's prominent chemical company, is set to establish its first international water-desalination device plant in Saudi Arabia by 2026. This venture is in collaboration with Alkhorayef Group, a Saudi conglomerate involved in water, energy, and agriculture. The project involves a $86 million investment into a reverse osmosis (RO) membrane plant, supporting the goals of Saudi Vision 2030 by localizing strategic industries and enhancing the non-oil sector GDP. The initiative addresses the increasing local demand for RO membranes in the Middle East, where Saudi Arabia, accounting for 21% of global demand, heavily relies on desalination for its water supply.

records.title: The National Agricultural Services Company (NADEC) and Delphy have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at enhancing capabilities and loc...
records.description: The National Agricultural Services Company (NADEC) and Delphy have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at enhancing capabilities and localizing technologies in Saudi Arabia's agricultural sector. The agreement, witnessed by Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture officials, aligns with Saudi Vision 2030 objectives. It focuses on qualifying and training agricultural advisors, building capacities, and adopting best agricultural practices and technologies. This collaboration seeks to improve efficiency among farmers and foster the development of the agricultural sector in the country through modern systems and innovations. NADEC, established by a Cabinet decision, will work alongside Delphy, a global leader in agricultural services, to achieve these goals.

records.title: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen and the Selah Foundation for Development have joined forces on a renewable-ene...
records.description: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen and the Selah Foundation for Development have joined forces on a renewable-energy water-security project in Yemen's Hadhramaut region, benefiting approximately 1.7 million people. This initiative will utilize solar power stations to enhance water sources sustainably. The agreement, signed by officials from both organizations, underscores Saudi Arabia's commitment to supporting Yemen's development efforts. Hadhramaut's governor expressed gratitude for Saudi assistance, highlighting the positive impact of ongoing projects across various sectors. As part of the project, solar power stations will be established in nine areas to improve water availability, accompanied by training for local technicians.
records.institution: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen & Selah Foundation for Development

records.title: India has relaxed its export restrictions on onions, aiming to alleviate high onion prices and meet demand from Sri Lanka and the UAE.
records.description: India has relaxed its export restrictions on onions, aiming to alleviate high onion prices and meet demand from Sri Lanka and the UAE. This adjustment is part of India's broader strategy to manage regional trade dynamics, especially in light of China's growing influence. The move follows similar easing of restrictions for the Maldives due to tense bilateral relations. Previously, India, a major onion exporter, had imposed limits that contributed to price surges in dependent countries. The new "special quota" system now allows onion exports to several nations including Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Bahrain, and Bhutan, with resumed shipments to the Maldives under an exemption from future export bans valid through the 2024-25 fiscal year.

records.title: Masdar, the Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company, has partnered with Bahrain's Bapco Energies to potentially develop up to 2 gigawatts of wind...
records.description: Masdar, the Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company, has partnered with Bahrain's Bapco Energies to potentially develop up to 2 gigawatts of wind energy projects in Bahrain. This collaboration marks Masdar's entry into the Bahraini market, aligning with its goal to expand its renewable energy capacity to 100 gigawatts by 2030. The initiative is part of Bahrain's National Energy Strategy, aiming for a 30% reduction in emissions by 2035 and achieving net-zero by 2060.

records.title: The Mleiha dairy farm in the UAE is set to become the largest clean milk production project within three years, boasting 1,250 cows initi...
records.description: The Mleiha dairy farm in the UAE is set to become the largest clean milk production project within three years, boasting 1,250 cows initially with plans to expand to 5,000 cows. Daily milk production is expected to surge from 75 to 310 tons, backed by a budget of approximately Dh600 million. Operational insights reveal a meticulous approach, with cows not subjected to medical interventions or growth enhancers, and a focus on A2A2 protein-rich milk known for its health benefits. Cutting-edge technology, including smart collars monitoring various aspects of cow health, enhances efficiency and animal welfare. The farm integrates innovative systems like water sprinklers and autonomous robots for streamlined operations. Packaging innovation ensures milk quality preservation, aligning with the farm's commitment to sustainable, high-quality production.

records.title: Egyptian authorities have intensified their enforcement of price controls, focusing on restaurants, supermarkets, and bakeries to prevent...
records.description: Egyptian authorities have intensified their enforcement of price controls, focusing on restaurants, supermarkets, and bakeries to prevent price gouging, especially in the Gharbia governorate, located 100km north of Cairo. This crackdown extends previous measures targeting businesses, such as food vendors selling popular items like foul and falafel, for not adhering to government-mandated price reductions. Despite over $50 billion in international financing aiding Egypt to reduce food prices by up to 35%, many small businesses continue to defy these controls, leading to multiple violations and increased governmental scrutiny.

records.title: At the inaugural World Economic Forum Special Meeting held in Riyadh, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has pledged a substantial $500 million...
records.description: At the inaugural World Economic Forum Special Meeting held in Riyadh, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has pledged a substantial $500 million over the next five years to support the Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI). This significant increase in funding aims to vaccinate over 370 million children annually against polio, bolstering efforts to end the disease globally. The pledge, made in collaboration with key partners including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Gavi, Rotary International, and others, underscores Saudi Arabia's commitment to improving global health outcomes. In addition to addressing polio, the funding will strengthen health systems and provide essential interventions to underserved communities, aligning with broader efforts to enhance healthcare resilience worldwide.

records.title: Iraq and Germany have engaged in discussions to enhance development cooperation, with a focus on various sectors.
records.description: Iraq and Germany have engaged in discussions to enhance development cooperation, with a focus on various sectors. This dialogue, facilitated by the Iraqi Ministry of Planning, involved key figures including Dr. Saher Abdul Kadhim Mahdi, Director General of the International Cooperation Department, and the economic advisor from the German Embassy along with his delegation. The discussions reviewed the development activities funded by Germany and outlined the upcoming development negotiations scheduled for July. Additionally, the meeting delved into the governmental work mechanisms for monitoring international commitments financed by Germany.

records.title: The Arab-British Chamber of Commerce (ABCC) has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Baghdad Chamber of Commerce to...
records.description: The Arab-British Chamber of Commerce (ABCC) has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Baghdad Chamber of Commerce to strengthen their partnership and enhance support for their members.
