records.title: Iraq is preparing to construct its largest sustainable city in Karbala, as part of an environmental protection plan to address the challe...
records.description: Iraq is preparing to construct its largest sustainable city in Karbala, as part of an environmental protection plan to address the challenges posed by urban expansion and development projects encroaching on farming areas. Al-Zahra University in Karbala has drafted preliminary designs for the project, which will soon be discussed by local authorities, according to reports from the official Alsabah newspaper. The city aims to mitigate the environmental impact of rapid urbanization and ensure a sustainable future for the region, marking a significant step towards environmental conservation in Iraq.

records.title: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) predicts that Jordan will import up to 1.2 million tonnes of wheat...
records.description: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) predicts that Jordan will import up to 1.2 million tonnes of wheat in the 2024-25 period to address demand, a measure taken to alleviate inflationary pressures amid geopolitical uncertainties. This projection matches the import level of the previous year but marks an increase from 2022-23's 1 million tonnes. Jordan, known for its arid climate, heavily relies on global trade for food security, with its population doubling over the past two decades. The country predominantly imports bread wheat from Black Sea origins like Romania, Ukraine, and Russia. Despite some beneficial rainfall in early 2024, wheat production is expected to remain stagnant, covering only a fraction of national consumption. Consequently, wheat exports are projected to decrease, with barley consumption and imports expected to rise due to increased feed use. Corn consumption is also forecasted to increase significantly, with imports necessary to meet demand.
records.institution: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS)

records.title: This season, Moroccan avocado exporters achieved a record performance, exporting 60,000 tonnes, signaling a strong demand, particularly f...
records.description: This season, Moroccan avocado exporters achieved a record performance, exporting 60,000 tonnes, signaling a strong demand, particularly from the European Union and the UK markets, according to Salah Eddine Belkadi, CEO of Unique Packing. While the British market showed significant interest, with prices remaining high until the end of the season, the Dutch market emerged as another key destination for Moroccan avocados. Belkadi attributes this preference to the post-ripening performance of Moroccan avocados, which result in lower waste compared to avocados from other origins like Peru or Colombia. Looking ahead, changes in Moroccan production sizes are expected to impact market dynamics, with a shift towards larger sizes likely to increase European demand.

records.title: Pakistan has presented over 25 projects with an estimated potential investment of more than $32 billion to a high-powered delegation from...
records.description: Pakistan has presented over 25 projects with an estimated potential investment of more than $32 billion to a high-powered delegation from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), aiming to bolster bilateral cooperation and economic ties. These projects span various sectors, including rail infrastructure, dams, luxury hotels, smart device manufacturing, semiconductor development, mining, power transmission, tourism, and refineries. The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), jointly run by military and civilian authorities, highlighted the evolving economic landscape of Pakistan and emphasized initiatives to stimulate investment and achieve macroeconomic stability. Key sectors identified for investment include defense, agriculture, mines and minerals, IT, telecom, and energy. Additionally, the discussions addressed the resolution of pending agreements and financial settlements, indicating progress in addressing concerns raised by Saudi investors.

records.title: Saudi Arabian developer Red Sea Global has partnered with Warner Bros.
records.description: Saudi Arabian developer Red Sea Global has partnered with Warner Bros. Discovery to produce a documentary titled "Beneath the Surface: The Fight for Corals," which explores the critical importance of combating climate change's impact on coral reefs. Scheduled to launch on Earth Day, April 22, 2024, on the Discovery Channel across various regions, the film showcases Red Sea Global's commitment to environmental care and regeneration in its development projects. Through the journey of Saudi free diver Salma Shaker, viewers will witness innovative coral research conducted by scientists at Red Sea Global and King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), highlighting the global dangers facing coral reefs. The documentary also delves into the uncharted reefs along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline, emphasizing their biodiversity and ecological significance while exploring the potential benefits of Red Sea coral research for global ecosystems.

records.title: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly underscored Egypt's commitment to bolstering hard currency reserves through industrial growth and exports...
records.description: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly underscored Egypt's commitment to bolstering hard currency reserves through industrial growth and exports, particularly in response to recent dollar shortages stemming from external economic shocks. With current annual exports totaling $53 billion, Madbouly aims to increase this figure by 17-18 percent by 2030, reaching nearly $145 billion. To achieve this ambitious goal, Madbouly convened a meeting to strategize on increasing export rates and supporting local industries. He emphasized the government's readiness to facilitate industry localization and expansion, offering incentives for manufacturing specific products identified for localization. The meeting also addressed the need for practical implementation plans, with a follow-up session scheduled to finalize strategies. The Minister of Trade and Industry presented a report highlighting a 5.3 percent increase in merchandise exports in the first quarter of 2024, with key sectors including building materials, food industries, chemical products, and engineering goods. The export councils stressed the importance of supporting industries with competitive advantages, advocating for measures such as indicative pricing for crops, improved land shipping rates, and tax exemptions for exporters to stimulate demand and attract foreign investments.

records.title: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) announced on Monday an increase in the daily maximum limit for cash withdrawals from ATMs, raising it to...
records.description: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) announced on Monday an increase in the daily maximum limit for cash withdrawals from ATMs, raising it to LE 30,000 from the previous limit of LE 20,000. Additionally, the CBE revealed that the daily maximum limit for cash withdrawals from bank branches has been raised to LE 250,000 for both individuals and companies, up from LE 150,000. As part of these adjustments, banks are required to update their internal policies to align with the revised limits, including the policies governing maximum cash withdrawal limits for foreign currencies, which are determined by each bank's Board of Directors. These changes build upon the CBE's instructions issued on August 25, 2022, regarding maximum limits for cash withdrawals and deposits, and are aimed at further facilitating transactions for citizens and companies.

records.title: The health insurance budget has been significantly increased to 42.5 million pounds, aimed at broadening coverage to encompass new segmen...
records.description: The health insurance budget has been significantly increased to 42.5 million pounds, aimed at broadening coverage to encompass new segments of the population, ensuring access to essential drugs and medical supplies, and extending health insurance coverage to over 70% of Egyptians. This announcement came from the spokesperson of the Ministry of Health and Housing, Hossam Abdel Ghaffar, during an interview with "Al Masriya" TV satellite channel. These enhancements align with the renovation efforts led by the Health Ministry, which are part of the presidential initiative "Decent Life." Furthermore, the expansion of health insurance coverage will now include previously underserved groups such as farmers, drivers, and irregular workers, reflecting a commitment to address the healthcare needs of diverse segments of the population.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Housing

records.title: In the Marrakech-Safi region of Morocco, efforts to support local farmers are evident in the distribution of subsidized barley, with over...
records.description: In the Marrakech-Safi region of Morocco, efforts to support local farmers are evident in the distribution of subsidized barley, with over 454,500 tonnes allocated to benefit more than 31,115 farmers across eight provinces and prefectures. As of April 3, significant progress has been made in the distribution process, representing a removal rate of 31 percent from the total allocation of nearly 1.4 million quintals earmarked for the region under the initial phases of the operation.

records.title: Naman Keita, CEO of Agroplus Mali and a prominent mango exporter, provides an update on the ongoing Malian mango season, expressing optim...
records.description: Naman Keita, CEO of Agroplus Mali and a prominent mango exporter, provides an update on the ongoing Malian mango season, expressing optimism about its progress. Notably, there is a significant increase in volumes compared to the previous year, especially for the Kent variety, which bodes well for meeting demand. The season's success is attributed to favorable climatic conditions during the flowering phase, resulting in a higher abundance of large calibers. Moroccan demand at the campaign's onset is strong, with Agroplus-Mali alone exporting over 100 tons of Amelie mangoes to Morocco within a month. Anticipation mounts for increased demand with the introduction of the Keit variety and potential interest from European markets post-Fruit Logistica exhibition participation. Keita underscores the unique qualities of Malian mangoes, such as taste, juice content, and longer season duration, setting them apart from counterparts in Côte d'Ivoire or Senegal. Despite these developments, prices remain unchanged this season, as determined by the interprofession.

records.title: Recent data from the Spanish Department of Customs and Special Taxes, analyzed by FEPEX, underscores Morocco's pivotal role as Spain's pr...
records.description: Recent data from the Spanish Department of Customs and Special Taxes, analyzed by FEPEX, underscores Morocco's pivotal role as Spain's primary non-EU provider of fruits and vegetables in early 2024. In January 2024, Spain's imports from non-EU nations constituted 67% of its total fruit and vegetable imports, valued at €261 million, surpassing imports from EU countries at €129 million. This trend, consistent with previous years, reflects Spain's increasing reliance on non-EU sources, with overall imports in January 2024 experiencing a 26% year-over-year increase to €390 million. Notably, Moroccan imports saw a significant surge, reaching €134 million in value and 57,534 tons in volume, representing a 45% and 31% increase, respectively.
records.institution: Spanish Department of Customs and Special Taxes

records.title: The inauguration of the new regional slaughterhouse in Bouknadel marks a significant milestone in bolstering the red meat sector's develo...
records.description: The inauguration of the new regional slaughterhouse in Bouknadel marks a significant milestone in bolstering the red meat sector's development in the Rabat Salé Skhirat Témara region of Morocco. With a capacity of 30,000 tonnes per year, this state-of-the-art facility, covering an area of 4 hectares, including 15,000 m2 of covered space, represents a substantial investment of 267 million dirhams. Equipped with modern amenities such as cold rooms, advanced slaughter lines, administrative spaces, and a wastewater treatment plant, the slaughterhouse is designed to meet health standards while ensuring efficient processing and marketing of red meat and animal products. Moreover, incorporating digital systems for livestock identification and monitoring, as well as compliance with National Office for Food Safety (ONSSA) standards, underscores its commitment to quality and transparency throughout the production chain.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: In Muscat on April 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources reported a total of 4,881 fishing violations in 2023,...
records.description: In Muscat on April 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources reported a total of 4,881 fishing violations in 2023, representing a decrease of approximately 4.96% from the previous year's total of 5,136 violations. These violations encompassed various infractions, including issues related to licenses, lack of identification marks on boats and ships, use or possession of prohibited fishing tools, and unauthorized use of tracking devices. Additionally, violations were recorded for fishing in prohibited areas, unauthorized fishing of rock lobster and ear shell, and various other infractions. The ministry also seized 24,398.3 kilograms of various types of fish in 2024, along with the arrest of 420 foreign workers, representing a decrease of 19.39% from the previous year's total of 521 workers. Furthermore, there was a 51.51% increase in the confiscation of boats and fishing equipment by the ministry in 2023 compared to the previous year, with a significant rise in the total number of confiscated items. Fishing in Oman is regulated by the Law of Marine Fishing and Protection of Living Aquatic Resources, which mandates the acquisition of licenses and permits for fishing activities. Violations of these regulations can result in fines, equipment confiscation, or license revocation.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has announced the appointment of a fresh board of directors for the Palestine Investment Fund, as rev...
records.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has announced the appointment of a fresh board of directors for the Palestine Investment Fund, as revealed by the Palestinian news agency WAFA. The newly constituted board comprises notable personalities such as Eyad Judah, Maher al-Masri, Mohammad Nasr, Tamer Bazzari, Atef Allawneh, Mohammad Abu Ramadan, Ali Abu Diyak, Lena Abu Hajleh, and Firas Malham. Established in 2003 and functioning as a public shareholding company under the Ministry of National Economy, the Palestine Investment Fund endeavors to fortify the Palestinian economy through strategic investments spanning various sectors, including energy, healthcare, telecommunications, digital economy, industry, trade, agriculture, real estate, and tourism. Its inception involved the transfer of assets previously managed by the Palestinian Authority, amplifying its capacity to drive economic advancement. Mohammad Mustafa, who had chaired the fund since January 2009, assumed a new role as the Palestinian prime minister on March 14, paving the way for the newly appointed leaders to steer the fund's direction.

records.title: A high-level Saudi delegation, led by Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan, convened in Islamabad for the joint Special I...
records.description: A high-level Saudi delegation, led by Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan, convened in Islamabad for the joint Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) meeting with Pakistani counterparts, chaired by Pakistan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Ishaq Dar. The discussions centered on leveraging economic cooperation opportunities across various sectors and enhancing bilateral trade. Prince Faisal emphasized the longstanding Saudi-Pakistani relations, highlighting the significance of the visit in alignment with previous high-level engagements between leaders of both nations. The meeting aimed to bolster investment prospects and provide support to investors from both countries.

records.title: Tolga Soytekin, founder of Bare Foods Global, has introduced the Meatless Monday campaign to the Middle East, aiming to promote sustainab...
records.description: Tolga Soytekin, founder of Bare Foods Global, has introduced the Meatless Monday campaign to the Middle East, aiming to promote sustainable and healthy eating habits. By partnering with third-party catering companies, schools, universities, and hospitals across the UAE are encouraged to offer plant-based dishes every Monday. Drawing on his culinary expertise, Soytekin emphasizes the importance of familiar comfort foods to ease the transition for students and diners. Through social media advocacy and recipe inspiration, Bare Foods Global seeks to raise awareness about the environmental and health benefits of reducing meat consumption. With plans to expand outreach through seminars and educational initiatives, the ultimate goal is to instill a culture of plant-based eating across households in the UAE, driven by the influence of children on family dining choices.

records.title: A significant step towards enhancing bilateral relations between Algeria and Belarus was taken during a constructive meeting between Pres...
records.description: A significant step towards enhancing bilateral relations between Algeria and Belarus was taken during a constructive meeting between President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and Mr. Aleïnik, the Belarusian representative. The discussions, held in a spirit of cooperation, underscored the shared interests in various sectors, including industry, food security, agriculture, and culture. Of particular note was the decision to convene inaugural meetings focusing on tourism and education, signaling a joint commitment to advancing trade and collaboration in strategic areas beneficial for the economic and social progress of both nations. Furthermore, the exchange provided an opportunity to address common international concerns, with emphasis placed on supporting the efforts of international organizations towards a multipolar world and the importance of global cooperation in addressing shared challenges.

records.title: Egypt has made significant strides in becoming a major supplier of fresh strawberries to Kazakhstan, securing the third spot in the 2022/...
records.description: Egypt has made significant strides in becoming a major supplier of fresh strawberries to Kazakhstan, securing the third spot in the 2022/23 season and poised to further expand its market presence. With a notable increase in exports in the 2023/24 season, Egypt's fresh strawberry shipments to Kazakhstan have nearly tripled compared to the previous season, indicating a growing demand for Egyptian strawberries in the Kazakhstani market. The exponential growth in exports has propelled Egypt into the top three exporters of fresh strawberries to Kazakhstan, trailing only behind Turkey and Azerbaijan. This surge in demand aligns well with Kazakhstan's increasing appetite for fresh berries during festive periods, offering opportunities for Egyptian exporters to meet consumer needs during key occasions such as the New Year, St. Valentine's Day, and International Women's Day. Despite logistical challenges, Egypt has effectively competed with Turkish suppliers, with both countries capitalizing on the rising demand for off-season berries among Kazakhstani consumers. Moreover, the trade opens avenues for broader regional market access, with potential opportunities to supply neighboring countries like Uzbekistan through Kazakhstan-based retailers..

records.title: Egypt's agricultural prowess continues to make strides as Egyptian potatoes gain entry into the Moroccan market, a significant achievemen...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural prowess continues to make strides as Egyptian potatoes gain entry into the Moroccan market, a significant achievement revealed by Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Elsayed Al-Qasir. This milestone aligns with the ministry's overarching strategy to broaden the scope of Egyptian agricultural exports, thereby bolstering economic resilience through strengthened cash reserves. The official announcement underscores the approval granted by Moroccan agricultural authorities (ONSSA) for the importation of Egyptian potatoes, facilitating immediate export operations to Morocco and fostering greater diversity in Egypt's agricultural export portfolio. This expansion comes amidst a backdrop of robust growth in Egypt's agricultural sector, evidenced by first-quarter exports surpassing 2.2 million tons, valued at approximately $1.5 billion. Despite challenges posed by global supply chain disruptions and targeted export limitations, Egypt's agricultural exports remain a cornerstone of the economy, generating $9 billion in revenue last year and significantly contributing to the nation's foreign currency reserves and economic stability.
records.institution: The National Office of Food Safety (ONSSA)

records.title: Egypt's agricultural sector celebrates significant milestones as the nation ventures into new markets, marking the inaugural exports of p...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural sector celebrates significant milestones as the nation ventures into new markets, marking the inaugural exports of potatoes to Morocco and strawberries to Canada. Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Elsayed Al-Qasir, proudly heralded the successful entry of Egyptian potatoes into the Moroccan market, signaling a pivotal moment in Egypt's quest to broaden its global agricultural footprint and bolster economic resilience through enhanced cash reserves. The official statement from the Egyptian Ministry underscores the approval received from Moroccan agricultural authorities (ONSSA) for potato imports, paving the way for immediate export operations. Simultaneously, Egyptian authorities have fulfilled all technical requirements from Canada for fresh strawberry exports, underscoring Egypt's commitment to tapping into new markets and meeting rising global demand for its high-quality agricultural products. Despite challenges such as supply chain disruptions and domestic export bans, Egypt's agricultural sector continues to thrive, with first-quarter exports in 2024 surpassing 2.2 million tons valued at approximately USD 1.5 billion. This reflects a substantial increase of USD 300 million compared to the same period last year, highlighting agriculture as Egypt's second-largest export sector, generating USD 9 billion in revenue in the previous year. Egypt's proactive pursuit of new export markets underscores its strategic vision to expand foreign currency resources and solidify its position as a key player in the international agricultural landscape.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Iraq has achieved a significant milestone in its economic journey, with the government announcing a remarkable 50% reduction in its forei...
records.description: Iraq has achieved a significant milestone in its economic journey, with the government announcing a remarkable 50% reduction in its foreign debt. This achievement underscores the administration's commitment to fostering a positive transformation in the Iraqi economy. According to Bassem Al-Awadi, the Iraqi government spokesman, a series of executive measures and financial decisions contributed to this reduction, with the external public debt decreasing from $19.729 billion in 2022 to $15.976 billion in 2023, further plummeting to approximately $8.9 billion in the current year. These measures included halting unproductive debt operations, restructuring debts towards strategic projects, and improving debt management practices. Al-Awadi emphasized that these initiatives align with Iraq's national development goals, emphasizing urban renewal, infrastructure reconstruction, and economic revitalization. Furthermore, these efforts aim to integrate Iraq further into the global economic landscape, stimulate domestic output growth, and finance national expenditures. Despite these strides, Iraq faces ongoing challenges related to bureaucracy and private sector obstacles. However, with a strong emphasis on economic reform and diversification, Iraq is poised to navigate these challenges and capitalize on its vast potential for industrial and agricultural investments.

records.title: The Moroccan watermelon export season faced an unexpected hurdle as Spanish authorities accused the produce of containing high pesticide...
records.description: The Moroccan watermelon export season faced an unexpected hurdle as Spanish authorities accused the produce of containing high pesticide residues, leading Moroccan food safety authorities to impose stringent new export requirements. These measures include additional pesticide residue tests for each batch harvested, causing delays in obtaining phytosanitary certificates and increased costs for exporters. While denying the Spanish accusations, industry insiders like Said Aghzou, CEO of Valyour, acknowledge the necessity of the new measures to safeguard Moroccan origin and ensure product quality. Despite production restrictions in key regions like Zagora and Tata, Aghzou remains optimistic about meeting demand, citing new cultivation strategies extending to other regions of the Grand Moroccan Sahara. The quality of this year's harvest is reported to be excellent, with desirable sizes suitable for various markets.

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality in Qatar is actively engaged in stabilizing prices for local agricultural produce, especially during peak se...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality in Qatar is actively engaged in stabilizing prices for local agricultural produce, especially during peak seasons when both Qatari farms and international sources contribute to the market. Through its Agricultural Affairs Department, the Ministry has initiated programs to reduce production costs for local farms, enhancing their competitiveness against imported goods. One crucial strategy involves promoting high-quality agricultural produce during peak seasons to manage market saturation effectively. Ahmed Salem Al Yafei, Head of the Agricultural Guidance and Services Section at the Ministry, highlighted collaborative efforts with relevant ministries to address challenges faced by local farmers due to large imports of agricultural produce. Measures include regulating imports to meet local quality standards and providing agricultural inputs like fertilizers, pesticides, seeds, irrigation systems, and greenhouses at no cost to farmers. Additionally, marketing platforms are being developed to ensure profitable returns for local producers.

records.title: Land Bank Insurance's pioneering training program for Black assessors in South Africa's agricultural sector marks a significant step towa...
records.description: Land Bank Insurance's pioneering training program for Black assessors in South Africa's agricultural sector marks a significant step toward inclusivity and empowerment within the industry. Unveiled at the esteemed Mzansi Young Farmers Indaba, this groundbreaking initiative promises to revolutionize agricultural assessment and insurance practices, thereby ensuring that all farmers, regardless of background, have access to tailored insurance solutions that meet their unique needs. Spearheaded by Land Bank's Insurance Company managing director, Pascal Siphugu, the program's comprehensive curriculum encompasses a wide array of topics crucial to agricultural assessment and insurance, including crop valuation, risk management, and the utilization of cutting-edge technology.

records.title: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) has pledged $10 million to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) to...
records.description: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) has pledged $10 million to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) to provide daily hot meals to 140,000 vulnerable Ukrainians across 1,200 institutions, including hospitals, shelters, and orphanages. This initiative, aimed at alleviating the hardships faced by those affected by the ongoing conflict, underscores KSrelief's commitment to humanitarian assistance. By procuring and delivering essential food commodities locally in Ukraine, WFP's institutional feeding program not only addresses immediate food needs but also supports the country's economy and food systems. Through this collaboration, KSrelief and WFP demonstrate their dedication to mitigating the impact of the conflict and providing vital support to communities in need.
records.institution: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief)

records.title: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan recently hosted a delegation led by Suhail Al-Mazrui, the Minister of Energy and Infrastructur...
records.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan recently hosted a delegation led by Suhail Al-Mazrui, the Minister of Energy and Infrastructure of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), on April 15, coinciding with the second meeting of the "Central Asia-Gulf Arab States Cooperation Council" ministerial dialogue. During the discussions, Minister Al-Mazrui conveyed warm regards from prominent UAE leaders and both sides expressed satisfaction with the expanding economic ties, noting a consistent increase in bilateral trade volume. Particularly noteworthy was the significant presence of UAE investments in Uzbekistan, with over 300 UAE enterprises operating and a joint project portfolio exceeding $4 billion, highlighting the depth of economic engagement between the two countries. The discussions also centered around exploring potential projects in sectors such as green energy, metallurgy, agriculture, transport, and communication, indicating fertile ground for mutually beneficial collaboration and economic growth. A key highlight was the deliberation on the Trans-Afghan railway project, showcasing strategic importance in bolstering regional connectivity and facilitating trade.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure

records.title: Finance Minister: State to Prioritize Human Development in Next 6 Years
records.description: Finance Minister Mohamed Maait announced that the state will prioritize human development in the next six years, starting from the new fiscal year 2024-2025. Following presidential directives, increased financial allocations will be allocated to health, the Universal Health Insurance System, and education to advance the strategy of building the Egyptian personality. Maait revealed that allocations for the health sector will rise to 495.6 billion pounds, marking a 24.9 percent annual growth rate, while allocations for education will increase to 858.3 billion pounds, representing a 45 percent annual increase. Additionally, allocations for scientific research will be boosted to over 139.5 billion pounds, recording a 40.1 percent annual growth. Maait emphasized the ministry's efforts to enhance the efficiency of human resources in the health and education sectors, highlighting the allocation of 15 billion pounds for medical and teaching staff in the last social package.

records.title: The Coalition of Civil Society Organizations in North and East Syria (CSO-NES) convened a forum in Qamishli, northeast Syria, aimed at en...
records.description: The Coalition of Civil Society Organizations in North and East Syria (CSO-NES) convened a forum in Qamishli, northeast Syria, aimed at enhancing the education system in the region. As part of a series of meetings throughout April, the forum featured research presentations on various sectors, including agriculture, healthcare, and education, within areas administered by the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES). Ahmad Abu Shakir, an education expert, presented research findings detailing challenges within the educational process and proposed recommendations. Faisal Khudr, co-chair of the Education Board in Hasakah Governorate, highlighted the significance of the forum in addressing identified difficulties and formulating strategies for improvement. Academic participant Farid Saadoun emphasized the broader relevance of the challenges facing education in Syria and underscored the potential impact of implementing the forum's recommendations. Nasser Hajj Mansour, a coordinator in CSO-NES, emphasized the importance of addressing key sectors like education to foster a prosperous and secure society, despite the complex challenges encountered in project implementation. With over 860,000 students in AANES-administered schools, Mansour stressed the need for significant financial resources and international collaboration to achieve desired outcomes in agriculture, healthcare, and education.
records.institution: The Coalition of Civil Society Organizations in North and East Syria (CSO-NES)

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has issued guidelines for farmers and livestock breeders to navigate unpredi...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has issued guidelines for farmers and livestock breeders to navigate unpredictable weather conditions, urging precautionary measures to safeguard crops and animals. Highlighted measures include clearing water drainage channels, securing tools and equipment, and inspecting structures for damage to mitigate risks during heavy rain and strong winds. Livestock should be housed in barns with access to food and water, while feed stocks must be stored safely to prevent moisture damage. Greenhouses require attention to reduce humidity and block dust, with a focus on ventilation, fencing integrity, and electrical system functionality. Monitoring drainage near greenhouses is crucial to prevent waterlogging, while suspending agricultural work during storms is advised for worker safety. Additionally, crops may require preventative fungicides post-rain to combat diseases, with ADAFSA recommending seeking assistance from their guidance centers or veterinary clinics if necessary.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Finance Minister Mohamed Maait revealed that Egypt's Customs Authority has cleared goods worth over eight billion dollars since March.
records.description: Finance Minister Mohamed Maait revealed that Egypt's Customs Authority has cleared goods worth over eight billion dollars since March. Maait emphasized the collaborative efforts with state agencies to address import practices leading to port congestion, affirming decisive action against goods left beyond legal periods. Despite available US dollar resources in banks, some importers are withholding shipments without legal grounds. Maait underscored the serious handling of such cases, ensuring adherence to legal procedures and preventing disruptions to trade flows.

records.title: Jordan has reported a significant increase in its industrial exports to Iraq during the first quarter of 2024, according to a report from...
records.description: Jordan has reported a significant increase in its industrial exports to Iraq during the first quarter of 2024, according to a report from the Jordanian Chamber of Industry. The chamber's exports totaled 1.776 billion Jordanian dinars (JOD) during this period, compared to 1.813 billion JOD in the same period of 2023. The United States, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, and India were the top importing countries, with exports to these nations accounting for over half of the total exports. Specifically, exports to Iraq surged to approximately 267 million JOD, marking a notable 20% increase from the previous year. These exports were primarily from sectors such as chemical and cosmetic industries, mining, engineering, electrical, and information technology. Other sectors contributing to exports included supply, food, agriculture, medical treatment, textiles, construction, and wooden industries, among others.

records.title: Amidst ongoing military confrontations initiated by Israeli aggressors in southern Lebanon since October 2023, the Kuwait Red Crescent So...
records.description: Amidst ongoing military confrontations initiated by Israeli aggressors in southern Lebanon since October 2023, the Kuwait Red Crescent Society (KRCS) has emerged as a crucial lifeline, providing essential relief aid to affected residents. Despite the persisting challenges of the conflict, the KRCS has demonstrated unwavering commitment by delivering critical supplies, including foodstuff and necessities, benefiting approximately 2,500 families in the region.

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality in Qatar has intensified efforts to ensure fair prices for local agricultural produce, particularly during p...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality in Qatar has intensified efforts to ensure fair prices for local agricultural produce, particularly during peak seasons when the market is flooded with vegetables from both Qatari farms and abroad. Through initiatives led by the Agricultural Affairs Department, the Ministry aims to reduce production costs for local farms by providing agricultural inputs and marketing platforms. One key initiative involves allowing only high-quality agricultural produce during peak seasons, thereby preventing the market from being overwhelmed with vegetables. Additionally, the Ministry offers support to local farmers by providing agricultural inputs and facilitating marketing platforms to enable them to achieve better returns for their efforts. These efforts, including direct selling yards and marketing programs like "Premium Qatari Vegetables" and "Qatar Farms," reflect Qatar's commitment to bolstering its agricultural sector and achieving greater self-sufficiency in fresh food production, with the self-sufficiency rate rising from 27 percent in 2011 to about 45 percent in 2024.

records.title: Egypt is broadening its agricultural export horizons, venturing into new markets with the export of potatoes to Morocco and strawberries...
records.description: Egypt is broadening its agricultural export horizons, venturing into new markets with the export of potatoes to Morocco and strawberries to Canada for the first time. The Ministry of Agriculture in Egypt has emphasized its strategic efforts to strengthen foreign currency reserves through agricultural initiatives. With Moroccan authorities approving potato imports and Egypt meeting Canadian technical requirements for fresh strawberry exports, significant strides have been made in diversifying Egypt's agricultural export portfolio. The ministry highlighted the increasing global demand for Egypt's agricultural products, driven by their recognized quality. Despite ongoing supply chain disruptions and selective export bans aimed at bolstering the domestic market, Egypt's agricultural exports during the first quarter of 2024 surpassed 2.2 million tons, amounting to approximately $1.5 billion—an increase of $300 million compared to the previous year. Agriculture remains Egypt's second-largest export sector, generating $9 billion in revenue from fresh and processed products last year.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Egypt is expected to import 3.1 million metric tons (MMT) of soybeans in 2024-25, a 14.8% increase attributed to an influx of foreign cur...
records.description: Egypt is expected to import 3.1 million metric tons (MMT) of soybeans in 2024-25, a 14.8% increase attributed to an influx of foreign currency into its banks and rising feed demand. This surge in imports comes as domestic production covers less than 3% of demand, with soybeans mainly used in full-fat soybeans for feed rations. Meal production is estimated to increase by 28% to 2.5 million tonnes, with consumption at 2.85 million tonnes. Additionally, Egypt is anticipated to import around 700 thousand tons of sunflower oil by the end of the 2024/25 season, driven by competitive pricing and a trend towards blending sunflower oil with soybean oil. This surge in imports reflects an increase in population, higher demand, and the influx of foreign currency, with both soybean and sunflower oil production forecasted to rise.
records.institution: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS)

records.title: The Council of the European Union greenlit €1 billion in financial aid for Egypt, aiming to bolster economic stability amidst recent chal...
records.description: The Council of the European Union greenlit €1 billion in financial aid for Egypt, aiming to bolster economic stability amidst recent challenges. This support, characterized as urgent short-term macro financial assistance, targets addressing Egypt's financial situation, exacerbated by events like the Gaza war, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, and fallout from the Russian-Ukrainian conflict. The approved aid forms part of a larger package, including an additional €4 billion yet to be ratified, slated for disbursement between 2024 and 2027. Alongside this EU assistance, Egypt will also benefit from an up to €8 billion support program with the International Monetary Fund. The aid, provided as loans in one lump sum, will enter into force following publication in the Official Journal of the European Union, with loans sourced from the EU budget at a rate of 9% (€90 million) in accordance with Financial Regulations.

records.title: The influx of Egyptian oranges into the Spanish market has sparked concern among Andalusian citrus producers, who are witnessing a signif...
records.description: The influx of Egyptian oranges into the Spanish market has sparked concern among Andalusian citrus producers, who are witnessing a significant decrease in orange prices for juice alongside a collapse in national production. Traditionally destined for other regions, Egyptian exports are now being redirected to European Union markets due to geopolitical conflicts, exacerbating the situation. This surge in imports has led to calls for stricter labeling regulations to ensure consumers are informed about the origin of the oranges they purchase. Additionally, agricultural organizations have raised complaints about misleading labeling practices, highlighting the need for transparency in the fruit supply chain.

records.title: Despite a decline in export volume, Morocco achieved a significant increase in earnings from vegetable exports, reaching nearly USD 1.6 b...
records.description: Despite a decline in export volume, Morocco achieved a significant increase in earnings from vegetable exports, reaching nearly USD 1.6 billion in 2023, marking a 12% rise compared to the previous year. Despite facing challenges such as adverse weather conditions leading to a 14% reduction in export tonnage, Morocco exceeded its five-year average by 5%. Greenhouse tomatoes notably drove the country's export revenue, comprising nearly three-quarters of the total fresh vegetable export value. Despite a setback due to soaring summer temperatures, resulting in an 11% decline in greenhouse tomato exports, Morocco maintained its position as the world's third-largest exporter of fresh tomatoes. Sweet peppers also contributed substantially to revenue generation, with both volume and value of exports increasing. Zucchini and pumpkins secured the third position in export revenue, while greenhouse cucumbers witnessed a significant growth of 60% in 2023.

records.title: The Moroccan watermelon season faces a substantial setback this year as production restrictions, particularly in the province of Tata, ha...
records.description: The Moroccan watermelon season faces a substantial setback this year as production restrictions, particularly in the province of Tata, have led to a complete suspension of watermelon cultivation due to severe water stress, resulting in an estimated loss of over 110,000 tonnes from the market. Despite the growth of commercial watermelon cultivation in recent years, ongoing drought conditions and climatic challenges have necessitated restrictive measures by local authorities, aiming to transition farmers to alternative crops. Moulay Ahmed Errahmani, a farmer in Tata, highlights the necessity of adapting to the region's water scarcity issues, leading him and others to switch to crops like spring onions, with promising prospects for yields and potential exportation, reflecting a shift in agricultural focus amidst challenging environmental circumstances.

records.title: In 2023, despite a 14% decline in the tonnage of Moroccan fresh vegetable exports due to adverse weather events, the nation saw a robust...
records.description: In 2023, despite a 14% decline in the tonnage of Moroccan fresh vegetable exports due to adverse weather events, the nation saw a robust increase in export revenue, totaling nearly $1.6 billion, marking a 12% surge from the previous year and nearly 50% higher than the five-year average, as reported by EastFruit. Greenhouse tomatoes remained the primary contributor, accounting for almost three-quarters of the total fresh vegetable export value, despite an 11% decrease in exports caused by extraordinary summer temperatures. Sweet peppers followed, experiencing a 55% increase in monetary value to reach $230 million, while zucchini and pumpkins remained stable, contributing $45 million. Greenhouse cucumbers showed significant growth, contributing $23 million to the economy, with various other vegetables also playing a significant role in the export figures.

records.title: The conclusion of Ramadan has brought a much-needed surge in demand for Egyptian citrus, particularly from Arab nations like Saudi Arabia...
records.description: The conclusion of Ramadan has brought a much-needed surge in demand for Egyptian citrus, particularly from Arab nations like Saudi Arabia and Jordan, along with some European countries. However, the usual Asian demand associated with Ramadan was notably absent this season due to disruptions in shipping lines caused by the Red Sea crisis, resulting in reduced orders from countries like India, Bangladesh, Malaysia, and Indonesia. To adapt to this situation, exporters are exploring new markets, focusing on regions like the CIS countries, Azerbaijan, and Africa. This uptick in demand during Ramadan comes as a relief for Egyptian exporters, who have been grappling with surplus supply and declining prices exacerbated by regional tensions and a domestic currency crisis. Despite stable dollar prices, the devaluation of the Egyptian pound has impacted margins, necessitating price adjustments to offset rising transportation costs and exchange rate discrepancies.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: OCP Group, a global leader in plant nutrition and phosphate-based fertilizers, has teamed up with Fortescue Energy, a division of Fortesc...
records.description: OCP Group, a global leader in plant nutrition and phosphate-based fertilizers, has teamed up with Fortescue Energy, a division of Fortescue Ltd specializing in green energy, metals, and technology, to establish a groundbreaking joint venture in Morocco. This collaboration, founded on equal partnership, is aimed at providing green hydrogen, ammonia, and fertilizers to Morocco, Europe, and global markets while advancing renewable energy technologies. With a shared commitment to reducing emissions and promoting sustainability, the venture outlines ambitious plans for several key projects in Morocco, including large-scale green ammonia and fertilizer production, green technology manufacturing, and an R&D and Technology Hub near Marrakech in partnership with Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) to advance research in renewable energy and minerals processing. The primary objective is to supply green hydrogen and ammonia for clean energy applications and carbon-neutral fertilizer production, making these products accessible and affordable for farmers worldwide. Mostafa Terrab, Chairman and CEO of OCP Group, stressed the commitment to decarbonization and the development of renewable energy products and technology, highlighting the venture's significance in addressing global food security and climate change. Dr. Andrew Forrest AO, Fortescue Executive Chair and Founder, expressed excitement about establishing a globally competitive platform for green energy production and industrial development in Morocco, leveraging the country's abundant wind and solar resources. Mark Hutchinson, CEO of Fortescue Energy, emphasized the alignment of ambitions between OCP and Fortescue, aiming to create one of the world’s leading integrated renewable energy and manufacturing enterprises in Morocco. The joint venture, facilitated by INNOVX, a multi-sectoral venture platform, is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals, marking a significant advancement in sustainable energy production and technology development on a global scale.

records.title: Green Corp has completed the acquisition of Emad Bakeries, a Jeddah-based producer of Arabic bread and pastries, as part of its strategy...
records.description: Green Corp has completed the acquisition of Emad Bakeries, a Jeddah-based producer of Arabic bread and pastries, as part of its strategy to bolster investments and expand its portfolio in the Saudi food processing sector. Established in Bahrain in 2023 by Gulf Islamic Investments (GII), Green Corp serves as a platform for sustainable agricultural, aquaculture, food processing, and production projects across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. The acquisition, supported by a US$150 million fund managed by GII, underscores Green Corp's commitment to creating an integrated food platform across the food value chain to reduce food import dependency and ensure sustainable benefits for consumers. Emad Bakeries, operating the largest industrial fresh flatbread bakery in western Saudi Arabia, brings fast-growing food production capabilities to Green Corp's investment platform. Mohammed Alhassan, co-founder and co-CEO of GII, highlighted Emad Bakeries' heritage and quality commitment, emphasizing its resonance with Saudi customers. Pankaj Gupta, fellow co-founder and co-CEO of GII, stressed the strategic alignment of the acquisition with Green Corp's vision of establishing a comprehensive GCC food investment platform. RidgePoint Advisors served as the sole financial advisor to Emad Bakeries, with legal advisory provided by King & Spalding and AlAmmar Law Firm. Looking ahead, Green Corp aims to make further acquisitions in the Kingdom as it continues to build its asset portfolio and enhance Gulf food security.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's First Milling Company, a prominent milling firm, has unveiled its latest venture, the establishment of "First Food Supplie...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's First Milling Company, a prominent milling firm, has unveiled its latest venture, the establishment of "First Food Supplies Company," a wholly-owned subsidiary aimed at supporting future business expansion and strategic goals. With a capital of SAR 100,000 (approximately US$27,000) and headquartered in Jeddah, the new entity will specialize in various areas including bakery product manufacturing, grain mills products, starches, pasta, and more. Additionally, it will engage in storage, transportation, wholesale and retail of agricultural raw materials and food products. The financial impact of this venture is expected to positively contribute to First Milling Company's results starting in 2025. This move follows the company's recent announcement regarding its intention to conduct an initial public offering (IPO) of 16.65 million shares representing 30% of its share capital on the Saudi Exchange. With a wheat milling capacity of 4,200 tons daily and a feed mixing capacity of 900 tons per day,

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Egypt is intensifying efforts to bolster domestic wheat and corn production by the year 2025/2026, aiming to enhance food security and re...
records.description: Egypt is intensifying efforts to bolster domestic wheat and corn production by the year 2025/2026, aiming to enhance food security and reduce dependence on foreign imports. Revealed by Ali Al-Moselhy, the Minister for Supply and Internal Trade, the government aims to increase wheat production by 53% and corn production by 56% during the specified period, with the goal of substantially reducing dependency on foreign markets. This initiative underscores Egypt’s commitment to strengthening its agricultural self-sufficiency. The government's ambitious plan includes procuring 3.5 million tons of local wheat during the upcoming 2024 season, set to commence in April, according to Minister Al-Moselhy. The upcoming wheat harvest season is anticipated to span several months, during which significant gains in wheat production are expected. Since November 2023, Egypt has allocated three million feddans (acres) to wheat cultivation, marking a substantial increase of nearly half a million acres year-on-year, as announced by the cabinet in January 2024. Egypt’s recent efforts are driven by a surge in wheat imports, which rose by 14.5% to 11 million tons in 2023 compared to the previous year, according to Assistant Supply Minister Ibrahim Ashmawy. As a major wheat importer, Egypt relies on foreign sources for over 50% of its wheat requirements, with annual consumption standing at 18 million tons. To incentivize local farmers to sell their produce to the state, the Egyptian Cabinet increased the local wheat procurement price to EGP 1,600 per ardeb (150kg) for the upcoming harvest season, up from EGP 1,500 previously. These efforts come amid global challenges, including the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, key wheat suppliers to Egypt, leading to a surge in wheat prices worldwide. Despite economic challenges, Egypt has shown resilience in its agricultural sector, with agricultural exports reaching US$ 1.5 billion (EGP 71 billion) in the first quarter of 2024, a significant increase compared to the same period last year, according to Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Al-Sayed Al-Kosayer.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry for Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: In response to the ongoing sugar shortage crisis, the Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, through the General Authority for S...
records.description: In response to the ongoing sugar shortage crisis, the Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, through the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC), has sealed a deal to import 250,000 tons of raw sugar. This decision follows the cabinet's approval to import one million tons of sugar last month, aiming to tackle the severe shortage gripping the nation. The ministry announced that the sugar shipments from the newly signed contract are set to begin arriving next month. This move underscores the government's commitment to bolstering strategic sugar reserves and stabilizing prices in the market. GASC had previously issued an international tender to procure 50,000 tons of raw sugar cane from any origin. The payment terms for the tenders were set to be at sight, with the initial shipment scheduled to arrive between April 15-30 and/or May 1-15. Despite the challenges posed by soaring sugar prices, Minister of Supply and Internal Trade Ali Moselhi assured citizens of the government's efforts to stabilize prices, projecting that they would not exceed EGP 24-27 in the near future. To address concerns and mitigate the crisis, the government has implemented various measures, including increasing the distribution of subsidized sugar, launching initiatives to reduce prices, imposing temporary export bans, and intensifying control measures. Additionally, the prime minister has classified sugar and six other commodities as strategic products under Consumer Protection Law No. 181 of 2018, prohibiting withholding these goods from circulation and mandating immediate notification to the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade regarding stocks of these commodities.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade & General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.domain: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), in collaboration with the European Union (EU), is working on enhancing Egypt's food control...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), in collaboration with the European Union (EU), is working on enhancing Egypt's food control system through the "Strengthening of Capacities and Governance in Food and Phytosanitary Control" project. With an extension granted by the EU, Egypt joins Djibouti as the latest beneficiary of this initiative, aiming to improve public health, economic development, and trade within the region. Initiated in December 2021, the 6.4-million-euro project focuses on enhancing capabilities and governance in food safety and plant health, aligning with the Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Policy Framework for Africa developed by the African Union (AU). Co-signed by the Government of Egypt, the project underscores a collaborative effort to align national standards with international norms and foster regional harmonization. FAO introduces the FAO/WHO Food Control System Assessment Tool to evaluate Egypt’s food control system comprehensively. Dr. Tareq Al-Houby, Chairman of the Egyptian National Food Safety Authority, highlights the project’s significance in achieving a unified and coherent system essential for scientific-based compliance and international standards adherence. The project involves workshops and training sessions engaging focal points of Competent Authorities, fostering discussions, presentations, and case studies to identify food safety priorities and strengthen the overall system. Ms. Hanan Fouad Hamed, Manager of Food Standards and Codex Unit at the Standards and Quality Organization, emphasized how the assessment would aid in monitoring foodborne diseases and enhancing the system’s resilience. The culmination of the assessment will involve stakeholders, experts, and officials convening to review findings, endorse recommendations, and develop a strategic action plan for implementation, aiming to shape the future of food safety in Egypt and promote greater harmonization and trade in the region.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) & The European Union (EU)

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Khazaen Economic City is on the verge of unveiling the Khazaen Central Market for Fruits and Vegetables, scheduled for completion by the...
records.description: Khazaen Economic City is on the verge of unveiling the Khazaen Central Market for Fruits and Vegetables, scheduled for completion by the end of the first half of 2024, with construction already surpassing 98%. CEO Salim bin Sulaiman Al Zahli emphasized the market's pivotal role within Khazaen Economic City, serving as a hub for marketing, distribution, storage, export, and re-export of agricultural produce both domestically and internationally. With over OMR50 million in private sector investments, the project aims to become a national platform for Oman's agricultural products, spanning an expansive 500 sq. meters, five times larger than its predecessor. Al Zahli highlighted the market's potential to foster SME growth and revolutionize the agricultural marketing landscape, aiming to reduce current produce waste levels significantly.

records.title: Diaa Rashwan, Head of Egypt's State Information Service (SIS), announced a significant increase in humanitarian aid trucks entering the G...
records.description: Diaa Rashwan, Head of Egypt's State Information Service (SIS), announced a significant increase in humanitarian aid trucks entering the Gaza Strip through the Rafah border crossing, now totaling 300 trucks daily as of Sunday. This action is in line with President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi's directives amid the unprecedented humanitarian crisis in Gaza. Rashwan emphasized Egypt's substantial aid efforts, including dispatching 322 aid trucks to northern Gaza since Ramadan's start and facilitating the entry of over 19,000 tons of essential supplies since the onset of Israel’s war on Gaza. Egypt has also provided medical assistance, evacuated foreign nationals and Egyptians, and established a logistics hub at Rafah to coordinate aid efforts.

records.title: The National Council of Wages declared a significant raise in the minimum wage for private sector employees, elevating it to EGP 6,000 st...
records.description: The National Council of Wages declared a significant raise in the minimum wage for private sector employees, elevating it to EGP 6,000 starting in May, marking the fifth increase in two years. Minister of Planning and Economic Development Hala El-Said underscored the government's commitment to safeguarding workers' rights amid evolving economic conditions, aiming to ensure a decent standard of living for all. The decision, which encompasses all wage components including employer contributions to insurance, exempts workplaces with fewer than 10 employees. Minister of Labour Hassan Shafie emphasized the importance of fostering a conducive work environment to enhance productivity, with labour directorates tasked with overseeing the implementation of the new wage policy.

records.title: In an endeavor to bolster local agriculture and diminish reliance on imports, Tunisia's Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fis...
records.description: In an endeavor to bolster local agriculture and diminish reliance on imports, Tunisia's Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries has sanctioned the irrigation of cereal crops in multiple regions of the country. Ridha Gabouj, the Secretary of State for Water Resources, disclosed this decision and emphasized the necessity for collaboration among farmers, civil society, and authorities to address the ongoing issue of unregulated well drilling. Responding to farmers' concerns regarding damage from insufficient irrigation and quota enforcement, Gabouj underscored the significance of boosting local grain production to curtail costly foreign imports. He announced that regional agricultural services in Jendouba, Béja, and Bizerte have been authorized to commence cereal crop irrigation to assist local farmers. Nevertheless, Gabouj highlighted the challenges faced by Tunisia's agricultural sector, citing the previous season's dismal cereal production and the consequent need to import a substantial quantity to meet domestic demand. This dependency on imports incurs significant financial strain on the state budget. Another pressing issue is the proliferation of unregulated well drilling, particularly evident in the governorate of Kébili, where numerous wells are deemed unlawful. This phenomenon exacerbates strain on the water table, exacerbating Tunisia's already limited water resources. To address this, the Ministry of Agriculture is collaborating with other ministries, notably the Ministry of the Interior, to identify violators and enforce stricter measures.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries
