records.title: Canon Central and North Africa has partnered with KidZania Cairo to introduce a Canon Photography Studio, aimed at providing children age...
records.description: Canon Central and North Africa has partnered with KidZania Cairo to introduce a Canon Photography Studio, aimed at providing children aged 8-14 with an immersive learning experience in creativity and technology. Amine Djouahra, B2C business unit director at Canon Central and North Africa, emphasized the significance of this collaboration, marking Canon's commitment to empowering local talent in Africa and its first venture of its kind in the region. The partnership with KidZania Cairo, known for its interactive role-playing activities, offers children an opportunity to delve into the world of photography in a playful yet educational environment, fostering exploration and potential career interests. Djouahra highlighted Canon's broader ambition to enhance daily lives through digital technologies, particularly in Egypt, given its dynamic profile and strategic partnership with KidZania Cairo. He underscored Canon's corporate philosophy of Kyosei, emphasizing initiatives like the Young People Programme and Miraisha, which aim to equip young individuals with skills and empower local communities. Egypt's strategic importance for Canon, both geographically and economically, was also emphasized, with Djouahra expressing confidence in leveraging Egypt's vibrant media landscape and reinforcing Canon's vision as a preferred imaging brand while nurturing the next generation through initiatives like the collaboration with KidZania Cairo.
records.institution: Canon Central and North Africa & KidZania

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt's Minister of International Cooperation, Dr.
records.description: Egypt's Minister of International Cooperation, Dr. Rania A. Al-Mashat, convened with Dr. Patrick Jean Guillabert, UNIDO's Regional Director in Egypt, to explore avenues for bolstering cooperation on green projects and the National Water, Food, and Energy (NWFE) nexus program, aligning with the Egypt - United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2023-2027. Held at the ministry's headquarters in the New Administrative Capital, the meeting underscored the significance of collaboration in Egypt's pursuit of comprehensive and sustainable industrial development, particularly through the Country Partnership Program (PCP) 2021-2025. Discussions delved into UNIDO's pivotal role in advancing the NWFE program, focusing on priority projects under the National Climate Change Strategy 2050 and leveraging expertise in green hydrogen. Dr. Al-Mashat commended previous cooperation with UNIDO, citing initiatives like the ClimaTechRun competition and UNIDO's engagement in the Private Sector Engagement Portal. Dr. Guillabert, in turn, acknowledged Egypt's national efforts and UNIDO's commitment to supporting sustainable industry solutions, with the ongoing portfolio in Egypt emphasizing projects worth $52 million aimed at promoting green growth and enhancing energy efficiency across sectors.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of International Cooperation & UNIDO

records.title: The Egyptian government, led by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, has announced the completion of the development of the "Price Radar" mob...
records.description: The Egyptian government, led by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, has announced the completion of the development of the "Price Radar" mobile application, slated for launch in July. This app aims to combat price monopolies and provide consumers with transparent information on prices and goods. Users can specify their location, store, and the price of items, along with attaching pictures and sharing prices in the area. The announcement coincided with Madbouly's chairing of a meeting to oversee the Supreme Committee for Regulating Markets and Commodity Prices. Additionally, another app is in development to facilitate complaints and provide consumer protection services, offering advice and warnings on defective products. Assistant Prime Minister Osama al-Gohary outlined proposed actions, including data provision on food production and distribution companies, electronic tracking of strategic goods, and expanding monitoring of wholesale markets.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries in Tunisia has given regional directorates the green light to commence irriga...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries in Tunisia has given regional directorates the green light to commence irrigating grain crops, announced Secretary of State for Water Resources Ridha Gabouj. In an interview with TAP, Gabouj emphasized the importance of addressing the issue of illegal well drilling, stressing the need for collaboration between farmers, civil society, and authorities. Responding to farmers' concerns regarding irrigation shortages and the failure of quota system implementation, Gabouj highlighted the government's reliance on local grain production to reduce the need for imports, which strain foreign currency reserves. He noted that the previous season saw a "catastrophic" grain output of 5 million quintals, leading to the importation of nearly 25 million quintals at a cost of TND 3 billion. Gabouj underscored the financial and logistical support provided by the ministry to farmers while expressing concern over the widespread issue of illegal drilling, which has adversely affected Tunisia's groundwater table. He revealed that out of approximately 42,000 wells in the country, 30,000 are illegal, with a significant concentration in Kébili. This unauthorized drilling has exacerbated groundwater depletion, posing a serious threat to Tunisia's limited water resources. Gabouj urged licensed well owners to address this issue promptly. With annual water demand exceeding 3.8 billion m3, and 75% of water resources supplied by wells tapping into groundwater, Gabouj emphasized the critical need for sustainable water management practices to safeguard Tunisia's water security.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) has reported that Tunisia is poised to achieve above-average wheat...
records.description: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) has reported that Tunisia is poised to achieve above-average wheat and barley yields for the 2024-25 season, buoyed by favorable winter rainfall and moderate temperatures following a challenging planting period. The latest Global Agricultural Information Network (GAIN) report forecasts wheat production in Tunisia to reach an impressive 1.25 million tonnes, a substantial increase from the previous season and aligned with estimates from previous years. The final wheat yields are contingent on April rainfall, which could further bolster yields by 10% to 20% if conditions remain favorable. Despite the rise in production, domestic wheat consumption is expected to only slightly increase, supported by government subsidies ensuring affordable access to wheat products for Tunisia's population. The FAS underscores the strain wheat subsidies place on the state budget. In response to domestic demand, wheat imports for 2024-25 are forecasted at 1.8 million tonnes. Additionally, barley production is experiencing a remarkable rebound, projected to reach 660,000 tonnes for the upcoming season, driven by wheat seed shortages and dry weather during planting. Barley imports are anticipated to decrease significantly due to the notable increase in domestic production.
records.institution: The US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS)

records.title: Amid supply chain disruptions, Egyptian citrus exporters faced challenges during the season, but Ramadan demand provided a crucial boost,...
records.description: Amid supply chain disruptions, Egyptian citrus exporters faced challenges during the season, but Ramadan demand provided a crucial boost, especially for Citrus Agro, according to CEO Mahmod Allam. Allam highlights the significance of the Ramadan period, typically the busiest for the Valencia variety, with exports reaching 4,000-5,000 tonnes. Despite regional challenges, preparations were intensified for this phase, focusing on accessible Arab and African markets, leading to successful outcomes comparable to the previous year. However, Allam acknowledges persistent challenges in other markets, particularly exacerbated by the Red Sea crisis. Transit times exceeding 50 days to certain African markets have led to customer reluctance. Efforts to sustain deliveries to Asian markets, amidst increased transport costs and currency fluctuations, have been met with mixed responses, with markets like India rejecting prices. Consequently, loading usual quantities has been hindered in many markets. Allam underscores the varying impacts across exporters, citing Citrus Agro's fortune in maintaining its main market in Russia, facilitated by direct vessel shipments with shorter transit times and minimal obstacles.

records.title: Egypt's agricultural sector is experiencing a notable upturn, with first-quarter exports surpassing USD 1.5 billion in 2024, reflecting a...
records.description: Egypt's agricultural sector is experiencing a notable upturn, with first-quarter exports surpassing USD 1.5 billion in 2024, reflecting a substantial increase of USD 300 million compared to the previous year. Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, El-Sayed El-Quseir, disclosed these encouraging figures, attributing the growth to concerted efforts over the past decade, including market diversification and the opening of 95 new markets. Egypt's agricultural exports, totaling over 2.218 million tons during Q1 2024, showcased a remarkable surge, with citrus fruits, potatoes, sweet potatoes, pomegranates, garlic, and strawberries among the leading exports. Oranges emerged as the top commodity both in volume and value, reflecting the country's intensified cultivation efforts and expanded market reach, particularly in Southeast Asia. With projections indicating a 25% increase in fresh orange exports for the marketing year 2023/24, Egypt's agricultural sector is poised for further growth, fueled by improved yields, favorable environmental conditions, and effective market expansion initiatives.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture in Mauritania has announced the successful completion of the first large-scale wheat cultivation experiment c...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in Mauritania has announced the successful completion of the first large-scale wheat cultivation experiment covering an area of ​​200 hectares. This initiative, conducted through a public-private partnership involving the National Society for Rural Development (SONADER), the Timar group specializing in logistics and warehousing, and the Biladi Company for Agricultural and Animal Production, focused on two wheat varieties, yielding between 4 and 5 tonnes per hectare. Isselmou Ould Sid El Mokhtar, the regional delegate of the Ministry of Agriculture, sees this achievement as a promising step toward establishing a local wheat sector, emphasizing the favorable environmental conditions and the crop's resilience to diseases over multiple cultivation cycles. This success not only holds potential for enhancing domestic food production but also for reducing reliance on wheat imports, which currently account for the majority of Mauritania's wheat needs. In recent years, the country has faced significant challenges due to its high grain import dependency, particularly highlighted by vulnerabilities exposed by external supply shocks such as the conflict in Ukraine. Despite these challenges, Mauritania's progress in wheat cultivation underscores efforts within the region to develop local agricultural sectors and reduce import reliance, even in the face of unfavorable biophysical conditions.

records.title: Invictus Investment Company, a major agro-food enterprise operating across the Middle East, Africa, and Asia, has acquired a 60% stake in...
records.description: Invictus Investment Company, a major agro-food enterprise operating across the Middle East, Africa, and Asia, has acquired a 60% stake in Graderco and its subsidiaries, a leading grain and cereal trading firm based in Morocco, from Zalar Holding. The acquisition, following regulatory approvals, marks Invictus Investment's strategic expansion in key African markets, particularly Morocco. Graderco, headquartered in Morocco, holds a significant market share with revenues exceeding AED 1.5 billion (US$410 million) in 2023. It imports, stores, and trades between 2.5 and 3.0 million metric tonnes of grain and derivatives annually, representing over 25% of the country’s imports. With Invictus Investment reporting revenues of AED 8.1 billion (US$2.2B) and 5.37 million metric tonnes in commodity transactions for 2023, the acquisition is expected to generate substantial synergies. The strategic partnership aims to achieve around 20% growth in consolidated revenues for Invictus Investment over the nine-month post-acquisition period in 2024. This move aligns with Invictus Investment’s long-term strategy to expand its presence in key African markets, forge new partnerships, and enhance operational capabilities. Amir Daoud Abdellatif, CEO of Invictus Investment, emphasized Morocco's strategic importance, highlighting the acquisition as a significant step toward becoming a fully integrated agro-food enterprise. He cited Graderco’s product diversity, strong sourcing network, and robust distribution capabilities as factors driving synergies with Invictus's global operations. Driss Chaouni, CEO of Zalar Holding, welcomed Invictus Investment as a partner, expressing confidence that their experience and global relationships would accelerate Graderco’s growth. He highlighted the transaction's potential to leverage Graderco's established position in grain importation across Morocco. In 2023, Invictus Investment expanded into new markets and increased commodity transaction volumes in existing markets.

records.title: Sudan has received a shipment of 14,600 tonnes of wheat flour from Ukraine as part of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky’s Grain from...
records.description: Sudan has received a shipment of 14,600 tonnes of wheat flour from Ukraine as part of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky’s Grain from Ukraine initiative, supported by the World Food Organization. This delivery, the second under the initiative, is intended to aid 2 million people affected by the war in Sudan. The first batch, totaling 7,600 tonnes, arrived in Khartoum on February 22, 2024. Germany and several other countries financed this second shipment, contributing a total of USD 23.8 million to cover transportation expenses and distribution within Sudan. The World Food Programme (WFP) reported that the first batch was sufficient to sustain a million people for a month. With this donation, the WFP aims to provide food packages to 2 million people in Sudan affected by the war. Given the escalating conflict and rising food insecurity in Sudan, this timely assistance is crucial, particularly as the lean season approaches in May, exacerbating food scarcity and hunger. The WFP emphasizes the importance of this aid in addressing Sudan’s hunger crisis, especially as staple crop harvests have fallen significantly below average, further straining food availability.

records.title: Morocco's avocado production and export sector continues to soar, with the 2023/24 season poised to set another record for avocado exports.
records.description: Morocco's avocado production and export sector continues to soar, with the 2023/24 season poised to set another record for avocado exports. Between July 2023 and January 2024 alone, Morocco exported nearly 40,000 tons of avocados, valued at $120 million, marking a new milestone for the period. With four more months left in the season and preliminary data suggesting exports could surpass 60,000 tons for the entire season, the outlook remains promising. A 20% increase in avocado harvest in 2023, driven by favorable weather and expanded cultivation areas, has fueled this growth. However, challenges such as droughts, water scarcity, and discontinued government subsidies for irrigation may impact future exports. Currently, Moroccan avocado exports are concentrated in a few EU countries, with efforts to diversify markets progressing slowly. Despite this, recent developments, like the introduction of Moroccan avocados to new markets like Georgia, signify potential for expansion beyond traditional destinations.

records.title: Qatari food company Baldana is on the verge of finalizing an agreement with the Algerian government to establish a vast farm dedicated to...
records.description: Qatari food company Baldana is on the verge of finalizing an agreement with the Algerian government to establish a vast farm dedicated to milk production, as part of Algeria's efforts to achieve self-sufficiency in this sector. Baldana, well-known in Qatar for its milk and dairy products, plans to inaugurate a sprawling farm covering 100,000 hectares. Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune confirmed the upcoming agreement, specifying that the farm will be located in Adrar, southwestern Algeria.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) in Saudi Arabia has embarked on a significant initiative aimed at agricultural...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) in Saudi Arabia has embarked on a significant initiative aimed at agricultural innovation and sustainability by localizing the production of banana seedlings, with a particular focus on the Jazan region. Leveraging advanced tissue culture and propagation techniques, MEWA's center for plant tissue culture and biotechnology has successfully cultivated various banana varieties tailored to the Kingdom's climate. These high-quality, disease-free seedlings, cultivated both in greenhouses and open fields, represent a notable advancement in the agricultural sector, enhancing sustainability and productivity. The localization of seedling production is anticipated to attract investment in tissue culture technology, with a focus on intensifying the production of nutritionally rich varieties to yield higher economic returns. Importantly, local production of seedlings is projected to significantly reduce economic losses, estimated at around 25% incurred from importing seedlings. MEWA's initiatives, aligned with the Saudi Green Initiative, include plans to plant 45 million fruit trees on agricultural terraces and four million lemon trees using renewable water by 2030..
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: Algeria has demonstrated solidarity with Gaza by dispatching 168 tons of humanitarian aid through Egypt.
records.description: Algeria has demonstrated solidarity with Gaza by dispatching 168 tons of humanitarian aid through Egypt. The Algerian Ministry of National Defense announced the delivery via two Air Force aircraft, containing essential supplies such as tents, food items, medical equipment, and medicines. The aid is destined for El-Arish International Airport in Egypt, from where it will be transferred to Gaza through the Rafah crossing.

records.title: The commencement of the potato harvest campaign for the 2023-2024 agricultural year in Mostaganem marks a pivotal moment for local farmer...
records.description: The commencement of the potato harvest campaign for the 2023-2024 agricultural year in Mostaganem marks a pivotal moment for local farmers, officially inaugurated under the guidance of Wali Ahmed Boudouh and in the presence of regional authorities. With promising prospects, farmers aim to yield approximately 56,000 quintals of potatoes across 196 hectares of cultivated land. Notably, areas such as Hassi Mameche, Aïn Nouissy, Bouguirat, Sirat, and Touahria serve as primary potato cultivation sites, boasting an average yield of 300 quintals per hectare. Emphasizing the utilization of local seeds underscores the commitment to leveraging regional resources for development. Forecasts suggest a robust total potato production of 4,312,000 quintals in Mostaganem, including a significant portion reserved for seed cultivation, further solidifying the region's status as a national leader in this agricultural sector. Additionally, measures have been implemented to stabilize market prices, ensuring the availability and affordability of potatoes, particularly during the holy month of Ramadan. With the current price estimated at 60 DA/kg, authorities anticipate a decline due to increased local market supplies.

records.title: The construction progress of five new seawater desalination stations across five coastal wilayas in Algeria has exceeded 50%, according t...
records.description: The construction progress of five new seawater desalination stations across five coastal wilayas in Algeria has exceeded 50%, according to Mohamed Boutabba, President and CEO of the Algerian Energy Company (AEC), during a recent intervention on Algerian Radio Channel 1. These stations, each with a production capacity of 300,000 m3/day, are scheduled to become operational by December 2024 and will be situated in the wilayas of Oran, Tipasa, Boumerdes, Béjaia, and El Tarf. Leading the progress is the Fouka station in Tipasa, reaching a rate of 60%, while others range between 52% and 54%. This ambitious initiative aims to significantly enhance Algeria's seawater desalination capacity, elevating it from 18% to 42% and thereby crucially impacting the country's drinking water availability. Beyond these five stations, plans are underway to create six additional stations, aiming to further increase the desalination rate to 60%. Additionally, a project involving mobile desalination stations, with a production capacity ranging from 2,500 to 2,700 m3/day, is also under consideration. Boutabba stressed the strategic significance of seawater desalination in addressing water stress, highlighting the AEC's prioritization of national companies to ensure local equipment, achieving a national integration rate of 30% to 40%. Recognizing the sector's promising potential, he called for streamlined access for businesses and investors to stimulate further development, alongside advocating for enhanced training in seawater desalination through the introduction of advanced scientific standards and modules in collaboration with ministries of Higher Education and Vocational Training.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Algeria has announced the commencement of the General Agricultural Census (RGA), sch...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Algeria has announced the commencement of the General Agricultural Census (RGA), scheduled to start on May 19 and conclude on July 17, 2024. This ambitious initiative aims to gather precise data on the country's agricultural sector. The decision on the start date was made during the 5th meeting of the National Commission for the General Census of Agriculture, presided over by Minister Youcef Cherfa. Highlighting the strategic significance of this endeavor, Minister Cherfa emphasized the importance of accurate scientific data for informed decision-making, echoing President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's directives during the Council of Ministers in March 2024. The commission validated the final questionnaire model during the meeting and presented a dedicated application for data collection, showcasing a commitment to leveraging modern technologies for efficiency and accuracy.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: Al-Azhar's Zakat and Charity House has launched its sixth relief convoy to provide support to the people of Gaza as part of its "Aid Gaza...
records.description: Al-Azhar's Zakat and Charity House has launched its sixth relief convoy to provide support to the people of Gaza as part of its "Aid Gaza" international campaign. Under the patronage of the Grand Imam of Al-Azhar, Sheikh Ahmed El-Tayyeb, this convoy marks the continuation of efforts to alleviate the suffering in Gaza. Comprising 100 trucks laden with 2,000 tons of essential supplies including food, water, medical supplies, blankets, and mattresses, this convoy aims to address the urgent humanitarian needs of the affected population. Since the commencement of the conflict, the Egyptian Zakat and Charity House has dispatched a total of 325 trucks carrying around 6,000 tons of aid to Gaza. The convoy will deliver the aid through the Rafah border crossing.

records.title: The Egyptian government's six-month ban on onion exports has concluded, marking the beginning of April with the resumption of export acti...
records.description: The Egyptian government's six-month ban on onion exports has concluded, marking the beginning of April with the resumption of export activities. Mohamad Hassan, Export Sales Manager at Al Gamal, confirms that this year's onion production surpasses local demand, prompting the availability of surplus onions for international markets. The ban's expiration, initially scheduled until the end of 2023 and later extended until March, signifies a significant milestone for Egyptian onion exporters. With production reaching 3 million tonnes this season, an increase of 1 million tonnes from the previous year, Egypt is well-positioned to meet both domestic needs and export demands. The stabilization of onion prices in the local market further underscores the adequacy of supply. Hassan anticipates strong demand for Egyptian onions globally, emphasizing their quality and durability. European buyers have already shown readiness to resume imports from Egypt, signaling a promising season ahead, expected to extend until September.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry

records.title: The Tahya Misr Fund has launched its fourth relief convoy destined for Gaza, reflecting its commitment to humanitarian solidarity in alig...
records.description: The Tahya Misr Fund has launched its fourth relief convoy destined for Gaza, reflecting its commitment to humanitarian solidarity in alignment with President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi's directives. Named "We Share for Humanity," the initiative aims to address the increasingly challenging conditions faced by Palestinians ahead of Eid Al-Fitr. Tamer Abdel-Fattah, the executive director of the Tahya Misr Fund, revealed that the convoy comprises 94 trucks laden with over 1,504 tons of aid, including vital medical supplies and equipment essential for providing healthcare to the injured, such as medications and wheelchairs. Given Gaza's restrictive blockade and severe shortages in medical resources, particularly for individuals with disabilities, this assistance is critically needed. Additionally, the convoy contains substantial quantities of basic food items, hygiene products, blankets, and tents, aimed at alleviating various needs and mitigating the severity of the crisis, especially during the winter season.

records.title: The Chinese government has sent a substantial aid shipment of 450 tons of rice to the Gaza Strip via the Port Said port in Egypt.
records.description: The Chinese government has sent a substantial aid shipment of 450 tons of rice to the Gaza Strip via the Port Said port in Egypt. This humanitarian gesture, announced by the Chinese Embassy in Cairo, underscores China's commitment to supporting the Palestinian people during times of need. The aid, coordinated with the Egyptian Red Crescent Society, aims to alleviate the suffering of those affected by the conflict in Gaza. Additionally, another 450 tons of flour are expected to arrive in Port Said later in April. Chinese Ambassador Liao Liqiang expressed gratitude for Egypt's efforts to address the situation in Gaza and facilitate the delivery of aid.

records.title: Ridat, a thermoforming equipment manufacturer based in the UK, has secured its first project in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) by partner...
records.description: Ridat, a thermoforming equipment manufacturer based in the UK, has secured its first project in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) by partnering with major dates and confectionery specialist, Al Wathba Dates & Sweets, to support a new packaging facility. Located in Abu Dhabi, Al Wathba Dates & Sweets specializes in fresh dates, date syrup, and confectionery products. Ridat will supply technology and expertise for the new plant, which includes a Model 2420AFCS-P Automatic Thermoforming, Cut & Stack machine designed for high-speed production and precise forming. This machine utilizes air pressure for improved forming definition and features water-cooled molds to prevent overheating, offering a comprehensive packaging solution for Al Wathba Dates & Sweets.

records.title: Yemen Launches a Pandemic Fund Project to Protect the Most Vulnerable Communities From Epidemic Disease Threats
records.description: Yemen has initiated the Pandemic Preparedness and Response Project (PPRP) to safeguard its vulnerable population from epidemic disease threats. Launched in Aden, Yemen, the project aims to enhance the country's ability to prevent, detect, and respond to endemic and pandemic threats over a three-year period. Through a collaboration of stakeholders including the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, FAO, and the World Bank, the project targets four key objectives: strengthening disease prevention, enhancing laboratory capacities, building multisectoral workforce capabilities, and improving coordination among One Health stakeholders. With a US$26 million grant from the Pandemic Fund and complementary actions from other World Bank grants, PPRP builds upon previous successful investments in outbreak preparedness and response.
records.institution: Yemeni Ministry of Public Health and Population, Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Fisheries, & Pandemic Fund Secretariat

records.title: The Egyptian government has disclosed the latest statistics regarding the 'Forsa' initiative, which aims to facilitate employment opportu...
records.description: The Egyptian government has disclosed the latest statistics regarding the 'Forsa' initiative, which aims to facilitate employment opportunities for beneficiaries of the Takaful w Karama monetary subsidies program. The initiative targets the creation of 800 job opportunities at a cost of $400,000 in the governorates of Sharqia and Asyut by June, contributing to a total of 9,500 employment opportunities. Notably, 1,500 individuals secured jobs through four employment fairs, while others ventured into self-employment ventures supported by microfinancing initiatives in various sectors such as agriculture, animal production, textiles, furniture, and metal forging. Funded by a grant from the Norwegian government and implemented in collaboration with the International Labor Organization (ILO), the 'Forsa' program has also focused on capacity-building efforts, benefiting 56 NGOs, 19 microfinancing associations, and 105 instructors involved in training program beneficiaries. Meanwhile, the Takaful w Karama program will continue disbursing monetary subsidies for 6-12 months after beneficiaries commence employment to ensure their stability in their new roles. Minister of Social Solidarity Nevine al-Qabaj revealed that the Takaful w Karama program currently serves 4.7 million families with a budget of LE41 billion for the year 2024.

records.domain: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
records.title: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MoCCAE) has issued a decree banning the fishing of Golden trevally and Painted sweetlips...
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MoCCAE) has issued a decree banning the fishing of Golden trevally and Painted sweetlips during their breeding season from April 1 to April 30, a measure set to last until 2026. This ruling, outlined in decree no. 24, aims to safeguard fish stocks' sustainability in UAE waters and bolster the nation's food security. Additionally, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Endangered Safety Authority has launched a two-day awareness campaign targeting various stakeholders involved in the regulation of fish hunting and marketing, emphasizing the importance of responsible fishing practices.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MoCCAE)

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Finance, Mohamed Maait, has announced the allocation of LE 120 billion in soft financing for agricultural and industr...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Finance, Mohamed Maait, has announced the allocation of LE 120 billion in soft financing for agricultural and industrial production activities during a meeting with representatives from various sectors. This financing initiative, aimed at reducing production costs, promoting exports, and sustaining economic growth, will have an interest rate capped at 15 percent. The funds will be divided into two categories: LE 105 billion for working capital and LE 15 billion for acquiring machinery, equipment, or production lines. Additionally, the state's public treasury will annually cover an interest rate difference of approximately LE 8 billion for beneficiaries. Moreover, Minister Maait revealed that the interest rate of 11 percent will remain unchanged for both current financing and balances used for working capital purposes. Notably, the maximum financing limit for a single company will be raised to LE 100 million, and for multilateral entities, it will increase to LE 130 million. This financing is directed towards new and renewable energy ventures, free zone factories, and agricultural cooperative societies, with a strict prohibition on using these credit facilities to settle outstanding debts owed to the banking sector.

records.title: Minister of Social Solidarity Nevine El-Qabbaj has announced the launch of special bank accounts by the Arab Fund for Social Work to faci...
records.description: Minister of Social Solidarity Nevine El-Qabbaj has announced the launch of special bank accounts by the Arab Fund for Social Work to facilitate public donations for aid and relief to Palestinians in the Gaza Strip. The announcement, made in her capacity as chairperson of the Arab Council of Ministers of Social Affairs overseeing the fund, aims to provide a streamlined avenue for those wishing to contribute to the humanitarian efforts in Gaza. The newly opened accounts are designated for donations in US dollars, Egyptian pounds, and euros, with the respective account numbers provided for each currency. This initiative reflects a concerted effort to support those in need and alleviate the challenges faced by communities in Gaza.

records.title: Jordan Ramps up National Campaign to Halve Food Waste by 2030
records.description: Jordan is intensifying its efforts to combat food waste with the launch of the "No to Food Waste" initiative, announced by Agricultural Minister Khaled Hneifat on the occasion of the International Day of Zero Waste. With annual food waste in Jordan reaching 1.136 million tons, equivalent to 101 kg per capita, urgent action is needed to conserve natural resources and address water scarcity. The initiative, aligned with the National Food Security Strategy 2021-2030, aims to change public behavior leading to food wastage through innovative solutions and enhanced public awareness. Supported by entrepreneurial and research tracks, the campaign seeks to establish a national waste index and foster a culture of responsible consumption across various sectors.

records.title: The World Bank has allocated over $32 million to Jordan in 2024 for two projects aimed at bolstering the energy and agricultural sectors,...
records.description: The World Bank has allocated over $32 million to Jordan in 2024 for two projects aimed at bolstering the energy and agricultural sectors, as reported by Al-Mamlaka TV. Under the Electricity Sector Efficiency and Supply Reliability Enhancement Program, $85.1 million has been disbursed to date, with a total of $250 million allocated to enhance the efficiency of Jordan's electricity sector and integrate renewable energy sources into the power grid. The Agriculture Sector Resilience and Value Chain Development Program (ARDI), funded with $95.6 million, has seen disbursements of $34.1 million to date, aiming to support around 30,000 farming families and create 12,000 job opportunities, particularly for women and youth. This initiative focuses on implementing climate-smart agricultural practices and promoting innovative social enterprise models to enhance agricultural productivity in marginalized areas while conserving water resources.

records.title: The National Food Loss and Waste Initiative, ne'ma, has launched the Food Rescue Programme as part of its Count Your ne’ma campaign durin...
records.description: The National Food Loss and Waste Initiative, ne'ma, has launched the Food Rescue Programme as part of its Count Your ne’ma campaign during Ramadan, aiming to reduce food waste and redistribute surplus meals. This initiative aligns with the UAE’s goal of halving food waste by 2030. With the participation of 300 volunteers, including prominent figures like Mariam Almheiri, ne’ma has successfully rescued and distributed over 156,000kg of surplus local produce, benefiting thousands of families. The initiative emphasizes the UAE’s commitment to sustainability and encourages collaborative efforts across the private and public sectors to achieve significant reductions in food waste, reflecting the nation's values and traditions.
records.institution: UAE National Food Loss and Waste Initiative

records.title: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) has unveiled a groundbreaking initiative aimed at supporting data-driven agricultur...
records.description: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) has unveiled a groundbreaking initiative aimed at supporting data-driven agriculture in Libya. In collaboration with partners such as the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the Ministry of Water Resources, and others, AICS has launched a geospatial platform called MIRWAT-Libya. This platform will serve as a vital tool for informed decision-making in agricultural development by providing advanced information and data. It aims to support sustainable land and water management in Libya by offering geospatial information for water resource management and facilitating access to extensive spatial data. Funded by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation with a grant of 830,000 euros, this innovative program underscores the growing importance of geospatial technology in modern agriculture. The MIRWAT-Libya platform integrates datasets on various aspects of agriculture, including crop types, hydrological basins, and soil classification, empowering stakeholders to make well-informed decisions for sustainable water and crop production while considering available natural resources.
records.institution: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS)

records.title: Feerum Egypt, a prominent player in the grain storage industry, is investing US$33 million in establishing a cutting-edge factory dedicat...
records.description: Feerum Egypt, a prominent player in the grain storage industry, is investing US$33 million in establishing a cutting-edge factory dedicated to grain storage silos in Egypt's East Port Said region. This move, backed by an investment of EGP 1.6 billion, aims to bolster Egypt's grain storage capabilities and enhance food security. The agreement, recently signed between East Port Said Development and Feerum Egypt, underscores the government's support for strategic industries within the Suez Canal Economic Zone, with Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly attending the signing ceremony. With a planned area of 51,950 square meters, the factory aligns with President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi's vision to localize key industries within the SCZone. Feerum Egypt aims to source 80% of the final product locally within three to five years, supporting the Egyptian economy and fostering domestic production. The investment positions Feerum Egypt as a leader in the grain storage sector, highlighting Egypt's growing significance as a regional hub for agricultural infrastructure development.

records.title: The Oman Investment Authority’s newly launched Future Fund Oman has earmarked $4.7 billion for investment in large-scale projects within...
records.description: The Oman Investment Authority’s newly launched Future Fund Oman has earmarked $4.7 billion for investment in large-scale projects within the country over the next five years. The fund, with a total capital of $5.2 billion, will primarily focus on investing directly in economically viable projects, allocating 90% of its capital for this purpose. Additionally, 7% of the fund will be allocated to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), while 3% will be invested in startups. These investments, amounting to approximately $1 billion annually, will target eight key sectors, including tourism, manufacturing, green energy, fisheries, agriculture, ports and logistics, mining, and information and communication technologies.

records.title: The Imperial College London Diabetes Centre (ICLDC), part of the M42 group, is launching a specialized facility in Madinat Zayed to provi...
records.description: The Imperial College London Diabetes Centre (ICLDC), part of the M42 group, is launching a specialized facility in Madinat Zayed to provide comprehensive care for diabetes and endocrine patients, reducing travel time by over 75% for the Abu Dhabi population, catering to over 6,000 diabetes sufferers in the Al Dhafra region. This expansion aims to extend accessibility to diabetes care across Al Dhafra, including residents in Liwa, Mirfa, Gayathi, Ruwais, and Tarif. Alongside clinical care, ICLDC emphasizes preventive solutions through community outreach programs, promoting active lifestyles and healthy eating habits. Hasan Jasem Al Nowais, Managing Director of M42, highlights the commitment to delivering world-class health solutions, while Dr. Mai Al Jaber, CEO of ICLDC, stresses the urgent need for accessible and comprehensive diabetes care. Over the past two decades, ICLDC's efforts have led to a significant decrease in HbA1c levels among patients, demonstrating expertise and commitment across facilities. The new Al Dhafra center will offer the latest diagnostic and management facilities, supported by a multi-specialty team, providing specialized care for diabetes and endocrine-related complications, and complementing existing clinics within the UAE.
records.institution: The Imperial College London Diabetes Centre (ICLDC)

records.title: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly met with Ali Al-Ghamrawy, Head of the Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA), to discuss the authority's pursuit o...
records.description: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly met with Ali Al-Ghamrawy, Head of the Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA), to discuss the authority's pursuit of accreditation from the World Health Organization (WHO) in the field of medicines, emphasizing the government's commitment to health and medicine. Madbouly highlighted support for modernizing EDA's operations, echoing President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi's directives to prioritize citizen well-being and localize the pharmaceutical industry. Al-Ghamrawy outlined EDA's initiatives for WHO accreditation, citing potential benefits such as solidifying Egypt's leadership role regionally and globally, shaping international pharmaceutical policies, and attracting foreign investors. WHO accreditation would signify adherence to international standards, expedite product registration in export markets, and boost confidence in Egypt's regulatory system, ultimately leading to increased export volumes.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's wheat production is set to increase by 25% in the upcoming 2024-25 season, reaching 1.5 million tonnes, in line with its e...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's wheat production is set to increase by 25% in the upcoming 2024-25 season, reaching 1.5 million tonnes, in line with its efforts to boost agricultural self-sufficiency amid rising domestic demand. The Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) of the US Department of Agriculture notes that this surge aligns with the maximum allowed production quota, which may be adjusted by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA) based on various factors. Competitive wheat prices have incentivized farmers to cultivate wheat over alfalfa hay, with domestic consumption projected to rise by 5% to reach 4.75 million tonnes, driven by factors such as tourism growth and infrastructure development projects. Despite advancements in domestic agriculture, Saudi Arabia remains dependent on rice imports to meet consumption demands, with imports expected to increase by 4% in 2024-25, fueled by expansions in the food service sector and rising demand for rice and poultry.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA)

records.title: Authorities in Tunisia have announced the successful recovery of 56 hectares of state agricultural land in Béni Khallad, located in the N...
records.description: Authorities in Tunisia have announced the successful recovery of 56 hectares of state agricultural land in Béni Khallad, located in the Nabeul governorate. Executed by the regional directorate of state domains and land affairs of Nabeul, this action signifies a crucial advancement in the management of agricultural land in the region. The recovery follows the enforcement of a decision to forfeit rights jointly issued by the Ministries of State Domains and Agriculture, underscoring the government's dedication to ensuring the efficient allocation and preservation of land for the common good. Immediately transferred to the State Land Office, the land will undergo rehabilitation and reintroduction into the economic circuit, fostering its productive utilization for the local community's benefit. This initiative aligns with broader efforts to rationalize land resource management, combat speculation, and promote sustainable development, particularly within the agricultural sector—a cornerstone of the local economy.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of State Domains and Land Affairs

records.title: The National Health Insurance Company-Daman, part of PureHealth, has partnered with AXA – Global Healthcare to enhance International Priv...
records.description: The National Health Insurance Company-Daman, part of PureHealth, has partnered with AXA – Global Healthcare to enhance International Private Medical Insurance (IPMI) options for members in the UAE. Daman's customers with international coverage plans gain access to AXA's Select network of 1.9 million healthcare providers worldwide through the new Global Healthcare Plan, administered by Daman and supported by AXA. This partnership reflects Daman's commitment to meeting evolving client needs, especially given extensive overseas travel from the UAE's global business hub status. Karim Idilby, Managing Director for AXA – Global Healthcare, emphasizes the strategic alignment between Daman's distribution reach, domestic network, and digital platform with AXA's vision for IPMI growth in the UAE. This collaboration not only enhances international medical insurance options but also underscores both entities' dedication to meeting client needs with top-notch healthcare services worldwide.
records.institution: The National Health Insurance Company-Daman & AXA – Global Healthcare

records.title: Dr.
records.description: Dr. Ahmed Taha, Chairman of the General Authority for Health Accreditation and Control, announced the authority's commitment to establishing standards of excellence for maternal and child health facilities in Egypt. These standards will align with international best practices, incorporating guidelines from UNICEF and the World Health Organization, to support the national initiative "The Golden Thousand Days." This initiative aims to enhance the well-being of Egyptian families and improve population characteristics. The meeting, attended by experts from the World Health Organization and UNICEF, discussed the dimensions of these standards, focusing on enhancing maternal health before and after childbirth and providing quality services for mothers and children to reduce newborn mortality rates. Dr. Taha emphasized the importance of these standards in primary care units, ensuring the safety and health of mothers and newborns through early interventions and health education. Committee members expressed their enthusiasm for contributing to the formulation of these standards, recognizing their role in supporting better health outcomes for mothers and children. Among the attendees were Dr. Kawthar Mahmoud, Dr. Nanis Abdel Mohsen, Dr. Alia Talaat, Dr. Naglaa Arafa, Dr. Hala El-Hanawy, and Dr. Omaima Idris, representing various health organizations and syndicates.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Health Accreditation and Control

records.title: Dr.
records.description: Dr. Sherif El-Feel, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Holding Company for Vacsera and Vaccines, announced significant progress in the company's efforts to meet Egypt's vaccine and serum needs. He emphasized the ongoing development of Vacsera to establish it as a crucial African hub for vaccine provision, aligning with the country's strategic objectives. Dr. El-Feel revealed that Egypt is nearing completion of its first factory for manufacturing bird flu vaccines, a project expected to be finished within 90 days. Once operational, this factory will position Egypt as a key provider of bird flu vaccines in Africa. The factory, equipped with the latest international technologies and meeting World Health Organization standards, will have a production capacity of 400 to 800 million doses annually, meeting 70% of the country's needs. Additionally, Dr. El-Feel highlighted the establishment of a large laboratory for quality analysis and the development of facilities for producing vaccines against scorpions, snakes, and other diseases.

records.title: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture has refuted recent claims of a new lethal poultry virus, purportedly a variant of avian influenza, assert...
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture has refuted recent claims of a new lethal poultry virus, purportedly a variant of avian influenza, asserting that no avian viruses currently affect farms. To reassure the public, nationwide health checks on fowl are being conducted as a precaution. Avian influenza, which first struck in 2006, poses a threat to various bird species. This denial follows the avian H5N1 outbreak in 2021/22, causing millions of bird deaths globally. Small-scale poultry farmers, reliant on this livelihood, fear the virus's mutative nature, prompting the ministry to caution against unverified reports to prevent public panic. The ministry vows ongoing efforts to maintain poultry production and ensure farmers' welfare nationwide.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Egyptian government has finalized agreements for the fifth phase of solid waste management infrastructure across key governorates, in...
records.description: The Egyptian government has finalized agreements for the fifth phase of solid waste management infrastructure across key governorates, including Matrouh, Beheira, Damietta, Sharqeya, and Giza. The ceremonial signing, attended by notable figures like Hala El-Said, Yasmine Fouad, Hisham Amin, and Mukhtar Abdel Latif, signifies Egypt's commitment to waste management. These contracts involve constructing secure sanitary landfills and burial cells, totaling EGP 480 million, overseen by the Arab Organization for Industrialization. An additional investment of EGP 85 million will clear over 500,000 tonnes of waste. El-Said highlighted the system's role in environmental development, aligning with UN goals and Egypt's Vision 2030. The Ministry of Planning supports the initiative, aiming to integrate environmental considerations into national planning and increase green investments. Minister Fouad emphasized the significance of the fifth phase contract, spanning 2023-2025, for municipal waste management infrastructure, detailing the ministry's extensive involvement to ensure project success and environmental sustainability.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Local Development, & Arab Organization for Industrialization

records.title: The Government of National Unity (GNU) has announced the forthcoming launch of the "Dawlati" platform, Libya's first e-government platfor...
records.description: The Government of National Unity (GNU) has announced the forthcoming launch of the "Dawlati" platform, Libya's first e-government platform for electronic services, scheduled for May 1st. This initiative aims to streamline government transactions for citizens by enabling the electronic submission of documents, as part of the government's digital transformation plan. The Telecommunications Holding Company has played a significant role in contributing to this project. "Dawlati" centers will be established across all Libyan cities within the locations of the Libya Post Company, facilitating access to these electronic services. Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah inspected the first center in Tripoli, overseeing the final preparations for the platform's launch. Minister of State for Communication and Political Affairs, Walid Al-Lafi, provided an overview of the platform's concept, project implementation stages, and the implemented systems. Additionally, Omar Butalaq, the project manager for implementing e-government services at the Telecommunications Holding Company, shared insights into the experience of utilizing the e-government system for document acquisition.

records.title: Morocco is preparing for increased wheat imports in 2024 due to a climate-induced drought, with expectations of a significantly reduced c...
records.description: Morocco is preparing for increased wheat imports in 2024 due to a climate-induced drought, with expectations of a significantly reduced crop yield compared to the previous year. Rachid Benali, Chairman of Comader, highlighted the adverse effects of prolonged dry spells, emphasizing the country's rainfall deficit during the critical autumn season. This deficit is anticipated to result in a wheat crop substantially lower than the previous year's 4 million tons, falling short of the government's budgeted 7.5 million tons. Benali stressed the necessity of heightened wheat imports due to relatively low commodity prices and underscored the cyclical nature of agriculture, lamenting the unfavorable start to the year's cycle due to adverse weather conditions. To address the challenges, the government, through the National Grain Agency (ONICL), is providing subsidies to incentivize grain imports, aiming to mitigate the impact of the rain deficit on agricultural yields. Despite efforts to diversify the economy, agriculture remains a significant contributor to GDP, and persistent droughts have hampered local supplies, exacerbating job losses and unemployment rates. Planting challenges extend beyond wheat to other vital crops, compounding the agricultural difficulties faced by the nation.

records.title: Saudi-based amplifAI Health and Canadian Healthspan Digital Inc.
records.description: Saudi-based amplifAI Health and Canadian Healthspan Digital Inc. have forged a strategic partnership to revolutionize vascular health management, combining amplifAI Health’s AI-powered thermal hyperspectral technology with Healthspan Digital’s longevity clinical protocols. This collaboration aims to enhance healthspan and quality of life, particularly as global life expectancy rises. By addressing vascular aging, the partnership seeks to mitigate chronic conditions and develop therapeutic interventions. Dr. Meshari F. Alwashmi, CEO of amplifAI Health, and Dr. Fady Hannah-Shmouni, CEO and Founder of Healthspan Digital Inc., expressed enthusiasm for the collaboration, highlighting its potential to advance thermography and AI in vascular aging assessment. Leveraging AI algorithms, the partnership aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and reliability, ultimately enhancing personalized healthcare. With a vision for global expansion, the partnership strives to prolong health and well-being worldwide.
records.institution: Saudi amplifAI Health & Healthspan Digital Inc.

records.title: Mubadala Investment Company PJSC (Mubadala) has finalized the acquisition of KELIX bio, a specialty pharmaceutical business focusing on c...
records.description: Mubadala Investment Company PJSC (Mubadala) has finalized the acquisition of KELIX bio, a specialty pharmaceutical business focusing on complex generics across emerging markets, from Development Partners International (DPI), British International Investment (BII), and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). Founded in 2020, KELIX bio operates in six countries and generates revenues exceeding $150 million. Mubadala's acquisition aims to strengthen the UAE's position in the global life sciences sector, aligning with its goal to establish the UAE as a leader in this field. Dr. Bakheet Al Katheeri, CEO of Mubadala's UAE Investments Platform, highlights the acquisition's role in accelerating economic diversification and delivering socio-economic returns, including improved healthcare, job creation, and GDP impact. Ismail Ali Abdulla, Head of UAE Clusters at Mubadala, emphasizes the commitment to enhancing community well-being and healthcare infrastructure through strategic investments. Hocine Sidi-Said, CEO of KELIX bio, sees Mubadala's acquisition as a driver for economic returns and societal impact in the UAE, aiming to advance national life sciences capabilities and address prevalent diseases while fostering innovation and manufacturing partnerships regionally.

records.title: Bahrain Real Estate Investment Company (Edamah), in collaboration with Badia Farms, a leading controlled environment food producer, has u...
records.description: Bahrain Real Estate Investment Company (Edamah), in collaboration with Badia Farms, a leading controlled environment food producer, has unveiled plans for a new sustainable farm in Bahrain. This strategic partnership aims to revolutionize Bahrain's agricultural industry by introducing innovative farming practices. Badia Farms, renowned for its mission-driven sustainability efforts, will invest millions of dollars in the project, leasing a 50,000 sq.m. area from Edamah to implement cutting-edge hydroponic farming techniques. The initiative focuses on year-round crop production, bolstering food security and addressing challenges like limited arable land and water scarcity. The signing ceremony, attended by dignitaries including Bahraini Minister for Sustainable Development and CEO of the Bahrain Economic Development Board (EDB), underscores the commitment to environmental stewardship and economic growth through sustainable agriculture.

records.title: Mumtalakat, Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund, has announced the establishment of the Bahrain Food Holding Company (BFHC) to bolster the ki...
records.description: Mumtalakat, Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund, has announced the establishment of the Bahrain Food Holding Company (BFHC) to bolster the kingdom's agri-food sector and tackle food security challenges. Chaired by Basim Al Saie, the BFHC board of directors comprises experienced individuals such as Sami Zainal, Khaled Al Amin, and others, who will contribute to enhancing BFHC's capabilities and driving future growth. Mumtalakat will consolidate its existing food sector assets under BFHC, facilitating collaboration and integration while fostering Bahraini expertise in the field. BFHC will prioritize investments in ventures and technologies to improve food production, processing, and distribution. Shaikh Abdulla bin Khalifa Al Khalifa, Mumtalakat's CEO, emphasized the company's commitment to promoting sustainability in the national food industry and addressing food security priorities through innovative solutions and sustainable practices. BFHC aims to invest in agri-food technology, sustainable agriculture, and food services to achieve long-term sustainable growth and reduce reliance on imports while providing nutritious food for the kingdom's population.

records.title: Spinneys, a prominent retail chain, strengthens its presence in Egypt with the launch of a new store in October City, west Cairo, marking...
records.description: Spinneys, a prominent retail chain, strengthens its presence in Egypt with the launch of a new store in October City, west Cairo, marking a significant milestone in its expansion strategy. CEO Mohanad Adly highlights the strategic importance of this opening amidst economic challenges, affirming the company's commitment to the Egyptian market with plans for further expansion. With 25 stores nationwide and employing approximately 2500 individuals since its establishment in 2006, Spinneys focuses on delivering quality goods and services to consumers. The newly inaugurated 750 m2 supermarket offers a diverse range of products, including fresh produce, deli items, and general merchandise, catering to varied consumer preferences. Spinneys also provides online shopping options for added convenience. This expansion in October City follows previous store openings, reflecting Spinneys' dedication to growth and excellence in serving Egyptian consumers amidst economic uncertainties.

records.title: The First Deputy Prime Minister of the Government of National Unity and Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Hussein Al-Qatrani, held d...
records.description: The First Deputy Prime Minister of the Government of National Unity and Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Hussein Al-Qatrani, held discussions with the French Ambassador to Libya, Mustafa Mihraje, aimed at enhancing cooperation in agriculture, food security, and animal and veterinary health. The meeting explored opportunities for coordinating domestic and international efforts to expedite agricultural and livestock development, including the activation of agricultural projects. Both parties agreed to formulate a collaborative vision encompassing cooperation between the agricultural and livestock sectors of both countries.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The Noor III solar power plant in Ouarzazate, Morocco, will temporarily halt operations until November 2024 due to a leak in the molten s...
records.description: The Noor III solar power plant in Ouarzazate, Morocco, will temporarily halt operations until November 2024 due to a leak in the molten salt tank, resulting in estimated initial losses of approximately US$47 million for Acwa Power, which holds a 75% stake in the project. Acwa Power plans to rectify the issue, possibly by constructing a new reservoir. Noor III, operational since October 2018, boasts 150 megawatts capacity and utilizes Sener engineering's technology for optimal performance. Despite economic council recommendations to abandon concentrated solar power (CSP) due to higher costs, Morocco aims to increase renewable energy capacity to 52% by 2030, with a focus on wind and solar projects. While falling short of earlier solar capacity targets, Morocco is embracing green hydrogen initiatives, leveraging abundant natural resources and international investment. Despite ambitious renewable energy goals, Morocco remains heavily reliant on fossil fuels, with coal, gas, and oil constituting 62% of electricity production in 2022.

records.title: Thuraya Telecommunications Company, a subsidiary of Al Yah Satellite Communications Company PJSC, has partnered with Niflink to deliver c...
records.description: Thuraya Telecommunications Company, a subsidiary of Al Yah Satellite Communications Company PJSC, has partnered with Niflink to deliver customizable telemedicine and eLearning solutions across its network, leveraging Niflink’s advanced video compression technology. This collaboration aims to benefit health and education ministries, military entities, first responders, and NGOs by optimizing Niflink’s solutions to operate seamlessly across Thuraya’s extensive satellite network, covering 80% of the globe. Sulaiman Al Ali, CEO of Thuraya, and Cav. Bruno Iacone, CEO of Niflink, expressed enthusiasm for extending essential services to more individuals, emphasizing adaptability and efficiency in delivering critical healthcare and educational content, particularly in remote and rural areas. Niflink’s technology enables high-quality transmission of multimedia content, facilitating remote medical services and eLearning initiatives even in challenging environments and disaster response scenarios.

records.title: The Egyptian Group for Multi-Purpose Terminals Company (EGMPT), in collaboration with the Inventure Alliance and Turkish company DOGUS, s...
records.description: The Egyptian Group for Multi-Purpose Terminals Company (EGMPT), in collaboration with the Inventure Alliance and Turkish company DOGUS, signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a Turkish logistics industrial zone in the Jarjoub Economic Zone. Attended by Egyptian Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir and other officials, the agreement aims to leverage the strategic location of Jarjoub Port to develop various projects, including commercial ports, free zones, logistical facilities, and railway connections. The initiative seeks to boost trade with African nations, enhance Egypt's role in the region, attract global investments, and create job opportunities, with immediate implementation planned following a six-month feasibility study period.
records.institution: Egyptian Group for Multi-Purpose Terminals Company (EGMPT), Inventure Alliance, & Turkish DOGUS

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), in partnership with the Egyptian government, initiated a plan to transition...
records.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), in partnership with the Egyptian government, initiated a plan to transition 6th of October City into a green urban center. Under the Green Cities Program, part of the collaborative strategy between Egypt and the EBRD for 2022-2026, the plan aims to promote sustainability and environmental consciousness in Egypt's economy. Rania al-Mashat, Minister of International Cooperation and Egypt's Governor at the EBRD, highlighted the significance of this initiative in aligning with Egypt's National Climate Change Strategy 2050 and Sustainable Development Goals. The plan involves various pioneering projects across sectors, with investments mobilized to support its implementation, including the establishment of the first dry port in Egypt. Through strategic partnerships and initiatives, the plan seeks to address environmental challenges, promote green investment, and drive comprehensive growth in 6th of October City, positioning it as a leading Egyptian city committed to sustainability and digital transformation.
records.institution: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)

records.title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia reaffirmed their commitment to further deepening bilateral ties during a meeting between President Asif Ali Zar...
records.description: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia reaffirmed their commitment to further deepening bilateral ties during a meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud at the Aiwan-e-Sadr. President Zardari emphasized the utmost importance of Pakistan's relations with the Kingdom, citing their fraternal bond and shared faith. He expressed gratitude for Saudi Arabia's support during challenging times and praised the leadership of King Salman bin Abdul Aziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud. Prince Khalid highlighted the strong historical, strategic, and defense cooperation between the two countries and emphasized the need for further collaboration to deepen bilateral relations. In recognition of Prince Khalid's contributions, President Zardari conferred the Nishan-i-Pakistan award on him. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also met with Prince Khalid, discussing bilateral matters, regional peace, and security. The Prime Minister expressed Pakistan's appreciation for Saudi Arabia's support and highlighted the close brotherly ties between the two nations. He emphasized the need for increased cooperation in defense and economy and reiterated Pakistan's eagerness for the visit of the Saudi Crown Prince. Prince Khalid thanked Pakistan for the warm welcome and expressed his appreciation for attending the Pakistan Day parade as a special guest, noting the importance of promoting defense relations between the two countries.

records.title: Acasia Ventures has made a substantial investment of US$2 million into Pharmacy Marts, a Cairo-based B2B digital marketplace, signaling a...
records.description: Acasia Ventures has made a substantial investment of US$2 million into Pharmacy Marts, a Cairo-based B2B digital marketplace, signaling a significant milestone for the emerging startup. Pharmacy Marts operates as a crucial link between pharmacies and medical suppliers in Egypt, facilitating access to a wide range of medicines, medical supplies, and cosmetics. With a focus on digitizing supply chain processes, Pharmacy Marts aims to improve patient access to essential medications. The platform boasts a user-friendly interface, empowering pharmacists to efficiently manage inventory needs, place orders, and receive deliveries within 24 hours. Moreover, Pharmacy Marts addresses financing challenges for pharmacies by offering access to working capital and long-term financing options, including a buy now, pay later model. Founded in 2021, Pharmacy Marts has quickly gained traction, serving approximately 20% of Egypt's pharmacy market share and engaging over 200 suppliers. The investment from Acasia Ventures underscores the critical role of reliable medication distribution in Egypt and demonstrates confidence in Pharmacy Marts' growth potential. The partnership aims to streamline pharmacy operations, benefiting both pharmacies and millions of patients across the country.

records.title: Fresh produce exporters are showing interest in the currency reforms underway in Egypt, particularly regarding the devaluation of the Egy...
records.description: Fresh produce exporters are showing interest in the currency reforms underway in Egypt, particularly regarding the devaluation of the Egyptian Lira by the Egyptian Central Bank. Riccardo Martini, CEO of DCS Tramaco, a company specializing in refrigerated transport, commented on the potential impact of these measures on Italian fruit exports to Egypt. He noted that the recent depreciation of the Euro against the Egyptian Pound by 40% could rejuvenate the export market for Italian fruit to Egypt. However, it is still early to assess the full effects, but there is cautious optimism among traditional Italian exporters. Martini highlighted the importance of stability in the Egyptian monetary system to attract foreign investments and unlock funding from international organizations. He also mentioned the flexibility and dynamism of the Egyptian fresh produce sector, with local producers increasingly seeking partnerships with European exporters to navigate currency exchange challenges. While the currency revaluation might affect Egyptian exports, Martini noted that Egypt's role as a supplier of counterseasonal produce to Europe remains crucial. Additionally, he highlighted the challenges faced by exporters due to the crisis in the Red Sea, impacting transportation costs and delivery times. Despite these challenges, exporters remain hopeful for a resolution before the next season to mitigate the adverse effects on exports.

records.title: In 2023, Egypt witnessed a remarkable surge in fruit and vegetable exports to Canada, with imports more than doubling compared to the pre...
records.description: In 2023, Egypt witnessed a remarkable surge in fruit and vegetable exports to Canada, with imports more than doubling compared to the previous year, marking a notable growth trend in the import sector. This expansion underscores Canada's increasing significance as a trade partner for Egypt and diversifies Egypt's export destinations beyond the EU, the Middle East, and Russia. Notably, citrus fruits experienced a substantial boost, with orange shipments increasing ninefold and lemon exports surging by 6.5 times. Additionally, there was significant growth in frozen vegetable exports, pomegranates, and cherimoya fruits. Despite a slight downturn in frozen strawberry exports, Egypt managed to bolster its export volumes across various commodities, marking a commendable milestone in international trade relations with Canada.

records.title: The Egyptian government's decision to increase fuel prices, announced through official channels and effective immediately, is expected to...
records.description: The Egyptian government's decision to increase fuel prices, announced through official channels and effective immediately, is expected to have significant implications for the country's inflation rates and the financial stability of its citizens. With diesel prices rising from 8.5 to 10 Egyptian pounds per liter and 95 octane gasoline increasing to 13.5 Egyptian pounds per liter from 12.5 pounds, the adjustment reflects Egypt's challenges as a net energy importer amid global price surges and local currency depreciation. These changes are likely to further strain consumer budgets and exacerbate inflationary pressures, as recent data indicates a notable increase in both the annual urban inflation rate and food prices compared to the previous year.

records.title: Morocco has achieved a significant milestone in the avocado export market by reaching its target of 60,000 tons during the 2023/2024 seas...
records.description: Morocco has achieved a significant milestone in the avocado export market by reaching its target of 60,000 tons during the 2023/2024 season, marking a notable 33% increase from the previous season. This success positions Morocco as Africa’s third-largest exporter of avocados, following Kenya and South Africa. President Abdellah Elyamlahi attributes this accomplishment to a substantial 50% surge in avocado harvests, exceeding 70,000 tons, and highlights the surge in demand from the European Union, particularly amidst Spain's decline in avocado production due to drought. Looking forward, Morocco aims to further amplify its avocado exports, targeting a volume surpassing 100,000 tons by 2027, with the Hass variety dominating 90% of the production. Moroccan avocados maintain a competitive edge in the European market, offering competitive prices and swift delivery compared to South American alternatives. This achievement comes amid concerns over Morocco’s water crisis, with government interventions to ration water usage, though northern regions with higher groundwater reserves foster conducive conditions for avocado cultivation.
