records.title: Nafath Renewable Energy Company and Takhzeen Oman Company have taken a significant stride towards advancing Oman's renewable energy secto...
records.description: Nafath Renewable Energy Company and Takhzeen Oman Company have taken a significant stride towards advancing Oman's renewable energy sector by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at developing renewable energy storage projects. This partnership is aligned with Oman Vision 2040 and the Sultanate's broader sustainability goals. By collaborating on renewable energy storage initiatives, the two entities aim to contribute substantially to Oman's renewable energy landscape and promote sustainable development. Through their combined expertise and strategic cooperation, they seek to address Oman's energy requirements while minimizing environmental impact. This MoU underscores their shared commitment to sustainability and highlights the importance of collaboration in driving Oman towards a greener and more sustainable future.

records.title: The governments of Kazakhstan and Qatar have initiated an ambitious $17.6 billion investment drive, signaling a significant milestone in...
records.description: The governments of Kazakhstan and Qatar have initiated an ambitious $17.6 billion investment drive, signaling a significant milestone in their bilateral economic relations. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov's recent visit to Qatar further solidified the burgeoning partnership, emphasizing the commitment to elevate cooperation across various sectors. Discussions between Bektenov and Qatari officials, including Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, centered on the expedited implementation of key investment projects spanning energy, agriculture, and more. These projects, ranging from gas processing plants to agricultural facilities, signify the depth of collaboration between the two nations. Additionally, Kazakhstan expressed readiness to supply halal and organic agricultural products to Qatar, enhancing bilateral trade ties. The visit culminated in the signing of a long-term strategic partnership agreement, underscoring the commitment to comprehensive cooperation and mutual development.

records.title: Syrian-Russian talks held in Moscow aimed to bolster cooperation in the agricultural sector, focusing on both plant and animal agricultur...
records.description: Syrian-Russian talks held in Moscow aimed to bolster cooperation in the agricultural sector, focusing on both plant and animal agriculture to enhance food security in both nations. The discussions, held at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the Russian Federation, underscored the mutual commitment to strengthen bilateral relations in these vital areas. Both sides exchanged lists of necessary materials to advance their cooperation goals effectively. Muhammad Janan, head of the Chamber of Agriculture of Damascus, emphasized the importance of deepening this collaboration, particularly highlighting past exchanges in grain trade between the two countries. The talks also addressed reactivating livestock laboratories and providing support materials for both plant and animal agriculture sectors. Chekmaryov Pyotr Aleksandrovich, Head of the Agricultural Department of the Russian Chamber of Commerce, described the meeting as fruitful, expressing Russia's readiness to collaborate across various agricultural fields to elevate food security levels in Syria and Russia.
records.institution: Syrian Chamber of Agriculture of Damascus

records.title: Tunisia's citrus fruit exports reached TND 22 million by March 11, 2024, as reported by the National Observatory of Agriculture (Onagri).
records.description: Tunisia's citrus fruit exports reached TND 22 million by March 11, 2024, as reported by the National Observatory of Agriculture (Onagri). This marks a 2.8% increase in value compared to the previous year, despite a 10% decline in exported volume. Malta oranges dominated the export market, comprising 95% of total citrus exports, with France emerging as the primary market, receiving 97% of the exports. Other destinations included Libya and Qatar, importing notable quantities of Tunisian citrus fruits.

records.title: UAE Reveals Details of National Policy on Biofuels
records.description: The UAE has unveiled its National Policy on Biofuels, endorsed by the UAE Cabinet, signaling a pivotal move towards clean and sustainable energy sources. Developed by the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI) in collaboration with public and private sector partners, the policy aims to diversify the energy mix and provide sustainable fuel alternatives. Minister of Energy and Infrastructure, Suhail bin Mohammed Al Mazrouei, emphasized the policy's role in decarbonization, aiming to increase biodiesel consumption by 20% and reduce the carbon footprint of diesel cars by 75% by 2050. Al Mazrouei highlighted the policy's alignment with the UAE Energy Strategy 2050 and its contribution to economic growth through waste utilization and circular economy principles. The policy encompasses regulations for biofuel distribution, production standards, and investment criteria, supporting the UAE's sustainability goals and the Net Zero by 2050 Strategic Initiative. Industry leaders, including Ali Khalifa Alshamsi of Emirates General Petroleum Corporation (Emarat), Saif Humaid Al Falasi of ENOC Group, and others, expressed support for the policy, underscoring its significance in advancing the country's energy transition and sustainability agenda.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI)

records.title: Egypt has extended its ban on sugar exports for another three months to combat a domestic supply shortage that has led to record-high pri...
records.description: Egypt has extended its ban on sugar exports for another three months to combat a domestic supply shortage that has led to record-high prices. The Ministry of Trade and Industry, led by Minister Ahmed Samir, announced the extension to ensure an adequate sugar supply for domestic consumption amidst soaring market prices reaching EGP 50 per kilogram. Despite government measures, including subsidies and temporary export bans, sugar prices remain significantly above the targeted EGP 27 per kilogram. The extension reflects a preventative approach to stabilize the market, allowing sugar exports only when domestic needs are fully met, as per Ministerial Resolution No. 88/2023. Egypt's annual sugar production falls short of domestic consumption, prompting initiatives to secure sugar beet supplies for sugar factories. However, the sugar shortage adds to broader inflationary pressures, with Egypt's inflation rate reaching 36 percent in February, driven largely by rising food and beverage prices. The ongoing conflict in Ukraine further exacerbates the situation by disrupting global food grain supplies, making it challenging for Egypt to secure essential imports amid foreign currency shortages.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry

records.title: Iraq has achieved wheat self-sufficiency for the 2023 season, surpassing expectations amidst water scarcity challenges.
records.description: Iraq has achieved wheat self-sufficiency for the 2023 season, surpassing expectations amidst water scarcity challenges. Trade Minister Atheer Daoud Al-Ghurairy announced this milestone, highlighting Iraq's newfound capability to meet wheat demands locally without imports, thanks to ample reserves and government support for farmers. Despite facing the worst recorded drought, Iraq produced over 5 million tons of wheat by cultivating desert areas using groundwater. This achievement is significant, considering the decline in wheat production in previous seasons due to water scarcity and desertification. Iraq's success in achieving wheat self-sufficiency ensures food security and reflects resilience in agricultural practices amid evolving climatic challenges.

records.title: Almarai Announces US$4.8B Investment in Saudi Dairy Farms to Boost Food Security
records.description: Almarai Co., Saudi Arabia’s leading dairy business, has announced a US$4.8 billion investment program over the next five years to enhance food security within the kingdom. The Riyadh-based company plans to diversify production, focusing on core dairy, juice, and baked goods products, alongside technological advancements and supply chain logistics improvements. This initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 plan to diversify the economy away from oil by investing in other industries. Investments will also bolster poultry sales and introduce new products, aiming to reduce the kingdom’s reliance on food imports. Almarai’s board revealed a detailed strategic plan, allocating funds for poultry expansion, fortifying core product categories, exploring new food segments, and technology development. The initiative will be financed through operational cash flows, with the aim of enhancing food security while adding value to shareholders amidst transformations in the region’s food industry.

records.title: Syria and Venezuela have ratified bilateral cooperation agreements, as evidenced by a meeting between the Venezuelan Ambassador to Syria,...
records.description: Syria and Venezuela have ratified bilateral cooperation agreements, as evidenced by a meeting between the Venezuelan Ambassador to Syria, José Gregorio Biomorgi, and the Syrian Minister of Oil and Mineral Resources, Firas Qaddour. The discussions focused on joint action mechanisms and pathways for oil development in both countries, emphasizing the importance of expanding cooperation in oil, gas, and mineral resources sectors to foster economic development. Additionally, the Syrian minister extended a formal invitation to Venezuelan companies to participate in development fairs, exchange experiences, and explore joint investment opportunities. The Venezuelan diplomat affirmed Venezuela's commitment to collaborating with Syria and strengthening economic ties, with plans for a videoconference between the oil ministers of both nations. Furthermore, Biomorgi also met with Syria's Minister of Agriculture, Mohamad Hassan Qatana, to discuss agricultural relations, product exchanges, and the significance of bilateral agreements in this domain.
records.institution: Syrian Ministry of Oil and Mineral Resources

records.title: The World Bank has approved two loans totaling US$520 million to support projects in Tunisia, aiming to boost cereal production and enhan...
records.description: The World Bank has approved two loans totaling US$520 million to support projects in Tunisia, aiming to boost cereal production and enhance regional connectivity. The first loan of US$300 million is designated for the Emergency Food Security Response Project, aimed at mitigating the impact of drought on cereal production by rationalizing wheat imports and supporting small farmers. The second loan, amounting to US$220 million, focuses on the Tunisia Economic Development Corridor project, which seeks to address regional economic disparities through infrastructure development along the Kasserine – Sidi Bouzid – Sfax corridor. These projects align with Tunisia’s national strategies and signify the World Bank’s commitment to fostering economic opportunities and strengthening human capital in the country. This funding follows Tunisia's recent agreements with the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation and the European Union to subsidize cereal cultivation, aiming to reduce production costs for small farmers.

records.title: An interministerial meeting was convened in Algiers, jointly chaired by the Minister of Finance, Mr.
records.description: An interministerial meeting was convened in Algiers, jointly chaired by the Minister of Finance, Mr. Laaziz Faid, and the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Mr. Youcef Cherfa, with the aim of addressing obstacles related to financing and implementing investment programs in Algeria's agricultural sector. The session, as per a press release from the Ministry of Finance, emphasized the strategic significance of the agricultural sector for the national economy and discussed solutions to overcome current challenges. Minister Faid reiterated his department's commitment to supporting agriculture, emphasizing the need for diversified financing sources to ensure sustainable growth. Minister Cherfa underscored the importance of ensuring food security and advocated for close cooperation among stakeholders to stabilize the market and ensure the availability of essential food products. Commitments made during the meeting include targeted financial measures to enhance the sector's resilience against global market fluctuations and climate change, reflecting a joint effort to promote national food security and sustainable agriculture growth. This collaborative effort between the Ministries of Finance and Agriculture demonstrates a proactive approach to addressing agricultural challenges and ensuring the country's food security through targeted initiatives and financial support.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Finance & Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, and Rasha Ragheb, Executive Director of the National Academy for Trainin...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, and Rasha Ragheb, Executive Director of the National Academy for Training and Rehabilitation of Youth, have signed a cooperation protocol to enhance healthcare services. This agreement aims to provide comprehensive training programs and consultations across various fields, aligning with the Ministry's commitment to delivering superior healthcare and advancing the health system. The collaboration focuses on improving administrative, leadership, clinical, and medical skills to meet developmental goals and contribute to economic and social development plans. The Academy will offer training in public administration, policy, leadership, sustainable development, etiquette, and media relations, while the Ministry will provide lectures on first aid, disease prevention, health education, and more. The Ministry will also support the Academy's trainees in participating in presidential health initiatives and ensure emergency medical services for trainees and visitors through established protocols.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population

records.title: Egypt has commenced the construction of eight solar-powered groundwater pumping stations in South Sudan, as revealed by the Ministry of I...
records.description: Egypt has commenced the construction of eight solar-powered groundwater pumping stations in South Sudan, as revealed by the Ministry of Irrigation and Water Resources. Over the past few years, 20 such stations have been established to serve 100,000 South Sudanese citizens, alongside four rainwater harvesting dams. Minister Hani Sweilam stated Egypt's investment of LE106 million in Africa's water sector in 2022. Projects include weed removal in African Great Lakes and Ugandan lakes, solar-powered water treatment plants near Juba, and rainwater harvesting dams in South Sudan's Khor Wara region. Additionally, efforts include developing the Egyptian-Sudanese Permanent Technical Authority for Nile Water and capacity-building through training programs for Arab and African professionals.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Irrigation and Water Resources

records.title: Egypt's Ambassador to Thailand, Hala Youssef, held discussions with Nalinee Taveesin, the Advisor to the Prime Minister and Thailand Trad...
records.description: Egypt's Ambassador to Thailand, Hala Youssef, held discussions with Nalinee Taveesin, the Advisor to the Prime Minister and Thailand Trade Representative, focusing on enhancing joint economic, trade, and investment relations between the two nations. The talks aimed to elevate these relations to a higher level, particularly as both countries commemorate the 70th anniversary of establishing diplomatic relations in 1954. They reviewed the trade volume, which reached $1.350 billion in 2023, and explored ways to facilitate the entry of Egyptian goods into the Thai markets. Youssef emphasized Egypt's efforts to improve the business climate and highlighted key investment opportunities, including food industries, new and renewable energy, electronics, and the localization of automotive industries. Additionally, Youssef outlined the incentives offered by the Egyptian government to both local and foreign investors. On the Thai side, the official expressed Thailand's keen interest in developing economic relations with Egypt, leveraging the country's strategic location and free trade agreements, particularly with African countries.

records.title: Egyptian orange imports in the EU hit record levels in February, with a total of 2,149,041 tons of citrus fruits imported in 2023, markin...
records.description: Egyptian orange imports in the EU hit record levels in February, with a total of 2,149,041 tons of citrus fruits imported in 2023, marking a 16.5% increase compared to 2022. Oranges constituted 43.6% of this total, with a significant 32.6% increase in purchases compared to the previous year. However, in the current 2023/24 campaign, there's been a slight drop in imports compared to the same period last year, although still surpassing the average. South Africa remained the main supplier, despite reduced supplies, while Egypt's share notably increased, with a 55.5% growth compared to the previous campaign. In the first two months of 2024, Egyptian imports surged by 46.4%, contributing significantly to the overall increase, emphasizing Egypt's growing prominence in supplying oranges to the EU.

records.title: Finance Minister Mohamed Maait announced that, in line with President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi’s directives, the Egyptian government has hono...
records.description: Finance Minister Mohamed Maait announced that, in line with President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi’s directives, the Egyptian government has honored its commitment to the financial resolution agreement with the National Social Insurance Authority, despite facing budgetary constraints exacerbated by global crises and geopolitical tensions. The Ministry of Finance revealed on Sunday that since September 2019, the general treasury has disbursed over EGP 818 billion to the Social Insurance Authority, spanning 55 months. This allocation addresses the accumulated dues of insurance funds over half a century, as outlined in the Social Insurance and Pensions Law No. 148 of 2019, ensuring the availability of funds for pensioners, beneficiaries, and insured individuals, thereby reinforcing the pension system. Additionally, Maait emphasized the government’s commitment to strengthening the pension system with an additional EGP 202 billion in the current fiscal year, aligning with the ongoing financial transfers mandated by the Social Insurance Law. It is projected that by 2050, the general treasury will have allocated a total of EGP 46.478 trillion to the Social Insurance Authority.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Oman has initiated the process of inviting developers for five wind projects across the Sultanate, collectively valued at USD 1.2 billion...
records.description: Oman has initiated the process of inviting developers for five wind projects across the Sultanate, collectively valued at USD 1.2 billion, aimed at bolstering its renewable energy portfolio. The Nama Power and Water Procurement Company (PWP), responsible for procuring electricity from independent power plants in Oman, issued a request for qualifications (RFQ) for these projects, slated to be operational by 2027 as independent power projects (IPP). The largest among these ventures is the Mahoot I project, with a planned capacity ranging from 342 MW to 400 MW, requiring an estimated investment of OMR 187 million. Scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2027, Mahoot I is expected to generate 1,226 GWh of power annually. Other projects include Jaalan Bani Bu Ali, Dhofar II, Duqm Wind IPP, and Sadah Wind IPP, each contributing significantly to Oman's renewable energy objectives with their respective capacities, locations, and estimated investments.
records.institution: Nama Power and Water Procurement Company (PWP)

records.title: The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) has forged a significant partnership with Najd Gateway Holding Company of Saudi Arabia...
records.description: The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) has forged a significant partnership with Najd Gateway Holding Company of Saudi Arabia, aiming to enhance Pakistan's thriving livestock sector. As per the agreement, a substantial 5,000-acre tract will be allocated for cultivating alfalfa, a crucial cattle fodder, with plans for subsequent exportation. Alfalfa, renowned for its nutrient-rich composition and role as a primary protein source for various livestock, holds immense promise for Pakistan's agricultural landscape. Leveraging Pakistan's fertile soil and agricultural potential, this collaboration signifies a strategic move towards bolstering the country's agricultural sector and fostering mutual benefit for both nations.
records.institution: Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) & Najd Gateway Holding Company

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: In Damascus, Minister of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform, Mohamed Hassan Qatana, engaged in discussions with Indian Ambassador to Syria,...
records.description: In Damascus, Minister of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform, Mohamed Hassan Qatana, engaged in discussions with Indian Ambassador to Syria, Irshad Ahmed, centered on enhancing cooperation in agricultural scientific research. They explored avenues for collaboration in agricultural product exchange, the development of existing agreements, and leveraging Indian expertise in various agricultural domains. Qatana underscored the significance of utilizing Indian experiences in scientific research, applying modern agricultural technologies, and fostering cooperation in training and capacity-building. The focus also extended to organizing plant and animal quarantine systems to facilitate product exchanges and implementing the principle of bartering for essential supplies. The Indian ambassador echoed the importance of updating and implementing existing agreements, expressing readiness to relay discussed ideas to the Indian government for further action and cooperation.
records.institution: Syrian Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform

records.title: SILAL, a leading agri-food diversification entity, and Bayer, a global life sciences leader, have embarked on a strategic partnership aim...
records.description: SILAL, a leading agri-food diversification entity, and Bayer, a global life sciences leader, have embarked on a strategic partnership aimed at revolutionizing agriculture in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Announced during the World Agri-Tech Innovation Summit in Dubai, this collaboration underscores a joint commitment to combatting climate change while enhancing agricultural practices in the face of challenging climatic conditions. Through essential training modules and comprehensive vegetable seed trials, targeting local agronomists and growers, the partnership seeks to bolster sustainability and resilience within the UAE's agricultural sector. As discussions on climate change intensify globally, this collaboration not only addresses immediate challenges but also contributes to broader efforts in fostering innovation and ensuring food security for the future.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Egypt's Minister of Environment, Yasmine Fouad, held discussions with the French Ambassador to Cairo, Eric Chevalier, focusing on bolster...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Environment, Yasmine Fouad, held discussions with the French Ambassador to Cairo, Eric Chevalier, focusing on bolstering bilateral cooperation concerning environmental issues. Fouad emphasized Egypt's dedication to addressing climate change and biodiversity, underscoring the country's successful establishment of natural reserves as part of its broader ecological transformation strategy, achieved through collaboration with local communities and the private sector. Highlighting the ongoing partnership with the French Development Agency, Fouad emphasized joint projects targeting industrial pollution control and the implementation of a climate financing system to support national banks. Looking ahead, Fouad aims to expand collaboration in industry and climate sectors, with a specific focus on achieving carbon neutrality in the petroleum and industrial sectors. The discussions also addressed the Blue Mediterranean Partnership, with Fouad expressing interest in establishing a nature fund with national banks and development partners to support biodiversity conservation projects in collaboration with the private sector. Ambassador Chevalier praised Fouad's commitment to climate issues and expressed readiness to continue collaboration, particularly in industrial pollution control and climate financing initiatives, while also supporting Egypt's efforts in achieving carbon neutrality and reframing environmental discourse to attract private sector partnerships and investments.

records.title: Private investments in Tunisia surged by almost 70% year-on-year in January, with renewable energy projects emerging as a significant ben...
records.description: Private investments in Tunisia surged by almost 70% year-on-year in January, with renewable energy projects emerging as a significant beneficiary, attracting over a third of the capital. According to data released by the Tunisia Investment Authority, investments amounted to approximately 705.8 million dinars ($228 million) during the period, leading to the creation of nearly 8,792 jobs. Solar and wind energy projects garnered substantial attention, with investments totaling around 273.9 million dinars ($88.6 million), representing close to 39% of the total capital. The industrial sector captured nearly 22% of investments, while farming accounted for approximately 17%, highlighting a diversified investment landscape in Tunisia.

records.title: Egypt is ramping up sugar production in the current season, targeting approximately 140,000 tons of sugar from locally supplied sugar bee...
records.description: Egypt is ramping up sugar production in the current season, targeting approximately 140,000 tons of sugar from locally supplied sugar beet crops to alleviate the country's persistent sugar crisis. The Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has initiated the reception of sugar beet crops from farmers at the Abu Qurqas sugar factory in Minya, one of Egypt's key sugar production facilities. With the goal of receiving nearly 1 million tons of sugar beet throughout the season, farmers have cultivated around 600,000 tons across various governorates. Essam El-Din El-Bedewy, Chairman of the Egyptian Sugar and Integrated Industries Company (ESIIC), anticipates a resolution to the sugar crisis within the next two weeks as production increases across factories. To incentivize farmers, the ministry has announced additional incentives per ton of sugar beet delivered to state-owned factories, aiming to boost supply and address the shortage that has plagued the country in recent months. This initiative aligns with broader efforts to stabilize the sugar market and ensure sufficient domestic supply amidst ongoing economic challenges.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: The joint humanitarian aid operation conducted by the US and Jordan involved airdrops of food supplies to Palestinian civilians in the Ga...
records.description: The joint humanitarian aid operation conducted by the US and Jordan involved airdrops of food supplies to Palestinian civilians in the Gaza Strip. The operation utilized a US Air Force C-130 aircraft and a Royal Jordanian Air Force C-130 aircraft. This initiative came in response to alarming reports of acute malnutrition among children under age two in Gaza, with one in three children affected. The US Central Command described the airdrops as part of a sustained effort, with plans for additional aerial deliveries in the future. The aid operation aimed to address serious food shortages faced by the 2.3 million Palestinian residents of Gaza, particularly in the aftermath of previous conflicts and amid ongoing humanitarian challenges.

records.title: Morocco Allocates 1M Hectares for Green Hydrogen Initiative
records.description: In a strategic move to bolster its green energy sector and attract investors, the Moroccan government has announced plans to allocate approximately 1 million hectares of land for green hydrogen projects. Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch emphasized the initiative's role in advancing Morocco's renewable energy ambitions and attracting investments. The allocation will be carried out in phases, with an initial release of 300,000 hectares, and over 100 investors have already expressed interest in participating. Allocations will be governed by a contractual framework to ensure responsible land use. This initiative aligns with King Mohammed VI's directive to present a comprehensive green hydrogen strategy, leveraging Morocco's abundant solar and wind resources. By utilizing renewable energy for electrolysis, Morocco aims to become a key exporter of green hydrogen, driving sustainable growth and innovation across various sectors. This initiative builds on previous partnerships and signifies Morocco's commitment to transitioning towards cleaner energy sources and fostering a green hydrogen revolution under visionary leadership.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Dubai Can, an ambitious sustainability initiative led by Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, has achieved a significant mil...
records.description: Dubai Can, an ambitious sustainability initiative led by Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, has achieved a significant milestone by reducing the consumption of nearly 18 million 500ml single-use plastic water bottles within just two years of its launch. With the installation of 50 public water stations across key locations in the city and the dispensing of close to nine million liters of water, Dubai Can has provided residents and visitors with an eco-friendly alternative to plastic bottles. This initiative, aligned with Dubai's 2040 Urban Masterplan and the UAE's commitment to UN Sustainable Development Goals and Net Zero 2050 targets, represents a major step forward in environmental conservation. As part of the broader sustainability efforts, Dubai recently implemented a ban on plastic bags and other single-use disposable products, signaling the government's dedication to promoting sustainable practices and reducing environmental impact. Through awareness campaigns and collaboration with relevant entities, Dubai aims to encourage citizens to embrace eco-friendly alternatives and contribute to a greener future.

records.title: The 'GigaFarm' project, nestled within the visionary Food Tech Valley in the UAE, promises to revolutionize sustainable food production w...
records.description: The 'GigaFarm' project, nestled within the visionary Food Tech Valley in the UAE, promises to revolutionize sustainable food production with its expansive 12-meter-high, 83,612-square-meter facility set to yield an impressive 3 million kilograms of food annually. Spearheaded by UAE-founded enterprise ReFarm, the initiative embodies a commitment to innovation and sustainability, aiming to mitigate environmental concerns while meeting the escalating demand for sustainable food sources. By integrating advanced technologies to repurpose waste streams into valuable resources like compost, animal feed, clean water, and energy, the GigaFarm endeavors to significantly reduce the carbon footprint of food production and foster a more sustainable ecosystem. Leveraging vertical farming techniques and efficient production methods, the project aims to enhance food security in the region while addressing critical environmental challenges, marking a significant stride towards a more sustainable future for food production in the UAE.

records.title: Japan has allocated a grant of US$55,240 to the New Horizon Association for Social Development (NHASD) to establish a dairy facility in B...
records.description: Japan has allocated a grant of US$55,240 to the New Horizon Association for Social Development (NHASD) to establish a dairy facility in Balat, New Valley, Egypt. This project includes constructing livestock barns, a dairy factory with production machinery, and youth training programs. It marks the fourth collaboration under Japan's Basic Human Security Assistance Project, KUSANONE, aiming to enhance food security, create jobs, and raise income levels in the region. Japanese Ambassador Oka Hiroshi and NHASD's Executive Director Nady Kamel Youssef signed the grant contract, expressing optimism about the project's potential to bring prosperity to Balat, building on the success of previous KUSANONE endeavors. Japan's support, spanning various sectors in Egypt since 1994, has totaled over US$10 million, benefiting numerous NGOs and community initiatives. This initiative is anticipated to boost the local economy and empower youth through comprehensive training programs, fostering sustainable development in the region.
records.institution: New Horizon Association for Social Development (NHASD)

records.title: The European Union is poised to elevate its relationship with Egypt to the status of a "strategic partnership," a significant development...
records.description: The European Union is poised to elevate its relationship with Egypt to the status of a "strategic partnership," a significant development that could catalyze substantial funding and investments for the North African nation. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is scheduled to visit Cairo alongside the prime ministers of Italy, Greece, and Belgium. The EU is considering extending an aid package totaling approximately €7.4 billion ($8.1 billion) to Egypt, comprising grants and loans aimed at alleviating the country's severe economic crisis. This support is deemed crucial for the stability of the Middle East region. The EU envisions channeling €5 billion of private-sector investments into Egypt, particularly focusing on industries like green hydrogen, agriculture, and water management. Egypt, grappling with acute foreign exchange shortages, recently secured a $35 billion investment from the United Arab Emirates, enabling the flotation of its currency and unlocking a new IMF loan. Expectations are high for funding agreements to be signed soon with the EU, World Bank, UK, and Japan, signaling a potential turning point for Egypt's economic outlook.

records.title: Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met to discuss enhancing bilateral relations and addressing...
records.description: Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met to discuss enhancing bilateral relations and addressing the issue of PKK militants in Iraq. They agreed to draft a memorandum of understanding to establish a strategic framework for coordinated efforts between their countries. Additionally, joint committees will be formed to address various areas such as terrorism, trade, agriculture, energy, and transportation. Preparation for the upcoming visit of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to Baghdad was also discussed. Both sides acknowledged the PKK's threat to both Turkey and Iraq and agreed that its presence in Iraq violates Iraqi sovereignty. Turkey welcomed Iraq's stance on considering the PKK a banned organization and discussed measures to counter PKK activities in Iraqi territory.

records.title: India has resumed onion exports to the UAE, offering relief to consumers grappling with inflated prices after a three-month hiatus.
records.description: India has resumed onion exports to the UAE, offering relief to consumers grappling with inflated prices after a three-month hiatus. The decision, prompted by India's ban on exports in December 2023 due to domestic price surges, allows for the export of 14,400 tonnes of onions through the National Cooperative Exports Ltd (NCEL). This move is expected to have a significant impact on the UAE market, where onion prices soared during the ban, prompting consumers to seek alternatives from countries like Turkey, Iran, and China. Abdullah Sultan Al Fan Al Shamsi, Assistant Undersecretary for the Monitoring and Follow-up Sector at the Ministry of Economy, highlighted ongoing dialogues with India to address supply challenges. Dr. Dhananjay Datar, Chairman and Managing Director of Adil Group, and Kamal Vachani, Group Director and Partner of Al Maya Group, expressed optimism about the forthcoming imports, predicting a potential 20% reduction in local onion prices and improved affordability and quality. Abubakker TP, Director for the Abu Dhabi and Al Dhafra region at Lulu Group, acknowledged interim reliance on imports from Turkey and Sudan, anticipating a price correction as India resumes exports. This development not only addresses immediate pricing concerns but also showcases the resilience of global supply chains amidst complex market dynamics.

records.title: The UAE Food Bank is launching five initiatives aimed at distributing five million meals during Ramadan, under the leadership of H.H.
records.description: The UAE Food Bank is launching five initiatives aimed at distributing five million meals during Ramadan, under the leadership of H.H. Sheikha Hind bint Maktoum bin Juma Al Maktoum, Chairperson of the UAE Food Bank. These initiatives include providing daily meals to over half a million families and three million workers. Various sub-initiatives and campaigns are part of this effort, such as 'Your Iftar is on Us,' 'No for Wasting Food,' 'Cook of Thousand Meals,' 'Food Parcel,' and 'Iftar with the Workers,' along with educational programs focusing on environmental sustainability and social responsibility. Over 5,000 volunteers will support these initiatives, and strategic partnerships with more than 350 organizations are expected to enhance the bank's efforts. The UAE Food Bank aims to divert 975 tons of food waste from landfills during Ramadan and has distributed meals to over 35 million beneficiaries globally since its establishment in 2017.

records.domain: Price intervention on cash crop commodities
records.title: Egypt, a significant wheat importer, has implemented a 25% increase in the procurement price of local wheat for the 2024/25 season, now s...
records.description: Egypt, a significant wheat importer, has implemented a 25% increase in the procurement price of local wheat for the 2024/25 season, now set at EGP 2000 (US$41.32) per ardeb (150 kilograms). This adjustment aims to incentivize farmers to sell their wheat to the state, thus addressing rising inflationary pressures. The initial price announced in November 2024 was EGP 1600 (US$33.16), which, prior to Egypt's recent currency devaluation, equated to US$51.86. President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi's interest in bolstering wheat cultivation aligns with these measures, as Egypt, despite being Africa's top producer, heavily relies on imports to meet its substantial wheat consumption demand. The government's efforts to support local production include revising incentives on wheat purchases, with the aim of reducing the import bill and enhancing food security. In 2023, the Finance Ministry allocated 45 billion EGP (US$1.5 billion) to procure local wheat, signaling a significant investment in supporting farmers and encouraging strategic crop cultivation.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia is urging the adoption of responsible consumption practices to addres...
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia is urging the adoption of responsible consumption practices to address the significant challenge of meat waste in the Kingdom, aligning with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030 for sustainability and food security. Annually, the country grapples with substantial meat waste, including poultry, sheep, camel, fish, and other meats. To tackle this issue, the ministry emphasizes the importance of raising awareness about reducing meat loss and promoting responsible consumption habits among the population. It sees these measures as vital for curbing food waste, achieving sustainable development objectives, and preserving natural resources. The ministry advises individuals to plan food purchases according to their family's needs, minimize meal variety to reduce waste, and utilize leftovers effectively. Additionally, it warns against falling prey to marketing strategies that encourage unnecessary purchases and encourages repackaging surplus food for future use or donation. The ministry has also initiated educational initiatives to inform the public about reducing food waste, improving storage and cooling techniques, and enhancing meat quality and preservation methods.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Iraq's Ministerial Economic Council recently announced a significant reduction in customs duties on live animals, specifically calves, sh...
records.description: Iraq's Ministerial Economic Council recently announced a significant reduction in customs duties on live animals, specifically calves, sheep, and cattle, imported for either slaughter or breeding objectives. The new tariff rates are set at 2 percent for imported animals designated for slaughter and 5 percent for those intended for breeding purposes. This strategic move is aimed at stimulating the livestock sector by facilitating the importation of animals required for both immediate consumption and long-term breeding programs. The decision is subject to review after one year, reflecting the government's commitment to periodically reassess and adjust policies in response to evolving market dynamics and economic conditions.

records.title: Ocean Network Express (ONE) has established its West Asia Regional Headquarters in Dubai as part of its strategic expansion plan in the I...
records.description: Ocean Network Express (ONE) has established its West Asia Regional Headquarters in Dubai as part of its strategic expansion plan in the Indian Subcontinent, Middle East, and East Africa markets. The new headquarters will serve as a central hub for commercial activities, customer service, and digitization, aiming to enhance ONE's presence and accelerate growth in these rapidly developing regions. Sundeep Sibal has been appointed as the Regional Director, bringing with him extensive experience in the shipping industry, particularly in the Middle East, Indian Subcontinent, and Southeast Asia. Jeremy Nixon, CEO of ONE, highlighted the significance of the move, emphasizing the region's importance as a key growth market for the company. Sibal expressed his honor in leading ONE's efforts in the region and outlined plans for deploying new services to cater to customer needs effectively.

records.title: Egypt's Ministry of Environment has partnered with the UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in a $3 million initiative aimed at...
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of Environment has partnered with the UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in a $3 million initiative aimed at mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and conserving biodiversity in Hurghada City's tourism industry. Dubbed the "Green Hurghada" project, it seeks to foster a green recovery in Hurghada's tourism, energy, and transportation sectors, in alignment with COVID-19 recovery plans. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the project spans five years and focuses on implementing sustainable technology applications, promoting green investments, and raising awareness about biodiversity conservation. By developing a more resilient tourism industry and addressing the impact of tourism and fishing activities on biodiversity, the project aims to encourage sustainable tourism practices and mitigate climate change effects and air pollution. Additionally, it includes technical assistance programs, technology development, and investment incentives. The project builds upon Egypt's successful experience in transforming Sharm El-Sheikh into a green city and underscores the country's commitment to eco-friendly initiatives in its major tourist centers.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Environment & the UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)

records.title: iyris, formerly known as RedSea, a pioneer in sustainable AgriClimate Tech, has inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Magrabi Ag...
records.description: iyris, formerly known as RedSea, a pioneer in sustainable AgriClimate Tech, has inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Magrabi Agriculture, a leading Egyptian fresh produce provider to over 60 countries. This strategic partnership entails the deployment of iyris' cutting-edge technologies, including its acclaimed SecondSky greenhouse covers and data platform, in Magrabi Agriculture's Egyptian farming facilities and international operations. With SecondSky covers alone capable of reducing energy consumption by over 40% and water use by 30%, Magrabi Agriculture anticipates a transformative impact on its farming operations, enhancing sustainability, profitability, and produce quality. This collaboration underscores iyris' transition to a pure-play technology company, dedicated to advancing AgriClimate technology solutions globally, with a particular focus on hot climates. The MoU marks a significant stride towards advancing commercial farming practices in the region and beyond, reinforcing iyris' reputation and engagement success with major growers worldwide.

records.title: President Abdel Fatah al-Sisi has directed the Egyptian government to prioritize the education and healthcare sectors in the upcoming 202...
records.description: President Abdel Fatah al-Sisi has directed the Egyptian government to prioritize the education and healthcare sectors in the upcoming 2024/2025 budget. This instruction, given during a meeting with Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouli and Minister of Planning and Economic Development Hala al-Said, underscores the importance of investing in key social sectors to enhance public services and support the well-being of Egyptian citizens. Additionally, the government aims to identify lucrative investment opportunities across various industries to bolster revenues. This directive follows a recent meeting with the Minister of Public Enterprise to oversee the progress of new projects implemented by state-owned companies, particularly in pharmaceuticals, tourism, spinning and weaving, construction, chemical industries, and electric cars.

records.title: SIG, in collaboration with Plastic Bank and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, has launched a groundbrea...
records.description: SIG, in collaboration with Plastic Bank and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, has launched a groundbreaking recycling initiative in Egypt to revolutionize waste collection practices and uplift the livelihoods of local waste collectors. With Egypt facing significant challenges in waste management, the partnership aims to address these issues by leveraging PlasticBank's blockchain technology and innovative app, which provides transparency and incentives for waste collection. Over the course of three years, the initiative aims to collect 700 metric tonnes of beverage cartons while improving the lives of around 1,000 waste collectors through various social benefits and training programs. Additionally, the project seeks to integrate recycling into Egypt's legislative framework with the support of the Egypt Waste Management Regulatory Authority, paving the way for an extended producer responsibility (EPR) model. Abdelghany Eladib, President & General Manager of SIG India, Middle East, and Africa, highlighted the initiative's role in advancing towards a circular economy and reducing environmental impact, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation in driving sustainable development and environmental stewardship in Egypt. Supported by funding from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ Egypt, this project represents a significant step towards promoting environmental sustainability and social inclusion in Egypt's waste management sector.
records.institution: SIG, Plastic Bank, & Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)

records.title: The Ministry of Health and Population in Egypt has announced plans to construct 18 new hospitals in 2024, following the completion and de...
records.description: The Ministry of Health and Population in Egypt has announced plans to construct 18 new hospitals in 2024, following the completion and development of 30 hospitals in 2023. With a budget of LE10.9 billion, these new hospitals will be distributed across 11 governorates, adding a total of 2,747 beds to the healthcare system. This expansion includes the addition of 459 beds in intensive care units (ICUs), 527 dialysis devices, 441 incubators, and 96 operation theaters. Among the new hospitals planned for construction are facilities such as Ain Al Sokhna Emergency Hospital, Kom Ombo Hospital, and Al Sebaeya Hospital in Aswan; Al Dakhla Hospital in the New Valley; Tanta General Hospital and Central Santa Hospital in Gharbia; Central Badr Hospital in Beheira; Obour Hospital in Qalyoubiyah; Saqetla Central Hospital and General Girga Hospital in Sohag; Deshna Hospital, Abou Tesht Hospital, and New Qena Hospital in Qena; Central Bani Mazar Hospital in Menya; Tor Specialized Hospital and Central Nueiba Hospital in South Sinai; and East Qantara Hospital and Al Tal El Kebir Hospital in Ismailiyah. Additionally, existing establishments like Al Adwa Central Hospital in Menya, and Manfalout Central Hospital and Central Dayrout Hospital in Asyut, will undergo development as part of this initiative.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population

records.title: The Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has announced updated regulations and revised costs for mooring services during vessel crossings of the wa...
records.description: The Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has announced updated regulations and revised costs for mooring services during vessel crossings of the waterway, effective from 1 May onwards. Under the new regulations, mooring services in the Suez Canal will primarily be shore-based, with strategically positioned mooring boats along the canal. However, 30 percent of ships transiting the canal will still require onboard mooring services, including vessels with significant windage area, gross tonnage, or draft, as well as those with specific inter-ship distances. Vessels that refuse or cannot accommodate onboard mooring services will incur an additional charge of $5,000. Exceptions for shore-based mooring services will be granted to certain types of vessels, including warships and specialized units. A fixed total fee of $3,500 will be charged for mooring and lighting services, applicable to all ships. Additional charges may apply for lighting services and non-compliance with navigation rules. These changes come amidst efforts to enhance operational efficiency and revenue generation for the Suez Canal, a vital artery for global trade.

records.title: Iraq is confronting a dire agriculture crisis as the Ministry of Agriculture discloses a staggering loss of arable land due to water shor...
records.description: Iraq is confronting a dire agriculture crisis as the Ministry of Agriculture discloses a staggering loss of arable land due to water shortages and climate change. Ali Hamoud al-Shamari, Director General at the Ministry, highlights the severity of the situation, revealing that around 27 million dunams of agricultural land have been decimated, representing half of Iraq's arable land. This leaves only 24 million dunams currently available for agriculture. Climate change emerges as a significant factor, with the country experiencing its second major drought in four decades in 2021, resulting in a drastic decrease in water levels in critical rivers like the Tigris and Euphrates. Illegal disputes among farmers over the remaining arable land and water resources exacerbate the crisis, underscoring the urgent need for effective water management and dispute resolution mechanisms. Beyond the immediate agricultural implications, these environmental challenges endanger the ancient Mesopotamian culture of the Marsh Arabs, disrupting the delicate ecosystem of the region and threatening the livelihoods of local communities. To navigate this crisis, Iraq must adopt sustainable water management practices, modern agricultural techniques, and foster global cooperation to safeguard its agriculture, environment, and cultural heritage.

records.title: Ericsson and stc Group’s iot squared have forged a strategic partnership by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at Mobile World C...
records.description: Ericsson and stc Group’s iot squared have forged a strategic partnership by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at Mobile World Congress Barcelona 2024, Spain, with the aim of revolutionizing waste management practices in Saudi Arabia. Through this collaboration, the Ericsson Connected Recycling (ECR) platform will be introduced as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution in the Kingdom, marking a significant leap towards sustainable waste management. The ECR platform, designed to digitalize reverse supply chains, offers a holistic approach to addressing the environmental impact of waste by optimizing processes, enhancing traceability, and promoting the monetization of waste materials. By focusing initially on Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) streams, the partnership aims to contribute to the Saudi Green Initiative's sustainability goals. Othman Aldahash, CEO of iot squared, and Håkan Cervell, Vice President of Ericsson Middle East and Africa, expressed their commitment to leveraging technology to drive sustainability and foster a circular economy, underscoring Ericsson's dedication to innovation and environmental responsibility. This collaboration represents a significant milestone in Saudi Arabia's technological landscape, paving the way for a more sustainable future by promoting transparency and environmental stewardship in waste management practices.

records.title: Abu Dhabi-based Novel Foods Group, a subsidiary of Gewan Holding, has recently sealed a significant agreement to establish a US$500 milli...
records.description: Abu Dhabi-based Novel Foods Group, a subsidiary of Gewan Holding, has recently sealed a significant agreement to establish a US$500 million biotech production hub in the UAE, with a focus on precision fermentation. This ambitious endeavor, involving partnerships with industry leaders such as Glatt Group, BioEngineering AG, and CB Consultancy AG, aims to capitalize on the commercial potential of Brazzein, a natural sweet protein known for its remarkable sugar-like taste. With applications spanning various sectors including beverages, confectionery, and dairy, Brazzein offers a healthier alternative to traditional sucrose. Amidst a growing global demand for alternative sugar solutions, the Novel Foods Group is poised to leverage precision fermentation technology to overcome challenges associated with traditional harvesting methods, ensuring a sustainable and economically viable supply of Brazzein to the market. This initiative underscores the company's commitment to innovation and health, exemplified by its collaborative efforts with universities and research institutions to develop brazzein-infused recipes and gather valuable consumer feedback, ultimately aiming to provide consumers with a sweet experience without compromising on taste or health.

records.title: The Unifrutti Group has finalized the acquisition of Bomarea and AvoAmerica Peru, securing 100% ownership of both entities in collaborati...
records.description: The Unifrutti Group has finalized the acquisition of Bomarea and AvoAmerica Peru, securing 100% ownership of both entities in collaboration with Solum Partners and Alpine Fresh. With a combined area of nearly 2,000 hectares, these companies are renowned for producing premium blueberries and avocados in Peru, aligning perfectly with Unifrutti's goal to expand its presence in Peru and diversify its multi-fruit portfolio. This strategic move positions Unifrutti to meet the growing global demand for these superfruits, particularly in key markets like the US and China. Mohamed Elsarky, CEO of Unifrutti Group, emphasized the significance of this acquisition in enhancing their product range and customer service excellence, highlighting the increasing popularity and rapid expansion of blueberries and avocados as desired superfruits. This acquisition follows Unifrutti's earlier acquisition of Verfrut in January 2024, signaling the beginning of its ambitious journey to become a leading sustainable multi-fruit company globally. Currently pending customary closing conditions, the transaction underscores Unifrutti's commitment to growth and quality in the global fresh fruit market. Established in 1948, Unifrutti Group maintains vertical integration in production, marketing, and distribution, spanning over 14,000 hectares across various countries and serving customers in more than 50 countries year-round. With over 11,000 employees, Unifrutti is now part of ADQ, an Abu Dhabi-based investment and holding company.

records.title: In response to recent floods affecting seven wilayas in Algeria, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has swiftly taken action to support affec...
records.description: In response to recent floods affecting seven wilayas in Algeria, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has swiftly taken action to support affected farmers. He has announced immediate financial aid of 50,000 DA to alleviate the burdens faced by farmers whose fields have been damaged or destroyed. Emphasizing the urgency of assistance, Tebboune mandated a maximum one-week deadline for affected farmers to receive the aid, particularly with Ramadan approaching. Additionally, the President instructed compensation for affected farmers through the National Agricultural Cooperation Fund, underscoring the government's commitment to bolstering the agricultural sector during challenging times. Tebboune's rapid response demonstrates the importance of national solidarity and swift action in addressing emergency situations, especially as the nation prepares for Ramadan. This gesture not only provides material support but also reflects compassion towards farmers facing significant losses, affirming the government's dedication to citizens' well-being, particularly in times of natural disasters.

records.title: Cleopatra Hospitals Group has announced a substantial investment of EGP 2 billion (US$41 million) over the next 18 months, part of its pr...
records.description: Cleopatra Hospitals Group has announced a substantial investment of EGP 2 billion (US$41 million) over the next 18 months, part of its profit expectations strategy for the coming two years. Managing director Ahmed Ezz revealed plans for a phased expansion project, beginning with the establishment of a 40-bed hospital featuring essential facilities like a radiology center, emergency department, operating rooms, and pharmacy. Subsequent phases will see capacity expansion to accommodate 254 beds by August 2025. The investment will also extend to bolstering Cleopatra October facilities in Western Cairo and adding more outpatient clinics, focusing primarily within Cairo. Funded through internal sources and existing bank facilities, this initiative reflects the company's optimistic outlook, anticipating robust revenue growth rates of 35% for 2023 and a notable 29% surge in profits during the first nine months of the previous year, driven by increased cases handled and improved operational efficiency.

records.title: In 2023, Egypt marked a significant milestone in its export of fresh, frozen, and dried fruits and vegetables to Germany, setting a new r...
records.description: In 2023, Egypt marked a significant milestone in its export of fresh, frozen, and dried fruits and vegetables to Germany, setting a new record, as reported by EastFruit. German importers purchased over 190 thousand tons of Egyptian produce, representing a notable 25% increase from the previous year. Among the exported products, potatoes, frozen strawberries, grapes, onions, and oranges constituted the majority, collectively accounting for approximately 85% of the total volume. Each of these key products experienced substantial growth in exports compared to the previous year, with notable increases in potato, grape, onion, and orange exports. Notably, Egypt emerged as a top supplier in various segments, dominating the German market for frozen strawberries and ranking as a leading non-EU supplier for potatoes and onions. Despite facing competition from other countries like the Netherlands, France, Spain, and South Africa, Egypt's consistent growth in fruit and vegetable exports underscores its growing importance in the German market.

records.title: The Arab Organization for Industrialization (AOI) has secured a significant contract worth €38.8 million through an international tender...
records.description: The Arab Organization for Industrialization (AOI) has secured a significant contract worth €38.8 million through an international tender facilitated by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to establish four waste recycling plants for the Kitchener Drain in Egypt's Delta region. This project, funded by a combination of EBRD financing totaling 79 million euros and an 8 million euro grant from the European Union, is a crucial component of the Kitchener Drain depollution initiative. The drain, one of Egypt's most polluted waterways, stretches across three governorates and discharges into the Mediterranean Sea, posing severe environmental and health hazards. The establishment of waste recycling plants aims to address the contamination issues and improve waste management services in the region, benefiting millions of residents. Under the contract, the Ministry of Local Development and the Arab-British Dynamics Company (ABD), affiliated with AOI, will oversee the construction of four plants, each with a daily capacity of 600 tons, with completion expected by December 2025.

records.title: The Tahya Misr (Long Live Egypt) Fund has launched a significant humanitarian effort, dispatching a convoy of 101 trucks loaded with over...
records.description: The Tahya Misr (Long Live Egypt) Fund has launched a significant humanitarian effort, dispatching a convoy of 101 trucks loaded with over 1,600 tons of medical supplies, food, and essential items to support Palestinians in Gaza during Ramadan. This initiative aims to address urgent medical needs and provide essential food and supplies amid the challenging conditions faced by Gazans. The convoy includes crucial medical equipment such as anaesthesia machines, ventilators, and kidney dialysis equipment, as well as staple dry food items, beverages, dairy products, blankets, hygiene products, and clothing. The aid will be sent through the Rafah Border Crossing and distributed by the Palestinian Red Crescent to ensure it reaches displaced children and families. Tamer Abdel-Fattah, executive director of the Tahya Misr Fund, highlights the involvement of young volunteers in this humanitarian effort, which builds upon previous relief convoys sent by the fund in November 2023 and 2021.

records.title: In recent years, Lebanon has witnessed a remarkable surge in avocado production, leading to a substantial increase in exports, particular...
records.description: In recent years, Lebanon has witnessed a remarkable surge in avocado production, leading to a substantial increase in exports, particularly to European markets. This growth is attributed to the adoption of international certifications and standards in avocado farming, allowing Lebanon to expand its export reach to countries like the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and various Eastern European nations. The Lebanese Avocado Association reports a significant rise in avocado export revenues, from 40 tons in 2020 to 1,000 tons in 2023, marking considerable progress for the agricultural and export sectors. Despite facing competition from American and European producers, Lebanon has maintained its position as a key exporter, notably to Arab nations such as Egypt, Jordan, Iraq, and the Gulf states. In 2023, Lebanon exported approximately 9,000 tons of avocados, valued at around $15 million, representing a notable increase from $10 million in 2020. Entities like the Rene Moawad Foundation and the Embassy of the Netherlands have played crucial roles in supporting Lebanon's avocado industry by funding agricultural development programs aimed at enhancing the capabilities of Lebanese farmers in cultivating and exporting avocados, cherries, and apples, further contributing to the growth of the agricultural sector.

records.title: The National Office for Food Safety in Morocco (ONSSA) has recently confirmed the safety of Moroccan strawberries exported to Europe, add...
records.description: The National Office for Food Safety in Morocco (ONSSA) has recently confirmed the safety of Moroccan strawberries exported to Europe, addressing concerns regarding potential Hepatitis A virus contamination. This assurance follows a thorough investigation prompted by the activation of the Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF) in Europe. ONSSA conducted extensive analyses, including sampling irrigation water and strawberries at production sites, all of which returned negative results for contamination. Officials emphasized their prompt response to the health notification, swiftly identifying the implicated field and packaging unit. Importantly, it was clarified that the strawberries under scrutiny were intended solely for export and did not reach the local market, reassuring domestic consumers. The ONSSA reaffirmed its commitment to food safety, highlighting the effectiveness of its monitoring and surveillance program. Despite historical concerns about Hepatitis A outbreaks linked to fruit consumption, Moroccan authorities' rigorous protocols and swift action demonstrate their dedication to upholding safety standards in the food supply chain.
records.institution: National Office for Food Safety in Morocco (ONSSA)

records.title: PureHealth has partnered with the Emirates Foundation to launch the Active Abu Dhabi initiative, aiming to promote active and healthy lif...
records.description: PureHealth has partnered with the Emirates Foundation to launch the Active Abu Dhabi initiative, aiming to promote active and healthy lifestyles in Abu Dhabi. Scheduled to commence on March 18, 2024, for 14 days, the initiative will feature a year-long schedule of fitness activities. Notably, H.H. Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, attended the launch, underscoring its significance. With 37.3 percent of the population already meeting the WHO's physical activity criteria, Active Abu Dhabi seeks to enhance sports participation, foster positive societal interaction, and encourage a broader community segment to embrace an active lifestyle. Powered by Pura, PureHealth’s AI-enabled longevity app, the initiative will provide challenges and incentives to participants, thereby promoting greater involvement and progress toward healthier living. This collaboration reflects PureHealth’s mission to improve lifespan and prioritize holistic health and well-being. The partnership between PureHealth and Active Abu Dhabi is hailed as a milestone by Ahmed Al Shamsi, CEO of the Emirates Foundation, who emphasizes the potential to effect positive change and redefine health, wellness, and community engagement standards. Shaista Asif, Group CEO of PureHealth, highlights the initiative's role in advancing a health-conscious community and realizing the vision of a thriving, wellness-oriented society. Mansour Al Dhaheri, Founder of Active Abu Dhabi, emphasizes the initiative's aim to unite the community and promote health and well-being as essential components of a fulfilling life. The first event, "First Steps," is a 14-day walking challenge set to commence on March 18, 2024, at Umm Al Emarat Park, open to individuals of all fitness levels and accessible both in-person and virtually through the Pura app. This initiative underscores a concerted effort to foster healthier lifestyles and community engagement in Abu Dhabi.

records.title: Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani inaugurated two fertilizer factories in Basra, southern Iraq, signaling a significant step t...
records.description: Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani inaugurated two fertilizer factories in Basra, southern Iraq, signaling a significant step towards enhancing the country's agricultural capabilities. The factories, including a urea fertilizer factory and a di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) fertilizer factory, aim to meet the fertilizer demands of all Iraqi governorates, aligning with the nation's agriculture plan. This move is expected to reduce reliance on imports and save considerable funds previously allocated for fertilizer procurement. With production capacities of 1,000 tons per day for the urea factory and 500,000 tons per year for the DAP factory, these strategic projects are poised to contribute substantially to Iraq's food security and expand crop cultivation areas. Additionally, the rehabilitation of these previously inactive factories follows agreements with international companies, underscoring efforts to revitalize Iraq's industrial infrastructure and stimulate economic growth.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has announced a relief package for the rain-affected city of Gwadar, where torrential rains caused significant damage, resul...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has announced a relief package for the rain-affected city of Gwadar, where torrential rains caused significant damage, resulting in five fatalities and hundreds of houses being damaged. Saudi Arabia's Ambassador to Pakistan, Nawaf Bin Saeed Ahmad Al Maliky, visited Balochistan and met with Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, where he pledged humanitarian assistance for the residents of Gwadar. The ambassador announced the provision of 9,000 shelter camps and ration packs for those affected by the calamity, emphasizing Saudi Arabia's commitment to supporting its Pakistani brothers during this challenging time. Chief Minister Bugti appreciated Saudi Arabia's gesture and highlighted the impact of climate change, particularly noting the unprecedented rainfall in Gwadar this year. Efforts are underway to rehabilitate the victims, with governmental support and assistance from the Pakistan Army and Navy establishing hospital camps to provide healthcare to those affected by the disaster.

records.title: M42, a prominent Abu Dhabi-based health company, marked International Women’s Day by inaugurating the "Laha Wellness Hub," a women’s well...
records.description: M42, a prominent Abu Dhabi-based health company, marked International Women’s Day by inaugurating the "Laha Wellness Hub," a women’s wellness clinic at HealthPlus Family Clinic in Al Bandar, Abu Dhabi. Tailored for women aged 35 and above, the clinic emphasizes preventive care, personalized plans, and educational support, addressing issues such as menopause and fertility. Notably, M42 extends access to the clinic to its staff as part of a new corporate policy supporting female staff through menopause and promoting gender equity. With a mission to advocate for women’s health locally and internationally, the clinic offers comprehensive services facilitated by a team of dedicated female healthcare professionals, aiming to create a transformative space fostering community and support networks for women. The initiative aligns with M42's commitment to prioritizing employees’ health and well-being, highlighted by the implementation of a half-day wellness leave policy for all workers. Through its extensive network and state-of-the-art facilities, including Danat Al Emarat Women & Children’s Hospital and the HealthPlus Fertility Center, the Laha Wellness Hub ensures accessibility to high-quality medical treatment for women across Dubai and the northern Emirates, underscoring M42's proactive approach to promoting wellness and health equality for women.
