records.description: Mr. Abdul Razzaq Al-Zuhairi, President of the Federation of Iraqi Chambers of Commerce (FICC), hosted a delegation from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) at the Federation's headquarters. Led by Dr. Heike Harmgart, the EBRD's Managing Director for the Middle East, the delegation included His Excellency, Mr. Thomas Seiler, the EU Ambassador, and several other members. The meeting centered on various topics aimed at advancing the Iraqi economy, including discussions on the support extended by the European Bank to Iraqi businessmen for financing critical sectors such as industry, agriculture, and other priority areas essential for enhancing the local economy's growth.
records.institution: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)

records.title: Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani welcomed a delegation consisting of businessmen, economists, and representatives from various sect...
records.description: Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani welcomed a delegation consisting of businessmen, economists, and representatives from various sectors of the Egyptian private sector on Wednesday. During the meeting, Prime Minister Al-Sudani reiterated the government's commitment to strengthening cooperation between Egyptian companies and various investment and industrial sectors in Iraq. He emphasized the importance of fostering partnerships and exchanges with the Iraqi private sector while underscoring the government's dedication to financial and banking reforms aimed at improving the investment environment and facilitating necessary procedures. Al-Sudani commended the success of Egyptian companies in sectors such as housing, real estate development, and various industries, highlighting opportunities for them to venture into the Iraqi pharmaceutical industry. He also discussed the government's program focused on enhancing investment in industry and agriculture, citing the submission of around 40 requests for the establishment of local pharmaceutical factories. Additionally, Prime Minister Al-Sudani addressed the second phase of new residential cities, stressing the need for factories producing construction materials and mentioning ongoing efforts to complete the Basmaiyah residential city, which presents promising opportunities for Egyptian companies renowned for their expertise in this domain. The Egyptian businessmen expressed practical interest in entering the Iraqi market, highlighting their willingness to collaborate with the Iraqi private sector on investment plans and infrastructure projects. They emphasized Iraq's attractiveness as an investment destination, highlighting the potential for cooperation and partnership that could enhance mutual development and communication between the two countries.

records.title: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) concluded discussions with Mauritanian authorities in Nouakchott regarding the second reviews of th...
records.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) concluded discussions with Mauritanian authorities in Nouakchott regarding the second reviews of the economic program supported by the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) and the Extended Fund Facility arrangements, as well as the first review of the program under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) arrangement. IMF staff and Mauritanian authorities reached a preliminary agreement, subject to approval by IMF Management and the Executive Board, which would result in disbursements totaling approximately SDR 21.3 million (about $28.4 million). Economic growth in Mauritania is projected to reach 4.3 percent in 2024, up from 3.4 percent in 2023, driven by the non-extractive sector. Inflation has slowed significantly, and the economic outlook, while uncertain, reflects stability in international reserves and improvement in the current account deficit. The performance of IMF-supported programs under the ECF/EFF arrangements is deemed satisfactory, with most structural benchmarks already implemented. The IMF team expressed gratitude to Mauritanian authorities and other counterparts for their cooperation during the discussions.

records.title: During a bilateral meeting held at his royal palace in Al Ain, Abu Dhabi, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan expres...
records.description: During a bilateral meeting held at his royal palace in Al Ain, Abu Dhabi, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan expressed a keen interest in elevating the country's relationship with Bangladesh to a strategic partnership. He proposed the signing of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement and activating the Joint Business Council to enhance economic collaboration between the two nations. Bangladesh Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud presented an invitation letter from Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to the UAE president, inviting him to commemorate the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Both ministers emphasized the importance of exploring new areas of cooperation, such as energy security, food security, environmental issues, climate change, renewable energy, and people-to-people communication, to bolster bilateral trade. Mahmud highlighted investment opportunities for the UAE government and businessmen in developing the Matarbari Exclusive Economic Zone and infrastructure projects in Rangunia. Regional issues, including Rohingya repatriation and efforts to resolve the Gaza conflict, were also discussed, with Sheikh Abdullah expressing willingness to simplify the visa process for various professionals from Bangladesh and facilitate the transfer of work permits between employers. The meeting was attended by the Bangladesh Ambassador to the UAE Md Abu Zafar and Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Md Shafiqur Rahman.

records.title: The Egyptian government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have reached an agreement to bolster their financial partnership, expan...
records.description: The Egyptian government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have reached an agreement to bolster their financial partnership, expanding Egypt's bailout loan from the initial $3 billion to $8 billion under the Extended Fund Facility, initiated in December 2022. This decision comes in the wake of the Central Bank of Egypt's adoption of a free-floating exchange rate for the pound and a substantial interest rate hike of 600 basis points, aimed at stabilizing the country's economy amid various pressures, including those stemming from the conflict in Gaza. Consequently, the Egyptian pound witnessed a significant depreciation against the dollar, prompting further monetary measures such as raising the benchmark interest rate to 27.25% and the overnight lending rate to 28.25%. Prime Minister Moustafa Madbouly emphasized that this expanded IMF arrangement not only bolsters Egypt's financial resilience but also facilitates access to additional loans from international financial institutions, including a $1.2 billion loan earmarked for environmental sustainability initiatives.

records.title: The Egyptian Red Crescent Society (ERCS) has announced its initiative to distribute 30,000 iftar and suhoor meals daily to Palestinians f...
records.description: The Egyptian Red Crescent Society (ERCS) has announced its initiative to distribute 30,000 iftar and suhoor meals daily to Palestinians facing severe conditions in the Israeli-besieged Gaza Strip during the Holy month of Ramadan. To address the pressing humanitarian needs, ERCS is setting up a makeshift kitchen at its food supply center in North Sinai’s Sheikh Zuwaid City to provide support and alleviate the suffering of displaced Palestinian families in the region. The ERCS emphasized the symbolic significance of each hot meal, conveying a message of solidarity and support to the affected communities. The initiative comes amidst challenging circumstances in Gaza, where more than 85 percent of the population has been displaced multiple times, with significant damage to homes and infrastructure. Egypt, through the Rafah border crossing, has been at the forefront of delivering humanitarian aid to Gaza since the onset of the Israeli war on Gaza, underscoring its commitment to addressing the crisis.

records.title: The European Union's updated environmental policies, emphasizing 'reduce, reuse, recycle,' have sparked concern within Egypt's fruit and...
records.description: The European Union's updated environmental policies, emphasizing 'reduce, reuse, recycle,' have sparked concern within Egypt's fruit and vegetable sector, with industry representatives warning of potential adverse impacts on their operations and consumer access to nutritious produce. Criticism centers on the perceived disproportionate targeting of their sector, potentially exacerbating food waste while yielding minimal benefits to recycling efforts. Simultaneously, disruptions in the Red Sea region have prompted Egyptian citrus exporters to explore new markets, shifting focus from Asia to regions like Brazil and Canada. Despite challenges posed by the Red Sea crisis, exporters report a successful season marked by high-quality citrus crops, attributed to favorable weather conditions and enhanced volumes compared to the previous year.

records.title: In response to ongoing drought challenges and diminishing water resources in Morocco's primary vegetable-growing regions, the emergence o...
records.description: In response to ongoing drought challenges and diminishing water resources in Morocco's primary vegetable-growing regions, the emergence of the Green Ygran cooperative in Tata, a mountainous area traditionally limited to date cultivation, signifies a significant shift towards exploring new agricultural production areas. Led by grower and cooperative member Mbark Kaffa, the cooperative has initiated a 20-hectare commercial trial of various early vegetables, including peppers, beans, tomatoes, and others. Unlike the production model in Agadir, the cooperative opts for open-field cultivation, leveraging Tata's specific climate advantages and agroecological production methods to ensure high yields while reducing costs. Tata's isolation offers a unique advantage, free from the viral challenges present in other regions, albeit with salinity concerns manageable through irrigation. Supported by commercial initiatives and governmental backing, including participation in major trade fairs and support from the Ministry of Agriculture, the cooperative has secured contracts with customers in the UK, Germany, and the Netherlands, demonstrating both the technical feasibility and commercial viability of vegetable production in Tata. Alongside agricultural development, the cooperative has established a solar-powered packing house and cold storage station in Tata, enhancing product shelf life and contributing to sustainable practices. While Tata's agricultural transformation is in its early stages, plans for further infrastructure development, including strengthened irrigation facilities, underscore its potential as a burgeoning vegetable production region in Morocco.

records.title: In response to economic challenges, Egypt's Central Bank has implemented a policy of exchange rate flexibility, allowing the market to de...
records.description: In response to economic challenges, Egypt's Central Bank has implemented a policy of exchange rate flexibility, allowing the market to determine the value of the Egyptian pound, alongside a substantial interest rate hike of 600 basis points. This strategy aims to address inflationary pressures and foreign exchange shortages that have hindered economic growth and fueled a parallel exchange market. Following these measures, the Egyptian pound experienced a sharp depreciation against the US dollar, prompting a temporary suspension of operations in the parallel market. With recent data indicating a decline in net foreign assets, the Central Bank has eased restrictions on credit card usage abroad, highlighting the ongoing economic pressures and the need for measures to stabilize the economy amidst fluctuating exchange rates.

records.title: Karry Foods Industries has unveiled plans for a USD 35 million investment in a cutting-edge tomato processing plant in Sadat City, Egypt,...
records.description: Karry Foods Industries has unveiled plans for a USD 35 million investment in a cutting-edge tomato processing plant in Sadat City, Egypt, tapping into the country's thriving tomato market. The move comes amid increasing private investments attracted by Egypt's vast tomato production potential and favorable cultivation conditions. The first phase of the plant, boasting a processing capacity of 600 tons/day, is set to begin operations by May. Additionally, the company plans to complete a second phase by the end of 2024, further expanding capacity to 1,600 tons per day. With strategic farm acquisitions and an export-oriented approach, Karry Foods aims to meet the demand from EU countries, contributing to Egypt's status as a significant exporter of industrial tomatoes. This substantial investment underscores Egypt's robust agricultural landscape and promises to bolster its position in the global tomato market while driving economic growth.

records.title: The Iraq Ministry of Commerce has unveiled plans to construct four silos and seventeen underground bunkers across six governorates, aimin...
records.description: The Iraq Ministry of Commerce has unveiled plans to construct four silos and seventeen underground bunkers across six governorates, aiming to bolster the nation's grain and cereal storage capacity. Haider Nouri Al-Karaawi, Director General of the General Company for Grain Trade, disclosed that the project has secured cabinet approval and is anticipated to accommodate the expected increase in wheat production resulting from enhanced rainfall and modern agricultural practices. Last year, 830 tons of wheat were delivered from Salah al-Din Governorate, but this season's production is projected to exceed one million tons. Al-Karaawi outlined the ministry's ongoing initiatives, including the construction of silos, with each typically taking one to two years to complete. Recent cabinet approvals include the establishment of two silos in Kirkuk and Wasit, along with two others funded by a Saudi loan in Diwaniyah and Maysan governorates. Additionally, plans for fourteen bunkers in Kirkuk Governorate and others across various regions aim to further augment storage capabilities. The ministry also intends to introduce new transportation routes, such as trains, to facilitate wheat transport, previously deemed impractical. Al-Karaawi emphasized effective collaboration between ministries and assured ample treasury capacity to accommodate the incoming wheat quantities during the current season.

records.title: Morocco has seen a consistent increase in its fruit and vegetable exports to Canada for the fourth consecutive year, with shipments growi...
records.description: Morocco has seen a consistent increase in its fruit and vegetable exports to Canada for the fourth consecutive year, with shipments growing by 14% in volume and 33% in value annually from 2018 to 2023, according to EastFruit. In 2023, Moroccan exporters sent nearly 94 thousand tons of fresh, frozen, and dried produce to Canada, amounting to $95 million, a significant rise from four years prior when the figures stood at 56 thousand tons and $30 million, respectively. Mandarins accounted for the majority of Moroccan exports to Canada, comprising 83% of the total weight, followed by oranges at 12%, with other items including frozen fruits and vegetables, fresh blueberries, lemons, and grapefruits. The surge in mandarin shipments was the primary driver behind the export growth, while oranges and frozen strawberries experienced declines. Morocco's position as a leading supplier of mandarins and oranges to Canada underscores its significant presence in the Canadian fruit market, despite facing competition from other countries.

records.title: The harvest season for peppers in the Chtouka region near Agadir, Morocco, has concluded its peak period, according to Obeida Mansour, CE...
records.description: The harvest season for peppers in the Chtouka region near Agadir, Morocco, has concluded its peak period, according to Obeida Mansour, CEO of Universal Peppers. Unusually high temperatures this year accelerated the peak harvest, occurring in January-February, a month earlier than usual, owing to the effects of climate change. However, harvested volumes during this period were lower compared to the previous season, partly due to weather conditions. Mansour also notes the impact of TSW and PMMV viruses on pepper crops in Morocco, though Universal Peppers has been relatively fortunate with only a small percentage affected. Additionally, sluggish foreign demand, attributed to market restrictions and weakened European demand amid warmer weather, poses challenges for Moroccan pepper exports. Despite these hurdles, Mansour remains optimistic about the season's continuation until June, with the possibility of a second harvest peak if stable temperatures persist. Looking ahead, he intends to maintain the same acreage for peppers next season, expressing hope for smoother operations after navigating the complications encountered at the season's start.

records.title: Dan Company is making significant investments in Saudi Arabia's Al-Ahsa region, renowned for its rich agriculture and natural diversity,...
records.description: Dan Company is making significant investments in Saudi Arabia's Al-Ahsa region, renowned for its rich agriculture and natural diversity, by unveiling plans for the development of an agri-resort, an eco-resort, and an adventure resort. His Highness Prince Saud bin Talal, Governor of Al-Ahsa, and Abdulrahman Abaalkhail, CEO of Dan Company, convened recently to discuss the company's ambitious agenda to establish a premium farm-based tourism destination in the heart of the Al-Ahsa Governate, an area celebrated for its agricultural significance and UNESCO World Heritage status. Following the recent partnership agreement with Hilton to manage Dan Company's initial three projects, the company aims to attract tourists seeking immersive experiences amidst lush green landscapes and breathtaking natural vistas. Dan Company envisions creating a world-class tourism ecosystem that promotes sustainable, social, and economic growth while showcasing Saudi Arabia's diverse agricultural and natural heritage through agritourism, ecotourism, and adventure tourism initiatives. This strategic endeavor aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 objectives of economic diversification and community empowerment, with Dan Company projected to contribute approximately $1.6 billion (SR6 billion) to the kingdom's non-oil GDP by 2030, underscoring its commitment to expanding its footprint and fostering inclusive prosperity.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power Company has embarked on the ambitious task of constructing two wind-power plants in Uzbekistan, with a combined...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power Company has embarked on the ambitious task of constructing two wind-power plants in Uzbekistan, with a combined capacity of 800 MW, estimating investments totaling $1.085 billion. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has greenlit the investment agreements inked between the Uzbek government and ACWA Power for wind farm projects in Karakalpakstan, set at 500 MW, and in the Bukhara Region, slated for 300 MW. The investment agreements outline the design, financing, construction, and operation of the wind farms and overhead power lines by the investors and project companies. The resolution also sanctions agreements between JSC National Electric Grids of Uzbekistan and the project companies for the purchase of electrical energy over a 25-year period. These projects mark a significant step in Uzbekistan's energy landscape, which has traditionally relied heavily on oil and gas, with more than 90% of its fuel and energy resources sourced from these sectors.

records.title: Abu Dhabi-based food company Agthia Group has witnessed a notable surge in its net profits, reaching US$71.06 million for 2023, marking a...
records.description: Abu Dhabi-based food company Agthia Group has witnessed a notable surge in its net profits, reaching US$71.06 million for 2023, marking a 16% increase from the previous year. This growth is attributed to the strong performance of the company's snacking and agri-business sections. Agthia Group, listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, operates through its consumer business and agribusiness segments, which include Grand Mills flour and Agrivita animal feed products. The company's revenue in the snacking vertical experienced a significant 38% year-on-year growth, fueled by robust value growth across retail channels in the UAE and internationally. Despite challenges such as currency headwinds in Egypt affecting the protein and frozen business, the overall group net revenue increased by 12.1% year-on-year to AED4.56 billion. This positive performance has led Agthia's board of directors to recommend a full-year cash dividend payment and bonus shares, reflecting the company's strong financial position and growth trajectory.

records.title: The challenges encountered by Egyptian citrus exporters in Asia, spurred by the Red Sea crisis, have prompted a shift towards exploring a...
records.description: The challenges encountered by Egyptian citrus exporters in Asia, spurred by the Red Sea crisis, have prompted a shift towards exploring alternative markets, reveals Amr Kadah, Export Manager of Fruit.Farm. While Asia traditionally served as a key destination for Egyptian citrus alongside Gulf countries, Europe, and Russia, efforts to diversify destinations have gained traction. Kadah highlights Brazil and Canada as emerging dynamic markets witnessing substantial citrus imports this season, fueled by Egypt's superior citrus quality and increasing volumes year by year. Despite facing competition from Spain, Turkey, and Morocco, Egypt's citrus sector has thrived due to favorable weather conditions and competitive pricing, with oranges currently fetching USD 400-450/tonne FOB, offering advantageous rates for customers. Fruit.Farm is presently marketing a variety of citrus fruits including Valencia oranges, Murcott, Adalia lemons, and mandarins, expressing optimism for successful ventures ahead.

records.title: The Jordan Farmers Union (JFU) has sounded the alarm on a grave threat to the nation's potato yield as late blight, a fungal disease, rav...
records.description: The Jordan Farmers Union (JFU) has sounded the alarm on a grave threat to the nation's potato yield as late blight, a fungal disease, ravages potato crops across the Jordan Valley. With over 10,000 dunams (1,000 ha) already affected, the agricultural sector is grappling with substantial losses amounting to millions of dinars. Despite the disease's historical presence dating back to 1850, its resurgence poses a formidable challenge exacerbated by recent weather conditions conducive to its rapid spread, engulfing 80-90% of potato farms in the region. Attempts to combat the disease with potent pesticides have been hindered by labor shortages, prompting unconventional measures such as employing female agricultural workers for spraying duties. As a result, potato production has plummeted by an estimated 80%, raising concerns of potential shortages and price hikes for consumers. The Ministry of Agriculture is actively conducting tests to confront this crisis, recognizing the distinct challenges late blight presents compared to other agricultural afflictions, necessitating tailored strategies for mitigation and containment.

records.title: Marjane, a prominent name in Moroccan retail, has unveiled its latest hypermarket in Laâyoune, Western Sahara, marking a significant stri...
records.description: Marjane, a prominent name in Moroccan retail, has unveiled its latest hypermarket in Laâyoune, Western Sahara, marking a significant stride in its national expansion efforts. Spanning 12,500 m², with 5,500 m² dedicated to sales, the hypermarket commenced operations on March 2, 2024, following a total investment of MAD 210 million (US$21 million). With this addition, Marjane now boasts 171 stores nationwide, including 42 hypermarkets. Emphasizing freshness and quality, the Laâyoune hypermarket offers a diverse array of fresh products, supported by a selection of over 25,000 references across various departments. Noteworthy is Marjane's commitment to local employment, with 80% of the 210 hypermarket employees hired locally. Moreover, extensive training programs totaling nearly 34,000 hours have been conducted to ensure exceptional service. Marjane's strategic expansion reflects its dominance in Morocco's retail landscape, aligning with its mission to deliver quality products and services while consolidating market leadership.

records.title: The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) unveiled plans to launch a $1 billion Fund of Fund (FoF) on February 24, aimed at investing in inter...
records.description: The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) unveiled plans to launch a $1 billion Fund of Fund (FoF) on February 24, aimed at investing in international venture capital firms across the Gulf region. This initiative targets sectors such as financial technology, education technology, and healthcare, with the goal of attracting global venture capital funds and startups to Qatar and neighboring Gulf countries. By providing dedicated capital for startups transitioning from seed rounds to Series A to C rounds, QIA seeks to bolster the startup ecosystem in Qatar, bridging the gap with neighboring economic powerhouses like Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Mansoor Ebrahim Al-Mahmoud, Chief of Qatar Investment Authority, emphasized the FoF's role in facilitating access to venture capital for innovative companies, enabling them to expand locally and internationally, thus contributing to Qatar's economic development and global competitiveness. With QIA's vast experience and substantial assets, including its extensive portfolio covering various sectors globally and its strategic partnerships with Chinese companies, the FoF represents a strategic move to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in the region while strengthening ties with international markets.

records.title: Turkmenistan's Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov held talks with Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister of Investment Badr Al-Badr in Ashgabat, ind...
records.description: Turkmenistan's Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov held talks with Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister of Investment Badr Al-Badr in Ashgabat, indicating a burgeoning interest in investment collaboration between the two nations. The discussions primarily focused on exploring the potential of bilateral relations, with particular emphasis on the activities of the joint intergovernmental Turkmen-Saudi commission dedicated to trade and economic cooperation. Experts suggest that promising areas for business partnership encompass trade, transportation, communication, as well as industries like chemicals, textiles, agriculture, and the oil and gas sector. Notably, Saudi Aramco and Somo Al Mamlakah have expressed interest in supporting the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline project, which commenced construction in 2015. The Saudi Fund for Development has already contributed to the initiative by financing the procurement of pipes for the Turkmen section of the pipeline, underscoring the growing economic ties between the two countries.

records.title: As Ramadan approaches, Algerian consumers receive good news with the official announcement from the Algerian Interprofessional Cereals Of...
records.description: As Ramadan approaches, Algerian consumers receive good news with the official announcement from the Algerian Interprofessional Cereals Office (OAIC) regarding a drop in prices of rice and pulses, effective from March 3, 2024. This reduction follows the government's decision to eliminate the 9% value-added tax (VAT) previously applied to these essential goods. The OAIC, playing a central role in food management in Algeria, aligns with the government's directive by lowering the prices of legumes across the food chain. This decision brings significant relief to consumers, particularly crucial during the period leading up to Ramadan, where purchasing power holds utmost importance. The revised prices, applicable at all levels of the supply chain, are set for various legumes and rice varieties, ensuring accessibility for Algerian consumers.

records.title: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission met with Iraqi authorities in Amman from February 20-29 for the 2024 Article IV consultation...
records.description: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission met with Iraqi authorities in Amman from February 20-29 for the 2024 Article IV consultation, revealing several key insights. Despite a 6% non-oil GDP growth in 2023 and a decline in inflation from 7.5% to 4%, fiscal challenges persist, with a deficit of 1.3% of GDP in 2023 and a projected 7.6% deficit for 2024, contributing to a significant rise in public debt. Policy priorities outlined include fiscal adjustment, monetary policy improvements, and wide-ranging structural reforms aimed at fostering private sector development, enhancing financial sector stability, and combating corruption.

records.title: Officials from Jordan and Kuwait convened in Amman to discuss opportunities for enhanced economic collaboration at a meeting of the Jorda...
records.description: Officials from Jordan and Kuwait convened in Amman to discuss opportunities for enhanced economic collaboration at a meeting of the Jordanian-Kuwaiti Trade Technical Committee. Led by representatives from Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply and Kuwait's Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the committee explored initiatives to strengthen commercial ties across various sectors. Discussions focused on areas such as industrial development, support for small- and medium-sized enterprises, standardization, customs procedures, agriculture, transportation, and healthcare. Both sides expressed optimism regarding the meeting's outcomes and anticipated that it would contribute to the improvement of trade and economic relations between the two countries.
records.institution: Jordananian Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply

records.title: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture, led by Minister Elsayed Elkosayer, has greenlit the allocation of EGP 307.35 million to benefit 426 indi...
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture, led by Minister Elsayed Elkosayer, has greenlit the allocation of EGP 307.35 million to benefit 426 individuals, including small-scale breeders and recent graduates, as part of the national project for fattening cattle. This initiative falls under President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi's "Decent Life" campaign, aimed at uplifting rural areas and enhancing the livelihoods of small farmers and breeders. Mostafa El-Sayyad, Deputy Minister of Agriculture for Livestock, Fisheries, and Poultry, highlighted that this funding, totaling approximately EGP 8.572 billion to date, will support over 43,500 beneficiaries in raising and fattening more than 505,000 head of cattle. The project seeks to bolster the availability of meat and dairy products in the market while stabilizing prices. Coordination efforts between various governmental entities ensure thorough inspections of beneficiaries' facilities to guarantee suitable conditions for the cattle's well-being. Interested individuals can access the project through agricultural administrations, branches of the Agricultural Bank of Egypt and the National Bank of Egypt, or by contacting the Livestock and Poultry Wealth Development Sector electronically.

records.title: Fresh Energy has become a pioneering force in Egypt's agricultural landscape, particularly in controlled environment agriculture, address...
records.description: Fresh Energy has become a pioneering force in Egypt's agricultural landscape, particularly in controlled environment agriculture, addressing challenges posed by temperature fluctuations and climatic uncertainties. Reham Kamal, the Export and Marketing Manager at Fresh Energy, highlights the transformative impact of their advanced greenhouse technology on crop quality, particularly in pepper production. She emphasizes the consistent quality maintained throughout the year, attributing it to their state-of-the-art greenhouse technology. While traditional open-field farming remains prevalent in Egypt, Fresh Energy's adoption of greenhouse production has positioned them as resilient competitors in European markets. Their diverse range of peppers cultivated in optimal conditions within greenhouses ensures consistent quality, making them a trusted supplier in Europe and the UK. With strategic facilities and efficient logistics, Fresh Energy has secured a strong market presence and intends to expand its reach to Russia and Asia in the future. This success story reflects the broader trend in the agriculture industry towards controlled environment agriculture, addressing global food demand and land scarcity challenges. Fresh Energy exemplifies the potential of controlled environment agriculture in ensuring reliable and high-quality crop yields, driving transformative change in the agricultural sector.

records.title: Suez Canal Bank, under the leadership of Hussein Refaie, has reported exceptional financial performance for 2023, with net profits surgin...
records.description: Suez Canal Bank, under the leadership of Hussein Refaie, has reported exceptional financial performance for 2023, with net profits surging by an impressive 121% to EGP 2.3 billion. This growth was driven by significant increases in net income from returns and fees/commissions, along with a robust rise in total revenues. Refaie attributed this success to a strategic approach of diversifying financing across various sectors. The bank also saw a substantial increase in total assets, loans, and customer deposit balances. Additionally, it received multiple awards, recognizing its outstanding performance in 2023. Looking ahead, the bank aims for further growth, planning to increase its authorized capital. However, disruptions in vessel movement through the Suez Canal have impacted economies like Kenya and Tanzania, highlighting the interconnectedness of global trade routes and their economic implications.

records.title: Following a health alert raised by the Spanish authorities regarding the detection of the hepatitis A virus in Moroccan strawberries, an...
records.description: Following a health alert raised by the Spanish authorities regarding the detection of the hepatitis A virus in Moroccan strawberries, an escalation of reactions has ensued, prompting the implementation of new temporary requirements for exporting soft fruit from Morocco. The ONSSA, Morocco's food safety authority, conducted extensive testing and denied the presence of hepatitis A or Norovirus in Moroccan production. However, exporters are now mandated to provide negative test results for hepatitis A and Norovirus for each truckload and grower, adding to the already existing tests for pesticide residues. While some exporters view this measure as necessary to safeguard against potential accusations, others consider it excessive and detrimental to the industry. Concerns have been raised about the logistical challenges and increased costs associated with complying with the new requirements, particularly given the limited capacity of approved laboratories and the short timeframe between order, harvest, and delivery in the sector. The impact on the upcoming blueberry season is also a point of concern, prompting calls for the lifting of these requirements.
records.institution: National Office for Food Safety in Morocco (ONSSA)

records.title: India's Commerce Ministry has approved the export of 64,400 tonnes of onions, with 50,000 tonnes allocated to Bangladesh and 14,400 tonne...
records.description: India's Commerce Ministry has approved the export of 64,400 tonnes of onions, with 50,000 tonnes allocated to Bangladesh and 14,400 tonnes to the UAE through the National Cooperative Exports Ltd (NCEL). The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) specified that the UAE would receive quarterly shipments of 3,600 metric tonnes. Despite a general ban on onion exports to stabilize domestic markets, exceptions were made for these nations upon their requests. The modalities for exports to Bangladesh will be determined by the NCEL in coordination with the department of consumer affairs. This decision follows an export ban implemented on December 8 of the previous year, aimed at improving local availability and controlling prices, set to expire on March 31.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Albania have inaugurated a Business Council, signaling a new era of economic cooperation between the two nations.
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Albania have inaugurated a Business Council, signaling a new era of economic cooperation between the two nations. The launch of the council marks a significant step towards fostering bilateral trade and investment opportunities. Spearheaded by the Federation of Saudi Chambers and its Albanian counterpart, the council aims to enhance collaboration across various sectors, facilitating mutual growth and prosperity. This initiative underscores the commitment of both countries to strengthen economic ties and explore avenues for joint ventures and business partnerships.
records.institution: The Federation of Saudi Chambers & the Union of Chambers of Commerce & Industry of Albania (UCCIAL)

records.title: Dubai Municipality's latest agricultural beautification endeavor at the intersection of Al Meydan and Al Khail Streets aims to enhance th...
records.description: Dubai Municipality's latest agricultural beautification endeavor at the intersection of Al Meydan and Al Khail Streets aims to enhance the city's aesthetics, sustainability, and green spaces across an extensive 302,266 square meter area. This ambitious project incorporates cutting-edge automated irrigation systems, eliminating the need for human intervention while ensuring efficient water usage. Under the leadership of H.E. Dawoud Al Hajri, Director General of Dubai Municipality, the initiative aligns with the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum to position Dubai as a global leader in environmental sustainability. Drawing inspiration from horse hoof prints, the project's design integrates natural elements with carefully selected ornamental plants, creating a visually striking landscape. Notably, the introduction of Chorisia trees marks a significant addition to Dubai's biodiversity, underscoring the Municipality's commitment to implementing innovative and sustainable beautification projects that adhere to international standards and promote environmental stewardship.

records.title: Egypt’s Central Administration for Plant Quarantine (CAPQ) is gearing up to combat grape export frauds in the upcoming 2024 season by dep...
records.description: Egypt’s Central Administration for Plant Quarantine (CAPQ) is gearing up to combat grape export frauds in the upcoming 2024 season by deploying advanced DNA testing. This initiative marks a departure from previous reliance on European Customs Authorities. It follows Egypt's accession to the UPOV 91 treaty, demonstrating its commitment to robust measures against Plant Breeders’ Rights infringements. Ministerial decrees mandate farms and packhouses to obtain approval and a code for grape exports, warning of potential export bans for violators. The Breeders Alliance has played a crucial role in supporting these measures. CAPQ plans to equip a new DNA Laboratory and conduct staff training for grape DNA fingerprinting. This system will create a reference database to verify the authenticity of export consignments swiftly. Despite weather-related challenges, Egypt's table grape export industry remains resilient, with consistent demand from key markets like the EU and record-breaking exports to Saudi Arabia in 2023. The implementation of DNA testing by CAPQ is expected to further enhance Egypt’s credibility in the global grape market.
records.institution: Egyptian Central Administration for Plant Quarantine (CAPQ)

records.title: Iraq's Ministry of Water Resources has unveiled plans for the construction of "over 36" water harvesting dams across the country, with Pr...
records.description: Iraq's Ministry of Water Resources has unveiled plans for the construction of "over 36" water harvesting dams across the country, with Prime Minister Mohammed Shiaa Al-Sudani showing keen interest in the project. Ali Radi, Director-General of the General Authority for Dams and Reservoirs, highlighted the necessity for small dams due to existing storage capacity issues, emphasizing their role in water harvesting. Sites for these dams have been identified, with plans for execution underway, including coordination with the Ministry of Planning. Some projects have progressed to the final design stages, with implementation assigned to a government-owned company. Field surveys and soil investigations are ongoing, with teams deployed across Iraq for this purpose, reflecting the government's commitment to addressing water scarcity and enhancing water resource management, agricultural irrigation, groundwater replenishment, and regional settlement stability.

records.title: Kenya and Saudi Arabia have forged a voluntary agreement on carbon credit deals to address land degradation issues, with Saudi Arabia's D...
records.description: Kenya and Saudi Arabia have forged a voluntary agreement on carbon credit deals to address land degradation issues, with Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister for Environment, Osama Faqeeha, emphasizing Kenya's strategic importance as a partner. However, carbon offsetting has sparked controversy in Kenya, with President William Ruto denying the signing of carbon credit deals with a Dubai-based company last year, although discussions were ongoing. The agreement aims to support Kenya's readiness for Article 6 of the Paris Agreement by generating carbon credits aligned with national climate targets. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia, aiming to have 50% of its energy mix from renewable and chemical sources by 2030, sees potential collaboration in carbon credits within a circular carbon economy framework. Despite Saudi Arabia's status as a polymer producer and opposition to global efforts to eliminate plastic pollution, Dr. Faqeeha stresses the importance of addressing land degradation, which threatens global stability and prosperity. He warns of the alarming rate of land degradation and its implications for Africa's GDP, highlighting the need for concerted efforts to mitigate this environmental challenge.

records.title: Ukraine has demonstrated solidarity with Sudan by donating 7,600 tonnes of wheat under the Grain from Ukraine initiative, facilitated by...
records.description: Ukraine has demonstrated solidarity with Sudan by donating 7,600 tonnes of wheat under the Grain from Ukraine initiative, facilitated by the German Federal Foreign Office. The donation, valued at EUR €15 million (US$16M), covers transportation costs from Ukraine to Sudan and distribution within the country, benefiting a million people for a month, according to the UN World Food Program (WFP). This timely aid arrives amid Sudan's protracted conflict, providing crucial sustenance to families grappling with food insecurity exacerbated by the ongoing war. As Sudan's hunger crisis intensifies, with nearly 18 million people facing acute food insecurity and 5 million in emergency levels of hunger, the donation underscores the urgent need for international assistance. This gesture of goodwill from Ukraine aligns with efforts by other nations, such as Russia, which recently concluded a grain donation program to several African countries affected by conflict and food insecurity.

records.title: Tunisia has raised the price of drinking water by up to 16% in response to a five-year drought and ongoing economic crisis.
records.description: Tunisia has raised the price of drinking water by up to 16% in response to a five-year drought and ongoing economic crisis. Despite recent increases in rainfall, Tunisian dams are only at 35% capacity. Last year, the country implemented a quota system for drinking water and prohibited its use in agriculture, along with nighttime water supply cuts. The price hike affects consumers exceeding certain consumption thresholds, with the highest increase of 16% applied to those using over 150 cubic meters and tourist facilities. Tunisia has also initiated water desalination projects to address water shortages exacerbated by climate change and insufficient dam capacity.

records.title: Cairo 3A for Poultry, a subsidiary of the Cairo 3A agri-food group, has unveiled a state-of-the-art poultry processing plant in the indus...
records.description: Cairo 3A for Poultry, a subsidiary of the Cairo 3A agri-food group, has unveiled a state-of-the-art poultry processing plant in the industrial zone of Tenth of Ramadan City, Egypt. With an investment of US$19 million (EGP 600 million), the facility aims to address the growing domestic demand for poultry products while opening doors for increased export opportunities. Spanning 10,000 square meters, the factory is equipped with advanced technology to produce a variety of poultry products. Initially set to produce 9,000 tonnes per year, the plant's capacity is planned to double to 18,000 tonnes annually. Ibrahim Wajdi, CEO of Cairo 3A for Poultry, emphasized the plant's role in the company's integrated poultry production strategy, covering breeding, raising, feed production, and final manufacturing. This inauguration aligns with Cairo 3A's expansion plans, including a US$32 million program slated for 2024, aiming to strengthen its position in Egypt's agri-food sector and create opportunities for exporting high-quality poultry products.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Algeria has announced the commencement of a pilot census operation in six wilayas, m...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Algeria has announced the commencement of a pilot census operation in six wilayas, marking a critical phase in preparation for the upcoming general agricultural census. Running from Sunday to March 3, this pilot operation targets strategic communes in Adrar, Biskra, Djelfa, Mascara, El Tarf, and Tipasa. The main objective is to assess the effectiveness of the operational plan devised by the technical committee, ensuring adequate human and technical resources are mobilized. This preparatory phase aims to lay the groundwork before expanding the census nationwide. Field teams will gather comprehensive data on farms, crops, and production techniques during this period, refining the census process for national implementation. Tailored to each region's agricultural challenges, this strategic approach will inform precise agricultural policies, fostering sustainable sector development. Cooperation from farmers and stakeholders is crucial for the success of this initiative, promising enhanced sector knowledge and management for informed policy-making.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

records.title: Emirates Flight Catering, a global leader in aviation hospitality, has completed the full acquisition of Bustanica, formerly known as Emi...
records.description: Emirates Flight Catering, a global leader in aviation hospitality, has completed the full acquisition of Bustanica, formerly known as Emirates Crop One, the world’s largest indoor vertical farm. Located adjacent to Al Maktoum International Airport at Dubai World Central, the 330,000sqft facility has an annual capacity of over 1 million kilograms of high-quality leafy greens, achieved with a remarkable 95% reduction in water usage compared to conventional agriculture. Bustanica's produce is available in major UAE retailers and served on Emirates flights, offering pristine greens cultivated without pesticides. The acquisition aims to bolster the UAE’s commitment to food and water security while showcasing local sustainability and innovation. With advanced technologies and a dedicated team, Bustanica exemplifies Emirates Flight Catering's dedication to excellence, innovation, and sustainability, contributing to a more resilient and self-sufficient food supply chain in the UAE.

records.title: Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia are set to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in environmental protection,...
records.description: Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia are set to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in environmental protection, wildlife preservation, and climate change mitigation. The decision emerged from a bilateral meeting between Bangladesh's Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Saber Hossain Chowdhury and Saudi Arabia's State Minister for Environment Dr. Osama Ibrahim Faqeeha during the UN Environment Assembly in Nairobi, Kenya. The MoU aims to enhance cooperation in various critical areas, including environmental protection, wildlife conservation, climate change mitigation, and pollution control. State Minister Faqeeha extended an invitation to Minister Chowdhury to attend the United Nations Convention on Desertification in December 2024, highlighting the growing partnership between the two countries in addressing global environmental challenges. Discussions during the meeting covered knowledge exchange programs, agricultural sustainability, mangrove conservation, waste management, smart city development, and strategies to combat land degradation, emphasizing the joint commitment of Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia to finding innovative solutions to environmental issues. Minister Chowdhury also highlighted Bangladesh's dedication to promoting environmental sustainability both domestically and internationally, showcasing initiatives like the Mujib Climate Prosperity Plan and the National Adaptation Plan aimed at addressing climate change.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: South Africa and Saudi Arabia are forging a partnership aimed at significant agricultural exports, with South African Agriculture Ministe...
records.description: South Africa and Saudi Arabia are forging a partnership aimed at significant agricultural exports, with South African Agriculture Minister Thoko Didiza highlighting Saudi Arabia's role as a pivotal market, annually importing around R380 billion (US$20 billion) worth of agricultural products. South Africa, aiming to expand domestic production on over two million hectares of underutilized land, sees Saudi Arabia as a crucial partner in deepening trade relations across various value chains. The recent negotiations on red meat exports have paved the way for expanded bilateral agricultural relations, with South African livestock industries now able to export to Saudi Arabia. Both nations envision a fruitful partnership with strengthened trade and investment relations, showcasing South Africa's high-quality agricultural products and presenting attractive investment opportunities. While Saudi Arabia's agricultural imports primarily come from other countries, South Africa's recent market access for beef exports to Saudi Arabia signifies a promising development, aligning with South Africa's ambition to expand its export markets while maintaining strong ties with existing partners.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The "Oman Conference on Environmental Sustainability" has commenced at the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre, focusing on environment...
records.description: The "Oman Conference on Environmental Sustainability" has commenced at the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre, focusing on environmental, research, and scientific areas related to carbon neutrality. The head of the Environment Authority, announced that Oman has initiated a series of renewable energy projects aimed at achieving 39% of its total energy production from clean sources by 2040. He highlighted the Oman Blue Carbon Project, which plans to plant 100 million mangrove trees to absorb 14 million tons of carbon dioxide equivalents, garnering significant global and scientific acclaim for its first update to the second nationally determined contribution report.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA) announced on Feb.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA) announced on Feb. 25 that it convened the first Korea-Qatar Smart Farm Cooperation Committee in Doha, Qatar, aiming to facilitate exchanges and cooperation in smart agriculture between the two nations following an MOU signed in October 2023. The Qatar-Korea Smart Farm Cooperation Committee, chaired by Lee Sang-man, an official from MAFRA, discussed smart agriculture policies, research collaboration, and joint technology demonstrations in smart farming. A proposal was made to establish an innovation valley in Qatar based on the Korean smart farm innovation valley model. MAFRA has been actively promoting domestic smart agriculture policies and is now focusing on expanding Korean smart farms overseas, particularly in countries like Qatar. Qatar, in line with its national food security strategy, is keen on adopting smart agriculture practices and plans to visit Korea to explore cooperation opportunities, including potential business forums between Qatar's Hassad Food and Korean companies. Hassad Food, an investment arm of the Qatar Investment Authority, aims to meet a significant portion of Qatar's food demand and is interested in collaborating with Korean entities. Lee emphasized the importance of international cooperation in smart agriculture and expressed MAFRA's commitment to supporting Korean smart farming technology's entry into promising export markets like the Middle East.
records.institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA)

records.title: In February 2024, Saudi Arabia achieved a significant milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, leveraging high...
records.description: In February 2024, Saudi Arabia achieved a significant milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, leveraging high-tech greenhouses and vertical farming techniques pioneered by Dava Agricultural Co. Founded in 2019 with a mission to ensure year-round agricultural production for food security, Dava's innovative approach enabled them to overcome the challenges posed by the nation's harsh climate and reliance on imports. With meticulous planning and support from governmental entities and CEO Mr. Faisal Al Batal's leadership, Dava successfully shipped 5 tonnes of premium tomatoes to Europe, marking the beginning of a promising export venture. Looking ahead, the company aims to expand its exports, diversify its product range, and establish a sister company dedicated to vegetable and fruit distribution, signaling Saudi Arabia's growing presence in the global agricultural market.

records.title: During the ordinary meeting of the regional commission responsible for state agricultural lands in Bizerte, a significant decision was ma...
records.description: During the ordinary meeting of the regional commission responsible for state agricultural lands in Bizerte, a significant decision was made to renew multiple rental contracts for agricultural land in the region, totaling over 100 hectares. Led by the president of the commission and governor of Bizerte, Samir Abdellaoui, the meeting underscored the commission's pivotal role in preserving local agricultural heritage and enhancing productivity, with a steadfast commitment to public interest. The renewal of these contracts is poised to not only ensure stability in livelihood resources but also create employment opportunities for the region's inhabitants. Additionally, the commission approved the rental of approximately 80 hectares of state agricultural land across various delegations of the Bizerte governorate, aligning with efforts to efficiently utilize agricultural resources in the region. Furthermore, the meeting addressed applications from local youth seeking to utilize state agricultural plots, with file selections slated for Tuesday, February 27. Currently, around 50 hectares of state agricultural land are earmarked for allocation to eligible young entrepreneurs, reflecting an initiative aimed at fostering agricultural entrepreneurship and rural development in the Bizerte region. These decisions underscore the local authorities' dedication to agricultural and rural advancement, forming part of a broader strategy to ensure the sustainability of agricultural resources and stimulate the local economy.

records.title: Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abu Dhabi to enhance agricultural innovation an...
records.description: Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abu Dhabi to enhance agricultural innovation and research, specifically focusing on the development and promotion of various aspects of Date Palm cultivation and related industries. The signing ceremony was witnessed by the UAE's Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence, H.E. Sheikh Nahyan Mubarak Al Nahyan. The MoU aims to foster joint cooperation and expertise-sharing between the two countries, offering Pakistani farmers opportunities to expand date palm cultivation through innovative approaches. With the UAE providing technological support, Pakistan aims to capitalize on its rich topography, which holds significant potential for date palm cultivation. Additionally, the agreement paves the way for organizing the First Pakistan International Date Palm Festival 2024. Pakistan and the UAE maintain a fraternal relationship and collaborate on various mutually beneficial projects spanning political, economic, agricultural, cultural, energy, and defense sectors.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Tolerance and Coexistence

records.title: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has initiated discussions with business delegations from Estonia and the Russian Fede...
records.description: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has initiated discussions with business delegations from Estonia and the Russian Federation to bolster investment cooperation in the agricultural sector. During a meeting between Abdullah Sultan Al Owais, Chairman of the SCCI, and Madis Kallas, Minister of Regional Affairs of Estonia, held at the SCCI's headquarters, various avenues for joint work and enhanced communication among the business communities of Sharjah and Estonia were explored. The focus was on leveraging mutual expertise and experience to ensure the success of agricultural projects and stimulate investment in this crucial sector. High-profile officials, including HE Mohammad Ahmed Amin Al Awadi, Director-General of the SCCI, and Abdul Aziz Al Shamsi, Assistant Director-General for Communication and Business Sector, attended the meeting. Al Owais reiterated the Chamber's commitment to supporting investment development in the agricultural sector, driven by Sharjah's strategic approach towards sustainable agricultural development and food security. The discussions with the Estonian delegation reaffirmed the Chamber's eagerness to tap into global agricultural expertise and broaden the base of companies in this sector, making Sharjah an attractive destination for agricultural investment. Additionally, Al Owais met with a delegation from Russia, led by Vitaly Stepanov, CEO of the Moscow Export Centre, to discuss cooperation and trade exchange in agriculture and food production, emphasizing the importance of achieving food security and participating in exhibitions dedicated to modern agricultural techniques. Meanwhile, the SCCI explored avenues for bolstering investment and fostering partnerships with an Indian delegation during the "Sharjah-India Business Forum," highlighting Sharjah's attractive investment climate and the opportunities it presents across various sectors. The forum shed light on the comprehensive economic partnership agreement between the UAE and India, aiming to expand cooperation, increase investments, and boost trade exchange volumes between the two nations. Al Owais emphasized the strong and growing economic and trade relations between India and the UAE, particularly with Sharjah, aiming to enhance bilateral trade volume and mutual investments for common interests.
records.institution: The Sharjah Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI)

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Trade and Industry, Ahmed Samir, has called upon the business communities in Arab and Turkish nations to leverage the...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Trade and Industry, Ahmed Samir, has called upon the business communities in Arab and Turkish nations to leverage their strong political ties to enhance economic cooperation across various sectors. Speaking at the Fifth Joint Meeting of Arab and Turkish Chambers in Cairo, Samir emphasized the importance of joint manufacturing, integration of inputs, bilateral trade, transportation, logistics, agriculture, food production, and energy networks. Highlighting the disruptions in global supply chains caused by the pandemic and recent geopolitical events, Samir urged industries to increase local content and achieve industrial integration to access regional and global markets effectively. The meeting, attended by key figures from Egyptian, Arab, and Turkish chambers of commerce, aimed to foster development amidst the current global economic challenges. Samir also praised the recent thaw in relations between Egypt and Turkey, citing opportunities for enhanced economic ties. He emphasized Egypt's strategic advantages, including the New Suez Canal Axis and the Golden License, to attract investments. Samir urged chambers of commerce to capitalize on these opportunities and emphasized Egypt's plans to privatize sectors and stabilize investments, inviting local, Arab, and foreign investment. Additionally, he highlighted the potential for collaboration in the reconstruction of Africa and sister countries like Iraq and Libya, leveraging Egyptian expertise in various sectors and Turkey's prowess in contracting.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: The Egyptian government is expected to increase the local wheat procurement price per ardeb this year to support farmers amidst inflation...
records.description: The Egyptian government is expected to increase the local wheat procurement price per ardeb this year to support farmers amidst inflation, as announced by the Cabinet. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly chaired a meeting to review measures aimed at securing foreign currency for essential commodities like wheat, cooking oil, and powdered milk. Governor of the Central Bank of Egypt, Hassan Abdullah, emphasized the priority of securing foreign currency for strategic goods and medicine. Positive developments in foreign currency influx have led to a decrease in prices of corn and soybeans in local markets. Additionally, Egypt disclosed a groundbreaking $35 billion deal with the United Arab Emirates for a development project in the Ras El-Hikma area, representing the largest amount of foreign direct investment in Egypt's history, aimed at alleviating the country's foreign currency shortage. Amidst economic challenges, including currency devaluation and inflation, Egypt is in the final stages of securing an agreement with the International Monetary Fund to address financial stability and economic reforms.

records.description: During the Qatar International Agricultural Exhibition 2024, Qatar and South Korea initiated discussions on smart agriculture cooperation, marking the inaugural consultative meeting of their joint committee. Dr. Masoud Jarallah Al Marri, Director of the Food Security Department at Qatar's Ministry of Municipality, highlighted the significance of this meeting in activating a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the two countries. The MoU aims to bolster the smart agriculture industry, foster agricultural research collaboration, and facilitate mutual cooperation guided by principles of equality and shared interests. Dr. Al Marri underscored ongoing collaboration within the Knowledge Program project, in partnership with the Korea Trade and Investment Promotion Agency, focusing on addressing climate change impacts on Qatar's food production. The project emphasizes enhancing production efficiency, resource utilization, and developing resilient crop varieties. He emphasized the importance of sharing successful Korean smart agriculture experiences, advocating for further projects, research, and knowledge exchange to fortify bilateral relations and advance agricultural practices.

Pascual, the Secretary for Trade and Industry of the Philippines, anticipates fruitful negotiations on fisheries subsidies, agriculture, and climate issues at the upcoming World Trade Organisation’s (WTO) 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13) in Abu Dhabi. Expressing enthusiasm about welcoming Comoros and Timor-Leste as the latest additions to the WTO, Pascual emphasizes the significance of reaching agreements to enhance food security and address environmental concerns. Acknowledging the UAE's pivotal role in hosting MC13 following the successful COP28, Pascual highlights the conference as a platform for critical dialogues on e-commerce, environmental sustainability, and inclusive trade practices. He underscores the Philippines' commitment to advocating for WTO reforms and leveraging multilateral trade to mitigate climate change impacts, stressing the importance of sustainable trade practices and the exchange of eco-friendly goods and services. Pascual also commends the UAE's efforts to enhance global trade relations through Comprehensive Economic Partnerships (CEPAs) and anticipates the Philippines-UAE CEPA to bolster trade and investment flows between the two nations.

records.description: Bilateral discussions between Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica of Fiji and Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of State for Foreign Trade of the UAE, primarily focused on economic growth, fisheries, agriculture, and e-commerce negotiations. These talks, held in preparation for the 13th Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization (WTO) in Abu Dhabi, aimed to achieve substantive outcomes fostering inclusive and sustainable development. Both leaders expressed dedication to collaborating on constructive solutions, emphasizing the pivotal role of MC13 in addressing urgent global trade challenges and advancing the interests of all WTO members. Additionally, they underscored the enduring relations between Fiji and the UAE, highlighting their commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties and cooperation.

records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has reaffirmed its dedication to fostering a fair and sustainable global trading system by pledging a $10...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has reaffirmed its dedication to fostering a fair and sustainable global trading system by pledging a $10 million grant to support vital World Trade Organisation (WTO) initiatives. This announcement comes ahead of the WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13), which the UAE will host from February 26 to 29 in Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE Minister of Foreign Affairs, lauded the UAE's role as the host of MC13, welcoming leaders and representatives from 166 member states. Stressing the importance of collaborative negotiations to modernize global trade rules and promote sustainable economic growth, Sheikh Abdullah emphasized the significance of the grant in advancing key WTO programmes. The $10 million grant will be allocated to three critical initiatives: the Fisheries Funding Mechanism to promote sustainable fishing practices, the Enhanced Integrated Framework to support Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in utilizing trade for growth and poverty reduction, and the Women Exporters in the Digital Economy (WEIDE) Fund to empower women-led businesses in LDCs to access global markets through digitalization. These initiatives align with the UAE's strategic objectives of promoting sustainable development and fostering international partnerships. Sheikh Abdullah reiterated the UAE's commitment to expanding economic cooperation globally through its comprehensive economic partnership agreements programme. The MC13 conference is expected to serve as a crucial platform for addressing key trade issues and shaping the future of the global trading system.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has achieved a groundbreaking milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, overcoming its arid climat...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has achieved a groundbreaking milestone by exporting fresh tomatoes to Europe for the first time, overcoming its arid climate and traditional reliance on imports. Spearheaded by Dava Agricultural Co., which employs advanced greenhouses and vertical farming techniques, the initiative aims to ensure year-round food security. With support from government entities like the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, as well as Saudi Export and Saudi Cargo, Dava successfully shipped 5 tonnes of tomatoes to Europe in collaboration with Dutch company Lehmann & Troost. This inaugural export, followed by a planned 10-tonne shipment and projections of 12 tonnes per day by 2025, marks a significant achievement for Saudi agriculture. Dava’s commitment to freshness and innovation, including refrigerated trucks and advanced packaging, underlines its dedication to revolutionizing the country’s agricultural landscape. With plans for further expansion into various crops and the establishment of distribution centers, Dava aims to bolster Saudi Arabia’s export capabilities and enhance global trade while contributing to the growth of the domestic agricultural sector.

records.title: Saudi, Bangladesh in Talks for Skilled Worker Migration to Support KSA's Green Initiatives
records.description: Saudi Arabia is engaging in discussions with Bangladesh to bolster its green initiatives by attracting more skilled workers, as articulated by the Saudi ambassador during a meeting with Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud. The Kingdom's Vision 2030 plan aims to further augment its expat community, particularly skilled professionals equipped with expertise relevant to the vision's projects. Ambassador Essa Al-Duhailan highlighted the potential for Bangladeshi farmers and experts to contribute to initiatives such as the Saudi Green Initiative and Middle East Green Initiative, which aim to plant over 50 billion trees in the region. These initiatives, spearheaded by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman, prioritize combating climate change and preserving the environment through afforestation and emissions reduction efforts. Additionally, discussions encompassed plans to streamline the employment process for Bangladeshis and preparations for the upcoming Hajj season, including the implementation of the Makkah Route initiative for the fourth consecutive year, facilitating pilgrims' journey to Saudi Arabia.

records.title: In preparation for Ramadan, Tunisia's Trade Office announces plans to import 2,000 tons of bananas from Egypt, aiming to diversify fruit...
records.description: In preparation for Ramadan, Tunisia's Trade Office announces plans to import 2,000 tons of bananas from Egypt, aiming to diversify fruit supplies and maintain affordability, with prices capped at TND 5 per unit. Houssemeddine Touiti, from the Ministry of Trade and Export Development, underscores the importance of this decision to meet consumer demands and stabilize prices during festive periods. Tunisia's proactive measures to ensure a well-rounded fruit supply during Ramadan align with its recent surge in fruit exports, notably to Libya, Italy, France, and the UAE. The strategic banana import plan reflects Tunisia's commitment to sustainable sourcing and meeting both domestic and international market demands, highlighting its dynamic approach in the global fruit market.

records.title: The World Bank reaffirmed its commitment to assisting Tunisia in devising strategies to confront the repercussions of water scarcity and...
records.description: The World Bank reaffirmed its commitment to assisting Tunisia in devising strategies to confront the repercussions of water scarcity and climate change, as emphasized by Ferid Belhaj, the World Bank Group Vice President for the Middle East and North Africa. Speaking at a regional conference on climate and development in Tunis, Belhaj underscored the necessity of implementing policies that urgently address the challenges posed by water scarcity and climate issues, particularly within sectors like agriculture. He further announced forthcoming financial support for Tunisia to tackle the pressing issue of food security. Tunisian Economy and Planning Minister Feryel Ouerghi Sebai echoed the gravity of climate change as a primary challenge confronting Tunisia, with significant ramifications across vital sectors such as agriculture, industry, and tourism. She highlighted the detrimental impact of desertification expansion, frequent droughts, and coastal erosion on economic and social progress, urging continued commitment from the World Bank and all partners to confront these challenges head-on.

records.description: Agthia Group, a prominent player in the region's food and beverage industry, showcased its extensive brand portfolio at the Gulfood 2024 Exhibition, coinciding with the company's 20th anniversary. The exhibition served as a platform to highlight Agthia's growth and expansion across water, food, snacking, frozen, and protein business verticals, demonstrating its commitment to innovation and value-added categories. Mubarak Al Mansoori, President of Snacking & Government Relations, emphasized the significance of Agthia's presence at Gulfood 2024 in advancing the F&B sector regionally and globally. Strategic partnerships were forged during the event, including agreements with Alpha Flight Catering and North Atlantic Research and Survey, reflecting Agthia's focus on sustainability and premium product offerings. Despite challenges such as inflation and supply chain disruptions, Agthia remains dedicated to its long-term strategy of achieving leadership in the food and beverage sector by 2025, driven by a commitment to growth, efficiency, and capability. Furthermore, Agthia prioritizes sustainability, aligning its ESG strategy with global standards to enhance the consumer experience and deliver favorable returns for stakeholders.

records.title: Ugandan Foreign Minister, Gen.
records.description: Ugandan Foreign Minister, Gen. Odongo Jeje Abubakhar, highlighted the potential for synergy between Uganda's agriculture and the UAE's technological expertise to bolster bilateral relations. Speaking in Dubai, he emphasized Uganda's agricultural capacity to meet the UAE's food requirements and the opportunity to leverage UAE technology to enhance the value of Uganda's agricultural products. Gen. Abubakhar underscored the importance of this collaboration in fostering wealth and stability within Uganda. He also highlighted the strengthening bilateral relations, citing frequent high-level visits and increased flight connectivity between the two countries, with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni visiting the UAE multiple times in recent years. Gen. Abubakhar expressed Uganda's eagerness to deepen cooperation with the UAE in international security and the economy, with a focus on enhancing business partnerships. Additionally, he sought the UAE's cooperation in promoting peace and development in the Horn of Africa region, emphasizing the UAE's proximity to East Africa. The Foreign Minister also praised the UAE's successful organization of COP28, expressing optimism about joint efforts to address climate change challenges, especially given Uganda's role as chair of the Group of 77 plus China and the UAE's chairmanship of COP28. Gen. Abubakhar's extensive experience in government and the military positions him well to navigate and strengthen Uganda's ties with the UAE, emphasizing collaboration across various sectors for mutual benefit.

records.title: The Netherlands experiences a surge in demand for Egyptian onions, attributed to heightened interest from Dutch importers following the F...
records.description: The Netherlands experiences a surge in demand for Egyptian onions, attributed to heightened interest from Dutch importers following the Fruit Logistica trade show in Berlin. Freeland, a Netherlands-based trading company specializing in vegetables, anticipates a strong season with significant volumes of Egyptian onions, including organic variants, while also strategically sourcing carrots from Egypt due to prevailing circumstances. Despite challenges such as wet weather impacting leek supply and fluctuations in cauliflower pricing, Freeland remains vigilant, emphasizing its commitment to organic offerings and sustained growth in the market. Jordi van den Bosch, representing Freeland, underscores their adaptability and innovative approach in navigating the complexities of the vegetable industry, emphasizing the enduring potential of the organic sector for future growth.

records.title: Agritech Cmte Promises to Improve Iraqi Agriculture
records.description: The Iraq Britain Business Council (IBBC) has initiated a significant endeavor to enhance agriculture in Iraq, spearheaded by its Agritech Committee chaired by Dr. Amet Selman, founder of AAA Holding Group. Tasked by the Deputy Minister for Agriculture and the General Manager for Agricultural Supplies, the committee aims to revolutionize agricultural practices across the country. Formalizing its commitment with the Iraqi Prime Minister, the committee, in collaboration with IBBC, pledges to introduce agritech to the sector, working closely with farmers to improve agricultural productivity. With the Ministry of Agriculture expressing urgency and enthusiasm for this partnership, the committee's initial focus includes conducting pilot studies to assess soil conditions and establishing communication channels with farmers. Addressing issues such as the importation of low-quality fertilizers, the committee aims to educate farmers on proper fertilization techniques to enhance soil health and crop yields. Moreover, the project has garnered interest from the Iraqi diaspora, presenting an opportunity for them to contribute to the country's agricultural prosperity. Comprising a diverse group of professionals, the IBBC Agritech Committee is poised to make substantial strides in revitalizing Iraq's agricultural sector.
