records.title: Ahmed El-Sobky, Chairperson of the General Authority for Health Care and General Supervisor of the Universal Health Insurance and Decent...
records.description: Ahmed El-Sobky, Chairperson of the General Authority for Health Care and General Supervisor of the Universal Health Insurance and Decent Life projects at the Ministry of Health and Population in Egypt, convened with Joseph Ntshikiwane Mashimbye, South African Ambassador to Egypt, and Fulufhilo Themele, First Secretary at the Embassy, to explore avenues for collaboration and knowledge exchange in healthcare. The meeting spotlighted Egypt's advancements in health reform, comprehensive health coverage, and health governance, emphasizing the achievements of the Health Care Authority in enhancing the Egyptian healthcare system. Deliberations included comparisons of healthcare systems between Egypt and South Africa, the implementation of comprehensive health insurance, and the role of the private sector. El-Sobky proposed opportunities for cooperation in medical tourism, health investment, and health expertise with South Africa, suggesting collaboration with "Steiff Big Hospital," the largest hospital in South Africa, to integrate medical tourism services and attract patients from across the continent. Mashimbye lauded President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi's initiatives, particularly in health reform, expressing gratitude for Egypt's support in advancing health in Africa. He also praised Egypt's efforts in treating COVID-19 patients and enhancing healthcare services.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population

records.title: During his official visit to Cairo, Brazilian President Lula da Silva presided over the signing of two significant agreements with the Eg...
records.description: During his official visit to Cairo, Brazilian President Lula da Silva presided over the signing of two significant agreements with the Egyptian government, in the presence of President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi. The first agreement, a protocol, simplifies the export process for Brazilian beef, poultry, and pork to Egypt, ensuring food safety and quality standards while streamlining bureaucratic procedures through a "pre-listing" mechanism. Roberto Perosa, the Secretary of Trade and International Relations in Brazil’s Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, emphasized the importance of this protocol, which reflects high confidence in Brazilian sanitary control. Egypt, a major importer of Brazilian beef and poultry, stands to benefit from this streamlined process, which replaces costly and time-consuming in-person audits with automated recognition of Brazilian certifications. The second agreement, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), focuses on enhancing cooperation in science, technology, and innovation. Both presidents expressed the significance of these agreements, highlighting their potential contributions to strategic development areas. President El-Sisi emphasized broader intentions to strengthen relations across various sectors, including agriculture, science, culture, economics, and politics. The formalization of these agreements marks a milestone in bilateral cooperation, with tangible benefits expected for both nations.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Tunisia's Ministry of State Domains and Land Affairs is set to introduce a groundbreaking strategy aimed at invigorating the national eco...
records.description: Tunisia's Ministry of State Domains and Land Affairs is set to introduce a groundbreaking strategy aimed at invigorating the national economy through the utilization of state lands for non-agricultural purposes. The forthcoming decree will facilitate the allocation of such lands to investors engaged in projects of national significance, offering options for symbolic dinar-based allocation or long-term rentals spanning up to 50 years or more. To qualify, investors must adhere to investment guidelines, with projects targeting objectives like value addition, competitiveness, job creation, and regional development. Projects meeting specific investment thresholds or job creation criteria stand to benefit from financial incentives including investment bonuses, tax exemptions, infrastructure support, and social security coverage for employees, heralding a significant shift in Tunisia's economic landscape and fostering anticipation for its potential impact on national development.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of State Domains and Land Affairs

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Coffee Renaissance: Transforming Global Perceptions and Boosting Sustainable Development
records.description: Saudi Arabia's coffee sector is undergoing a remarkable transformation, highlighted by a recent event in Jazan that signals a shift in global perceptions and a commitment to sustainable development. At the International Saudi Coffee Exhibition, Deputy Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, Mansour Al-Mushaiti, unveiled a strategic initiative aimed at elevating the nation's coffee industry. With over 2,000 farms in Jazan producing more than 1,000 tons of coffee annually, Saudi Arabia is poised for a cultural renaissance, showcasing its agricultural diversity and dedication to sustainability. This initiative, supported by the Sustainable Rural Agricultural Development Program, reflects a broader strategy to enhance rural livelihoods and foster economic diversification. The International Saudi Coffee Exhibition has played a key role in promoting Saudi coffee globally, with the Deputy Minister acknowledging the significant improvement in quality and positioning Saudi coffee as a premier product in the international market. This shift not only promises economic benefits but also signifies a deeper appreciation for Saudi Arabia's cultural heritage and agricultural innovation on the world stage.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: In alignment with the national objective of safeguarding state assets and combating encroachments, the regional directorate of State Doma...
records.description: In alignment with the national objective of safeguarding state assets and combating encroachments, the regional directorate of State Domains and Land Affairs in Tozeur has successfully reclaimed 100 hectares of state agricultural land in the Nefta delegation of Tozeur governorate. This decisive operation, conducted with the involvement of various government entities and executed under an evacuation order from the regional governor, aimed to rectify the unlawful occupation and exploitation of the land by unauthorized parties. Following the reclaiming process on February 14, 2024, the regional directorate has assumed control of the recovered land pending its reintroduction into the region's economic cycle in adherence to existing legal frameworks. This proactive stance underscores the government's commitment to transparent land resource management and local economic advancement, reinforcing confidence in its ability to uphold public interests and preserve national land assets.

records.title: WILOC, a global leader in track and trace solutions for the energy industry, has partnered with Al Ghaith Energy, a prominent service pro...
records.description: WILOC, a global leader in track and trace solutions for the energy industry, has partnered with Al Ghaith Energy, a prominent service provider in the oil and gas sector in the GCC and North Africa, aiming to capitalize on the UAE's growing emphasis on digitization and IoT technologies in its oil and gas industry. The collaboration leverages WILOC's expertise in providing compliant and streamlined solutions for operational processes, complementing Al Ghaith Energy's diversified services portfolio. With a focus on enhancing traceability and optimizing operations, the partnership underscores the industry's commitment to adopting cutting-edge technologies for sustainable growth and operational excellence in line with the UAE's Digital Government Strategy 2025.

records.title: The Federal Center for Agri-Food Exports, under the Russian Ministry of Agriculture, recently announced a remarkable surge in Russian agr...
records.description: The Federal Center for Agri-Food Exports, under the Russian Ministry of Agriculture, recently announced a remarkable surge in Russian agricultural exports to Algeria, underscoring the nation's growing significance as a key importer of Russian agricultural products. The data revealed an impressive 81% increase in volume, with Algeria importing over 2.7 million tons of Russian agricultural goods, accompanied by a 20% rise in export value. Notably, wheat emerged as a primary driver of this growth, with exports reaching 2.5 million tonnes in 2023, reflecting a substantial 91% surge compared to the previous year, indicative of Algeria's robust demand for this commodity. Additionally, Algeria ranks as the second-largest importer of Russian soybean oil. The resurgence of barley exports to Algeria in November 2023, following a hiatus of two and a half years, underscores growing confidence in Russian product quality and renewed interest in barley within the Algerian market. Forecasts suggest this positive trajectory will continue, potentially surpassing the $1.5 billion mark in agri-food exports, solidifying Algeria's status as a significant trading partner for Russia in the agricultural sector. This burgeoning collaboration not only meets Algeria's increasing appetite for Russian products but also bolsters the nation's food security and agricultural diversification efforts, presenting mutually beneficial opportunities for both countries while showcasing the competitiveness of Russia's agricultural industry on the global stage.

records.title: Japan has granted $60,000 to the Future Girls Association for Society Development in Giza, Egypt, to improve access to safe water and mit...
records.description: Japan has granted $60,000 to the Future Girls Association for Society Development in Giza, Egypt, to improve access to safe water and mitigate health risks related to water pollution in the El-Ayat area. The project involves installing water purification stations and providing tricycles for water delivery, aiming to enhance the living environment and reduce health hazards. This collaboration marks the first joint effort between the Embassy of Japan and the Future Girls Association for Society Development. Ambassador Oka Hiroshi emphasized Japan's longstanding commitment to grassroots projects like this through the Grant Assistance for Grassroots Human Security Projects (KUSANONE) initiative, which has supported numerous NGOs in Egypt over the past 30 years. Zeinab Mekky, chairwoman of the Future Girls Association, expressed gratitude for Japan's support and anticipated further opportunities for collaboration. KUSANONE's contributions to Egypt have totaled over $10 million since 1994, benefiting 178 projects across various sectors including education, health, water and sanitation, vocational training, women empowerment, and special needs support.

records.title: In a significant stride towards bolstering Tunisia's cereal agriculture, four prominent collectors - COSEM, SOSEM, CMA, and SSCC - inked...
records.description: In a significant stride towards bolstering Tunisia's cereal agriculture, four prominent collectors - COSEM, SOSEM, CMA, and SSCC - inked pivotal agreements in Tunis, facilitated by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), culminating in a collective investment worth approximately 8.71 million euros (equivalent to over 29.3 million dinars). These agreements, spanning the 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 campaigns, are poised to fortify the Tunisian cereal sector by disbursing subsidies to cereal farmers through the signatory collectors, encompassing discounts on inputs, services, and agricultural machinery. With a targeted outreach to over 3,000 Tunisian cereal farmers, these subsidies are strategically aimed at curbing production costs, thereby fostering sustainable and resilient agricultural practices tailored to combat climate adversities. Notably, the European Union's delegation underlined the significance of this endeavor, citing its pivotal role in promoting environmentally conscious farming methods while propelling the adoption of modern, high-yield agricultural technologies and practices. Furthermore, the initiative, bolstered by the oversight and support of the National Institute of Field Crops (INGC), is poised to empower cereal producers in embracing contemporary and eco-friendly agricultural methodologies, thereby aligning with Tunisia's overarching agricultural objectives. This initiative forms a pivotal component of the ADAPT Cereals program, a concerted effort backed by the European Union with an allocation of 24.82 million euros, spearheaded by AICS in collaboration with the World Food Program (WFP). By addressing the pressing need to stabilize Tunisia's cereal sector amidst challenging climatic and economic landscapes, this substantial investment underscores the European Union's steadfast commitment to fostering sustainable agricultural development in Tunisia while lending crucial support to cereal farmers navigating multifaceted challenges.

records.title: The National Alliance for Civil and Development Work (NACDW) has launched its fourth humanitarian convoy destined for Gaza through the Ra...
records.description: The National Alliance for Civil and Development Work (NACDW) has launched its fourth humanitarian convoy destined for Gaza through the Rafah crossing, comprising 438 trucks laden with essential supplies such as medicines, medical equipment, clothing, food, and blankets. The convoy, organized by various NGOs from the National Coalition, including the Egyptian Food Bank and Orman Association, among others, is part of Egypt's ongoing efforts to provide immediate support and relief to Palestinians, following President El-Sisi's directives. This initiative, initiated in March 2022, involves over 30 associations and civil society organizations. Additionally, on the same day, 80 humanitarian aid trucks entered Gaza via Rafah, carrying vital supplies like foodstuffs, medical supplies, and tents, with more trucks being prepared for dispatch. Since the beginning of Israeli aggression, a substantial volume of aid, including food supplies and medical equipment, has been delivered to Gaza, sourced from various Arab and foreign countries as well as regional and international organizations, highlighting the global solidarity with the Palestinian people during times of crisis.
records.institution: The National Alliance for Civil and Development Work (NACDW)

records.title: An Indonesian Navy hospital ship, KRI Dr.
records.description: An Indonesian Navy hospital ship, KRI Dr. Radjiman Wedyodiningrat-992, carrying humanitarian relief aid for Gaza, docked at Egypt's Arish maritime port in North Sinai. The ship, dispatched by Indonesia with supplies including food, medicine, tents, and clean water, began unloading its cargo upon arrival. Diplomats from the Indonesian embassy in Cairo and Egyptian officials, including representatives from the Egyptian Red Crescent Society (ERCS), were present to receive the aid. This collaborative effort reflects Indonesia's commitment to supporting humanitarian initiatives, with contributions from the Indonesian people further bolstering relief efforts through donations of various essential items.

records.title: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) has committed to bolstering cereal production in Tunisia through a US$9.4 million c...
records.description: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) has committed to bolstering cereal production in Tunisia through a US$9.4 million contract deal aimed at subsidizing cultivation efforts. Supported by the European Union's "Support for Sustainable Development in the Agriculture and Artisanal Fishing Sector in Tunisia (ADAPT)" program, spanning from 2020 to 2028, the funding agreements, inked between AICS and four designated grain collectors, aim to enhance cereal cultivation during the agricultural seasons of 2023/2024 and 2024/2025. With a focus on assisting over 3,000 Tunisian cereal farmers, the subsidies will be channeled through the collectors to offset production costs, fostering sustainable and resilient agriculture amidst climate challenges. This initiative aligns with Tunisia's broader efforts to reduce reliance on cereal imports and promote local production, further underscored by recent collaborations such as the partnership with the African Development Bank to enhance grain sector infrastructure and seed provision plans for the upcoming campaign.
records.institution: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS)

records.title: The recent authorization of six irrigation projects utilizing treated wastewater in the Governorate of Siliana signals a pivotal advancem...
records.description: The recent authorization of six irrigation projects utilizing treated wastewater in the Governorate of Siliana signals a pivotal advancement in the region's water resource management amidst the backdrop of climate change and erratic precipitation patterns. Spearheaded by Ali Slimi, the head of the water and rural equipment department at the regional agricultural development commissioner of Siliana, these approved projects encompass a total expanse of 13.5 hectares, dedicated predominantly to fodder cultivation and almond tree orchards. This strategic initiative not only addresses pressing water supply challenges plaguing agricultural activities but also underscores the imperative to explore innovative solutions in safeguarding the sustainability of farming practices amid evolving climatic conditions. Crucially, adherence to stipulated usage conditions outlined in a joint circular issued by the ministries of health, interior, and agriculture is emphasized, ensuring regulatory compliance and efficient resource utilization. Moreover, with the irrigation area within the public irrigated zone of Mediouna spanning 76 hectares, inclusive of both fodder and fruit tree cultivation, and daily water extraction averaging at 3,700 cubic meters, the imperative for diversifying water sourcing mechanisms to bolster local agriculture becomes increasingly apparent. This decision epitomizes a concerted commitment by local authorities towards fostering sustainable and forward-thinking agricultural methodologies, emblematic of their unwavering dedication to resource stewardship and rural development.

records.title: With the green light given to 370 investment operations in Kasserine, the region is poised to embark on a transformative journey towards...
records.description: With the green light given to 370 investment operations in Kasserine, the region is poised to embark on a transformative journey towards agricultural prosperity, as announced by Jamel Chatty, the regional director of the Agricultural Investment Promotion Agency (APIA), during a recent press conference. Marking a significant stride, the approved operations entail grants totaling approximately 14 million dinars, aimed at catalyzing promising agricultural ventures with a cumulative investment value estimated at 42 million dinars. This substantial financial injection is strategically designed to invigorate the local agricultural landscape, thereby fortifying the region's economic foundation. Emphasizing the multifaceted impact of these projects, Mr. Chatty underscored their role in not just bolstering the financial landscape but also in generating approximately 330 employment opportunities, thus addressing crucial socioeconomic challenges and fostering community resilience. Integral to a broader vision of economic revitalization and unemployment reduction, this initiative is set to diversify agricultural activities across Kasserine, spanning crop production, livestock, and agro-industrial ventures. The enthusiastic response from local authorities underscores the shared commitment to agricultural advancement and underscores the ripple effects of these investments, which are poised to transcend the agricultural sector, permeating into ancillary domains such as trade, logistics, and services, thus heralding a new era of holistic development in the region.

records.title: The UAE has unveiled the inaugural Dubatt Battery Recycling plant, the first fully integrated facility of its kind in the country, locate...
records.description: The UAE has unveiled the inaugural Dubatt Battery Recycling plant, the first fully integrated facility of its kind in the country, located in Dubai Industrial City under TECOM Group PJSC. The formal inauguration, attended by esteemed dignitaries including Cabinet Member and Minister of Economy His Excellency Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, highlights the plant's crucial role in advancing sustainable industrial practices in the UAE. Government officials, including Minister of Climate Change and Environment Her Excellency Dr. Amna Al Dahak, emphasized its alignment with the UAE Industrial Decarbonization Roadmap and Circular Economy Policy 2031, signaling a significant step towards sustainable industrial and economic development. With an initial investment of AED 120 million (US$32.67m), the Dubatt plant utilizes state-of-the-art technologies to recycle up to 80 percent of battery waste generated in the UAE, significantly contributing to the circular economy and national sustainability goals. Planned expansion with an investment of AED 96 million (US$26.14m) aims to increase the factory's lead acid battery recycling capacity to 75,000 metric tonnes per year, further supporting the UAE's sustainability objectives. Dubatt's strategic location within Dubai Industrial City, a hub for manufacturing, underscores its role in driving sustainable expansion in the manufacturing sector while aligning with national economic agendas such as Operation 300bn and Dubai Economic Agenda 'D33'. Moreover, the plant's export aspirations to the GCC, Europe, and the Far East support the Make it in the Emirates initiative, strengthening the supply chain for locally manufactured products.

records.title: Egypt's Ministry of Health and Population has taken a significant step towards combating cancer by signing a protocol with Al-Burj Labora...
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of Health and Population has taken a significant step towards combating cancer by signing a protocol with Al-Burj Laboratories and Al-Mokhtabar for Medical Analysis, enabling citizens to undergo laboratory tests for cancerous tumors free of charge. The initiative, aimed at early detection and treatment of cancer, underscores the cooperation between the public and private sectors in addressing healthcare challenges. Witnessed by Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, the protocol was signed by Mohamed Hassani representing the Ministry of Health and Population, Manal Abdel Aziz from Al-Mokhtabar Laboratories, and Abdel Aziz Al-Naqli from Al-Burj Laboratories. The protocol facilitates cooperation between the laboratories across Egypt, providing free colon and prostate cancer tests to beneficiaries of the initiative. The Ministry of Health oversees service provision and connectivity between laboratories and the ministry through electronic means, ensuring efficient delivery of services. With a commitment to promoting early detection and treatment, the protocol represents a significant milestone in Egypt's efforts to combat cancer and improve public health.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population

records.title: In a significant move towards fostering sustainable urban development and infrastructure in Egypt, the United Kingdom and Egypt have inke...
records.description: In a significant move towards fostering sustainable urban development and infrastructure in Egypt, the United Kingdom and Egypt have inked a memorandum of understanding (MoU), underscoring their joint commitment to this critical endeavor. The MoU establishes a collaborative framework through a joint working group, slated to meet biannually in London and Cairo, facilitating the exchange of knowledge and expertise. Comprising representatives from government bodies and industry leaders from both nations, this platform aims to share best practices in infrastructure project prioritization, financing, and management, along with providing training opportunities. Ambassador Gareth Bayley highlighted the robust trade relationship between the UK and Egypt, with bilateral trade reaching £4.8 billion in goods and services in the 12 months preceding September 2023, with UK exports to Egypt alone valued at £2.6 billion. The UK's substantial investments in Egypt, totaling $48 billion across various sectors, underscore its unwavering support for Egypt's economic advancement and its pivotal role as a strategic partner in the region.

records.title: Slovenia and Egypt have reaffirmed their commitment to peace in the Middle East, emphasizing cooperation and dialogue.
records.description: Slovenia and Egypt have reaffirmed their commitment to peace in the Middle East, emphasizing cooperation and dialogue. Discussions between the two countries' ministers addressed concerns about the humanitarian situation and civilian casualties in Gaza, with Slovenia condemning attacks on civilians and infrastructure and advocating for a ceasefire. The importance of stabilizing the Red Sea region, given its significance as a trade route, was also highlighted. Both nations expressed interest in further developing political and economic relations, focusing on areas such as ICT, AI, digitalization, trade, education, tourism, agriculture, and sport. The Slovenian-Egyptian Joint Commission on Economic Cooperation plays a vital role in enhancing bilateral economic ties, with ongoing efforts to identify new business opportunities and strengthen existing partnerships.
records.institution: The Slovenian-Egyptian Joint Commission on Economic Cooperation

records.title: Iraq and Lebanon have recently solidified their cooperation in the agricultural sector by signing a memorandum of cooperation.
records.description: Iraq and Lebanon have recently solidified their cooperation in the agricultural sector by signing a memorandum of cooperation. The agreement, inked by the Ministers of Agriculture of both countries, Dr. Abbas Jaber Al-Maliki and Mr. Abbas Al-Hajj Hassan, aims to establish a framework for future collaboration beneficial to stakeholders in the agricultural industry. The memorandum seeks to stimulate trade and economic activity through joint projects and increased trade volume. Furthermore, it intends to improve land transport via the transit route linking Lebanon to Gulf countries and Iran through Syria and Iraq. As part of the collaboration, Lebanese companies are invited to participate in Iraq's agricultural week organized by the Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture in early March.

records.title: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), in collaboration with the Directorate of Agriculture in Ninawa Governorate and the Univers...
records.description: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), in collaboration with the Directorate of Agriculture in Ninawa Governorate and the University of Mosul, is undertaking a transformative agricultural project aimed at enhancing food security and sustainability for small-holder farmers in Ninawa governorate. Through this multi-year initiative, over 500 farmers are being trained in conservation agriculture, water management, and modern irrigation techniques to mitigate the adverse impacts of the climate crisis on agricultural production and livelihoods. By integrating conservation agriculture methods with modern irrigation practices, the project seeks to improve natural resource management, reduce labor and cost for farmers, and address water scarcity in arid regions. Moreover, the initiative aims to bolster biodiversity and long-term resilience by promoting soil conservation, native seeds usage, and drought-resistant species cultivation. Supported by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), this project underscores WFP's commitment to fostering sustainable agricultural development in Iraq and supporting vulnerable communities in adapting to climate change.
records.institution: World Food Programme of the United Nations

records.title: The International Institute for Central Asia (IICA) hosted a meeting with Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Uzbekistan Yousef Al-Otaibi to ex...
records.description: The International Institute for Central Asia (IICA) hosted a meeting with Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Uzbekistan Yousef Al-Otaibi to explore avenues for enhancing cooperation between the two nations. Discussions revolved around the outcomes of the historic Summit of the Heads of State of Central Asia and the Cooperation Council of the Arab States of the Gulf, which catalyzed collaboration in various sectors including trade, transport, agriculture, industrial cooperation, green energy, digital economy, and innovation. Emphasis was placed on implementing initiatives proposed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, such as the Agreement on Friendship, Regional Connectivity and Cooperation, and the creation of a single visa-free tourist space "Gulf – Central Asia." Highlighting the development of partnerships in tourism, the meeting underscored the strategic significance of visa regulation innovations, including the introduction of electronic visas for Uzbekistan tourists visiting Saudi Arabia. The parties also discussed plans to increase mutual air flights from the current 28 to 50 flights per week, illustrating the commitment to bolstering bilateral relations and fostering collaboration between expert and analytical communities of Central Asia and the Gulf countries.

records.title: The Bir el-Kassaâ wholesale market in Tunisia is experiencing a notable upswing in the supply of fruits and vegetables, signaling an impr...
records.description: The Bir el-Kassaâ wholesale market in Tunisia is experiencing a notable upswing in the supply of fruits and vegetables, signaling an improvement compared to the previous year, as affirmed by Minister of Trade and Export Development, Kalthoum Ben Rejeb. With the advent of the holy month of Ramadan on the horizon, the minister conducted a comprehensive inspection of the market to gauge the inventory status and pricing dynamics of wholesale produce. Expressing satisfaction with the available quantities and prevailing prices, deemed reasonable and within reach for consumers, Ben Rejeb underscored the importance of vigilant oversight at the retail level to ensure price stability. Emphasizing the imperative for adherence to international standards and leveraging best practices from analogous markets to enhance operational efficacy, she advocated for bolstering the Tunisian wholesale markets company's activities and service offerings to attract more suppliers. In line with this vision, Sofiène Tarmiz, the Chairman and CEO of the wholesale markets company, unveiled ambitious plans for the year, including the installation of automated barriers in key sections like the fish pavilion and parking areas, alongside the widespread implementation of electronic invoicing systems across municipal markets, in response to growing demand.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Trade and Export Development

records.title: Masdar City, Abu Dhabi's center for sustainability and innovation, has inaugurated its indoor vertical farm in collaboration with Alesca...
records.description: Masdar City, Abu Dhabi's center for sustainability and innovation, has inaugurated its indoor vertical farm in collaboration with Alesca Technologies, an agricultural technology (AgriTech) firm, to tackle food security challenges. Utilizing automated equipment and AI software, the project grows various fresh leafy greens, lettuce, and herbs devoid of harmful chemicals, offering ready-to-eat produce. Housed in repurposed shipping containers near Masdar City's Eco-Plaza, the farm is already operational, with plans to expand further. Once fully operational, it aims to produce over 650 kilograms of leafy greens per month year-round, while consuming 90-95% less water than conventional farms. The initiative serves to educate visitors about vertical farming's potential in addressing food security challenges and minimizing environmental impact. Masdar City's collaboration with Alesca underscores its commitment to innovative climate change solutions and multifunctional land use, essential in densely populated urban areas. Alesca Technologies' involvement aligns with Masdar City's AgriTech cluster, demonstrating a concerted effort towards sustainable food production and technological advancement.

records.title: Culture Minister Nevine al-Kilany and Country Director of the British Council Mark Howard convened to discuss enhancing cultural cooperat...
records.description: Culture Minister Nevine al-Kilany and Country Director of the British Council Mark Howard convened to discuss enhancing cultural cooperation and exchange between their respective entities in the forthcoming period. Assistant Culture Minister Mohamed Abdel Dayem also participated in the meeting. Howard provided insights into the ongoing cooperation since the signing of a protocol between the ministry and the council in November, as well as the progress of a training program aimed at supporting policymakers in cultural and creative industries. The meeting emphasized the significance of expanding cooperation over the next three years, particularly in the realm of the creative economy.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Oman's Environmental Authority has issued a phased plan to eliminate all forms of plastic shopping bags within a specified timeframe, acc...
records.description: Oman's Environmental Authority has issued a phased plan to eliminate all forms of plastic shopping bags within a specified timeframe, according to Decision No. 2024/8. This decision aligns with Oman's environmental protection and pollution prevention laws established by Royal Decrees No. 114/2001 and No. 106/2020, and Ministerial Decision No. 2020/23. The new regulation prohibits companies, institutions, and individuals from using single-use plastic bags and other plastic materials thinner than 50 micrometers. Violators of this regulation will face administrative fines ranging from 50 to 1,000 Omani Rials, with increased penalties for repeated offenses. This policy becomes effective the day after its publication in the official gazette, enforcing a gradual ban on plastic shopping bags according to an attached schedule.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Environment Authority (EA) of Oman has issued Decision No.
records.description: The Environment Authority (EA) of Oman has issued Decision No. 8/2024 to gradually phase out all types of plastic shopping bags by January 2027, with specific sectors targeted in six-month intervals. Starting from July 1, 2024, pharmacies, hospitals, and clinics will be required to stop using plastic bags, followed by other sectors such as shops selling fabrics, textiles, clothing, furniture, and household supplies by January 1, 2025. The decision, which has been in the works since 2012, aims to curb plastic bag usage and promote environmentally friendly alternatives. EA has collaborated with various authorities to facilitate the transition, including initiatives to distribute eco-friendly bags and raise public awareness. Violators of the ban will face fines ranging from RO50 to RO1,000, with penalties doubling for repeat offenses. The phased approach aligns with Oman Vision 2040's goal of achieving sustainable development and fostering a cleaner, healthier environment for future generations.

records.title: In the past five years (2019 - 2023), Saudi Arabia's non-oil exports to Africa have surged to more than SAR128 billion ($34.1 billion), w...
records.description: In the past five years (2019 - 2023), Saudi Arabia's non-oil exports to Africa have surged to more than SAR128 billion ($34.1 billion), with the chemicals and polymers sector leading the list with exports exceeding SAR83 billion ($22 billion), as reported by SPA. Following closely, the construction-materials sector recorded exports exceeding SAR10 billion, while the packaging sector followed with exports of over SAR9 billion. Key exported products include polypropylene, polyethylene, and fertilizers, with Egypt, Algeria, South Africa, Morocco, Sudan, Kenya, and Nigeria among the top importers of Saudi products from a list of 55 African countries. The strategic, commercial, and economic relations between Saudi Arabia and Africa are robust and deeply rooted, driven by mutual interests in progress and prosperity. To further enhance these ties, the Saudi Exports Development Authority (Saudi Exports) is actively engaging with African markets, organizing trade missions and participating in specialized international exhibitions across the continent to promote Saudi products and services and facilitate commercial partnerships.

records.title: Saudi Arabia has recently deposited $250 million as the second tranche of economic aid to the legitimate Yemeni government, part of a lar...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has recently deposited $250 million as the second tranche of economic aid to the legitimate Yemeni government, part of a larger $1.2 billion package aimed at alleviating Yemen's economic struggles. This aid, directed by King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, targets the budget deficit, salaries, wages, operating expenses, and economic reforms, reflecting Saudi Arabia's commitment to Yemen's security, stability, and development. With previous economic aid totaling around $11.2 billion from 2012 to 2023, Saudi Arabia's ongoing support has significantly impacted Yemen's economy, stabilizing prices, boosting GDP growth, and strengthening the Yemeni riyal. Additionally, Saudi Arabia has provided grants for oil derivatives to generate electricity, creating job opportunities and supporting logistical movement, while implementing numerous development projects through the Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen to enhance vital sectors and government capabilities.

records.title: Egypt and Bulgaria recently solidified their cooperation with the signing of three pivotal agreements, marking a significant milestone in...
records.description: Egypt and Bulgaria recently solidified their cooperation with the signing of three pivotal agreements, marking a significant milestone in their bilateral relations. Among these agreements is a memorandum of understanding focused on collaborative efforts in the natural gas sector. Furthermore, both nations have mutually exempted holders of diplomatic and service passports from short-stay visa requirements, underscoring their commitment to facilitating ease of travel between the two countries. Additionally, an agreement on cooperation between the defense ministries of Egypt and Bulgaria highlights their shared commitment to bolstering security and defense ties. The joint committee meeting, chaired by Egypt’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Sameh Shoukry and Bulgaria’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Maria Gabriel, reaffirmed their dedication to deepening bilateral relations in alignment with the EU-Egypt partnership. Emphasizing economic and trade cooperation, both sides expressed a keen interest in expanding trade and investment opportunities, particularly in the realms of digital innovation and sustainable practices. Discussions also centered on leveraging the potential of the Suez Canal Economic Zone to attract Bulgarian investment. Moreover, collaboration in information technology and efforts to enhance connectivity through improved transport links and airline cooperation were key focal points of the meeting, demonstrating a shared vision for a more interconnected future between Egypt and Bulgaria.

records.title: Egypt is embarking on a significant initiative to enhance its wheat storage infrastructure by establishing six new wheat silos in 2024, r...
records.description: Egypt is embarking on a significant initiative to enhance its wheat storage infrastructure by establishing six new wheat silos in 2024, requiring an investment of US$145.6 million. The French Development Agency (AFD) will contribute US$61.5 million to the project, with the Egyptian government financing the remaining US$84.1 million. This strategic move aims to increase the country's wheat storage capacity by 420,000 tons, reaching a total capacity of 4.620 million tons, approximately 10% of the nation's current total capacity. With plans to further augment the storage capacity of state-owned wheat silos by 2.5 to 3 million tons within the next three to four years, Egypt aims to achieve a capacity ranging between 6.4 and 7 million tons. This initiative aligns with Egypt's efforts to bolster its wheat reserves, as evidenced by the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) revealing intentions to purchase over 5 million tonnes of wheat in 2024 through international tenders—an increase of 500,000 tonnes compared to the previous year. With domestic wheat consumption exceeding production, resulting in a significant import deficit, Egypt's commitment to fortifying domestic agricultural production is underscored by its aim to procure approximately 3.5 million tons of locally produced wheat in the upcoming season.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Tunisia is bracing itself for an unprecedented challenge in the upcoming 2023-2024 season, with projected cereal import requirements soar...
records.description: Tunisia is bracing itself for an unprecedented challenge in the upcoming 2023-2024 season, with projected cereal import requirements soaring to a record 4.7 million tonnes, as reported by the Global Information and Early Warning System on Food and Agriculture (Smiar) of the FAO. This staggering increase of 80% from the previous year's average needs is primarily attributed to the adverse impact of the winter drought in 2023, resulting in a meager harvest of only 700 thousand quintals. Of this paltry yield, a mere 302 thousand quintals were officially collected, with the remainder retained by cereal growers for personal consumption and seed reserves. Despite these precarious circumstances, Tunisian authorities reassure that cereal cost management will remain manageable, ensuring price stability and market availability. Encouragingly, cereal prices have shown a downward trend since 2022, with durum wheat prices dropping by 25%, soft wheat by 22%, and barley by 22% until September 2023. To address the heightened demand, Tunisia is forging partnerships with key international suppliers, notably France and Russia. Philippe Houssal, director of international relations at Interserial France, projects France to cater to approximately 35% of Tunisia's soft wheat requirements for flour milling and 50% of its barley needs during the 2023-2024 campaign. Russia, renowned for its grain exports, has also pledged support during a recent visit by its Foreign Minister, Sergei Lavrov. With Tunisia expected to import 1.1 million tonnes of soft wheat, 1.1 million tonnes of durum wheat, 0.8 million tonnes of barley, and 0.85 million tonnes of corn grains for the upcoming season, ensuring adequate grain supplies remains a critical priority for the nation.
records.institution: Global Information and Early Warning System. on Food and Agriculture (Smiar)

records.title: During a plenary session at the National People's Assembly (APN), Mohamed Arkab, the Minister of Energy and Mines, revealed a significant...
records.description: During a plenary session at the National People's Assembly (APN), Mohamed Arkab, the Minister of Energy and Mines, revealed a significant achievement in rural electrification, with over 52,000 farms out of the planned 84,000 connected to electricity by the end of 2023. This milestone, representing 62% of the targeted agricultural operations, marks a crucial advancement in rural development and infrastructure modernization within the agricultural sector. Minister Arkab outlined that of the 84,762 planned agricultural operations, 52,741 have been successfully connected, with 45,245 already operational. Additionally, 21,327 operations are in the study or launch phase, while 10,694 are currently under construction. The minister emphasized that the year 2024 will witness the completion of connection operations for all scheduled agricultural operations, reflecting the government's commitment to enhancing the country's energy infrastructure and bolstering the agricultural sector. The electrification of these farms is poised to improve working conditions for farmers, enhance sector productivity, facilitate the adoption of modern technologies, and promote agricultural mechanization, fostering efficiency and sustainability in agriculture. This initiative underscores the government's dedication to rural development and agriculture promotion, with access to electricity in rural areas expected to unlock new economic prospects, spur investment, and fortify local communities.
records.institution: Algerian Ministry of Energy and Mines

records.title: In response to the pressing issue of dwindling precipitation levels, the government of Morocco is proactively implementing innovative str...
records.description: In response to the pressing issue of dwindling precipitation levels, the government of Morocco is proactively implementing innovative strategies for the efficient management of water resources within the agricultural sector. This emphasis on water conservation and rational utilization was underscored during a recent press briefing by Mustapha Baitas, the Minister Delegate responsible for Relations with Parliament and Government Spokesperson, following the weekly Government Council. Baitas emphasized the necessity of exploring viable alternatives for crop irrigation to enhance production output, stabilize market prices, and safeguard rural employment opportunities. Stressing the inseparable link between agriculture and water, the minister called for constructive dialogue regarding water resource management in the agricultural domain. Concrete measures have already been initiated to tackle the challenges posed by diminishing rainfall, including the establishment of a hydraulic basin in the Dakhla region by 2026, which will be supplied with treated water. This initiative mirrors the success of the Souss irrigated basin in preserving agricultural productivity. Additionally, the government has enacted emergency measures to counteract the significant decline in water resources allocated for agricultural use in recent years. Such proactive approaches underscore the government's dedication to adapting agricultural policies to contemporary environmental challenges, ensuring the resilience and prosperity of the agricultural sector, a cornerstone of the national economy.

records.title: The year 2023 posed substantial challenges for Moroccan exports of frozen products, particularly in the fruits and vegetables sector, wit...
records.description: The year 2023 posed substantial challenges for Moroccan exports of frozen products, particularly in the fruits and vegetables sector, with exports hitting their lowest levels in at least six years. From January to October of that year, Morocco shipped less than 70,000 tonnes of frozen fruits, berries, and vegetables, indicating a notable decline exacerbated by adverse weather conditions and intensified international competition. The period from February to May 2023 proved especially difficult, marked by storms, cold spells, and drought, significantly impacting strawberry plantations, a traditionally dominant export. Frozen raspberry exports also faced hurdles, with oversupply in the European Union market dampening Moroccan exports. While frozen vegetable exports showed some improvement compared to 2022, reaching double the volume, they still constituted a relatively small portion of the overall export volume. Geographically, Europe remained the primary market for Moroccan exports, but concerning trends emerged, with notable declines in exports to the EU and North America offset by modest increases in other regions, signaling shifting trade dynamics amidst challenging conditions.

records.title: Salman Fazlur Rahman, the private industry and investment adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, revealed Saudi Arabia's interest i...
records.description: Salman Fazlur Rahman, the private industry and investment adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, revealed Saudi Arabia's interest in establishing a special economic zone (SEZ) in Payra, located in the Patuakhali district of Bangladesh's Barisal division. During his recent three-day visit to Saudi Arabia, Rahman stated that Bangladesh is also eager to reciprocate by offering Saudi Arabia an economic zone within its borders. He mentioned that Saudi Arabia's investment minister has expressed interest in developing an economic zone in Payra. Additionally, Rahman announced Bangladesh's plans to establish a urea fertilizer factory in Saudi Arabia through a joint venture, with the intention of importing all fertilizer produced there.

records.title: Recently, the National Association of Algerian Traders and Craftsmen organized a significant meeting at the Specialized Technological Ins...
records.description: Recently, the National Association of Algerian Traders and Craftsmen organized a significant meeting at the Specialized Technological Institute for Training in Animal Production, aiming to foster collaboration between Algerian and Tunisian stakeholders in the beekeeping sector. Led by Tahar Boulenouar, the gathering welcomed representatives from the Tunisian Association of the Honey Festival and the Promotion of Sidi Alouane Heritage, highlighting the importance of cross-border partnerships in honey production and marketing. Beekeeping holds considerable economic potential, yet Algeria's current production, ranging between 600 and 700 tonnes annually, falls short of global demand, estimated at 2 million tonnes. Recognizing this gap, the National Association of Algerian Traders and Artisans is committed to enhancing national honey production through training and partnerships, aiming to equip beekeepers with the necessary tools to thrive in the global market. The meeting also served as a platform for collaboration with various sectors, including agriculture, commerce, and crafts, with plans to facilitate beekeepers' access to support services through agreements with entities like the National Agency for Micro-Enterprise Management (ANGEM). Fathi Sefari and Nadjib Benaïcha, leaders of the Tunisian Association, emphasized the potential for fruitful partnerships between beekeepers from Algeria and Tunisia, leveraging favorable political, geographical, and historical conditions. Their exchange of expertise and experiences signals a promising collaboration that could bolster beekeeping in both countries and cater to the increasing demand in the global honey market.
records.institution: National Association of Algerian Traders and Craftsmen

records.title: Egypt has decided to extend its partnership with Saudi Advanced Energy Systems (ADES) for three offshore platforms, with the extension va...
records.description: Egypt has decided to extend its partnership with Saudi Advanced Energy Systems (ADES) for three offshore platforms, with the extension valued at $120 million, according to sources cited by Asharq Bloomberg. ADES currently operates ten offshore drilling rigs in Egypt as part of its larger fleet of 49 rigs. In December 2023, ADES announced securing a service contract agreement with the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) to boost production in key oil brownfields, specifically the SUCO and OSOCO fields. This contract, part of a consortium with a local partner, initially spans ten years with an option to extend for another ten years. Saudi Arabia has expressed its commitment to bolster bilateral trade with Egypt, aiming for a target of $100 billion. Fayez Alharbi, the Second Vice Chairman of the Federation of Saudi Chambers, announced this goal in November, while Ahmed Samir, the Minister of Trade and Industry, disclosed that Saudi investments in Egypt amounted to $6.3 billion across 7,444 projects, spanning various sectors.

records.title: President Abdelfattah El Sisi, in a meeting with Prime Minister Moustafa Madbouli and Finance Minister Mohamed Maeet, announced significa...
records.description: President Abdelfattah El Sisi, in a meeting with Prime Minister Moustafa Madbouli and Finance Minister Mohamed Maeet, announced significant economic measures aimed at alleviating financial burdens on Egyptian citizens. These measures include raising the minimum wage for civil servants to LE6000, increasing monthly salaries by LE1000-1200, and expanding tax exemption thresholds to LE60,000. Additionally, a comprehensive social protection package valued at LE180 billion will be implemented, featuring a 15% increase in pensions for 13 million citizens, LE41 billion allocated to pension programs, and LE15 billion designated for salary increases for various professionals including doctors, nurses, teachers, and university staff. President Sisi's directive aims to mitigate the impact of global economic crises and inflation on citizens while supporting essential workers and public servants.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Omani-Scottish waste-to-value startup X2E is poised to invest $1.6 billion in projects across the alternative fuel value chain, including...
records.description: Omani-Scottish waste-to-value startup X2E is poised to invest $1.6 billion in projects across the alternative fuel value chain, including biodiesel and Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), over the next two years. CEO John Jones revealed plans to cultivate Camelina seeds for biofuel production initially, with future expansion into SAF. The company aims for vertical integration, with separate entities managing feedstock cultivation, water treatment, seed extraction, and refinery operations. X2E is collaborating with partners for each venture, with investments earmarked for various stages of the value chain, from agriculture to biodiesel and SAF production. The first capital close is expected in the second quarter of 2024, with construction projected to take another 18 months. Additionally, X2E plans to acquire biodiesel plants globally, with expansions aimed at tripling current capacity. Discussions for contract farming of Camelina are underway in Africa and Malaysia, signaling X2E's global ambitions in the alternative fuel sector.

records.title: Bühler, a renowned provider of milling and food processing technologies, is eyeing promising rice processing opportunities in Saudi Arabia.
records.description: Bühler, a renowned provider of milling and food processing technologies, is eyeing promising rice processing opportunities in Saudi Arabia. Mohamed Jebabra, Bühler's Country Manager in Saudi Arabia, highlighted the growing interest among existing customers and new investors in leveraging the immense potential of the rice processing market. With Saudi Arabia being one of the largest importers of rice globally, at 1.35 million tonnes annually, and facing concerns about food security amid rising global rice prices, there is a pressing need to diversify food strategies. Jebabra emphasized the demand for Bühler's state-of-the-art rice processing technology, particularly in light of the government's initiatives to localize food production and enhance food security. Bühler's comprehensive storage solutions and advanced technology, coupled with their longstanding presence and local capabilities in Saudi Arabia since 1978, position them as a reliable partner in meeting the evolving needs of the market. Moreover, Bühler offers tailored customer service and performance assessment workshops, underscoring their commitment to supporting efficiency enhancement and sustainable growth in rice processing operations.

records.title: Tunisia is poised to embark on a new phase in its drive to attract investors and invigorate the national economy through an innovative dr...
records.description: Tunisia is poised to embark on a new phase in its drive to attract investors and invigorate the national economy through an innovative draft decree. Naceur Ridane, project manager to the Minister of State Domains and Land Affairs, revealed that a decree concerning the allocation of non-agricultural state land is nearing finalization. In an announcement to the TAP Agency, Ridane outlined that the decree, currently undergoing finalization following a ministry headquarters meeting, will present fresh avenues for investors engaged in projects of national significance. The decree proposes two allocation methods: a symbolic allocation in dinars, offering land at a nominal cost, and a long-term rental option extending up to 50 years and beyond, aiming to provide accessible land for large-scale economic ventures. Crucially, regardless of the chosen option, state land remains state property, ensuring the government retains the right to reclaim land if projects are halted. Aligned with Article 19 of Law 2019-47 of May 29, 2019, focused on enhancing the investment climate, this initiative complements existing incentives like financial, customs, and tax benefits, underscoring Tunisia's commitment to fostering a business-friendly environment to spur economic growth and innovation. Against the backdrop of the current economic landscape, this decree holds strategic significance, offering investors greater flexibility and enhanced legal certainty. By making state land available, Tunisia reaffirms its resolve to attract investments and bolster its regional economic standing.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of State Domains and Land Affairs

records.title: Despite economic challenges both regionally and globally, Minister of Trade and Industry Ahmed Samir announced on Tuesday that Egypt has...
records.description: Despite economic challenges both regionally and globally, Minister of Trade and Industry Ahmed Samir announced on Tuesday that Egypt has achieved significant growth in its commodity exports. According to a report from the General Organization for Exports and Imports, Egypt's commodity exports surged to $35.631 billion in the previous year. Minister Samir attributed this increase to heightened demand for Egyptian goods, facilitated by the opening of new export markets. He also noted a reduction in imports, which decreased by 14 percent to approximately $72 billion compared to $83 billion in the previous year. Notably, Egypt's exports to various regions saw positive trends, with exports to African countries rising by 7 percent, exceeding $2 billion, exports to Arab countries surpassing $13 billion, exports to EU countries reaching over $9 billion, exports to the United States totaling around $2 billion, and exports to other countries amounting to more than $9 billion.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: Egypt Commences 2nd Phase of Economic Reforms
records.description: Egypt has initiated the second phase of its economic reforms spanning from 2021 to 2024, aiming to establish a diverse, competitive, and sustainable economy, announced Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly during his address at the 33rd Summit of the APR Forum of Heads of State and Government. Highlighting the government's commitment to achieving balanced, green, and comprehensive growth, Madbouly outlined measures to attract more domestic and foreign private sector investments, including the issuance of a State Ownership Policy document in 2022. This document delineates sectors earmarked for government withdrawal, aiming to bolster the private sector's role in the economy. Notably, Egypt has allocated approximately EGP 15.3 billion to support small, medium, and micro enterprises, underscoring its dedication to fostering their development. Madbouly also underscored Egypt's intention to bolster trade and investment ties with African nations, leveraging its membership in COMESA. These proposed structural reforms align with the ongoing reform agenda initiated in 2016, particularly in the financial and monetary sectors, in collaboration with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). As part of the state ownership policy, the government plans to exit from 62 sectors, reduce involvement in 56 sectors, and increase participation in 76 others, according to the cabinet's statement, reflecting a strategic shift towards greater private sector involvement in Egypt's economic landscape.

records.title: Egypt is set to conclude the sale of shares of the National Company for the Sale and Distribution of Petroleum Products (Wataniya) within...
records.description: Egypt is set to conclude the sale of shares of the National Company for the Sale and Distribution of Petroleum Products (Wataniya) within the next 48 hours, according to Minister of Planning Hala al-Saeed. This announcement signals the impending reveal of the buyer for the highly anticipated deal. Saeed indicated that the government plans to finalize the sale of wind power plants in Jabal al-Zeit by the end of March, emphasizing that the rationalization of expenditures will not hinder economic growth projections, which are expected to reach three percent for the 2023-2024 fiscal year. Wataniya, currently owned by the National Service Projects Organization (NSPO) of the Egyptian Armed Forces, has garnered interest from companies such as Taqa Arabia, ADNOC and ENOC of the UAE, and Petromin of Saudi Arabia. Additionally, the Jabal al-Zeit wind energy projects, boasting a total capacity of 580 MW, are nearing completion in collaboration with the Spanish government.

records.title: Minister of Trade and Industry Ahmed Samir announced that Egypt's commodity exports surged to over $35 billion in 2023, despite economic...
records.description: Minister of Trade and Industry Ahmed Samir announced that Egypt's commodity exports surged to over $35 billion in 2023, despite economic challenges both regionally and globally. The increase in exports was attributed to heightened demand for Egyptian goods facilitated by the opening of new export markets. Samir highlighted a decrease in Egypt's imports by 14 percent, totaling nearly $72 billion compared to $83 billion in the previous year. Additionally, he noted significant increases in exports to various regions, including African countries (up 7 percent to over $2 billion), Arab countries (over $13 billion), EU countries (more than $9 billion), and the United States (approximately $2 billion). Egyptian commodity exports to other nations amounted to more than $9 billion.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: The persistent foreign exchange shortage in Egypt, prevailing for over two years, emerges as a central concern for the nation's economy,...
records.description: The persistent foreign exchange shortage in Egypt, prevailing for over two years, emerges as a central concern for the nation's economy, particularly impacting the industrial sector, according to industry experts at a workshop hosted by the Egyptian Centre for Strategic Studies (ECSS). Mohamed El-Sewedy, head of the Federation of the Egyptian Industries (FEI), highlighted the severity of the US dollar scarcity in the local market, hindering effective expense planning for manufacturers and businesspersons. El-Sewedy emphasized the critical need for hard currency liquidity, especially in vital sectors like industry and agriculture, pivotal for Egypt's economic advancement. He advocated for a unified exchange rate to restore confidence among foreign investors. Additionally, El-Sewedy addressed the issue of escalating interest rates, reaching approximately 25 percent, asserting their disproportionate impact on the investment climate and the industry sector, exacerbating local market product prices. Hassan Allam, CEO of Hassan Allam Holding, echoed concerns about the dearth of US dollar liquidity, citing it as a key deterrent for foreign investors. Allam underscored the significance of the private sector in driving growth, particularly in the construction sector, which has significantly contributed to Egypt's infrastructure development. He stressed the importance of private sector involvement in government projects and urged for more initiatives to enhance collaboration between the public and private sectors. Sherif El-Kholy, head of MENA at Actis, emphasized the importance of completing ongoing loan agreements and expediting the government's IPO program to attract foreign direct investments and alleviate the US dollar shortage crisis. El-Kholy emphasized the need for a level playing field between public and private sectors, ensuring fair competition and unrestricted market access for investors. Contrary to El-Sewedy's stance, Ahmed Sobhy, Banque Misr's equity sector head and Misr Capital CEO, advocated for tightening the Egyptian monetary policy by raising key interest rates to stimulate investor interest in the local market. He emphasized the importance of sustainable economic growth, long-term vision, and fair market competition to address the ongoing economic challenges in Egypt.
records.institution: The Egyptian Centre for Strategic Studies (ECSS)

records.title: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture announced that Saudi Arabia has lifted restrictions on importing strawberries from Egypt, effective...
records.description: The Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture announced that Saudi Arabia has lifted restrictions on importing strawberries from Egypt, effective February 1. The decision comes after Saudi Arabia placed a temporary hold on issuing import permits for Egyptian strawberries. The ministry clarified that the previous measure was an internal regulatory action by the Kingdom, applicable to various agricultural imports from all countries, and was not specifically targeted at Egyptian strawberries. The decision aimed to regulate the domestic market in Saudi Arabia based on supply and demand dynamics, rather than concerns related to quarantine or health issues with Egyptian strawberries.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Tunisia is currently witnessing a remarkable olive picking season, with progress reaching an impressive 80% to date, as reported by the N...
records.description: Tunisia is currently witnessing a remarkable olive picking season, with progress reaching an impressive 80% to date, as reported by the National Oil Office (ONH). This advancement represents a significant increase compared to the same period last year when the rate stood at 68%, signaling notable progress for this season. However, while the overall progress is substantial, governorates in the center-west, including Kairouan, Sidi Bouzid, and Kasserine, which collectively contribute two-thirds of the national olive oil production, exhibit a more modest progress rate, not surpassing 55%. Despite this, their combined production is estimated at 74 thousand tonnes, constituting 35% of the country's total output. This season's optimistic outlook suggests a plentiful harvest for Tunisia, consolidating its status as a leading global producer of olive oil. The favorable weather conditions have contributed to an early harvest and enhanced yield, promising positive economic benefits for farmers and stakeholders in the olive oil industry, thereby reinforcing financial stability in these regions. Nevertheless, while the national figures are promising, the ONH underscores the importance of closely monitoring progress in the central-west governorates. Implementing initiatives to optimize harvesting and processing procedures could further maximize production potential in these crucial regions. Tunisia's continued prominence in the global olive oil market underscores promising prospects for the country's economy, bolstered by the optimism surrounding this season's harvest.

records.title: In the face of challenging climatic conditions, Algeria, the second-largest consumer of wheat in Africa, is poised to experience its high...
records.description: In the face of challenging climatic conditions, Algeria, the second-largest consumer of wheat in Africa, is poised to experience its highest wheat imports in eight years, according to the latest report from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA). Adverse weather conditions have led to a projected 27% decline in local wheat production for the 2023/2024 season, amounting to 3.7 million tonnes, with drought affecting approximately 40% of the total cereal cultivation area. To address this situation, Algeria is expected to import 8.7 million tonnes of wheat for the upcoming campaign, a 7.4% increase compared to the previous season, with consumption needs projected to rise to 11.2 million tonnes. This increased dependency on wheat imports highlights the importance of ensuring a stable and reliable supply to safeguard the nation's food security, while underscoring the urgency of investing in sustainable agricultural solutions to bolster the sector's resilience against future challenges.
