records.title: Bahrain's food industry is set to showcase its offerings at Gulfood, the world's largest food exhibition, taking place at the Dubai World...
records.description: Bahrain's food industry is set to showcase its offerings at Gulfood, the world's largest food exhibition, taking place at the Dubai World Trade Centre from February 19 to 23. With the Bahraini Pavilion nearly fully booked, the event aims to support Bahraini institutions involved in the food and beverage sector, providing them with a platform to launch their exports globally and gain insights into international advancements in various areas of the industry. This initiative aligns with Bahrain's efforts to enhance food security, elevate local food production, seek sustainable solutions, and attract investments in the food sector. The significant turnout underscores the valuable prospects recognized by Bahraini companies, offering opportunities to showcase products, services, and innovations alongside global counterparts. The Bahraini Pavilion will feature prominent companies and brands such as Awal Dairy Company, Deeko Bahrain, and Kazerooni Brothers, alongside a diverse representation from notable international food and beverage companies. Participation in the exhibition presents a unique opportunity for Bahraini companies to forge agreements, expand distribution networks, establish a stronger international presence, and contribute to the kingdom's position as a prominent global hub in the food and beverage industry.

records.title: Egypt aims to strengthen its cooperation with the World Bank in managing state-owned enterprises and enhancing their efficiency, Prime Mi...
records.description: Egypt aims to strengthen its cooperation with the World Bank in managing state-owned enterprises and enhancing their efficiency, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly expressed during a meeting with bank officials. Stephane Guimbert, the World Bank's country director for Egypt, Yemen, and Djibouti, presented proposals to support the governance of Egypt’s state-owned companies, emphasizing their alignment with the State Ownership Policy Document for comprehensive reform. Minister of International Cooperation Rania Al-Mashat underscored the importance of collaboration to maximize private sector participation in investments and highlighted successful initiatives, including the initial public offering (IPO) program supported by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the World Bank's financial arm. The government plans to offer stakes in 35 state-owned companies to strategic investors by June 2024, aiming to expand private sector participation in public investments to 65 percent within three years, as outlined in the State Ownership Policy Document initiated in late 2022.

records.title: Egyptian Minister of International Cooperation Rania al Mashaat announced that Egypt has benefited significantly from financing provided...
records.description: Egyptian Minister of International Cooperation Rania al Mashaat announced that Egypt has benefited significantly from financing provided by the Islamic Development Bank Group (IsDB), with the bank funding 382 projects across various sectors in the country. These projects encompass domains such as electricity, energy, agriculture, education, health, industry, and more, with total funding amounting to approximately $21 billion. Of these projects, 332 have been completed, while 50 are still underway. Mashaat emphasized the ministry's commitment to enhancing cooperation with the IsDB in the future, aligning with Egypt's ambitious development plan to accelerate sustainable development in accordance with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). She highlighted cooperation activities with the IsDB in transportation projects and support for the private sector through the Private Sector Portal. Additionally, Mashaat stressed the importance of cooperation with the IsDB in implementing projects addressing environmental impact and combating climate change. The IsDB President, Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser, highlighted the growing partnership between the bank and Egypt, expressing the bank's interest in financing priority projects for the Egyptian government and supporting cooperation between Egypt and African countries.

records.title: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly chaired a meeting aimed at ensuring the availability of goods and products across Egypt ahead of the Rama...
records.description: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly chaired a meeting aimed at ensuring the availability of goods and products across Egypt ahead of the Ramadan season. The meeting, attended by several ministers, focused on reviewing initiatives and coordinating efforts among ministries to address challenges related to fluctuating prices of essential goods. Measures to enhance the inflow of foreign currency into the market were highlighted as part of the government's strategy to stabilize prices. Efforts to attract foreign direct investment and agreements with the International Monetary Fund were discussed as means to ensure a sufficient supply of goods at reasonable prices. Additionally, support for the industrial sector and the provision of necessary raw materials were emphasized to contribute to stability in prices and the overall market. Discussions also centered on expanding distribution networks and establishing stable outlets nationwide to meet citizens' needs efficiently. Furthermore, collaborations with commercial chains and producers were highlighted to ensure the availability of goods and products across the country.

records.title: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly discussed with officials from Samsung Electronics the potential for increased investments in Egypt, empha...
records.description: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly discussed with officials from Samsung Electronics the potential for increased investments in Egypt, emphasizing the government's incentives to encourage local industries and capitalize on export opportunities. Present at the meeting were Trade Minister Ahmed Samir and Hossam Heiba from the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), indicating a concerted effort to explore collaboration prospects. Madbouly praised Samsung's significant contributions to Egypt's electronic appliance market, highlighting its role as a key supplier to the Ministry of Education. The discussion also included Samsung's plans to boost exports from Egypt to the European market, capitalizing on incentives provided through a partnership agreement with the EU, thereby fostering stronger trade relations and market expansion.

records.title: Waleid Gamal El-Dein, Chief of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), revealed ongoing discussions regarding the establishment of a Turki...
records.description: Waleid Gamal El-Dein, Chief of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), revealed ongoing discussions regarding the establishment of a Turkish industrial zone within the Suez Canal Economic Zone during his meeting with Turkish Ambassador to Egypt Salih Mutlu Şen. The economic zone already hosts various Turkish investments, including the "Hayat Egypt" healthcare products factory in the Sokhna area and potential textile and clothing companies in the West Qantara Industrial Zone. SCZONE highlighted its competitive advantages, such as owning six maritime ports and four industrial zones spanning 21 sectors, reaffirming its commitment to supporting investors and implementing its strategic vision for industrial localization. The Turkish Ambassador praised SCZONE's potential and expressed Turkey's eagerness to enhance partnerships, particularly in garment industries and the textile sector. Discussions also included cooperation in renewable energy fields and the establishment of a vocational training center in the West Qantara Industrial Zone to meet the demand for skilled labor in ongoing projects.

records.title: Tunisia's Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Abdelmonaem Belati, has unveiled an ambitious plan to counteract the c...
records.description: Tunisia's Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Abdelmonaem Belati, has unveiled an ambitious plan to counteract the country's declining water reserves and safeguard food security by accelerating the construction of new dams. Against the backdrop of dwindling rainfall patterns, exacerbated by climate change, the initiative aims to diversify water sources and mitigate water scarcity challenges. Emphasizing the need to reduce water demand while ensuring adequate supply, the plan prioritizes strategies such as desalination of seawater and wastewater treatment to augment usable water resources. This comprehensive approach not only addresses water security concerns but also underpins Tunisia's agricultural sector, which heavily relies on adequate water supplies for sustainable production. As Tunisia emerges as an active participant in regional water management discussions, the implementation of these innovative measures holds promise not only for the country's resilience but also as a potential model for addressing global water crises.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: During a recent Council of Ministers meeting chaired by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, strategic decisions regarding digitization, pilot...
records.description: During a recent Council of Ministers meeting chaired by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, strategic decisions regarding digitization, pilot farms, and the status of imams took center stage. The meeting focused on accelerating the pace of digitalization efforts to transition the country into a more advanced digital era, with the president emphasizing the need for progress reports to be presented promptly for further evaluation. Regarding pilot farms, the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development was directed to redefine their concept and integrate them into the national production process, particularly emphasizing their role in addressing deficits, notably in the pulse sector. Additionally, President Tebboune commended the efforts of Sonelgaz company executives and workers, acknowledging their positive impact on the agriculture and national production sectors, highlighting the significance of intersectoral collaboration for overall development.

records.title: Egypt’s Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, and the Ambassador of Tunisia to Egypt, Mohammed bin Youssef, convened t...
records.description: Egypt’s Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, and the Ambassador of Tunisia to Egypt, Mohammed bin Youssef, convened to discuss deepening cooperation in the health sector. The Tunisian ambassador conveyed greetings from Ali Al-Murabit, the Tunisian Minister of Health, highlighting the robust bilateral relations. Conversations focused on exchanging expertise in medical tourism, with Tunisia's prominence in seawater treatment techniques noted. Discussions also revolved around enhancing collaboration in the pharmaceutical industry, aiming to expand market reach in Africa and Francophone countries. Minister Abdel Ghaffar directed efforts to review existing agreements, reactivate joint technical committees, and prepare for an upcoming visit to Tunisia, underscoring Egypt's commitment to fostering healthcare partnerships.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population

records.title: Egyptian carrot grower, AfriGoodGrows, expands operations to 170 hectares and invests in top-tier equipment to meet surging demand, inclu...
records.description: Egyptian carrot grower, AfriGoodGrows, expands operations to 170 hectares and invests in top-tier equipment to meet surging demand, including a hydrocooler and vega polisher, upgrading its processing line to handle 3-6 tons per hour. CEO Zayed Lasheen highlights the exceptional 50% increase in volume compared to the previous season, attributing Egypt's prominence in the carrot market to cost-effectiveness and superior quality, particularly amid rising energy costs in Europe. Despite a dip in demand from Gulf countries, Africa, and Jordan, there is sustained interest from the UK, the Netherlands, Russia, and France. Egypt emerged as the EU's third-largest carrot supplier in 2022/23, driven by local harvest issues in EU countries like Poland, emphasizing Egypt's competitive advantage in offering carrots at up to 40% lower prices.

records.description: Rania A. Al-Mashat, Egypt’s Minister of International Cooperation, convened with Patricia Danzi, the Director General of the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, and Maya Tesavi, the Head of the Middle East and North Africa Department at the Swiss Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to discuss the forthcoming cooperation programme spanning 2025-2028 between Egypt and Switzerland. The meeting underscored the significance of enhancing economic cooperation between the two nations to advance national development agendas across various sectors. Al-Mashat highlighted the ongoing collaboration under the Team Europe Initiative and emphasized the evolving Egyptian-European relations within an integrated partnership framework aligned with national development priorities. Danzi emphasized Switzerland's recent disbursement of additional funds to address the humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip and surrounding areas, focusing on essential needs such as water, food, and medical care.

records.title: The fifth round of political consultations between Egypt and Singapore, held in Cairo, underscored the focus on economic cooperation alon...
records.description: The fifth round of political consultations between Egypt and Singapore, held in Cairo, underscored the focus on economic cooperation alongside diplomatic discussions. Singapore expressed its interest in organizing a visit for business leaders to explore investment prospects in tourism, hospitality, and banking sectors in Egypt. Conversely, Egyptian diplomats expressed eagerness to leverage Singapore's expertise in civil aviation, maritime transport, and port management. Discussions also encompassed key international and regional matters of mutual interest. Previously, in November, the Foreign Ministers of both nations discussed the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with Singapore acknowledging Egypt's efforts to mitigate escalation, provide humanitarian aid, and facilitate the evacuation of foreign nationals from the region.

records.title: The Ministry of Social Solidarity, in collaboration with multiple banks, orchestrated "Diarna" exhibitions across various bank locations,...
records.description: The Ministry of Social Solidarity, in collaboration with multiple banks, orchestrated "Diarna" exhibitions across various bank locations, aligning with the Central Bank of Egypt's (CBE) endeavors to bolster financial inclusion and economic empowerment for diverse societal segments. These exhibitions provided a platform for skilled artisans to showcase their crafts and artwork while granting them access to an array of banking services, including opening Economic Activity Accounts and obtaining credit to fulfill their financial requirements. The second round of "Diarna" exhibitions in 2023, part of the CBE's annual "Financial Inclusion Events," featured 111 exhibitors and aimed to extend banking services beyond branch networks to reach populations in Egyptian governorates and remote areas. Sherif Lokman, the CBE's Sub-Governor for Financial Inclusion, highlighted the collaboration's significance in advancing the state's vision for financial inclusion and supporting Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to foster job creation and achieve sustainable development goals. Mervat Sabreen, Assistant to the Minister of Social Solidarity, emphasized the exhibitions' role in backing the handicrafts sector and fostering economic development, noting the issuance of approximately 11.5 million "Meeza" cards to beneficiaries of various social programs. These exhibitions, forming part of the CBE's initiatives, aim to facilitate access to banking services for all segments of society, with recent regulations allowing entrepreneurs and freelancers to open Economic Activity Accounts using only their National IDs, thus breaking down previous barriers to formal financial services.

records.title: Morocco, grappling with the impact of a rain deficit on its agriculture yield, has introduced subsidies to encourage grain imports, parti...
records.description: Morocco, grappling with the impact of a rain deficit on its agriculture yield, has introduced subsidies to encourage grain imports, particularly soft wheat. The government, through the National Grain Agency (ONICL), announced a subsidy of MAD 2.5 (US$0.25) per quintal every two weeks for up to 1 million tons of imported soft wheat stored between February 1 and April 30. Companies eligible for the subsidy are required to maintain the stored wheat for a minimum of three months. Agriculture remains a crucial sector in Morocco, accounting for over 10% of the country's GDP, despite efforts to diversify the economy. Persistent dry conditions have led to a decline in cereal production, prompting the government to implement measures to facilitate imports. These subsidies aim to address challenges stemming from the country's cereal production shortfall exacerbated by adverse weather conditions, ensuring adequate market supply and stabilizing grain prices.

records.title: Alstom has secured a significant $540-million contract to construct the world's longest battery-powered tramway in Saudi Arabia, aligning...
records.description: Alstom has secured a significant $540-million contract to construct the world's longest battery-powered tramway in Saudi Arabia, aligning with the country's Vision 2030 plan. The project, spanning 22.4 kilometers and featuring 20 Citadis B battery trams, aims to provide access to several UNESCO World Heritage sites in Saudi Arabia's northwest region. As part of the contract awarded by the Royal Commission for Al-Ula, Alstom will handle the comprehensive design, integration, installation, testing, and commissioning of the battery-powered system, along with providing maintenance services for a minimum of 10 years. Leveraging its predictive maintenance tool, HealthHub, Alstom plans to monitor the health of trains and infrastructure using advanced data analytics. With a history of infrastructure projects spanning 70 years in Saudi Arabia, Alstom aims to deliver innovative, climate-adapted trams for both residents and tourists, emphasizing environmental stewardship in alignment with Saudi Arabia's focus. This project marks another step forward in Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 plan, which prioritizes the development of tramways and other rail systems to enhance accessibility to key cultural, tourism, agricultural, and residential destinations across the country.

records.title: The acting government in army-controlled areas of Sudan has recently implemented new duties on essential commodities and raised customs t...
records.description: The acting government in army-controlled areas of Sudan has recently implemented new duties on essential commodities and raised customs tariffs on imports in response to escalating war costs, leading to a renewed surge in prices for the public. This abrupt imposition of duties on fuel, gas, wheat, and medicine comes amidst a backdrop of soaring exchange rates, with the US Dollar now trading at an unprecedented rate against the Sudanese Pound. The ongoing conflict between the army and paramilitary forces has exacerbated an already dire economic situation, pushing millions into hunger and significantly inflating food and fuel prices. Economist Muhammad Absher highlights the government's strategy of importing basic goods while liberalizing prices and imposing fees to cover budget deficits, which, coupled with disruptions in agriculture due to the conflict, has precipitated dangerous spikes in food prices. Furthermore, the diversion of funds from social services to military expenditures has worsened the crisis, leaving civilians vulnerable to the impacts of both war and economic hardship, with little hope for immediate relief or economic reform in sight.

records.title: Egypt's Deputy Minister of Tourism and Antiquities for Tourism Affairs, Ghada Shalaby, announced plans to launch a unified platform for h...
records.description: Egypt's Deputy Minister of Tourism and Antiquities for Tourism Affairs, Ghada Shalaby, announced plans to launch a unified platform for health tourism, encompassing both medical and healing services. This initiative, to be unveiled during the Egypt Health Tourism International Conference scheduled for March 2-3, aims to position Egypt as a prominent destination in the global health tourism landscape. The Tourism Ministry intends to collaborate with international experts to identify medical tourism destinations in Egypt and develop a cohesive strategy to attract investments in this vital sector. The initiative underscores Egypt's commitment to fostering growth in health tourism and expanding its presence on the global stage.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), in collaboration with Iraqi governmental partners and funded by the Sw...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), in collaboration with Iraqi governmental partners and funded by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA) and the Canadian government, is leading transformative projects in Southern Iraq to address climate change challenges. Through initiatives like Farmer Field Schools and Climate Wise Women approaches, FAO aims to improve agricultural practices and empower farmers and women. A recent five-day Training of Facilitators workshop in Najaf gathered participants from multiple governorates to encourage the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices. Special emphasis was placed on women's involvement, acknowledging their crucial role in achieving agricultural goals. Field training sessions demonstrated sustainable practices and crop management strategies, with a focus on empowering rural women. The initiative aligns with various Sustainable Development Goals, highlighting FAO's commitment to promoting sustainable food systems, gender equality, climate action, and partnerships for the goals.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

records.title: Chairman of the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), Admiral Osama Rabie, and Minister of Transport Kamel Al-Wazir, have discussed strategies to l...
records.description: Chairman of the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), Admiral Osama Rabie, and Minister of Transport Kamel Al-Wazir, have discussed strategies to localize the shipbuilding industry in Egypt. This discussion took place during an inspection tour of the Suez Marine Shipyard Company, an affiliate of the SCA, to assess progress and outcomes of the company’s comprehensive development plan. The tour included visits to various workshops, such as electrical, mechanical, and carpentry, which have been upgraded with modern equipment. Additionally, maintenance and repair work on the dry dock at the Suez Shipyard Company were reviewed. The officials' efforts align with Egypt's broader objectives to strengthen its maritime capabilities and leverage the strategic importance of the Suez Canal.

records.title: Minister of Military Production, Mohamed Salah Eddin Mostafa, met with the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Green Tech Egypt, Robert...
records.description: Minister of Military Production, Mohamed Salah Eddin Mostafa, met with the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Green Tech Egypt, Robert Falk, to discuss the establishment of Egypt's first station to treat municipal solid waste and convert it into electrical energy. Mostafa emphasized Egypt's commitment to creating a supportive environment for environmental investments to combat climate change and involving the private sector in projects supporting this field, particularly waste recycling factories. He highlighted the ministry's eagerness to contribute to national projects supporting Egypt's comprehensive and sustainable development by utilizing surplus production capacities of its various companies. The ministry, in cooperation with Green Tech Egypt and OAK companies, has commenced the project's execution to establish a treatment plant in the Abu Rawash area in Giza Governorate. The station aims to convert 1,200 tons of waste per day into electricity at a rate of 30 megawatts per hour, contributing to environmental cleanliness, enhancing climate security, and improving citizens' living conditions. Falk outlined the project's executive procedures and praised the coordinated efforts between concerned parties, foreseeing significant positive impacts on the environment and the Egyptian economy. He also commended Egypt's efforts to expand clean and renewable energy projects and its commitment to integrating the private sector into waste management systems.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Military Production & Green Tech Egypt

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Presidential Decree No.
records.description: Presidential Decree No. 403 of 2023 has ratified an agreement between the Egyptian and Canadian governments aimed at implementing a project to enhance climate-smart agriculture and agricultural biodiversity. The initiative aims to increase adaptability in rural areas most affected by climate change in the Delta and Upper Egypt regions. The agreement, worth 10 million Canadian dollars, was approved by the House of Representatives during a session held on November 13, 2023, and the decree was officially published in the gazette on Thursday. This decree underscores Egypt's commitment to addressing the impacts of climate change on its agricultural sector through international cooperation and strategic initiatives.

records.title: European Commissioner for Neighborhood and Enlargement, Oliver Varhelyi, conveyed to Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs Sameh Shoukry t...
records.description: European Commissioner for Neighborhood and Enlargement, Oliver Varhelyi, conveyed to Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs Sameh Shoukry the European Union's approval of additional financial and economic assistance for Egypt, reinforcing their strategic partnership. In a phone call, Varhelyi briefed Shoukry on recent decisions made during the EU Summit, including the allocation of extra financial resources to neighboring countries like Egypt as part of the mid-term review of the EU long-term budget 2021-2027. The discussion also emphasized deepening cooperation across various sectors between the EU and Egypt within the framework of a new comprehensive strategic partnership, encompassing political, economic, trade, cultural, and scientific ties. Furthermore, they addressed the humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip, stressing the importance of increasing and ensuring effective delivery of humanitarian aid to the region's people, and discussed removing obstacles hindering sustained aid provision. These discussions underscore the shared commitment to addressing the humanitarian situation in Gaza and the mutual desire to strengthen Egypt-EU relations.

records.title: Egypt’s Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, and his Emirati counterpart, Abdul Rahman Al Owais, met during the Arab...
records.description: Egypt’s Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, and his Emirati counterpart, Abdul Rahman Al Owais, met during the Arab Health Exhibition in Dubai to discuss enhancing cooperation in the health sector. They focused on training human resources in the latest medical technologies and digital health, as well as collaborating on health research, pharmaceutical industries, and medical supplies. Additionally, they discussed supporting Palestinians in Gaza with humanitarian aid and medical treatment, and explored joint efforts in areas such as One Health Strategy, antimicrobial resistance, and disease prevention. The meeting also addressed Egypt’s comprehensive health insurance system, digital transformation, and governance, drawing insights from the UAE's experience in this field.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population

records.title: President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi emphasized Egypt's commitment to enhancing cooperation with Comoros across various sectors during a phone...
records.description: President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi emphasized Egypt's commitment to enhancing cooperation with Comoros across various sectors during a phone call with Comoros President Azali Assoumani. Sisi highlighted that such collaboration aims to fulfill the aspirations of both nations for sustainable development. He congratulated Assoumani on his re-election for a new presidential term, underscoring the special relationship between the two countries. The leaders also discussed bolstering mutual understanding on African issues of common interest, reflecting their shared commitment to regional cooperation and development.

records.title: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), represented by Jihad Azour, Director of the Middle East and Central Asia Department, has confirmed...
records.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), represented by Jihad Azour, Director of the Middle East and Central Asia Department, has confirmed ongoing negotiations with Egypt regarding the completion of the first and second reviews of their loan agreement. Azour emphasized that the program's objectives and details agreed upon in December 2022 remain unchanged. He highlighted the impact of the conflict in Gaza on Egypt's growth expectations, resulting in a reduction to three percent. Discussions between the IMF and Egypt have focused on addressing the economic repercussions of the conflict, combating inflation, and resolving currency shortage crises. Additionally, talks regarding additional financing are underway to address the country's economic challenges and financing gap. Despite a nearly year-long delay, an IMF delegation recently visited Egypt to discuss the loan program's progress, structural reform details, and economic performance indicators. The IMF had approved a $3 billion loan to Egypt over 48 months, with the first tranche of about $347 million received in December 2022.

records.title: Bank ABC has closed a $27.1 million sustainability-linked credit facility for Saudi Paper Manufacturing Company (SPMC), with support from...
records.description: Bank ABC has closed a $27.1 million sustainability-linked credit facility for Saudi Paper Manufacturing Company (SPMC), with support from the Italian Export Credit Agency SACE, spread across a term of five years. The loan aims to facilitate SPMC's expansion plan by financing the procurement of advanced machinery from Toscotec, enhancing efficiencies in scale and scope for future business operations. The signing ceremony, held at Bank ABC's Head Office in Bahrain, marked a significant milestone, attended by key officials from both entities. This transaction highlights Bank ABC's commitment to supporting the manufacturing sector in the region, with SPMC expressing gratitude for the bank's support and professionalism throughout the financing process. The collaboration between Bank ABC, SACE, and Toscotec underscores strategic efforts to promote industrial growth and sustainable practices, reflecting a shared commitment to driving economic development and environmental stewardship.

records.title: Tunisia has taken a significant stride towards sustainable water management with the signing of a 276 million dinars financing agreement...
records.description: Tunisia has taken a significant stride towards sustainable water management with the signing of a 276 million dinars financing agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB). Led by the Minister of Economy and Planning, Feriel Ouerghi, and the Deputy Director General of the ADB regional office in Tunisia, Malinne Blomberg, the agreement aims to bolster the Project to Improve the Quality of Purified Water for Better Resilience to Climate Change (PAQEE-RCC). This ambitious endeavor targets the irrigation of 3,000 hectares of agricultural land and aims to enhance the living conditions of over 670,000 citizens across 11 governorates. Additionally, it foresees the creation of 250 direct jobs and 1,000 indirect jobs. By focusing on upgrading electromechanical equipment and integrating photovoltaic energy into 19 wastewater treatment plants across various governorates, the project aligns with the principles of the circular economy, promoting the reuse of treated wastewater to bolster the country's water balance amidst climate change challenges. The installation of photovoltaic solar energy systems at treatment facilities is also envisioned to enhance energy self-sufficiency while fostering the development of renewable energy sources. This initiative represents a pivotal advancement in Tunisia's efforts towards more efficient water resource management, given that the country currently reuses only 20% of treated wastewater, despite treating approximately 290 million cubic meters annually through its limited 125 treatment plants.

records.title: Serco, an international public services company, has acquired Climatize, a renowned sustainability and engineering consultancy, to streng...
records.description: Serco, an international public services company, has acquired Climatize, a renowned sustainability and engineering consultancy, to strengthen its capabilities in empowering governments and businesses to achieve their Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) goals. This acquisition marks Serco's commitment to delivering top-tier sustainability services, blending its international capabilities with Climatize's expertise. Climatize, known for its green building engineering and sustainability strategies, will offer consultancy services including net-zero strategies, resource efficiency management, and green technology integration. The move aligns with Serco's purpose-driven approach and aims to accelerate clients' journey towards net-zero while reducing operational costs and creating employment opportunities. The acquisition, coming timely after COP28, signifies a shared passion for sustainability between Serco and Climatize, promising innovative solutions and growth in new markets.

records.title: The Bahrain-Hungary Joint Economic Commission recently held a meeting in Budapest, co-chaired by Dr.
records.description: The Bahrain-Hungary Joint Economic Commission recently held a meeting in Budapest, co-chaired by Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Bahrain's Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Péter Szijjártó, Hungary's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade. During the meeting, both parties explored opportunities for cooperation in various sectors, including economics, the environment, education, culture, energy, and agriculture, with the aim of boosting trade, attracting investments, enhancing food security, and adopting modern technology. The significance of strengthening joint political and diplomatic efforts between the two countries was also emphasized, encompassing areas such as political consultation, diplomatic training, support in international forums, and the implementation of bilateral cooperation decisions.

records.title: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has implemented new measures, capping daily cash withdrawals in Egyptian pounds at EGP 150,000 for both c...
records.description: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has implemented new measures, capping daily cash withdrawals in Egyptian pounds at EGP 150,000 for both corporations and individuals, a reduction from previous limits. Banks are required to report requests exceeding this amount to the CBE for approval, with reports submitted twice daily. These actions follow previous efforts by Egyptian banks to limit transactions, both domestically and internationally. Notably, in August 2022, the CBE had increased daily withdrawal limits from bank branches to EGP 150,000 for individuals and companies, while maintaining the maximum ATM withdrawal limit for individuals at EGP 20,000. These measures aim to regulate cash flow and transactions in alignment with financial stability goals.

records.title: The Egyptian Cabinet has approved a plan to reduce public investments for the fiscal year 2023/2024 by 15%, as part of efforts to rationa...
records.description: The Egyptian Cabinet has approved a plan to reduce public investments for the fiscal year 2023/2024 by 15%, as part of efforts to rationalize public spending and address economic challenges. The decision includes postponing new projects until June 2024 and prioritizing completion of ongoing projects with at least 70% completion rates. Additionally, the measures prohibit entering into contracts for new projects, external financing, or projects requiring borrowing. The decision also suspends the purchase of new passenger cars for government bodies. These measures align with the International Monetary Fund's loan agreement with Egypt and aim to enhance government spending efficiency while managing the deficit, which is expected to remain at 6.9% of GDP for the current fiscal year, reflecting a commitment to fiscal stability.

records.title: In Muscat, the Environmental Authority has commenced the initial phase of planting frankincense trees in the Madam area of Salalah.
records.description: In Muscat, the Environmental Authority has commenced the initial phase of planting frankincense trees in the Madam area of Salalah. This initiative is part of a broader plan to develop a series of environmental parks in Dhofar province, aimed at showcasing prominent native trees. Madam is set to be part of this environmental park network and will accommodate over 11,000 trees across 181,000 square meters. In this first phase, 500 frankincense trees were planted in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, the yet-to-be-established Nature Protection Association, and the local community.

records.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for All Initiative
records.description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, through the Minister of Communications and Information Technology, Engineer Abdullah bin Amer Al-Sawaha, unveiled the Generative Artificial Intelligence for All initiative during the third General Assembly meeting of the Digital Cooperation Organization. This initiative, tailored for members of the Digital Cooperation Organization under the auspices of the International Center for Artificial Intelligence Research and Ethics (ICAIRE), aims to promote generative artificial intelligence research, enhance awareness of AI ethics, and govern policies related to generative AI. The initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia's commitment to advancing digital transformation and supporting inclusiveness and digital prosperity globally, particularly in developing countries. The announcement follows the launch of principles of artificial intelligence ethics by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) during the World Summit on Artificial Intelligence, emphasizing the Kingdom's dedication to ethical AI practices and governance.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Communications and Information Technology

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Morocco have strengthened their economic ties with a new agreement signed between chambers of commerce from both countries.
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Morocco have strengthened their economic ties with a new agreement signed between chambers of commerce from both countries. The agreement encourages cooperation among businesses and companies and includes provisions for financial collaboration, the exchange of economic and legislative information, and the organization of conferences, seminars, workshops, expos, and markets. It also focuses on facilitating the exchange of trade delegations, removing investment barriers, and resolving disputes amicably. This agreement reflects the commitment of both countries to promote bilateral cooperation and create a conducive environment for business growth.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) have signed an agreement to host the 16th session of the...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) have signed an agreement to host the 16th session of the Convention’s Conference of the Parties (COP16) in Riyadh from 2-13 December 2024. This event will be the largest-ever meeting of UNCCD’s 197 Parties and the first held in the Middle East, marking the 30th anniversary of the UNCCD. Eng. Abdulrahman Abdulmohsen Alfadley, Saudi Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture, emphasized Saudi Arabia's commitment to environmental protection through initiatives like the Saudi Green Initiative and the Middle East Green Initiative. UNCCD Executive Secretary Ibrahim Thiaw stressed the urgency of addressing global land degradation and drought, which currently affect up to 40% of the world's land and threaten food, water, and energy security. The Riyadh COP16 aims to mobilize global efforts towards land restoration and drought resilience, showcasing sustainable land stewardship initiatives in Saudi Arabia and the broader Middle East region.
records.institution: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)

records.title: Tunisia and the African Development Bank (AfDB) have entered into loan and guarantee agreements amounting to €81.9 million (approximately...
records.description: Tunisia and the African Development Bank (AfDB) have entered into loan and guarantee agreements amounting to €81.9 million (approximately TND 276.14 million) to finance the Treated Wastewater Quality Improvement Project For Climate Resilience Building (PAQEE-RCC). This project aims to produce treated wastewater that meets regulatory standards, with a focus on tertiary treatment. Additionally, it will facilitate irrigation of 3,000 hectares of farmland, enhance living conditions for over 670,000 citizens across 11 governorates, and generate 250 direct jobs and 1,000 indirect jobs. The project will also incorporate renewable energy by utilizing photovoltaic solar energy in 19 water treatment plants. Overall, it aims to improve the water balance, build resilience to climate change, and enhance living conditions, according to Minister of Economy and Planning Féryel Ouerghi. The project aligns with a strategy to reinforce the results of the first phase of the PAQEE, completed in 2020 and funded by AfDB. Currently, only 27 out of 125 wastewater treatment plants in Tunisia have tertiary treatment, underscoring the significance of this initiative. It will contribute to resource-efficient agriculture and reduce energy costs through solar energy utilization, emphasizing the circular economy and water-energy-agriculture nexus approach.

records.title: Significant progress has been achieved in various areas of cooperation between Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
records.description: Significant progress has been achieved in various areas of cooperation between Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). In 2022, the volume of mutual trade increased by 2.1 times, reaching $518.6 million, and in 2023, it further increased by nearly 21 percent to $625.9 million. The number of enterprises with UAE capital involvement has also grown to 300. These developments were highlighted during a meeting between Tanzila Narbayeva, Chairperson of the Senate of the Oliy Majlis, and Abdulla Nasser Lootah, Director General of the UAE Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Authority, and Deputy Minister of Cabinet Affairs for Competitiveness and Knowledge Exchange. The discussion emphasized the need to enhance trade indicators by strengthening the activities of the joint Intergovernmental Commission. The meeting also covered various aspects of the multifaceted relations between the two countries, including trade, economics, social, cultural, and humanitarian aspects, as well as cooperation in digital technologies, youth support, and business development, in line with Uzbekistan's designation of the Year of Support for Youth and Business in 2024.
records.institution: UAE Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Authority

records.title: The ongoing Red Sea crisis could lead to a rise in stock prices for UAE-based shipping companies as global counterparts struggle to navig...
records.description: The ongoing Red Sea crisis could lead to a rise in stock prices for UAE-based shipping companies as global counterparts struggle to navigate the situation. Dubai-listed Gulf Navigation (GULF NAV) and Abu Dhabi-listed Al Seer Marine saw share price growth in 2023. GULF NAV's stock price increased by 424% over the year. While the crisis has caused concern for global liners, local experts believe that UAE-based shipping companies could benefit if the situation escalates further. However, this is speculative, and the impact on the shipping industry remains uncertain.
records.institution: Dubai-listed Gulf Navigation (GULF NAV) & Abu Dhabi–listed Al Seer Marine

records.title: Yemeni Ambassador to Jordan, Jalal Ibrahim, expressed appreciation for His Majesty King Abdullah's strong support for the Palestinian peo...
records.description: Yemeni Ambassador to Jordan, Jalal Ibrahim, expressed appreciation for His Majesty King Abdullah's strong support for the Palestinian people and his efforts to end the war on Gaza, as well as providing humanitarian aid to the region. He also commended the Jordanian Armed Forces–Arab Army for their air-drop relief aid operations. Ambassador Ibrahim highlighted Jordan's hospitality in hosting Yemeni people and providing them with support in education, healthcare, and training. He praised Jordan's role in promoting peace in Yemen by hosting various Yemeni political parties for meetings in Amman. Additionally, he discussed the strategic importance of Jordan as a gateway for Yemen in aviation, healthcare, education, and various other sectors. Yemen intends to expand its investments in Jordan and is planning a forum for Yemeni businesspeople to explore investment opportunities in the country. On the Palestinian issue, Ambassador Ibrahim emphasized the centrality of this matter in Yemeni foreign policy and the importance of establishing a sovereign Palestinian state based on the pre-1967 borders and relevant UN Security Council resolutions to enhance regional and international security.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's decision to halt strawberry imports from Egypt and other countries is a regulatory measure aimed at balancing the supply a...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's decision to halt strawberry imports from Egypt and other countries is a regulatory measure aimed at balancing the supply and demand in the Kingdom's internal market, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation. The decision is not a ban or a rejection of shipments for health or quarantine reasons. It applies to various crops imported by Saudi Arabia from around the world, and Egypt is not the only affected country. Strawberry exporters need to obtain an export permit valid for 15 days from January 24, 2024, and the Saudi Ministry will resume issuing import permits for strawberries in the future.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: The UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and Tunisia have entered into an agreement aimed at enhancing social protection for agricu...
records.description: The UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and Tunisia have entered into an agreement aimed at enhancing social protection for agricultural workers in Tunisia. The agreement, signed in Tunis, establishes action programs to provide social security benefits to farmers and fishers in the country. Tunisia's Minister of Social Affairs, Malek Ezzahi, emphasized the significant role of agricultural workers in the nation's economy and food security and underscored the importance of improving their working conditions through this initiative.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: Tunisia and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) have forged a historic agreement aimed at bolstering social...
records.description: Tunisia and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) have forged a historic agreement aimed at bolstering social coverage within the agricultural sector, signifying a significant milestone in the nation's endeavors to enhance the welfare of agricultural workers. The agreement, inked at the Ministry of Social Affairs in Tunis, underscores a commitment to elevating sectoral policies geared towards amplifying the social coverage rate among Tunisia's agricultural workforce. Beyond mere expansion, the collaboration seeks to fortify institutional capacities within Tunisia, with the overarching goal of universalizing social coverage while enhancing the quality of social benefits for farmers and fishermen. By leveraging FAO's expertise and technical assistance, Tunisia aims to not only uplift the living standards of agricultural workers but also foster sustainable and equitable agricultural development. This partnership epitomizes a shared vision for a resilient agricultural sector, underpinned by robust social safety nets, thereby advancing the nation's progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and exemplifying its dedication to fostering a more inclusive and sustainable future.
records.institution: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

records.title: A new partnership between Bayer and agri-tech company Silal, part of Abu Dhabi-headquartered ADQ, aims to enhance sustainable agriculture...
records.description: A new partnership between Bayer and agri-tech company Silal, part of Abu Dhabi-headquartered ADQ, aims to enhance sustainable agriculture in the UAE. The collaboration will conduct trials on over 30 varieties of vegetable seeds, including tomato, cucumber, and melon, to assess their performance under the challenging desert conditions in the country. The data from these trials will not only benefit UAE agriculture but will also inform agricultural practices in other countries facing the challenges of climate change. Bayer and Silal will also focus on capacity-building programs for farmers and addressing climate change challenges in the region. In addition, they will explore innovative solutions and advanced technologies to improve agricultural practices in arid desert conditions, such as no-till farming, crop protection, and breeding technology, while also leveraging precision seed application and irrigation to conserve resources.

records.title: Egypt is planning to construct six wheat silos in 2024, with a total investment of $145.6 million, aiming to increase the country's wheat...
records.description: Egypt is planning to construct six wheat silos in 2024, with a total investment of $145.6 million, aiming to increase the country's wheat silo storage capacity by 420,000 tons to reach a total of 4.620 million tons. The French Development Agency (AFD) will finance $61.5 million of the project, with Egypt providing the remaining $84.1 million. The government's goal is to boost the storage capacity of state-owned wheat silos by 2.5 to 3 million tons within three to four years, reaching a capacity between 6.4 and 7 million tons.

records.title: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) is planning to procure over 5 million tonnes of wheat in 2024 through internation...
records.description: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) is planning to procure over 5 million tonnes of wheat in 2024 through international tenders, an increase of 500,000 tonnes compared to 2023, according to the Ministry of Supply and Domestic Trade. This increase is driven by domestic consumption exceeding 20 million tonnes annually, while total production is just over 9 million tonnes, resulting in the need to import 11 million tonnes to meet demand. In 2023, Egypt purchased approximately 4.5 million tonnes of wheat through GASC tenders, primarily from countries like Russia, Romania, France, Bulgaria, and Ukraine. Additionally, GASC has initiated an international tender to acquire white, wholly milled short grain rice for Egypt's Holding Company for Food Industries, with delivery scheduled from March 15 to April 15.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Caretaker Minister of Agriculture Abbas Hajj Hassan welcomed Algerian Ambassador to Lebanon Rachid Belbaki to discuss bilateral relations...
records.description: Caretaker Minister of Agriculture Abbas Hajj Hassan welcomed Algerian Ambassador to Lebanon Rachid Belbaki to discuss bilateral relations between the two countries, with a particular focus on enhancing cooperation in the agricultural sector.

records.title: A meeting was held between the Agricultural and Fishery Development Fund, affiliated with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Wat...
records.description: A meeting was held between the Agricultural and Fishery Development Fund, affiliated with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources in Oman, and the Agricultural Development Fund in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Both sides emphasized the financing mechanisms for the two funds to enhance agricultural development programs and projects in both countries. The meeting was attended by His Excellency Dr. Saud bin Hamoud Al-Habsi, Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources and Chairman of the Agricultural and Fishery Development Fund in Oman, along with Munir Fahd Al-Sahli, the General Manager of the Agricultural Development Fund in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Omani Agricultural Fisheries Development Fund of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Agro-food Industry Attractive Investment Niche for Tunisia’s Female Entrepreneurs
records.description: The agro-food industry emerged as an attractive investment opportunity for Tunisia's female entrepreneurs in 2023, accounting for 37.1% of their projects, as reported by the Agency for the Promotion of Industry and Innovation (APII) in its economic bulletin for December 2023. Approximately 85% of these projects were directed toward the domestic market. In total, there were 729 projects with TND 144.3 million in earmarked investments. The textile and clothing sector ranked second, with Tunisian female entrepreneurs initiating 223 projects in 2023. These investments represented 26% of total investment intentions in the industrial sector and 6% of overall reported investments, while contributing to the creation of 18% of jobs. However, the volume of reported investments decreased to TND 2,291.6 million compared to TND 2,417.4 million in 2022, and the number of reported projects also declined to 2,854 from 2,978 in 2022.
records.institution: Tunisian Agency for the Promotion of Industry and Innovation
