records.title: Rebound, a recycled plastic trading platform based in the UAE, has partnered with the Circular Packaging Association (CPA) to advance sta...
records.description: Rebound, a recycled plastic trading platform based in the UAE, has partnered with the Circular Packaging Association (CPA) to advance standardization efforts for plastic recyclates. This collaboration, announced at the 28th Conference of Parties, aims to work toward material standards convergence in the UAE and globally. The partnership will focus on developing data analytics and insights, specifically related to material volume estimates in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region and the UAE. Rebound, as a Knowledge Partner to the Circular Packaging Association, will provide insights on global recycled plastics quality and infrastructure. The collaboration aims to promote high-quality recycled plastics in both food-grade and non-food-grade materials and accelerate sustainable packaging solutions.

records.title: Saudi aid agency KSrelief has launched 24 humanitarian aid projects in Somalia, with a total value of over SR 171.8 million (approximatel...
records.description: Saudi aid agency KSrelief has launched 24 humanitarian aid projects in Somalia, with a total value of over SR 171.8 million (approximately $45.8 million). These projects span various sectors, including healthcare, food security, water sanitation, education, shelter security, volunteer programs, and education. The initiatives aim to benefit nearly 5.8 million people across Somalia, focusing on improving healthcare, reducing child mortality, providing education support, ensuring food security, and enhancing access to clean water. These projects demonstrate Saudi Arabia's commitment to humanitarian assistance and its desire to strengthen bilateral relations with Somalia, as the country highly values Saudi Arabia's contributions to its development and welfare.

records.title: Ali Saeed bu Sherbak al-Mansouri, the acting general manager of Qatar Chamber, met with a delegation from Nepal led by Chandra Prasad Dha...
records.description: Ali Saeed bu Sherbak al-Mansouri, the acting general manager of Qatar Chamber, met with a delegation from Nepal led by Chandra Prasad Dhakal, the president of the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry. During the meeting, they discussed enhancing commercial and economic bilateral relations between Qatar and Nepal, explored investment opportunities, and identified key sectors for cooperation between the Qatari private sector and its Nepalese counterpart. Two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) were also mentioned, which aim to boost cooperation and partnership between the private sectors of both countries. Both sides emphasized the importance of trade and business visits to foster collaboration and learn about investment opportunities in various sectors. Nepal invited Qatari investors to participate in an Investment Summit scheduled for April.

records.title: In a historic development, Saudi Arabia has seen the opening of its first liquor store in over seven decades, signifying a notable shift...
records.description: In a historic development, Saudi Arabia has seen the opening of its first liquor store in over seven decades, signifying a notable shift towards liberalization in the once-conservative kingdom. Located in Riyadh, the store is exclusively accessible to non-Muslim diplomats and is in alignment with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's efforts to transform Saudi Arabia into a prominent tourism and business hub as part of broader economic diversification initiatives. The newly established store, situated in Riyadh's Diplomatic Quarter, offers a selection of liquor, wine, and two types of beer, with customers required to present their diplomatic identification for entry. The opening coincides with recent reports of new regulations governing alcohol sales to diplomats in the kingdom, indicating a change in the country's historically strict stance on alcohol, which has been in place since the early 1950s when King Abdulaziz imposed a ban following a significant incident involving alcohol.

records.title: During a visit to Saudi Arabia by a delegation led by First Deputy Minister of Economy Elnur Aliyev, discussions were held to expand econ...
records.description: During a visit to Saudi Arabia by a delegation led by First Deputy Minister of Economy Elnur Aliyev, discussions were held to expand economic cooperation between Azerbaijan and Saudi Arabia. Meetings were held with Saudi officials, including the First Deputy Minister of Economy and Planning and the Deputy Minister for International Economic Affairs. The talks emphasized the growing economic relations between the two countries, with a focus on increasing trade turnover and exchanging expertise in priority economic sectors. The parties also explored areas for private sector cooperation and discussed mutual investments, as well as opportunities for collaboration in trade, investments, energy, infrastructure, tourism, and other sectors.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Economy and Planning

records.title: Saudi Arabia is set to begin importing South African beef and lamb products, marking the end of a 20-year ban that was lifted by the king...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is set to begin importing South African beef and lamb products, marking the end of a 20-year ban that was lifted by the kingdom's Food and Drug Administration in August. Final approvals for shipping halal cuts to Saudi Arabia are in place, with exports expected to commence in the coming weeks. The move aims to tap into Saudi Arabia's $2 billion meat market as part of its efforts to diversify its economy away from oil. South Africa and Saudi Arabia are also exploring potential cooperation in pharmaceuticals, technology, and sports investments, including falconry and equestrian disciplines.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Launches National Biotechnology Strategy Set to Transform the Kingdom
records.description: Saudi Arabia has launched the National Biotechnology Strategy, with the goal of positioning the country as a biotechnology leader in the Middle East and North Africa region by 2030 and an international biotechnology hub by 2040. The strategy will focus on four strategic areas: vaccines, bio-manufacturing and localization, genomics, and plant optimization. It aims to enhance the domestic biotechnology industry, strengthen food security, and promote economic growth, job creation, and sustainability. The strategy is part of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 initiative to diversify its economy and reduce dependence on oil revenue.

records.title: South Africa and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia have committed to enhancing trade relations to promote economic growth in both countries.
records.description: South Africa and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia have committed to enhancing trade relations to promote economic growth in both countries. President Cyril Ramaphosa and Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition Ebrahim Patel have been leading discussions to facilitate local businesses' entry into the Saudi Arabian market. Stavros Nicolaou, Co-Chair of the South African–Saudi Arabia Business Council, emphasized the significant growth opportunities in Saudi Arabia for South African companies. Dr. Hisham Al Amoudi, Vice-Chairman of the Saudi–South Africa Business Council, reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's commitment to investing in South Africa, with Saudi investments contributing to South Africa's Gross Domestic Product. In 2023, South Africa's exports to Saudi Arabia increased to R7.3 billion, while imports from Saudi Arabia decreased to R54.6 billion. Saudi Arabia is the largest investor in South Africa's local renewable energy sector, with overall Saudi investment estimated at $1.62 billion.

records.title: New Provisions to Encourage Agricultural Communitarian Companies in Tunisia
records.description: Tunisia's Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Abdel Moneim Belati, has introduced a series of measures to support communitarian companies in the agricultural sector. These measures include the establishment of a focal point within the ministerial cabinet, the development of a monitoring mechanism for communitarian company projects, and the identification of challenges faced by each company along with solutions provided by relevant authorities. Additionally, the plan involves offering regional support through the regional agricultural development committees to stimulate economic growth in various regions and enhance the value chains of agricultural products. Training sessions for young promoters will also be organized to strengthen their capacity in the sector, and administrative procedures will be streamlined to facilitate access to state-granted privileges. Currently, there are 100 communitarian companies in Tunisia, with 60% of them operating in the agricultural sector. The Tunisian Solidarity Bank has provided nearly 4 million dinars in funding to support 15 communitarian companies active in agriculture, contributing to the expansion of business projects and improved access to financial resources.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries

records.title: Algeria has donated 16,000 metric tonnes of fertilizer to Kenya, which was received by Agriculture and Livestock Cabinet Secretary Mithik...
records.description: Algeria has donated 16,000 metric tonnes of fertilizer to Kenya, which was received by Agriculture and Livestock Cabinet Secretary Mithika Linturi. The donation comes as Kenya seeks to address its fertilizer needs, with CS Linturi mentioning that the country requires about 900,000 metric tonnes of assorted fertilizer annually to support food production. He expressed gratitude for the donation, emphasizing the government's commitment to ensuring smallholder farmers have access to subsidized fertilizer to mitigate the high cost of production. Additionally, the government plans to acquire 630,000 metric tonnes of fertilizer in the current financial year to enhance food and nutrition security, particularly for prioritized crop value chains. The Algerian Ambassador to Kenya, Mahi Boumediene, commended the donation, emphasizing its role in strengthening bilateral ties between the two nations.

records.title: The Iraqi Cabinet has granted the Minister of Agriculture the authority to contract with the Austrian company Bauer for an amount of 300...
records.description: The Iraqi Cabinet has granted the Minister of Agriculture the authority to contract with the Austrian company Bauer for an amount of 300 million euros, which will be converted to dollars at the exchange rate of 1,300 Iraqi dinars. This decision follows Cabinet approval of a deal in December, which did not specify a value, and was "subject to legal considerations." Bauer is known for manufacturing and selling sprinklers and irrigation systems, and the Ministry of Agriculture bears the responsibility for ensuring the correctness of the contractual procedures.

records.title: SUEZ and AZURA Group Join Forces to Recycle Organic Waste in Southern Morocco
records.description: Suez and the Azura Group have signed two six-year agreements to establish two platforms dedicated to transforming organic waste into compost in Southern Morocco. These platforms will have a combined capacity of 116,000 tonnes of organic waste annually, producing 42,000 tonnes of compost and 43,000 tonnes of semi-finished Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF). This initiative aims to promote a circular economy, resource preservation, and soil quality enhancement by reintegrating carbon into the soil. The resulting compost will be sold to local agricultural producers, benefiting the local economy. Additionally, the project is expected to reduce carbon emissions by around 16,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually.

records.title: Al Jouf Agricultural Development Company of Saudi Arabia has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Korean company E Green G...
records.description: Al Jouf Agricultural Development Company of Saudi Arabia has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Korean company E Green Global (EGG) to transfer technology for potato seed production, enabling local production in Saudi Arabia for 180 days. The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture will conduct necessary studies to establish a partnership between the two companies for seed production in the Kingdom. This agreement is expected to enhance Al Jouf Agricultural's position in both domestic and international markets. In August 2023, Al Jouf Agricultural and the French energy company Engie signed a solar energy purchase deal.
records.institution: Al Jouf Agricultural Development Company of Saudi Arabia

records.title: Unifrutti Group, based in Abu Dhabi, has acquired Chile-based fruit supplier and exporter Sociedad Exportadora Verfrut.
records.description: Unifrutti Group, based in Abu Dhabi, has acquired Chile-based fruit supplier and exporter Sociedad Exportadora Verfrut. Verfrut is a well-known fresh produce company with operations in Chile and Peru, covering over 7,500 hectares of farming and processing facilities. They produce a variety of fruits, including grapes, cherries, apples, and blueberries, and have a distribution network spanning from South America to the US and China. Unifrutti, majority-owned by the Abu Dhabi government investment fund ADQ, plans to retain Verfrut's management team and production operations following the acquisition, which was made for an undisclosed sum. This strategic move aligns with Unifrutti's ambition to become a leading global multi-fruit company with a strong commitment to sustainability.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Egypt is offering its expertise in agriculture, irrigation, and infrastructure development to Angola to support the African nation's growth.
records.description: Egypt is offering its expertise in agriculture, irrigation, and infrastructure development to Angola to support the African nation's growth. Egyptian Ambassador Neveen El-Husseiny expressed Egypt's willingness to strengthen relations with Angola and highlighted Egypt's experience in crop irrigation, agricultural development, and infrastructure. Egyptian companies are ready to collaborate with Angola on projects related to irrigation, energy, water management, and infrastructure. This cooperation builds on a long-standing relationship between the two countries, formalized in the General Agreement for Economic, Scientific, and Technical Cooperation in 1987. The upcoming inaugural meeting of the Bilateral Commission will assess existing cooperation and explore new areas of collaboration. Egypt has also been a reliable partner for Angola, providing support during the COVID-19 pandemic.

records.title: The UAE has dispatched an aid plane carrying 50 tonnes of food assistance to Burkina Faso, as part of its ongoing humanitarian efforts to...
records.description: The UAE has dispatched an aid plane carrying 50 tonnes of food assistance to Burkina Faso, as part of its ongoing humanitarian efforts to support nations facing adversity. This gesture underscores the UAE's commitment to extending aid to vulnerable populations, particularly children, the elderly, and women, who are most affected by food security challenges. Sultan Al Shamsi, Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs for Development Affairs and International Organisations, highlighted that this aid shipment aligns with efforts to address Burkina Faso's pressing food security issues, aiming to alleviate the suffering of its residents severely impacted by ongoing challenges. The UAE's assistance not only reinforces bilateral relations but also contributes to broader national and international initiatives aimed at achieving food security and supporting vulnerable populations.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Development Affairs and International Organisations

records.title: Three Abu Dhabi-based logistics companies, including Etihad Airways' cargo division Etihad Cargo, Abu Dhabi Airports, and Abu Dhabi Food...
records.description: Three Abu Dhabi-based logistics companies, including Etihad Airways' cargo division Etihad Cargo, Abu Dhabi Airports, and Abu Dhabi Food Hub, have entered into an initial agreement to establish an air corridor aimed at enhancing food trade and investment diversification. This collaborative effort, known as Fresh Corridor 2.0, seeks to position the UAE as a significant player in the global food supply chain by facilitating two-way food trade between the UAE and other nations. The initiative aims to expand food sources, establish new trade routes, and enhance product options for regional consumers. Elena Sorlini, Managing Director and Interim CEO of Abu Dhabi Airports, emphasized that this corridor would foster diversification and growth in imports and exports, benefiting both UAE consumers and global markets. The partnership aims to develop a comprehensive food trading corridor with advanced infrastructure, regional market access, and reliable logistics, addressing evolving demands in the food trade sector. The collaboration also intends to engage with government stakeholders, facilitators, and key industry players to ensure seamless trade operations. By leveraging Abu Dhabi's strategic location and infrastructure, Etihad Cargo customers are expected to benefit from enhanced connectivity to global markets, as noted by Antonoaldo Neves, CEO of Etihad Airways. This initiative aligns with the UAE's broader objectives to bolster its food security strategy and stimulate economic growth in the food and agriculture sector.
records.institution: Etihad Cargo, Abu Dhabi Airports & Abu Dhabi Food Hub

records.title: Dutch shipping company WEC Lines is introducing an innovative shipping route connecting Morocco's Agadir and the UK's Port of Liverpool,...
records.description: Dutch shipping company WEC Lines is introducing an innovative shipping route connecting Morocco's Agadir and the UK's Port of Liverpool, offering a swift and eco-friendly option for importing fresh produce without overland trucking. This service responds to the rising prominence of Morocco as a tomato supplier to the UK and aligns with evolving industry preferences, with a survey showing that 76% of retail leaders prefer importing goods closer to their final destinations. Additionally, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi emphasizes his nation's commitment to enhancing global logistics and trade capabilities through partnerships with companies like "CMA CGM," highlighting the importance of developing Egyptian ports into trade and service hubs to strengthen Egypt's position as a global logistics and trade center.

records.title: The agricultural ministers of Morocco and Cote d'Ivoire met in Berlin to discuss strengthening agricultural cooperation between their cou...
records.description: The agricultural ministers of Morocco and Cote d'Ivoire met in Berlin to discuss strengthening agricultural cooperation between their countries. During their meeting on the sidelines of the Berlin International Green Week, Moroccan Agricultural Minister Mohammed Sadiki highlighted the potential for both nations to share experiences and expertise in the agriculture sector. They specifically discussed water management, with Morocco sharing its techniques for water mobilization and conservation, particularly through modernized irrigation systems. Morocco's experience in transferring water from water-rich to water-poor regions was seen as beneficial for Cote d'Ivoire, which expressed interest in exploring cooperation prospects with Morocco in this regard.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Unveils Priority Specializations Eligible to Obtain Special Talent Residency
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Premium Residency Center has unveiled the priority specializations eligible for obtaining Special Talent Residency. This type of residency is designed for individuals with expertise in scientific, administrative, and research fields who possess exceptional capabilities and experiences that can contribute to strengthening local capabilities and knowledge exchange. Saudi Arabia aims to attract top talents from around the world to reside and work in the country, fostering development, creativity, and investment in human resources while supporting the stability of expatriates benefiting from this residency type. The eligible specializations include healthcare and life sciences, digital technologies, financial services, advanced manufacturing, space and defense, energy and circular economy, metals and mining, logistics and transport, tourism infrastructure, and technologies in food and agriculture. Additionally, there are various categories in research and innovation, such as space and aviation, environment, water and agriculture, energy, materials and production, health, urban transformation, logistics, and digital technologies.

records.title: Basrah Gas Company (BGC) and the United Nations World Food Program (WFP) have launched a climate adaptation project in Iraq's Al Zubair d...
records.description: Basrah Gas Company (BGC) and the United Nations World Food Program (WFP) have launched a climate adaptation project in Iraq's Al Zubair district, aimed at boosting smallholder farmers' incomes and agricultural production. The initiative will introduce innovative strategies to combat desertification and promote water conservation in farming, focusing on training farmers in smart agriculture techniques, modern farming methods, and water-saving irrigation systems. Additionally, the project will empower female farmers, enhancing their capacity and self-employment prospects. This collaboration reflects a collective commitment to addressing climate change in Iraq and promoting sustainable livelihoods in the face of environmental challenges such as sandstorms, heatwaves, and water scarcity in the region.
records.institution: Basrah Gas Company (BGC) & the United Nations World Food Program (WFP)

records.title: The Iraqi government's "Ur" electronic portal has expanded its e-government services, now offering a total of 708 services, with 352 bein...
records.description: The Iraqi government's "Ur" electronic portal has expanded its e-government services, now offering a total of 708 services, with 352 being electronic and 356 paper-based. This portal has more than 2.3 million registered users and comprises 6,358 governmental websites representing 68 institutions. These services span various sectors such as education, justice, law, complaints, loans, finances, transportation, infrastructure, housing, citizenship, youth and sports, culture, electricity, water, agriculture, irrigation, retirement, health, and electronic information systems. Additionally, there is an advisory service accessible at the number 5599, operating from 8 AM to 12 PM, for inquiries about available services. The portal has successfully canceled and replaced 4,203,795 paper-based documents with electronic versions, involving 81 key entities, including ministries, provinces, presidential authorities, unions, and various agencies. It also offers a company registration service to support public-private partnerships and national data center plans. Plans for collaboration with the private sector and further expansion of electronic services are in progress.

records.title: The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) has issued a third-class license to Oman Lens Company, marking a significant milestone...
records.description: The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) has issued a third-class license to Oman Lens Company, marking a significant milestone as the first of its kind in Oman. This license permits the establishment of a ground station connected to a satellite network, specifically for monitoring, tracking, and controlling satellites within the Star Vision Aerospace Limited network. The license will enable the provision of imaging services from space, facilitating the collection and analysis of satellite image data for various applications, including mapping, environmental monitoring, resource management, agriculture, and disaster management. This initiative aligns with the TRA's strategic objectives to enhance local value, promote investment in innovative technologies and services, and foster technology localization.

records.title: Saudi Tadawul Group Holding Company (STG), a prominent capital markets group in the MENA region, has inked a binding agreement with exist...
records.description: Saudi Tadawul Group Holding Company (STG), a prominent capital markets group in the MENA region, has inked a binding agreement with existing shareholders of DME Holdings Limited, securing a 32.6% stake in the Dubai Mercantile Exchange (DME), a leading international commodities exchange. This agreement positions STG as the joint largest shareholder in DME Holdings alongside CME Group, and other shareholders include the Oman Investment Authority (OIA), Dubai Holding, and global financial and commercial industry leaders. The deal also allows STG to potentially increase its shareholding in the future, with the proceeds from new shares supporting DME's growth efforts. The partnership aims to leverage the Middle East's strategic location between commodity production hubs and end-markets, capturing demand for energy, metals, and agricultural commodities while promoting the transition to a sustainable economy through next-generation derivatives contracts.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Fourth Milling, known for its flour, feed, bran, and wheat products, has selected Riyad Capital to manage its upcoming ini...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Fourth Milling, known for its flour, feed, bran, and wheat products, has selected Riyad Capital to manage its upcoming initial public offering (IPO) on Tadawul, marking a significant milestone for the company, which has experienced remarkable growth since its establishment in 2017. With a daily production output of 3,150 tonnes and a strong presence in Madinah, Fourth Milling is planning to go public, and the IPO could potentially raise over $200 million. This development aligns with Saudi Arabia's "Vision 2030" framework, which aims to diversify the economy away from oil by privatizing certain industries and attracting investments. The IPO launch, expected in the first half of the year, signifies a noteworthy event for the Saudi food processing sector and offers investors an opportunity to be part of this flourishing enterprise.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture has signed a strategic partnership agreement with the King Abdullah University...
records.description: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture has signed a strategic partnership agreement with the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) to accelerate innovation and sustainability in environmental and agricultural science within Saudi Arabia. This partnership aims to align KAUST's research efforts with the ministry's strategic plan, enhance environmental protection, and contribute to sustainable food and agriculture security in the country. Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture Abdulrahman Al-Fadli visited KAUST to tour the KAUST-MEWA Algal Biotechnology Development and Aquaculture Facility, which plays a crucial role in transforming food production to meet the Kingdom's animal-feed demand while creating local job opportunities.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture & the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

records.title: The first-ever forum connecting various components of the animal wealth sector was held in Saham, Oman, with the aim of highlighting the...
records.description: The first-ever forum connecting various components of the animal wealth sector was held in Saham, Oman, with the aim of highlighting the sector's role in achieving food security, employment generation, and economic growth. The event celebrated Livestock Breeders' Day and was organized under the patronage of Eng Yaqoub bin Khalfan al Busaidy, Under-Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources for Fisheries. The forum included an exhibition featuring local goat breeds, rare animals, and distinctive birds. Animal wealth is a vital economic resource in Oman, contributing to self-sufficiency in animal products and food security. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources works on improving local breeds and enhancing the sector's growth rate.
records.institution: The Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources in Saham

records.title: The Ministry of Municipality (MoM) in Qatar has initiated a project to develop "protected farms" and climate-smart agriculture in collabo...
records.description: The Ministry of Municipality (MoM) in Qatar has initiated a project to develop "protected farms" and climate-smart agriculture in collaboration with South Korea. This project aims to convert open farm areas into closed farms to reduce evaporation, water loss, and address soil issues. It will assess climate changes that may impact food production in Qatar and propose measures to mitigate these effects, including the development of drought-resistant crops and modern agricultural practices. Workshops and capacity-building activities will be conducted to share knowledge and technology, fostering sustainable and resilient agriculture in Qatar.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia and the World Economic Forum's (WEF) innovation platform UpLink signed two agreements at the WEF Annual Meeting 2024 in Davo...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and the World Economic Forum's (WEF) innovation platform UpLink signed two agreements at the WEF Annual Meeting 2024 in Davos, Switzerland, to foster innovative global solutions for environmental and sustainability challenges. The agreements, titled 'Catalysing Innovation for an Ocean Positive Economy' and 'Catalysing Innovation for a Positive Circular Carbon Economy (CCE),' aim to support early-stage impact entrepreneurs and stimulate investments in solutions addressing issues such as ocean degradation, biodiversity loss, and circular carbon economy. The initiative, led by the Ministry of Economy and Planning (MEP) and involving multiple Saudi ministries and initiatives, emphasizes the importance of innovation and collaboration in addressing climate and sustainable development challenges. John Dutton, Head of UpLink, highlighted the significance of early-stage entrepreneurs in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and the role of UpLink in creating a supportive ecosystem for them.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Economy and Planning

records.title: African Development Bank and UK Select Tunisian Cereals Project as Prime Climate Finance Transaction Under Landmark Room to Run Sovereign Programme
records.description: The Inclusive and Sustainable Development of the Cereal Sector Project in Tunisia has been selected as a landmark project under the Room to Run Sovereign transaction (R2RS) by the African Development Bank and the United Kingdom. This project, approved in July 2023, aims to enhance the resilience of Tunisia's cereals sector against external shocks and climate change, benefiting up to 250,000 cereal farmers. Facilitated by a UK Government guarantee, it unlocks up to $35 million of the $87 million financing from the African Development Bank allocated for climate adaptation. R2RS, announced at COP26, enables the Bank to provide an additional $2 billion in climate finance to Africa by 2027, supporting adaptation and mitigation efforts. This project is the third selected by the UK under R2RS, reflecting its commitment to accelerating climate finance across the continent.
records.institution: African Development Bank & the United Kingdom

records.title: Egypt's Holding Company for Silos and Storage (EHCSS) has secured a $110 million loan from the World Bank to advance its National Silos P...
records.description: Egypt's Holding Company for Silos and Storage (EHCSS) has secured a $110 million loan from the World Bank to advance its National Silos Project. The funding will support the purchase of specialized equipment for field silos, as announced by EHCSS head Sherif Basily during the Egyptian Commodity Exchange conference. The project aims to establish 60 new silos nationwide, with six already completed and several under construction. Mechanization of 22 silos has been completed in the initial phase, integrating them into a unified information network system to enhance operational efficiency. This initiative, launched in 2015, utilizes cutting-edge technology to optimize wheat storage and distribution, crucial for Egypt, the world’s largest wheat importer consuming 18 million tons annually.
records.institution: Egyptian Holding Company for Silos and Storage (EHCSS)

records.title: Tanmeyah, a subsidiary of EFG Holding and a leading financial services provider in Egypt, has expanded its partnership with Gulf Insuranc...
records.description: Tanmeyah, a subsidiary of EFG Holding and a leading financial services provider in Egypt, has expanded its partnership with Gulf Insurance Group (GIG - Egypt), a major provider of non-life insurance solutions in the country. This collaboration will allow Tanmeyah to offer a range of innovative micro-insurance products aimed at promoting financial inclusion. The newly introduced insurance offerings cover various areas, including personal accidents, businesses, health (including cancer treatments and family health plans), funeral expenses, livestock, roadside assistance, and housing. These affordable and accessible micro-insurance products have received regulatory approval from the Financial Regulatory Authority. This partnership aims to enhance customer satisfaction, portfolio quality, and overall community well-being by providing essential insurance solutions to a broad customer base through Tanmeyah's network.

records.title: LyondellBasell (LYB) has announced its acquisition of a 35% stake in Saudi Arabia's National Petrochemical Industrial Company (NATPET) fr...
records.description: LyondellBasell (LYB) has announced its acquisition of a 35% stake in Saudi Arabia's National Petrochemical Industrial Company (NATPET) from Alujain Corporation for approximately $500 million. This joint venture, empowered by LYB's Spheripol polypropylene (PP) technology, provides LYB with opportunities to expand and enhance its core PP business by gaining access to beneficial feedstocks and increased product marketing capacity in a strategically important region. The completion of the transaction is subject to regulatory and customary closing conditions, and both Alujain and LYB are exploring the possibility of constructing a new propylene facility and a PP facility at the NATPET site in line with Saudi Arabia's 2060 carbon reduction strategy. This investment aligns with LYB's strategy of growing and upgrading its core assets and businesses.

records.title: Egyptian food manufacturing companies participated in the Nile Food Africa trade initiative, showcasing their products at the Egyptian tr...
records.description: Egyptian food manufacturing companies participated in the Nile Food Africa trade initiative, showcasing their products at the Egyptian trade mission to Kenya, held in Nairobi. The event aimed to connect Egyptian food manufacturers with trade opportunities in Kenya and link Kenyan business communities interested in the Egyptian market with suitable trade partners. Organized by the Egyptian Food Export Council (FEC) in Kenya, in collaboration with USAID-funded projects and the Egyptian Commercial Service (ECS), the Business-to-Business (B2B) mission forum featured over 26 Egyptian food manufacturers, including companies like Egyptian Swiss, Juhayna, Edita Foods, and Agthia Foods, among others. The Egyptian Ambassador to Kenya highlighted the importance of infrastructure development to facilitate trade within Africa and praised the role of the port of Mombasa in enhancing trade between Egypt and Kenya. Additionally, CIB Kenya CEO Daphne Maina discussed the bank's role in facilitating trade between the two COMESA nations.
records.institution: The Egyptian Food Export Council (FEC) in Kenya

records.title: Minister of Investment Khuloud Saqqaf highlighted Jordan's efforts to become one of the most attractive and conducive business and invest...
records.description: Minister of Investment Khuloud Saqqaf highlighted Jordan's efforts to become one of the most attractive and conducive business and investment environments by fostering collaboration between the public and private sectors. She emphasized Jordan's commitment to attracting more investments, particularly from Arab countries, and providing support for their empowerment. Saqqaf mentioned key reforms that have been implemented to enhance the investment and business environment, including the Investment Environment Law, the Investment Policy, and the Public-Private Partnership Law. These reforms have led to a 34% increase in investments benefiting from the law during the first nine months of 2023, totaling approximately JD879 million. The minister also discussed the "invest.jo" platform, which offers 36 different investment opportunities across various sectors and regions, with a total investment volume of $1.4 billion. These sectors encompass agriculture, education, energy, trade, transportation, ICT, tourism, and more. Additionally, the Ministry has automated 95 services related to licensing and economic activities, with future phases aiming to automate services related to other relevant authorities and investment references. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources has launched an e-platform to showcase investment opportunities in mineral resources, petroleum, and oil shale, facilitating interaction with relevant government agencies and allowing investors to submit their applications electronically.

records.title: In 2023, the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) reported a 12.07% increase in container handling across its managed ports.
records.description: In 2023, the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani) reported a 12.07% increase in container handling across its managed ports. May 2023 saw the highest monthly container handling statistics, with an 18.8% increase in handled containers. A total of 8,443,746 TEUs were handled, up from 7,534,307 TEUs the previous year. The annual container handling at Saudi Arabia's ports increased by 9.01%, reaching 11,380,302 TEUs compared to 10,439,620 TEUs. Exports and imports of containers increased by 15.56% and 12.68%, respectively, while transshipment containers rose by 8.96%. The number of vehicles imported increased by 40.54%, and passenger traffic grew by 41.3%. Maritime traffic also increased by 7.16%, with 12,130 vessels in 2023 compared to 11,320 vessels in 2022. Mawani signed contracts worth over SAR 1 billion in December 2023 to support Saudi Arabia's national transport and logistics strategy, including the introduction of new tugboats and maritime units.

records.title: Saudi Coffee Company, in collaboration with The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah), hosted...
records.description: Saudi Coffee Company, in collaboration with The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah), hosted a sustainability workshop titled "Fertilization Programs to Improve Coffee Production in the Kingdom" in Jazan, Saudi Arabia. The workshop aimed to advance coffee farming and production methods in the Kingdom, engaging local and international experts in soil management and fertilizers. Key stakeholders including Saudi Coffee Company, Estidamah, and Sabic participated to benefit from international expertise and develop specialized fertilizers for local coffee plantations. This initiative aligns with Saudi Coffee Company's commitment to drive sustainable practices and elevate the coffee industry's quality standards in Saudi Arabia, supporting the Kingdom's Vision 2030 goals. The workshop featured sessions on enhancing coffee quality, sustainable production, and strategies for resilient coffee planting in the face of climate change.
records.institution: Saudi Coffee Company & The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah)

records.title: KSrelief, the Saudi aid agency, has been actively involved in various health and aid projects in Yemen, particularly focusing on helping...
records.description: KSrelief, the Saudi aid agency, has been actively involved in various health and aid projects in Yemen, particularly focusing on helping people who have lost limbs due to the conflict. Through a prosthetics center in Aden governorate, KSrelief has provided physical therapy, prosthetic limb manufacturing, fitting, delivery, and maintenance services to 314 beneficiaries, including 73 patients who received prosthetic limbs. Additionally, the agency has distributed tents and shelter bags in Aden governorate, supported school bags initiatives, and worked on water supply and environmental sanitation projects. Yemen is among the top beneficiaries of KSrelief assistance, with numerous projects addressing food security, health, sanitation, shelter, nutrition, education, telecommunications, and logistics.

records.title: Iran's ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Alireza Enayati, and the Chairman of the Federation of Saudi Chambers of Commerce and Industry met to...
records.description: Iran's ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Alireza Enayati, and the Chairman of the Federation of Saudi Chambers of Commerce and Industry met to discuss expanding bilateral relations, particularly in the area of trade. They emphasized the potential for cooperation in various fields such as industry, agriculture, technical and engineering services, energy, and tourism. Both parties expressed their willingness to enhance economic ties between the two countries, aligning with Saudi Arabia's "Vision 2030" and emphasizing the importance of cooperation between the private sectors of Iran and Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: The Federation of Saudi Chambers of Commerce and Industry

records.title: The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a loan of US$302.9 million to support the construction of an electricity transmission li...
records.description: The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a loan of US$302.9 million to support the construction of an electricity transmission line connecting Mauritania and Mali. The loan includes US$269.6 million for Mauritania and US$33.3 million for Mali. The project involves the construction of a 225 kV high-voltage transmission line spanning a total length of 1,500 km, with two 50 MWp solar power plants in Mauritania. It will enable 100,000 new households to be connected to the electricity grid and create opportunities for agricultural entrepreneurship and services for young people and women. The project is part of AfDB's Desert to Power program, aiming to develop an installed solar capacity of 10,000 MW in the Sahel region.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Unveils Plan to Recycle up to 95% of Waste in 2024
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture has unveiled an ambitious plan to recycle up to 95% of the country's waste by 2024. This initiative is expected to contribute SR120 billion ($31.99 billion) to the gross domestic product and create over 100,000 jobs for Saudi nationals, with a goal of recycling up to 100 million tons of waste annually to promote sustainability. The plan is aligned with the Kingdom's sustainable development goals and includes more than 65 initiatives with an investment exceeding SR55 billion. In addition to waste recycling, the ministry's efforts have preserved over 90,000 hectares of land, planted 50 million trees across the country, and increased community awareness and environmental commitment, improving the quality of life. To further support waste management solutions, King Abdullah Financial District Development and Management Co. signed a memorandum of understanding with Saudi Investment Recycling Co. to promote recycling initiatives and environmentally friendly practices.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Salix Fruits, a US-based import-export company specializing in fresh fruits, is strengthening its partnerships with citrus producers in M...
records.description: Salix Fruits, a US-based import-export company specializing in fresh fruits, is strengthening its partnerships with citrus producers in Morocco, particularly mandarins and oranges. Vince Biasibetti, Executive Sales for the US at Salix Fruits, visited Morocco to deepen connections with growers, understand their operations, and secure sufficient volume for programs with US clients. Despite a previous reduction in production due to drought, there is optimism for a partial recovery in the current season. The focus will be on smaller-sized fruits, given the impact of drought in certain regions. Salix Fruits is also expanding its global presence by opening a new office in Singapore, aiming to enhance its presence in Asian markets and provide better support to clients while gaining deeper insights into the region's market dynamics.

records.title: Egypt has received Cabinet approval for a groundbreaking US$3.1 billion green hydrogen project developed in collaboration with Belgium's...
records.description: Egypt has received Cabinet approval for a groundbreaking US$3.1 billion green hydrogen project developed in collaboration with Belgium's DEME. The project will unfold in three phases and is strategically positioned near the Jarjoub sea port and the Jarjoub Special Economic Zone. Egypt aims to meet the growing demand for green hydrogen in the European market and strengthen its position as a regional and global energy exporter. The project reflects Egypt's commitment to sustainable energy practices and combating climate change. Additionally, the European Investment Bank (EIB) is in discussions with Norwegian renewable energy specialist Scatec to establish a partnership in green hydrogen production in Egypt, aligning with EIB's commitment to renewable energy.

records.title: Swedish company S2H2+Bm plans to establish a green hydrogen production facility in Morocco by 2025, with an anticipated annual capacity o...
records.description: Swedish company S2H2+Bm plans to establish a green hydrogen production facility in Morocco by 2025, with an anticipated annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes of green hydrogen by 2030. The company aims to disrupt the green hydrogen landscape by leveraging innovation and low-cost renewable energy sources, particularly solar energy, to achieve a highly competitive production cost of less than $2 per kilogram of green hydrogen in Morocco. The project is supported by the Moroccan government, and the specific location in the southern region of Morocco is being considered for its favorable photovoltaic power potential. S2H2+Bm plans to raise additional capital in Q1 2024 to support the venture.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Aster Pharmacy in the UAE has made a significant shift towards sustainability by replacing plastic bags with recyclable paper bags as par...
records.description: Aster Pharmacy in the UAE has made a significant shift towards sustainability by replacing plastic bags with recyclable paper bags as part of its Green Choices initiative. Over the past three years, the company has successfully implemented this change, using 7.4 million paper bags annually to serve customers. This transition aligns with the UAE's Green Agenda 2023 and global efforts to combat plastic pollution. Aster Pharmacy, part of the Aster DM Healthcare Group, has been committed to eco-friendly practices, including using sustainable and recyclable materials for store interiors. The organization's waste recycling initiatives have contributed to a more sustainable environment.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power, leading a coalition, has signed a leasing agreement with Egypt's New and Renewable Energy Authority to establi...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power, leading a coalition, has signed a leasing agreement with Egypt's New and Renewable Energy Authority to establish a 1.1 gigawatt wind farm in the Suez Gulf and Gabal El Zeit regions. The project, valued at $1.5 billion, aims to reduce carbon emissions by 2.4 million tons and fuel consumption by 840,000 tons. It is expected to create around 6,000 direct and indirect jobs and provide electricity to approximately one million residential units. The wind turbines to be installed will be among the tallest in the Suez Gulf, reaching a height of 220 meters. The agreement outlines that the coalition will conduct the site feasibility study and secure financing for the project.

records.title: A UAE-based company is set to invest $30 million in a berry farming project in Uzbekistan's Andijan region, as reported by the Ministry o...
records.description: A UAE-based company is set to invest $30 million in a berry farming project in Uzbekistan's Andijan region, as reported by the Ministry of Agriculture. The project, a collaboration between the Agency for Agricultural Services under the Ministry of Agriculture and the Emirati company, will establish a 470-hectare berry farm in the Pakhtaabad district. Initially, the focus will be on cultivating blueberries using drip irrigation systems on 20 hectares. The project's long-term plan includes the cultivation of blueberries, raspberries, and vegetable products. With an estimated yield of 400-500 tons per hectare when planting 4,000 bushes, special nets will be used to protect the berries from heat. The investment is part of the UAE company's broader initiative to create an agricultural cluster in the Andijan region, encompassing berry plantations and fisheries.

records.title: Egypt's plastic product exports have surged to $1.75 billion in 2023, accounting for 27% of total exports from the chemical and fertilize...
records.description: Egypt's plastic product exports have surged to $1.75 billion in 2023, accounting for 27% of total exports from the chemical and fertilizer sector, according to the Chemical and Fertilizers Export Council (CEC). The CEC has launched PLASTEX 2024 and Egypt Plast 2024 exhibitions, featuring intermediate and final plastic products, petrochemical raw materials, and related equipment. These exhibitions have attracted numerous participating companies from various countries. In 2021, Egypt's plastic product exports reached $2 billion, marking the growing significance of the plasticware industry in the country's local manufacturing landscape. The government's support and investments in this sector have played a crucial role in its growth.
records.institution: The Chemical and Fertilizers Export Council (CEC)

records.title: In 2023, Egypt's plastic product exports surged to a significant figure of US$1.75 billion, accounting for 27% of total exports from the...
records.description: In 2023, Egypt's plastic product exports surged to a significant figure of US$1.75 billion, accounting for 27% of total exports from the chemical and fertilizer sector, according to the Chemical and Fertilizers Export Council (CEC). This announcement came during the launch of PLASTEX 2024 and the Egypt Plast 2024 exhibitions, supported by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and Minister of Trade and Industry Ahmed Samir. These exhibitions featured intermediate and final plastic products, petrochemical raw materials, and related equipment, with 118 participating companies in Egypt Plast and 242 companies in PLASTEX, including international participants from countries such as China, Turkey, Taiwan, India, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, Morocco, and Italy. Egypt's plasticware industry has grown over the past decade, with plastic materials increasingly replacing other materials like glass and metals in manufacturing. The government's support for this industry is evident through the establishment of industrial complexes for tupperware industries in Alexandria, providing a significant boost to the plastic sector.
records.institution: Egyptian Chemical and Fertilizers Export Council (CEC)

records.title: Pakistan aims to increase its trade exchange with Egypt by tenfold in the coming years, according to Gohar Ejaz, the Pakistani Federal Mi...
records.description: Pakistan aims to increase its trade exchange with Egypt by tenfold in the coming years, according to Gohar Ejaz, the Pakistani Federal Minister for Industries and Commerce. He made this announcement during the fourth edition of the Pakistan Africa Trade Development Conference (PATDC) and Single Country Exhibition (SCE) held in Cairo. Egypt serves as a gateway to Africa and already maintains strong trade relations with Pakistan. The conference's goal is to facilitate joint agreements between African and Pakistani parties across various sectors, including agriculture, textiles, engineering, services, and energy. During the fiscal year 2021/2022, the trade exchange between Egypt and Pakistan reached $400 million, with Egypt exporting $300 million worth of natural gas, oil products, cotton, and other goods to Pakistan in that period. The event provides a platform for business collaboration and has previously resulted in agreements worth millions of dollars between Pakistani and African companies.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry

records.title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are expected to advance discussions on a potential investment deal regarding the Reko Diq copper and gold proje...
records.description: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are expected to advance discussions on a potential investment deal regarding the Reko Diq copper and gold project during the three-day mineral forum in Riyadh. Led by Energy Minister Muhammad Ali, a high-level Pakistani delegation is attending the Future Minerals Forum (FMF) to promote mineral value chains. Officials from various Pakistani organizations, including SIFC, PMDC, OGDCL, PPL, and GSP, are part of the delegation. Besides the Reko Diq project, the delegation is likely to discuss Saudi Arabia's interest in constructing a refinery in Pakistan. Saudi Arabia aims to attract significant investments in its mining industry, estimated to exceed $1.3 trillion, and the visit may lead to a deal between the two countries for the Reko Diq project and a state-of-the-art deep conversion refinery. Saudi Arabia's interest in various sectors, including mining, agriculture, and energy, reflects its commitment to enhancing its investment footprint in Pakistan.

records.title: Egypt has planted 3 million feddan (acres) of wheat since November 2023, representing a year-on-year increase of nearly half a million ac...
records.description: Egypt has planted 3 million feddan (acres) of wheat since November 2023, representing a year-on-year increase of nearly half a million acres. This information was shared during a meeting between Egypt's Minister of Agriculture, and Prime Minister where they discussed the cultivation of wheat and its significance for achieving food security in Egypt. The meeting also addressed the status of various agricultural crops in the market, emphasizing the Ministry's efforts to supply sufficient quantities of these crops across the country. Additionally, Egypt's wheat imports saw a 14.5% increase to 11 million tons in 2023 compared to 9.6 million tons in 2022. Egypt raised the local wheat procurement price to LE 1,600 per wheat ardeb (around 150 kilograms) from LE 1,500 to incentivize domestic wheat production. Egypt also signed a $500 million agreement to purchase wheat from Al-Dahra in a 5-year deal worth $100 million per year.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Supply, Ali Al-Moselhi, has provided assurance regarding the country's strong strategic reserves, stating that Egypt'...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Supply, Ali Al-Moselhi, has provided assurance regarding the country's strong strategic reserves, stating that Egypt's wheat reserves can sustain the nation for approximately 4.3 months. This announcement follows the General Authority for Supply and Commodities' (GASC) procurement of 480,000 tonnes of wheat from Russia to enhance the stock of basic commodities. The purchased wheat includes 180,000 tonnes for shipment from February 1-14 and 300,000 tonnes for shipment from February 15-29. Al-Moselhi also highlighted the government's ambitious plan to cultivate approximately 3 million acres of wheat during the ongoing season, along with a goal to procure around 3.5 million tons of locally produced wheat in the upcoming season to bolster domestic agricultural production. Despite a recent report from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) projecting Egypt's wheat ending stocks to reach their lowest level in 20 years due to increased demand and trade flow changes, Egypt is committed to meeting the growing consumption demand, with imports expected to rise by 7% to 12 million tonnes in 2023-24. Additionally, Egypt's strategic reserves of sugar and vegetable oils are sufficient to meet national requirements for 5.3 months.

records.title: Arab Planning Institute Launches Entrepreneurship Project In Lebanon
records.description: The Arab Planning Institute (API) has launched a project in Tripoli, Lebanon, aimed at promoting entrepreneurship and self-employment. This initiative, launched under the patronage of Lebanon's Prime Minister Najib Mikati, underscores API's vision of a unified Arab world and the need for increased capabilities, strategic planning, and development to achieve the development goals of Arab states. Recognizing Lebanon's economic challenges, the project focuses on training and empowering Lebanese youth to foster innovative and productive ventures. Tripoli's Chairman of Chamber of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture, Tawfiq Dabousefi, expressed optimism about the partnership with API and emphasized Lebanon's potential to contribute to economic development in the Arab world. The project includes training programs, contests, and support for establishing and maintaining private businesses to combat unemployment and empower the youth population and graduates in entrepreneurship and self-employment endeavors.

records.title: ADAFSA Launches Ambitious Plan to Expand Recycled Water Use in Abu Dhabi Farms
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has unveiled an ambitious plan to expand the use of recycled water in agriculture in Abu Dhabi. ADAFSA, in collaboration with strategic partners including the Department of Energy - Abu Dhabi (DoE), the Environment Agency - Abu Dhabi (EAD), and TAQA, aims to deliver recycled water to over 1,600 farms in Al Khatam, Al Khaznah, and Al Nahda areas. This initiative aligns with sustainability goals and aims to reduce pressure on groundwater resources, ultimately conserving non-renewable water resources and promoting the sustainable development of the agricultural sector. By utilizing recycled water, ADAFSA intends to reduce groundwater depletion and reliance on desalinated seawater, fostering more sustainable agricultural practices and systems. The project corresponds with the UAE Water Security Strategy 2036 objectives and Abu Dhabi's recycled water policy to maximize recycled water usage. Additionally, it offers environmental and economic benefits by cleaning and disinfecting discharged water and contributing to the rational use of groundwater in agriculture.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Dubai has implemented a ban on single-use plastic bags starting from January 1, 2024, through Executive Council Resolution No.
records.description: Dubai has implemented a ban on single-use plastic bags starting from January 1, 2024, through Executive Council Resolution No. (124) of 2023 concerning single-use products. The resolution, championed by Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, aims to promote sustainable recycling practices and reduce the environmental impact of plastic waste. The ban covers various single-use disposable products, including plastic bags, food delivery packaging, and containers. While there are exceptions for specific items like waste bags and packaging for food items, non-compliance can result in fines ranging from Dh200 (US$54.46) to Dh2,000 (US$544.60) for repeat violations within a year. Dubai's government is also launching awareness campaigns to encourage citizens to minimize plastic use and opt for eco-friendly alternatives, alongside initiatives to enhance recycling efforts and reduce plastic waste's environmental impact. This move aligns with Dubai's commitment to environmental sustainability and waste management goals, contributing to the UAE's broader vision of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.

records.title: Tunisia has significantly increased its wheat imports from Russia in the first half of the 2023/2024 agricultural year (July-December), i...
records.description: Tunisia has significantly increased its wheat imports from Russia in the first half of the 2023/2024 agricultural year (July-December), importing 412,000 tonnes of wheat, which is 50% more than the total wheat imports of 278,000 tonnes during the entire 2022/2023 marketing campaign. This surge in imports reflects Tunisia's desire to source more wheat from Russia. Soft wheat accounted for 66% of the imported stock, while the remainder was made up of durum wheat. Barley exports from Russia to Tunisia also saw significant growth in the same period, reaching 248,000 tonnes, exceeding the figure of 160,000 tonnes for the entire 2022/2023 agricultural year. Russia, as the world's leading exporter of wheat, is looking to expand its grain shipments to several North African countries in the 2023/2024 marketing campaign.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: Cairo 3A for Poultry, a subsidiary of Egypt's agri-food group Cairo 3A, is planning to invest $32.3 million in Egypt's poultry industry i...
records.description: Cairo 3A for Poultry, a subsidiary of Egypt's agri-food group Cairo 3A, is planning to invest $32.3 million in Egypt's poultry industry in 2024. This investment will be split between the construction of a poultry products processing plant, covering 3 hectares in the Sharkia governorate, with approximately $26 million allocated for this purpose, and the establishment of new poultry fattening farms aimed at increasing bird production for slaughter. The CEO of Cairo 3A for Poultry, Ibrahim Wagdy, believes that these investments are crucial for consolidating the company's position in the frozen and chilled chicken segment, where it currently holds a 25% market share. Despite facing challenges in 2023, including a 40% sales decline, the company anticipates a rebound of 20% to 25% in 2024.

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is facilitating a training program to enhance animal feeding practices in southern governorat...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is facilitating a training program to enhance animal feeding practices in southern governorates of Iraq. This initiative, supported by the Iraqi government and the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), aims to assist 15,000 buffalo breeders and their 263,000 buffalos in Basra, Muthana, Thi-Qar, and Missan. A "Training of Trainers" (ToT) program was conducted, involving 100 MoA extension officers trained by their peers, who had previously received training from FAO experts and were involved in implementing successful FAO-EU funded projects. The program focuses on sustainable animal feeding practices, climate-smart agriculture, and the optimal use of resources, including molasses and fodder crops. It aims to strengthen Iraq's agricultural sector and aligns with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals, particularly in promoting food security and responsible consumption and production.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: Morocco significantly increased its soft wheat imports from Russia in 2023, with approximately 81,300 tons of soft wheat imported from Ru...
records.description: Morocco significantly increased its soft wheat imports from Russia in 2023, with approximately 81,300 tons of soft wheat imported from Russia by December, making Russia Morocco's third-largest soft wheat exporter. France and Lithuania were the top two exporters of soft wheat to Morocco in 2023. This surge in Russian wheat imports comes as Morocco explores diversifying its sources of wheat imports due to concerns about the reliability of traditional suppliers like France. Nearly 70% of these shipments were unloaded at the port of Casablanca. The move highlights the importance of international cooperation in addressing energy and food crises.
records.institution: Moroccan National Federation of Cereals and Legumes Traders (FNCL)

records.title: Tunisia Will Soon Have a “Water 2050” Strategy
records.description: Tunisia is embarking on a comprehensive strategic planning initiative known as "Water 2050" to address water security concerns in the context of climate change. Tunisia is particularly vulnerable to water stress and persistent drought, and while recent rains have positively impacted grain crops, the dam fill rate remains below the required level at 27%. Despite maintaining water reserves at the same level as the previous year, distribution among reservoirs, especially for drinking water, is a concern. Tunisia ranks as the 30th driest Mediterranean country and faces challenges related to uneven geographical water resource distribution and frequent droughts, particularly in the northwest. The country is implementing strategies to link dams to ensure resource supply, focusing on meeting high demand areas like major cities and the coast. Additionally, there are plans to cope with peak consumption in the summer of 2024, including the opening of two seawater desalination plants. A strategic study will extend water sector planning up to 2050, emphasizing integrated and sustainable resource management, supply of drinking water as a priority, and utilizing modern technologies for sustainable food security and climate change mitigation.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries (MAHP)

records.title: In response to a severe economic crisis and a shortage of foreign currency, Egypt's cabinet has approved the sale of specific parcels of...
records.description: In response to a severe economic crisis and a shortage of foreign currency, Egypt's cabinet has approved the sale of specific parcels of land to foreign companies in US dollars. These lands will be designated for various purposes, including commercial, administrative, and residential projects, although specific pricing details were not provided. This move aims to attract foreign investment, allow foreigners to purchase real estate without restrictions, and enable expatriates to import duty-free cars. Egypt has been actively selling state assets to wealthy Gulf nations to bolster its foreign currency reserves and reduce state and military control over the economy, as part of a $3 billion loan program signed with the IMF. Additionally, the planning ministry reported a significant drop in remittances from Egyptians working abroad, signaling concerns about the local currency's stability against the US dollar. The Egyptian pound has faced ongoing challenges in its exchange rate against the US dollar, leading to increased import costs and rising prices for goods.

records.title: Prime Minister Bisher Khasawneh held a meeting with Thani Al Zeyoudi, the United Arab Emirates' Minister of State for Foreign Trade, to d...
records.description: Prime Minister Bisher Khasawneh held a meeting with Thani Al Zeyoudi, the United Arab Emirates' Minister of State for Foreign Trade, to discuss investment cooperation and strengthen bilateral ties between Jordan and the UAE. During the meeting, Khasawneh emphasized the close relationship between the two nations and discussed mutual cooperation in trade and investment. They explored ways to enhance collaborative projects that would benefit both countries. Khasawneh expressed Jordan's support for the UAE hosting the 13th Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and confirmed Jordan's participation in the event. Additionally, they discussed opportunities for Jordan to share its expertise in the food and drug sector with the UAE, particularly in light of the establishment of the UAE Drug Authority.
records.institution: Jordanian Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply

records.title: Turkish milling equipment company, Alapala, has successfully completed the construction of a semolina production plant for Imandy Mills i...
records.description: Turkish milling equipment company, Alapala, has successfully completed the construction of a semolina production plant for Imandy Mills in Morocco. This state-of-the-art facility, with a daily processing capacity of 240 tonnes of durum wheat, maize, and barley, also boasts a cereal storage capacity of 120,000 tonnes to support market demands. The plant is expected to enhance Imandy Mills' production capabilities and promote sustainable and technologically advanced agro-processing practices in Morocco. Founded in 2014, Imandy Mills, a subsidiary of the Africa Feed and Food Group, will expand its product offerings to meet a broader consumer base. This collaboration highlights the significance of international partnerships in driving innovation and progress in the agribusiness sector and is deemed mutually beneficial for both companies and the Moroccan economy. For Alapala, this success strengthens its presence in the African region and demonstrates its commitment to delivering seamless international services. Alapala utilized its expertise in design, automation, and remote service support, enhancing efficiency and product quality throughout the production process.

records.title: EY to Advise Iraq on Banking and Insurance Reforms
records.description: The Iraqi Cabinet has approved a series of contracts with Ernst & Young (EY), a UK-based professional services firm, to initiate reforms in Iraq's banking and insurance sectors. The first contract focuses on a comprehensive study to restructure state-owned Rafidain Bank and Rasheed Bank, with recommendations and a roadmap expected within six months. The second contract involves studying the merger of Industrial Bank, Real Estate Bank, and Agricultural Bank into a single entity, with EY providing expertise and recommendations, along with determining the merger timeline and balance transfer mechanisms. The third contract addresses the merger of the National Insurance Company with the Iraqi Insurance Company, with EY providing recommendations on the process and fund transfer to a new entity.

records.title: Jordan is in the process of establishing its first national seeds bank, with 30% of the work already completed, and the bank is expected...
records.description: Jordan is in the process of establishing its first national seeds bank, with 30% of the work already completed, and the bank is expected to be operational in 2024. This initiative aligns with Jordan's efforts to protect its national food security by creating a research and conservation facility for local plant seeds. The focus will be on genetic resources related to food and agriculture. Jordan's Hashemite University, in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, is responsible for launching the seeds bank, which began construction in 2022 in the capital city, Amman.

records.title: Morocco is establishing a monitoring committee to ensure the availability of affordable seafood products during the holy month of Ramadan...
records.description: Morocco is establishing a monitoring committee to ensure the availability of affordable seafood products during the holy month of Ramadan, which is expected to begin in March. This initiative was discussed during a meeting between Minister of Agriculture Mohamed Sadiki and fisheries sector professionals in Rabat. The central committee will oversee the consistent supply of high-quality seafood products across Morocco's markets, ensuring an adequate quantity of fresh and frozen fish. The committee will also conduct daily price inspections along the value chain, including wholesale and retail markets. This effort aims to provide consumers with reasonably priced seafood while maintaining health and quality standards during Ramadan, a month of fasting observed by Muslims.

records.title: Egypt's membership in the BRICS economic bloc became officially activated under Russian leadership.
records.description: Egypt's membership in the BRICS economic bloc became officially activated under Russian leadership. The BRICS, originally formed by Russia, Brazil, China, and India in 2006 and later joined by South Africa in 2011, expanded to include Egypt, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iran, and Ethiopia in August 2023. Egypt's move to join BRICS comes amid a severe economic downturn, record inflation, and rising external debts. By participating in BRICS, Egypt aims to reduce its dependence on the US dollar in its economy, particularly in international trade. The inclusion of Egypt and other new member countries is expected to enhance the group's economic and political influence on the global stage, potentially challenging the dominance of the US dollar in international commerce.

records.title: Privately-owned MAFI For Agricultural Produce Industries has entered into contracts with international agricultural companies to establis...
records.description: Privately-owned MAFI For Agricultural Produce Industries has entered into contracts with international agricultural companies to establish a $300 million food production complex in Sadat City, which will become the largest of its kind in the Middle East. This initiative aligns with the Egyptian government's goals to enhance the country's industrial capabilities and exports. The complex, spanning 154,000 square meters, will consist of five plants and produce a wide range of food products, including orange concentrates, tomatoes, various fruits, and essential oils. It will also feature cutting-edge freeze-drying technology and a plant for freezing fruits and vegetables. In its initial stage, the complex is expected to produce up to 100,000 tons of food products annually, creating over 7,000 direct and indirect jobs. The signing ceremony, attended by Egypt's Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, underscores the government's commitment to supporting production expansion, attracting investments, and strengthening the role of the private sector in driving economic recovery and growth in the country throughout 2024.
records.institution: Egyptian MAFI For Agricultural Produce Industries

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Tunisia have signed seven memoranda of understanding (MoUs) during the 11th session of the Saudi-Tunisian Joint Committe...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Tunisia have signed seven memoranda of understanding (MoUs) during the 11th session of the Saudi-Tunisian Joint Committee in Tunis, aiming to strengthen cooperation in various fields. Two of the MoUs focus on agricultural scientific research and environmental protection, involving the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture and the Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, as well as the Ministry of Environment. Additionally, an MoU on industrial cooperation was signed between the Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources and the Tunisian Ministry of Industry and Energy, while another MoU pertained to tourism between the two countries. Further agreements covered labor, climate, and meteorology cooperation. During Q3 2023, Saudi non-oil exports to Tunisia amounted to SR513.42 million ($140 million), primarily consisting of chemicals, polymers, packaging, and building materials, while imports from Tunisia reached SR206.59 million, primarily in food products, textiles, heavy machinery, and electronics. The Saudi Industrial Development Fund contributed SR3.8 million to finance one project in Tunisia.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources

records.title: Agriculture Ministry, MSSRP Ink MoU for Sustainable Agriculture, Municipal Growth
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in Jordan has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Municipal Services and Social Resilience Project (MSSRP) to foster sustainable agriculture and municipal development initiatives across the country. The MoU aims to promote sustainable agriculture practices that engage the community in production activities, thereby enhancing local economies and driving social change. The project is funded by several governments, including Canada, the UK, the Netherlands, and the USAID, through a multi-donor trust fund managed by the World Bank. It seeks to establish a municipal culture focusing on human development elements like food, energy, water, and the environment. By investing in municipality-owned assets and existing resources, the project aims to create specialized agricultural initiatives that generate employment opportunities.
records.institution: Jordanian Ministry of Agriculture & the Municipal Services and Social Resilience Project (MSSRP)

records.title: German Bank Provides 257 Million Euros in Loans and Grants for Morocco
records.description: Rabat has entered into agreements with the German Development Bank, securing three loan contracts totaling 250 million euros and two grant contracts worth 7 million euros. These agreements encompass financial support for social protection, sustainable mobility, and irrigation projects in Morocco. The first subsidized loan of 120 million euros, along with a 2 million euro donation, aims to enhance living conditions through a social protection initiative. The second loan, amounting to 100 million euros and accompanied by a 5 million euro donation, will be directed towards supporting urban and interurban road transport reforms. The third loan of 30 million euros is dedicated to improving water consumption efficiency in irrigated agriculture.

records.title: Tunisia and Saudi Arabia have signed seven memorandums of understanding (MoUs) aimed at bolstering bilateral cooperation in various fields.
records.description: Tunisia and Saudi Arabia have signed seven memorandums of understanding (MoUs) aimed at bolstering bilateral cooperation in various fields. These MoUs encompass cooperation in water management, environmental protection, agricultural scientific research, climate and meteorology, tourism, industry, and employment. The agreements were formalized during a signing ceremony in the Tunisian capital of Tunis between Tunisian Finance Minister Sihem Boughdiri Nemsia and Saudi Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Bandar bin Ibrahim Alkhorayef.
