Both countries expressed their commitment to enhancing cooperation, particularly in trade and investment.

records.title: An agreement between the Associations Support Fund (ASF) and the Sekaya Charitable Foundation in Saudi Arabia aims to strengthen collabor...
records.description: An agreement between the Associations Support Fund (ASF) and the Sekaya Charitable Foundation in Saudi Arabia aims to strengthen collaboration in water irrigation projects. The agreement intends to establish a sub-fund known as the Water Associations Support Fund, which will focus on developing and empowering entities involved in the water irrigation sector in the Kingdom. This initiative aligns with the goals outlined in Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. The Sekaya Charitable Foundation specializes in organizing and providing charitable water resources and plays a vital role in executing charitable watering projects in underserved villages and areas across the country. The foundation's efforts aim to enhance the sustainability and efficiency of charitable organizations involved in managing and operating such projects in line with national objectives.
records.institution: The Associations Support Fund & The Sekaya Charitable Foundation

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the National Co.
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the National Co. for Agricultural Services (AgriServ) to enhance support for the agricultural sector. AgriServ, a government-owned entity founded in 2018, is dedicated to achieving the goals of the agricultural sector outlined in Vision 2030. Under the agreement, the Environment Ministry will offer data, monitoring, compliance, and coordination support to AgriServ's operations, while AgriServ will carry out all operational tasks for the services it is responsible for, following an agreed-upon timeline. This collaboration aims to improve the quality of services provided to the beneficiaries of the farming sector, promoting agricultural growth and food security in Saudi Arabia.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Egyptian Parliament Committee Approves Draft Law Regarding Incentives for Green Hydrogen Projects
records.description: Egypt's Energy and Environment Committee of the House of Representatives, led by MP Talaat Al-Suwaidi, has approved a government-drafted bill offering incentives for green hydrogen projects and their derivatives. The draft law provides both tax and non-tax incentives as part of Egypt's commitment to optimizing the production, use, and export of clean green energy. The strategy aims to position Egypt as a leading country in the low-carbon hydrogen economy, creating jobs, increasing national income, and reducing emissions. The National Green Hydrogen Council previously approved the National Green Hydrogen Strategy, which targets a 5 to 8 percent share of the global hydrogen market, job creation, and GDP growth.
records.institution: Egyptian Energy and Environment Committee of the House of Representatives

records.title: Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture has confirmed that an Iran-backed company will implement a controversial project to plant one million palm...
records.description: Iraq's Ministry of Agriculture has confirmed that an Iran-backed company will implement a controversial project to plant one million palm trees across two million dunums of land in the Southern Iraqi Samawah desert, near the Saudi Arabian border. The project will use modern irrigation systems and wells powered by solar energy.

records.title: Despite rising tensions in the Red Sea, Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply assures that over 90% of the country's wheat and...
records.description: Despite rising tensions in the Red Sea, Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply assures that over 90% of the country's wheat and barley imports remain unaffected. These imports primarily come from Eastern European countries like Romania and Montenegro, and they reach Jordan's Aqaba port via the Suez Canal. However, disruptions in Red Sea shipping have led to some operations being suspended, causing shippers to explore alternative routes and adaptations. The Jordanian government is actively seeking alternative sea freight routes to ensure a stable supply of essential commodities like wheat and barley, especially given the country's reliance on the Bab Al Mandeb Strait, where tensions are escalating. Jordan aims to maintain a sufficient wheat stockpile to cover local consumption for nine months, and it has recently issued a tender to purchase an additional 120,000 tonnes of wheat to strengthen its reserves.
records.institution: Jordanian Ministry of Industry, Trade, and Supply

records.title: Jordan and Egypt have agreed to activate a new maritime route between Aqaba in Jordan and Egyptian ports on the Mediterranean Sea.
records.description: Jordan and Egypt have agreed to activate a new maritime route between Aqaba in Jordan and Egyptian ports on the Mediterranean Sea. This decision comes in response to several major shipping companies suspending their operations in the Red Sea and seeking alternative routes due to rising tensions in the region, particularly in the Bab el Mandeb Strait. The new maritime route will connect Aqaba to Egyptian ports like Alexandria, Port Said, and Damietta. It is expected to serve the transportation needs of both land and sea trade, offering an alternative path for Jordanian exports to the United States and Europe, including industrial and agricultural products. This initiative aims to diversify trade routes, reduce transportation costs, and enhance Jordan's competitiveness in emerging supply routes. It also seeks to streamline the movement of Jordanian exports to their final destinations and boost transit trade through the ports of Aqaba and Nuweiba in Egypt, increasing their regional competitiveness.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Morocco is facing its sixth consecutive year of drought due to a significant drop in rainfall in recent months linked to climate change,...
records.description: Morocco is facing its sixth consecutive year of drought due to a significant drop in rainfall in recent months linked to climate change, according to Morocco's Minister of Equipment and Water, Nizar Baraka. Rainfall has declined by 67% in recent months compared to a normal year. This extended period of drought poses a significant challenge for Morocco, where agriculture is a crucial sector, employing a third of the working-age population and contributing 14% of the country's exports. Rising temperatures have exacerbated water stress in Morocco, increasing water evaporation from dams. The country's reservoirs are currently only 23.5% full, compared to 31% at the same time last year. To address the water crisis, Morocco is focusing on seawater desalination projects, with plans to build seven desalination plants by the end of 2027, totaling 143 million cubic meters per year in capacity.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Equipment and Water

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Permanent Executive Committee for Fuel Stations and Service Centers has announced updated terms and conditions for fuel st...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Permanent Executive Committee for Fuel Stations and Service Centers has announced updated terms and conditions for fuel stations and service centers to regulate and develop the sector in line with global energy industry standards and Vision 2030 goals. The updated requirements aim to improve the establishment, management, operation, and maintenance of these facilities and enhance the services they offer. Key requirements include the operation of fuel stations by qualified facilities, specific distances between gas stations within and outside urban areas, and criteria related to pumps, tanks, cleanliness, maintenance, product quality, and service provision. Existing stations have a 12-month corrective period from the date of publication to comply with the updated terms.
records.institution: Saudi Permanent Executive Committee for Fuel Stations and Service Centers

records.title: Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov announced during a visit to Tunisia that Russia is prepared to supply more grain to Tunisia, whic...
records.description: Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov announced during a visit to Tunisia that Russia is prepared to supply more grain to Tunisia, which is facing grain shortages due to drought. Tunisia heavily relies on grain imports, particularly durum wheat, soft wheat, and barley, and is in need of these imports until at least spring 2024. Lavrov did not specify the conditions or cost of the increased grain deliveries but expressed Russia's willingness to assist Tunisia. Tunisia's President Kais Saied met with Lavrov in Tunis, where they discussed enhancing cooperation in various sectors, including agriculture, energy, nuclear power, and technology. Lavrov also emphasized that Russia's intent is not to replace Tunisia's other partners, such as the United States and the European Union.

records.title: During the sixth meeting of the Kazakh-Saudi Intergovernmental Joint Committee on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technical, and Cultural Co...
records.description: During the sixth meeting of the Kazakh-Saudi Intergovernmental Joint Committee on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technical, and Cultural Cooperation in Riyadh, Kazakh Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Murat Nurtleu emphasized the strategic importance of enhancing cooperation between Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia. He highlighted the significant potential of the Saudi market for strengthening trade and economic relations, particularly in sectors such as green energy, food security, transport and logistics, mining, petrochemicals, agriculture, finance, and tourism. Nurtleu regarded Saudi Arabia as a crucial partner for Kazakhstan in the Middle East and the international arena. The meeting also included a Kazakh-Saudi investment round table, bringing together business representatives from both countries, and discussions on deepening collaboration and establishing joint ventures in various sectors. Saudi Minister of Investment Khalid Al-Falih expressed his country's keen interest in strengthening ties with Kazakhstan, and the event featured speeches from heads of large Saudi companies, including Saudi Aramco and ACWA Power. Additionally, Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia signed agreements related to visa exemptions for diplomatic and service passport holders and the establishment of a joint innovation hub.

records.title: Jordan Boosts Agricultural Investment to Drive Economic Resilience Amid Water Scarcity
records.description: In a bid to foster sustainable growth and economic resilience in the face of water scarcity, Jordan is increasing its investment in the agricultural sector. The Agriculture Ministry's capital expenditure is set to reach JD40 million in the coming year, highlighting the country's commitment to maximizing the value of agriculture in its economy. Despite water challenges, Jordan currently produces 60% of its agricultural products for local consumption and exports to over 60 countries. The agricultural sector contributes 20% to the country's GDP and plays a vital role in ensuring food security, generating employment opportunities, addressing climate change, and supporting the green economy. Efforts to reorganize the sector include agricultural guidance, collaboration with farmers, training, and marketing initiatives. The Agricultural Credit Fund has also expanded lending to support farmers' initiatives. Jordan aims to address production surplus challenges by processing surplus produce and investing in agricultural manufacturing and technology.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The African Development Fund’s Board of Directors has approved a $302.9 million loan for the Mauritania-Mali Electricity Interconnection...
records.description: The African Development Fund’s Board of Directors has approved a $302.9 million loan for the Mauritania-Mali Electricity Interconnection Project, which is part of the Desert to Power Initiative. This initiative aims to benefit 100,000 households in both Mauritania and Mali. Of the total project cost estimated at $888 million, $269.6 million will be allocated to Mauritania, and $33.3 million to Mali. The project involves a 225kV electricity interconnection between the two countries and the establishment of solar power facilities to rapidly increase solar energy production and expand electricity access in the Sahel region. It includes a 1,373-kilometer high-voltage electrical interconnection, a 50 MW solar power plant, and integration of 100,000 households into the power grid. The project is part of a broader plan connecting Mauritania to Chad via Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, with the goal of enhancing access to eco-friendly electricity and fostering economic development.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Climate change is having a significant impact on Moroccan farmers, especially in regions like Fez-Meknes, where drought has become a stru...
records.description: Climate change is having a significant impact on Moroccan farmers, especially in regions like Fez-Meknes, where drought has become a structural problem. Fatima Zahrae Lamnassra, a farmer in Oued Roumane, has experienced firsthand the challenges of climate change, including drying rivers and unpredictable weather patterns. In response, Moroccan farmers are adopting more resilient production techniques to safeguard their livelihoods. They are exploring drought-resistant seed varieties, slow-release nitrogen applications, drip irrigation, and no-tillage systems for better soil and water conservation. Additionally, strategies like storing harvests and staggered sales are being employed to cope with food insecurity. The World Bank is supporting Morocco's efforts to build a more resilient and sustainable agricultural system through projects like the Resilient and Sustainable Water in Agriculture Project (RESWAG) and the "Green Generation" Programs-For-Results program. These initiatives aim to modernize irrigation, enhance water governance, provide agricultural advice, and promote youth employment in the agricultural sector. Moroccan farmers are increasingly recognizing the need for innovative solutions and climate-smart practices to address the challenges posed by climate change.

records.title: The Omani-Austrian Business Forum recently convened to explore avenues for enhancing cooperation across multiple sectors, encompassing to...
records.description: The Omani-Austrian Business Forum recently convened to explore avenues for enhancing cooperation across multiple sectors, encompassing tourism, industry, construction, infrastructure, information technology, and medical education. Organized by the Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI) in partnership with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion in Muscat, the forum also delved into incentives and investment prospects within the Sultanate of Oman. Faisal Abdullah al Rawas, Chairman of the OCCI Board of Directors, emphasized the potential for joint projects between Oman and Austria to bolster investment and trade exchanges. Dr. Martin Kocher, Austrian Minister of Labour and Economy, highlighted the opportunity for economic collaboration, particularly in industry, green hydrogen, and tourism, aligning with Oman's Vision 2040 goals. The forum served as a platform for Omani and Austrian businesses to foster trade relations and explore collaboration opportunities.

records.title: Construction has commenced on Saudi Arabia's largest indoor vertical farming project in Riyadh.
records.description: Construction has commenced on Saudi Arabia's largest indoor vertical farming project in Riyadh. The project, spearheaded by YesHealth Group, a Taiwanese controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) construction company, will encompass 20,000 square meters with 19 layers and a height of 15 meters. This facility is expected to yield up to 2,200 kilograms of leafy greens daily, including various types of lettuce, cruciferous vegetables, baby leaves, and specialty crops like edible flowers. The vertical farm will also include an experiential center with exhibition and dining areas for visitors to enjoy meals while observing the farm's operations. The project involves close coordination between teams in Saudi Arabia and Taiwan, with YesHealth Group supplying the equipment and technology needed for efficient indoor farming.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: In the Asir region of Saudi Arabia, traditional farming practices have been a reliable source of food for the population.
records.description: In the Asir region of Saudi Arabia, traditional farming practices have been a reliable source of food for the population. However, an increasing number of farmers in the region are transitioning to organic farming with the support of the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. Saad Al-Damik, a farmer with over 20 years of experience, has praised the benefits of organic farming, citing the negative effects of chemical fertilizers on soil quality and crop yields. The government's organic scheme offers educational and awareness programs to support farmers in this transition. Organic farming in the region aims to promote ecological sustainability, healthy food production, and the preservation of natural resources. The Ministry's Asir branch has been actively encouraging and assisting farmers in adopting organic farming practices, with several farms already making the transition and many more in the process of doing so. The Saudi government has been working to expand organic production and related services since 2005 to meet the growing demand for organic products.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) has announced a tender to import natural white wholly milled short-grain rice fro...
records.description: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) has announced a tender to import natural white wholly milled short-grain rice from India, with shipments expected between February and March 2024. The rice should have a 10% breakage rate, packed in 50-kilo containers, and be from the 2023/2024 crop. Price offers should be in U.S. dollars or Egyptian pounds, with payment at sight and in 180- and 270-day suppliers' facilities. Offers in Egyptian pounds will be given priority. Bids must be accompanied by an initial deposit, and the deadline for offers is December 21, with delivery to specified warehouses. Egypt is looking to enhance its stock of basic commodities, including rice and wheat, as it grapples with a smaller crop and decreasing wheat production.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Morocco and Malawi are set to strengthen their bilateral ties and partnership in 2024, following discussions between Moroccan Foreign Min...
records.description: Morocco and Malawi are set to strengthen their bilateral ties and partnership in 2024, following discussions between Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita and his Malawian counterpart, Nancy Tembo, in Rabat. The two nations have entered a "very positive" phase of bilateral relations, exemplified by the recent signing of a cooperation roadmap for 2022-2024. They anticipate expanding their ties into a substantial partnership in 2024. Malawi expressed its interest in deepening cooperation with Morocco in various sectors, including agriculture, tourism, and mining. Plans for the inaugural session of the Joint Cooperation Commission in early 2024 were also revealed, with discussions covering multiple areas such as agriculture, food security, mining, water and sanitation, energy, transportation, infrastructure development, land planning, housing, urban development, higher education, and scientific research.

records.title: The inaugural Agri'Expo event, organized by Green Open Lab in Sefrou, central Morocco, focused on promoting the integration of technology...
records.description: The inaugural Agri'Expo event, organized by Green Open Lab in Sefrou, central Morocco, focused on promoting the integration of technology into Moroccan agriculture. The event facilitated discussions among agriculture experts, entrepreneurs, academics, and startups regarding the challenges and opportunities related to agri-tech adoption in Morocco. Panel discussions explored topics such as the agri-tech entrepreneurial ecosystem, technology recommendations, farmer participation, and the role of universities in supporting talent development and entrepreneurial initiatives in agriculture. The event also featured a pavilion for companies and startups to showcase innovative technologies aimed at improving agricultural production and resource optimization. Additionally, an olive oil producers' competition and the Green Open Challenge, a collaborative project with public and private sponsors, were highlights of the event. Amine Zerouk, Founder of the Green OpenLab Foundation, emphasized the foundation's role in providing advice and technological solutions to enhance farming practices through the integration of advanced technology. The event aligns with Morocco's Generation Green strategy for 2020-2030 and aims to modernize agriculture and strengthen its resilience against climate challenges while ensuring food sovereignty.

records.title: The largest grain growing operation in Western Australia, known as Merredin Farms, is up for sale and expected to fetch close to $200 mil...
records.description: The largest grain growing operation in Western Australia, known as Merredin Farms, is up for sale and expected to fetch close to $200 million. The portfolio, spanning nearly 80,000 hectares, produces wheat, barley, and canola. The Saudi Arabian government and the Perth-based agricultural investment fund PenAgri, which jointly own Merredin Farms, have decided to sell. The buyer will become the state's largest broadacre farmer. This sale marks another significant deal in Western Australia's agriculture sector, following other notable transactions in the region throughout the year. Merredin Farms was part of a 200,000-hectare portfolio acquired by the Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company (SALIC) from John Nicoletti in 2019, while PenAgri owns the remainder. SALIC Australia is owned by the Saudi Arabian government and focuses on investments to ensure food security. PenAgri, run by agriculture investor Greg Harvey, owns two other large-scale mixed-cropping and livestock aggregations in the state. The sale is part of SALIC Australia's plans to reshape its strategic focus on various agricultural value chains in the region.
records.institution: The Saudi Agricultural and Livestock Investment Company

records.title: BlackRock Commits US$400M to Dubai’s Positive Zero for Decarbonization Initiatives
records.description: BlackRock has pledged to invest up to $400 million in Dubai's decarbonization company, Positive Zero, through a diversified infrastructure fund. This substantial investment is aimed at supporting Positive Zero's efforts in advancing energy transition initiatives across Gulf countries. Positive Zero was formed last year through the merger of solar enterprise SirajPower, energy efficiency services provider Taka Solutions, and on-demand battery operation HYPR Energy. The investment aligns with the objectives of the UAE-hosted COP28 summit, which seeks to triple renewable energy capacity by 2030 and double global energy efficiency improvements. BlackRock is among the institutional investors supporting the UAE's $30 billion climate fund called Alterra.

records.title: IFFCO Group, a fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company, has entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Tetra Pak, a leading...
records.description: IFFCO Group, a fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company, has entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Tetra Pak, a leading provider of food processing and packaging solutions. Their collaboration aims to enhance sustainability initiatives across IFFCO's manufacturing facilities, focusing on reducing the environmental impact. They plan to implement global standards and leverage advanced technologies to achieve this goal. IFFCO's objective is to produce sustainable, high-quality products while contributing to the Saudi Arabian economy and championing waste reduction, emission mitigation, and compliance with green industry protocols. They also aim to support long-term sustainable production and packaging of culinary creams in Saudi Arabia. This partnership underscores IFFCO's commitment to sustainability and economic growth in the region.

records.title: Tanmiah Food Company to Plant 100,000 Trees in Bahrain
records.description: Tanmiah Food Company has launched a tree planting campaign in Manama, Bahrain, with the goal of planting 100,000 trees. This initiative aligns with the Saudi Green Initiative and the Middle East Green Initiative, emphasizing collaborative environmental efforts between Saudi Arabia and Bahrain to combat the impacts of climate change through afforestation. Afforestation is vital for improving air quality, preventing soil erosion, supporting wildlife, absorbing carbon dioxide, and mitigating the effects of climate change. The campaign, symbolized by the slogan "Planted in Saudi Arabia, to be grown in Bahrain," demonstrates Tanmiah's commitment to global sustainability goals and a cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable future for the region and beyond. The initiative was inaugurated by Dr. Khaled bin Abdullah Al-Abd Al-Qader, Executive Director of the National Center for Vegetation Development and Desertification Control, representing the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. This tree planting effort reflects the united commitment of both countries to create a greener and more sustainable future for the Middle East region.

records.title: Egytrans, a leading Egyptian logistics and transport provider, and Links Investment, a prominent Saudi-based investment firm, are collabo...
records.description: Egytrans, a leading Egyptian logistics and transport provider, and Links Investment, a prominent Saudi-based investment firm, are collaborating to establish a joint venture in Saudi Arabia. The new company, with a total capital of 10,000,000 SR and equal 50% ownership by both partners, is set to become operational by the end of the first quarter of 2024. Headquartered in Riyadh, the joint venture will offer transport and logistics services, particularly in the oil, gas, and renewables sectors, aligning with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 for renewable energy projects. This partnership combines Egytrans' logistical expertise with Links Investment's assets and aims to capitalize on opportunities in the Saudi logistics sector.

records.title: Lebanese entrepreneur Nada Ghanem has founded Dooda Solutions, an agricultural technology company specializing in vermicompost products p...
records.description: Lebanese entrepreneur Nada Ghanem has founded Dooda Solutions, an agricultural technology company specializing in vermicompost products produced by earthworms. Recognizing the vital role earthworms play in soil fertility, Ghanem aims to raise awareness among farmers and the public about their significance. Dooda Solutions manufactures vermicompost using organic waste, with products including soil and liquid fertilizers. The company plans to expand its reach across the MENA region, supported by winning PepsiCo's Mena greenhouse accelerator program. Dooda Solutions emphasizes organic fertilizers for regional agriculture, offering sustainable solutions tailored to the region's sandy soil and high salinity. The company's goal is to enhance local food security and climate resilience while reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers. Ghanem envisions establishing Dooda farms in multiple countries to ensure localized fertilizer solutions and promote food security even during challenging times.

records.title: The Saudi General Authority for Food Security has disclosed that Saudi Arabia has successfully procured approximately 1.3 million tons of...
records.description: The Saudi General Authority for Food Security has disclosed that Saudi Arabia has successfully procured approximately 1.3 million tons of wheat in a recent tender. These shipments of wheat are anticipated to reach the kingdom between February and May 2024. The tender specifically sought hard wheat with a 12.5% protein content and was concluded on Friday. Various source options were presented in the tender, enabling sellers to choose their preferred source from regions such as the European Union, the Black Sea region, North America, South America, and Australia. The wheat shipments will be distributed to different ports in Saudi Arabia, including Jeddah Islamic Port, Yanbu Commercial Port, King Abdulaziz Port in Dammam, and Jazan Port.
records.institution: Saudi General Authority for Food Security

records.title: Oman Flour Mills Co.
records.description: Oman Flour Mills Co. (OFMC) celebrated the official inauguration of its new feed mill in Muttrah, marking a significant advancement in Oman's efforts to bolster local animal feed production and reduce dependence on imports. The state-of-the-art facility has a production capacity of 20 tonnes per hour and was constructed to cater to the distinct nutritional needs of various livestock. OFMC's CEO, Haitham Mohamed al Fannah, highlighted the facility's commitment to sustainability and environmental responsibility, with cutting-edge technology like robotics for packaging and advanced control systems for real-time adjustments. This initiative aims to enhance efficiency, reduce production costs, and support Oman's agricultural and livestock sectors while fostering self-sufficiency in animal feed production.

records.title: The Egyptian government has extended its ban on sugar exports for an additional three months, with the exception of surplus quantities, d...
records.description: The Egyptian government has extended its ban on sugar exports for an additional three months, with the exception of surplus quantities, due to ongoing sugar supply challenges and surging prices. The move aims to address the sugar market's instability, which has led to price increases and a shortage of unsubsidized sugar in various stores across Egypt. Despite previous efforts to stabilize the market, including the introduction of sugar trading on the Egyptian Mercantile Exchange platform, supply challenges persist. The recent arrests related to a large-scale corruption network scandal brought some relief to sugar stocks and prices, but the government continues to take measures to mitigate the impact of rising sugar prices on consumers, including increasing the rations of subsidized sugar distributed to families.
records.institution: The General Authority for Supply Commodities

records.title: India and Oman have unveiled a roadmap to strengthen their cooperation across various sectors, including green energy, maritime affairs,...
records.description: India and Oman have unveiled a roadmap to strengthen their cooperation across various sectors, including green energy, maritime affairs, digital payments, agriculture, and food security. These agreements were reached during a meeting between India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Oman's Sultan Haitham in New Delhi. Both countries are also fast-tracking negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement to boost bilateral trade. The expansion of this partnership aligns with Oman's Vision 2040 and India's development goals, reflecting their shared commitment to enhancing economic ties and trade relations. The two nations have witnessed significant growth in their bilateral trade and investment relationship, with India ranking among Oman's top trading partners.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's state wheat buying agency, GFSA, has issued an international tender to purchase approximately 715,000 metric tons of milli...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's state wheat buying agency, GFSA, has issued an international tender to purchase approximately 715,000 metric tons of milling wheat between February and May 2024. The tender seeks hard wheat with 12.5% protein content, sourced from optional origins in 12 consignments, mostly of 60,000 tons each. The consignments are intended for arrival in different Saudi ports, including Jeddah, Yanbu, Dammam, and Jizan, within specific timeframes. The GFSA reserves the right to buy 10% more or less than the standard 60,000-ton consignment size. This tender is part of Saudi Arabia's efforts to secure its wheat supply. In the last reported international wheat tender in June, Saudi Arabia purchased 624,000 tons of wheat.

records.title: Investments in the aquaculture sector are set to flourish as Saudi Arabia and China explore opportunities for growth and collaboration at...
records.description: Investments in the aquaculture sector are set to flourish as Saudi Arabia and China explore opportunities for growth and collaboration at the Global Investment Promotion Conference in Shenzhen, China. Representatives from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture engaged with over 60 specialized Chinese firms to expand the aquaculture sector's prospects. This initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 plan to diversify the economy and generate employment opportunities through the production of 600,000 tons of fish annually. By fostering expertise exchange and private sector involvement, this partnership aims to bolster economic cooperation and job creation while enhancing the sustainability of the aquaculture industry.
records.institution: Saudi Arabian Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: Saudi Arabia is continuing its efforts to become a tourism powerhouse with the launch of the "Dan Company," an organization under the sov...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is continuing its efforts to become a tourism powerhouse with the launch of the "Dan Company," an organization under the sovereign wealth fund aimed at promoting and developing agritourism and eco-tourism. The first project by Dan will be situated in the Al Ahsa region, covering 1.8 million square meters and featuring an eco-resort, agri-resort, and adventure resort. The initiative is expected to contribute approximately $1.6 billion (SAR 6 billion) to Saudi Arabia's non-oil GDP by 2030, with a focus on offering travelers "traditional farming experiences" in the Gulf state. The Public Investment Fund (PIF) sees Dan as a means to stimulate economic development, integrate sustainability, and involve the private sector and local farmers in agritourism and ecotourism. PIF, chaired by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman, has substantial assets, making it a key player in financing various tourism projects in the country, such as ski resorts, mega-yacht hubs, archipelagos, and entertainment-focused cities.

records.title: Stella Okotete, the Executive Director of Business Development at the Nigeria Export – Import Bank, visited Qatar to explore opportunitie...
records.description: Stella Okotete, the Executive Director of Business Development at the Nigeria Export – Import Bank, visited Qatar to explore opportunities for boosting bilateral trade between Qatar and Nigeria. She highlighted the potential for job creation and food security in both countries through strong partnerships. The trade volume between the two nations has steadily grown, reaching QAR 298 million in 2023, with cashew nuts being a significant export. Okotete emphasized Nigeria's commitment to economic reforms, including diversifying the non-oil sector, under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's leadership. She sees these reforms as an investment in global peace and prosperity, with the potential to create over 40 million jobs for Nigerians. Okotete has a background in humanitarian work and women's empowerment, aiming to improve livelihoods and quality of life in her community and beyond.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) has launched a Millet Demo Farm in alignment with the objectives of the Interna...
records.description: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) has launched a Millet Demo Farm in alignment with the objectives of the International Year of Millets and COP28 on climate action, sustainable agriculture, food security, and nutrition. Established in partnership with the SELCO Foundation, the Millet Demo Farm aims to demonstrate the complete value chain of millets, from seed production to consumption, with a focus on raising awareness about the benefits of millets in adapting to climate change in agriculture. Dr. Tarifa Alzaabi, Director General of ICBA, emphasized the importance of embracing neglected and underutilized crops like millets to build sustainable and resilient agrifood systems. The initiative also aims to promote millet production and consumption in the Middle East North Africa and other regions through technology transfer and capacity development. ICBA has been a pioneer in the research and development of climate-resilient and nutritious crops suitable for arid and salt-affected environments for over two decades, and this initiative is part of their commitment to advancing sustainable agriculture globally.
records.institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA)

records.title: COP28: Lebanon's Environment Minister Unveils Groundbreaking Green Investment Facility Aligned with Climate Action Commitments
records.description: Lebanon's Caretaker Minister of Environment, Nasser Yassin, unveiled a groundbreaking green investment facility during COP28 in Dubai. The facility is a result of collaborative efforts between the Ministry of Environment, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), and other partners. It aligns with Lebanon's Fourth National Communication on Climate Change and its ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The facility, in collaboration with the 'Lebanon Economic Empowerment Fund,' adheres to European financial standards to ensure governance and transparency. It aims to channel investments into sectors like renewable energy, sustainable transportation, solid waste management, agriculture, and irrigation to support climate-friendly initiatives. Lebanon's commitment to addressing climate change is demonstrated by its actions, including productive dialogues with global entities, such as the World Bank and the Green Climate Fund, to access climate finance and advance environmental initiatives. Minister Yassin also highlighted the importance of adapting Lebanon's healthcare system to climate exigencies and its commitment to the Alliance for Climate Action on Health (ATACH) initiative. Amid economic and security challenges, Lebanon views the green investment facility as a beacon of hope, showcasing its dedication to climate action and resilience.

records.title: During the China-Saudi Investment Conference in Beijing, over 60 memorandums of understanding and agreements were signed, amounting to a...
records.description: During the China-Saudi Investment Conference in Beijing, over 60 memorandums of understanding and agreements were signed, amounting to a total value of $25 billion. These agreements span various sectors, including energy, agriculture, tourism, mining, financial services, logistics, infrastructure, technology, and healthcare. Notable deals include an $8.5 billion agreement between the Saudi Esports Federation and Chinese esports tournament operator VSPO in the information and communication technology sector, as well as a $7.5 billion collaboration between China's Oriental Energy Co. and Saudi Arabia's Ajlan & Bros Holding Group Co. in manufacturing. The conference also saw nine Chinese companies receive licenses to open regional headquarters in Saudi Arabia. These developments are expected to strengthen trade and economic ties between the two nations.

records.title: Tunisia: African Development Bank Lends Nearly €82 Million for Wastewater Reuse in Agriculture, Strengthening Climate Resilience
records.description: The African Development Bank Group has approved a loan of €81.9 million to Tunisia for the implementation of the Treated Wastewater Quality Improvement Project For Climate Resilience Building (PAQEE-RCC). The project, to be carried out from 2024 to 2028, aims to enhance the treatment of wastewater to meet reuse standards. It will upgrade electromechanical and electrical equipment and introduce photovoltaic solar energy in 19 water treatment facilities across 11 governorates, benefiting more than 670,000 people. The project will promote the water-energy-agriculture nexus, increase agricultural production, create jobs, and improve food security against a backdrop of drought and water scarcity.

records.title: Egypt's Ministry of International Cooperation has unveiled a partnership with the World Bank Group (WBG) aimed at fostering innovation in...
records.description: Egypt's Ministry of International Cooperation has unveiled a partnership with the World Bank Group (WBG) aimed at fostering innovation in climate-smart agriculture. This collaboration was announced at the UN climate conference COP28 in the United Arab Emirates and will utilize the EgCITE initiative, supported by the Korean Green Growth Trust Fund, to adapt international technologies and best practices for climate-smart agriculture in Egypt. Part of the Climate Adapted Agri-Food Transformation (CRAFT) project within the “NWFE” program, this effort seeks to enhance the efficiency and environmental sustainability of Egypt's agricultural food systems. It aligns with sustainable economic development, green growth, and resilience against food security and climate change challenges. This partnership reflects Egypt's commitment to climate action and sustainable development, as well as the localization of climate-smart agricultural technologies to address climate change and improve local production and support networks. The session at COP28 also showcased successful startup companies from the Climatech Run competition, demonstrating their expansion plans in Egypt and the Middle East.

records.title: Qatari private sector exports to Jordan have experienced robust growth, increasing by more than 11.7% during the first nine months of 202...
records.description: Qatari private sector exports to Jordan have experienced robust growth, increasing by more than 11.7% during the first nine months of 2023 compared to the same period in the previous year. The total value of Qatari private sector exports to Jordan from January to September 2023 amounted to approximately $136 million, a notable increase from the $120 million recorded in the same period in 2022. These exports from the Qatari private sector to Jordan covered a wide range of products, including organic fertilizer, iron bars, medical solutions, food items, chemical materials, chemical fertilizers, plastic bags, and car engine oils. The Qatar Chamber of Commerce and Industry's report for the third quarter of 2023 revealed that the volume of Qatari private sector exports during that period amounted to about 3.25 billion Qatari riyals, equivalent to $892.8 million.
records.institution: Qatari Chamber of Commerce and Industry

records.title: Pure Harvest Smart Farms, a UAE-based agritech company, has acquired Red Sea's controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) production facili...
records.description: Pure Harvest Smart Farms, a UAE-based agritech company, has acquired Red Sea's controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) production facility near Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as part of its expansion strategy. Pure Harvest will assume operations of the farm in January 2024 and will invest capital to enhance production and climate control capabilities. The deal also allows Pure Harvest to benefit from Red Sea's SecondSky technology, a heat-blocking roofing solution that improves energy efficiency, reduces water consumption, and enhances crop health in greenhouses. As part of the transaction, Pure Harvest will secure a 40-hectare land bank co-located with the existing production facility, positioning the company to expand its franchised farm footprint in the region.

records.title: In response to the growing shortage of sugar in the market, the Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has announced an increase...
records.description: In response to the growing shortage of sugar in the market, the Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has announced an increase in the rations of subsidized sugar distributed to families. This decision aims to alleviate concerns over the scarcity of sugar and ensure continued access for citizens. Under the new plan, families with up to three individuals will receive an additional one kilogram of subsidized sugar, while those with four individuals or more will receive a more substantial increase of 2 kilograms. The distribution effort is coordinated by the Holding Company for Food Industries (HCFI), which is supplying up to 10,000 tons of sugar daily to meet the increased demand. This step is part of the government's proactive measures to address the sugar shortage and stabilize the market, ensuring access to this essential commodity for citizens.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Drought Pushes Morocco to Adapt Water Policy
records.description: Morocco's Minister of Equipment and Water, Nizar Baraka, highlighted the need to adapt the country's water policy due to the severe drought experienced in recent years. To address this challenge, Morocco is expanding its seawater desalination facilities along its coasts. The country aims to achieve a desalination capacity of 1.5 billion cubic meters by 2030, with a focus on improving access to drinking water in coastal cities and satisfying irrigation needs. Morocco is leveraging the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems Nexus approach to integrate renewable energy sources into desalination processes. Baraka also mentioned specific projects, such as the Agadir seawater desalination plant and the Dakhla seawater desalination plant, which will operate using wind energy for irrigation. Morocco is committed to diversifying its agricultural water supplies and linking them to renewable energy sources. Additionally, nine other desalination projects are planned for completion by 2027, including one for agriculture. Baraka emphasized the importance of international organizations in providing funding and technical assistance to build capacity for these initiatives.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Water and Equipment

records.title: Jazan City Completes 53 Key Projects Valued at $2.39bn
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Jazan City for Basic and Transformative Industries has completed 53 capital projects valued at over SR9 billion ($2.39 billion), according to Saudi Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Bandar Alkhorayef. These projects span multiple sectors, including infrastructure, public facilities, housing, and other services. Private sector investments in Jazan City have exceeded SR32 billion, with discussions ongoing for future projects estimated at around SR10 billion. These developments align with national strategies and demonstrate the economic viability of the region's projects, fostering economic and industrial growth.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s NEOM: $500 bln Mega-Project Unveils New Food Company Topian
records.description: NEOM, Saudi Arabia's ambitious $500 billion mega-project, has unveiled Topian, the NEOM Food Company, aimed at redefining food production, distribution, and consumption with a focus on sustainability. Topian will work across five vertical pillars: climate-proof agriculture, regenerative aquaculture, novel foods, personalized nutrition, and sustainable food supply and ESG. Supported by the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, this initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals for food security, climate change mitigation, and achieving net-zero emissions by 2060. Topian aims to introduce innovative solutions to address global food system challenges related to population growth, climate change, and resource depletion.

records.title: Saudi FDI Reforms Poised to Deliver Transformative Impact
records.description: Saudi Arabia remains committed to its reform agenda, focusing on boosting foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows and diversifying investment strategies despite a recent decline in FDI, which saw a 21 percent drop in the second quarter of 2023. This decline, however, contrasts with a 94 percent increase in the number of investment licenses issued during the same period, reaching 1,819. The regional headquarters program, offering tax incentives and a 30-year corporate income tax exemption, is expected to expedite FDI. Despite the recent drop, Saudi Arabia achieved the second-highest amount of FDI in the Middle East and Africa region during the period. France, Japan, Kuwait, Malaysia, Singapore, the UAE, and the US are among the main contributors to this investment surge. Key sectors attracting FDI include chemicals, real estate, fossil fuels, automobiles, tourism, plastics, and machinery, indicating growing international investor interest and confidence in Saudi Arabia's economic landscape. The Kingdom's financial account, reflecting net values for direct investment, portfolio investment, and reserve assets, amounted to SR42.97 billion, a 70 percent decline compared to the same period last year, primarily due to increased borrowings. Despite the decline in reserves, public debt remains sustainable, staying below the 50 percent debt to gross domestic product ceiling, and the fiscal capacity remains substantial.

records.title: Saudi Fund for Development Supports Africa's Sustainable Development and Climate Resilience at COP28
records.description: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) is actively participating in initiatives to support sustainable development and climate resilience in Africa. During the 28th Conference of Parties (COP28) of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), H.E. Sultan Al-Marshad, CEO of SFD, took part in a high-level panel discussion at the Saudi Pavilion. The discussion focused on the $50 billion funding allocated by the Arab Coordination Group (ACG) to promote sustainable development in Africa until 2030. This funding pledge was announced during the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference in Riyadh in November 2023. The panel discussion featured experts from ACG institutions, emphasizing their commitment to building resilient and inclusive societies in Africa and supporting the continent's development aspirations. SFD has played a significant role in financing projects in Africa, contributing over $11 billion to more than 400 projects in 46 African countries, aligning with ACG's commitment to the global energy transition and sustainable development.

records.title: Iraq: Promoting Sustainable Agriculture and Empowering Rural Women
records.description: Under the "Restoration and Strengthening the Resilience of Agri-Food Systems in Southern Iraq" project, funded by the European Union and executed in cooperation with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is taking significant steps to boost the buffalo breeding sector in Southern Iraq while promoting sustainable agriculture and empowering rural women. The initiative is primarily focused on supporting rural women, improving livelihoods, and implementing sustainable agricultural practices. This includes distributing marketing points (Caravans) to women's groups in various regions, empowering them and enhancing the marketing potential of dairy products. Additionally, the project introduces advanced machinery to reduce manual labor and increase efficiency, ultimately improving the livelihoods of rural women. The project's success demonstrates its positive impact on sustainable agriculture and local communities in Southern Iraq, aligning with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and the Government of Iraq have launched the Land Use Land Cover (LULC) project in Baghdad,...
records.description: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and the Government of Iraq have launched the Land Use Land Cover (LULC) project in Baghdad, marking a significant step in the fight against climate change. This project, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), leverages high-resolution satellite imagery to comprehensively map Iraq's diverse ecological zones and changing landscapes. The detailed maps enable decision-makers to identify critical environmental factors, inform evidence-based policies, and allocate resources effectively to address climate-related challenges. By focusing on urban areas, water bodies, ecosystems, and sustainable land use, the project supports initiatives such as sustainable urban planning, efficient water resource management, conservation of ecosystems, and the promotion of sustainable agricultural practices. In a country highly affected by climate change, this initiative is crucial for responsible natural resource management and advancing Iraq's development goals.
records.institution: Iraqi Central Statistics Organization (CSO) of the Ministry of Planning

records.domain: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
records.title: In 2023, Morocco's Agricultural Development Fund (ADF) allocated MAD 3.6 billion (approximately $355.4 million) for agricultural investme...
records.description: In 2023, Morocco's Agricultural Development Fund (ADF) allocated MAD 3.6 billion (approximately $355.4 million) for agricultural investment, marking a significant 38% increase compared to previous averages under the Green Morocco Plan. The ADF is directing 70% of these funds to support small-scale farmers cultivating plots under 10 hectares. Agriculture contributes 13% to Morocco's national GDP and employs over a third of the country's active workforce, making it a pivotal sector in the national economy. This year's investment budget, although 7% lower than the previous year, covers a wide range of agricultural investments, with a focus on localized and complementary irrigation, animal production, and farm equipment. The increased subsidy amount reflects a commitment to bolstering direct aid within the agricultural sector, but public opinion remains divided on the Green Morocco Plan's effectiveness, with many expressing dissatisfaction regarding its impact on rural living conditions, food security, and water resources.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: At the COP28 climate summit in Dubai, the United States and the United Arab Emirates announced that funding for the Agriculture Innovatio...
records.description: At the COP28 climate summit in Dubai, the United States and the United Arab Emirates announced that funding for the Agriculture Innovation Mission for Climate (AIM for Climate) has grown to over $17 billion. AIM for Climate, launched in 2021 at COP26, receives funding from governments, companies, and non-governmental organizations. It aims to address climate-friendly farming practices globally, as food and farming contribute to approximately one-third of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. The initiative has announced nearly 80 projects since 2021, with goals to expand agricultural research, promote sustainable farming practices, and reduce methane emissions. The funding has increased from $8 billion at COP27 to the current $17 billion, including $12 billion from governments and $5 billion from non-government parties such as companies and humanitarian organizations. The projects announced at COP28 range from $150,000 to $500 million in size and include initiatives to expand regenerative agriculture practices. Agriculture is a major focus at this year's climate summit, with a dedicated day on food and farming topics.
records.institution: The Agriculture Innovation Mission for Climate (AIM for Climate)

records.title: International Center for Biosaline Agriculture & Schneider Electric Advance Youth & Women Roles in Sustainability at COP28
records.description: Schneider Electric has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) at COP28 to collaborate on empowering youth and women in sustainability. The MoU encompasses several initiatives, such as educational tours and social mentorship programs, aiming to foster environmental leadership and green education. By joining forces with ICBA, Schneider Electric seeks to equip future sustainability leaders with the skills and knowledge necessary to tackle climate change impacts and drive innovation, contributing to global food security, climate action, and social empowerment in line with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals.

records.title: Silal and Bayer Partners to Strengthen the Agricultural Landscape in the UAE
records.description: Silal, the UAE's leading Agri-Tech Food Company, has formed a strategic partnership with Bayer, a global leader in life sciences with a focus on healthcare and nutrition, to strengthen the agricultural landscape in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) while addressing climate change as a central concern. The collaboration was announced during the World Agri-Tech Innovation Summit in Dubai on December 4th, 2023, and it aims to enhance the capabilities of local agronomists, fostering an environment conducive to agricultural innovation and excellence. This partnership will leverage Bayer's BayG.A.P. capacity-building program to advance best-in-class agricultural practices, especially under the challenging climatic conditions of the UAE. Both Silal and Bayer are committed to mitigating climate change and enhancing resilience in the agricultural sector, recognizing its critical role in addressing global warming. The program includes modules on Integrated Pest Management, Safe Use, Crop Protection Products, Application Technology, and Irrigation, and it will follow a train-the-trainer approach to reach growers in the UAE. This collaboration represents a significant step in advancing sustainable agriculture and addressing climate change challenges in the UAE and beyond.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Government and business leaders from Saudi Arabia and France convened in Riyadh to discuss economic cooperation, global aid initiatives,...
records.description: Government and business leaders from Saudi Arabia and France convened in Riyadh to discuss economic cooperation, global aid initiatives, and human rights. Dr. Abdullah Al-Rabeeah, supervisor-general of KSrelief, highlighted Saudi Arabia's global efforts, including 2,625 projects in 94 countries worth over $6 billion. Discussions also included ways to improve cooperation in the realm of human rights. The conference, titled "France 2030 and Vision 2030: Toward Energy and Industry Transformation," featured over 40 French companies, 16 governmental entities from both countries, and 90 Saudi Arabian firms. The collaboration will extend to skills training and support for startups.
records.institution: Saudi KSrelief, Business and Trade Officials

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Indonesia's state-owned electricity company, PLN, is collaborating with Saudi Arabia's energy firm, ACWA Power, to construct two floating...
records.description: Indonesia's state-owned electricity company, PLN, is collaborating with Saudi Arabia's energy firm, ACWA Power, to construct two floating solar power plants in West Sumatra's Lake Singkarak and West Java's Saguling Reservoir. These projects take advantage of Indonesia's substantial solar potential and abundant lakes and reservoirs to promote renewable energy. The Singkarak floating solar farm, covering 0.26% of Lake Singkarak's total area, is expected to have a capacity of up to 77 MWp, while the Saguling floating solar farm, occupying 1.69% of the Saguling Reservoir, will have a capacity of up to 92 MWp. The electricity generated will contribute to regional power systems.

records.title: COP28: CGIAR Secures Over US$890 Million to Combat Global Food and Climate Crises
records.description: CGIAR, a global agricultural research network, has secured over US$890 million to address the ongoing global food and climate crises. These funds will be used to support smallholder farmers in low- and middle-income countries and build more resilient, sustainable, and equitable food systems. The investments were announced during COP28 at a pledging event hosted by the UAE, with commitments from countries like the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, the United States, the World Bank, and Norway. CGIAR has laid out a case for US$4 billion in investments for its 2025-2027 research portfolio, highlighting the importance of increased investment in agricultural R&D to address food and climate challenges. The organization aims to support innovations and technologies that benefit smallholder farmers, vulnerable communities, and ecosystems, with a focus on climate resilience and sustainable agriculture.

records.title: U.S. and UAE-Backed Initiative Announces $9 Billion More for Agricultural Innovation Projects
records.description: An additional $9 billion in funding to address agriculture's role in the climate crisis has been announced on the sidelines of the United Nations climate talks. The Agriculture Innovation Mission (AIM) for Climate, led by the United States and the United Arab Emirates, now has a total of $17 billion to invest in agriculture and food systems innovation. Food systems contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. This funding comes at a time when the COP28 climate summit is emphasizing the importance of addressing farming's impact on climate change. The projects funded by AIM cover various areas, including regenerative agriculture, food manufacturing, and reducing synthetic nitrogen use, with a focus on low- and middle-income countries.
records.institution: The Agriculture Innovation Mission (AIM) for Climate

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture in Jordan is adopting cutting-edge forestry management technologies, such as remote sensing and artificial in...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture in Jordan is adopting cutting-edge forestry management technologies, such as remote sensing and artificial intelligence, to safeguard the country's forests against illegal logging and wildfires. This initiative is part of the ministry's strategy for 2022-2025, which focuses on modernizing forestry management practices to address climate change and its impact on the agricultural sector. By employing digital technologies and remote sensing, the ministry aims to enhance its ability to monitor and protect forests, combat climate change, and reduce pollution. A memorandum of understanding was signed with Growtech Company to study the use of remote sensing in forest management, with a focus on monitoring deforestation, illegal logging, and natural disturbances. Remote sensing will provide valuable data for inventorying and monitoring Jordan's forests efficiently and cost-effectively. Additionally, ground-based sensors will be used for real-time monitoring of forest temperature, fires, and logging activities, enabling prompt responses to any incidents and reducing violations and fires significantly.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Qatar have solidified their bilateral cooperation by signing multiple agreements and memorandums of understanding during...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Qatar have solidified their bilateral cooperation by signing multiple agreements and memorandums of understanding during the visit of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to attend the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit and the Saudi-Qatari Coordination Council's seventh meeting. In a joint statement, both nations expressed deep concern over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, condemning Israeli actions and emphasizing the need to stop military operations and protect civilians according to international law. They reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing bilateral cooperation across various sectors, including politics, security, sports, culture, trade, investment, energy, infrastructure, and media, reflecting their determination to strengthen ties and contribute to regional stability and development.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has designated $3 billion for investments across various sectors in Iraq, as announced by Sau...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has designated $3 billion for investments across various sectors in Iraq, as announced by Saudi Ambassador to Iraq Abdulaziz Al-Shammari. This allocation is part of an effort to enhance economic cooperation between the two nations. The PIF, in conjunction with the Iraq Fund for Development, is currently identifying investment opportunities in areas such as infrastructure, mining, agriculture, real estate development, and financial services. These endeavors reflect the improved diplomatic relations between Iraq and Saudi Arabia and the desire to strengthen economic ties, particularly following Saudi pledges of investment in various Iraqi sectors.

records.title: Saudi Environment Ministry Initiates Programs to Propel Agricultural Sector Growth
records.description: The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture in Saudi Arabia has initiated various programs to stimulate the growth of the agricultural sector and enhance its contribution to the country's GDP. These efforts include comprehensive training programs aimed at localizing agricultural professions, such as fishing, livestock management, beekeeping, and honey production. Legislative decisions have been implemented to enforce high-quality standards for Saudi products, including food quality certificates and streamlined agricultural licensing procedures. The ministry provides support through subsidies and soft agricultural loans via the Agricultural Development Fund. Distinct labels like "Organic," "Fish," "Saudi Dates," and "Saudi Qab" certification have been introduced to promote and export agricultural products, ensuring quality and safety standards. These initiatives align with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 objectives for food security and sustainable agricultural development, resulting in significant contributions to the GDP and increased food production in the country.
records.institution: Saudi Arabian Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Tunisian-Saudi Working Group to Develop Cooperation Programme in Water Sector
records.description: Tunisia and Saudi Arabia have agreed to establish a joint Tunisian-Saudi working group to develop an executive program for bilateral cooperation in the water sector. This decision was made during a meeting between Tunisia's Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Abdelmomen Belati, and Saudi Minister of Environment and Agriculture, Abderrahmen Fadli, held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Minister Belati emphasized Tunisia's commitment to enhancing joint investments in the agricultural sector, highlighting ongoing projects such as the use of treated wastewater in agriculture through the development of necessary infrastructure for water transfer from urban areas to agricultural regions. The Saudi minister expressed Saudi Arabia's readiness to collaborate with Tunisia on agricultural projects.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: A consortium called ReFarm in the United Arab Emirates, formed by SSK Enterprises and Christof Global Impact (CGI), is partnering with Du...
records.description: A consortium called ReFarm in the United Arab Emirates, formed by SSK Enterprises and Christof Global Impact (CGI), is partnering with Dubai's FoodTech Valley to create a circular, closed-loop "GigaFarm" aimed at enhancing food security and reducing the carbon footprint of the UAE's food industry. Vertical farming technology firm Intelligent Growth Solutions (IGS) will provide the infrastructure for the farm, which is set to grow 2 billion plants annually, replacing 1% of the country's fresh produce imports. The project integrates IGS' vertical towers with five other technologies to create a closed-loop system capable of recycling over 50,000 tonnes of food waste annually. It aims to generate water without desalination or rain, divert waste from landfills, and achieve a return rate of 20-25%. The GigaFarm will utilize solar energy and low-voltage direct current to minimize carbon usage and be nearly 98% more water-efficient than field farming. Labor costs will be reduced as the IGS system eliminates the need for human intervention in the growing area. The project could set a precedent for food security strategies worldwide, with IGS planning to roll out similar systems across four continents. The UAE government has prioritized diversification and sustainability in its economic growth strategy, making innovative, low-carbon agriculture a key focus.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Dubai-based Amea Power has signed two agreements during the Cop28 climate conference to develop renewable energy projects in Africa.
records.description: Dubai-based Amea Power has signed two agreements during the Cop28 climate conference to develop renewable energy projects in Africa. The company plans to build a $600 million wind farm in Ethiopia, potentially generating 300 megawatts of energy. It is in discussions with organizations such as the African Development Bank, the International Finance Corporation, and the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) for financing. Ethiopia aims to increase its hydropower capacity to 13.5 gigawatts by 2040 to meet rising electricity demand. Amea Power is also partnering with Zimbabwe's state-owned power utility Zesa to create a solar plant with an initial capacity of 30 megawatts, with the potential to expand. The project aligns with the UAE's initiative to invest $4.5 billion in clean energy projects in Africa.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has made a significant investment in the UK's wind energy sector by acquiring a 49% stake in the East Angl...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has made a significant investment in the UK's wind energy sector by acquiring a 49% stake in the East Anglia Three offshore wind farm from Spanish developer Iberdrola. This move follows another recent deal in which UAE's state-backed company, Masdar, purchased 49% of the £11 billion Dogger Bank South project in the North Sea. The UK's wind energy industry has faced financial challenges due to historical agreements that locked in low electricity prices, while costs have surged by over 40% due to inflation. Masdar's investment reflects the increasing overseas ownership of key renewable energy assets in the UK, with the company having a decade-long presence in the country's wind energy sector.

records.title: Nawah Scientific, a leading institution in analysis and scientific research in Egypt, has achieved accreditation from the U.S.
records.description: Nawah Scientific, a leading institution in analysis and scientific research in Egypt, has achieved accreditation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for food analysis and safety. This accomplishment is a historic milestone, as Nawah Scientific becomes the first African center to earn FDA accreditation in this field, marking a significant moment for the continent's scientific and research community. Nawah Scientific, an Egyptian startup specializing in research and scientific analysis, has been at the forefront of supporting scientific research and industrial analysis in the region since its establishment in 2015. The center's online platform empowers researchers and companies with advanced scientific capabilities, allowing them to conduct complex laboratory tests remotely. With over 400,000 samples analyzed from 12 countries and a remarkable annual growth rate of 250%, Nawah Scientific is a leader in advancing scientific research and innovation. The achievement of receiving the Africa Business Heroes Award further solidifies its position as one of the fastest-growing scientific companies in Africa. Supported by Egypt Ventures, Nawah Scientific's accreditation eliminates the need for Egyptian and African companies to send samples abroad for FDA compliance testing. This recognition streamlines the export process for Egyptian companies aiming to enter the U.S. market and opens doors for collaborations with international organizations like the UN World Food Programme. Nawah Scientific plans to leverage its FDA accreditation for expansion into key African markets, including Nigeria and South Africa, while contributing to the growth of Egyptian agricultural exports in global markets. The achievement reflects the government's commitment to supporting Egyptian startups in their regional and global expansion efforts, aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals 2030.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: Morocco's Bouregreg Med-O-Med Gardening School, established in 2018 on the outskirts of Salé, offers a three-year training program with a...
records.description: Morocco's Bouregreg Med-O-Med Gardening School, established in 2018 on the outskirts of Salé, offers a three-year training program with a focus on environmental awareness. The school primarily targets young individuals at risk of social exclusion or facing academic challenges. Recognized with the European "Green Skills" award, the school aims to raise climate change awareness, promote youth inclusion, particularly for those impacted by unemployment, and advocate for gender equality. The institution adopts an eco-responsible approach, with an entirely ecological gardening model, bioclimatic buildings constructed with raw earth, and solar-powered electricity. The program not only prepares students for careers in gardening but also nurtures their environmental consciousness and sense of responsibility.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen their cooperation in marine environment...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen their cooperation in marine environmental protection. This agreement was reached at the Saudi Green Initiative forum during the UN Climate Change Conference. The MoU will facilitate collaboration between the two nations in various aspects of marine environmental protection, including monitoring, evaluation, preservation, and biodiversity conservation. Additionally, the countries will work together to reduce pollution in Saudi Arabia's territorial waters. The agreement underscores their commitment to climate change science and efforts to enhance the marine ecosystem in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia's selection to the 40-member council of the International Maritime Organization for 2024-2025 reflects its dedication to marine environmental preservation and sustainable maritime transport.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Tunisia has grappled with a severe water crisis due to prolonged drought and insufficient rainfall, resulting in a significant decline in...
records.description: Tunisia has grappled with a severe water crisis due to prolonged drought and insufficient rainfall, resulting in a significant decline in crop production. However, the Chinese-built Sousse wastewater treatment plant has provided a lifeline to local farmers by ensuring a stable source of irrigation water. This facility, which includes the Hamdoun and expanded Sousse South sewage treatment stations, has not only mitigated pollution but also delivered critical irrigation water to farmers, preserving crop yields amid challenging conditions. The success of this project has prompted interest from other regions in Tunisia, seeking to replicate its benefits in addressing water scarcity and enhancing water resource management practices.
records.institution: The Chinese Sino-hydro Corporation Engineering Bureau

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Leaders from Africa and the Middle East have introduced the $10 billion SAFE Initiative, a public-private-partnership initiative announce...
records.description: Leaders from Africa and the Middle East have introduced the $10 billion SAFE Initiative, a public-private-partnership initiative announced during COP28 to address climate-induced food insecurity in the region. The initiative, spearheaded by the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), will mobilize at least $10 billion to implement climate-smart agricultural practices, including regenerative agriculture, soil fertility management, and solar-powered irrigation. SAFE aims to attract strategic investments from both public and private sectors to enhance food security, improve livelihoods, and create green jobs. African and Middle Eastern leaders stressed the importance of tackling climate change and food security together, emphasizing the need for international collaboration and support to address these interconnected challenges.
records.institution: The SAFE Initiative of the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI)

records.title: Tadweer has launched a $2.5 million pilot project in partnership with Aquagrain, a company specializing in soil-enhancing technology usin...
records.description: Tadweer has launched a $2.5 million pilot project in partnership with Aquagrain, a company specializing in soil-enhancing technology using organic waste to reduce water and fertilizer usage by up to 50 percent in arid land and sandy soils. Supported by an AED 100 million research and development fund from ADQ, this initiative is part of ADQ Growth Lab's efforts to drive innovation and sustainability in the UAE. The project involves constructing Abu Dhabi's first commercial-scale Aquagrain facility, converting organic waste into a biodegradable polymer that acts as a water reservoir for plants, ultimately reducing carbon emissions and enhancing land utilization. This collaboration underscores the commitment to circular waste management and sustainable practices in the UAE, aligning with global goals of environmental responsibility and food security.
