records.title: UAE’s ADQ Announces Co-Investment Platform with Kazakhstan’s QIC
records.description: Abu Dhabi's investment company, ADQ, has announced a co-investment platform partnership with Kazakhstan's Qazaqstan Investment Corp. This collaboration will focus on sectors with substantial growth potential, including food and agriculture, mobility, healthcare, energy transformation, clean technology, financial services technology, and education technology. The platform aims to identify and capitalize on investment opportunities not only in Kazakhstan but also across Central Asia and the Caucasus region. Both ADQ and QIC have committed to providing equal financial and operational support for each investment under this partnership, aiming to contribute to the economic growth of the UAE, Kazakhstan, and the wider region. This initiative strengthens bilateral relations between the UAE and Kazakhstan, dating back to 1992.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Egypt has transitioned from the presidency of COP27 to COP28, currently being held in Dubai, with a focus on addressing climate change im...
records.description: Egypt has transitioned from the presidency of COP27 to COP28, currently being held in Dubai, with a focus on addressing climate change impacts and mitigation. During its leadership of COP27 in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt launched various initiatives to combat climate change, including the establishment of the Loss and Damage Fund. Egypt's commitment to climate justice and supporting developing countries' needs for climate adaptation funds were highlighted. President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi emphasized the urgency of collective action to address climate change and mentioned initiatives like the Loss and Damage Fund, the "Just Transition Action Plan," and the "Emissions Reduction Action Plan." The Egyptian Pavilion at COP28 is promoting environmental sustainability, climate financing, and engaging various stakeholders, while an agreement was signed to establish the African Center of Excellence for Resilience and Adaptation to Climate Change. Egypt continues its efforts to address climate change during COP28.

records.title: Egypt to Develop ‘Detailed Roadmap’ to Cut Methane Emissions
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, Tarek El-Molla, announced at the COP28 climate summit in Dubai the country's intention to create a comprehensive plan to reduce methane emissions. This roadmap is set to be formalized during the COP28 summit and will receive technical support from the US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA). Egypt's commitment to mitigating climate change involves efforts to reduce methane emissions, which is a vital component of its carbon reduction strategy. As part of its National Climate Change Strategy 2050, Egypt is actively working to decrease carbon emissions and transition towards renewable and alternative energy sources, including the use of natural gas as a low-carbon transition fuel. The nation aims to become a regional hub for green energy and has signed agreements with international corporations for green hydrogen investment. Despite contributing only 0.6 percent of global emissions, Egypt is significantly impacted by climate change's adverse effects on its various sectors, necessitating substantial funds for climate adaptation. The COP28 summit, which began on November 30 and concludes on December 12, serves as a platform for Egypt to showcase its commitment to climate action.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources

records.title: President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi has issued a new regulation, leading to the reformation of the General Assembly of the Sovereign Fund of E...
records.description: President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi has issued a new regulation, leading to the reformation of the General Assembly of the Sovereign Fund of Egypt (TSFE), now chaired by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly. The reconstituted assembly includes key figures like Minister of Planning and Economic Development Hala El-Said, Minister of Finance Mohamed Maait, and a deputy governor of the Central Bank as permanent members. It also includes non-permanent members such as economic experts, former central bank governors, and business leaders, who will serve for four years. This move aims to accelerate the implementation of the IPO program, which is crucial for Egypt's commitment to the International Monetary Fund's loan deal, involving the sale of stakes in state-owned assets to bridge a financing gap. Egypt has already made significant progress in this regard, with plans to continue offering stakes in more state-owned companies in the near future, despite some delays in specific offerings.
records.institution: General Assembly of the Sovereign Fund of Egypt (TSFE)

records.title: Morocco and the UAE have signed a joint declaration titled "Towards an Innovative, Renewed, and Deep-rooted Partnership" to strengthen bi...
records.description: Morocco and the UAE have signed a joint declaration titled "Towards an Innovative, Renewed, and Deep-rooted Partnership" to strengthen bilateral ties and cooperation. During King Mohammed VI's official visit to the UAE, both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to enhance cooperation and foster economic partnerships. The declaration highlights the goal of elevating economic, commercial, investment, and industrial cooperation to the level of deep political ties, focusing on socio-economic sectors, infrastructure, transportation, agriculture, energy, tourism, real estate, and more. Both countries expressed their determination to prioritize various sectors and explore investment opportunities, including in infrastructure, railways, airports, ports, dams, green hydrogen production, energy transport, food security, tourism, real estate, and socio-economic development. The partnership also aims to engage in economic partnerships and energy infrastructure development in African countries, leveraging Morocco as a gateway to Africa.

records.title: FarmERP, a leading Agri-Tech company with a presence in over 30 countries, has announced plans to expand its footprint into the Saudi Ara...
records.description: FarmERP, a leading Agri-Tech company with a presence in over 30 countries, has announced plans to expand its footprint into the Saudi Arabian market. The company is establishing a registered regional office as part of its growth strategy. FarmERP is already providing technology solutions to major agricultural and food supply chain companies in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Oman. It is also exploring collaborations with government entities and private stakeholders in the region. FarmERP aims to leverage advanced data science and technology, including AI and ML, to enhance food security, address climate change, optimize resource management, monitor crop and soil health, and digitize agriculture in Saudi Arabia. The company plans to expand its clientele by 200% annually, establish a registered office in Saudi Arabia, and target a 3x increase in revenue through these expansion initiatives.

records.title: Banks in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have made a significant commitment at the COP28 climate talks by pledging to mobilize 1 trillion...
records.description: Banks in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have made a significant commitment at the COP28 climate talks by pledging to mobilize 1 trillion dirhams, equivalent to approximately $270 billion, in green finance. This announcement, made during the finance-focused day of the event in Dubai, reflects the UAE's ambition and commitment to addressing climate change. The funds will support various initiatives, including renewable energy projects and efforts to improve soil quality for farmers.

records.title: WEF's First Movers Coalition for Food supported by Bain & Company
records.description: The World Economic Forum (WEF), in partnership with the Government of the UAE and more than 20 corporate and research partners, including Bain & Company, has launched the First Movers Coalition for Food during the COP28 climate change conference. This initiative aims to drive market demand for sustainable and low-emission agricultural products. The coalition plans to use its collective procurement power to accelerate the adoption of sustainable farming practices and innovations in the food sector, potentially reaching a value of $10 billion to $20 billion by 2030. Participating companies, with a combined revenue of $2.1 trillion, aim to shape the future of sustainable food production and contribute to global climate goals, reducing emissions and the environmental impact of food systems.

records.title: The Transport General Authority of Saudi Arabia has announced that Saudi Arabia has secured a seat on the International Maritime Organiza...
records.description: The Transport General Authority of Saudi Arabia has announced that Saudi Arabia has secured a seat on the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Council for the years 2024-2025. This consecutive membership in the IMO Council reflects the country's dedication to promoting secure and environmentally friendly maritime transport on a global scale. It also highlights Saudi Arabia's commitment to fostering growth and innovation in the global maritime ecosystem. Saudi Arabia's participation in the IMO Council will enable the country to enhance its support for the organization's projects and contribute to global maritime transportation initiatives, aligning with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. The IMO, a United Nations entity with 175 member nations, plays a vital role in establishing international standards for maritime security and environmental protection. Saudi Arabia's maritime fleet, ranking twentieth globally, contributes significantly to the country's status as a leading logistics hub. Prince Khalid bin Bandar bin Sultan has been proposed to lead the 33rd IMO Assembly meetings in London, further demonstrating Saudi Arabia's active involvement in the global maritime transportation sector. The Kingdom has also been making strides in green initiatives, empowering women in the maritime sector, and developing maritime expertise as part of its commitment to a sustainable maritime future.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Tunisian farmers in the region of Nabeul are turning to drones to combat the challenges posed by climate change, such as drought and erra...
records.description: Tunisian farmers in the region of Nabeul are turning to drones to combat the challenges posed by climate change, such as drought and erratic weather patterns. Start-up RoboCare, founded by Imen Hbiri, uses drones equipped with multi-lens cameras and sensors to assess the hydration levels, soil quality, and overall health of crops. This technology provides farmers with precise information on water requirements, allowing for efficient irrigation and reduced water consumption. By relying on these drones, farmers can save up to 30% of water consumption, reduce fertiliser and medicine costs by about 20%, and increase crop production by 30%. As Tunisia faces its eighth year of drought, such innovations are seen as crucial for adapting to changing agricultural conditions.

records.title: Green Future for Iraq - Nationwide Tree Planting Campaign
records.description: In alignment with Iraq's Prime Minister's vision for environmental sustainability, a nationwide tree-planting campaign is set to be launched in collaboration with United Nations agencies in Iraq, the Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, the Mayoralty of Baghdad, the Department of Media and Information in Kurdistan Region of Iraq, and other partners. This ambitious initiative aims to plant over 500,000 trees across Iraq, with a focus on addressing climate change challenges, enhancing biodiversity, and improving community well-being. The campaign will involve UN agencies, young volunteers, and the private sector, emphasizing local community engagement and supporting Iraq's national goal of planting five million trees. This initiative aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), particularly Goal 13: Climate Action and Goal 15: Life on Land, reflecting a commitment to these objectives.
records.institution: Iraqi Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, the Mayoralty of Baghdad, the Department of Media and Information in Kurdistan Region of Iraq, and other partners

records.title: Lebanese PM Calls for Arab Support to Rebuild Green Economy
records.description: Lebanese Prime Minister Najib Mikati has called for Arab support to rebuild a sustainable green economy in Lebanon, highlighting the destructive impact of recent Israeli attacks on the country's agriculture and environment. Mikati made this appeal at the 28th session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP28) held in Dubai, UAE. He urged for an expansion of the financing scope of the $30 billion climate-focused investment fund established by the UAE to support clean energy and climate projects globally. Mikati emphasized that Israel's attacks had caused extensive damage to forests, agricultural lands, and olive trees in Lebanon, adversely affecting livelihoods and the environment. He also called for concrete measures at COP28 to ensure a sustainable future.

records.title: The Iraqi Cabinet has taken steps to promote efficient irrigation in the country's agricultural sector by approving a contract with the A...
records.description: The Iraqi Cabinet has taken steps to promote efficient irrigation in the country's agricultural sector by approving a contract with the Austrian equipment company Bauer. This decision is subject to legal considerations. In February, a delegation from Bauer, led by Financial Director Andreas Schitter, visited Iraq and met with the Minister of Agriculture, Abbas Jabr al-Olayawi. The company presented its pivot and linear mobile spray systems and discussed potential financing options through the Austrian Central Bank.

records.title: Tunisia: BNA Dedicates Funds to Support Farmers in 2023/2024 Agricultural Season
records.description: The National Agricultural Bank (BNA) in Tunisia has allocated TND 120 million to support farmers at the beginning of the upcoming agricultural season, specifically for the purchase of seeds and fertilizers. Of this funding, 60% is earmarked for small-scale farmers facing financial challenges. The Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS) has also dedicated about TND 20 million to assist small farmers and microfinance associations. The Ministry of Agriculture's strategic objectives include increasing grain production and harvesting 12 million quintals of hard wheat. This initiative aims to bolster national grain production, reduce reliance on imports, and preserve foreign currency reserves, especially after a year of low production, resulting in seed shortages.

records.title: Gates Foundation Announces Partnership with United Arab Emirates to Accelerate Action on Climate and Strengthen Food Systems Through Investment in Agricultural Innovation
records.description: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has partnered with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to invest a total of $200 million in innovations aimed at helping smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia adapt to climate change. The announcement was made at the World Climate Action Summit, with the foundation committing $100 million to support organizations like CGIAR, which focuses on developing agricultural innovations. The funding will also support the AIM4Scale climate adaptation initiative launched by the UAE. The goal is to reach 500 million farmers by 2030 and reduce emissions from the agriculture sector by 1 gigaton per year.

records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is focusing its investments in Pakistan on various sectors, including agriculture, ports and logistics, po...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is focusing its investments in Pakistan on various sectors, including agriculture, ports and logistics, power, and more. During Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar's recent visit to the UAE, the two countries signed memorandums of understanding (MoUs) worth up to $25 billion, indicating significant investment opportunities. The UAE is committed to supporting Pakistan's development in multiple areas, and the investment is expected to enhance bilateral economic cooperation. These agreements are seen as mutually beneficial, and the UAE also expressed interest in private sector investments in sectors like food security, health, and education. Additionally, an export hub in Karachi and logistic support for remote areas of Pakistan's Balochistan and Sindh provinces are planned as part of the UAE's investment in the country.

records.title: Algeria is set to receive 2.5 million tonnes of wheat from Russia by June 2024, as revealed by Eduard Zernin, head of the Russian Associa...
records.description: Algeria is set to receive 2.5 million tonnes of wheat from Russia by June 2024, as revealed by Eduard Zernin, head of the Russian Association of Wheat Exporters, during a trade mission to the North African nation. Algeria stands as Africa's second-largest wheat market after Egypt, with an estimated wheat consumption of 11.15 million metric tons (MMT) for the 2022/23 season, primarily met through imports due to limited domestic production capacity. While Algeria's local wheat production has improved, it remains insufficient to meet national demand, creating a reliance on global exporters. The wheat shipments from Russia have shown substantial growth, with 1.3 million tonnes already delivered since July, a notable increase compared to the previous year. This surge in exports is attributed to established contacts through agricultural diplomacy efforts, showcasing a favorable quality-price ratio for Russian wheat, enhancing its competitiveness against European counterparts like France.

records.title: Egypt's government has restructured its bread subsidy policy, permitting the sale of discounted bread to individuals not enrolled in the...
records.description: Egypt's government has restructured its bread subsidy policy, permitting the sale of discounted bread to individuals not enrolled in the ration card program through prepaid cards starting January 2024. Minister of Supply Ali Al-Moselhi announced this shift during a televised discussion, aiming to extend subsidized bread access beyond the 72 million citizens on 21 million ration cards. Egypt produces a massive 250 to 275 million loaves of bread daily under the existing subsidized system. Abdullah Ghorab, head of the bakeries division at the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce, confirmed that citizens can buy bread for 1 Egyptian pound each from all 30,000 government-run bakeries nationwide through prepaid cards available via the Egyptian postal service. The move is intended to reflect the actual production cost. Notably, there will be no purchase limit per person, unlike an earlier announcement by Minister Moselhi. This change arrives amidst wheat shortage challenges due to the Russian-Ukrainian crisis, disrupting Egypt's usual wheat imports. The World Bank identifies Egypt's food subsidy program, catering to 72 million citizens through bread subsidies and 64 million via food ration cards, as the largest in the MENA region.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, el-Sayed el-Qoseir, inaugurated the Middle East's largest artificial insemination center si...
records.description: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, el-Sayed el-Qoseir, inaugurated the Middle East's largest artificial insemination center situated in Alexandria Governorate as part of the Decent Life presidential rural development initiative. Aligned with the Sustainable Agricultural Investments and Livelihoods Project, this center boasts an annual production capacity of 600,000 semen doses. El-Qoseir emphasized that the facility, housing 62 top breed bulls, will significantly enhance semen quality, advancing livestock breeding practices. Highlighting its pivotal role, the minister noted its potential to bridge food gaps, curtail meat imports, and uplift farmers' livelihoods. Encouraging livestock breeders to adopt modern techniques for increased income, el-Qoseir stressed the center's services in genetic enhancement, envisioning a doubled output in meat and milk production through the development of superior breeds.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: Morocco has taken a significant step in advancing its marine research capabilities with the introduction of the "Ibn Sina II," a fisherie...
records.description: Morocco has taken a significant step in advancing its marine research capabilities with the introduction of the "Ibn Sina II," a fisheries research vessel by the National Institute of Halieutic Research (INRH). This unveiling, led by Minister Mohamed Sadiki, signifies Morocco's commitment to collaborating with the European Union for sustainable maritime fishing and ocean exploration. Costing MAD 34 million (US$3.4 million), the 22-meter-long vessel joins the INRH research fleet, aiming to bolster the nation's blue economy by conducting high-level oceanographic studies along the Moroccan coast. The vessel's cutting-edge features include two laboratories for biological and chemical analyses, advanced oceanographic tools, and the ability to deploy various research equipment, facilitating comprehensive studies of coastal marine ecosystems. Minister Sadiki emphasized the vessel's role in strengthening scientific research, aligning with the Halieutis strategy to enhance research capabilities by 2030. Additionally, the event highlighted aquaculture projects in the Souss Massa region, showcasing substantial potential for the fisheries sector's growth. Morocco's fisheries industry, largely reliant on Atlantic harvesting, holds significant economic importance, with fisheries exports valued at US$2.2 billion in 2017. The "Ibn Sina II" is poised to play a pivotal role in advancing sustainable practices within this vital sector through enhanced ocean research.
records.institution: Moroccan National Institute of Halieutic Research (INRH)

records.title: Algeria to Receive First Irish Beef Shipment in 30 Years, Aims to Diversify Livestock Sources
records.description: Algeria has embarked on a strategy to diversify its sources of red and white meat imports to address domestic market price surges. This shift led to the authorization of meat imports, notably marking the arrival of Ireland's first 20-tonne vacuum-packed beef shipment in three decades, facilitated by the Emerald Isle Beef Producers (EIBP) in partnership with Algerian importer Al Mawashi Group. EIBP aims to establish a regular supply chain to meet Algeria's halal-certified meat market demand, potentially delivering fresh beef weekly. This diversification drive aligns with Algeria's efforts to secure alternative livestock sources, especially after the suspension of live cattle imports from France due to concerns about livestock diseases. As the third-largest beef consumer in Africa, Algeria's move to import Irish beef is a strategic effort to fortify food security and economic resilience, recognizing agriculture's pivotal role. Despite a 19% growth in the red meat sector over two decades, challenges persist in sustaining the current consumption rate of 20 kg per capita annually. Algeria's local red meat production involves cattle, sheep, and goats, amounting to about 320,000 tons annually, with over 330,000 locally produced cattle slaughtered yearly, contributing to a total meat production of nearly 120,000 tons. Although red meat consumption has increased to 11 kg per capita annually, it remains lower than developed countries due to the relatively high cost of fresh red meat in Algeria.

records.title: Iraq's government, in collaboration with the Kurdistan Regional Government and the private sector, unveiled the Distar Factory, a state-o...
records.description: Iraq's government, in collaboration with the Kurdistan Regional Government and the private sector, unveiled the Distar Factory, a state-of-the-art wheat flour mill in Domiz, Duhok Governate. Prime Minister Masrour Barzani highlighted its role in creating jobs and fortifying the region's agricultural foundation. With a capacity of 52,300 tonnes of wheat storage and a monthly production capability of 500 tonnes of flour, this $22 million project signifies a significant step. Barzani encouraged Kurdistan's investors to explore agricultural and industrial opportunities, emphasizing their potential to bolster the regional economy and decrease reliance on external sources. The mill serves as a reliable platform for farmers to sell their produce, incentivizing continuous cultivation. Iraq's focus on wheat, a critical crop, has faced challenges due to depleted water sources, impacting yields. However, recent government measures, including utilizing groundwater for farming, have led to a bumper harvest, doubling wheat cultivation to about 850,000 hectares and yielding approximately 4 million tons of wheat—80% of the country's bread consumption needs for its 43 million population, a significant achievement.

records.title: Merchants in Egypt face a 10-day ultimatum to regulate sugar prices, with the government warning of enforced pricing measures if complian...
records.description: Merchants in Egypt face a 10-day ultimatum to regulate sugar prices, with the government warning of enforced pricing measures if compliance fails. Minister Ali Moselhi, speaking at Cairo's Nebu Gold Expo, urged merchants to adjust prices within the specified period, highlighting Egypt's sufficient strategic sugar reserves, capable of meeting demand for over five months. Moselhi assured that the ministry won't flood the market to preserve reserves. Egypt's domestic sugar consumption, as per Statista, reached 3.43 million metric tons in 2021/2022, with an anticipated increase to 3.49 million metric tons in 2022/2023 and a further rise to 3.77 million metric tons in 2023/24, attributed to population growth and the confectionery sector expansion. Recent soaring sugar prices, exceeding EGP 39 per kilogram, triggered widespread concerns, prompting the government to impose export bans in March and September to stabilize prices. Egypt's efforts to boost agricultural production include a land reclamation program targeting 3.5 million feddan, resulting in increased sugar beet cultivation by 620,000 feddans this year, with incentives like raised earnings for local sugar beet production to encourage more cultivation.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Saudi Arabia Implements Stringent Visa Rules for Foreign Domestic Workers
records.description: Saudi Arabia has recently implemented updated regulations for issuing work visas to foreign domestic workers, part of a broader push to modernize its labor market and foster equitable relationships between employers and domestic staff. The Ministry of Human Resources has raised the visa standards for hiring foreign domestic workers, particularly emphasizing individuals aged 24 and above to ensure a more responsible workforce. Eligibility for visas extends to Saudi citizens, Gulf nationals, foreign wives of Saudi men, their mothers, and holders of Saudi premium residency permits, contingent upon the employer's financial capacity. The Musaned platform, spearheaded by the Ministry, serves as a digital system educating users about rights and responsibilities, managing visa applications, recruitment, and financial transactions via apps like STC Pay and Urpay. Encompassing various domestic worker categories, from housekeepers to nannies, these regulations aim to enhance transparency, efficiency in recruitment, and establish a solid dispute resolution framework, aligning with Saudi Arabia's drive for a modernized, fair domestic labor market.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Supply and Internal Trade, Ali Moslehi, disclosed plans to potentially shift from subsidizing commodities to offering...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Supply and Internal Trade, Ali Moslehi, disclosed plans to potentially shift from subsidizing commodities to offering cash support, contingent on stabilizing economic conditions. Moslehi clarified that if enacted, this measure would be optional for citizens, part of the government's strategy to address economic challenges. During a TV interview, Moslehi outlined that subsidized bread, currently sold at five piasters despite costing the government one pound per loaf, might be offered at its actual market price of one pound. He highlighted global events like the Russia-Ukraine conflict and events in Gaza impacting Egypt, leading to escalated shipping costs worldwide. The state's general budget for 2023/2024 estimates approximately LE 127.7 billion for food commodity support, a significant increase from the previous year. Over 60 million people benefit from the ration cards system, receiving LE50 ($1.62) monthly per person to purchase subsidized items. Moreover, more than 70 million citizens receive heavily subsidized bread. Plans to adjust the subsidized bread price, unchanged for decades, have been postponed due to the Ukrainian conflict's aftermath.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Oman's Khazaen Economic City is poised to host a $97 million animal feed factory, a pivotal move by the Omani Bioproducts Company—formed...
records.description: Oman's Khazaen Economic City is poised to host a $97 million animal feed factory, a pivotal move by the Omani Bioproducts Company—formed through a collaboration between the Omani Mills Group and Nakheel Oman Development Company. Located in Khazaen, the factory aims to produce specialized feeds for aquatic organisms, bolstering Oman's sustainability and agricultural endeavors. Spanning three phases with an investment cost of OMR 37 million, construction tendering began in June, with the construction contract slated for approval by year-end. Nine local companies have bid for the project, and machinery is already on-site. The factory will convert agricultural and biological by-products into value-added products, recycling date by-products like kernels, pulp, and palm fronds. It plans to annually produce 100,000 tonnes of grass feed from agricultural residues enhanced with dates, along with 300,000 tonnes of marine life feed for shrimp and fish cultivation in cages. The use of local raw materials will support food security projects, covering red meat, dairy products, aquaculture, and marine agriculture, aiming to serve domestic and export markets. This aligns with the "Oman 2040" vision, focusing on circular and bioeconomy concepts, promoting environmentally friendly and sustainable production. The collaborative efforts involve various entities, including companies under the Oman Investment Authority, partnerships with "be’ah," and support from the Ministry of Agricultural Wealth, Fisheries, and Water Resources.

records.title: The General Authority for Healthcare Accreditation & Regulation (GAHAR) has initiated the "Egypt Health Indicator" project, introducing s...
records.description: The General Authority for Healthcare Accreditation & Regulation (GAHAR) has initiated the "Egypt Health Indicator" project, introducing standardized measures to evaluate healthcare quality across various sectors in Egypt's hospitals. Ahmed Taha, GAHAR's Head, emphasized the project's significance during an expert meeting co-hosted by GAHAR and the World Health Organization. The initiative aims to routinely assess healthcare quality in facilities, facilitating continuous enhancement by identifying strengths and weaknesses. Taha highlighted that GAHAR's accreditation certificate serves as a means to ensure quality and initiate ongoing improvements rather than being an end goal. The "Egypt Health Indicator" seeks to establish a universal reference for measuring healthcare facility performance at national and regional levels. These benchmarks will gauge the impact of adhering to quality standards and accreditation on enhancing the healthcare system within these facilities.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Healthcare Accreditation & Regulation (GAHAR)

records.title: Morocco’s Agriculture Minister Oversees Rural Development Projects in Driouch and Nador
records.description: Morocco's Minister of Agriculture, Mohammed Sadiki, embarked on a tour of the provinces of Driouch and Nador within the Oriental region, aiming to oversee and launch projects under the Generation Green 2020-2030 strategy, designed to transform the agricultural sector. Initiatives included kickstarting a 3.5 km rural road in Oulad Mohand, part of a broader rural road development program in Driouch, with an investment of 58.14 million dirhams for 57 km of roads. In Douar Lahbara, the minister reviewed the Integrated Rural Development Support Project, covering 100 hectares of carob trees, additional plantations, irrigation systems, and road enhancements, benefitting 40,750 farmers. Meanwhile, in Nador province's Oulad Settout community, a project worth 1.25 billion dirhams focused on converting 13,500 hectares to localized irrigation systems, benefiting 3,325 farmers, aiming to bolster water supply security, crop productivity, and regional economic growth, all contributing to Morocco's sustainable agricultural advancements.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.title: Oman saw a significant 13% drop in its producer price index during the third quarter of 2023, compared to the same period in 2022.
records.description: Oman saw a significant 13% drop in its producer price index during the third quarter of 2023, compared to the same period in 2022. Data from the Omani National Center for Statistics and Information revealed a consistent decrease in the PPI, measuring the price changes of goods leaving the producer. The report detailed a 13.7% decrease in oil and gas product prices and an 8.2% decrease in non-oil products. This decline was influenced by various factors such as lowered costs associated with crude oil and natural gas (16% decrease), manufacturing industry expenses (10.2% dip), and reduced prices in several categories including transportation, food, beverages, textiles, and specific metal products. Conversely, some product prices like woven fabric, shoes, and clothing experienced slight increases.
records.institution: Omani National Center for Statistics and Information

records.title: Oman's Consul General in Karachi, Engineer Sami Abdullah Salim Al Khanjari, expressed discontent with the limited trade between Oman and...
records.description: Oman's Consul General in Karachi, Engineer Sami Abdullah Salim Al Khanjari, expressed discontent with the limited trade between Oman and Pakistan, highlighting the substantial potential for stronger ties. Despite their proximity, trade is predominantly limited to exports of rice, mangoes, and potatoes from Pakistan to Oman. Engineer Khanjari urged for the exploration of additional exports such as onions, chillies, carrots, and other agricultural produce, emphasizing their freshness and proximity as key advantages. He encouraged the Karachi business community to diversify exports, particularly in fruits, vegetables, and textiles, aiming to boost bilateral trade volumes. Highlighting Oman's substantial port infrastructure and significant investments from various countries, he stressed the need for increased Pakistani presence in Oman's trade and investment landscape. The Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) President, Iftikhar Ahmed Sheikh, echoed the call for fostering deeper bilateral relationships, extending full support for augmenting trade and investment collaborations.

records.title: KSrelief from Saudi Arabia dispatched aid containing food, medical, and shelter supplies to Gaza via the Rafah crossing on Sunday.
records.description: KSrelief from Saudi Arabia dispatched aid containing food, medical, and shelter supplies to Gaza via the Rafah crossing on Sunday. Twenty planes landed at Al-Arish airport in Egypt, delivering the aid, which was subsequently loaded onto trucks for transfer to the Palestinian side of the Rafah crossing. The United Nations highlighted that the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas facilitated the largest increase in the delivery of essential resources such as food, water, and medicine since the conflict's onset. This period also marked the first fuel delivery since the war commenced and enabled access to northern regions after a month.

records.title: The Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD) unveiled a pioneering air quality modeling system, a sophisticated toolset aimed at augmenting t...
records.description: The Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD) unveiled a pioneering air quality modeling system, a sophisticated toolset aimed at augmenting the region’s air quality monitoring endeavors. This system, tailored for Abu Dhabi, holds the capacity to evaluate cumulative air quality impacts anticipated from new infrastructures and urban projects. Its primary objectives encompass mitigating public exposure to air pollutants, fortifying air quality across the region, and gauging the effectiveness of future environmental strategies. This innovation is poised to pinpoint pollution hotspots, create detailed air quality maps, and contribute to environmental assessments. Engineer Faisal Al Hammadi, EAD's Executive Director of the Environmental Quality Sector, emphasized the criticality of evidence-based tools to manage air quality effectively, citing the system's pivotal role in fostering a balance between economic growth, environmental conservation, and societal well-being. The system's scope extends to supporting compliance evaluation, air quality forecasts, public awareness, and emergency response, championing a healthier environment and quality of life. Additionally, the initiative will bolster collaboration with key partners, including the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, the Abu Dhabi Executive Office, health and law enforcement departments, and various governmental bodies, reaffirming a concerted effort toward improving air quality.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Olive Odyssey, a Palestinian collective, embodies resilience amidst ongoing conflict, striving to sustain olive oil production—a prof...
records.description: The Olive Odyssey, a Palestinian collective, embodies resilience amidst ongoing conflict, striving to sustain olive oil production—a profound symbol of Palestine's identity—even in challenging times. Amidst difficulties and dangers, they persist during the harvest season, maintaining an age-old tradition despite obstacles such as restricted access to farmlands. Despite these challenges, the collective, driven by determination, successfully crafted seven signature bottled olive oils from hard-working farmers across six regions in Palestine. Their organic cultivation methods, devoid of artificial intervention, honor traditional harvest practices, fostering a narrative that embodies the Palestinian story and their connection to the land. With global outreach, the Olive Odyssey's olive oil represents not just a product but a testament to Palestine's soul and heritage, finding resonance and appreciation worldwide.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s Economic Reforms are Boosting M&A Activity
records.description: Saudi Arabia's economic reforms are proving to be a catalyst for increased mergers and acquisitions (M&A) activities in the country. The nation's economic growth, buoyed by non-oil sectors, has generated favorable conditions for robust M&A activity. Amid a global economic slowdown and various geopolitical tensions worldwide, the region's economic reforms, including those in Saudi Arabia, are expected to spur this trend further. The Kingdom's economy, among the largest in the region and one of the fastest-growing globally, presents a promising landscape for investors. Despite forecasts of a slowdown in the GCC's growth due to a decrease in contributions from hydrocarbons, the momentum in non-hydrocarbon sectors is anticipated to persist. Saudi Arabia has seen a substantial increase in outbound investment, with figures for the first half of 2023 reaching $10.9 billion, part of a projected MENA total of $31.9 billion. This upswing in M&A activity is not limited to Saudi Arabia alone but extends across the MENA region, showcasing an active and diverse investor base. Economic diversification efforts in sectors like technology, renewable energy, e-commerce, and infrastructure have bolstered the country's attractiveness for investment. The Saudi Public Investment Fund's ventures, including acquisitions in various sectors and a significant stake in a Japanese gaming giant, exemplify the nation's openness to global investment and collaboration. The Saudi government's initiatives, such as Vision 2030 and the Public Investment Fund, serve as key indicators of Saudi Arabia's commitment to inviting global investors and fostering economic growth. This upward trajectory in M&A activity and economic diversification signals a promising future not only for Saudi Arabia but also for the entire region, showcasing substantial potential for further growth and expansion.

records.title: The recent Saudi-Algerian Business Forum in Riyadh marked a significant step in deepening trade, investment, and tourism ties between Alg...
records.description: The recent Saudi-Algerian Business Forum in Riyadh marked a significant step in deepening trade, investment, and tourism ties between Algeria and Saudi Arabia. This event led to the signing of eight agreements spanning various sectors, including business accelerators, elevators, and spare parts, signaling an intent to boost commerce between the nations from an estimated $837 million. Algeria's Minister of Trade and Export Promotion highlighted upcoming changes in investment laws that are poised to elevate economic exchanges between the two countries. The establishment of the Saudi-Algerian Supreme Coordination Council and other collaborative entities was heralded as a transformative leap in economic relations, demonstrating the commitment to fostering partnerships. Algerian officials emphasized incentives for investment, including a skilled workforce, energy cost efficiency, robust infrastructure, and tax facilities. Moreover, both sides noted the potential for Saudi businesses to bring expertise and innovations to Algeria's industrial, tourism, agricultural, and service sectors, capitalizing on each country's economic strengths and reinforcing the foundation for bilateral trade. Algeria's ongoing reforms aiming to create a diversified economic model and an investor-friendly legislative framework were also highlighted, offering a fertile ground for fostering partnership and bilateral trade.

records.title: Elsayed Elkosayer, Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, recently sat down with a delegation of Saudi businessmen and inv...
records.description: Elsayed Elkosayer, Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, recently sat down with a delegation of Saudi businessmen and investors to explore avenues for bolstering Saudi agricultural investments in Egypt. Elkosayer highlighted the strategic nature of Egyptian-Saudi relations across various domains and emphasized Egypt's fertile ground for agricultural investment. He underscored the government's commitment to fostering an environment conducive to local, Arab, and foreign investors, showcasing specific opportunities in plant, animal, fish, and poultry production, as well as food manufacturing. Expressing eagerness to amplify Saudi investments in Egypt, Elkosayer extended invitations to serious investors, offering support in navigating procedures and overcoming obstacles they might encounter. The Saudi investors, recognizing the strong bilateral ties and Egypt's recent achievements, voiced their intentions to expand their investments in Egypt, particularly within the agricultural sector, building upon their successful ventures in real estate.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: In light of Egypt's water scarcity and dwindling arable land, a transition to soilless farming, exemplified by Plug'n'Grow's initiatives,...
records.description: In light of Egypt's water scarcity and dwindling arable land, a transition to soilless farming, exemplified by Plug'n'Grow's initiatives, has emerged among certain Egyptian smallholders. This innovative technique, known as hydroponics, involves cultivating plants in controlled environments without soil, utilizing nutrient-rich water instead. Plug'n'Grow's efforts showcase how hydroponics drastically reduces water consumption by about 90% compared to traditional methods and lowers the need for expensive fertilizers by roughly 60%. Despite its potential, hydroponics currently focuses mainly on crops like leafy greens and simpler vegetables, posing limitations for cultivating strategic crops such as wheat or rice through this method. Additionally, the high initial costs of establishing commercial hydroponic farms, starting at over €100,000, present a challenge for widespread adoption, despite its promise in addressing Egypt's water scarcity challenges and advancing agricultural sustainability.

records.title: Mitsui & Co., a Japanese conglomerate, is strategically fortifying its presence in the food industry by acquiring an undisclosed stake in...
records.description: Mitsui & Co., a Japanese conglomerate, is strategically fortifying its presence in the food industry by acquiring an undisclosed stake in Egypt's Wadi Poultry. This deal signifies Mitsui's entry into the poultry and agri-food sectors in collaboration with Wadi Group's diversified business encompassing food production, poultry processing, and animal feed. The agreement positions Wadi Poultry's holding company as an associated entity of Mitsui, although the specific financial terms and the extent of the investment remain undisclosed. This move aligns with Mitsui's broader strategy of integrating food production, ranging from grain procurement for feed to broiler production, processing, and food distribution. It's part of a series of strategic investments by Mitsui in various segments of the food industry globally, aiming to expand its food and nutrition business cluster. The collaboration aims to leverage Egypt's growing market by expanding Wadi's agri-business both locally and for export, considering Egypt's significant population and rapid growth in Africa.

records.title: On November 19, 2023, Prime Minister Masrour Barzani of the Kurdistan Regional Government inaugurated the Distar Factory, a state-of-the-...
records.description: On November 19, 2023, Prime Minister Masrour Barzani of the Kurdistan Regional Government inaugurated the Distar Factory, a state-of-the-art wheat flour mill situated in Domiz, Duhok Governorate. In his address, Prime Minister Barzani underscored the KRG's commitment to fortifying the agricultural sector and ensuring food security as paramount objectives. He outlined the collaborative strategy with the private sector, highlighting various initiatives aiming to effectively market the wheat cultivated by Kurdish farmers and bolster the local agricultural economy. The Prime Minister emphasized the government's role in supporting farmers by providing reliable platforms to sell their produce, encouraging continued cultivation, and facilitating product exports. He stressed the region's potential to significantly contribute not only to Iraq's sustenance but also to the broader region's through effective resource utilization. Prime Minister Barzani commended the private sector's role in advancing the economy and encouraged further collaboration, inviting investors to explore opportunities in agriculture and industry to boost regional economic growth, reduce external reliance, and elevate citizens' quality of life.

records.title: Pakistan's Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar is poised to ink seven MoUs valued at $10 billion during an upcoming visit to Kuwait, as ap...
records.description: Pakistan's Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar is poised to ink seven MoUs valued at $10 billion during an upcoming visit to Kuwait, as approved in a recent federal cabinet meeting. These memoranda, born from the efforts of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), aim to bolster Pakistan's economy by inviting investments from Kuwait across various sectors including agriculture, mining, IT, defense production, energy, and food security. These initiatives underscore Pakistan's efforts to attract foreign investment, particularly from Gulf nations, to navigate challenging economic conditions. The proposed projects encompass endeavors like expanding water reservoirs, enhancing mining facilities, fortifying mangrove forests along coastal areas, and investment schemes in the information technology sector. Pakistan and Kuwait, rooted in shared cultural and faith-based values, seek to strengthen their economic ties beyond existing diplomatic relations, with the aspiration to elevate mutual trade to $1 billion annually within the next few years, marking a significant milestone in their growing economic partnership.

records.title: Caretaker Minister of Agriculture Abbas Hajj Hassan recently hosted Ali Dagman, the Chargé d'Affaires of the Syrian Embassy in Lebanon, t...
records.description: Caretaker Minister of Agriculture Abbas Hajj Hassan recently hosted Ali Dagman, the Chargé d'Affaires of the Syrian Embassy in Lebanon, to delve into the bilateral agricultural ties between Lebanon and Syria. Their discussions centered on various aspects of agricultural cooperation and the shared agricultural calendar between the two nations. Minister Hajj Hassan expressed gratitude to the Syrian government for facilitating Lebanese products, underscoring the enduring and robust bond that unites the two nations, aiming to benefit both peoples in this fraternal relationship.

records.title: FAO and MoA Sign an Agreement to Enhance Food and Nutrition
records.description: Minister of Agriculture Abbas Hajj Hassan and FAO Representative in Lebanon Nora Ourabah Haddad have sealed an impactful agreement underwritten by the Government of Canada with a funding amount of CAD$20 million. This vital initiative focuses on elevating agricultural practices by enhancing gender-responsive, nutrition-sensitive, and climate-smart methodologies. It strives to elevate the performance of fruits and vegetables value chains while fortifying the conducive environment for value chain stakeholders. The overarching aim encompasses bolstering resilience against climatic and economic upheavals within Lebanon's fruits and vegetables value chains, ultimately fortifying food and nutrition security in the nation. The project particularly targets small-scale fruits and vegetables farmers, with a specific emphasis on women, offering support to enhance their technical and organizational capacities to engage more effectively in designated value chains and augment their income. Further, the endeavor extends its backing to input producers, processors, and traders, aiding them in formulating innovative business strategies and adopting contemporary technologies across production, marketing, and processing levels. This strategic alignment aims to render these sectors more competitive, inclusive, and sustainable, aligning closely with farmers' requisites. By empowering farmers' associations and cooperatives to synchronize their strategies and operations, the project endeavors to make safer, healthier, and more affordable food accessible, consequently fortifying the resilience of Lebanon's food systems. Overall, this collaborative effort marks a significant stride in the enduring partnership between the Government of Canada, the Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture, and the Food and Agriculture Organization, dedicated to bolstering Lebanon's agricultural sector's sustainability.

records.title: The African Development Bank reinforced its support for Libya through the signing of three technical assistance grant agreements, undersc...
records.description: The African Development Bank reinforced its support for Libya through the signing of three technical assistance grant agreements, underscoring its commitment to the country. These agreements, inked in Tripoli by a delegation led by Mrs Malinne Blomberg, signify critical aid in the aftermath of the Derna floods. Among the grants is a $1 million emergency support fund, facilitated in collaboration with UNICEF and the Libyan government, aiming to swiftly procure wash and hygiene kits and aid for temporary learning spaces and classrooms. Mrs Blomberg expressed solidarity during the signing, acknowledging Libya's recovery efforts. Dr Khalid El Mabrouk, Libya’s finance minister, applauded the Bank's prompt response, highlighting their strong partnership and instrumental support in advancing Libya's development agenda. The agreements, drawing from the Bank’s Middle-Income Technical Assistance Fund, include support for a Food Security and Nutrition Strategy and the implementation of a Financial Management and Information System, showcasing the Bank’s dedication to enhancing Libya's overall well-being and financial transparency. During the visit, the delegation discussed proposed initiatives and projects for 2024, furthering the Bank's commitment to Libya's sustainable development.

records.title: Morocco is contemplating diversifying its wheat import sources, particularly eyeing the Russian market as a potential alternative to thei...
records.description: Morocco is contemplating diversifying its wheat import sources, particularly eyeing the Russian market as a potential alternative to their traditional suppliers, notably France. In a recent meeting in Rabat between wheat professionals and Russian suppliers, the National Federation of Grain and Legumes President, Omar El Yaacoubi, highlighted challenges faced by importers and emphasized the need to broaden the countries supplying wheat to Morocco. The federation discussed Russia's potential involvement in ensuring secure ship passages from the Black Sea to the Mediterranean, reflecting efforts to stabilize wheat imports. Despite these discussions, reassurances were made regarding Morocco's market stability, asserting no shortages in grain resources to meet consumer needs. Moulay Abdelkader Alaoui, President of the National Federation of Mills, emphasized the preference for high-quality imported grains, particularly from Europe, Russia, and Latin America, underlining their substantial impact on flour quality. Russia's readiness to collaborate with Morocco in the wheat sector was expressed in September, with the Russian ambassador highlighting the mutual interest in their market demands. These developments occur amidst a notable decline in French wheat exports to Morocco and Algeria, with these regions increasingly turning to Russia for their wheat imports due to their high consumption rates and the changing dynamics in global grain markets.
records.institution: Morccan National Federation of Grain and Legumes

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Planning and Economic Development, Dr.
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Planning and Economic Development, Dr. Hala El-Said, and Oman's Minister of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion, Qais bin Mohammed Musa Al-Yousef, recently convened to bolster collaboration between their nations. Their focus lies in establishing a joint fund aimed at investing in specific sectors like agricultural industries, food processing, and pharmaceuticals. Dr. El-Said commended Oman's Sovereign Investment Fund's efforts, citing Egypt's keenness to learn from Oman's experience in setting up the Egyptian Sovereign Fund. Al-Yousef echoed the sentiment, emphasizing the importance of reciprocal discussions to strengthen economic ties, culminating in agreements to form technical teams to explore industrial integration, discuss free trade agreements, and strategize around incentives and industrial strategies for mutual benefit. This meeting underscores the burgeoning economic and investment bonds between Egypt and Oman, signifying a shared commitment to expanding collaboration in vital sectors through the proposed joint fund.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Commerce, Industry, and Investment Promotion

records.title: AAAID to Invest $100mln in Egypt Within 3 Years
records.description: The Arab Authority for Agricultural Investment and Development (AAAID) is set to reinforce its commitment to Egypt's agricultural and livestock sectors by injecting $100 million in fresh investments within the next three years, as revealed by Chairman Mohamed Bin Obaid Al Mazrooei during the Gulf-Egyptian Business Forum. This substantial investment initiative aligns with AAAID's ongoing support for Egypt's agricultural landscape, which currently stands at approximately $158 million. The organization's existing investments include a 27% stake in Faiyoum Sugar Company, an 82% stake in the Arab Company for Production and Preservation of Crops, and a 5% stake in the Middle East for Vaccines (MEVAC). AAAID's strategic focus on augmenting these sectors within Egypt underscores its dedication to fostering sustainable growth and development in the country's crucial agricultural domain.
records.institution: The Arab Authority for Agricultural Investment and Development (AAAID)

records.title: RedSea, stemming from Saudi Arabia, is rapidly expanding its climate-controlled hydroponics greenhouse enterprise across Egypt and East A...
records.description: RedSea, stemming from Saudi Arabia, is rapidly expanding its climate-controlled hydroponics greenhouse enterprise across Egypt and East Africa, tapping into hot climate markets to address water scarcity and energy consumption. Bolstered by a substantial $20 million USD capital infusion this year, the company, founded in 2018 by Mark Tester and Ryan Lefers, is led by Bruno De Oliveira, leveraging extensive experience in commercial farming and business development. Their focus on utilizing hydroponics in desert regions, powered by saltwater and solar energy, aims to revolutionize local produce cultivation sustainably, prioritizing reduction of carbon emissions and alleviation of food and water scarcity in these regions.

records.title: Largest Afforestation Project Ever in Iraqi Kurdistan
records.description: The International Labour Organization (ILO) unveiled a pioneering afforestation endeavor in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, funded by the Government of the Netherlands through the PROSPECTS Partnership. This innovative project targets climate-related challenges while generating more than 700 short-term employment opportunities for local Iraqis, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and Syrian refugees. The initiative not only focuses on environmental sustainability but also emphasizes the creation of decent work opportunities to support the community's livelihoods.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Jordan are deepening their collaboration in the water sector, with Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadhli, Saudi Minister...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Jordan are deepening their collaboration in the water sector, with Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadhli, Saudi Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, meeting Jordanian Minister of Water and Irrigation, Raed Abu Soud, to discuss bilateral cooperation. The meeting, held during the Arab Ministerial Water Council's 15th session and the 5th Arab Water Conference in Riyadh, highlighted the significance of joint cooperation in addressing water scarcity, climate change, and enhancing sustainable water resources. The ministers discussed knowledge exchange, particularly on alternative water resources like desalination and recycled water, to tackle water scarcity challenges in the Arab region. Abu Soud supported Saudi Arabia's initiative to establish a global water organization aimed at improving water resource management through technical exchanges, research, development, and funding for essential projects. Jordan has been proactive in addressing water scarcity challenges, implementing innovative solutions such as treated water reuse and enhancing water supply efficiency. Al-Fadhli praised the strategic relations between Jordan and Saudi Arabia, acknowledging efforts to secure Jordan's water needs sustainably. Additionally, during the council meeting, there was a strong condemnation of Israel's actions against Gaza, citing severe disruptions to basic services like electricity and water, causing significant damage to water infrastructure and posing serious humanitarian concerns. The council urged the international community to take action to stop these actions and fulfill their responsibilities in resolving the situation.
records.institution: Jordanian Ministry of Water and Irrigation

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: ACWA Power, a prominent developer and operator of power generation and desalinated water plants based in Saudi Arabia, has successfully c...
records.description: ACWA Power, a prominent developer and operator of power generation and desalinated water plants based in Saudi Arabia, has successfully clinched a contract to establish a substantial 200 MW wind power plant across Uzbekistan's Karaozak and Beruniy districts. The endeavor, financed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, saw stiff competition with two bidders vying for the project. ACWA Power's offer, priced at $4.09 per kWh for both electricity generation and storage, outpaced its competitor, Masdar, whose bid stood at $4.99. This new project marks ACWA Power's continued expansion in Uzbekistan, following its prior success in securing the country's initial wind power plant contract. Their earlier 100 MW facility in Karaozak was secured with a winning bid of $2.57 per kWh of electricity. ACWA Power's robust commitment to renewable energy extends globally, with projects spanning diverse regions like Azerbaijan and Egypt, showcasing their pivotal role in accelerating the shift towards sustainable energy sources. These endeavors not only contribute to reducing carbon emissions but also stimulate economic growth within the regions they operate in, reinforcing their position as key players in fostering the renewable energy transition.

records.title: Reef Saudi has initiated a significant venture by establishing bee clinics in major Saudi cities—Jeddah, Jazan, Madinah, and Abha—dedicat...
records.description: Reef Saudi has initiated a significant venture by establishing bee clinics in major Saudi cities—Jeddah, Jazan, Madinah, and Abha—dedicated to beekeepers. These clinics offer crucial services encompassing examination, diagnosis, guidance, and assistance, thereby empowering small-scale producers. The clinics' objectives include safeguarding the nation's bee population from diseases and pests, fostering self-sufficiency by increasing local bee colonies, and deploying mobile clinics to directly aid beekeepers on-site. The initiative, backed by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, received appreciation from beekeepers like Hasan Al-Qarni, who underscored the clinics' role in diagnosing diseases, providing guidance, and devising sustainable solutions for beekeepers in the Kingdom. This support has translated into significant achievements, such as Al-Qarni winning top honors in an Arab honey competition, further highlighting the Ministry's backing for local beekeepers. Reef Saudi, focusing on enhancing the honey sector, has substantially bolstered food security, showcasing a 49 percent progress rate toward self-sufficiency, notably increasing honey production from 2,100 tons in 2020 to 3,748 tons in 2023. Moreover, since the launch of the bee clinics, over 6,000 samples have been processed, enabling examinations and the development of a comprehensive database for diseases and pests impacting bees in the region. Reef Saudi's overarching aim remains to bolster farmers' capabilities, enhance agricultural productivity, and elevate the living standards of rural families by facilitating market access and agricultural resources. This program continues to play a pivotal role in advancing crop cultivation throughout Saudi Arabia.

records.title: The decline in local palm cultivation in Syria has led to soaring prices of dates, impacting the affordability of this staple food item,...
records.description: The decline in local palm cultivation in Syria has led to soaring prices of dates, impacting the affordability of this staple food item, particularly during significant occasions like the holy month of Ramadan. Import restrictions and the fluctuating Syrian pound against the US dollar have exacerbated this situation. The Syrian government has encountered challenges in increasing local date production due to security issues in traditional palm-growing areas and the spread of the palm tree weevil disease. Although efforts have been made to reassess suitable cultivation areas and enhance production by establishing propagation centers, the sector faces hurdles, including a lack of skilled workers, outdated cultivation methods, and insufficient modern irrigation technologies. Despite plans to modernize and expand palm cultivation, these initiatives have faced setbacks, especially in regions where government control has been limited. Experts highlight the need for adopting advanced techniques like tissue culture for larger-scale seedling production, suggesting a path to revitalize the declining local date production industry in Syria.
