records.title: DANA Global and Rivulis, two influential entities in the sustainable agriculture domain, have joined forces to establish an innovative de...
records.description: DANA Global and Rivulis, two influential entities in the sustainable agriculture domain, have joined forces to establish an innovative demo farm in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi. This groundbreaking collaboration aims to exhibit and educate farmers on sustainable farming solutions tailored for extreme weather and arid environments. By leveraging advanced micro irrigation systems and climate farming models, Rivulis will demonstrate efficient crop production methods that combat climate change effects, water scarcity, biodiversity loss, and enhance food security while ensuring sustainable livelihoods for growers. The initiative, part of Masdar City's beta site, emphasizes the transition to more sustainable farming practices by showcasing Rivulis' cutting-edge irrigation and fertigation systems, echoing DANA's commitment to fostering sustainable agricultural practices in the region. The partnership's focus on fostering innovative solutions aligns with the UAE's National Food Security Strategy, marking a significant step towards addressing critical agricultural challenges posed by climate change in the Middle East and Africa. Furthermore, Rivulis is pioneering socio-economic initiatives like Impact Financing and Rivulis Climate programs, aiming to democratize sustainable farming by empowering small-scale farmers and promoting accessibility to advanced technologies for all growers.

records.title: Dubai has opened a trade office in Lagos, Nigeria, to enhance cross-border trade and investment opportunities between the two countries.
records.description: Dubai has opened a trade office in Lagos, Nigeria, to enhance cross-border trade and investment opportunities between the two countries. The office will serve as a platform for communication and collaboration, facilitating business matchmaking and networking events. Dubai sees Nigeria as a strategically important market, offering access to the broader West African region. In turn, Nigeria views the UAE as a key gateway to the Middle East. The establishment of the trade office is expected to strengthen economic ties and boost bilateral trade.

records.title: Algeria Signs Third Country Programme Framework (CPF) for 2024-2029
records.description: Algeria recently inked its Country Programme Framework (CPF) for 2024–2029, solidifying a collaborative roadmap with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). H.E. Larbi Latroch, Resident Representative of the Permanent Mission of the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria, and Mr. Hua Liu, IAEA Deputy Director General and Head of the Department of Technical Cooperation, officiated the signing on November 22, 2023. The CPF serves as a blueprint for medium-term technical cooperation between a Member State and the IAEA, focusing on priority areas aligned with national development objectives. Algeria, an IAEA Member State since 1963, outlines five key priorities in its 2024–2029 CPF, encompassing nuclear and radiation safety and security, energy, medical radioisotope production, monitoring and detection of animal and zoonotic diseases, and water resource mapping and management.

records.title: Turkey Extends LNG Supply Deal with Algeria
records.description: Turkey has prolonged its liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply contract with Algeria for an additional three years, as per Reuters. The agreement, facilitated between Turkish Government-supported energy entity Botas and Algerian state-owned oil and gas company Sonatrach, was formalized during Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan’s official visit to Algiers. This extension solidifies Turkey's commitment to purchasing 4.4 billion cubic meters (bcm) of LNG annually from Algeria. The original gas supply pact, initiated in 1988 between Botas and Sonatrach, has undergone renewals over the years. With this extension, the existing contract, which was initially set to terminate in October 2024, will now endure until 2027. Erdogan emphasized Turkey's interest in broadening its energy and renewable energy associations with Algeria, aiming to forge new alliances for mutual benefit.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Iraqis continue to suffer the consequences of climate change.
records.description: Iraqis continue to suffer the consequences of climate change. In a country of 43 million people, nearly one Iraqi in five lives in an area suffering from water shortages and 74 percent of climate refugees resettle in urban areas. The story of Nasser Jabbar and his family epitomizes the struggle of Iraqis displaced by the crisis. Formerly a successful herder and farmer, Jabbar was forced to abandon his rural life due to persistent drought, plunging him into urban poverty in southern Iraq. His neighborhood mirrors the destitution faced by climate refugees, with dilapidated infrastructure and sanitation issues prevalent. Despite efforts to adapt, such as digging a well that eventually dried up, Jabbar's transition to urban life was marred by health issues that halted his employment in construction, leaving his teenage children as the family's primary breadwinners, earning meager wages at the local market. This plight highlights the broader challenges faced by climate-displaced Iraqis, including strained urban resources, a lack of economic opportunities, and limited access to education for children, underscoring the urgent need for comprehensive interventions and sustainable solutions.

records.title: The dwindling cultivation of Iraq's signature anbar rice due to severe water shortages has significantly impacted farmers like Salah Fare...
records.description: The dwindling cultivation of Iraq's signature anbar rice due to severe water shortages has significantly impacted farmers like Salah Fareeq Al-Feroun, who, for generations, relied on farming in southern Iraq. Climate change, along with geopolitical tensions, has led to a diminishing water supply, rendering it impossible for Al-Feroun and others to cultivate anbar rice, a unique long-grain variety integral to Iraqi cuisine. The government's ban on anbar rice cultivation to conserve water has forced Iraq to import rice from other countries, altering the traditional rice flavors. While climate journalist Achref Chibani attributes the water scarcity to climate change and poor governance, farmer Al-Feroun underscores the need for serious diplomatic negotiations with neighboring countries, international organizations, and forums to secure Iraq's water rights. Despite promises of compensation from the government, tangible assistance is yet to materialize, leaving farmers like Al-Feroun eager for genuine efforts and solutions to protect their agricultural heritage and ensure the continuation of their family legacies.

records.title: Lebanon's Dooda Solutions has emerged as the triumphant recipient of a $100,000 grant through PepsiCo's Greenhouse Accelerator Program: M...
records.description: Lebanon's Dooda Solutions has emerged as the triumphant recipient of a $100,000 grant through PepsiCo's Greenhouse Accelerator Program: MENA Sustainability Edition, an initiative conducted in partnership with the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and Food Tech Valley (FTV). From a pool of over 180 candidates, Dooda Solutions, founded by Nada Ghanem in 2018, stood out for its expertise in producing premium-grade vermicompost and organic fertilizers on a commercial scale. Their vermicompost, rich in nutrients, revitalizes soil fertility, enhancing crop productivity and soil health. Following a comprehensive selection process and six months of mentorship, the award was bestowed upon Dooda Solutions, recognizing their innovative and scalable approach in sustainable agriculture. The closing ceremony, held at the Museum of the Future, witnessed the announcement in the presence of distinguished figures like His Excellency Eng. Mohammed Mousa Alameeri from the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, affirming the commitment to promoting sustainable solutions and fostering entrepreneurship in the region. The program's focus on sustainable agriculture aligns with PepsiCo's sustainability strategy, pep+, and demonstrates a commitment to supporting startups that drive tangible, positive change. The endeavor, catalyzed by PepsiCo, aims to spotlight these solutions on a global stage, showcasing them at COP28, thereby expanding their growth opportunities and solidifying the program's enduring impact.

records.title: Saudi specialists, led by the head of KSrelief, initiated Saudi Arabia’s first aid convoy from Egypt to Gaza following directives from Ki...
records.description: Saudi specialists, led by the head of KSrelief, initiated Saudi Arabia’s first aid convoy from Egypt to Gaza following directives from King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The convoy, comprising 30 trucks with essential supplies like food, medicine, and shelter goods, along with 14 fully-equipped ambulances, aims to support Palestinians in Gaza. Dr. Abdullah Al-Rabeeah signed a cooperation agreement worth $40 million with various humanitarian organizations. Challenges persist due to restrictions imposed by Israel, limiting aid entry. Displaced Palestinians in Egypt shared harrowing stories, highlighting Gaza’s dire health and food shortages. The recent ceasefire between Israel and Hamas may alleviate some obstacles to aid delivery.

records.title: UAE Launches Power, Water Saving Project in Public Buildings
records.description: The UAE has initiated a collaborative project aiming to significantly curtail power and water consumption across over 400 federal government buildings in its first phase, as announced by Sharif Al-Olama, Undersecretary of the Energy and Infrastructure Ministry for Energy Affairs. The initiative, developed in partnership with the private sector, is geared towards reducing electricity usage by 20 percent and water consumption by 30 percent within these buildings. Al-Olama emphasized that this undertaking aligns with a broader strategy aimed at long-term energy management and water security in the UAE, slated until 2036, and is an integral component of the nation's 2050 national energy program. The project's expansion plan extends beyond federal buildings to encompass government facilities across the emirates, including agricultural entities grappling with energy and water cost challenges, signifying a concerted effort toward sustainability and resource optimization.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure

records.title: Tetra Pak's collaboration with HSA Group in Yemen brings fortified flavored milk to 10,000 school children, addressing nutritional challe...
records.description: Tetra Pak's collaboration with HSA Group in Yemen brings fortified flavored milk to 10,000 school children, addressing nutritional challenges amidst conflict-related food insecurity. The initiative, starting in the Taiz governorate, aims to bolster students' health and regular attendance, crucial in a country deeply affected by prolonged conflict, disrupting essential services and food access. Tetra Pak's aseptic packaging ensures freshness for up to 12 months, pivotal in Yemen's compromised infrastructure. Local production by HSA Group fortifies UHT milk, battling nutritional deficiencies. Overseen by HSA's Humanitarian Development Program, this effort engages various stakeholders, including the Ministry of Education and UN agencies, ensuring safe delivery, storage, and awareness campaigns. Notably, this venture integrates recycling education, emphasizing environmental consciousness. The collaboration's broader vision includes enhancing food systems, aiding farmers, and expanding nutrition access, with plans to diversify food offerings for children, aiming for sustainable impact and future growth through partnership expansion.
records.institution: Tetra Pak & Hayel Saeed Anam (HSA) Group

records.title: Morocco’s Agriculture Ministry Guides Plan for Oasis and Argan Zones
records.description: Morocco's Minister of Agriculture, Mohammed Sadiki, chaired the 10th session of the Strategic Orientation Council of the National Agency for the Development of Oasis and Argan Zones (ANDZOA) in Rabat, focusing on evaluating the previous decade's strategy implementation (2012-2022) and planning for the future. The session highlighted improved human development indicators in these zones, emphasizing reduced poverty rates and enhanced infrastructure access. Sadiki emphasized the importance of coordination and partnerships for prioritizing the New Development Model (NMD), especially focusing on employment, youth, and women's integration. Director-General Latifa Yaakoubi showcased ANDZOA's decade-long achievements, emphasizing health services, rural entrepreneurship, women's economic empowerment, and environmental preservation. The session unveiled the action plan for 2024-2026 and the guidelines for the new development strategy for oasis and argan zones by 2030, with a commitment to overcome significant challenges. Key stakeholders, including regional council presidents and ministry representatives, actively participated in this pivotal session.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests

records.title: The SRTF (The Syria Recovery Trust Fund) has announced a significant stride in its Agriculture project, delivering 500 metric tons of whe...
records.description: The SRTF (The Syria Recovery Trust Fund) has announced a significant stride in its Agriculture project, delivering 500 metric tons of wheat seeds to the Implementing Entity (IE). This particular initiative, titled "Support Farmers for the Production of Wheat Crop in North Aleppo," targets the distribution of wheat seeds to 1,000 farmers, facilitating the cultivation of 2,000 hectares of land. Each farmer will receive 500 kilograms of wheat seeds, sufficient for planting two hectares. This endeavor, combined with the provision of additional agricultural resources like fertilizers, agrochemicals, and capacity-building sessions in Farmer Field Schools, aims to rejuvenate wheat production. The ultimate goal is to elevate food security and enhance livelihoods in the Northern Aleppo regions where the project operates. Spanning a budget of EUR 2.07 million over 18 months, this project directly benefits 1,000 farmers and indirectly impacts 5,000 family members. Additionally, about 45,000 individuals per month will benefit from the availability of wheat flour used in bread production, showcasing the extensive reach and positive impact of this agricultural endeavor.

records.title: Sugar prices in the UAE have soared by as much as eight percent in recent months, stemming from a global surge due to reduced supplies fo...
records.description: Sugar prices in the UAE have soared by as much as eight percent in recent months, stemming from a global surge due to reduced supplies following droughts impacting harvests in India and Thailand, two major exporters. However, the outlook appears promising as India prepares to resume exports through the National Cooperative for Exports Ltd (NCEL). This initiative seeks to bypass intermediaries by facilitating direct dealings between the government and farmers, potentially leading to a decline in sugar prices in the UAE. Dr. Dhananjay Datar, chairman of Al Adil Trading, highlighted that the current market stock primarily originates from Brazil, signaling a potential shift once Indian sugar enters the local market. Kamal Vachani from Al Maya Group noted that besides traditional suppliers like Brazil and Thailand, the UAE can explore importing from countries like Mexico, Australia, and Africa, which have been ramping up sugar production. With potential openings in markets like Thailand and Germany, there's optimism about diversifying sugar imports and stabilizing prices in the UAE.
records.institution: Indian National Cooperative for Exports Ltd (NCEL)

records.title: Egypt is expected to witness its lowest wheat ending stocks in two decades during the 2023-24 marketing year, as reported by the Global A...
records.description: Egypt is expected to witness its lowest wheat ending stocks in two decades during the 2023-24 marketing year, as reported by the Global Agricultural Information Network from the US Department of Agriculture. The dip in stocks is attributed to decreased wheat production stemming from factors like increased demand, trade flow shifts due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and a reduction in the harvested wheat area. The area allocated for Egyptian clover and sugar beets has expanded, contributing to the decline in wheat harvest area. In response to dwindling stocks and to encourage local sales to the government, Egypt increased the wheat procurement price significantly. However, despite these measures, wheat consumption is projected to rise, reaching a near-record high of 20.6 million tonnes in 2023-24. Egypt's population is swelling and expected to hit 124 million by 2030, intensifying pressure on the wheat supply. As a result, wheat imports are estimated to surge by 7% to 12 million tonnes in the upcoming marketing year, notably from Russia, as imports from Ukraine decrease due to the ongoing conflict. Russia and the European Union have historically been primary wheat exporters to Egypt, but disruptions caused by the war are expected to impact Ukraine's wheat exports to Egypt significantly. This drop in wheat production and anticipated increase in imports pose significant challenges for Egypt, the world's largest wheat importer, as it navigates disruptions in global grain markets.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Egypt's emergence as a linchpin in European hydrogen trade marks a pivotal shift in the EU's energy focus, highlighted during President U...
records.description: Egypt's emergence as a linchpin in European hydrogen trade marks a pivotal shift in the EU's energy focus, highlighted during President Ursula von der Leyen's recent visit, where substantial investments were pledged to Egypt's clean energy sector, particularly in green hydrogen. This strategic pivot positions Egypt beyond a mere recipient of political support, aiming to foster private investments and become a catalyst for the EU's clean energy transition. This transformative partnership transcends diplomatic ties, presenting Egypt as a central figure in the EU's ambitious green hydrogen agenda, heralding a significant role in shaping the future of clean energy across the continent. Meanwhile, Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida's collaborative proposal with South Korea to establish a robust network for hydrogen and ammonia supply signals a significant transformation in bilateral relations, leveraging the strengths of both nations to drive widespread adoption of these elements across multiple sectors. This joint initiative signifies a remarkable step in reshaping global energy dynamics, emphasizing collaboration for technological innovation that surpasses national borders.

records.title: The recent visit of Saudi Commerce Minister Majid bin Abdullah Al-Qasabi to Egypt marked a significant step in strengthening economic tie...
records.description: The recent visit of Saudi Commerce Minister Majid bin Abdullah Al-Qasabi to Egypt marked a significant step in strengthening economic ties between Cairo and Riyadh. Accompanied by a delegation of 90 top-tier businessmen and leaders from prominent national firms, the visit aimed to elevate bilateral trade exchanges, capitalizing on economic reforms in both nations. Discussions centered on transforming the region into a global logistics hub, emphasizing increased economic integration within Africa. Al-Qasabi highlighted opportunities in key sectors aligned with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, advocating for joint projects and the removal of obstacles hindering progress. Meetings with Egyptian business leaders focused on legislative reforms and their impact on enhancing the economic climate. Anticipated agreements worth $1.5 billion, set to be signed during the Egyptian-Saudi Business Forum, align with Egypt's objective of attracting foreign investments, particularly from Gulf nations, across energy, real estate, agriculture, and tourism sectors. Additionally, the upcoming Gulf-Egyptian Business Forum aims to forge robust economic partnerships, bringing together officials and entrepreneurs from the Gulf Cooperation Council and African nations to explore further collaboration opportunities.

records.title: A 15th Saudi plane carrying aid for Gaza on Monday took off from King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
records.description: A 15th Saudi plane carrying aid for Gaza on Monday took off from King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The Gaza relief operation is being coordinated by the Saudi aid agency KSrelief, with Al-Arish International Airport in Egypt acting as the transit point. The latest plane was loaded with a range of essential supplies, including 31 tons of food and shelter materials.

records.title: Anticipated agreements worth $1.5 billion are poised for signing during the Egyptian-Saudi Business Forum, reflecting burgeoning economic...
records.description: Anticipated agreements worth $1.5 billion are poised for signing during the Egyptian-Saudi Business Forum, reflecting burgeoning economic ties between Saudi Arabia and Egypt. Scheduled alongside Saudi Commerce Minister Majid bin Abdullah Al-Qasabi's visit to Cairo on November 20, the event aims to fortify trade and investment channels between the two nations. Turki Al-Hokair, a member of the Egyptian-Saudi Business Council, highlighted the concentrated investment focus across various sectors like energy, real estate, agriculture, and tourism, aligning with Egypt's strategy to attract foreign investments, particularly from Gulf countries. Additionally, the impending first Gulf-Egyptian Business Forum, set for November 22-23 in Cairo and organized by the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce, seeks to foster robust economic partnerships among involved parties, drawing participation from GCC nations and African countries. The depth of historical relations between Saudi Arabia and Egypt, coupled with mutual economic strengths, underpins the endeavor to amplify investment opportunities. These efforts coincide with growing trade volumes, surpassing $30 billion in 2022, and a considerable influx of Gulf investments exceeding $62 billion into Egypt, propelled by the nation's economic reforms and improved investment climate.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Jordan's olive oil production faces a dire situation due to climate change, impacting farmers like Hasan Smadi, who experienced a signifi...
records.description: Jordan's olive oil production faces a dire situation due to climate change, impacting farmers like Hasan Smadi, who experienced a significant reduction in olive oil yield due to altered weather patterns and prolonged heatwaves. The National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC) is exploring adaptive measures, focusing on cultivating climate-resilient olive varieties like Mehras known for drought resistance and higher oil yield. Additionally, sustainable farming practices, such as supplementary irrigation and the use of potash fertilizers to mitigate water stress in olive trees during heatwaves, are being recommended. Digital climate modeling is predicting changes in cultivation patterns, signaling the need for farmers to consider crops requiring less water. However, concerns loom over a projected decline in olive yields by 2050, posing a threat to Jordan's olive oil self-sufficiency, necessitating urgent adaptation strategies and the development of resilient crop varieties to combat climate change's adverse effects on the olive sector.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The inaugural International Forum and Exhibition for Sustainable Agriculture in Riyadh gathered over 55 speakers from 35 nations, conveni...
records.description: The inaugural International Forum and Exhibition for Sustainable Agriculture in Riyadh gathered over 55 speakers from 35 nations, convening experts and researchers to facilitate knowledge exchange and cultivate networks within the field. Hosted by the National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture and inaugurated by Minister Abdulrahman Al-Fadhley of the Kingdom’s Environment, Water, and Agriculture Ministry, the three-day event aimed to foster innovation and closer professional ties. The agenda focused on leveraging natural resources in agricultural production, featuring discussions led by experts like Naser Eddin Al-Obaid on sustainable water use, soil enhancement techniques, and the utilization of wild plant species for increased productivity. Subsequent days delved into the realm of digital agriculture, with sessions led by David Muath and Abdulaziz Al-Malik, addressing smart agriculture and environmental aspects. The forum also highlighted marketing strategies and sustainable food value chains, supported by an exhibition showcasing cutting-edge products and innovations from over 35 companies and organizations dedicated to sustainable agriculture.
records.institution: Saudi National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture

records.title: The Libyan Ministry of Agriculture and the World Food Program (WFP) solidified their collaboration by signing a memorandum of understandi...
records.description: The Libyan Ministry of Agriculture and the World Food Program (WFP) solidified their collaboration by signing a memorandum of understanding aimed at bolstering resilience and adaptation within national food systems. During a meeting between Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Hussein Al-Qatrani, and WFP's representative in Libya, Maysaa Al-Gharbawi, the agreement was formalized, intending to uplift areas with limited income, elevate citizen living standards, and provide necessary agricultural resources to farmers and breeders in those regions. The Ministry highlighted the agreement's focus on addressing challenges faced by farmers, fostering self-sufficiency, sustainable development, and food security while adapting to climate change. Al-Qatrani emphasized the significance of fostering collaboration with specialized international organizations in the food systems domain, underscoring the importance of this agreement.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Marine Resources

records.title: ALPLA Group’s acquisition of a majority stake in Atlantic Packaging alongside the formation of ALPLA Morocco through a joint venture mark...
records.description: ALPLA Group’s acquisition of a majority stake in Atlantic Packaging alongside the formation of ALPLA Morocco through a joint venture marks a strategic move in their packaging industry expansion. With a focus on PET preform production, plastic pallet manufacturing, and packaging film extrusion, ALPLA aims to capitalize on the Maghreb and Western African markets. Their Tangier facility, host to cutting-edge manufacturing, has experienced significant growth, almost tripling preform output and expanding capacity from 100 to approximately 300 million units yearly. Christian Fessler, ALPLA Middle East and North Africa managing director, underlined their collaborative intent with Diana Holding to explore new market segments and provide expertise in the regional plastic packaging industry. This strategic venture echoes ALPLA's broader strategy in North Africa, indicating a commitment to delivering sustainable and cost-effective packaging solutions to the region while eyeing further expansion with plans to increase operational space by approximately 20,000m² in the near future. Moreover, ALPLA’s recent investment in a PET recycling plant in Ballito, South Africa, underscores their thrust into African recycling markets, aiming for substantial annual recycling capacities, positioning them at the forefront of sustainable packaging solutions.

records.title: At the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference, a pivotal Saudi-African Summit convened to fortify economic and trade connections between...
records.description: At the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference, a pivotal Saudi-African Summit convened to fortify economic and trade connections between Saudi Arabia and Africa. Both regions share parallel economic sectors, offering vast opportunities across mining, industry, tourism, finance, and more, with a combined economy of $4 trillion. Positioned at the crossroads of three continents, Saudi Arabia has the potential to emerge as a vital economic hub for Africa. Africa, as the second-largest continent globally, boasts a $3 trillion economy and houses five of the world's fastest-growing economies. With the Saudi economy ranking as the largest in the MENA region, valued at over $1 trillion and experiencing rapid growth, bilateral trade between Saudi Arabia and African countries has exceeded SR74 billion in 2003, favoring Saudi Arabia in terms of trade balance. Non-oil exports from Saudi Arabia to Africa have shown substantial growth, reaching SR31.94 billion last year, and Saudi investments in Africa over the past decade have reached SR49.5 billion, with 47 Saudi companies presently operating in the continent. The recent conference witnessed the signing of over 50 agreements and MoUs, spanning various sectors like tourism, investment, finance, energy, mining, agriculture, and more, reflecting a shared commitment to mutual development aligned with Saudi Vision 2030 and Africa’s Agenda 2063. This deeper economic and trade collaboration is anticipated to yield mutual benefits for both regions and their respective developmental frameworks.

records.title: The collaboration between a UAE-based virtual assets consultancy, PXDX, and a Pakistani software house intends to introduce healthcare se...
records.description: The collaboration between a UAE-based virtual assets consultancy, PXDX, and a Pakistani software house intends to introduce healthcare services into the Saudi market, initially targeting the healthcare sector before expanding into other domains. The founding CEO of PXDX, Dr. Rehan Al Taji, highlighted their collaboration during The Future Summit in Karachi, emphasizing the importation of services from the Pakistani software house into Saudi Arabia. While specific details were not disclosed, Dr. Al Taji expressed admiration for Pakistani startups, acknowledging their innovation and potential in expanding business under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. This initiative aims to diversify the Saudi economy and enhance sectors like health, education, infrastructure, recreation, and tourism. Additionally, Dana Al Salem, a Kuwaiti tech entrepreneur, stressed the importance of countries projecting a clear purpose to attract investors, citing the significance of Pakistan refining its global image and focusing on leveraging its agricultural sector to address food scarcity concerns.

records.title: Egyptian East Delta Flour Mills (EDFM) has reported a significant 17% year-on-year surge in net profits after tax for the first quarter o...
records.description: Egyptian East Delta Flour Mills (EDFM) has reported a significant 17% year-on-year surge in net profits after tax for the first quarter of fiscal year 2023/2024, reaching EGP 33.852 million (US$1.1 million) as stated in the financial report filed with the Egyptian Exchange. Situated in Zagazig, Egypt, EDFM operates within various sectors, manufacturing, processing, and distributing a range of grains and food products. The company's portfolio encompasses bread, baked goods, pasta, fodder, and real estate investments. This increase in profits follows a positive trend among Egyptian flour milling companies, reflecting growth despite challenges in the global grain sector. Moreover, Middle Egypt Flour Mills Company (CEFM), another EGX-listed entity, saw a 4.96% year-on-year rise in net profit after tax for the same quarter, reaching EGP 28.801 million (US$931,298). CEFM specializes in the manufacturing, trade, import, export, and distribution of grains and related products. The company's revenue also experienced growth, climbing by 7.03% year-on-year to EGP 143.341 million in the three-month period ending September 31. These positive financial outcomes signify a resilient performance for Egyptian flour milling entities despite broader market challenges.

records.title: African Development Bank approves Desert to Power RIMDIR Mini Grid Electrification Project in Mauritania
records.description: The African Development Bank Group approved a EUR 14.42 million contribution toward the RIMDIR Mini Grid Electrification Project in Mauritania, as part of the Desert to Power Initiative. This grant from the Bank’s Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa (SEFA) aims to electrify 40 local communities by establishing seven mini-grids in the South East region of Mauritania. The project also allocates funds for income-generating activities. Through collaboration with the Société Mauritanienne d'Electricité (SOMELEC), this initiative intends to lower electricity production costs, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and bolster the resilience of agro-pastoral communities. The project aligns with Mauritania's policy of universal electricity access by 2030 and supports economic growth, particularly in rural areas, while demonstrating the African Development Bank's commitment to fostering private sector engagement in rural electrification. The Desert to Power Initiative aims to provide electricity to 250 million people in the Sahel region through renewable energy by 2030.

records.title: Paris-based agribusiness giant InVivo is set to establish a marketing office in Saudi Arabia's port of Dammam early next year, strategica...
records.description: Paris-based agribusiness giant InVivo is set to establish a marketing office in Saudi Arabia's port of Dammam early next year, strategically positioning itself to capitalize on evolving global grain demand, particularly in the Middle East. In an interview with Reuters, InVivo CEO Thierry Blandinieres underscored the office's pivotal role in securing grain supplies for local feed makers in Saudi Arabia amid shifting dynamics in the grain market. Traditional markets like Algeria have seen a decline in French wheat exports, yet Blandinieres remains optimistic, highlighting potential sales growth in China and renewed interest from Egypt. While emphasizing the fluctuating nature of market demand, particularly in China, InVivo is actively exploring alternative markets and eyeing expansion into West African territories. Aman Sethi, leading the Saudi office from Dubai, brings extensive experience, emphasizing InVivo’s focus not just on the Middle East but also on securing West African markets. Moreover, InVivo’s recent acquisition of Australia’s United Malt Group strengthens its position as the world's largest maltster, marking a significant milestone in its strategic growth trajectory. This expansion illustrates InVivo's commitment to a diversified global presence and its proactive stance in responding to evolving market dynamics.

records.title: Oman Investment Authority completed six major projects valued at $10.3 billion, aiming to diversify the economy, foster regional growth,...
records.description: Oman Investment Authority completed six major projects valued at $10.3 billion, aiming to diversify the economy, foster regional growth, attract investments, and create job opportunities, particularly for SMEs. The Duqm Refinery and Petrochemical Industries project, the most significant endeavor, is set to transform Duqm into a key industrial hub with a 230,000-barrel-per-day refinery and storage facilities. Other projects include the Ras Markaz Crude Oil Storage Terminal, Duqm Integrated Power and Water Project, Rabt project for electricity transmission, Khuweimah Shrimp Farm for food security, and JW Marriott Hotel Muscat to boost tourism. Additionally, Oman launched three digital platforms to enhance its investment climate and facilitate business processes, signaling a push towards modernizing the economy and fostering a more efficient business environment.

records.title: Saudi aid agency KSrelief extended assistance to Afghan quake victims by distributing 1,000 food packages in Zinda Jan District, benefitt...
records.description: Saudi aid agency KSrelief extended assistance to Afghan quake victims by distributing 1,000 food packages in Zinda Jan District, benefitting 375 families and 6,000 individuals. This aid followed the recent provision of 550 winter bags to 3,850 individuals in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province. The relief efforts align with KSrelief's global humanitarian assistance program. Additionally, discussions between KSrelief and the EU's special representative for the Horn of Africa focused on supporting humanitarian efforts in the east African peninsula region.

records.title: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa convened to bolster their countries' bilateral ties,...
records.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa convened to bolster their countries' bilateral ties, emphasizing a shared interest in enhancing development cooperation. Their discussions centered on strengthening collaboration in agriculture, emphasizing agro-manufacturing initiatives, optimizing livestock and fisheries, and ensuring food security for both nations. Additionally, they explored opportunities for joint development in diverse infrastructure sectors. President Mnangagwa's visit to Egypt, during which he attended the third Intra-African Trade Fair (IATF), allowed him to witness Egypt's notable development progress, prompting Zimbabwe's interest in benefiting from Egypt's experiences. The leaders underscored the importance of collective African action, particularly amid global challenges, highlighting the significance of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) in advancing comprehensive continental development. In a separate meeting, President Al-Sisi discussed Egypt's efforts to maintain adequate reserves of essential goods despite international crises and directed the completion of national strategic warehouses and silos to secure year-round stocks of basic commodities. He also pledged additional food supplies totaling 650 tonnes to support the Palestinian people in Gaza, underscoring Egypt's continual commitment to aiding Gaza's residents.

records.title: Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani inaugurated Iraq's most extensive private poultry venture situated in Karbala.
records.description: Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani inaugurated Iraq's most extensive private poultry venture situated in Karbala. The project boasts an annual output capacity surpassing 3 billion eggs and 340,000 tons of meat, strategically aiming to fulfill domestic market needs. Al-Sudani highlighted the project's pivotal role in fostering self-sufficiency, elevating agricultural sectors, and enhancing animal husbandry practices in the region during the inauguration ceremony.

records.title: The Biden administration extended a sanctions waiver for Iraq, allowing it to continue purchasing electricity from Iran and enabling limi...
records.description: The Biden administration extended a sanctions waiver for Iraq, allowing it to continue purchasing electricity from Iran and enabling limited access to funds for buying humanitarian goods. Secretary of State Antony Blinken signed the 120-day extension, drawing criticism from Iran hawks concerned about Iran's support for destabilizing proxy groups. Approximately $10 billion in Iraqi payments for Iranian electricity sits in escrow accounts, and the waiver permits Iraq to maintain energy imports without facing US penalties. The extension includes provisions allowing portions of the proceeds to be transferred to Oman for conversion to non-sanctioned currencies for Iran's essential purchases, monitored under strict guidelines to ensure funds are solely used for approved items like food, medicine, and medical equipment.

records.title: PepsiCo, a global food and beverage giant, has unveiled plans to invest over 200 million Saudi Riyals (US$53.3 million) in expanding its...
records.description: PepsiCo, a global food and beverage giant, has unveiled plans to invest over 200 million Saudi Riyals (US$53.3 million) in expanding its snack facility at the Dammam plant in Saudi Arabia. The initiative, shared during the Future Investment Initiative conference in Riyadh, aligns with PepsiCo's commitment to sustainable agricultural practices in Saudi Arabia and supports the Kingdom's food production goals outlined in Vision 2030. This investment aims to bolster the plant's production capacity, marking a significant step toward enhancing the Saudi agricultural sector and fostering sustainable food production. The expansion is set to be completed by next year and represents PepsiCo's ongoing efforts to reinforce its presence in the region, where it manufactures brands like Lay’s, Doritos, Quaker Oats, and the local crisp brand Tasali. This substantial investment highlights PepsiCo's dedication to promoting sustainable agriculture and strengthening its foothold in the food and beverage industry, reinforcing its commitment to sustainable practices in Saudi Arabia.

records.title: Expo City Dubai is unveiling the Expo City Farm, a groundbreaking addition offering a glimpse into desert farming methods for fruits and...
records.description: Expo City Dubai is unveiling the Expo City Farm, a groundbreaking addition offering a glimpse into desert farming methods for fruits and vegetables, just in time for COP28. This innovative farm, situated within Expo City Dubai, is set to become a permanent fixture, showcasing resilient crops that thrive in arid conditions. During COP28, the farm will host workshops, cooking classes led by sustainability-focused chefs, and other community engagements, inviting the public to participate freely. As part of the broader climate summit, Expo City Dubai's initiative encourages residents and visitors to actively pledge their commitment to the planet's well-being, creating an inclusive space for dialogue and action around climate change within the Green Zone of COP28. This zone aims to engage the public, fostering discussions, artistic displays, and educational sessions to promote climate awareness and proactive measures for a sustainable future.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and Slovakia recently inked an agreement aiming to prevent double taxation, a move aligning with Saudi Arabia's aspirations...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and Slovakia recently inked an agreement aiming to prevent double taxation, a move aligning with Saudi Arabia's aspirations to establish itself as a prominent global business center. The accord, signed by Saudi Minister of Economy and Planning Faisal bin Fadhil Al-Ibrahim during his visit to Slovakia, focuses on offering tax benefits and exemptions for government investments. It also emphasizes fostering fairness, equal opportunities for investors, and enhancing economic collaboration between the two nations. This aligns with Saudi Arabia's recent achievements in attracting more than 180 regional headquarters of global companies, surpassing the earlier target of 160 firms for this year. Minister Al-Falih highlighted the accelerating rate of licensing companies in Saudi Arabia, providing them with favorable incentives. Additionally, Minister Al-Ibrahim's meeting with North Macedonia's Economy Minister Kershnik Bekteshi centered on discussions about expanding economic cooperation, exploring potential opportunities in various sectors like agriculture, energy, and infrastructure.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Economy and Planning

records.title: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning in Oman, utilizing the Tatweer platform, has opened investment prospects within the wilayats o...
records.description: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning in Oman, utilizing the Tatweer platform, has opened investment prospects within the wilayats of Sinaw and Al Mudhaibi in North Al Sharqiyah Governorate, focusing on fish projects. These opportunities aim to bolster citizen and resident services while incentivizing private sector engagement in pivotal services supporting the fishery sector. By proposing diverse investment avenues in these wilayats, the Ministry intends to augment production across fishery-related activities, ultimately aiding in local and regional market supplies, fortifying food security, and generating added value within Oman's fisheries sector. This initiative is part of a larger endeavor wherein the Ministry has announced a total of 40 investment opportunities in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, spanning various governorates in Oman.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning

records.title: KSrelief collaborated with the UN Development Programme to initiate a substantial food assistance project in Yemen, targeting the most vu...
records.description: KSrelief collaborated with the UN Development Programme to initiate a substantial food assistance project in Yemen, targeting the most vulnerable families. The joint effort aims to distribute 119,394 food parcels to approximately 170,487 individuals across Aden, Abyan, Lahj, Dhale’a, and Taiz provinces. Yemen's Deputy Minister of Social Affairs emphasized Saudi Arabia's pivotal role in supporting Yemenis, highlighting the project's significance in easing the plight of affected families during challenging times. Suhaib Joban, assistant director of the project, highlighted the swift implementation achieved through coordinated efforts with partners.

records.title: During a recent official visit to North Macedonia, Saudi Minister of Economy and Planning Faisal bin Fadel Al-Ibrahim engaged in discussi...
records.description: During a recent official visit to North Macedonia, Saudi Minister of Economy and Planning Faisal bin Fadel Al-Ibrahim engaged in discussions with Kershnik Bekteshi, the country's Minister of Economy, focusing on enhancing economic ties and exploring potential collaborations. The talks revolved around various sectors such as agriculture, energy, and infrastructure, emphasizing the mutual benefit of boosting commerce and investment opportunities between the two nations. Al-Ibrahim also held a separate meeting with Bujar Osmani, North Macedonia's Minister of Foreign Affairs, to further deliberate on expanding economic relations through bilateral agreements. Ambassador Faisal bin Ghazi Hefzy, serving as the Kingdom's ambassador to Albania and non-resident ambassador to North Macedonia, was also present during these pivotal discussions, underscoring Saudi Arabia's commitment to strengthening ties with North Macedonia.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Economy and Planning

records.title: Saudi Arabia has intensified its economic collaboration with Africa, evident through a sequence of roundtable discussions hosted by the M...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has intensified its economic collaboration with Africa, evident through a sequence of roundtable discussions hosted by the Ministry of Investment, marking an upsurge in trade relations. Minister of Investment Khalid Al-Falih and Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadhli engaged in talks with heads of state from Chad, Somalia, and Nigeria on the sidelines of the inaugural Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh. These discussions, inclusive of representatives from both public and private sectors, focused on fortifying investment relations, fostering economic ties, and augmenting bilateral trade. Emphasis was laid on devising strategies to encourage quality investments and ensuring the private sector benefits from the abundant business opportunities in both regions. During the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference, Al-Falih emphasized Africa's immense economic potential and the need to mitigate investment risks to attract more investors. Highlighting the historical ties and shared cultural bonds, Al-Falih emphasized Saudi Arabia's commitment to Africa, a sentiment echoed by Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, who highlighted the Kingdom's robust partnership with African nations, particularly in energy, education, and agriculture. The forum witnessed several agreements and memorandums of understanding being signed, including plans for the establishment of the Saudi-Ivorian Business Council, aiming to bolster trade and investment between Saudi Arabia and the Ivory Coast by fostering collaborative commercial activities and joint ventures. These engagements underscore Saudi Arabia's continuous endeavors to foster growth and reinforce its commercial ties across the African continent.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is poised to bolster its fresh commodities production and distribution with a groundbreaking joint venture between the Natio...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is poised to bolster its fresh commodities production and distribution with a groundbreaking joint venture between the National Agricultural Development Co. (NADEC) and Del Monte Saudi Arabia Factory Co. Ltd. This collaboration, emphasized in a memorandum of understanding, targets specific goods such as fruits, vegetables, fresh juices, and potato processing, intending to distribute these products extensively across Saudi Arabia. Per the terms, NADEC will hold a 37.5 percent stake in the new company's capital. The venture aims to establish manufacturing facilities for a range of products, including canned fruits and vegetables, frozen fruits, and various processed items, diversifying the available product line in the Saudi market. Abdul Qader Al Muhaidib and Sons Co. is also part of this venture. This strategic initiative falls in line with NADEC's commitment to contributing to Saudi Vision 2030's food security goals. Moreover, this collaboration aligns with NADEC's recent entry into the red meat market in collaboration with Minerva Foods, further enhancing its presence and distribution network within the Kingdom. The partnership with Minerva Foods seeks to meet the escalating demand for high-quality meat products in Saudi Arabia, strengthening the companies' position and offering closer proximity to end customers.
records.institution: The National Agricultural Development Co. (Nadec) & Del Monte Saudi Arabia Factory Co. Ltd

records.title: Tabuk Region Leads the Way in Organic Farming
records.description: In Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, farmers are embracing organic crop cultivation to meet the demand for safer, healthier food choices. Twelve farms in the region have transitioned to organic methods, using natural fertilizers and steering clear of synthetic inputs like chemical fertilizers and pesticides. This shift responds to consumers seeking high-health-value food products, prompting increased supply and promotion of organic foods. Tabuk, known for agriculture, is transforming into a sustainable farming model through collaboration between government bodies and local farmers. Similar transitions to organic farming are occurring in other provinces as part of Saudi Arabia's focus on sustainable agriculture, aligning with Vision 2030 goals. Additionally, the country's emphasis on water-saving methods and technology showcases efforts toward responsible water management practices in farming.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) concluded a crucial project by distributing 4,000 shelter kits to those severel...
records.description: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) concluded a crucial project by distributing 4,000 shelter kits to those severely affected by recent floods in Punjab, Pakistan. The initiative targeted the most impacted districts including Kasur, Vehari, Layyah, and Rajanpur, providing essential items like shelters, solar panels, kitchen sets, mats, and blankets to over 28,000 individuals. This emergency relief effort forms part of KSrelief's broader Shelter NFIs project for 2023-2024, reinforcing their significant humanitarian work in Pakistan. Over the years, KSrelief has executed 170 projects in Pakistan, focusing on education, healthcare, water, sanitation, hygiene, and community support, investing approximately $163 million since its inception in 2015.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's engagement with Africa soared with the signing of agreements totaling SR2 billion ($533 million) during the Saudi-Arab-Afr...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's engagement with Africa soared with the signing of agreements totaling SR2 billion ($533 million) during the Saudi-Arab-African Economic Conference in Riyadh, amplifying the Kingdom's alliance with the continent. The deals, covering energy, roads, and health, will be facilitated through the Saudi Fund for Development and included various memorandums of understanding. Among the significant milestones, Saudi Arabia lifted a ban on red meat imports from South Africa. Minister of Investment Khalid Al-Falih hinted at potential game-changing announcements from the Public Investment Fund (PIF) focused on investments in Africa's critical minerals. Describing the current $75 billion Saudi investment in Africa as the tip of the iceberg, Al-Falih underscored the abundant prospects for further trade and economic bolstering. The conference aimed to fortify Saudi Arabia's ties with Africa across various sectors, including finance, trade, and government, emphasizing partnerships and discussions on the establishment of additional trade agreements. Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan highlighted the burgeoning partnership with African countries, particularly in energy, education, and agriculture, positioning Africa as a robust investment destination for the Kingdom. The conference witnessed numerous cooperation agreements and developmental loan agreements aimed at fostering infrastructure development, education, and healthcare in several African nations. This event marked an influential step towards nurturing sustainable partnerships, enhancing trade, and fostering economic development between Saudi Arabia and Africa.

records.title: The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture, Ithra, delved into the forefront of digital library systems during the Sharjah International...
records.description: The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture, Ithra, delved into the forefront of digital library systems during the Sharjah International Library Conference. This cultural session, titled “The Library as a Sustainable and Creative Source, the Ithra Library as a Model,” highlighted Ithra's evolution into a competitive global library in design and technology integration over five years. The session outlined the library's extensive programs and its expansion beyond Saudi Arabia, reaching multiple international cities. Innovations like radio frequency identification technology for book borrowing, interactive screens aiding book searches, and sustainable practices in waste management were showcased. Additionally, the discussion emphasized the role of libraries in nurturing creativity and intellectual growth, spotlighting Ithra's initiatives such as the iRead Reading program, book exchange programs, tree-planting rewards for reading, and cultural discussions fostering literary engagement among Arab nations.
records.institution: The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)

records.title: Tunisia is set to import 385,000 tonnes of soft wheat from France, marking a 54% increase from the previous year's 250,000-ton shipment.
records.description: Tunisia is set to import 385,000 tonnes of soft wheat from France, marking a 54% increase from the previous year's 250,000-ton shipment. Facing a five-year drought affecting its productivity, Tunisia aims to import a total of 2.2 million tonnes of wheat to meet its yearly consumption of around 3 million tonnes. To counter this dependency, the Ministry of Agriculture plans to expand cereal cultivation to 1.2 million hectares by 2035, with a specific focus on wheat—targeting 500,000 hectares for durum wheat and 100,000 hectares for soft wheat. To support this initiative, the country’s Cereals Office has invested 13 million dinars in expanding cereal storage capacity in Bizerte from 13,000 to 30,000 tonnes. This move aligns with France's broader strategy to export 9.5 million tonnes of soft wheat outside the EU by the end of the 2023/2024 campaign, with plans to ship 4.3 million tonnes to Algeria and Morocco as well.
records.institution: Tunisian Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: Regenerative Agriculture Venture Programme Launched to Enable Climate-Resilient Agriculture in MENAT
records.description: Goumbook, in collaboration with HSBC Bank Middle East Limited and SAB (Saudi Awwal Bank), has launched the Regenerative Agriculture Venture Programme to address critical agricultural challenges in the MENAT region. This pioneering initiative aims to empower researchers and students to develop innovative solutions focused on sustainability, climate change, and food security. By encouraging resilient crop varieties and sustainable farming practices, the program seeks to combat issues such as hunger, declining topsoil quality, and water scarcity prevalent in the region. With a strong emphasis on research-driven solutions and entrepreneurship, the program aims to bridge the gap between academia and practical application, fostering a regenerative agriculture movement that responds to climate change challenges and promotes resilience in the MENAT region's harsh farming conditions.

records.title: Saudi agencies have launched an impactful series of solar-powered housing projects in three Yemeni governorates, marking a milestone in t...
records.description: Saudi agencies have launched an impactful series of solar-powered housing projects in three Yemeni governorates, marking a milestone in the "Using Renewable Energy to Improve the Quality of Life in Yemen" initiative. The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY), along with the Arab Gulf Programme for Development (AGFUND) and the Sela Foundation for Development, inaugurated 133 housing lighting systems and 20 public utilities run by solar energy in Hadhramaut, Taiz, and Hodeidah. These initiatives cater to various needs, providing electricity for health and educational facilities, powering medical equipment, and enhancing learning environments. Additionally, the project encompasses the restoration of drinking water wells, installation of agricultural irrigation systems using solar energy, and the provision of renewable energy to homes and facilities across five governorates, ultimately benefitting over 62,000 Yemenis. Furthermore, it includes training sessions for engineers focused on utilizing solar energy systems, demonstrating a holistic approach to alleviating challenges like water scarcity.
records.institution: The Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY) & the Arab Gulf Programme for Development (AGFUND), & the Sela Foundation for Development

records.title: Amidst a scarcity of US dollars and consequential economic challenges in Egypt and Kenya, a creative proposal has emerged: a barter trade...
records.description: Amidst a scarcity of US dollars and consequential economic challenges in Egypt and Kenya, a creative proposal has emerged: a barter trade system between the two nations specifically for tea. Egypt’s Ambassador, Wael Nasr El-Den, pitched this innovative solution to sustain the tea trade. Under this setup, Egypt would procure Kenyan tea while allowing Kenya the liberty to choose goods for import from Egypt. Egypt, grappling with a dearth of US dollar reserves necessary for vital imports and to meet bond maturation, aims to reduce its dollar dependency through this arrangement. Egypt's efforts to address the shortage include presenting investment opportunities in state-owned firms, revealing strategies to attract significant inflows, and combating global price hikes in beverages that have influenced tea prices. Both Egypt and Pakistan, major purchasers of Kenyan tea, have observed declines in tea exports, sparking the potential adoption of this barter system to relieve pressure on dollar reserves. Simultaneously, Kenya is focusing on elevating tea earnings by investing in specialty tea processing units and establishing an incubation hub for specialty tea, a move set to diversify tea products, enhance earnings for farmers, and generate employment opportunities.

records.title: Iraq's Ministry of Finance has initiated compensation payments totaling more than 175 billion dinars to the Ministry of Agriculture, addr...
records.description: Iraq's Ministry of Finance has initiated compensation payments totaling more than 175 billion dinars to the Ministry of Agriculture, addressing damages incurred due to floods and rains across several provinces. The allocated compensations for various provinces include Basra with 32.69 billion dinars, Maysan with 7.91 billion dinars, Wasit with 12.41 billion dinars, and Muthanna with 122.87 billion dinars. These disbursements, aligned with Cabinet Decision No. 294 of 2022, are set to continue upon the submission of compensation reports from other affected provinces. The Ministry of Agriculture has furnished detailed tables specifying the affected individuals, damage types, and corresponding compensation amounts, all sanctioned by the ministerial committee overseeing these compensations.

records.title: The Saudi aid agency, KSrelief, initiated a volunteer-based program, the Saudi Noor program, in Boulemane Province, Morocco, aimed at com...
records.description: The Saudi aid agency, KSrelief, initiated a volunteer-based program, the Saudi Noor program, in Boulemane Province, Morocco, aimed at combating blindness and associated ailments. Collaborating with the Al-Basar International Foundation, the initiative has provided eye examinations to 1,345 individuals, performed 82 surgeries, and distributed 345 eyeglasses. This effort forms part of KSrelief's broader medical program targeting blindness globally. Additionally, KSrelief has conducted medical projects in Yemen, Pakistan, and Lebanon, showcasing a diverse range of humanitarian efforts worldwide. Since 2015, KSrelief has executed over 2,500 projects, totaling more than $6.4 billion across 94 countries, focusing on various sectors including food security, health, shelter, education, and more.

records.title: Over the past two years, Saudi Arabia's Jazan region has attracted an impressive SR1 billion ($266 million) in investments, marking a sig...
records.description: Over the past two years, Saudi Arabia's Jazan region has attracted an impressive SR1 billion ($266 million) in investments, marking a significant surge for this commercial hub. This amount represents a substantial 40 percent of the region's total investments amassed over the last two decades. Jazan's appeal stems from its expansive coastline, favorable for maritime and oil industries, coupled with its strategic pivot to evolve into a special economic zone tailored for the logistics sector. Hosting the Kingdom's third-largest ports and housing one of the world's largest refining stations, the region's development of robust infrastructure has been pivotal in luring investments. Reports suggest that Jazan's economic zone anticipates drawing SR11 billion in foreign investments by 2040, leveraging unused mining reserves valued at over $1.3 trillion, positioning itself as a significant mining industry player. With these reserves, the region is poised to contribute significantly to Saudi Arabia's national industry, generating an estimated 17,000 direct jobs by 2040. Situated along the Red Sea coast, the region's Special Economic Zone (SEZ) serves as an advanced industrial city, fostering favorable conditions for business growth, proximity to a major export port with a substantial capacity, access to abundant natural resources for the agricultural sector, and its strategic position as a gateway to Europe and Africa. This promising landscape positions Jazan as a cornerstone for Saudi-Chinese investments, projecting a potential contribution of SR39 billion to the country's gross domestic product.

records.title: Agthia Group, a prominent UAE-based food and beverage company situated in Abu Dhabi, disclosed a remarkable 10.9% revenue surge to Dh3.27...
records.description: Agthia Group, a prominent UAE-based food and beverage company situated in Abu Dhabi, disclosed a remarkable 10.9% revenue surge to Dh3.27 billion (US$882.9 million) for the first nine months of 2023, despite facing challenges in Egypt due to currency devaluation. Operating in consumer and agribusiness sectors, which encompass Grand Mills flour and Agrivita animal feed products, Agthia features a diverse product portfolio spanning flour and animal feed, water and beverages, processed fruits and vegetables, and dairy and frozen baked goods. The group's net revenue hike of 10.9% was propelled by growth in volume (9.1%) and pricing (1.8%) across segments like Snacking, Agribusiness, and Water and food, offsetting difficulties such as currency devaluation in Egypt, increased localization in Saudi Protein, and heightened competition in Jordan. Chairman Khalifa Sultan Al Suwaidi emphasized Agthia's strategic progress and vision to establish itself as a leading F&B company in the MENA region and beyond. The group's net profit climbed by 12.7% to AED 205.6 million (US$55.5 million), reflecting expanded EBITDA margins and substantial debt repayments totaling AED 928 million (US$250.5 million) in 2023. The acquisition of a majority stake in Egyptian coffee maker Auf Group aligns with Agthia's strategy to expand in MENAP, catering to fast-growing consumer markets and underlining the company's commitment to growth and operational enhancement.
