records.title: The National Company for Agricultural Services, "AgriServ," is preparing to participate in the upcoming Saudi Agriculture exhibition sche...
records.description: The National Company for Agricultural Services, "AgriServ," is preparing to participate in the upcoming Saudi Agriculture exhibition scheduled to be held at the Riyadh International Convention and Exhibition Center from October 23 to 26, under the auspices of the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. AgriServ's exhibition booth will feature an introductory presentation on the company, highlighting its objectives concerning plant, animal, and fishery resources, as well as its vital role in supporting the agricultural sector. Additionally, the exhibition will include a workshop designed to demonstrate the company's services and educate attendees about its role, including import and export, licensing, permitting, registration of agricultural production inputs, and veterinary services. Eng. Omar bin Mohammed Al-Suhaibani, AgriServ's CEO, emphasized the company's mission to enhance service efficiency, customer satisfaction, and modern agricultural practices to support the private sector and achieve institutional excellence.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Elsayed Elkosayer, has reported that in the past year, Egypt released over 8 millio...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Elsayed Elkosayer, has reported that in the past year, Egypt released over 8 million tonnes of animal feed from its ports, valued at $3.9 billion. This move is part of the government's initiatives to support the livestock sector and ensure food security. The release of feed was carried out in coordination with the Central Bank of Egypt and under the guidance of Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly. Elkosayer noted that between September 22 and October 12, 2023, the ministry released 319,000 tonnes of corn and soybeans, along with feed additives, valued at $170 million. These corn and soybeans are crucial for the production of poultry and dairy products, both of which are in high demand in the local market. The ministry aims to provide adequate and affordable feed for farmers and producers, emphasizing the importance of supporting the agricultural sector.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: In response to escalating food prices and ongoing inflation, Egypt's Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has purchased 250,000 tons of...
records.description: In response to escalating food prices and ongoing inflation, Egypt's Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has purchased 250,000 tons of rice to support the country's strategic rice reserves over a six-month period. This acquisition aims to stabilize the market by providing rice at competitive prices. Despite a slight decrease in annual headline inflation to 38% in September, down from 39.7% in August, it remains significantly higher than the 15% recorded in September 2022. The purchase aligns with President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi's directives to bolster strategic reserves of essential commodities and is part of Egypt's broader efforts to enhance the supply of basic goods, control rising prices, and improve people's purchasing power. Additionally, the Egyptian government has recently announced an ambitious plan to reduce prices of various food commodities by 15% to 25% for six months, providing relief to consumers and streamlining customs procedures to alleviate economic pressures.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has reported the remarkable success of its "Fodder Market" platform, a pione...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has reported the remarkable success of its "Fodder Market" platform, a pioneering and record-breaking initiative in the Middle East for both trade volume and value. Launched in collaboration with the Abu Dhabi Government Services Platform "TAMM" to support livestock breeders, the platform facilitated sales of approximately 294.2 million tonnes of fodder, totaling around 477.5 million dirhams. Notably, 412.6 million dirhams were transacted through the platform's electronic wallet, and an additional 64.9 million dirhams through credit card payments by livestock breeders. Since its launch in June, the platform has seen over 771,546 visitors, issued approximately 168.2 thousand purchase invoices, and uploaded around 209 thousand invoices. Supported by HH Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, this initiative serves as a significant step towards promoting safe and sustainable solutions for the local fodder trade, benefiting both livestock breeders and fodder companies in the UAE. With the capacity to serve over 40,000 breeders and more than 5 million livestock, it not only fulfills feed demands but also drives growth in the feed trade and encourages fair competition among suppliers. The platform is integrated with physical markets located near livestock farms (Ezbah), with plans to establish more such markets to expand the reach of companies specializing in feed sales and marketing.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) is set to purchase 480,000 metric tons of Russian wheat in a private deal with Ru...
records.description: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) is set to purchase 480,000 metric tons of Russian wheat in a private deal with Russia's United Grain Company (OZK), comprising eight wheat shipments in November and December. Egypt is a significant wheat importer, and Russia is a top global exporter. The purchase, estimated at around $265 per ton FOB with payment in 270-day letters of credit, raises questions about Russia's unofficial price floor aimed at domestic price control. Following disruptions in global wheat markets caused by Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Egypt has shifted toward direct purchases for better prices, even as it explores deals with France and Bulgaria after a Russian government deal was hindered by pricing objections. There are concerns about potential reductions in Russian wheat exports, but the situation remains uncertain. Both GASC and Russian suppliers have been affected by the unofficial price floor, with no official responses provided by OZK or GASC.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Saudi Arabia PIF Announces the Launch of “Ardara”
records.description: His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Chairman of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), has introduced "Ardara," a significant venture focusing on the development of AlWadi in the Aseer Region of southwest Saudi Arabia. The flagship project of Ardara, AlWadi, sprawls over 2.5 million square meters and is inspired by Aseer's unique architectural style and rich history. It emphasizes sustainability and green spaces, with over 30% of the area dedicated to open spaces, 16 km of waterfront, and 17 km of sports trails and cultural activities. AlWadi comprises five distinct districts, offering various residential, hospitality, and recreation options. It aims to attract local and international investors in multiple sectors, enhancing Saudi Arabia's economy diversification and strengthening partnerships with the private sector, aligning with PIF's strategy to unlock potential in sectors like tourism and entertainment, in line with Vision 2030.

records.title: iFarm, a pioneer in vertical farming technologies, has inaugurated the UAE's first vertical farm using its innovative solutions in Dubai.
records.description: iFarm, a pioneer in vertical farming technologies, has inaugurated the UAE's first vertical farm using its innovative solutions in Dubai. This cutting-edge facility is set to produce a variety of fresh, high-quality crops including leafy greens, baby leaves, microgreens, herbs, and edible flowers, catering to premium retail establishments and HoReCa businesses. With the Middle East and Africa's vertical farming market anticipated to reach USD 6.2 billion by 2030, there's a growing trend towards locally produced food, supported by recent food security policies in the region. The Dubai-based vertical farm, equipped with iFarm technologies, is well-positioned to meet the city's demand for top-quality, sustainably grown produce, with its strategic location just a 30-minute drive from Dubai's center. The farm boasts an extensive growing area of 712 square meters and is projected to yield approximately 3 tonnes of produce per month under the Mama Natura Greens brand. What sets this farm apart is its pioneering iFarm Multigreens technology, designed for both microgreens and full-cycle greens cultivation, and its capacity to adapt to market demand, business objectives, and seasonal variations. This venture aligns with the UAE's commitment to sustainable agriculture, enhanced food security, and the growing preference for high-quality, locally sourced, and environmentally friendly produce.

records.title: TNA, a provider of food processing and packaging equipment, has successfully installed two production lines for potato products commissio...
records.description: TNA, a provider of food processing and packaging equipment, has successfully installed two production lines for potato products commissioned by the Egyptian Army through the National Services Projects Organization (NSPO). The first production line, designed for Hash Browns and Rosti, produces two metric tonnes per hour, while the second line, dedicated to French fries, wedges, and disks, produces up to 10 metric tonnes per hour. TNA offers a comprehensive production process, from potato washing and destoning to product packaging. The company has also integrated advanced distribution and arctic packaging systems for frozen potato products. This effort is part of a broader initiative to achieve self-sufficiency in meeting the needs of the armed forces and local and export markets. Discussions are underway to expand operations to include new potato products and the processing of various agricultural products. In addition, TNA has recently partnered with Mister Bee Potato Chips, an iconic American brand, to optimize its snack production, resulting in a remarkable 400% increase in capacity.

records.title: Madinah is currently in the midst of its annual date season, where over 50 million kg of dates have been produced in the past three month...
records.description: Madinah is currently in the midst of its annual date season, where over 50 million kg of dates have been produced in the past three months, contributing more than $149 million to the Saudi economy. Themed "From Madinah to the World," this season is a platform for experts and prominent farmers to showcase diverse date varieties and emphasize the industry's economic significance. It encompasses cultural exhibitions in central hotels and major malls, offering visitors Saudi coffee, regional dates, and informative descriptions of different date types. Additionally, agricultural workshops educate attendees on effective pest control measures. This seasonal initiative, reflecting the goals of Vision 2030, underscores the vital role of the palm and date sector in agricultural and economic production, ultimately fulfilling local and global market needs through the vast number of palm trees in the region.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: ADAFSA Launches ''Jahaziya'' Early Warning Platform
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has launched the "Jahaziya" platform, a comprehensive system dedicated to risk and crisis management, early warning systems, and the One Health framework covering health risks for humans, animals, and plants. This platform is designed to ensure business continuity, crisis and emergency response, and global communication by integrating internal and external systems, collaborating with local, regional, and international partners, and automating response plans for significant risks at Emirate and country levels. "Jahaziya" not only predicts impending risks but also provides early detection, proactive foresight, and immediate response to incidents related to food safety, epidemics, diseases, pests, and more. It is aimed at enhancing the response to emergencies in agriculture and food sectors while preserving the Emirate's prestigious position as a safe and stable city. The platform aligns with the Abu Dhabi Government's vision for crisis and disaster management and exemplifies the Authority's commitment to preparedness, adaptability, and business continuity. It offers real-time interactive dashboards, automates incident and crisis management, and provides a unified view of operations for decision-makers.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The UK's Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO) has pledged £1.45 million (MAD 17.9 million) to aid Morocco in recovering f...
records.description: The UK's Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO) has pledged £1.45 million (MAD 17.9 million) to aid Morocco in recovering from the recent earthquake that struck the Al Haouz region. This funding is designated to address both immediate necessities and long-term development in the affected areas, aligning with Morocco's 5-year recovery plan. The financial assistance will be allocated to various sectors, including healthcare services and housing, with a particular emphasis on collaborating with local farmers and cooperatives to bring high-quality agricultural products to the market. This initiative will not only stimulate the local economy but also prioritize the preservation of Morocco's biodiversity. Chancellor of the Exchequer Jeremy Hunt acknowledged the resilience of the Moroccan people and their determination to rebuild after the earthquake, emphasizing the UK's willingness to support Morocco in this endeavor. Lord (Tariq) Ahmad of Wimbledon, Minister of State for Middle East, North Africa, South Asia, United Nations, and the Commonwealth, underscored the UK's commitment to assisting Morocco's recovery efforts and affirmed the thriving UK-Morocco partnership. The UK's support coincides with the Annual Meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund in Marrakech, where the UK is actively participating. In addition to financial aid, the UK has deployed the International Search and Rescue Team (UK-ISAR) and the UK Emergency Medical Team (UK EMT) to assist Moroccan authorities in search and rescue operations. This comprehensive approach is part of the ongoing UK-Morocco partnership, which aims to provide both immediate relief and long-term development assistance, while also promoting sustainable agriculture and biodiversity preservation in the earthquake-affected areas.
records.institution: The UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO)

records.title: Qatar's Minister of Municipality, H.E.
records.description: Qatar's Minister of Municipality, H.E. Dr. Abdulla bin Abdulaziz bin Turki Al Subaie, held discussions with Italy's Minister of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty, and Forests, H.E. Francesco Lollobrigida, during his visit to Qatar. The meeting centered on enhancing cooperation between the two nations, particularly in agriculture, food security, infrastructure, municipal services, and the application of modern agricultural technology and smart city solutions. Additionally, the talks included Italy's participation in the International Horticultural Expo 2023 Doha, a significant event that began on October 2 and will run for six months at Al Bidda Park.

records.title: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Committee on Agricultural Cooperation and Food Security has officially accredited the Saudi Plant Gene...
records.description: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Committee on Agricultural Cooperation and Food Security has officially accredited the Saudi Plant Genetic Resources Bank, making it the first of its kind in the Gulf region. This announcement was made during the 34th Meeting of Ministers Responsible for Agriculture and Food Security in GCC countries held in Muscat, Oman, with the participation of Eng. Abdulrahman Al-Fadhli, the Minister of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. The Saudi Plant Genetic Resources Bank holds a wide array of plant genetic resources, including field and horticultural crop seeds, seeds for natural plants in pastures and forests, medicinal seeds, aromatic plants, and genetic pools. The bank also incorporates herbaria and biotechnology laboratories to facilitate genetic studies and research on the genetic diversity of plant resources from GCC member states.
records.institution: The Gulf Cooperation Council Committee on Agricultural Cooperation and Food Security

records.title: In collaboration with South Korean ag-tech company Midbar and H.E.
records.description: In collaboration with South Korean ag-tech company Midbar and H.E. Rashed Bin Khalfan Al Mutawa Al Dhaheri Holding company (RBK), Abu Dhabi University (ADU) has inaugurated its first on-campus AirFarm. This inflatable and portable farm, as part of ADU's Innovate Strategy, integrates IoT and AI technologies to promote sustainable agriculture and interdisciplinary collaboration. The facility aims to provide students, faculty, and the wider UAE community with practical learning opportunities and contribute to food security and sustainable farming practices, aligning with the UAE's vision for sustainable development. The project showcases innovative smart farming solutions that increase crop yields and reduce resource inputs. Professor Ghassan Aouad, ADU Chancellor, emphasized the commitment to empowering students and nurturing innovation for a sustainable future.

records.title: Saudi Investment Recycling Company (SIRC), an entity of the Public Investment Fund, has partnered with Edama Organic Solutions to create...
records.description: Saudi Investment Recycling Company (SIRC), an entity of the Public Investment Fund, has partnered with Edama Organic Solutions to create a joint firm aimed at revolutionizing organic waste recycling in Saudi Arabia. This project is aligned with the country's Vision 2030 and will focus on sustainable waste management, contributing to a national circular economy while reducing harmful emissions and promoting a greener future. Through research, innovation, and expertise in desert agriculture, the partnership seeks to enhance local agricultural productivity, support green initiatives, and reduce reliance on imported soil amendments. This project will play a significant role in achieving Vision 2030's sustainability objectives and building a more sustainable future.

records.title: Tunisia's President Kais Saied met with the Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Abdelmonem Belaati, addressing issue...
records.description: Tunisia's President Kais Saied met with the Minister of Agriculture, Water Resources, and Fisheries, Abdelmonem Belaati, addressing issues in the agricultural sector, particularly the need to end the monopoly on animal feed supply. President Saied emphasized that supply should occur transparently, free from monopolies and speculation. He expressed concern for small farmers, who suffer due to this monopolistic practice, leading to livestock losses daily. Additionally, President Saied stressed the importance of enhancing efforts in desalinating water, especially in light of climate change and rainfall retention. The meeting also discussed preserving national seed resources, critical for Tunisia's climate and achieving self-sufficiency, with a particular focus on durum wheat. Draft decrees for various agricultural issues were also part of the discussion.

records.title: IFC, Morocco's OCP Launch $800mln Africa Food Supply Project
records.description: The International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private investment arm of the World Bank, and Morocco's OCP Group, the world's largest phosphate-based fertilizer company, have launched an agri-finance platform with the goal of mobilizing $800 million for African countries by 2030. This platform aims to establish and support sustainable food production and distribution systems in Africa, with a focus on skill development, job creation, and food security. By providing access to financing and skills training, the platform seeks to strengthen 30 agricultural value chains across Africa through 60 agri-finance operations, covering a wide range of crop types. Agriculture is a crucial sector for Africa, contributing approximately 20% of the continent's GDP and employing over 60% of its workforce. However, Africa currently imports a significant portion of its food, making it vulnerable to external shocks. The platform's investment strategy is designed to promote sustainable growth in the agricultural sector and enhance food security across the continent. Both IFC and OCP Group are committed to allocating resources to expand the platform and are actively seeking potential investors to join the initiative. In addition to providing funding, the platform will conduct in-depth studies of targeted value chains to identify challenges and design solutions. Already, the platform has developed new projects to support cashew and rice value chains in Côte d'Ivoire and is working on new projects in Cameroon, Gabon, and other countries. The IFC is the largest global development institution focusing on the private sector in emerging markets, with operations in over 100 countries. Meanwhile, OCP Group, a state-controlled company, reported record-high revenue of $11.2 billion in the previous year, representing a 36% increase due to strong fertilizer prices. This partnership between IFC and OCP is poised to harness Africa's potential to not only feed itself but also contribute to global food production.
records.institution: The International Finance Corp (IFC) & Morocco’s OCP Group

records.title: EDB Supports Food Security with over AED721mn Under its Five-Year Strategy
records.description: Emirates Development Bank (EDB) has reported its strong support for food security by approving over AED 721 million for food security projects since the launch of its new strategy in April 2021. EDB has dedicated AED 30 billion to aid 13,500 SMEs in five key sectors, including food security. During its participation in the Agra Middle East Exhibition (AgraME 2023), EDB showcased financing solutions for food production innovations and regional food security. These initiatives aim to boost national food security and promote sustainable agriculture in the UAE. EDB's financing solutions align with the country's National Food Security Strategy 2051, supporting climate-smart agriculture and economic development.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Mariam bint Mohammed Almheiri, the Minister of Climate Change and the Environment, has expressed the UAE's commitment to enhancing collab...
records.description: Mariam bint Mohammed Almheiri, the Minister of Climate Change and the Environment, has expressed the UAE's commitment to enhancing collaboration between Middle East and North Africa (MENA) countries to bolster their climate ambitions. The UAE is dedicated to reducing carbon emissions, increasing climate adaptation, and reallocating climate financing and investments to drive sustainable development in the region. Almheiri made this statement during her participation in the Middle East and North Africa Climate Week (MENACW 2023) in Riyadh. The UAE Minister highlighted the importance of swift action to lead a just and equitable energy transition by replacing traditional energy systems with clean and renewable alternatives, especially in the context of climate change. She also invited GCC agriculture ministers to support the Emirates Declaration on Resilient Food Systems, Sustainable Agriculture, and Climate Action. Climate change disproportionately affects certain communities, emphasizing the need for inclusivity in the collective response to the climate crisis, noted Almheiri. She emphasized the importance of technology and financing in achieving climate goals and called for dialogue and cooperation to ensure environmental conservation objectives are met.

records.title: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture Uses Agricultural Waste as Feed and Organic Fertilizers
records.description: Dr. Alaa Azouz, Head of the Guidance Sector at the Ministry of Agriculture, announced that the ministry has developed a plan to utilize agricultural waste residues for various objectives, including environmental preservation and preventing pollution and its potential adverse effects on public health. This initiative contributes to improving the income of Egyptian farmers from agricultural residues that lack economic value. Azouz emphasized that, at present, these agricultural residues, which were previously wasted, are being used in the production of unconventional animal feed or organic fertilizers. This transformation provides economic value to these residues and helps enhance the livelihoods of rural communities. The plan is executed through instructional and awareness campaigns, involving experts and researchers with significant experience in the field, who conduct theoretical and practical training for farmers to convey the information on environmental preservation and how to benefit from agricultural waste effectively.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture and Jordan Enterprise Development Corporation (JEDCO) have signed a memorandum of understanding to initiate a...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Jordan Enterprise Development Corporation (JEDCO) have signed a memorandum of understanding to initiate a project focused on organizing the agricultural sector by strengthening the value chains of agricultural alliances. Minister of Agriculture Khalid Hneifat emphasized that this memorandum aims to establish a partnership between both parties to develop value chains for agricultural alliances, which include cooperatives, companies, associations, and unions. The primary objectives are to reduce operational costs and expedite project implementation. This initiative aligns with the National Plan for Sustainable Agriculture for 2022-2025. JEDCO CEO Abdulfattah Al Kayed highlighted the corporation's efforts in designing and implementing private sector-oriented development programs across various sectors, including industry, agriculture, and services. The project's goal is to align Jordanian products with global demand by providing technical and financial support to startups and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to enhance their sustainability and expansion.

records.title: Dr.
records.description: Dr. Fatma Al-Kiyumi, Assistant Director of Fish Wealth Research at Oman's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, shared findings from an extensive research project that identified 51 fish species in Oman, including 11 entirely new species, boosting the nation's reputation as a diverse marine life hub. Of these species, 31 are commercially traded, offering opportunities for economic growth in Oman's fishing industry. The research underscores the importance of sustainable fishing practices to protect marine biodiversity in Oman, emphasizing the need for effective conservation strategies.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Saudi Arabia Pioneers the Next Era of Food Security Innovation
records.description: Saudi Arabia is leading the way in addressing global food security challenges by making significant advancements in diversifying and localizing food sources, reducing dependence on imports, and employing modern agricultural techniques to enhance local production. The Kingdom's efforts have led to self-sufficiency in the production of key food items like dates, dairy products, and eggs. Saudi Arabia has also invested in precision agriculture, employing data analytics, drones, and IoT to monitor crop health and manage resources efficiently. Additionally, technological solutions, including hydroponics and aquaponics, are being used to conserve water and ensure consistent food production. Collaborative efforts between government entities, SMEs, and innovation across various subsectors are driving Saudi Arabia's journey towards enhanced food security and sustainability.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Petrofac Ltd, a UK-based energy services provider, has secured a $615 million engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract f...
records.description: Petrofac Ltd, a UK-based energy services provider, has secured a $615 million engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract from Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. (ADNOC) for a carbon capture and storage (CCS) project in the UAE. The project, set to be completed in 2026, will allow for the capture and permanent storage of 1.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually from ADNOC's Habshan gas processing plant. This initiative aligns with ADNOC's goal to achieve net-zero emissions by 2045 and reduce carbon intensity by 25% by 2030, in line with the UN's net-zero target of 2050. Petrofac aims to leverage its CCS expertise and project delivery experience to support ADNOC's decarbonization plans and the UAE's energy transition.

records.title: The UAE-Vietnam Joint Committee meeting in Hanoi has advanced economic ties between the two nations.
records.description: The UAE-Vietnam Joint Committee meeting in Hanoi has advanced economic ties between the two nations. Co-chaired by Dr. Thani Bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister of State for Foreign Trade, and Dr. Nguyen Hong Dien, Vietnam's Minister of Industry and Trade, the meeting involved discussions across various sectors, including trade, investment, digital technology, agriculture, energy, transport, higher education, culture, tourism, and labor. The UAE is Vietnam's leading trade partner in the Arab World, with $8 billion in non-oil trade in 2022. Both countries are expected to conclude the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) this year, further strengthening their bilateral relations.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of State for Foreign Trade

records.title: The UAE's rapidly growing food and agriculture sector is set to become a top job creator, offering 20,000 job opportunities over the next...
records.description: The UAE's rapidly growing food and agriculture sector is set to become a top job creator, offering 20,000 job opportunities over the next five years with salaries ranging from Dh12,000 to Dh50,000. This sector is expected to contribute $10 billion to the nation's economy. The industry is undergoing significant transformation, with a focus on food security, local production, vertical farming, and aquaponics. Key roles in demand include geneticists, nutritionists, agriculture engineers, and experts in food technology. Agri-tech positions are particularly lucrative, with salaries averaging between Dh16,000 and Dh20,000 per month. Overall, the industry is evolving to meet consumer demands for quality, innovation, freshness, and traceability of products.

records.title: The Fisheries Resources Ministry in Yemen has announced the closure of the coastal shrimp fishing season in the Red Sea region's territor...
records.description: The Fisheries Resources Ministry in Yemen has announced the closure of the coastal shrimp fishing season in the Red Sea region's territorial waters, effective from October 9, 2023, until further notice. In an issued decision, the Ministry urged shrimp fishermen to remove their equipment and refrain from shrimp fishing during this period. The Ministry warned that any fresh or frozen shrimp caught during the closed season would be confiscated, and it called on fish and marine life merchants to comply with the decision. Legal penalties will be imposed on those found violating this decision, in accordance with the Law Regulating Fishing, Exploitation, and Protection of Aquatic Life and its executive regulations, with the aim of safeguarding shrimp populations.

records.title: UAE: MOCCAE and Tadweer Sign Deal to Launch Global Initiative to Decarbonize Waste Management
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and Abu Dhabi Waste Management Company (Tadweer) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to launch 'Waste to Zero,' a global initiative to promote waste decarbonization efforts and establish a circular economy platform. This initiative aims to enhance the UAE's leadership in global climate action, contribute to achieving a 43% emission reduction target by 2030, and encourage nations to adopt advanced technology-based solutions for decarbonizing sectors like waste management. The collaboration will address the waste management sector's role in greenhouse gas emissions and promote solutions that align with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and climate objectives, including emissions reduction and improving recycling quality. It will also attract investment in infrastructure projects, create employment, reduce global reliance on natural resources, strengthen regulatory frameworks, and enhance sustainable resource management.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and Abu Dhabi Waste Management Company (Tadweer)

records.title: Egypt Signs 7 Development Grant Agreements with Italy, UN with Total Cost of $34M
records.description: Egypt's Minister of International Cooperation, Rania Al-Mashat, presided over the signing of seven development grant agreements, valued at $34 million, funded by the Italian government and implemented by United Nations organizations, the World Bank, and relevant national entities. These agreements cover a range of sectors, including education, health, economic empowerment of rural women, child labor, entrepreneurship, and climate change. Al-Mashat emphasized the importance of these agreements in promoting Egypt's development agenda through effective international cooperation, while the Italian Ambassador, Michele Quaroni, highlighted their aim to enhance economic growth, support vulnerable groups, and develop Egypt's entrepreneurship system. These agreements signify the collaborative efforts between Egypt and Italy in various development sectors, building on their long-standing bilateral relations since 1975.

records.title: The Moroccan government has taken measures to control the rising prices of olive oil in the domestic market by approving a decree that te...
records.description: The Moroccan government has taken measures to control the rising prices of olive oil in the domestic market by approving a decree that temporarily bans the export of olive oil to prioritize domestic supply. The decree, officially approved by Mohamed Sadiki, the Minister of Agriculture Fisheries, and Rural Development, is currently awaiting the signature of the Minister of Trade and Industry, Riad Mazour, before being published in the Official Gazette. The ban will exclude high-value-added oil products and canned table olives prepared for export. The increase in olive oil prices, reaching nearly 10 euros per liter, is primarily attributed to prolonged drought conditions affecting olive production in Morocco. The government's decision aims to ensure stable supplies to the domestic market and protect consumers' purchasing power. Morocco ranks second in olive oil production in North Africa and the Middle East and ninth globally, with a harvest of over 217 million liters in 2022. The move is seen as a response to sector professionals' demands and aligns with government efforts to support the olive oil industry, including a significant investment plan to increase olive grove areas and production.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture Fisheries, and Rural Development

records.title: Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure Highlights UAE's Approach to Engage Youth in Energy Transition at ADIPEC 2023
records.description: At the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) 2023, Eng Sharif Al Olama, Undersecretary for Energy and Petroleum Affairs at the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI), highlighted the UAE's commitment to engaging youth in the energy transition. Speaking during the Future Leaders Conference, Al Olama emphasized the UAE's approach to empower and involve young leaders in decision-making processes. He emphasized the importance of nurturing talent in fields such as engineering, renewables, sustainability, AI, and digitalization to address the challenges of the energy transition. Al Olama also discussed the National Water and Energy DSM Program's efforts to improve energy efficiency and commended the International Youth Climate Delegate Programme as a means to empower young people and engage them in climate dialogue, demonstrating the UAE's commitment to youth involvement in sustainability and climate action.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure

records.title: The UAE has officially launched its first utility-scale wind project, capable of providing power to approximately 23,000 homes and mitiga...
records.description: The UAE has officially launched its first utility-scale wind project, capable of providing power to approximately 23,000 homes and mitigating the emission of 120,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually. Developed by Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar), the project spans four locations in the UAE, including Delma Island (27 MW), Al Sila (27 MW), Sir Bani Yas Island (45 MW), and Al Halah in Fujairah (4.5 MW), with a total combined capacity of 103.5 megawatts (MW). This initiative marks the introduction of utility-scale wind power to the UAE's energy mix, complementing its existing generation sources such as solar, nuclear, and waste-to-energy plants.
records.institution: UAE’s Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar)

records.title: In the context of the presidential initiative "Haya Karima," aimed at improving the lives of small farmers and herders and enhancing Egyp...
records.description: In the context of the presidential initiative "Haya Karima," aimed at improving the lives of small farmers and herders and enhancing Egypt's rural areas, a veterinary caravan operated in Kafr El-Sheikh. This initiative, which was executed from September 30, 2023, to October 5, 2023, involved a mobile clinic traveling through villages and outskirts of Kafr El-Sheikh to provide free healthcare for the livestock of small-scale farmers. The caravan, a collaborative effort between the Animal Reproduction Institute, the Directorate of Veterinary Medicine, and the Livestock Insurance Fund, conducted numerous veterinary procedures, including testing, treatment, ultrasound examinations, and surgical operations, benefiting a total of 2,027 beneficiaries among young livestock raisers in the governorate. The initiative aligns with the broader goal of elevating the agricultural sector and enhancing the livelihoods of rural communities as part of Egypt's commitment to rural development and agricultural progress.
records.institution: The Animal Reproduction Institute, the Directorate of Veterinary Medicine, and the Livestock Insurance Fund,

records.title: During its 40th regular session, chaired by Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, the Iraqi Cabinet approved a nearly 30 percent increa...
records.description: During its 40th regular session, chaired by Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, the Iraqi Cabinet approved a nearly 30 percent increase in the capital of the Agricultural Cooperative Bank. This capital increase amounts to IQD 29,476,500,000 (approximately $22.6 million) and will be added to the bank's existing capital of IQD 100,600,000,000. The decision aims to strengthen the agricultural sector and provide support to farmers in implementing their agricultural plans, reflecting the government's commitment to agricultural development.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Affirms Commitment to Sustainable Fishing
records.description: Saudi Arabia has reaffirmed its commitment to protecting sustainable fish stocks, the welfare of fishermen, and investments in aquaculture projects. During the MedFish4Ever conference in Malta, the country also pledged to establish regulatory frameworks and management plans for its fishing industry. Mansour Al-Mushaiti, Saudi deputy minister of environment, water, and agriculture, highlighted the importance of sustainable aquaculture, biodiversity, and protecting marine ecosystems. He noted that the national aquaculture production in 2022 exceeded 120,000 tons and that Saudi Arabia aims to increase production to around 500,000 tons of fish in the coming years. Additionally, Al-Mushaiti emphasized the Kingdom's responsibility in coordinating efforts for the effective management of natural resources in the Red Sea, given its substantial coastal area.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Abu Dhabi's wealth fund, ADQ, is reportedly in discussions with Turkey regarding the construction of a railway over the Bosporus in Istan...
records.description: Abu Dhabi's wealth fund, ADQ, is reportedly in discussions with Turkey regarding the construction of a railway over the Bosporus in Istanbul as part of a proposed trade corridor connecting Europe to the Middle East and Asia. This initiative, if realized, would rival the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), a project supported by the United States and the European Union. The railway is intended to traverse the Yavuz Sultan Selim suspension bridge, which links Istanbul's European and Asian sides. Turkey aims to leverage its strategic geographical location to establish a trade corridor connecting London, the Gulf, and Beijing. These developments come as there is growing cooperation and business partnerships between Turkey and the UAE, with bilateral trade expected to increase significantly in the coming years.

records.title: In the governorate of Lahij, 40 hand plows were distributed to small-scale farmers in Tuban as part of an initiative by the organization...
records.description: In the governorate of Lahij, 40 hand plows were distributed to small-scale farmers in Tuban as part of an initiative by the organization "Pure Hands" and executed by the "Youth Horizons Foundation." The distribution event was attended by the president of Pure Hands, Dr. Mohammed Al-Hajaji, and the president of the Youth Horizons Foundation, Iyad Mahdi, along with several local officials. These hand plows, aimed at supporting small-scale farmers, will contribute to cost-effective land cultivation and farming. This project is one of many initiatives undertaken by Pure Hands to aid beneficiaries, supported by the Yemeni community abroad. It is part of their efforts to alleviate the challenges faced by their compatriots in Yemen during the current challenging circumstances. The organizers expressed their gratitude to the generous donors and local authorities for their collaboration on this humanitarian initiative and highlighted the importance of continued support to reach more beneficiaries in the future.

records.title: Egypt's General Authority of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) has signed a framework agreement with C2X, a subsidiary of Maersk, to...
records.description: Egypt's General Authority of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) has signed a framework agreement with C2X, a subsidiary of Maersk, to develop a massive green fuel production facility for ship bunkering services, aligning with Egypt's decarbonization goals. The first phase of the project will see investments of around $3 billion. The SCZone consortium, including the Sovereign Fund of Egypt (TSFE), the New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA), and the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC), will work on these green hydrogen projects within the green corridor sites, with plans to export the output to European markets. Egypt is making strides in green hydrogen production to reduce carbon emissions and promote renewable energy use in line with its National Climate Strategy 2050.
records.institution: Egypt's General Authority of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Kuwait is set to initiate a tender for the first phase of its ambitious 4.5-GW Shagaya solar project, with an expected start in the next...
records.description: Kuwait is set to initiate a tender for the first phase of its ambitious 4.5-GW Shagaya solar project, with an expected start in the next two to three months. The initial phase will add 1,100 MW of photovoltaic (PV) capacity. The request for qualifications (RFQ) document for this phase is prepared and will be issued soon. Subsequent phases will include a 200-MW concentrated solar power (CSP) plant with storage, 1,500 MW of solar PV in phase three, and an additional 1,700 MW in the final phase. The choice of solar energy over wind is due to the alignment of peak demand in Kuwait with solar power generation during the day. The Shagaya project is a significant component of Kuwait's aim to achieve 15% renewables in its energy mix by 2030.

records.title: Minister of Municipality Calls for Joint Action to Achieve Food Security
records.description: Minister of Municipality HE Dr. Abdullah bin Abdulaziz bin Turki Al Subaie, who also chairs the General Assembly of the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), emphasized the importance of collaborative efforts, cooperation, and unified action to achieve sustainable development in agriculture and food security. He highlighted Qatar's commitment to hosting the 6th General Assembly of IOFS as a means of fostering solidarity among member states and providing an opportunity for consultation and knowledge sharing. Minister Al Subaie announced a grant of $2 million from Qatar to support IOFS's activities and areas of operation. He also discussed Qatar's efforts to enhance food security, including its national strategy and commitment to Qatar National Vision 2030's development goals.

records.title: OIC Has Unveiled a Groundbreaking Framework Centered on Contract Farming
records.description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) is driving innovation in food security through its visionary framework centered on contract farming, forging agreements between farmers and agribusinesses to enhance productivity and market stability. Resilient infrastructure, bilateral cooperation, and financial inclusion for farmers are pivotal elements, along with strategies to mitigate climate change challenges. Recognizing the importance of small farmers, the OIC aims to empower them with modern farming techniques. This collaborative and innovative initiative holds great promise for transforming agriculture and ensuring food security across the Muslim world, offering a beacon of hope for a more secure and sustainable future amidst global food security concerns.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: ADNOC has chosen Carbon Clean's CycloneCC carbon capture technology for deployment at Fertiglobe's nitrogen fertilizer plant in Abu Dhabi...
records.description: ADNOC has chosen Carbon Clean's CycloneCC carbon capture technology for deployment at Fertiglobe's nitrogen fertilizer plant in Abu Dhabi, UAE. This marks the world's first deployment of a fully modular, 10-ton-per-day industrial CycloneCC carbon capture unit. The CycloneCC unit is designed to significantly reduce equipment size and overall footprint, making it a crucial advancement in industrial decarbonization. The project aims to help achieve the UAE's decarbonization goals and net-zero commitments, demonstrating the nation's commitment to climate action and sustainable industrial practices.

records.title: During the UAE-Armenian Business Forum in Yerevan, Abdulla Mohamed Almazrui, the Chairman of the Federation of the UAE Chambers of Commer...
records.description: During the UAE-Armenian Business Forum in Yerevan, Abdulla Mohamed Almazrui, the Chairman of the Federation of the UAE Chambers of Commerce and Industry (UAE Chambers) and Deputy Prime Minister Tigran Khachatryan of Armenia discussed ways to enhance economic cooperation between their two countries. Almazrui emphasized the UAE's commitment to strengthening ties with Armenia, particularly in trade, investment, and tourism. He also highlighted the UAE's significant investments in Armenia, spanning various sectors including energy, agriculture, and manufacturing. Khachatryan reciprocated Armenia's commitment to deepening relations with the UAE and expressed interest in expanding cooperation in trade, tourism, and education. The discussions centered on areas of cooperation and practical projects that would contribute to the economic development of both nations. The meeting was attended by Dr. Nariman Al Mulla, the UAE Ambassador to Armenia, and other high-ranking officials from both sides.
records.institution: UAE Chambers of Commerce and Industry (UAE Chambers)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: National Dairy and Masakin Dairy, both entities under Emirates Food Industries, have entered a groundbreaking partnership with Alltech, a...
records.description: National Dairy and Masakin Dairy, both entities under Emirates Food Industries, have entered a groundbreaking partnership with Alltech, a global leader in animal nutrition and sustainability solutions. This collaboration represents a significant milestone in the dairy industry as they aim to revolutionize carbon footprint benchmarking and reduction efforts while introducing the innovative methane-reducing technology, Agolin, in the Middle East. The partnership includes access to cutting-edge carbon footprint benchmarking technologies and tools to measure their environmental impact accurately. Additionally, they will be the first company in the Middle East to implement Alltech's methane-reducing technology, which can lower methane emissions by 10% while increasing feed efficiency and milk production. This initiative aligns with the companies' commitment to sustainability and sets an example for the dairy industry in the UAE, contributing to climate action and aligning with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

records.title: The Implementation of the Rural Livelihoods and Agricultural Sector Development Project
records.description: During a meeting held in Aden, the steering committee of the Rural Livelihoods and Agricultural Development Project in Yemen discussed the project's progress and its implementation in accordance with its operational plan, specific activities, and future objectives. The project, which is jointly implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the Social Development Fund, and the Yemeni Ministries of Planning, Agriculture, Irrigation, and Fisheries, receives funding from the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), with a total cost of $3 million. The project is designed to enhance food and nutritional security, boost smallholder farmers' incomes, increase agricultural production, and enhance resilience to climate risks, focusing on 20 districts across five Yemeni governorates. The discussion highlighted the project's components, such as climate-resilient community infrastructure, agricultural livelihood protection, and ongoing development initiatives, as well as its accomplishments and contributions to achieving food security and mitigating the impact of climate-related crises and natural disasters on food security in Yemen. The meeting was attended by various officials, including the Ministers of Agriculture and Irrigation, as well as representatives from IFAD and FAO, emphasizing the importance of the agricultural sector for Yemen's economic growth and rural development, and the necessity of investing in agriculture to improve living conditions in rural areas, especially amid the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and external shocks, such as the Russia-Ukraine conflict, which have affected food prices and the Yemeni economy. The project's significance in building climate-resilient community infrastructure, protecting agricultural livelihoods, and promoting food security and the well-being of vulnerable households was also highlighted. The participants underscored the need for continuous collaboration among all involved entities to ensure the successful execution of the project's plan and activities, achieving its strategic and developmental objectives.
records.institution: The Steering Committee of the Rural Livelihoods and Agricultural Development Project

records.title: Yemeni Cabinet Approves 163 Projects in 20 Governantes
records.description: The Cabinet has given the green light for Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate to proceed with the sale of a 3.17-acre piece of land in the Sakkha area near the Urban Development Housing Project, catering to a specialized food supply company. Additionally, the Cabinet approved 163 diverse projects spanning 20 governorates in alignment with the "Decent Life" initiative. These projects encompass infrastructure development, public facilities, and services such as electrical transformers, youth centers, public markets, parking complexes, sewage treatment facilities, government and agricultural service centers, medical facilities, and more, aiming to enhance public services and promote community development across the nation.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Fayoum Governorate is taking significant steps to control commodity prices, combat inflation, and establish outlets for the sale of s...
records.description: The Fayoum Governorate is taking significant steps to control commodity prices, combat inflation, and establish outlets for the sale of subsidized goods in an effort to alleviate the burden on citizens. This initiative involves a full collaboration between the Chamber of Commerce, the Directorate of Supply, and civil society organizations. The governorate is also implementing strict measures against merchants who violate regulations and conducting regular inspections in various centers and villages across the governorate to monitor prices and ensure merchant compliance. The Ministry of Supply, in cooperation with the Chamber of Commerce, is creating a detailed list of food merchants and suppliers, categorizing them based on wholesale, semi-wholesale, retail, and semi-retail, along with their locations in each center and village. This effort aims to target a wide range of citizens by providing food products at reduced prices through exhibitions and sales outlets. The governorate is also increasing the diversity of exhibitions and sales outlets to include schools' necessities and school uniforms. Fayoum's governor emphasized the importance of coordinating with the Ministry of Agriculture, agricultural cooperatives, and women's organizations to optimize the utilization of their products in sales outlets. This collaborative approach involves multiple entities, both government and non-governmental, working within the legal framework to control markets, counter monopolistic practices, and ensure citizens are not burdened with additional costs. The governor welcomed input, suggestions, and insights from various participants, including feedback on the current exhibitions and sales outlets selling food products, school uniforms, and stationery. Additionally, they discussed proposed locations for new outlets, methods for providing food commodities in these outlets, and the roles of various governmental and non-governmental entities operating within the law. Challenges related to ration card registration and the delivery of food supplies for subsidized goods were also reviewed, with logical solutions in place to address these issues.

records.title: Iraq to Construct 36 Rainwater Dams to Confront Drought
records.description: Iraq is planning to construct 36 dams in 2024 to harness rainwater and address the ongoing drought crisis affecting the Tigris and Euphrates rivers due to reduced water releases and the impact of climate change. The dams will be located in various governorates across the country to collect and store rainwater during the summer. The Minister of Water Resources, Aoun Diab, stated that Iraq is expected to experience early rainfall during the upcoming fall and winter seasons, which will help ensure sufficient water reserves for drinking and agriculture. Construction will commence on a dam near Sinjar in northern Iraq and another in the western desert as part of the government's efforts to combat the prolonged drought crisis in Mesopotamia caused by decreased water flow from Turkey and Iran.

records.title: Minister of Agriculture in Lebanon's caretaker government, Abbas Al-Hajj Hassan, commended Qatar's proactive initiatives, especially in r...
records.description: Minister of Agriculture in Lebanon's caretaker government, Abbas Al-Hajj Hassan, commended Qatar's proactive initiatives, especially in relation to the Lebanese presidency, recognizing the urgency of addressing food security challenges amid a significant crisis. He emphasized the need for cooperation and the formulation of a collective vision for food production and consumption in the Arab world. Despite acknowledging the historical neglect of Lebanon's agricultural sector, he stressed that Lebanon can no longer afford to sideline it, as many Lebanese have turned to farming due to the ongoing crisis. He also expressed hopes for expanding trade and transportation cooperation between Lebanon and Qatar and emphasized the importance of Arab-Arab collaboration to bolster the region's global food production capabilities.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture Launches a Campaign to Combat Agricultural Pests
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture has launched a campaign to combat agricultural pests in rural farming areas, as part of the measures taken to ensure the success of the 2023-2024 agricultural campaign. The campaign was inaugurated by Minister of Agriculture Emam Ould Beibacama, who emphasized that its goal is to enhance efforts aimed at increasing national agricultural production. He expressed hope that this campaign would contribute to achieving self-sufficiency in food security, noting its alignment with the directives of President Mohamed Ould Ghazouani to ensure the success of the agricultural campaign for the season. Minister Beibacama highlighted the various challenges faced in agriculture, such as grain-eating birds, seasonal locusts, and other pests. He also mentioned the deployment of well-equipped all-terrain vehicles for pest control, supported by mobile teams, with plans to further reinforce these teams with military aircraft when needed. Sidi Mohamed Al-Qasim, the Director of Plant Protection at the Ministry of Agriculture, pointed out that a significant presence of seasonal locusts is expected, with adverse effects on crops due to the drying of natural pastures. He stressed the campaign's timeliness to mitigate significant losses in traditional crops, which are the livelihood of many low-income farmers. Mr. Al-Qasim urged the intervention teams to coordinate with regional authorities and engage with farmers to facilitate their tasks. He mentioned the positive impact of previous pest control campaigns in protecting crops from various agricultural pests, including seasonal locusts, the maize stalk borer "Sesamia," and grain-eating birds.

records.title: Morocco is anticipated to import 2.5 million tonnes of soft wheat, covering 50% of its soft wheat requirements, from France this season d...
records.description: Morocco is anticipated to import 2.5 million tonnes of soft wheat, covering 50% of its soft wheat requirements, from France this season due to a significant decrease in wheat supplies from Eastern Europe. In response to a severe drought in 2022, Morocco had already imported 1 million tonnes of wheat from France during the summer. A report from the European Commission revealed that Morocco continues to be the primary destination for EU wheat in the 2022/23 agricultural campaign, with the country purchasing 4 million tonnes of European wheat during the first four months of 2023, up from 1.4 million tonnes the previous year. This increased import of wheat is a result of Morocco's wheat supply shortage from Eastern Europe and the severe drought of 2022, which had a devastating impact on the country's agricultural production. Given the significant role of wheat in the Moroccan diet, the drought amplified the country's dependence on wheat imports, underscoring the need for Morocco to diversify its sources of food supply. In the first eight months of 2022, wheat imports soared to MAD 18.8 billion ($1.7 billion), nearly double the MAD 9.2 billion ($842 million) recorded during the same period in 2021, emphasizing the severe consequences of the drought on Morocco's agriculture sector.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Qatari company Nebras Power is planning to develop a 1 GW wind farm in Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, as part of its initiatives in the ener...
records.description: Qatari company Nebras Power is planning to develop a 1 GW wind farm in Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, as part of its initiatives in the energy sector of the country. During negotiations with Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the chairman of Nebras Power, Muhammad al-Hajri, discussed various investment projects, including the creation of 600 MW energy storage systems in the Tashkent region. Nebras Power has already initiated the construction of a 1.6 GW combined cycle power plant in the Syrdarya region and is preparing for another thermal power plant in Surkhandarya. The company aims to expand its involvement in green energy partnerships in Uzbekistan.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks to Expand Coffee Production to Boost Economy
records.description: Saudi Arabia is actively pursuing the expansion of its coffee production to support economic diversification efforts and bolster its economy. With more than 400,000 Arabica coffee trees currently yielding over 800 tonnes of coffee annually, the kingdom has ambitious plans to plant an additional 1.2 million coffee trees by 2026, as reported by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture is focusing on developing 15 provinces in the southwestern part of Saudi Arabia as major coffee producers, particularly of the Arabica variety, aligning with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. The southern region of Saudi Arabia already hosts more than 2,535 coffee farms, including over 500 "model" coffee farms. Saudi Arabia ranks among the world's top ten consumers of coffee, and the global coffee market was valued at approximately $127 billion in 2022, with expected growth at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.72% from 2023 to 2030, according to Coherent Market Insights.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Saline Water Conversion Corp.
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Saline Water Conversion Corp. (SWCC) has signed five agreements with various organizations and companies as part of its efforts to localize the water industry and advance innovative technologies. The agreements include partnerships with the Small and Medium Enterprises General Authority (Monsha’at) and the University of Tabuk, focusing on empowering entrepreneurs and innovators in water technologies and developing a robot for cleaning water intake pipelines. Additional deals were made with UiPath to utilize artificial intelligence, Fluid Equipment Development Co. to develop pumps and energy recovery devices, and Dow for a study on cleaning materials for reverse osmosis membranes. These collaborations reflect SWCC's commitment to enhancing the water industry, innovation, and environmental sustainability.
records.institution: Saudi Government Firm Saline Water Conversion Corp (SWCC)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: ADNOC has announced that its Ruwais Refinery received International Sustainability Carbon Certification (ISCC) for the production of Sust...
records.description: ADNOC has announced that its Ruwais Refinery received International Sustainability Carbon Certification (ISCC) for the production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), becoming the first company in the Middle East to achieve this distinction. This significant achievement highlights ADNOC's commitment to partnering with its customers to accelerate their decarbonization efforts. The ISCC EU/CORSIA PLUS "Co-Processing" international certification allows ADNOC to supply its SAF to international airlines at Abu Dhabi Airport. The fuel is produced by blending used cooking oil feedstock with jet fuel at ADNOC's Ruwais Refinery and will be available later this month, with the first batch sufficient to fuel a return 787-10 Dreamliner flight from Abu Dhabi to Paris. This move represents a key part of ADNOC's strategy to provide lower carbon fuels to its customers and support the aviation industry's efforts to decarbonize air travel. ADNOC continues to take transformative steps to make energy cleaner and invest in clean energies to strengthen its role as a responsible global energy provider, aligning with the UAE's Net Zero by 2050 Strategic Initiative and advancing its net-zero ambition to 2045.

records.title: Agrointelli, the pioneering Danish field robotics company, is eager to participate in the upcoming COP28 and highlight the company's cont...
records.description: Agrointelli, the pioneering Danish field robotics company, is eager to participate in the upcoming COP28 and highlight the company's contributions to the agricultural industry and global sustainability initiatives. Agrointelli focuses on its autonomous Robotti, designed to revolutionize agriculture through cutting-edge robotics and automation, aiming to make precision farming more efficient and accessible for farmers worldwide. Robotti has already made a significant impact in 16 countries, providing autonomous operation, simplicity, reliability, customization, precision, safety, and low environmental impact. Its participation in COP28 underlines its commitment to leading the way towards a more efficient and environmentally conscious future for agriculture, emphasizing the role of technology in reducing farming's environmental impact and striving for a more sustainable future.

records.title: NUTRIDOR Limited, a subsidiary of Nigeria's Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group, inaugurated its advanced dairy production facility...
records.description: NUTRIDOR Limited, a subsidiary of Nigeria's Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group, inaugurated its advanced dairy production facility in Dubai Industrial City, marking a historic event as the first factory commissioned by a Nigerian business subsidiary in the UAE. The factory is capable of producing over 120,000 liters of liquid dairy daily and was established under the UAE's 'Foreign Investment Liberalization Scheme.' The operation is committed to clean energy, zero waste practices, automation, digital technology, sustainability, skillset development, and local value addition. Senior Emirati and Nigerian officials attended the inauguration, highlighting the significance of this achievement for both nations. TGI Group, with operations spanning multiple sectors, has been active for 43 years and operates in 13 countries across Africa, the Middle East, and Asia.

records.title: Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group, a Nigerian conglomerate, is gearing up to inaugurate a cutting-edge dairy production facility i...
records.description: Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group, a Nigerian conglomerate, is gearing up to inaugurate a cutting-edge dairy production facility in Dubai Industrial City, marking its expansion into the global market. The subsidiary, Nutridor Limited, plans to produce over 120,000 liters of liquid dairy daily, becoming the first Nigerian business subsidiary to commission such a facility in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Established under the UAE's 'Foreign Investment Liberalization Scheme,' the factory will prioritize clean energy, zero waste practices, advanced technology, sustainability initiatives, and local value addition. This significant event is expected to be attended by senior Emirati and Nigerian officials. With operations spanning 13 countries across Africa, the Middle East, and Asia, TGI Group has been a prominent player in various sectors for over four decades. The inauguration of Nutridor's dairy production facility represents another milestone in the conglomerate's global expansion, underlining its commitment to innovation, sustainability, and international growth. The facility, with its substantial daily liquid dairy production capacity, aims to meet the rising demand for high-quality dairy products in the UAE and the wider Middle East. It will produce a range of dairy products, including milk, yoghurt, and cheese, employing the latest technologies and sustainable practices. A notable feature of the Nutridor dairy production facility is its strong focus on sustainability, with a commitment to clean energy solutions and advanced waste management systems. This aligns with the UAE's sustainability goals and its vision to become a global leader in sustainable practices. Nutridor also plans to integrate cutting-edge automation and digital acceleration into its operations to ensure efficiency and product consistency, meeting the high standards of the UAE's competitive dairy market. Beyond production, Nutridor's presence in the UAE aims to contribute to the local economy by creating job opportunities and promoting skillset development among the local workforce. The emphasis on local value addition means the company will engage with local suppliers and partners, strengthening economic ties between Nigeria and the UAE and aligning with the economic diversification strategies of both nations.

records.title: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Mr.
records.description: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Mr. El-Sayed El-Quseir, announced the ongoing release of feed supplies in coordination with the Central Bank. Between September 8, 2023, and September 21, 2023, approximately 260,000 tons of maize and soybeans were released, amounting to approximately $133 million. This release includes significant quantities of maize and soybeans, essential components of poultry and livestock feed, aiming to support the local market and agricultural industry. The minister emphasized that the government, along with the Central Bank's support, is committed to maintaining a steady supply of these crucial agricultural commodities.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Faculty of Agriculture at the University of Menoufia is launching specialized programs in Food Quality, Safety, and Biotechnology, ta...
records.description: The Faculty of Agriculture at the University of Menoufia is launching specialized programs in Food Quality, Safety, and Biotechnology, taught in English, starting in the first semester of the 2023/2024 academic year, with the support of the university's president, Dr. Ahmed Al-Qasid, and the oversight of the college dean, Dr. Ayman Hafez. These programs are open to students with a background in scientific studies, and those holding bachelor's degrees from recognized universities in various related fields, who meet the English language proficiency requirements. The emphasis on food quality and safety reflects the growing importance of these factors in the agricultural and biotechnology industries, making this initiative a significant step in advancing the knowledge and skills of future professionals in these fields.
records.institution: The Faculty of Agriculture at the University of Menoufia

records.title: Iraq's Minister of Agriculture, Abbas Jabr Al-Maliki, has directed the release of funds for compensating farmers affected by hail damage...
records.description: Iraq's Minister of Agriculture, Abbas Jabr Al-Maliki, has directed the release of funds for compensating farmers affected by hail damage in the provinces of Najaf, Diwaniyah, and Muthanna. These funds amount to 136 billion Iraqi dinars and will be distributed among the affected farmers. Minister Al-Maliki, in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and following discussions with Prime Minister Mohammed Shiaa Al-Sudani, facilitated the transfer of these funds to the Ministry of Agriculture. The ministry has promptly initiated the disbursement of these funds to the relevant agricultural directorates in the affected provinces to ensure a swift distribution to the farmers, who have long awaited this compensation. The minister emphasized that these efforts are geared towards fulfilling the aspirations of farmers throughout Iraq, from the northern regions to the south.

records.title: Tripoli Municipalities Launch US$1M Plastic Waste Management Program
records.description: The Greater Tripoli area, encompassing Souq Al-Jumaa, Abu Salim, and Central Tripoli, has launched a 30-month project valued at $1 million, aimed at enhancing plastic waste management. Supported by the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) and the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat), this project holds significance as more than 85% of Libya's population resides in cities, particularly along the northern coastal strip. The initiative addresses the challenge of reducing the per capita negative environmental impact in urban areas, emphasizing air quality and municipal waste management. The project seeks to use plastic waste management as a foundation for recycling, mitigating environmental pollution, creating employment opportunities, and promoting circular business models in Libya. The country has grappled with bureaucratic hurdles, limited waste management infrastructure, and the prevalence of open dumping and unofficial landfills. By prioritizing plastic waste management, the project aims to address environmental issues, foster sustainability, stimulate economic development, and enhance the quality of life in the Greater Tripoli area. Moreover, Tripoli's Mediterranean coast faces pollution from untreated sewage and litter, prompting beach closures and adversely affecting residents' well-being amid the country's infrastructure challenges stemming from years of conflict, state collapse, and neglect since 2011.
