records.title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have signed an agreement to strengthen their bilateral cooperation in the field of information technology, with...
records.description: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have signed an agreement to strengthen their bilateral cooperation in the field of information technology, with a focus on accelerating digital transformation, promoting innovation, and developing digital infrastructure. The agreement includes the establishment of a task force to promote digital corporations and collaboration on strengthening the SME and startup sectors, drafting policies and regulations, supporting innovation, emerging technologies, research and development, training programs, and infrastructure development. Both countries aim to enhance digital connectivity, encourage participation in international events, and explore opportunities in chip manufacturing, electric vehicles, lithium-ion batteries, agriculture technology, and mining technologies.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Communications and Information Technology

records.title: Saudi Arabia is making significant strides in coffee production, currently cultivating over 400,000 Arabica coffee trees and producing mo...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is making significant strides in coffee production, currently cultivating over 400,000 Arabica coffee trees and producing more than 800 tons of coffee annually in the regions of Jazan, Aseer, and Al-Baha. The country aims to expand its coffee cultivation efforts further, with plans to plant 1.2 million coffee trees by 2026. Saudi Arabia, one of the top 10 coffee-consuming nations globally, is focusing on developing its coffee sector, particularly Arabica coffee, known for its quality. The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture has launched initiatives and programs, including support from the Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (REF), to boost coffee production in alignment with Saudi Vision 2030 and enhance the national economy.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture

records.title: Israeli Minister of Agriculture Avi Dichter and his Moroccan counterpart Mohamed Sadiki have inked an agreement to enhance agricultural c...
records.description: Israeli Minister of Agriculture Avi Dichter and his Moroccan counterpart Mohamed Sadiki have inked an agreement to enhance agricultural cooperation between their respective nations. Dichter underscored the significance of this collaboration, stating that it's a crucial step in the plan to expand Israel's and Morocco's international food security network. This cooperation plays a vital role in global food security, especially given mounting concerns about climate change and environmental sustainability. The agreement covers various areas of collaboration, including support for private agro-tech companies, the development of food supply chains, rural development, and agricultural production under challenging conditions like drought. Israel's status as an agro-tech innovation hub is pivotal, as the nation offers cutting-edge solutions for food production amidst a changing climate. Dichter has made food security and sustainable agriculture a top priority, emphasizing the quality and sustainability of locally-grown produce. This agreement signifies a significant step in bolstering agricultural and diplomatic ties between the two countries and underscores Israel's commitment to the region.

records.title: Dubai Municipality Organizes Several Events and Initiatives to Combat Food Loss, Further Ensuring Sustainability
records.description: In commemoration of the International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste on September 29th, the Dubai Municipality orchestrated an array of educational workshops, activities, and global awareness seminars. The primary objective was to foster public awareness regarding food waste and loss, induce behavioral changes, and safeguard local and global environments. Aligned with the principles of the circular economy and sustainable development, the municipality intends to implement sustainable food practices and concepts that bolster Dubai's food security strategy, promoting sustainable production and consumption. H.E. Dawoud Al Hajri, Director General of Dubai Municipality, emphasized the importance of such initiatives in preserving food systems, reducing environmental impact, and supporting the goal of climate neutrality by 2050. These efforts include collaborations with organizations like the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations to enhance responsible food shopping and consumption. In addition, global symposiums and educational programs were organized to raise awareness and provide guidance to retail food businesses, food importers, and exporters on reducing food loss and waste, thereby fostering sustainable and environmentally friendly food practices throughout Dubai.

records.title: Tunisia has prolonged its quota system and ban on agricultural use of tap water due to an ongoing five-year drought, as announced by the...
records.description: Tunisia has prolonged its quota system and ban on agricultural use of tap water due to an ongoing five-year drought, as announced by the Agriculture Ministry. Initially, these measures, which also included night-time water cut-offs and bans on using tap water for car washing, watering green areas, and cleaning public spaces, were to last until September 30. However, the severe drought, characterized by extended summers and dwindling groundwater sources, has compelled the extension. Notably, there's a significant fall of about one billion cubic meters in dam capacity due to scarce rainfall from last September to mid-March. Particularly, the Sidi Salem Dam, a primary drinking water source for various regions, has seen its level plummet to 16% of its 580 million-cubic-meter capacity. Offenders of the water-use restrictions face penalties including fines and up to six months imprisonment. This situation in Tunisia echoes the broader global challenge where climate change-induced prolonged droughts are becoming increasingly common.

records.title: Tunisia Works to Support Some Agricultural Sectors Which Generate Foreign Currency
records.description: The Tunisian Agriculture Ministry is actively supporting foreign exchange-generating agricultural sectors like olive, citrus, and date palm cultivation, while also emphasizing self-sufficiency in hard wheat production equivalent to 12 million quintals, according to Minister Abdel Monême Belâati. During a meeting in Kébili, he highlighted the ministry's efforts to facilitate a successful date season, vital for bolstering the country's budget amid climate change challenges and the global economic effects of the Russian-Ukrainian conflict. Belâati emphasized the importance of ensuring farmers' profitability to sustain the date sector and mentioned seeking financial support from various sources, including the Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS), to aid farmers in advancing their activities.

records.title: Egypt, World Bank Forge Deeper Partnership to Drive Sustainable Development
records.description: Egypt's Minister of International Cooperation and World Bank Governor for Egypt, Dr. Rania Al-Mashat, led a collaborative workshop with the World Bank to align ongoing development projects with Egypt's new 2023-2027 national strategy. The workshop focused on overseeing project implementation, enhancing coordination with the World Bank's missions, and outlining the institution's evolving role in Egypt's development. Dr. Al-Mashat emphasized the importance of international partnerships with the World Bank, which play a crucial role in advancing Egypt's development vision, including investments in human capital, sustainable infrastructure, private sector empowerment, and addressing shared concerns like climate change. The World Bank presented its current portfolio of 14 projects worth $6.9 billion in various sectors, discussing alignment with Egypt's strategy and its expanding role in global development efforts, particularly in climate action and COP27 presidency.
records.institution: Egyptian Minister of International Cooperation and Governor for Egypt at the World Bank

records.title: Egyptian Advisor to the Minister of Agriculture: The State is Making Great Efforts to Provide Strategic Goods
records.description: Dr. Fahim, in a statement to the Middle East News Agency, emphasized that self-sufficiency is a matter of national security, and ensuring food availability is a goal pursued by most countries. He acknowledged challenges such as limited agricultural land and land fragmentation but mentioned efforts to utilize available resources for secure self-sufficiency in various commodities. He added that the Ministry of Agriculture is making significant efforts to achieve agricultural development through horizontal expansion projects, including reclaiming new lands or vertical expansion by developing new high-quality and productive crop varieties to maximize land and water utilization. The expansion of agricultural land in new areas is considered one of the key strategies to support self-sufficiency policies and reduce the gap. This includes reclaiming desert areas to increase agricultural acreage, with notable projects like Toshka Al Khair spanning 1.1 million acres, the massive New Delta project covering over 2.2 million acres, the North and Central Sinai development project spanning 456,000 acres, and the Egyptian countryside development project covering 1.5 million acres. Dr. Fahim also highlighted the importance of agricultural hubs, which have provided stability during global crises by ensuring a consistent supply of vegetables. Egypt remained unaffected by these crises due to the abundance of agricultural crops, marking a significant advancement in crop productivity and quality. He explained that the government encourages individuals and the private sector to establish agricultural projects that maximize the utilization of land and water resources.

records.title: Expo 2023 Doha: Qatar Makes Noticeable Progress in Self Sufficiency from Agricultural Products
records.description: Qatar has made substantial progress in achieving self-sufficiency in agricultural products, driven by increased focus on plant and animal agriculture with strong support from the government and visionary leadership. Amidst challenges posed by climate change and global food security concerns, Qatar has prioritized agricultural development, emphasizing self-sufficiency and sustainability through innovative techniques. These efforts have included technology investment, research and development, and food control measures, in alignment with national development goals and Qatar National Vision 2030. The Ministry of Municipality has played a pivotal role in driving agricultural production forward, providing support to farmers, livestock breeders, and fisheries. Qatar's dedication to enhancing food security is reflected in its rise in the Global Food Security Index rankings and its commitment to reducing dependence on groundwater, promoting sustainable agriculture, and adopting modern irrigation systems. A new National Food Security Strategy 2024-2030 is set to further boost local production and technology adoption, ensuring food self-sufficiency and sustainable agriculture practices. Qatar's livestock sector has also thrived, contributing significantly to self-sufficiency rates in animal products. With various initiatives, agricultural exhibitions, and green projects, Qatar is on a path towards a sustainable and secure food future, demonstrating its commitment to achieving comprehensive economic development and food security.

records.title: ADAFSA to Develop Integrated Strategy to Reduce Food Loss & Waste
records.description: In alignment with its pivotal role in agricultural and food sustainability in Abu Dhabi, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) is amplifying its efforts to devise an integrated strategy for minimizing food loss and waste (FLW) and enhancing production chain efficiency. Revealed on World Day of Awareness on Food Loss and Waste on September 29, this strategy encompasses several key pillars such as revising agricultural and food safety legislation, launching behavior-altering programs from production to consumption, implementing training for food agricultural establishments' personnel, and initiating awareness campaigns to encourage rational consumption. Among the significant measures, ADAFSA is updating legislative systems to reduce food spoilage by promoting good handling practices throughout the food chain, and working federally to align food labelling and expiration dates regulations with international standards. To curb loss post-harvest, farmers are advised on rapid cooling and optimal storage temperatures for fruits, planting suitable varieties for the UAE climate, and employing agricultural technologies to boost production efficiency while leveraging renewable resources like solar energy and recycled water. Moreover, ADAFSA has issued guidelines and 36 extension manuals covering 41 crops for post-harvest handling, aiming to extend shelf life, decrease production loss by 20-50%, and support food security. Special training is provided to food sector workers on safe food handling to prevent spoilage or contamination, alongside a guidance manual for the catering sector on reducing food waste, aligned with ADAFSA's strategic plan and food security system. ADAFSA also collaborates with entities like the UAE Red Crescent for educational workshops in educational institutions, urging all food chain stakeholders to adopt responsible behaviors from farm to table to mitigate FLW, particularly from harvest to retail stages, and promoting consumer education on proper food storage and consumption based on need, aiming for a substantial reduction in food waste and a sustainable food security framework.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: Egypt, a major wheat consumer in Africa, is in discussions to acquire 1 million metric tons of wheat from Russia, the world's leading whe...
records.description: Egypt, a major wheat consumer in Africa, is in discussions to acquire 1 million metric tons of wheat from Russia, the world's leading wheat exporter, as reported by undisclosed sources via Bloomberg. Russia is set to produce 92 million metric tons of wheat and export 46 million metric tons for the 2022-2023 marketing year. However, Egypt's attempt to secure Russian wheat previously faced obstacles due to pricing objections from Moscow, leading Egypt to explore alternatives such as procuring wheat from France and Bulgaria. This disruption in wheat trade is a consequence of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, both significant wheat suppliers to Egypt, resulting in fluctuating prices and trade patterns. Egypt has consequently diversified its wheat suppliers, including purchasing from India and entering a $500 million deal with a UAE company for a five-year wheat supply, as economic challenges persist due to the Ukraine conflict.
records.institution: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Ghana and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) celebrated their 63-year-long cordial relations, expressing their commitment to deepen develo...
records.description: Ghana and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) celebrated their 63-year-long cordial relations, expressing their commitment to deepen development cooperation and bilateral ties. During the celebration of the 93rd KSA National Day in Accra, Ghana's Interior Minister, Ambrose Dery, and the KSA Ambassador to Ghana, Sultan Abdul-Rahman Al-Dhakel, commended their countries' strong relations. Mr. Dery conveyed Ghana's warm felicitations to King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Prince Mohammad Bin Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. He highlighted Ghana's collaboration with Saudi Arabia in maintaining global peace and its appreciation for support in various sectors like energy, education, health, humanitarian assistance, agriculture, and infrastructure development. Mr. Dery emphasized the need to enhance private sector cooperation and invited Saudi investors to leverage Ghana's natural resources, stability, and the presence of the Africa Continental Free Trade Area secretariat to do business in Ghana.

records.title: Morocco's National Interprofessional Office for Cereals and Legumes (ONICL) has disclosed that subsidies will be provided for soft wheat...
records.description: Morocco's National Interprofessional Office for Cereals and Legumes (ONICL) has disclosed that subsidies will be provided for soft wheat imports from October 1 to December 31, as approved by the Finance and Agriculture Ministries. This initiative follows a revision of grain subsidies to motivate wheat importers to opt for more cost-effective grain suppliers, aiming to ease the import of cheaper Black Sea grain despite the proximity advantage of Western European suppliers, particularly France. This subsidy program, which intends to bridge the price gap between the cost of wheat and the reference import price of MAD 270 (US$27) per quintal, is part of Morocco's response to last year’s severe drought that impacted agricultural output negatively. In the 2022-2023 season, Morocco witnessed a 61.8% surge in cereal production to 55.1 million quintals, reflecting recovery efforts. Furthermore, the recent re-opening of wheat import avenues from Russia, as emphasized by the National Federation of Mills President and the Russian ambassador to Morocco, denotes a stride in diversifying wheat import sources, potentially enhancing Morocco's food security and economic resilience amidst agricultural challenges.
records.institution: Morocco’s National Interprofessional Office for Cereals and Legumes (ONICL)

records.title: The inaugural InFlavour event in Saudi Arabia is set to bring together over 200 prominent investors and venture capitalists, including fi...
records.description: The inaugural InFlavour event in Saudi Arabia is set to bring together over 200 prominent investors and venture capitalists, including figures like HRH Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed Al Saud and Andrew D. Ive, to explore opportunities in Saudi Arabia's rapidly growing food service market. With the Kingdom's Ministry of Investment projecting a conservative annual growth rate of six percent in the sector over the next five years, reaching $30.47 billion by 2029, InFlavour aims to be a key industry summit. It will focus on sustainability, technology, and social impact, reflecting Saudi Arabia's potential transformation in the food industry due to increasing tourism and major development programs like The Red Sea Project and Qiddiya. InFlavour, curated by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment Water & Agriculture (MEWA), will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of the industry, fostering innovation, and supporting food security initiatives.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water & Agriculture (MEWA)

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Dubai-based Amea Power is set to develop an $86 million, 120-megawatt solar power project in Tunisia, marking a significant step in the n...
records.description: Dubai-based Amea Power is set to develop an $86 million, 120-megawatt solar power project in Tunisia, marking a significant step in the nation's move towards clean energy. This venture is noted as Tunisia's "first large-scale, privately financed" solar project, making it one of the major infrastructure public-private partnership endeavors in over a decade, as stated by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a World Bank Group member. The IFC, alongside the African Development Bank, will provide a combined debt financing of up to $52 million, aiding various project phases from development to maintenance in Tunisia's Kairouan governorate. This project, part of Tunisia's 2018 renewable energy initiative and ratified by its government last March, aligns with Tunisia's goal of attaining 35% clean energy by 2030, addressing its climate vulnerability and reducing reliance on imported hydrocarbons for electricity. The Kairouan solar project also aims to boost the competitiveness of Tunisia's power sector and contribute towards macro-fiscal stability. IFC's Hela Cheikhrouhou emphasized the project's alignment with enabling South-South investments from Gulf Co-operation Council nations to emerging markets. Amea Power, expanding its clean energy investments across 20 countries, continues to support solar and wind projects in the region, reflecting its commitment to aiding Tunisia's clean energy transition amidst market challenges post-Covid pandemic.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: Uterra Middle East Agro Industries, part of the multinational UniPax Investment Group, is investing $20 million over the next three years...
records.description: Uterra Middle East Agro Industries, part of the multinational UniPax Investment Group, is investing $20 million over the next three years in Ras Al Khaimah's inaugural organic soil fertiliser project, aiming to transform agriculture, tackle environmental issues, and foster sustainability. Acquiring a 33,000 m2 plot in Al Ghail Industrial Zone, Uterra plans a sustainable biosphere cluster to produce high-efficiency microbiological organic fertiliser and pioneer unique plant cultivation methods, alongside farming fruits, vegetables, berries, and organic animal husbandry. Targeting both UAE and global markets, the initiative seeks to provide ample high-quality, eco-friendly products under the 'uTerra' brand, devoid of pesticides, harmful chemicals, or GMOs, promoting healthy food sources and mitigating soil resource depletion. Uterra founder Dr Anatoli Unitsky cited Ras Al Khaimah's socio-economic developmental vision and logistical advantages, including the forthcoming Etihad Rail, as key factors for location choice, also appreciating the support from RAKEZ (Ras Al Khaimah Economic Zone) in facilitating the setup. RAKEZ Group CEO Ramy Jallad welcomed Uterra's alignment with their commitment to sustainability and innovation, emphasizing the project's potential in addressing environmental challenges, advancing a sustainable agricultural sector, and contributing to a greener, responsible economic growth in line with the Year of Sustainability.

records.title: Egypt's Foreign Minister Sameh Shoukry, along with his Greek and Cypriot counterparts, expressed commitment towards exploring new avenues...
records.description: Egypt's Foreign Minister Sameh Shoukry, along with his Greek and Cypriot counterparts, expressed commitment towards exploring new avenues of tripartite cooperation. They underscored the necessity of convening the 10th summit among their nations and expediting the implementation of joint projects in sectors like gas, electricity, tourism, transportation, and agriculture. Discussions also touched upon enhancing coordination within the East Mediterranean Gas Forum to optimize gas resources utilization, and regional crises such as the Libyan conflict, Palestinian territories' situation, Sudan's developments, and the Russia-Ukraine crisis. Shoukry further briefed on the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam negotiations, emphasizing water security. Post-meeting, Shoukry held bilateral discussions with Cyprus and Greece to enhance economic, investment, and sectoral cooperation, reflecting on the significant strides made in their tripartite collaboration over the past decade across political, energy, economic, and defense fronts, and reiterated Egypt's focus on solidifying regional cooperation and investment ties.

records.title: H.E. Abdulla bin Touq al Marri Unveils Key Pillars for Transforming UAE Food and Agriculture Sector into Global Power
records.description: The UAE Minister of Economy, H.E. Abdulla bin Touq al Marri, has outlined a comprehensive strategy aimed at elevating the UAE's food and agriculture sector to a global powerhouse. The strategy focuses on increasing the sector's contribution to GDP by $10 billion and creating 20,000 jobs within the next five years. The seven key pillars of this strategic direction include nurturing local innovation, fostering a UAE-first culture in the food supply chain, providing support to farmers for agri-food innovation and sustainability, establishing global regulatory standards, ensuring sufficient funding for industry players, promoting world-class research and development, enabling diversification and access to new markets, and developing the next generation of farmers. The UAE's food and agriculture sector has grown significantly, contributing to economic development and playing a crucial role in global food logistics.

records.title: The Lulu Group, a prominent UAE-based retailer, is embarking on the establishment of a sourcing and export hub in Poland to serve Central...
records.description: The Lulu Group, a prominent UAE-based retailer, is embarking on the establishment of a sourcing and export hub in Poland to serve Central Europe. The group has inked two separate Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with Polish government entities, Olsztyn Mazury Airport, and the Polish Investment & Trade Agency, to realize this initiative. The first MoU outlines plans for Lulu to create a new facility at Olsztyn Mazury Airport in northeastern Poland, which will function as a gateway for sourcing, packaging, and exporting fresh produce such as apples, berries, cheeses, meat, and other packaged food items to the MENA, India, and the Far East regions. The second MoU with the Polish Investment & Trade Agency will facilitate a smooth investment process and identify business opportunities across Poland. Initially, the group aims to export products worth 50 million euros, with expectations of substantial growth as new product lines are introduced. This endeavor aligns with Lulu Group's strategy to enhance food security and ensure a stable supply in the market through global sourcing and food processing units.

records.title: Egypt is considering importing nearly 500,000 tons of wheat from France and Bulgaria after Russia halted its supply of Russian grain.
records.description: Egypt is considering importing nearly 500,000 tons of wheat from France and Bulgaria after Russia halted its supply of Russian grain. This decision was made in response to Russia's objections regarding the pricing of a mega-deal and its efforts to impose an unofficial minimum price on grain transactions. Egypt, which has one of the highest per capita consumption rates of wheat globally, has faced challenges in wheat imports due to disruptions caused by the Russo-Ukrainian war and the end of the Black Sea Grain Initiative. Additionally, Egypt has been dealing with foreign currency shortages and economic instability. The country has recently deferred payments for wheat imports and sought financing from various sources to address its economic challenges. Egypt's strategic wheat reserves are reported to be sufficient for five months of local consumption.

records.title: Egypt is reportedly in discussions with an Abu Dhabi-based bank to secure a loan facility aimed at financing wheat purchases from Kazakhs...
records.description: Egypt is reportedly in discussions with an Abu Dhabi-based bank to secure a loan facility aimed at financing wheat purchases from Kazakhstan, as reported by three traders to Reuters. This potential move could offer Egypt a more cost-effective alternative to Russian grain, which has been a significant source of wheat for Egypt but recently presented challenges due to pricing disputes. Egypt has been working to reduce its import expenses as it grapples with a foreign currency shortage. Talks regarding this loan arrangement are still in the early stages, with negotiations covering the price, quantity of wheat, and loan value. The specific Abu Dhabi-based bank involved has not been disclosed.
records.institution: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Egyptian snacks giant Edita Food has secured two medium-term loan agreements totaling EGP 390 million (US$12.60 million) to finance inves...
records.description: Egyptian snacks giant Edita Food has secured two medium-term loan agreements totaling EGP 390 million (US$12.60 million) to finance investments related to its newly acquired frozen bakery segment for the next seven years. The first loan of EGP 190 million ($6.1 million) will be used for acquisition finance to cover 50% of the acquisition amount related to Fancy Foods. The remaining EGP 200 million ($6.5 million) will fund the investment cost for the new subsidiary, Edita Frozen for Food Industries. Edita Foods entered the frozen bakery segment through the acquisition of Fancy Foods S.A.E., which specializes in the production of frozen foods. This move is expected to expand Edita Foods' business portfolio in the frozen food segment and strengthen its presence in the local food industry. The company's strong performance in Q1 2023, including a 146.20% YoY increase in net profits after tax, has further supported these investments.

records.title: CARE Morocco, a humanitarian organization, has initiated the distribution of relief supplies to families affected by the earthquake in th...
records.description: CARE Morocco, a humanitarian organization, has initiated the distribution of relief supplies to families affected by the earthquake in the Atlas Mountains on September 8th. The organization plans to assist up to 50,000 individuals in close coordination with Moroccan authorities. The initial distribution took place in Outghal village, part of the Aghouatim commune, providing blankets, food, water, and hygiene kits to families who have suffered extensive damage to their homes. Many of those affected have also lost their livelihoods, including farmers, tailors, and small-scale producers. CARE Morocco aims to support their economic recovery, with a focus on women and girls, and provide psychological support for the mental health impact caused by the disaster. This earthquake, measuring 6.8 on the Richter scale, was Morocco's most powerful in over a century and has resulted in significant casualties and damage. CARE Morocco, operating since 2008, is dedicated to promoting equal access to economic opportunities and works extensively in the affected region of Al Haouz province.

records.title: The Omani-Tunisian Olive Forum took place in the Green Mountain Governorate under the auspices of His Excellency Sheikh Hilal Said Al-Haj...
records.description: The Omani-Tunisian Olive Forum took place in the Green Mountain Governorate under the auspices of His Excellency Sheikh Hilal Said Al-Hajri, the Governor of the Interior. Organized by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources in collaboration with the Embassy of the Republic of Tunisia in Oman, the forum served as a platform for exchanging expertise and exploring investment prospects in cultivating various olive tree varieties. It also aimed to promote cooperation within the olive oil industry by showcasing diverse olive oil products and highlighting efforts in the development of olive cultivation and oil production.

records.title: Najran Becomes an Incubator for Saudi Agricultural Experiments
records.description: Agriculture plays a pivotal role in Saudi Arabia's food security, and the Najran region has become a hub for innovative agricultural experiments contributing to environmental sustainability. Farmer Ali Dhafir Al-Harith, for instance, has established a model farm with around 2,000 coffee trees and is expanding coffee plantations in collaboration with local farmers. The success of these experiments is attributed to the region's favorable environmental conditions, including fertile soil, freshwater availability, and moderate weather. Other farmers in Najran are also achieving success with crops like herbal stevia and finger limes, further enhancing agricultural diversity and food production in the Kingdom.

records.title: Sharjah Approves $71mln Al Mudina Water Tank
records.description: Sharjah has given the green light for the construction of the Al Mudina Water Tank project in the emirate's Central Region, with an estimated cost of AED 261 million ($71 million). The project, directed by HH Dr Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, will have a capacity of 6 million cubic meters, equivalent to 1.3 billion gallons of water. Its primary objective is to ensure a stable water supply in the region, benefiting agriculture and livestock projects. The tank will support the cultivation of wheat in Mleiha, with plans to expand wheat cultivation to 1,500 hectares in 2024. Additionally, it will facilitate cattle, poultry, sheep, and goat projects in the region.

records.title: Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad embarked on his first official trip to China in nearly two decades, signifying an effort to strengthen b...
records.description: Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad embarked on his first official trip to China in nearly two decades, signifying an effort to strengthen bilateral relations and initiate practical cooperation projects. Upon his arrival at Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport in East China's Zhejiang Province, President Assad was warmly welcomed. China-Syria relations, which have thrived for 67 years, are poised to deepen mutual political trust and cooperation in various sectors, reaching new heights. Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders will engage in extensive discussions with President Bashar Al-Assad on bilateral ties and mutual interests. Syria's visit to China marks its return to the international community after years of isolation, reflecting the changing dynamics in the Middle East. With Syria prioritizing reconstruction and development, China is expected to play a pivotal role in cooperative projects, considering the substantial potential for collaboration between the two nations, particularly in trade and agriculture. Syria's participation in China's Belt and Road initiative in January 2022 further underscores the likelihood of new collaborative efforts between the two countries.

records.title: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has taken significant steps to strengthen the UAE's Fodder Market by enterin...
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has taken significant steps to strengthen the UAE's Fodder Market by entering into collaborative agreements with Al Dahra Agriculture and Elite Agro Holding. These strategic partnerships aim to ensure a consistent supply of high-quality grass and concentrated fodder to support the country's thriving livestock sector. Al Dahra Agriculture, known for its expertise in cultivating and supplying animal fodder and food crops, will facilitate large-scale animal feed distribution through 15 dedicated outlets within the Fodder Market. Elite Agro Holding, a prominent local agricultural investment entity, will provide a wide range of high-quality animal feed through four designated outlets within the Fodder Market. These initiatives align with the UAE's goal of bolstering food security and promoting agricultural sustainability through partnerships with the private sector.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: The Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the World Bank Group's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), hosted two worksho...
records.description: The Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the World Bank Group's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), hosted two workshops in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, aimed at bolstering opportunities for the UAE's private sector in emerging economies. These workshops brought together government officials, business leaders, and investors, with MIGA presenting its array of financial products and services designed to enhance credit for entrepreneurs and facilitate business expansion in emerging markets. The collaboration is seen as a significant step in supporting sustainable economic development and job creation while mitigating risks for private investments in these emerging markets, ultimately contributing to the UAE's global business outreach and long-term economic growth.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is leveraging its space agency as a catalyst for accelerating its transition to carbon neutrality and esta...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is leveraging its space agency as a catalyst for accelerating its transition to carbon neutrality and establishing itself as a focal point for climate technology and research. Through initiatives like the National Space Strategy 2030, backed by substantial government investments, and the Space Data Center, facilitating access to space data for sustainability solutions, the UAE Space Agency is at the forefront of climate monitoring and mitigation efforts. By investing in satellite technology and data analysis, it aims to tackle climate change, enhance food security, and monitor environmental changes. These endeavors align with the UAE's broader commitment to combat climate change, diversify its energy mix, and promote clean and renewable energy sources, positioning the country as a global leader in climate technology and research, exemplifying its determination to drive climate action while advancing its space capabilities.

records.title: The Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has successfully purchased 3.8 million tons of wheat from local farmers during this ye...
records.description: The Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade has successfully purchased 3.8 million tons of wheat from local farmers during this year's harvest season, which ran from April to September. This procurement aligns with the government's initial plan to acquire four million tons of local wheat supplies from farmers during the season. The Ministry of Finance allocated 45 billion EGP (US$1.5 billion) to support this initiative, surpassing the previous year's allocation by over 19 billion EGP. The government also approved incentives to raise local wheat prices, encouraging greater production and aiming to reduce wheat imports, which currently account for a significant portion of Egypt's consumption due to high domestic demand.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Morocco’s King Launches Five-Year Reconstruction Program Worth $12bln in Earthquake-Hit Regions
records.description: King Mohammed VI of Morocco has launched a five-year reconstruction and general upgrading program for regions affected by the Al Haouz earthquake. The program has an overall budget of $12 billion (120 million DH) and will target six provinces and prefectures, impacting a population of 4.2 million. The program includes projects to rebuild dwellings, refurbish and upgrade affected infrastructure, strengthen socio-economic development, and promote local initiatives. It will also establish essential reserves in each region to swiftly respond to natural disasters. Funding will come from the general State budget, local authorities, a Special Solidarity Bank Account, donations, and international cooperation, with the Hassan II Fund contributing 2 billion dirhams. The King emphasized the importance of efficient governance and balancing development while respecting local heritage and traditions.

records.title: Oman Tackles Water Scarcity with Innovative Irrigation Techniques
records.description: To address potential water scarcity challenges, Oman, represented by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, is implementing several projects aimed at enhancing water efficiency in the agricultural sector. One key initiative is the Al Aflaj Agricultural Development Project, which seeks to replace traditional flood irrigation methods with modern irrigation systems like drip and spray irrigation. These systems are more water-efficient and can save up to 70 percent of water. The government also provides technical and financial support to farmers interested in transitioning to modern irrigation systems, offering engineering designs and irrigation schedules. Additionally, Oman explores innovative techniques, such as using treated sewage water and seawater for irrigation purposes, contributing to water conservation and increased agricultural production. These efforts are crucial for ensuring food security in Oman by preserving water resources and boosting agricultural output.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Elmedin Konaković, met with the Minister of Tourism and Chairman of the Board...
records.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Elmedin Konaković, met with the Minister of Tourism and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Saudi Fund for the Development of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Ahmed Aqeela Al-Khateeb, during the 78th session of the United Nations General Assembly. They discussed bilateral relations and common interests, emphasizing the strong and friendly relations between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Saudi Arabia. The meeting also addressed the liberalization of the visa regime between the two countries, with Minister Konaković welcoming Saudi Arabia's initiative to abolish the visa regime for holders of diplomatic and official passports. They also discussed simplifying the visa application process and exploring opportunities for economic cooperation, particularly in tourism, defense industry, agriculture, and food industry, with a focus on increasing investments in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Both sides expressed mutual interest in strengthening overall cooperation between the two nations through high-level visits.
records.institution: Saudi Fund for the Development of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

records.title: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture has introduced stringent punitive measures against individuals involved in envi...
records.description: The Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture has introduced stringent punitive measures against individuals involved in environmental pollution and damage to environmental sites. The ministry is actively working to incorporate violations and penalties into the executive regulations governing the rehabilitation of damaged environmental sites and the treatment of contaminated areas. According to these new regulations, individuals found guilty of tampering with and damaging land and environmental sites will be referred to the Public Prosecution, and they will be obliged to rectify the violation and rehabilitate the contaminated areas. The violations encompass providing false information or data related to environmental rehabilitation and treatment plans, with fines ranging from SR10,000 to SR100,000, depending on the severity of the incorrect information. Additionally, failure to implement the environmental rehabilitation and treatment plans may result in fines of SR15,000 for the first category of violation, SR30,000 for the second, and SR100,000 for the third. These rules aim to oversee the rehabilitation of damaged sites and the treatment of polluted areas, specifying the necessary terms and conditions and identifying which sites require attention.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Emirates Development Bank Underlines Commitment to UAE Food Security at 5th Future Food Forum
records.description: Emirates Development Bank (EDB) is actively participating in the fifth annual Future Food Forum to emphasize its commitment to enhancing food security in the UAE. This forum, taking place from September 20th to 21st, 2023, brings together prominent regional and international stakeholders in the food industry to bolster the sustainable future of the MENA region's food sector. Food security stands as one of EDB's five priority sectors, significantly contributing to the UAE's national development and economic diversification plans. EDB extends substantial financial support and tailored solutions to advance technology-driven local food production. Recently, EDB launched the AgriTech Loans Programme, dedicated to injecting essential capital into the agritech industry. This initiative aims to provide critical support in the form of favorable, longer-term loans of up to AED 5 million with a tenor of 10 years to local producers, farmers, agribusinesses, and food-related projects. Ahmed Al Naqbi, CEO of Emirates Development Bank, expressed, "As the UAE's development bank and a key financial engine for national economic development, food security is a top priority for us. We aspire to align with the objectives of the UAE National Food Security Strategy 2051 by offering value-added financing support to businesses, tailored agritech loans, and by fostering partnerships with emerging companies and key stakeholders. Our efforts reflect our dedication to advancing national agriculture industries and food production capabilities, positioning the UAE as a regional leader in both sectors."

records.title: The Future Food Forum 2023, the Middle East's largest annual gathering of industry leaders, commenced in Dubai, addressing key themes of...
records.description: The Future Food Forum 2023, the Middle East's largest annual gathering of industry leaders, commenced in Dubai, addressing key themes of food security, sustainability, innovation, and consumer well-being. The event, featuring over 70 prominent leaders and industry stakeholders, explores new trends and opportunities in the food industry. It was inaugurated by Abdulla Al Saleh, the Under Secretary of Foreign Trade and Industry at the UAE Ministry of Economy. The forum focuses on the theme of "Inspiring Sustainable Wellbeing," emphasizing self-reliant food supplies and agri-tech utilization for enhanced food security in the Middle East. Discussions also highlight the UAE's advancements in the F&B sector, innovations in 'Made in the UAE' products, and the importance of Emiratization in building a sustainable F&B ecosystem.

records.title: UAE Recruits More Than 40 ITTI Certified Assessors to Help Transform Factories Across Emirates
records.description: The Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MoIAT) in the UAE has certified over 40 assessors with the goal of facilitating technological transformations in factories across the Emirates. Recently, a group of 18 assessors completed training to support the implementation of the Industrial Technology Transformation Index (ITTI), an initiative under Operation 300bn. The ITTI, launched in 2023, is designed to assess the digital maturity and sustainability of factories, enabling them to create a roadmap for digital transformation and the adoption of Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies and sustainable practices. The assessors, selected from a pool of applicants with STEM degrees and extensive manufacturing and consultancy experience, underwent rigorous training to become proficient in ITTI methodologies and Industry 4.0 concepts. These certified assessors will play a vital role in helping companies maximize their capabilities and embark on their Industry 4.0 journey, ultimately enhancing industry competitiveness, promoting innovation, and supporting sustainability and resource efficiency in the industrial sector. The ITTI initiative is aligned with the UAE's vision of becoming a global hub for advanced manufacturing and investment.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MoIAT)

records.title: Syria and Cuba are actively exploring opportunities to strengthen cooperation across various domains, as discussed during conversations b...
records.description: Syria and Cuba are actively exploring opportunities to strengthen cooperation across various domains, as discussed during conversations between Syrian Finance Minister Kinan Yaghi and Cuban authorities. Their talks encompassed political, economic, commercial, cultural, scientific, and agricultural collaboration. Syria expressed its eagerness to enhance bilateral relations, particularly in science, universities, scientific research institutions, and the exchange of scholarships for undergraduate and graduate students.

records.title: LuLu Group International, the Abu Dhabi-based retail giant, has inaugurated its state-of-the-art sourcing, food processing, and export hu...
records.description: LuLu Group International, the Abu Dhabi-based retail giant, has inaugurated its state-of-the-art sourcing, food processing, and export hub in Italy, located at the World Trade Center Malpensa Airport Milan. This facility aims to strengthen food security and sourcing operations, not only in Italy but also from nearby European countries, ensuring a stable supply and pricing of food products. Over the next two years, LuLu Group plans to export food products valued at 200 million euros. The facility will focus on sourcing, processing, storing, packaging, and exporting high-quality food products to more than 255 LuLu Hypermarkets across GCC countries, Egypt, India, Indonesia, and Malaysia. It will include various categories such as cheeses, chocolates, fruit jams, sweet and puff pastries, organic pasta, extra-virgin olive oil, and high-quality sea salt from renowned Italian brands, as well as a wide range of fruits and vegetables. LuLu Group intends to promote Italian brands through "Italian Food Festivals" across its hypermarkets, working closely with the Italian Trade Agency. This project aims to create jobs in Italy and initially targets food exports worth 50 million euros, with a goal of reaching 200 million euros in two years, while also supporting Italy's agricultural sector through partnerships with farmers' cooperative societies.

records.title: National banks in the UAE are taking a leading role in advancing sustainable financing and climate initiatives, aligning with the governm...
records.description: National banks in the UAE are taking a leading role in advancing sustainable financing and climate initiatives, aligning with the government's vision of sustainable economic growth and achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. These banks have made substantial investments in sustainable financing, fostering the transition to a green economy and pioneering efforts in the region. For example, six major banks, including FAB, ADCB, ENBD, DIB, Mashreq, and ADIB, have collectively committed over AED 190 billion (US$51.8 billion) in green financing for projects related to renewable energy, waste-to-energy, and green technology. These initiatives are in line with the UAE's goal of promoting COP28 as a significant milestone in addressing climate change. Banks like FAB have committed to providing substantial green financing, while others like ADCB have joined the Climate Responsible Companies Pledge initiative to accelerate their contribution to achieving climate neutrality. Additionally, ADIB's environmental, social, and institutional governance strategy prioritizes green financing and investment initiatives. Emirates NBD has been actively involved in COP28 as a supporting partner, focusing on meaningful dialogue and measures to address climate change and achieve a climate-neutral future. Banks like Dubai Islamic Bank have issued significant sustainable sukuks, while Mashreq is committed to providing substantial sustainable financing. These banks play a pivotal role in combating climate change by encouraging sustainable investments in areas such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, sustainable agriculture, and waste management, ultimately supporting the UAE's transition to a sustainable future.

records.title: The Iraqi Parliament's Agriculture and Water Committee has disclosed that the Canadian government has allocated a grant exceeding $3.7 mi...
records.description: The Iraqi Parliament's Agriculture and Water Committee has disclosed that the Canadian government has allocated a grant exceeding $3.7 million to support the revitalization of the southern province marshlands and safeguard them from the impacts of climate change. Committee member Ibtisam Al-Hilali stated that this grant is part of the broader Iraqi Marshlands Revitalization project, which encompasses improving living conditions for rural inhabitants, providing clean drinking water, enhancing livestock, and combating illegal fishing in the marshes and southern regions of Iraq. The project's objectives encompass safeguarding the marshlands and their global heritage from drought and climate change, supplying freshwater to marshland residents through desalination projects, and preserving the region's wildlife. Iraq's southern marshlands have been grappling with a severe humanitarian and environmental crisis due to water scarcity, raising concerns of a repeat of the extensive marshland drying experienced in the 1990s, which poses threats to agriculture, fisheries, and wildlife resources in the area. This year, the region has faced severe drought due to reduced winter rainfall, compounded by neighboring countries' water-sharing encroachments and the closure of tributaries of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers originating in their territories.
records.institution: Iraqi Parliament's Agriculture and Water Committee

records.title: Tabuk Region in Saudi Arabia has become renowned for its agricultural development, particularly in date production.
records.description: Tabuk Region in Saudi Arabia has become renowned for its agricultural development, particularly in date production. The region boasts over 40 varieties of palm trees, with the Halwa Tayma palm being the most productive. Tabuk is home to 1,012,499 palm trees, yielding an annual production of 51 tons of dates, according to the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture's Tabuk branch. The high productivity is attributed to diligent farmers who adhere to the highest care standards throughout the cultivation process. Tabuk dates are highly sought after for their exceptional taste, influenced by the region's soil quality and access to fresh water. Dates are not only delicious but also nutritious, rich in iron, potassium, calcium, and fiber, as well as vitamins B and A and proteins.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.title: Pakistan's Ministry of Climate Change has entered into a collaboration with UAE's Blue Carbon to tap into economic opportunities within f...
records.description: Pakistan's Ministry of Climate Change has entered into a collaboration with UAE's Blue Carbon to tap into economic opportunities within forestry, aligning with global climate objectives and prioritizing carbon reduction initiatives and their community advantages. The ministry recently organized a four-day technical workshop in partnership with UAE's Blue Carbon, drawing participation from representatives of provincial forestry departments, Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), and Gilgit-Baltistan. The primary objective of the workshop was to assess the potential for Pakistan's Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector to generate carbon credits, specifically Internationally Transferable Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. Discussions during the workshop underscored Pakistan's forest resources and their suitability for Article 6 mechanisms, paving the way for potential collaboration with Blue Carbon in this regard.

records.title: The United Arab Emirates and Serbia are in the process of negotiating a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to enhance ec...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates and Serbia are in the process of negotiating a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to enhance economic collaboration. This agreement, initiated during high-level talks in Dubai, reflects the strengthening trade and investment ties between the two nations. In the first half of 2023, bilateral non-oil trade exceeded $57.6 million, making the UAE the third-largest market for Serbian exports in the Middle East. The CEPA aims to reduce or eliminate customs duties, remove trade barriers, protect intellectual property rights, and support small and medium-sized enterprises. Additionally, it seeks to bolster cooperation in various sectors, including aviation, agriculture, construction, real estate, defense industries, and more, paving the way for increased economic growth and collaboration.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of State for Foreign Trade

Almheiri highlighted the importance of climate action, emphasizing the role of science, technology, and innovation in addressing current development challenges. She also discussed UAE-Cuba relations in food and agriculture sectors, as well as preparations for COP28, which the UAE will host. records.title: Algeria and Morocco, both significant players in Africa's wheat trade, have shifted away from French wheat in favor of Russian wheat due...
records.description: Algeria and Morocco, both significant players in Africa's wheat trade, have shifted away from French wheat in favor of Russian wheat due to deteriorating diplomatic relations between the North African nations and France. Alexandre Marie, chief analyst for Agritel, estimated that France would need to export 4.3 million tonnes of common wheat to Algeria and Morocco in the 2023/2024 season. However, this represents a significant decline from previous years when France regularly shipped over 7 million tonnes to these countries. French wheat exports to Algeria and Morocco have been diminishing as both nations increasingly turn to Russia for their wheat imports. Changes in import policies and price competitiveness have contributed to this shift, with Russian wheat often being more affordable. Additionally, the strained diplomatic relations between France and Morocco, and to some extent, Algeria, have played a role in the decline of French wheat exports to these North African countries.

records.description: Algeria is actively pursuing potential investments in renewable energy and green hydrogen initiatives, marking a shift towards sustainability. Senior representatives from the state-owned Sonatrach oil company and Sonelgaz, responsible for electricity and natural gas distribution, will engage in discussions with major US oil corporations, including ExxonMobil, Chevron, and Occidental Petroleum, during the Algerian-US Forum meetings in Washington from November 7 to 9. This effort reflects Algeria's commitment to exploring opportunities for renewable energy projects, particularly in the realm of green hydrogen. Additionally, the talks will encompass other projects, notably fertilizer production to support Algeria's agriculture sector. Ismail Shaikhoon, the head of the Algerian-US Business Council, emphasized the primary focus on establishing US-backed renewable energy initiatives within Algeria.

records.description: Egypt is poised to launch its MisrSat-2 satellite in December 2023, a remote sensing satellite designed to monitor climate change, desertification, land degradation, and Egypt's crucial water resources. Developed with Chinese assistance and supported by a $92 million grant from China, MisrSat-2 will play a pivotal role in enhancing resource planning, land management, agricultural productivity, and urban planning within Egypt. The satellite's creation marks a significant milestone in Sino-Egyptian collaboration and positions Egypt as the first African nation capable of establishing its space program. EgyptSat-2 will be transported to China for launch by the end of the year, with Egypt's space agency, EgSA, also working on plans to establish the African Development Satellite in partnership with other African nations and a remote-sensing camera for the International Space Station's Bartolomeo platform, further solidifying Egypt's leadership in African space technology.

records.title: Major Agri Initiatives to Strengthen Oman’s Food Security
records.description: Oman, represented by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, is taking proactive steps to promote research and development within the agricultural sector, with the aim of enhancing food security. These initiatives encompass the development of new crop varieties, pest-resistant plants, and sustainable farming practices. Among the key initiatives is the Omani Seed Bank, designed to collect and preserve seeds of local crops, which can be utilized to develop new environmentally suitable crop varieties for Oman. The seed bank also provides seeds to farmers to help improve their yields. Another noteworthy initiative is the Oman Plant Protection Center, specializing in conducting research on crop pests and diseases and formulating strategies for their control. Additionally, the center offers training to farmers on pest management techniques. The government is also investing in research related to sustainable agricultural practices, such as drought-resistant crops and water-saving irrigation methods. These efforts reflect Oman's commitment to strengthening its agricultural sector and ensuring food security in the face of challenges like climate change.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water & Agriculture Sector and Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) are anticipated to initiate...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Environment, Water & Agriculture Sector and Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) are anticipated to initiate the tendering process for the Al Shuqaiq 4 Independent Water Plant (IWP) project in the first quarter of 2024, as revealed by a knowledgeable source. The project encompasses the development of a desalination plant with a daily capacity of 400,000 cubic meters under a build-own-operate (BOO) agreement lasting 25 years. Project completion and commissioning are slated for the fourth quarter of 2026.

records.title: ADAFSA Implements Integrated Strategy to Develop Date Palm Cultivation, Production in Abu Dhabi
records.description: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) has announced the implementation of a comprehensive strategy aimed at advancing date palm cultivation and production in Abu Dhabi. This strategy is designed to enhance food security and safeguard the biological security of farms within the emirate. It encompasses several programs, including the Integrated Date Palm Management Programme, Good Post-Harvest Practices for Dates, and the Integrated Date Palm Pest Management Programme. In the initial part of this year, ADAFSA conducted a thorough inspection of 22,581 palm tree farms, inspecting over 6.7 million palm trees for pests. This survey covered various regions, with a significant portion in Al Ain. Subsequently, pest control measures were enacted based on the survey's findings, as part of ADAFSA's Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program for palm trees. On the occasion of Arab Date Palm Day, ADAFSA emphasized the sector's development and sustainability, encouraging farmers to adopt best agricultural practices, reduce pesticide usage, transition to organic cultivation, and plant commercially viable date palm varieties. The Authority highlighted the achievements of its Date IPM Programme in controlling pests, employing traps to minimize pesticide usage and effectively manage pests while ensuring environmentally safe practices. The strategy reflects ADAFSA's commitment to fostering the date palm sector's growth and ensuring the production of high-quality, pesticide-free dates in Abu Dhabi.
records.institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.description: Turkey is currently engaged in discussions with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) regarding the production of hydrogen and the development of an offshore wind facility, according to the country's Energy Minister, Alparslan Bayraktar. The agreements, valued at approximately $29.7 billion, were signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in July. The Emirati companies involved are interested in Turkey's energy transformation project, which aims to produce 3.5 gigawatts of solar energy and 1.5 gigawatts of wind energy annually. Negotiations for hydrogen production from wind energy are ongoing, with the participation of the Abu Dhabi Development Fund (ADQ) and European companies. Additionally, discussions are underway for an offshore wind farm project in Turkey's Black Sea region as part of the country's goal to generate 5,000 megawatts of wind energy by 2035. Furthermore, the UAE has expressed interest in Turkey's gas hub project, which was initially proposed by Russia for the Eastern Thrace region.

records.description: Egyptian cabinet ministers convened to expedite the "Kitchener Drain" de-pollution project in North Egypt, seeking to enhance the efficiency of Egypt's largest agricultural drain and improve local health and environmental conditions. This initiative, funded by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (ERBD) and the European Investment Bank (EIB) through soft-term loans totaling $444 million, was discussed by officials in the New Administrative Capital. The ministerial committee overseeing the project, formed in 2020, emphasized the need to accelerate execution. Water Resources Minister Hani Suweilim outlined the Ministry's role in constructing sewage stations, bridges, and monitoring systems for sewage water. International Cooperation Minister Ranya Al-Mashat stressed the importance of stronger coordination among project stakeholders. The Kitchener Drain, a major farming and de-pollution channel, spans nearly 69 km and serves over 11 million people in 182 villages in Lower Egypt. It suffers from severe pollution due to domestic wastewater, uncontrolled solid waste, industrial discharges, and agricultural runoff, causing significant environmental, economic, and social damage. The EU loan will fund various aspects of waste management and environmental improvement along the drain.

records.title: The Sovereign Fund of Egypt (TSFE) has reached a preliminary agreement with Actis, a British direct investment company, to purchase the G...
records.description: The Sovereign Fund of Egypt (TSFE) has reached a preliminary agreement with Actis, a British direct investment company, to purchase the Gabal El-Zeit wind farm for $350 million. This deal is expected to be finalized in early November, subject to Actis completing the due diligence process and obtaining approval from the New and Renewable Energy Authority. The agreed-upon value for the deal is higher than Actis' initial offer of $300 million made in April when the station was first put up for sale by the sovereign fund. The Gabal El-Zeit wind farm, located in the Red Sea governorate, has a capacity of 580 megawatts. Hala El-Said, Egypt's Minister of Planning and Economic Development, confirmed the initial agreement, mentioning that Egypt received five offers for the station but did not disclose further details. The sale is based on an energy tariff price of 2.4 US cents per kilowatt-hour, with 25% to be paid in Egyptian pounds, and the buyer will have land usage rights for 25 years.

records.title: Oman aims to triple its wheat production to approximately 7,000 tons in 2023, compared to 2,167 tons in 2022.
records.description: Oman aims to triple its wheat production to approximately 7,000 tons in 2023, compared to 2,167 tons in 2022. This ambitious increase in wheat production serves three main goals: enhancing food security, supporting sustainable development in agriculture, and providing new sources of income for Omani farmers. The area allocated for wheat cultivation has been expanded to 6,000 acres in the current year, compared to 2,422 acres in 2022. About 1,900 Omani farmers are expected to contribute to this growing production. The government has allocated a budget of 5 million Omani rials to support wheat cultivation, aiming to promote research and development, expand wheat cultivation, and enhance marketing strategies. Additionally, the ministry provides financial support and technical guidance to farmers, including training in sustainable agricultural practices, effective pest and disease management, and the adoption of modern technologies like drip irrigation and precision farming. These efforts aim to create a more resilient and sustainable food system for Oman in the years ahead.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: In August 2023, Saudi Arabian ports experienced a notable annual increase of 4.79% in cargo operations, handling a total of 721,629 conta...
records.description: In August 2023, Saudi Arabian ports experienced a notable annual increase of 4.79% in cargo operations, handling a total of 721,629 containers, as reported by the Saudi Ports Authority, also known as Mawani. This growth was attributed to ongoing development efforts aimed at enhancing operational and logistical performance. During the same period, the number of exported containers rose by 5.98% to reach 218,051 containers, while imported containers increased by 1.91%, totaling 226,738 containers. Transshipment containers witnessed a 6.29% yearly increase, reaching 276,840 in August 2023. However, food cargo experienced a 29.48% decline, falling to 1,570,665 tons, and overall cargo handled by Mawani decreased by 17.2% to 24,118,698 tons compared to the same period last year. Livestock also surged by 273.82% to 557,849 cattle heads in August 2023, and maritime traffic increased by 8%, with approximately 1,026 ships compared to 950 in August 2022.

records.title: MHP, Tanmiah Food Sign Deal in Fresh Saudi Food-Security Move
records.description: Poultry groups MHP and Tanmiah Food Company have formed a joint venture to enhance Saudi Arabia's food security. The partnership will involve farming operations, including a hatchery and a feed mill, with an investment of SR 200 million ($53.3 million) split between MHP and Tanmiah Food's subsidiary Desert Hills Veterinary Services (DHV). DHV will own 55% of the venture, which is expected to produce approximately 175 million hatching eggs annually. This initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 strategy, aimed at diversifying the country's economy and improving food security. The collaboration aims to integrate international expertise with local insights to meet Saudi Arabia's food security goals.

Minister Al Marar emphasized the importance of these meetings in identifying new opportunities for economic growth, prosperity, and elevated bilateral cooperation. The meeting concluded with the signing of the Joint Committee's minutes, and both sides expressed appreciation for the efforts involved in convening the committee, highlighting the significance of continued dialogue among relevant authorities in both public and private sectors.

records.title: UAE's Economy is no Longer Fully Dependent on Oil
records.description: Mariam bint Mohammed Almheiri, UAE Minister of Climate Change, highlighted the nation's pragmatic approach to sustainability during her address at the 12th edition of the International Government Communication Forum (IGCF). She praised UAE leaders for their visionary moves toward sustainability, emphasizing that the country's approach is grounded in reality and practicality, even as an oil-based economy. Almheiri noted the UAE's leadership in solar energy and its plans to triple solar energy production by 2030. She urged individuals to adopt sustainability as a lifestyle and emphasized the importance of environmentally conscious choices in everyday life. She also highlighted initiatives such as the Al Barakah nuclear plant, investments in renewable energy in Africa, smart farming, and environmental conservation efforts. Additionally, she mentioned the UAE's preparations for COP28, where global leaders will discuss concrete steps to protect the Earth.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Elsayed Elkosayer, has announced significant increases in funding for farmers and a...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Elsayed Elkosayer, has announced significant increases in funding for farmers and agricultural projects through the Agricultural Bank of Egypt (ABE). The ABE will provide approximately EGP 7 billion per year in financing for farmers and crops, with an additional annual EGP 500 million in state support. The minister also highlighted the ABE's efforts to assist farmers and peasants with outstanding debts by deferring their installment payments, benefiting around 330,000 farmers with a combined debt of EGP 9 billion. The ABE offers various financing programs for individuals and companies involved in agriculture and livestock, including support for land reclamation, greenhouse cultivation, and agro-based industries. These initiatives aim to boost production, promote development in the agricultural sector, and align with the state's sustainable development strategy. Additionally, the ABE plays a crucial role in rural development, supports micro-enterprises, empowers women and youth, and enhances access to banking and financing services in rural areas. Minister Elkosayer also highlighted the success of the national veal project, with funding reaching EGP 8 billion for 43,000 beneficiaries, totaling 500,000 heads of livestock. Moreover, he mentioned the completion of the "Falah Card" system, developed in collaboration with the ABE, which facilitates access to subsidies and benefits for farmers and contributes to financial inclusion by evolving into the Meeza card. The card can be easily replaced if lost or damaged at the nearest ABE branch within 15 days. These initiatives demonstrate Egypt's commitment to supporting its agricultural sector, rural communities, and sustainable development goals.
records.institution: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.description: Iraq's Prime Minister, Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, has announced that the country boasts a year's worth of wheat reserves following a successful harvest season. This declaration was made during a recent interview. With a population of 43 million, Iraq typically requires between 4.5 million and 5 million tons of wheat annually. The impressive yield in 2023 reflects a shift towards cultivating wheat in desert regions using groundwater due to a decline in river water availability caused by the country's worst recorded drought. The Iraqi Minister of Agriculture, Abbas Jabr, projected wheat production to reach four million tons for the 2022-2023 season, attributing the increase to the government's cultivation plans in desert and other areas. Iraq had been self-sufficient in wheat production before the war in Ukraine but faced challenges such as water scarcity and desertification, leading to a decline in local production, necessitating wheat imports to meet demand.

records.title: King Calls for Comprehensive Plan to Develop Tourism, Agriculture in Madaba
records.description: During his visit to Madaba, His Majesty King Abdullah called for the formulation of a comprehensive plan, in collaboration with the local community, to harness the tourism and agriculture potential of the region, with a focus on alleviating poverty and unemployment. He emphasized the importance of bolstering agricultural activities in Madaba and the Dhiban District, particularly in wheat and grain cultivation, to enhance Jordan's food security. The King also stressed the need for improved tourist services to prolong visitors' stays, as the number of tourists to Madaba has doubled compared to the previous year. The attendees expressed gratitude for His Majesty's commitment to modernization, the welfare of Jordanians, and support for Palestinians, as well as his dedication to safeguarding Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem. Prime Minister Bisher Khasawneh highlighted the government's plans to develop the Fortress of Machaerus as a key tourist attraction, connecting it to the Baptism Site as part of the Vatican-approved Christian pilgrimage trail. The government is also exploring additional incentives for investors in Madaba's industrial city. Projects initiated through Royal initiatives in Madaba, valued at over JD23 million, have covered education, youth empowerment, healthcare, social and municipal services, and support for productive ventures. The meeting was attended by various officials, including Chief of the Royal Hashemite Court Yousef Issawi, Interior Minister Mazen Farraya, and Madaba Governor Nayef Hedayat.
