records.description: Red Sea Global (RSG), the developer of Amaala, has signed a 25-year concession agreement with EDF (Électricité de France) and Masdar to develop a multi-utilities infrastructure facility for Amaala. Amaala, like The Red Sea, will be powered entirely by solar energy, reducing CO2 emissions by nearly half a million tonnes annually. The facility includes an off-grid renewable energy system, a battery energy storage solution, a desalination plant, and a wastewater treatment plant, all powered by renewables. Amaala's renewable supply system can generate up to 410,000 MWh per annum, with a 700 MWh battery storage facility ensuring continuous renewable power. The contract covers design, construction, operation, and associated infrastructure. The utilities concession agreement has an initial 25-year term with the option to extend and supports Amaala's net-zero goals, focusing on a 30% conservation benefit to local ecosystems by 2040.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and India have signed a bilateral agreement to strengthen the investment climate in both countries, with 47 memorandums of u...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and India have signed a bilateral agreement to strengthen the investment climate in both countries, with 47 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) signed, including agreements between private and public sector entities. The deputy minister of investor outreach at the Saudi Ministry of Investment, Badr Al-Badr, highlighted the growing trade ties between the two nations, with Indian exports to Saudi Arabia reaching $10.7 billion in 2022, and Saudi exports to India reaching $42 billion in the same year. Both sides expressed a strong commitment to developing their bilateral relationship further and exploring investment opportunities across various sectors, including information and communications technology, entrepreneurship, chemicals, energy, and advanced manufacturing. Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's ambitious economic plan, has improved the business environment and made it more attractive for investors. The India-Saudi Investment Forum coincided with the official state visit to India by Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, further enhancing economic ties between the two countries.

records.title: Saudi Arabia and India have solidified their economic ties by signing over 50 agreements spanning various sectors, including information...
records.description: Saudi Arabia and India have solidified their economic ties by signing over 50 agreements spanning various sectors, including information and communication technology, entrepreneurship, chemicals, energy, and advanced manufacturing. These agreements were formalized during the India-Saudi Investment Forum in New Delhi, coinciding with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's official state visit for the G20 summit. The Ministry of Investment of Saudi Arabia announced plans to open a country office in India, simplifying the investment process for Indian companies in Saudi Arabia and facilitating venture capital and funding for startups. Notable agreements include partnerships in energy, technology, and agribusiness. The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor was also announced at the G20 meeting, aiming to bolster regional investment and cooperation. In 2022, India ranked second in terms of trade volume with Saudi Arabia, totaling 196.7 billion Saudi riyals ($52.45 billion) and exhibiting a 51% annual growth rate. Additionally, more than 3,000 Indian companies hold foreign investment licenses in Saudi Arabia, highlighting the depth of economic engagement between the two nations.
records.institution: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman

records.title: Saudi: Crown Prince Calls for Diligent Efforts to Transform Economic Corridor Into Reality
records.description: Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman emphasized the importance of concerted efforts among signatory countries to the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEE) during the India-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council Meeting. He praised the successful management of the G20 Summit and stressed the need to diligently work towards making the ambitious economic corridor project a reality. The Crown Prince highlighted the enduring partnership between Saudi Arabia and India, emphasizing their extensive agenda for cooperation and the promising prospects ahead. He also acknowledged the significant Indian community in Saudi Arabia and expressed the country's commitment to their well-being. The meeting covered various areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy security, trade, defense, healthcare, culture, and community welfare, with both leaders solidifying their commitment to strengthening relations through the signing of minutes. Numerous Memoranda of Understanding were also signed between Indian and Saudi Arabian companies across various sectors.

records.title: Morocco has been struck by its deadliest earthquake in over six decades, with a death toll exceeding 2,000 and expectations of it rising...
records.description: Morocco has been struck by its deadliest earthquake in over six decades, with a death toll exceeding 2,000 and expectations of it rising further. A significant search and rescue operation is underway, yet survivors face dire challenges accessing essential supplies like food and water. The 6.8 magnitude quake primarily hit the remote and rugged Atlas mountains, posing difficulties for assistance efforts. Caroline Holt, Director of Disaster, Climate, and Crises at the International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, emphasizes the urgent need for basic necessities, shelter, and clean water. Additionally, they are working to evacuate those trapped under rubble and provide support to those living in fear. Concerns linger about potential aftershocks, and international aid from countries like Spain, France, and Turkey is being offered. Over 2,000 are injured, with more than 1,400 in critical condition, affecting over 300,000 people. Roads are blocked due to debris, hindering access. The primary focus is on finding survivors, as the window for rescue efforts is limited. King Mohammed VI declared three days of mourning, and the situation's full scale remains uncertain. Psychological and mental health support is critical, given ongoing aftershocks and the trauma experienced by affected individuals. The last major earthquake in Morocco occurred in 1960, claiming approximately 12,000 lives.

records.title: Oman has advocated for a global initiative aimed at advancing nutritional development by moderating daily food intake, transforming consu...
records.description: Oman has advocated for a global initiative aimed at advancing nutritional development by moderating daily food intake, transforming consumption habits, and enhancing food production efficiency. H E Dr Ahmed Nasser al Bakri, Undersecretary for Agriculture in the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, made this call during the International Conference on Food Security held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, from September 7-8. The conference, a collaboration between the Ministry of Agriculture of Uzbekistan and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), focused on current food production conditions, challenges in eradicating hunger, and improving agricultural food systems, resulting in the 'Samarkand Declaration on Food Security.' H E Bakri highlighted Oman's commitment to strengthening its food security framework, which includes boosting competitive goods production, solidifying import supply chains, and improving storage and distribution logistics within Oman. He also mentioned the Sustainable Agriculture and Rural Development Strategy 2040 and the Fisheries Sector Strategy 2040, aiming to create a more resilient agricultural and fishery sector in Oman, leading to increased economic returns, job opportunities, and support for rural communities. Oman has initiated a food security investment laboratory focusing on short to medium-term projects, aligning with Oman Vision 2040. Additionally, H E Bakri shared that Oman had climbed from 40th to 35th place globally in the Global Food Security Index 2022 and ranked 3rd in the Arab world, a significant improvement from its 5th position the previous year. The conference concluded by examining innovative global practices in food safety and quality.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: Skretting Middle East and Africa has selected International Fish Feed Company (IFFC) as its official distributor in Oman to expand its pr...
records.description: Skretting Middle East and Africa has selected International Fish Feed Company (IFFC) as its official distributor in Oman to expand its presence in the country's growing aquaculture sector. Skretting, a global aquafeed leader, aims to capitalize on IFFC's expertise and regional presence to establish a robust business in Oman. IFFC will offer a wide range of Skretting feed products to fish and shrimp farmers in Oman and plans to build a fish feed plant in Duqm with Nutreco's support, set to commence commercial production next year with a capacity of 31,200 metric tons. This partnership aligns with Oman's efforts to diversify its economy, enhance food security, and boost its thriving aquaculture industry, positioning both companies to meet the rising demand for sustainable aquafeed solutions.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: National Dairy Farms and Masakin Dairy Farms, both entities under Emirates Food Industries (EFI), have joined forces with Alltech in a pi...
records.description: National Dairy Farms and Masakin Dairy Farms, both entities under Emirates Food Industries (EFI), have joined forces with Alltech in a pioneering partnership called 'Planet of Plenty' to revolutionize the Middle East's dairy industry by introducing advanced technologies for carbon footprint assessment and methane reduction. These dairy giants, known for their Hayatna milk brand, are committed to quantifying and mitigating their carbon footprints in line with global climate change goals. Through this collaboration, they will leverage Alltech's carbon footprint assessment tools and nutritional technologies to reduce environmental impact, improve feed efficiency, and enhance milk production. This initiative underscores their dedication to sustainability and sets a powerful example for the region's dairy industry, aligning with EFI's vision of eco-friendly practices throughout the dairy value chain and contributing to the UAE's commitment to the Paris Agreement's targets.

records.title: MHP Agroholding, Ukraine's largest poultry producer, has signed a shareholder agreement with Desert Hills Veterinary Services Company Lim...
records.description: MHP Agroholding, Ukraine's largest poultry producer, has signed a shareholder agreement with Desert Hills Veterinary Services Company Limited (DHV), a subsidiary of Tanmiah Food Company, a leading Middle Eastern poultry and meat supplier listed on the Saudi stock market. The partnership will see a joint investment of over 200 million Saudi riyals (approximately $53 million) to establish farms with a capacity exceeding 1 million breeder flocks, expected to produce about 175 million hatching eggs annually, along with the construction of a modern hatchery and poultry feed mill in Saudi Arabia. DHV will hold a 55% stake, with MHP holding the remaining 45%. This collaboration reflects a strategic move for MHP's global expansion and aligns with Saudi Arabia's food security goals. Tanmiah Food Company, founded in 1962, operates 114 farms, six hatcheries, two feed mills, and four primary processing plants, serving markets in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Oman, Jordan, and Kuwait. The agreement is subject to necessary approvals, including those from the Saudi Arabian Competition Authority and other relevant authorities.

records.title: Israel and Morocco have made history by entering into a groundbreaking free trade agreement, further strengthening their evolving relatio...
records.description: Israel and Morocco have made history by entering into a groundbreaking free trade agreement, further strengthening their evolving relationship. Signed on September 9, 2023, in Rabat by Israeli Economy Minister Orna Barbivai and Moroccan Industry and Trade Minister Ryad Mezzour, this pact is poised to boost trade, eliminate tariffs, and foster cooperation across sectors like agriculture, tourism, and technology. It solidifies the normalization of relations between the two nations, which began in 2020, and adds to a growing list of bilateral agreements, including defense and visa waivers. Economically, the agreement is expected to increase trade by 50% over the next five years, remove tariffs, and promote investment and business expansion. It also opens doors to collaboration in multiple areas, including agriculture, tourism, and technology. This agreement demonstrates the potential for peaceful collaboration in a region often marked by discord, and its ratification and implementation are eagerly awaited as a stepping stone to regional cooperation and prosperity.
records.institution: Moroccan Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: Saudi Arabia has attained self-sufficiency in key agricultural sectors, including dairy, eggs, and fish, as per the latest report from th...
records.description: Saudi Arabia has attained self-sufficiency in key agricultural sectors, including dairy, eggs, and fish, as per the latest report from the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) for the year 2022. The report reveals that among animal products in the Kingdom, fresh dairy achieved the highest self-sufficiency rate at 118%, followed by table eggs at 117%, and fish at 48% during the same year. In terms of plant products, dates led with a self-sufficiency rate of 124%, producing 1.61 million tons locally in 2022. Tomato and onion had self-sufficiency rates of 67% and 44%, respectively. GASTAT also noted that the total area of organic agriculture in Saudi Arabia reached 19,100 hectares in 2022, with fruit crops (excluding dates) occupying the majority at 60.3%, followed by date palms at 20.8% of the total organic agriculture area.

records.title: Jordan is actively working to facilitate the distribution of Saudi products in the local market, recognizing that nearly 60 percent of Jo...
records.description: Jordan is actively working to facilitate the distribution of Saudi products in the local market, recognizing that nearly 60 percent of Jordan's agricultural exports head to Saudi Arabia, according to Minister of Agriculture Khaled Hneifat's statement on Wednesday. This announcement follows a recent agreement between the Ocean Centre for Fresh Fish and the Saudi Alrowia Cooperative Society, aimed at enhancing trade in agricultural products, particularly fish. Hneifat emphasized that this agreement is part of the broader effort to bolster connections between Jordanian and Saudi private sectors and promote the exchange of agricultural goods. Additionally, the ministry has allocated JD5 million in funding to advance the fisheries industry, with the intention of further developing the sector in Jordan through such collaborations.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: In 2022, Oman achieved a remarkable milestone in honey production, surpassing 533,701 kilograms of locally produced honey, with major hon...
records.description: In 2022, Oman achieved a remarkable milestone in honey production, surpassing 533,701 kilograms of locally produced honey, with major honey-producing regions including North and South Al Sharqiyah Governorate, North and South Al Batinah Governorate, and Al Dakhiliyah Governorate. However, beekeepers face numerous challenges, such as environmental pressures, climate change, dwindling food resources, diseases, parasites, and the use of harmful pesticides, which pose long-term environmental risks as bees play a vital role in pollination, food production, and ecological balance. A significant hurdle is the importation of honey from foreign countries, which has prompted calls for measures to restrict such imports to prevent losses for local beekeepers and potential consumer deception. Efforts are also needed to establish demand-driven honey markets and address logistical challenges in honey delivery to consumers. Additionally, educating consumers about different honey varieties can enhance product awareness and quality perception.

records.title: SABIC Agri-nutrients, a chemical manufacturing company, is collaborating with American firms ADM and BiOWiSH to promote sustainable farmi...
records.description: SABIC Agri-nutrients, a chemical manufacturing company, is collaborating with American firms ADM and BiOWiSH to promote sustainable farming practices that enhance productivity. This partnership involves various ADM units, including the Farm Direct Fertilizer and Climate-Smart Ag Origination teams, joining forces with SABIC AN and BiOWiSH for a pilot project. The goal is to reduce the carbon footprint in the agricultural supply chain, aligning with SABIC Agri-Nutrients' commitment to carbon neutrality by 2050. This initiative follows SABIC's achievement of independent certifications for low-carbon ammonia and blue hydrogen. Among their products is the BiOWiSH-powered Bio-Enhanced Urea Fertilizer, designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, enhance carbon sequestration in the soil, and improve nutrient delivery to crops. The pilot project will involve farmers using this bio-fortified urea for the 2023 agri-nutrient season, enrolling in ADM's Re: Generations program, which offers support for regenerative farming practices. This collaboration aims to gather data for advancing emission reduction concepts using biofortified urea, with ADM providing financial rewards to participating growers. SABIC Agri-Nutrients' acquisition of a 49% stake in ETG Inputs Holdco Limited earlier this year aligns with its strategy to integrate the value chain for agri-nutrient blending and distribution in global markets.

records.title: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) has initiated a survey aimed at supporting Omani frankincense produc...
records.description: The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) has initiated a survey aimed at supporting Omani frankincense producers by enhancing production through research insights. Oman's history with frankincense production has contributed to its reputation, and the survey seeks participation to gather data that will benefit the trade. In a separate effort, the Environment Authority (EA) has disclosed the results of its survey on Arabian Myrrh Trees in Oman's second phase. The study, conducted in Dhofar, highlighted key threats to myrrh trees, including overgrazing, insect infestation, drought, and unsustainable harvesting methods. The findings emphasize the need for sustainable practices to preserve these valuable resources.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP)

records.title: Bilateral trade between Qatar and Malaysia has surged, reaching a remarkable $1 billion last year, marking a 79.5% increase compared to t...
records.description: Bilateral trade between Qatar and Malaysia has surged, reaching a remarkable $1 billion last year, marking a 79.5% increase compared to the previous year, largely attributed to Qatar's World Cup hosting and extensive exports. Malaysia's Ambassador to Qatar, Zamshari Shaharan, highlighted that the World Cup played a significant role in boosting trade volume despite temporary declines due to COVID-19. Malaysia's exports to Qatar include diverse categories like palm oil-based products, electrical and electronic goods, processed food, machinery, and petroleum products. On the other hand, Qatar's imports to Malaysia mainly consist of crude petroleum, chemicals, petroleum products, metal manufactures, and other vegetable oils. Additionally, Malaysia's Ranhill Utilities and Worley are pursuing a joint venture for Qatar's North Field Production Sustainability project, while Saipem's contract for offshore gas compression complexes aims to maintain production levels at the North Field.

records.title: Saudi Arabia’s Agricultural Fund Launches New Financing Product
records.description: The Saudi Arabian Agricultural Development Fund has introduced a new financial product to enhance rural farms and promote sustainable practices. This initiative focuses on diversifying income sources, ensuring long-term sustainability, and utilizing unique rural opportunities while contributing to preserving local ecosystems and fostering environmental and rural tourism. The fund's approach involves offering financial support to existing productive agricultural businesses for both investment and operational expenses. Eligibility criteria encompass property ownership or advanced agricultural records, along with licenses from the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture. Applicants must also provide a simplified technical study outlining funding needs, possess productive farms suitable for agriculture and agricultural tourism, and aim to improve visitor services to enhance agricultural and rural tourism. This initiative aligns with the fund's goal to enhance the developmental and financial aspects of agricultural activity while supporting the Kingdom's food security strategy and supply chain.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's support for Malawi's agricultural sector through a donation of fertilizer and maize seeds is highly appreciated by the Min...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's support for Malawi's agricultural sector through a donation of fertilizer and maize seeds is highly appreciated by the Ministry of Agriculture. Principal Secretary Dixie Kampani expressed gratitude during a ceremony in Lilongwe where the donation was received from the Saudi Arabian Government via the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre. The donation includes 50 metric tonnes of UREA, 50 metric tonnes of NPK, and 1000 metric tonnes of seeds, which Kampani highlighted as timely and essential, particularly for families affected by Cyclone Freddy. The Ministry is actively aiding winter cropping and advancing the Affordable Inputs Program to further support the agricultural sector, emphasizing Saudi Arabia's crucial contribution to benefiting farmers and communities in need.
records.institution: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre

records.title: The Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock has unveiled its participation plans for the twelfth edition of the International Gov...
records.description: The Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock has unveiled its participation plans for the twelfth edition of the International Government Communication Forum 2023 (IGCF), taking place on September 13-14. Hosted under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Dr. Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, the forum's theme "Today's Resources... Tomorrow's Wealth" aligns with the focus on sustainable development, climate change, and government communication. The agenda features sessions and workshops led by experts in various fields, highlighting Sharjah's achievements in agriculture, responsible natural resource management, and contributions to food security and sustainable development. The platform will showcase Sharjah's innovative agricultural initiatives, such as the pioneering wheat farm in Mleiha, emphasizing self-sufficiency and environmentally friendly practices. The Department's workshops will delve into topics such as biodiversity, pastoral strategies, and technology adoption to boost production and sustainability.
records.institution: Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock

records.title: The United Arab Emirates (UAE), the host of this year's United Nations climate summit, has committed $4.5 billion to support clean-energy...
records.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE), the host of this year's United Nations climate summit, has committed $4.5 billion to support clean-energy projects in African nations. The funds will be provided by entities including Abu Dhabi's clean-energy producer Masdar, Abu Dhabi Fund for Development, Etihad Credit Insurance, and Dubai-based renewable-energy company AMEA Power. The initiative emphasizes the importance of African leaders improving policy and regulatory frameworks to attract long-term investments for clean and renewable energy deployment. With Africa contributing only 3% of global emissions but experiencing severe consequences, the initiative aims to address investment barriers and prioritize projects in countries with transition strategies and enhanced regulatory frameworks. This move aligns with the goal of achieving greater access to clean energy and promoting social and economic development across the continent.

records.title: Under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, ADAFSA has launched the second round of the Sheikh Mansour bin Za...
records.description: Under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, ADAFSA has launched the second round of the Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Agricultural Excellence Award, with an increased value of AED10 million to be distributed among participants in the main Award categories as well as associated competitions within the "Sheikh Zayed Festival" in Al Wathba and various festivals linked to the Award. This initiative aims to boost the agricultural sector in the UAE, recognizing exceptional farmers and livestock breeders for their role in achieving agricultural sustainability, food security, and improving local production quality. The Award promotes positive competition among farmers and breeders, highlights the UAE's commitment to sustainable agriculture, innovation, and honors ADAFSA's achievements in agricultural sustainability and food security. The award features new categories for female farmers and livestock breeders, while diverse accompanying competitions and festivals further enrich the initiative, with registration closing on November 30 and the winners being honored in February 2024.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: IFC Signs PPP Agreement with Iraqi Government to Modernise Baghdad Airport
records.description: The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, has signed an agreement with the Iraqi government to develop Baghdad International Airport through a public-private partnership (PPP) model. This marks Iraq's first airport PPP project and IFC's initial PPP mandate within the country. IFC will lead as a transaction advisor for the rehabilitation, expansion, financing, operation, and maintenance of the airport, aligning its facilities, safety, and services with international standards. The PPP aims to enhance global connectivity, create jobs, and diversify Iraq's economy, in line with the nation's 2030 Vision for Sustainable Development. This initiative supports private sector involvement in vital infrastructure assets to reduce dependence on oil revenues.

records.domain: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
records.title: The Agricultural Credit Corporation (ACC) and the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Jordan have inked a memorandu...
records.description: The Agricultural Credit Corporation (ACC) and the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Jordan have inked a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to collaborate on various initiatives, with a particular emphasis on the "Sustainable Production and Utilisation of Agro-natural Resources (SPUAR)" project in Maan Governorate. This project aims to establish a sustainable system utilizing agro-natural resources such as land, water, and vegetation. The ACC will provide loans through its regular programs to individuals qualified by the FAO project management. Key project objectives include rainwater harvesting for vegetable and herb production, skill enhancement for rural communities, and improved access to financing.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Establishes New Global Organization to Address Water Challenges
records.description: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has announced the establishment of a global water organization to address water challenges, with its headquarters based in Riyadh. This initiative aligns with Saudi Arabia's dedication to environmental sustainability and aims to integrate global efforts to ensure sustainable water resources. The organization will promote the exchange of expertise, technological advancements, innovation, and research experiences, facilitating high-priority projects for water resource sustainability and accessibility. The organization reflects the Kingdom's commitment to addressing global water supply challenges and enhancing economic and social growth across sectors through unified global endeavors. This initiative further aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, with a significant commitment of SR92 billion ($24.5 billion) towards water, environment, and agriculture to achieve interconnected social, environmental, and economic objectives. As urban water scarcity increases worldwide, the establishment of this international organization addresses pressing challenges, including climate change impacts, water loss, pollution, and ecosystem degradation, to ensure a sustainable future for all.

records.domain: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
records.title: Saudi Arabia is set to make a substantial investment of up to $25 billion in Pakistan within the next two to five years, across multiple...
records.description: Saudi Arabia is set to make a substantial investment of up to $25 billion in Pakistan within the next two to five years, across multiple sectors, according to Pakistan's caretaker Prime Minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar. This move is part of an effort to boost foreign direct investment and revive the country's economy. The investments are expected to span mining, agriculture, and information technology sectors. Kakar's announcement comes as Pakistan faces an economic recovery challenge under its caretaker government following a $3 billion loan program approved by the International Monetary Fund to prevent a sovereign debt default. While specific projects have not been outlined, Barrick Gold Corp has indicated potential Saudi Arabian investment in Pakistan's Reko Diq gold and copper mine. Additionally, Kakar mentioned the government's intent to complete privatisation deals for state-run power sector entities and explore privatisation options for non-energy government-owned enterprises.

records.title: Saudi-listed ACWA Power has established strategic agreements with six Italian partners during the Saudi-Italian Investment Forum in Milan.
records.description: Saudi-listed ACWA Power has established strategic agreements with six Italian partners during the Saudi-Italian Investment Forum in Milan. These collaborations focus on green hydrogen, water desalination, and research and development. The Italian entities involved, including Confindustria, Eni, A2A, Industrie De Nora, Italmatch Chemicals, and RINA, aim to exchange expertise, products, and equipment with ACWA Power, contributing to initiatives such as green hydrogen and technical expertise. These partnerships align with ACWA Power's commitment to fostering Italian companies' presence in Saudi Arabia, driving research and development efforts, and promoting sustainable progress through green initiatives. Additionally, ACWA Power has successfully installed the first wind turbine for its 500MW Bash wind farm project in Uzbekistan, featuring a capacity of 6.5MW, with the turbine manufactured by Envision and installed by China Energy Engineering Corporation (CEEC).

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Saudi's Al-Jouf Agricultural Development Company has entered into an agreement with the French multinational utility firm Engie for the e...
records.description: Saudi's Al-Jouf Agricultural Development Company has entered into an agreement with the French multinational utility firm Engie for the establishment of an 8-megawatt (MW) solar power project. The construction of the project is set to commence on September 20, 2023, with operations expected to initiate by September 30, 2024, as announced in a statement to the Saudi stock exchange. The solar power plant will be constructed to support Al-Jouf Agricultural's industrial complex, catering to olive oil and pickles factories, as well as the French fries factory located in Busaita. The collaboration also includes a 25-year solar power purchase agreement (PPA) between the two entities.

records.title: The Ugandan government has allocated land to investors from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for the establishment of a pineapple juice pro...
records.description: The Ugandan government has allocated land to investors from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for the establishment of a pineapple juice processing plant in Luwero district. Pineapple growers in Luwero have invested heavily in pineapple farming, yet lack of processing facilities has led to selling pineapples at low prices in roadside markets. With about 2000 acres of pineapples grown by local associations, farmers have faced challenges in finding better markets and value addition opportunities. Responding to these concerns, Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja announced the allocation of land to Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed from UAE for the pineapple juice processing plant at Bukalasa Agricultural College in Luwero. The government plans to provide 100 acres of land to the investor at Bukalasa Agricultural College and another 100,000 acres of land at Kaweweta Military Training School for pineapple cultivation for the processing plant. This initiative aims to support pineapple growers, enhance value addition, and create a sustainable market for their produce.

records.title: Under an agreement established earlier this year, Turkey will grant duty exemptions on agricultural imports from the United Arab Emirates...
records.description: Under an agreement established earlier this year, Turkey will grant duty exemptions on agricultural imports from the United Arab Emirates within specified quotas. This arrangement encompasses products like vegetables, legumes, and milk, and the duty waivers apply to quantities ranging from 50 to 40,000 tons. The primary objective of this pact is to minimize or eliminate duties on 82 percent of goods, covering over 93 percent of non-oil trade, with the aim of enhancing bilateral trade to reach a yearly total of $40 billion within a five-year timeframe.

records.title: Egypt Aims to Increase Agriculture Exports to 6.3 Million Tons in 2025/2026
records.description: The Egyptian government, under the leadership of Dr. Mostafa Madbouly, has adopted an ambitious plan aimed at significantly increasing agricultural exports by the end of the medium-term plan in 2025/2026 to around 6.3 million tons annually. This plan, outlined in the Economic and Social Development Plan for the fiscal year 2023/2024, seeks to address challenges hindering optimal export capacity utilization, enhance quality standards, and open new markets for agricultural products. The plan emphasizes expanding investments in both horizontal and vertical agricultural expansion programs, utilizing modern techniques, improving water efficiency, and promoting organic farming practices. These efforts align with the overall goal of boosting self-sufficiency, reducing import dependency, and fostering sustainable agricultural development.

records.title: Egypt Vaccinates 240,000 Heads of Livestock
records.description: The General Authority for Veterinary Services, under the Ministry of Agriculture, announced that all required vaccines for livestock immunization have been provided. They have also taken necessary measures and preparations to commence and complete a comprehensive immunization campaign throughout the country. The veterinary services highlighted their awareness programs for livestock breeders, which include counseling seminars aimed at educating breeders on how to protect animals from contagious diseases. These initiatives are part of the presidential initiative "Decent Life," launched by President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi to develop the Egyptian countryside, improve the living standards of small breeders and farmers, and safeguard animal wealth. Dr. Fathi Abdel-Aal, the Director of Veterinary Medicine in Minya Governorate, emphasized the importance of enhancing animal wealth to meet local market demands for meat and dairy products at affordable prices. He discussed the efforts made to support and provide veterinary care for livestock to maintain both animal health and public health. The director mentioned that during July, they immunized 240,378 cattle, with specific numbers vaccinated against various diseases. Field visits and counseling sessions were conducted to educate and encourage citizens to participate in the immunization campaign.
records.institution: Egyptian General Authority for Veterinary Services

records.title: The Agricultural Innovation Incubator at the Youth Association of Maan for Environmental Preservation, established by youth in Maan in 20...
records.description: The Agricultural Innovation Incubator at the Youth Association of Maan for Environmental Preservation, established by youth in Maan in 2018 with support from the Ministries of Environment and Agriculture, focuses on sustainable agriculture and environmental preservation. Notably, the Smart Village for Sustainable Development project, under the association's leadership, has introduced innovative practices such as aquatic organic fertilizer and AI-driven desert farming. This initiative has provided job opportunities for locals, and future plans include a training center for sustainable agriculture concepts. The project aligns with national policies for afforestation, environmental protection, and economic empowerment, contributing to a transition towards a sustainable green economy in Maan Governorate.

records.title: Qatar's ports experienced a notable increase of 19 percent in container handling during August 2023 compared to July of the same year.
records.description: Qatar's ports experienced a notable increase of 19 percent in container handling during August 2023 compared to July of the same year. Mwani Qatar, the maritime organization, reported that container volumes at Mwani Qatar surged by around 19 percent in August 2023, with building materials, livestock, and RORO cargo witnessing growth rates of 31 percent, 215 percent, and 30 percent respectively. Throughout August, 249 vessels visited Hamad Port, Ruwais Port, and Old Doha Port, collectively handling 119,936 containers, 160,131 tonnes of general and bulk cargo, 7,875 vehicles, 17,231 heads of livestock, and 46,075 tonnes of building materials. The maritime sector's expansion aligns with Qatar's aspirations to become a regional trade hub, with initiatives like the General Cargo Terminal equipped to manage diverse cargo types and volumes. The rise in container transshipment by 32 percent in the first half of 2023 further solidifies Qatar's position as a growing trade player.

records.title: As part of the "Hayat Kareema" initiative, the free veterinary caravan was launched today in Damietta Governorate, organized by the Insti...
records.description: As part of the "Hayat Kareema" initiative, the free veterinary caravan was launched today in Damietta Governorate, organized by the Institute of Animal Reproduction Research and under the patronage of the Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation. The caravan aims to provide veterinary services to small livestock owned by farmers in villages across Damietta, Al-Zarqa, Kafr Saad, Faraskur, and Kafr El-Bateekh. The services include reproductive examinations, ultrasound-based pregnancy diagnosis, treatment of calf and udder diseases, as well as vaccinations and deworming to ensure animal health. Various entities, such as the General Authority for Veterinary Services and institutes for animal health research, animal production, and veterinary vaccines, are collaborating in this effort to support animal welfare and livelihoods.
records.institution: Egyptian Institute of Animal Reproduction Research

records.description: Dr. Mohamed Al-Qurash, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of Agriculture, stated that the ministry is working on expanding the cultivated area for forage crops. In a phone interview with the media host Shimaa Moussa on the "Business" program aired on Sada El Balad channel, Dr. Al-Qurash mentioned that for the first time, the ministry is implementing a contractual agriculture system that includes crops like corn, sunflowers, soybeans, and others, with pricing included. He emphasized that the state has abundant raw materials for animal feed, contributing to the stability of feed prices in the Egyptian market and consequently enabling many breeders to resume their work, stabilize prices, create job opportunities, and enhance feed stability with the availability of corn in the upcoming harvesting season.

records.title: The Agricultural Economics Research Institute organized a workshop titled "Agricultural Cooperatives: Goals, Potentials, Challenges, Deve...
records.description: The Agricultural Economics Research Institute organized a workshop titled "Agricultural Cooperatives: Goals, Potentials, Challenges, Development" in line with the directives of the Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation. The aim was to address issues related to agricultural cooperatives, explore solutions to their challenges, and discuss avenues for their development under the auspices of the President of the Agricultural Research Center, Dr. Mohamed Suleiman. Dr. Dalia Youssef, the institute's director, emphasized that addressing the agricultural cooperatives issue is crucial for advancing the agricultural sector and achieving sustainable development goals. The workshop delved into the problems faced by agricultural cooperatives and proposed solutions to fulfill their designated roles, including structural reforms. Additionally, Dr. Duaa Mamdouh Suleiman, head of the Finance and Agricultural Cooperation Research Department, presented a comprehensive report on implementing the workshop's suggestions and recommendations to align with local and global changes.

records.title: A drop in water reservoir levels in Istanbul, Turkey, has sparked worries about potential water scarcity in the nation.
records.description: A drop in water reservoir levels in Istanbul, Turkey, has sparked worries about potential water scarcity in the nation. The Süleyman Demirel Law is being applied as Turkey constructs 11 dams on its borders with Iraq and Syria, exchanging energy for water. Istanbul's dam reservoirs now stand at only 29.7% of their capacity due to disrupted rainfall patterns caused by climate change and rising temperatures. Unsustainable water infrastructure projects, including hydroelectric power plants, dams, and water transfer schemes, as well as inefficient water use in agriculture and contamination from waste, contribute to water depletion. Turkey's growing population and climate change compound the "water stress" situation, leading to droughts and reduced water availability. The risk of earthquakes and a subsequent need to release dam water for safety further impact reservoir levels. While some attribute Turkey's declining dam reserves to energy and electricity shortages, the reduced flow of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers into Syria and Iraq due to dam-building and climate change significantly affects their agriculture, water security, and overall stability. This scenario brings forth concerns about drought, decreased crop yield, food security, public health, and geopolitical tensions over shared water resources.

records.title: Iraqi Trade Center to be launched in Amman before end of 2023
records.description: The Amman Chamber of Commerce (ACC) and the Iraqi Embassy in Jordan have agreed to establish the Iraqi Commercial Center at the ACC's headquarters by the end of 2023. ACC's president, Khalil Haj Tawfiq, emphasized the significance of Iraq as a trade partner and its role in the national economy, aiming to enhance cooperation between the two countries based on mutual interests for economic integration. The center will enable Jordanian businesses to explore Iraqi industries and agricultural products, thereby fostering increased trade between the nations and facilitating the creation of collaborative economic partnerships. The Chargé d’Affairs of the Republic of Iraq, Munif Ali Hussein, highlighted the Iraqi government's keenness to establish the center to enhance commercial and investment prospects, benefiting both economies. Notably, Jordan's exports to Iraq in the first half of the year reached JD261 million, surpassing imports valued at JD74 million.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture conducted raids on animal shops and closed two veterinary clinics in Al-Awza'i and Al-Jannah areas.
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture conducted raids on animal shops and closed two veterinary clinics in Al-Awza'i and Al-Jannah areas. The Veterinary Patrol, consisting of the head of the Export and Import Control and Veterinary Quarantine Service, Dr. Yahya Khattar, and the head of Animal Health Service, Dr. Basel Al-Bazal, under the directives of the Minister of Agriculture, Dr. Abbas Al-Hajj Hassan, and the Director-General of Agriculture, Engineer Louis Lahoud, with the assistance of the State Security Apparatus, the oversight of the Special Public Prosecution, and the presence of the Syndicate of Veterinary Doctors represented by Dr. Ihab Shaban, raided four animal shops, seized all vaccines, medicines, and veterinary equipment, and closed two veterinary clinics—Pet Mart in Al-Awza'i and Pet House in Al-Jannah areas. The owners of these establishments were summoned to the Ministry of Agriculture and were required to commit to refraining from engaging in any unlawful activities related to animal vaccination, treatment, and the sale of veterinary drugs, under the threat of closure and legal action, subject to referral to the appropriate judiciary.

records.title: Libyan Ministry of Agriculture and Marine Resources Signs a Memorandum of Understanding to Enhance the Production and Multiplication of Improved Seeds
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Marine Resources in the Government of National Unity has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Arab Organization for Agricultural Development to enhance the production and multiplication of improved seeds. The project aims to strengthen the role of agricultural research centers, variety control authorities, and seed accreditation, along with supporting and developing seed propagation efforts in both the public and private sectors through a 3-year project. Another agreement was signed between the organization and the Arab Center for Dryland Studies and Arid Zones Development (ACSAD) to provide Libya with improved wheat seeds produced by ACSAD, aiming for self-sufficiency in this strategic resource. These agreements were signed during a meeting in Egypt attended by the ministry's representative for the Diwan and Agricultural Reform Affairs, Mohamed Al-Turki, and the accompanying delegation, along with the Director-General of the Arab Organization for Agricultural Development, Ibrahim Al-Dakhiri.
records.institution: Libyan Ministry of Agriculture and Marine Resources

records.title: The agricultural region of Najd in Dhofar Governorate, Oman, has emerged as a significant hub for agricultural production, yielding an im...
records.description: The agricultural region of Najd in Dhofar Governorate, Oman, has emerged as a significant hub for agricultural production, yielding an impressive annual output of 52,000 tons of diverse agricultural products. The area also offers attractive incentives for investors interested in expanding projects related to food security. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources recently signed around 40 contracts worth 9 million Omani rials as part of a larger investment to enhance food security in Oman. New infrastructure initiatives are being implemented to prepare the region for strong investment flows, including the construction of a 44-kilometer road and plans for a facility dedicated to collecting and selling agricultural goods. Dr. Khaled bin Salem Al-Mashiki, the Head of Operations at the Najd Agricultural Development Office, emphasizes the ministry's commitment to sustainable development in the region, with a focus on wheat cultivation due to high domestic demand. Despite current relatively low global wheat prices, government support and incentives enable Omani farmers to expand wheat cultivation, addressing international market challenges and enhancing food security. The comprehensive approach in Najd's economic development strategy takes into account not only wheat production but also the broader agricultural landscape and the country's overall economic flexibility, reflecting Oman's commitment to achieving self-sufficiency and promoting economic growth in the region.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: The commencement of the 2023 shrimp fishing season has been declared by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources (MAFWR).
records.description: The commencement of the 2023 shrimp fishing season has been declared by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources (MAFWR). This season spans from September to November annually. The authorized technique for fishing is exclusively through the utilization of a specific net referred to as the 'ghaddaf'. Engaging in any alternative fishing methods constitutes a breach of the Living Aquatic Wealth Law and its associated executive rules.
records.institution: Omani Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR)

records.title: New Zealand's trade agenda progresses as Trade and Export Growth Minister Damien O'Connor announces the start of exploratory discussions...
records.description: New Zealand's trade agenda progresses as Trade and Export Growth Minister Damien O'Connor announces the start of exploratory discussions on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with the United Arab Emirates (UAE). O'Connor held talks with UAE officials to enhance mutual interests and understanding of the benefits of a CEPA, citing the UAE's significance as a trading partner with exports nearing $1 billion annually. The potential agreement could boost cooperation in agriculture, services, government procurement, sustainability, and reducing non-tariff barriers. O'Connor views a New Zealand-UAE CEPA as a testament to strong rules-based trade architecture. The UAE, hosting the 2024 World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference, is welcomed as a partner in open, rules-based trade by New Zealand. O'Connor also discussed trade matters in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming New Zealand's commitment to finalizing the New Zealand GCC-FTA and emphasizing momentum in trade agreements since 2017.
records.institution: UAE Ministry of State for Foreign Trade

records.title: Minister of Supply and Internal Trade Ali El-Moselhy inaugurated a new phase of the national project in Luxor Governorate to build strate...
records.description: Minister of Supply and Internal Trade Ali El-Moselhy inaugurated a new phase of the national project in Luxor Governorate to build strategic food warehouses, with an investment of $48.52 million. This initiative is part of the larger plan to establish seven such warehouses across Egypt, aimed at boosting food reserves and reducing losses. The warehouses will adhere to international standards and use advanced technology for storage operations to ensure product quality and year-round availability. The effort is essential for Egypt, a major wheat importer, to enhance its food security, particularly after disruptions caused by geopolitical events. The initiative aligns with Egypt's push for local production and resilience against climate change, and it will contribute to efficient storage systems and inventory management across governorates.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: The Egyptian New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA) has entered into a land allocation agreement with a consortium composed of Orascom...
records.description: The Egyptian New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA) has entered into a land allocation agreement with a consortium composed of Orascom Construction PLC, ENGIE, and Toyota Tsusho Corporation to establish a wind farm with a capacity of three gigawatts (GW) in west Sohag. This initiative aims to deliver clean and sustainable energy to approximately 2 million households and contribute to an annual reduction of 6.5 million tons of carbon emissions. Additionally, the project is set to generate 2,000 direct job opportunities annually during the construction phase, along with 5,000 indirect job opportunities, and provide 1,000 permanent job positions after its operational phase.
records.institution: Egyptian New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA)

records.title: The President of Iraq, Abdullatif Jamal Rashid, met with the Turkish President's Special Envoy for Water Affairs, Mr.
records.description: The President of Iraq, Abdullatif Jamal Rashid, met with the Turkish President's Special Envoy for Water Affairs, Mr. Veysel Eroglu, along with a high-level delegation of Turkish experts and consultants in water, dams, irrigation, agriculture, energy, and environment. The meeting highlighted the diplomatic efforts and mutual interest of Iraq and Turkey in collaborating to find solutions to their shared water challenges. Discussions revolved around joint decision-making, operational plans, minimum water release amounts, and technical notes for the Tigris and Euphrates basins. This signifies potential opportunities for collaboration in water infrastructure development, technology transfer, and environmental projects. The presence of ministers specializing in water resources and environment underlines the significance of water-related matters for both countries. The discussions also focused on climate change, drought, desertification, and declining rainfall, highlighting the urgency of addressing environmental challenges in the region. The Turkish Special Envoy's detailed report suggested opportunities for joint ventures and projects in water crisis mitigation, desertification prevention, and modern irrigation systems, offering openings for collaboration and investment by businesses specializing in water technology, irrigation equipment, and environmental solutions.

records.description: Oman Electricity Transmission Company (OETC), part of Nama Group, has officially inaugurated the 400/132 kV Suwayhat grid station, a significant achievement within the national infrastructure project, Rabt. Valued at over RO 19 million, the project is set to provide a robust and stable electricity supply to Al Wusta Governorate and areas linked to Petroleum Development Oman (PDO). The Suwayhat grid station is a key component of the Rabt initiative, which focuses on enhancing Oman's electricity transmission network to meet growing demand and improve power supply reliability. This project is in line with Oman Vision 2040's goals, supporting economic diversification and sustainable development. It is anticipated to stimulate economic growth, attract investments, and contribute to the country's energy sector transformation.

records.title: During a meeting at the Executive headquarters, both parties engaged in discussions about collaborative measures aimed at overcoming chal...
records.description: During a meeting at the Executive headquarters, both parties engaged in discussions about collaborative measures aimed at overcoming challenges, enhancing the role of the business sector, and fostering increased bilateral trade. They also delved into mechanisms for monitoring the execution of agreements and understandings, as well as strategies for reinforcing relations across diverse domains to serve the shared interests of the two nations. The head of government acknowledged the Syrian economy's challenges due to an unjust blockade and the occupation of oil fields and agricultural resources by US forces, expressing gratitude for Iran's multifaceted support. The Iranian diplomat emphasized a long-term commitment to expanding cooperation, particularly in energy, using national currencies for trade, and exchanging essential products. He reiterated Iran's dedication to aiding Syria against its economic constraints. The enduring alliance between Damascus and Tehran, forged since the Islamic Revolution in 1979, has been reinforced by Iranian assistance in countering terrorism amid Syria's ongoing conflict since 2011.

records.description: Afreximbank has granted a $400 million loan to support a phosphatic fertilizers project in Egypt, according to government officials on August 30th. The loan will fund the phosphatic acid production project undertaken by El Wady for Phosphate Industries and Fertilizers (WAPHCO) in the New Valley governorate. The project, which has completed all technical, economic, and financial studies, is expected to commence production in two and a half years, followed by a six-month trial operation period. Spanning a 560,000-square-meter area, the project will incorporate a 3 million-square-meter storage facility, require an investment of $1 billion, and have an annual production capacity of 1 million tons.

records.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sirojiddin Muhriddin, held a meeting with Palestine's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Riyadh Al-Maliki, in Dushanbe on August 29. Discussions centered around enhancing mutually beneficial cooperation between the two nations. Following the bilateral meeting, the third round of political consultations was conducted between the foreign ministries of Tajikistan and Palestine. The diplomats exchanged perspectives on various aspects of bilateral relations, including politics, economics, trade, investment, tourism, culture, and education, along with collaboration within regional and international organizations. Notably, the diplomats signed protocols and agreements on political consultations, higher education and scientific research, and agricultural cooperation, solidifying their commitment to strengthened ties.

records.title: Saudi technology leaders are participating in the G20 India Agritech Summit in New Delhi, where they are discussing innovative solutions...
records.description: Saudi technology leaders are participating in the G20 India Agritech Summit in New Delhi, where they are discussing innovative solutions to revolutionize agricultural services. The leaders represent various Saudi companies specializing in areas such as food security, agricultural investment, robotics, aquaculture, and artificial intelligence. The summit, organized by the Indian government, aims to explore the integration of technology into agriculture and food security. Saudi Arabia's presence at the summit highlights its commitment to leveraging innovation to address agricultural challenges and its interest in collaborating with India in the field of agriculture technology. The summit showcases various futuristic agricultural solutions, including drones, robotics, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and the Internet of Things. This engagement underscores the intent of Saudi tech leaders to drive transformative change within the agriculture sector, addressing challenges related to food security, resource optimization, and sustainability. The G20 platform serves as a catalyst for knowledge exchange and collaborative research, transcending geographical boundaries for the exchange of ideas and innovative solutions.

records.title: In a collaborative effort to address food insecurity and support vulnerable communities in Yemen, Life for Relief and Development (LIFE)...
records.description: In a collaborative effort to address food insecurity and support vulnerable communities in Yemen, Life for Relief and Development (LIFE) has partnered with the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives in the United Arab Emirates One Billion Meals Endowment Campaign. This partnership aims to provide consistent food assistance to underserved populations worldwide. Yemen has been grappling with a severe humanitarian crisis due to conflict, displacement, food insecurity, and limited access to essential services. LIFE's Operations Manager, Omar Elridi, emphasized the significant impact of providing food aid to Yemenis in six governorates, highlighting the happiness and comfort it brought amidst the challenging humanitarian situation. The distribution of 3,500 boxes of staple food items to families in Yemeni regions including Aden, Lahj, Al-Dhalea, Abyan, Shabwah, and Al-Mahrah has not only addressed malnutrition-related diseases but also contributed to economic relief by mitigating high food prices for vulnerable families. The partnership between LIFE and MBRGI aligns with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goal 2 to end hunger by 2030. Dr. Hany Saqr, CEO of LIFE, emphasized the unity, commitment, and collective compassion demonstrated through the partnership's efforts, which have delivered over 1.5 million meals to the resilient people of Yemen.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: As the urgency to combat climate change grows, carbon credits are gaining traction as a solution to offset carbon emissions.
records.description: As the urgency to combat climate change grows, carbon credits are gaining traction as a solution to offset carbon emissions. The Regional Voluntary Carbon Market Company (RVCMC), backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), is a pioneer in this field, helping companies offset their environmental footprint. Carbon credits represent avoided or removed carbon dioxide emissions and can be purchased to fund projects that mitigate emissions elsewhere. RVCMC aims to shape sustainable business practices and climate action, aligning with stringent climate policies, commitments under the Paris Agreement, and corporate sustainability goals. The company plans to launch a carbon credit trading platform and has conducted significant carbon offset auctions, aligning with Saudi Arabia's transition to greener practices and climate initiatives.

records.description: During a workshop organized by the National Center for Wildlife, Engineer Abdulrahman Al-Fadhli, Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture, unveiled the discovery of "blue holes" in the Red Sea, a breakthrough in marine exploration and conservation. These geological formations, discovered along the southern Saudi coasts in 2022, harbor diverse marine life and present a unique opportunity for ecological study. The National Center for Wildlife, in collaboration with King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, plans to conduct comprehensive research and conservation efforts to safeguard these environments. This discovery aligns with Saudi Arabia's commitment to environmental preservation and sustainable tourism, demonstrating the Kingdom's dedication to its natural heritage.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

records.description: FRV-X, the Australian arm of Saudi-based Abdul Latif Jameel Energy's renewable business, is expanding in New Zealand through a joint venture with Genesis Energy. The partnership plans to build three new solar farms on New Zealand's North Island, generating enough electricity for around 85,000 homes and removing approximately 500,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually. This expansion is part of FRV-X and Genesis Energy's larger plan to develop up to 500MW of solar capacity in New Zealand, in line with the country's goal of being net-zero by 2050. The combined generation from four sites puts the joint venture on track to achieve its targets.

records.title: The Cabinet has granted its approval to the 2023 compensation system for farmers impacted by agricultural risks.
records.description: The Cabinet has granted its approval to the 2023 compensation system for farmers impacted by agricultural risks. Aligned with the amendments to the Agricultural Risk Management Fund Law No. 5 of 2009, this system provides compensation for non-fund-enrolled farmers, acknowledging the influence of climate change, floods, and storms on crop productivity in the Kingdom. In a session led by Prime Minister Bisher Khasawneh, the Cabinet also greenlit the Settlement and Reconciliation Committee's recommendations to address the tax status of 626 companies and taxpayers. Moreover, the Council of Ministers sanctioned the committee's proposals to resolve 15 cases involving taxpayers and violators with the Jordan Customs Department, stipulating that these parties must fulfill outstanding obligations within two months of the decision's issuance. Additionally, the Cabinet decided to retire Ibrahim Al Majali, the secretary-general of the Audit Bureau.

Discussions centered around mutual interests and avenues for cooperation between the two countries in sustainable development and innovative solutions for environmentally friendly agricultural practices and renewable energy. A work program was signed between the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, the Korean Institute for Environmental Industries and Technology, and the Korean agency for promoting commercial investment in Muscat. The program's focus is on research and capacity-building activities to achieve sustainable development goals in agriculture, fisheries, and water resources in Oman.

records.title: Morocco has unveiled a pioneering vegetable oil production plant in the El Marsa industrial park, located in the Laâyoune province in the...
records.description: Morocco has unveiled a pioneering vegetable oil production plant in the El Marsa industrial park, located in the Laâyoune province in the southern region of the country. The plant, inaugurated by project investor El Moussaoui, boasts a total investment of 190 million dirhams ($52 million). Spanning an area of 19,000 m2, the facility has a daily production capacity of 100 tons of vegetable oils and is projected to generate 120 direct jobs and 250 indirect jobs in the region. Notably, 60% of its output is intended for export, primarily targeting African nations such as Mauritania, Mali, Niger, and Chad. This venture is expected to curtail the $900 million spent on importing vegetable oils and contribute to local economic growth. The plant's establishment aims to elevate Morocco's domestic production of oilseeds, addressing the nation's structural gap in this sector. Currently, only about 2% of national demand for vegetable oil seeds is met through local production. Consequently, by relying on imports for 98% of raw materials needed for edible oil manufacturing, Morocco has faced challenges related to international market price fluctuations. The launch of this plant marks a significant step towards reducing these import dependencies and mitigating the impact of price volatility on consumer purchasing power.

records.title: Egypt's General Authority for Land and Dry Ports (GALDP) and Ocean Express Shipping have inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for th...
records.description: Egypt's General Authority for Land and Dry Ports (GALDP) and Ocean Express Shipping have inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for the development and operation of the Burj Al-Arab Dry Port. The signing took place in the presence of Egyptian Minister of Transport, Kamel Al-Wazir. The projected Dry Port, spanning 120 acres and situated on the highway connecting Burj Al-Arab city and Banjar al-Sukkar's agricultural region, is strategically positioned for railway and road connectivity to major ports like Alexandria, Dekheila, and Abu Qir Al Bahri. The initial phase, encompassing 40% of the area, will include a railway freight terminal, container handling yards, storage and inspection spaces, a customs building, facilities for empty container services, and administrative offices. Minister Al-Wazir estimated the project's infrastructure and superstructure costs at 780 million Egyptian pounds (approximately $25 million), with the first phase slated for completion within a year. The Dry Port's initial phase aims to handle 2.5 million tonnes of dry bulk and general goods annually.
records.institution: Egypt’s General Authority for Land and Dry Ports (GALDP)

records.title: Egypt has joined forces with China to enhance drought-resistant strains of strategic crops, specifically rice, corn, and soybeans.
records.description: Egypt has joined forces with China to enhance drought-resistant strains of strategic crops, specifically rice, corn, and soybeans. This collaboration, formalized through an agreement between the Ministers of Agriculture and Land Restoration, El-Sayed El-Quseir and Tang Renjian, outlines a 2023-2025 agricultural cooperation program. This initiative seeks to fortify farmers' resilience against climate change impacts, crucial considering Egypt's annual water deficit of approximately 21 billion m3. The plan encompasses sharing expertise on irrigation, organic and biodynamic farming, and eco-friendly biopesticides to combat plant pests and diseases. Additionally, the partnership extends to animal production, agricultural mechanization, and capacity building via a joint technical committee. Egypt, housing a population of 105 million, heavily depends on food imports and faced disruption due to the Russia-Ukraine crisis, which increased prices and strained foreign currency reserves. Despite challenges, the nation aims to bolster self-sufficiency, particularly in soybean production, projected to rise to 85,000 metric tons in the 2023/24 marketing year. This collaboration reflects Egypt's ongoing efforts to elevate the agricultural sector, which contributes 11% to GDP and employs around 20% of the workforce according to World Bank data.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Restoration

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture, El-Sayed El-Qusair, has announced the release of a combined 284,000 tons of corn and soybeans valued at...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture, El-Sayed El-Qusair, has announced the release of a combined 284,000 tons of corn and soybeans valued at approximately $141 million. This release occurred from April 8, 2023, to August 17, 2023. The allocation encompassed 224,000 tons of corn valued at around $81 million, 60,000 tons of soybeans valued at about $45 million, and feed additives with a value of roughly $15 million. Minister Al-Qusayr highlighted that the overall release from October 16, 2022, to August 17, 2023, reached 7.2 million tons, which includes 5.2 million tons of corn and 2 million tons of soybeans and feed additives, accumulating to a total value of $3.4 billion.

records.title: Papyrus Australia, a sustainable technology developer, has completed the fabrication, assembly, and testing of its banana fiber moulding...
records.description: Papyrus Australia, a sustainable technology developer, has completed the fabrication, assembly, and testing of its banana fiber moulding line, which will soon be dispatched to Egypt after a six-month process. This technology transforms banana waste into fiber, enabling the production of biodegradable food packaging. With the final equipment payment made to the fabricator, Papyrus Australia fulfills its commitment under the Egyptian Government contract, paving the way for the equipment's installation. This development signifies a crucial milestone for both the company and the environment, as it empowers Egypt's green industry by utilizing innovative technology to address waste issues. The project, established through a partnership with Egypt’s National Authority for Military Production, holds potential to revolutionize the banana industry, converting environmental challenges into profitable opportunities while reducing CO2 emissions. Papyrus Chairman Edward Byrt expressed satisfaction in witnessing years of effort culminate in this endeavor, recognizing the positive impact on sustainability and the recognition it brings to Australian innovation.
records.institution: Egypt’s National Authority for Military Production (MP)

records.title: Fisheries Development Oman (FDO), a key player in Oman's fisheries sector, is pleased to introduce the 'Acila' to its subsidiary, Oman Pe...
records.description: Fisheries Development Oman (FDO), a key player in Oman's fisheries sector, is pleased to introduce the 'Acila' to its subsidiary, Oman Pelagic's fleet. This state-of-the-art vessel, constructed in 2023, adheres to the highest global standards and showcases FDO's dedication to sustainable fishing practices and the economic advancement of Oman's fisheries industry. With a length of 84 meters and a capacity of 1,800 cubic meters, the 'Acila' is designed for operations in the Indian Ocean, targeting various tuna species in international waters. Equipped with efficient and reliable Guascor Energy engines, the vessel ensures minimal fuel consumption even in challenging conditions. This investment underscores Oman's attractiveness for local and international investors interested in aquaculture growth. Aligned with FDO's values, the vessel maximizes catch potential while minimizing environmental impact. Partnered with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Water Resources, FDO aims to sustainably exploit Oman's fisheries resources for the benefit of future generations, continuing the country's maritime heritage. The 'Acila' represents the future of Oman's fisheries, embodying innovation, sustainability, and economic progress in alignment with Oman's Vision 2040 objectives for food safety and security.
