records.description: Nailesh Kanaksi Khimji (NKK) Investments, a company engaged in agritech, green hydrogen, and sustainability sectors, has entered a partnership with UrbanKisaan, a US-based agritech startup with a research center in India. This collaboration aims to revolutionize hydroponic farming practices in Oman, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. By introducing UrbanKisaan's advanced hydroponic and vertical farming technology to Oman, NKK Investments intends to popularize these innovative techniques and make them accessible to local farmers. This joint venture seeks to empower agriculturalists with environmentally conscious and resource-efficient practices, enabling higher yields with minimal water and land usage. The strategic partnership also envisions extending this technology to benefit farms in the UAE and Saudi Arabia, aligning with regional efforts to enhance domestic food production and bolster food security.

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Supply and Internal Trade, Ali Al-Moselhi, has announced that the implementation of an agreement signed with the UAE'...
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Supply and Internal Trade, Ali Al-Moselhi, has announced that the implementation of an agreement signed with the UAE's Abu Dhabi Fund for Development is set to begin in January. The agreement, spanning five years and totaling $500 million, aims to finance wheat imports, providing a strategic reserve of wheat for six months. The Emirati Agricultural Company, backed by the fund, will be responsible for supplying the wheat to Egypt. The financing will be facilitated by Abu Dhabi Exports Office (ADEX) after contracts are awarded to specific companies, relieving pressure on Egypt's Commodity Authority and conserving foreign currency. The agreement is pending approval by Egypt's House of Representatives, expected in November, with supply operations commencing in January. The Emirati company, which already cultivates 70,000 feddans in Egypt, contributes to Egypt's wheat supply through its locally produced wheat.
records.institution: Egyptian Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

records.title: Iraqi Minister of Water Resources, Awn Dhiyab, has announced the successful implementation of a Japanese technique aimed at reducing wate...
records.description: Iraqi Minister of Water Resources, Awn Dhiyab, has announced the successful implementation of a Japanese technique aimed at reducing water consumption in agriculture. With a proven track record spanning over 130 years, as confirmed by the Japanese Embassy in Baghdad, the technique's success has been acknowledged. Minister Dhiyab explained that the technique was discussed during a meeting involving the Ministry of Agriculture and the Japanese Embassy, focusing on forming water users' associations to enhance water conservation and agricultural productivity. Deputy Minister of Agriculture, Mithaq Abdulhassan, emphasized the importance of adapting to water scarcity and climate changes, highlighting collaboration with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to establish water users' associations. JICA's model, based on years of experience, aims to support efficient water utilization and higher agricultural production. Japanese Ambassador to Iraq, Futoshi Matsumoto, stressed the significance of forming water users' associations in Iraq, drawing on Japan's 130-year experience in efficient water use in agriculture. The initiative introduces methods for land leveling, water reduction, and increased agricultural yields using less water, offering a cost-effective solution for Iraq's water scarcity and drought challenges.

records.domain: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
records.title: The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology of Saudi Arabia has signed a cooperation agreement with the Republic of India t...
records.description: The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology of Saudi Arabia has signed a cooperation agreement with the Republic of India to enhance collaboration in digital infrastructure, e-health, e-learning, digital research, and innovation. The agreement aims to strengthen the two countries' partnership in emerging technologies, promote innovation, and support the growth of the digital economy. This move aligns with Saudi Arabia's goal to become a regional hub for technology and innovation and an attractive destination for investment, in line with the Vision 2030 initiative.
records.institution: Saudi Ministry of Communications and Information Technology

records.title: Egypt's commodities landscape is witnessing a significant shift as sugar joins the traded goods on the Egyptian Commodities Exchange, a m...
records.description: Egypt's commodities landscape is witnessing a significant shift as sugar joins the traded goods on the Egyptian Commodities Exchange, a move aligned with the government's strategic market regulation policy. Ibrahim Ashmawy, the head of the platform, emphasized that this inclusion aims to ensure fair competition, transparency, and price stability for essential commodities. By establishing direct trade connections among producers, manufacturers, and supply chain entities, sugar trading seeks to manage prices effectively. The Egyptian Commodities Exchange, formed through collaboration between the Egyptian Exchange, Internal Trade Development Authority, and General Authority For Supply Commodities, has previously successfully introduced wheat and yellow corn commodities. Despite governmental efforts to stabilize sugar prices, which involved a temporary export ban, prices have surged by about 26% recently. Notably, officials affirm that strategic sugar reserves will adequately meet consumption until spring 2024. While the commodities exchange offers a new avenue, some experts, like Medhat Nafei, former advisor to the minister of supply and internal trade, caution that addressing the underlying shortage might require measures beyond the exchange platform, such as import prioritization and crop cultivation choices.

records.title: A significant stride towards data-driven collaboration has been achieved through the formalization of a memorandum of cooperation between...
records.description: A significant stride towards data-driven collaboration has been achieved through the formalization of a memorandum of cooperation between the Agricultural Development Fund and the General Authority for Statistics in Riyadh. The focus of this agreement lies in exchanging data, information, and statistical indicators pertaining to the ADF's economic activities. Adhering to guidelines and privacy regulations set by the National Data Management Office (NDMO), this data exchange aims to enhance mutual consultation, knowledge sharing, and support across various fields of common interest, including research and studies. It also facilitates professional development opportunities through courses, seminars, conferences, and workshops. NDMO underscores the value of government data as a national asset for improving performance, transparency, and decision-making. This aligns with global trends wherein data is recognized as a crucial economic resource for innovation, growth, and competitiveness. Saudi Arabia's focus on enhancing food security is evident in recent ADF financing contracts totaling SR926 million ($246.8 million) for the feed industry, animal production, and dairy sectors. These contracts support crucial agricultural imports like maize, soybeans, and barley, vital for the nation's food supply. The agreements encompass initiatives like establishing marketing centers, cold storage facilities, and poultry farming projects. These efforts align with the overarching food security strategy and underline the fund's commitment to agricultural sector development and financing.

records.title: The Saudi Arabian government has recently ended a 21-year prohibition on imports of South African meat.
records.description: The Saudi Arabian government has recently ended a 21-year prohibition on imports of South African meat. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SAFDA) announced the lifting of the ban, which had been in effect since 2002, after successful inspections were conducted in South African abattoirs and feedlots in June. These inspections ensured compliance with Saudi Arabian market access protocols and halaal certification for meat products. Stravos Nicolaou, co-chairperson of the South African Saudi Business Council (SASBC), explained that issues related to veterinary and halaal certification were the original reasons behind the ban. He noted that the ban emerged due to a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak two decades ago and required veterinary certification to be addressed for its removal. The SASBC welcomed this development as an opportunity for South African meat producers to enter a significant market. Trade, Industry, and Competition Minister Ebrahim Patel highlighted that this move grants South African meat producers access to the global halaal meat industry. The lifting of the ban followed discussions between South African ministers and Saudi Arabian officials during a state visit, which also resulted in various agreements covering renewable energy, industry, mining, tourism, and logistics sectors.

records.title: After the Saudi Cabinet's recent endorsement of the National Institute for Health Research, Saudi Health Minister Fahd Al-Jalajel express...
records.description: After the Saudi Cabinet's recent endorsement of the National Institute for Health Research, Saudi Health Minister Fahd Al-Jalajel expressed gratitude to King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for their unwavering backing of the nation's healthcare sector. The minister underscored the importance of advancing translational research, converting theoretical findings into practical applications that directly benefit people, as well as clinical trials, pivotal for transforming the country's healthcare sector and fulfilling the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030, the national development and diversification plan. Al-Jalajel emphasized the initiative's alignment with health priorities and the crown prince's focus on research and innovation. The establishment of the National Institute for Health Research, Al-Jalajel noted, supports healthcare researchers and enhances the translation of cognitive outcomes into tangible health solutions. This move not only aids the health sector's evolution but also addresses urgent national health concerns, bolsters national health security, attracts international medical investment, and maximizes research funding returns. The institute's role encompasses overseeing and boosting translational research and clinical trials to extract practical health and economic benefits, subsequently elevating overall population health and well-being. The institute, a facet of the Health Sector Transformation Program, operates in harmony with Vision 2030, contributing to the development of innovative disease prevention, diagnosis, and treatment systems, and shaping health strategies.

records.title: Kyle Lauersen's motivation to make a tangible impact in Saudi Arabia led him to KAUST, where he now heads an exclusive algal biotechnolog...
records.description: Kyle Lauersen's motivation to make a tangible impact in Saudi Arabia led him to KAUST, where he now heads an exclusive algal biotechnology lab. Over the course of nearly four years, Lauersen and his team have identified and cultivated algal species adapted to Saudi Arabia's extreme temperatures in purpose-built bioreactors. With an expansive suite of bioreactors, the lab tests new strains under diverse conditions, evaluating their performance for growth, particularly during seasons like spring and winter. Algae's ability to thrive in waste waters, converting them into biomass rich in oil, protein, carbohydrates, and pigments, is exploited for environmental benefits. The lab's efforts address the need for specific species for various conditions, such as those suitable for low pH waste waters from industries like dairy. Characterizing each strain's growth conditions and production (oil, protein, carbohydrate) informs applications like animal feed, though the process is time-intensive. Lauersen's team has amassed over 60 strains, building a living library or biobank that serves as a Saudi Arabian natural resource. Lauersen collaborates with a new pilot algal facility supported by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture, focusing on high-protein algae production for aquaculture feed. Strains resilient to Saudi summer heat are tested in outdoor conditions, while Lauersen's plans include an educational program to nurture the next generation of algal bioprocess engineers.
records.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

records.title: UAE-based agribusiness Al Dahra and the Abu Dhabi Exports Office (ADEX), the export financing arm of the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development,...
records.description: UAE-based agribusiness Al Dahra and the Abu Dhabi Exports Office (ADEX), the export financing arm of the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development, have entered into a significant deal worth US$500 million to provide Egypt with wheat. The five-year agreement, amounting to US$100 million annually, aims to supply Egypt with imported milling wheat at competitive prices. Due to its substantial per capita wheat consumption, which is nearly three times the global average at 180kg, Egypt heavily relies on imports as its local wheat production, although the highest in Africa, falls short of meeting domestic demand. This situation worsened due to disruptions caused by the Russo-Ukrainian war and the conclusion of the Black Sea Grain Initiative. Egypt's economic challenges, including a currency depreciation of around 50% against the dollar and soaring inflation at 36.5%, have led to deferred payments for wheat imports and difficulties in servicing foreign debt. The ADEX financing package offers a solution, enabling Egypt to procure high-quality wheat with favorable payment terms. The deal with Al Dahra will further alleviate the wheat supply situation. The company is already engaged in providing domestically produced wheat to the Egyptian government through its local subsidiary.

records.title: The launch of a new floating dock is set to enhance the repair and maintenance capabilities of Asyad Drydock's facility at Duqm on Oman's...
records.description: The launch of a new floating dock is set to enhance the repair and maintenance capabilities of Asyad Drydock's facility at Duqm on Oman's southeast coast. Dr. Ibrahim al-Nadhairi, CEO of Asyad Shipping & Drydock, stated that the operationalization of this mid-sized floating dock will enable the handling of 40 additional vessels annually, raising the target capacity to around 240 ships from the previous 200. Acquired in 2022, this floating dock is the first of three that the Duqm yard aims to accommodate, aligned with its long-term growth strategy. This expansion is in line with the yard's ambition to evolve into a comprehensive shipyard, supported by the recent delivery of indigenously built ships and ongoing projects like constructing a fishing trawler and a landing craft ferry. Furthermore, Asyad Drydock is considering venturing into industrial manufacturing, eyeing opportunities related to the supply of equipment for Oman's upcoming green hydrogen projects.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: ACWA Power has achieved a significant milestone by installing one of Central Asia's largest wind turbines in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region,...
records.description: ACWA Power has achieved a significant milestone by installing one of Central Asia's largest wind turbines in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region, as part of the expansive 500MW Bash wind farm project. This showcases ACWA Power's commitment to expanding renewable energy in the region and positions Saudi Arabian firms as influential contributors to the global shift towards eco-friendly solutions. Manufactured by Envision in China, the impressive 6.5 MW wind turbine generator (WTG) was efficiently installed by China Energy Engineering Corporation. Although the world's most massive wind turbine, located in China, surpasses these figures with a capacity of 16 MW, this comparison underscores rapid advancements in renewable energy technology. The Bash wind farm, designed with 79 WTGs, is set to generate over 1,650 gigawatt-hours of electricity annually, significantly reducing carbon emissions by 750 tons. ACWA Power's 25-year power purchase agreement with JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan reinforces their commitment to sustainable energy development. With a total investment of US$7.5 billion in Uzbekistan, ACWA Power's portfolio includes ten power projects, supporting economic growth and Uzbekistan's renewable energy objectives. The Bash wind farm project is anticipated to conclude in Q1 2025.

records.title: Two parallel economic-focused sessions in the National Dialogue started discussing agriculture, food security, and private investment.
records.description: Two parallel economic-focused sessions in the National Dialogue started discussing agriculture, food security, and private investment. Earlier, a session addressed municipalities, resulting in proposals for the electoral system of municipal councils. The Recommendations and Proposals Committee is finalizing three electoral system proposals for the president, including maintaining the current system or altering it to open lists. Also, proposals for anti-discrimination and legal amendments are being finalized.

records.domain: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
records.title: About 58 billion Iraqi dinars were transferred to the Kurdistan Ministry of Trade and Industry, settling dues for farmers' 2023 wheat cro...
records.description: About 58 billion Iraqi dinars were transferred to the Kurdistan Ministry of Trade and Industry, settling dues for farmers' 2023 wheat crop contributions. This payment, divided among provinces, includes 27 billion dinars for Al-Sulaymaniyah, 18 billion for Erbil, and 13 billion for Duhok. Efforts are underway for smooth fund distribution. The 2023 Iraqi budget designates about $12 billion to the Kurdistan Regional Government, covering reconstruction, salaries, and infrastructure, but some Kurdish leaders find it insufficient for essential services.

records.title: Saudi Arabia is collaborating with a Dutch greenhouse company to create a "synthetic climate" for desert agriculture.
records.description: Saudi Arabia is collaborating with a Dutch greenhouse company to create a "synthetic climate" for desert agriculture. The endeavor involves establishing a horticulture oasis on the outskirts of Neom, a new city being built on the Red Sea coast. The initiative aims to combat food import dependence by fostering year-round produce growth in challenging conditions. The Dutch firm, with a $120 million contract, will construct test facilities using advanced technologies like AI-driven crop cultivation and water filtration systems. Neom's aspiration is to eventually produce over 300,000 tonnes of fruits and vegetables annually. The project aligns with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman's vision to diversify the economy and develop innovative solutions for food security in arid environments.

records.title: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries has unveiled a development strategy targeting an increase in cereal cultivatio...
records.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries has unveiled a development strategy targeting an increase in cereal cultivation area to 1.2 million hectares by 2035, from the current average of less than 900,000 hectares. The plan emphasizes growing wheat on 650,000 hectares, including 500,000 hectares for durum wheat and 100,000 hectares for soft wheat. Barley cultivation is set to expand from 341,000 to 500,000 hectares, and triticale will cover 50,000 hectares. The strategy aims to ensure sustainable development of cereal production, finance stakeholders, enhance value chains, and improve the economic and social sector environment. This approach is vital as Tunisia, facing prolonged drought and rising input prices, aims to bolster cereal production to meet over half of its consumption demand, emphasizing storage capacity expansion and strategic grain storage projects.
records.institution: Tunisia The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries

records.title: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) has secured a deal to import 360,000 tons of wheat, sourced from Russia and Roman...
records.description: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) has secured a deal to import 360,000 tons of wheat, sourced from Russia and Romania, aimed at maintaining strategic reserves for six months and compensating for Russia's withdrawal from the Black Sea Grain deal. This move aligns with the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade's strategy to bolster staple commodity stocks. The purchase encompasses 60,000 tons of Romanian wheat and 300,000 tons of Russian wheat. Egypt, the world's leading wheat importer, has been challenged by increased grain prices following the Russia-Ukraine conflict, prompting the country to seek alternative sources and encourage local farmers to boost supply. The GASC has organized an international tender for wheat, particularly focusing on the US, Canada, France, Bulgaria, Australia, Poland, Germany, and the UK, as well as expressing openness to various milling wheat varieties from several countries. Despite a decrease from 2022, Egypt's wheat import bill is expected to reach US$2.5 billion annually, impacting the nation's balance of payments and foreign reserves and potentially driving inflation due to the significance of bread as a daily staple.
records.institution: Egypt's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC)

records.title: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Mr.
records.description: Egypt's Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation, Mr. Al-Qusayr, announced the continuous release of feed supplies in response to directives from Prime Minister Dr. Mostafa Madbouly and in coordination with the Central Bank. He stated that during the period from July 20 to August 3, 2023, approximately 378,000 tons of corn and soybean were released, amounting to about $183 million. This effort aims to address feed supply needs and support the agricultural sector.
records.institution: Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

records.title: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) has signed a $77 million development loan agreement to establish a solar power plant in Belize, furt...
records.description: The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) has signed a $77 million development loan agreement to establish a solar power plant in Belize, furthering its commitment to supporting sustainable development in developing countries and Small Island Developing States (SIDS). The agreement underscores SFD's focus on clean energy in developing nations, aiming to build a 60-megawatt solar power plant that will reduce emissions, stimulate social and economic growth, improve electricity quality, and align with Sustainable Development Goals 7 (Affordable and clean energy) and 13 (climate action). This agreement reflects SFD's dedication to international cooperation, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company (ADQ) has partnered with Netherlands-based Safe Haven Solutions to establish a technologically ad...
records.description: Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company (ADQ) has partnered with Netherlands-based Safe Haven Solutions to establish a technologically advanced greenhouse at ADQ’s AgTech Park in KEZAD, aiming to enhance sustainable food production in the UAE. The automated 10-hectare facility, designed with sustainability in mind, will use an efficient cooling system for carbon and water footprint reduction, allowing year-round cultivation of tomatoes and cucumbers. In its second phase, the project will double the crop area to 20 hectares. The initiative focuses on offering high-quality local produce, reducing food waste, and nurturing local expertise. The collaboration is part of ADQ's AgTech Park efforts to drive domestic produce growth.

records.title: Kazakhstan is in discussions with Abu Dhabi Ports to establish a joint venture facilitating the transportation of Kazakh agricultural exp...
records.description: Kazakhstan is in discussions with Abu Dhabi Ports to establish a joint venture facilitating the transportation of Kazakh agricultural exports via Iran and Gulf ports, as announced by the Kazakh government. The country aims to ship its agricultural goods to Iranian Gulf ports, such as Amirabad and Bandar Abbas, using the Caspian Sea route, enabling further distribution to Gulf, Asian, and African destinations. Kazakh Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin engaged in talks regarding this initiative with Davood Tafti, CEO of Simatech Shipping and Forwarding, identified as a subsidiary of AD Ports Group. Traditionally exporting primarily to neighboring Central Asian countries, China, and Black Sea ports via Russia, this venture aims to diversify Kazakhstan's export routes.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: The animal feed production plant being undertaken by the Oman Flour Mills Company in the Muttrah region has reached 70% completion.
records.description: The animal feed production plant being undertaken by the Oman Flour Mills Company in the Muttrah region has reached 70% completion. This project aligns with Oman's Vision 2040, focusing on circular economy principles and local resource utilization. The plant employs locally available raw materials to produce various animal feed products in an economical and sustainable manner, contributing to food security. The factory's completion is anticipated by October 2023, featuring innovative technology and automation. The facility will be capable of producing 20 tonnes of animal feed per hour, including a pre-mixing unit to meet specific nutritional needs for different animal species. The project aims to enhance local livestock development, self-sufficiency in feed, and the quality of products while reducing dependence on imports, furthering the growth of Oman's agricultural and livestock sector.

records.title: According to a report by the Ministry of International Cooperation, the Saudi Arabia Grant Management Committee (SAGMC) has allocated $1....
records.description: According to a report by the Ministry of International Cooperation, the Saudi Arabia Grant Management Committee (SAGMC) has allocated $1.5 billion to fund projects across 27 governorates in Egypt. These projects aim to create approximately 17,000 job opportunities in sectors like industry, agriculture, livestock, healthcare, trade, and the industrial sector. The ministry's report emphasizes the ongoing efforts to enhance micro, small, and medium-sized projects through a sustainable cooperation agreement between SAGMC and the involved agency. This marks the third agreement between the parties, following two previous financing deals worth LE350 million.

records.title: The National Interprofessional Office of Cereals and Legumes (ONICL), Morocco's grains market regulator, has announced a reduction in gra...
records.description: The National Interprofessional Office of Cereals and Legumes (ONICL), Morocco's grains market regulator, has announced a reduction in grain subsidies for imported wheat, aiming to encourage wheat importers to seek cost-efficient suppliers. Starting from August 1, 2023, subsidies will be calculated based on the average cost prices of the lowest origin among Germany, Argentina, France, and the USA. This change follows a circular issued by ONICL in June, outlining a subsidy program to cover the difference between the cost of wheat and a reference import price of MAD 270 (US$27) per quintal, from July 1 to September 30, 2023. The policy shift is a response to last year's severe drought and aims to bolster Morocco's agricultural industry while safeguarding food security and the economy. The government's measures include 'The Generation Green Plan 2020-2030,' aiming to enhance food security for cereal crops, halting the common wheat import support program to alleviate inflation, and strengthening the certified seed sector. Morocco is a significant cereal importer, being the EU's largest wheat importer for the 2022/2023 agricultural campaign.
records.institution: The National Interprofessional Office of Cereals and Legumes (ONICL)

records.title: The UAE and Pakistan are working on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to boost bilateral trade and exports, creating...
records.description: The UAE and Pakistan are working on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to boost bilateral trade and exports, creating opportunities for entrepreneurs from both countries. Rashid Abdul Rehman Al Ali, Deputy Head of Mission of UAE Embassy, expressed optimism about Pakistan's economic future, citing increasing foreign direct investment (FDI) from UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and China. Al Ali highlighted UAE's interest in investing in Pakistan's agriculture, textiles, marble & tiles, gemstone, mining, and petroleum sectors. He emphasized the importance of strengthening government-to-government and business-to-business relations to explore new business opportunities.

records.title: In Jendouba, private investments have remarkably increased by 40.66%, reaching an impressive total of approximately TND 273 million as pa...
records.description: In Jendouba, private investments have remarkably increased by 40.66%, reaching an impressive total of approximately TND 273 million as part of the 2016-2020 development plan that spans a diverse array of sectors. Notably, the agricultural sector received a substantial allocation of TND 111 million. It's worth highlighting the noteworthy growth in investments for small-scale farmers in the agriculture domain, with annual approved amounts rising from TND 675,000 (2012-2017) to TND 1.8 million (2018-2022). The year 2022 witnessed the approval of 142 projects valued at TND 1.8 million specifically targeting small-scale farmers, complemented by additional subsidies amounting to TND 616 million. These investments have found their way into multiple sectors, including the livestock industry, agricultural machinery, fisheries, and agricultural irrigation equipment. This multifaceted investment approach underscores substantial strides in regional economic growth and diversification efforts.

records.domain: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
records.title: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment hosted the "Farmers' Forum" in Sharjah's Al Dhaid Cultural Center, aiming to foster dialog...
records.description: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment hosted the "Farmers' Forum" in Sharjah's Al Dhaid Cultural Center, aiming to foster dialogue with farmers and bolster local agricultural product marketing for increased food security and sustainability in the UAE. This initiative aligns with the Ministry's ongoing efforts to empower the national agricultural sector and support local farmers. Key figures from the Ministry and farmers from various regions attended the event, alongside partners like Emirates Development Bank and "Manbat." The forum facilitated discussions about challenges, solutions, market access, and sales outlets for national agricultural products. Emphasizing the UAE's commitment to sustainable food security, the forum showcased the nation's advancements in modern agricultural technology, and plans to integrate food sustainability with climate change initiatives. The dialogue underscored the importance of cooperation between stakeholders and initiatives that enhance the sustainability of national farms, striving to elevate local agricultural production, support farmers, and ensure a sustainable food future.
records.institution: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment

records.title: IVECO, in partnership with Arabian Auto Agency (AAA), successfully delivered 20 S-Way vehicles to Arabian Agricultural Services Company (...
records.description: IVECO, in partnership with Arabian Auto Agency (AAA), successfully delivered 20 S-Way vehicles to Arabian Agricultural Services Company (ARASCO) in Saudi Arabia. The handover took place during a ceremony in Dammam on June 8th. These vehicles, specifically IVECO S-Way AT440S47T, 4×2 tractors, will be locally assembled at AAA's Riyadh plant and deployed in ARASCO's fleet for transporting chicken feed. ARASCO is a prominent Saudi company specializing in high-quality animal feed products and is ranked among the top 100 companies in the country. With a strong presence in the food supply and security sector, ARASCO produces poultry, agricultural, veterinary, and animal farming products. Additionally, the company provides essential logistic services for handling and transporting agri-bulk commodities and finished goods.

records.title: The Public Investment Fund (PIF) has introduced Sawani Company, aiming to advance the Saudi camel farming industry by becoming a prominen...
records.description: The Public Investment Fund (PIF) has introduced Sawani Company, aiming to advance the Saudi camel farming industry by becoming a prominent producer of camel dairy products. Aligned with Vision 2030, the company seeks to enhance the domestic production ecosystem, modernize operations, and elevate standards by collaborating with the private sector and implementing cutting-edge technologies. PIF's strategic investments in the Food and Agriculture sector include the creation of the Saudi Coffee Company and the Halal Products Development Company. Sawani will prioritize sustainability in production, distribution, and marketing, promoting the health benefits of camel dairy while showcasing Saudi Arabia's cultural heritage in camel husbandry. Camel milk is recognized for its nutritional value, including minerals, vitamins, protein, and antioxidants. The establishment of Sawani aligns with Vision 2030's sustainable economic and social development goals.

records.title: India recently enforced a ban on lower-grade rice exports, including de-oiled rice bran, until November 30, in an effort to ensure suffic...
records.description: India recently enforced a ban on lower-grade rice exports, including de-oiled rice bran, until November 30, in an effort to ensure sufficient availability of non-basmati white rice in its domestic market and to control price inflation. The United Arab Emirates (UAE) swiftly followed suit by announcing its own four-month ban on rice exports and re-exports, which includes Indian-origin rice. These developments have disrupted the global food market, compounded by drought conditions in Thailand, the second-largest rice exporter, and Russia's withdrawal from the Black Sea Grain Initiative. The implications of India's ban on rice exports have led to concerns about global food inflation, particularly in regions highly dependent on Indian rice, like Sub-Saharan Africa and the Middle East. While UAE's move to protect its local market and India's ongoing monsoon season could potentially stabilize the rice market, there have been price fluctuations and supply challenges across various regions due to these export restrictions.

records.title: The UAE-Korea smart agriculture research collaboration aims to use the latest technology to detect infections and control factors affecti...
records.description: The UAE-Korea smart agriculture research collaboration aims to use the latest technology to detect infections and control factors affecting plant growth. Recently, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) delegation attended a scientific symposium in Korea to review joint research projects with the Rural Development Department of Korea. The symposium featured presentations from three ADAFSA researchers who discussed the outcomes of the Korean Protected House project. This project focuses on creating a smart cultivation system that utilizes advanced technologies to monitor and manage environmental factors impacting plant growth.
records.institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

records.title: During a meeting in Beijing, Chinese Premier Li Qiang and Mauritanian President Mohamed Ould Cheikh Ghazouani aimed to elevate their bila...
records.description: During a meeting in Beijing, Chinese Premier Li Qiang and Mauritanian President Mohamed Ould Cheikh Ghazouani aimed to elevate their bilateral cooperative relations. Both being developing nations, the leaders highlighted their shared stance on various global and regional matters, reinforcing their profound friendship. Collaborative plans were set in motion to intensify bilateral ties, with China expressing its commitment to aligning development strategies, sharing experiences, and supporting Mauritania's sovereignty and national integrity. They emphasized expanding practical cooperation in agriculture, fishery, animal husbandry, energy, and infrastructure through the Belt and Road initiative, while promoting cultural exchanges and mutual support for development and revitalization. President Ghazouani underscored the deep and solid friendship between the countries, thanking China for its backing of Mauritania's independence and development and expressing a commitment to strengthening cooperation in various fields.

records.title: Saudi humanitarian agency KSrelief has made a significant impact in Sudan by distributing 1,332 food baskets in Madani, the capital of Al...
records.description: Saudi humanitarian agency KSrelief has made a significant impact in Sudan by distributing 1,332 food baskets in Madani, the capital of Al-Gezira state, benefiting around 13,186 individuals. This initiative is a vital component of KSrelief's broader mission to enhance food security in Sudan and provide aid to those in need. Simultaneously, KSrelief successfully concluded an emergency medical project in Banjul, Gambia, enlisting the dedication of seven male and female volunteers. Over the course of the project, the medical team conducted 66 surgeries spanning gynecological oncology, vascular procedures, and pediatric interventions. This endeavor not only reinforces KSrelief's commitment to bolstering the Gambian medical sector but also aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 by cultivating a culture of volunteerism among its citizens.

records.title: The Jordan Valley Authority (JVA) is working on facilitating the leasing of agricultural facilities as per the 2022 bylaw.
records.description: The Jordan Valley Authority (JVA) is working on facilitating the leasing of agricultural facilities as per the 2022 bylaw. Currently, JVA has leased 3,843 dunums for fruit projects through 55 contracts, with more expected soon. Additionally, 18 investment project contracts have been signed for various purposes, including quarries, tourism, and commercial/industrial investments, covering 238 dunums in total.

records.title: As part of Egypt's presidential initiative "Decent Life," aiming to improve rural development and livelihoods of small farmers and breede...
records.description: As part of Egypt's presidential initiative "Decent Life," aiming to improve rural development and livelihoods of small farmers and breeders, a veterinary caravan treated livestock for small farmers in Beni Suef province from July 22 to 27. This effort aligns with the state's plan to enhance local cattle breeds, including through importing cattle or using imported semen for artificial insemination to increase meat and dairy production. Dr. Mustafa Fadel, Director of the Animal Reproduction Institute, highlighted the collaboration between the institute, veterinary departments, and livestock insurance funds, providing medical care, surgery, and treatment for thousands of animals, benefiting over 3,920 breeders and farmers. The initiative aims to uplift livestock production and enhance the local cattle sector.

records.domain: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
records.title: AAA Holding Group (AHG) is expanding its fertilizer plant in Khor al Zubair, Basra governorate, doubling its capacity to one million tons...
records.description: AAA Holding Group (AHG) is expanding its fertilizer plant in Khor al Zubair, Basra governorate, doubling its capacity to one million tons annually, with a new production line for di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) fertilizer. Construction is already underway, and the new line is expected to be operational by the end of September 2023. This investment is aimed at boosting Iraq's agricultural productivity, enhancing food security, and supporting the national economy. The Ministry of Agriculture will purchase all of the fertilizer produced at the expanded facility. Iraq has substantial phosphate deposits, and further investments are planned in phosphate mining in the region.

records.title: During a meeting at the 2nd United Nations Summit on Food Systems in Rome, Agriculture and Agrarian Reform Minister Mohammed Hassan Qatan...
records.description: During a meeting at the 2nd United Nations Summit on Food Systems in Rome, Agriculture and Agrarian Reform Minister Mohammed Hassan Qatana emphasized the importance of enhancing trade between regions and facilitating direct access for Syrian agricultural products to Saudi markets. Qatana highlighted the challenges faced by the Syrian agriculture sector due to unilateral coercive measures and discussed the difficulties encountered by Syrian trucks traveling to Saudi Arabia. He urged Saudi Arabia to participate in the Quartet Agreement signed by Syria, Jordan, Iraq, and Lebanon to strengthen trade cooperation and exchange of agricultural products. Saudi Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture Abdulrahman Al-Fadley welcomed the idea of reactivating memorandums of understanding between the two countries and underscored the strong relations between them.
records.institution: Syrian Agriculture and Agrarian Reform Ministry

records.title: Sharjah's Electricity, Water, and Gas Authority (SEWA) has teamed up with the Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC) to enhance en...
records.description: Sharjah's Electricity, Water, and Gas Authority (SEWA) has teamed up with the Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC) to enhance energy infrastructure and boost electricity production efficiency. They'll also implement low-carbon reverse osmosis water desalination plants to support the clean energy strategy and achieve the UAE's climate neutrality vision by 2050. Under the guidance of H.H. Dr. Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah, SEWA is committed to collaborating with various entities and using advanced technologies to support the UAE's Energy Strategy 2050, aiming to improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, and promote optimal energy consumption.
records.institution: Sharjah's Electricity, Water, and Gas Authority (SEWA)

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: The COP28 UAE Presidency has introduced its Food Systems and Agriculture Agenda, urging governments to sign the first-ever Leaders Declar...
records.description: The COP28 UAE Presidency has introduced its Food Systems and Agriculture Agenda, urging governments to sign the first-ever Leaders Declaration on Food Systems, Agriculture, and Climate Action during the Food Systems Summit in Rome. The Declaration aims to align national food systems and agriculture strategies with Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), and National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs). The COP28 Presidency is also calling for collaboration with stakeholders in the food and agriculture sector to accelerate initiatives across food systems, agriculture, and climate action. The Presidency aims to drive transformative change, promote regenerative agriculture, and contribute to the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030.

records.title: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) has been actively executing various projects across Yemen, including a wate...
records.description: The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) has been actively executing various projects across Yemen, including a water supply and environmental sanitation initiative to improve clean water accessibility. In the Al-Khawkhah directorate of Hodeidah, Yemen, the project successfully delivered over three million liters of water in June. This encompassed 1,890,000 liters of potable water and 1,890,000 liters of usable water, with 130 operations to clear waste from displaced camps and two cleaning campaigns for camp sanitation. Additionally, KSrelief's Mobile Medical Clinics attended to 698 beneficiaries in Yemen, addressing diverse medical needs. Meanwhile, KSrelief extended assistance to flood-affected regions in Pakistan, distributing 2,398 food parcels in Baluchistan and Pakhtunkhwa provinces. In Sudan, KSrelief's aid efforts persisted, delivering five tons and 355kg of food parcels to the city of Gedaref.

records.title: Tunisia's grain harvest for the year has fallen by 60% to 250,000 tonnes due to drought, resulting in financial challenges for the countr...
records.description: Tunisia's grain harvest for the year has fallen by 60% to 250,000 tonnes due to drought, resulting in financial challenges for the country as it seeks an international rescue package. The decline in the grain crop was anticipated by the farmers union, and a significant portion of the crop is durum wheat. The drought's impact has led to measures like cutting off nighttime drinking water in certain areas to curb consumption amid severe water scarcity.

records.title: Mauritania is set to receive $767,000 from the African Development Fund, a branch of the African Development Bank Group, to bolster its l...
records.description: Mauritania is set to receive $767,000 from the African Development Fund, a branch of the African Development Bank Group, to bolster its livestock farming industry - a crucial livelihood source in the country. The funding agreement, inked by Mauritania's Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development, Abdessalam Ould Mohamed Saleh, and the Bank Group's Deputy Director General for North Africa, Malinne Blomberg, initiates the implementation of the Inclusive Livestock Sector Development Project (AWKAR). This project focuses on enhancing agropastoral resources in the Hodh Chargui region's northeastern part (Dahr), addressing sector challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, limited regional services capacity, conflicts over natural resources, and low value addition. Livestock farming is pivotal for Mauritania's food security, with 60 to 70 percent of its populace relying on it for income. The project aligns with the African Development Bank's strategy to transform African agriculture, fostering competitive, inclusive agro-food sectors that improve living conditions while respecting the environment.

records.domain: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
records.title: Abu Dhabi's Masdar has successfully concluded its inaugural green bond issuance of $750 million, earmarked specifically to finance renewa...
records.description: Abu Dhabi's Masdar has successfully concluded its inaugural green bond issuance of $750 million, earmarked specifically to finance renewable projects in developing and climate-vulnerable nations. The oversubscribed 10-year unsecured notes witnessed an overwhelming response, reaching an order book of $4.2 billion, indicating substantial investor interest. With the majority of bonds allocated to international investors, this initiative aims to bolster climate finance and decarbonization efforts, a priority highlighted by Sultan Al-Jaber, the UAE Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology and Masdar's Chairman. Al-Jaber emphasized the importance of enabling more accessible and affordable finance for developing economies to meet sustainability objectives. This debut issuance adheres to Masdar's green finance framework, concentrating on crucial investments in developing economies and regions vulnerable to climate impacts. The proceeds will primarily fund renewable energy projects encompassing solar, wind, and renewable power transmission, underscoring Masdar's commitment to combating climate change while positively impacting local communities. Masdar's ambitious goals include expanding renewable energy capacity to 100 gigawatts and producing 1 million tons of green hydrogen annually by 2030, aligning with their commitment to sustainable development.

records.title: Dr.
records.description: Dr. Waleed Yahya, head of the Cotton Breeding Research Department at Egypt's Ministry of Agriculture, announced an expansion in cotton cultivation to 252,000 feddans in 2023, highlighting farmers' shift towards food and fodder crops due to global shortages. The Deputy of the Cotton Improvement Fund noted the government's focus on the textile industry, emphasizing the importance of cotton as a fiber and food source. This year, a climate-resistant cotton variety named "Giza 98" was cultivated in Sohag, boasting high yield and water-saving qualities. Additionally, colored cotton cultivation expanded in research stations, with Egypt standing out as a top global producer. Egyptian cotton is renowned for its quality and competitiveness on international markets.

records.title: Ethiopia and Egypt have declared their intention to finalize an agreement on the operations of Africa's largest dam within four months, m...
records.description: Ethiopia and Egypt have declared their intention to finalize an agreement on the operations of Africa's largest dam within four months, marking a significant advancement after years of unsuccessful talks. The announcement followed discussions between Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sissi during a regional meeting on the Sudan conflict. This breakthrough, as stated in a joint release by Ethiopia's government, offers hope in a dispute Cairo has deemed existential. The negotiations, including Sudan as a third party, concern the $4.6 billion Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam located near Sudan's border. While the statement doesn't specify the agreement's legal nature or the mediator's role, it underscores the progress made. Egypt relies on the Nile River for water supply, contrasting Ethiopia's view of the dam as a poverty-reducing effort. The ongoing discussions address unresolved issues such as potential disputes and water release during prolonged droughts downstream.

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has launched an emergency seeds distribution campaign to support farmer...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has launched an emergency seeds distribution campaign to support farmers in critical regions during the ongoing main crop production season (June – October 2023). In partnership with USAID's Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance, Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, and the Central Emergency Response Fund, FAO aims to aid over a million vulnerable farmers and families (5 million individuals) by providing 10,000 tonnes of sorghum, millet, groundnut, and sesame seeds across 17 States. Despite security and logistical challenges, FAO has already delivered 3.3 tonnes of seeds to 8 states and initiated distribution. The initiative is crucial to enabling farmers to plant and harvest up to 3 million tonnes of cereals by November–December 2023, fulfilling the cereal needs of approximately 13-19 million people. FAO's mission is to preserve livelihoods, ensure food access, and alleviate acute food insecurity in Sudan. With a goal of $95.4 million, FAO has garnered nearly $20 million to date, supporting various life-saving interventions for 15 million individuals, encompassing seed provision, farming equipment, and livestock protection.
records.institution: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

records.title: Dubai Investments and E20 Investment, an Abu Dhabi-based agribusiness investment company, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)...
records.description: Dubai Investments and E20 Investment, an Abu Dhabi-based agribusiness investment company, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to develop 3,750 hectares of agricultural land in Angola. The collaboration aims to cultivate rice and avocado crops, leveraging Angola's fertile soil and climate conditions for substantial yields. Over 18 months, the joint venture intends to create an agricultural hub, projecting 28,000 tons of rice and 5,500 tons of avocados. The initiative aligns with Dubai Investments' commitment to Angola's food security and economic value generation. E20 Investment's experience in managing large-scale agricultural projects and sustainable practices is expected to contribute to the project's efficiency and profitability, fostering economic diversification and sustainable growth.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's commitment to strengthening food security has received a notable boost through the Agricultural Development Fund's signing...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's commitment to strengthening food security has received a notable boost through the Agricultural Development Fund's signing of financing agreements totaling SR926 million ($246.8 million) in sectors including the feed industry, animal production, and dairy. These contracts are designed to provide essential financial support for importing key agricultural commodities like maize, soybeans, and barley, crucial for maintaining the nation's food reserves. The agreements encompass a range of initiatives, including the establishment of an agricultural product marketing center, cold storage facilities, and a broiler and poultry farming project. The Agricultural Development Fund, founded in 1961, plays a pivotal role in providing financial assistance to agricultural initiatives within the country, with the overarching goal of reinforcing food security, mitigating potential supply shortages, and ensuring the resilience of food supply chains.

records.title: When Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo, it marked the first visit by an Indi...
records.description: When Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo, it marked the first visit by an Indian head of state to Egypt since 1997. This summit aimed to bolster economic and diplomatic ties, especially important as emerging markets collaborate to address the impacts of global rising interest rates, inflation, and the shifting US foreign policy. Egypt seeks to enhance its economic recovery plan and attract investment, while India is striving to position itself as the voice of the Global South. Both nations aim to increase bilateral trade, economic cooperation, and political influence. This renewed relationship holds historical significance, harking back to their collaboration in the Non-Alignment movement. It could also potentially align with Egypt's interest in the BRICS expansion.

records.title: The Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO), in collaboration with the National Centre for Security and Crisis Mana...
records.description: The Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO), in collaboration with the National Centre for Security and Crisis Management (NCSCM), has initiated a training course to enhance the food security control system in Jordan. This training, held as part of the Technical Cooperation Programme (TCP), aims to empower 25 participants from various governmental departments with expertise in food security monitoring and reporting. The "Establishing a Food Security Monitoring and Reporting Dashboard for Jordan" project contributes to sustainable economic growth by bolstering data-driven decision-making, aligning with FAO's commitment to SDG2 (zero hunger). The initiative includes support from Jordan in managing food security crises and advancing resilient, sustainable sectors. The dashboard created will serve as a valuable tool for timely updates and crisis readiness, benefiting both Jordan and the region at large.
records.institution: National Centre for Security and Crisis Management (NCSCM)

records.title: Two leading Saudi science institutions, namely King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) and The National Research and D...
records.description: Two leading Saudi science institutions, namely King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) and The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah), have entered into a partnership aimed at advancing research in the field of food security. The memorandum of understanding, signed recently, seeks to bolster collaboration between the two entities. The partnership is centered around enhancing research endeavors and student training to enhance sustainable agricultural practices in Saudi Arabia. Specifically, the focus of the collaboration is to further the joint efforts of Estidamah and KAUST in studying sustainable planting methods, particularly for crucial crops in the Kingdom and the broader region.
records.institution: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture

records.title: Silal, a subsidiary of Abu Dhabi's state-owned company ADQ, has teamed up with Desolenator from the Netherlands to initiate a trial initi...
records.description: Silal, a subsidiary of Abu Dhabi's state-owned company ADQ, has teamed up with Desolenator from the Netherlands to initiate a trial initiative involving solar-powered desalination technology for producing clean water for irrigation purposes. With support from a 100 million UAE dirhams ($27.23 million) ADQ development fund, the project intends to play a role in reducing the carbon footprint of desalination, thus contributing to the decarbonization of food production in arid climates. By showcasing the potential of innovative collaborations, this project seeks to address the interconnected challenges of water, food, and energy while serving as a sustainable agriculture model that could be adopted globally. Notably, Desolenator also partnered with the Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) to create a solar energy-driven, carbon-neutral water purification and desalination system.

records.title: The Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock (SDAL) has partnered with Majid Al Futtaim's Carrefour to boost local agricultural an...
records.description: The Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock (SDAL) has partnered with Majid Al Futtaim's Carrefour to boost local agricultural and animal products, share expertise, and develop marketing strategies. This collaboration aligns with SDAL's strategy to enhance private sector ties, utilizing Carrefour's substantial experience in retail and marketing. By leveraging Carrefour's expertise, the partnership aims to diversify national agricultural offerings in its UAE stores, bolstering the local economy, improving food security, and aligning with the National Strategy for Food Security 2051. The agreement was formalized between SDAL's Dr. Khalifa Musabah Al Tunaiji and Majid Al Futtaim Retail's GCC COO, Bernardo Perloiro.
records.institution: The Sharjah Department of Agriculture and Livestock (SDAL)

records.title: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation El Sayed El Quseir held discussions with Mauritanian counterpart Yahya El Waqf to enhance bi...
records.description: Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation El Sayed El Quseir held discussions with Mauritanian counterpart Yahya El Waqf to enhance bilateral collaboration in various agricultural domains. El Quseir expressed Egypt's commitment to aiding Mauritania's agricultural progress through research, seed development for drought-resistant crops, advanced farming techniques, and water harvesting. The ministries aim to jointly produce high-quality date palms, with an upcoming cooperation protocol. El Waqf seeks Egypt's expertise in cultivating strategic crops, such as wheat, and dates. Both sides plan to establish a technical committee comprising agricultural experts from each nation to oversee joint projects and exchanges in agricultural guidance and staff training.

records.domain: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
records.title: Persistent droughts in Iraq, exacerbated by reduced river flow and overuse of water, have led farmers to turn to drilling desert wells fo...
records.description: Persistent droughts in Iraq, exacerbated by reduced river flow and overuse of water, have led farmers to turn to drilling desert wells for irrigation. This shift has allowed Iraq to double its wheat cultivation areas to address food security concerns, but experts warn that heavy use of these wells could deplete desert aquifers. Iraq's government is focusing on sustainable use of water, supporting modern irrigation systems, and engaging in water diplomacy with neighboring countries to increase river flows. While the desert well approach offers immediate relief, experts emphasize the need for long-term solutions to climate change impacts, including modernizing agriculture and revitalizing war-affected areas.

records.title: The Saudi EXIM Bank has established a SAR75-million [$20 million] credit line with the Iraqi Islamic Bank for Investment and Development,...
records.description: The Saudi EXIM Bank has established a SAR75-million [$20 million] credit line with the Iraqi Islamic Bank for Investment and Development, as part of efforts to enhance trade between the two countries and bolster Saudi exports to Iraq. The agreement aims to increase non-oil exports, improve global competitiveness, and minimize risk, while supporting financial institutions in both nations to provide funding for Iraqi importers of Saudi goods. The partnership aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals of raising non-oil exports in the country's GDP. Mutual trade between the nations has been growing, driven by the quality reputation of Saudi products in Iraq.
records.institution: Iraqi Islamic Bank for Investment and Development

records.title: Yemen's government, recognized internationally, has imposed a ban on the export of fruits and vegetables to alleviate rising prices durin...
records.description: Yemen's government, recognized internationally, has imposed a ban on the export of fruits and vegetables to alleviate rising prices during the holy month of Ramzan. The Ministry of Industry and Trade, situated in Aden, issued the decree, aiming to ensure a stable domestic market and lower consumer prices. Aden and neighboring provinces have experienced significant price hikes for essential goods, worsening the economic crisis in Yemen due to the prolonged civil war. The conflict, ongoing since 2014, has led to famine, high prices, and food supply disruptions, leaving millions without proper nourishment. Yemen's agricultural exports, valuable to neighboring Gulf nations, have diminished in local markets.
records.institution: Yemeni Ministry of Industry and Trade

records.title: Yemen's recognized government has ceased fresh fish exports due to local market shortages and soaring prices.
records.description: Yemen's recognized government has ceased fresh fish exports due to local market shortages and soaring prices. Major Salem Abdullah Al-Soqotri, the Minister of Agriculture, Irrigation, and Fisheries, has issued a directive prohibiting fish exports by land, sea, and air ports. An operations room has been set up to monitor the decision's implementation, providing updates on fish prices, local supply, and catches. The move follows public outcry as fish prices reached record highs, attributed to the devalued riyal and supply scarcity. The ban seeks to balance local supplies and exports, involving local authorities and engaging stakeholders. Despite the ban, high fish prices continue due to limited supply, overfishing, and increased costs. The ban's efficacy is doubted given past unenforced decisions. Yemen annually exports fish to Saudi Arabia and the EU. Local consumers cope by switching to cheaper alternatives or reducing fish consumption due to the inflated prices.
records.institution: Yemeni Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation, and Fisheries

records.title: Morocco and Mauritania have solidified their collaborative efforts in fisheries research through a specialized cooperation protocol, sign...
records.description: Morocco and Mauritania have solidified their collaborative efforts in fisheries research through a specialized cooperation protocol, signed during the 6th International Fair Halieutis in Agadir from February 1 to 5. The accord, established between Morocco's National Institute of Fisheries Research (INRH) and Mauritania's Institute of Oceanographic Research and Fisheries (IMROP), aims to enhance assessment processes and bio-ecological studies of fish stocks, expand understanding of biodiversity and critical ecological habitats, and intensify collaborative investigations into climate and human-induced impacts on shared ecosystems. This agreement also focuses on aligning data collection and processing methods, reinforcing socio-economic studies on shared challenges, and promoting the exchange of insights on aquaculture development. The protocol serves to operationalize commitments outlined in the overarching cooperation framework, initially forged on October 3, 2022, in Nouakchott, between INRH and IMROP.

records.title: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has partnered with US-based AeroFarms to establish a company in Riyadh, focusing on indoor ve...
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has partnered with US-based AeroFarms to establish a company in Riyadh, focusing on indoor vertical farms in the Kingdom and the wider Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. The joint venture will utilize AeroFarms' proprietary smart agriculture technology platform, AgTech, to produce high-quality crops year-round, optimizing natural resources such as water and agricultural lands. Indoor vertical farming eliminates the need for arable land, resulting in significantly higher yields and up to 95 percent less water usage compared to traditional field farming, as stated by PIF. Over the next few years, the joint venture plans to build and operate multiple farms across the region. The first farm in Saudi Arabia, expected to be the MENA region's largest indoor vertical farm, will have an annual production capacity of up to 1.1 million kilos of agricultural crops.
